'¡Les aseguro que tengo información de excelente fuente de que en sus viajes Bilbo se encontró con un enorme oso! Sí, un oso enorme, nada que ver con los pequeños osos que viven por aquí. ¿Y qué hizo Bilbo?
'No, no seas imbécil, el oso no se lo comió de un bocado. ¡Imagínate la indigestión con todos esos botones de cobre!
'Ahora, Bilbo puede que no sea un hobbit respetable, pero sigue siendo un hobbit, y eso significa que llevaba consigo una gran cantidad de cosas deliciosas que ese oso nunca había olido o probado antes. Con eso, el astuto Bilbo domó a ese oso, ¡de hecho lo hizo! Y eso no es todo, no, no es así. Justo llegamos a la mejor parte, si lo crees.
'Radagast el Pardo, ¿has oído hablar de él? Guardián de los animales dicen y un mago respetable por derecho propio, bueno, Radagast escuchó sobre Bilbo y el oso y estaba tan impresionado que entrenó al viejo Bilbo para que se convirtiera en un Sabio.
'Ni bromeando ni jugando estoy hablando en serio, así es, el primer Sabio Hobbit es nuestro Bilbo, y ahora cabalga por ahí en su gran oso, acompañando a Radagast por todas las tierras!'
'¿Qué es eso? Oh, ¿te preguntas dónde está Bilbo ahora? ¡Resulta que has preguntado a la hobbit correcta!'

'¿Quieres saber dónde se ha metido Bilbo? Bueno, si preguntas por aquí, la gente te contará todo tipo de tonterías. ¡Que lo secuestraron o que vuela en su propio dragón o que lidera una tribu de arañas guerreras!
'La credulidad de los hobbits a veces es increíble. Se aferran a cualquier historia que escuchan, ¡y cuanto más exótica, mejor! ¿Puedes imaginar a Bilbo haciendo alguna de esas cosas a su edad? ¡Dios mío, es un hobbit único pero tiene límites!
'Puedo ver que eres del tipo sensato, así que te diré la verdad real: Bilbo siempre ha tenido una terrible afición por los Elfos. Francamente inquietante si me preguntas, pero él nunca fue de los que se preocupan por las convenciones. De todos modos, decidió pasar el resto de sus días con ellos, ¡invitado por los líderes elfos y todo!
'Ha pasado sus años de declive viviendo con ellos y disfrutando de su hospitalidad, mientras escribe sus memorias en forma de una obra de un solo acto “Donde hay Smaug, hay fuego.” He oído que la Gala de la Hermandad de la Brigada del Cubo Benevolente para los Magullados y Quemados de Los Gamos tiene los derechos exclusivos para la apertura!'
'¿Buscas historias sobre Bilbo, verdad? Bueno, como cartero, conozco a la mayoría de la gente y escucho muchas cosas. Sin duda puedo dedicar un poco de tiempo para contarte un relato.'

'Sigun me cortejó primero, ¿saben?, pero era a Sigmar a quien amaba. Pero Sigmar estaba celoso y pensaba que Sigun todavía intentaba reclamarme.
'No podía soportar tales tonterías. No me arrepiento de haber rechazado a ninguno de los dos hombres, porque mi difunto esposo tenía más sentido que ambos juntos.
'¡Imagínense! Todavía están usando esta disputa como excusa para pelear como niños, cuando todo lo que su madre o su padre alguna vez quiso fue verlos reconciliados. Han alejado a todos. Es una locura.'

'¡Esta casa debería ser mía, sin importar lo que diga el testamento de mi padre! Después de todo, soy el mayor. Si me voy, ese hermano mío intentará arrebatármela, como hizo con Elfwyn hace tantos años.
'No, debo permanecer aquí y vigilarlo, porque no confío en él.'

'El testamento de mi padre no estaba claro, y por lo tanto ninguno de los dos o ambos somos dueños de esta casa. Mi hermano quiere quedársela para sí mismo, tal como intentó hacer con Elfwyn hace tantos años.
'Nunca pudo permitirme tener nada para mí. Pensaba que todo le pertenecía por derecho.
'No, no me iré. Se mudará y cambiará las cerraduras en cuanto yo desvíe la mirada.'

Le cuentas a Mágla sobre tus tratos con los comerciantes y Hildulf.

Nunca ha sido de los que se alteran por los acontecimientos fortuitos de un día, para bien o para mal. Y todos estos tratos sospechosos con el aprendiz, los caballos desaparecidos y los envíos fallidos... algo se está tramando aquí, ${PLAYER}.
'Comencemos con Hildulf. Tráelo aquí, y veremos qué tiene que decir sobre estos asuntos.'

'Hildulf se ha ido, ¿no es así?
'Eso pensé por lo que me contaste antes, ${PLAYER}. Por mi parte, envié a unos guardias a su casa tan pronto como te fuiste, y me informaron que su hogar había sido destrozado como si se hubiera marchado con gran prisa. Entre sus pertenencias, encontraron los restos destrozados de una nota firmada por Lengua de Serpiente.
'Creo que hemos encontrado a nuestro traidor, ${PLAYER}.'

'Ahora bien, ¿qué es lo que Mágla quiere que hagas? ¿Ayudarnos? Seguro que no puede ser todo... ${PLAYER}, si querías pasar más tiempo con nosotros, ¡no tenías más que pedirlo!
'Los comerciantes son más que capaces de gestionar sus propios asuntos, pero si insistes en ayudar, ¿quién soy yo para detenerte? Folcbur, Déorwald y Béored están muy ocupados, pero, llámalo mala suerte si quieres, todos han tenido problemas desagradables últimamente. 'Quizá sea bueno que hayas venido a ayudarlos entonces... ¡porque quién sabe qué otros problemas podrías ayudarles a evitar!'

'Bah. ¿Qué quieres?'

'¡Ay de nuestro destino! ¡Qué época tan desgraciada! ¿Por qué debe suceder esto ahora, en mi vida?
'Justa Edoras, Justa Edoras, Ciudad de la tristeza, Qué lejos has caído desde Brego y Eorl.'

'¿Cómo podemos esperar ganar esta guerra? Piensa en estos versos:
'Justa Meduseld, Justa Meduseld, Allí se sienta el rey marchito, Desde allí da órdenes Lengua de serpiente, según dicen.
'Es tan cierto. Sin líder nos desmoronaremos.'

'Corremos hacia El Sagrario, pero Rohan arderá de todos modos. Los fuegos de los Orcos nos perseguirán allí, después de que lleguen aquí. Mejor que muramos en nuestro glorioso hogar....
'Hermoso Rohan, Querido Rohan, Llanuras de verde y oro, ¿Cuánto tiempo hasta que las hierbas se quemen negras y carbonizadas?'

'El fin llegará para nosotros, ya sea en Dunharrow o aquí....
'Es la guerra, es la guerra, La marea sube alta, Viene a ahogar a los últimos Jinetes en fuego y sangre.'

'Lo sé, lo sé. Debería estar empacando para el viaje. Pero no puedo obligarme a hacerlo.
'Justa Edoras, Gran Edoras, No nos envíes lejos de casa. ¿Qué quedará a nuestro regreso?'

'¿Te gustaría escuchar una canción antes de partir, ${PLAYERNAME:viajero[m]|viajera[f]}? Aquí está la favorita del momento:

El Uruk nota tu confusión y levanta su arma.
'Bueno, si no estás involucrado, ¡entonces te toca!'

'Y yo estaba a punto de reprender al muchacho por tardar en regresar... qué pérdida.

'Con mi tío Théoden llevando la guerra a Saruman, quedan muchas cosas por hacer en el Oestemnet.
'Al este, el fuerte fluvial de Vado del Entaguas se encuentra a lo largo de las orillas del Entaguas, y ha mantenido el Vado durante años incontables. El Thane Edric comanda el puesto y cuenta con pocos hombres a su servicio. La Mano Blanca ha presionado en las tierras del Rey últimamente, y el costo de perder el Vado sería incalculable.
'Tengo muchos asuntos que atender en lugar de mi tío, pero sé que esta es una tarea para la que tus habilidades son adecuadas. Si me ayudas, prepararé tu corcel para el viaje de inmediato.'

'Esto es interesante. No sé si hay alguna conexión, pero vale la pena investigarlo.
'Este tótem podría haber sido hecho como una broma, o podría haber algo más malévolo detrás de él.'

'No vemos mucho tumulto aquí, pero me imagino que los Orcos no consideran que los pantanos sean de gran ventaja.
'No quiero ser brusco contigo, pero tengo mucho que hacer. ¡Estos pollos me mantienen ocupado!'

'No era un jabalí gigante... al menos no uno que todavía esté vivo. Salí a dar un paseo para despejar mi mente y casi tropiezo con él.
'Me sorprendió un poco, porque había un cráneo de jabalí asegurado a un tocón de árbol con una cuerda, y había otros huesos por todas partes. Corrí de regreso aquí lo más rápido que pude.
'No estoy segura de quién hizo esa cosa horrible. Podrían ser los Orcos, pero no puedo estar segura.'

'Querida mujer, por favor perdóname, pero debes excusarme de tus elogios. No soy más que un Juglar ocioso, revolcándome en sombrías predicciones. Solo es ${PLAYERNAME:digno[m]|digna[f]} de tus amables palabras.
'He aprendido hoy que el heroísmo toma muchas formas. Puede que no tenga habilidad con la espada, pero si puedo inspirar a nuestro pueblo durante este tiempo difícil, será suficiente.'

Has inspirado a Atwald a ser más positivo e inspirar a sus compañeros Rohirrim en lugar de deprimirlos. Todos los corazones están cargados de tristeza en Edoras, y lo último que la gente necesita es estar abrumada por más pensamientos tristes.

'Nunca en mi vida he estado tan agradecido de ver una tarea completada. ¿Es realmente así como eliges pasar tu tiempo? Nunca podría soportar tal tedio miserable.
'Supongo que mi propia situación se ve bastante mejor en comparación. Al menos te concedo eso. Tal vez mi próxima canción toque el tema:
'No te preocupes por la guerra, Porque tu vida no es aburrida. Tus días podrían ser peores, Si el tedio es tu maldición.'

Céolthryth estalla en lágrimas cuando le entregas las hierbas y las pieles.
'¡Oh, cielos! ¡Tú y Atwald sois demasiado amables con esta inútil anciana! Gracias, queridos.
'Los demás me ven como una carga molesta, un saco al que ignorar, pero me habéis hecho útil de nuevo, y además me habéis traído hierbas calmantes para mis doloridas manos. ¡Una vez fui una excelente costurera, pero ahora... la vejez me lo ha arrebatado todo.'

'Vamos... ¿de verdad? ¿Esta es tu obra heroica? Está sucia, lo admito, y también aburrida. La anciana no tiene preocupaciones: la llevarán a El Sagrario sin ningún esfuerzo. Debería considerarse afortunada.
'Si prometo dejar de cantar canciones amargas, ¿me liberarás de este tedio?'

'¡Oh, joven ${RACE}! ¿Me ayudarías? Quiero ser más que un saco en un carro durante el viaje a El Sagrario, pero no tengo nada que me ocupe.
'¿Serías tan amable de traerme algunas pieles de las bestias que deambulan por las Tierras del Rey? Puedo coser mantas y capas mientras viajo.'

'Elda said that he diverted monies elsewhere? But who else is protecting the city, if not the city guard? My father trusted this man and paid for it with his life....
'He either kept that money and is a thief, or he gave it to someone, as he said, and is a traitor.'

'The advisor responsible for funding the protection of the city put those funds elsewhere? He should hope that I never see him again. However, if anyone is truly to blame, it is Reeve Heremond for entrusting someone like that to handle such important affairs.
'You have my thanks for uncovering this plot.'

'${PLAYER}, you have my thanks. Collecting these supplies was no small task, but I am afraid that I have not much to repay you with.
'I still find it difficult to believe that the Reeve would not set aside funding for the city guard. You seem to be in good standing with his advisors. Could you speak with them for me to determine why we are receiving so little support?'

'That is not possible. I know for certain that my father set aside a considerable portion of the city's monies to fund the guard. It is vital for any city.
'Where did the money go if not to the guards? Elda has been involved in the planning for some time, and perhaps he knows what happened. Please find him and speak with him about this.'

'Begone, I have nothing to say to you. Are you accusing me of thievery? You have no evidence and are fortunate that I do not dispose of you right now.
'I was instructed to fund the city's protection. I diverted funding to those who could actually protect us. The guards do naught, and I am not afraid to say it. Tell him what you want. I do not fear him... or you.'

Talk to Gifemund

'You are not the first Gifemund has sent here with offers. He is conniving, and I want nothing to do with it. He is a powerful man, but he is also a wealthy man with a greedy heart. How can I trust his judgement, especially with my life or shop on the line? I will trust the guards.'

'Are you here to threaten me too? I mean no offence to you, ${CLASS}. You seem of a better kind than the last fool Gifemund sent with this offer. I cannot trust him or the guards.
'What are we to do if we cannot afford to leave and cannot trust those who should protect us? Where is Reeve Heremond to put an end to this?'

'It is an interesting offer, and one I must consider. It is true that the guards do not seem able to protect us, but I wonder what price he will demand when the time comes. He is a wise merchant, and this service will not be free.
'I accept, though I may regret this decision someday. I only hope the price is not too high when he comes to collect it.'

'This is not only an offer of protection, it is leverage to obtain what he wants. From what we have heard, Gifemund speaks true when he says that the guards are not doing enough... and my own family was but one example of that.
'This offer of protection is dubious at best and is likely only a bid for power.'

'They have a right to be suspicious. I have my motives, as do you. I simply offered what I have as a courtesy, but they are right... it is not free. I would not be the man I am today if I gave anything for free.
'Now that more have seen the wisdom of my offer, I may yet be able to achieve my goals....'

'It is important that the people of Woodhurst feel safe again. I think safety is something that I can provide. It is known that the guards are struggling to maintain control and will sometimes avert their eyes when they should not.

'At least Elda had the courtesy of resigning, but if he returns he will have much to answer for. I am concerned that he could unravel everything that we have done, but I must trust that he told you the truth and will keep my secrets safe.
'His service to Gifemund is also concerning, for they make a powerful alliance that could unite Woodhurst behind them. For now, I need you to work for Gifemund and learn what he is up to....'

'I have seen what you are doing for Gifemund, and I may have been wrong about you. I have been harsh towards you on a number of occasions, but you may yet prove useful. I still have my eye on you, though.
'I need you to deliver a letter for me. It has come time for me to step down as an advisor and better fulfil my role here.
'I now work with Gifemund, but I will not betray Herubrand's secrets. They are safe with me.'

'You accept my offer? Then I welcome you, ${CLASS}. I will not deceive you: I have had my eye upon the seat of power here in Woodhurst for some time. I think you can help me acquire it.
'First, anyone who serves me must dedicate some time in my mine. Anything good in this life comes from hard work and dedication. Even Elda spent time there when he first came to me. Speak with the overseer there when you are ready.'

'Se han ido, ${PLAYER}.
'Mientras preparabas las carretas, mis guardias reunieron a la gente. Ahora pueden marcharse con un atisbo de esperanza de que les esperan días mejores.

La mirada fría de Mágla delata una gran inquietud.
'${PLAYER}, prepara las carretas, por favor. El tiempo se agota para que mi gente viaje a Edoras, y no quisiera que permanecieran aquí más tiempo del necesario.

'¿Mamá dice que puedo quedarme con su espada?
Séoca coge la espada y la gira, observando cómo cambian los reflejos con una mirada de fascinación en el rostro.

'¿Qué es esto?'
'¿Has hablado con mi familia?'
'¿Has preparado las carretas?'

'Fue Hildulf...
'Debería haberlo sabido, viendo cómo se han ido agotando nuestros recursos estas últimas semanas. El miserable pretendía hacernos morir de hambre entregando nuestros bienes al Enemigo, ¡malditas sean tales artimañas! Que se vaya, y mientras recupera el sentido, mi gente se dirigirá a Edoras.
'${PLAYER}, queda un asunto pendiente antes de que pueda despedir a mi pueblo. Quiero que traigas a mi mujer y a mi hijo a mi lado, en este salón. Debo hablar con ellos antes de que sea demasiado tarde.
'Los encontrarás en mi casa, y por favor date prisa.'

'¿Dices que mi esposo desea vernos en el salón?
'Muy bien, Séoca y yo nos dirigiremos allí tan pronto como podamos, pero... me gustaría pedirte que me ayudaras con algo primero.
'Mi esposo ya no puede empuñar una espada como antes, y le ha preocupado mucho quedarse de brazos cruzados mientras se libran y se ganan batallas. Séoca está a punto de alcanzar la mayoría de edad, y me gustaría que empuñara la espada de Mágla para que su legado como guerrero pueda comenzar de nuevo.
'La espada está arriba, en nuestra habitación, y aunque a Mágla no le gusta verla, la encontrarás allí.'

Talk to Gifemund

'Hildegard's gifted insight is hard to understand, but seems so clear to her. That she said there is more than one champion of Woodhurst is interesting, because I must be one of them. But who is the other... or others?
'The enemy unopposed must be Guard-captain Thurferth. It is as I thought, and the time has come to oust him from this city.'
The grim words Hildegard shared with you are invaluable, and you should inform Herubrand

Hildegard the soothsayer resides in a cave on the cliff overlooking Woodhurst.
Gifemund asked you to speak with Hildegard the Soothsayer on his behalf.

Herubrand is in the cellar of the farmhouse.

Talk to the soothsayer
Habla con Herubrand

'I see many things... some things clearer than others. I saw you with Herubrand, yet you come to me now seeking my vision for another man. You come with payment from him?
'Darkness grows below, as hate rules the minds of most. The champions of Woodhurst squabble while the true enemy remains unopposed. The city will fall before it is saved.'

'The soothsayer, Hildegard, has a unique gift. She may be able to reveal things unseen to me and those of my cause. I feel my position is strong, but if I move too hastily, I might risk everything.
'Please, take this payment to her and ask her to speak of what she sees in my future.'

'Hildegard speaks in riddles, but I have found her words to be surprisingly truthful. Her telling was grim and does not bode well for us. I must ponder the meaning behind her words. You should return to Gifemund, since he paid handsomely for that information.'
Hildegard and the Fate of Woodhurst

Gifemund awaits your return in the ore refinery near the centre of Woodhurst.
Herubrand bade you return to Gifemund with Hildegard's words.
The wealthy merchant Gifemund is in a strong position to make a move for the throne of Woodhurst, but is uncertain of the situation and seeks perspective from an unusual source.
Bring the letter to Herubrand

'This is bold and will likely result in a confrontation. It was a gamble for Gifemund to do this, and it seems that they are vying for my seat. Are they the champions Hildegard said would squabble?
'I suspect this conflict will become bloody. They now fight for the seat of my father, but I am still too weak to claim it myself. I shall wait to decide who receives my support until I hear their perspectives.'

Guard-captain Thurferth is near the fountain around the centre of Woodhurst.
You should bring the letter to Guard-captain Thurferth.

Herubrand is in the cellar of the farmhouse.
Herubrand would probably like to see the letter Gifemund prepared for Thurferth.
Bring the letter to Guard-captain Thurferth

'I assume this letter is a poor jest. That man has no leverage to threaten me and certainly cannot remove me from my post.
'He claims that I drove the Rohirrim out of this city? I will admit, I do not favour them and prefer we no longer exile the Dunlendings in lower Woodhurst. I will face his challenge for the seat in Woodhurst, as I have just as much claim as he.'

'The time has come to confront Guard-captain Thurferth. Since I have taken it upon myself to provide protection to the city, his services and influence are no longer needed.
'Elda and I have prepared a letter that lists the terms of his removal from his post. Please deliver this letter to him as soon as you can. If he does not leave quietly, then he must be removed by force... let us hope it does not come to that.'
The Ultimatum to Guard-captain Thurferth
The wealthy merchant Gifemund has determined that he feels Thurferth is a direct threat to his designs for the seat of Woodhurst. A confrontation is imminent.

'Todavía no puedo evitar sentirme triste; sin embargo, me doy cuenta de que tengo suerte de tener mi vida después de haber sido capturada por esos horribles Orcos. Sé que con el tiempo el dolor disminuirá, pero por ahora no puedo evitar lamentar mi desgracia.
'No debería agobiarte tanto con mis problemas. No puedo agradecerte lo suficiente por tu valentía y honor. No hay forma de saber lo que esos Orcos habrían hecho si no hubieras llegado.'

'Ahora que has despejado un camino a través del campamento, creo que será seguro para mí irme.
'Viajaré a Atalaya de la Almenara, ya que está más cerca y mejor fortificada que la Frontera de los Pantanos. Hay un lugar cerca del Salón del Hidromiel que tiene vistas al Bosque de Firien. Me gusta ir allí cuando necesito estar sola.
'La Atalaya de la Almenara está justo al sur por la carretera. Encuéntrame allí cuando hayas terminado aquí.'

Habla con el Thane Cútha

'¡Cómo puede el Thane Cútha permitir que esto ocurra bajo su vigilancia! Entiendo que está obligado por el deber, pero hay algunos asuntos que deben tener prioridad.
'Permítame un momento para pensar.'

'Agradezco que me haya traído esto a mi atención; sin embargo, ¿entiende que soy el Thane Cútha de la Atalaya de la Almenara y que estoy obligado a esta guardia?
'Mi único deber es vigilar la iluminación de Halifirien. Si esa almenara se enciende, cabalgaré personalmente hacia el este. Además, no he oído hablar de estos Orcos. No pueden ser un gran problema.
'Lo siento, pero no podemos proporcionarle ninguna ayuda en este momento. Sin embargo, le doy permiso para actuar como considere oportuno si considera que estos Orcos representan una amenaza.'

El Thane Cútha se encuentra en el Salón del Hidromiel de la Atalaya de la Almenara.

'Esta tribu del Jabalí es peligrosa y debe ser tratada con rapidez. Me temo que si no se les detiene pronto, solo se harán más fuertes.
'Nuestros números aquí en el Folde Este son bajos y no se esperan refuerzos en el corto plazo.
'Ve a hablar con el Thane Cútha en la Atalaya de la Almenara y pide los efectivos que pueda ofrecer para ayudar en esta empresa.'

'¡Ella me va a echar de casa! No puedo encontrar mi anillo por ningún lado. He estado entregando heno durante muchos veranos y nunca lo he perdido. Apuesto a que está cerca de uno de los montones de heno... pero ¿cuál?
'Debo empezar a preparar la cena. Si no lo hago, estaré en problemas aún mayores de los que ya tengo.

'I believe he is sincere in providing adequate protection and in his desire to bring everyone in Woodhurst together. However, the soothsayer mentioned a growing darkness, and someone or something powerful is working against us, driving our people apart.
'I agree with his sentiment that our Rohirrim and Dunlending brothers should be able to co-exist. Most in this city have the blood of both. I believe they are who Gifemund seeks to align to his cause more than anyone else.'

'I cannot believe they are gone....
'I am devastated by what is happening to this once fair city. Stuck in this cellar, I am unable to take in the beauty of Woodhurst. But, it would be hard to enjoy such beauty when surrounded by malice and the blood of my family and friends. The violence is a stark contrast to the beauty this city holds.
'Please speak with Gifemund about his security efforts here in Woodhurst. We must do something about this.'

'I am sad to hear that Woodhurst has lost more good men. We were not watching those fields as closely as we should have, and it seems we are too late now. The fields will be watched from now on.

Talk to Thane Nothmar

'I have tried arguing with these guards, but to no avail. It has taken all day to get to the front of this line, and my children are hungry and restless! I do not understand why they demand so much just to enter and make camp.'

'There is nothing I can do. My hands are tied. You can shout at me as well, if you would like. My duty is to keep trouble out of Gapholt, and we cannot be too cautious. I simply need their papers.
'Anyone seeking refuge here needs papers, but you are seeking aid for Woodhurst? That is a matter you must bring to the Thane.'

'There is irony in the fact that Woodhurst has fallen to those the ruling family swore were 'brothers.' I have told them many times the Dunlending half-bloods cannot be trusted. Can you not see the destruction below us? I have no men to spare for a hopeless Woodhurst!
'Woodhurst fell through the greed of Rohirrim and an invasion force? You have a valid point. We cannot risk being trapped here. My bitterness towards Herubrand and his father clouded my judgement. I will bring aid to them, but only if you help my men prepare Gapholt for an attack, should an attack come while we are gone.'

'I am torn in this decision. I have said that I would aid Woodhurst, but their fall was of their own doing. It was inevitable, yet now I must help clean up the mess they made?
'I worry for Gapholt. We are ill-prepared for a serious attack by the armies of the White Hand. I will depart with some of my men, but only if we are better prepared for an attack.'

'We have been waiting in this line for too long. Why must we wait? I can see empty places over there for us to set camp, yet we must wait here on this bridge...for what?
'I may just stake my tent here and make them move me when they are ready to finally acknowledge my presence!'
'Very well. As promised, you will have my aid. I will gather the men, and we will soon depart for Woodhurst.'

'This is absurd! How long must we wait?
'I think the horses in this line are more agitated than I am. We cannot have any horses become unruly on this bridge, or we may lose all of them!'

Gapholt is south and west of Woodhurst, nestled on a cliff well above the Gap of Rohan.
Gapholt is one of the few places still untouched by the war that surrounds it and has become a safe haven for Rohirrim refugees.

'It pains me to ask this of you. The Thane in Gapholt has long despised my family and will blame me and my father for allowing the city to fall; however, we need his aid now more than ever.
'He is of pure Rohirrim blood, which is rare in these parts, and is not understanding of the Dunlending half-bloods. Please leave for Gapholt at once and try to convince him to aid us.'

Speak with Gandalf in the Westfold

'I passed the wizard Gandalf upon the road not long ago, and he mentioned that he wishes to speak with you. The king is in the Westfold, at Helm's Deep -- he braces for war!
'Will you ride to him? Gandalf is apparently searching high and low for Erkenbrand, Elfhelm, Grimbold, and all their company. He needs your help.'
'We meet again! Good, I am glad. I have great need of you. The more eyes I have out upon the plains, the better.'
To the Westfold

Find Oter in the Stonedeans

'I have just come from the Stonedeans. A fellow I met on the road there, Oter, told me of the many problems afflicting those folk.
'It would seem that people are beginning to flee the land. Who will help them, when everyone is looking west to the Fords and to Helm's Deep?'

'Beware, traveller! We are trying to flee this land, and I hate to see unwary folk risk their lives by going in.
'You are here to help, are you? Well! That is a surprise unlooked-for!'
To the Stonedeans
A scout has just come from the Stonedeans, and it would seem that the people of that land are in need of aid.
Noticias del Valle Sagrado

'Ah, so Ellen has made ready the preparations?
'I am glad to hear such tidings. She and I have not seen eye to eye on many matters, but surely, we both see the importance of sheltering the people of Rohan from harm.
'When we have made ready here in Edoras, we can begin our journey to Dunharrow!'

Éowyn can be found outside Meduseld in Edoras.

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}! I have heard of trouble in the Broadacres, but I must continue my search for Erkenbrand, Grimbold, and Elfhelm, for I can find no trace of them since the Fords.

Habla con el Thane Cútha

'Sé que el Thane está obligado por su deber, pero no me di cuenta de que también carecía de corazón. Parece que debemos prescindir de su ayuda.
'Cúthing anticipó esto y ha estado trabajando en un plan para atacar a la tribu del Jabalí.'

'Es desafortunado escuchar lo que le ocurrió a mi hijo y a su grupo de caza, pero eso no cambia mi posición.
'Como ya he dicho, como Thane de Atalaya de la Almenara, mi único deber es vigilar Halifirien y cabalgar hacia el oeste cuando se encienda la señal.
'Haré una pequeña concesión: permitiré que Cúthing ayude en la medida de sus posibilidades. Ahora déjenme, debo volver a mi vigilancia.'

'Ahora tenemos más información que la última vez que hablamos con el Thane Cútha. Quizás reconsidere su posición.

Habla con Aragorn y aprende sobre el Mérito
Batallas Épicas: Entrenamiento Básico

'Contar con la mera supervivencia de la batalla sería un éxito, dado los enemigos desplegados ante nosotros, pero la victoria más verdadera es aquella en la que superamos todos los desafíos que trae la batalla. 'A medida que la batalla fluye y refluye, se nos pueden presentar objetivos secundarios opcionales. 'Estos no son necesarios para la victoria, pero completarlos con éxito añadirá al Mérito que ganemos en la batalla: la medida de nuestra victoria.'
'Es muy complicado, pero creo entender lo que Aragorn nos ha dicho. ¡Lo haremos bien, ${PLAYER}, estoy seguro de ello!'

'Hemos luchado contra grandes cantidades de enemigos antes, ¡pero nunca contra tantos como ahora! Habrá simplemente demasiados enemigos para que un solo héroe los derrote por sí mismo. 'Debemos usar otros métodos contra ellos si queremos sobrevivir.'

'Si quieres destacar en la construcción, mejora y uso de equipos de asedio, deberías centrarte en el Rol de Ingeniero en Combate. 'Los ingenieros pueden construir equipos de asedio y otros dispositivos más rápidamente. También tienen más opciones para mejorar y reparar tales dispositivos, y pueden colocar trampas para obstaculizar al enemigo. 'Los ingenieros también pueden desactivar trampas enemigas.'

'Si quieres destacar al dar órdenes a los Comandantes y proporcionar mejoras útiles a tus aliados, deberías centrarte en el Rol de Oficial en Combate. 'Los oficiales pueden dar órdenes más efectivas a los Comandantes. También tienen más comandos a su disposición, y pueden hacer que un grupo de soldados se concentre en objetivos específicos o cambie sus armas. 'Los oficiales pueden ordenar a los soldados que se refugien de los proyectiles o flechas entrantes. 'Además, los oficiales pueden colocar estandartes que ayuden a los Ingenieros y Soldados de Primera Línea cercanos.'

'Si quieres enfrentarte cara a cara con las fuerzas enemigas, debes enfocarte en el Rol de combate 'Soldado de Primera Linea'. Los Soldados de primera Linea desbloquean ataques poderosos al obtener rachas de muertes, es decir, al derrotar a muchos enemigos seguidos. También obtienen beneficios al infligir y recibir daño, y pueden correr más rápido que otros héroes. 'El soldado de primera linea se siente más feliz cuando se involucra en combates cuerpo a cuerpo.

'Los enemigos marcharán en formaciones hacia nosotros. Cuando una formación llegue a nuestra posición, los enemigos entrarán en combate cuerpo a cuerpo. ¡Debemos usar equipo de asedio para reducir su número primero, antes de que eso suceda!\ n 'Cualquiera puede construir y usar equipo de asedio básico. 'Hay otras opciones disponibles al gastar puntos en el rol de batalla de Ingeniero. ' Si quieres destacar en la construcción, mejora y disparo de equipo de asedio, debes enfocarte en el Rol de Combate de Ingeniero. 'Los ingenieros pueden construir equipo de asedio y otros dispositivos más rápidamente. También cuentan con más opciones para mejorar y reparar dichos dispositivos, y pueden colocar trampas para obstaculizar al enemigo. 'Los ingenieros también pueden desactivar las trampas enemigas

'Seleccionar al Comandante resaltará a todos los soldados bajo su mando. 'Durante la batalla, al hablar con alguien que esté 'Esperando órdenes', como un Comandante, puedes cambiar las tácticas de un grupo de soldados. 'Algunas opciones están disponibles desde el principio, como curar a los soldados con el tiempo y aumentar su daño. 'Otras opciones se vuelven disponibles gastando puntos en el Rol de Batalla del Oficial. 'Si quieres destacar al dar órdenes a los Comandantes y proporcionar mejoras útiles a tus aliados, deberías centrarte en el Rol de Oficial en Combate. 'Los oficiales pueden dar órdenes más efectivas a los Comandantes. Tienen más órdenes a su disposición y pueden hacer que un grupo de soldados se concentre en objetivos específicos o cambie de armas. 'Los oficiales también pueden ordenar a los soldados que se pongan a resguardo de los proyectiles de catapulta o las flechas que se aproximan. 'Además, los oficiales pueden colocar estandartes que ayuden a los Ingenieros y Soldados de Primera Línea cercanos.'

'Si quieres enfrentarte cara a cara con las fuerzas enemigas, debes enfocarte en el Rol de combate 'Soldado de Primera Linea'. Los Soldados de primera Linea desbloquean ataques poderosos al obtener rachas de muertes, es decir, al derrotar a muchos enemigos seguidos. También obtienen beneficios al infligir y recibir daño, y pueden correr más rápido que otros héroes. 'El soldado de primera linea se siente más feliz cuando se involucra en combates cuerpo a cuerpo.

'¡Hemos luchado contra grandes cantidades de enemigos antes, pero nunca contra tantos como estos! Habrá simplemente demasiados enemigos para que un solo héroe los despache por sí mismo. Debemos usar otros métodos contra ellos si queremos sobrevivir.'

'Las fuerzas de Saruman llegarán pronto, ${PLAYER}, pero temo que mis compañeros no sepan qué esperar. Una Batalla Épica no es como los enfrentamientos que hemos tenido hasta ahora, y quiero asegurarme de que nuestros amigos estén preparados. 'Contar con la mera supervivencia de la batalla sería un éxito, dado los enemigos que se nos presentan, pero la verdadera victoria es aquella en la que superamos todos los desafíos que trae la batalla. 'This is a proud day for the Riders of the Mark, ${PLAYER}. We have wrested victory from the very claw of Saruman, even as he thought his triumph assured. The House of Eorl is stronger than he supposed, despite thrice-cursed Wyrgende and the whispers of frailty that have been uttered throughout the Mark. Théoden King has fight in him still, as does his sister-son Éomer!'
Erkenbrand strikes his shield with the side of his sword, and cries 'Victory for the Eorlingas!' a cry that is answered from others of the Rohirrim throughout the field. After a moment he turns again to you with a smile.
'We have put the Dunlendings to work, ${PLAYER}, hauling away the bodies of the Orcs and cleaning the field of battle. Any who take a solemn vow not to cross the Fords in war ever again will have the forgiveness of our King.'
'Find Erkenbrand on the field of victory and give him my thanks for his timely arrival. This victory would not have been possible without him.'

'Gandalf has decided to ride to Isengard to confront Saruman, and my uncle has determined he should ride with him. Some others will go as well, but first we have need of rest. It will be a few hours before we ride for the Ring of Isengard and its evil master, and all of us toiled greatly during the night.
'Find Déorwine inside the Hornburg. He has begun to arrange bedrolls for those seeking to rest for the journey.'
'Éomer has indicated to me a desire to ride with the King to Isengard. He will wish for you to ride there as well.'
'We spoke yesterday, around sunset, do you remember? It feels a lifetime ago, ${PLAYER}!'
'Find Déorwine inside the fortress of the Hornburg. He will arrange a place for you to rest before the company sets forth for Isengard.'

'The battle is won, my friend, and now we must look to the future! The design of Saruman has been ruined, not by any spell or magic, but by the stout hearts of the Rohirrim and the swift speed of Shadowfax!'
Gandalf notices your study of the curious trees beyond the Dike.
'Ah, that forest is no magic of mine, ${PLAYER}. A power much older than my own drives it to be here, and I could not have hoped for a more timely arrival than this!'
He hands you a number of healing poultices.
'Before we can proceed, we must attend to the hurts of those injured during the battle. These poultices will bring them some measure of relief. Speak with the King and see if he has need of such treatment, and then do what you can for the wounded.'

'We have seen victory this day, but our work is not ended. We have earned a brief respite only, and must take steps to ensure the safety of the Mark without much pause.'
The King sees the bundle of poultices in your hands and shakes his head.
'I am fine, ${PLAYER}. I have suffered bruises only, and the strength of my fathers has kept me from sustaining grievous injury. Many of my men will have need of that healing; bring those packets to them and see to their hurts. Look too for men with swift horses, and command them to ride for all corners of the Mark with news of what happened at the Hornburg. I want every vale in the Riddermark to have tidings of our victory, and to send their strongest fighters to Edoras by the second day of the full moon.
'After you have exhausted the poultices and the riders have set forth, find Erkenbrand and give him my thanks for his timely arrival. Without his men this sun might have risen on a different day for Rohan.'
'You will find Théoden King to the south, enjoying the victory. Tend to his hurts, if he is injured, and heed any commands he may have.'

'Many of our injured men have need of the poultices you carry. Bring them to those who do, and ease the sting of their wounds. Look too for men who own swift horses, and send them to every corner of the Mark with tidings of our victory here!
'I want every able-bodied warrior summoned to Edoras by the second day of the full moon. Our work here is only beginning, but it is far better to begin with a victory than from a defeat!'

'It seems you found Aragorn before we did, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps we should have gone with you.'

'This is truly an unexpected encounter, ${PLAYER}! I am glad to see you are well, and in the company of Aragorn, no less! Our errand has not ended, though its first goal be now accomplished. Now we must lend what aid we can to Aragorn.
'Is it true you take the road to Isengard? Whatever other objective Aragorn has with Saruman, we must add this one as well: the rescue of Lothrandir my kinsman, if he yet lives!'
'Halbarad has given me much to think about, ${PLAYER}. We have more reasons to converse with Saruman than I believed.'

'Many good men fell at the Fords, but their kingdom still stands. We are almost to Isengard, and will bring report of their valiant sacrifice to the Wizard who forced its need.
'Let us rejoin our companions, ${PLAYER}.'
'I hear the sound of swift hoof-beats approaching from behind us. Let us confront this rider before he overtakes us and offers some harm to the King!'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! I knew in my heart we would see you once more, but I did not think to find you in the company of my chieftain Aragorn! Much has happened since we parted, and little of it good, but we will need to speak of our respective deeds when there is time to breathe.
'We have found Aragorn between perils, it seems. He had your help for the first, and he has all of us for the second. May it be enough!'

'We are well-met once again, ${PLAYER}, but in hardship. I sought the treacherous leader of the Falcon Clan, but he gave me the slip and escaped into the mountains. He lives still the life of a coward.'
You tell Golodir that Lheu Brenin's flight brought him into your path, and he has been slain.
'You tell me true? Then he has paid for his crimes. He abandoned some of his own people when he fled, and we left them in a place of peace, where they should be safe. I worried that their former chieftain might seek them out and visit upon them further harm, but even Saruman's magic cannot help Lheu Brenin now. I am satisfied, ${PLAYER}. Thank you, on behalf of my fallen kinsmen and also for those of his own people he betrayed.'

'It was not a long good-bye after all, ${PLAYER}, though the intervening days have been eventful. I think Halbarad keenly felt the burden of his duty after you left us, for he was not sure how best to proceed. But it seems he chose a-right, for we have found Aragorn as the words of Galadriel bade us.
'The sons of Elrond bear messages for him from their father, and Halbarad carries the gift of Arwen. I trust that Aragorn will know what to do with each of these gifts.'
'I feel confident that we can accomplish anything, ${PLAYER}, now that my kinsmen are here. Can it be that the tides turn in our favour this day?'
The Fords of Isen are a sad reminder of the good folk who fell in defence of Rohan
Aragorn has turned back to hear your opinion of the mysterious wood through which the company now travels.
Legolas has dismounted and is staring into the trees.
Gandalf is on the road, waiting to proceed.

'I hope you found rest before we set out, ${PLAYER}. I tried to do so, but I could not quiet my roving mind, and I am still greatly fatigued. What will we find in Isengard?'
Aragorn looks from side to side at the towering trunks of the forest.
'These trees were not here when we arrived at Helm's Deep yesterday. I think we both know what brought them here, to the foot of the Dike, but that makes it no less frightening a sight, does it?'
'${PLAYER}, wait! Do you hear that? I hear a great sound of creaking timbers and rustling branches. It comes this way!'

'I never believed I would see such things, ${PLAYER}. Ents! I am filled with wonder at the sight, wonder of a kind I thought was the sole reserve of children. I am an old man, a white-beard of many winters, and still I have seen things this day I would not have believed yesterday.
'They tower above mortal men, and cover such a span with each stride! What damage they could do to the homes of my people, if that was their thought! But I do not believe that is their desire.'

'These Ents are herdsmen, not warriors. The people of Rohan need not fear them, as long as they cause no harm to their flock. There is one in this land that would have done well to heed the Ents before now; if he had heeded them the battle that is lately ended might have come to a different conclusion.
'It is good for Rohan, and for all free folk, that he did not take them into account. Let us proceed, ${PLAYER}. There are still many miles to go before we reach Isengard.'

'I am delighted to see you again, my friend! The Grey Company has accomplished this first leg of its journey, and now we turn to our new purpose!'
'I will show you to a quiet corner of the keep where you can rest, my friend. And then it is my understanding that you will set forth with the King for Isengard?'
''This is an unexpected joy, my friend!'
Aragorn is beyond the Fords of Isen, and wishes to speak with you.

'The King and some others of his guard plan to ride for Isengard, but first they will take some hours rest. You should do so as well, ${PLAYER}.
'Speak to me if you are ready and I will prepare a place for you.'

'I believed we would see each other again, my friend, but I did not know it would be so soon! Sending you from us was not an easy decision, but I knew Théodred had need of your aid. What sadness that he could not be saved from that fate, but perhaps that too contributed to the resolve of the Eorlingas.
'The Grey Company has done what it set out to do; we have ridden to our chieftain in Rohan, and it seems we have come in time, after all. Some of our number were lost on the way, but those of us that remain will do everything in our power to ensure that Aragorn can fulfill his destiny.
'I am glad to see you again, ${PLAYER}.'
'Hold on a moment, friend. Did you sleep too long? The company has already departed for the Fords of Isen!'

'This is an unexpected joy, my friend! Had I known they were journeying to find me...'
Aragorn looks at you wryly.
'When you spoke to me of the Dúnedain, I did not suspect you had travelled with them in recent days, ${PLAYER}. I do not think I would have changed my course had I known, but perhaps that is the power of hindsight. Perhaps it is the wisdom of Elrond behind your silence, my friend. He is never quick to volunteer information, which makes the word of his sons even more curious.
'I have much to think about, and little time in which to do so!'

'The most peculiar thing happened, ${PLAYER}. Saruman and Gandalf engaged in a debate a few moments ago, and just when Gandalf seemed to get the upper hand, this object came hurtling down toward us from an upper window! It hit no one, thank goodness, but it would have quite hurt had the aim been better.
'It was a dark globe of crystal, but with a fiery core deep in its heart. I picked it up and it seemed much heavier than its size. Very odd. I carried it up the steps to give it to Gandalf, but when he saw what I bore he hurried down and took it from me quickly. He says it was thrown not by Saruman but by Gríma Wormtongue, who I had the distinct displeasure of meeting just yesterday.
'The globe is a mystery. I wonder what it was?'
'Gandalf will tell you more of what happened. I suspected some further mischief of Saruman, and I was not wrong to expect it! But all is ended now, and safely.'

'Is it true? The threat of Isengard has ended? Saruman has occupied our thoughts for so long, and caused so much hardship, I never believed he would not!
'We have come so far, ${PLAYER}: from Rivendell, through Hollin, into Enedwaith and Dunland, and here at last to the stronghold of Saruman. Many of my kin fell along the way, but each of them, all of them, were allies of the king to come: Aragorn, son of Arathorn, heir of Isildur.
'You, too, have been a friend of Aragorn, and to all the Grey Company. I thank you, ${PLAYER}. Wherever our road leads now, know that you have my thanks and my friendship.'
'Saruman's power is at an end. He will do us no more harm this day.'
'Gandalf says that Saruman can do us no more harm, but I do not know if he is right.'
'I cannot help but wonder about that dark crystal globe. What was it, do you think?'
Aragorn is on the stairs at the base of Orthanc.
Gandalf, Théoden, and Pippin all witnessed the confrontation with Saruman and wish to speak with you about the Wizard's schemes.

'Lothrandir suffered greatly at the hands of his captors, but his will remains strong, and I am certain he will recover from their torments. But what has become of Saruman? A crowd gathers by the foot of Orthanc. Go learn from them what has happened, and I will rejoin you shortly!'

Aragorn listens to your account of Lothrandir's rescue.
'I am pleased to hear my kinsman is safe! I wished often that my friends might be close at hand, but I did not give voice to that desire, for I would not have wanted them put in danger. It is well that Lothrandir has emerged from the pit of Isengard unharmed.
'Saruman emerged too, but not for long, and though he has returned to the tower I feel that his threat is ended! Gandalf will tell you more, if you would listen. I suspected some further mischief of Saruman, and I was not wrong to expect it! But all is ended now, and safely.'
'A crowd has gathered at the foot of Orthanc. Go there and see what has happened, and I will rejoin you shortly.'

'Saruman has come to the end of his power, ${PLAYER}. I think he will no longer be a danger to Rohan.'
Gandalf sighs heavily, and you are surprised to see a deep sadness in his eyes.
'I offered him his freedom, but after working such deceits as he has done for so long he did not see that it was an offer made in good faith. The treacherous see only treachery, and so it was with Saruman at the end. He has his life, but I fear he will not see this as a mercy. I have cast him from the order and from the White Council. His staff is broken, and he will work no further plots.
'But he has his life. He will remain within Orthanc, and think on his old designs, and mourn. But he will no longer endanger Rohan, and I think he knows that if Mordor does have victory in the days ahead, the servants of that land will not forget the treacheries he worked on his own behalf.'

'The Riddermark has suffered greatly at the hands of Saruman, but it will suffer no longer. He is locked in his tower, and Gandalf has cast him from the Order of the Wizards.
'The traitor used one last weapon, and it may have been his deadliest: the power of his voice. I know the extent of his crimes, and even so I nearly succumbed to the soothing persuasion of his words. We are fortunate Gandalf was here and could shatter the reverie.'

'¿Quieres investigar los Campos de Fornost? No podrás seguir mis pasos sin perder acabar loco de remate.

'Has sido de gran ayuda para quienes vigilamos el Bosque de los Trolls, ${PLAYER}. Recuperar las piedras robadas a los mensajeros de Heithur no fue una tarea sencilla, pero la cumpliste sin queja alguna. Sé que Heithur está satisfecho con tu servicio, y me uno a su agradecimiento.

Han establecido un campamento en las ruinas de Thorenhad, al este de aquí y al norte, en las Gargantas del Bruinen, y sé que tus servicios serían bien recibidos. Thorenhad está en lo alto de una colina, al norte de las guaridas de osos de las Gargantas del Bruinen.
'Si sigues la carretera hacia el este, encontrarás el campamento de Narlinn y Fimgris. Ellos podrán dirigirte hacia Thorenhad.'
'¿Vienes de parte de Barachen, buscando ayudar a Elladan y Elrohir? Me alegra oírlo, pero antes quisiera pedirte tu ayuda, si tienes un momento...'

'Todo ha estado tranquilo. ¡Si me asignaran a Nan Tornaeth, vería algo de aventura!'

Los lobos de las Gargantas del Bruinen merodean en el valle entre el camino principal y Thorenhad. Fimgris te dijo que siguieras la carretera hacia el este hasta la piedra blanca y luego giraras al norte.
Fimgris te ha pedido que derrotes a algunos de los lobos enloquecidos de las Gargantas del Bruinen con la esperanza de descubrir qué los ha perturbado.

'En los últimos meses ha habido señales inquietantes de que algo no anda bien en el Bosque de los Trolls: trolls que descienden de las montañas, siervos del Enemigo sobre el camino..... pero incluso las bestias del bosque están perturbadas de formas que no puedo explicar. Los lobos han vivido durante mucho tiempo en estas tierras y, aunque malvados por naturaleza, generalmente se mantenían alejados. Ahora, sin embargo, se han vuelto audaces y peligrosos. Me atrevería a decir que he visto miedo en sus ojos como nunca antes.
'Es cierto que los siervos del Enemigo persiguieron a un pequeño grupo por el camino hace no más de dos meses, pero los lobos se han vuelto mucho más incontrolables en estos últimos días, y no puedo determinar la razón.
'Si puedes, caza a los lobos de las Gargantas en el valle entre aquí y Thorenhad. Quizá encuentres alguna prueba de lo que los ha perturbado. Sigue este camino hacia el este hasta encontrar la piedra blanca. Allí, toma el camino hacia el norte y comienza tu cacería.'

Pothlorn estaba explorando el sendero que lleva hacia el norte y el este a través de las Gargantas hasta Ost Thondol.
Elladan te pidió que buscaras al explorador elfo desaparecido, Pothlorn, y averiguaras si aún vive.

'${PLAYER}, la agitación de los lobos no era desconocida para nosotros, aunque la causa de su locura ciertamente lo era hasta que llegaste. De hecho, enviamos a otro de nuestros Elfos, Pothlorn, a explorar el sendero que conduce a las ruinas de Ost Thondol. También se vieron lobos en esa dirección, y queríamos saber hasta dónde se había extendido su merodeo. Por desgracia, no hemos tenido noticias de Pothlorn.
'¿Podrías buscar a Pothlorn a lo largo de ese sendero y averiguar si aún vive? Puede que algún mal le haya sobrevenido... y aun así, deseamos conocer su destino.
'El sendero comienza justo hacia el este y se adentra en las Gargantas del norte, girando luego hacia el este, alejándose de Nan Tornaeth.'

'Ah, un ${RACE}... es bueno para mí que hayas venido, aunque quizá no lo sea para ti. Este lugar no es seguro...'

Habla con Pothlorn
Ost Thondol

'¿Una sierpe espectral? Eso explica la inquietud que muchos hemos sentido aquí estas últimas semanas. Pothlorn tiene razón... un mal mayor debió haber puesto a esa criatura en Ost Thondol. El primero que viene a la mente es el Capitán Negro, pero fue derribado en el Bruinen y enviado sin montura de vuelta a su amo.
'Aun así, debemos encontrar al maestro de la sierpe espectral a cualquier costo. Mi hermano Elrohir envió un explorador a Nan Tornaeth, donde habitan algunas sierpes. Deberías hablar con Elrohir.'

'¿Qué? ¿Un espectro con forma de sierpe? Es un presagio verdaderamente siniestro. Un espectro no actúa por sí mismo: está infundido por un espíritu maligno, puesto allí por un mal mayor. Debes regresar con Elladan de inmediato y contarle lo que has descubierto. Yo acudiré cuando me sea posible.'

Pothlorn te pidió que buscaras en las ruinas de Ost Thondol la fuente del mal que sintió durante su lucha contra los trolls de piedra.

'Había muchos lobos en el sendero, y se volvían más enloquecidos cuanto más me acercaba a Ost Thondol, que se alza sobre mí. Sin embargo, no se atrevían a pasar el pie de la colina, así que continué... solo para encontrarme con trolls de piedra en las ruinas.
'También sentí otra presencia allí, aunque no sé qué era, pues los trolls eran demasiados para mí y tuve que retirarme. Estuve cerca de la muerte.
'Si deseas ayudar de verdad a Elladan y Elrohir, sube la colina hacia Ost Thondol y busca la fuente del mal que hay aquí. Sea lo que sea, hasta los lobos le temen...'

'No me sorprende, dadas tus experiencias previas, que hayas encontrado un espectro tras la locura de los osos; sin embargo, no estamos más cerca de descubrir qué poder hay detrás de la creación de estos repugnantes espectros.
'No debería decir que no estamos más cerca, pues estas runas en el collar pertenecen a un estilo usado antaño en el reino de Rhudaur. Los Corcur, un remanente del antiguo reino que buscó refugio en Angmar hace mucho, han regresado y han establecido un campamento en las ruinas de lo alto. Buscan reclamar Rhudaur y devolverle su antigua grandeza, pero no son más que hombres salvajes... no puedo imaginar que posean el poder para alzar espectros.
'Aun así, envié a mi compañero, Malloval, a explorar su campamento, pero no ha regresado...'

'${PLAYER}, el mal que encontraste en Nan Tornaeth no puede ser ignorado. Mi padre debe ser informado, pues necesitaremos refuerzos aquí en Thorenhad. Donde hay un hombre demacrado, habrá más..... o incluso un Señor Demacrado.
'Viaja a Rivendel y comunica a mi padre, Elrond, la amenaza que se cierne aquí. Regresa al camino principal y ve hacia el este hasta cruzar el Vado del Bruinen. Después gira al sur y sigue el sendero ascendente hacia el Páramo Alto. La entrada a Rivendel está en la esquina nororiental del Páramo Alto, señalada como siempre con piedras blancas.
'¡Apresúrate, no te retrases por nada! Habla con el Guardián del Camino, Anhebir. Él te indicará el camino a la Última Morada.'

'¡Mae govannen! ¿Vienes de parte de Elladan y Elrohir con mensajes para el señor Elrond? Entonces te enviaré rápidamente en tu camino.
'Desde aquí, sigue la carretera hacia el este y cruza el primer puente. Continúa por el camino hacia el norte y el noreste, y pronto verás la Última Morada. El señor Elrond suele encontrarse en su biblioteca, en el piso superior.'

'Saludos, ${RACE}, ¿en qué puede ayudarte el señor de Rivendel?
'¿Qué dices? ¿Un hombre demacrado ha estado alzando espectros en Nan Tornaeth? Mi hijo tenía razón. Este acto no puede quedar sin respuesta.
'Te agradezco que me hayas traído esta noticia. Me aseguraré de que el mal sea purgado de las ruinas.'

El descubrimiento de un hombre demacrado y sus esbirros no-muertos en Nan Tornaeth ha causado gran preocupación a Elladan y Elrohir.

'Ten la seguridad, ${PLAYER}, de que el mal que permanece en Nan Tornaeth será enfrentado, aunque debo considerar el mejor modo de hacerlo.
'Mientras tanto, deberías aprovechar para descansar. Rivendel es un refugio para todos los que llegan en paz. Hay, en verdad, quienes en esta casa ya han decidido hacer una pausa en sus pruebas. Deberías buscarlos y hablar con ellos.
'Bilbo Bolsón pasa gran parte de su tiempo en el Salón del Fuego, interpretando canciones y poemas que compone para su amigo, Lindir. También encontrarás a Gandalf el Gris en los aposentos de Bilbo..... tiene muchas preocupaciones, pero Frodo Bolsón es la mayor de ellas. Deberías verlos a ambos mientras estás aquí.'

'Es bueno ver rostros conocidos, ¿verdad?

'Tras meditar largamente lo que me informaste sobre las zonas occidentales del Bosque de los Trolls, estoy convencido de que los siervos del Enemigo no fueron atraídos aquí por la breve presencia del Nazgûl que pasó hace poco, sino que responden a uno de los Señores Demacrados... burlas de los Magos creadas por Morgoth hace mucho tiempo.
'Basándome en los poderes de este Gúrdring con el que te enfrentaste en Nan Tornaeth, creo que el Señor Demacrado es Ferndúr el Virulento, maestro de la pestilencia. Debe ser derrotado a toda costa, pero no puedo enviar a alguien como tú en solitario para enfrentarlo. Su poder es demasiado grande.
'Solo tres dentro de este valle son lo bastante fuertes para oponerse a un Señor Demacrado, y ni Gandalf ni yo podemos partir ahora. Por tanto, te pido que hables con Glorfindel y le informes de lo que hemos descubierto. No tengo duda de que te acompañará contra este mal.'

'Así que es tal como temía. Un Señor Demacrado ha llegado al Bosque de los Trolls siguiendo el rastro del Nazgûl y está alzando un ejército contra Rivendel.
'El señor Elrond tiene razón. Debemos hacer frente a esta criatura de inmediato, y debo ser yo quien lo haga. Te pido que me acompañes para derrotar a los esbirros del Señor Demacrado... pero no intentes enfrentarte a Ferndúr en soledad, pues te destruiría.
'Háblame cuando puedas partir.'

'Lamentablemente, Ferndúr escapó. Es un enemigo terrible y representa una amenaza incluso para el poder de Rivendel. Debemos mantenernos vigilantes.
'Regresa con el señor Elrond y cuéntale cómo nos fue contra el Señor Demacrado.'

'¡De cuánta ayuda nos has sido, ${PLAYER}! Imagino que con los huargos dispersados, podemos volver a poner todo en orden por aquí.
'Debo pedirte una última cosa. Mi amigo, Orthonn, vigila Annúndir desde un puesto de avanzada solitario. Muy poca gente va en esa dirección. ¿Podrías comprobar que se encuentra bien, y contarle noticias del oeste de las Quebradas mientras estás por allí?'
'¡Saludos, caminante! Ah, ¿Amarion te envía? ¿Qué noticias hay de Amon Raith?'

Amarion te ha pedido que ofrezcas tu ayuda y compañía a Orthonn, un Montaraz que tiene la misión de mantener un puesto de vigilancia en la espesura de Annúndir.

'Has sido de gran ayuda para nosotros, ${PLAYER}, y estamos agradecidos. Nos alegraría seguir contando con tu ayuda, pero si sientes que ha llegado el momento de continuar tu viaje, te sugeriría que hables con Ringhul, montaraz de las marchas del Páramo Alto. Hazle saber que te envío yo y cuéntale tus hazañas... los amigos de Rivendel siempre son bienvenidos.
'Para llegar al Páramo Alto, debes regresar al camino del Tâl Bruinen y seguirlo hacia el norte hasta la carretera principal en las Gargantas del Bruinen. Sigue la carretera principal hacia el este hasta el Vado del Bruinen y cruza el río, girando hacia el sur. Encontrarás un sendero que asciende hacia las colinas... te llevará al Páramo Alto y al puesto de Ringhul.
'Adiós, ${PLAYER}.'

'¿Candelleth te envía? ¿Cómo le va a su compañía?
'¡Ah! Parece que las preocupaciones del señor Elrond eran fundadas. El Tâl Bruinen y la carretera hacia Acebeda están acosados por nuestros enemigos. En días como estos anhelo viajar por tierras lejanas, pues mi puesto se presta demasiado a la soledad y al tedio.'

Fish up and defeat the turtles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ever seen a swamp turtle? They're rascally creatures, the ones out here. Eat the bait from your hook without you even knowing. Why, I've even heard tale of one who would eat the fish right off the hook while you were trying to reel it in. Would wait for you to do all the hard work and then swoop in at the end and steal your dinner.
'They're also dangerous creatures, with jaws that can snap a man's leg clear in half. I love just about everything in the water, even some of the things from the true depths, but turtles we cannot tolerate any longer.
'Head to the swamps north of Calembel, to the north-east of here, and spend some time fishing. When you get a turtle on the line, pull hard and make sure that it comes ashore. When it does, take care of it. There are a lot of them out there in the shallows, so make sure you clear out a couple.'
'I'm sure the fresh tide will bring in more, but for now we should be able to get a couple of hours of unmolested fishing in. Thank you.'
Turtles in the Depths
A turtle has been defeated (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Turtles are the bane of the Dol Amroth fishermen. They eat the bait, and even sometimes the fish on the hook itself! Catching some and dispatching of them will aid the food supplies of the beleaguered Gondorian city.

'The salmon have begun their yearly run. They are making their way up the rivers, from Edhellond to beyond Calembel, pushing to the White Mountains where they will spawn in the gravel shallows.
'Salmon make up a great deal of our foodstocks for the long winters. When they head up the rivers we must take advantage and catch as many as we can.
'Head north-east to Calembel, within Lamedon, and do your best to catch some salmon. You will need to stay on your toes, with the running they will not be in any one location for long. Look for where the fish are jumping and the water is rolling and disturbed.'
'This will serve to keep at least three families fed for a month when the cold strikes. I will be sure to mention your name when I bring the fish to them.'

'How did you come to be here? I must be mistaken, but I am certain I saw you come from those haunted paths under the mountain.
'If that is true and you are as mighty as you appear, the steward will want to speak with you. We are in need of hardy folk, especially now that Lord Duinhir has ridden east.
'Follow the river Blackroot to the south, and you shall find a settlement called Morlad upon a hill to the west. There you shall find Malthellam, our steward.'

'I thought naught but death itself would ever wander forth from those wretched paths... I now see my folly.
'Tell me, stranger, what has brought you to Gondor?'
Out From The Darkness
After travelling through the Paths of the Dead, you have arrived in Gondor at long last. With war looming on the horizon, your skill shall once again be tested.
Talk to Malthellam

'I am thankful the others had time to spare to speak with you, and I am sure you can aid them all. Landiach is a trusted advisor of Lord Duinhir and a friend to my family... if he believes you can aid us, I do not doubt him.
'It is true that I have made... mistakes since taking stewardship of Blackroot Vale, but to appear weak or unwise would undo everything Duinhir hoped for me to embody in his stead.'

'Greetings and well met, traveller. I did not expect any to visit during such times, much less enter the vale through the dark paths. I am Landiach, ward of Lord Duinhir and protector of Lady Rosfin.
'As you have heard, troubles loom to the south and east, and we are too few to move against them. Acting on one would leave us defenceless against the other.
'If you would lend us your might, perhaps we can begin to push back our foes after all. Please tell Malthellam I would have you fight on our behalf.'

'These are dangerous times, ${PLAYER}, as I am certain you know well.
'Long has it been since Gondor faced such a conflict, and should we fail now, I doubt there shall be any battle left to fight. Ever since Lord Duinhir, his sons, and our warriors rode east to Minas Tirith, we have stood nearly defenceless. For our own part, we have held the line... but it has not been without cost.
'My guards know well what troubles face the vale, and I would ask that you speak to them. One as skilled as yourself would be a powerful ally, should you wish to aid us.'

'I saw you arrive earlier, traveller, and I knew it only a matter of time before you came to me.
'The old man is a wise advisor, but he is not as well suited to leadership. What few of us remain have held the lands west of the river Blackroot, but our archers have grown weary. Ever since the Orcs sacked Tingobel to the east, our troubles have only grown more dire.
'Belegant seemed pleased by your arrival, so perhaps you should seek him above.'

'Ah, you must be the traveller that arrived today. It is true that the vale faces many problems in recent days... some much more tangible than others.
'Word from the south speaks of something stirring the beasts of the vale, but little else is known. I am unsure if he knows of your arrival, but I am certain Landiach would be pleased to speak with you on these matters as well.
'If you have a moment, I have a more personal request of you.'

'${PLAYER}, I have served Lord Duinhir as his chief counselor and one of his most trusted friends for many years.
'It was for this reason I was chosen to be Steward during his absence. Yet, where leadership came to him naturally, I have not found any comfort in this role. I am without counsel of my own, for none of the guards can be spared and too few of the townsfolk have any tactical knowledge.
'I would ask Lady Rosfin for aid, but she is... disinclined to speak to me as of late. If you would, try to persuade her to aid me - for the good of Blackroot Vale.'

'Hello, traveller...
'Forgive me if I seem distracted, but my people are my sole cause as of late. My husband has ridden to Minas Tirith as have my sons, so steward or not, I shall see my people through these times.
'Am I right in suspecting that Malthellam sent you? After all, he has already sent most of my people to me for the same reason. I shall not forgive him for abandoning Tingobel to strengthen Morlad's defences. It was unwise, costly, and resulted in many deaths.
'He is welcome to pore over my husband's notes, but that is where my aid shall end.'

'Oh! Imagine if Candúr came through here. He might have murdered us where we sit!
'Nay, I do not believe he came this way. I do not even like to think of it....'

'Ah, so you are the brave stranger who wishes to hunt down Candúr! Good luck; he is a violent criminal, from what I understand. He did not pass through this gate, for I have it well guarded, as you see.'

'Finally, someone hoping to track down the escaped killer. Yes, I saw him, running along the rooftops across from this very spot. He disappeared over the wall to my right.
'I wish I could describe the chill that shook me when I met his eyes. It was as if he dared me to scream with his glaring eyes. It took my voice away.'

'Aye, I was guarding the dungeons when Candúr escaped. Overpowered me, he did. Nearly ripped my shoulder out of its socket when he threw me down.
'I didn't see which way he went, but he was a mean fellow, and strong as an ox. Dark hair, dirty, dark beard.
'I don't want a man like that running loose in Lamedon.'

'You are hunting Candúr? Good. He is a murderous man, and must be kept away from people. Killed his own brother, that one.
'He did not come this way. I stand guard, for the soldiers have gone off with Angbor. I would have seen him if he dared to cross this gate.'
'Candúr has been defeated? You have done well, ${PLAYER}. Here is a reward on behalf of Calembel for your endeavour, as promised.'

'Hey! You there! Help! Someone stole my sword!
'I demand justice! Where is Angbor? He has abandoned us to thieves and robbers. Is no one safe?
'I suspect my neighbour's boy. He claims he saw a wild-looking man running north upstream, but it sounds like a tall tale to me....'

'I did not mean for it to go so far! We watched the men ride to the mountain in the morning, and then Elfdag challenged me to follow them, and I did the same to him, and before you could say 'Helm Hammerhand' we were right up to the Dark Door.
'I returned to the camp after that, and I thought he followed at my heels... but now he is gone, and no one has seen him!'
'It was just a game! I did not think he would go inside! S'truth!'
'Troubles follow us like a storm-cloud, ${PLAYER}! Speak to Radwine and tell me they do not!'

'Several of the Men saw Aragorn go, and speak words of despair. Find these Men and set their minds aright, if you can. And when you return, do the same for me, ${PLAYER}! I do not think you can, but I must wear a brave face for the Men and will not give in to sorrow, for their sake.'
'Aragorn must have had a good reason to take that road, but I cannot think of a single one. The Dead Men are not to be crossed lightly!'
'I have the desire to ride with my King and fight at his side, but this injury will keep me from it! Must my sword and armour go to waste in this fashion?'

'I would ride with my King anywhere, even along the Dimholt road. I am glad he does not wish to go that way! I do not doubt our destination will be as dangerous as Aragorn's passage, but I want to be sure to arrive as a living man!'

'We are plagued with ill fortune, ${PLAYER}! An encampment of this size is bound to attract the attention of children and others who live near, that much I expected. But I did not expect even children to act in such reckless, foolhardy fashion!
'This boy tells me one of his friends, Elfdag, may have followed Aragorn into the Paths of the Dead! I thought it the mere boast of a child, but none have seen Elfdag today. I dispatched a number of men to find him, but they too have not returned.
'Elfdag is the grandson of Elfhelm, ${PLAYER}. We cannot have lost him in this fashion!'
Darláf shakes his head, but his mood is improved
Bosa remains dissatisfied that his injury will keep him from war
Sídrac believes the fighting strength of Rohan is insufficient to aid Gondor

Darláf, Sídrac, and Bosa can be found at the encampment in Dunharrow, south of Éowyn's position.
Éowyn has asked you to comfort some of the Men at the encampment in Dunharrow, for they heard of Aragorn's departure and have begun to question the wisdom of Théoden's ride to Minas Tirith.

Éowyn is at the muster of the Rohirrim, at Dunharrow.
You have spoken with some worried soldiers of the camp, and should return now to Éowyn.

'${PLAYER}! I am glad you have come with such haste, for these troubles weigh heavily upon me and I do not know how they may be o'erthrown! It is my uncle's choice to ride to Minas Tirith, and thereby satisfy the vows of his forefathers, but why should he not ride for Gondor with every sword he can command, either by oath or love? It is folly to allow proven warriors to abandon my uncle's course, lest it be doomed by their absence!
'And yet, in the early hours, Aragorn and his kinsmen departed Dunharrow for the Paths of the Dead! He spoke of need, but I can see no need on that road, save that of a yawning tomb that hopes to be filled. The dead men of Dunharrow do not suffer the living to pass.
'Several of the Men saw him go, and speak words of despair. Find these Men and set their minds aright, if you can. And when you return, do the same for me, ${PLAYER}! I do not think you can, but I must wear a brave face for the Men and will not give in to sorrow, for their sake.'

'This road leads to the Dwimorberg, friend. Why would anyone go to that Haunted Mountain, or tread the paths beneath it? That is not bravery! Only folly could lead my feet there.'
You assure Darláf that Aragorn considers his reasons for braving that road sufficient, but the soldier shakes his head.
'I hope he is not wrong, ${PLAYER}. It seems a great shame to allow a skilled warrior to disappear into such a place when we could use his talents elsewhere, at other battles.'

'Men are still arriving at Dunharrow from all corners of the Mark, but I do not think it will be enough. I rode forth from the Hornburg, as my King commanded, and most hamlets and villages responded to his call with clear voices and proud hearts, but this day I see few of those who spoke loudest.
'On my return from Forlaw, in Wildermore, I was beset by an Orc raiding party. The injuries I sustained will keep me from riding in my King's train, to my frustration and disappointment! Swords and spears need men to wield them, and that resource is in short supply. I say 'men,' but the blood of Théoden King's niece Éowyn burns for Rohan, and she would fight bravely for the kingdom, were it permitted.
'Alas, it is not so, and the both of us will be kept from doing what we desire, for I am a man injured and she a woman unwounded. Unhappy fortunes!'

'The grim northerners departed Dunharrow at first light, and did not stay to explain their course. I would think them cowardly had I not seen the road they took: south, along the Dimholt road. That way lies death.'
You explain that Aragorn had his reasons for taking such a road, but Sídrac waves away your words.
'I do not doubt he had reasons, friend, but it is clear his loyalty is not to Théoden King. We will have need of every man if we are to ride to Minas Tirith, as my King commands, and I see we are cheated of a powerful fighting force by Aragorn's choice. I count the chances of our success against the Enemy less and less with each sword he takes with him into the mountain. I saw the winged beast over Edoras. I know what dangers we face.'
Book 1, Chapter 1: The Muster of the Rohirrim

'So Elfdag really braved the Dwimorberg! I thought he would turn up hiding in back of one of the tents of the encampment!'
Radwine suddenly blanches.
'What I mean to say is... when I told you he might have passed the Dark Door, I absolutely believed that was true. Maybe. Well he is safe, and so are you! There is no reason to be upset.'

'It was dark beneath the Mountain, and there were shadows flitting all about. But if you really strained your ears, you could hear whispers and sighs: the voices of the Dead. I gathered from their talk that a Man had come through hours before, and claimed he could free them from their curse. Some of the Dead followed him, and left in his wake... but others of the Dead did not believe his claim, and they stayed behind. These are especially cruel, and they have abandoned any hope of escaping the curse; these are now the Ruthless Dead, and they hate the living and the Dead alike.'
Elfdag is safe, but his words raise further questions

'You are a hero, are you not? I overheard some of the men speaking of your deeds, and by their account you seem an accomplished adventurer! If I bring you to the entrance, will you enter the mountain and search for Elfdag? I will not follow you in... I promise!
'Let me know if you are ready, and I will bring you to the place. If you have a Fellowship of like-minded adventurers, bring them along too... I daresay there will be a place for them as well!'
'I am not afraid, ${PLAYER}! I will bring you to the Dark Door and I will wait outside for you! I hope you are able to find Elfdag!'

'You are not going to tell my grandfather, are you? I had everything in hand, but I am certain he would not think so. If you tell him of this adventure of mine he is bound to lock me up in Underharrow, and the wife of the Thane does not appreciate young lads or lasses underfoot! She always scowls when she sees my friends and me about... I daresay we would be safer 'neath the Dwimorberg than in the house of Ellen Fremedon!'
Elfdag's expression is one of horrified fear, and you quickly assure him that he will keep his freedom if he tells you what he saw.
'Well, it was dark, and there were shadows flitting all about. But if you really strained your ears, you could hear whispers and sighs: the voices of the Dead. I gathered from their talk that a Man had come through hours before, and claimed he could free them from their curse. Some of the Dead followed him, and left in his wake... but others of the Dead did not believe his claim, and they stayed behind. These are especially cruel, and they have abandoned any hope of escaping the curse; these are now the Ruthless Dead, and they hate the living and the Dead alike.'
Elfdag shivers.
'I suppose I am glad to be back above-ground, after all.'

'I cannot believe that Elfdag really braved the Dwimorberg! I thought he would turn up hiding in back of one of the tents of the encampment!'
Radwine suddenly blanches.
'What I mean to say is... when I told you he might have passed the Dark Door, I absolutely believed that was true. Maybe. Well he is safe, and so are you! There is no reason to be upset.'

'You have exceeded your reputation this day, ${PLAYER}! I did not relish the thought of telling Elfhelm that his grandson had disappeared beneath the Haunted Mountain. Perhaps I would have had my brother do it.'
Éowyn thinks for a moment, and then nods.
'Yes. But his grumbling would have been insufferable.'

'If you are a friend of Gondor, welcome to Morlad! If you are not, listen to my words and hasten your feet elsewhere. We have troubles enough in the Vale without your adding to them.
'Strange things have been happening here of late, and it has stirred in the creatures of the Vale a form of madness. I could not say what has caused it, but I know the creatures are oft driven into a frenzy when approached. I have seen beasts cast themselves at the very walls of Morlad for no reason at all, doing themselves great injury in the process. Do you want to know what I think? I think it is the whisper of Death that has done this. But let us not speak of that now.
'It is but a matter of time before one of the beasts is driven into the heart of the city. It would ease my mind some if you could defeat a number of the frenzied creatures in the Vale, or the bears and birds that might be next. We might speak again once that is done.'
'It would ease my mind some if you could defeat a number of the frenzied creatures in the Vale, or the bears and beasts that might turn that way next. We might speak again once that is done.'

'Thank you for the assistance, ${PLAYER}. I do not know what has caused this madness in the birds and beasts of the Vale, but there have been strange happenings here of late. If we learn the truth of them, we may learn what has so disturbed the creatures as well.
'I have heard whisperings on the wind. Whispers of Death.'

'You must be mighty indeed to have braved the paths under the mountain! Follow the road and it will bring you to the hilltop on which sits Morlad, my home. Help my people in any way you can and I will be most grateful to you.'
