'If you have the stomach for it, a journey to the Hill of Erech might reveal if my supposition is true. If something did come out of the dark reaches under the mountains, I feel certain that is where it would have gone. It has always been an ill-omened place.'

'I did not mean to startle you, but judging from your look you have seen your own share of surprises. You may be a seasoned adventurer, but I daresay what I beheld in the reaches of the night would make your blood run cold, as it did mine.
'From afar I heard the blast of a great horn, and then a multitude of horns in echoing answer. I felt then the gathering of a great company of shadows all about the Stone atop this hill. A group of horsemen stood there, and their leader was grim of face and stern of countenance. Flesh and blood treated with the shadows, and though I could not understand the words, his purpose was plain enough. The company's grim leader charged the Dead with a task, and when the dawn came they departed.
'I feel no shame when I tell you I hid myself as they passed, for the men of this company were as real as you or me, but in their train travelled countless shadows. This man commanded the Dead to follow, and follow him they did, down from Erech, through Tarlang's Neck, to where I do not know. I fear great evil has come to the kingdom I serve, Gondor that I love.'

The heavy weight of the silence before the coming of the Heir has been lifted. Now the darkness is busy with the sighing whispers of the Dead. Tenval's gaze is piercing and eager.
'What moved the Heir of Isildur to come beneath the Mountain, Lûtkal...? Has he forgiven us our treason...? I will follow him to Erech, and whither then...? I cannot see it, but I care not....'

You knew Dûgden long ago, before the two of you succumbed to weakness and fell beneath the heavy weight of the Curse of Isildur. His presence is cold, but he burns with a fierce agony.
'What has brought the heir of hated Isildur to this place, Lûtkal...? Untold years we have suffered the Curse of his cruel ancestor... has it not been enough...?'
Dûgden's resolve is sudden and frightening.
'I will cast my lot in with Sauron, as we did before...! Drugât speaks the truth: only Sauron will reward us for our service. Only he can banish the chains of our curse! I will follow our true master!'

Years have no meaning beneath the Mountain for the likes of you, but even so, you hold the memory of a time when the passage of day and night mattered. A new feeling has crept into your being, but you cannot place it. Tenval senses it too.
'Something feels different in the dark, Lûtkal,' he murmurs, and you know it is true.
Dûgden has chosen to follow Drugât, and Sauron

The heavy silence beneath the Mountain remains unbroken, a held breath beneath the still waters of Time, an expectant hush. Dûgden feels it too.
'I swore I would never forget this presence,' he breathes without air or voice, giving thought to the idea that has come to all who now walk the undying paths beneath the Mountain.
'Isildur the Hated has come again, to deepen the burden of his curse.'
Tenval and Dûgden were your closest friends when you walked the earth as a living man, in the days before the Curse. Now they must decide where their course lies, as must you.

'I need to return to my father's cart, up the road that way, in the Neck. Have you come from there?'
Nethadan grimaces and clutches his leg.
'We were bringing several bottles of Cemenduril liquor to sell at towns throughout the Vale, on behalf of Galengam's Divine and Delicate Draughts, but the cart succumbed to the harsh passage. My father sent me down to that village yonder to bring back supplies to fix the cart, and I did my duty. Well, as far as it went, for I was jumped by raiders and hurt my foot quite grievously. They ran off, but be warned: they may return in time!
'If you could bring one of these barrels back to my father, I will follow with the other. I think I am just about ready to walk once more.'
'If you could bring one of these barrels back to my father, I will follow with the other. I think I am just about ready to walk once more.'

'I sent my boy Nethadan to the nearest village for supplies we can use to fix it, but he has yet to return. Can you keep one eye open for him? The road leads south-east to the nearest village, and I hope you find him there. I need those supplies, and I need to know he has not run into trouble.'

'Did you find my boy? Did you find Nethadan?'
You tell Bandron his son was attacked by raiders, but survived and seemed well enough to return very soon.
'That is a relief, ${PLAYER}. I have many daughters, but he is my only son. Who else will carry on the legacy of my house, as common as it is? He is my blood, and in him I see my own visage at that age. Young, but full of dreams for the road to come. He is dear to me. You have done well by my son and my family! Now, my benefactor, what supplies have you brought from him? Give them to me and I will repair this axle, the better to return to my employer's errand.'
You hand over the barrel of nails, and Bandron's eyes widen with surprise.
'What is this? An entire barrel of nails?'
You tell Bandron that his son should be by soon with another, similar barrel.
'No, that cannot be! What am I supposed to do with two barrels of nails? I need to fix an axle, not put a nail in every tree from here to the Grey Wood! This repair will take two nails, at the most. And now we have two barrels of the things! How much coin did he spend on these barrels? Every one I gave to him, I do not doubt! All of our profit on this expedition will have gone to buying nails!
'Oh, ${PLAYER}. I recommend to you a life without heirs. Every hair on my head was the colour of coal before Nethadan was born, and ever since: white hairs, each and every one!
'My employer is Galengam, of Galengam's Divine and Delicate Draughts. He runs a shop in the town of Calembel, to the south-east. Kindly go to him and tell him that we ran into some difficulty, and will return as soon as the Cemenduril liquor is delivered. If you have a kindly heart, ${PLAYER}, weave a tale of raiders and robbers... and leave the nails quite out of it!'
'Bring that barrel of nails to my father, and with haste! I will be along quite soon.'

'Ah, welcome to Galengam's Divine and Delicate Draughts, purveyor of healing remedies and wholesome poultices! If you are here to purchase some of my goods, I must sadly report that you have come at a poor time; my last shipment of Cemenduril liquor is already bound for the Blackroot Vale, and my remaining stock is set aside for the Houses of Healing at Minas Tirith.'
You tell Galengam of your encounter with Bandron and his son Nethadan.
'The delay is unfortunate, but not unexpected. A successful merchant accounts for such things. Theirs will be the last delivery of Cemenduril liquor to the Vale for some time, because now all my goods will be needed at Minas Tirith.'

'My employer is Galengam, of Galengam's Divine and Delicate Draughts. He runs a shop in the town of Calembel, to the south-east. Rovalang has asked you to travel south-east through Tarlang's Neck, and to help any people of Gondor who may have run afoul of the Dead in their passage.
A waggon has come to an early stop in Tarlang's Neck, and its driver could use your assistance.
Nethadan went to the town of Dínadab in Lamedon, south-east of Tarlang's Neck, to recover supplies to fix his father's broken waggon, but he never returned. Bandron asked for you to find him.

'My name is Rovalang, and I am proud to serve Imrahil, Prince of Dol Amroth. He has marched for the White City with a company of knights and more than five hundred men at arms to defend it 'gainst all enemies. I and several of my order he commanded to remain in the service of his daughter Lothíriel, who rules now while he is gone.
'Her safety is paramount, and I and the other swan-knights who remained would die to defend her, but we are sworn to obey her commands. She sent several of us from the city to protect her people in the Vale and in Lamedon, and we could not refuse. So I came to the Vale, and beheld the scene I have reported to you. It seems Lothíriel was right: there is danger outside the walls of Dol Amroth, and the Swan-knights are needed here too.
'Not just Swan-knights; brave adventurers too, as I deem you to be! Follow the Dead south-east through Tarlang's Neck, and help any of the people of Gondor that may have been endangered by their passage. I will remain to aid the people of the Vale, but I value your help, my new friend. May the people benefit from our friendship!'

'Follow the Dead south-east through Tarlang's Neck, and help any of the people of Gondor that may have been endangered by their passage. I will remain to aid the people of the Vale, but I value your help, my new friend. May the people benefit from our friendship!'

'Take care, traveller! You pass through Tarlang's Neck, and the road here is treacherous. Many an ankle has been turned by the rough going in this pass, riders and walkers sent to the ground by one misstep. It has claimed the axle of my cart, and now my business is halted.
'I sent my boy Nethadan to the nearest village for supplies we can use to fix it, but he has yet to return. Can you keep one eye open for him? I am afraid he may have run into trouble... or into the town's tavern for a short drink that became a long one!
'The nearest town is called Dínadab, and it is to the south-east along the road. Nethadan may be a fool, but he is my boy and I do not want him to run afoul of trouble. Not when we have a task to perform!'
'The road through Tarlang's Neck is treacherous. Keep your eyes open for any danger!'

'I sent my boy Nethadan to the nearest village for supplies we can use to fix it, but he has yet to return. Can you keep one eye open for him? The road leads south-east to the nearest village, and I hope you find him there. I need those supplies, and I need to know he has not run into trouble.'

'Do you have news from the fields? Oh, you have more than that! These bundles of harvested flowers will allow me to brew a good quantity of my healing liquor... but what are these?'
Galengam squints critically at the Corsair weapons you have set before him.
'I do not like the look of these weapons at all. These are weapons of Umbar, I'll warrant, and that means the raiding parties that plague Lamedon come from the coast. If Prince Imrahil were here, they would not dare to land! But we have only his daughter Lothíriel to keep the coast safe, and she is not the leader that is her father.'

'Yours is not the first report I have heard of raiders in Lamedon, ${PLAYER}. I am worried they may do some harm to the fields where my workers grow Cemenduril blossoms. With these crops I brew the healing liquors I sell throughout the kingdom; if they are ruined, more than my business will suffer.'
Galengam scowls. 'Prince Imrahil rode east for Minas Tirith, leaving his daughter to rule Dol Amroth. Is it any wonder that raiders have taken advantage to cause trouble while the Prince is away? I wager they would not dare do so if he remained in the city, but alas! War threatens in the east, and draws him thither. Lothíriel sits in Dol Amroth, where she is safe, but what of the people outside the walls?
'Several farmers in my employ work the fields even now. Will you protect them while they go about their business? I would greatly appreciate it, and you would be doing me, and Gondor, a favour.'

'These Corsair raiders likely landed at the shore west of here, in Belfalas. I expect they have established a foothold in the old ruins on the coast. People say Elves once lived there, but that must have been a thousand years or more ago. No Elves have come near Calembel for as long as I have run my shop, at any rate.
'If you are of a mind to deal with these Corsairs, that would be the place to do it! And while you're at those ruins, if you happen to see any old remnants of the Elves, bring them back to me and I will pay you good coin for them. The Elves won't be needing them, after all.

'If you are a friend, you are welcome to share my watch. I would be pleased to have your company, for Men of Umbar have brought their ships to shore, and threaten Edhellond. 'If their goal is plunder, they will be disappointed. The only relics that remain will be of historical value only. Any valuable artifacts or jewels were taken long ago.
'There are others of my people nearby. If you can defeat some of the raiders throughout Edhellond, I will bring you to them. Return hither with any relics you find, and I will be doubly-pleased, for I do have an interest in curiosities from my people's history.'

'I know your face, ${PLAYER}, for I came to Imladris some months ago and saw you there. A council was held and many courses decided, but we will not speak of them here. Know that I hold you in esteem and consider you an ally, and we bear friends in common.
'It is that sense of kinship that drives me to tell you this: do not underestimate the Corsair threat! I gave Dorthaneth the same warning. In my journey here I came near to a group of Umbar-Men and overheard their talk. They spoke in reverent tones of 'the Heirs of Castamir' and 'the Scourge,' but it is not these names that fill me with anxiety. No, the flame of my concern is kindled by the passion with which the Umbar-Men spoke of their loyalty. Any of them would die in the name of the Heirs, and gladly, which is not a trait I have heard associated with that people before now. Something has changed.
'I will set out for Mithlond in a few days, but do not forget my warning!'
'Speak with Galdor and hear what he has to say, for his news signals trouble for the Avorrim, and for the folk of Gondor as well.'

'Galdor is right to worry. The Men of Umbar have not possessed loyalty like this for many years, and it was once believed their people would decline and no longer pose a threat to their neighbours across the Bay. I do not believe these Heirs of Castamir are truly descended from that king, but I have paid little attention to the histories of Gondor and could not say for certain. The lives of Men are brief; before many a season has passed they fall, like the leaves of the trees in my home. I have never recorded either.'
Dorthaneth is silent for a long time, and you have almost decided to leave her in peace when she speaks again.
'I would be content to remain alone, listening to the sound of the water falling and the sighing of the wind in the trees, but as long as the Avorrim must remain here I will care for and protect them. There are others, too, with whom I feel a kinship and would safe-guard.'

'It is time for me to introduce myself properly, my friend. I am Lathlorn, and I am proud to count myself among the Avorrim. We were tasked by Círdan the Shipwright with maintaining a watch on Edhellond, and have done now for some time: removing overgrown brush and keeping the paths clear, and ensuring that the docks remain free of debris. If the Havens of Mithlond become untenable, this would be the last place from which my people could depart this Middle-earth for the Undying Lands. The Men of Umbar that occupy Edhellond do us a grievous turn, and do not even know of it!
'Dorthaneth is the leader of the Avorrim, and you can find her in the cave where we reside for now. If you follow the road south-west on the way to Dol Amroth, you will come to a rocky cleft in the ground to your right. Follow it down to a cliff-side path over the water, and you will come to the entrance.
'Tell Dorthaneth of your experiences in this land, for she has a wisdom about her and has proven a capable leader of the Avorrim for as long as I have known her.'

'Welcome to Belfalas, ${PLAYER}. I am called Dorthaneth, and I have chosen to care for the Elves here as a mother does. They are the Avorrim, and they have come to this land to watch over the refuge of Edhellond and keep it safe from danger.
'Danger threatens it now, as you have seen. Men of Umbar have come ashore in great number, too many for my few Avorrim to drive away. A guest is lately arrived, and we just spoke about these raiders. Go to him and hear what he has to say, for his news signals trouble for the Avorrim, and for the folk of Gondor as well.
'Do you see him across the way? His name is Galdor, and he is lately arrived from Imladris.'

'You must think I speak of leaving the world to its troubles, but even I, with every reason to do so before me, cannot truly withdraw. I have grown fond of Lothíriel, the daughter of the Prince of Dol Amroth who rules now in his absence. On several occasions she has escaped the watchful eyes of her guard, and come to visit me outside the walls of her city. The matters of which we spoke? Not war, nor armies, nor weapons. They were matters of love and of marriage, for Lothíriel is betrothed to a Man she does not wish to marry. Such things are a Lady's concerns, and I counseled her on them as best I could.
'But now I must counsel her on these other concerns as well: weapons, and armies, and war. I echo the worry of Galdor: she must not underestimate the Heirs of Castamir, and the one they call 'The Scourge.' Lothíriel's father has been called to war in the East; but war finds her now in the West, and if either is lost there will be no hope for the other when the night has come.
'Go to Dol Amroth and give her my warning. There is Elvish blood in her line, but it is no sense of kinship that drives me in this; it is the love I bear for the dark-haired woman who spoke to me of her hopes and her fears when the moon was high over the Sea, and banished sadness for a time.'

'Go to the libraries of Dol Amroth and speak to Pethebir, the master of the archives. Learn from him everything you can about the Corsairs and their masters. Perhaps in so doing you will discover something we can use to our advantage.'

'Naremil and Nosseth have travelled extensively throughout the kingdom of Gondor, and can tell you a great deal about the land and our rich history. Nosseth has a particularly keen insight for the lineages of the Kings and of the Stewards, and the political intensions of various Lords and Ladies. Cirhael can tell you a great deal about the Corsairs, and the land from which they hail: Umbar, to the south across the Bay.'

'The kingdom was first established in the wake of disaster. The land of Númenor fell beneath the waves; only fast ships could save the household of Elendil and bring them to these shores. High King Elendil's sons ruled the kingdom together, but when the Dark Power returned to Middle-earth, Elendil and his sons Isildur and Anárion were slain. The line continued by way of Anárion's son through many years, until Eärnur, the last king of Gondor, disappeared into Minas Morgul and was never seen again.
'For more than nine hundred years, rule of the kingdom has passed down through the hereditary line of the Ruling Stewards, charged with maintaining the peace and welfare of Gondor until the line of Kings is restored. Few believe that can ever happen. Any claimant would need to prove an unbroken blood-line, a task that seems insurmountable to this poor scholar.'

'South of Dol Amroth, across the Bay of Belfalas, the city of Umbar stands. Its large harbour provides the mooring for many great ships, and a mighty fortress was built there. It was an important port for the Númenóreans, but when strife split the loyalties of that people, Umbar became a contested land.
'It remained so throughout history, at times taken by Gondor and at others occupied by Black Númenóreans and their Haradrim allies. One of the most devastating losses of Umbar occurred following the Kin-strife, one of Gondor's darkest periods. The sons of Castamir the Usurper, chief architect of the Kin-strife, escaped from Gondor and named themselves 'Corsairs of Umbar.'
'Castamir's sons were all slain, but their legacy remains. The Corsairs have caused much hardship along the coastline over the years.'

'Lord Imrahil is the Prince of Dol Amroth, and he is the wise ruler of the city and its surrounding lands. He has gone to Minas Tirith with many soldiers, but he has left some of his swan-knights to serve his daughter Lothíriel, who now rules the city during his absence.
'Imrahil is well-loved by the people of Belfalas, but his daughter is untested and unproven. Númenórean tradition allows women to rule, but not all folk in Gondor remember such things; I have heard some dissatisfaction that she was chosen to rule the city while her father is away.
'But Lothíriel is loyal and complies with her father's wishes, despite her young age and a tendency toward recklessness. She recently disagreed with an arrangement of marriage, but it is my understanding she will go through with the proposed match, despite her feelings, or the feelings of a great many of her people. Some things are not meant to be, and I fear there will be a reckoning for it.'

'Ah, did my scholars help you learn anything of use, ${PLAYER}? It seems to me that the Corsairs are a dangerous threat, and Lothíriel would be wise to recall the swan-knights she sent from the city. I hope the information of my scholars proves helpful to you and to Lothíriel, and awakens her to the uncertain future that awaits.'
Pethebir notices your expression, and sighs.
'I see that Nosseth spoke to you of Lothíriel's betrothal to Boromir. I should have counseled her to exercise restraint! None are happy about this match, save Denethor, and as he is the Ruling Steward there are none willing to speak against his wishes. All I know of it is that he had a dream of some sort that convinced him of the rightness of this match, but I do not know what it could have been.'
You decide not to tell the earnest archivist that you know Boromir will never wed Lothíriel, but the young ruler of the city should be told the fate of her intended.

'You have returned from the library archives, ${PLAYER}? Have you learned anything that will help us defend against the attacks of Umbar? Why do you appear so sorrowful? What is wrong?'
There is no easy way to give such tidings as you have of Boromir, but you do the best you can, and tell Lothíriel that he fell in battle protecting those who could not protect themselves. Her face betrays a confused mixture of emotion.
'I do not know what to say, ${PLAYER}. Boromir was a good man. He always had my love and my respect, and I would have married him for Gondor. His father the Steward dreamed of the triumph of the kingdom, and in the dream I was a garlanded queen in Minas Tirith, beneath a fair and golden sun. My father, too, had a similar dream: he dreamt that I was in a high place, wearing a golden crown.'
Lothíriel wipes at the dampness in her eyes with the back of her sleeve.
'I mourn for my cousin, ${PLAYER}, and for Gondor. I was unhappy with the marriage match, but now that he is gone I am sad for his passing, glad that he attained glory, and angry for my relief. I do not know how I feel.'

'It seems to me that the Corsairs are a dangerous threat, and Lothíriel would be wise to recall the swan-knights she sent from the city. I hope the information of my scholars proves helpful to you and to Lothíriel, and awakens her to the uncertain future that awaits.'

'My father has always said the finest way to combat a new foe is to learn as much of his history and temper as you can, before facing him on the battlefield. I think this is wisdom. Nedhros is on the hill of Amon Lontir, by the great beacon.
Lothíriel has sent you to recall Nedhros, the swan-knight she sent out of the city into the lands of Belfalas.

'While my father is away, I must rule in Dol Amroth. I do not have the time to come to terms with this loss, ${PLAYER}. I will grieve at another time, and reconcile my feelings then. For now I must be strong.'
By the set of her jaw you see that Lothíriel is resolved, and the strength of her father is in her.
'I sent forth the swan-knights for two purposes. One was the purpose of a ruler, to ensure the safety of her people. The other purpose was that of a rebellious child, acting out against the wishes of her father in the only way she could. That purpose I regret. Now is the time for the swan-knights to return to Dol Amroth, for I will have need of them if we are to survive the menace of Umbar and these Heirs of Castamir.
'Travel first to the beacon on Amon Lontir, east of the city, and tell Nedhros to return. He is the nearest swan-knight, and is advanced in age, but it has not decreased his skill one measure. Travel then to the beacon of Maegond, in Lamedon. Heledir is the knight I sent to Lamedon, and he is also brave of heart.
'The last of the knights I sent forth is named Rovalang, and he will be somewhere in the Blackroot Vale, I know not where.'

'You say that Lothíriel has commanded my return to the city? I will return, of course, but there is something I must say to you first, young one!'
Nedhros laughs sharply.
'You have interrupted me during a brief lull in the battle, my timely new friend! I routed a group of Corsair raiders, but they are certain to return. Indeed, I hear them approach once more!'

'Lothíriel wishes for me to return to the city? I will do so at once.
'If you have a taste for adventure, friend, you might travel up the hill to scout the beacon. I was just atop the hill, but saw no one, though I felt a watching presence. I think someone might be up there now, hiding from me.
'If you climb the hill now, but quietly, you might surprise a hidden villain. I think you should do so, my friend!'
Book 1, Chapter 11: The Swan-knights

'A cold sensation has gripped my heart, ${PLAYER}. Do you feel it too? I believe we draw near to the creature I beheld above the mountains!
'Before we proceed, are there any companions on which you can rely? Are we on our own, or do you have a Fellowship near at hand? Speak to me again and tell me which is true!'
'I have never before been in the presence of such evil, ${PLAYER}! Let us leave this place, and then we will speak of it... but not before!'

Rovalang is on the slopes of the Hill of Erech, in the Blackroot Vale.
With the help of Rovalang, you have driven off the Nazgûl that threatened to learn of Aragorn's passage with the army of the Dead.

'You have heard of this winged creature, ${PLAYER}... I can see it in your eye. Will you help me find it and keep it from harming the people of the Vale?'
You nod in agreement. If the Nazgûl learns that Aragorn commands an army of the Dead, much harm might be done to the desperate hope that drives him, and to the people that depend on him.
'Well, let us go at once! If you have a Fellowship at your call, bring them along as well. There will be danger enough for all... but now let us chase this foe! I saw it fly in the direction of the haunted cave to the north-west. Perhaps we can bring it down, if we hurry!'

'I think you knew more about that creature than you let on, my friend. I am glad you were here! My tale might have ended in the shadow of the haunted mountain if you were not! But we have both faced great evil and lived, and our tales go on.
'That creature brings to mind a name from the ancient years, a name of great evil. I will not speak this name, but I have now seen with my own eyes the servant of that terrible Enemy.
'The time has come to return to Dol Amroth. Lothíriel must be told.'

'My swan-knights have returned, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for bringing them my message. I see from your face that you have more to say to me. What is on your mind?'
You tell Lothíriel of your encounter with the Nazgûl in the Blackroot Vale. She is silent for a long time. When she speaks again, her voice is very quiet, the words not much more than a whisper.
'I remember the heat of summer on the stones of the White City, ${PLAYER}. It was late in the month of June, and my father brought me and my brothers to Minas Tirith with a dozen riders. He did not reveal the purpose of the journey until we were in the Steward's chamber: I was to marry Boromir, the son of my father's sister. He was tall, and confident, and a great warrior, and I could tell that he too did not want the match.
'But he was an obedient son, and consented to the betrothal. There would have been a wedding on that warm night of June, but Boromir had a journey of his own to make, and it was decided the wedding would occur on his return. 'I will bring you a wedding gift,' he said to me before I joined my father and brothers in the courtyard for the return to Dol Amroth. 'I will win this war and bring you the peace you deserve!' he called to me. I never saw him again.'
Lothíriel's eyes are fierce, her mouth a thin line sharp with resolve.
'I did not want to marry him, and he did not want to marry me. But we wanted the same thing. We wanted peace and happiness for our people, and we were willing to sacrifice whatever we needed to achieve it for them. Our enemies have underestimated us. They think we are soft. They think we will give in to despair and give in to grief. But we will not.
'I spent more time in study than the archivist Pethebir believed. I know the name of the Great Enemy, the master of the foe you faced in the Blackroot Vale. I am not afraid to utter his name. He is Sauron, and we will stand against him to the last man, woman, and child. Gondor is not without strength. We will face the great strength of Sauron and we will defeat him, or we will die. There are no other choices for us.
'I will call for you, ${PLAYER}. Enemies are everywhere, and we have only just begun to fight.'
'We should return to Dol Amroth at once. Lothíriel must be told that servants of the Great Enemy walk in Gondor!'
'I do not know what that creature might be, but I know it is my duty to face it. We will face it together! If you have a Fellowship at your call, bring them along as well!'
Book 1, Chapter 12: The Shadow in Morthond

Rosfin has asked you to travel to the village of Lancrath and aid the people in repelling the Orcs of the White Mountains.
Talk to Osbenn in Lancrath

'We have waited long enough, ${PLAYER}. If the Dead seek to overrun the vale, we cannot abide another Orc. We must crush their forces at Tingobel and ready ourselves for war.
'Far to the south-east, you will find Lancrath nestled in the hills. There, seek a man named Osbenn. He is a wise hunter, and though he is no longer fit for battle, he can aid you in directing the attack on Tingobel.
'Go with haste, ${PLAYER}. Every minute we delay allows the Orcs to creep further south towards Lamedon.'

'Hail, traveller. You must be a friend of Lady Rosfin, for none have been so bold... or foolish enough to journey here as of late.
'The Orcs have starved us for resources by sacking Tingobel and its mine, and it is unlikely that we can hold out much longer. I must admit, I know less than I would like to about what occurred to the north, but the people who escaped know it well.
'If you would aid us, I ask that you speak to them, for they might be able to aid you in planning an attack.'
Loss for Loss

Talk to Calennen in Alagrant

'After speaking with Rosfin, I have decided that our first course of action must be to protect the villages that still stand to the south.
'I do not know how far the Orcs have ventured into the vale, but I can only hope that our archers have deterred them from straying too far beyond Tingobel. To the south lie the villages of Alagrant and Sardol... small settlements full of fishermen and hunters. They must stop their hunts for a time if they are to remain safe.
'I would ask that you travel to both and warn them of danger. Meanwhile, Rosfin and I shall form a plan to deal with the Orcs.'

'Welcome to Alagrant, traveller. What is this, now?
'We are but a small village of hunters, friend. If Malthellam's concern is that the beasts have grown wild, I do not believe such a thing will trouble us.
'However, there is another matter which may....'
A Cost Yet Unpaid
In an effort to prevent further tragedy from befalling the people of Blackroot Vale, Malthellam hopes to safe-guard the people of Alagrant and Sardol from the Enemy.

'We are in a bind, ${PLAYER}.
'The last of our hunters to go missing left last night, and he has not returned. He spoke of venturing into the hills to the east where the spiders dwell, but they have grown strangely aggressive as of late. Most of our remaining hunters are now too fearful to journey out of Sardol, and those that would are bound by Malthellam's edict.
'Since you can move freely through the vale, I would ask that you search for him in the hills to the east. Be wary of the spiders lurking there!'

The hunter's flesh is marked with numerous raised bites, and it appears he tried to flee before succumbing to the spiders' poisons.

'The waters of the Blackroot itself rose against you? That is not the work of any corsair I've ever heard of, ${PLAYER}.
'You mentioned that the tracks continued into the vale, so perhaps the invader still lurks our lands... I only hope this corruption he has surrounded himself with spares the rest of the vale.
'Many foul things are at work, ${PLAYER}, and I fear too many remain beyond our control.'

'If someone has been stealing away our goods, they must have come from the south.
'I have heard news of corsairs landing near Dol Amroth, but none of us have seen any in the vale. If they have truly come this far north, we shall have more to worry about than Orcs and the Dead...
'They must have travelled the river's edge to send the barrels downstream, so if you find any sign of their passing, it may aid us in routing them out.'

'Before you go, I have something else to ask of you.
'Spiders have long lived under Tarlang's Peaks, but we have never seen them in such force until very recently. I am hesitant to suggest this... but if the Dead have returned to the vale, I cannot help but think they may be involved somehow.
'You are the mightiest among us, ${PLAYER}, and I would ask that you search Lhingroth for anything that could be agitating the spiders. Please... I wish to be wrong, but I cannot quiet these thoughts until I know the truth.'

'The Dead have never left the hill before... this does not bode well for the vale, nor does it bode well for Gondor.
'If the Dead have somehow managed to pledge themselves to this powerful ally, their aggression is likely being guided. They must know that such an agreement is folly though... the curse can only be broken by one.
'I must think on what is to be done, but Malthellam must be told of this... and soon!'

Speak to Beriaudur to learn more about the city guard

'Welcome to Dol Amroth, ${PLAYER}. I have seen you about the city as of late, and you appear to have done much to aid Belfalas and our peoples here. But the threat against us looms ever present, and one must be vigilant in their watch for the shadows.
'If you are interested, we could find a place for you within the city guard. You would need to prove yourself, many times over. Should you rise to the mark though, Dol Amroth would consider you one of her own.
'Speak to me again if you wish to know more.'

'Dol Amroth is not a small city. We have stretched and sprawled over the years to cover many an acre, and that's without considering the docks and port. It is a large area for us to patrol and cover. Each section of the city has its own personality and people who call it home. Each has its own needs and dangers.
'Our guards are not all allowed to patrol and keep watch over every section of the city. You must learn that section to earn the right and privilege of serving it.
'You shall start where all young recruits do, with the library. Do a series of tasks for Tolrían and you shall receive some recompense. Return when you have it.'
Dol Amroth - Joining the City Guard

<rgb=#FF0000>Once accepted, this quest cannot be cancelled. You must complete the training exercise to finish the quest.</rgb>

'Join us on a patrol of the area surrounding the city. This will be a full march, all of the city guard participating in an exercise and show of force. We shall meet outside the gate, ride to Amon Lontir and then loop our way back.
'Along the way we will stop to practice certain maneouvres and do a mock assault on Amon Lontir. We shall be gone for several hours and return to the city around nightfall.
'Speak to me when you are ready to depart.'

'The corsair camp to the south has mostly been nothing more than a nuisance, but lately there has been a lot of activity there. A group of ships were anchored offshore for several days and we observed a number of captains disembark. When the ships left, they weren't on them.

'There are few things in this world that make me truly angry. Make my spine shudder and fingers clench with rage. Seeing a man enslaved by another, reduced to nothing but property, makes my teeth gnash.
'The corsairs are men who do not share this belief. Instead, they would enslave all of their enemy. Put them into camps making ships and weapons, and whip and beat them until they died, then simply replace them with the next.
'Several slavers are working out of the camp to the south. Ensure they never get the chance to take another as property again.'
'Such vile men deserve a punishment far worse than what you were able to deliver, but for now it will have to satisfy.'

'These Corsairs are not like us... they are Men of the worst sort. Wherever their ships make landfall, they pillage... they ruin... and they enslave all in their path.

'Honour or not, I am still not certain if I regret joining you here, ${PLAYER}. I suppose I shall soon find out....
'We should advance as quietly as possible, for I do not wish to alert this man to our presence until the time comes.
'Let us begin our ascent, ${PLAYER}. I hope the Dead are kind enough to leave us be....'

'We have kept our lives, ${PLAYER}, but I fear we won little else.
'This Heir of Castamir, Azruthor, threatens the whole of Gondor and we may only count ourselves lucky that all of the Dead did not heed his call. He has fled to Tarlang's Crown, but he may not stay long there before waging war to the south... or even the West for the Anfalas is all but empty.
'You must warn Malthellam and Lady Rosfin at once so the people of Dol Amroth might ready themselves for war in time!'

'You speak of deception, ${RACE}... yet you know nothing of our plight. Azruthor has given us a means of escape!
'The curse that binds us shall be lifted at this war's end and the line of Isildur shall finally be broken! We shall have no one left to answer to save for the Dark Lord, as it always should have been!
'You are too late, ${PLAYER}... we will overwhelm these lands and the Heirs of Castamir shall lead us all to freedom!'

'You bring word from Lamedon? I thank you for that. This Jajax seems like a helpful ally. The Corsairs you seek most likely reside in Belfalas.

'On my last journey home from visiting Calembel, I met a man named Gladion near Tarlang's Neck. You should speak to him for he may know more of what troubles our lands.'

'Ah, I do not believe I have seen you before, traveller, but... Lady Rosfin, that is a name I know!

The City of Dol Amroth

'Welcome, honoured guest. Did you enjoy your tour of our fair city? It is a beautiful and peaceful place, full of art, music, and bustling markets.
'Alas for the war that threatens us all. I fear that we will lose our way of life, if my father Imrahil cannot help Denethor uphold Minas Tirith against the shadow that looms in the east.'

'Have you ever seen a finer fountain? I have lived here all my life, but I still come every day just to gaze upon it. It is the pride of Dol Amroth.
'If you are travelling through, the Court of the Fount is where you want to be. Here we have the finest goods for sale from all over the world, brought from our ships. It is always bustling here. Never a dull moment!'
'Are you a travelling artisan, friend? If so, you have come to the right place, for you'll not find a better crafters' area for leagues upon leagues.'

'We get many travellers in Dol Amroth. I bid you welcome! I also say to you: Mind your behaviour while you are here. Drink and make merriment as you will, but do try not to cause a disturbance.
'Here is the Keep of the Swan-knights, where the finest soldiers of Dol Amroth execute the will of Prince Imrahil, or the lady Lothíriel who now governs in his place. A fine prospect, is it not?'
'I am the master stone-mason in these parts. Only the best stoneworkers in Gondor may study under me, and most will never master the art themselves.'
'This is the finest place for a concert in all the world. Musicians come here to practice, too, so there is always music upon the air. Oh, but how I love a sweet melody!'
'My pardons, I was lost in thought. People often come here to lose themselves in their thoughts, for this is the Scholar's Quarter. Here you will find the great minds of Dol Amroth.'

'Well met, stranger. Are you here to see the wharf? It is perhaps not the best view of Dol Amroth, but I have always found it the most beautiful place in the city.
'Here you will find all of the fishermen hard at work, and the tall ships rest ere they set out for another great adventure.
'Is there a better smell on earth than clean sea air and fresh fish, and the salt of sea and sweat?'

True Artistry

'What is this you have brought me? Ah, that girl Barían who comes to me every day, did her father do this? He was a great stone-mason.'
You explain that this is Barían's own work, and Laegened stares at you incredulously.
'I confess that I had no idea she was so advanced in her artistry. I have never had a young lady as an apprentice before, but I can see that she has what it takes. She may even become a master someday.'

'He has accepted me as an apprentice!? This is wonderful, ${PLAYER}, truly wonderful. I cannot wait to start!
'Thank you so much for your help. I did not know if he would even like the stone, but getting it to him has been such a great hassle.'

'What do you mean, not interested? You mean she would rather dirty herself with rocks and dust than accept my courtship? I do not understand.'
You decide it is best to leave this poet to ponder the state of the world on his own, rather than try to explain to him that he has thoroughly misjudged the character of the woman he claims to love.

'Here, I did away with your odd notes and composed a poem of better taste, more suited to woo a lovely young lady such as Barían.
'Bring this to her, if you please. I know she will not be able to resist my sweet words. Do tell her where to find me when you're done, please.'

'I am sorry, but I'm busy. I am trying to get Master Laegened's attention.'
You apologetically hand Barían the poem written for her, and she reads it with a scowl.
'I don't have time for this nonsense. I'm trying to get an apprenticeship, but Master Laegened won't even see me. He says he has too many worthless apprentices already. I want to show him my work, but I cannot haul it up the stairs!
'My work is down in the Scholar's Quarter. If only I could lift it!'

Artamir takes the crumpled parchment from you and unfolds it, but in mere moments he shakes his head.
'This is written in the speech of the Orcs, and no reputable Man of Gondor ever studied such words. My father never trusted the written word to begin with; Ilcamir was a man of action and of deeds, and I am no different than my sire!

'I trust you, ${PLAYER}. I will tell you the nature of my errand in this miserable land, and perhaps you can better help me accomplish it and then return to my home in triumph. I would give anything for this victory, my friend! The gratitude of the Steward would do much for my family's position.
'Long ago, the peace of Gondor was threatened by Wainriders from the East, cruel men who rode down their enemies in great wheeled chariots. It is said that Ondoher, one of the last of the true line of Kings, faced the Wainriders in battle on the great plain but was defeated. No sign was ever found of the King or his force, and Steward Denethor believes that the Wainriders might have driven him into the Dead Marshes before he perished.
'You think it unlikely? I would say so too, but for this. Denethor had of late a dream, in which he beheld the banner of the King flying proudly against the night sky. Could it be the banner of Ondoher, last of the line of Kings descended from Meneldil, Anárion's son? The strange waters of the swamp must have preserved it, after all this time, and I must find it and return with it to Minas Tirith!
'If these Orcs have found the King's Banner, they might be keeping it in a storage cache in their camp. Return to their camp and search these caches to ensure they have not!'

He was accompanied on his final journey by two of his sons, and they perished with him, perhaps in these very marshes. The names of these sons were Faramir, and, well... Artamir.'
He laughs wryly.
'Were it not for your help, ${PLAYER}, I would have met my end in the same foetid swamp that claimed my namesake! I will find no honour when I return to the White City without the prize I sought, but I will still have my life, and that is more than enough for Artamir son of Ilcamir! You have my thanks and that of my family. I will leave these miserable marshes, and at once!'

There are many threats in this place, from the treacherous terrain to the searching Orcs, and any might have claimed the life of poor Artamir.

'Step with care, hobbitses... the ground underfoot is not to be trusted, oh no it is not. Sméagol will show you where to go.'

'What... what is it, Sam? Were you... were you calling for me? I felt as if I heard you from a long way off, but there was something....'
Frodo shakes his head, trying to remember something.
'There were faces in the water. I could see them by the light of the candles, I think. But how could that be? There were so many: good faces and proud faces, stern faces and evil faces too. But why?'

'How are you holding up, Sam? This is a hard land... it seems so many of the places we must journey through are hard lands! I miss my own comfortable bed, and Bag End!
'There's nothing for it, is there? We have to keep going, one foot in front of the other. Sméagol will show us the way, if we are kind to him. He was treated very cruelly in Mordor, Sam. He has been through a lot.
'I suppose that is true for all of us, now. Just keep going, that is all we can do.'

'Did it see us? Aaaaach! Did it see us? Winged wraiths, terrible, terrible! They see everything, precious, everything! And they tell Him all that they see, they do! Did it see us?'
Gollum is shaking, his eyes wide with the terror of the experience. He will not move for some time.

'That was a Black Rider! I hoped we had seen the last of them, but I suppose that was an idle daydream. They are still searching for us.
'The Ring is so heavy, Sam. I know we need to keep going, but perhaps we can rest for a moment? Sméagol is beside himself... I do not think he will want to move for a while. Look at him! The poor creature. Not just him: all three of us! I will be glad to leave these Dead Marshes, but... just a rest... a short one.
'Then we will keep moving. Is that all right, Sam?'

'Nice hobbit, nice Sam, nothing to worry about, no, precious! Gollum, gollum! Did you get the sleepies you needed, did you, gollum? We needs to be moving again, yes, yes we do! No time for delays now!
'Master says we must go, so go we must, yes! Time to go, precious! Time to move!'

Frodo blinks at you for a moment and slowly rouses from his slumber.
'I suppose it is time to set out again? I am ready to be out of this wretched swamp, and the only way for it is to get moving again, I suppose. I am very tired, Sam.'

'Go to the Wharf and speak to the captains of the ships moored there. They will know the sea-worthiness of their own ships, and whether they might be made battle-ready.
'The true sea-power of Gondor is harboured at the city of Pelargir, but that port is far to the east and we cannot depend upon its ships for aid in time.'

'Before I became captain of my own ship, I served two years before the mast on the Alphroval. I know Maeral to be a wise captain and judge of the seas, but he is prone to recklessness. If he believes passage through the Sea-gate is a foolish journey, it must truly be so.
'Do you see the mighty ship in the waters outside the city? <rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> through the Sea-gate and tell me what you see.'

'See how that monster makes the other ships look like children's toys floating in a stream? That is the flagship of the Umbar fleet, Nûluzimir in their tongue: 'Night-jewel.'
'Many Gondorian ships have succumbed to the attacks of the Night-jewel during the years since the disappearance of Thorongil, greatest foe of the Corsairs! Would that he had returned before the Night-jewel was constructed, and might have prevented it! But none have seen Thorongil since he routed the Corsairs almost forty years ago. He is likely dead.
'I would not sail my ship against the Night-jewel unless I wanted her to lie on the sea-bottom, ${PLAYER}. None of our ships are a match for that one, not even Cirnaith's Súlrohir. Speak to him and see if he thinks otherwise.'

'Lothíriel wants a report from the captains of the ships docked at her city? There are no good tidings, friend. If there is any good fortune here it is that very few ships are trapped at the wharf, and most of Gondor's fleet must be found at the port city of Pelargir, to the east.
'They are too far away to help us here, but at least those ships are not caught like rabbits in a trap, as we are. It is hopeless!'

'I have only met Captain Cirnaith of the Súlrohir in passing, but I do know that he sent his crew into the city to make what merriment they might. He must believe there is nothing they can do ship-side to face the dangers that approach.'
'<rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> to the Sea-gate, if you wish to know the truth of the situation we face.'
'We are hemmed in and cannot escape. If you speak to Captain Noreth of the Rosigil, she will tell you much the same.'
'<rgb=#FF0000>Look</rgb> through the Sea-gate and you will see why we cannot hope to leave the city that way.'

'The Corsairs range far and wide upon the seas, ${PLAYER}, and have taken bottles of wine for my collection from every land lapped by the waves. You are welcome to sample any of my finest.'
'Well, you have heard my demands. You are not devising a counter-proposal, are you? You are in no position for this, my foolish ${CLASS}!'
'What advice would you give to me, ${PLAYER}?'

'This is the Nûluzimir, the jewel of Umbar and flagship of Balakhôr the Scourge. You are here under a flag of peace, but if it were otherwise you would never leave it, ${PLAYER}.
'I will bring you to Balakhôr. He will not be pleased that you have come instead of Imrahil's daughter, but that is not my concern. That must be yours.'

'So Umer delivered the message, but Lothíriel elected to send you in her stead? How am I to interpret this response? It reveals that she does not respect my wishes, and distrusts my word. It is a cowardly response, for it shows she values her own life and safety above those of others.'

'But you must already have known this, ${PLAYER}. Most of Gondor's warriors have been called to battles elsewhere. Even were they here, there is little they could do against the fleet of Umbar.
'But I have been a poor host. You must be quite parched, and I have done naught but tell you things you already know.'

'That seems to me a wiser course, ${PLAYER}, if you are willing to risk the adventure. Balakhôr cannot be trusted, but you may be better-prepared to deal with any treachery he might think to enact.
'Walk with me and I will do my best to prepare you for this errand.'

'I thank you, ${PLAYER}. Stay watchful in the company of Balakhôr. I know he is not to be trusted, and you should watch him carefully.
'Do what you can for the people of Dol Amroth! I would have gone myself, but if this plan eases Dorthaneth's mind....'

'Look around you, ${PLAYER}. What do you see? You see the sea-faring power of Umbar, rebuilt from nothing!
'Thirty years ago, a hero of Gondor sailed to Umbar at the head of a fleet. He burned the ships he found at the port and took the city. The Corsairs have spent the time nursing their hurts and rebuilding their power. No hero will save Gondor from them this time.
'Where is that hero now, ${PLAYER}? He is gone, and now I have come to return that overdue favour. I will burn his fleet as he did that of Umbar. But there will be nothing left to rebuild when I am finished with it.'

'I thank you for this favour, young one. It has been long years since I cast my eye beyond the banks of the stream. When last I did it brought only grief.'
Sadness wells in the deep pools of Roamingstar's eyes, and her words are nearly whispers.
'An Elf-maid tarried on the banks of Gilrain, lulled to sleep by the beauty of my song. She was reminded of her home, and I delighted in her presence, for my sisters had gone away and I was filled with loneliness.
'But she was needed, and when she awoke the delay had cost her the life of her love. He was an Elf-lord and a prince, Amroth by name, and he waited for her... but she never came. He died believing she was lost forever, and when she awoke it was he who was lost.'
Roamingstar's words trail away into silence. After a moment, the girl Roniel stirs.

'Oh, hello! Are you a friend of my mother? I was separated from her during the fighting. I ran and ran, and at some point I dropped my doll, but then I was just so tired and fell asleep.
'I think I had a lovely dream, but I cannot remember much of it now. I suppose it is time to return to Linhir. Do you think it is safe? Tell my mother I am on my way home. Her name is Mornil.'
Roamingstar is silent, lost in her thoughts.

'My brothers Erchar and Herion are fine warriors, though a bit rash in their decisions.
'We defended Linhir valiantly but the constant watch left us tired. Like brothers often do, we fall to quarreling. I was convinced by Aragorn's word that defending Linhir would be the best use of our skills. Erchar disagreed and convinced Herion that staying in Linhir was a fool's errand. He wanted to take the enemy by surprise. In an instant of protest, both Erchar and Herion took their forces into the field.
'I am afraid they may have met with slaughter. ${PLAYER}, would you ride out to the west and look for any signs of them? They may still be alive. Search for Erchar first. You will need to convince him to return before Herion will follow.'

'The size of that creature.... How did it ambush us?!
'It is no man. This much is certain. Perhaps these half-trolls are an experiment of Sauron, and a gift to the Haradrim.
'Now we know that the enemy is searching for us. With these weapons, my men can defend themselves from any additional scouts sent our way.
'Let us turn our attention to Herion.'

Le hablas al ciervo con palabras tranquilizadoras en la lengua de los animales, palabras que Grimbeorn y otros de los tuyos te enseñaron en tu juventud. El pánico del ciervo se atenúa poco a poco, aunque sus orejas aún se agitan ante cualquier sonido.
La actitud de la criatura asustada te indica que Clothar tiene razón en preocuparse: un gran depredador anda cerca.

'¿Qué es, qué es? No puedo soportarlo... ¿es el oso?
'¡No! ¡No me digas!'

'¡Sabía que había algo peculiar en ti, ${PLAYER}! Después de todo, no cualquiera puede hablar con los animales. ¡Tú... tú eres ${PLAYER:una[f]|un[m]} cambiaformas! ¡No solo son historias... también escorias, como decía mi viejo padre! ¡No puedo creer que de verdad exista gente como tú en este mundo!
Por un momento, Clothar parece a punto de desmayarse, pero luego se recompone y extiende la mano.
'Sería un honor estrechar tu mano, . Debe de haber muy poca gente como tú en este mundo. Es una lástima, porque podrías haber matado a ese oso y elegiste no hacerlo. En cambio, mostraste contención y misericordia. ¡Este mundo necesitaría más gente como tú, si este hobbit tiene voz!'
'Dejemos atrás este bosque, ${PLAYER}. Ya he tenido suficientes aventuras por hoy, ¡muchas gracias!'

Vuelves a tender la mano hacia el oso, recurriendo a tu afinidad natural con las criaturas. Un gruñido bajo confirma tu sospecha: algo ha infundido en el oso un miedo grande y terrible, poniendo en marcha este ataque frenético.
'Amigo', le hablas con tono tranquilizador, y el oso te dice su nombre.
De pronto, un fuerte estremecimiento sacude el cuerpo de la criatura, ¡y vuelve a atacar!

El miedo ha desaparecido de los ojos de Zarzagruño y ha sido reemplazado por otras emociones: respeto y admiración.
Tus palabras apaciguadoras y la firmeza de tu determinación han devuelto a Zarzagruño la razón. En la lengua de su especie, te cuenta sobre un espectro aterrador que rondaba las llanuras donde yacen los túmulos de Hombres muertos hace mucho tiempo. El rostro de ese terrible rey despertó en Zarzagruño un miedo primigenio, y no pudo sacudirse la locura que se apoderó de él.
Con un resoplido agradecido, Zarzagruño se da la vuelta y se interna de nuevo entre los árboles.

Tu ancestro Beorn tenía un vínculo especial con las criaturas que vivían cerca de su morada, y tú también has heredado parte de esa cualidad.
Intentas recurrir a ese aspecto de tu naturaleza para calmar a la poderosa bestia que tienes delante. ¿Qué ha llevado a esta criatura a semejante furia?
Parece que tus palabras surten efecto, pero de repente la criatura sacude su enorme cabeza y redobla su ataque.
Ahora estás seguro: el miedo se refleja en los ojos del oso
Ves algo en el ojo de la criatura que te hace dudar
Clothar Hojarena se encuentra en el Bosque Viejo y no está nada contento con ello.

Clothar se sobresaltó por la aparición repentina de un animal, pero solo era un ciervo nervioso, no el oso gigante que esperaba ver.
Deberías hablarle en la lengua de los animales y averiguar si ha visto al oso enloquecido.
¡Has encontrado al oso que amenazó a Clothar y lo llenó de miedo!
El oso es enorme y parece dominado por la furia, pero aun así ves algo en su mirada que te hace dudar.
'Oh, no sé nada de esto, ${PLAYER}. Sé que dije que te mostraría dónde vi al oso gigante, pero cuanto más nos acercamos, menos me gusta estar aquí. ¡Esto fue un error!'

'Te oí, ${PLAYER}, ¡y ese ciervo también! Y no en el sentido de hablarle a los conejos que rondan un jardín para ahuyentarlos con la voz. Lo que sea que le dijiste a ese ciervo, te entendió, ¡igual que yo!
'¿Cómo aprendiste la lengua de los animales?'
Instancia: El lenguaje de los animales
Clothar Hojarena se encuentra en el Bosque Viejo y apenas puede creer lo que ven sus ojos y oyen sus oídos.
Has aprendido el nombre del gran oso, Zarzagruño, y que algún mal ha infundido en la criatura un miedo grande y terrible, llevándola a un estado de frenesí.
El miedo ha desaparecido y ahora ves algo distinto en los ojos de Zarzagruño: respeto y admiración. Has salvado al oso de sí mismo.
Te encontraste con un ciervo nervioso en el Bosque Viejo y supiste que hay un depredador cerca. ¿Podría ser el oso gigante con el que se topó Clothar Hojarena?

Has encontrado al oso que amenazó y aterrorizó a Clothar.
Parecía que casi lograbas calmar al gran oso con tus palabras, pero la criatura logró sacudirse tu influencia.
Has visto miedo en los ojos del gran oso y ahora estás seguro: algo contrario a su naturaleza ha empujado a esta criatura a atacar.
Clothar Hojarena te ha llevado al Bosque Viejo en busca del oso gigante que tanto lo aterrorizó.
Clothar Hojarena se encuentra en el Campamento de Adso y quiere que investigues al gran oso que lo aterrorizó.

Clothar Hojarena se encuentra en el Campamento de Adso. Lo ayudaste a rastrear al gran oso que lo había aterrorizado y también ayudaste al oso a encontrar consuelo.
Clothar ahora sabe que perteneces a la estirpe de Beorn y le está costando adaptarse a ese conocimiento.
Habla con Clothar Hojarena y te mostrará dónde vio al gran oso
Habla con Clothar Hojarena en el Campamento de Adso

'¿Estás aquí para ayudarnos? ¡Por favor, dime que estás aquí para ayudar!'
Le aseguras a Clothar Hojarena que harás todo lo que esté a tu alcance y le preguntas qué lo aqueja.
'¡Un oso, una cosa enorme y monstruosa! Intentamos no acercarnos demasiado al bosque si podemos evitarlo, pero a veces no hay otra opción y Adso necesita que vayamos bajo el dosel por una razón u otra. Bueno, ayer por la tarde yo estaba justo entre los árboles cuando vi la enorme silueta de un oso avanzando pesadamente hacia mí. ¡Era grande, incluso más grande que tú, y su sola presencia me llenó de terror!'
'Si crees que puedes hacer algo con respecto a este demonio con forma de oso, porque sin duda debe serlo, dímelo y te mostraré dónde vi a la bestia'

'Muy bien, ven conmigo. Te mostraré dónde vi a ese enorme oso. Pero si lo vemos otra vez, tendrás que protegerme. ¿Estás de acuerdo? ¡Porque, de lo contrario, me quedo aquí mismo, muchas gracias!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Esta es una misión en solitario y no puede completarse con una comunidad.</rgb>

'He oído historias sobre cambiaformas, ¡pero nunca pensé que conocería a ${PLAYER:una[f]|uno[m]}! Creo que esperaba que dieran más miedo o que fueran más salvajes, pero pareces una persona bastante agradable. Solo pensé que eras muy ${PLAYER:alta[f]|alto[m]}.
'Mostraste una verdadera compasión por ese oso. No creo que la mayoría de los aventureros hubiera hecho lo mismo: hablar con él en lugar de matarlo, quiero decir. A veces hablar es más difícil, pero diría que el esfuerzo vale la pena si salva la vida de un inocente.
'Bueno, cambiaformas, ¡me abriste los ojos! Creo que ya he tenido suficiente autodescubrimiento por hoy. Ahora me vendría bien una buena porción de tarta de arándanos y una siesta!'
El lenguaje de los animales
Clothar Hojarena dice que la gente del campamento de Adso ha estado aterrorizada por un gran oso que anda merodeando por el Bosque Viejo.

Jon Helecharroyo está frente a los restos de la Taberna del Tejón Loco, en la aldea incendiada de Archet.
Letty Colazorro te ha dicho que hables con Jon Helecharroyo sobre el paradero de Aragorn, quien dejó la aldea de Archet poco antes de que fuera atacada por los bandidos Montebruno. Jon está a cargo de reconstruir la aldea ahora que su padre ha muerto.
Habla con Jon Helecharroyo frente a los restos de la taberna, en la aldea de Archet

'Debo decir, ¡eres alguien muy alto! ¿De dónde has venido y cómo te llamas? ¿${PLAYER}? Ese es un nombre bastante inusual. ¿Qué asuntos te traen a Archet? Tenemos nuestros propios problemas, y poca necesidad de que forasteros traigan los suyos.'
Le dices a la mujer que has viajado desde lejos buscando al montaraz Aragorn. Ella piensa por un momento y luego niega con la cabeza.
'Es cierto que estuvo aquí, pero se ha marchado. Se fue justo antes de que los bandidos Montebruno lanzaran su ataque sobre nuestra aldea, reduciéndola a este estado. Podríamos haberlo usado en la defensa. A decir verdad, también podríamos haberte usado a ti, si hubieras llegado un poco antes. Pareces ser fuerte.
'No sé adónde ha ido ahora el montaraz, pero Jon Helecharroyo podría saberlo. Él ha asumido el mando del proceso de reconstrucción, ahora que su padre ha fallecido. Lo encontrarás frente a los restos de la taberna, imagino. Lo vi allí más temprano.'

'Bueno, ¡debo decir que nunca esperé ver a alguien de tu gente por estas tierras! Eres de la línea de Beorn, ¿no es así? Tu estatura y tu porte me parecen inconfundibles. Nunca había conocido a alguien de tu familia hasta hoy, pero he oído hablar de tu pueblo por montaraces y otros habitantes de la naturaleza.'
Le cuentas a Jon Helecharroyo por qué has venido a Archet, y él asiente.
'Sí, Aragorn estuvo aquí, aunque en estas tierras se hace llamar Trancos. Se fue con cierta prisa, pero oí de otros que lamentaba hacerlo y deseaba quedarse para ayudarnos con nuestros problemas. Se dirigió a Bree, a menos que haya oído mal.
'¡Pero espera, ${PLAYERNAME:mi alto amigo[m]|mi alta amiga[f]}! No te apresures a marcharte aún. Vienes a nosotros en nuestra hora más oscura, cuando los bandidos Montebruno han quemado nuestra aldea y matado a muchos de nuestros amigos. Mi propio padre pereció en la noche, abatido por los Montebruno y sus odiosos aliados del norte... de Angmar. Sé que deseas encontrar a Aragorn, pero si realmente compartes sus ideales, dedicarás un momento aquí o allá para ayudar a quienes lo necesitan. La experiencia te hará más fuerte, y juntos podremos impedir que otras aldeas sean quemadas en nombre del mal. Piénsalo, .'

'El montaraz Aragorn estuvo aquí, es cierto, pero se marchó antes del ataque de los Montebruno. No sé adónde fue, pero Jon Helecharroyo podría saberlo. Jon está a cargo de reconstruir la aldea ahora que su padre ha muerto.'
El Rastro del Montaraz
Ayudando a la gente de las Tierras de Bree te volverás lo bastante fuerte como para encontrar a Aragorn
Tras un largo viaje de muchas millas, has llegado por fin a la aldea de Archet. Aragorn fue visto recientemente viajando en las cercanías de este tranquilo pueblo.
Habla con Sterkist y convéncelo de que no permanezca como un oso malhumorado

'Aragorn es un Montaraz, lo que significa que viaja a menudo por lo Salvaje, y la gente de las aldeas más allá de las montañas lo mira con desconfianza. ¡Muy parecido a mí, ahora que lo pienso!
'Aquí, te acompañaré un trecho, y te contaré lo que sé del camino a través de las montañas, y cómo encontrar las Tierras de Bree...'
Te has preparado para el viaje, y ahora ha llegado el momento de dejar la tierra de tu hogar en busca del Montaraz Aragorn.
Langhár te sonríe, pero antes de hablar con tu hermana deberías terminar tu primera tarea: derrotar a las moscas guadaña que zumban cerca.

'¿Estos trasgos creyeron que podrían superarme? ¡Criaturas necias! Harían falta dos docenas de trasgos para sacarme una gota de sangre, ¡y aun así yo sería superior!
'Date prisa hacia el refugio y dile a Grimbeorn que los trasgos han perdido cualquier pizca de sensatez que quizá tuvieron alguna vez.'

Le cuentas rápidamente a Sterkist sobre los trasgos que te atacaron a ti y a Langhár.
'¡Eso es muy extraño, ${PLAYER}! Beorn infundió el miedo de los nuestros en los trasgos cuando acechaba estos valles, y nosotros hemos hecho nuestra parte para mantener su terror de nosotros, ¿no es así? ¿Qué podría hacerles pensar en volver una vez más a este lado del río?'

'Sí, joven. He tomado mi decisión. Dejarás esta tierra protegida y llevarás un mensaje de advertencia donde el Mago crea que debe ir. Por mucho tiempo pensé que nuestro pueblo podía permanecer separado de las demás gentes, como deseaba mi padre, pero esos días han quedado atrás.
'Quizá envíe a otros en los días venideros, pero por ahora tú representarás el linaje de Beorn en el mundo más amplio. Actúa con fuerza y claridad de propósito, , y que todos los que te vean digan: 'Allá va ${PLAYER:una mujer[f]|un hombre[m]} del linaje de Beorn. ¡Crúzate con ${PLAYER:él[m]|ella[f]} bajo tu propio riesgo!'.
'No creo en despedidas largas, joven. Aprende tu tarea del Mago, despídete de tus hermanos, y no traigas deshonra a nuestro linaje.'

'¡Bien, bien, bien! Temía que Grimbeorn no comprendiera la urgencia de este asunto, pero la razón ha prevalecido. Siempre he tenido mano con osos y bestias, y bueno... ya ves... nada, nada. ¡No es importante!
'Un poder oscuro está creciendo, ${PLAYER}. No puedo ponerle un nombre, si es que tiene uno, pero algo ha alterado el mundo natural. Buscaré al mayor de los Cinco Magos, pues él ha estudiado muchas cosas que desconozco y puede saber qué está ocurriendo.
'Quiero que tú busques a otra persona. Es un Montaraz, y su nombre es Aragorn. Ha estado enredado en los asuntos de los Magos desde hace tiempo, y si los temblores que percibo representan un peligro real, como temo, sé que Aragorn deberá tener especial cuidado para no caer presa de ellos.
'Lo último que supe de él es que viajaba por las Tierras de Bree, más allá de las montañas.'
Sterkist gruñe en el lenguaje de los osos, pero tus palabras están llenas de afecto. Él se eriza, y finalmente cede.

'¿Hemos llegado a esto, ${PLAYER}? ¿Sirves a quienes son más perezosos que tú, buscando vacas perdidas y haciendo recados?'
Ofolmóth ríe con rudeza.
'Eres del linaje de Beorn, igual que yo, pero no he olvidado lo que eso significa. ¡Para ti significa poco! Deberíamos vivir nuestras vidas con ferocidad, aprovechando cada momento con dientes y garras. Nadie es mi amo.
'Temo que te has vuelto ${PLAYER:blando[m]|blanda[f]}, . ¡Solo aprovechando tu Ira en combate podrás honrar verdaderamente tu herencia! ¡Prepárate para la batalla y pon a prueba tus habilidades contra mí!'

'Somos pocos como nosotros, ${PLAYER}. Por eso te pongo a prueba como lo hago. El legado de Beorn es raro y menguante. ¡Debemos usarlo para ser los más fuertes de sus hijos y nietos! Mientras combatimos, la Ira llena nuestros corazones y nos impulsa con gran ferocidad, potenciando las habilidades que usamos en batalla.
'¡Que nuestros enemigos tengan cuidado! ¡Se enfrentan al linaje de Beorn bajo su propio riesgo!'

'Nada me enoja tanto como la debilidad, ${PLAYER}. ¡Expúlsala de tu cuerpo con entrenamiento y práctica! El linaje de Beorn no merece menos.
'Sigue la cerca que rodea y practica tus habilidades contra las moscas-guadaña que encuentres. ¡Ese entrenamiento te hará más fuerte y más feroz!'

'¡No pensaba volver a verte hoy, mi ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}! La mayoría de las tardes las pasas soñando al sol con Sterkist. ¿Qué tiene de diferente este día?'
Le dices a Langhár que Radagast el Mago ha visitado a Grimbeorn, y que Ofolmóth te puso a luchar contra moscas-guadaña como práctica. Tu hermana sonríe y adopta una voz ronca y feroz.
'¡Lucha! ¡Ruge! ¡Batalla! ¡Gruñe! ¡El linaje de Beorn es el mejor de todos!', vocifera, en una imitación aceptable de Ofolmóth.

'¿No te dije que tu momento llegaría pronto, mi ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}? ¡Quizá sea tan Mago como el propio Radagast!'
Langhár se ríe alegremente.
'No, eso no es lo que quiero. Quiero explorar las tierras más allá de nuestro hogar, , como tú estás a punto de hacer. ¡Quiero buscar aventura! Te seguiré más pronto que tarde, , ¡te lo aseguro!
'¡Hasta que nos encontremos de nuevo, ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}! Encuentra a ese Montaraz, entrega el mensaje de Radagast, ¡y no sacies tu sed de aventura hasta que Sterkist y yo podamos unirnos a ti!'

Te acercas a la vaca lechera y ella brama nerviosamente. Algo la ha alterado. ¿Qué podría ser?
Cuando eras joven desarrollaste la habilidad de comprender muchos de los lenguajes animales, un don de tu ancestro Beorn. Ahora recurres a esa facilidad natural para hablarle suavemente a la vaca lechera.
Al poco tiempo recupera la calma y comienza a volver lentamente a su corral.
Ofolmóth está rodeado por los cuerpos de trasgos
Moscas-guadaña derrotadas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

El Mago Radagast ha venido al refugio de Grimbeorn, y tu mente corre intentando averiguar la razón. Tu hermano Sterkist quiere tu ayuda para descubrir qué ha traído al Mago desde su hogar en el Bosque Negro.

Varthmath quizá sepa qué trajo a Radagast fuera del Bosque Negro, y deberías encontrarlo en el corral de animales al oeste del refugio. Tu primo es un hombre de pocas palabras, pero sus oídos atentos no se pierden nada.

'¿Cuántas tardes hemos pasado así, ? Una vez terminado el trabajo y las tareas hechas, parece que todos los días nos encuentran mirando el estanque del viejo Grimbeorn, pensando pensamientos livianos.'
Sterkist suspira, como suele hacerlo en estas tardes, y se rasca distraídamente el brazo.
'Eres mi ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}, , y no guardamos secretos entre nosotros. ¿Es esto todo lo que podemos esperar? ¡La sangre del cambiapieles fluye en nosotros y debe impulsarnos a hazañas mayores que estas!'

'He visto a Radagast solo una o dos veces, y fue cuando éramos muy pequeños; ¿lo recuerdas? Éramos muy pequeños entonces, y él fue amable con nosotros, pero no creo que disfrutara dejar su hogar en el Bosque Negro.
'¡Algo serio debe haber ocurrido para traerlo hasta aquí, mi ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}! Olfatearé alrededor del refugio e intentaré escuchar algo de su conversación con nuestro padre, y tú deberías hablar con Varthmath en los corrales. Nuestro primo habla poco, pero oye mucho, y podría saber algo.'

'¿Qué te trae por aquí, ${PLAYERNAME:primo[m]|prima[f]}?'
Le cuentas a Varthmath que Radagast el Mago ha dejado el Bosque Negro y está hablando con Grimbeorn, y que esperabas que él hubiese oído por qué. Varthmath responde con un resoplido brusco.
'Sé qué lo trae aquí: sus propios asuntos. Si llega a ser un tema nuestro, Grimbeorn nos lo dirá. Hasta entonces deberías atender tus propios asuntos. Mejor aún: deberías hacer algo útil para mí.
'Una de nuestras vacas lecheras se ha alejado del corral. Encuéntrala antes de que salga del muro que rodea, y dile que regrese.'
Instancia: La Herencia del Cambiapieles

Ofolmóth quiere que pongas a prueba tu temple contra las moscas guadaña alrededor de la cerca. Si rodeas la cerca hacia el oeste y el sur, encontrarás suficientes molestias para obtener una buena práctica.

Tu hermana Langhár suele pasear por los campos de trébol, vigilando cualquier amenaza que se acerque demasiado al hogar de Grimbeorn. Ella te llamó después de que derrotaras a muchas moscas guadaña, y puede encontrarse al suroeste.
Los trasgos han llegado a los valles del Anduin, y deberías llevar noticia de su presencia a Grimbeorn en su refugio.
Parece que Radagast ya sabía del movimiento de los trasgos, y que su visita a Grimbeorn está relacionada de algún modo con los crecientes problemas del mundo.
Grimbeorn ha tomado su decisión: te enviará en el encargo de Radagast, para llevar una advertencia sobre la oscuridad creciente que amenaza la Tierra Media.
Radagast tiene un encargo urgente para ti, y te llevará lejos de las tierras familiares de tu hogar.
Ha llegado el momento de despedirte de tus hermanos antes de salir hacia el mundo más amplio.

Tú y tu hermano Sterkist han pasado muchas tardes mirando las aguas quietas del estanque junto al refugio de Grimbeorn una vez terminado el trabajo.
Sterkist está filosófico esta tarde en particular y desea continuar vuestra conversación.
Una de las vacas lecheras ha salido del corral, y Varthmath quiere que la encuentres y la envíes de vuelta antes de que salga del recinto de Grimbeorn.

Ofolmóth cree que el linaje de Beorn se sirve mejor mediante batalla constante y feroz. Quiere asegurarse de que seas tan fuerte como puedas ser, y quiere que pongas a prueba tus habilidades contra él en combate.
Te ha pedido que hables con él cuando estés ${PLAYERNAME:listo[m]|lista[f]}.
Los trasgos han llegado a los valles del Anduin, y deberías volver al refugio de Grimbeorn y advertir a tu familia del peligro.
Has vivido en los valles protegidos del Río Anduin toda tu vida, pero ahora las tierras salvajes te llaman, y la aventura se abre ante ti.

'Sal de estas salas y abre camino hacia la superficie. En la cima de Zirakzigil, <rgb=#FF0000>ruge</rgb> nuestro legítimo dominio sobre los cielos, ${PLAYER}. Encuentra un lugar lo bastante impresionante, un punto de referencia con algo de majestuosidad, desde el cual llevar a cabo este acto. Quiero que todos, enanos y orcos por igual, sepan que la estirpe de Beorn reclama las laderas de las montañas y no teme a nada.'

'Sé que hiciste lo que te pedí, . Los enanos pueden reclamar estas antiguas salas, y son bienvenidos a ellas. No siento afecto alguno por estos pasajes sombríos. Lo que extraño es el aire frío y puro de las montañas. Algún día, cuando los orcos se hayan ido y los enanos también se hayan ido, regresaremos al hogar que dejamos hace tanto tiempo y correremos por las laderas de las montañas, y allí encontraremos alegría.
'Ese día aún no ha llegado, ${PLAYERNAME:primo mío[m]|prima mía[f]}, pero llegará, y entonces nuestro audaz ancestro estará orgulloso de nosotros.'

'Lo hiciste bien, ${PLAYERNAME:primo mío[m]|prima mía[f]}. Los orcos y trasgos creían estar a salvo en las salas de esta ciudad maldita, pues la estirpe de Beorn estaba en la superficie y muy lejos. Ahora saben que nuestro alcance es grande, pero quiero que sepan que no somos simples visitantes. Tenemos un derecho sobre las laderas de las montañas que se alzan sobre estas salas, un derecho más fuerte que el de los enanos sobre estos pasajes sombríos.
'Sal de estas salas y abre camino hacia la superficie. En la cima de Zirakzigil, <rgb=#FF0000>ruge</rgb> nuestro legítimo dominio sobre los cielos, . Encuentra un lugar lo bastante impresionante, un punto de referencia con algo de majestuosidad, desde el cual llevar a cabo este acto. 'Ah, ${PLAYERNAME:primo mío[m]|prima mía[f]}, ¡es bueno ver un rostro conocido! Hice venir a Sterkist hasta aquí, pero parece que te envió a ti en su lugar. No lo culpo por haber decidido no venir. Yo no habría entrado en esta oscuridad si hubiera tenido elección, pero esa es precisamente la situación. ¡Son esos enanos! Incitan a los trasgos innecesariamente y despiertan criaturas del mal que deberían permanecer dormidas.
'Sabes que Beorn y su estirpe se originaron en las montañas. Las montañas que se alzan sobre estas salas malditas son el verdadero hogar de nuestro pueblo, por derecho. Estos enanos agitan a los trasgos y las criaturas se desparraman por todas las montañas. ¿Cómo podemos esperar recuperar algún día nuestro territorio si está constantemente amenazado por enanos u orcos?
'¡Combate contra orcos por todos los confines más lejanos de Moria, , y enséñales a temer a la estirpe de Beorn!'

'Sabía a qué veníamos, pero aun así me resistía a herir a Ofolmóth. Él no mostró tal reparo, y sus garras cortaron hondo.
Langhár se estremece por el dolor de su herida.
'No sé mucho acerca de Skorgrím, pero lo poco que he aprendido es inquietante. Me queda claro que manipuló de algún modo a nuestro antiguo pariente, aprovechándose de sus debilidades.
'Hemos hecho lo que Grimbeorn nos pidió y puesto fin a la amenaza que Ofolmóth representaba para la gente inocente. Eso debe ser suficiente por hoy. Quizá mañana hagamos algo respecto a Skorgrím Duramano, pues su peligro aún persiste.'
'Regresemos a Ost Guruth. Estoy herida, pero puedo caminar.'
¡Langhár está en dificultades!
Has llegado con Langhár a las Ciénagas del Sur en busca de Ofolmóth. Ella espera hablar contigo antes de continuar hacia las ruinas donde se vio por última vez a tu pariente.
Has encontrado a Ofolmóth, y se pregunta si has venido a unirte a él.
'Ofolmóth fue visto por última vez entre las ruinas que tenemos delante. Avancemos con cautela, ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}.'

'Tu expresión me da la respuesta, ${PLAYER}. Ya lo suponía. Fue una vana esperanza creer que honrarías la memoria de nuestro pueblo y la sangre de Beorn. En cambio, te pones del lado de quienes no son dignos de ti.
'Creí que podía hacerte fuerte, ${PLAYER}. Fracasé en eso, y lo lamento.'

'¿Estás ${PLAYER:listo[m]|lista[f]}, ? Ofolmóth no vendrá con nosotros, pero no podemos dejarlo libre, pues es un peligro para la gente inocente de la Tierra Media. No sé mucho sobre estos enanos, pero puedo decir que este Skorgrím corrompe a cualquiera que entra en contacto con él.
'¡Yo me encargaré de Ofolmóth si tú puedes ocuparte de estos enanos, ${PLAYER:hermana[f]|hermano[m]}!'
