Libera al lince de la trampa
Habla con Bingo de vuelta en el camino al sureste del Claro de los Trolls de Piedra
'Oh no, ${PLAYER}. ¡Una criatura indefensa ha caído en una trampa! ¿Puedes ayudar al pobre animal? ¡Qué crueldad! ¡Me duele solo verlo!'

'Me alegro de que el lince esté libre, ¡y espero que no haya sufrido daños permanentes!
'Vayamos hacia el sureste, y decidamos dónde ir a continuación cuando hayamos vuelto al camino.'
'Es ese lince nos ha estado siguiendo desde hace un rato, ¡y nos mira fijamente desde el otro lado del camino! ¿Puedes... crees que puedes <rgb=#FF0000>hacerle señas</rgb> para espantarlo?'

El lince devora alegremente la carne, y después te mira de forma enigmática.
Quizá Willem Bigotes sea un nombre apropiado, ahora que te paras a pensarlo.
'Creo que Willem debe estar hambriento. Mira a ver si puedes conseguir algo de carne de las ciervas y venados de estos bosques. ¡Estoy seguro de que lo agradecerá!'
'¿Por qué el retraso? ¡Lleva esa carne de ciervo a Willem Bigotes! ¡Debe estar muerto de hambre!'

'¡Lo sabía! ¡Sabía que le encantaría la carne de ciervo! ¡Buen trabajo, ${PLAYER}!
'Lo he estado pensando, y creo que deberíamos permitirle que se quede con nosotros tanto como quiera. Es un buen chico, me atrevería a decir, y será bueno tener otro compañero en este viaje. Sin ánimo de ofender, ¡por supuesto! Pero no eres tan peludito como Willem Bigotes, ¿no?
'¡Por aquí, W.B! ¡Eres bienvenido a viajar con nosotros tanto como desees! ¡Marchemos hacia la siguiente parada en mi mapa: la entrada de Rivendel, el valle escondido!'
'El valle escondido de Rivendel está marcado en mi mapa. Parece que está en las tierras altas del Bosque de los Trolls, al este.'

'¿Qué propósito trae a tu grupo al valle escondido, ${PLAYER}? ¿Tienes buena relación con quien te sigue? Parece comportarse bien por el momento, pero me pregunto si eso cambiará en el momento en que tenga hambre.'
El centinela ríe, con un sonido musical.
'¿El lince? No, no hablo del lince, ${PLAYER}. ¡Hablo del hobbit de aspecto hambriento!'

'Bien hecho, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. ¡Pobre animal! Entiendo la necesidad de cazar animales para comer, por supuesto, pero fabricar esa trampa parecía innecesariamente cruel. Me alegro de que el lince esté libre, ¡y espero que no haya sufrido daños permanentes!
'Vayamos hacia el sureste, y decidamos dónde ir a continuación cuando hayamos vuelto al camino.'

'${PLAYER}, no quiero preocuparte pero... ¡nos están siguiendo! ¡No, no hagas movimientos bruscos!
'Es ese lince... nos ha estado siguiendo desde hace un rato, ¡y nos mira fijamente desde el otro lado del camino! ¿Puedes... crees que puedes <rgb=#FF0000>hacerle señas</rgb> para espantarlo?'

'¡No ha funcionado, ${PLAYER}! ¡Tdoavía nos mira fijamente! Mmm... ¿crees que Willem Bigotes tiene hambre?'
Bingo se pone rojo ante tu expresión de duda y, de repente, se muestra cohibido.
'¿Qué? Necesitaba un nombre, ¿no? Willem Bigotes parece apropiado. ¡Mira qué cara! De cualquier manera, creo que debe tener hambre. Mira a ver si puedes conseguir algo de carne de las ciervas y venados de estos bosques. ¡Estoy seguro de que Willem lo agradecerá!'
'¡Espero que nos dejen pasar al valle! ¡Deseo enormemente verlo!'
'¡Según mi mapa esta es la entrada al valle escondido!'

'¿De verdad? ¿Este elfo cree que soy más peligroso para la paz de Rivendel que nuestro nuevo amigo W.B?'
El rostro de Bingo rebosa indignación, pero no logra mantener la máscara mucho tiempo y pronto vuelve a su habitual y jovial humor.
'¡Estos elfos son perspicaces, ${PLAYER}! Willem Bigotes no les causará ningún problema, ¡pero si hay ricos platos que comer en Rivendel yo sí seré una amenaza!'
<rgb=#FF0000>La semana que viene: 'Un hogar hospitalario' (Nivel recomendado: 39)</rgb>
'Espero que no causes ningún problema en Rivendel, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}.'

Tres grandes figuas de piedra se alzan en el claro
Carne de ciervo conseguida (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bingo está en el Claro de los Trolls de Piedra, en el Bosque de los Trolls.

'He estado revisando el mapa que me hizo comenzar mi gran aventura, ¡y ya sé el próximo lugar donde quiero ir, ${PLAYER}! Si mis cálculos son correctos, deberíamos estar cerca. ¿Ves esta zona donde los árboles hacia el este y un poco al norte? El autor de este mapa ha dibujado tres figuras aquí, en este claro. ¡Mira qué sonrientes están!
'Quiero encontrar el Claro de las Figuras Sonrientes. Debería estar al este de nuestra localización y un poco al norte, pero también podría haber paredes de roca impenetrables en nuestro camino. Quizá necesitemos volver al camino antes de que podamos encontrar un camino hacia el claro al noreste.'

'Si mis cálculos son correctos, deberíamos estar cerca. ¿Ves esta zona donde los árboles hacia el este y un poco al norte? El autor de este mapa ha dibujado tres figuras aquí, en este claro. ¡Mira qué sonrientes están!
'Quiero encontrar el Claro de las Figuras Sonrientes. Debería estar al este de nuestra localización y un poco al norte, pero también podría haber paredes de roca impenetrables en nuestro camino. Quizá necesitemos volver al camino antes de que podamos encontrar un camino hacia el claro al noreste.'

'¡Mira qué piedras tan enormes! ¡Trolls! ¡Tenemos suerte de que son simples estatuas, y no de verdad!'
La sonrisa de Bingo se desvanece cuando mira al noroeste entre dos de las figuras, y frunce el ceño.
'Oh no, ${PLAYER}. ¡Una criatura indefensa ha caído en una trampa! ¿Puedes ayudar al pobre animal? ¡Qué crueldad! ¡Me duele solo verlo!'
'¡Mira eso! ¡Me alegra que estén hechos de piedra, y que no sean trolls de verdad!'

El Claro de las Tres Figuras Sonrientes está al noreste de donde Bingo y tú habéis acampado para la noche. Bingo te ha sugerido volver al camino antes de poner dirección norte hacia el claro.
Bingo ha visto a un lince capturado en una trampa en el Claro de los Trolls de Piedra, y te ha pedido que liberes a la pobre criatura.

Pueden encontrarse ciervas y venados por todo el Bosque de los Trolls, y de ellos deberías ser capaz de conseguir la carne de ciervo que Bingo te ha pedido.

'¡Mira quién está aquí!'
'¿Podría ser que hayamos encontrado al mismo hobbit que dibujó el mapa que encontré en ese libro de cocina?'

'Antes de dejar la Comarca, pasé algo de tiempo visitando mis rincones favoritos para grabarlos en mi memoria. Incluso ahora, puedo ver muchos de mis senderos soleados favoritos y mis bancos más tranquilos donde descansar. Pero algo trajo la tristeza a mi corazón: el que ninguno de los queridos hobbits que estaba dejando atrás no experimentaría nunca las mismas alegrías que yo al explorar el mundo. Oh, supe que Frodo estaría bien; siempre ha sido un chico con ganas de aventura, pero eso era algo inusual.
'Concebí un plan, ${PLAYER}. Dibujaría un mapa del ancho mundo, y lo dejaría en un libro de recetas en la biblioteca de Alforzaburgo. Quizás lo encontraría un hobbit curioso, o alguno que solo necesitara un pequeño empujoncito para embarcarse en una gran aventura.
'¡Y mira! ¡Tenía razón! ¡Gandalf estaría muy orgulloso de mi inventiza, ${PLAYER}! Espero, por el bien de Bingo, que no haya dragones involucrados, como pasó conmigo. Me sentiría responsable si fuera así, ¡aunque por ahora me parece una aventurilla y una alegría!'

'Ah, ¿querías decirme que Bingo encontró mi mapa de Eriador? ¡Me alegra mucho, ${PLAYER}!
'Antes de dejar la Comarca, pasé algo de tiempo visitando mis rincones favoritos para grabarlos en mi memoria. Incluso ahora, puedo ver muchos de mis senderos soleados favoritos y mis bancos más tranquilos donde descansar. Pero algo trajo la tristeza a mi corazón: el que ninguno de los queridos hobbits que estaba dejando atrás no experimentaría nunca las mismas alegrías que yo al explorar el mundo. Oh, supe que Frodo estaría bien; siempre ha sido un chico con ganas de aventura, pero eso era algo inusual.
'Concebí un plan, ${PLAYER}. Dibujaría un mapa del ancho mundo, y lo dejaría en un libro de recetas en la biblioteca de Alforzaburgo. Quizás lo encontraría un hobbit curioso, o alguno que solo necesitara un pequeño empujoncito para embarcarse en una gran aventura.
'¡Y mira! ¡Tenía razón! ¡Gandalf estaría muy orgulloso de mi inventiza, ${PLAYER}! Espero, por el bien de Bingo, que no haya dragones involucrados, como pasó conmigo. Me sentiría responsable si fuera así, ¡aunque por ahora me parece una aventurilla y una alegría!'

'Apenas puedo creerlo, ${PLAYER}. Bilbo Bolsón, el gran autor y aventurero, ¡es el responsable de que me embarcara en este gran viaje! Tengo muchas cosas que preguntarle, ¡tanto sobre sus aventuras como sobre sus escritos!'
<rgb=#FF0000>La semana que viene: 'Notas del autor' (Nivel recomendado: 40)</rgb>

'Deberías presentarte ante el gran Elfo y decirle que hemos venido a hacerle una breve visita. No he oído hablar sobre la hospitalidad de los Elfos, ¡pero seguro que no carecen de ella! No nos cerrará la puerta, eso seguro.'

'¡Siempre es un placer ver a un hobbit fuera de la Comarca, ${PLAYER}! Bingo parece ser un individuo interesante, ¡y me alegra verle probando sus límites!
'He dibujado un mapa rápido con algunas de las vistas más notables de Rivendel. ¡Encontrad cada una de estas localizaciones y habréis visto algunos de los lugares más bellos del valle! Si tuviera más tiempo podría hacer un mapa más decente, pero es lo que he podido hacer con las prisas. ¡Ve, antes de que Bingo pierda su afán por explorar y vivir aventuras! ¡Es el miedo que tengo con todos los hobbits: que las ansias de aventura se marchen tan rápido como llegaron!'

'Ha sido muy divertido, ¡y en cada lugar me maravillaba de nuevo con la belleza tan pura de Rivendel! Espero que no fuéramos una molestia para los Elfos que viven aquí, ¡ya que a veces me quedaba embobado y tenía que retenerme para no darle a la lengua!
'Gracias de nuevo por encargarte del mapa, ya que yo era incapaz de mantener mis ojos apartados del paisaje en vez de mirarlo. Es un mapa bastante bien dibujado, ahora que lo miro más de cerca.'
Bingo para de hablar y coge el mapa.
'Espera un momento, ${PLAYER}... ¡hay algo muy característico en este mapa! ¿Ves cómo el artista ha usado estas líneas de aquí para dar forma a las montañas? ¡Me es muy familiar, ya que las montañas de mi mapa están dibujadas de la misma manera! Recuerdas el mapa, ¿verdad? ¡Es el mapa por el que comencé mi aventura, hace ya tanto! ¿Podría ser que hayamos encontrado al hobbit que dibujó el mapa que encontré en el libro de recetas?'
'Deberías presentarle a este Bingo Boffin a Bilbo Bolsón, en el Salón del Fuego. Deben tener mucho en común; a pesar de mis bromas, los hobbits siguen siendo algo inusual de ver en Imladris.'
'Deberías presentarle a este Bingo Boffin a Bilbo Bolsón, en el Salón del Fuego. Deben tener mucho en común; a pesar de mis bromas, los hobbits siguen siendo algo inusual de ver en Imladris.'
'Bilbo ha tenido la formidable idea de dibujarme un mapa para explorar mejor Rivendel y no perderme nada. ¡Es fantástico!'
'He dibujado un mapa rápido con algunas de las vistas más notables de Rivendel. ¡Encontrad cada una de estas localizaciones y habréis visto algunos de los lugares más bellos del valle!'
'Bilbo ha tenido la formidable idea de dibujarme un mapa para explorar mejor Rivendel y no perderme nada. ¡Es fantástico!'

El aire de Imdolen, en lo alto de Rivendel, es puro y fresco
Muchas mercancías de calidad se venden en el mercado de Rivendel
El lago de Hidhuinen es apacible y calmado
Esta aguja sirve como un popular lugar de reunión para la gente de Rivendel
El Refugio de Orladion es silencioso y apacible
Has encontrado a Bingo y Bilbo ya en plena conversación

Elrond está en su biblioteca en la Última Morada, en Rivendel.
Bingo ha ido a buscar algo de comida para W.B. y para él, y te ha encomendado la tarea de decirle a Elrond que otro hobbit ha llegado a Rivendel.
Bingo Boffin está en el Salón del Fuego, conversando alegremente con Bilbo Bolsón.

'Estoy emocionado por explorar el valle escondido de Rivendel, ¡pero mi estómago está rugiendo! Los Elfos deben tener un comedor o almacén para sus comidas. ¡Voy ir con W.B. en busca de algo que podamos comer!
'Deberías presentarte ante el gran Elfo y decirle que hemos venido a hacerle una breve visita. No he oído hablar sobre la hospitalidad de los Elfos, ¡pero seguro que no carecen de ella! No nos cerrará la puerta, eso seguro.'

'¿Más invitados? Esto es lo que pasa cuando permites que un hobbit se instale en tu hogar, ${PLAYER}: ¡no tardan en llegar más! No le diré a Bingo que se vaya, mientras sea un invitado educado y decente.
'Deberías presentarle a Bilbo Bolsón, en el Salón del Fuego. Deben tener mucho en común; a pesar de mis bromas, los hobbits siguen siendo algo inusual de ver en Imladris.'

'¡Mira quién es, ${PLAYER}! ¡Es Bilbo Bolsón, el famoso aventurero de Hobbiton! Le he estado poniendo al día de las noticias de la Comarca, ¡y él me ha estado hablando sobre su estancia con los Elfos de Rivendel!'
Bingo te mira con aire conspirados y murmura rápidamente: 'Me parece un tipo ordinario, ¡y para nada un loco!' antes de continuar con tono normal.
'Bilbo ha tenido la formidable idea de dibujarme un mapa para explorar mejor Rivendel y no perderme nada. ¡Es fantástico!'

Bilbo os ha proporcionado a Bingo y a ti con un mapa de localizaciones importantes de Rivendel.
Bingo y tú habéis explorado varias de las vistas más notables de Rivendel, y ahora deberíais volver al Salón del Fuego, en la Última Morada.

Bilbo está en el Salón del Fuego, en la Última Morada.
Bingo se ha percatado de que el mapa de Rivendel dibujado por Bilbo tiene cierto parecido con el mapa que encontró en la Comarca.

Bingo está en el Salón del Fuego, en la Última Morada.
Has averiguado que Bilbo Bolsón es el responsable de haber dibujado el mapa que fue dejado en el libro de recetas que provocó que Bingo comenzara su aventura.

Habla con Bilbo Bolsón en el Salón del Fuego

'No sé qué pensar. Respeto la opinión de Bilbo así que no insistiré, pero me preocupa que mi vieja no haya sido tan emocionante como para retener el interés del lector, ${PLAYER}. Intentaré idear alguna forma de emocionar a mis futuros lectores, y espero que tú también pienses en algo. He llegado a Rivendel, ¡pero mi viaje acaba de comenzar! ¿Dónde deberíamos ir a continuación?'
<rgb=#FF0000>La semana que viene: 'Una escalada nevada' (Nivel recomendado: 42)</rgb>
'¿Puedes darle a Bilbo mi manuscrito y pedirle que lo lea? Soy muy tímido para pedírselo yo mismo, ¡pero quizá si se lo pides tú esté dispuesto a emplear algo de su tiempo para leerlo!'

'He disfrutado mucho leyendo de nuevo sobre la Comarca. Confieso que echo de menos la paz y tranquilidad de mi hogar, y que la forma de escribir de Bingo me la ha recordado con gran acierto: metódica y sosegada.
'También he disfrutado leyendo sobre la gente que ha conocido por el camino: Tom Bombadil, los buscadores de tesoros de la Posada Abandonada y también sobre su amigo el lince, ¡Willem Bigotes! ¡Bingo tiene suerte de haberse enfrentado a pocas adversidades hasta este punto, y espero que su viaje siga libre de peligro según avance! Mi propia aventura estuvo llena de trolls, trasgos y dragones, ¡y también de obstinados enanos y elfos!
'Dile a Bingo que he disfrutado mucho leyendo su relato, ${PLAYER}, ¡y que espero leer el resto cuando su viaje concluya!'

'¿Y bien? ¿Qué piensa Bilbo de mi relato hasta ahora?'
Le dices a Bingo lo que Bilbo opinaba sobre su forma de escribir, pero mientras más hablas más decepcionado parece.
'¿Le gustó la paz y tranquilidad de la Comarca? ¡Estoy escribiendo un relato de aventuras, ${PLAYER}! ¿Calma y tranquilidad? ¡Es lo último que quiero que transmita mi relato! ¿Y esperaba que el resto de mi viaje estuviera 'libre de peligros'? ¡Qué desastre!

'We still have our own parts to play, and I deem it important that we play them well! I wish to sail up the river on the deck of the Corsair ships, and come by that route to the aid of Minas Tirith. It is my hope that we will arrive in time and with such surprise that we can strike a blow to the fighting will of those who threaten the city.
'We do not have much time to prepare, but there are a number of tasks I have given my friends to perform that will help us set forth as quickly as possible. Help them with these tasks, if you would, for every moment we hesitate is a moment the Enemy would relish!'

'I asked that you help prepare the ships with haste, but I did not expect such speed even from you, ${PLAYER}! I thank you for your efforts and know that we are put in the best position we could be as a result.
'I have given some thought to this next request, my friend, and I hope you agree with me on this. I do not ask you to accompany me on the ships. Instead, I ask you to travel by land through Upper Lebennin and Lossarnach. We must learn the state of the war to the east. The vale of Tumladen and the town of Imloth Melui had strong walls of old, and were used as places of safety for the people in times of war. The people there will tell you much of what has transpired elsewhere in Gondor. Angbor will go that way as well, with his men, and will be a boon companion as you go.
'I have another purpose for you, my trusted friend. I want you to find Gandalf or true-hearted Faramir in Minas Tirith and tell them about our victory here. Tell no others! In Faramir I place the trust I would not give to the father. There is too much I do not know about the situation in the White City.'

There is an angry fire in Golodir's eyes, an unfamiliar, smouldering rage.

My grief was strong and will never truly pass, but this treatment fills me with such an anger I would strike them all down: Corunir, Halbarad, even my own chief, Aragorn!'
He falls silent. When he speaks again, his voice is little more than a whisper, and there are tears in his eyes.
'I... I do not know from where this anger comes, ${PLAYER}. It feels as if I hear voices of the past, unflagging and unrelenting, calling my name, taunting me...
'I will master these voices. I have been troubled by these feelings ever since we began this journey, and I have managed to stifle them. It has become more difficult of late, perhaps because of the unnatural skies... the evil presence of the Dead Men...
'Do not worry about me, my friend. I will apologize to Corunir, and my outburst will remain between us, I hope?'

'Did you find Halbarad? Were you able to help him with whatever it was he needed?'
You ask Calenglad how he feels about the mood of the Grey Company.
'I think we are doing fine, for the most part. We have been through a great deal already, and there is more hardship ahead, but if we stay true to each other there is nothing we need fear.
'We have lost friends along the way, and brothers, but our memories of them give us the strength to go on. If I close my eyes I can still hear their voices, and they urge me to stand with Aragorn and honour my pledge. And one day, you will buy Radanir and Daervunn and me a meal, and drinks, and we will all toast the successful journey of the Grey Company.
'Oh, yes. I told Daervunn about our agreement once this is all done. I did not think you would mind.'

'With all my musings I forgot to tell you something! Halbarad wanted me to send you to him. He has returned to Pelargir already. If you leave now you should find him just inside the north-west entrance to the city.'

'The appearance of the Dead Men may weigh heavily upon some others of our company. Golodir in particular seemed distraught by the passage under the mountain. Find Corunir, somewhere to the south of here, and see if he knows where Golodir can be found. The two of them are rarely apart.'

'Golodir's ill mood has returned after a short time at low ebb, and now he shouts at his own dear friends! If you seek him out, know that I left him standing on a dock to the south, looking out at the water. I will not be held responsible if he treats you unkindly, for it seems he does not know his friends.'
Halbarad is located in the large courtyard just inside the north-west entrance to the port-city of Pelargir.
Corunir left Golodir standing on a dock somewhere to the south, in the city of Pelargir.

'I like this land, ${PLAYER}. It reminds me of the twilit wilds, far away in the North, where my heart remains. The wooded slopes encircling Lake Nenuial must be slowly shaking off the grip of winter, and in a few weeks the leaves of their trees may begin to fight through the remaining chill. No Winter lasts forever, and the coming of Spring will banish even the coldest of memories. Will this war be any different?'
Calenglad stands silently for a short while, musing on the question. Eventually he smiles, and gives you a conspiratorial wink.
'Radanir told me you agreed to treat him to a meal and drinks at a tavern of your choosing, once this is all over. If you have no objection, I would like to join the two of you there. I will look forward to that happy meeting!
'But there is still much hardship ahead of us, and with all my musings I forgot to tell you something! Halbarad wanted me to send you to him. He has returned to Pelargir already. If you leave now you should find him just inside the north-west entrance to the city.'

'I would follow Aragorn anywhere, ${PLAYER}, and standing here with the smell of smoke on the air and the memory of battle still fresh in my mind, I feel as if I have done so!
'I did not blanch when he led us through the Dimholt road, nor when we emerged from the mountain with the shades of Dead Men all around us. Still, I am glad they have departed. It is not natural for such men to linger in the world. An Elf once told me that death is a gift for all Men, but I did not understand what he meant until today. I think now he was right.
'The appearance of the Dead Men may weigh heavily upon some others of our company. Golodir in particular seemed distraught by the passage under the mountain. Find Corunir, somewhere to the south of here, and see if he knows where Golodir can be found. The two of them are rarely apart.'

'I am not in the mood to talk, ${PLAYER}. This has been a trying experience for all of us. I hope you do not mind.'
As you turn to go, Corunir holds up his hand.
'I am sorry, friend. I am fine. With what can I help you?'
You tell him that you are looking for Golodir, and thought he might know where you could find the Ranger.
'Golodir is the cause of my ill temperament and I have no desire to speak with him any further. Do you remember the fell mood that seized him in Angmar, before the Grey Company was assembled? I thought he had left it behind him. Indeed, it seemed that the journey was doing him some good, but it returned again in Tûr Morva, only to be overcome by the gentle laughter of the Dunlending girl, Wenda.
'But like the rising and falling brimstone pools of Malenhad, his ill mood has returned after a short time at low ebb, and now he shouts at his own dear friends! If you seek him out, know that I left him standing on a dock to the south, looking out at the water. I will not be held responsible if he treats you unkindly, for it seems he does not know his friends.'

'These need to go to the Corsair flagship, for that's the one that has the most room. Techeron is waiting for these supplies on the flagship moored at the large southern dock of the Market Ward. You can't miss it: it's the big one.'

'These need to go to the Corsair flagship, for that's the one that has the most room. Techeron is waiting for these supplies on the flagship moored at the large southern dock of the Market Ward. You can't miss it: it's the big one.'

'Hold a moment, ${PLAYER}. Did you know that Radanir and I had a bit of a friendly wager? It was just to amuse us during a bit of tedium, and I do not want you to take it too greatly to heart.
'You see, I wagered that Lothrandir would return to the city and finish the task of loading the ships, instead of you, but I did not mean to disparage your strength or ability! All know of your great deeds and the help you have provided to us on this journey!
'No, I based my wager on how hardy Lothrandir always appears. He chose to live in distant Forochel, after all! Such inhospitable places breed stalwart men, and Lothrandir was strong to start! He is the toughest Ranger I have ever met, and... well... perhaps that is the reason for my wager, ${PLAYER}.
'I simply could not believe that Lothrandir's strength could be taken from him, but Saruman has turned him into a shell of his former self. Such treatment in the dungeons of the Wizard would kill a lesser man, I have no doubt, but it pains me to see Lothrandir so weak, so tired. I think I wagered against you with the hope that it was not so.
'I am sorry for taking up so much of your time, my friend. I wanted you to know.'
'You should go back to Techeron and ask him about my coins. You know, just to make sure he has not forgotten about our little wager.'

'Thank you for doing my part, ${PLAYER}. Asking for help does not come naturally for me, and I beg you forgive me for it. I hope to regain my strength before long. This weakness and fatigue pains me more than any of the injuries I sustained in Saruman's care!'
'Find Radanir and help him carry my share of the supplies onto the Corsair flagship. You will find him in the West-garth, by one of the bridges that leads to the Court of the Ship-kings.'

'Very good, my friend. You have disrupted the preparations of the Haradrim, and my men will be able to cross the Erui without fear of Southron fortifications. Even a force of four thousand can suffer many losses when attacking a much smaller force, provided the smaller force has time to prepare.'
'Find the vale of Tumladen in Upper Lebennin, and see how the war has treated the rest of the kingdom. I will follow behind with four thousand swords and strong men to wield them!'

'They say I am too old to fight, even if the desire to protect my home and my family burns as brightly within my bosom as it does within those of younger men. I am not afraid to die, if that death were to be in service of Steward Denethor or his brave sons!
'Still I have been carted here to wait for the end with the children and the women. What justice is there in that? They say the son of the Steward holds Osgiliath, but how long can he hope to stand against all the armies that pour out of the East? That city has changed hands before, but it seems to this old man that the next time it falls may be the last.
'When that happens, I think they will rue sending us away. The White City will have need of folk to wield swords, no matter their ages. Mark my words, and mark them well!'

'You have done good work here. I suspected that we would find these havens full of refugees from the White City, which means that the war will soon be joined if it has not already begun.
'Four thousand swords travel slowly, but when they arrive they will make all their points, with sharp arguments! We must make sure their path is free of obstruction. There is a good place to cross the River Erui, to the south, but it is held by the Haradrim. Let us go to the Crossings and defeat these Southrons so my army can pass.
'Any Haradrim in Upper Lebennin pose a threat to the Crossings, and they must be stopped!'
'The Haradrim hold the Crossings. They must be defeated.'

'As we left Minas Tirith, I saw smoke rising from Osgiliath. I hope Faramir holds it still, but I do not know how long even he can last. He is the son of the Steward and very brave, but I have heard that the armies arrayed against us are vast and uncaring. I have heard also that Boromir left on an errand to the north, and has not yet returned. I would feel better for my sons if Boromir returned and stood on the front lines... may it be soon!
'Right now we await word that it is safe to return to the city. Tumladen has enough supplies for its garrison, now absent, so we should be able to stay as long as necessary. But I hope this is resolved quickly.'

'I heard there was a Halfling in the White City! I did not see him, but he could not have been much taller than I am, and I wager he will be allowed to fight! Why not me? I heard tell he was a friend of Mithrandir, the Grey Pilgrim. Perhaps that is the reason.
'Some folk have all the good fortune, and leave none for the rest of us! It is not fair!'

'They say the son of the Steward holds Osgiliath, but how long can he hope to stand against all the armies that pour out of the East? That city has changed hands before, but it seems to this old man that the next time it falls may be the last.

'Before he departed for Minas Tirith, Prince Imrahil charged me with the defence of the fiefs he left behind. I accepted this duty, knowing it might end in death, and left my son to protect my own lands. I engaged the Corsairs and Southrons at the city of Linhir, but we were heavily outnumbered and our defeat seemed certain.
'And then a new force joined the fray: a vast army of shadows from the forbidden paths under the mountains! They were Dead Men, and they brought death with them, silent and sure. My men cast aside their weapons and fled, but I stood my ground, and when I saw the banner of he who led them I was glad, for it was Aragorn, and he rode 'neath the standard of the King. 'Fearless' he called me, but what man can be afraid when a King has returned to a kingdom that needs him?
'I have four thousand men with me, and they will travel behind us. It will be slow going for them, so we will ride ahead and see what awaits them. Let us fight the Southrons in Upper Lebennin and clear the way for their swords! Then we will come to the vale of Tumladen and see the state of the war.'

'I have four thousand men with me, and they will travel behind us. It will be slow going for them, so we will ride ahead and see what awaits them. Let us fight the Southrons in Upper Lebennin and clear the way for their swords! Then we will come to Tumladen and see the state of the war.'
'Find the vale of Tumladen in Upper Lebennin, and see how the war has treated the rest of the kingdom. I will follow behind with four thousand swords and strong men to wield them!'

'Do you plan to travel to Minas Tirith? I would advise you to rethink your course! If the city is not already besieged, it soon will be! Much of my family has been evacuated, but my sons remained behind at the request of their commander. They will defend the city, and are glad for the chance, but I am afraid for them.
'As we left Minas Tirith, I saw smoke rising from Osgiliath. I hope Faramir holds it still, but I do not know how long even he can last. He is the son of the Steward and very brave, but I have heard that the armies arrayed against us are vast and uncaring. I have heard also that Boromir left on an errand to the north, and has not yet returned. I would feel better for my sons if Boromir returned and stood on the front lines... may it be soon!
'Right now we await word that it is safe to return to the city. Tumladen has enough supplies for its garrison, now absent, so we should be able to stay as long as necessary. But I hope this is resolved quickly.'

'Hullo there! You look like a real adventurer! Are you really a hero?'
The boy looks at you with wide eyes and an admiring expression.
'You must be journeying to Minas Tirith! They are going to need you there, I am certain of it! There is going to be a war... it may have already started! Are you going to be in the thick of the fighting? I would be, if they'd let me!
'I heard there was a Halfling in the White City! I did not see him, but he could not have been much taller than I am, and I wager he will be allowed to fight! Why not me? I heard tell he was a friend of Mithrandir, the Grey Pilgrim. Perhaps that is the reason.
'Some folk have all the good fortune, and leave none for the rest of us! It is not fair!'

'The waggon-driver's son speaks wisdom. I have heard that Imloth Melui is known for the quality of its healers, and the folk here will know the value of the goods on this waggon.'

'We must go to Minas Tirith. The fields of the Pelennor outside the White City are encircled by a great wall, the Rammas Echor, through which we must pass.
'The south-gate in the Rammas is located in the haven of the Harlond. That is where we must go. Let us go there and assess the situation.'
'I did not expect to see you again, ${PLAYER}.'

'Oh, hello there, ${PLAYER}. How have you been keeping? I have been doing well.
'My father was not pleased with me when I returned to him in Tarlang's Neck, but he is always looking for a reason to be unhappy. I told him to look on the bright side, as I do. After all, we will never want for nails! I have never known him to have enough of something before, and now he does. How many can say that? Very few folk!'

'The Harlond is overrun? If we cannot get to the south-gate in the Rammas, we will not be able to bring our wares to Minas Tirith! What is it like to have good fortune? I would truly like to know, for I have never had it!
'If there is a bright side to this news, it is that I suspected it was so. No ill news is truly surprising to me anymore, ${PLAYER}! We cannot return to Galengam without selling his goods, so I sent Nethadan to Imloth Melui to find a purchaser for our Cemenduril liquor. Go north to the town and find my son, for he has not yet returned.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! What good timing! I was just telling these ladies about some of our adventures. Do you remember when we fought off those Corsair raiders together? That was really something, was it not?'
Nethadan already looks happier than you have ever seen him, and his mood only improves when you tell him that the road through the Harlond is closed.
'How unfortunate! How ill-fated! Even so, I think this will be a fine place to stay until the road is clear. This is the perfect place to bring our waggon of valuable healing liquors. Did you know that this town has produced some of the finest healers in all the kingdom?
'Now where was I? Oh yes! I have always sought to provide for my family and my dear old dad. He will never want for nails, for example....'

'I did not know you travelled with Lord Angbor of Lamedon, ${PLAYER}! It is my honour to serve him in any way I can, and I truly hope you have no tidings of Nethadan that might embarrass me in the presence of my liege!'
Bandron is shaking with obvious terror of what you might say, and he exhales with obvious relief when you tell him that Nethadan believes Imloth Melui will be a good place to stay until the road through the Harlond is open.
'That is my responsible boy! I have often prided myself on the example he sets for others, my Lord Angbor! Why, I think he seeks to model his behaviour after your own son, Drambor. That is my Nethadan, all right!'
Privately, you think to yourself that perhaps both father and son have more in common than either would admit.

'Enemy forces must have crossed the Anduin and taken the port of the Harlond by surprise. They have had time enough to fortify the south-gate of the Rammas against us. That makes things more difficult to be sure. Only that road can support the movement of my four thousand men. We simply do not have the time or the resources to ferry that many warriors across the Anduin, and moving them through the forests of Ithilien in a wide sweep would be far too slow and take too much time. If we take such a course, the war will be ended before my men get there! No, they must retake the Harlond, and they will need me to lead them in this effort.
'You, however, have another errand. Aragorn wanted you to reach either Gandalf or Faramir? You can take a single craft across the Anduin and move more swiftly than four thousand. You must pass into Ithilien and come by that way to Osgiliath. Meanwhile, my men will assail the Harlond.
'My scouts learned that a friend to Gondor operates a secret ferry to the east, among the high reeds that border the river. Find her and see if she will bring you across the river into Ithilien, ${PLAYER}.'

'You approach from the west? I have seen precious few foe-men come from that way. Most enemies to Gondor have come from the east. Why do you seek to cross the river?'
You tell the woman that you have important tidings of the war, but have sworn to give them only to Gandalf the Wizard or to Faramir of Minas Tirith.
'I suspected as much, and will not ask for you to break your vow. I have not seen any Wizards in these parts, and the name Gandalf is unknown to me, but Faramir has spent more time of late ranging in the woods of Ithilien than he has in the White City. You are welcome to use my boat, and to have this advice: seek for Faramir and his Rangers at Bâr Húrin, to the east. I ask only this: defeat any Haradrim you encounter in Ithilien. They are a danger to my friends and my kingdom.'

'I have slain a number of Haradrim warriors on the road through this land already, but I have not seen a single Mûmak at which to let fly my arrows.
'But there is a trembling in the earth. Do you feel that? Is it possible our prey approaches?'

'My brother and I rarely hunt together, ${PLAYER}. We find that we have much more success when tracking a foe if we travel alone. That way, if one of us frightens the beast, the other may be able to take advantage of the confusion of our prey.
'My chosen weapon is this longbow, and my accuracy with it is legendary among the folk of the Blackroot Vale. If you come with me, I suggest that we travel eastward by way of the road, and the long sight-lines will give us the advantage over any raiding parties we encounter while we search for a Mûmak.'

'We should not all tramp through the wild together, ${PLAYER}. The two of us would be silent enough, I expect, but my brother makes more noise in the brush than even the largest Mûmak!
'This sword of mine has proven the better of every creature upon which I set my mark, and today will be no different. If you choose to hunt with me, we will travel up the slope to the north for a better view, the better to surprise our prey.'

'I will be pleased to have you join me, ${PLAYER}! Let us waste no more time! I want to be the first to find a Mûmak, and if we are to bring one down before my brother finds one we will need to hurry!'

'I am ready to take to the wild in search of Mûmakil! Waste no time, and we might find one of the great beasts before my brother. There will be glory enough for all, but it brings me no shame to confess I want to be the first!'

'I encountered a number of Orcs ranging through the forested hills of this land, but I caught no sign of any Mûmakil. How can such large beasts evade us?
'And yet, I feel the earth tremble. Do you feel that? Can it be?'

'The Rangers have seen these great beasts in the service of the Haradrim of the south, but so far none have felled even a single Mûmak. My brother and I will be the first to do so, and we would be honoured for you to accompany us on this hunt!'
You tell Duilin that you are looking for Faramir, and cannot delay from that errand.
'He is not here, but if you help us hunt the mighty Mûmakil, you have my word that the sons of Blackroot will help you find him! Speak to me when you are ready to depart, ${PLAYER}!'

'What a delight! Did you see the size of those Mûmakil? They were even larger than I expected, and twice as ferocious! I am still winded from their pursuit, and I could not be happier about it!'
Duilin's eyes are bright and words tumble from him in an excited torrent.
'Next time we will have one for sure! Their hides are thick, but seeing them up close has shown me where to aim: their eyes! That is the only unprotected spot... I see that now! And you too, ${PLAYER}!
'But for now we are to help you with an errand of your own, I suppose.'
'I can hardly contain my excitement! It is time to hunt the mighty Mûmakil the Haradrim have brought to Gondor!'

'You are a friend? I am Inthol, soldier of Gondor. The pain is still overwhelming, but I feel it less keenly to know there are still good folk fighting to defend the city!
'Captain Faramir is not here, friend. He went north with Gelnor, but they were pursued by a terrible apparition and I do not know what became of them. 'I would never question Faramir's courage or his resolve, but I hope for his sake, and for Gondor's, that he remained two steps ahead of this terrible commander!'

'Faramir is in charge of the defence, but we were separated during the fighting and no man has seen him. 'You there! You are a friend, I can tell from your dress and bearing. You have to help me! I was separated from Faramir and sustained this injury, and it keeps me from doing something that I must!

'What a terrible weapon, ${PLAYER}. My brother and I took solemn vows when we were children to always look upon the bright side of a situation, but I must tell you that I am finding it difficult to maintain this outlook while confronted with the terrible Grond!
'And yet, you managed to disable it, at least for a time. Even a weapon as frightful as this can be slowed! Hope springs in my breast even as I worry, and the worry passes!'

'I stand in awe of your deeds, ${PLAYER}! You have managed to inflict some damage on the great weapon of the Enemy! It seems clear that the destruction of Grond itself is beyond our means, but you have inflicted enough damage to the structure that bears it, and that may slow its progress toward the gates of Minas Tirith!
'My brother fought a number of Orcs within the city, well more than we encountered. He thinks they are preparing for a renewed assault.'

'I can tell by your face that something has you in its grip, ${PLAYER}, and it is frustrating to see you experience this devilry and be unable to help in any way! All I can say to you is to master your eyes, and distrust even convincing visions of horror, for they surely seek to lead you astray!
'Duilin and I grew up in the Blackroot Vale, and we are no strangers to feelings of dread. But why do you feel this presence so keenly and I feel nothing?
'The sooner we find Grond and destroy it, the sooner we will leave this place. If you are well enough to continue, you should search to the north and I will search to the east. Stand strong against whatever evil you find, my friend, and know that you are its better!'

As you approach the fallen Ranger, your mind rebels at the thought that Golodir might have somehow gotten ahead of you and come to Osgiliath against Aragorn's command. How could he have come more swiftly than the Corsair ships, more swiftly than your own tread?
The merest flickering doubt is enough to dispel your wondering mind, and you see now that the body lying on the cold stones of war-torn Osgiliath is not that of Golodir after all, but another soldier fallen in the defence.

'My brother is already searching for adventure throughout the city, ${PLAYER}. We will find him and seek this weapon together!'

'Our enemies have brought a great weapon to Osgiliath, a mighty ram that bears the name 'Grond.' The message you recovered is addressed from Gothmog to 'the master of the great beasts,' and it commands this master to pull the ram through the city to the West-gate. We must assume that Gothmog or his superiors plan to use Grond to smash the gates of Minas Tirith.
'We have to stop it! If this message has not been delivered by another of Gothmog's runners, we have a brief window available to us before Grond begins to move once more. This hunter from the Blackroot Vale has been itching for a chance to prove himself. Take him and find Grond before it leaves the city, and damage or destroy the ram before it reaches the Pelennor. Once it leaves Osgiliath we will not be able to halt its progress, ${PLAYER}!'

'You look as if you have seen a ghost, ${PLAYER}, and if that terrible apparition's words are to be believed, mayhap you have!
'Is it true? Was this creature spared death? How can we hope to fight against such foes, if even a true strike with a keen blade cannot cure them of this existence?'
You ask Derufin that he not tell anyone of Gothmog's words, and he nods his assent, if reluctantly.
'I suppose that is for the best, but I do not like it. If the armies we face are led by creatures that cannot die, how long must we be expected to fight? How long must we stand, ${PLAYER}? I hope you understand that I am not afraid, but my brother is not as brave as I am, and I fear that he will not be willing to go on endlessly without victory.'

'Quickly stranger, untie me so that I may live another day. Curse these damned Haradrim!'

'My thanks for helping me out back there. I was on routine patrol with a comrade when we were ambushed. One moment we were fighting back to back and the next our foes fell back - a clever ploy! - and we pursued them separately. Before I knew it, I was surrounded, alone, and taken as you found me.
'Now forgive me, but I must ask what brought you to these wooded shores?'
You explain that you are trying to reach Faramir with important information, and also that Luntil sent you to the Rangers' camp to lend what aid you could.
'I look into your eyes, ${RACE}, and see that you speak the truth. Alas, I can help you little, for I have not seen Faramir nor heard of his whereabouts for many weeks. I hope for your sake that the information is important enough to traverse these lands. Southern Ithilien is crawling with the Morgul-host.
'Now, let us speak of the debt you owe to Luntil. She is wise in many ways, and I will confess your help is sorely needed, so I deem that I should not release you from your word.'

'Now that we stand at the base of the Emyn Arnen, do you see the beauty of these lands? This rugged beauty is my home. My parents lived here for as long as they could but the threat in the east grew too great and we fled to Lossarnach when I was young. I vowed to do everything I could to save Ithilien so that one day my children may live here in peace. Now I ask of you: protect these lands.
'The Rangers have a camp-site - the Western Post - just north of here. Tell them I sent you to aid them. Some of the Rangers can be stubborn, at times, but I know they are in need of someone like yourself.'

'Greetings, adventurer. Have you come to hunt wild game in Emyn Arnen?'
You ask Duilin about Anborn.
'If you're looking for Anborn, he's at the keep. He seems awfully busy though. He doesn't even have the time to hunt with us! Isn't that right, Derufin?'

'Stranger, you are bold to come and ask me where my leader is. You should not even be in these lands. But you speak Gladhir's name, so I will allow you here for now. It will take more than that to earn my trust, however.'

'Duilin and Derufin? Anborn allows those two to stay, I think, because they amuse our fellow Rangers with their cheerful antics. There is little to lighten our hearts in these days. They cheer us, but they are of little use. I hope that you may prove otherwise, for we are in need of some extra hands in Bâr Húrin, presently.'

Gladhir can be found on the bridge to Bâr Húrin in Southern Ithilien.

Speak with Gladhir
'Return to Gladhir and tell him of the Haradrim scaling the cliffs. I shall continue to monitor the situation and thwart their efforts until others arrive. Take care.'

'This is indeed dire. I do not wish to make you tarry longer than need requires if you do indeed have important news for Lord Faramir. I will muster nearby Rangers to put an end to the Haradrim plans to scale the cliffs. Pressing further into South Ithilien will be difficult. You should make your way to Bâr Húrin, the main stronghold of the Rangers south of Osgiliath.
'You will not be welcomed there as warmly as you might wish or deserve, I am afraid. Anborn, leader of Bâr Húrin, is distrustful of outsiders, perhaps to a fault. I do not think he will turn you away, however. He did not turn away two others, like you, who came recently to Ithilien. If you take a little time to earn his trust, I feel sure he will assist you.
Have hope, for I know you will find Faramir. May our paths cross again, ${PLAYER}.'

'My brother and I come from across the river. We're preparing to hunt a simply grand beast. Have you heard of the Mûmakil? They are giant, tusked creatures from lands south of here.'
You ask Derufin about Anborn.
'You can try talking to Anborn but I don't know how far you'll get. He admires our skill with the bow, but it ends there. You may have better luck with Thurindol. That Thurindol is a pleasant fellow, wouldn't you agree, Duilin?'

'Whilst Dagor dreams of playing at war, he ignores the plain facts before him. Though we are many, we are ill-trained and poorly organized. If the Haradrim who have crept into Lossarnach were to attack now, we would be done for!

Much of Lossarnach's farmland is burned and the first planting has been missed. Indir fears that if the Haradrim discover Arnach's grain supplies, no victory will forestall thin crops and starvation in seasons to come.

'The truth is, Lord Forlong left me with too many men. We sent as many as we could up to Imloth Melui, but the lads with war in their eyes couldn't bear to be cooped up behind those walls. I couldn't handle them all myself, so I made Dagor and Indir my captains.
'Like the sun and moon, those two are! Dagor's the more soldierly and fit for the role. Whereas Indir is clever and steady enough, but he worries and broods. We have enough darkness from the skies above! A captain should keep his head high.'

'Do not let my furrowed brows weigh on your heart, ${CLASS}.
'Dagor plays at war and good-hearted Baranor keeps watch over the township as if these were times of peace. While I would curb the one and rouse the other, to do so would be out of my place. So I, who harbour no dreams of war and glory, take the burden willingly. I will plan and brood so that their dreams are not darkened... and so Arnach remains safe.'

'Ah, would that I were off, marching with Forlong to war! Still, I will not let ill chance rob me of any glory. There are enemies in Lossarnach, now, and I may prove my mettle as a captain and warrior here, as well.
'Baranor sees. He smiles on me, and when Forlong returns victorious, Baranor will tell him of my deeds.'

Baranor, Captain of the Guard, is who I am, and I must do my best to fill his shoes. Only he left me with such a great lot of green lads, all restless and rousting about. It's like herding mice!
'So I've made captains of Dagor and Indir. There's Dagor over there. Destined for greatness, if you ask me. At any rate, between guarding Arnach and keeping watch on these damned Haradrim, we three have had our hands full, and then some!

'Ah, you have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. I see a few of my men have returned already, and I am certain the rest shall soon follow.
'Yet, I know little of the fate of my captain, Faramir, and I shall not count him among the dead while he remains lost. I have a mind to search for him within Osgiliath, for none that survived our flight into the tunnels saw him escape.
'If you will join me and my men in our search for Faramir, you are welcome among us for as long as your journey allows it.'

Mablung's Rangers can be found throughout Osgiliath.
Mablung has asked you to seek the Rangers he sent to scout the surface of Osgiliath and order them to return to his post.
Search for Mablung's Rangers in Osgiliath (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

'It will be some time before I can return you to Arodor, stranger. Faramir is lost, as is Osgiliath, save for the secret ways beneath the city. You are fortunate, indeed, to have made it down here alive... for many of our company were not so swift.
'Our number is few, but several of my men scout even now from hidden ways within the city's walls. However, we cannot remain scattered any longer if we are to hold against the Enemy, so I would ask that you seek my men among the Enemy's forces in the city and order their return.
'If I know my men, they shall be well-hidden!'

The Ranger noticeably flinches and readies his weapon as you approach.
'I feared my position was discovered... I am sorry, stranger. Mablung has sent you?
'I shall return to the tunnels with haste, but I cannot abandon my post until my friend returns and we have saved more of our old records.'

'So, Mablung sends me to the surface to search for arms and now he wishes for me to return just as soon as I find a secure position? Faramir would not have us hide in the culverts and cower while our people die!
'I will return when I finish my task, and not a moment sooner. If I should die, it will be in the aid of my brothers, not backed into a corner like a hunted beast.
'The host of Minas Morgul has no shortage of workers and warriors, and I would deprive them of any advantage that may be left behind. Aid me, and I shall return!'

'You are fortunate that you did not bear the markings of the Morgul-host, stranger, else I would have struck you down before you dared step so close.
'I shall heed Mablung's order in time, but if you wish to count yourself among us, you shall aid me first - for there are far more pressing matters at hand.
'What shall it be, ${CLASS}?'

'You startled me, stranger! I have almost finished my patrol, but I could use your aid if I am to quicken my pace and return to the culverts.
'I promise you, I shall be a more gracious companion than any others you might find roaming the City of Stars.'
Lost, But Not Forgotten

'Have you passed through the square, stranger? I doubt you have... for your head still sits upon your neck.
'They gather the imprisoned in the theatre to the south, and then they drag them out into the square to be tortured... and beheaded. They play with the bodies, and they toss around the heads laughing with those horrible Orkish tongues. After a time they burn the corpses, but the heads they keep, and I do not know to what vile end - nor do I wish to.
'This is war, ${PLAYER}... make no mistake of that. If you are to be one of us, you must know the horrors we have endured. Make for the square and free any of our men that yet live, and slay any of those Troll-men that stand in your way!'

'Those fell-beasts and their dark riders seem to delight in dropping the wounded from above - Man and Orc alike. Let us hope that no others must suffer this sorry fate.'

'When last I saw him, he made for the eastern bridge into the old Dome of Stars, but I hope his pursuers did not drive him there... for all manner of evil things have taken hold of it.
'You are a hardy ${CLASS} and might be able to bear the dread that surrounds the Dome. Will you search for him there? I will not abandon him until I am assured of his fate, but death has not been a stranger to our men in these dark days.'

'I saw him scout near the old Palace of King Eldacar, but then he was lost from sight and I had to fall back. The Palace is a grim place, and I believe the Enemy seeks to use it as a stronghold for his servants - the Nazgûl. They spend much of their time up above on those vile beasts, but I have seen them pass among the forces here in Osgiliath and even the Orcs recoil at their approach.
'If he has gone into the palace, he is likely dead, but I wish to know for certain. Search the palace, and return to me here when you have finished. Only then shall we speak of returning to the tunnels.'

'My ally, Echil, has delayed in his return, and I fear that the Easterlings or the flames within have overwhelmed him.
'I must keep guard here, but if you could seek him out, I would be most grateful. He was to collect some of our writings as well as a few of the crumbling works that were never moved from the city long ago for fear that they might turn to dust at a touch.
'Aid him, and then return to me for then I shall heed Mablung's call and sneak back to the culverts.'

'Ah, a friendly face, I hope? I am fine but for a wounded leg... alas, these Easterlings gave me some trouble. Unfortunately for them, I gave them more. They spoke of some \qLord of Pinions\q, but I know none who bear such a title.
'I can return to Candúr, but I have not finished collecting our writings. We keep many of our writings as well as those we have taken from the Enemy's forces within the old archives, but the Easterlings have set flame to it all.

'This does not bode well for us or the White City, ${PLAYER}.
'Faramir and Boromir threw down the Great Bridge when last the Enemy tried to sack Osgiliath, but it appears that the Orcs have found a way to rebuild it... and allow it to bear the weight of enormous siege weapons.

'The host of Minas Morgul intends to siege the White City, but we do not yet know when the attack shall begin.
'We observed the Orcs hauling supplies to the Great Bridge, and have heard a thundering from above in the tunnels, but we do not know their vile designs. They have built several siege weapons on the western bank, but the bridge is broken and cannot bear the weight of the Mûmakil or their siege weapons on the eastern bank. I do not believe they will strike until their weapons can cross the river unhindered!
'If they have found a way to traverse the broken span, it could spell doom for Minas Tirith. Search the Great Bridge, and tell me of any Orkish craftwork you discover!'

When we still held the western shore, we stored a great deal of weapons within the armoury. Yet now, the Orcs and trolls roam its ruins and our weapon-stores are exposed.
'I have not been able to get close enough to gather many, but perhaps you can. If you return these weapons to me, I shall be able to hasten my return to the tunnels.'

Over in the western streets, by Meneldil's Square, the half-trolls sharpen their axes and await more men to bring them down upon. My brothers must be avenged, and I would have the honour be yours.

'I hope they suffered as much as my brothers did, ${PLAYER}.

'Orcs, Trolls, Uruk-hai, Haradrim, Half-trolls, and now Easterlings... it has not done much for the spirits of my men, as you might suppose. It is a truly daunting force, but we cannot lose hope... not yet.

Travel to the eastern streets and slay many of their numbers. If their morale might yet be broken, I can think of none other than Faramir or such a fine ${CLASS} who might drive them from our lands.

'I do not wish their blades or armour to fall into the hands of the Enemy, for they would better serve us, even in the absence of the dead. Search the western streets and ways through the city, and return what you find to us here in the tunnels. Go with haste!'

Brunil scowls at you.
'The sick are sick and the well are weary. I would not expect the Lady to come to these halls, but I suppose sending you shows that at least she thinks of us on occasion, toiling away for the health of her people. Tell her that we do what we can with less than we need, and if we complain we do it only as a result of much hardship.'

'Lady Vanyalos wishes to know the mood of the people? That is why Imloth Melui will thrive even in the absence of Lord Forlong, ${PLAYER}. What ruler cares as much about her people as Lady Vanyalos? Very few, I wager!
'When you return to her hall, please bring my assurances that we keep good watch on all who approach the vale. Nothing will threaten Imloth Melui without me hearing of it first!'

'How am I feeling? I have seen better days and better nights, ${CLASS}! Most of the warriors have already left this city, and now I am forced to remain behind and train youths and old men!
'This is a city of healers and potion-makers, not fighters. Even with the finest training I can give to them, this vale is nearly undefended! Tell Lady Vanyalos we must hope the enemy does not come to Imloth Melui, for that is the only way we might survive!'

'I thank you for judging the mood of my people, ${PLAYER}. If I were a potion-maker, I would think two parts despair and one part hopefulness a poor mixture indeed, but perhaps I should be grateful it is no worse.'

'I ask you to speak with the few trusted folk who remain, and learn if they have given up hope of victory and peace in Imloth Melui.
'Hathalon is my Master-at-arms, and he is responsible for training the few warriors who remain. If he has given in to despair, I fear the sickness will spread to his recruits. Merenir, my Captain of the Guard, oversees the flow of refugees by the fountain in the middle of town. And Master Healer Brunil treats the injured within the Hall of the Gentle Hand, on the western side of town. I rely on all three of these good people, and I need to know they are still able to carry out their duties.'

Lady Vanyalos listens intently as you describe your exploration of her city. When you are finished, she sighs happily.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I think I will sleep now, and perhaps I shall dream of the places you have described to me. I am quite transported, in time if not in place, to the years of my youth, when I saw those sights beneath sun-filled skies, with a sun-lit heart.'

'I ask you to take note of the loveliest sights you see here. When you return to me, you may recount them and so I will relive the pleasures I knew, through your fresh eyes.'

'¡Qué emocionante, ${PLAYER}! Este valle es tán recóndito... ¿cuántos hobbits crees que habrán visto alguna vez esta inmensidad nevada? ¡No muchos, diría yo!
'Tenemos que encontrar a estos nómadas Corcur y hacer que devuelvan a Spalvi su tesoro. ¡Es una injusticia!'
'Ya basta de hablar. ¡Oigo a los Corcur aproximándose! ¡Sorprendámosles antes de que nos vean!'

'Cubriremos más terreno si nos separamos,${PLAYER}. Yo daré un rodeo y veré si puedo encontrar a los nómadas Corcur que me atacaron. Tú deberías continuar junto con nuestro amigo Bingo a la escalera de la entrada. Yo me reuniré con vosotros en ese punto, y si ninguno de nosotros ha recuperado mi tesoro consideraremos subir a la puerta principal.
'¡Que la suerte nos acompañe, ${CLASS}!'

'¿Así que el plan es reunirse con Spalvi en la escalera principal? Creo que será mejor que vayas primero, ${PLAYER}. Estaré justo detrás de ti. Bueno... quizá no justo detrás de ti, pero a una distancia prudencial. Pero detrás de ti, ¡cuenta con ello! ¡Espero que tengamos buena suerte!'

'Si pudieras... darme un momento... para recuperar el aliento...'
Bingo respira profundamente y se frota sus piernas doloridas.
'¡Nunca había subido tantos escalones en mi vida, ${PLAYER}! Espero que Spalvi sepa cómo abrir la puerta, o tendremos que darnos la vuelta y volver, y estoy menos preparado para BAJAR estos escalones de lo que estaba para SUBIRLOS hace un rato!'
'No encontré a los Corcur que me atacaron. Deben estar tras esta puerta, y cuando la crucemos les haré pagar por sus crímenes contra mí y mis hermanos, ¡y recuperaré el tesoro que robaron!'

'Tienes toda la pinta de que te gusta la aventura. ¿Tenías algo que ver con esta escoria Corcur? Ya hemos pueesto fin a sus fechorías. La Piedra de Roth, la Estrella de Skorgrím, es nuestra de nuevo.'
El Duramano mira más allá de ti, y su cara se ilumina al reconocerte.

'La cosa se ha complicado, ¿no? Bueno, estoy seguro de que es un simple malentendido y lo arreglaré todo con estos Duramano.
'Deberías decir lo que dicen, ${PLAYER}. No quiero que te hagan daño por mi culpa. Arreglaré todo esto y me reuniré contigo en el campamento de Glóin.
'¡Qué aventura! ¡Este va a ser un capítulo muy emocionante!'
'Esto no me gusta, ${PLAYER}, pero la situación es delicada y esta es la única manera de que todo el mundo esté a salvo. Te llevaré a la salida, y te imploro que no intentes nada.'

Glóin escucha tu relato, y cuando le hablas sobre la traición de Spalvi y la llegada de los Duramano, su cara se ensombrece y aprieta los puños.
'¡Qué deslealtad! Los Duramano han sido una espina que tengo clavada desde hace muchos años, ¡pero últimamente se han vuelto más descarados! ¡Rescataremos a ese hobbit, y pagarán por lo que han hecho! Pero no debemos apresurarnos a actual o pondremos en riesgo nuestras posibilidades de éxito. Necesitamos un plan: un plan audaz.'
<rgb=#FF0000>La semana que viene: 'Un plan audaz' (Nivel recomendado: 45)</rgb>

'Nuestro enano prácticamente está recuperado, y ha estado contándome qué le pasó. Es un aventurero, ¡como sospechábamos! Se llama Spalvi, ¡y ha sido víctima de una injusticia! Él y sus hermanos estaban llevando un valioso artefacto a través de las montañas cuando fueron atacados por un grupo de nómadas Corcur, ¡y el artefacto fue robado!
'Debemos hacer lo que podamos para ayudarle a recuperarlo, ${PLAYER}. Cree que los Corcur se llevaron el artefacto a una vieja fortaleza, un lugar llamado Helegrod. ¡Debemos ir allí y entregar a esos individuos a la justicia! Esa será una historia emocionante, ¿no crees? Pero primero, deberías presentarte a Spalvi para que te cuente a qué nos enfrentamos.'
Spalvi, el nuevo amigo de Bingo, está en el paso estrecho en las Montañas Nubladas, al norte del campamento de Glóin, en el camino hacia la Fuente norte del Bruinen.

'Nuestro enano prácticamente está recuperado, y ha estado contándome qué le pasó. Es un aventurero, ¡como sospechábamos! Se llama Spalvi, ¡y ha sido víctima de una injusticia! Esa será una historia emocionante, ¿no crees? Pero primero, deberías presentarte a Spalvi para que te cuente a qué nos enfrentamos.'

'¡Es un placer tener el gusto de conocerte, ${PLAYER}. Ya he dado las gracias a tu entusiasmado amigo, pero desearía extender mi gratitud a ti también. Sin tu ayuda, seguramente habría perecido.
'Mis hermanos y yo estábamos transportando un objeto muy valioso a través de las montañas, un collar de oro adornado con un bello rubí: la Piedra de Roth. Es una reliquia familiar de los enanos y tiene gran valor para mi gente, pero fuimos emboscados por la tribu de los Corcur que acechan en las laderas nevadas. Mataron a varios de los míos; si yo vivo es solo porque creyeron que estaba muerto. Robaron la Piedra de Roth y algunos otros objetos de valor, y luego huyeron al norte. Creo que fueron hacia la fortaleza de Helegrod, que una vez estuvo abandonada.
'Te pido que me ayudes a seguir a estos villanos Corcur para recuperar el tesoro robado. Habla conmigo si aceptas acompañarme. Parece que tu amigo Bingo es un valiente aventurero, y ya ha aceptado venir conmigo pero valoraría también contar con tu ayuda.'
'No sé mucho sobre este lugar llamado Helegrod, ¡pero suena muy emocionante!'
'Estoy listo para vengar a los míos y recuperar nuestro tesoro. ¡Muerte a los Corcur! ¡Marchemos hacia la fortaleza de Helegrod!'

'I do not question the efficacy of your search, ${PLAYER}! I think the true problem here is that our sneak must be even more stealthy than I supposed!
'I think perhaps I have gotten ahead of myself. We need to ask the right questions, and I think we should start with the most basic one of all. If I wanted to poison that healing draught, how would I go about doing it? Why, I would taint one of the components that goes into it!
'I have collected the ingredients that go into the mixture, and I give them to you. Will you take them to the field beneath the long stairs, in the northern area of town, and feed them to the goats there, one by one? I think the goats will tell us if one of these ingredients is tainted.'

'The Maresfoot that goes into the healing draughts is gathered by a man named Egind, and delivered to me daily. I have never had any problems with him before now, but it seems he has shown his true colours at last, the treacherous knave!
'Egind will likely be somewhere near the front gate of the city, hoping to hand us another bushel of poisoned greens! Confront him with our discovery and see what he has to say for himself!'

'Please don't hurt me! I'm sorry, so sorry! I beg of you, mercy!
'I could not get the proper Maresfoot by the banks of the river, on account of all those Orcs haunting the place. So I picked some ones that looked just like 'em, up in the hillside scrub. I didn't mean for any harm to come of it!
'Please tell Brunil to spare my hide, ${PLAYER}! I feel terrible about this, but we cannot all be warriors! I am an old man, and my fingers are for picking herbs and flowers, not for swinging swords in anger!'

'Well, ${PLAYER}? What did Egind have to say for himself?'
You explain what the old man said about his ill-advised substitution of another herb for the Maresfoot, and Brunil scowls.
'I should have known! He must have given me Beruthiel's Rue instead of Maresfoot! They bear similar appearances, it is true, but they could not be more different in effect! It seems there was never a rat in Imloth Melui after all... merely a frightened old man making things worse instead of better! I cannot blame him for his fear, ${PLAYER}. I am not a warrior either, and these Southrons are fearsome indeed. What did you say? Orcs? No, I am certain Egind was frightened of the Southron warriors I have heard rumour of in these lands. There are no Orcs in Lossarnach.'

'Lady Vanyalos has always spoken of her visions as if she could see things hidden to others, and I had become numb to it after so long. But now she has left her chambers... indeed, she has left Imloth Melui altogether, and she called out to folk unseen as she went!
'What has come over her? Why did no one hinder her flight? There are Southrons out there, and Orcs, and who knows what other dangers await in the brush?
'${PLAYER}, I beg you: go after Lady Vanyalos at once, and bring her back to safety! Speak to me and we will choose separate paths to take, the better to find my lady!'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, though they are not equal to the good you have performed for me and my house. If only I could tell you it will matter in the days ahead, but I cannot!
'I dreamed I saw my husband Forlong, his hands covered in blood. I saw too my brother Denethor. He wore a fiery crown, and his expression was one of madness! This must mean that my husband is doomed to die, and my brother... I know not, but surely it is an ill omen.
'I was taken by despair, ${PLAYER}, and would have died to the river or to the Orcs if you had not found me. Would that you could save my family from the visions I foresaw!'
'I will search the high-lands, if you will search the banks of the river. Go swiftly, and may one of us find Lady Vanyalos before she walks heedlessly into harm!'

'As my men and I journeyed to Pelargir from Linhir, we felt a great weight upon us.
'Days without rest and the fatigue of battle had worn on us all, but this filled me with dread in a way that I had never known. And just as it took hold, it faded away, and those of my men that had cowered found their way to their feet once more.
'I have heard many rumours of what happened that day, but I do not know if there is any truth in them. I have not had much time to think on this matter until now, yet it still troubles me.
'Speak to my men of this, and see if there is any truth to these tales.'

'Since the sun was blotted out days ago, we have seen little without the use of torches, but what I saw I shall never forget.
'A flying beast bore a rider in darkened robes and the blade he held reflected what little light passed through the murky sky. As I looked upon him, a great pain overtook me and I turned away.
'When I turned to look again to the sky, he had gone.'

'Why do you ask me to recall such things?
'Before terror pulled me to the ground, I saw the form of a great beast above the ashen clouds. It let out a shrill cry as it flew overhead and then it was gone. I swear to you, I speak true!'

'As with Lord Angbor, I wish I knew what happened in that moment.
'My armour grew heavy and I fell to the ground before I could realize what happened. I regret that I cannot be of more help to you, ${CLASS}.'

'I do not doubt their words, my friend. Could this be one of the nine wraiths of which Aragorn spoke?
'Let us hope it has flown back to its master and shall not harry our journey to Minas Tirith. I will not allow its dread to burden my mind any longer.
'My men and I must press on into Upper Lebennin!'
Above the Ashes
Lord Angbor has heard tales of a great beast flying in the darkened sky above Gondor and seeks to learn more of what his men have seen.

'Will you aid me in this, ${PLAYER}?

'I know you have come to dissuade me, friend, but I cannot be turned from my task.
'So much has happened in so swift a time... it has been but a few days since Pelargir was reclaimed, but still many more troubles weigh on me...'

'Los Duramano han lanzado ataques contra mi gente desde una fortaleza en el Risco Alto. Ese lugar se llama Gabilazan, y parece ser su base de operaciones en esta parte de las Montañas Nubladas.
'¡Ve a Gabilazan y derrota a los Duramano que encuentres allí para averiguar dónde están reteniendo a Bingo Boffin!'

'Los Duramano han lanzado ataques contra mi gente desde una fortaleza en el Risco Alto. Ese lugar se llama Gabilazan, y parece ser su base de operaciones en esta parte de las Montañas Nubladas.
'¿Has derrotado a muchos Duramano pero no has encontrado a Bingo? ¡Deberías volver a Gabilazan y llevar a cabo una búsqueda más exhaustiva!'

'¡Espera! ¡Escúchame, ${PLAYER}! ¡No soy tu enemigo!
'Es cierto que os engañé a tu amigo hobbit y a ti, pero no deseaba que ninguno de vosotros sufriera daño alguno. Mientras más pensaba en ello, más me daba cuenta que no podía estar de parte de mis hermanos en esto. Cuando su guardia se relajó, liberé a Bingo de su jaula y huimos de Gabilazan. Pero en lo apresurado de nuestra huida, el pobre hobbit no prestó atención a donde pisaba, ¡y el suelo cedió!
'Bingo cayó por este agujero, y me temo que cayó más allá del alcance de mi voz, ya que no respondía cuando lo llamaba. Creo que escuché un chapoteo desde muy abajo, pero no podría asegurarlo. Si sobrevivió, necesitará provisiones. ¡Si vuelves a Gabilazan y recoges fardos de comida y botellas de agua que llevan los enanos, podemos dejarlos caer por el agujero tras de Bingo! Si sobrevivió, necesitará toda el agua y comida de la que podamos proveerle.
'¡Por favor, confía en mí, ${PLAYER}! ¡Haré todo lo que pueda para hacer lo correcto!'
'¿Y bien? ¿Dónde está Bingo?'
'¡Deja caer estas provisiones por el agujero, ${PLAYER}! ¡Si Bingo sobrevivió a la caída, se alegrará de tenerlos!'

'Me siento realmente mal por lo que he hecho, ${PLAYER}. Te juro que te ayudaré a encontrar a tu amigo, donde quiera que haya terminado es por mi culpa. Estoy seguro de que estará bien, y que todos nos reiremos recordando esto cuando termine. Pensaré un poco sobre qué hacer a continuación, pero ten seguro que no abandonaré la búsqueda hasta que le encontremos sano y salvo. ¡Enmendaré mi error!'

'I have been trying for days now to convince the people to leave... to seek shelter in Tumladen.
'It is a great and fortified shelter for our people, one of a few in Gondor, and the brother to one that lies within the lands of Rohan. It is more than able to house all of the people of Lebennin and beyond, and its walls would keep us from the growing war in Gondor.
'My folk are headstrong, traveller. They think that since Pelargir has been reclaimed and no foes have come to our doors that we are safe. I do not think it so!
'Would you speak to them for me? Urge them to reconsider before it is too late!'

'I cannot say I'm surprised that many of them ignored your advice to seek shelter... they have paid me no mind either since the skies went dark.
'Still... I thank you for trying on my behalf. I only wish to see my people safely through this war, but it remains their choice to make.'
An Uneasy Peace

'Skorgrím Duramano encargó a algunos enanos trazar mapas de las cavernas de las Montañas Nubladas. Nunca volvieron de la Ciudad de los Trasgos hasta donde yo sé, pero los encontráramos sus mapas podrían decirnos si hay túeneles que pudieran llevarnos hasta el lugar donde se encuentra Bingo.
'Me reuniré contigo en el Paso Alto del Sur, lejos hacia el este, después de que hayas encontrado algunos mapas útiles del sistema de cuevas subterráneo.'

Willem Bigotes lloriquea lastimeramente, y puedes ver claramente su frustración por la ausencia de Bingo, y que su búsqueda en la Fisura de Erforgh no ha sido fructífera. Le aseguras que no abandonarás al hobbit. Él olfatea ruidosamente, poco convencido.
Le hablas sosegadamente al lince, diciéndole que con tus esfuerzos, los de Spalvi y los suyos, encontraréis la caverna en la que ha caído Bingo y lo traeréis de vuelta.
El lince bufa, pero a regañadientes agita sus orejas en señal de asentimiento. Ahora deberías volver con Spalvi y ver si ha averiguado algo útil del mapa que recuperaste.

'Has encontrado al lince de Bingo, y ha regresado en son de paz. ¿Pero por qué me enseña los dientes?' pregunta Spalvi, repentinamente asustado.
Le dices que Willem Bigotes no es la mascota de Bingo, sino más bien su amigo, libre de irse cuando quiera.
'Supongo que debe ser eso, ${PLAYER}, porque de otro modo ya se habría ido hace mucho. ¡Mira este mapa que me has traído! Me temo que tengo noticias tanto malas como buenas.
'Las buenas noticias es que según este mapa, hay un río subterráneo que fluye bajo las montañas y parece viajar una gran distancia hacia el sur. Podría ser que Bingo fuera arrastrado por la corriente a salvo. Las malas noticias, bueno...
'Creo que deberíamos viajar hacia el campamento Barbiluengo en la zona de la Fuente occidental del Bruinen de las Montañas Nubladas para las malas noticias. Yo me quedaré fuera del campamento... no les digas que soy un Duramano, ya que temo que mi recepción no sea la mejor.'

'Debes estarte preguntando por qué quise venir al campamento Barbiluengo, ${PLAYER}. Bueno, ya te conté las buenas noticias: que Bingo podría haber sobrevivido a la caída y haber sido arrastrado por la corriente de un río subterráneo. 'Skorgrím Duramano envió a un grupo de enanos para cartografiar las cavernas de las Montañas Nubladas. Nunca volvieron de la Ciudad de los Trasgos hasta donde yo sé, pero si encontraras sus mapas podrían decirnos si hay túneles que pudieran llevarnos a donde se encuentra Bingo.

'Bueno, me siguió durante un rato y luego se alejó corriendo hacia el surete. ¿Crees que ha podido captar el rastro de Bingo? En cualquier caso, los Gauredain viven en la Fisura de Erforgh que se encuentra hacia allí, y no querría que le pasara nada malo.'

'Creo que deberíamos viajar hacia el campamento Barbiluengo en la zona de la Fuente occidental del Bruinen de las Montañas Nubladas para las malas noticias. Yo me quedaré fuera del campamento... no les digas que soy un Duramano, ya que temo que mi recepción no sea la mejor.'

'Los dos hemos viajado hasta Eregion porque pensé que las ruinas élficas podrían albergar algunos tesoros perdidos y podría usarlas como una buena práctica, ¡pero Teodoro parece incapaz de encontrar o aprender nada útil!
