'Can I trust you to deliver that report to Thalhír, the Warden of Laws? Many of the farms there have been evacuated, and this report may help their owners receive recompense if their homes are destroyed by the Orcs. Thalhír can be found in the Second Circle of the city.'
'Bring that report back to Arodor for filing. If we do survive the siege that must be coming, we may need paper to burn, and Parthadan's report may be good for that, at least.'

'Echadon sent you? I have nothing to say to him. As the Warden of the Green, it is my duty to preserve the townlands and its people. I refuse now as I refused then to call back the few scouts and guards that now defend them! They are the folk who will first face the swords and axes of the Orcs!
'Ah, I have recovered my temper. The Council dismissed his suggestion. That made me feel rather better.
'I have compiled a report of the situation on the Pelennor Fields. Can I trust you to deliver it to Thalhír, the Warden of Laws? Many of the farms there have been evacuated, and this report may help their owners receive recompense if their homes are destroyed by the Orcs. Thalhír can be found in the Second Circle of the city.'

'Echadon wanted you to speak with Parthadan? That is a good idea, ${PLAYER}. The two of them became quite heated during the last Council meeting, and those bridges ought to be repaired before the next.'

'What is this? It is a report concerning the land holdings of folk who had to abandon their homes on the Pelennor? I see. I suppose Parthadan is doing his duty to take care of the townlands by preparing this report, but I think he is dreaming if he thinks the city will repay the owners of these farms for any damage the Orcs inflict upon them.'
Thalhír snorts mirthlessly.
'He may be dreaming if he thinks there will be anyone left to repay them, ${PLAYER}. The word out of Osgiliath is not good, and the army arrayed against us sounds vast.
'Well, I promise nothing, but bring this report back to Arodor for filing. If we do survive the siege that must be coming, we may need paper to burn, and Parthadan's report may be good for that, at least.'

'Thank you very much, ${PLAYER}. Those Council resolutions will help the defenders of Minas Tirith work to safe-guard the city!
'I will take this report from you and make sure it is put in the proper place, but I share Thalhír's belief that we should first survive the battle before thinking about the aftermath!
'I am sure I will see you again, friend. Take care of yourself until then.'
'Ah, thank you very much. Let me copy down any of the important matters from these papers, and then I will have another request for you. It will not be long.'

'There we go! I have finished writing out the Council of Gondor's most recent resolutions. Now I need someone to bring these throughout the city so the city leaders can take the appropriate action. Normally I would send an errand-rider, but if you'd like to meet some members of the Council perhaps you would like to perform this duty?
'Very good! Here is the stack of resolutions that will require immediate action. They are labeled with the correct recipient, do you see? Here is the list:
Torchún, the Warden of the Houses of Healing. Echadon, the Captain of the Garrison. Celephir, the Warden of the Coffers. Mirudil, the Warden of the Stores.
'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}. You will be doing the city a great service!'

'That was very fast, ${PLAYER}! Perhaps you should become an errand-rider for the city! I suppose it would be difficult for you to leave the adventuring life behind, but prompt delivery of messages is something to be prized, and you seem quite skilled at it.
'As you know, I am the Warden of the Houses of Healing. At the Council-meeting that just concluded, I requested an increase in supplies and goods for the use of my healers: spare cloths, water for boiling, warm blankets. The Council agreed with the principle of my request, but not to its whole extent. I have been granted an increase, but a small one.
'It is better than no increase at all, I suppose. We will take blankets and cloths from evacuated houses, for their owners have no current need of them, and I will arrange with the Warden of the Wells to provide me with spare buckets.'

'Thank you for bringing this to me so quickly, ${PLAYER}. I am the Captain of the Garrison, which means the training and command of warriors in the city falls to me. I take this duty very seriously.
'At the latest Council meeting, I spoke on behalf of my men. The garrison lacks the weapons and armour needed to mount a true defence of the city, should our enemies breach the gate. Furthermore, we simply do not have enough men! To that end, I argued that the scouts should be recalled from the Pelennor and Talath Anor and put to work as part of the garrison. Parthadan did not like this suggestion. When you have finished with this duty, perhaps you can see if his temper has cooled?
'The Council did not agree with me, and there was much sympathy for the ideas of Parthadan. Still, the Guild of Smiths has been commanded to double its production of weapons and shields, so the men I do have can hope to be better equipped for the battle ahead. It is not everything for which I hoped, but it is something, at least.'

'I am grateful that you have brought the Council's resolution to me with such haste, ${PLAYER}. As the Warden of the Coffers, it is my duty to maintain the guard upon the treasury.
'To my relief, the Council agreed with my proposal that the guard upon the treasury doors be increased. If the city is soon besieged, as seems certain, the gravest threat to the coin of the city might not be the enemies outside the walls but the folk within them. Indeed, an unsavoury group has already begun speaking out against the Council and the Steward, and I am sure they would try and pilfer the treasury if given the opportunity.
'I thank you once more for bringing this resolution to me.'

'Ah, the Council resolutions are already written? That was very fast. It is good to see such haste, for it usually takes much longer for the orders of the Council to be put into action. Everyone is worried about what lies ahead, and it spurs them to move with haste.
'I am the Warden of the Stores, which means that all the food and goods brought into the city fall within the scope of my duty. I find where they can be stored safely and free from theft or spoilage, and ensure that the folk who need access to them have it.
'I must confess some trepidation to you, ${PLAYER}. If the city is besieged, I will surely become the most hated man in Minas Tirith. The man who rations the food is never loved by the hungry.
'This resolution will allow me to conduct a full inventory of the stores, so I will know how much food and other supplies we will have at our disposal. If the gates are sealed by war, that inventory may become very important indeed!'

'Thank you again for agreeing to deliver those resolutions, my friend. Here is the list of recipients:
Torchún, the Warden of the Houses of Healing. Echadon, the Captain of the Garrison. Celephir, the Warden of the Coffers. Mirudil, the Warden of the Stores.
'You will be doing the city a great service!'

'You have just missed a meeting of the Council, but if you go within you may be able to lend some aid to Arodor, chief scribe of the Council. The meetings have been contentious of late, and the number of raised voices I have heard from my position here has only increased in recent days.'

Duinhir thunders his displeasure, and some of the men nearby shrink away involuntarily.

You ask Pippin how he came to the White City.
'Oh, Gandalf brought me here. I slept much of the way, but Shadowfax is the swiftest of his kind and he was at a gallop for most of the journey. Why did we leave our friends behind? Well... Gandalf thought... he just thought I should see Minas Tirith, is all. The others had their own plans, and... you know. He's a Wizard.'
Pippin awkwardly stops speaking and picks at the food in silence. You wonder at his sudden evasiveness, and decide to have a little more of the lunch.

'I... wasn't entirely honest with you, ${PLAYER}, and I am sorry for it. Gandalf did not bring me to Minas Tirith without cause, or as a simple sight-seeing trip. I know you were not deceived, but... it is difficult to speak of, and I am still ashamed that I might have worked some harm. Not on purpose! Gandalf called me a fool once, or twice, and he was right to do so! But I would never endanger my friends on purpose.
'There was an artifact at Isengard. Wormtongue threw it down from the tower, intending to do some harm to either Saruman or Gandalf, and I saved it from rolling away into a pool. Gandalf claimed it soon afterward, but not soon enough... I found I could not stop thinking about the dark globe.
'I... I stole it away from the Wizard when he slept, and looked into it, ${PLAYER}. I saw... I saw...'
Pippin trails away into silence, shame and fear written upon his face.

'I saw... a tall tower and a black sky, and wheeling shapes... like bats, but much larger, and more frightening. And then... I saw... I saw him, ${PLAYER}. He looked at me, and his voice came not to my ears but to my mind, if that makes any sense. He asked me questions, and when I did not answer, I felt searing pain. I told him I was a hobbit, and his laughter was cruel. He said I would see him soon, and then Gandalf broke the spell and took away the stone.
'The artifact was a seeing-stone, a palantír, and Saruman had used it to communicate with... with his dark master. Gandalf would not tell me very much about the stone, but he seemed to think we escaped a much worse fate through a lucky chance of good fortune. I... I think he was right. I could not turn my eyes from the stone, and if that horrible figure had continued his questions, I know I would have answered him. What else might he have showed me in the palantír? I cannot guess, and do not wish to!
'This is not the sort of conversation that suits a picnic, ${PLAYER}! Let us clean up our food, and we can speak again back at my post!'

'We are still working to repair the wall. I cannot return to the city just yet! I have disturbing news, and it enforces my desire not to leave my post until the last possible moment.

'I do know that Orcs, Wargs, and a strange group of Easterlings have overrun the plain of Talath Anor. It is this last that gives me the most concern. 'Aid me in this! You are an adventurer and can do a great deal of good in this land beyond the Rammas! Once we have faced these threats, I give you my word that we can return to the North-gate.'

'Eärnur was mighty, and he did not lack for courage, but he possessed none of the caution that could have saved him from doom. He had great victory at Fornost, when he defeated the Witch-king of Angmar, but that victory stirred his pride to great heights. The Witch-king fled; Prince Eärnur believed he had nearly rid Middle-earth of that terrible foe, and cursed his failure to end it there.
'Years later, the Witch-king issued a challenge to Eärnur, now the King of Gondor, and summoned him to Minas Morgul. Eärnur went to that dark city to face his hated foe, and was lost.
'We know now that his will was mastered, and he became the loyal servant of his former enemy. He took a new name, Mordirith, and was given the rule of Angmar while the Witch-king managed the interests of Mordor elsewhere in Middle-earth. Through your own efforts and those of the Rangers and the Champion of Angmar, he was defeated, but it seems that victory was not to last. He maintains some bond to his former life, and it allowed his dark master to draw him back before he was lost for good.'

'You had better fortune than I did, ${PLAYER}, for I have yet to find anything. Let me see this scroll.'
Mithrandir takes it from you and quickly reads the yellowed parchment. After a moment he looks up at you again.
'There are matters of interest in this scroll. It speaks of not one challenge but two, a detail of which I was not aware. It appears that the Witch-king challenged Eärnur to ride forth, and the King was dissuaded from that foolishness by his Steward, a wise man named Mardil. That name I do know, for he would become the first of the Ruling Stewards when Eärnur disappeared into Minas Morgul. It is from his line that Denethor draws his authority.'

'You found something else? Ah, yes, this book contains diagrams describing the passage of succession through the line of Kings, and then through the line of the Ruling Stewards.
'Do you see? Here is Mardil, the first of the Stewards, who ruled Gondor after Eärnur was taken into the darkness of Minas Morgul. Mardil swore an oath to rule only until the King returned, and each Ruling Steward has made the same vow.'
Mithrandir looks around, furtively, ensuring that you are alone. When he is satisfied that you are alone in the Archives, he continues.
'Perhaps at one time the Stewards believed the line of Kings would return, but that possibility must now seem quite unlikely. We should not speak of it, even here, but there is one on his way to Minas Tirith who will remind Denethor of his vow. The King may very well return to Gondor, and the rule of the Stewards will no longer be necessary.'

'It may come to nothing, ${PLAYER}. There are few in the city who would believe that a man might return from the darkest depths of evil. Though he was once Eärnur, he has worn many guises since he was King of Gondor. He cannot be the man he was, and despite the rules of succession he has been corrupted by Angmar, and by Mordor.
'But we must remain alert. If Gothmog does seek to seize the throne of Gondor, we must oppose him... no matter the cost.'
'We should leave this place. It is no longer as comfortable or as familiar as it once was.'

'These names are not familiar to me, but I do have a dim recollection that a man named Orolang may have committed some heroic deed at the Battle of Fornost. It is the barest hint of a memory, but I have not even that for these others. Macilnis is a common name among the women of Gondor; none of the histories I have seen include any women in the retinue of Eärnur's knights, but this scroll appears genuine to me and I have no reason to doubt it.
'Some of Eärnur's knights have returned to trouble Middle-earth as Cargûl, but the power he wielded as Mordirith seems more deadly than theirs. We should expect he will be more powerful still in his guise as Gothmog.
'And yet, somewhere behind these masks, does any of Eärnur remain? He was bold but foolish. Can it be that Gothmog will be the same?'

'How do the inventories compare, ${PLAYER}? Do we have all the goods we expect?'
You tell Mirudal that the Upper Stores are fully accounted, but Dírion believes that rats are to blame for a disparity between the inventory of the Lower Stores and the goods actually kept there. Mirudal nods.
'Ah, I see. That is a shame, but it is not terribly surprising. Rats need to eat as well, and they can sense coming danger as well or better than we can! It makes sense to me that rats might covet our goods. I will set the total amount of food to be rationed slightly lower than I planned, in order to account for the rats. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'You should tell Mirudal about the rats. He may need to account for slightly lower totals of food for the coming siege. It might be best if he lowers the tally of food he expects to ration. The rats will keep getting into it, I imagine. Nothing to be done.'
'It makes sense to me that rats might covet our goods. I will set the total amount of food to be rationed slightly lower than I planned, in order to account for the rats. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'Yes? Are you finished?'
You tell Dírion that some of the food appears to be missing.
'I see. I should have mentioned this when you arrived, but I have had my suspicions for some time now that there might be a rat problem inside the Stores. They must have gnawed their way in and spirited away some of the food, especially the grains and cheeses. You should tell Mirudal. He may need to account for slightly lower totals of food for the coming siege.
'It might be best if he lowers the tally of food he expects to ration. The rats will keep getting into it, I imagine. Nothing to be done.'

'You... you have come back? Did you tell Mirudal about the rats?'
You tell Dírion that you do not believe his story about rats, and that you think he has been stealing food from the Stores. His brow knits with rage, and his eyes darken. When he finally speaks, his voice is desperate.
'Have mercy upon me, ${CLASS}! I admit the deed. My family could not bear to leave the city, and when the order to evacuate came, they hid within the house; they are there still! This is their home, and they could not bear to leave it, or me! My wife Mundil, my son Cúnir, my daughter Fionel... they will not be accounted-for when Mirudal rations out the food! If I do not steal some of the food for them, they will go hungry! So I have set aside a small amount. Is that a crime? Have mercy!
'What will you do? If you turn me in, you will doom my family! Help me, ${PLAYER}, or do nothing! Better that than have my family's lives upon your conscience!'

'Merethien and Mirudal have been working on a plan to assess the food-stocks and other supplies within the city, and they could use your assistance. They are right over there, and will be glad to have your help.'

'Stop, friend. On whose authority do you seek to gain access to the Upper Stores?'
You show Túlharil the inventory from Mirudal, and she recognizes the mark of the Warden of the Stores.
'Aye, that is his mark. You are welcome to enter the Stores and compare its contents to your inventory, but remove nothing.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}! I suppose you have been north of the Rammas Echor on Imrahil's errand? I told you to assist the Prince of Dol Amroth, but soon afterward I regretted doing so! There were some matters I should have asked you about in greater detail, but I gave away my chance by sending you away!
'It is all set right now, for you have returned, and I will worry at it no longer. I must hear what you saw in Osgiliath, and I must hear it quickly.
'No, not here! Speak to me if you are ready, and we will depart together for the Old Archives, where we will find the first and oldest collection of scrolls in the city. I think your tale may require further study, and that is where we may conduct it.'

'Let us go to the Old Archives. You may begin the tale of your experience in Osgiliath as we walk, and perhaps I will have heard its full extent by the time we have arrived. We must not spend too long poring over old scrolls when battle is so close upon us, but my heart tells me that there is something we have overlooked, some detail that may be of use to us in the days ahead!
'We must know what this thing may be!'

'We must keep each other's confidence on this matter, and tell no one the true nature of Gothmog's lineage. No good can come of it, for Gondor or for this Middle-earth.
'I do thank you for your tale, ${PLAYER}, though it be unpleasant and worrisome. Better to know and prepare than to be taken unawares!
'For now there is a city to defend. We must set our will to its defence, and let all other matters fade into the background. They are lesser matters for as long as the gate and the men defending it stand strong. May that be a long time. May that be long enough.'

And I know it has failed! Whatever that fool brought with him is now gone, and if it is the weapon I perceive, it will not matter if the gates of Minas Tirith last five minutes or five hours. The end will come!
'Listen to my words, ${PLAYER}. Hear what I say, and tremble at the truth in them! There can be no turning back from this doom. It comes even now...'

'No one is coming to help us!'

'Mithrandir does not share his mind with me, but I know of the dream that came to my sons, the dream that tried to snare Faramir but stole Boromir instead. This must be the Halfling, captured by the Enemy and held in his tower!

'This is the Tower Hall, ${PLAYER}. Do not tell anyone, but the Steward makes me nervous. I will show you where to go and then return to my posting outside, glad he does not need me at the moment!'

'Imrahil told me you were with my son when he fell before the city, ${PLAYER}. Would that you had drawn his foes away, or put yourself between his horse and the wraiths! He fights still, but it is an unnatural wound. It saps his strength, and his body is wasting away. My son!'
Denethor's voice breaks, and his eye is drawn back to Faramir's bed. He shakes his head, and when he speaks again his voice is full of iron and his fists are clenched.
'Do you know what it is like to live so near to Mordor, ${PLAYER}? Do you know what it is like to stand on the wall of your city and see flames on the horizon, knowing that they signal some terrible work of evil? Do you know what it is to be always in the thought of creatures so vile and so terrible that even Death cannot master them?
'I know what it is like, ${CLASS}. Every morning I wake up knowing it, and every evening I retire to my chamber knowing it. And in the darkest reaches of the night, I wake from troubled dreams knowing it.
'I have struggled long with this knowledge, and I struggle still, though my sons and heirs be taken from me. I struggle for my people.'

'No one comes to this chamber without my leave, ${PLAYER}, and I grant that sparingly! When I look at you I see a student of Mithrandir. The Wizard has been a friend to Gondor, so far, but he does not have the full measure of my trust. Why should he possess it? He is not of this land, and if the battle turns ill he will simply leave it, leaving my people to suffer and die!
'I am not without weapons, ${PLAYER}. I brought you here so you will see that I still fight the Enemy, though none appreciate the battle I wage within this high chamber!
'This is a seeing-stone, an heirloom of the Kings of old. I have turned it to my will.'

'You found supporters of the Withered Tree throughout the lower Circles of the city? I knew you would, ${PLAYER}. There are more and more of them with every passing hour! I have been kept quite busy keeping them away from the gate. Can you believe they think they will find mercy with the armies of Mordor? They are disloyal and foolish both!
'Keep fighting for Gondor, ${PLAYER}, and I will do the same, 'gainst any and all foes!'

'Captain of Tidings is not my only title. I am also the Spy-master of Minas Tirith, and I know how a group like the Withered Tree operates. They must have gained some of the pass-words for the upper Circles of the city. Húrin must change the pass-words, ${PLAYER}. We have not used the current set for as long as usual, but in time of war three hours may seem like days! Ask him for new pass-words, and give them to the guards at the gates in the upper Circles. Then find members of the Withered Tree in the lower Circles and make them cease their hateful whisperings! I will meet you in the First Circle when you have proved successful.'

'I believed we would soon need new pass-words. This is Húrin's mark, and now I will recognize only the new pass-word: <rgb=#00FF00>Flame of Victory</rgb>.
'I hope it is our victory, and not the victory of Mordor, that this pass-word presages!'

'The Steward is a fool! He has sold the city to our enemies, and now he asks us to die for him? None of us will see the dawn!
'Die, ${PLAYER}, and know that the Withered Tree has ended your tale!'
'Supporters of the Withered Tree may be lurking within the lower Circles of the city. Search among the citizenry for such dangerous men!'

'There is no hope for us! The Council of Gondor and the Steward have failed, and doomed this city to fall! Can you not hear the harsh cries from beyond the walls?
'We should have listened to the Withered Tree, and cast these leaders from the highest level of Minas Tirith! Perhaps then we would have been spared!'

'We must open the gates! Have you not seen the parchments that the Withered Tree has placed throughout the city? The host of Mordor will spare us if we open the gates! The Orcs only want the Steward and the Council; they will allow the common folk to live if we let them in!
'It is wisdom! We must open the gates! I will kill you if you try to stop me!'
'Supporters of the Withered Tree may be lurking within the lower Circles of the city. Search among the citizenry for such dangerous men!'
'Supporters of the Withered Tree may be lurking within the lower Circles of the city. Search among the citizenry for such dangerous men!'
'How will we survive the coming storm? Can there be any hope?'
'The armies of the Enemy press close about the walls! How can there be any victory against such numbers?'
'Will the gates hold? I have never seen such evil, not in all my days!'

'A new pass-word, already? I think the time for pass-words is behind us, ${PLAYER}! The Orcs of Mordor will not turn away from my gate because they lack the pass-word! But this is Húrin's mark, and I am bound to obey. The new pass-word will be: <rgb=#00FF00>Triumphant</rgb>.
'But whose triumph will it be, I wonder?'

'Show those pass-words to the guards and then destroy this parchment. Perhaps that will hinder the movement of the Withered Tree into the upper levels.
'After the pass-words have been set, Lamlor wants you to find members of the Withered Tree urging dissent in the lower Circles? If you will be able to recognize them, I suppose. They have become more brazen in recent days, and now that the siege has begun I suppose they have nothing more to lose. They may be obvious to you now, ${PLAYER}.
'Go with haste, and remain loyal to the Council and to the Steward!'

'Go and die, ${PLAYER}! There can be no avoiding the doom of which I have spoken!'

'Do you understand, ${PLAYER}? It is not needless cruelty that drove this tale of mine. No, it is kindness. For my words wove a picture of the fate that awaits us all. It cannot be avoided. Better to accept the road and set our affairs in order than to fight it fruitlessly. In fewer than three hours it will be the fourteenth of March. We are unlikely to live until dawn on the fifteenth!'
You shake your head to clear it, but still your mind is foggy. Is it really only half past nine in the evening of the thirteenth of March? The account seemed so vivid, so real...
Your eyes turn toward the palantír. Denethor laughs, but there is no humour in it.
'I have wrestled with the seeing-stone for many days, ${CLASS}. I am not surprised that the experience left you feeling unwell, and particularly susceptible to the words I spoke. Can you not see how the tale I spun you must surely follow from the images you beheld in the stone? The end has come. The end has come! The armies have not yet surrounded Minas Tirith, but they will. The folk have not yet thrown in with the Withered Tree, but they will! Grond has not yet come to the gates, but it will! How long can they stand against that ram? If they last even a minute longer than I believe, that will be a triumph. But it will not matter. All that I have told you will come to pass.'
You try to tell the Steward that he is wrong, but you cannot find the words.
'You have seen what I saw in the stone. Hirgon and the Red Arrow did not make it to Rohan, and the foolish one Mithrandir sent to Mordor is a captive in Cirith Ungol! Yes, I know of that errand. And I know it has failed! Whatever that fool brought with him is now gone, and if it is the weapon I perceive, it will not matter if the gates of Minas Tirith last five minutes or five hours. The end will come! It has already come!
'Go, ${PLAYER}! Go and die! Every person in this city will follow you soon!'
'Do you at last understand the words I have spoken, ${PLAYER}? Do you finally see that this doom cannot be avoided?'

'And so it ends, ${PLAYER}. The Wizard is slain, and will trouble my Master no longer. The city is taken!
'What few defenders remain in the city will be rooted out and brought to this high place, and it is here they will die. You live only because I commanded it, but once the last cries of the dying have faded into the wind, you too will follow them.'
'${PLAYER}... what could... we have done...?'
The Witch-king is victorious!

At the sound of the young hobbit's voice, a tremendous smile brightens your face and you fight the urge to clasp Pippin in a tight embrace.
'What is the joke, ${PLAYER}? I've never seen you this happy! It's a little peculiar, if you ask me, this being war-time and all, but I suppose that's no reason not to look on the bright side, is it?
'You do seem a little flustered, now that I think about it: both happy and sad at the same time, if that makes any sense. I saw you not ten minutes ago, when the Steward summoned you before him. What could you have talked about in so short a time that would work such a change in you?'

Habla con Mithrandir en el Patio de la Fuente

'I understand you had an audience with Denethor, ${PLAYER}. I might have given you some wisdom concerning how to handle the Steward, but I was not consulted. I trust you did not spoil any of our plans, or cause any harm that cannot be undone?'
You tell Mithrandir that Denethor spoke to you of many things that he saw within the depths of a palantír. At that, Mithrandir looks up sharply.
'So the Anor-stone did remain within the tower. I wondered if it was so. Denethor has had a stubborn and strong will for all the years of his life, but if he seeks to gain some advantage over the enemy by using the palantír...'
You interrupt the Wizard, and his initial offence is quickly assuaged as you recount the worrying tale of Denethor's prophetic words concerning the siege to come. Mithrandir is silent for a long while. Finally he speaks.
'I do not think he has seen the siege itself in the Anor-stone, ${PLAYER}, and that is very important to us. A palantír cannot be made to lie, though its images might deceive if the user interprets them incorrectly. But I fear that the future in which Denethor believes, while not certain, could still come to pass. There is a question that his tale raises in my mind, a question I had not fully considered before now.
'Where was Rohan? If the events of the coming siege will indeed transpire as Denethor foretells, and Théoden does not come to the aid of Gondor, I fear that the Steward of Gondor may be right. Minas Tirith will fall.
'It is absolutely imperative that you learn what has happened to the Riders of Rohan. They must come to Minas Tirith in time, or all is lost. The siege is still ahead. Time yet remains.'
<rgb=#00FF00>To be continued in Volume IV, Book 5, 'The Ride of the Rohirrim.'</rgb>

'But you should find Gandalf! I know that he is very worried about the city, and about Gondor, and any information you might have about the Steward's state of mind could be useful to him. Did I say Gandalf? I mean you should find Mithrandir. I will never get used to calling him that, ${PLAYER}. Why does he need two names, anyway? It's not proper!'
You point out that the young Took himself has two names, going sometimes by Peregrin and sometimes by Pippin.
'Well, that's different. That's different! Ah, you got me. Well-played, ${PLAYER}. Well-played indeed.'
'You should find Mithrandir! I know that he is very worried about the city, and about Gondor, and any information you might have about the Steward's state of mind could be useful to him.'

Speak with Tolwin.
You and Tolwin encounter a group of Orcs building machines of war. These Orcs should be stopped at once.
Speak with Dúneth
Speak with Dúneth

'My son Tolwin and I are bound to this task of defeating those who destroyed our home. My husband and sons will not rest soundly until Korpûrta is defeated.
'${PLAYER}, you do not need to put yourself in danger as you have no ties to Talath Anor. However, I see it in your eyes that you have done much to help this land and wish to see a better life for all Gondorians.
'Also, I see in Tolwin's eyes that he looks up to you. Should you accept this final attack, you will give Tolwin the strength he needs to face the man who killed his father and kin.'
'I will not mourn the loss of my husband Gilgír and my sons until The First Blade falls.'

'We have made it back safely to Crithost. Tolwin and I shall spend our time vigilantly protecting this village. I am certain that some of the enemy in Cair Andros will retaliate.
'Crithost will stand. You have my word that we will rebuild Talath Anor in time.'

Dúneth can be found just outside Jal Kepir in Talath Anor.
You should speak with Dúneth.
The First Blade

Dúneth can be found in the hall of Crithost.
You should speak with Dúneth.
The fearsome Sûhalar, Korpûrta, must face the consequences of his actions for the slaughter of Gilgír and Tolwin's older brothers.

'I shall always remember this day. You have taught me much, ${PLAYER}, in our short time together. I shall continue to practice my fighting techniques until we meet again.
'Thank you again for your assistance in finding my mother and reuniting me with the family I still have. You should make sure to speak with Ceveneth before you head south. Farewell, my friend.'

'You would not believe it but those saplings you brought back are growing better in Crithost than they were in the orchard! I'll see to it that these fields are as beautiful and plentiful as they once were.
'It's a shame you have to leave so soon but I do understand. This is a hard time for everyone in Gondor and the White City needs as many able warriors as they can get.
'Good luck and don't be a stranger around here in more peaceful times!'

'${PLAYER}, you were gone longer than expected. You say you were able to help establish a Gondorian stronghold in Crithost? That is good news.
'While Cair Andros may be lost, we still hold a patch of ground in Talath Anor. Slowly we will push the enemy back.
'Perhaps it would be wise of you to return to Minas Tirith. I am sure there are those in the city that could use your aid. I shall remain here to hold the North-gate for the arrival of the Rohirrim.'
You vow to Tolwin to help him take back Cair Andros after the war
Ingold will continue to watch from the North-gate for signs of the Rohirrim
Ceveneth will do her part in rebuilding the once fertile farmlands and orchards of Talath Anor

'I know you must depart, for the enemy marches south from Cair Andros towards Minas Tirith. You must defend the White City from the forces of Mordor. Do not fear, we shall be able to hold our own at Crithost.'
You vow to Dúneth and all the people of Talath Anor to return after the battle and help her retake Cair Andros. You do not know when you will be able to fulfill this promise but you assure her that you will keep it.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Your vow means much to me. It is what Gilgír would have done and would have wanted. I shall await your return, brave ${RACE}. Please make sure to speak to Tolwin before you leave.'
The Vow to Cair Andros

'Let us all retreat to Crithost.'
'We have accomplished what we came here for. Let us retreat to Crithost.'

Teodoro hace lo posible por susurrar.
'La Piedra de Roth estará a salvo aquí, ${PLAYER}. ¡Que le dé a este dragón toda la mala suerte que pueda producir y nos deje en paz a Haley y a mí!
'Es curioso, pero al mirar todo este tesoro me doy cuenta de que no deseo ni la porción más pequeña. Tal vez ya haya terminado con la búsqueda de tesoros, después de todo. No tenías por qué venir a buscarme, pero aun así me conmueve. He entregado un tesoro, pero he encontrado otro: ¡qué buenas amistades tengo!
'Deberíamos ir hacia la salida antes de que esta criatura despierte. Yo sé que cuando me levanto por la mañana, ¡lo primero que quiero es algo para picar!'

'Bueno, ¡eso estuvo cerca! Aun así, todo salió bien, ¿no? ¡Y me alegra haberme deshecho de la Piedra de Roth!
'Entonces, ¿qué haremos ahora, mis amistades aventureras? ¡Teodoro Tojo está listo para lo que sea!'
'¿Es un pueblo lo que se ve allá abajo, al otro lado de la llanura? ¡Vayamos de inmediato y dejemos atrás a este dragón!'
¡Has fallado, y Draigoch se cobra otra víctima!
¡Bingo ha sido derrotado!
Haley Pradodulce desenrolla su cuerda y la ata firmemente a un saliente rocoso
Hasta ahora, la suerte te ha acompañado. El dragón está dormido
Bingo está en la entrada de la guarida de Draigoch y espera rescatar a Teodoro Tojo antes de que sea demasiado tarde.
Haley Pradodulce te ha seguido hasta un saliente con vista al dragón dormido.
Teodoro Tojo está en el fondo de la guarida de Draigoch y debes descender para alcanzarlo.
Bingo está en el fondo de la guarida de Draigoch y quiere hablar contigo de algo urgente.
¡Has encontrado a Teodoro Tojo en la guarida de Draigoch!

'Oh cielos... ¡mira a este pobre infeliz! Este no es un lugar seguro en absoluto, ${PLAYER}. Parece que ladrones han entrado aquí de vez en cuando, y quienes no cayeron víctimas del fuego del dragón quizá encontraron su final a manos de quienes los acompañaban. Cuando hay tesoro de por medio, incluso los buenos amigos pueden convertirse en enemigos por el reparto de una sola moneda.
'¡Pero ahora mismo es el dragón lo que debe preocuparnos!'

'No podía esperar más, ${PLAYER}, y menos mal que los seguí cuando lo hice, porque parece que no tienen forma de bajar desde este saliente hasta el fondo de la guarida. ¿Cómo van a rescatar a Teodoro si no pueden llegar hasta él?
'Bueno, tengo una cuerda. La ataré a una roca aquí arriba y podremos bajar hasta el fondo para salvar a Teodoro. Tendremos que ser muy, muy sigilosos, así que actúa con cuidado.
'¡Bien, dejemos esta cuerda atada!'

La voz de Bingo es poco más que un susurro.
'Camina con cuidado, ${PLAYER}. No queremos despertar a este dragón.'
Instancia: Tesoro perdido, tesoro encontrado
Has encontrado a Teodoro Tojo en las profundidades de la guarida de Draigoch.
¡El dragón empieza a despertarse!
¡El dragón está despierto! ¡Debes llegar a la cuerda antes de que la guarida se llene de fuego!
¡Has escapado de la guarida del dragón... pero justo a tiempo!
Bingo ha entrado en la guarida del poderoso Draigoch para rescatar a Teodoro Tojo... ¡si no es ya demasiado tarde!
Protege a Egwylf y Willem del Nazgûl

Protege a Bingo del Nazgûl

'Tenemos que encontrar a Bingo, ${PLAYER}. ¡Esa criatura podría volver!'
'¡Busquemos a Bingo antes de que la tormenta empeore!'
¡La llama prende!
¡Necesitas tomar la antorcha para poder prender fuego a la hierba!
La lluvia y el viento se han vuelto muy intensos, y Bingo quiere encontrar un lugar resguardado donde quedarse.
Habla con Bingo antes de que la tormenta empeore

'¡Esta tormenta surgió muy de repente, ${PLAYER}! ¡Deberíamos buscar un lugar donde refugiarnos de la lluvia y el viento!
'¡También estoy bastante nervioso por los rayos!'
Instancia: Identidad equivocada
Un Nazgûl ha descendido sobre las llanuras de Rohan, ¡y Bingo está en peligro!
Egwylf cree que podrías ahuyentar al Nazgûl si logras prender fuego a la hierba.
El Nazgûl sisea con furia. ¡No quiere acercarse a las llamas!

Te has visto ${PLAYERNAME:atrapado[m]|atrapada[f]} en la tormenta junto a Bingo, Egwylf y Willem.
Mientras viajas por las llanuras de Rohan con Bingo, Egwylf y Willem Bigote, una fuerte tormenta ha estorbado vuestro avance.
Habla con Myrtle en el sendero fuera del agujero hobbit de Bingo
Recibe a los invitados de la fiesta de Bingo a medida que llegan
Recibe a las nuevas llegadas
Habla con Bert Bartolín fuera del agujero hobbit de Bingo
Entra en la casa de Bingo para la fiesta
¡Socializa!
Recibe a los vecinos de Bingo fuera de su agujero hobbit
Habla con Bingo en su casa

'Esta ha sido toda una aventura, ${PLAYER}. No sé qué haremos Haley y yo a partir de ahora, pero no dudo que será una experiencia llena de peligro y emoción.
'No se lo digas, pero creo que sin ella a mi lado podría haberme metido en problemas una o dos veces durante esta aventura. Nada que no pudiera resolver por mí mismo, ¡por supuesto! Tú también ayudaste, de vez en cuando, una o dos veces. Lo que intento decir es que incluso un aventurero experimentado como Teodoro Gorse necesita amigos de vez en cuando.'
Teodoro tose con vergüenza, y su habitual fanfarronería vuelve.
'¡Bien! ¡Suficiente de palabras empalagosas! ¡Mi pasado es magnífico! ¡Mi presente es satisfactorio! ¡Desafío al futuro a decepcionarme!'
'Debo preguntarle a Teodoro dónde consiguió su sombrero. ¡Quiero añadirlo a mi colección!'

'¿Es fiable este mapa? Hay realmente muchos pueblos en la Comarca. Respeto sus madrigueras, y un agujero hobbit parece un lugar muy ordenado para vivir, pero no me vendrían mal unas cuantas cámaras grandes y resonantes. ¡Y ni un gran salón a la vista!
Ketill suspira.
'¿Cómo viven así los hobbits, ${PLAYER}?'

'¡Me gusta esta joven hobbit! Es muy atenta, y me recuerda un poco a mí cuando tenía su edad.'
Haley se pone intensamente roja.
'Oh, lo siento mucho. Los hobbits envejecen de manera diferente a mi gente, ¿no es así? ¿Caléndula es realmente una niña? Aun así, lamento haber hablado tan a la ligera. ¡Pasar tanto tiempo cerca de Teodoro debe haberme vuelto descuidada como él! ¡Qué pensamiento tan aterrador!'

'Es agradable sentarse un momento. Todos mis hijos están ocupados por ahora, ¡y puedo tener un rato para mí!
'Debo decirle al primo Bingo que organice estas fiestas más a menudo!'

'El manuscrito de Bingo es muy bueno hasta ahora, ${PLAYER}, pero me gustaría que mostrara un poco más de destreza con la ortografía y la gramática. ¡Este libro necesitará algo de refinamiento antes de que me sienta cómodo colocándolo en una estantería de biblioteca!'

'¡Bingo ha reunido una colección de libros bastante impresionante! Me impresiona su dedicación académica, y me pregunto qué les falta a las grandes colecciones de mi pueblo por no incluir literatura hobbit.
'¡Fue muy amable de parte de Bilbo Bolsón darme su invitación cuando visité Imladris!'
'¡Estoy listo para cenar, amigo mío! ¡Unámonos a los invitados y comamos hasta saciarnos!'

'Me entristece decir que ninguno de mis hermanos podrá venir a la fiesta hoy, ${PLAYER}. Todos tienen obligaciones en otras tierras, pero prometí que el viejo Rattlepacks y yo representaríamos a la familia Bartolín lo mejor posible.
'Ahora bien, ¿dónde está nuestro anfitrión? ¡Estoy listo para servirme uno o dos platos de sabrosas viandas! ¡Entremos!'

'Ya casi es hora de cenar, ${PLAYER}, pero aún hay un pequeño asunto al que me gustaría atender. No tomará mucho tiempo.
'¿Tienes un momento?'

'¡No esperaba que viniera tanta gente a mi fiesta! ¡Seguro que no envié tantas invitaciones!
'¡Hasta Willem ha venido... y trajo a su compañera y a todos sus cachorros! Los hijos de Prisca parecen encantados con ellos... ¡tendré que recordarle a Willem que cuente bien a sus pequeños cuando llegue el momento de que mis amigos lince regresen a casa!'

'¡Haley es increíble y extraordinaria, especialmente para ser una de la Gente Grande! Me está contando todas sus aventuras. ¿De verdad descendió a la guarida de un DRAGÓN... y logró salir de allí, DESPUÉS de despertarlo?
'¿Tú estabas allí también, ${PLAYER}? ¡Vaya! ¡Necesito encontrar un dragón al que vencer yo también!'

'Realmente vivimos una buena aventura, ¿no es así, ${PLAYER}? Espero que le recuerdes a Bingo nuestra participación para que no deje fuera nuestra contribución en su relato. Él pasó buena parte de mi parte empapado y sin saber quién era, así que quizás no tenga mucho que decir.
'Pensándolo bien... quizá no deberías recordarle mi contribución, ${PLAYER}. Puede que no todos los enanos debamos ser mencionados en los libros.'

'Hay muchas criaturas feroces en los bosques de los Valles Sombríos, pero siendo primos lejanos debéis poseer las mismas habilidades que nosotros. ¡Podrás evitar que te noten, Merrimac, y venir a visitarnos sin problemas!
'¡Hola, ${PLAYER}! Les estaba diciendo a estos buenos amigos que deberían venir a visitarnos a Maur Tulhau y disfrutar de un tradicional Festín de Bienvenida, ¡como hizo Bingo!
'Y si comen tanto como lo hizo él, también deberán disfrutar de la tradicional semana de recuperación después de un festín así, ¡pero encontraríamos un lugar para ellos! ¡Espero que vengan a visitarnos!'
'Mi hermana está muy interesada en ese tal Merrimac. ¡No creo que él esté tan contento al respecto como ella!'

'¡No he podido meter ni una palabra! No recuerdo haber aceptado dejar la Comarca, ¡pero Violed parece convencida de que sí lo hice!
'¿En qué lío me ha metido esta fiesta, ${PLAYER}?'

'Cuando tú y Bingo vinisteis a visitarme a Nuevoburgo, me visteis en mi peor momento, ${PLAYER}. ¡Pero tras un año de cortejo, Celandine Brandigamo por fin aceptó asistir a una reunión social conmigo! ¡Solo necesitaba una fiesta para venir con ella!
'Y cuando mi madre dijo que Bingo, mi primo segundo, estaba organizando una cena... bueno, ¡me pareció una oportunidad providencial!
'¡Pero ay! ¡Se ha pasado todo el tiempo encariñándose con estos cachorros de lince y no me ha dedicado ni un momento! ¡Cruel destino!'
'¡Ooooh, mira qué adorables son! ¡Y su pelaje parece tan suave! ¡Los amo a todos!'

'¿No se supone que esta es una cena? ¿Por qué tarda tanto en aparecer la comida?
'¡El gruñido de mi estómago ahogará todas las conversaciones si no comemos pronto!'
'Esta es una mesa muy bonita. No veo ni una sola marca en ella. Y, sin embargo, sabiendo cómo bailaba Bingo sobre las mesas del Poney Pisador, ¡debe haber practicado en algún lugar!'

'¡Ah, recuerdo fiestas tan buenas como esta! Ha pasado tanto tiempo, y aún más que la muerte, pues en Audaghaim no había ocasión para festejos. Pero cuando era apenas una niña, de ocho o nueve años, recuerdo la emoción de reunirme con amigos.
'¿Cómo llegué aquí? Pues he sentido una extraña afinidad por esa herradura que llevas contigo. Quizá una pequeña parte de su metal vino alguna vez de Audaghaim, hace mucho tiempo, y se mezcló con otros metales con los años. No puedo asegurarlo... pero al estar ligada al lugar de mi maldición, esa explicación es tan buena como cualquier otra que pueda imaginar.
'Me alegra ver una reunión tan alegre una vez más, aunque no la merezca. ¡Aun así, gracias por traerme aquí, aunque fuera sin saberlo!'
'Esta muchacha no ha dejado de bailar desde que llegó. Parece encantada... aunque admito que no entiendo por qué.'
Bingo está recordando aventuras con Egwylf y Langhár
Caléndula y Spalvi escuchan embelesados las aventuras de Haley
Los vecinos de Bingo y los visitantes de Maur Tulhau intentan encontrar puntos en común

Teodoro y Bert intentan superar las historias del otro, ¡pero los hobbits solo quieren comer!
Donnamira Tuk examina el manuscrito de Bingo para ver si sería adecuado para su biblioteca
La expresión recelosa de Myrtle sería más adecuada para una batalla que para una fiesta
¡En poco tiempo, la fiesta está en pleno desarrollo!
Myrtle Cenagales encabeza un pequeño grupo de vecinos de Bingo en el sendero fuera de su agujero hobbit.
Myrtle Cenagales está fuera del agujero hobbit de Bingo. ¿Viene también a la fiesta?
Siguen llegando más invitados a la fiesta de Bingo, y deberías recibirlos para que se sientan bienvenidos.
Siguen llegando invitados a la fiesta de Bingo, pero no hay garantía de que todos se lleven bien.
Habla con el recién llegado

'Bueno, supongo que sería grosero no asistir a la fiesta de Bingo, así que aquí estamos, ${PLAYER}. ¿Crees que habrá olvidado aquel asunto de la petición que comencé antes de que se marchara en su aventura? Te agradecería que no se lo recordaras.'

'Saludos, ${PLAYER}. Sé que no recibí una invitación para la fiesta de Bingo... no, ¡no te preocupes! No le guardo rencor, ni tampoco lo esperaba. Hablé con él solo brevemente hace mucho tiempo, y entonces me reclamaban otros deberes.
'Hace poco estuve en Rivendel a petición de la Dama Galadriel, y allí hablé con un personaje muy interesante. Bilbo es su nombre, y parece estar muy ansioso por leer el libro de Bingo. Me contó sobre esta fiesta y que, lamentablemente, no podría asistir. Yo le dije que vendría en su nombre y que le informaría del progreso del libro.
'Con ese fin he preparado una gran cantidad de tinta y la he traído como regalo para Bingo. ¡Que su pluma nunca se quede sin tinta!'

'${PLAYER}... No sabía adónde ir. Vagaba sin rumbo, sin saber por qué los Montaraces me habían perdonado la vida, o por qué Bingo me mostró bondad. Mis pasos sin guía me llevaron al norte, sin plan alguno, solo porque mis pies me llevaron allí. ¿Me llevarían a Angmar donde habitaba Avair, o a Forochel, morada de Gun Ain? ¿Dónde podría empezar de nuevo, como Clemencia?
'En Galtrev encontré un pergamino flotando en el viento. Era una invitación a una cena, dirigida a un hombre al que nunca conocí, alguien llamado Hunfredo. Debió dejarla caer, y así llegó a mí. No sabía a dónde ir... pero no había olvidado la bondad de Bingo, y no la olvidaré. Quería decirle que le estaba agradecida, y así mi viaje hacia el norte encontró su destino.
'En el camino me crucé con varios hombres, antiguos bandidos, que hablaban en voz alta de las hazañas de Bingo. Parece que serán granjeros. No sé si ese será mi destino, pero quizá pueda encontrar mi propio camino una vez que haya agradecido a Bingo su bondad.'
Instancia: La receta perfecta
¡Más invitados están llegando a la fiesta de Bingo!
Bert Bartolín ha llegado fuera del agujero hobbit de Bingo, ¡y está listo para comenzar el banquete!
¡La fiesta está en pleno apogeo!
Bingo está cerca de la cocina de su agujero hobbit. Ahora que ya has conversado con algunos invitados, deberías ver cómo está disfrutando tu anfitrión de su fiesta.
La casa de Bingo está llena de muchos de los amigos que hizo durante su viaje, y deberías socializar con los invitados antes de que suene la campana para la cena.
Ha llegado el día de la fiesta de Bingo... ¿vendrán los invitados?

Habla con Bingo
Escucha lo que Egwylf tiene que decir sobre Rohan
'Egwylf dijo que había pueblos no muy lejos de aquí. ¡Encontrémos uno y continuemos nuestro viaje... a pie!'

Willem te mira con indiferencia, como diciendo: '¿Qué te tomó tanto tiempo?'
De pronto, sus orejas se mueven y tú también oyes voces guturales. ¡Orcos se acercan desde el sur!
Bingo está listo para cruzar al reino de Rohan.
Willem está al sur del puente, en el reino de Rohan.
Una mujer de Rohan ha llegado galopando por el camino, impresionada por tu victoria sobre la partida de saqueo orca.

'¡Un paseo nos hará bien a ambos, ! No necesitamos montar caballos en Rohan. Nuestros pies servirán perfectamente. Si no me crees, ¡camina conmigo y verás!
'¡Te sorprenderá lo rápido que pasa el tiempo una vez que volvamos a movernos, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}! ¿Quién necesita caballos?'

'Soy Egwylf, y estoy en una misión urgente, pues el mensaje que llevo debe llegar a Stangard lo antes posible; no me detendré mucho, aunque parece que los cuatro compartimos el odio hacia los orcos y podríamos pasar un tiempo contando historias.'
Te presentas a ti y a tus compañeros, y Egwylf examina a Bingo con atención.

'Parecía muy agradable, pero creo que Egwylf está equivocada sobre la necesidad de montar un caballo en Rohan. Me las he arreglado bastante bien hasta ahora, ¿no es así? Y no habríamos apreciado tanto ese puente si hubiéramos pasado al galope o al trote, ¿verdad?
'No, no lo habríamos hecho.'
Instancia: La carga de Bingo
Bingo está al sur del puente, en el reino de Rohan.
Has conocido a una mujer llamada Egwylf justo dentro de los límites de Rohan, y está muy interesada en las aventuras de tu pequeño grupo.
Bingo ha decidido cruzar el reino de Rohan a pie para evitar tener que montar un caballo.

Deja que Bingo diga lo suyo, pero permanece alerta

Examina el cofre del tesoro que William quiere darle a Bingo
Habla con Haley en el camino a través de Enedwaith
Habla con Bingo en el camino a través de Enedwaith
<rgb=#FF0000>¡Bingo no debe ser derrotado!</rgb>
Habla con Bingo en la barrera

'Quiero darte las gracias por dejar que tu amigo hiciera entrar en razón a Graham. No estaba seguro de que este intento fuera a funcionar, y cuando vimos a tu grupo acercarse por el camino, me convencí de que íbamos a morir todos. Nuestra carrera como bandidos ha sido corta, pero mejor eso que que nuestras vidas fueran cortas.
'Los orcos habían abandonado este bloqueo cuando llegamos. Graham cree que algo tuvo que alejarlos, y deprisa. Sea cual sea la razón, dejaron algo de botín atrás. Quiero que se lo des a Bingo, ¡como regalo de quienes salvaron su vida hoy!
'¡Adiós! Ahora nos volveremos granjeros, como siempre deberíamos haber sido.'

'¿William quiere que tenga el tesoro? Bueno, supongo que podemos llevarlo con nosotros. No hice nada para merecerlo, pero sus dueños legítimos probablemente no vendrán a buscarlo. Los orcos que lo reunieron se habrán encargado de eso.
'Me alegra que no haya habido derramamiento de sangre hoy, ${PLAYER}. Solo tuve que mirar a los bandidos para saber que no podían compararse con ninguno de nosotros. Necesitaban palabras, no castigo por su pobre decisión de detenernos.
'¡Estoy listo para continuar nuestro viaje de regreso a casa!'
'Este camino lleva hacia el norte durante muchas millas. ¡Haley me dice que nos llevará a las Tierras de Bree!'

'Cuando Teodoro y yo pasamos por aquí en nuestro viaje hacia el sur, había una gran concentración de orcos y semi-orcos en las ruinas justo más adelante. Pudimos escabullirnos sin ser vistos, pero no creo que tengamos tanta suerte esta vez.
'Si llega a haber combate, deberías intentar proteger a Bingo de las espadas y flechas de los orcos. ¡Yo tendré las manos llenas tratando de evitar que derriben a Teodoro con un golpe afortunado!
'Quizá podamos rodear las ruinas si su número ha aumentado. No lo sabremos hasta acercarnos.'

'En lo que a mí respecta, nunca he sido muy amigo de los caballos. ¡Son tan grandes y aterradores, siempre pisoteando con sus pesadas pezuñas y mordiendo a hobbits desprevenidos con sus fuertes dientes! Me mordió casi un caballo cuando era un tween, ¿sabes?, y nunca he conseguido perdonar a esas criaturas.
'¿Crees que podrías bajar a la puerta este de Stangard y preguntarle a Sabert si podríamos disfrutar un recorrido a pie por el reino de Rohan? No es un lugar muy grande, ¿verdad? Si nuestros pies bastan, entonces digo que eso es lo que debemos hacer, ¡y dejar completamente fuera a los caballos!'

'¡Estoy listo para una buena caminata si tú lo estás, ${PLAYER}! Nunca habría sugerido algo así al inicio de nuestro viaje, ¡pero ahora somos aventureros curtidos y no temo una caminata de este tamaño!'

'¿Así que este es Rohan, eh? La gente de aquí parece muy tensa, como si estuvieran esperando que algo malo ocurriera. ¡No sé si culparlos, ${PLAYER}! Es un bonito pueblo, pero parece rodeado por todos lados de peligro, ¡y no hay suficientes guardias para protegerlo!
'Bueno, están de suerte, porque tres valientes aventureros han llegado a Largafortín: tú, yo y Willem Bigote, ¡por supuesto! Una breve charla con algunos niños me ha dado toda la información necesaria para ayudar a mejorar la situación. Si derrotamos salamandras, bandidos y orientales por todo el Páramo, creo que habremos hecho este lugar mucho más seguro para la gente de Largafortín. ¡Vamos, amigo mío!'

'¡Esto es terrible, ${PLAYER}! ¡Acabamos de llegar a Rohan y ya veo que el mal ha llegado realmente a este reino! Puede que este pueblo haya sido agradable antaño, pero ahora está abandonado, ¡una cáscara quemada!
Le dices a Bingo que la gente de Largafortín huyó hacia Harwick, y él asiente.
'Me alegra saber que algunos escaparon, pero si se parecen a los hobbits que conozco, querrán volver a sus hogares en cuanto puedan. ¡Deberíamos hacer la zona lo más segura posible para ellos! ¡Luchemos contra los enemigos que acechan cerca: salamandras, bandidos y orientales! Entonces habremos hecho nuestra parte para ayudar a la gente de Largafortín a regresar algún día a sus hogares.'
'He oído que el primer pueblo que encontraremos en el reino de Rohan se llama Largafortín. ¡Vamos allí sin demora!'

'¡Buen trabajo, ${PLAYER}! La gente de Largafortín sigue pareciendo preocupada, pero hemos mejorado la situación en el Páramo, ¡aunque no estén seguros de que sea prudente alegrarse!
Bingo respira hondo, preparándose aparentemente para algo.
'Sabes, ${PLAYER}, quizá tenías razón con lo del caballo. Sabert y Egwylf también. Rohan es bastante más grande de lo que pensaba, y quizá yo también deba conseguir un caballo. Hablé con un hombre de aquí y dijo que hay caballos a la venta en la ciudad de Harwick, al sur. Supongo que deberíamos ir y ver.'
'Si podemos derrotar salamandras, bandidos y orientales por todo el Páramo, creo que habremos hecho este lugar mucho más seguro para la gente de Largafortín. ¡Vamos!'

'¡Luchemos contra los diversos enemigos que acechan cerca: salamandras, bandidos y orientales! Entonces estaremos haciendo nuestra parte para ayudar a la gente de Largafortín a regresar algún día a sus hogares.'

'¡Buen trabajo, ${PLAYER}! Largafortín no está en condiciones de recibir a su gente todavía, y no lo estará por un tiempo, pero quizá nuestros esfuerzos en el Páramo les ayuden cuando regresen.'
Bingo respira hondo, preparándose aparentemente para algo.

Sabert está en la puerta este de Stangard, el puesto avanzado de Rohan junto a las orillas del Gran Río.
Bingo es reacio a montar un caballo en Rohan y quiere saber por Sabert si el reino es lo bastante pequeño como para recorrerlo a pie.

'No sé realmente adónde deberíamos ir ahora, ${PLAYER}. Hemos ido más allá del borde del viejo mapa de Bilbo, ¡y nuestros pasos nos han llevado a un territorio desconocido! Podríamos viajar al reino de Rohan propiamente dicho, supongo, pero... bueno, quizá haya otro camino que seguir. Aman a sus caballos, ¿ves? Mira cuántas figuras equinas han tallado en los edificios de Stangard, ¡y esto es solo un puesto avanzado, fuera de las fronteras del reino!
'En lo que a mí respecta, nunca he sido muy amigo de los caballos. ¡Son tan grandes y aterradores, siempre pisoteando con sus pesadas pezuñas y mordiendo a hobbits desprevenidos con sus fuertes dientes! Me mordió casi un caballo cuando era un tween, ¿sabes?, y nunca he conseguido perdonar a esas criaturas.
'¿Crees que podrías bajar a la puerta este de Stangard y preguntarle a Sabert si podríamos disfrutar un recorrido a pie por el reino de Rohan? No es un lugar muy grande, ¿verdad? Si nuestros pies bastan, entonces digo que eso es lo que debemos hacer, ¡y dejar completamente fuera a los caballos!'

'¿El reino de Rohan es adecuado para recorrerlo a pie? ¿Me estás preguntando si es buena idea caminar de un extremo al otro de Rohan en vez de montar un caballo?'
Sabert estalla en sonoras carcajadas y, aunque es una respuesta un poco descortés, admites que más o menos lo esperabas. A Bingo no le va a gustar nada esto.

'¿Qué dijo Sabert sobre recorrer Rohan a pie, ${PLAYER}? ¿Es el reino lo bastante pequeño como para que eso sea razonable?'
Le dices a Bingo que Sabert realmente cree que es mejor montar a caballo en Rohan.
'Él diría eso, claro. Los rohirrim sin duda aman a sus caballos. Yo no siento necesidad alguna de subirme a una de esas temibles bestias. ¡Yo digo que caminemos! ¿Qué piensas tú, ${PLAYER}? ¿Es esta nuestra aventura o la de Sabert? ¡Un poco de ejercicio no nos vendrá mal! Háblame cuando podamos comenzar nuestra caminata por Rohan.'
Sabert parece a punto de echarse a reír otra vez ante la idea de cruzar Rohan a pie, así que decides no decir nada.

'First, let us go and look upon the ranks of soldiers by the gate. There have never been so many out and at the ready, as far as I can recall. And I am no small boy.
'I am ten years old, and soon shall be five feet tall!'

'Why, were I the Enemy I would throw down my weapons and despair!
'What are those soldiers, over there? We should see.'

'There they are! If only the sun were shining, how fine their gleaming arms and armour would be.
'Look, there are others, over there. Let us get a look at those ones, too!'

The Knight gives the slightest of nods to you, and then addresses Bergil.
'It pains me that even in this dark hour, we cannot count on each other for common kindness. Yet it is ever so.
'Young man, know that had he raised his arm to you, I would have intervened. I saw clearly that this ${RACE}, your companion, was one breath from doing the same.
'But someone elder and stronger than you cannot be always by your side. I therefore council you to look before you step, and to learn to judge the character of men before they are within striking range. Look into their eyes. You will learn to know. See that one there, who so discourteously spoke to you? An unhappy storm is writ upon his face.
'You may grow to be strong and maybe even take the trappings of a knight in your time. But a cautious step and keen judgement will guard you from blows that no armour ever can.'

'A cautious step and what was it, clear judgement? I must commit those words, for they seem good ones to live by.
'Fa! I am shaking a bit from that mean fellow, though I do not like to admit it. Let us look elsewhere, on something more pleasant.
'See the horses over there? Shall we feed them some apples?'

'I bid you heed Oryat's words. If this boy or any other children venture into the Second Circle, he will do them harm.'
'That man would not truly do harm to me, would he?'
'Second Circle between the tavern and the Feasting Hall, O Champion of Brats. We can settle this there.'

'What fun we've had, strolling about, ${PLAYER}! I will not let that last grim turn spoil my enjoyment of the day, and I hope you won't either.
'Still, it will be hard not going to any Upper Circles. I owe it to the others to find some way out of this - or around it - if I can.'

'Got a spine then after all, have we? I reckoned there was a chance you might - so I made sure I had some friends at hand.
'Ha ha! Why should I chance a wound for the sorry likes of you!'

'You showed bravery just now, both of you. Sometimes we rush into a fight that might be averted. Other times we do what must be done, even though the consequences of our acts bring us no good fortune. You must ask yourself which you have chosen. But regardless of what lesson you draw, you will live with the result.
'You have won yourself freedom in the First Circle, but neither you nor any of the other children should venture up here anymore. Oryat will surely do you harm. I read that plainly in his eyes.'

'Not venture into the Second Circle? I suppose we dare not, lest Oryat find us. Oh, ${PLAYER}! What have we done? Somehow I felt for sure that if only you bested Oryat, he would never trouble us anymore.
'We had better not stay. I shall go back to the Old Guest-house now. I must think and talk with the other children.
'Will you meet me there?'
'A cautious step and keen judgement. Remember that!'
'They brought out new apple crates just this morning. Let us feed the horses!'
'Isn't it funny how their lips brush against your hand?'

'No doubt you saw, when we met, that I am not the only youth in Minas Tirith. Mind you, most left with the wains some days past. But a dozen of us remained for this reason and that.
'It is for them, as well as I myself, I wish to ask Himnir for some treats.'
'The Wrights' Market! I wouldn't mind poking my nose in there, anyway. This Amonel, she must be awfully clever with her hands. Tinkers are, you know!'
'Bring that broken whisk to Amonel, around or about the Wrights' Market, and I'll send treats for all your friends.'
'Run along. This will take a moment... or two. I haven't decided yet how the whisk could be fixed.'
'A tour of the city walls is just the thing. I wish to see everything I can up there!'
'Come! Come! You must see the ranks of soldiers. They are a sight to see!'

'She speaks nearly as well as the swan-knight, ${PLAYER}. Some things must be faced bravely...
'Do you know what I think? I think that you must face that swaggering soldier, Oryat! Surely you are a match for him. Surely you can cow him and make him relent.
'Please, ${PLAYER}. He will not leave us children alone until someone stops him. Oh, and how I would love to see you stand him on his head!'
'There are others over there!'
'Those soldiers, there. Let us get closer to them.'
'Run along. This will take a moment... or two. I haven't decided yet how the whisk could be fixed.'
'You - you talk to him, ${PLAYER}.'
'Second Circle between the tavern and the Feasting Hall, O Champion of Brats. We can settle this there.'
'Yes, let us go. Amonel will have mended the whisk, and Himnir will give all the children treats!'
'Run along, you two. I will go see Himnir myself, shortly, and tell him the ill news of his broken whisk.'
'Please, ${PLAYER}. Oryat will never leave us children be, if you do not face him. And how I long to see that sneer wiped from his face!'
'By the kings of old! You showed Oryat a thing or two!'
'I bid you heed Oryat's words. If this boy or any other children venture into the Second Circle, he will do them harm.'

'It's not only horses who enjoy a treat now and then. With you along, I might be allowed in the Foodmongers' Market. There is a 'monger there, Himnir he is called, who likes me well enough and might give me something to eat.'
Bergil's face grows serious and seems to think a moment.
'What that knight said about kindness was also very fine. Perhaps if I ask the right way, Himnir will send food to all the children.
'Yes, let us go find him!'

A thought seems to suddenly strike Bergil.
'Say, when did you get here, ${PLAYER}? Were you upon the Pelennor when Lord Faramir came back to us? How I should like to have seen that! I went to the gates with Pippin - that's the prince of the halflings I spoke of - when all the men arrived from Belfalas and Lossarnach and elsewhere. That was a sight to see. But they only rode in on their horses. That is fine, but it is nothing to a fight!
'How would you like to go up upon the walls and see what we can? I hear the Enemy is within the Rammas Echor now and would like dreadfully to see how that is. I can hardly imagine it!'

Himnir smiles indulgently at Bergil.
'Sweets not just for you, but also for the other children? Well, that is a bold thing to ask! Others would pay good coin for such a parcel of my goods. Ah, but who am I fooling? Like as not, I would have given it to you freely.
'Today, however, I have an errand you may run to earn your treat. This whisk I use to whip up cream for my pastries has come apart, and it is my favourite whisk!
'I ask you to bring it to Amonel, a tinker in the Wrights' Market, and beg her to set it right. In return, I'll have a bounty of sweets sent over for the whole lot of you.'

'Well, this is an odd pairing!'
The tinker eyes you and Bergil.
'So, old Himnir's favourite whisk finally failed him. Go lightly with it, I told him! Ah, well. Let me have a look and see what I can do.
'You come back in a while and with any luck, I'll have it fixed.'
'Let us go, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps Amonel has finished mending that whisk.'

Amonel greets you and Bergil with a low sigh.
'The whisk is not mended. Nor shall it be, for it is beyond repair. Himnir should not go so hard on so delicate a tool and I have told him so...
'Nor will I send you to bear this ill tiding for me. Some things must be faced bravely. A knight cannot send someone in his stead to face the foe, nor can he shirk his duty and let innocents come to harm.
'Go now. Somehow I think Himnir will send some sweets to your friends all the same.'

'And just what are you then, the champion of orphans and wretches? What gives you the right to stand between me, a soldier of Gondor, and that impudent, sniveling, little...'
He makes as if to go past you, then sees the dangerous look in your eye.
'Oho, is that how it is? You'd strike at me, would you, just to spare this urchin a bit of a thrashing? Just you try it. I'm a soldier trained and hardened, and I'll strike back. I'll strike whatever cheeky boy or foreigner I choose, to let them know their place.
'Now skulk away - or if you've any spine, meet me up in the Second Circle later, between the Feasting Hall and the tavern, and we'll see who strikes who, when it comes to it.'

'Greetings! I am friend to the prince of the halflings. Have you ever seen a halfling? I'll wager you haven't.'
When you tell him that you in fact have, he seems crestfallen. A moment later, his face lights up again.
'All the same, you are a stranger in the city. Will you walk with me? I'll show you things to see. And we can go places I would be shooed away from, were I alone!
'Here, take this whistle. If we somehow get separated, you sound it and I'll come running.'

'Crinloca es increíblemente quisquilloso para comer. ¡Le hace ascos a casi cualquier cosa! Si encuentras algo en Harwick que quiera comer, te lo daré gratis. Si no, tendré que negarme. Estoy seguro de que lo entiendes. ¡Encuentra algo que acepte y será completamente tuyo!'
'Bueno, ¿qué piensas?'
'¡Míralo, ${PLAYER}! No da miedo para nada. De hecho, ¡es bastante pequeñito!'

'¡Este poney no da miedo en absoluto! Parece de muy buen carácter, y me atrevería a decir que podría acercarme a él sin temer que me muerda. Es bastante del tamaño de un hobbit, si me preguntas a mí, ¡y creo que ese es el tamaño justo!
'¿Se llama Crinloca? ¡Le queda muy bien! Me pregunto cuántas monedas pedirá Cuthbald para separarse de él.'
'¡Creo que le caes bien, Bingo!'

'¡Me alegra que a Bingo le guste! Para ser sincero, no he tenido mucho éxito encontrando un dueño para Crinloca, así que me alegrará dejar que Bingo lo tenga gratis. Sin embargo, tengo una condición.
'Crinloca es increíblemente quisquilloso para comer. ¡Le hace ascos a casi todo! Si encuentras algo de comida en Harwick que él quiera comer, te lo daré sin costo. De lo contrario, tendré que negarme. Lo entiendes, ¿verdad? Encuentra algo en Harwick que pueda comer, ¡y será completamente tuyo!'
'¡Ya lo quiero! ¡Qué gran poney es!'

'¡No puedo hacerlo, ${PLAYER}, lo siento! ¡Estas enormes bestias me dan demasiado miedo como para siquiera pensar en montarlas! Y si lo hiciera, ¿cuánto tardaría en caerme de la silla? ¡Qué caída sería esa! ¡Demasiado para este hobbit, te lo digo de verdad!
'¡No montaré ninguno de estos caballos! Dale a Cuthbald mis saludos y mis disculpas, pero hoy no habrá ninguna venta. ¡Ni hoy ni ningún día! ¡Al menos, no para este hobbit!
'¿Entonces? ¿Qué te parecen estos magníficos corceles? ¿Criaturas nobles, verdad?'

'Esto no servirá. Si tu amigo piensa recorrer el reino, necesitará un caballo. ¡No permitiré que los dos salgan de Harwick sin una montura adecuada para Bingo! Si los dejo partir sin preparación, dañaría mi reputación como el mejor mercader de caballos de esta parte de El Páramo —esto es, toda la zona cercana a Harwick, pero no tan al norte como Largafortín ni tan al sur como Santuario de Eorl. ¡Dentro de esos límites soy el mejor, y seguiré siéndolo!
'¿Sabes qué? Creo que puedo tener una última oportunidad de darle a tu amigo lo que necesita. Encuéntrame en el lado oeste de Harwick, cerca de la Sala de Artesanía, y veré qué puedo hacer.'
'No montaré ninguna de estas bestias. Lo siento, ¡pero simplemente no lo haré!'

'No suelo quedarme con ponies, pero este llegó a mis manos después de una incursión de orcos, y aún no he encontrado dueño para él.
'¿Qué te parece? Su nombre es Crinloca, pero puedes llamarlo como quieras. No estaba seguro de qué hacer con él.'
'¡Mira a este amiguito! ¡No da miedo para nada!'
'¿Me pregunto qué comida querrá comer Crinloca? ¡Tenemos que encontrar algo!'

'¡Nunca había visto a este poney devorar algo tan rápido como devoró esa manzana! Parece que has encontrado su comida favorita, ¡y también parece que Bingo ha encontrado un noble corcel que lo llevará por todo Rohan!
'Ha sido un placer hacer negocios con ustedes dos, y si pueden recomendarme ante cualquiera que busque caballos, ¡se los agradeceré!'

'¡Estoy encantado de haber conocido a Crinloca! Él debe ser, sin duda, el Bingo Boffin del mundo de los ponies, ${PLAYER}: pequeño, amistoso y un comensal quisquilloso.
'A él le gustan las manzanas, lo cual es perfecto, porque yo no las soporto, como creo que ya te he dicho antes. ¡Puede tener todas las manzanas de la Tierra Media si quiere! Seremos un gran equipo, ya lo puedo ver. ¡No codiciaremos las cenas del otro!'
<rgb=#FF0000>La semana que viene: 'El Rastreador' (Nivel recomendado: 82)</rgb>

'Siempre es un placer concretar una venta, incluso cuando no hay monedas de por medio. Crinloca era un poco molesto para alimentar, así que me están haciendo un favor. Y, por supuesto, tu amigo necesitaba una montura también. Todos ganamos, ${PLAYER}.'

'¡Cuidado con tus manos cerca de ellos! Podrían darte un mordisco si no prestas atención. Son todos unos príncipes, no de los Mearas, claro está, pero sí muy cercanos a esa noble estirpe.
'Siéntete libre de examinar estos nobles corceles y hazme saber cuál te gusta.'
Bingo luce una enorme sonrisa. Este no parece darle miedo.
Crinloca come una manzana con entusiasmo. ¡Has encontrado su comida favorita!

'Ahora que estamos aquí, supongo que necesitaré un caballo. ¡El reino de Rohan es grande, y mis piernas son cortas, al fin y al cabo! Hará el viaje más fácil... siempre que ninguno de los caballos que veamos intente morderme con sus dientes terribles o pisotearme con sus pezuñas espantosas. ¡Te haré personalmente responsable si lo hacen, ${PLAYER}!
'La gente dice que hay un mercader de caballos llamado Cuthbald en el lado este de Harwick. Podemos ir a verlo, si es que es necesario.'

'Ay, cielos. ¡Espero que estas criaturas no se acerquen más! Parecen bastante feroces, ¡y podrían dar un bocado a este pobre hobbit sin pensárselo dos veces! Sería poco más que un bocado para ellos, ¡pero este bocado preferiría no ser almuerzo, si no te importa!
'¿Tienes la seguridad de que necesito un caballo para esta aventura?'

'Ah, ¿vienes a comprar un buen caballo para este compañero? Tengo varios que podrían servir; cada uno es fogoso de temperamento y galopará por los campos a una velocidad que nunca has visto.
'¡Cuidado con tus manos! Podrían darte un mordisco si no prestas atención. Todos ellos son príncipes, no de los Mearas, por supuesto, pero sí muy cercanos a esa noble estirpe.
'Siéntete libre de examinar estos nobles corceles y dime cuál te agrada más.'
'Ay, no sé sobre esto. ¡No sé sobre esto en absoluto!'
'Ay, no sé sobre esto.'
¿Sí o no?
Cuthbald está en el lado oeste de Harwick, cerca de la Sala de Artesanía.

Cuthbald está en el lado oeste de Harwick, cerca de la Sala de Artesanía.
Has encontrado la comida favorita de Crinloca, y ahora Cuthbald estará encantado de darle el poney a Bingo.
Bingo se encuentra en el lado oeste del pueblo de Harwick, cerca de la sala de artesanía.

Cuthbald te ha pedido reunirte con él en el lado oeste de Harwick, cerca de la Sala de Artesanía.
Cuthbald cree que puede tener una oportunidad más de encontrar una montura adecuada para que Bingo recorra Rohan.
Cuthbald te ha mostrado un poney en el lado oeste de Harwick, y debes decidir si sería una buena montura para Bingo.

Cuthbald te ha desafiado a buscar en Harwick comida que el quisquilloso Crinloca quiera comer.
