'The only hope of victory lies with Frodo, but we still have a part to play in this great struggle, ${PLAYER}. I asked Daervunn to prepare the men for departure, for I believed it might take longer than expected for the Host of the West to set out upon this last march. Heavy are the feet that dread the approaching road, but still they must step one before the other!
'Look for Daervunn where the northward road departs from the camp, my friend, and ask him if the men are ready to leave.'

'This road will take us across the blasted plains of Dagorlad, to the very gate of Mordor. The men stir with restlessness, but they will obey their liege, whether he be Éomer or Aragorn. Others there are, too, who have joined this host in cause of allied friendship; if they have not turned back now, I believe they will never abandon us.
'I have shared words with Peregrin Took here, and he too has a courage about him.'

'This is the road to Mordor? No one could mistake it for anything else, ${PLAYER}! It looks as I would have expected it to look, had I ever wanted to fill my heart with fright and my mind with unease at the considering... and I did not!
'Daervunn has had some kind words to say concerning my \qcourage,\q and I did not want to offend him by disagreeing, but I think he sees what is not there. If I were truly brave, would I feel so frightened at the prospect of taking this road? Certainly not! But Aragorn believes that we have to do this, and I have smarts enough to know he is more wise than I am. If he says there is no other way, this hobbit will not gainsay him. This is the road we must take!'

Calenglad is lost in his thoughts.
Aragorn is lost in his thoughts.
'None of us are free of worry, ${PLAYER}, or free of regret. But still we move forward in spite of those feelings. That is all we can do. That is what we must do.'

'Some of my kinsmen are deep in thought, contemplating the roads that have led them here, while they ready themselves for the road to come. Will you speak with some of them and put into words how grateful I am for all they have done? This is likely to be our last battle, and I want them to know that I appreciate their service not only as their captain or their king, but also as their friend and kinsman. This may be my last chance to tell them so, and I do not want to miss that opportunity.'

'I watched the departure of the Faint-hearted, ${PLAYER}, and I felt no scorn for them, though there was a time in my life when I might not have understood their choice. I see that their path too was in service of the Host of the West. Our own road takes us to Mordor, for we have the courage to go that way.
'I am not afraid of Mordor or its Black Gate. Neither am I afraid of the Dark Lord or his armies. I am not afraid of Mordirith, no matter what he names himself. I am not afraid of death, for I have lived a life enriched by friendship and laughter, and I know that endings must always come, soon or late.
'I am made strong by the love of my friends and the memories I carry with me, and no Orc or wraith or beast can conquer that strength. At long last I am at peace, ${PLAYER}. I will follow Aragorn to the end, with an unburdened heart.'

'Have you ever broken a promise, ${PLAYER}?'
Calenglad looks at you sadly, and holds up a finger to halt your reply.
'I have sought to live my life with honour, making good upon my promises and the oaths I have taken. I swore an oath to aid Aragorn my chief in all things, and I have done so as best I could. That oath has taken me far from my home and to the very doorstep of Mordor.
'But my heart remains on the shores of Lake Nenuial. I promised to return when my duty in the south-lands was done, but... it does not seem that any of us will return, after all. What were the words of Gwindeth? That the return of Elendil's kingdom would be worth some measure of sorrow? Did she speak the truth? I do not know, even now.'

'We have been through a lot together, ${PLAYER}, and most of it was unpleasant. I am not complaining, not really. If it was to be easy, it need not have been the Dúnedain's task to face it! I said as much to Elweleth once, but she has gone away, and will never return.
'Do you think that the folk of Middle-earth will appreciate everything Aragorn has done? I do not expect our names to be remembered, but if there is any justice, Aragorn will be remembered fondly and well by the people of Gondor and Rohan, at least.'
Radanir is silent for a long while, and you are about to leave him be when he speaks at last.
'It seems there will be no peaceful tavern for us at the end of this road, ${PLAYER}. After everything we have gone through, I suppose I am not really surprised.'

Aragorn wanted you to express to some of his kinsmen how grateful he is for the sacrifices they have made, and will make, in his service.

'It is our misfortune that we must march to the Black Gate with little hope of our own survival, ${PLAYER}. So many good men have placed their lives in my hands, trusting that this course is important. I believe that it is, but it does not make the burden of that choice any lighter.
'Some of my kinsmen are deep in thought, contemplating the roads that have led them here, while they ready themselves for the road to come. Will you speak with some of them and put into words how grateful I am for all they have done? This is likely to be our last battle, and I want them to know that I appreciate their service not only as their captain or their king, but also as their friend and kinsman. This may be my last chance to tell them so, and I do not want to miss that opportunity.'

'Once I spoke to you of my travels, ${PLAYER}, of my adventures in the wooded lands of Enedwaith and the rocky heights of Thrór's Coomb, but they are dwarfed now by the memory of these last few weeks. From the dungeons of Isengard to the fighting on the Pelennor, our journey has been full of hardship.
'My mind turns now to my home, at Sûri-kylä in Forochel. I do not think I will see it again, but I am at ease knowing that I have done what I can for the Snowmen, and they will persevere as they always have done.
'I will follow Aragorn wherever he leads.'
Book 8, Chapter 2: Last Chances

'What did you see from atop the slag-hill?'
Aragorn listens to your account.
'All was quiet and still? I see, and I am not surprised. Sauron is waiting. I do not take the empty calm before the Gate to be fact, and neither should you. The Dark Lord's armies are arrayed before us, though we see them not. He waits to unleash them, for he wants to see what we will do.'
'Good luck, ${PLAYER}! Good luck to all of us!'

'This is a dead place, an empty place. I do not like it. There will be many places such as these as we get nearer to Mordor, ${PLAYER}. How could anyone live here?
'The answer to that question is a simple one, I suppose: no one does live here, not truly. Not good folk, at any rate.
'I have heard tell from the Rangers of Ithilien that there are a few sites throughout the Wastes in which evil folk dwell. These places should be scouted before the Host passes near. Find Dûm Boha in the Noman-lands, and Dol Acharn and Ondoher's Folly in Dagorlad, and defeat any enemies that may endanger the passage of the Host. Once the way is safe, the Host of the West will assemble outside the Black Gate and we will see what awaits us there.'

'Stand fast, men! They seek to cow us with their numbers, but each of us is worth a dozen of their mindless thralls!
'My limbs are heavy and my breath is short, ${PLAYER}, but I will do what I can to support Aragorn and my kinsmen.
'Fight on! Fight on!'

'I see that you have already slain your share of Orcs, ${PLAYER}! Legolas has also cut an impressive swath, but he tells me his supply of arrows will not last long. Perhaps you can help him with this?
'The battle has only just begun, but there is no need to worry about our respective tallies this time. There will be plenty of foes for all of us!'

'I have enough arrows for the moment, but Gimli is right: my supply will run low soon if the tide of enemies does not slow!
'Many archers of Gondor and Rohan have already fallen to the arrows of Mordor; some of their quivers remain full, or nearly so. Go to the archery lines and look for our fallen unfortunates. If you return to me with a number of their full quivers I will be able to maintain my current pace, and continue to support Gimli with my bow.
'I thank you for undertaking this helpful task, grim though it may seem!'

'Thank you, my friend. Set the quivers at my feet and I will use them as the need arises.'

'I heard Aragorn shouting his commands from the top of the slag hill to the south-west, ${PLAYER}. Climb the hill and see if you can aid him!'

'We have held the line of battle for now, keeping our foes from ascending the eastern hill, but it seems that our foes have redoubled their efforts to take the western hill.
'We are hard-pressed and can spare no man, but someone must go to the western hill and keep it from being taken! Can you go to the aid of Imrahil with haste enough, ${PLAYER}? I know you can! Fight your way to the slope of the western hill, and help the Prince of Dol Amroth throw back the tide!'
'${PLAYER}! The fighting here goes poorly, but with you here my spirits are lifted!'

'Is this to be the last battle, ${PLAYER}? My heart tells me this is so, and though it be a sorrowful thing I will be glad to see the end of war-time, and to have rest.
'A palpable hit, and another! I find no joy in battle, my friend, but I find that I am uncommonly good at it, truly! I will use that skill to defend the men at my side, until my last breath is stolen away by some lucky stroke!
'Fight onward, ${PLAYER}! Make our foes pay for the evils they have done, and hope still to do!'

'How goes the fighting on the western hill, ${PLAYER}? I trust that Éomer and Imrahil stand still against the forces of Mordor?'
You tell Aragorn that they are still defiant, but injuries have begun to mount among their soldiers.

'All those quivers you brought me are spent, ${PLAYER}! There is knife-work to be done all around the hill, and plenty for all!
'I have this fight in hand, but I am certain there will be enough foes for you to slay if you go a-looking for them, or wait for them to seek you out!'

'I am glad the flow of the battle has brought you to me, ${PLAYER}. I wanted to speak with you again.'
You study the Ranger's face and see little of the doubt that troubled him at the Camp of the Host. He seems curiously calm for one who stands amid such tumult.
'After battle was joined, I stood with Aragorn and felled Orc after Orc; soon I lost count of the bodies, but there were ever more to replace them. With each swing of my blade, my sword lost its individuality. It was no longer my weapon only, but it was the weapon of every Dúnadan that ever took up sword for his king.
'With every swing, it seemed to me I was conducting a great music, and the tides of battle moved through and around me in a great swelling chorus. It was a drowning tide, and it swept the foes of Men beneath it, cleansing the land of their foul mark.
'I saw the great beauty of the land returning in full measure, the deep forests growing anew and the rivers flowing swift and clean. I saw twilight pooling in the hills, and the stars reflected in mountain lakes, crisp and cool.
'My eyes were opened to this vision of a new age, and though I saw it only for the span of a breath, I knew in that moment that Gwindeth had been right: such a kingdom would be worth some measure of sorrow. She will see it, though she fade into myth, and men question whether she ever existed at all. But still she will be there, among the falls and waters of Lake Nenuial, and she will remember.
'I am at peace, my friend. The evil of Sauron cannot last, even if every last one of us perishes before his gates. But let us hope we do not, ${PLAYER}! A new age is coming!'

'Help! Can you help me? I have slain a number of Orcs, but the last one staggered away with my sword still stuck in its gut, and now I have no weapon!
'Can you find me a sword? There must be a blade somewhere at the base of the hill, abandoned or dropped by a coward or by a corpse! Without a weapon I cannot do any good for Gondor, and I have no way to protect myself from the throng!'

'We are being overwhelmed, ${PLAYER}. I sustained an injury from an Orc's lucky swing, and now my arm hangs loosely; I cannot lift up my shield. My men have fallen back a short distance, but they cannot stand long against the tide. They will soon need to retreat once more.
'I ask that you fight across to the eastern slag hill once again; if the battle is turning against us here, it must also be going ill with Aragorn. Look for his friends, the Elf and the dwarf. I saw them from afar, but could not tell how they fared.
'They will need you as the battle goes on.'
'Help! Will no one help me? Alas for my injuries!'

'Be careful, ${PLAYER}! This beastly brood is out for blood!'

'The tide of enemies has swelled, and soon it will crash upon the shore of our shield wall; the tide will not draw back again until we are slain.

'If what you relate is true, why then an entire army hides in wait below the ground! We know full well that overwhelming odds stand locked behind the Morannon. But we shall not face those until the ordained time of battle, according to Lord Aragorn's plan.

'I tell you, ${PLAYER}, I have wondered whether I were going mad. I would track an Orc Captain climbing the nearby eastern hills, only to lose track of him. Then, as if by some sorcery, I would espy him far west, where I should surely have seen him pass.
'The riddle has evaded me until now. The maggot-holes must communicate in tunnels deep beneath these midden-heaps, and access fundaments beneath the Towers of the Teeth, as well. It is the only answer!
'Will you investigate? Find a way into Carchost and discover what pathways lie below.
'Ah, but I forget myself. You should speak with Candúr before you go.'

'¿Tesoro? ¡Ja, ja! Sí, ya veo, ahora llegamos al fondo de esta tonta idea.
'Te lo digo una vez más: Mordor no es lugar para hobbits. Hay cosas en ese camino más allá de lo que cualquiera de ustedes haya imaginado o encontrado. En verdad, debería pensar que ya han tenido suficientes aventuras para tres vidas de hobbits juntas, ustedes dos.'

'¿Más de lo que hemos imaginado o encontrado dices? Y sin embargo, hemos encontrado bastante entre la Comarca y aquí. No solo Moria y los Campos del Pelennor, que supongo recuerdas algo, sino mucho más entre medias cuando no estabas para cuidarnos. Digo que somos capaces de más de lo que imaginas, muchas gracias.'
'El viejo Bilbo volvió a casa con un montón de tesoros, ¿sabes? Estoy seguro de que esperarán que hagamos lo mismo.'

'Realmente, Gandalf, no veo por qué no se nos debería permitir ir. Muchos otros han ido, incluidos Sam y Frodo. Bueno, lo admito, no son los mejores ejemplos.
'Pero no estamos proponiendo marchar directamente por la ladera del Monte del Destino. Solo deseamos dar unos breves paseos por el lugar, para poder decir que lo vimos con nuestros propios ojos, tal vez encontrar un poco de tesoro para llevar a casa con nosotros...'

'Además, no olvides que Merry y yo nos hemos perdido parte de la emoción que todos los demás pudieron vivir, a causa de esos orcos secuestradores y de los golpes en la cabeza y de los severos curanderos gondorianos.'

'¡Mi querido Gandalf! Mis palabras superan mis pensamientos en este frenesí y me avergüenzo de ellas. Por favor, perdona a este pobre Hobbit.
'Pero de todos modos, hemos hecho tanto. No nos tomes por ingenuos que acaban de salir de la Comarca.'

'Bueno, no se queden ahí parados. ¡Vamos a comer!'
'Todo este correteo y búsqueda me ha dejado con un hambre tremenda.'

'¡Qué lugar tan extraordinario ha encontrado Gandalf para nosotros! ¡Es increíble pensar que es nuestro! ¿Puedes imaginar cómo se verá después de que los gondorianos lo hayan arreglado? Debería hablar con ellos y asegurarme de que algunas de nuestras cosas se coloquen en algunas de las habitaciones y que las cocinas, en particular, se restauren, si es posible.
'¡Vaya, pero escúchame! Una comida, buena compañía y algo que hacer y en qué pensar es bienvenido en este extraño tiempo libre después de nuestra victoria. Pero espero que el viejo Gandalf no piense que nos ha engañado para olvidar Mordor. Todavía nos gustaría mucho ir.'
'Bueno, supongo que deberíamos echar un vistazo para ver qué podemos ver, ¿no es así?'

'¿Es esto lo que la gente grande considera un hogar común por aquí? Es más grande que cualquier casa que hayamos visto en Breeland, y me atrevo a decir que toda la Comarca cabría en este salón principal!'

'Este lugar, Bâr Thorenion, les pertenece por decreto real del reino de Gondor. Tal vez piensen que esto es una broma de nuestro viejo amigo Aragorn, pero en verdad fueron los soldados y los montaraces de Ithilien quienes le pidieron que así fuera.
'Confieso que los he traído aquí prematuramente. No sé cuántos hombres estarán aquí mañana para hacer el lugar un poco más habitable. Sin embargo, pensé que les gustaría verlo antes, para que pudieran hacer sus propios planes.
'Servirá como una excelente residencia, de hecho, para el tiempo que pasen aquí en Gondor antes de regresar a la Comarca. Y, con un poco de suerte, los mantendrá fuera de problemas y lejos de algunas de sus ideas más tontas, al menos por unos días, si tenemos suerte.
'Bueno, vamos entonces. ¡Entremos!'

'No sé si se han dado cuenta, pero tenemos todo lo necesario para organizar una comida improvisada, comenzando con esta vieja mesa que alguien dejó aquí.
'Sé que me vendría bien un bocado de comida. ¿Y ustedes dos?
'Hay cajas de comida y algunas botellas de vino viejo con los sellos intactos. Un poco de luz, un poco de paja para sentarse y algunos platos ayudarán. Si reúnen esos elementos, ${PLAYER}, Merry y yo nos encargaremos de las copas, los cuchillos y cualquier otra cosa que podamos conseguir.'
Queda poco de los hornos o la cocina, pero estas debieron ser impresionantes en el pasado.

'Nosotros hemos hablado mucho sobre esto, Merry y yo, y hemos tomado una decisión... Pero antes de todo, me gustaría que miraras a tu alrededor. Que vieras el trabajo realizado por toda esta Gente Grande. Es difícil creer que la última vez que vinimos aquí solo había ruinas. Todo ha cambiado tanto. Gandalf debía estar realmente desesperado para desviarnos del camino hacia Mordor si sintió la necesidad de traernos aquí antes de que comenzaran los trabajos.
'¡Ah, qué tonto soy! Pero Mordor es exactamente la razón por la que queríamos hablar contigo. No hemos abandonado la idea de ir allí, solo... bueno... esperábamos que pudieras pedirle a Éomer y Aragorn en nuestro nombre. Verás, tenemos algunas cosas que atender aquí antes de partir. Y si me preguntas, Merry no podría soportar ver la expresión decepcionada en el rostro de Éomer si desaprobara la idea.
'¿Lo harás? Ambos han estado ocupados con sus asuntos reales cerca de las Puertas Negras. Los encontrarás justo afuera, en las Colinas de Escoria, me imagino.'

'Hablemos un poco, ${PLAYER}. Sé que no he hecho mucho para impedir que Merry y Pippin se aventuren en Mordor. Sin embargo, espero haberles dado algo de seriedad al asunto. Más importante aún, les pido que se queden con ellos.
'En este punto, les pido un favor. Llévenlos a Udûn cuando vayan, y estén atentos a cosas que no deberían estar allí. Tengo razones para creer que podrían encontrar algo de interés para ustedes y para nuestros dos amigos entrometidos.'

'Con Pippin acabábamos de disfrutar del paisaje, preguntándonos si alguna vez llegarías. Supongo que deberíamos empezar a bajar por allí. Bueno, no hay razón para holgazanear ahora. ¡Vamos!
'¿Qué te parece si nos dirigimos al primer cruce de caminos en el valle? Desde aquí apenas se puede ver.'

'Deambular por el reino del Señor Oscuro está muy bien, aunque no entiendo por qué todavía no nos hemos topado con una cueva de trolls llena de espadas élficas. Pero no puedo seguir así con el estómago rugiendo, cuando tantas buenas provisiones pesan en mi mochila.
'Dijiste que querías ir hacia el norte, Merry. ¿Por qué no vamos por allí y nos detenemos en ese terreno llano? No parece que nadie nos vaya a molestar, y podremos reponer fuerzas antes de continuar.'

Merry se ve inusualmente pálido.
'He perdido el apetito por la comida, la aventura y cualquier promesa de tesoro u oro, Pippin. Mejor demos por terminado el día y regresemos, ¿no crees?'
'¡Ah, ahí estás, ${PLAYER}! Te estábamos buscando. ¡Qué suerte que estés aquí ahora!'

'¿Meter la nariz en Mordor? Me imagino que eso es exactamente lo que dirían. Bueno, para ser honesto, no me gusta la idea de que esos dos vayan solos. Pero si prometes estar cerca y cuidarlos, entonces tienen mi bendición.
'A Pippin le concedo permiso.'
'¿El maestro Merry desea ver Mordor? No se lo negaría, por todo lo que ha hecho y vivido.'

'¿Dijeron que sí? ¡Ah, como lo esperaba! Pippin y yo ya hemos preparado nuestras cosas. Con la ayuda de todos estos amables de la Gente Grande, tenemos provisiones de sobra.
'Reunámonos en... ¿Cómo se llama eso...? ¿El fuerte de Udûn?'

'Ve por delante, ${PLAYER}. Si realmente escuché algo, está justo en el camino. Pippin y yo iremos justo detrás de ti.'
'¡Chist, los dos! ¡Quiero escuchar más!'
'¿Mago? ¿Tierras de los hobbits? Y esa voz. Hubiera jurado que era uno de los amigos de Bill Helechal, venido hasta Mordor.'

'¿Tú también oíste eso? No estoy muy seguro, pero me pareció escuchar algo... algo parecido a una voz, que venía de más arriba.
'Rápido y en silencio, amigos, vamos a ver qué fue - si es que fue algo.'
'¿Entonces nuestro pequeño plan ha avanzado? Sabía que podíamos contar contigo, ${PLAYER}.'
'Imagina cómo debió de verse con todos los ejércitos del Señor Oscuro reunidos allí.'
'Hasta el primer cruce de caminos, y luego veremos qué encontramos y decidiremos qué hacer a partir de ahí.'
'¿Cuál crees que encontraremos primero, aventura o tesoro?'
'No hay señales de tesoros ni de aventuras por aquí, pero supongo que apenas estamos empezando. Si me preguntas, deberíamos ir hacia las tiendas de los soldados que están allí.'
'Piénsalo, ${PLAYER}. Estamos al otro lado. En el portón del enemigo, por así decirlo, aunque me alegro mucho de que no esté en casa, ¡ni lo estará!'
'Todas estas tiendas vacías me recuerdan lo horribles que son la guerra y los conflictos. Tal vez deberíamos ir a ver las forjas. Sigamos un poco más y busquemos un camino que vaya hacia el norte.'
'Bueno, no me imaginaba que fuera tan ruidoso - ¡ni tan apestoso!'
'Bueno, ¿qué pasa, Pippin?'

'Digo que nos sentemos en ese terreno plano que vi, justo al norte del camino principal y detrás de algunas tiendas. Sería el lugar perfecto para comer algo y recuperar nuestras cansadas extremidades.'
'¡Bien! Puedes imaginarte lo difícil que ha sido para Pippin y para mí. Aun así, me preocupa que su cabeza se caiga de los hombros, ¡por lo rápido y a menudo que ha estado girando de un lado a otro!'

'¿Podrías pedirles permiso por nosotros? Iríamos nosotros mismos, pero de alguna manera sería mejor si lo hicieras tú. Aragorn y Éomer están probablemente justo fuera de las Puertas Negras, en las Colinas de Escoria.'

'Pippin está bromeando, por supuesto. No me da vergüenza pedirlo, pero a él sí. Oh, sólo hazle caso.
'Y antes de irte, asegúrate de ver los jardines y los baños. ¡Es más que notable, eso es lo que es!'
'Los dos Periain, Meriadoc y Peregrin, estuvieron aquí hace poco buscándote. Regresaron a Bâr Thorenion, pero te suplicaron que te unieras a ellos lo antes posible.'

'Cómo nos encantaría acompañarte y volver a ver a nuestros viejos amigos Bárbol y Ramaviva. Pero eso requeriría aún más permiso de nuestros señores, y además, los gondorianos nos necesitan mucho en este momento. ¡Sería completamente imposible!'
'Saruman aún no ha salido, pero lo hará en un rato, ¡hoo! ¿Por qué no buscas por aquí y ves qué puedes encontrar, y luego vuelves aquí?'

'¡Vaya, si no es ${PLAYER}! ¿Has estado en Isengard? ¿Y ya estás de vuelta? Debes contarnos todo lo que viste.'
Mientras lo cuentas, los ojos de los dos hobbits se abren de par en par.
'Viejo y astuto es Saruman', dice finalmente Pippin. 'Pero te diré lo que no me gusta: esa parte sobre ayudar a los Pueblos Libres. Algo en eso me pone los pelos de punta.
'Y luego está el asunto de esos barriles de hierba para pipa. Había muchos más que los dos que encontramos, en algún lugar, supongo. Fue muy inteligente de tu parte tomar nota de las fechas estampadas en ellos. Debemos pensar en eso, Merry. Ha pasado bastante tiempo entre el verano de hace dos años y el primero de este mismo marzo. ¿Qué estará tramando, crees?'
'Es bueno que estés aquí, justo cuando te hemos querido, como siempre, ${PLAYER}. Tenemos algunos asuntos graves que discutir.'

'Si recuerdas, los Ents se supone que lo vigilan en su torre, donde está prisionero de alguna manera. Tal vez veas a algunos de nuestros amigos Ents cuando estés allí. Si lo haces, envíales nuestros saludos y averigua cómo les va. A este ritmo, parece que pasará mucho tiempo antes de que podamos volver a verlos.'

'¡Hrum, brum, hroom! Después de todo, no has tenido una conversación tan cortés con el viejo Saruman, ¿verdad?'
Le cuentas a Bárbol lo que dijo Saruman y lo que juzgas que quiso decir con ello. Los ojos del viejo Ent se entristecen.
'Sí, hrm. Bueno, hm. Tal vez dejarlo ir ahora sería un poco precipitado, después de todo. A veces siento lástima por él, porque no me gusta encerrar a ninguna criatura de cualquier temperamento en piedra como está encerrado él. Y sin embargo nos has demostrado que no está roto y que aún podría intentar hacer mucho daño si fuera liberado.
'No, hm. No lo liberarás. Al menos no ahora.
'Me alegra que nos hayas visitado de todos modos, ${PLAYER}, y debes enviar mis saludos a los hobbits Pippin y Merry, y recordarles que siempre son bienvenidos en mis bosques!'

'¡Hm, hoom! Aquí está ${PLAYER} de nuevo. Es sorprendente que aparezcas justo cuando estábamos discutiendo todos los eventos que llevaron a esto.'
Bárbol indicó el desierto inundado a su alrededor.
'Y qué, realmente, se debe hacer con Saruman. Oh, sí, lo sé, hm, hm, Mithrandir nos pidió que lo mantuviéramos allí arriba. Y ahora que nos hemos asentado, no estamos de humor para ser apresurados, ¡hoom! Pero aún así la pregunta sigue siendo, ¿por cuánto tiempo? ¿Y según el cálculo de quién? ¿Un ${RACE} como tú? Eso es un tiempo, supongo. Todo, incluso los Elfos', parece apresurado para nosotros los Ents, y por eso nos resulta extremadamente difícil juzgar. ¡Hm, hm! Y sin embargo, al mismo tiempo, no puedo evitar sentir que ha sido suficiente tiempo y que deberíamos liberarlo.
'Pero vamos, estoy siendo muy inhóspito. Dime, ¿qué te ha traído aquí hoy, hm?'
Le cuentas a Bárbol el enigma de lo que escuchaste en Mordor.
'¿Saruman? Podría muy bien ser Saruman, hoom hom! Se está escondiendo en algún lugar dentro de su roca en este momento, pero estará afuera en ese lugar alto muy pronto, creo. ¿Por qué no buscas algo más para explicar este pequeño misterio hasta que él salga, y luego veremos qué veremos.'

'Vaya, ¿no es nuestro pequeño amigo el ${RACE}? Me pregunto qué te ha traído de vuelta hasta aquí. Por lo que sé, tú y muchos otros habíais ido hacia el este, muy lejos, para ocuparse de asuntos que no tenían nada que ver con la tierra de los Ents.
'Quizá sea para entregar un mensaje a Bárbol. O para interrogar a ese mago. O... ¿ex-mago? No estoy muy seguro de qué es ahora, ni de cómo llamarlo. Bueno, como sea, los encontrarás a ambos más adelante, porque Bárbol y varios otros Ents se han reunido para vigilarlo. Solo han estado allí unos días, y podrían irse en unos cuantos más, así que tienes suerte de encontrarlos.'

'¡Vaya, el regreso de ${PLAYER}, y tan pronto! Hm, hm, pero tampoco demasiado tarde, creo, porque Saruman está en lo alto de su torre. Has venido hasta aquí. ¿Por qué no vas a ver qué tiene que decir? 'Mira lo que he encontrado. Allí, entre esas rocas. Huellas de botas, y son demasiado suaves y estrechas para ser pies de orco, según mi opinión.

'Si tienen un mínimo de decencia entre los tres, estarán de nuevo en lo alto de una roca, hablando lo suficientemente alto como para poder escucharlos y encontrarlos.'

'¡Bah! Sé que me voy a quedar aquí, no hay duda. Y vosotros también. ¿Habéis encontrado unos barriles en Isengard? Aún no habéis visto nada. Ja, ja.'
Se pone a toser con dolor durante varios momentos.
'Esto es solo el principio para vuestra preciosa Comarca. Este país está totalmente indefenso. Su conquista será un juego de niños.'

'Pobre muchacho. Supongo que nadie lo echará de menos, ni siquiera sus cobardes camaradas. No puedo decir que esté satisfecho, pero creo que hemos hecho todo lo que podíamos hoy. Es hora de regresar.'
'Esas - esas no eran respuestas. Eran acertijos. ¡Acertijos que volverían loco incluso al viejo Bilbo!'
'Merry tiene razón, por supuesto. Hemos terminado con Mordor por ahora. Quizás para siempre. ¡Vamos, antes de que ocurra algo más desagradable!'

Solo pensábamos en el cofre del tesoro con el que se decía que Bilbo había regresado, y en ver lo que aún no habíamos visto. Pero eso no es en absoluto lo que encontramos.'
Merry continúa describiendo los dos encuentros con los semi-orcos, los acertijos que dejaron caer y todo lo que siguió con la esperanza de desentrañarlos.
'Y así, ves Frodo, hemos tenido nuestra propia aventura, al final.'

'No, Pippin, hablo en serio. Esos argumentos ingeniosos podrían funcionar con Aragorn o Gandalf, que no ven las cosas exactamente a nuestro nivel, por así decirlo, pero soy yo con quien estás hablando. Creo que el tiempo de los hobbits yendo a Mordor debería terminar. De hecho, he estado pensando mucho en cómo el tiempo de nuestras aventuras está llegando a su fin.'

'Ah, ves en nuestros corazones, Frodo, como solo un hobbit y un viejo amigo podrían hacerlo. Bueno, entonces tienes mi palabra. ¿La tuya también, Merry? Bien. Ninguno de nosotros volverá a Mordor durante nuestra estancia en Gondor.
'Pero si el enigma de esos tipos entrecerrando los ojos me lleva a balbucear, ¡será tu responsabilidad!'

'No eran tan lujosos como dices, y además, menos de la mitad eran míos, realmente, sino solo los regalos que el Sr. Frodo rechazó. No ha aceptado ni un solo regalo, ¿verdad, aunque se le hayan presentado muchos en estos últimos días?

'¿Otra vez tú? Debería haberlo adivinado. No trajiste a tus dos pequeños amigos, ¿verdad? Demasiado peligroso, ¿eh? Bueno, no importa.'
El semi-Orco es sacudido por un doloroso ataque de tos.
'¿No vas a golpearme? Entonces solo has venido a burlarte de mí. A reírte de cómo no hay Ojo Rojo en esa torre derruida allá afuera. Nada que valga la pena vender y nadie que compre. Nada más que malicia *tos* *tos* y muerte e ilusiones en este lugar maldito. Tengo medio pensamiento de que tú mismo eres una ilusión. ¡Ptah!
'Supongo que te encantaría saber todo sobre tu preciosa *tos* *tos* - preciosa Comarca y el resto de esa podredumbre. El Mago tiene sus planes para ello, lo tiene, y ha estado entrando y saliendo de allí durante algunos años. Oh, no dejes que esa mirada agria arruine tu bonita cara. Él tiene muchos planes de mejoras, él y ese Lotho lo hacen. Incluso ahora hay una puerta en el Puente del Brandivino.
'¡Ah ha! Ja ja *tos* *tos* *tos*...ugh. Oh. Déjame, miserable ${RACE}. Déjame morir en paz.'

'Para empezar, ya no estarán en Udûn. He mirado los mapas, y estaban cerca de Dor Amarth cuando los encontramos. Si los desgraciados todavía piensan que hay alguien en Barad-dûr para comprar sus miserables noticias, entonces allí es donde han ido.
'Entonces, ahí es donde deberías comenzar tu búsqueda.'

'Me alegra que estés aquí, ${PLAYER}. Si quieres saber la verdad, estábamos hablando de ti.
'Verás, no podíamos dejar de pensar en esos dos tipos que huyeron, y lo que podrían saber, y cómo todavía están por ahí en Mordor. Y pensamos para nosotros mismos, hicimos una promesa a Frodo y no por todo el mundo la romperíamos. ¡Pero ${PLAYER} no hizo tal voto! Oh, pero ves a dónde va esto, ¿verdad? ¡Eres lo suficientemente inteligente para un ${RACE}, y no hay duda al respecto!
'Y de todos modos, hemos oído algunas de las aventuras que has tenido allí afuera, y sabemos que volverás allí afuera, de todos modos. Mientras estás allí, ¿por qué no rastrear a esos dos tipos? Oh, di que sí, ${PLAYER}, ¿no lo harás?
'Merry, tú dices la parte sobre dónde podrían estar.'

'Un momento, ${PLAYER}. Sé dónde has estado y adivino lo que has aprendido, porque yo mismo he conocido la verdad de ello durante un tiempo, aunque por medios algo diferentes.
'Por supuesto, no puedes ocultar la verdad a Pippin y Merry en un sentido amplio, pero permíteme aconsejarte que no necesitan escuchar cada detalle doloroso que has aprendido.
'Piensa por un momento en los muchos días de felicidad que les esperan, y el amargo desafío que les espera después del largo camino a casa. ¿Ese conocimiento previo trae algún bien? No creo que lo haga. Prepáralos para la dura verdad cuando puedan verla con sus propios ojos, porque eso es una bondad honesta, pero quizás, no más.
'Pesa mis palabras y actúa según tu propio juicio. Eso es todo lo que pido.'

'¡Ahí estás! Qué cara tan grave. Cuéntanos lo que has aprendido. Por favor, no puedo soportar la espera ni un momento más.'
Eligiendo tus palabras cuidadosamente, confirmas lo que los dos hobbits creían saber: que el Mago debía ser Saruman y que tenía planes para la Comarca. Sugieres más generalmente que la Comarca a la que regresan podría no ser exactamente la misma Comarca que dejaron, pero, con las palabras de Gandalf resonando en tus oídos, no puedes traerte a ti mismo a decirles más.
Después de una larga pausa, Merry finalmente habla.
'Ya veo entonces. Esos tipos trabajaban para Saruman, y huyeron de él con la esperanza de beneficiarse de un nuevo maestro. ¡Mala suerte para manzanas podridas, digo yo! Y así todos esos barriles de hierba para pipa eran para algo más que sus propios hábitos de fumar, supongo. Aún así, no veo cuánto daño puede hacer eso. Solo hay tanto que Hornblower cultiva cada temporada, y si falta demasiado seguro que se notará.
'Pippin, ${PLAYER}, ¿podemos hacer un pacto para no cargar a Frodo o Sam con esto? Ya han pasado por suficiente, y si hay algún problema en la Comarca, preferiría mucho más que lo aprendan cuando lleguemos allí, y no arruinar estos días dorados de celebración. Sé que pesará bastante en mi propio corazón, aunque creo que trabajaré duro para olvidarlo por un tiempo.
'Y sin embargo, sé que no puedo olvidar ir a casa por más tiempo. Me temo que recordaré cada momento desde este momento en adelante.'

'I have outstayed my welcome in these lands, I think. I have found my mind unsettled and my thoughts drawn to my own death.
'This is no place for one such as me, ${PLAYER}. Twice you have helped me to realize my own peril, and I hope I shall not have need of a third opportunity.
'As much as I desire to spend more time speaking with Faramir of his life, our duties are to the Host of the West - and it is my duty to no longer impede them.
'All we have learned of the foes we now face... it goes beyond my knowledge and beyond my skill. Those we left behind at Haerondir, though... they could stand against them. Let us return there and tell them of what we have learned!
'I shall ride as swiftly as I am able, and I would ask that you do the same. Without your voice, I fear they shall not heed my warnings....'

'You have returned to us so late, ${PLAYER}, and I am afraid you have much to answer for in the eyes of captain Anborn. Artamir's errand may have endangered our entire cause, and for what? The chance to speak to a spirit?
'His foolishness may cost us more than time. You see, we returned to Haerondir after you departed and spoke to Anborn of your efforts to rescue Artamir from his delusions. He thought long on the matter and then chose his course. You must understand, my friend, Anborn sent an entire company to find you and Artamir on the battle plain. You have returned, but we have heard naught from them....'

They have twisted the loss of Gondor into a monument to their own Master.
'It is clear that these Orcs have defiled the hill and I fear many of the Dark Lord's prisoners have met their end on its summit - and without the mercy of a swift death. Even in war-time, and with a great battle looming, I cannot abandon those that still remain to such a fate.

'I have looked upon the faces of the Wainriders at Dol Acharn, and though many of them are lost to my memory - one has never been forgotten. It is the face of their chieftain - the face of the man who slew me!
'Even now, I remember facing down the Wainrider chieftain with the north-men. All at once, it felt as if each of us stood alone in the battle against him and his kin. After his horse and chariot became stranded in the marshes, he ran me down himself and I could not flee in the shallows. The mud and murk held my feet and soon he was upon me. I fell, and the blood of the king's line spilled into the marshes. My folly had grown a terrible defeat into no less than a disaster for my people.
'His spear tasted the blood of Númenor, and he knew the victory he had won over Gondor could not be contested by any Man. Such a triumph grew a great arrogance within him, and as your friend Artamir told us, his death soon followed.
'You must gain an audience with the Wainrider chieftain if our ruse is to succeed, but it seems you shall find no such kindness without bearing a trinket of their peoples.
'I would have you seek the very spear that slew me in the marshes to the north. It is unlikely they will yield even once you bear it, but it is the only means we have to speak to their master.'

'Yes, ${PLAYER}... that is the one.
'It is rotted and rusted with the passage of time, but it can be no other. I can feel the spear piercing my chest anew even now...
'This pain... it cannot stop me now. It is time our ruse is tested! Let us see if the chieftain's weapon of old might be wielded against him, ${PLAYER}!'

'${PLAYER}, I believe all who wish to hear the tale have arrived by now. I can see men of Rohan, Gondor, and Ithilien gathered about... and still I can sense the unease in them.
'Elrohir and I shall do our best to ease it, but I cannot promise it shall be enough. Each of us shall be called to confront our fates soon enough, and it is likely some of us shall be more fortunate than others. But none should dwell on such things...
'As for the tale, it shall be a story of the Battle of Dagorlad's final hours and of my father's triumph over the servants of the Dark Lord. It is a lengthy tale, but my brother and I shall make sure the message of hope is not lost in its telling.
'Elrohir shall begin at your request, so when you believe everyone is ready, you should speak to him.'
'Let us begin, ${PLAYER}.'

'I have told it as best I can, ${PLAYER}. I hope it is enough to give these men comfort before we confront the Dark Lord.
'I must admit, I left out some of the more dreadful scenes that father described in the battle and embellished a few details... but I believe the full account is best left for times of peace and reflection. These men needed a tale of hope, and so that is what I told.
'It shall be as it was -- Elves and Men shall stand together again! Let us hope victory can be won once more and that the Ring of Power meets its final doom!'
As the Second Age approached its end, Elrond stood with the Last Alliance against the forces of Sauron and won a decisive victory that led to the Dark Lord's defeat.

'I am filled with sorrow that I could not aid you further before the battle's end, ${PLAYER}, but I am glad the Wainriders arrived in time to draw his attention from you. It seems the folly of my past has been answered this day -- perhaps it was once true that my allies were fated to a greater end without my hand in battle, but no more!
'As I look at my father's banner now, I see the might of a Gondor that once was... and may be again. For all the defilement Burudagath brought upon it, it resisted any final destruction. Gondor itself must now press onward through the darkness in much the same way, it seems.
'We have won a great victory this day... but I believe it time I leave this place and its painful memories behind.
'Go, return to your friends in the ruins and tell them of our victory. I shall see you again soon enough, ${PLAYER}...'

'Although I have spent many years upon this hill, never once have I raised a weapon against the Orcs. They came to regard me as nothing more than some sort of twisted amusement for their Master, and in time, I began to believe it myself.
'You have freed me from such delusions, my friend. It may have been folly for me to join the battle long ago, but to flee this fight could bring ruin to Gondor -- to my people!
'${PLAYER}, we must rid the hill of Orcs and leave none but the Bloodletter to the Wainriders. If they encounter even one Orc that is loyal to him, it may reveal our deception... and that is a chance we can ill-afford to take.
'We must move now! I shall do what I can to aid you!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! I hope I have not frightened your friends, but I felt compelled to stand amongst my own people once more. Who is the captain of these men?'
You inform Faramir that King Elessar commands the Host of the West, but Anborn is the captain of the Rangers of Ithilien who serve within the Host.
'Ithilien! It has been centuries since I travelled the gardens, but their beauty has never faded from my mind. And you, Anborn, you are one of its wardens?'
Anborn appears stunned by Faramir's remarks, but nods.
'I know not what ${PLAYER} has told you of me, but I am Faramir, son of King Ondoher. I pledge my sword to you, to Gondor, and to the King.'
Faramir bows deeply before Anborn.
'If my curse should ever be lifted, it shall be in the service of Gondor!'

'I... I am honoured to have one of the king's line amongst our forces.
'Faramir, your fate seemed always a tragic one, but perhaps more of it remains to be written in the days to come. My captain shares your name, Faramir, and though he was not well enough to travel with us, I feel a queer hope in your presence.
'I shall not deny you, son of Ondoher. Gondor has need of you once more!'
Anborn turns to you, his face a mix of awe and amusement.
'Perhaps now the Orcs shall have good reason to think Haerondir haunted!'

'The time is upon us, ${PLAYER}!
'Burudagath must be brought low before your allies think to approach the Black Land, but such a feat shall not be simple -- even with the aid of the Wainriders. Fear is powerful, but he is a man unlikely to succumb to it unless he senses that fate or the will of his Master has turned against him.
'Knowing this, we must be wary. The Bloodletter is of considerable strength, my friend, for I have seen him lift his prisoners with a single hand. The blood of his ancestors runs true within him, and it shall be either our bane or his greatest undoing.
'There remains one final problem in assuring the success of our ruse, but that is one I shall explain once we arrive at the hill.
'Tell me when you are prepared, my friend. Fate awaits us!'
'It is time to see if our ruse has succeeded, ${PLAYER}. Are you prepared?'

'Although we did not achieve such a victory without the loss of some of my men, I am gladdened that our foes shall trouble us no longer before we reach the Black Gate. Who would have thought that spirits might be turned against another evil? You continue to surprise me, ${PLAYER}... though I'd honestly prefer fewer surprises as we approach the Land of Shadow.
'As for those we lost, they shall be given fitting burials here within Haerondir. We are all called to sacrifice in such times, and they served Gondor faithfully to the last.
'I remain curious why that spirit would linger in such a grim place, but perhaps such things are beyond my understanding...
'Let us hope your victory is a sign of things to come!'

'What have you learned of the Orcs' plans, ${PLAYER}? Were you able to recover any orders from them?'
You show Laeglaw the orders, but his face twists in concentration when he sees the phrase in the Black Speech.
'Our foes to the north are great in number as we expected, but I am left with more questions. The identity of this Bloodletter is unknown to us. They also have many unfortunate prisoners in their keeping, but we do not know what or where this \qFaltor-shík\q could be. It troubles me, my friend. Much of this writing is in Westron - for what purpose is a single phrase in the tongue of the Orcs?
'I assumed that bringing along a lore-master such as Artamir might have been of great help to us for such a chance find, but the man seems repulsed at the mere mention of the Black Speech. The poor fellow should have stayed back at Haerondir....
'It seems Maendal was wise to ask for Mincham's aid after all -- the Ranger is well-learned in the languages of the Enemy. Bring this missive to Mincham and see what he can make of it.'

'What is this missive you bear?'
You explain to Mincham that you have need of his knowledge of the Black Speech once more. He takes the orders from you, and begins to read it. When he reaches the phrase in the Black Speech, he suddenly halts.
'By my reading of these orders, I understand Ondoher's Folly and Faltor-shík to be the very same, and it seems the Orcs have made something far worse of that hill than a mere strategic holding. That phrase, Faltor-shík, it... it means the Fane of Screaming. Such a name... it affords new significance to the grim structures that tower over the hill.
'It is not merely an Orkish encampment, my friend, but a temple of slaughter.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}.
'Do not worry - I have learned my lesson from the time I spent in the Dead Marshes!
'It is a sorry fate that befell the Steward, though, is it not?'

'Bah! The Ranger knows the Black Speech?
'I knew he was a queer fellow! No self-respecting man would learn such a vile tongue, I say!'
The orders demand slaves and captives be delivered to somewhere known as Faltor-shík for slaughter

Talk to Laeglaw at Tham Durlan

'I have a favour to ask of you, my friend. One of our own, Laeglaw, has set out to scout the hill of Ondoher's Folly. He fears a company of Orcs lay in wait and seek to encircle the Host as it draws closer to the Black Gate.
'Laeglaw was firm in his desire to scout the hill, but these lands are hostile to us all. We cannot risk scouting alone any longer - for the Enemy's forces may be arrayed against us just out of sight. Thus, I bid the Ranger Mincham accompany him in his patrol.
'${PLAYER}, I know that you and the Ranger have crossed paths many times, and I trust that he shall be of aid to Laeglaw - especially with his knowledge of the Enemy's language. Patience also seems to be a virtue of his, as a lore-master of sorts named Artamir begged to follow him out to Ondoher's Folly, and he was gracious enough to escort the fellow there. The man is no warrior, and it troubles me that he might endanger their cause through carelessness.
'As far as I know, they have travelled to ruins due north of here. The ruins are known as Tham Durlan, but with so little left intact, it is difficult to tell them from any other. Meet them there, and aid Laeglaw and Mincham if you are able... and keep a close watch on Artamir for me.'

'${PLAYER}! Keep your head low and your voice lower lest we alert the Orcs nearby....
'I have not come alone, but Mincham and I cannot defend against their numbers. As for the lore-master, Artamir does not even have a weapon to wield! He imagines this some sort of careless expedition, I think. I hope he realizes his folly soon, but not by an Orkish blade!
'Most of their forces are gathered up ahead upon the hill of Ondoher's Folly, but a small outpost lies to the north-east just over this ridge. We know little of their intent, but I worry they aim to endanger the Host of the West before it reaches the Black Gate - even if their Master wishes otherwise.
'We must learn more of their purpose at Ondoher's Folly, but I shall not risk a direct attack until we know more. Travel to their outpost and see if you can discover anything from the Orcs encamped there.'

'Wainriders? They have not been a threat to Gondor, much less seen at all, for hundreds of years now. Perhaps this spirit has mistaken the Easterlings for their old ancestors, else I cannot say. To have silently watched for so long, it is possible he has lost his understanding of the passing peoples and creatures of these lands.'
Artamir's face still betrays his fear, but you sense a renewed resolve rising within him.
'Fate and chance drove me to the Dead Marshes, and now they have guided me thus. I... I shall resist them no longer. I may not be the man this spirit seeks, but his knowledge of these lands and our enemies may be turned to our benefit. I... I believe I know this spirit's identity, my friend, but more questions still linger... and answers seem unlikely unless he and I speak alone.'

The shade wailed the name Artamir, and spoke as if Artamir were his brother. Without pausing to consider the absurdity of what you are about to speak, you tell the shade that a man named Artamir is among your company in the ruins to the south.
A puzzled expression washes over the shade's face, and his gaze swiftly shifts to meet your own. However, before speaking a word, he vanishes.

'You say a spirit of some kind knew my name, ${PLAYER}? That he called out for an Artamir?
'I have had quite enough dealings with spirits for my liking, I'll have you know. There must be some mistake...
'You see, it is common in Gondor to honour our ancestors by bestowing their names upon our children, and even within Minas Tirith, I know no fewer than two others bearing my name. If I am recalling correctly, I even once told you of old King Ondoher's son named Artamir.
'No, no. That man cannot be me, my friend. How long has this spirit lingered in the Wastes? How many have fallen since he met his own end?'
Artamir begins to trail off as a look of horror appears on his face.
'D-do not move, ${PLAYER}!'

Listen to Elrohir's tale of the Last Alliance

'And so, the Battle of Dagorlad drew to a close...
'The Last Alliance won a decisive victory over the Dark Lord and banished his mightiest servants back to the Black Land. The might of Men and Elves proved the greater that day, and let us hope it shall prove true once more!
'Although the fighting within Mordor lasted over seven more years before Sauron himself was finally defeated, this battle turned the tide in a war that many thought unwinnable.
'Yet many victories and defeats still laid ahead...'
'Quite the tale, my friend, was it not?'

'Victories over the Dark Lord's servants would not come easily for long...
'Although Orcs and evil Men fell in scores upon the battle plain, Sauron soon loosed his nine greatest servants upon the Last Alliance. Once they were Men, but twisted by the Rings given to them by the Dark Lord, they grew stretched and withered into unseen forms. As the corruption of the Rings consumed them, these Men grew beyond death itself! For in truth, the Dark Lord held their Rings and thus tethered them to service and life unending. Even if they were struck down, they were not slain -- merely banished for a time!
'Many names have been bestowed upon them by those who have beheld their terrible shapes: Dwimmerlaik, Dúrchir, Gwetherain, and Nazgûl. In the tongue of Westron, their name is perhaps the most precise -- Ringwraiths!'

'Although many of their kin fled before the Ringwraiths, Gil-galad and Elendil did not falter. Gil-galad held close the mighty spear, Aiglos, and Elendil bore the blade, Narsil -- the very sword that was broken, reforged, and wielded anew by King Elessar! They fought as one and cut through the Dark Lord's forces with a fury unlike any the Elves or Men had ever witnessed.
'They soon stood before the Black Gate itself, but the battle would not be won so easily!
'Alas, the Ringwraiths and a vast army of Orcs had gathered beneath the dark ramparts of the Black Gate, and they sought to stand between the Last Alliance and their Master!
'¡Los Nueve blandieron el miedo mismo contra la Última Alianza y todos, excepto los más audaces, temblaron ante ellos!'
'¡Ni siquiera los Nueve pudieron resistir a Aiglos y Narsil, y fueron derribados y desterrados de vuelta a Mordor!'

'In an age long-ended, a great battle was fought upon Dagorlad between the numberless armies of the Dark Lord and the Last Alliance of Elves and Men. For years, they clashed upon the battle plain, and each momentary victory and defeat dimmed the hope of the war ever coming to an end.
'After many trying battles, the Last Alliance pressed southward and approached the Black Gate of Mordor. Yet, the nearer they drew to the Black Land, the more foes the Dark Lord sent forth.
'But lo, Elendil the Tall and High King Gil-galad of the Noldor possessed much wisdom and valour, and soon the plans were drawn for a final assault against the Black Gate.
'The Last Alliance assembled at a great bulwark and it was there they made their stand against Sauron and his armies.

Watcher of the Wastes

'A man of true Númenórean blood to have survived so long in Mordor...
'This is unthinkable, ${PLAYER}. If he is responsible for the fates of those at Ondoher's Folly, he is also a danger to the Host of the West. I still am not certain what to make of Faramir's claims about the Wainriders, but I would not dismiss them so carelessly.
'We must send word at once to the Rangers at Haerondir and ready ourselves for what may come.'

'I... I had to follow where he led, ${PLAYER}. Steward Denethor would have commanded it if he still lived, and I cannot abandon his task now.
'I sensed that the Rangers would not wish me to go, so I sent you to hold their attention as I departed. I apologise for the deception, but you must understand the significance of the man we have encountered this day. As I suspected, he is none other than Faramir, son of Ondoher!
'How capricious of fate that I should find a Faramir here amid the wastes when I so recently bid a farewell to Steward Denethor's son in the Houses of Healing...'
Artamir looks around with a sense of wonder, but soon meets your gaze again.
'Faramir, son of Ondoher, met a grim end here in the Wastes, but perhaps more tragic, he was never meant to journey to these lands at all. King Ondoher and Faramir's brother, Artamir, rode to repel the forces of the Wainriders in the Wastes, but they were caught unprepared and vastly outnumbered. They were soon aided by a company of North-men, but even still, their forces were slain on the fields and driven into the Dead Marshes. Amid all this, Faramir was bidden to remain in Minas Anor when Minas Tirith was still called as such, but he defied his father's wishes and secretly rode to join the North-men as they rode southward toward the battle. Thus, Ondoher and his two sons met their ends in the Wastes...
'As with so much of Gondor's history, there is much more to be said on these events, but I would prefer to tell it when we return to Minas Tirith. The air here has left my throat quite dry, indeed. In the meantime, Faramir has told me much of what he has seen in recent days, and I must admit... it gives me great concern for the Host of the West.
'It took some great efforts on my part, but I have convinced Faramir to trust you with his burdens. You should speak to him and learn how we might aid both him and the Host.'

'As I said, I have many suspicions about the identity of this spirit... but those shall remain mine alone until I learn more of this spirit's purpose.
'If you and the Rangers would grant me leave, I shall follow where he leads and learn what I can of him and his fate in the Wastes. Think what he may have seen - such experiences are beyond the life of any mortal Man!
'Talk to Mincham and see what he makes of this. I have heard tell he is no stranger to spirits of the Dead. If he grants my request, I would ask that you - and you alone - follow us to the north after a short time.
'I shall speak well of you to him, and perhaps he shall be more willing to speak to you directly. That is my hope, ${PLAYER}, for safety seems so far away now... and I would much like to return to it.'

'A spirit here... in the ruins?
'I fear this shall not portend any good at all, and I would caution Artamir to put the safety of the Host before his own misguided studies. It may be true that the spirits of the Dead that followed Aragorn were honourable enough when they fulfilled their oaths, but do not forget those we lost when they felt no such duty.
'If one has been cursed by the breaking of an oath, you should not assume them a friend. We of the Grey Company have learned this all too painfully.
'I shall not stop him, but I hope he considers the great risk he would impose on all of our company.'

Artamir and the accursed warrior have vanished!
The accursed warrior has seen much in his days upon the battlefield, and now the foes of the past may become the foes of the present.
'So the banner of Ondoher did survive! What a shame that it has been used to such an end...'

The cage-waggons can be found to the south-east of Ondoher's Folly.
Faramir has asked you to dismantle the cage-waggons making for Ondoher's Folly and free any slaves you encounter. He also hopes you can learn the identity of the true master of Ondoher's Folly.

Artamir can be found to the south outside Ondoher's Folly in Dagorlad.

Free slaves from the cage-waggons
Talk to Artamir outside Ondoher's Folly

'It is time you learned of the greatest insult dealt against me and my family...
'When my father fell on the hill above, his banner was paraded by the Wainriders and the Orcs as the rest of his company fell. Our foes chased them as they fled into the marshes, and for many years I saw naught of my father's heraldry.
'Not long ago, a man returned to the hill bearing the banner... but it had changed. Age had worn it thin, but what remained was perverted into something between the familiar and the horrid. With the banner unfurled, he called forth the first of the slaves the Orcs had captured in Ithilien... and one by one he tortured and beheaded them beneath my father's banner as the others watched. After all were slain, the bodies were defiled in such terrible ways... I cannot speak them.
'This man dishonours the memory of my father, Ondoher, and twists it to suit his own cruelty. His name is unknown to me, but the Orcs must know it well... for they avert their eyes in his presence.
'If you wish to aid me, learn what you can of this man and free the poor men that have fallen into his hands. The slaves and prisoners are drawn by cage-waggons to the hill along a rough pathway to the east.'

'The Orcs slaughtered them in their cages... like beasts. How horrid...
'Our foe may be of Númenórean blood, but he is no man. Burudagath the Bloodletter... who would hold such a title willingly?
'If he is the true master of Ondoher's Folly, the Host of the West should remain vigilant. You slew so many at Ondoher's Folly, but still their numbers do not dwindle... and this Burudagath seems to hold sway over them all.
'Mincham learned from Orcs and evil Men that the Enemy wishes us to come to the Black Gate safely, but how can such words be trusted now?
'Ruse or not, my friend, I believe only one course remains.'
The Impostor King
Damaged wheels on Mordor cage-waggons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
In his time wandering the Wastes, Faramir has learned the identity of the true master of Ondoher's Folly: a vile Black Númenórean bearing a perverted banner of Gondor.
Talk to Faramir, son of Ondoher

A Brother Lost
'I know of his brother's fate, ${PLAYER}, so perhaps it would be best if I told him. Do as he asks, but I shall work to soften the blow he shall soon be dealt.'
You notice a foot-print, but by its shape and size it seems to have been made by an Uruk-hai...

'In all the years I have wandered these lands, I have never learned of the true fate of my brother. When I awoke from what I learned to be my death, I saw a great force of Wainriders moving westward and then southward, but I could not follow them from these lands. Did my brother stand against them? Did he fall as I did?
'Search the low-lands to the west of this hill. If my brother fled the battlefield alive, he would have taken such a path. If not, perhaps... he too has been cursed.
'Please do this for me, ${PLAYER}, and tell me if you discover any sign of him. I must learn the truth of his fate.'

'In all my time here, I could not face the truth of my fate...
'Father and Artamir have found the peace they deserved in death, but I... I deserve no such comfort. Father laid his curse upon me, and I do not think ill of him for it. I failed him as a son and heir, and I shall remain alone and bound to this land far longer than it took me to realize my folly.
'I thank you for offering the truth to me, sorrowful as it may be.'

Faramir can be found on the plains south of Ondoher's Folly.
You did not discover any sign of Artamir or any spirit that might appear to be him. You should now return to Faramir.

The Dead Marshes can be found to the west and north of Ondoher's Folly.
Faramir believes his brother might be found somewhere in the Dead Marshes to the west of Ondoher's Folly. You should search for any sign of Artamir, son of Ondoher.
The murky water of the Dead Marshes churns violently...
A bow of Ranger make rests on the ground and its wood is warped and swollen...
An Orc lies in the shallows of the marshes, but appears to have been dead for some time...
Artamir, son of Ondoher, was lost in a great battle against the Wainriders and his accursed brother, Faramir, has long searched for him within the lands of the Wastes.
Relics of Victory

'Oh, ${PLAYER}... what is all this?'
You explain to Artamir that you recovered a collection of relics from the hill of Dol Acharn.
'I would prefer to study these relics in the more well-kept Houses of Lore, but Haerondir shall have to do for now...
'No, what am I saying? You are perhaps the only one in Haerondir who will still look at me, much less speak to me, and I should not belittle a gift unasked for.
'You are too kind to bring such artifacts to me, especially after how much trouble I have caused you and the Rangers. I think it shall be some time before they let me out of their sight again... but ah, what an adventure it was!'

Talk to Artamir outside Ondoher's Folly

'I must admit, my friend, I am still vexed by Faramir's insistence on the threat of Wainriders upon the battle plain.
'The Wainriders have not been a threat to the peoples of Gondor in over a thousand years, and yet Faramir speaks of them as a foe with which we shall soon contend. The might of the Easterling clans has diminished much since their earlier, more unified days, and it seems unlikely to me that they have suddenly reforged a kinship that broke over many long years.
'He has asked to speak with you, and I do not doubt his words shall again concern the Wainriders.
'See what you make of his claims, ${PLAYER}. The Wainriders are dead and gone, but so too was Faramir, son of Ondoher....'

'If you are to survive long in these lands, ${CLASS}, you must first learn the history of the Wainriders as I and my father once did.
'The hatred between Gondor and the Wainriders is a tale of fathers and sons. Our lands were stolen and reclaimed through the passing of the years, but the Wainriders shaped the line of Kings in a way that no other foe could equal.
'After losing his own father to their hordes, King Calimehtar, father of my father, rode against the Wainriders in vengeance. With the help of the North-men, he devastated their ranks, broke their wains and chariots, and slew them upon the hill to the east - a hill which came to be known as Dol Acharn. Such a victory brought peace to Gondor for many years, and Calimehtar never again had to contend with the Wainriders before his death.
'Peace, such as it is, is always short-lived. Calimehtar's son and my father, King Ondoher, was forced to meet them in battle. Alas, you are aware of the loss Gondor suffered as a result.
'Artamir here has told me much of the days that followed the King's death as well as my own. He tells me that the Wainriders made camp to the south-west, but were ambushed and slain to the last by a vast army under the command of a man named Eärnil. He claims that Eärnil soon became king of Gondor, even in the face of the claim made by my sister's husband, King Arvedui of Arthedain. What tales he has told me of these new days...
'Ah, but now the past has risen to confront the present. Fate is a curious thing, ${PLAYER}... is it not?

'This... cannot be! If the Wainriders again roam the battle plain, they may meet the Host of the West on the field. Their hatreds will not have dulled with time, and they shall strike at those that bear the king's banner with a vengeance renewed.
'We must bring word to Haerondir and soon!'
Old Hatreds
Although they have not been seen for hundreds of years, the Wainriders of the East have shaped the history of Gondor in both victory and defeat.

Faramir's Ruse

'Our ruse may yet succeed, ${PLAYER}, but the Wainriders do not sound like any ally of ours -- even after we offered them the location of their hated foe.
'It seems time cannot change some men... they are ever the stubborn folk they once were.
'Now, my friend, we must move against the Bloodletter while the Wainriders prepare else all shall be lost!'

The Wainrider chieftain can be found somewhere within Dol Acharn. Disturbing an object of his people might rouse him to step forth from the shadows.
Faramir has asked you to draw forth and defeat the Wainrider chieftain in the hope you might gain an audience with him.
Confront and defeat the Wainrider chieftain at Dol Acharn
Talk to Chieftain Zhan Ashû at Dol Acharn

'Through all the years I wandered the Wastes, I felt as if a great fog surrounded me -- blinding my sight and clouding my mind. Whether it was borne of confusion, fear, or the pains of this curse... I cannot say. I had centuries to overcome this illusion, and never did I succeed until I was convinced of my folly by you and Artamir.
'${PLAYER}, do you understand? As I once did, the Wainriders must now suffer the same sickness of the mind. They are men outside their time in this age, and the truths of their past are all they shall see fit to believe.
'As the men of Gondor were in the time of the Wainriders, Burudagath the Bloodletter is a man of Númenor. Although the Númenóreans were once one people, their fates were divided through the influence of the Dark Lord. The Faithful defied Sauron and believed not his lies, but many others fell to evil and became known as Black Númenóreans -- and Burudagath is but one of them in service of the Dark Lord. Even with how far he has fallen, he cannot deny his heritage... and the blood he shares with my people of old.
'I understand you may have heard these tales, my friend, but this shared lineage might be turned to our advantage. To a man of Gondor, the history of Númenor is great and terrible... yet to a foe of our peoples, such tales and truths are but a trifle. A hatred so blind does not measure the goodness or evil in Men.
'The Wainriders at Dol Acharn need only understand that a man of Númenor flies the banner of a king of Gondor -- and of their hated foe, Ondoher.
'My friend, go to Dol Acharn and call forth their chieftain... he must be convinced of Burudagath's heritage and the banner he bears. If you succeed, his deeds, good or ill, shall be but a whisper in their ears as their hatred calls them to battle!'

'You have my attention, ${RACE}. You stand before Zhan Ashû of the Wainriders! Speak quickly or I shall remove you from my sight!'
You warn Zhan Ashû that Burudagath of Númenor has come to the Wastes and stands upon the western hill of the battle plain in defiance of the Wainriders under the banner of a king of Gondor.
'Gondorian dogs! No matter how many we slay, they rise against us anew! They think themselves our betters, but we do not shrink from battle so easily!'
Zhan Ashû begins to shout to nearby Wainriders.
'Ready the wains and chariots, men! Gondor shall breathe its last this day, and the men of Númenor shall finally be vanquished!
For merely a moment, a wave of confusion washes over Zhan Ashû's face.
'Yet, why would one such as you offer us knowledge of our greatest foe? I do not understand...'
Zhan Ashû seems to steady his resolve.
'...but I shall not dismiss it!
'Go, ${RACE}! Warn this Burudagath if you must, but do not attempt to stand between us and our prey!'

Chieftain Zhan Ashû can be found atop Dol Acharn in eastern Dagorlad.
You have bested the chieftain in combat and he now wishes to speak to you. You should attempt to convince him of the Bloodletter's danger to his people.

Faramir can be found due west of Dol Acharn in Dagorlad.
You have told the Wainrider chieftain of the Bloodletter's heritage and of the banner he bears, but his people still remained hostile despite their apparent gratitude. You should return to Faramir.
A chill washes over you as the Wainrider chieftain appears!
The Wainrider chieftain fades into shadow, but immediately reappears atop Dol Acharn!
Faramir, son of Ondoher has devised a ruse to confound the Wainriders into both ending the treachery of the Bloodletter at Ondoher's Folly and ignoring the advance of the Host of the West.

'What is it, my friend?'
You tell Legolas of Echil's sense of wonder about the Elves at Haerondir, and how he wishes that he and the other Men might be so at ease as well. Legolas chuckles to himself, and Gimli scoffs quietly beside him.
'Your Ranger friend is perhaps too eager to think such things of the Elves. Isn't he, Gimli?
'It is not a lack of fear that drives me forth, but a sense of duty to Aragorn and to our kin in the Host. You and I have shared this long journey together and fear has not yet broken us even if it has lingered at every step of our adventures.
'These Men are the bravest of this Age, and I would not see them falter now. Victory can be won over the Enemy, and none would know that better than the sons of Elrond.
'Why don't you speak to them, ${PLAYER}? I wonder what they would make of Echil's talk of fearless Elves!'

'What troubles you, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Elladan and Elrohir of Echil's hope that the Elves in the Host of the West are without fear. Elladan stifles a laugh, but Elrohir is unable to hold back. Before Elladan is able to speak, Elrohir quickly interjects.
'I am sorry, my friend. Were that the truth, he would be the first to know! These Men should not think so little of themselves!'
Elladan gestures to Elrohir to be silent and begins to speak.
'No, there is no hidden bravery within us, my friend. Perhaps we benefit from knowledge of the past, but in matters of the Enemy, fear is ever present. The Ringbearer's quest is unlike any errand in the time of our father and the alliance of Men and Elves.
'You say these Men are fearful, but they still march forth knowing their doom. That is the truest bravery, and they must be made to see it.'

Legolas can be found on the north-western ramparts of Haerondir.
Echil has asked you to speak to the Elves at Haerondir as their resolve has not visibly faltered. You should speak to Legolas first.

Elladan and Elrohir can be found on the eastern ramparts at Haerondir.

Talk to Legolas at Haerondir
Talk to Elladan and Elrohir at Haerondir

'It has been a long march, ${PLAYER}...
'I can speak only for myself, but I am prepared for what may come when we reach the Black Gate. If my death awaits, I shall welcome it in the service of Gondor and of King Elessar. Even still, it is a weight to bear... and each man here bears it.
'I have seen much in these last days that I never imagined, and I am sure more still awaits beyond my sight. For all of these unknown joys or ills, I have not seen the Elves in this company falter even once. Whether they fear or not as Men do, they seem charmed.
'I wonder what eases them so in such times, and I wonder if it might offer some comfort to our company. Would you speak to them, my friend?'
A Cloud of Despair
As the Host of the West approaches the Black Gate, a sense of despair has taken root in even the hardiest warriors.
Talk to Laeglaw at Tham Durlan

'You have done well, my friend.
'With this accomplished, the Orcs at Ondoher's Folly should no longer pose a threat to the Host of the West or to any that still remain in their thrall.
'Let us hope it was enough, ${PLAYER}.'

'Once those Orcs are gone, I would much like to study the location of King Ondoher's fall.
'Steward Denethor's dream has come to pass through the leader of this Host, but I wonder yet why Ondoher's banner came so clearly to his mind.'

Orcs can be found throughout Ondoher's Folly in north-western Dagorlad.
Laeglaw has asked you to assault the hill of Ondoher's Folly and defeat the Orcs who have claimed it.
Defeat Orcs at Ondoher's Folly (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'What did the Ranger make of that missive, ${PLAYER}?'
You inform Laeglaw that Faltor-shík translates to \qthe Fane of Screaming\q and what Mincham takes that to mean. His face is aghast for a moment, but he is able to summon his words once more.
'The Fane of Screaming... is this truly the name they have bestowed upon the site of our king's fall? If the Orcs sought to provoke us through insults, I shall let them consider this a victory... but it will be their last.
'It has been long since we moved against the Orcs in the Wastes directly, and I believe it likely an assault would catch them by surprise. I no longer doubt your place among the Rangers, my friend, for you have done much to aid my company and I trust that you would do so again.
'For the sake of our king's memory and for the fallen, ride to Ondoher's Folly and put an end to those Orcs!'
The Fane of Screaming

'When you find them, send them back to Haerondir by our safest paths. They will know the way.'

'You did well to ensure the safety of your allies and kin, ${PLAYER}. It is something I wish I could have done...
'They would be wise to avoid the marshlands should they pass through the Wastes again... for the lights can take a hold on any man.

'The Wainriders must be made to pay for defiling these lands once more, ${PLAYER}, but your allies are in grave danger and their lives cannot wait on my designs for vengeance.
'The six men you found were caught unawares by the Wainriders, but four more yet lived last I saw them.
'They fled the battle plain northward into the marshes... but they shall find no refuge there. As the north-men and I learned all too well, the waters are muddy and slow any retreat to a crawl... and now even worse things dwell within its shallows. There are lights... the Dead without form that lurk within the marshes, and they hold the power to sway any to their will.
'These Rangers may have escaped the Wainriders, but they will not escape the Dead in the marshes... not when fear has such a hold on them.
'Go now! Save your allies, and do what I could not!'

Talk to Faramir near Dol Acharn

'Your friends can rest easy for the moment, ${CLASS}, but rest shall not soon come to me.
'Even in this form beyond death, I have done naught to stop the countless horrors I have witnessed, and I can bear it no longer. This fallen man of Númenor, Burudagath, perverts the banner of my father and kills without mercy... and the Wainriders that rose in answer to the strife in these lands have slain the men of your company with fear alone. These two foes stand in defiance of Gondor on the hills of Dagorlad... and there remains no force to stop them.
'Yet, I believe that I have found a means to set our foes upon each other.
'However, such a ruse demands swaying the attention of the Wainriders... and that shall be no simple task.'

'It is as I feared... it seems only the Wainriders themselves can stand upon the hill without succumbing to fear.
'I had hoped you would not encounter such resistance from the Wainriders before even confronting them, but it seems our cause grows more desperate.
'I may know a way to allow you to travel onto Dol Acharn without hindrance, but it shall not be an easy task.'
The Cursed Hill
<rgb=#FF0000>An unseen force saps your will to press forth and your morale begins to waver!</rgb>
The Wainriders have claimed the hill of Dol Acharn, but they must be challenged if you are to stand between them and the Host of the West.

'You have done well, my friend! I see many have come to hear our father's tales, and we shall soon begin.
'Let us hope it can bring some comfort to these men before we make for the Black Gate!'

Elladan has asked you to gather the soldiers of the Host of the West stationed in Haerondir in the hope that he and his brother might ease their worries through the telling of an old victory over the Enemy.

Elladan can be found on the eastern ramparts of Haerondir.

Gather bands of Men from the Host of the West (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Talk to Elladan at Haerondir

'${PLAYER}, my father's tales can do much to inspire hope and awe. Elrohir and I have heard them many times, and they are known to us now perhaps even more clearly than to our father after these long years.
'His tales are full of both glory and despair, but certain moments carry with them no sadness even in the face of loss. He told us many tales of the battles during the Last Alliance, and while no moment can match the joyous defeat of the Enemy at the end of the Second Age, there are others that might inspire those in times such as these.
'My mind is drawn to father's tales of the Battle of Dagorlad. It was a great and terrible battle that raged for many long years, and even after victory was won many more passed before the Ring was cut from the Dark Lord's finger. Even still, it was a victory that marked a turning point in what to many seemed a hopeless war against Sauron. Men, dwarves, Elves, and even the High Elves stood fast against the Enemy's forces and though many were lost in the fighting, they pushed forth and threw down the Black Gate.
'It is a tale of victory against great odds, and it seems we march to a battle that shall be much the same. Brother, can you think of a greater tale to tell these men?'

'The carving has been cleansed of its corruption, and the shade of Darothild has escaped from her long captivity. Those are both worthy goals to have accomplished this day!
