'I have already been approached about making a place for the Nurnhoth in Gondor, for their enslavement in Mordor has stirred the hearts of the folk who freed them. I do not know if Ayorzén merits the same treatment, ${PLAYER}. The Nurnhoth were cruelly mistreated by their overlords in Udûn and elsewhere; freedom was just a distant, half-remembered tale to them.
'But Ayorzén led armies against us. He commanded his people to fight during the war, and many good men died on Khundolar blades before the White City. This is not an easy choice to make.'
Aragorn is silent for a moment, considering. Then he comes to a decision.
'The words of Mithrandir have not oft led me astray, ${PLAYER}. Ayorzén will be given a new start in Gondor, in return for the knowledge he can give to us of Mordor. Speak to the waggon-driver, Rathnor, and arrange for Ayorzén's passage to the city.'
'What's that? There's another fellow that needs passage back to the city? Aye, I'll accommodate him. There won't be much room, but I've got a little more space if folk are willing to sit close.'

'Eärendil was a mariner, ${PLAYER}, and he braved storm and roaring wave; he bore shining light out of the darkness. He voyaged through sadness and woe, cresting the waves of his sorrow and braving the winds of wrath to bring hope from afar. He travels still upon his errand, not upon the seas of the world but those of heaven, the light of the Silmaril on his brow showing the way.'
Elrond falls silent and gazes up at the sky, remembering distant memories.
'For all the Eldar, the light of Eärendil's star is counted most precious. It is a sign of hope for all who labour against the Great Enemy or the multitude of his servants. For me it is something more.
'Eärendil was a mariner, but he was also my sire. When I look to the stars, I remember much that has now gone beyond the circles of the world, and the joy of memory is tinged with the sorrow of loss. I give you this gift so you may bear the light of Eärendil with you, and it will be a shining lamp in the darkness.'

'Ah, you have cleansed the corruption from the artifact that Ayorzén brought from Durthang. I never doubted you would be equal to the task, ${PLAYER}.
'The Light of Eärendil will serve you well within Gorgoroth. I deem that few of the commanders of which Ayorzén spoke will be able to endure its presence, and none will enjoy it. It will bring them discomfort and aid you in piercing the shadow.
'It is time to press further into Mordor.'

'Did I not tell you? Digging in the debris is never a waste... not for a scholar of history!
'This broken piece of metal is unremarkable, save for this marking right here. Do you see it? That is half of a sigil of Gondor. Nay, not even a half! It may be more of a small portion of a small portion, but even a portion's portion is a delight to one who thirsts for knowledge!
'This tiny remnant of history has emerged from the ash, a reminder to us of Gondor's resilience. My master will surely find value in this discovery, even if I was not supposed to adventure here. The House of Lore will benefit from this, I do not doubt it! This is much more interesting than anything I might have found in Osgiliath, so close to Minas Tirith. This is a land of danger, an unknown land, and the rewards are greater to match!'

'I believe that you can advance into the Doomfold of Dor Amarth. Pass through the guarded Isenmouthe and find Brungos on the other side. He will tell you somewhat of what he has done, and what has yet to be accomplished.'

'There is no shortage of enemies stalking Dor Amarth. Defeat any you find and the land will be made not safe, but safer at the least.'

'I have faced many foes here myself, but still my mind worries at the subject about which we spoke, ${PLAYER}. Can it be that this land was once much the same as any other, but the coming of Sauron laid waste to it? There are countless reasons to rejoice that he is gone, but even for one among many it must approach the top of the list.
'If he could do this to Mordor, could he not have worked such a change upon Gondor, or upon Rohan, or upon Eriador? I deem that he could. Further I contend that the transformation of Dor Amarth to this blasted plain was not accidental. I believe he did it purposefully, with malicious intent, if not for some scheme then merely for the hateful joy of it.
'I spoke about this with Covadil, who dared the passage of Isenmouthe with me; I think it was she who first planted these thoughts in my mind, and now I cannot stop thinking on them! She intended to travel north-east to Lûghash. I warned her to be careful, but she found that mirthful and laughed at my warning. She is a scholar, and a bit odd, but I do hope she is being careful all the same. Perhaps you could find her and see how she fares?'

'Will you look at that, ${PLAYER}? A fortress was built there upon the lowest slopes of Ered Lithui when Gondor established its watch upon Mordor. It was called the Peace-hold of Sídhost, and nothing moved on Orodruin without alerting the attention of its defenders.
'But the vigilance of Gondor failed, in time, and it was abandoned. The Orcs burrowed beneath its foundations, and the earth shook, and Sídhost crumbled into ruin. The Spire of Lûghash arose in its place. That is it right there! If it weren't for the scholarly pursuit of knowledge, you would think that was merely an evil tower, but now you know some of its history. Isn't that fascinating?
'But there was once a Gondorian fortress there, and I wonder if there might still be signs of it. You should do what we scholars of the House of Lore often do when we want to unearth lost knowledge. We dig about in the debris, ${PLAYER}! You never know what you might find!
'Search the old ash piles all around the Spire, and see if you can find some remnant of the Gondorian presence here. For knowledge, and for knowing!'

'You saved Rhogrin from himself? I am glad to hear it, and your story confirms to me something I had suspected!
'Sauron instructed his servants to build him a kingly castle, a stronghold on a hill that was called Amon Dûr. Over the long passage of years, his servants expanded the castle to cover all of the hill, and it grew with new construction until it towered into the air. It became Barad-dûr, the Dark Tower, and reached so high that only Sauron's magic could keep it aloft.
'But the tower did not only reach skyward. Beneath Barad-dûr, the Orcs delved fathomless dungeons for their master, until the Ered Lithui were riddled with pits and chasms. When the tower fell, the land gave way and a great abyss opened where Barad-dûr once stood. Sauron's dungeons were exposed to the sky: the Abyss of Mordath.'
Covadil shivers.
'Brrrrr! Knowledge can be frightening! Anyway, Sauron may be gone, but he dwelt at Barad-dûr for so long that the land has not forgotten him. It sounds to me as if he left his impression on the Abyss and the lands around it. You should find Mithrandir and tell him this, and I think it is time I returned to the House of Lore. I am not afraid of danger... in moderation. But this is more than moderately terrifying!'

'The tidings you bring of Barad-dûr do not surprise me, but they will need to await proper consideration. Something has happened.

'We learned two useful pieces of information from Dulgabêth. The first is this: the forces of Mordor are not unified, and they might be turned against one another. Indeed, they may already be doing so on their own, without our assistance! He seems most concerned about his rival, who sent forces to reinforce Cirith Ungol. This rival is the one he called Ugrukhôr, the Captain of the Pit, and I have heard tell of him before. He is cruel and without mercy, and it was he who promised the Thandrim of Durthand peace and gave them slaughter instead.
'The second piece of information Dulgabêth unwittingly gave to us might not be as immediately useful, but still I want to learn what it signifies. He spoke of the Gúrzyul, and the name makes me uneasy for its evocation of the Nazgûl. The Nine are slain, destroyed alongside Sauron, and few could rival them in malice or power, but we should tread carefully near any reminder of them.
'I understand that Ayorzén the Wily refused my offer of a place in Gondor, and has been haunting the pass of Cirith Gorgor just inside the Black Gate. See what he makes of the information we have learned, ${PLAYER}, and follow that knowledge where it leads.'

'Your adventures in Lhingris and Talath Úrui have proven most informative, but they raise further questions. Why would the Ghâsh-hai pledge to support Ugrukhôr? What has become of Borangos following the defeat of Sauron? And to what end does Urudanî walk the land once again, so changed?
'These questions must wait. I have heard worrisome tidings from Agarnaith, the Bloody Gore. Few have gone there, but those who have returned speak of a dangerous and growing threat.'

'I leave the choice of path to you. Learning of Ugrukhôr and Cirith Ungol will take you into Lhingris. The dwarf Atli has designs on exploring Lhingris, and he will accompany you there. I believe exploration of the Gúrzyul will require exploring to the south of Orodruin, in Talath Úrui. Harthalín will accompany you thither.
'Follow both of these leads to their ends, and we will be well-equipped to deal with Dulgabêth.'

'Ugrukhôr and Dulgabêth hate each other. If they spent less time quarrelling between themselves and more time opposing Gondor, the war might have gone differently. They say that once, long ago, Ugrukhôr plotted to ambush and murder Dulgabêth and place the blame on Gondor. Sauron learned of it before the plan could be executed, and he fed all of Ugrukhôr's servants to the Fire. When he was the only one left, Sauron held him to the flames; the pain was to serve both as punishment and as a reminder not to plot against Sauron's chosen servant. It left Ugrukhôr scarred and twisted, on the outside as already he was on the inside.
'How do I know this? To this day Ugrukhôr still speaks of it! While Sauron lived, the Captain of the Pit knew not to move against Dulgabêth, but now Sauron is gone. It cannot be long now before his simmering revenge comes to a boil, and one of them will die at the hands of the other.'

You place the skull at the base of the stone, and the images return.
Once again you see the prison of Naerband, but something this time is different. It takes you a moment to reconcile what has changed, but held in the grip of the spirit it is impossible to tell how long the moment might have been. The prison stands in the shadow of Orodruin, and then you see it: the southern slope of the Mountain is intact; the Ghâshghurm has not yet been made.
The images flicker behind your eyes, and you see that Naerband is filled with prisoners. Downtrodden Nurnhoth, rebellious Easterlings, and Haradrim deserters rattle the cages of their cells. Their jailors walk the corridors of Naerband, and they tap their weapons on the iron doors, and they scrape their blades on the iron walls, and they tap their boots on the iron floor. You are seized by a sensation of eager anticipation, but it does not belong to you. It comes from the whispering spirit, and fills you with revulsion and dread.
Then the Mountain blazes, and the southern slope explodes in a shower of rock and flame. The torrent flows inexorably down the side of Orodruin, and the rocky plain becomes a lake of fire: the Ghâshghurm.
The images become sharper and more distinct, as if the spirit seeks to draw your attention. At last you understand. As the lava pooled at the foot of Orodruin, the iron prison of Naerband became super-heated by its proximity to the lake of fire. Naerband became more than a prison. It became an oven.
You close your eyes to shut out the sight, and at last the spirit relents, its price paid.
'Zaghárog,' it says to you: the name of the spirit in the stone.
'I do not trust this spirit, but perhaps we can make use of it to learn that which we seek and be safely away before it works some treachery upon us!'

The carven stone is dreadful in form, and it does not seem out of place within Gorgoroth. But there is something else that sets it apart, a cold and watchful presence. And then, there is more: a voice that whispers in your head. Images rise unbidden behind your eyes. They are drained of colour, as if the one who creates them has no knowledge of shade or hue.
You see a place of darkness, and a tiny point of light flickering high above. Then, below, there is a knife held in a cruel fist. It descends in an arc, and blood flows from a wound. The darkness deepens.
The voice in your head speaks no words, but you are suddenly awash on a questioning sea.
You recover your own words enough to reply, 'Yes, the Gúrzyul.'
The interrogative waves vanish as quickly as they had arrived. In their place is an overwhelming sensation: the promise of knowledge and secrets held close for centuries. As you try to express that such knowledge will be welcome, it is whisked cruelly away, dangled just out of reach.
The giving sensation is gone, replaced with a taking desire. You see a prison in your mind's eye, and the details are so clear you know it is a real place. The spirit shows you a certain cell in this prison, and a scorched skull in one corner. The images fade, and the whispering voice returns. It speaks a single word, but the word is enough. The word is 'want.'
You are released from the spirit's hold and the whispering in your head fades away. The presence remains, regarding you silently.

It will not be easy to reach them, for when the southern face of Orodruin exploded, it created a lake of fire between here and there: the Ghâshghurm.'

'Mithrandir spoke at length to me about the Gúrzyul, but much of what he had to say was speculation. We do not know very much about them.
'They seem to have been Black Númenóreans that swore to serve Sauron during the later years of the Second Age, before the Last Alliance of Elves and Men besieged Barad-dûr. Many were the cruel Men who sought to serve the Dark Lord in those days, but few only won his favour. Mithrandir would not say how he came to know this, but he believes Sauron bled his favourites with the edge of Gulthauk, his prized morgul-knife.
'They need no longer fear the passage of time, for by this act they were made Deathless. They are like to the Nazgûl, but lesser in power, and unlike those wraiths they can be slain. There will be no returning from death for such as they.
'I understand you wish to add to our store of knowledge concerning the Gúrzyul? I will travel with you into Talath Úrui. Let us first find the settlement of Fushaum Bal. Reports indicate it is a lawless settlement on the south-western side of Orodruin.'

'It is so strange to me, ${PLAYER}. This place is both alike to and very different from when I last was here at the close of the Second Age. For all the tumult within its heart, Orodruin seemed as if it would always endure. And yet, even the Mountain of Fire has changed since then: the southern face blown open, a lake of fire spilt onto the plain.
'This settlement was not here then, but I recognize its type. Military encampments have a sense of order and of place about them. Well do I know it, for I served beneath High King Gil-galad at Dagorlad and during the Siege!
'But once the campaign is ended, all such order is discarded alongside the attention of the commanders. This settlement, Fushaum Bal, has that air about it. Many inhabit it now, and lawlessness runs rampant, but some of the Easterlings within might be high enough in the hierarchy to have information of use to us. Hunt them down around Fushaum Bal and its environs, and see what they might know of the Gúrzyul.'

'I have never seen this city from the inside before. It is... it is quite a sight, ${PLAYER}. I believed that Sauron's armies were so near to victory, but now I am not certain. The city appears much stronger from up here.'
Ayorzén stands silently, gazing out over Minas Tirith. When he speaks again, his voice is low and quiet.
'I fought on the field down there. It is hard to tell, but I think I can see where my sworn men joined the battle. I slew many men myself, wielding swords, wielding axes. That is the way of war; if it was not to be their blood, it would have been mine. Eventually, things began to go wrong. Some of my sworn men were themselves slain. Others turned and ran.
'I ran with them. Later, when we formed up again, word came down that some of the leaders were dead: the Lord of the Nazgûl, maybe others. And I thought to myself, \qWhy should I die as well?\q I thought to take my men and go home, leave the war behind... but I received new orders. I was to set an ambush for the force that had started to march in the direction of Mordor.
'I left that task for the Orcs. I tried to lead my men home, and I was betrayed on the road. It was Ortakûl who betrayed me, the treacherous dog. He was rewarded with my command, and I was brought to Udûn, there to rot.'
Ayorzén clenches his fist.
'The Captain of the Pit, Ugrukhôr, did not plan to keep me there for long. He planned to send me to Agarnaith. Durthang was a nightmare, but it would be a pleasant daydream compared to that. Sweet Lara is there, ${PLAYER}. She is still there, and she is working on something behind the walls of Seregost. If you had not opened my cell, I would have been sent to Seregost, and death could not come quickly enough for Ayorzén the Unlucky.
'Once Sweet Lara got her claws in me... once she made me drink of her concoctions, her vile potions... I do not think I would be Ayorzén anymore. So I... I thank you for freeing me, ${PLAYER}, if for nothing else.
'Now that is done, and we will speak of it no more.'
Ayorzén shakes his head abruptly and laughs.
'Perhaps I was wrong! This city is not so strong after all. Do you see the cracks there, and there? Another hour or two, and Sauron would have had it quite in hand. You are lucky that his commanders were not as capable as I, Ayorzén the Strategic! You are lucky indeed in this, ${PLAYER}. So very lucky.'
'After you have visited the Houses of Lore, you should speak with the Easterling. He appears more willing to speak to you than any other.'
'You are lucky to have a friend such as Ayorzén the Knowing, ${PLAYER}.'

'Now Lhaereth has returned, and she is trying to finish her master work. Within the fortress of Seregost she seeks to create a strain of the plague that cannot be cured with athelas. She seeks to perfect the Great Plague.'

This musty tome provides a dry account of the Great Plague that ravaged Gondor beginning in the year 1636 of the Third Age. The forgotten scholar that wrote these pages noted that the plague arose somewhere in the East and many of the folk there were consumed by the disease before it spread to the Northmen of Rhovanion.
The account spends slightly longer detailing the effect of the Great Plague on the rule of Gondor, including the deaths of King Telemnar and all of his children, and the abandonment of Osgiliath for lack of men healthy enough to man its defences. The author of these pages mentions in passing that the watches at Minas Ithil, the Morannon, Ost Daethír, and Durthand were severely undermanned as a result of the disease, and you cannot help but wonder if he foresaw the problems that would cause in future days.
The account further notes the discovery that the leaves of the athelas plant were found to have a beneficial effect upon the progression of the plague, and that the disease finally ran its course in Gondor by the year 1637.

'There is one who has demonstrated a familiarity of this land to us. Do you remember? I do not trust him, for who truly could, but he has watched the movements of our enemies and knows somewhat of their motivations.
'I speak of Zaghárog, ${PLAYER}. The spirit in the stone may have seen more than we, and know of the place the Masters will settle upon for their council.'

There is silence in your mind for so long you begin to doubt that Zaghárog will speak to you. Then, just as you are about to turn away, the presence returns. The questioning sea buffets you as before.
'Where will the Masters seek to meet?' you ask of the spirit. The only reply is silence.
'Have such meetings occurred before?' you try again, but Zaghárog does not reply. The questioning sea recedes, leaving behind only sand and silt. Skeletal fish wriggle madly on the dry bed, gasping and dying.
Then you notice their number: nine fish die in the water's absence. The presence in the darkness that is Zaghárog watches you closely, and the fish are gone. A sudden flash of light blinds you with its brilliance, and you recognize a flat space with sparse trees near many falls, in the southern reaches of Lhingris. Hateful chittering fills your ears, and you know there is a malevolent creature behind you, but you are unable to turn and face it. Then you hear the voice of Atli Spider-bane, and you know he hunts the creature that stalks you.
Zaghárog makes his demand, and his desire fills your mind and echoes in your ears.
'Kill,' he says.

The images return. You recognize a flat space with sparse trees near many falls, in the southern reaches of Lhingris. Hateful chittering fills your ears, and you know there is a malevolent creature behind you, but you are unable to turn and face it. Then you hear the voice of Atli Spider-bane, and you know he hunts the creature that stalks you.
Zaghárog makes his demand, and his desire fills your mind and echoes in your ears.
'Kill,' he says.
'Thank you for finishing the job, ${PLAYER}! That was quite a fight!'
'I do not trust this creature, but he may have seen that which is hidden to us.'
'Zaghárog has proven he gives nothing for free, ${PLAYER}. What has he asked you to do this time?'
'You have done as the spirit asked. Now let us see if he will do as he promised.'
'They will meet to the north-west? That is all he has given us?'

'Of course! How did I not see it? Orodruin stands between the lands the Masters of Mordor have claimed for themselves, and on the slopes of Mount Doom they will feel most secure from the treachery of their rivals!
'That is where the meeting will take place, I am certain of it.'

Unlike your previous visit, Zaghárog does not make you wait this time. He is present immediately, with a hungering and eager need.
'The spider is slain,' you say, and Zaghárog's confusion is apparent. You see the hidden gully in Lhingris once again, and feel the stalking shadow, and hear Atli Spider-bane bellow his battle-cry. A feeling of great insistence spears at you, over and over.
'The spider,' you say once again, and Zaghárog responds at once: 'The dwarf.'
'No,' you respond.
You are buffeted by disappointment and anger. The spirit's rage is a crushing ceiling that presses down on you. It is a cauldron of boiling fire that scalds you. It is a torrent of icy rain that freezes and pierces your skin. It passes, and Zaghárog's rage is replaced with a sullen resentment.
'Where will the Masters meet?' you ask once again, and Zaghárog shows you the nine dying fish, inexplicably and inexorably breathing their last.
Finally, the images fade, and your feet are compelled to walk to the north-west. Zaghárog remains, nursing his disappointment, but you are confident that he has given you what you need.

'Where will the Masters meet?' you ask once again, and Zaghárog shows you the nine dying fish, inexplicably and inexorably breathing their last.
Finally, the images fade, and your feet are compelled to walk to the north-west. Zaghárog remains, nursing his disappointment, but you are confident that he has given you what you need.
Mount Doom fills your vision, and you know at once: the Masters will meet on the slopes of Orodruin

'You are up to something, ${PLAYER}. I overheard your directions for the tailor, and there can be only one reason for you to wear the clothes of the Nurnhoth. You plan to sneak into one of the fortresses in Mordor! Do not try to deny it. Ayorzén knows whatever you might say would be a lie; he is often called Ayorzén the Perceptive, after all.'
Ayorzén looks from side to side and shifts his weight from one foot to the other. When he speaks again, the words come in a rush and a tumble, as if he were embarrassed to speak them.
'There are none in this city that Ayorzén would consider a friend, but you may be nearest to that lofty prize, ${PLAYER}. If you do not get yourself killed climbing the walls of Seregost, or rattling the bars of Naerband, you might hope to achieve my friendship, in time! But Ayorzén does not befriend corpses.'
Ayorzén speaks more softly now, and his words are earnest in a way you have rarely heard from the Khundolar chief.
'I think you are a fool to attempt this, but I will share something with you in the hope that it may improve your chance of survival. The bosses pay no heed to their servants or their slaves, as long as they are obedient. That will change in an instant if the servant disobeys. You must do whatever you are commanded to do, or they will see through your disguise. This should serve you well with Ugrukhôr, Dulgabêth, or any of their minions.
'But there is one you should beware, in any circumstance. Whatever Urudanî has become, I do not think she will be blinded by your appearance. She may be more sensitive to your deception. You must try and keep away from Urudanî, at any cost.
'I have done all I can do, ${PLAYER}. It is more than anyone else would do, but this city is confusing and unpleasant, and if I am stuck here I would rather have someone such as you to hear my complaints. Keep that in mind when you sojourn on your foolish errand, and let it inspire you to subtlety!'
'As I told you already, I will do what I can. I will send the clothes along to you when they are finished.'
'Did you arrange for a disguise? It is nearly time!'

'You will need a disguise of some kind to get near to any of the Masters without their knowledge, but what sort of raiment will serve that purpose I cannot say.
'Mithrandir may know better than I, ${PLAYER}. Return to him in Minas Tirith and consult the Wizard, and I will continue to monitor Lhaereth's progress in plague-making.'

'The Gúrzyul, and indeed many others in Mordor, rely upon their slaves for labour and the many menial tasks that keep the iron wheel of Gorgoroth turning. As a result, obedient slaves often pass beneath notice; I suspect that the Masters of Mordor do not even see them, though they rely upon their presence. If you were to obtain the rags worn by the freed Nurnhoth that were brought to the city, a tailor in Minas Tirith might be able to fashion a suitable disguise for you.
'I last saw some of the freed Nurnhoth on the north-east side of the Third Circle, trying to become comfortable in their new home.'

'You are not here to send us back to Mordor? Promise me!'
Hujâ listens to your request, and slowly his look of fear is replaced with caution.
'You do not want to do this, ${PLAYER}. Arâm and Itli were in the service of Ugrukhôr's table, and the tales they have told of his cruelty are beyond belief. If you try to deceive him, you will be found out, and death could not come swiftly enough for you.
'I retained the clothes I wore in servitude, for some part of me believed I would not long be free of it. There was a part of me, too, that feared to dispose of them. Why? The reason must appear foolish to you, but I thought if I no longer had them at hand I would forget the time I spent in servitude, or the family and friends I lost in those years.
'I will give them to you for this reason, ${PLAYER}: that you will use them to help put an end to Ugrukhôr and the others like him, for Arâm and for Itli and for their families and mine. May they be of use to you, and I will try not to feel their loss overmuch. It will not be easy, but it will be worthwhile if this act helps free my people and puts an end to their misery and torment in Mordor.'
'We are... we are doing the best we can. It is not easy.'
'Every moment that comes I think we will be brought back. I cannot believe this will last.'

'You wish for me to modify these garments so you may wear them? Are you sure you would not prefer the latest fashions of the city instead? These are little more than dirty rags!
'Very well, I will do what I can. I will send them along to you when they are finished.'

'Good! We friends now. First thing, fix sickness! I discover making tasty drink from swamp stuff make it go away! Don't know how, don't care. You go get stuff, mix in bowl, and drink! All better. You and grumpy better drink it, too. You not sick now, but you will be! Here, I make you list.'

'So wanna know about Seregost and Blight Lady? I hear rumours while sneakin' around Uruks. Blight Lady, her name 'Lhaereth the Stained.' Kala-gijak Uruks serve her after Eye go away. They say she need 'test subjects,' workin' on some bad plague, kill lots of people. She strong, and she in Seregost. Only way into Seregost is to fly! So far, anyway, Viznak hasn't tried to get in yet. Hehe!
'You strong, but not strong enough to beat Blight Lady. Need an army! But, I know for sure Blight Lady not home right now. I help you sneak into Seregost, maybe I get some shinies, maybe you get some information. Sound good?'

'Parsâ-dhug-Bhêr has provided us with some useful information, but not enough to confront our enemies. We should return to Viznak's hideout and ensure Rhadrog's health has returned. There we can formulate a plan. I suspect Viznak knows more than he admits.'

'You're back! I'm feeling much better. Viznak has been keeping me company. You know, he is not so terrible, for a goblin. Don't tell Faeron I said that.
'Viznak told me you found a long-isolated village of Drúedain, earned their trust, and then helped them take out a fort full of Uruks! Is that true? How incredible! I am a bit ashamed that I managed to nearly die and was not there to help. It must have been some battle; I have not seen Faeron this happy since... well, ever.
'Viznak has been telling me about Seregost, and it honestly horrifies me. I am sure he will share what he knows with you as well if you ask him.'

'Glad to see Rhadrog is on his feet again. I am loath to say Viznak is trustworthy, but he at least seems to be keeping on our good side. I cannot think of a reason why he would be luring us into Seregost as a trap. His actions made clear that he is no ally of the Orcs and Uruks in this region.
'I think it is best we part ways for now, friend. Rhadrog and I will return to Udûn Foothold and report all we have learned. I will return with enough force to strike at the heart of Seregost. You work with Viznak, discover a way inside, and see what you can learn about this plague he mentioned.

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, just in time. My preliminary scouting has revealed some holes in Kala-gijak's defences. Exploit them, and we can win this battle with minimal casualties.

In the depths of the Mountain of Fire, Frodo Baggins at last reaches the Cracks of Doom, the only place where the One Ring can be destroyed. As he stands at the brink, he makes a decision that will determine the fate of the Ruling Ring and the power of Sauron that is bonded within.
But he is not alone...

'You know the truth now, ${PLAYER}. So many good people suffered, so many good people died, so that I could get to the Mountain. And at the end, I could not bring myself to do what everyone depended upon me to do! How can I live with the shame of it?'
You tell Frodo that what little you learned of the Ring during your own adventure has taught you that it was an artifact of great power and great evil, and that it could work its temptation upon even those of good hearts and strong will.
'Maybe you are right, ${PLAYER}. Your words do not erase my shame, but even though the Ring is gone I can still remember how I felt in that moment, standing above the Fire. I did not wish to destroy it. I would have rather died than allow it to be taken from me. I cannot imagine how Sméagol survived for so long after the Ring came to Bilbo. Or perhaps I can. It was the desire for it that drove him, and that feeling is familiar to me, and painful.
'Pippin worries that I will forget the details of my journey if I do not write them down? But the details are etched upon my memory. I cannot believe that I would forget how I felt in that moment. But perhaps I should write it all down. Perhaps I should write it all, and it will serve as a reminder and as a warning. A reminder that Good purpose can go ill, but that Evil purpose might still serve Good. And a warning not to judge either too readily.'

'Frodo has retired to the bower that was prepared for him. I will see that Samwise has a task to undertake that will free Frodo from his watchful gaze, and perhaps we can learn what still troubles our victorious Ringbearer.'
Frodo smiles weakly at you as you approach

'Frodo's ordeal in Mordor was a costly one, and it has left its mark upon him. No, I do not speak only of the finger he lost to Gollum's biting teeth! I speak of a mark that none can see, but still persists, casting a pall upon his heart.
'He has retired to the bower that was prepared for him. I will see that Samwise has a task to undertake that will free Frodo from his watchful gaze, and perhaps we can learn what still troubles our victorious Ringbearer.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. Gandalf came by and had a task for Sam; the two of them have gone off somewhere. If you're looking to speak with them they are not here right now. My mind is still caught in a whirlwind of confusion. I cannot believe that the Quest is over! I am not used to the idea that the Ring is gone! In Mordor, I would shut my eyes and still see it, burning inside my mind, tearing me apart. But it has been destroyed.
'Pippin insists that I write everything down before I forget the details, but... I do not want to remember them, ${PLAYER}. I do not! If my friends knew the truth about what happened within Mount Doom...'
Frodo shakes his head, and holds up his injured hand. It has been wrapped in a bandage and treated with care by Aragorn, but you remember the grisly sight of it.
'I laboured beneath the burden of the Ring as Sam and I crawled through Mordor and up the slope of Mount Doom. Much of the journey is hazy to me, even now, and dear Sam told our friends most of the tale. But he did not tell it all. I think he wanted to spare me the shame of it. Ah, that is the truth: shame, deserved shame!
'Sam said that Gollum tracked us to the Mountain, and at the end the pitiful creature overpowered us and stole the Ring before we could cast it into the Fire. But that is not the truth, not all of it.
'I... I will tell you the truth, ${PLAYER}. I want to do what is right.'
'I will tell you the truth of what happened inside Mount Doom, ${PLAYER}. I want to do the right thing.'

'Sauron is no more, and can no longer burden Middle-earth. Some of my folk may come to live in this land for a time, and I delight in knowing that it will remain green and growing for years to come, untroubled by Sauron's evil. But I will not stay long here.
'The first days of Gondor's new year will be filled with happiness, and I share the joy of its people, but my heart has another longing. The Sea calls to me, and I would follow.
'But I will not follow that longing just yet, ${PLAYER}. Food, and drink, and celebration must come first. We have all seen enough of darkness. Let us enjoy some lighter fare, and savour the taste!'
'Ah, ${PLAYER}. I am glad you have returned to me, for there is a small matter about which I wish to speak with you.'
'If Frodo says he's fine, I suppose it is all right. But I do wish he would get more rest! He went through a great deal in Mordor, as you know!'

'Three cheers for Frodo Baggins, who destroyed the Ring! And save a cheer or two for Samwise Gamgee, who got to go with him and managed to miss out on a great deal of the fighting! Oh, I'm only teasing. I know that Sam saw some danger, although he doesn't want to talk about any of it. Both he and Frodo are awfully tight-lipped about their journey in Mordor.
'I don't blame them. Battles are nasty things. Merry and I certainly ended up seeing more than our share, and it was all very dirty and confusing. I wouldn't recommend it! Do you know that a troll fell on top of me?
'It's easy to laugh about now that it's done, but no one was laughing when we were in the thick of the fighting. I am glad we are still here, ${PLAYER}. Three cheers for Frodo and his friends!'

'I am glad to have this time to catch up with Frodo and Sam. Pippin and I are knights of the City and of the Mark, respectively, and we have been kept busy with those duties. At last we can chat, and they do not want to talk about it, or at least not in the detail our curiosities demand!
'Well, I can respect that. After the Pelennor Battle I could barely stand to tell Pippin what befell poor Théoden. In time, perhaps it will become easier for them to talk about the journey. It was like that with Éowyn. By the time I left Minas Tirith to come here, she had emerged from silent sorrows and had taken to speaking with Steward Faramir in the gardens. It seems to me that time and distance helps many shadows lessen.
'I wonder why Éowyn has not yet arrived? Éomer King called her hither, but she has not yet come to Cormallen.'
'I do not think I want to speak of Mordor anymore, ${PLAYER}.'

'My uncle Théoden is avenged. Sauron is no more. It cannot be questioned that soldiers of Rohan and of Gondor played their parts, but in the end the fatal blow was struck by two hobbits alone in the Black Land. It is an amazement to me!
'I have heard that the Nazgûl came to fiery ends, speeding back to Mordor at their Master's call when he learned of his true peril. With my mind's sight I can see them, caught in the blast of the flaming mountain: eight fireballs scorching the sky, plummeting earthward and shrieking their final desperate cries.
'I wish that those of my soldiers who were carried aloft by those creatures during the Battle of the Black Gate could have known the fate their murderers would shortly suffer. It gives me great satisfaction to picture it on their behalf. Ride, Eorlingas, ride! You are avenged!'

'The fall of Sauron worked a great madness in his servants, ${PLAYER}, and many of them despaired once he was gone. Did some spell hold them ensorcelled while he yet lived, and death broke his hold upon them? I cannot say, but I did witness that many of the Orcs cast themselves into pits or fell upon their weapons once he was gone.
'There were others among his servants that were made more ferocious by the fall of their master, and these fought long and with desperation. Some of them fled back through the ruins of the gate; I do not doubt that my King will send me against these others, in time.
'But that is a thought for tomorrow. Today we celebrate the fall of Sauron!'

'That was quite a feast, and most well-deserved! It is not every day that an evil such as Sauron is laid low, after all! It seems as if Elrond and Gandalf made the right choice back in Rivendell, doesn't it? Frodo Baggins may not be a dwarf, but he has proven to have the determination of my kind!
'All these hobbits seem to have it! Young Peregrin Took could use a portion less of it, if you ask me. He is fortunate I saw him lying beneath that troll before the Black Gate, and heaved the great beast off him. I might have sworn up and down that he was dead, and yet he lives and is up and about already. He has caused me so much trouble, and yet still I am fond of him for all the bother.
'There will be days of merriment aplenty, ${PLAYER}, but sometime in the weeks ahead I must set my eyes to the north and return to the Lonely Mountain. My mind is full of ideas, and what dwarf wants that? I must speak to the King of Durin's Folk and let these ideas out before they do me some harm! Ha ha ha ha!'

Radanir looks at you grimly.
'I was speaking with some of the others, and they agree that you have a decision to make. Weigh your options carefully, ${PLAYER}, for this could be a costly choice.'
A rare smile illuminates Radanir's features.
'You need to choose the tavern at which we can all meet, now that the Grey Company has accomplished its mission and we have fulfilled our oaths. You agreed to buy me three mugs of ale, as I recall, so you will want to select an establishment with a barkeep who sets a reasonable price. I recommend the Forsaken Inn, east of Bree. The fare is of low quality, but it was Candaith's favourite, and that is enough for me.
'We will not depart just yet! There is work still to be done for Aragorn to claim his throne, and many of us wish to help him set his kingdom in order. Some of us will remain here in the south-lands, even when others return to their homes. I think I will travel with Lothrandir when he returns to Sûri-kylä; it is a long road, and he would welcome the company. Also, there is a lake on the way to Forochel, and I promised a friend I would see it for myself.'
'Now that he is awake, you should speak to Frodo. He is still recovering from his ordeal, but I know he will wish to see you.'
Sam beckons for you to speak to him instead of Frodo

'Do not let me keep you, ${PLAYER}! Our heroic friends have been through much, but I know they will want to speak with you now that the danger has passed! Frodo and Sam have rested from their journey, but it will take more than these few days to recover from the exertion of their ordeal!
'You will find them in a bower on the south-eastern side of the field.'

'Now that he is awake, you should speak to Frodo. He is still recovering from his ordeal, but I know he will wish to see you. You will find him in a pleasant bower in the south-east of the field of Cormallen.'

'I beg your pardon, ${PLAYER}, but Mister Frodo needs his rest. So many folk have come calling on him, some of them even bending the knee, and those who bowed the lowest were kings and princes themselves! Now, my master deserves every bit of it, but some of these even bowed to me, and I can't say I liked that at all! Frodo carried the real burden, and he did all the hard work, if you ask me.
'Can you believe that old Strider turned out to be a king as well? When I first met him, I said to myself, \qThis Strider has a kingly air about him, doesn't he, Sam?\q but I didn't say anything of it to my master or to Merry or Pippin. There was enough going on in Bree that there wasn't time for it.
'So many high important folk paying attention to hobbits! There's no mistaking that these are queer times!'

'Please forgive Sam, ${PLAYER}. He has spent so long worrying about me that I think it became natural for him, especially after our experience in Mordor.'
Frodo shivers, despite the warmth in the air.
'I know Sam does not want to talk about it, but I would never have made it to the Fire without him. If you had the joy of knowing old Hamfast, you would know that Gamgees love to talk, but the Gaffer and his son would prefer most any topic to speaking about themselves. So it falls on me to tell you that I may have carried the burden, but it was the strength of my dear Sam that guided me through despair and across the dead lands. And at Mount Doom...'
Frodo's face is pale, and he stops speaking. He seems relieved when Pippin breaks the silence with a boisterous cheer.

'Frodo has earned his rest, ${PLAYER}. His adventure has ended. And yet, Middle-earth still has need of heroes. Gondor will need you, as will others among the Free People: dwarves, Elves, and hobbits. Be ready for their call, my friend. A great evil of the world has departed, but there are others that will need heroes to face them.
'Do not face them alone! Some measure of the strength of Sauron was bound to his Ring, but much of his strength was derived from his mastery over the weak, and the weak of will. I foresee that some of those freed from his dominance will seek to gain advantage from his fall. The shroud over Gorgoroth is a veil that must be pierced if Middle-earth is to live free from fear.
'Frodo will write the tale of his adventure, but the next adventure will be yours alone to write. My own time on these shores is drawing to a close, for my purpose is ended.'
You look at him with the dawning understanding that his charge was to combat Sauron, and now that the Dark Lord is defeated, the Wizard must leave Middle-earth.
'Oh, do not look at me like that, foolish ${RACE}! I am not leaving tomorrow! I will not depart until I know things are well in hand, and your kind has not yet proven that you are able to manage on your own!'
He stands there spluttering for a moment. There is a twinkle in his eye when he speaks again, and he seems less like Mithrandir, or any of his many other names, and most like he was when you first met him: Gandalf.
'I will say this to you, and it will be my last word on the subject: As for this business with the Ring, I commend you on a job well-done, my dear ${PLAYER}. Very well-done indeed!'

'I am ready to have a rest, and an end to adventuring. I shall be content just to see Bilbo again, and to return to the Shire. I will write down my part of the Quest of the Ring, all of it, and I will be thankful for the opportunity to live in peace!'
'Aragorn has asked to speak with you, ${PLAYER}.'

'We have come through the long night to the dawn at last, ${PLAYER}! Many were the days I believed all my choices were going wrong, but despite those errors, we have seen the destruction of the Ring and the downfall of Sauron!
'When Frodo completed his task, Mordor was shaken to its very foundations by the eruption of Orodruin. The Black Gate and the Towers of the Teeth crumbled and fell, but who can say what lies behind them in the land that was Sauron's? There is a shroud over the plateau of Gorgoroth, and it masks our sight.'
Aragorn smiles wryly.
'I have not yet been crowned King, but already I am thinking about Gondor's future! Can we not have one day of satisfied peace? Sauron is no more! There will be a new ordering of the calendar to mark the occasion. In the Kingdom of Gondor, the New Year will now begin on March twenty-fifth, the day on which Sauron fell and hope was restored to Middle-earth. There are still many preparations to be made before I can ascend to the throne of Gondor, but today is a day of celebration. My friends and my kin have earned this day of victory! Enjoy this day, ${PLAYER}, for you too were instrumental in its arrival!'
'Today is a day of celebration. My friends and my kin have earned this day of victory! Enjoy this day, ${PLAYER}, for you too were instrumental in its arrival!'

'Thank you for easing my mind and my heart, ${PLAYER}. Gandalf has returned, and now I think I see the makings of a conspiracy! But thank you for the kind words, and I give my thanks to Gandalf as well. I am very fortunate to have such friends as you!
'I am ready to have a rest, and an end to adventuring. I shall be content just to see Bilbo again, and to return to the Shire. I will write down my part of the Quest of the Ring, all of it, and I will be thankful for the opportunity to live in peace!'

'I am glad to hear that Frodo has decided to write down his tale, after all. It has been my experience that sometimes a hobbit simply needs a bit of a push to get started on a thing, but once he has set his mind to do it the results are often admirable.
'I trust you told Frodo that no one could willingly have destroyed the Ring? I meant to return more quickly and tell him that, but Samwise grew suspicious that I was wasting his time and required more assurances or he would hastily return to his master. Wasting his time! Me!'
Mithrandir chuckles mirthfully.
'I was, of course, but that is neither here nor there. All that matters in the end is that you have assuaged Frodo's concerns and helped him come to terms with his experience. He deserves that and more for the deed he has done on behalf of Middle-earth.
'But enough chattering. Aragorn has asked to speak with you, ${PLAYER}.'

'Have you come to take me out from this place of my certain death or have you come to tell me only that my words rung true?'
You explain to Lômazar that he will be taken out of Mordor once the situation in Dor Amarth has improved.
'It seems I may be dwelling in this company for a time then. Be warned, it should be known that some of the relics Dulgabêth pursues are much more powerful than one of your ilk could imagine. You may have thwarted his efforts thus far, but let it be known, hidden objects lie in wait below the fortress of Barad-dûr.'

'Lômazar has been truthful with us up to this point, ${PLAYER}. While I have my doubts, it is not impossible that Sauron would have put such thought and effort into collecting many a valuable and powerful relic. You say that you have seen some of these already? Then perhaps we must act sooner than later in preventing The Black Word from finding any more lost trinkets of Sauron.'

'I say again, you must give your promise to send me away from these lands. Even rotting in a dungeon until the end of days would be better than endless pain and torture at the hand of the Black Word.'
You give your word that Lômazar will be treated fairly as a prisoner.
'Good. Now listen closely, as I have not the strength nor will to repeat what I am about to say.
'I do not know why only the most important and awe-inspiring bits fell to earth while much of the city remains. Dulgabêth the Black Word, known to you as the Mouth of Sauron, has claimed what still stands of Barad-dûr. He has many followers, myself once included. Now Dulgabêth seeks to rule all of Mordor and take Sauron's place, by use of powerful relics buried within the tower's walls. None will oppose him. His faithful servants are not to be trifled with either. Glúrugoth, the Hole-warden. Sapakár the Cleaver. Krassa-phûrsa, Bringer of Tears. These are all names that strike fear upon mention.
'Do you now possess the knowledge you seek?'
Lômazar explains to you all he knows of Dulgabêth's plans.

'If I speak to thee, Dulgabêth shall have me killed. The Black Word is not one to be reckoned with.'
'My name is Lômazar. I was once a faithful servant to Dulgabêth. I have made more than one mistake and as punishment was struck blind. To escape further torment, I severed my bonds, only to be captured again and brought here.'
'Perchance, will you spare me torment inside the walls of Mordor in the exchange of knowledge?'
'I have nothing to say to the likes of you.'

'As we have fought together on the Pelennor, I well know you can protect yourself. Still, the plains of Gorgoroth are filled with fires and crevasses caused by the eruption of Mount Doom. It is a dangerous place and we must tread carefully.
'Our first scouting party has just returned, and with them, they bring a captive. The man they have captured is a Black Númenórean servant. He refuses to speak to us. We must either persuade him of our cause or somehow convince him to talk.
'I was hoping that you would try speaking to the man. See if you can find out what he knows and who he serves.'
You question the captive. The man seems to have no interest in anything you tell him or any question you ask.

'Moreover, you have seen the Abyss of Mordath. Indeed, that great chasm is a place of horror. I shudder to think what still lives down there.'
'What, you are going to try and stop me? Ha ha. Good luck with that, little ${RACE}!'

'I sent down servants to bring back treasures and useful things for the Black Word. I sent them down quickly, but no one comes back! Good you are here. I can send you down real quick too. I must get something for the Black Word.'

'You have spoken to Coldan? He has decided to depart and take this news to Lothlórien. While I do not blame him for his excitement, I do wish that Coldan had consulted me first. My young apprentice has much to learn.
'I assume you have also spoken to Legolas. He shares my impatience to retrieve Aiglos and remove it from Mordor.'

You relay the information to Coldan.
'I cannot believe these words! To think this relic and pride of Elves has been recovered. I know what I must do then. I shall depart at once and inform those in Lothlórien of this news.'

'I have seen the spear with my own eyes, ${PLAYER}. Not that I disbelieved you, but you understand it is hard to believe.
'When you are ready to depart, we shall venture again to the site of Aiglos.'

'Legolas has scouted the location of the spear and informed me that it is indeed the lost spear of Aiglos. I understand that you might not share the same enthusiasm as I, but let it be known to you that this relic is of great pride to all Elves. During the Second Age, Gil-galad wielded Aiglos on the slopes of Mount Doom, lending to the defeat of Sauron. I know this, for I was there.
'Go, speak with my apprentice, Coldan. He should hear the news. Also I would like you and Legolas to retrieve the spear.'

'I know not what Krassa-phûrsa seeks. As I stated, she is a mystery. I do know the hills of Ered Lithui are a place of shadow that no Orc will set foot upon. There may be ancient, forgotten items there. If Krassa-phûrsa knew of something in the hills, it is remembered only by her.'

'I saw the wraith! She went towards the north! Don't kill me!'

'You have done much to weaken those who serve under The Black Word. If we are to make a stand against those of power in Dor Amarth, now is the time. Speak with Lômazar and see what else he knows. The captive won't say a word to me, but he has taken a liking to you.'
'I cannot identify the weapon we saw at a distance, but murmurs of excitement have swept through the encampment. Perhaps it is best to speak to Hithgol about it?'

'I have nothing else to say. Although… what have you heard of the Ithil-stone? Nothing?
'Dulgabêth seeks the powerful Ithil-stone to sway others, just as Sauron had done. For that reason alone it means much to Dulgabêth and many others. Ownership of the stone will gain Dulgabêth many allies in Mordor.'
'I am convinced. Let us go to Barad-dûr, ${PLAYER}. We shall scout the area together and plan our attack!'
'I have heard the rumours, ${PLAYER}. If your eyes have not been cruelly deceived, the missing spear of Aiglos may have been discovered.'

'Legolas has spoken to me and explained why we must not retrieve the spear of Aiglos from atop the spire it rests upon in Dor Amarth.
'Though it pains me not to remove the sacred weapon of the Elves from Mordor, I must agree with him.
'Aiglos has given hope to those of Elves and others in this company. The spear has become a beacon in Mordor, a banner planted, to show all those that the time of darkness in Mordor is at a close.
'The light of Aiglos will show the way for us and strike fear in those who believe they lay claim to the plains of Gorgoroth.
'Perhaps one day we will be able to construct a monument to Gil-galad and to all Elves who fought valiantly against Sauron, here in Dor Amarth, where Aiglos lies.'

You confront the devoted member of The Order of The Eye and ask him why they seek the spear.
'You know not the story? Indeed you are a fool, but I shall enlighten thee.
'In Sauron's great trickery, an Elf bearing this mighty spear fell into the Dark Lord's trap. The Elf perished, releasing the spear from his grasp. Many thought the spear lost, but it was not, for the Dark Lord knew of it. When his strength returned, Sauron retrieved the spear and kept it high in his tower as a remembrance to all who dare defy his rule.
'Rabôkhor, the leader of our sect, shall soon scale the spire and hold the spear in his hands.'
You decide you must find this Rabôkhor and show The Order of The Eye that the spear can never be wielded by them.

'${PLAYER}, I am not sure if we should scale the spire either. I have been thinking about it and would like to speak with Hithgol.
'Let us return to him and hear his thoughts on the matter.
'I know, we have come all this way, but you must trust me, as I have trusted you many times.
'Now let us depart.'

'It cannot be. You held the sacred idol of our sect up to the spear and now it is gone! Why would Sauron keep such an object of destruction when we could never use it?'
You tell the devoted member of The Order to share what he has seen today.
'No more shall we worship such a horrid object. I feel sickened being near it! If only I had the strength to slay you, ${RACE}!'

'You spoke to one of these devoted of The Order, yes? Perhaps we should find out why they are pursuing this mighty spear of the Elves.
'We must not let Aiglos fall into their hands. None but Gil-galad would be worthy to hold the spear.
'It is said that Aiglos can be touched by few, for the spear's power is great.'

'Han llegado noticias a mis oídos desde Lothlórien, camarada, y no sé qué pensar de ellas. Thranduil, Señor del Bosque Negro, se encuentra allí, pero ¿con qué propósito? En estos tiempos, la razón no puede ser ligera ni alegre.
'Sea cual sea el caso, Legolas puede desear estar al lado de su padre Thranduil. ¿Irás a Dor Amarth y le contarás todo lo que te he dicho?'
'Ve a ver a Legolas en Dor Amarth y dile que su padre, el rey Thranduil, ha llegado a la Corte de Lothlórien.'

'¿Dónde escuchamos esta noticia? Uno de los grandes Águilas avistó a Thranduil y a un pequeño grupo de sus parientes entrando en Caras Galadhon. Fue un vistazo fugaz, incluso para una bestia de vista tan aguda, y no pudo decirnos mucho más.'

'Al final, nuestras pérdidas fueron grandes, pero no tanto como las de nuestro enemigo. Se han retirado a sus fortalezas sombrías, heridos pero no tan dañados como para que no puedan causarnos problemas nuevamente. Por eso debemos elegir nuestras acciones con cuidado y reunir toda la sabiduría antes de actuar.'

'Estamos de hecho recién salidos de la batalla, como observa Legolas. Contra el dominio de su padre y el nuestro marcharon las fuerzas del Enemigo, incluso mientras la guerra se libraba en el lugar de donde has llegado. ¿Es de extrañar que el enemigo ponga en marcha todos sus planes a la vez?'

Legolas escucha las noticias con el ceño fruncido.
'Mi padre no se alejaría tanto de su dominio si la ocasión no fuera grande, y como Elladan, temo razones oscuras más que felices. Sí, creo que debo ir y aprender lo que ha pasado entre mis primos y mi gente.
'¿Viajarás conmigo, ${PLAYER}? Los kilómetros pasarán rápidamente con compañía y me resulta difícil separar a Gimli de esto, justo ahora. Estaré más feliz sabiendo que pronto me reuniré con él aquí.'
<rgb=#FF0000>Avanzar te teletransportará directamente a la Corte de Lothlórien.</rgb>

'¿Has venido para el Consejo de Guerra? Si no, es una extraña coincidencia que te traiga aquí ahora.
'¡Oh, no quiero parecer poco acogedor! Adelante, acércate al consejo. Sin duda tienes noticias y estoy seguro de que tendrán en cuenta tus palabras. ¡Aún están esperando y no pueden hacer nada todavía!'

'El tiempo de observar y esperar ha pasado por completo, o casi. Me gustaría moverme para retaliar rápida y absolutamente. Aunque este Señor y Dama no están en desacuerdo, en general, sienten que aún debemos esperar la llegada de otro, antes de hacerlo.'

'Esperamos la llegada del Elfo, Glorfindel, ${PLAYER}. Sin él, este consejo no está completo y siento que no podemos actuar.
'Me puse en contacto con él tan pronto como pude y juró que vendría con toda la rapidez posible. Aún no temo lo peor, y sin embargo, el hecho de que no haya llegado es preocupante.
'Tu llegada, amigo, es un consuelo, y tu servicio a nuestra causa alivia aún más mis temores. Poco más podemos hacer ahora, pero pronto, estoy seguro, nos volveremos a encontrar. Debemos esperar que para entonces, Glorfindel esté con nosotros.'
'Me quedaré aquí brevemente para hablar con mi padre. Tú regresa a Mordor. Como dijo la Dama Galadriel, seguramente nos volveremos a ver pronto.'
'Escucha, y te contaré sobre la Batalla Bajo los Árboles.'

'Mi corazón me dice que tienes un relato tan grande como el nuestro, no, creo que mayor. El hecho de que tu rostro no esté angustiado y agotado de esperanza me dice mucho, ¡pero quiero escuchar más!'
Dirigiéndote a todo el consejo, describes brevemente todos los eventos de la guerra entre el Pelennor y las Puertas Negras.
Un silencio cae sobre los presentes una vez que terminas.
'¡Entonces son noticias alegres!' pronuncia Galadriel, al fin. 'Y tales como se cantarán y contarán durante mucho tiempo. Aunque incluso los cambios más alegres vienen con un matiz de tristeza para nosotros que hemos vivido aquí durante tanto tiempo y nos hemos separado de tanto.'

'Saludos, ${CLASS}. Mi hijo viaja en compañía extraña, parece, pero estos son tiempos extraños y es a través de grandes penas que he aprendido recientemente la diferencia entre un extraño y un enemigo.
'Has contado tu historia de manera excepcional y llena mi corazón de asombro. Nosotros también hemos soportado mucho, y en nuestra historia hay mucho, creo, que deberías saber.'
'Ahí está mi padre Thranduil,' susurra Legolas. '¡Mira, están vestidos como si acabaran de salir de la batalla!'

'¡Ah, ahí está nuestro viajero veloz! He reservado un tiempo para ti. Ven, cuéntame los eventos en el Este.'
Le cuentas a Elrond todo lo que presenciaste en Gondor, desde los Senderos de los Muertos, pasando por Pelargir, el Pelennor, y hasta las Puertas Negras; de la caída de Théoden, el Último Debate, y lo que sabes de los propios viajes de Sam y Frodo. Hablas de lo que has visto en la tierra quebrada de Mordor. Finalmente, relatas las noticias de la Batalla Bajo los Árboles, y cómo Lothlórien espera la llegada de Glorfindel.
Elrond guarda silencio mientras escucha, y cuando terminas, asiente con la cabeza.
'Mucho de esto lo había adivinado, pero no todo, ni siquiera la mitad. Que Glorfindel haya dado su palabra de venir a Lothlórien y no esté allí me preocupa. No temo lo peor, y sin embargo, siento, de alguna manera, que tu camino está entrelazado con el suyo, y que ambos tienen un papel que desempeñar en estos eventos que pronto se desarrollarán.
'Dame estos libros que Arwen te pidió reunir. Ella tiene razón al llamarme de nuevo a asuntos serios, incluso en esta hora feliz. A cambio, toma estas semillas. Son un regalo para el futuro rey en Gondor, que llegará algún tiempo antes de que sea el prometido de Arwen.
'Ahora, adiós, ${PLAYER}. Hasta que nos encontremos de nuevo.'

'Ah, esos son todos los paquetes. Bien, ahora colócalos allí. Déjame contarlos.
'Sí... eso está bien... de hecho, todos están contabilizados.
'Excelente. Ahora puedes recoger el montón y llevarlo a las forjas para que se empaqueten para el transporte.'
'Aquí, estas son todas las cuerdas y tejidos que me pidieron. ¡Que les concedan un viaje rápido y fácil!'

'He trabajado muchas horas en estos finos y espléndidos atavíos. Asegúrate de que se manipulen con cuidado y se empaqueten bien. Viajaré con el señor Elrond y la dama Arwen y los veré al otro lado, ¡así que lo sabré!'
'Me entregaron estos paquetes de bienes para ser enlatados para el viaje sin decirme a dónde llevarlos. ¡Aquí, son tuyos!'
'Estos son cuchillos de mesa y hachas de madera para el grupo de viaje. ¿Qué, pensaste que todo lo que hacía eran espadas para aventureros?'
'Estamos en deuda contigo, ${PLAYER}. Si aún no has terminado de ser útil, podrías buscar a Pethelen justo afuera de la casa. Creo que está encargado de las tareas de aprovisionamiento.'
'Aquí tienes todas las mantas y el alimento necesarios para el viaje. ¡Con cuidado, es una carga pesada!'

'Es normal que una futura novia sueñe con un futuro prometedor, pero ¿cómo vamos a encontrar tiempo para preparar el vestido antes de partir? ¿Y si no está listo, tendremos que llevar las diferentes piezas de tela? ¿Y qué flores se pueden encontrar en el lejano Gondor? ¿Habrá que bordar lirios en los dobladillos, mientras que quizás encontremos campanillas y muchas otras flores bonitas en nuestro camino?
'Rivendel está lleno de sabiduría y conocimientos, pero no sabemos nada sobre cómo adornan los hombres de Gondor sus vestidos de novia.
'Temo que no tengamos otra opción que llevarlo todo y arreglárnoslas cuando lleguemos. ¡Y mi señora solo se preocupa por encontrar libros y semillas!'

Arwen se ríe suavemente, un tintineo de campanillas.
'Quizás soy negligente, Eliaril, pero debo agradecerte por recordarme las semillas. Aquí, ${PLAYER}. Toma estas, semillas de la Flor de Celebég. Son un regalo de Rivendel para el futuro rey. Porque eso vendrá antes de que sea mi prometido.
'Te pediría que hicieras otra cosa por mí, ${PLAYER}. Hay varios libros en los estantes de mi padre que no habría dejado atrás. Algunos se refieren a asuntos de importancia actual, otros dan orientación para los desafíos que mi Elfstone enfrentará como rey. ¿Te asegurarás de que lleguen a manos de mi padre?'
'Adiós, ${PLAYER}. Te veré en Gondor, si no antes, espero.'

'¿Reuniste todos los paquetes y luego los entregaste en las Forjas?'
Pethelen se ríe.
'Has hecho tanto como cualquiera aquí para preparar este viaje, creo. ¡No más trabajos para ti, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}! Mientras estabas en el mercado, la Dama Arwen se enteró de tu llegada y suplicó verte. Ella está dentro de Imlad Gelair.
'No te preocupes si nunca has estado allí. Serás ${PLAYERNAME:admitido[m]|admitida[f]} por su palabra ahora.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, eres tú. Pensé que debía haber oído mal cuando me dijeron que estabas en Rivendel.
'Podría hacerte mil preguntas, pero no, me abstendré. Sé que nuestros mayores temores se han desvanecido y eso es suficiente. Espero con ansias escuchar la historia completa al final del viaje.
'Conoces el propósito de esta peregrinación, ¿verdad? Nos dirigimos a Gondor, donde Aragorn - quiero decir Elessar - y yo nos casaremos, como nos prometimos hace mucho tiempo.
'¿Ves, Eliaril? No he olvidado ni descuidado la boda que nos espera al final de nuestro viaje. Tal vez puedas persuadirla de que no es algo por lo que preocuparse o inquietarse, ${PLAYER}.'

Lindir se ríe.
'Es cierto, ¡no puedes alegar enfermedad y edad como hace el Maestro Bilbo! De hecho, no rechazaremos la ayuda que se nos ofrece, ya que deseamos emprender nuestro viaje con cierta rapidez. ¡En cualquier lugar dentro de estos muros donde veas que se está empacando, eres bienvenido a echar una mano!'

'No pensé que te vería aquí tan pronto, ${PLAYER}. Me alegra el corazón, ¡porque solo puedes haber venido con buenas noticias!'
El Elfo con el que hablaba mira con significado y una sombra cruza el ceño de Elrond.
'Temo que hay varios asuntos a los que debo atender, y no pueden esperar. Perdona esta descortesía, ${PLAYER}. Si regresas en breve, me gustaría hablar más contigo.
'¿Por qué no vas a visitar a Bilbo el Mediano? Él estaría tan contento de verte como yo. Estará en el Salón del Fuego como siempre.'

'¿Deseas ayudar, ${CLASS}? ¡Qué buena voluntad entre los pueblos libres!
'He enviado varias solicitudes al mercado y se necesita a alguien para llevar esas cosas a las forjas para empacarlas en cajas y barriles. Tendrás que preguntar entre los comerciantes y artesanos. Me temo que algunos otros bienes han quedado por ahí. Todos están muy ocupados.'

'¡Todo este ir y venir... es agotador! Le digo a Lindir que es muy poco élfico de su parte, pero él solo me pregunta si me molestaría irme sin MI pipa y mi pañuelo. ¡Hmph!
'Bueno, yo no me voy, aunque echaré de menos ver al viejo Dúnadan con toda su corona y gloria. A Frodo y sus amigos los volveré a ver, pues pasarán por aquí. Elrond me lo asegura.
'Ah, pero toda esta charla me ha cansado, ${PLAYER}. ¡Me alegra haberte visto! Pero ahora creo que debo volver a estar en silencio, mirando el fuego y trabajando en las palabras de esta nueva canción.
'¿Por qué no le preguntas a Lindir si puedes ayudar? ¡Casi todos menos yo están colaborando!'

'Pocos viajan con la rapidez que tú lo haces, ${PLAYER:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. ¿Podrías apresurarte a Rivendel y ver cómo van las cosas? 'You may walk here in Fushaum if you like, but do not dwell too long. Not all of the men here are as compassionate as myself.'
Thâng wipes his blade upon his clothes.
'All we ask is that you leave the treasures of Mordor to their rightful owners. If you wish to help us, we will certainly reward you before we depart for Harad.'

'Any are welcome if not plotting to oust us. Thâng and I are rulers of Fushaum. As least we were until that Khirgi moved in. All we want is to collect what is rightfully ours and return to the east. Sauron promised us much and gave very little. Now he is gone and can trick us no longer.'

'I could have killed you like that.'
Khirgi snaps his fingers to simulate your death.
'Instead I was intrigued, so here you are, ${RACE}. You must wish to serve me, for I can think of no other reason you would seek an alliance.'
You decide to play along with Khirgi's assumption.
'I used to be in charge at Fushaum Tum, until that Olog, Thorakó usurped me! Now all I have to claim is the north side of Fushaum Bal until our forces are strong enough to seek revenge upon Thorakó for reducing me to this!
'Help see my plan through, and you will be greatly rewarded.'

'¿Te parece un acertijo lo que hemos visto esta noche? La luz era Lothlórien; o más bien, era yo misma; o más bien, era este anillo que llevo en mi dedo.'
De repente, puedes ver un anillo en su dedo, brillante como una estrella lejana.
'Y la oscuridad con la que competía era Dol Guldur. En el Espejo vimos dos posibilidades de lo que podría venir. Podemos abandonar nuestra lucha contra estos enemigos, y su poder crecerá y crecerá. O podemos extinguirlos... pero nosotros mismos siempre -- disminuidos. No puedo decirlo, precisamente. No pude ver tan claramente como estaba acostumbrada.
'Porque en verdad, algunos de mis poderes están fallando, ya sea que guerreemos contra Dol Guldur o no. Este anillo que te revelé hace un momento fue forjado en los mismos días en que el Señor Oscuro forjó su Único. Aunque siempre estuvo oculto para él y su propio poder se mantuvo seguro, aún así los anillos estaban ligados. Celebrimbor, por todo lo que hizo, no pudo romper ese vínculo, me temo. Ahora que el Único ya no existe, todos los demás se desvanecen y flaquean. Dudo que alguna vez vuelva a ver claramente dentro de mi Espejo, y mucho más se perderá para mí.
'Aun así, pagaría el precio de nuevo, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos.'

'Supongo que esto debe ser un vistazo al destino de los mortales, saber que todo lo que apreciamos se nos escapa. Es una sabiduría que hasta ahora me había sido en gran parte negada.
'No vacilaré en actuar, aunque el precio sea alto. Ven, ${PLAYER}, volvamos a la Corte y a nuestro consejo de guerra que nos espera.'

'Párate junto a mí. Mira en el Espejo conmigo. En verdad, no sé lo que veré aquí, aunque hay mucho que me gustaría saber si pudiera. Sin embargo, estoy segura de que ahora es el momento y que no debemos esperar.
'¿Quieres empezar?'

The carven stone does not move. There is a stillness in the air.
Again a mist envelopes you and the colours and light seems to fade. This time, the mist grows into a dense, dry fog until you can see nothing in front of you.
Images start to form in the fog. You see a young child fall playing in a field of arid grasslands. She stumbles and falls into a well. Time passes and you see the girl's parents mourning over the well. Time continues to pass, more rapidly this time. The arid plains become burnt. A mountain appears and bursts into flame. A vile statue is built over the well.
Suddenly, everything is returned to as it was. Ash and wind blow through the lifeless terrain.

As you approach the large carven stone, a strange, translucent mist starts to fill the air. The colours around you start to fade as if you are seeing a dream through someone else's eyes.
The unmoving stone seems to turn towards you. As it does, the air begins to feel damp and humid. Drops of water roll drown the face of the carven stone like tears down the face of a small child. Soon, everything is covered in a fine layer of cool mist.
Suddenly a string of words come to you: 'Cleanse, Ashronk, Krulronk, Gakhronk, Zagronk.'
Are these places that you know? It seems as if someone is speaking these thoughts to you.
As you start to ponder these words, the colour returns and the water vanishes. It is replaced by the expected, dry, scorched earth, created by the Ghâshghurm.
You believe the stone requires something of you.

The spite and anger start to fade. Still, the piercing gaze consumes you.
The low whispering begins to fade as well. The emotions the stone projects into your head are hard to make out. You see a turbulent flash of colours, then an overwhelming sensation of defeat. You see a man, slain by a Morgul blade. His life flashes, and his spirit is torn from his body. The body falls and topples on to the spirit. The spirit tries to escape but it seems to be unable to move. Slowly the slain body turns into twisted stone.
The dreamlike image fades and you are once again able to focus. A voice in your head again speaks. This time with no anger, only sadness. It says, 'leave.'

As you approach the carven stone, a sense of dread surrounds you. A nearby gaze envelops you. It is not a living gaze, but an ancient sight bored into your mind.
You start to hear whispers, of many voices, and languages. You cannot make out a single word. Then you start to notice an anger, a pure, spiteful, malice in all the whispers.
The whispers and spite seem to start focusing on you. They become one and focus into a single word. The statue seems to say, 'leave.'
You try to leave, but the spirit's hold is too heavy to break.

'Pensé que lo sabía todo sobre el Balrog Thaurlach. ¡Qué equivocado estaba! Aún me queda mucho por aprender.'

'Sentí la presencia oscura acechando cerca cuando entré por primera vez en este lugar, pero el premio que buscaba era demasiado importante y no iba a dejarme disuadir. Aún así, esperaba escabullirme tan silenciosamente como llegué, y en cambio casi caminé directamente hacia su boca abierta!
'Sin embargo, la fortuna me sonrió, y ustedes llegaron justo en ese momento. Ningún guerrero más poderoso de Elfos o Hombres se enfrentaría a un Balrog solo, voluntariamente, aunque aún me halago de que podría haber sido su igual.
'No deberíamos demorarnos aquí, creo. He encontrado lo que vine a buscar, aunque debo tomarme un tiempo en paz aislada para leerlo y penetrar su significado más profundo. Sin embargo, no puedo detenerme demasiado tiempo, porque se me espera en la Corte de Lothlórien. Ah, pero veo que ya lo sabías.
'Quizás, entonces, puedan hacerme un doble favor. Primero, regresen allí de inmediato y aseguren a Galadriel y Celeborn que estoy en camino. Segundo, díganle a Galadriel que deseo darle la Gwedluith que le confié a Arwen, como regalo de compromiso. De hecho, me gustaría que ustedes le llevaran el regalo a ella, ${PLAYER}.'

'No es fácil matar a un Balrog. Aunque puedan parecer derrotados, pueden curarse e incluso recuperar su forma con el tiempo. Esta lección la he aprendido, dolorosamente, en épocas pasadas.
'Afortunadamente, poseo el arte necesario para extinguir por completo a tal enemigo. Ven y lucha a mi lado. Juntos pondremos fin de una vez por todas a este vil sirviente de Morgoth.'

'${PLAYER}, debemos buscar pistas sobre el paradero de Glorfindel.
'No sabemos qué acecha en la Grieta de Nûrz Ghâshu ahora, así que prepárate.'
'Es hora de abandonar este lugar. Debo aislarme un poco y considerar la profecía de Gil-galad que he encontrado. Luego, tan pronto como pueda, encontraré mi camino hacia Caras Galadhon.'
