'Ah, ${CLASS}. Eres como la gaviota que sigue la vela llevada por el viento. Glorfindel ha estado aquí y se ha ido de nuevo. Lo saludé de pasada, pero creo que se fue de aquí habiendo encontrado lo que buscaba. ¿Quizás fue uno de los textos aquí? Mira por ti mismo y ve si puedes encontrarlo.'

'¿Qué es esto? Es un registro muy antiguo, de hecho. Creo que probablemente has encontrado lo que buscabas. Si fuera tú, lo llevaría a Celeborn y Galadriel en Lórien. Ellos sabrán perfectamente qué hacer con ello.
'Pero antes de hacerlo, toma esto. Son vainas de Parthríf, y crecerán en helechos de una complejidad y forma poco comunes. Es un regalo digno de un nuevo rey.'

'Ah, ${PLAYERNAME:querido amigo[m]|querida amiga[f]}. He estado pensando en el regalo de semillas que se te confió en Imladris. Debo confesar que me siento invadido por la envidia. Si pudiera reunir una docena de helechos y flores que se encuentran en el Bosque Negro... pero este viaje me ha llevado lo suficientemente lejos de Mordor y de mi amigo, Gimli.
'Si te diriges a lugares donde habitan los Elfos, quizás podrías pedirles tales regalos. Los reuniremos juntos, y ¡qué hermoso jardín tendrá el nuevo rey Elessar!'

La elfa parpadea ante ti con incredulidad.
'¿Eres tú... ${PLAYER}? Soy yo, Glathlírel. ¿No me reconoces? He cambiado mi hermosa armadura por la ropa de viajera.
'¿Significa esto que tú también has venido en busca de Glorfindel? No sé si debo alegrarme por esta coincidencia o tomarla como una señal más oscura. Pero dime, ¿por qué has venido?'
Le cuentas a Glathlírel sobre la Batalla Bajo los Árboles y el consejo de guerra en la Corte de Lothlórien.
'Entonces tienes una mejor razón para buscarlo que yo, que he venido solo por un sueño inquietante. ¿Has oído hablar de los Elfos que viven escondidos en una cueva en Belfalas? Se llaman Avorrim. ¿Por qué no buscas allí a una llamada Dorthaneth? Es sabia más allá de sus años. Iré hacia el oeste, a Lindon, y lo buscaré allí. Luego nos encontraremos de nuevo en la Corte de Galadriel.
'Ah, y por último, por extraña coincidencia, sí tengo un regalo de semillas para tu amigo Legolas. Estas crecerán en Rithlas y son de Annúminas. Sé que significará mucho para el nuevo rey de Gondor.'

'¿Glorfindel el Radiante? No he visto su rostro ni escuchado sus bellas palabras durante muchas vidas de Hombres. Sin embargo, su nombre ha llegado a mí aquí, donde me encuentro, de vez en cuando.
'Aquí tienes mi consejo, joven ${CLASS}. No intentes encontrar a un Elfo como Glorfindel, porque no será encontrado si no desea serlo. Sigue en cambio lo que él buscaba. Si no me equivoco, un tal Dorongur en Duillond sabía lo que Glorfindel buscaba, y puede incluso saber a dónde se ha ido.
'Ah ja ja. No te precipites todavía. Viniste por una segunda razón y eso lo tendrás sin acertijos. Estas semillas son de Tuilloth. Crece para cubrir el suelo, y las finas flores blancas que produce hacen que parezca un espejo del cielo nocturno bajo tus pies.'

'Te doy la bienvenida. Déjame mirar en tus ojos. No veo engaño ni mala voluntad, así que te diré lo que sé. Glorfindel vino hace unos días para consultarme sobre unas palabras que Gil-galad pronunció hace mucho tiempo, cuando puso por primera vez el pie en los Puertos de Lindon. Se referían a tiempos venideros, tiempos que él no viviría para ver.
'Yo mismo sabía poco de este discurso, y no estaba seguro de quién lo había escuchado en su totalidad. Por lo tanto, dirigí a Glorfindel hacia Lin Giliath. Sentí que si se había escrito, algún registro podría estar allí. Ve a Tham Giliath y habla con Gildor Inglorion. Él sabrá si Glorfindel pasó por allí o no.'
Luego, con un brillo en los ojos, Dorongur saca una pequeña bolsa.
'Tampoco podría olvidar esto, un regalo justo pedido justamente. Lodeledh crecerá alto y con hojas fragantes proyectará sombra moteada bajo sus ramas.'

'¿Qué es esto que has encontrado, ${PLAYER}? ¿Una pista sobre el paradero de Glorfindel? Este registro es muy antiguo. El señor Celeborn y yo necesitaremos algo de tiempo para estudiarlo detenidamente. Te enviaremos a buscar cuando hayamos terminado. Y - tienes mi más sincera gratitud por todo lo que has hecho.'
'¡Vaya, qué es esto? Te has superado a ti mismo, ${PLAYER}. Encontraré un recipiente adecuado para este regalo y lo llevaré a Gondor, para dárselo a nuestro amigo, el nuevo rey.'
'¡Salve, ${PLAYERNAME:querido amigo[m]|querida amiga[f]} ! Es hora de que regreses a la corte de Lothlórien, porque allí se te espera.'

'He reflexionado sobre las cosas que tú y yo vimos en mi espejo, ${PLAYER}, y algo de claridad ha llegado a mi mente sobre su significado. El consejo del Señor Elrond era realmente cierto: tienes un papel que desempeñar en los eventos que se están desarrollando y, creo, en traer a Glorfindel a nuestro consejo.
'Esto es lo que te pediría: ve a los lugares donde habitan los de mi especie, los Elfos, y pregunta por él. Es muy viajado y conocido por muchos. Pero ¿por dónde deberías empezar? Tal vez... Mirobel. Sí. Busca a Certhíril allí. Ella ha visto mucho y sabe aún más.
'Ah, pero antes de irte, habla con tu amigo Legolas. Él también tiene algo que pedirte, creo.'

'De hecho, puedes hacer ambas cosas a la vez. Ve, recoge semillas y aprende lo que puedas sobre Glorfindel mientras avanzas.
'Comienza con Certhíril y creo que tu camino se desplegará ante ti.'

'¡Qué extraño! Ayer mismo una alumna, o más bien una discípula de Glorfindel, se encontraba donde tú estabas y me hizo la misma pregunta: ¿lo había visto? Lamentablemente, no.
'La envié a Imladris, porque he oído que últimamente ha pasado mucho tiempo allí, contemplando entre la casa de Elrond y la cascada. Te sugiero que hagas lo mismo, y si no encuentras a ambos, quizás encuentres a uno de los dos.
'Tu otra petición tiene una respuesta más afortunada: estas son semillas de la vid Gaerthond, con hojas de plata brillante y flores que florecen por la mañana de un azul oscuro y dorado.'

You have gathered much obsidian, wood, and even a shard of Barad-dûr itself. You should now deliver them to Sversting at the forges of Lûghash.

Obsidian can be found near lava-floes around Orodruin, wood can be salvaged from ruined banner poles on the plains of Dor Amarth, and shards of Barad-dûr's steel can be found in the lands surrounding Sauron's fallen tower.
Sversting has asked you to gather obsidian, wood, and a shard of Barad-dûr's steel that he might craft a weapon of renown in honour of their lost King.

'Yes, yes! These will do the trick!
'The Dark Lord's steel is a curious creation - it is light, yet sturdy, and I have come to believe it cannot be dulled by the passing of time.
'In the hands of any dwarf, I say it still cannot match the beauty and strength of mithril! Even so, it has no equal in Mordor. If our King should ever return, he shall bear a weapon worthy of his line. I swear it!
'I have never given up hope that the King lived, for he spared me Sauron's ire when the Dark Lord took him and the others away. To have him back again would be my greatest joy!
'I shall set my smiths to work at once. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}.'

'At last we meet, ${PLAYER}! Spakorth told us of the aid you brought his expedition, and I wished to look upon the outsider myself!
'You may call me Sversting, and I am the forge-master of Lûghash - and the most skilled smith of all the Stout-axes that remain in Mordor! Aye, we are not as many as we once were... but it brings me great pride nonetheless!
'My works have earned me a great deal of Mistress Zôreth's favour, and she has told me of a great rumour she learned by spying upon the Men of Barad-dûr. She claims that our imprisoned King still lives, locked away in the depths of the Dark Tower!
'It is too great a tale for me to believe at once, but what if it were true? If King Greytooth were to return to his people at last, he must have a weapon befitting a King!
'Spakorth tells me you wish to aid us. Is that right? I would ask that you bring me wood from abandoned banner poles and chunks of sharp obsidian from the banks of the lava-floes. Also, should you encounter any of the shards of Barad-dûr that were hurled from the Dark Tower as it fell, gather as much as you can!
'It is time we Stout-axes took something from Sauron!'
Deliver the obsidian, wood, and steel to Sversting in Lûghash
Zôreth, Mistress of Lûghash, has sent the Stout-axes in her service to seek treasures that once belonged to the Dark Lord.

'I am saddened to learn that some of my folk fell into the fires of the mountain. It seems even keeping a careful pace is no longer enough....
'The tremors have grown more powerful since Sauron's fall, and new cracks form in the earth with each passing day. It is challenging to keep a steady footing when you cannot trust that the ground shall remain whole beneath you! We shall have to be more careful the next time the Mistress sends us out in search of whatever it is we're meant to find.
'For those that have returned, they shall enjoy a long-awaited rest. You have done my folk a great service, ${PLAYER}.'

'The tale of the Stout-axes is not a pleasant one, friend, but I would share it with you.
'Once we were Drása's Folk—a great kingdom of dwarves, but no longer, and it is only now that Sauron is gone that I dare to utter the name of the Father of our folk. Early in this Age, Sauron ordered us to return the Great Ring of Power he granted to our folk when still we dwelt in the East. The Dark Lord sought for it some unknown purpose, and when our King of old denied him his prize, Sauron summoned forth a vast army and razed our ancestral home and stripped the golden halls of Usk-tóga. Many of our clan were slain, and those few who survived were taken as thralls to Mordor to serve the Dark Lord. We were made to forsake our clan name of old and swear ourselves to Sauron, and so we became the Khirvísa: the Stout-axes of Mordor.
'Yet, throughout our long centuries of toil, we held to the old ways and the line of our Kings of old remained unbroken. We were slaves, yes, but some measure of who we were endured and we made for ourselves a small realm of our own in secret within the lands of Mordor. But Sauron knew all too well that which we had hoped to conceal from him....
'Seventy-eight years ago, the Stout-axes were unmade. In a rage, the Dark Lord returned to Mordor from lands unknown and imprisoned our King and countless other Stout-axes in the dungeons of Barad-dûr. What little freedoms we had were taken from us, and even the lowliest Orcs came to regard us as mere vermin. In the absence of our King, I and many others remained to toil in Lûghash, and whenever Zôreth was not summoned to Barad-dûr, she too dwelt within Lûghash.
'Now Sauron is gone, but still we serve - hated as we are now in the eyes of all in Mordor. After the fall of the Dark Lord, none but the Mistress of Lûghash, Zôreth, deigned to offer the rest of our kin shelter and keep us from the Orcs. In our desperation, it would seem we have traded one master for another, but we are too far from the Black Gate and escape now seems no more possible now than it did when Sauron ruled Mordor. And to where would we even escape? Zôreth desires the weapons and trinkets of the Dark Lord above all else, but what portion of his might remains in them I cannot say. We have sought them nearly every day since his fall, but every search has come to naught.
'Days we have searched now, and with little food or rest. It is time for my kin to return to Lûghash, even if Mistress Zôreth does not wish it.
'There are four other expeditions about in this land, ${PLAYER}. Find them, and send them home to Lûghash!
'If you wish to meet my folk, you shall meet us all!'
Oppressed by Zôreth and now by the Order of the Eye, the Stout-axes of Lûghash have long fought for their survival as slaves of Mordor.
Those We Have Lost

'May those Men rot upon the plains for what they have done! We may serve Mistress Zôreth, but we are not slaves to all the fools of Mordor! A fire burns within us yet!
'My kin have been given a final honour, and for that, I offer you my thanks.'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! So finally you come to Lûghash, eh?
'It is not a very fitting a home for dwarves, but the Mistress has kept us from the Deathless and the others of her kin. Or so she did until Sauron fell....
'Now this ridiculous \qOrder of the Eye\q won't leave us be! They actually believe he'll come back again! A foolish lot, they are!
'If they were harmless, I'd leave them to their fantasies, but now they have come to the Spire. They have tortured and killed my kin all to gain Mistress Zôreth's knowledge of Sauron's artifacts. What would we know? We are her servants - not her trusted allies and advisors!
'If you wish to aid me, bury my kin upon the fields surrounding Lûghash. They deserve that final honour!
'Come to think of it... if those cultists are still snooping about outside, bury them as well. Even if he does come back again, I don't want them to be around to see it!'

'Aye, that will do for now.
'We must share wisely the food that Mistress Zôreth provides us, friend. Hunger is a burden we Stout-axes must all bear, and as kin we bear it together.
'I hope some good fortune comes to us once we find what the Mistress desires....'

'Since I returned to the Spire, I have noticed a few of the smiths of my kin looking unwell. They have toiled tirelessly for the Mistress, and I think their hunger has finally caught up to them.
'In truth, we all hunger. We are allowed only meagre rations of old meat and overripe vegetables. The folk of Nurn bear the burden of feeding all of Mordor, and there is little left for us once Mistress Zôreth's kin and the Orcs have at it.
'The measly rations that still remain are piled about here in the barracks, and I would have you gather them for the smiths. My kin may be displeased, but the health of our folk is worth more than one missed meal.
'Offer the smiths a brief respite and some rations, and if the Mistress is displeased with me for allowing it, She can come speak to me herself!'
Worked to the Bone

Spakorth has asked you to retrieve missives from the Order of the Eye expedition-leaders searching the lands of Dor Amarth. Spakorth hopes they might reveal the whereabouts of the lost King of the Stout-axes.

'King Greytooth lives? Seventy-eight years he has been gone... and for seventy-eight years we have been without hope. Perhaps those days shall soon be behind us!
'Mistress Zôreth claimed he was still imprisoned by Sauron after all these years, but one detail in this missive has left me uneasy. You see, my folk have never been sent to seek him. I... I cannot recall a single expedition to rescue him from the Dark Tower. What attempts to free him could this missive speak of?
'That is a question I shall have to ask the Mistress, I think. Where her efforts failed, we must now succeed.
'It is time King Greytooth is freed from Barad-dûr and returns to lead his folk!'

'For my part, I have but one task for you, and it is one of dire importance to my folk, ${PLAYER}.
'The Men of the Order of the Eye have been searching Dor Amarth and the ruins of Barad-dûr for Sauron's artifacts since his fall, and they have taken careful note of all they have found as has Mistress Zôreth.
'One of my folk, Sversting, once told me of a rumour shared with him by Mistress Zôreth. She told him that King Greytooth was still held within the deeper dungeons of the Dark Tower, but she would speak no more of it when the rumour spread among us.
'I must know if the Mistress spoke true - does my King still live?
'The Order has sent expeditions all across Dor Amarth - from the deepest depths of the Black Pits of Mordath to the very gates of Lûghash!
'I would ask that you seek out their leaders, and see if they bear any missives or orders that speak of King Greytooth!'

'What is this?'
You tell Gimli of the slain dwarf you found and offer him the shield.
'By your description of his wounds, the dwarf you encountered must have been caught by a stray stone thrown from the depths of Mount Doom. A poor dwarf, indeed, but not one slain by malice. The Dark Lord must not have brought my kin to ruin after all!
'Ah-ha! Look at this, my friend. This shield is newly-forged... and crafted by skilled hands!
'So dwarves still dwell in Mordor, but where have they made their home?'

'Gimli and I have not ventured overfar into these lands, my friend, and I am not certain I wish to. The Men of Gondor call this place Dor Amarth; the Doomfold in the Common Speech.
'Its name was wisely chosen by those Men, for I feel a deep shadow looming over us even so far from the ruins of the Dark Tower. Gimli has found old tools of dwarf-make in this ruin, and though he will not speak of it, unease has crept into his mind. If ever dwarves dwelt within Mordor, it seems their fate was not a pleasant one and that their line is long ended.
'This causeway forks some distance to the south. One path leads southward and appears less well-kept by the Orcs, while the other rises and continues east to Barad-dûr. I would ask that you follow the causeway south to the fork and then beyond to the east. Search for foes or those still held as slaves, and perhaps we shall find something to raise Gimli's spirits and draw his thoughts from those of his distant kin.
'Do not stray far from the road, my friend, for we have much still to learn of the hidden evils of Mordor.'

'Ah! At last you have come!
'I spoke to Mistress Zôreth, and she was pleased to learn that the \qstrange invaders\q were driven out. She wishes to focus on her research in the heights of the Spire, so I do not think we need worry about her for now.
'Now that that's all settled, I have a few duties to perform about the Spire. If you would aid me with some of them, perhaps Gimli shall have more time to ask me his questions!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}.
'We stand before the main gate of Lûghash, but you must not enter it. The Mistress has watching-stones guarding the inside of the gate, and if you are detected, she shall bring her wrath down upon us all!
'Many years ago, she allowed us to construct a second, hidden gate leading from our barracks out to the parapet far above us. We grew weary of her spirits lingering near us and begged her to keep the watching-stones away from our barracks. We did not expect mercy, but she relented, and set them only as guards within the main gate.
'Do you understand? You must enter through the hidden gate if you are to remain beneath the Mistress's notice. It is not hidden in the ways of the dwarves, ${PLAYER}, but it is hidden from the Spire's face.
'Behind the Spire, you will find a dirt pathway leading onto Lûghash itself. You must follow our lamps of crystal to a small, shadowed alcove. It is there you shall find the hidden gate.
'Go now! I must still speak to the Mistress to calm her fears about the spirits you drove back to the Spire, but once that is done, you shall find me in the barracks on the central level of the Spire.'

'Some of the spirits fled into Lûghash, you say? That is no good, no good at all....
'It is certain that Mistress Zôreth shall wish to speak with me about what her spirits saw, so it shall be my task to convince her that no threat comes to the Flaming Spire.
'I doubt she shall protest when I tell her that we drove you and your armies from Mordor! Ha-ha!'

'Lûghash rises to the east, nestled within a rocky hill atop a deep valley. Alas, the Stout-axes are not the only ones in service of the Mistress of Lûghash....
'You see, Mistress Zôreth has grown emboldened since the fall of the Dark Lord, and she has drawn many vile spirits into the watching-stones of this land.
'Through their eyes, both servants and foes are revealed... and their designs exposed. She is distrustful, even of her own kin, and so she instead wields her spirits as servants and spies. In this way, She seeks to find the resting places of the Dark Lord's most powerful trinkets. We Stout-axes think it a foolish search and we would have no part of it... were the choice ours!
'If you wish to come to Lûghash, you must challenge Her Watching-stones and banish the spirits from them! If you do not, she shall soon know of you and Gimli!
'When it is done and Her spirits have been cast back to the shadows, I shall meet you at the lower gates of Lûghash!'

'It often falls to me to ensure that my folk best serve Mistress Zôreth, and as of late, that has meant tireless work. Even with so many new Stout-axes here after the fall of Barad-dûr, it seems like the work only grows more difficult. Our searches for Sauron's trinkets have not borne fruit, and the Mistress has become impatient. If we do not find something soon, I fear we shall lose her favour. And what would become of my folk then? Nothing good, I think!

'Aye, this is a tricky land. I do not know what beasts could live in such a place, but dwarves are hardy folk!

'You found the dwarf near the causeway that leads to the Dark Tower, didn't you? If you ask me, no dwarf would be wise to travel these lands alone, and even if one did, they would soon be sought out if they did not return.

'Gimli seems a fine dwarf, and I am glad to have met him. He has many questions, and I am pleased to say that I can provide him many of the answers he seeks. If there is time enough, I have questions of my own!
'We Stout-axes hold little sway in Mordor, but we dwell in peace within the Flaming Spire under the rule of Mistress Zôreth. We are no Dwarf-kingdom of old, but we are not so few as to be forgotten in this land -- for even Sauron could not forget us!
'If you or Gimli wish it, you are welcome to visit our home in Lûghash - provided the Mistress does not find out, of course.
'Hah! But if she didn't know you were there....'

'You found them after all, ${PLAYER}? Oh ho! Tell me of them!'
You tell Gimli of the Stout-axe Dwarves of Mordor and of their origins in the mountains to the East. You also mention that Spakorth has asked to meet with Gimli at the muddied cistern of Blozronk to the east.
'Stout-axe Dwarves? I have never heard of a House by that name in all my years. Perhaps it was a name given to them by the Dark Lord, or their line was broken...'
Gimli appears initially perplexed by this news, but a wave of merriment soon washes over his face.
'Still, they did you no harm, so I shall hear this Spakorth's words.'
Legolas lets out a stern cough.
'Oh, you think they're up to something, do you? Well, for all I know of them, they might well be. Why don't you come along too, Legolas?
'Let us go to Blozronk, ${PLAYER}. Lead the way!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: You will swiftly travel to Blozronk when you continue this quest.</rgb>

'Aye, he's a dwarf all right. Not that I doubted you, ${PLAYER}, but I am just as surprised as you to find dwarves here in Mordor!
'The Stout-axes... I must admit, I have many questions I wish to ask about the early years of their folk and how they came to dwell here. There is so much to be learned from them! Even if they toiled under the Dark Lord, I'd wager they're still a better lot than the Dourhands.
'See, Legolas? It's not like he's got evil eyes painted all over him!
'I think it's time we properly introduce ourselves, wouldn't you say?'

'It has been long since my folk last spoke to outsiders... especially those with the might to bring him low.
'For what purpose have you come to these lands? To liberate its peoples? Conquest? I suppose it does not matter now. You are here, and so that is that! The Deathless may not see it so, but their quarrels are their own!
'I must ask... in your vast armies, were there any dwarves? We have seen naught of our kin and cousins in the lands beyond Mordor since the early days of our folk in the mountains to the East, and I would be gladdened to learn that we are not the last dwarves in this realm.'
You tell Spakorth of Gimli and of the House of Durin's Folk.
'Ah! So one of my kin has come to these lands? If he so wishes it, I would much desire to meet him!
'Tell this Gimli of the Stout-axes of Mordor! If he wishes to meet with me, I would have us forge a new peace free of Sauron's influence.
'Go! I shall wait here for a time, and if you do not return, I shall honour his choice.'

'Estoy listo para partir hacia Nûrz Ghâshu, ${PLAYER}. Da la orden y nos iremos.'
'${PLAYER}, ¡ahí estás! Celeborn ha comprendido el significado del antiguo texto y sabe a dónde ha ido Glorfindel. ¡Vuela allí con gran rapidez!'

'Sabes, ${CLASS}, que lo que Glorfindel buscaba es lo que los Hombres o los enanos llamarían una profecía: palabras pronunciadas por Gil-galad en una época pasada, que conciernen tanto al amanecer como al ocaso de nuestro tiempo en la Tierra Media. Pocos estuvieron allí para escucharlo y aún menos son los que caminan por esta tierra y lo recuerdan en su totalidad. Tal vez previendo esto, las palabras fueron inscritas en once pergaminos y entregadas a guardianes de la sabiduría de confianza.
'Pero el texto que encontraste en Tham Giliath no era uno de esos pergaminos. No, era un mero recuento de los textos escritos por un erudito y a dónde habían sido enviados. Cuatro de los veinte que menciona eran del discurso de Gil-galad, y sé bien que tres de esos cuatro se perdieron para siempre por calamidad, locura y fuego.
'La cuarta grabación de la profecía encontró un hogar entre textos recopilados en lo que ha llegado a llamarse la Grieta de Nûrz Ghâshu. ¿Conoces ese lugar, ${PLAYER}? Lo conoces bien, Glathlírel.'

'¿Lo ves, ${PLAYER}? La naturaleza del sueño que me sacó de mi retiro no era un sueño vano. He llegado aquí, como tú, en un momento de necesidad.
'Aunque tiemblo ante la idea de regresar a ese lugar donde se luchó y se sometió al Balrog, sé que debemos hacerlo. Un miedo, no, una certeza me dice que el peligro acecha allí como antes. Si la Grieta estuviera tranquila y vacía, ¿por qué no ha regresado Glorfindel?
'Ni siquiera Lady Galadriel puede saber lo que se esconde en esa profundidad. Debemos ir, tú y yo, y descubrir la verdad. Eso es seguro.'

'¡Has regresado! En tus ojos leo mucho, mucho de lo que ha sucedido.'
Tú y Glathlírel cuentan al consejo reunido todo lo que ocurrió.
'Veo. Ha terminado bastante bien, y con el tiempo sabremos si el pergamino que buscaba Glorfindel valía el peligro que enfrentaste. Pronto estará con nosotros y nuestra espera terminará. Encontraré el regalo del que habló y me aseguraré de que se te entregue para que lo lleves a mi nieta, Arwen. Es un buen regalo, y apropiado. Además, es justo que ella lo reciba de tus manos.
'Adiós por ahora, ${PLAYER}. Nos veremos pronto.'
'${PLAYER}, ¡ahí estás! El Señor Celeborn ha comprendido el significado del antiguo texto y sabe dónde ha ido Glorfindel. Deberías hablar con él de inmediato.'

You were brutally attacked by the Firehorns, and they threatened the Dwarves of Durin's Folk. You should talk to Gimli and tell him what has happened.

The hidden gate of Lûghash can be found in an alcove high above the main gate, accessible by a rear pathway leading onto the Spire.
Gimli has asked you to deliver a message to the Firehorns in the Oath-taker's Horn. He hopes that King Greytooth might be convinced to treat upon the plains of Dor Amarth.

'The Firehorns did what now? They attacked you... and they threatened my folk?'
Gimli's face flushes with anger.
'Well, that settles it! The time for talk is ended!'

'This is not as simple a matter as it was with the Dourhands.... These Firehorns are not cruel or evil in their hearts, but the promise of a dwarf-ring's power has begun to chip away at their good sense!
'You and I saw what the Ring did to Frodo, even in the short span of months he bore it before our paths were forced apart! If Váskmun was forced to wear it in the dungeons of Barad-dûr during his imprisonment and then deprived of its power by Sauron, his mind may have withered into an obsession! Although, being a dwarf, I think he may have fared a bit better than Gollum!
'${PLAYER}, I do not wish to raise arms against Váskmun and his folk if it can be helped!
'Váskmun may not allow us inside the Oath-taker's Horn, but that does not mean we cannot come to the doors of the Spire! Ha!
'Go to the hidden gate of the Oath-taker's Horn and summon the Firehorns! Deliver them an invitation for King Greytooth to meet us upon the field!
'When that is done, we shall speak of peace... and of having some better dwarf-sense!'
When King Váskmun Greytooth was imprisoned by the Dark Lord, many of his most-trusted kin were brought to the dungeons of Barad-dûr as well.

You should free them from the dungeons of Barad-dûr and allow them to reunite with their kin in Lûghash.

Overjoyed by the return of their King, Váskmun Greytooth, the Stout-axes of Lûghash have asked you and Gimli to share your tales of valour among the Free Peoples that they might learn more of the world beyond Mordor.
A House Forged Anew
Talk to Gimli in Lûghash
Talk to Spakorth on the plains of Dor Amarth outside Lûghash

Spakorth can be found along the causeway outside Lûghash.
You have been cast out of Lûghash by King Greytooth and the Firehorns. You should speak to Spakorth.

Gimli can be found on the central level of Lûghash.
King Váskmun Greytooth desires to hear Gimli's tales of valour. You should join Gimli in recounting your adventures in Middle-earth.

'I am ashamed that I could not resist Zôreth, ${PLAYER}! I am ashamed that I could not even sense her deception—that she could spy upon the Stout-axes through my very eyes and work our ruin!
'I have failed you and I have failed Gimli. Leave me if you wish—it is the fate I deserve!'
Spakorth notices that you make no effort to leave, and smiles weakly.
'What sort of dwarf is so easily swayed by the power of evil? I suppose that is a foolish question to ask now....
'Zôreth may have planned to use me in her search of the Rings of Power, but now King Váskmun has forsaken us all for Manthríf!
'If this is the way of the Firehorns, I want no part in it!'

'Tales of valour, eh? I think we have a few we could tell.... Hah!
'Let's get on with it then!'

'This is a day of celebration, indeed! My people are united once more, and today we cast off the shackles by which Sauron himself bound us!
'You and Gimli have done my people a great honour, and one that shall not soon be forgotten by my folk.
'As a dwarf of the eastern mountains, I have always wished to learn more of the west. Ah, but such things could not be asked of the Dark Lord! I know not the reasons why, but Sauron was not over fond of dwarves, you see!
'But, such questions can be asked now! How came you to Mordor, ${PLAYER}? What trials have you and Gimli faced and overcome?
'Let us hear your tales of valour!'

Gimli is disheartened that Váskmun Greytooth desires to lead his people in search of the lost dwarf-ring, Manthríf, and he is overcome with regret for his role in further dividing the Dwarves of Mordor.
Of Pride, Greed, and Loss
You have found the spears of Lindon, Dernaith and Megoril, upon the plains of Dor Amarth!
You have found two Elves standing beneath the statue of Sauron...
Discover the identities of the strangers at the statue of Sauron
Talk to Megoril

The two Elves, Megoril and Dernaith, can be found at the foot of the statue of Sauron outside the Oath-taker's Horn in Dor Amarth.
You have come across a pair of Elves searching the ruins of Dor Amarth.

The strangers can be found to the south of Spakorth at the foot of the statue of Sauron outside the Oath-taker's Horn.
Spakorth has spotted two strangers at the foot of the nearby statue of Sauron and desires to learn their purpose in Mordor.

'What business have you in these lands, ${RACE}? Did you travel hither with the host of Men or is this land your home?
'Speak at once, or my spear shall be swift!'

'Gimli has not turned his eyes from the Spire since we were cast out, ${PLAYER}. I wonder... does he truly believe a share of the blame is his?
'In truth, the blame lies with Váskmun, Zôreth, and Sauron himself. By Sauron's own hand, Váskmun was corrupted by the Ring and he is now bound to it by pride and greed - as the Nazgûl were to their own Rings. Gimli is a fine dwarf, and he has done my people no ill! He must not believe that his efforts to aid us were the cause of such sorrow!
'It was Váskmun and his Firehorns! As he commanded, the Spire is now called the Oath-taker's Horn! What oath has been taken, I ask? An oath to bring ruin upon our people? Váskmun may as well consider it fulfilled then!'
Spakorth snorts indignantly.
'Now, what do we have over there? Do you see the two of them by the statue of Sauron? Well, they're certainly not dwarves... could they be allies of yours?'

After discovering that Váskmun Greytooth, the long-imprisoned King of the Stout-axes, lives still within the ruins of Barad-dûr, the Stout-axes hope to see him freed and returned to his folk in Lûghash.
Within the Bones of Barad-dûr
You find no trace of the lockbox that King Greytooth described...
It is no feast, but it will have to do...
The shadow-mantled ruins of Sauron's fortress still bear a twisted splendour...
As you pass downward into the darkness of Barad-dûr, you discover a stone room lined with cells...
Deep within Barad-dûr, you have found a haggard dwarf surrounded by slain Men and empty robes of the Unseen...
You discover a dwarf-make set of glinting, gold-wrought armour!
Find King Váskmun Greytooth's lockbox in Sauron's relic-chamber

You have found imprisoned Stout-axes, but you still have no found King Greytooth. You should proceed deeper into the dungeons of Barad-dûr and continue your search.

Barad-dûr can be found to the south-east of Lûghash in Dor Amarth.

Barad-dûr can be found to the south-east of Lûghash in Dor Amarth.

King Váskmun Greytooth can be found on the central level of Lûghash.

King Váskmun Greytooth's armour can be found among the collected weapons at the armoury, rations of some kind can be found in the larder within the dungeons of Barad-dûr, and his mithril lockbox can be found in a small chamber near the main gate of Barad-dûr.
King Váskmun Greytooth has asked for you to aid in his escape by finding him some food, his old armour, and a mithril lockbox that was taken from him by Sauron.

King Váskmun Greytooth can be found in his cell in the dungeons of Barad-dûr.
You have found King Greytooth some food as well as his ornate, golden armour, but you were unable to find his lockbox. You should deliver his equipment to him in his cell in Barad-dûr.

'Ah, I cannot say much for this food. It seems even Sauron's willing servants eat like animals!
'But look at this armour! It is as brilliant as it was the day Sauron stole it away from me! It was wrought by my finest smith, Sversting! Does he still live?'
You inform King Greytooth that Sversting dwells within Lûghash with the rest of his folk.
'These are joyous tidings! You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! Ah, but before we leave... did you by chance find that lockbox?'
You tell King Greytooth that you found the relic-chamber, but the lockbox and most of the other relics were missing or stolen.
'That is very disappointing... I suppose all his servants were merely waiting for something to slip, and they had their knives ready!
'I shall have to search on my own in the days ahead, but for now, I wish to return to my folk. Let us go!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: You will swiftly travel to Lûghash, the Flaming Spire when you continue this quest.</rgb>

'If I did not appear grateful in the dungeons of Barad-dûr, I wish to offer you my truest gratitude. ${PLAYER}, you have done me and my people a great service this day.
'Although I did not find all I sought in the depths of the Dark Tower, I am once again surrounded by my dear friends and kin, and there can be no greater joy for a King. Our people were broken for many years, but today, we are reunited as one!
'This is a day of celebration, and by its end, we will celebrate our freedom!'

'Stay back! Who are you and why should I not slay you where you stand?'
You quickly tell King Greytooth that you have come on behalf of his people, the Stout-axes, who now dwell in the Flaming Spire of Lûghash.
'Oh-ho! So Spakorth sent you! He was never much of a warrior, but his mind is sharper than any axe! If you are one of his allies, I will gladly spare you.
'One of the cultists has been slipping me shafts of metal and wood for weeks now... so I suppose I was meant to free myself? Well, I have! Hah! Seventy-eight years have gone by, but I am still the dwarf I was!
'If you still wish to aid me, you can help me find a few things that were taken from me by the Dark Lord. He took my gold-wrought armour, and I want it back! It's either kept in the armoury near the cells or in Sauron's relic-chamber near the main hall. Also, there's a larder near the armoury, so if you see anything that looks like it's meant for those snivelling Black Númenóreans and not for the prisoners, bring it here.
'Oh, one last request... if you happen to find a mithril-wrought lockbox in Sauron's relic-chamber, give it to me at once! It is an heirloom that belonged to my forefathers, and it means a great deal to me!
'Swiftly now, my new friend, and then we shall get out of this place!'

'If I am reading these missives correctly, King Greytooth can be found deep in the dungeons of Barad-dûr. Deeper still than any of the Stout-axes that were taken when he was imprisoned! Aye, it seems that Sauron did not want him too close to the others of his kin....
'As far as I know, only one entrance to Barad-dûr remains, and that is the main gate. It lies across a wide span from the causeway through Dor Amarth, and underneath it, the fires of Orodruin blaze without end. Once you enter the Tower, you must seek the dungeons and then travel as far within them as you are able. Only then may you find King Greytooth!
'Foes lurk around every corner in Barad-dûr, but do not forget that others of my kin may be there to aid you if you free them!
'I can offer no more advice than to watch your back, friend, for you must venture into the very heart of evil to find King Greytooth.
'If you return alongside the King, you shall be revered amongst my folk!'
Deliver the equipment to King Váskmun Greytooth in Barad-dûr

It remains uncertain if all the dwarves within the Oath-taker's Horn wish to follow King Greytooth in his quest to recover the dwarf-rings, but Gimli holds hope that a few might instead wish to ally with Durin's Folk.
A House Divided
Rescued intimidated Stout-axes from the Oath-taker's Horn (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Rescue intimidated Stout-axes from the Oath-taker's Horn (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
You have freed many of the intimidated Stout-axes from the Oath-taker's Horn.

Intimidated Stout-axes can be found throughout the Oath-taker's Horn.
Gimli has asked you to rescue any of the Stout-axes that do not wish to follow King Greytooth in his quest to recover the dwarf-rings and offer them a new home as part of Durin's Folk.

You have done well to free the Stout-axes from the Oath-taker's Horn. It is likely that King Váskmun Greytooth will lead the Firehorns to ruin in his search for the dwarf-rings.
Instead, you have offered the few remaining Stout-axes a new chance at freedom among Durin's Folk.

'Hold a moment, ${PLAYER}.
'You surely saw as I did that some among the Stout-axes seemed unsettled by the King's command that we be cast out from the Spire. What will become of them? Shall they be met now with threats and curses? Perhaps they shall even be unfairly marked as traitors!
'I cannot speak for King Dáin, but I would offer the Stout-axes a new home among my folk. We shall have need of hardy dwarves now that Sauron has fallen!
'If you find any who still name themselves Stout-axes in the Oath-taker's Horn, aid them and offer them my promise that they shall find refuge in the halls of Durin's Folk.'
After King Greytooth seized control of the Flaming Spire, Spakorth fears what may have become of his brethren in the Oath-taker's Horn.
Under a Wicked Crown
Regrettably, Sversting could not be turned from his loyalty to King Greytooth...
Tragically, Freki appears to have been slain by his own kin...
Ever the lickspittle, Eitur's eagerness to forsake his allegiances brought him to a sorry end...
Talk to Spakorth in the Oath-breaker's Horn
Find Sversting
Find Freki
Find Náth
Find Dréri

Spakorth can be found in the doorway to Zôreth's chambers alongside Gimli.
You have found all of Spakorth's brethren, but unfortunately Sversting and Eitur proved unwilling to abandon their King's quest. You should now speak to Spakorth in the Oath-breaker's Horn.

Dréri, Náth, and Freki can likely be found on the central level of the Oath-taker's Horn amidst the Firehorn barracks.
Sversting proved fiercely loyal to King Greytooth's quest and fought you valiantly. You should now seek Dréri, Náth, and Freki in the Firehorn barracks above.

Eitur can likely be found in Zôreth's chambers on the highest level of the Oath-taker's Horn.
You have found all of Spakorth's brethren except for Eitur. You should now seek him and defeat him if need be.

Sversting can likely be found about the forges on the lowest level of the Oath-taker's Horn.
Spakorth has asked you to seek his brethren with the Oath-taker's Horn. Since you are entering at the lowest level of the Spire, you should first seek Sversting and see if he might be convinced to abandon Váskmun Greytooth's quest for the dwarf-rings.

'It was not supposed to be like this....
'Those who would not follow Váskmun were slain by Eitur and the others, and now all I have are these stones by which to remember them.
'What have we done? Where is the honour among my people? Whether Manthríf holds any power or not, it has brought greater ruin upon our people than even Sauron could have devised.
'Gimli spoke true, but the truth came too late to save my kin....'

'Firehorns? Bah! These dwarves are no kin of mine!
'Say what you will of her - at least Zôreth never chained us to the doors!
'You and Gimli have seen much beyond these lands, and if this is what my home has now become, I should like to follow where you go and leave this land behind.
'It is good to be out of these chains, my friend, but I cannot leave just yet!
'For the honour of my family and my fallen kin, I shall gather what remains of the Stout-axes and find them a place of rest in the low hills of Dor Amarth.'

'What should have been a time of joy for my people has instead become a time of great sorrow....
'Sversting was a fine dwarf, and I am saddened that he could not be made to see the madness of his King. As for Eitur, he was just as swift to seek Zôreth's favour. He was naught but a lickspittle no matter his master! Such behaviour does not befit any proud dwarf!
'Aside from Náth and Dréri, I saw only a handful of my people leave the Spire for the western ruins. Poor Freki should have been among them, but Váskmun's petty Firehorns raised their axes against him. He has put his own foolish greed before the needs of his folk, and I shall never forgive him for that!
'Even so, I must speak to him at once! Where is he?'

'At my request, Gimli has offered to escort me to Zôreth's chambers in the heights of the Spire.
'We shall force Váskmun to hear my counsel, even if he heeds not a single word of it. Indeed, the Stout-axes may still be free of the tyrants of Mordor, but Váskmun has become one of them, whether he believes it or not.
'I trust Gimli's axe shall keep me from harm, but I would ask that you seek Sversting, Dréri, Náth, and Freki as we storm the Spire. If they have not already realized the King's folly, I would have you convince them to abandon the search for the dwarf-rings and seek refuge among Durin's Folk as Gimli has proposed.
'As for Eitur... he may stand in our way, but he is a dwarf of words and little else! He has always sought to please those in power, and I think his loyalty now as false as it has ever been. If he stands in the way of the King, he must be defeated or exposed as the coward he is!
'Go, ${PLAYER}! Gimli and I shall follow you into the Spire!'
Upon the plains of Dor Amarth, you have found two Elves, Dernaith and Megoril, who have come to Mordor in search of their long-lost companion.
The Fates of the Damned
Talk to Dernaith outside the Oath-taker's Horn
Talk to Gimli outside the Oath-taker's Horn

Gimli can be found outside the Oath-taker's Horn in Dor Amarth.
Dernaith has told you of a confrontation he had with an echo of the Dark Lord, a glamour, bound to the statue of Sauron. The glamour spoke cryptically, but told of the damned in the Mordath - the Black Pits of Mordor. You should return to Gimli and see if he has come to a decision about what is to be done about the Firehorns and King Váskmun Greytooth.

Dernaith can be found at the foot of the statue of Sauron near the Oath-taker's Horn in Dor Amarth.
Megoril has asked you to speak to Dernaith about the fates of the dwarf-rings and their bearers.

Gimli appears to be muttering to himself as you approach. You gently place your hand on his shoulder, but his gaze remains fixed on the Spire.
'I have made more than a few great mistakes in my time, ${PLAYER}, but as any fine dwarf would... and as I always have, I put them to rights.
'The tortures Sauron brought upon Váskmun might not be undone, but there is still a goodness in these dwarves - a fair few of them, anyway!
'To sulk here wishing of a different fate for the Stout-axes - that is not the way of a dwarf!
'The Ring he seeks, this Manthríf, it shall not free him from his delusion and greed! I say Váskmun must be convinced of his folly, or he must be brought low!'

'I... am still recovering from my encounter with one of the Enemy's fell spirits... and my will is exhausted. Allow me a moment, ${RACE}, and we shall speak.'
Dernaith takes a moment to steady himself.
'If Megoril had not wished us to speak, you would not stand where you are now. What is it you want?'
You tell Dernaith that Megoril mentioned the fell spirit that inhabited the watching-stone, and that she and Dernaith had come in search of an Elf called Thelaron. You also mention the dwarf-rings and ask if Dernaith knows any of their history beyond when they were first granted to the dwarf-kingdoms by Sauron.
'Indeed, we have come in search of our companion, Thelaron. This is a quest of our own, and one given to us long ago by the High King of my people before he was slain by Sauron.
'As for the fell spirit... the one that rose from the statue looked a shade of Sauron himself, but weaker and less wicked in form. It was an echo of Sauron's sorcery, an echo of the Dark Lord - a glamour! This glamour told me of the Mordath, a Black Pit, beneath Barad-dûr where the damned are imprisoned, and it also told me to leave these lands or I would join the forgotten in the depths of the Black Pits and never again find my way from Mordor.
'I do not heed the warnings of such spirits, but these tidings are both good and ill. If Thelaron lives, he may have been taken into the Black Pits. Thus, we would have never found him when last we destroyed Barad-dûr. He was hidden away, far beneath the scorched lands of Mordor, left to pass an Age in silence and darkness... and bearing whatever tortures the Dark Lord devised for him.
'To answer your questions of the dwarf-rings... I have heard a few tales and rumours of them, but little else. As I have heard it told, they did not work as Sauron had planned. The dwarf-rings granted might and luck as well as some manner of concealment, but they did not corrupt the dwarves into servants of the Dark Lord as the Rings of Men did. Instead, the dwarf-rings brought forth a powerful and insatiable greed from deep within the minds of the dwarf-kings - a greed that bred in them a compulsion to seek wealth by any means and to hoard it in their vast halls. Ah, but other creatures were as fond of gold as the dwarves... and so for some of the dwarf-kingdoms, the Rings brought them to ruin.
'I am afraid that is all I know of them. And so, I believe it is time that Megoril and I resume our search... and seek out the Mordath.
'Your allies here seem to have great need of you. If our paths cross again, Megoril and I shall stand at your side!'

'Did you not hear? I said speak! Why have you come here?'
You introduce yourself to Megoril and tell her of your journeys with the Host of the West and of your efforts to ensure the success of the Ring-bearer's quest and the downfall of Sauron the Enemy. You also tell Megoril of the Dwarves of Mordor and of their efforts to find the lost dwarf-rings in Sauron's hoards.
'Very well, ${PLAYER}. I am Megoril of Lindon, and my companion is Dernaith. We are among the last remnants of the great Alliance in this realm, and it brought us joy and relief to learn that Sauron had truly fallen. Death has always eluded the Dark Lord, but I have heard that his Ring is gone and his essence diminished to naught. I know not why any would seek the dwarf-rings or any other artifact that was wrought through Sauron's corruption, for now the evils he has done to the peoples of Middle-earth might now begin to heal at last....
'I never thought I would look upon the plains of Gorgoroth again, but fate has brought me hither once more. You see, Dernaith and I have returned to this land in search of our lost friend and kin, Thelaron.
'During what is now called The War of the Last Alliance, our friend was taken by the Enemy and borne into Mordor on the back of one of his winged fell beasts. Our efforts to rescue Thelaron before he was taken beyond the Morannon failed, and in so doing, we nearly lost another of Gil-galad's favoured warriors to the corruption of Morgul-steel.
'Even after Sauron fell at the end of the Second Age, we could not find Thelaron in Mordor. He was hidden somewhere beyond our sight, and the Enemy's forces still remained to harry us - as few as they were after the War. Thus, our search begins anew. If Thelaron lives still, we shall find him!
'Dernaith has been attempting to learn what the spirits residing in these watching-stones have seen that they might unwittingly aid us, but none have answered our challenges... other than this one. Dernaith beheld a terrible form rise from this statue of Sauron, and it spoke to him, warning he would share the fates of the damned in the Mordath.
'I have never known such a place in Mordor, but in the language of the Elves, it means Black Pit. Indeed, this has given us much to consider....
'Perhaps Dernaith might know the fates of the dwarf-rings you spoke of....'
The Firehorns loyal to King Greytooth must be deprived of their forges if his quest to seize the dwarf-rings is to be brought to an end.
Mastering the Forges
Defeated Firehorn smiths in the Oath-taker's Horn (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroyed weapon-racks in the Oath-taker's Horn (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Doused forges in the Oath-taker's Horn (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Firehorn smiths in the Oath-taker's Horn (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy weapon-racks in the Oath-taker's Horn (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

You have done much to hinder King Greytooth and the Firehorns in their efforts to prepare for the search for the dwarf-rings.

Firehorn smiths and their equipment can be found around the forges in the depths of the Oath-taker's Horn.
Gimli has asked you to hinder the Firehorns' efforts to amass armour and weapons for the quest to seek the dwarf-rings.

You have destroyed many of the forges, tools, and weapons vital to King Greytooth and the Firehorns' quest to seek the dwarf-rings.
It is possible the Firehorns still possess a great deal of armour and weapons in their stores, but for the moment, you have stopped them from forging new equipment.
Gimli and Spakorth will be pleased.

'Ah-ha! The Firehorns may have sealed the hidden gate, but they have left their greatest weakness exposed!
'Don't you see, ${PLAYER}? The lower gate is now the only passage into and out of the Spire, and it leads to the very heart of their forges!
'Ruin their forges and break their weapons, and I dare say their search will be over before it begins! If the Firehorns discover you, do what you must. When the Dourhands treated my folk as the Firehorns treat the Stout-axes now, I did not shy from battle.
'While you deal with that, I'll escort Spakorth into the Spire. He has a mind to speak with King Greytooth, but I do not think it wise. Ah well, I have my axe if talking won't do!'

'So Váskmun has led them into the Mordath... and into a trap laid by Sauron himself?
'The Order of the Eye has sent many of its number into the Black Pits in search of the hidden vault, and now, Váskmun and the Firehorns have travelled there.
'Is this the making of a new war for Mordor? Or had Sauron worked to ensure that he did not fall alone? Perhaps it is neither....
'Whether it is this day or another, Váskmun and the Firehorns must be freed from their delusions! He leads them down a treacherous path, and I do not think whatever is in that vault shall set all to rights.
'But in the meantime, my folk will keep a close watch on the abyss. When the time comes, we hope that you and Gimli will stand with us against whatever evils lurk in the Mordath!'

'We have done a good thing for these dwarves, ${PLAYER}.
'If they had rescued Váskmun themselves as Zôreth had hoped, I do not believe it would be any different. Perhaps worse, but certainly not better!
'It is a sorry fate that Sauron devised for Váskmun, and I refuse to abandon hope that he still might be freed from the Ring's influence. If that day should come, we must honour the dwarves who fell in service of their King. We must honour those whose blood was spilled to ensure the freedom of the Dwarves of Mordor!
'Spakorth and those who still call themselves Stout-axes have sworn oaths to keep watch on the lands of Dor Amarth while our friends and allies remain here, and once that is done, I shall escort them to Erebor myself!'
Gimli bows deeply before you.
'You have done me and the Dwarves of Mordor a great honour!'
'I brought enough rope for the both of us, ${PLAYER}. Let's get down there!'

'This is a mighty big chasm, ${PLAYER}! Sauron's sorcery must have been holding more than his tower together!
'So they have not come this way then? Good! After studying more of Zôreth's notes, Spakorth has learned of a new passage into the dungeons of Barad-dûr. And even better, it is not one of much use to those cultists in the tower!'
Gimli draws a coil of rope from his belt.
'Aye, that's right. We're going down right here!
'If Zôreth's notes were correct, there should be a rocky landing about twenty yards down. If they weren't, well... at least we'll find out just how deep this abyss is!'
Gimli ties the rope around a nearby boulder and tests its strength.
'Well, are you coming, ${PLAYER}? I would hate to go on such an adventure by myself!'

'Have you read what I have, ${PLAYER}?!
\qDevoured\q? What sort of creatures could have devoured four of the Dwarf-rings? Surely Sauron would have slain them at once for such an offence!'
Spakorth reads over Zôreth's notes again.
'Ah, yes, the key around the King's neck.... Sauron gave King Váskmun the key, and deceived him into believing that the mithril lockbox was all that stood between him and reclaiming Manthríf for his folk. It was likely never within... and who can say where it might be now?
'As Zôreth has written, the Order of the Eye has learned much of the Mordath through their expeditions in the deep dungeons of Barad-dûr. I thought they toiled for the return of the Dark Lord, but this vault she has written of... this is what must have drawn them into Barad-dûr! None but the Gúrzyul—the Deathless—may have ever known of such a vault, and what would be kept guarded and hidden so far beneath the earth?
'A great abyss has sunken into the Mordath to the north of Barad-dûr and the Order thinks it an omen that Sauron's secrets are to be laid bare for the most loyal of his servants. If there remains any chance of finding Manthríf, King Váskmun shall lead the Firehorns into the abyss of Mordath.
'Patrol the mouth of the abyss and see if King Váskmun and the Firehorns have left any sign of their descent. For my part, I shall study more of Zôreth's research—with Gimli's protection, of course!
'Once I have finished, I will send him to meet you at the abyss—and I shall travel far away from this place!'

'There she is, ${PLAYER}... the Mistress of Lûghash! \qSaviour\q of the Stout-axes! Bah!'
King Váskmun spits in anger and grips Dolgráth the Battle-hungry tightly.
'I think it is time we learned where Manthríf was taken!
'Let us go!'

'No! Manthríf is gone... lost... stolen! The death of this wretched woman means nothing!'
King Greytooth swings Dolgráth the Battle-hungry into Zôreth's lifeless body, and spits upon her corpse.
'What right had she to speak of my imprisonment? Zôreth knew of the tortures Sauron visited upon me in the dungeons of Barad-dûr. How could she know such things?! To spread such lies about me—to sow the belief that I could not resist the Dark Lord's tortures and fell prey to the weakness of my forebears... it is unthinkable! And you believe it, don't you?
'For how long have you and Gimli conspired against me? Durin's Folk damned my people! How do I know you did not find it in the Dark Tower when I asked you to search for it? Manthríf is mine—it is mine by right!
'None shall stand against me in my quest to reclaim it! Not Zôreth, not Spakorth, not even you and Gimli!'

'So Zôreth thinks she can steal Manthríf from my people?'
King Váskmun grasps the mithril-key tightly.
'No! It belongs to my family -- it belongs to me!
'Spakorth still lives, but I cannot know where his will ended and the will of the spirit began.
'We have no time for such things now. Zôreth has betrayed my folk to serve herself! Our time in her service ends today!'
'Time to go, ${PLAYER}.'

'A tale of valour....
'We have won many battles and many great victories together, my friend. It is hard to think of just one! Which among them speaks most of our trials and of the victories won by our peoples?
'King Greytooth awaits us, so I suppose I'll have to decide soon enough!'

It is not unlike the axe of mithril, Zigilburk, of which you once spoke. If the search does not bring them to ruin, finding it will not change their fortunes! You approach the ever-vigilant stone. It gazes at you silently and does nothing. You are to assume that you have not waited long enough.
A few moments pass and your eyes start to feel heavy as if you are being forced to close them. Giving in, a vision appears in the darkness. A giant being of fire sits alone. You know it to be called Borangos, the Great Rogmul, but you do not know why. Borangos the Horror leaves his throne and walks to the lake of fire, the Ghâshghurm. There he walks atop the fiery waters and proceeds slowly towards the erupted Mount Doom.
When you open your eyes, the vision has passed and the stone is silent and unmoving.

You place the volcanic trinket next to the watching stone. Its gaze engulfs your every movement. When the offering is placed and you step back, you start to feel strange. You close your eyes and see a large creature sitting atop a throne of fire.
Startled, you open your eyes and feel compelled to speak the words, 'Borangos, horror, Nargroth,' and 'wait.'
Again a pain swells in your head. This time, you hear a voice call out to you. It sounds both distant as a lost miner, yelling in a collapsed cavern and as near as a soft whisper in your ear.
'Path of Ember, Path of Fire, Path of Ash.'
With those words, you are released from the spirit's hold. You feel as if the statue has accepted your offering and will now permit you to freely explore the Caverns of Fire.

The stone statue before you seems to gaze upon your presence. You feel as if the statue is trying to greet you and impede you at the same time.
The gaze begins to burn into your head. There is a sharp pain and you feel compelled to utter the words, 'demand' and 'offering.' It almost feels as if someone is controlling your speech.
The pain slowly subsides. You are released from the spirit's hold, though it continues to cast its gaze upon you. Perhaps you should find an offering to appease it.

Borangos The Horror

'${PLAYER}, I have something I would like to share with you. I have been looking through my notes here and have come to a few truths about these ancient fragments you have brought back from Nargroth.
'From the visions you have described and from what I have learned of Nargroth, I believe that the fortress of Nargroth was built on top of something else. It seems that Nargroth has been a mighty structure in Mordor for many years. What was built in the Caverns of Fire before Nargroth's construction is much, much older. Looking at these fragments, I would say it is of a chamber of some kind. Perhaps with a ward or seal. I would put this structure as being built around the Second Age. Possibly early Second Age.
'From what you have told me, I believe all this has something to do with Borangos. This Rogmul is most powerful. In historic text, none have been seen such as Borangos since the times when great beasts of fire and shadow walked the lands for Regmyl to serve.'
'This place, Nargroth, seems important to the powers in Mordor. We must learn more. If you are ready to depart, all I ask is to please be careful.'

You relay the conversation you have overheard between Borangos and Urudanî, to Isnír.
'Oh my, this is indeed worrying. You say that Borangos has some sort of plan that involves Mount Doom? Nothing good can come of this. The more we study the mountain, the more I fear it to not be natural. Its fires seem to have strange properties. Sauron must have been behind these flames, but will the mountain slowly fade in Sauron's death? Bright flames still flow from chambers within. Orodruin seems to be just as active as ever.
'It may be some time before we can act upon this enemy, but rest assured, I will start discussion with those of rank in Udûn. I thank you for bringing this to our attention. We shall speak again soon, ${PLAYER}.'

'Greetings, my name is Isnír. I have been summoned from Gondor to help those with questions of history and lore here in Udûn. Have we met before? I do not think so but I am much better with books than with faces you see.'
You give Isnír the fragments that you have collected.
'Now what have we here? Hmm, these indeed look old, quite old! Give me a few moments to look over them with some detail. I may be able to tell you more about them. I must read through a few passages of this text over here. I shall only be a moment or two.'

The carven rock focuses a beaming gaze upon you. Strange sounds begin to echo in your head. There is a grinding of rocks, a pick-axe strikes and voices echo through a cavern.
A driving pain seems to emanate from the watching stone and seize your head and chest. Images swirls through you and time seems to stop. You close your eyes yet you can still see. Everything looks different as if you are seeing the world through another's eyes.
Before you is Nargroth, but it is not ripped apart by the flames and fires of Mount Doom. There are dwarves and men on scaffolding working on walls in the cavern. Some have stopped working and instead gaze upon a doorway that is much, much older.
The images fade and you hear an explosion and screams. Those sounds fade as well. The stone is silent and has released you from its grasps. You are uncertain if the watching stone has shown you this memory of Nargroth for a purpose. Perhaps you will be able to search for some of the remnants of the ancient seal you saw in the vision.

Pregunta a Galadriel por el regalo
'Vamos hasta el puente que tenemos delante. Ven, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}.'
'Vamos allí, donde se encuentra la estatua junto al agua.'
'Vamos, atravesemos el paso estrecho que tenemos delante.'

'Una edad está terminando, ${PLAYER}. Aún no ha terminado del todo, y según el conteo de los Hombres y los enanos, no terminará por un modesto período de tiempo. Pero para mí, haber conocido siglos... siglos antes de que mi corazón fuera entregado, moviéndome libremente de Imladris a Lorien, de Lorien a Imladris, como un pececillo despreocupado entre estanque y arroyo. Luego supe que nada sería como antes.
'¿Sabes qué son estas flores, ${PLAYER}? Son símbolos de amor, y están hechas con una habilidad poco común para que exista una simpatía entre ellas, como si estuvieran atadas por un hilo invisible sin importar la distancia. Si algo le sucediera al dueño de una flor - si se enferma o muere - entonces la otra flor se marchitará, se secará y se desmoronará. Así mi Aragorn siempre sabrá que estoy bien y sana, y yo podré saber lo mismo de él.
'Es a la vez un gran consuelo y un recordatorio constante de nuestro destino y de los finales por venir.'

'De hecho, he permanecido en Rivendel algunos años, aunque no se cuente demasiado según el cálculo de nuestro pueblo, ${PLAYER}. En estos últimos diez años, he vivido aquí en anticipación de una promesa, esperando saber si la fortuna decretaría que se mantuviera o se rompiera. Ese breve tiempo ha sido tanto como una eternidad y un solo aliento para mí.
'Pronto, partiremos hacia Gondor, como sabes, y poco después, cuando lleguemos a esa tierra, me convertiré en uno con el tesoro de mi corazón. Él será rey y yo reina. Como Lúthien y Beren, cuyo amor e historia está grabado en nuestros corazones. Mucho ganado, sí, y mucho perdido.
'Ven, sigamos más allá por el camino.'

Los ojos de Arwen se cruzan con los tuyos mientras te acercas, y le entregas el regalo directamente. Ella abre la caja de seda y le explicas que las flores son de parte de Glorfindel.
'Entonces sé qué son estas flores y cuál es su significado. Es un pensamiento bueno y hermoso que Glorfindel me ha dado en este regalo. Ven, ${PLAYER}. Camina conmigo un momento.'

'Mucho sucederá, ${PLAYER}. Sucederá pronto, rápido como un halcón en picada. Rápido como el último descenso del sol en la noche. Mucho se ganará, y mucho, también, se perderá.'
Arwen ríe, suavemente, dulcemente, y un poco tristemente.
'Estás pensando, estoy segura, que mucho ya ha sucedido desde que comenzó tu viaje. ¡Y no te equivocas! Has visto mucho, pero pronto toda la Tierra Media verá más. Y mientras has estado en muchas tierras y entre muchos pueblos, yo he estado aquí y entre los míos.
'A la izquierda ahora, donde está esa estatua.'

'Me voy a vivir a las tierras de los Hombres, y me convertiré en como aquellos que allí habitan, ${PLAYER}. Alcanzaré el deseo de mi corazón y seré Reina de los herederos de Númenor, al amanecer de una nueva era. Pero perderé el hogar que he conocido. Perderé tantos rostros que me son queridos, que dejo atrás y que ellos mismos emprenderán viajes aún mayores, muy pronto. Perderé la certeza profunda de días interminables. Donde voy, los días estarán contados, y también las vidas.'
Arwen se detiene y te mira con ojos llenos de muchas cosas.
'Gracias por caminar conmigo, ${PLAYER}. Gracias por escucharme con amabilidad y sin juzgarme. La tristeza y la alegría son como dos corrientes unidas en un río, y ni siquiera los más finos tejedores élficos podrían separarlas ahora. Pero tengo un viaje que preparar, y el tiempo no se detendrá.
'¿Te veré en Gondor? Espero que sí. ¡Me gustaría mucho!'
'Un regalo para Lady Arwen te espera en la Corte de Lothlórien. Es el regalo de compromiso de Glorfindel para ella, pero el honor es tuyo de entregárselo.'

'Un verdadero regalo es aquel que canta del receptor con la voz del donante, se dice. Por esa marca, Glorfindel ha elegido el regalo más verdadero.'
Lady Galadriel produce dos flores exquisitas, y solo después de un momento percibes que son broches, hechos de filamento de plata, seda verde y violeta, y el mejor tejido de oro, y no flores reales en absoluto. Los devuelve a una caja de seda, que te entrega.
'Lleva estos a Arwen, ${PLAYER}. Ella te dirá algo de lo que significan para ella, si lo desea.'

'¡Así que Padre por fin te ha dado permiso para viajar desde Imladris, ${PLAYER}! Debo decir que estoy emocionado por aprender más de las batallas de las Edades pasadas de parte tuya. Padre nos dijo que no te molestáramos con tantas preguntas, pero esta es seguramente nuestra última oportunidad. ¿No es así?
'Estoy seguro de que Padre te ha contado todo acerca del viaje que tienes por delante, pero no te preocupes — ¡el asunto de su sueño no debe inquietarte!
'Además, el viaje a Celondim nos dará tiempo suficiente para hablar de otras cosas. ¡Imaginaría que los acontecimientos de los últimos tres mil años serían de algún interés para ti!
'Mi hermano y yo estamos listos para partir hacia Ered Luin. Cuando tu quieras, ¡partiremos de inmediato!'

'${PLAYER}, antes de que llegaran los Nueve envié a las Lanzas de Lindon con un destacamento de elfos y hombres. Con las demandas de Sauron rechazadas, ya no podemos confiar en que los Gwetherain detengan su mano en esta batalla.
'Conoces a las Lanzas como Thelaron, Megoril y Dernaith, y han permanecido a mi lado en muchas grandes batallas contra Sauron y los más terribles de sus siervos.
'Antes de partir, juraron cruzar las zanjas del Enemigo y desmantelar su maquinaria de asedio. Es cierto que los disparos de catapultas no han alcanzado nuestra posición desde hace un tiempo, pero el frente más amplio ha sido reducido a ruinas por esas máquinas.
'Ahora debes ir en misión de reconocimiento y con un mensaje. Averigua qué ha sido de su destacamento y, si alguno de ellos aún vive, entrégales un mensaje de esperanza.
'La Alianza marcha hacia la Puerta Negra, ¡y ningún Hombre malvado u orco se interpondrá en nuestro camino hacia la victoria sobre Sauron!'

'Me alegra verte de nuevo, ${PLAYER}.
'Dernaith y Megoril me han hablado de la captura de Thelaron, y estoy preocupado por tan sombrías noticias. El Señor Oscuro no habría olvidado pronto las heridas que sufrió a nuestras manos, y temo la forma que pueda tomar su venganza. Incluso ahora que deseo abandonar mi deber, no puedo apartar mis ojos de la Puerta Negra en una hora tan crucial. Por ello, te doy esta misión de importancia extrema. Debes encontrar a Thelaron, y debes salvarlo de los Gwetherain.
'En cuanto a la Alianza, uno del Pueblo de Durin ha ideado un plan astuto para llamar la atención de las fuerzas del Señor Oscuro y permitir un golpe rápido contra la Puerta Negra. En verdad, no sé si este plan dará fruto, pero debemos conquistar la Puerta si Sauron ha de ser derrotado.
'Te pediría que hables con Slégar el Artero. Es un enano lo bastante honorable, pese a su título. Una vez cumplas lo que te pida, ¡persigue al Gwatharan y rescata a Thelaron!
'Nuestros caminos se separan ahora, pero esperemos que ambos lleven a la victoria. ¡Que la luz de los Valar brille sobre nosotros!'

'A tu servicio, ${PLAYER}, ¡o quizás tú al mío!'
'¿Has pensado en cómo las zanjas del Enemigo nunca dejan de arder? Pues yo sí.'
Slégar señala la pila de barriles a su lado.
'Estos barriles están llenos de polvora negra y tosco que explota al contacto con la llama. No solo eso, ¡sino que seguirá ardiendo horas después! Sí, si fuera más útil para la piedra, ¡creo que el propio Durin nos haría robar un poco!
'Los Jinetes Negros del Señor Oscuro... los malditos Espectros del Anillo como los llaman los Hombres, son astutos, pero estos trasgos no son muy brillantes. ¡Han dejado los barriles justo al lado de sus propias ballestas y catapultas!
'¿Por qué no haces estallar algunos? Eso debería poner fin a su asedio y desviar su atención el tiempo suficiente para que la Alianza llegue a la Puerta Negra.
'¡Solo asegúrate de no quedarte cerca una vez los enciendas!'

'El príncipe ha tenido suerte de sobrevivir al ataque de su padre en la Puerta Negra, pero las palabras del Gwatharan me inquietan...
'El Jinete pronunció un nombre en quenya antes de partir: ¡Ungwetári! ¡La reina-araña!
'Ungoliant ha desaparecido de este mundo y no volverá a atormentarlo, pero Sus hijas permanecen, depredando todo lo que puedan devorar y extendiendo Su oscuridad por la Tierra Media. Uno de ellos debe ahora sentir el mismo hambre que Ella... sin preocuparse por los poderes del Señor Oscuro y sin propósito alguno excepto consumir.
'Son malas noticias, ha sido afortunado que las Grandes Arañas se volvieran contra el Jinete. Si no hacemos frente a esta hija de Ungoliant en la guerra, es seguro que llegará el día en que su hambre busque saciarse más allá de las sombras de Mordor.
'El Alto Rey me dio permiso para seguirte por petición de las Lanzas de Lindon, pero pide tu regreso de inmediato. La Alianza ha llegado por fin al destacamento avanzado. Reúnete con ellos allí, ${PLAYER}, y prepárate para nuestro asalto a la Puerta Negra!'

'¡${PLAYER}! Me alegra este reencuentro, pero hay poco más que celebrar...
'El Alto Rey me envió con mi compañía hacia el este para saber qué había sido de los Elfos de Lórien, pero, por desgracia, solo el príncipe Amroth permanece en el campo. Su padre y los demás fueron expulsados hacia el norte, pero adonde hayan ido no podemos seguirlos. El príncipe está herido, pero sanará con el tiempo.
'Debo preguntar, sin embargo... ¿por qué has venido?'
Le cuentas a Harthalín la tarea que te dio el propio Alto Rey, y sobre Thelaron, la Lanza de Lindon perdida, tomado por uno de los Gwetherain.
'Tu relato me inquieta... pues Amroth habló de una figura terrible que pasó con un elfo colgado sobre su corcel.
'Puede que el tiempo se agote para Thelaron. Creo que es hora de que sepamos más de lo que el príncipe vio...'

'Cuando mi compañía acudió en ayuda del príncipe Amroth, oí un gran grito y un estruendo como alas batiéndose desde arriba. Sonaba como una criatura terrible y voladora, tan grande como las Águilas. No pude verla entre el humo, pero estoy segura de que acechaba fuera de mi vista. No sé si esta criatura sirve a Sauron, pero su presencia me hace temer aún más por Thelaron.
'Si el Rey Brujo lo ha llevado al mirador, debemos pasar por el campamento de los Hombres de los Orientales más adelante. Los orientales se han vuelto arrogantes con el poder de Sauron y han dejado un pequeño paso abierto desde su campamento hacia el bosque.
'¡Sígueme, e infiltrémonos para evitar los peligros de acercarnos a su puerta desde el camino!'

'Me trae gran alegría verte de pie una vez más, ${PLAYER}.
'Después de que caíste, intentamos sanarte en la llanura de batalla, pero el Rey Brujo de Angmar te había infligido una grave herida — una como ninguna que nuestras gentes hayan sufrido antes por mano del Señor Oscuro. Se tomó la decisión de llevarte a Imladris, lejos de las tierras del Enemigo. Sufriste durante años en una agonía inquieta mientras mis sanadores trabajaban para librarte de los males que persistían en tu herida. Cuando terminó la Guerra, regresé para ayudarlos y aprendí mucho sobre sanar las viles heridas del acero de Morgul. Cuando por fin pudiste descansar, lo hiciste durante muchos años. A pesar de mis esfuerzos, tu fuerza se ha debilitado mucho. Puede llevar tiempo, pero creo que volverás a conocer el poder que yace en tu interior.
'En cuanto a la tarea que te dio Gil-galad, no la consideres un fracaso, . Nadie podría haber previsto la malicia del Enemigo al enviar a sus Nazgûl a capturar a Thelaron. Trágicamente, nunca fue encontrado — ni siquiera después de que Barad-dûr fuera reducida a ruinas. Dolió profundamente a Gil-galad perderos a ambos en la Guerra, y se dice que su luz se apagó durante todas las batallas que siguieron. ¡Aun así, no flaqueó ante el Enemigo!
'No, no caíste en vano, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Nuestra victoria en la llanura de batalla aquel día dio fruto, sin duda. Sauron resistió nuestros asaltos durante siete años en la Torre Oscura, pero al final fue derrotado por Gil-galad y Elendil. El hijo de Elendil, Isildur, cortó el Anillo del dedo de Sauron, destruyendo al Señor Oscuro y expulsándolo de este reino.
'Hay más que decir sobre estos asuntos...'

'¡Habla rápido, pues nuestros enemigos avanzan desde el este!'
Le cuentas a Dernaith tu encuentro con los Gwetherain y entregas el mensaje del Alto Rey.
'¡Los Gwetherain... dos de ellos pasaron por nuestras posiciones desde el norte! ¡Uno cabalgó hacia el oeste y dispersó a nuestros hombres, pero el otro... se llevó a Thelaron!
'En medio de la batalla, atrapó el brazo de la espada de Thelaron con un cruel lazo de cuerda y lo arrastró hacia el este con su corcel funesto! No pude seguirlo entre la masa de orcos... Le fallé...
'¡Fallé al Alto Rey... pero aún debo seguir luchando!'

'¡Salve, ${PLAYER}! Soy Megoril de Lindon. ¿Cómo van las batallas al norte?'
Le cuentas a Megoril tu encuentro con los Gwetherain y entregas el mensaje del Alto Rey Gil-galad.
'Si realmente atacaremos la Puerta Negra hoy, la Alianza debe llegar aquí pronto. Cumplimos lo que mandó el Alto Rey y destruimos las armas del Enemigo, pero cuando aparecieron los Gwetherain, mataron a muchos de los nuestros y dividieron nuestras fuerzas en la Dagorlad. Los rostros por los que alguna vez reconocí a los Gwetherain cuando tomaron los Anillos han desaparecido hace mucho, pero a este lo reconocí por su hoja. Lo llaman el Jinete Maldito, y espoleó a su corcel sobre las espaldas de Elfos, Hombres y orcos por igual!
'Por desgracia, nos vimos obligados a retirarnos antes de poder ayudar a muchos en el campo de batalla. Ahora luchamos por mantener el único camino sobre las grandes zanjas, y las fuerzas del Enemigo han traído más trabuquetes y ballestas al Dagorlad.
'¡Ayuda a los heridos en el campo, y esperemos que la Alianza llegue pronto para expulsar a las fuerzas del Enemigo!'

'¡${PLAYER}! Parecías ${PLAYER:perdido[m]|perdida[f]} en un trance, y no pude despertarte hasta este momento. Mi ${PLAYER:queridísimo amigo[m]|queridísima amiga[f]}, ¡no permitas que el Enemigo nuble tus pensamientos con visiones de derrota! Como Sauron bien sabe, ¡el dominio es nuestro en esta batalla!
'¡Ay! Un enemigo acorralado es el más mortífero, y ninguno es más traicionero que el Enemigo en este reino. Debemos dejar de lado nuestras preocupaciones por ahora y aprovechar nuestra ventaja.'

'Está decidido. Los Elfos de Lothlórien y los Elfos del Bosque Negro se prepararán para asaltar Dol Guldur.'

'Es tal como vimos en mi Espejo, ${PLAYER}. No puede haber duda al respecto ahora. Está decidido.
'Toma tu lugar, me dirigiré al Consejo de Guerra.'
'¡Gi suilon! Nos están esperando. Ven.'

'Como saben, he recuperado un texto con las palabras pronunciadas por Gil-galad hace mucho tiempo. Solo hablaré un poco de lo que estaba escrito, que se refiere a lo que ahora está por suceder:
'Cuando la luz se desvanezca por primera vez del Bosque de Oro, entonces la Sombra en el Bosque Verde puede ser derribada. Pero si la Sombra es derribada, más rápido se desvanecerá el Bosque de Oro.
'Creo que las palabras son claras, y aunque nos cause gran tristeza, aún sabemos qué camino debemos tomar.'

'Ven conmigo, ${PLAYER}. Hay cosas que el consejo querría discutir. Pero hay más, porque has sido de gran ayuda para nuestra causa y el Señor y la Dama desean agradecerte por tu servicio.'
'¡Noticias urgentes y maravillosas, ${PLAYER}! Glorfindel ha llegado a la Corte de Lothlórien. Te esperan. ¡Ve! ¡Ve ahora!'

'Has hecho tanto por nosotros, ${PLAYER} y nuestra gratitud es casi inconmensurable. Por las bellas estrellas de arriba y el signo de las hojas doradas, te libero y te libero de tu juramento de servicio.
'Ve ahora y sirve a quien y como quieras. Tengo plena fe en que llevarás luz y bondad dondequiera que tus viajes te lleven.'

'Casi no creí tu relato, ${PLAYER}, pero ahora debo estar atento a los mentirosos, porque ahí está Glorfindel en persona, entre el Consejo de Guerra. Te ruego que hables con Orophin, quien te presentará, pues esta es una ocasión de alegre ceremonia.'
