'We have managed to push through Udûn with only a small resistance. Now the task before us is to see what remains of Sauron's citadel, Barad-dûr. I am glad you are with us.'

'It is good to be in the thick of things again, isn't it ${PLAYER}. It was odd to see dwarves in Udûn. I did not realize any lived in Mordor! Do you suppose there are more of my lost kin in these lands?'

'You have been a great help, in the wake of Lachír's folly. You have helped lead us to conquer what resistance and pitfalls we have encountered here in Mordor.
'Some of our company has pressed through, past the gates of Carach Angren, and into Dor Amarth. When you have accomplished all that you wish to do here with us in Udûn, those in Dor Amarth could use your aid.'

'Argh! This certainly did not go as planned, ${PLAYER}. This is not the fault of either of us. Not a one of us expected these Morroval to descend and snatch the Ithil-stone from us all!
'Now we must return empty handed. Our only solace is that we have defeated The Black Word's lieutenants once again.
'Come let us start on the return.'

'We have made it this far undetected. The path ahead to Barad-dûr will be difficult.
'What's this?! Look ahead ${PLAYER}. There seems to be some sort of meeting taking place on the road between us and the ruined tower.
'You have dealt with some of these foes before. Still, a meeting of Dulgabêth's minions does not bode well for us.
'We must attempt to get closer and listen in on their plans, whatever they may be. From there we should have enough information to devise a proper plan.'
'I am not sure what it is we are seeing over there atop that rock. Its glow is soft, almost Elven. Do you suppose it is some sort of weapon perhaps?'
'We should return swiftly and tell the Elves of our company about what we have seen here. They may want to investigate this further.'

The Captain was last seen turning south off the main road as they made their way farther into Udûn.
'Well? Lend a hand. We must get through these.'

At last, Iadan lifts his gaze. His eyes widen in surprise when he sees you are no common soldier. You explain that you have come looking for Captain Lachír.
'Well now, we were hardly with him long, were we? Got a ways down the road, saw some refuse and he set us on it. Seemed to think some treasure, real treasure, might be just under the next bit of rubble. I cannot rightly say he set out with that in mind, but the idea seemed to seize him, somehow, if you understand me.'
A distant look comes into his eyes.
'It comes to me now that we may have been the lucky ones.'
'What did the Captain even expect us to find? Tell me that, will you!'
'Didn't find anything either, did you? Well, never get your hopes up, I always say. Still, you gave it a try. That's something.'
'Finding Captain Lachír and the other men is of utmost importance, ${CLASS}. Search for them just east along the central road, and then to the south.'

'Ah, good. They've sent another.'
The soldier does not even look up to take you in.
'Well then, what are you waiting for? Lend a hand. The Captain's command was to roll over every stone and pry open every soldier's chest until we found something of value.
'If we don't step up the pace, we'll be out here yet another day!'
'Been out here more than a day, we have. Rummaging among old chests and broken pots and not found one thing. My back's sore. My arms are sore. Everything's bloody sore!'

'You find us bereft of command or purpose, ${CLASS}. The captain charged with overseeing this encampment marched off yesterday, nearly all the stationed men at his side. The scouting expedition, as he named it, disappeared into that smoky green miasma and we have not seen nor heard sign of them since.
'Captain Lachír's only orders to the few of us remaining were to stay put.
'Surely he meant to have returned by now and surely the thing of utmost importance is to learn what became of them...'
Mulnír then glares meaningfully at the other soldier.
'... no matter what my brother-at-arms here will attempt to persuade you. We cannot go after them - our orders forbid it - but you may. I beg of you, say that you will. Lives may depend on it.
'We saw them head east into Udûn, then turn south shortly down the central road. Any search for them must start there, I think.'
The encampment in Udûn, known as the Foothold, has not given any report in two days.

Mulnír sighs.
'Yes, you have my word that we will send a report - just as soon as we have gathered our wits and made sense of this mess.'
'Duties? Ha. You can tell that to Captain Lachír and all the men he took with him. Wherever they are.'

'I have expected a report these last two days from the Foothold, that is the near encampment of our men in Udûn. A large, well-provisioned force is stationed there, under Captain Lachír, and I can think of no reason for the silence.

'To be fully honest, I can't see how there could be treasure down those shafts. I reckon the Captain knows more about such things than I!'
'Maybe the Captain's treasure is all in this next one.'
'Shut the hatchways? Are you - are you sure it will be all right?'
'Open any hatchway you find that's still closed. Only... stand back a bit and take care when you do.'

'You found no treasure either, did you?'
Mellor looks deflated and tired.
'Only goblins and the like? Aye, that's the same rotten luck we've been having. Orders are orders, though, and if we keep at it I'm sure things will turn around.'
Alarmed, you tell them that you doubt there is any treasure down there, and that what they are doing is foolhardy and dangerous.

Othras looks relieved.
'You really think so? I - I thought it was a kind of madness, but then the Captain is so clever and self-sure. And as time went on, it seemed that after all, it was the reason for our search party. But now I feel as if some fog has lifted. You have given me the courage to trust my eyes and heart. What a relief, eh, Mellor?
'Will you help us just once more, friend? I think we should shut back up some of the hatches we opened, before an overwhelming number of Orcs and goblins come scuttling out of them all.'

'Well met! I cannot say how good it is to find a friendly face out here. Did you take note of the several hatchways positioned about this area? They lead down into crawl-ways among the forges.
'We were given the tiresome and dangerous charge of opening them up in search of, well, I cannot say why but the Captain felt sure some treasure, or artifact, or powerful weapon might lie within. In truth, as we went on he talked of little else. At every bend, under every potsherd, he felt, something marvelous must lie!
'Would you help us with our task? We have done some and do not have much farther to go.'
'Yes, before we are overwhelmed. Let us all shut some of these hatchways!'
'You have our solemn thanks, good ${RACE}, for freeing us from this folly. We will return to the Foothold with all speed, I assure you. But first, is there aught we can do for you?'
'I must confess, I will be glad to warm my hands by a fire back at the Foothold!'
'After leaving us to this hard work, the Captain and the rest of the party set off east down the road. Then, some ways off, they turned northwardly.'

'Perhaps it is well that you are looking after him. We know he carried on farther down the road. We watched him go - I'll confess it. Set his sights on something and after a stretch turned north. You go looking, you'll find signs of him, I guess.'

Captain Lachír's search party wandered the basin of Udûn, leaving men here and there to search in vain for some imagined treasure. After that, Lachír backtracked, leading his remaining company up the rising northward road.

The look-out shivers.

'That which you see is named Anglach, perhaps the greatest of forges in Mordor. I have stood and kept watch on it since yesterday, when Captain Lachír posted me here.'
The look-out seems scared and miserable. You tell him to return to the Foothold and it is as if a great weight has been lifted from his shoulders.

'You wish to know where Captain Lachír has gone? That I can say, and better than you might imagine.
'He set off east you see, after leaving us here, and was gone for some time. Then, some half a day later we saw him marching back along the road and our hearts leaped, only to sink again. They came not for us, nor were they returning to the Foothold. No, we watched them make their way down the central road, then turn up on the rising northward path. 'Tales of Old Gondor, it was. Oft around a camp-fire he would read out of it. Do you remember? Such fine old kings and warriors. Their weapons bore names and their raiments shone. Their deeds were great, their words were poetry, and their deaths brought tears to the eye.
'Perhaps that is what old Lachír wanted for himself. In some way it was like that, was it not? And yet unlike, too. Makes you wonder if the men in those old tales felt themselves in a book... or felt something more as we feel now.'

'Without your help, ${CLASS}, all this would have gone - well, more poorly than it has. I know well enough that our mourning is not truly ended, but we cannot linger on it.
'Please, accept our thanks. Do not you linger, either.'

'I deem that a proper rite for our lost captain. He died as he lived, sword in hand. We shall not forget him, but the empty space he leaves will not long stay vacant, I think. A new captain will likely be sent down, and with no great delay.
'If we wish to stay in good graces, we had best return to camp and see that all is returned to order. But that is on your own head, for I am no captain, not today and not tomorrow.'

'It is too easy by far to forget the Lachír we knew, just as Mulnír said. The one who led us into battle and was ever our protector and companion. That Lachír and the one we knew here, who strayed on foot and in reason from the path... from every path... I feel that they are the same man.
'For perhaps there was always some madness in his nature. Perhaps the dreams that lived in the old tales of Gondor led us bravely to war and then vainly, ruinously through the wreckage of Udûn.
'And before we condemn him in his memory, perhaps we should look within our own hearts and wonder what dreams and what in our own natures has been twisted and made monstrous by this place. Truly, perhaps it is only our humble stations that have kept each other of us from doing greater harm.'
'Across the road? Yes, you have my word.'
'My heart is full sore with many things, but I will go.'
'We owe him that, at least.'
'I will be there.'
'Yes, I will go.'
'Of course. I will see you there.'
'Fine. We will do this and then we will be done with him.'

Mulnír clears his throat, thinks for a moment, and begins.
'We all followed our Captain into battle. Beside him, we feared nothing and we risked all bravely, gladly, and with true honour. Whatever befell us in the last few days, let that not be forgotten.
'${PLAYER}, you have his effects?'

'Something must be done. We have no captain now and many lives have been lost. There are customs and rites to be observed - or are we not on the same perilous road he went down?
'We have no captain and so we will all stand about unless someone begins. Yes, there we have it.
'Will you help me once more, friend? Gather the men and what belongings of Lachír's you can find. We will meet on the high platform across the road. It is as good a spot as any.'

After a long moment, Mulnír nods.
'It is worse than I feared. Worse by far. But I will tell you this, ${CLASS}: I believe that flaw was always in the Captain's character. Udûn was but the flood that showed us the weakness in the flood-wall.
'You did all you could - more than most men would be capable of. We are in a hostile land and peril is ever at a soldier's heels. Only this - this was an awful sort of peril, was it not?'
'My men should be here any moment with more ingots. Wait with me. You will see!'

'We found quite a store of these, tucked away. I knew the moment I laid sight on them what they were. They are heavy. I have set my men to bearing them here. They have made many trips already. When we have all of it, we will rig a pulley to get it up.
'You see? I have it all worked out. At last, everything is falling into place.'

'I have found it at last. Not, I confess, as I imagined it, a bright sword or luminous pendant. I sought high and low for those, in vain. But these ingots, why, they are heavy with power. They are hot to the touch! Think what a sword forged from this metal might be. With the Enemy's own works shall I bow and break his kingdom!'

'Have you guessed it? It was into Anglach that Captain Lachír led the search party. He felt that for certain, that miraculous treasure he had become fixated on must lie within. I have watched for the better part of a day and still they have not returned. Does that mean they have found the treasure? I am unsure. I - I do not like lingering on the thought.
'If you seek him, that is where you are bound, too. As for me, I will take your good council and make straight for the Foothold!'
You have found Captain Lachír. He, in turn, has found ingots of metal he believes are imbued with great power, and ordered his men to gather all they could find.

When you meet Lachír's eyes in the light, there is a wildness behind a mask of bravery. It is fear.
'Have all my men turned on me? Can I have pushed them too far in search of something powerful, something truly magnificent? Can sullen resentment - or greed, greed and jealousy have driven them to such ends?
'But what am I saying? Did you see their faces? It was madness, madness and not mutiny written there, plain as day.'
The captain falls silent abruptly, brooding.
'Ah, and then there is this artifact! It is something else, entirely! It looks almost crusted over intentionally. Help me clear it off and we shall see what lies beneath.'
The meeting between the discontent forge-workers and the Easterlings has been arranged, the meeting place prepared, and the flag raised. Now for the meeting to begin.
What Was Spoken and What Revealed
Return to Barathron
Talk to Kurtil
You should return to Barathron in the Foothold in Udûn and tell him all about the disastrous meeting and the hopes that died there.
You should talk to Kurtil, who has arrived at the meeting place in Maudhúl Ghûg.

'Stand here. Wait with me. I will tell you more of the signs shared among our kind.'
Kurtil tells you more. Time passes.

'You return! You have been gone long. What do you know of the flags? What secret plans do the lurkers plan for us?'
You begin to tell him all that happened and his face goes slack.
'Captain of the Pit! And you know not what became of that Nurnhoth, Kurtil? He simply slipped off. It is all so peculiar. Nor did I ever imagine, friend, that I should feel sympathy for the bangers and the clangers here that armed the Enemy's armies against us. All suffered under the Dark Lord's reign, that much is clear!
'Now, at least, we know the name of our true adversary in this place. Perhaps with time we may earn the trust of those who fled and lived and with their help work against him.'

'They will all soon be here. Will it go well? We have done so much, have we not? Ah, but who can say! Still, we must wait, yes? Wait and try.
'Soon they will be here. Wait with me, ${CLASS}. Not long now. Not long.'

'Scout the camp top and bottom, thin how many prying eyes are thereabouts, and raise the meeting flag. Then I'll be there, though mark my word, it'll be the end of us all.'
'What choice do we have? You go ahead and do as he asks. We will meet there, no?'

'And how have you come into this whole affair, anyway, I'd like to know? Make no mistake, I'd rather leave this place than stay. No one's likely to live long, staying here. But if you ask me, this meeting is only going to hasten our end.
'Go right under the Captain of the Pit's nose and think he won't find out? True, the back of Maudhúl Ghûg is hidden enough. No spies or enforcers ever look there... still, precautions must be taken!
'I won't set foot within a stone's throw of Kurtil's little gathering unless Maudhúl Ghûg's been scouted out to the last inch. I suppose that's you doing this, isn't it? And while you're at it, see that there are not so many lads kicking around those tents. When everything is clear as good steel and as safe as caves... raise the meeting flag and, bah! I'll come. I'll come and bring my people with me, too.'
'I knew you would turn his mind, friend! You go ahead and do as he asks. Here, this is the meeting flag. I will follow.'
'Soon they will be here. Soon, yes! At last.'

'If Gradrágh agrees, many will follow. Such is an overseer's sway, yes? Only Gradrágh here, fears, well - you will see. Calm him, do as he asks, sing him sweet songs until he agrees.
'Without Gradrágh and without poor dead Ushkbál here, we have no mouth of authority and we have too few who follow. We have, in fact, nothing.'
Kurtil studies your face, seriously, for a moment.
'I am Nurnhoth. Do you know what that is? We are slaves of Nurn. A sea is there and grain growing leagues by leagues. Slaves, all slaves there, every last one of my kind. Not once may be. Not long, long ago, if you believe the tattered old tellings. But now, we know only slavery and work and doing as leader tells. One such as Gradrágh can lead us to foolish death or great deeds with only a command. But not one in a thousand Nurnhoth have will to command themselves.
'Now you understand why Gradrágh is needed, yes? My kind, Orc-kind, dwarf-kind, all must have a strong arm to follow.'

Elrond se encuentra dentro de Tham Send, en la Última morada.
Has reunido tus pertenencias y los escritos de Elrond y ahora deberías regresar junto a él.
'No deseo que dejes nada atrás, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}.'

'Es triste oír que Hithgol continúe aquejado por sus males, pero guardo la esperanza de que pronto se recupere como tú lo hiciste, ${PLAYER}. Verás, cuando por fin la batalla llegó a Barad-dûr, el propio Sauron abatió a Hithgol con un golpe mortal, y pareció que solo por la gracia de los Valar no fue aniquilado en el acto. Aun así, el acero de las armas del Señor Oscuro estaba corrompido de manera muy similar a la hoja que te atravesó, y él ha sufrido sus efectos durante muchos largos años, como tú. Ahora bien... hemos hablado bastante del pasado, ¡volvamos la mente a los días venideros!
'Mucho ha cambiado desde la última vez que viajamos juntos desde Imladris, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Parece ahora una Edad de los Hombres, y percibo que el tiempo de los Elfos en la Tierra Media se acerca a su fin.
'En efecto, muchos han abandonado este reino rumbo al Extremo Oeste a bordo de las naves de Círdan, nuestro antiguo amigo. Hoy es llamado el Carpintero de Barcos por quienes conocen su obra, y mora en Mithlond con los pocos que aún permanecen a su servicio como hábiles artesanos. Gran parte de la madera que utiliza Círdan es transportada a Mithlond por medio del puerto de Celondim, a lo largo de Ered Luin, y es allí adonde debes viajar para alcanzar los Puertos.
', he reunido tus pertenencias y algunos suministros para tu viaje. He dispuesto tu anillo en su estuche sobre la mesa al otro lado de la estancia, y tu armadura reposa en un arcón junto a tu lecho. Aún conserva las marcas de la batalla, pero el tiempo no la ha deteriorado más allá. En verdad, el paso de una edad solo ha empañado nuestra luz... y ha dado origen a la sombra en el Este. Sobre tales asuntos, también he preparado para ti un tomo de escritos sobre la historia de la Tercera Edad hasta ahora. Puedes reclamarlos antes de partir.
'Cuando estés ${PLAYER:preparado[m]|preparada[f]}, hablaremos más sobre tu viaje a Celondim.'

'Muy bien, ${PLAYER}.
'Con el tiempo tu fuerza regresará, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}, y el poder de tu anillo se alzará con ella. Espero que mis escritos también te resulten de utilidad. Relato gran parte del tiempo que transcurrió mientras sanaba tu herida, pero ni siquiera yo puedo conocer todo lo que ha acaecido desde el final de la Segunda Edad.
'En cuanto a tu viaje, mis hijos te acompañarán hasta Celondim en el curso de sus propios recorridos. Elladan y Elrohir seguirán una expedición a las ruinas de Edhelion, encabezada por el Elfo Dorollas en mi nombre. No hables de esto con nadie fuera de su compañía, pero tuve una extraña premonición... y en ella, en medio de un campo de visiones borrosas, una voz se alzó diciendo:
\qHuellas rojo sangre sobre negro color de nieve, donde camina el Rey Funesto para reclamar su trono y concluir lo que fue iniciado.\q
'Es un acertijo inquietante, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}, y no creo que encuentre pronta solución. ¿Tienes alguna idea sobre su significado?'
Escuchas un crujido amortiguado mientras las puertas de Tham Send se abren.
'¡Ah! Tanto mejor; tales preocupaciones conviene dejarlas a Dorollas y su expedición. Mis hijos te aguardan junto a la puerta del patio central, y cuando estés ${PLAYER:listo[m]|lista[f]} para partir, te guiarán hasta Celondim a lo largo de Ered Luin.
'Que tu viaje sea veloz y libre de penurias, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Namárië.'

Reúne los escritos de Elrond

Al asomarte, el tenue resplandor de tu antigua armadura capta la luz...

Elrond se encuentra dentro de Tham Send, en la Última morada.
Has reunido tus pertenencias y los escritos de Elrond y ahora deberías regresar junto a él.
'No deseo que dejes nada atrás, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}.'

'Es triste oír que Hithgol continúe aquejado por sus males, pero guardo la esperanza de que pronto se recupere como tú lo hiciste, ${PLAYER}. Verás, cuando por fin la batalla llegó a Barad-dûr, el propio Sauron abatió a Hithgol con un golpe mortal, y pareció que solo por la gracia de los Valar no fue aniquilado en el acto. Aun así, el acero de las armas del Señor Oscuro estaba corrompido de manera muy similar a la hoja que te atravesó, y él ha sufrido sus efectos durante muchos largos años, como tú. Ahora bien....... hemos hablado bastante del pasado, ¡volvamos la mente a los días venideros!
'Mucho ha cambiado desde la última vez que viajamos juntos desde Imladris, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Parece ahora una Edad de los Hombres, y percibo que el tiempo de los Elfos en la Tierra Media se acerca a su fin.
'En efecto, muchos han abandonado este reino rumbo al Extremo Oeste a bordo de las naves de Círdan, nuestro antiguo amigo. Hoy es llamado el Carpintero de Barcos por quienes conocen su obra, y mora en Mithlond con los pocos que aún permanecen a su servicio como hábiles artesanos. Gran parte de la madera que utiliza Círdan es transportada a Mithlond por medio del puerto de Celondim, a lo largo de Ered Luin, y es allí adonde debes viajar para alcanzar los Puertos.
', he reunido tus pertenencias y algunos suministros para tu viaje. He dispuesto tu anillo en su estuche sobre la mesa al otro lado de la estancia, y tu armadura reposa en un arcón junto a tu lecho. Aún conserva las marcas de la batalla, pero el tiempo no la ha deteriorado más allá. En verdad, el paso de una edad solo ha empañado nuestra...l...z... y ha dado origen a la sombra en el Este. Sobre tales asuntos, también he preparado para ti un tomo de escritos sobre la historia de la Tercera Edad hasta ahora. Puedes reclamarlos antes de partir.
'Cuando estés ${PLAYER:preparado[m]|preparada[f]}, hablaremos más sobre tu viaje a Celondim.'

'Muy bien, ${PLAYER}.
'Con el tiempo tu fuerza regresará, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}, y el poder de tu anillo se alzará con ella. Espero que mis escritos también te resulten de utilidad. Relato gran parte del tiempo que transcurrió mientras sanaba tu herida, pero ni siquiera yo puedo conocer todo lo que ha acaecido desde el final de la Segunda Edad.
'En cuanto a tu viaje, mis hijos te acompañarán hasta Celondim en el curso de sus propios recorridos. Elladan y Elrohir seguirán una expedición a las ruinas de Edhelion, encabezada por el Elfo Dorollas en mi nombre. No hables de esto con nadie fuera de su compañía, pero tuve una extraña premonición... y en ella, en medio de un campo de visiones borrosas, una voz se alzó diciendo:
\qHuellas rojo sangre sobre negro color de nieve, donde camina el Rey Funesto para reclamar su trono y concluir lo que fue iniciado.\q
'Es un acertijo inquietante, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}, y no creo que encuentre pronta solución. ¿Tienes alguna idea sobre su significado?'
Escuchas un crujido amortiguado mientras las puertas de Tham Send se abren.
'¡Ah! Tanto mejor; tales preocupaciones conviene dejarlas a Dorollas y su expedición. Mis hijos te aguardan junto a la puerta del patio central, y cuando estés ${PLAYER:listo[m]|lista[f]} para partir, te guiarán hasta Celondim a lo largo de Ered Luin.
'Que tu viaje sea veloz y libre de penurias, ${PLAYER:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Namárië.'
Preparativos para el Viaje

'Ah, you return. You have looked and looked, yes? And you have seen. I see it is so! Kurtil, I am named. And you are... ${PLAYER}, yes? It is well. Now tell me what you know and what you have learned.'
You tell the slave what Barathron thought they were and what he thought they might mean, and he frowns. You relate, to the best of your memory, what signal flags you found in the basin and a thin smile appears on his pained mouth. You get the uneasy impression that he may be learning more from you than you are from him.
At last, he nods.
'Keen eyes and swift legs. But are you help or are you hurt? Help, I think and no, no not cruel. Not... deceiving. Then I will offer help for your help. What I know of Udûn, so too will you know. And in truth, of Udûn I know much.'

'Know what that is?'
His eyes turn up to the signal flag. He speaks in clean, confident Westron.
'I would say that you do, yes. But... they tell no tales to you, no. Not yet, they do not. When you have seen them all and you have returned to me, then there will be much to say. Much to tell, yes? I think so.'

'Good. Now, listen closely. If the whispers are true, there are signal flags placed around the near basin of Udûn. Taken together, these symbols and signs, understood only by the forge-workers of this place, convey a message.
'For instance, a half-circle might be taken to mean dawn, or perhaps dusk, and three close lines might be taken for a meeting. A raised arm might be taken for taskmaster and one bent like a snake might be water - or drink. In truth, I know not.
'If you will go and make a study of these banners, however, I feel certain that together we may get to the root of it and so discover what plans the lurking dwellers of this place are making behind our backs. It is sure to be something treacherous and harmful to Gondor!'
'If you will go and make a study of these banners, I feel certain we will solve the riddle of this meeting and what mischief it portends.'

'A most intriguing riddle has come to us. Perhaps a riddle of great importance. Who can say? A dying Nurnhoth - those are the Mordor slave-men, you see - told us of a secret plan among the forge-labourers of Udûn. Stranger still, it is all arranged in a voiceless code!
'The poor soul could tell us little else before he passed, save that the plan should take place soon.
'How inconvenient that our Captain has not returned and that he left clear orders that we were to hold the camp until he did! No, Mulnír, I do not think he is lost or in peril. I fear what this plan will be. I fear that it will come and go before there is any chance to find it out. And what will happen if it does?
'Ah, good ${RACE}, you will unravel this riddle for me, won't you? Someone must!'

Captain Róglarg has asked you to take over the duties of the Orcs that were slain in Dath Nethryn. You should speak to other Orcs in Cirith Ungol and learn what needs to be done.

'All of them? Really now?'
You nod.
'I'm impressed, Silent One. Turning a new leaf, are you? Well, keep it turned.
'The Top Ones want this place to look like it did before Lugbúrz caved in on itself. Between Cirith Ungol and Durthang, we've got to find a way to keep those tarks out of Mordor!
'Ah, but it's not just the tarks, is it?'

'Ah, but now that you're back, I've got some work for you!
'We lost a couple more Orcs this morning in the swamp, so more work's got to fall onto less backs. And I think it ought to be yours, Silent One!
'Some have even been complaining that those Orcs shirked their duties by dying. Isn't that a shame? Well, it's all got to get done. The High Up sent a nosy Man to watch our backs, and I won't be made to look a fool like Shagrat!
'See what Práguk, Krúrglok, Lúksu, Danghát, and Shíkurz want, but don't go far. I have plenty of work for you, too!
'Now, unless I tell you otherwise, there's no need to report back to me or any of that lot. Believe me, I'll know if you didn't follow my orders, Silent One....
'Hah! Good to be back, eh?'

'I believe I have found the emissary to the Gúrzyul you spoke of, but we must deal with him before the tower is overrun!'

'Indeed, Shelob must desire something within the Tower of Cirith Ungol!
'The mind of a spider so ancient is unknown to me, but perhaps she seeks to expand her lair and heal her wounds within the walls of the fortress.
'I can hear the cries of her children within the walls, and they have only grown stronger. Captain Róglarg's garrison is failing without his leadership, and it is likely Cirith Ungol will soon fall.
'It pains me greatly to agree with one of the Gúrzyul, but Ugrukhôr was wise to reinforce the garrison. Shelob wields power few have ever known, and if she ventures from the Ephel Dúath, it could spell doom for not only Mordor, but also the lands of our peoples as well!
'Cirith Ungol must not fall to Shelob! You spoke of an emissary to one of the Gúrzyul, my friend. I shall seek him in the tower and attempt to convince him that the will of his master is imperiled! If they do not reinforce the tower with an even greater garrison, all will be lost!
'While I search for him, I would appreciate your skill in hindering Shelob's siege of the tower.'

'It seems that the Orcs have begun to fight amongst themselves, but I wonder why Orcs of Udûn and of Durthang would flee into this land?
'To flee into a land beset by hungering foes with allegiance to none...it is unwise, to say the least.'

'This bodes ill, ${PLAYER}.
'We have barely stepped into the lands of Lhingris and no sooner have we found the vile webs of Ungwetári's children. Indeed, I am reminded of the darkest days of Mirkwood....'
Legolas looks at the fallen Orcs.
'If the spiders no longer fear the Orcs, I doubt they shall remain in the shadows of Lhingris much longer. Their prey is plentiful, and no longer guarded by the might of the Dark Lord.
'I cannot discern whence these Orcs came for their armour is ruined and wreathed in webs, but to know it may help us learn how they found their way to Lhingris.
'I shall work to free these from their webs and uncover their heraldry, but would you examine the slain Orcs on the road? Perhaps some have met with a less gruesome fate....'

'Hah! An Elf-warrior? I think the Orcs may have misjudged Master Samwise! Although, from the sound of it, the Orcs of Lugvarg may have found some of our friends' belongings left behind from when they passed through Mordor.
'It is curious that the Orcs of this Kála-murg are unaware of the Silent One's treachery. They think him missing? I suppose they cannot spare much thought for him while a strange disease is spreading through the Orc-hold. The disease must be a potent one....'

'Be still, ${PLAYER}.
'Down in the vale, I see a few gatherings of Orcs positioned beside the road. Trackers of some kind, I believe. We shall have to move more carefully from here onward!
'What do they search for, I wonder? They must realize it is too late to secure the Enemy's Ring!
'Ah, but it seems they are more interested in talking than keeping to their posts. I see gatherings of Orcs by what I believe to be a watch-tower, by an Orc-hold of some sort, and another gathering of them beside the road in the vale.
'Will you eavesdrop on them, my friend? We might learn more of what has happened in Lhingris since the Enemy's downfall!
'I shall keep watch here and stop any other Orcs from approaching you!'

Captain Róglarg can be found in the courtyard of Cirith Ungol.

Belzagar can be found in the turret of the Tower of Cirith Ungol.
Captain Róglarg has ordered you to report to Belzagar in the Tower of Cirith Ungol. The emissary of the Pale Herald is curious to learn how you escaped the fall of the Towers of the Teeth.

'Welcome, Orc, are you the one known as the Silent One?'
You nod.
'Ah, very good. I am Belzagar, one of the many emissaries of Rûkhor the Pale Herald. Captain Róglarg has asked that he and his garrison be sent elsewhere, but it shall not be so. It is my duty to see that Cirith Ungol remains in the hands of Mordor, and the demands of a single Uruk will not impede it!
'Although it is indeed curious that you escaped alive, I did not ask you here to learn how you fled the Teeth. I am not of as simple a mind as Róglarg perceives. You shall deliver this message to him by whatever means you have:
\qCirith Ungol is to remain guarded against the foes of Mordor. Gothmog will not repel them from Imlad Morgul, so an attack from the west remains anticipated. Ungwetári, or Shelob in their Orkish tongue, must be kept sated in Torech Ungol. She remains a threat to the leaders of Mordor. Sacrifice as many Orcs as necessary to keep her from venturing out of her lair.\q
'I am aware that you cannot speak, and perhaps that will spare you Róglarg's wrath. I am wise enough to not deliver such a message myself.
'You may go now, Orc. Do as I bid!'

'Hoi! What'd the tark have to say?'
You attempt to demonstrate that Captain Róglarg and his garrison are not allowed to abandon Cirith Ungol by the will of the Gúrzyul. You are forced to repeat your demonstration a few times, but Captain Róglarg seems to understand its meaning.
'Damned tarks! And who's going to hold the tower, you ask? The Uruks! It's always the Uruks!
'Well, if that's how it's going to be, we need to get Her Ladyship's little biters off our backs! I think old Shelob's gotten just a bit too hungry....'

'Now that that's settled, we've got another problem. The Top Ones have their lackey, Belzagar, up in the turret watching all of us... and I don't like it.
'The Pale Herald sent him here because he thinks Ugrukhôr didn't set things right with all the Shagrat business! Aye, the Captain set it right all right, but the tarks never want to hear it from an Uruk!
'For some reason, he wants to speak with you about how you escaped the Teeth, but I don't think he's quite of the mind to understand your title.
'Ah well, best to not keep him waiting!'

'${PLAYER}, we must go down into Dath Nethryn at once! Our hunt could soon be ended -- for good or ill.

Captain Róglarg sees you and beckons you over.
'Well, now! Where'd you get off to, Silent One? Even the Silent Watchers are upset you've come back!
'Ah, but nowhere good, I bet. Offering more dead to Shelob, were you?'
You nod.
'Nar, I don't know why you bother. It's not as if Her Ladyship cares for you...or any of us!
'Ah...what's that fine weapon you've got there? Nabbed it off one of the tarks, I bet!'

'Judging by the missive we found in Kála-murg, it seems an Uruk by the name of Captain Róglarg is now in command of Cirith Ungol. Stranger still, it seems his Orcs have some sort of alliance with Ungwetári....
'I would ask that you take the Silent One's armour and sneak into Cirith Ungol. Perhaps what you learn there may lead us to Shelob or uncover some terrible plan for the armies of King Elessar. If the words of my father are to be trusted, Ungwetári... this Shelob, is beyond the skill of you or I alone. However, if she is found, we may prepare to move against her and ready our defences should she wander from the Ephel Dúath.
'It is fortunate, indeed, that the Silent One could not speak. If Frodo and Sam fooled them, I have no fear that you will do the same!
'${PLAYER}, I ask that you only return to me when you are able. I do not want them to become suspicious of you!
'I shall keep watch from afar, and attempt to aid you if your disguise fails.'

You tell Frodo that there's no time for tales until you get far, far away from this tower!

Legolas has grown concerned by the continued tremors beneath Lhingris and fears that Shelob shall soon venture forth from her lair.

'What have you found, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Legolas that the tunnel to Torech Ungol now lies open.
'Shelob is now free to venture from her lair if she wishes it, but I do not believe she will -- not yet.
'However, the smallest of her children have scaled the walls of Cirith Ungol. Whatever she seeks now lies within the walls of the tower....'

'${PLAYER}, these tremors only seem to be growing more terrible....
'Whatever the severity of her wounds, I worry that Shelob will soon find her way out of Torech Ungol and into the hills of Lhingris.
'I would ask that you return to Torech Ungol and see if the tremors have exposed any new paths into Shelob's lair.
'Be swift! I shall keep watch at a distance, and aid you if the need arises!'
Legolas spotted a wounded Orc of a similar stature and bearing to the Silent One travelling southward deeper into Rath Cail.

The trail of the Silent One's blood leads deeper into Rath Cail.
Legolas has spotted an Orc with a similar stature and bearing fleeing deeper into Rath Cail. You should follow the trail of Orkish blood and see where it leads.

'It appears the Silent One is disliked amongst the Orcs for a greater reason than his queer appearance. I think the Silent One has a taste for Orc-flesh!
'Ah, but what strange trinkets for an Orc to hoard....'
Legolas kneels before the armour and cloak piled in the Silent One's cave.
'Wait a moment, ${PLAYER}. There is a very familiar hair caught in this armour!'

'${PLAYER}, while you were gone I spied an Orc with a similar stature and bearing to your description of the Silent One.
'The Silent One must have met some foe on the road, for his arm was wounded. He left behind him a sparse trail of blood as he fled deeper into Rath Cail. I do not believe he thought himself watched by any other than the Orcs and creatures of Lhingris, so the advantage is ours.
'You said he had piled the bodies of his kin as an offering to the spiders? If he has some arrangement with Shelob or her children, he could be a very useful Orc!
'Let us follow his Orkish blood and see if it leads us to him!'
Desperate to capture an elusive Elf-warrior, the Orc-trackers of Kála-murg now keep a close watch on Rath Cail.
A gruesome figure shambles out of the shadows...

Glupronk can likely be found deep within the Orc-hold of Kála-murg.
The Orc, Glupronk, is in command of Kála-murg and seeks the Elf-warrior. Legolas hopes to learn more of the Orcs of Lhingris and of the hidden cavern where Shelob makes her home.

'What have you found, ${PLAYER}?'
You hand Legolas the missive from Cirith Ungol.
'Are you certain the Orcs have confused Master Samwise with the Elf-warrior? This Captain Róglarg seems to think Sam slew an entire garrison of Orcs by himself. Master Samwise is a loyal and brave hobbit, but he is not a practised warrior!
'Stranger still, Captain Róglarg speaks of the Elf-warrior sticking a pin in Shelob. A mere blade could not wound such an ancient creature... not on its own. If only Sam had told us of his encounter with Shelob!
'There can no longer be any doubt! Ungwetári still dwells in the Ephel Dúath, but she now tends her wounds in the shadowed caverns of the mountains...'

'${PLAYER}, what did you hear of Kála-murg?'
You tell Legolas about the disease ravaging Kála-murg and the Orc-tracker, Glupronk, that was mentioned by the Orcs.
'This Glupronk must lead the Orc-trackers in their search for the Elf-warrior. It is likely he knows many of the hidden paths of Lhingris, and his knowledge may be useful in our search.
'Travel to Kála-murg and seek the Orc, Glupronk. If he bears any orders, take them and we shall see what can be learned from them.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. We know little of the disease that has taken the Orcs....'

'Well, Silent One? Not so skilled at tracking today, are you?'
You shake your head.
'For your sake, you'd better hope he tripped into one of Her Ladyship's tunnels or caught his death in the swamp! The Top Ones will skin us both if he gets back to the tarks' city!
'I've got my eye on you, Silent One. No more mistakes!'

'It's the Elves, too. One of them at least!
'Shagrat's a lying fool. There isn't anything in Mordor worth enough to make a whole garrison draw their blades on each other. Not even the damned Rings!
'It was an Elf all right, and he made it clear he's got no business fighting Elves. We've held the tower for years and Shagrat nearly loses it in one day! Nar, the Black Pits are too good for him....
'Ah, but we're going to find him, Silent One!
'And I know just the places to look....'
As countless spiders of Shelob's brood pour forth from the Tower of Cirith Ungol, Legolas hopes to uncover their source and prevent more from swarming into the fortress.
Eyes in the Dark

Find the source of Shelob's brood in the Tower of Cirith Ungol

You should bring word to Legolas in the turret of the Tower of Cirith Ungol as soon as you are able.

'While I seek out this emissary of the Gúrzyul in the turret, you must find the source of the spiders!
'You spoke of a gate in the depths of the tower...perhaps the spiders of Shelob's brood have found a way to breach it.
'If that is so, we must move even more swiftly to stem the tide!
'Go now, and I shall meet you in the turret!'

Legolas is standing in the Silent Haunt.
You have tracked the Silent One to his lair in Lhingris and discovered a tattered black cloak and Orkish armour bearing a single strand of Frodo's hair. You should talk to Legolas and think of how Frodo and Sam came to disguise themselves as Orcs of Mordor.
'I wonder what became of the hobbits when they passed into Lhingris....'

'Whatever befell Master Samwise as he and Frodo passed near Cirith Ungol, he does not wish to speak of it. By the sound of this Róglarg's message, it seems as if he performed heroics far beyond that of a simple gardener!
'Ah, but his choices are his own, and I will not press him to recount such a tale.
'However, I remain curious about one thing. If their disguises fooled the Orcs of Cirith Ungol, I think we may have found a way to learn more of \qHer Ladyship\q!'

'This is very curious, indeed. A strand of Frodo's hair is caught in this armour....
'This \qSilent One\q is quite the clever Orc! I doubt most of his kin would have paid such a find any attention at all!
'How much did Master Samwise choose to omit from his tale of Frodo's journey through Mordor, I wonder? It seems clear that they took the guise of Orkish warriors to pass unhindered through those at Cirith Ungol that did not answer the call to the Morannon, but when did such a need first arise... and why?'
An Orc known as the Silent One has betrayed the inhabitants of Durthang to the children of Shelob, casting the lands of Lhingris and Udûn into turmoil.
The Silent One

The Silent One can likely be found off the road to the south of Durthang with the slain Orcs he took from Durthang.
A dying Uruk has asked you to kill the Silent One, an Orc who has seemingly aligned himself with the spiders of Lhingris.

'An Orc has slain his own kin to offer tribute to the spiders of Lhingris? These are very strange tidings, my friend. And the Uruk used the name Shelob? It seems Ungwetári is known by that name to the Orcs....
'As for the Silent One, I wonder how he gained such a curious title. Such a name would be well-earned of a skilled archer or huntsman. Ah, but these are Orcs we speak of! Perhaps his tongue was cut from his mouth for some trifle....
'If he truly does mean to serve the spiders of Lhingris, perhaps he can lead us to the lair of this Shelob. There is little time to consider such things here, my friend.'

'Nar, not long at all...
'That little sneak... the Silent One... he betrayed us! We were holding against the spiders until he showed up, and some help he was! The Silent One killed my Orcs with his arrows... and took some of them before the spiders got to them...
'Maybe the little rat is bringing them to Shelob... or maybe he's eating them himself!
'I won't beg, but if you find him... kill him! If he finds you... well....
'Now shove off, and let me die in peace!'

'Well, that lot there ought to do it! A sorry business, this, but it has to be done!'

'Nar, we can't go on like this!
'We haven't sent Shelob anything since Lugbúrz fell, and I think Her Ladyship's gotten a bit spoiled. Either that, or She's in a foul mood from whatever the Elf-warrior did to her....
'When Her Ladyship is hungry, there's only one thing for it. The garrison's going to have to get by with a few less Orcs, or we'll all be for the pot!
'Gather up eight Orcs, and make it quick! We'd best get this over with!'

'Hah! A clever Orc, indeed!
'${PLAYER}, the trails of blood converge here in this swamp!
'Even now, the Silent One must seek shelter in its shallows. We must find him before we lose the path!'

'${PLAYER}, we must find the Silent One.
'As his face is mostly obscured by his helmet, his armour could be of great use to us in learning more of Shelob and her children. If we can recover his armour, you might gain entry into Cirith Ungol and go unnoticed as one of the many Orcs in its garrison. Indeed, Captain Róglarg even expects the Silent One to report to Cirith Ungol!
'The Silent One knew well enough not to remain here, and he left two trails of blood leading deeper into Lhingris to escape our pursuit. I shall follow one, and you should follow the other.
'Let us see where they lead!'

Desperate to be rid of the relentless attacks by creatures of Her Ladyship's lesser broods, Captain Róglarg of Cirith Ungol prepares to sacrifice a company of Orcs to Shelob at her lair, Torech Ungol.

You have narrowly escaped the wrath of Shelob and her children. You should now speak to Legolas.

Captain Róglarg can be found in the courtyard of Cirith Ungol.
You have gathered several sacrifices and now Captain Róglarg is prepared to bring them to Torech Ungol. You should get Captain Róglarg's attention and signal that you are ready to depart.

'I do not like the look of this, ${PLAYER}. Spiders and other foul creatures have scaled the walls of the Tower....
'I sense Captain Róglarg has stirred something that was better left in darkness. Imagine if such horrors came before us at the Black Gate! We would have fallen long before the Eagles arrived!
'Indeed, there is an unseen malice guiding these creatures, but to what end?'
'Well, don't just stand there. Let's get a move on!'

'All right, Silent One.
'Her Ladyship will be pleased, or she had better be! Between her spiders and that damned Elf-warrior, I can't spare another Orc.
'We'll lead them up the hill to her lair, and we'll make sure none of them get any ideas about running away. You know how it goes, don't you? We get them up there, send a few into Torech Ungol, and have them make some noise. That riles her up right quick!
'If they're lucky, she'll eat them right away, otherwise they'll get her venom and then I'd almost feel sorry for them. Spending the rest of your days hanging about in her lair until she finally decides to eat you? Nar, that's no way to go....
'Let's get on with it.'

In an attempt to warn the Gúrzyul of Shelob's growing wrath and secure Cirith Ungol, Legolas has decided to allow an emissary of Rûkhor the Pale Herald the opportunity to escape by distracting Shelob's brood at the Under-gate.
Gnats in Her Net
Talk to Legolas in the Tower of Cirith Ungol

Legolas can be found beside the road to Cirith Ungol.
You battled one of Shelob's greater children, Saernaston, but it appears the great spider was dragged to its doom by Shelob herself. You have fled the Tower of Cirith Ungol and must now hope that Belzagar delivered your warning to his masters, Ugrukhôr and Rûkhor.

Legolas can be found in the turret of the Tower of Cirith Ungol.
In order to allow Belzagar to deliver a message of warning to his masters, Legolas plans to distract Shelob's brood at the Under-gate to provide a means for Belzagar to escape Cirith Ungol. You should talk to Legolas when you are ready to travel to the Under-gate.

'We cannot know if Shelob's wounds are healed, but we must hold hope that she still feels the sting of whatever hurts Master Samwise wrought against her. One thing is certain -- her hunger has not diminished!
'It may not be this day, but the time shall come when Shelob must be confronted and her evil at last banished from the world. Cirith Ungol shall remain in turmoil, but if Belzagar reaches his masters, an even greater garrison will surely be sent to stand against Shelob and her children.
'As grim a thought as it is, the fates of Cirith Ungol and of the lands beyond Mordor are now in hands of the Gúrzyul....'
'Are you prepared, ${PLAYER}? Our foes will be many, but we must hold out!'

'${PLAYER}, we must go to the Under-gate and draw the ire of Shelob's children. It is the only way!'
Legolas turns to Belzagar.
'My companion and I shall go to the Under-gate, and we will draw the spiders away from the courtyard. Bring word to your masters before it is too late!
'Go now, or die with the rest of the garrison!'
Legolas turns back to you.
'It seems our paths always lead us to battle, my friend. Are you prepared?'

Webs have shot forth from the hidden caves and tunnels of Torech Ungol, dragging many Orcs in your company to their dooms. You should flee Torech Ungol with Captain Róglarg.
'There is no time to speak, ${PLAYER}. Swiftly now, we must go!'

'I guess Her Ladyship isn't playing by the rules anymore...
'Shelob's got topsides on us, and I ain't putting this one right! If Lugbúrz wants the Tower so badly, the Big Bosses can sort it out themselves!'
'Nar, I'm not trusting them to understand this one. Old Shagrat did as he was told, and he still got the Pits! Ah, yes, I know just the place!
'Well, I guess it's just you and me now, \qSilent One\q....'

'What is this? A cave-in?!
'Must have been all that business with the mountain and Lugbúrz that brought it down! Her Ladyship must be trapped down there, and if that Elf-warrior actually stuck a pin into her, she might have trouble breaking free. Nar, she'll be none too happy about this....
'I'd be glad to be rid of Her Ladyship, but it's her children that are mucking about in Lhingris, and only she can bring them in line. We've got to get this sorted and fast, or we'll all have it much worse. Don't have the High Up to look out for us when it comes to her!
'You're the Silent One, right? Clear that debris there, and see if the tunnel opens up a bit. Maybe Her Ladyship won't notice you!
'Garn! Try to break through!'

'Well now, I didn't like the sound of that....
'Nar, you've probably gone and made it worse! Not a single way through that mess...and Her Ladyship's bound to be hungry if She's trapped down there!'
Captain Róglarg looks at the sacrifices.
'We'll wait a few minutes and see if anything comes of it.'

'They're begging for another rest, are they? Silent One can't protest, eh? Clever....
'If they're scared now, they're a foolish lot. They haven't even seen her! I have...and she looks even worse than you! Ha! Probably got more of a tongue than you do, too!
'Well, there'll be no more resting. They'll have plenty of time for that once she comes around!
'Keep an eye on them. I don't want ANY getting away!'
'Swiftly now!'

Captain Róglarg grumbles to himself.
'I've been over here keeping eyes on the lot of them, and now I count only six! Where did two of them get off to?
'Maybe they jumped into the tunnels. A lot of good that'll do them... she'll get them either way!
'Have you seen anything, Silent One? Your neck still works, doesn't it?'

'Belzagar has gone, and our hope now lies with him! We can do no more here!
'Shelob comes! We must leave this place at once!'

'Did you feel the change in the wind upon crossing the Black Gate, ${PLAYER}? Everything in this accursed land is tainted. The earth, the water, even the air.
'Allow me to introduce myself. I am Narthavron, master smith of the Noldor. I was present when the Last Alliance broke into this valley and defeated Sauron's army. I was filled with sorrow and anger seeing the atrocities they had committed here, and have made it my life's work to find a way to purge the corruption. I now believe I have the right tool to achieve this.
'I have recovered one of the adamants of old, the Flame of Ancalamír. It will unravel many items throughout Middle-earth into different components that I have named \qEmbers of Enchantment\q, \qFigments of Splendour\q, and \qMotes of Enchantment\q. What do you think? I thought those names might help bring a little more light into this dark place. Anyway, after I break the objects down, I am then able to use some of those components to fashion extraordinary equipment. I have a feeling you will be instrumental in the Conquest of Gorgoroth, and as such will be encountering many of these special items in your travels. I have a proposition for you.
'I will allow you use of the Flame. My assistants, the High-enchanters, will help you. You need only touch one of these objects to the Flame and it will be reduced to one of these components. I believe that dwarf over there has been scavenging through the Orcs' forges. Perhaps he is willing to let go of something for this purpose. Find a piece of equipment, touch it to the Flame, and then return to me.'

'Aye, the Elf's right. I am seeking anything of value that might have been left behind. The Orcs were churning out thousands of blades and armour pieces from these forges, but most of them are foul Morgul-steel. Nothing I want anything to do with!
'Here, take this dagger I found. It's worthless to me! And tell that Elf he's better off leaving this sort of thing to the dwarves!'

'The Flame of Ancalamír has performed as expected, then? Excellent.
'In your travels, should you find equipment for which you have no use, I ask that you destroy it with the Flame and give the results to one of my assistants. They will reward you with powerful items of my own making, free from the foulness of this land.
'Good luck, and safe travels, friend.'
The Flame of Ancalamír

'We will learn the reply to the first speaking. Seek it east and south, near the road that leads upward to Mornaur Forge.'

'Up here, you may look down on the Land of Making and Labour. Land of muddy marching. Land of swords made and swords raised. Look below and you will see. The shape is like a sword-gash, is it not? A tale is whispered among my kind: that Xayal Zangin, the Resplendant one, fought here, in this place, with the fire giant Zalim Atash, and their fighting broke the world. Many such tales are there among my kind.'
He laughs.
'Who can say what happened long ago? Not you or I? For who should remember. We have only tellings, and tellings tatter. Tatter and wear to dust. But now you must tell to me what flags it was you saw.'
You describe each symbol you saw, drawing in the barren dirt when necessary, and the Nurnhoth slave nods gravely.

'When two men speak, one talks and then the other. Back and forth. So it is when we speak with flags. Then only those with eyes can hear. The Captain of the Pit, our lord and taskmaster, he has no such eyes. Nor his enforcers. Nor his sorcerers. Nor even his spies! They hear not when the flags speak. Only we forge-workers do.'
Kurtil delves in his wandering patter into the meanings of the flags: how one describes the nature of the topic; another whether past, present, or future; a third whether a certainty, a possibility, a warning, or a wondering, and so forth. All in all, the flags are far more subtle and complex than Barathron took them to be.
'And now, let us seek out the second speech, the answering. We should look, I think, east of here and south, by the road up to Mornaur Forge. You will go and look. And when you have seen, there I will be upon the upward road.'

'Here, I will begin. Tell me, friend. When two men meet to speak, does one say a thing - and then both go off without another word? No, no, no.
'Ah, but first, this will not do. I must get up. Will you help me?'

Hear what Kurtil has to say.

The trail of footprints led straight from signs of a bloody struggle to two dwarf-forgeworkers standing over a corpse. You should speak to them.

The corpse and dwarves are behind a cart high up the path in northern Udûn, above Maudhúl Vôr.
You should inspect the overseer's corpse to verify the dwarves' claim that he bears sword-wounds, while they hold only hammers.

The dwarves are behind a cart high up the path in northern Udûn, above Maudhúl Vôr.
You should talk to the dwarves, now that you have verified that the overseer's corpse bears sword and not blunt wounds.
You have not found Ushkbál the Overseer, but you have found signs of a bloody struggle. You should follow the footprints leading from the place and see where they lead.
'The great foundry lies north of the road below, above Maudhúl Vôr. You go and seek Ushkbál the Overseer on the good legs you have. I follow behind.'
'Stéthi, you explain. I'll botch it up, properly. Besides, I'm still catching my breath from dragging old Ushkbál all the ways up here.'
'You speak to them, yes? I think that best.'
'Look and you will see. No hammer felled Ushkbál.'
'If it is so, then it is so, yes? The dwarf speaks true.'

''Twas not us who did this thing. I know full well how it may look. We only dragged him here, out of the sight of prying eyes.
'Hoy, you there, Kurtil! I know you by face and by name. Whatever trouble you're up to this time, you must bow to plain truth: Who in the northern 'works would touch a hair on Ushkbál's ugly pate? None, that's who! No overseer we'd more gladly work for, neither.
'Besides, you see we carry only hammers and these wounds be swords' work, plain to see. Look yourself, ${RACE}.'

'Now then, that's settled, I hope! A smouldering shame about Ushkbál, though! We know not if it were one of the enforcers or some wild-frenzied soldier who stuck him through, but there you have it. He was our hope and he's gone.
'Well, and if you are here then you followed the signal flags, too, just as we. Let us work the iron together, we four, while it's got any heat left. Perhaps the work might be salvaged. If only we can think what to do now that we are on our own. What say you Kurtil? ${RACE}?'

'This is how I see it, and pardon my speaking thus, Stéthi. There are two impurities we've got in this slag. First-wise, there's no one to do the deed. Second, there's someone, somewhere, who knows the signal flags and maybe doesn't want the deed done.'

'Yes, yes, yes. The iron is hot now, but cooling, cooling...'
For a moment, Kurtil seems lost in thought.
'We need only someone to go. Who to fill the post? No, not I, Nurnhoth that I am. Who am I? No one. Will Gradrágh go? Ha ha. We know the answer to that, my friends. What of you, Slárnur? You will not. A shame!
'No Orc, nor dwarf, nor Nurnhoth here among us...'
Then a smile slowly spreads across Kurtil's face, lighting the twinkle back into his eyes, which fix on you.

'We must seek Ushkbál the Overseer, then. It is he who will accomplish what we seek.'
Paying no heed of any surprise on your face, Kurtil thinks for a long moment.
'He has agreed, agreed to talk to us at least, and there is hope for more. Surely, he is found at his post, north of here by the great foundry, which lies above Maudhúl Vôr.'

Having secured the pledge from the Easterling Lord Khôpol, you should return to Kurtil and the other forge-workers where they had been, on the height above Maudhúl Vôr.

'You are returned! And they have pledged their word? Strong as iron, an Easterling's pledge.
'See now who has also arrived. It is Gradrágh, another overseer. He wants only some persuading.'

'I see. So it is as you spoke.'
The Easterling Lord thinks for a moment.
'Yes, we will meet with these forge-workers and speak to them. You may carry them this pledge, ${CLASS}.'
'Go with Yordam to the Great Banner, Maudhúl Vôr, and the Black Gates. You will see. The war is not lost, even if it is not yet won.'
'So you are the ${CLASS}. Kurtil did not mention you were ${RACE}! If you ask me, we're in a hard place, all told. I don't know where to turn.'

'The Captain of the Pit and the Men of the West are like two stones, ${PLAYER}, and we the roots who will be ground between them. We must beg the Easterlings safe passage back to their lands, and we rely on you to go before them.
'Go then. Go to Rhûd Vorn and hail them as I showed you.'

You begin to explain the case of the forge-workers, but he quickly interrupts you.
'You speak as if the Eye was fallen. You speak as if the Cause was lost. This is not so and cannot be. How could it be, for the Black Gates still stand and the great banner still waves like a lone wing above the parade grounds. Why, only this morning I sent an Orc with a letter to the Black Word's commissary in Maudhúl Vôr. As sure as the ground I stand on, it has been delivered and needed provisions are on their way.'
When you do not back down, he stares hard at you.
'Folly! There is deceit afoot, if not by you, then by someone. I will send Yordam. He will go with you so that the truth may be known to me. Go.'
'I have seen the proofs, though I hardly believed my eyes. A ${RACE} from the West has spoken the truth! I return to Rhûd Vorn, as should you.'
'I will go with you, as my Lord commands. We will see what we will see.'

'Long is the tale to tell, but short is the time. Do you remember that the Captain of the Pit does not hear the signal flags' speech? He is the master of all Udûn, but many do not wish it so.
'When the ground shook and the gates fell and the Eagles crossed the skies, a light dawned upon our minds - that we might fly ourselves. Fly like the eagles and in Udûn dwell no more. But how? And then we remember the Easterlings camped in Rhûd Vorn. Perhaps, we thought, perhaps we might go back with them, to the lands far from Captains and cruel Gondorians and Elves.
'And so in flags was it written and in flags was it read by you and me and by others. Ushkbál the goodly overseer agreed to go before the Easterlings and plead our case. Now Ushkbál is gone and our hope rests on you, ${RACE}-${CLASS}. We ask you to go in Ushkbál's place and parley with the Easterlings. Only to meet! To speak awhile of what may be.
'Stand before Rhûd Vorn high on the height and hail them with the words that I will teach you.
Kurtil teaches you a formal military hail in the Easterling tongue.
'If fortune smiles upon us, they will agree.'

Then, everything abruptly changes. Gruesome scenes flash before you, furious slashing, dismembered limbs and blood, so much blood. You see the man through the eyes of the woman, lying on a cold, stone floor, completely ripped apart. You see her reaching out to him, but the light is fading from your shared vision. She is dying, and the weight of this is suffocating you.
Just in time, she releases you. You gasp for air as one more image comes to you. A face, beautiful, but dark. Not the same as the woman's, but similar, related. Hatred comes to you; the most intense hatred you've ever experienced. Hatred is this being's purpose now. And then, realization. This face must belong to Lhaereth the Stained.

Before you looms a grotesque stone figure. The bloody waters of the Chaydash run down its features, making it almost feel alive. As you study its features, you are unsettled to realize that its gaze is piercing into you, examining your thoughts. Your mind drifts to your experiences in Seregost's prison and your successful escape. Suddenly, your mind is grasped by the spirit, and a stream of images comes to you, hazy and dream-like.
You see a man and woman, walking together through beautiful fields, hand in hand. They are clearly very much in love, but you notice the woman does not seem entirely normal. Her features are ever so slightly monstrous. Regardless, the man is enraptured by her. Emotions come to you that are not your own. Love and happiness, but in the background a deep and growing sorrow.

The spirit sees that you finally understand and shows you another image, this time different, clearer. This must be somewhere nearby, not a memory. You see another statue, a twin of this one, standing in the Chaydash. The red waters pass through an iron gate and stone walls behind it. It must be behind Seregost itself, further upstream. You can feel a forlorn attachment to this statue, as if the spirit yearns to be closer to it. The man's face appears in your mind for just a moment, and the spirit shows you an almost tangible connexion through the waters. You get the sense that you could pull on this connexion to travel to the other Watching-stone. The image fades away and you can feel the spirit trying to form a word in your mouth.
You allow the word to form: 'Bargain?'
The spirit shows you what you must do to be allowed passage. Your hate-fueled visions of slain merrevail, Lhaereth struck down in her throne room, and Seregost in ruins. You tell the spirit that you do mean to end Lhaereth's reign of terror, one way or another. You feel a bit uncomfortable at the spirit's murderous delight, but you believe she will now allow you access to Seregost and beyond.

'Hello again! Ready to help?
'There are many things that need doing out there in Gorgoroth. A huge amount of things! Right now, we really just need you to go out there, and do what needs doing! Check the Bounty Board to see what there is to do.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, just who I wanted to see.

'${PLAYER}, you are just in time.
'Our allies in Gorgoroth are struggling to keep control of the region. They need assistance in the field, and I can think of no one better to send than you. Check the Bounty Board to see who has requested aid.'

Taerthon se encuentra cerca de los muelles en Celondim.
Has viajado a Celondim, y pronto se acerca el momento de zarpar hacia el Lejano Oeste.
Habla con Taerthon en Celondim
Habla con Taerthon en Celondim

'${PLAYER}, ¿has oído las buenas nuevas? ¡Por fin ha llegado el momento de zarpar hacia Mithlond y hacia la bendita Valinor!
'Hemos esperado solo un mes, pero cada día ha parecido un año desde que llegamos a Celondim. Las cargas de este reino pronto quedarán atrás, pero me pregunto si los hijos de Elrond encontraron lo que buscaban en las ruinas de Edhelion. He oído muchas historias sobre la triste historia de ese lugar y cómo llegó a la ruina por la mano de un enano despreciable llamado Skorgrím Duramano, pero ha permanecido vacío durante muchos años. Me pregunto si queda algo por descubrir allí...
'Nunca he caminado por las costas del Reino Bendecido, pero he oído muchas historias sobre Valinor. Tus antepasados que una vez vivieron allí, ¿no es cierto? ¿Tú también?'
Taerthon hace una pausa y estudia tu rostro.
'Pareces ${PLAYER:inquieto, amigo mío.[m]|inquieta, amiga mía.[f]} ¿Qué te preocupa en un día tan alegre?'

Llegaste a Celondim con los hijos de Elrond hace un mes, y pronto se acerca el momento de zarpar hacia Mithlond. Sin embargo, la decisión de Elrond de ofrecerte la elección entre dejar la Tierra Media o quedarte para ayudar a sus pueblos ha pesado mucho en ti durante tus viajes. El elfo Taerthon también ha venido para zarpar hacia el Oeste, y has pasado mucho tiempo con él preparando tu viaje desde que Elladan y Elrohir partieron hacia Edhelion.
Por fin ha llegado el momento de viajar hacia el Oeste, y Taerthon te espera en los muelles de Celondim.
Prólogo: Un Mar Inquieto

Llegaste a Celondim con los hijos de Elrond hace un mes, y pronto se acerca el momento de zarpar hacia Mithlond. Sin embargo, la decisión de Elrond de ofrecerte la elección entre dejar la Tierra Media o quedarte para ayudar a sus pueblos ha pesado mucho en ti durante tus viajes.
Reflexiona sobre los caminos de tus amigos y parientes (${CURRENT}/${MAX})

'Ah, así que regresas. ¿A dónde te ha llevado tu reflexión, ${PLAYER}?'
Le dices a Taerthon que deseas permanecer en la Tierra Media.
'No es la elección que yo haría, pero la entiendo. Has hecho de ello tu propósito: enfrentar las fuerzas del mal dondequiera que se aferren, y aunque no lo parezca aquí en Celondim, es cierto que grandes males vuelven a obrar en este reino.
'Verás, mientras reflexionabas, Elladan y Elrohir llegaron a Celondim y pidieron hablar contigo de inmediato. Les dije que transmitiría su petición cuando regresaras, y ahora te esperan junto al maestro de establos.
'Mi camino conduce al Lejano Oeste, pero parece que el tuyo ahora lleva a otro lugar. ¡Que los Valar te guíen, y que algún día encuentres paz en Valinor!'

Reflexionas sobre el camino de Gil-galad, el Alto Rey de los Elfos, y el valor que mostró al luchar y caer para purgar los males de Morgoth y Sauron del mundo. Piensas en la pérdida del elfo Thelaron y el dolor de perder a un compañero durante la guerra, como le ocurrió a Gil-galad. Consideras la pérdida de tu Rey y comprendes lo que significó su sacrificio para los pueblos de la Tierra Media.

Reflexionas sobre el camino de Glorfindel, que permaneció en la Tierra Media para enfrentarse a los males del Enemigo y a los más viles de sus siervos. Piensas en las hazañas de Glorfindel en los Días Antiguos del mundo y en cómo su determinación nunca flaqueó, incluso ante la muerte.
Reflexionas sobre las decisiones de Círdan el Carpintero de Barcos, que permaneció en la Tierra Media para que otros de su linaje pudieran partir hacia el Reino Bendecido de Valinor.

Reflexionas sobre las decisiones de tu más querida amiga, Harthalín, que ha elegido permanecer en la Tierra Media y librarla de los males antes de que llegue el momento de legarla a los Hombres. Consideras su deber hacia la gente de este reino y que esperaba que tú también permanecieras para ayudarla en las batallas contra los males del mundo.

Reflexionas sobre las decisiones de Elrond el Medio Elfo, antaño heraldo de Gil-galad, cuyo tiempo en este reino se acerca a su fin. Consideras las palabras de Elrond, pues dijo que podrías partir hacia el Lejano Oeste si realmente lo deseabas y que las cargas de este reino ya no recaían sobre ti. Piensas que te mantuvo en Imladris para que la elección algún día fuera tuya, en lugar de enviarte a descansar en el Lejano Oeste.
¡Tu reflexión sobre el camino de Gil-galad te llena de determinación!
¡Tu reflexión sobre el camino de Glorfindel te llena de esperanza!
¡Tu reflexión sobre el camino de Círdan te llena de gracia!
¡Tu reflexión sobre el camino de Harthalín te llena de valor!
¡Tu reflexión sobre el camino de Elrond te llena de sabiduría!

Elladan y Elrohir se encuentran al oeste de los muelles, junto al maestro de establos de Celondim.
Taerthon está apenado, pero comprende tu elección de permanecer en la Tierra Media. También ha mencionado que Elladan y Elrohir han llegado repentinamente a Celondim y desean hablar contigo. Debes encontrarlos junto al maestro de establos de Celondim.
Habla con Elladan en Celondim
Encuentra a Elladan y Elrohir junto al maestro de establos de Celondim
Habla con Taerthon en Celondim

'¿Qué te preocupa, ${PLAYER}?'
Le dices a Taerthon que tus pensamientos se dirigen a tus amigos y parientes y a la elección que se te dio de permanecer en la Tierra Media si así lo deseabas.
'¿Por qué querrías quedarte aquí? Como bien sabes, las tierras de Valinor curan todos los males y renuevan nuestros espíritus. ¡Las preocupaciones de este reino ya no son nuestras!'
Taerthon percibe que sus palabras no te han convencido.
'Ya veo. Quizá deberías reflexionar sobre los caminos de tus amigos y parientes para guiarte.'

'${PLAYER}, ¡me alegra que aún no hayas partido! Temía que llegáramos demasiado tarde...'
Los rostros de Elladan y Elrohir revelan graves preocupaciones.
'Hay fuerzas sombrías actuando en Ered Luin. El terrible Señor Demacrado, Ivar, ha atado espíritus viles al cadáver del Señor Enano Skorgrím, y ahora los Duramano creen que su líder ha renacido. Nuestros enemigos escaparon, y ahora el Enemigo ha seducido a los Duramano para que le sirvan.'
Elrohir le da a Elladan una mirada significativa.
'En efecto, hermano, la verdad debe ser dicha. Cuando nuestro padre habló de la sombra en el Este, hablaba de Sauron. El Señor Oscuro ha regresado una vez más, ${PLAYER}, y ha enviado a sus siervos por muchas tierras de este reino en busca del Anillo que se perdió. Si Sauron recupera el Anillo, no quedará hueste que pueda resistirle y todo estará perdido.
'Pronto llegará el momento en que los pueblos de este reino sean llamados a la guerra, y te ruego que permanezcas para guiarlos y asegurar las tierras de la Tierra Media. Es una gran demanda para alguien tan ilustre como tú y en una hora tan decisiva, pero no lo pediría si la necesidad no fuera extrema. Pronto será un reino de Hombres, y debe sobrevivir para que ellos lo hereden. ¡Te lo ruego, ¿permanecerás?!'
Le dices a Elladan y Elrohir que has decidido quedarte en la Tierra Media.
'Tenerte entre las fuerzas que se alzarán contra Sauron me da nueva esperanza para los días que vendrán. Debes ayudar a la gente de Celondim y de las tierras más allá para perfeccionar tus habilidades para las batallas que sin duda nos esperan. Cuando llegue el momento, te llamaremos para que te unas a nosotros.'
Prólogo: Reflexiones del Pasado

Puedes reflexionar sobre tus amigos y parientes cerca de los muelles de Celondim.
Tras darte cuenta de que tus pensamientos se han vuelto inquietos y que podrías desear permanecer en la Tierra Media, Taerthon cree que te haría bien reflexionar sobre los caminos de tus amigos y parientes.

Taerthon se encuentra cerca de los muelles en Celondim.
Has reflexionado sobre los caminos de tus amigos y parientes, y has encontrado un nuevo sentido de propósito en la Tierra Media. Debes regresar con Taerthon.

'Parece que nuestros caminos se cruzan una vez más, ${PLAYER}!
'Luchamos a través de las ruinas de Barad-dûr y, hasta ahora, hemos perseguido en silencio a la Orden del Ojo hasta estas profundidades. Tanto Megoril como yo hemos conocido \qcreyentes\q de su tipo antes... ya que surgieron por primera vez después de la derrota de Sauron en las laderas de Orodruin. El destino demostró que sus creencias eran ciertas y ahora estos Hombres nunca se apartarán de la esperanza de que Sauron vuelva una vez más.
'Sin embargo, su presencia aquí parecía tanto inesperada como indeseada, y creemos que podría convertirse en una ventaja para nosotros. Han pasado por los Fosos Negros, cruzaron el propio abismo y lucharon hasta lo más profundo de los cimientos de Barad-dûr, todo ello mientras entonaban cánticos de odio contra un enemigo maldito, al que llaman Dientegrís. No sé qué disputa tienen con este Dientegrís, pero, a juzgar por sus gritos y cánticos desenfrenados, me temo que tiene que ver con los Anillos de Poder. A pesar de que su poder se desvanece, los Anillos siguen siendo un símbolo de estatus y fuerza para quienes habitan estas tierras.
'Haz lo que debas para combatir a la Orden e impedir que las fuerzas de este Dientegrís se acerquen a los Anillos, y nosotros buscaremos cualquier rastro de Thelaron. Si aún vive, debe estar escondido en las profundidades del Mordath. \'No podemos enfrentarnos solos a tantos enemigos, pero hemos encontrado pasadizos secretos a través de estas profundidades. Si consigues llegar a las cámaras más profundas del Mordath, Megoril y yo podremos ayudarte a regresar a ellas rápidamente.
'Incluso en un lugar tan oscuro, mantengo la esperanza de que ambos encontremos lo que buscamos en este Abismo.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión registra tu progreso en el nivel de dificultad 1 del Abismo de Mordath. Te permite a ti y a tus compañeros reanudar la aventura en el Abismo de Mordath desde el punto de control más lejano al que hayáis llegado en cada ciclo semanal. Esta misión se reiniciará automáticamente todos los lunes, jueves y sábados.</rgb>

Completado: Abismo de Mordath (Nivel 2)

'Parece que nuestros caminos se cruzan una vez más, ${PLAYER}!
'Luchamos a través de las ruinas de Barad-dûr y, hasta ahora, hemos perseguido en silencio a la Orden del Ojo hasta estas profundidades. Tanto Megoril como yo hemos conocido \qcreyentes\q de su tipo antes... ya que surgieron por primera vez después de la derrota de Sauron en las laderas de Orodruin. El destino demostró que sus creencias eran ciertas y ahora estos Hombres nunca se apartarán de la esperanza de que Sauron vuelva una vez más.
'Sin embargo, su presencia aquí parecía tanto inesperada como indeseada, y creemos que podría convertirse en una ventaja para nosotros. Han pasado por los Fosos Negros, cruzaron el propio abismo y lucharon hasta lo más profundo de los cimientos de Barad-dûr, todo ello mientras entonaban cánticos de odio contra un enemigo maldito, al que llaman Dientegrís. No sé qué disputa tienen con este Dientegrís, pero, a juzgar por sus gritos y cánticos desenfrenados, me temo que tiene que ver con los Anillos de Poder. A pesar de que su poder se desvanece, los Anillos siguen siendo un símbolo de estatus y fuerza para quienes habitan estas tierras.
'Haz lo que debas para combatir a la Orden e impedir que las fuerzas de este Dientegrís se acerquen a los Anillos, y nosotros buscaremos cualquier rastro de Thelaron. Si aún vive, debe estar escondido en las profundidades del Mordath. \'No podemos enfrentarnos solos a tantos enemigos, pero hemos encontrado pasadizos secretos a través de estas profundidades. Si consigues llegar a las cámaras más profundas del Mordath, Megoril y yo podremos ayudarte a regresar a ellas rápidamente.
'Incluso en un lugar tan oscuro, mantengo la esperanza de que ambos encontremos lo que buscamos en este Abismo.'

Permite que tú y tus compañeros reanuden la aventura en el Abismo de Mordath en el punto de control más lejano que hayan alcanzado en cada ciclo semanal. Esta misión se reiniciará automáticamente todos los jueves.</rgb>

'If you collect weapons and shields dropped by the Orcs, they can be melted down and used by our smiths. I sent Vágrek to Udûn, and he will wait there with his cart. Search the Orc camps at the valley floor of Udûn for discarded weapons and shields, and load them onto his cart. That gear will be melted down and turned into equipment worthy of our adventurers, and when they are damaged by Orc skulls and weapons, they can be replaced with little trouble!'

'A number of dwarves are hard at work in Gorgoroth, combatting the many dangers that lurk there, but they have encountered an unexpected difficulty: Orc skulls are harder than you'd think! They have been known to dent all but the finest of dwarf weapons. We needed some means of replacing our warriors' gear, as efficiently as possible, and I came up with just such a way!
'I have already set my plan into motion, ${PLAYER}, and it needs only you to apply the finishing touches. If you collect weapons and shields dropped by the Orcs, they can be melted down and used by our smiths. I sent Vágrek to Udûn, and he will wait there with his cart. Search the Orc camps at the valley floor of Udûn for discarded weapons and shields, and load them onto his cart. That gear will be melted down and turned into equipment worthy of our adventurers, and when they are damaged by Orc skulls and weapons, they can be replaced with little trouble!'
