'Before today, Vútro was one of our finest scouts, able to outrun even the West Wind. Alas for Vútro! This wound will keep him from the wild lands. A scout that cannot walk the wilderness is of no use to me or to my people.
'The Weeping Warrior is known to us, ${PLAYER}, even in the distant lands from which we came. His reputation for cruelty is unmatched; he has long had designs on the North, and has troubled both Longbeards and Zhélruka in pursuit of it. Even so, I do not fear him. I will bring a small force of my finest warriors for two purposes: as a wise exercise of caution, and also as a demonstration of our power. Perhaps Karazgar will decide he does not wish to oppose the Zhélruka in these mountains, and will leave us in peace.
'I would have you come with us, ${PLAYER}, but your friend Durin must remain behind. I gave him a task suited to his abilities, and at any rate this meeting will be too dangerous for an unproven king's son.'
'Vútro will tell us where he encountered Karazgar, and we will find the Weeping Warrior. Let us hear what he has to say, and if it is not to my liking he will regret it!'

'Karazgar thinks to frighten us with words, but he overestimates their power. Have I not told you that words mean little to me, and only actions earn my respect? Let Karazgar speak. We will blunt his words with hammers, and cut his intentions with our axes!
'The Zhélruka will prevail!'

'If I once believed the ill fortune of the Zhélruka had been exaggerated by the bards, I do no longer! The loss of Bótuz Frostblood must be a grievous injury to them, and I confess that it pains me also. Would Bótuz and the others who died during Karazgar's attack still be alive if I had not lowered my weapon in the Ironfold? Would they still live if I had kept them from crossing the Dale-lands? Ah, I will not dwell upon it. What was done is done, and might have been worse.
'It is good to hear that Inek will take up the mantle of leadership and ready his people for another attack. Karazgar promised to come to Skarháld three times? How much worse will be the following assaults, if this was merely the first? It bodes ill, ${PLAYER}.
'I know the Zhélruka do not care for me. Nay, do not seek to deny it! It is true. I am unproven. Did I count myself ready when we battled the Easterlings outside Utterby back in the Ironfold? That counted for naught, or less than naught! To do battle against Karazgar, in defence not only of my people but of another... that is where my true glory lies. We will stand with Inek and his Zhélruka to repel whatever Karazgar sends against us, and perhaps afterward I will feel my name deserved. It will be my honour to stand with them and with you, ${PLAYER}. There is much we must do if we are to be ready. The first promise is fulfilled. When the next comes, we must be ready. 'Here we are, you and I, ${PLAYER}, among strange mountains and stranger dwarves. Though in truth, we Longbeards have histories with both, but that is a thing of scrolls and more than living memory. Of course, I am a Lore-master and know many tales from scrolls. Would you like to hear such a one?
'It is known as the Tale of Borin. You see, Durin's Folk have also dwelled here. At the end of this chain of mountains lies Gundabad, where Durin first awoke! But this tale takes place long after that, when our home was Thikil-Gundu and our King was Dáin I. The dragons had gone quiet, and search was made for their whereabouts, for the dwarves distrusted this strange stillness. Thrór, Dáin's eldest son, searched Stormwall but found no dragon. Grór, his second, scoured Winterstith, and too found none. Only Dáin's brother, Borin, had fortune, ill or fair, within the depths of Glimmerdeep, where he came upon the fearsome dragon Etterfang - asleep! Wasting not a moment or a breath, he took his great spiked mace and began a furious assault. Dazed from sleep, the dragon must have thought a host of dwarves assailed her! Gravely wounded, maimed, and bleeding, she threw Borin across the cavern and when he arose, she was gone. Borin returned, having lost his quarry. Whether Etterfang lived or not, stayed or fled, none can say.
'If you should go to the Glimmerdeep mine, ${PLAYER}, you might look for signs of either dragon or hoard, and take notes in this journal here. How glad I should be to extend the tale!'

'Hórin vouches for Drengur. He is not a dwarf known to spin tales. This means that Etterfang yet lives. The Zhélruka are already organizing for an attack. You should join them. They are not as well prepared for such a fight as you are, ${CLASS}.'

'Two heads! Old tales are told of such trolls who lurk in the shadows of the northern mountains. Never have I dreamt to see one. But then, never had I dreamt the Zhélruka would come back here.
'And yet, it is clear, we alone do not seek to claim this place. These Orcs, these Hobgoblins, this two-headed troll sought the mine for wealth and not shelter. Treasure for some master or cause we know not of. It is troubling, ${PLAYER}! We must guard ourselves well. We must watch our backs.'

'I know not what it was, and I fear to know the truth, but within my heart know that is what we must face, if we are to claim those mines.'

'There you are. I have given Spall room to finish writing down his findings before he returns to the Lonely Mountain. I will send him back with an escort of my guards. I thank you looking after him, ${PLAYER}.
'You are most welcome here. As I mentioned before, I fear no such storm as we weathered in battle, yet troubles have a way of creeping in, and lingering. An adventurer such as yourself could do much good among the simple smiths of the Iron Hills. If you remain and lend your hand, you shall be rewarded richly and gratefully.'

'As you may be aware, a plague of injudicious rumours have come into this court, nearly all concerning affairs in the Iron Hills.
'In truth, we have heard little from my brother Náin in the month since the fighting ended, and I must grudgingly concede that a desire to hear how things go out there is reasonable, even if such wanton gossip is not.
'Now, I have heard a very wise and reasonable suggestion from one of my trusted Lore-masters. And who better to act on such a sensible sooth than to dispatch its author into the Ironfold, where he can determine the truth of each and every rumour, then return here and set the record straight.
'I am speaking of you Spall. You needn't look around as if it were someone else.'

'Mm - me? Well, in truth, I did make just such a suggestion to ${PLAYER} here, for I abhor these rumours just as you do, my lord. I cannot deny that, no matter my humility.
'And I will stand by what I have said. You should dispatch some dwarf keen of eye and stout of frame, fair of mind and with a good memory. And while many of those attributes this Lore-master would humbly claim to possess, surely King Thorin, you cannot mean to send me out there. I am no adventurer, or guard, or soldier.
'If half the rumours whispered in this court are true - and indeed, more than half would be most contradictory and impossible - then the Ironfold might be a truly dangerous place!'

King Thorin laughs unexpectedly.
'Well, Spall! You have talked yourself nearly in a circle, between worthiness and unworthiness and worthiness again. You have made a fair point, however, that the Iron Hills may yet hold peril. Jangovar yet linger by the Long Lake to the south, after all.
'I maintain that no dwarf in all the Lonely Mountain is more suited to this endeavour than you. However, perhaps what is called for is company. ${PLAYER}, would you do Erebor one more service, and go with Spall into the Ironfold? I dare say there is much there of interest for an adventurer like yourself.'

'There you are! What a long stroll this was. Longer than I am accustomed to, I confess. Spall, I said to myself, you are a proud dwarf and you must not tire so easily. Still, I have rarely gone so far in one day!
'Now then, we have work to do, do we not? One cannot see much from here, can one? Before we go on, however, let us review our task.
'First, many rumours circled around the stair at Skald's Drop, on the Ironfold's south. We should visit there and see for ourselves. Second, at least as many rumours circle the Dalish town of Utterby, due east of here. Third and hopefully last, many were the rumours of Járnfast and of Lord Náin who sits within.
'If we visit these three locations, we will have settled the majority of the claims.'

'Let us see then... first, the stair at Skald's Drop, which lies along the southern edge of the Ironfold. Second, the Dalish town of Utterby right in the middle of the Ironfold. Third, eastward built into the Hills, Járnfast where Lord Náin sits.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. I must thank you for being my travelling companion on this expedition. I think - I think perhaps I shall get out more often.
'Ah, but who are you trying to fool, Spall? You will go back to your scrolls and runes and objects of lore and forget the sky-topped lands.'
'Now how shall I go about this? False rumours first? Geographical? Alphabetical?'
'Hm... concerning the Jangovar upon the Ironfold...'
'...a most thorough survey of the foundations and supports...'
'We have done well and fully the task we were charged with, ${PLAYER}. Only, Lord Náin asked us to return to him once we were done. I will meet you there.'

'We are in this together it seems. I must gather some effects both here and down in Dale. Let us meet just where the road enters the Ironfold, then. If you leave Dale through the south-eastern gate, you will find the way.'
'Do see that Spall accomplishes his task safely, ${PLAYER}. And bear my greetings to my brother Náin in Járnfast, when you see him there.'

'Though we cannot be sure without, as I said, marching straight into the lion's mouth, I fear the rumours we had heard in court hold some truth here. Jangovar tents at both gates, their flags raised and the Dalish ones thrown down? That is truly an ill sign carved in plain runes, if you ask me.'
Investigate the rumours about the Dalish town of Utterby.

'Behold, ${PLAYER}: Utterby, a trading town of the Dale-men. At least, that is what it had been before the battles upon the Ironfold. Viewed from a distance, one cannot help but suspect some of the rumours we have heard are true.
'I am not a warrior and I have no desire to march into the lion's mouth, yet all the same, we must get a bit closer to be sure. Let us tour both the southern gate and the east gate, and see if we may learn who controls Utterby now, and how that has come to pass.'

'Me? I - before King Thorin? Oh, I must surely have stuck my foot in it now. Stuck my foot in what? ${PLAYER}, I cannot imagine. Some rumour about me has spread. Surely that is it. I would be the last to hear. Well, I suppose I shall hear it now.
'Gather your wits, Spall! You are a proud Lore-master. Not to mention, you have hardly done anything wrong.
'Ahem! Very well. I - I shall be there directly, I suppose.'
'Ah, there you are Spall, ${PLAYER}. Please, be at your ease. There is a matter about which I wish to speak.'

'What rumours do you think they have told about me, ${PLAYER}? If I am blamed for the ale spilled on that scroll, why, I shall have no choice but to out Mágsal as the true cause.
'But what am I doing? We are before the king. Look proud, Spall, and wear a grave face. There we have it.'

'Have you heard of the wounds Lord Náin took in the battle? He bears an agate eye now, and a gold ear beside. They say he sits in the Járnfast keep in the Iron Hills now, mired in despair, mourning his wounds and his lost comrades, and that he has ordered the gates sealed and no dwarves to come or go.
'Now strangers from the south, Men, yea, and dwarves too, wander the Ironfold as they will.'

'Lord Náin's new steel teeth, it is said, bedevil him with phantom pains. His false eye, too, aches in the dead of night and he cannot sleep. He has fallen into an eternal black mood, or so I have heard, and has ordered the north-eastern road in the Iron Hills walled off, and the stair at Skald's Drop broken so that it may no longer be traversed.'

'Did you feel the earth tremble the day the fighting ended? I can feel it as if it were moments ago, though more than a month has passed.
'Well, and some say the shaking was far more severe to the east in the Iron Hills. Some even say that Járnfast keep fell to the ground, if you can believe it!'

'If any dwarf tries to tell you that Járnfast fell when the ground shook the Iron Hills, it is nothing but a vicious lie. I have the truth, on good authority, too, and it is this: the keep stands, but something below that was sealed away has been freed, and the Dwarves of the Ironfold have all fled in terror, every one.'

'How glad I am you are here, ${PLAYER}. The war is done and the dust settled, yet there is such a wagging of tongues in my halls that you would think the mountain was falling in on itself!
'The talk runs eastward to the Iron Hills, mostly, but that is as much as I can make of it. My displeasure at such gossip is known in this court, and so they hide it from me.
'They hold no such fear of you, however, and would be eager to pour their rubbish into a fresh ear. Will you go about my hall and learn what you can? This tangle of tongues must be settled, and I cannot see how to do so if I cannot even learn what they are saying!'

'The latest word from the Iron Hills is this: that the Easterlings only feigned retreat, gathering their forces anew just beyond our ken. Then, not two days ago, under cloak of night they flooded the Ironfold and hold it in complete blockade.
'That is why we have had no other word from our brethren there. Dale is all but lost and we ourselves must prepare to seal our gates.'

You relate the rumours you heard and Thorin listens intently. After you finish, he thinks for a long moment and then speaks.
'From my own people, I have heard seven wastes of breath and one single, half-sensible thought. Would you be a good ${CLASS} once more and go tell Spall the Lore-master that he should come and stand before me?'

'In the land before the Iron Hills lies the small Dalish township of Utterby. If rumours are to be believed, Easterlings of all stripes have taken up there, pillaging and striking terror into all who travel through.'

'There are strange whispers these days... whispers of strange dwarves arriving in the Iron Hills. They come from the east, it is said, and have neither beard nor hair on the tops of their heads. Their ears face behind instead of ahead.
'Furthermore, when asked about good news, they always lie - but on subjects of bad news, tell ever the truth. Or so the whispers say. I know not. I have not set foot beyond the Lonely Mountain since the fighting began.'

'Rumours? Yes, I have heard rumours, but I am beyond my wits knowing which to believe. The Iron Hills are overrun, they say. The Iron Hills are blockaded. Lord Náin is dead - or he is mad - or he has second sight through his agate eye!
'Or the lot of it is nonsense and idle talk. Unless it is not.
'What someone really ought to do is go out there and settle all these rumours for once and for all. Then we should have some peace. Or at least a little certainty!'
'Find Spall the Lore-master, if you will, and tell him to come before me. He can be found midway down the court, I believe.'
'Will you go about my hall and learn what you can? I must settle these rampant rumours before they drive me mad.'
'You may tell King Thorin I will be there directly. And face - whatever slander has been spoken of me with my head up.'

'You talk to them, ${PLAYER}. You are the adventurer, after all!'
'Am I much mistaken, or did he say their axe ran off toward the river?'
'It ran off that way, across the river to I know not where.'

'Well, if you ask me, there is little doubt that these dwarves attempted to saddle that ox with all they owned and ease the load upon their own two backs. No doubt it belonged to some Man or dwarf of the Ironfold, though after all the war this place has seen, who can say if its master yet lives.
'My ire was up when I began my thoughts, ${PLAYER}, but on further reflection, the pathetic state of these dwarves, and the innocence of the crime, softens my heart.
'They called themselves Zhélruka, and indeed this is a name known in lore, belonging to another proud line of dwarves. A line that has dealings with Durin's Folk in past times. I wonder what these two fled, and if others of their kin also come this way.'

'Túmo. What is this word - ox? No? We do not know it. We have never seen such a beast. We are poor and weary travellers. Many, many, many leagues we have gone on foot, and without our few possessions we would be done for.
'Túmo and I, we thank you for helping recover them.'
'And what of that ox your axe was tied to? What of that, I should like to know? Did that belong to you? And how, now that I think of it, did your belongings become scattered in the first place?'

'It may not look it to you, but the Stair is as intact now as it was when last I came this way. Which... hm... I believe was the early days of my youth!
'There is a fair stream of travellers coming from the Stair. What can we say of them? I do believe I espied the smoke of a camp-fire as we approached, earlier. Let us make our way back and find what there is to be found.'

'What do you want?'
The dwarf eyes you suspiciously.
'I don't have to tell you anything. And besides, I have not time. As you can see, our possessions have become scattered - here, there, all about.'
The dwarf stands, waiting for you to move on. When you do not, he shakes his head.
'First, kízinek, help us, then talk. There - the small bags, the big parcels, the water-skins.'
'Can't you see I'm busy? Off with you.'
Investigate the rumours about Skald's Drop and the Stair with Spall.

'Well now, we have arrived at Skald's Drop. Properly speaking of course, the name refers to the cliff and, well, the drop. We had better get right up to it, enjoy the view, and see whether or not the Stair has been broken.'
'We had better get right up to the cliff's edge and see whether or not the Stair has been broken.'

'Look, Túmo! The kízinek has brought us back your axe. I told you it was a terrible idea to -'
The dwarf looks up at you and falls silent.
'You wish to know who we are? We are dwarves, just like your friend here. Only he is - what is that word? - Longbeard, while we are Zhélruka. Many thousands of leagues, as I have said to you, we have come from our home. Our home - it is no home. It is Dôm Fálesh.'
'Small bags, big parcels, water-skins - they are scattered all down there.'
'I suppose we'd better help them. Perhaps they'll be inclined to speak with us if we do.'

'The axe? Where is the axe? Ah, Túmo, you drak. You did not tell me that ran off, too. And how many thousands of leagues have we lugged that piece of iron?
'Ah, kízinek, this is a very sour thing to have lost. If you can return to us our axe, you will be owed a debt, I assure you.
'It ran off that way, across the river to I know not where.'

'If we have been quiet, it is because we have been hard at work repairing, reforging, and clearing the dust from our home. Yet we have ever been quieter and more industrious than our kin to the west.'

'I heard that a dragon had returned to Erebor, and that Jangovar roam freely through Dale, which burns both night and day. Is any of it true?'
When you tell the dwarf it is not, his face darkens for a moment, then brightens again.
'Then my cousins are well. I am happy to hear it!'

'Yes, the ground shook here. Many of us were in the midst of battle. When our foes fell back, we turned homeward fearing the worst. To our great relief, Járnfast still stood. It was days more before Lord Náin's face was seen. And how he has changed! We stood in awe of him before. Now... well, I will say no more. Have you seen him for yourself?'

'So there are rumours in my brother's court?'
A wry smile shows in the one living eye in Náin's face.
'There are rumours in Járnfast as well, I am certain, though a stern rebuke would meet the dwarf who brought them before me. It is a symptom of the quiet that follows the storm, no doubt, that many fear more storm.
'But I think we will have no more storms, not such as we have weathered, though other troubles may come to us, from other directions.
'But I wander in my thought. I grant you full leave to satisfy your curiosities. Or have you already done so? I would speak with you when your errand is at an end.'
'My kin in Járnfast will set to rest any rumours that remain. We must not forget to bear King Thorin's greetings to his brother Náin.'

'We should not attend only to the stonework while in Járnfast, ${PLAYER}. Good dwarves, kinfolk of mine, still dwell here, too - I hope!
'They will settle any last rumours we have been charged to test. Not only that, but I shall be glad to see the faces of my kin.
'Let us not forget, as well, King Thorin specially bade us bring his greeting to his brother Náin.'
'It was good to see my kinfolk, but better still to hear their voices, hearty and hale. I will return to Erebor with more news than just the task with which I was charged.'

Explicas que Vethúg fue asesinado, pero no estás seguro del destino de Karazgar. No logró convencer a Hrímil para que se pusiera de su lado y fue atacado por ella, pero encontraste pruebas de que sobrevivió y escapó.
'¿Escapó? ¿Podría haber pasado por nosotros mientras luchábamos contra los dracos? Ese canalla astuto. Si ese es el caso, debemos encontrarlo y hacer justicia de una vez por todas.
'En cuanto a ti, has ganado más que la gratitud del clan Zhélruka. Ve, descansa, festeja, cuídate. Te llamaremos cuando lo encontremos.'

'What is this?'
Dori begins to read the missive and his face sinks.
'This is some trick, ${PLAYER}. It must be!
'Nori would not have done this!'

'Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior... not since the days of Azog has a name been so reviled by my people!
'His cunning drew our foe of old, a great cold-drake, to Erebor. Dwarves, Elves, and Men battled against Vethúg Wintermind, but it seems our defeat of the great cold-drake only served to further his designs for the North.
'You see, after Vethúg fled the battle, Karazgar followed him into the Ered Mithrin. By Durin's beard, nothing good can come of that!
'Karazgar has left us in peace, but he will return. I am certain of it!'

'The great cold-drake, Vethúg Wintermind, has long been known to my people.
'When the Longbeards still dwelled among the Grey Mountains in the Dwarf-kingdom of Grárik, my people discovered a great delving beneath the slopes of the Wrathhorn. They restored it and built upon it, naming it Thikil-gundu, or the Steel Keep in the Common Tongue.
'It is true that the first mines and outposts in the Grey Mountains were delved by the Zhélruka, but the halls of the Steel Keep were shaped by the craft of the Longbeards. I will not speak of rightful claims or of the old conflict between our peoples -- they matter no longer. It was a great cold-drake that stole Thikil-gundu from us! Vethúg Wintermind!
'Vethúg devoured Dáin I, and slew his son, Frór. Grárik was ended, and if not for the flight of Thrór and Grór, the Longbeards would not have survived.
'Mere weeks after the War had ended, Karazgar drew Vethúg Wintermind to Erebor, and though my people suffered great losses, the cold-drake was defeated... but not slain.
'Whether he seeks to tend his wounds or die atop our hoards of old, I am certain he has returned to the halls of Thikil-gundu.'

'After Vethúg was defeated and Karazgar travelled into the North, I issued an edict forbidding any expeditions to the lost halls of Thikil-gundu.
'It seemed that my people had come to understand my wisdom, or so I thought.
'It was then I was betrayed by one of my father's oldest and closest friends. Nori, hero of Erebor and Keeper of the Coffers, had gathered an expedition in secret and set out in the night.
'In anger, I thought to leave him to his fate, but that is not the way of a King under the Mountain.'

'And now you understand, ${PLAYER}.
'It is true that Vethúg Wintermind was defeated, but that does not mean that Thikil-gundu has been left unguarded. Karazgar has pursued Vethúg into the Grey Mountains, and there are Orcs of Gundabad lurking in the foothills. If the Zhélruka hope to reclaim the Steel Keep, they will have to contend with the dangers of the Grey Mountains... and I am inclined to let them.
'However, their passage into the Ered Mithrin has not gone unnoticed by my people. Even now, they gather before my throne in anger and restlessness.
'Listen well to their grievances, ${PLAYER}, and then we will see if I cannot put their minds at ease.'

'It is as I expected, but not as I had hoped, ${PLAYER}.
'My edict was not firm enough to withstand the passage of the Zhélruka... and my people will not heed it. Nori has proven that much to be true. I may hold the rest of them back for days, weeks, or even years, but it will not last. There must be another way....'
King Thorin produces a small missive and glares at it.
'Nori left a missive behind when he made for Thikil-gundu with his expedition. I would ask that you deliver it to Dori.
'I think now it is time that he learns what his brother has done!'

'Do you have it? The dragon-stone?'
You produce a small fragment of dragon-stone and show it to Zádokh Flint-eye. His eyes widen in awe.
'I did not even believe it to be true! It is beautiful!'
Zádokh Flint-eye pockets the dragon-stone fragment and appears to collect himself.
'You have done as I asked, and I am nothing if not a dwarf of my word. The Longbeards have gone to Brúgrad, but they do not name it as we do. It is known to them as Tharrazhâr, and to those who speak in the Common Tongue: Skarháld.
'If they have remained there, they will not be as welcome as they may think. The great warriors of my people have travelled for many miles, and they are not eager to share in the lost wealth of the Grey Mountains.
'That is all I have to tell. Leave me to my gold!'

'I had begun to think you continued to Thikil-gundu without us, ${PLAYER}! Did you learn anything of my brother or Vethúg Wintermind?'
You explain that Vethúg Wintermind crashed onto the foothills of the mountain, Winterstith, and left the Bitter Scar in his wake. You also mention that Nori's expedition passed through the old dwarf-hold of Skarháld in the Ered Mithrin.
'Skarháld lies upon the Men Angrún, but the matter of Vethúg Wintermind cannot be put off any longer.'

'Very good.
'Listen well, ${RACE}. You'll have to scrounge around for ten more gold coins if you want me to repeat myself.
'You spoke of the cold-drake known to the Longbeards as Vethúg Wintermind. I know where he has gone! Such was the weight of his fall into the Grey Mountains that the ground was torn asunder. He fell broken into the foothills of Winterstith and left the Bitter Scar in his wake. Neither the Zhélruka nor the Longbeards knew such a ruin in the earlier years of the Grey Mountains, but it is here now, I assure you.
'Ah, and if you wish to learn the destination of your Longbeard friends, you'll see it soon enough.
'Have you heard of dragon-stone? It is normally found deep beneath the earth, but the creation of that black cleft by the Longbeards' cold-drake might have revealed some long-hidden deposits.
'If you find even the smallest fragment of dragon-stone in the Bitter Scar, give it to me and I will tell you where the Longbeards have gone.'
The dragon-stone appears to be a sort of hardened, shimmering coal...

''There is another matter to discuss, ${PLAYER}.
'While we waited on your return, a small company of Zhélruka passed through the Southgate. They spoke in hushed tones, but I heard enough. It seems they make for a small encampment named Dôm Goru in the foothills of the Ered Mithrin.
'The Zhélruka are not the most cooperative of dwarves, but I have known them to be keen observers. Either this company or their kinsfolk might know of Nori's passage into the Ered Mithrin... or perhaps where Vethúg Wintermind has fallen. Ask what you must, but do not speak of Thikil-gundu. The rightful claim to the Steel Keep is still a matter of contention between our peoples, and it would be unwise to provoke them needlessly.
'It seemed from their tone that they did not intend to remain there long, and so, I must ask you to ride ahead of our company.
'Once we have readied ourselves, we will join you at Dôm Goru.'

'Ah, what brings a ${RACE} like you so far into the Grey Mountains?'
You explain to Zádokh Flint-eye that you seek a company of Longbeards that passed through the Grey Mountains and that you have also come in search of the remains of the cold-drake, Vethúg Wintermind.
'Zádokh Flint-eye is my name, and if you are in search of something, I will know where to find it. Indeed, the fates of those Longbeards and the cold-drake are known to me, but information of that sort is valuable... very valuable.
'I will offer it to you... for a price. The worms, drakes, and Dragons of the Grey Mountains have slowed my journey. If you were to remove some of them from my path, I could be convinced to share what I know.
'Do we have a deal?'

'Drakes and worms? I think you misheard me, ${RACE}.
'I asked you to defeat dragons... not their feeble offspring! Do you expect me to part with any worthwhile information, and information about Longbeards no less, for such a pittance?
'You would have saved the both of us time if you had just handed me a bag of gold. In fact, why don't you do that?
'Ten gold coins, and I'll tell you what I know. It is a fair price for such knowledge!'

'At least Débel did not allow my brother's home to fall into disrepair....'
Dori glances around Nori's home and pauses upon a stack of papers piled on the dining table.
'I think my brother left more hastily than he expected to, ${PLAYER}. Look!
'There are papers piled upon the table, and I see other curiosities left about that I would like to examine. Take a look at those papers and see if my brother has left any hint of his course or the names of other dwarves that we might question.
'Once you have done that, let us meet back here.'

'My brother believes that because the great cold-drake was defeated that our old hoards lay unguarded? By dragons, perhaps, but the Orcs will not have abandoned them.
'As the King under the Mountain said, Thikil-gundu is best forgotten. The Longbeards have found only misfortune and death in the Steel Keep. If I do not aid my brother, this expedition will be his doom.
'We are forbidden from travelling to Thikil-gundu, but perhaps King Thorin will be merciful upon my family and allow me to pursue him into the Ered Mithrin. It is the only course!
'Come, we must go at once!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you continue this quest, you will swiftly travel to the Hall under the Mountain.</rgb>

'Did I not say I was a dwarf of my word?
'I knew very little of the plans of the Keeper of the Coffers, but I knew enough. He made for the Steel Keep of old... Thikil-gundu as it was once named in the tongue of the dwarves.
'I could not follow him as he wished, but I offered to keep his home in order until his return. I have borne Nori's secret faithfully, but I do not wish to lose the favour of the King under the Mountain.
'Here, take this key. Perhaps Nori left behind some clue for his brother to find....'

'I do not appreciate your gaze. What business have you in the New-lodes?'
You explain to the dwarf that he matches the description of a dwarf Dori believed to be in league with Nori's secret expedition. The dwarf lets out a long sigh.
'Very well... I am Débel. I am not so deeply involved as you might believe, but yes, I know of these things. I suppose the truth would come out sooner or later, but I had hoped it would be after Nori returned to Erebor.
'I cannot give such information freely, but I can offer it for a trifle. If you were to clear out some of the deep-claws that have burrowed into the New-lodes, I give my word that I will share all I know of Nori and his expedition.
'What do you say?'

'You found the dwarf, did you? Very good! What did he have to say of my brother?'
You explain to Dori that Débel did not offer much in the way of new information, but he did offer up the key to Nori's home.
'A key? My brother entrusted his key to this Débel before me? We shall have much to discuss when next I see him!
'My brother was not one to leave things unorganised... he is the Keeper of the Coffers after all! However, if Nori has travelled to Thikil-gundu, I must know his course through the Ered Mithrin. They are unfriendly lands, now home only to Orcs and dragons.
'It is to Tumnu-dûm we must go. Those are the dwelling-halls of Erebor, and it is there Nori makes his home.
'I will await you outside his home. After all, you have the key!'

'You have the spare key, yes?
'Let us see what my brother left behind, ${PLAYER}. I hope it is of some use to us....'

Dori seems fixated upon the King under the Mountain and barely seems to notice your approach.
'King Thorin III Stonehelm, King under the Mountain, I beg leave to travel into the Ered Mithrin. You have forbidden Durin's Folk to return to the Steel Keep, Thikil-gundu, but that is not my purpose. I go in search of my brother, Nori!
'I am a loyal dwarf of Erebor. I have fought and bled in its defence... from the Easterlings... from Bolg! All I ask is the chance to save Nori from his folly!
'Will you grant me leave, King under the Mountain?'

'I hear your words, Dori of the Company.
'Your deeds and those of your kin are not forgotten to any who dwell in Erebor, but Nori has acted in defiance of my edict. Whether his expedition is successful or not, there will be consequences for him.
'I know well that your brother, Ori, was among those lost in Balin's expedition, and I know as well as you do that this bears a resemblance to our efforts to reclaim Khazad-dûm. Both Balin's expedition and the Iron Garrison have failed, and if future losses may still be prevented, they must be. And so, Dori, I grant you leave to follow your brother and put an end to his expedition.
'You will travel on my behalf, but you will go in secret as your brother did. You may form a company of your own choosing, but do not spread word of this to any untrustworthy ears. In addition, I ask that you find the remains of Vethúg Wintermind. He flew from battle gravely wounded and passed into the Ered Mithrin, but I desire proof of his death.
'Heed my words. Deliver Nori from his folly and retrieve for me a bone of Vethúg Wintermind. Only then will we speak of forgiveness....'

'You have my truest gratitude, King under the Mountain. I will do as you have commanded.'
Dori turns to you.
'What do you say, ${PLAYER}? Let us begin our preparations!'
After countless hours of study, Nori learned that the hoarding-vault laid 'beneath the eyes of the Seven'...
After clearing the dust away, Nori drew forth his armour of old. The time had come!
Dori looks around the empty home of his brother...
Thikil-gundu was lost, Nori thought, but it was not the way of dragons to abandon their hoards...
Thikil-gundu had once possessed great wealth, Nori thought, and now it sat unguarded and unclaimed...
Dori shifts uncomfortably outside Nori's home...
After Vethúg's defeat at the gates of Erebor, Nori enlisted his kinsfolk to follow him to Thikil-gundu...
The earth shakes as a deep-claw bursts forth!

'I do not understand, ${PLAYER}.
'What has compelled my brother to act so foolishly? He has lived a life of wealth in Erebor! He is the Keeper of the Coffers! Or he was....
'Bah! I should have confronted him. I saw dwarves speaking with him in hushed tones, but I thought nothing of it. Nori is a dwarf of some repute, after all.
'If only I knew the names of those dwarves, but... wait. I do recall one of them. This dwarf seemed to be of a line descended from both the Longbeards and the Zhélruka of the East. He was thin in the beard, but any dwarf would be proud to have such a moustache.
'He is a miner, I think. Search for him in the New-lodes of Narathâk, and perhaps he will be better able to explain why my brother has left for Thikil-gundu.'

'So Vethúg has fallen upon Winterstith....
'If what the Zhélruka say is true, Nori has already passed beyond the easternmost mountains to Skarháld, but Winterstith lies not far to the north. From what you have told me, Vethúg must have carved a path of frozen ruin through the foothills of the Ered Mithrin as he fell. Ah, but where does it lead? To Winterstith? To the heart of the Anvil itself? We must find out!
'Come, ${PLAYER}. Let us follow the Bitter Scar to its end and see what we discover!'

'We have arrived, ${PLAYER}. It may be named Skarháld in the Common Tongue, but I know it as Tharrazhâr.
'I know well the history of Tharrazhâr, but I must appear to be an old dwarf, frail of mind, to Ingór and his kinsfolk... at least for now. These walls of stone and azurite... they were wrought by Longbeards! Though I cannot contest it, these Zhélruka have no claim to this fortress.
'I have seen more unfriendly glances fall upon our Stout-axe companions, and so, I think we should press on once we have rested.
'Yet, I have not forgotten that Zádokh Flint-eye spoke of a company of Longbeards in Tharrazhâr. He may have spoken half-truths of Vethúg Wintermind, but who can say what will we find here?'
'It is time, ${PLAYER}. Let us see where the old cold-drake has come to rest.'

'Our preparations are made, our goats are watered and well-rested, but one matter still remains.'
Dori gestures at the massive chest of gold and gem-stones before him.
'This is but a small measure of my share of the treasure reclaimed from Smaug the Golden, and it is still greater wealth than most dwarves will ever know.
'I want you to deliver it to Ravenhill, ${PLAYER}. The raven-chief, Arcah, and her people are fond of all that glimmers, and if her people would aid me in the search for my brother, I offer it all. I do not know if I could deliver it by my own hand, and so, I ask this of you.
'Once you have finished this business at Ravenhill, follow the long road beneath its heights into the Ered Mithrin. The Company shall await you along the road.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! It is done, then? Very good.
'I have known the raven-chiefs to be wise counselors, but whether their counsel is good or ill, they speak with sharp tongues. Has the raven-chief offered you any counsel on our task?'
You inform Dori that the raven-chief warned that Thikil-gundu was an accursed place, and that she would not send her ravens there.
'Accursed? I do not think so, ${PLAYER}. Thikil-gundu has been the doom of many Longbeards, but there is no curse upon it! A curse of dragon-kind, perhaps... but nothing more.
'That is enough talk of Thikil-gundu for now, I think. Let us hope the ravens find some sign of my brother's passage through the Ered Mithrin.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}.
'After dusk, we will gather before the gates of Erebor and begin our journey into the Ered Mithrin under the cover of darkness.
'If you have any unfinished business in Erebor, I would see to it. The hour soon approaches!'

'Humph!
'Of all the dwarves I hoped to gather, I have found only four. I spoke first to the dwarves I travelled with on the quest of old to the Lonely Mountain, but only Bofur and Glóin have agreed to join us. Bifur offered no reason for his refusal, but I do not doubt he has seen enough of battle. As for the others, Dwalin must tend to his duties at Thorin's Hall in the Ered Luin, and I would not ask Bombur or the fine dwarves who bear him about to make such a journey.
'Ah, but the elder of the Stout-axes, the one named Spakorth... he is a keen dwarf! I spoke to him of our task in the Ered Mithrin, and he offered two of his finest warriors to me. Náth and Dréri are young in the years of dwarves, but if the wisdom of my kinsfolk should fail us, the might of the Stout-axes will deliver us from trouble.
'I have spoken enough of such things! You have gathered what I asked, and now you should prepare six packs. One for each of the dwarves of the Company, and one for my brother, Nori, for when he is found.
'Once that is done, return to me.'
Arcah casts an inquisitive gaze in your direction...

'If Vethúg Wintermind lives still, he will not have forgotten the hurts done to him by the Longbeards and Bardings....
'We must go.'

'I do not like the look of this....
'Either we have been deceived by the Zhélruka or Vethúg was not as wounded as he appeared to be! There is no mistaking that Vethúg tore this rift in the foothills of Winterstith, but it is where he has gone that concerns me!
'Do you see these marks in the earth? I first thought nothing of them, but there are signs of battle here among the fallen stones of Winterstith! Unless the great cold-drake battled only against rocks and ice as they fell, some other foe must have come to this place. I know few who could withstand the might of Vethúg Wintermind, and so, I fear this is the work of Karazgar!
'Perhaps you can uncover the truth of what has happened here, ${PLAYER}.'
A company of Zhélruka blocks the way!
Ingór crosses his arms and waits for Dori's response...
You are able to free a bloodied, black arrow from the frozen earth...
Only Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior, could have left this behind...
Shards of ice litter the ground, betraying a final, futile struggle by Vethúg Wintermind...

'In truth, I feel a sense of dread in the shadows of the Grey Mountains. It is nothing more than a feeling, I think, but there is something about this place that has left me uneasy.

'These Ungoledain are indeed a threat. Many of my friends have perished to their poison. While you were away I began experimenting with a potion to protect against it. I think I have perfected the concoction.
'If you collect the ingredients, I will be able to make plenty to protect you, the Beornings, and most importantly, my friends.
'Here is what you must find: some poison of the Ungoledain, which is likely obtained most easily from their discarded weapons; clean water from a good source; the livers of animals sickened from the poison; and some of the common mushrooms that may be found all around Thornholt.'

Return to Threkmóth
'Your help is most welcome, ${RACE}. Vaskorn is my brother. I would have run off to stand by his side sooner, if I had known.'
'Threkmóth is not a bad sort, really, though sometimes I think he cares more for honey cakes than his folk, or anyone else for that matter.'
'I suppose I should take this potion too, hadn't I? Well, then. Preparations are nearly complete, I should say.'

'Your timing is remarkable, ${PLAYER}. The honey cakes have just finished baking. I may set them to cool properly while we deal with these bothersome Ungoledain.
'You may give the poison protection to Fiskvat and Hunulf, while I set the honey cakes out to cool. We share a fence, and therefore trust.'

'You think it was reckless to send Vaskorn by himself? Well... perhaps so. My mind was very much on my baking, you see, and it seemed sensible enough at the time.
'Every once in a while, one Beorning is not enough for the task. I do not think we are too late. We should help him. He thinks very highly of you, ${RACE}, so I will trust you. You have seen what we are up against, after all. You may lead us to their camp.
'Here is my plan: you return to the brown wizard and bring back this potion of his, while I will get the others prepared for the outing.'

Talk to Dori at Skarháld

'You have done us a great service, ${PLAYER}. I wish I could offer you more in return, but I have told you all there is to tell!
'Nori and his company continued onward to Thikil-gundu without us, but not long after, the Zhélruka arrived....'
Órug pauses for a moment and gazes into the fire.
'I have known the Zhélruka to embellish their tales, but there are often hints of truth within them.
'There are many Zhélruka in Skarháld... perhaps a few among them will have the answers you seek!'

'What have you learned, ${PLAYER}?'
You inform Dori that only a few Longbeards remain in Skarháld and that Nori and the rest of his expedition followed the Men Angrún to Thikil-gundu. You also inform Dori that the Zhélruka made mention of Karazgar, Vethúg Wintermind, and strange dwarves wandering in the night.
'Strange dwarves? The Zhélruka have called the Longbeards many things in many tongues, but I have never known them to call us strange. I wonder what the truth of that tale could be....
'If Nori and his expedition have travelled to Thikil-gundu by way of the Men Angrún, he will have passed through Óinsbridge. It is there we must go!'

'I never thought to see Tharrazhâr with my own eyes....'
Dori looks around and appears lost in thought for a moment.
'Long ago, these mountains were rich and little explored, ${PLAYER}, but in his wisdom, Thorin I reshaped them into the Dwarf-kingdom of Grárik. It flourished for a time and great wealth was found beneath the peaks of the Grey Mountains, but that very wealth proved the doom of Grárik. Drawn by a powerful greed, it was the dragons of the wastes beyond that laid siege to Grárik. First fell Ablâk-khadar, the Stormwall, and its forges were extinguished. Second fell Tharrazhâr, and its keep was shattered. Third fell Aglâmbazar, the great Glimmerdeep, and it was there Smaug the Golden made his lair. Last fell Thikil-gundu, the Steel Keep and seat of Grárik, and I need not name the great cold-drake who slew King Dáin I and his son, Frór, along with countless others. The Dwarf-kingdom of Grárik was no more.
'I tell you this so you understand, ${PLAYER}. Tharrazhâr... bah, Skarháld, belongs to Durin's Folk!
'Are there any other Longbeards here in the remnants of Grárik? If Zádokh Flint-eye has not spoken true, gold will be the least of his troubles.'

Collected fallen branches from the Thornholt (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Find the dwarves of Nori's expedition in Skarháld
Talk to Órug

'${PLAYER}....
'How have you come to be in this place? Does my mind now play tricks upon me?'
You inform Órug that you have come to the Grey Mountains with Dori and Company in search of Nori and his expedition.
'It has been many days since last we saw Nori and the rest of his expedition. Before we came to Tharrazhâr, the expedition was beset by Orcs of Gundabad. The Orcs were slain to the last, but a few of our number sustained grave wounds in the battle. It was decided that we would remain behind in Tharrazhâr and work to rebuild it as it was in the time of Grárik. After we restored the first hall of the keep, I saw that a small company of Zhélruka had arrived. At first, I thought nothing of it, but then more arrived... and more... and more out of the East. They must number in the hundreds now! There has been little talk between our peoples, but we have at least agreed to put aside our separate tongues. It is Skarháld now... not Tharrazhâr or Brúgrad!
'And so it has been! I wish there was more to be told, but I know only that Nori and his expedition continued to the south along the Men Angrún. It is the most well-travelled path to Thikil-gundu, but it was the work of Angmar... and even now, it is often travelled by the foes of the Longbeards.
'I have done my best to tend the wounds of my kinsfolk, but I am no healer. All I know is that a warm meal and a hot fire would do much to aid us!'
The Remnants of Grárik

'${PLAYER}! I feared you would not return!
'When Ingór returned in your stead, he spoke of... wights that clawed and hewed his company. That is not the work of dragons! What devilry is afoot in Thikil-gundu?'
You tell Dori that none of the newly-slain Longbeards or Zhélruka remained to be found in the Grey Wrack.
'Where have they gone? Where has my brother gone?'
You hand Nori's axe to Dori, and his face sinks.
'No... no!'

'Hmmph! There is no comfort to be found in this place, but it will have to do. At least we are sheltered from the wind!
'Alas, there was little room for the goats atop Stánbalk, so Náth has stabled them below as best he can. If this snowstorm does not soon relent, they ought to try growing their winter coats!
'Let me see if my eyes do not fail me...'
Dori gazes into the Grey Wrack, squinting as flakes of snow become entangled in his eyebrows and beard.
'I see the blurred shapes you described, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot say who or what they might be. You are a hardy ${CLASS}, my friend. Will you descend into the Grey Wrack and find out?
'If they are dwarves, they might belong to Nori's expedition. If they are not, well... it is better to know what lies before us, I think!'

'Malek... Vozdo... all of them... dead! Why... why have you come here, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Ingór that Dori's brother, Nori, made for Thikil-gundu. Ingór laughs weakly and grimaces. You notice several fresh gashes in his armour.
'So that... was the Longbeards' plan... eh? They can have it! Dómekh... is cursed! The Steel Keep is lost! It is not the drakes you should fear, ${CLASS}... for the Dead walk again! They have slain all in their path... Zhélruka... Longbeards... none have escaped but me!
'What am I to do now? Return to my people... as a coward? Beg the mercy of my own brother?'
You do not answer Ingór's questions, but you tell him that Dori and Company have made camp atop Stánbalk.
'Perhaps I will go to them, but... I beg you... do as I ask. Many Longbeards and Zhélruka lie slain before the Steel Keep... but that is no resting place for a dwarf! When the dwarves fought as one at Azanulbizar long ago, so many were the slain that they could not be borne away to the tombs of our peoples. And so, they were... burned... to spare them any indignity in death.
'Will you do this for my people, ${PLAYER}? Will you do this for the Longbeards? If the Dead seek to stop you, let them join the others as burned dwarves!'
'Go!'
You have not found any of the slain Longbeards or Zhélruka that Ingór described!

'After all these years, it is unchanged....
'When Vethúg Wintermind froze the Steel Keep and made it his lair, the lands surrounding Thikil-gundu were shrouded in winter. Grárik, the Grey Realm, was ended. All that remained was the Grey Wrack. I had thought in time these lands would heal, but it is not so.'
Dori looks sorrowfully at the bones scattered before Stánbalk.
'Stánbalk was once the greatest defence of Thikil-gundu, and now... it stands watch over the dead.
'I think it unwise to press on without scouting Stánbalk. There may be more unseen dangers lurking ahead!
'Scale the remains of Stánbalk, ${PLAYER}, and look into the lands of the Grey Wrack.
'If you deem it safe, we shall make camp atop it!'

'What did you spy from Stánbalk, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Dori that you did not encounter any foes near to the wall, but you noticed blurred shapes moving in the distance.
'It is strange that we have seen so few drakes this near to Thikil-gundu. If the Steel Keep remained the lair of Vethúg Wintermind since the time of Dáin, I would have expected more of his brood to lurk in the foothills of the Wrathhorn. Ah, but who am I to question a moment of good fortune? Perhaps my brother was right after all!
'I think we should make camp atop Stánbalk. Even if we are fortunate enough to encounter none of Vethúg's brood, the path to Thikil-gundu is still treacherous.
'Come, ${PLAYER}!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: You will swiftly travel to the top of Stánbalk when you continue this quest.</rgb>

'Are you all right, ${PLAYER}? Even a cold-drake as young as that one poses a great threat!
'Did you find the lost raven?'
You tell Dori that the lost raven was seemingly slain by a cold-drake.
'When the raven did not fly to answer the call of its kin, I feared it so. Though I did not wish to believe it, I knew in my heart what fate must have befallen it.'
Dori casts a sorrowful glance to the ravens, and shakes his head.
'So this is the way of the Grey Wrack....'
The raven perches silently....

'Ah, ${PLAYER}!
'Did you encounter the Orcs of Gundabad as well? Several harried us in our travels, but they were soon defeated. Give me the feathers you have recovered, and when at last we return to Erebor, I shall deliver them to Arcah myself!
'Two of the ravens are now found, but one remains lost. Though it is now broken and ruined, the great Stone Wall before us, Stánbalk, long stood in defence of Thikil-gundu. If Arcah forbade her people from venturing too near to the Steel Keep, they would have flown no further than Stánbalk.
'While the others and I take rest, I would ask that you search for the lost raven among the ruins of Stánbalk.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. I fear Vethúg was not the last of his kind in the Grey Mountains!'

'Just a moment, ${PLAYER}!'
Dori asks the raven if it has seen any sign of Nori or his expedition. The raven croaks and chitters in answer. All of a sudden, the raven spreads its wings and looses a shrill cry.
'I understand, friend.'
Dori turns his gaze to you.
'These are not glad tidings, ${PLAYER}. Nori is nowhere to be found, and two of the three ravens sent to search for my brother have become lost in the Grey Mountains. One flew for the Rushgate far to the north-west, and the other... the other may have gone to Thikil-gundu. And that is not the half of it! The ravens have spied black-arrows of Gundabad lying in wait beyond the forest, and they have fletched their arrows with the feathers of ravens! It is also said they are practised in the art of stealth, but I have not known many Orcs to possess such patience. If we are to reach Thikil-gundu, we shall have to remain on guard.
'Ride to the Rushgate along the Men Angrún and search for the lost raven. If you encounter any of those black-arrows, defeat them and reclaim the feathers they have stolen. Such an insult cannot go unanswered!
'When you have reached the Rushgate, turn back and ride to meet us along the road to Thikil-gundu. Our journey draws near to its end, ${PLAYER}. Let us not falter at so late an hour!'

'I cannot atone for what I have done, ${PLAYER}. I have disobeyed the King under the Mountain, I have deceived my brother... and for what? Naught, I say!
'Even the gold we found is no boon to my people! There is a curse upon Thikil-gundu... and nothing in the halls of the Steel Keep has gone untouched by it!
'Once I was renowned among Durin's Folk... a hero of the Lonely Mountain! Am I now to be known as the foolish, old dwarf who dreamt of treasures lost?
'No... I will not let this be the end of it!'

'Our journey is over, ${PLAYER}... at least for the moment!
'Nori thinks himself a disgraced dwarf, but these hurts will heal in time! He has adventured as few dwarves have in their lives! Was I disappointed in my brother? Was I fearful that he had led himself to certain doom? Of course I was! But... he is my brother! Even if the King under the Mountain will not forgive Nori as I have, this will not be the end of our adventures!
'There is a fire in the hearts of Durin's Folk! An unquenchable flame! And you have proven yourself among us, my friend.
'We have forced Karazgar out of Thikil-gundu, and that is enough! Even so, there is some unseen evil lurking in our delving of old... and many questions linger in my mind.
'But this day, we honour the lost here among the halls of Tharrazhâr!'

Dori stares at Nori's axe in disbelief.
'Has my brother gone into Thikil-gundu without the aid of his own expedition? Has Karazgar devised some cruel purpose for him?
'But what if... what if he has been taken like the others? No! I will not believe such things!
'We will enter Thikil-gundu together, ${PLAYER}, and we will find my brother!'

'What else did you find?'
You tell Dori that you found an abandoned camp-site in Óinsbridge, and that you believe Nori and his expedition rested a night before passing through the western reaches of the Thornholt.
'My brother and his expedition have kept quite the pace! Were I not so cross with him, I might be impressed!
'Once I have heard what Arcah's raven has to tell, we'll be off!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. Does Dori wish me to return?'
You explain that you followed a path of hoof-prints from the abandoned camp-site to Bofur.
'O! Those tracks were mine! Or my goat's, rather! You see, I found the old camp-site as well, but when I began to search the road I discovered tracks leading deeper into the forest. They are not unlike those of the goats of Erebor, and so, I think they belong to Nori and his expedition.
'It is likely they continue on the road ahead for some distance, but who can say if Nori has taken a less-travelled path through the Thornholt?
'If you were to follow them, we might learn if the path of the expedition strayed from the Men Angrún.
'Go on ahead, ${PLAYER}! I will keep watch!'

'It is time, ${PLAYER}. We have spent long enough in the ruins of Tharrazhâr!
'While I and the others set out on the journey to Óinsbridge, I would ask that you speak to Ingór, son of Vékun. I have felt many eyes upon us here, and I fear that my attempt at deception has not gone unnoticed. And so, I would have you tell Ingór that I seek my brother, Nori. It is the truth, and it should put his mind at ease. I seek not for wealth or glory... only for my lost kin.
'When that is done, ride for Óinsbridge. It is there we will reunite and take our next rest.
'Óinsbridge lies to the south beyond the forest, but the Thornholt is home to many dangers. Do not stray from the dark road!'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}.
'I do hope my kinsfolk have held their tongues in regards to your Kámbrada companions. From what Dori has told me, Náth and Dréri and the rest of their kinsfolk knew great hardship in Mordor before they came to dwell in the Lonely Mountain. Enough hardship, I think, that mere insults would do naught to wound them. Perhaps I am not so resilient, but I find the greatest insult to be dishonesty.
'Tell me, ${PLAYER}. Have you had any luck in finding heirlooms of the Longbeards or have you come to tell me the truth of Dori's little expedition? What is it you truly seek?'
You tell Ingór of Dori's lost brother, Nori, who travelled into the Grey Mountains against the will of his kin and the King under the Mountain.
'I see. Perhaps I have judged Dori too hastily....
'There is a byword among the Zhélruka. Its true meaning cannot be shared, but it speaks of one who is governed by a doomed obsession. Those unlucky few \qseek the Citadel\q. For Dori's sake, I hope his brother does not seek the Citadel.
'You may go, ${PLAYER}. May you find Nori before death or madness takes him.'

'At last, we have come to Óinsbridge.
'It is a fine respite from the gloom of the Thornholt, but the western reaches of the forest still lie ahead of us. If Nori and his expedition took rest here, it is likely that some sign of their passage has been left behind. And so, I have asked the others to search for signs of the expedition, ${PLAYER}. Would you join them?
'Oh, and do not be afraid to cross to the other side of the Forest River! The bridge may have fallen into disrepair, but it is still sturdy enough to bear the weight of a few dwarves and a ${RACE}, I think!'

El Yunque del Pico Invernal

'¡${PLAYER}! ¿Fue ese un ataque de Hrímil Corazónhelado en persona? ¡La engañaste para que se encerrara a sí misma! Parece que estamos a salvo por ahora. Le llevará algún tiempo abrirse camino a través de todo ese hielo. ¿Y Karazgar? ¿Lo encontraste?'
Le explicas que Vethúg fue asesinado, pero no estás seguro del destino de Karazgar. No logró convencer a Hrímil para que se pusiera de su lado y fue atacado por ella, pero encontraste pruebas de que sobrevivió y escapó.
'¿Escapó? ¿Podría habernos eludido mientras luchábamos contra los dragonzuelos? ¡Ese astuto bribón! Si ese es el caso, debemos encontrarlo y hacerle justicia de una vez por todas.
'En cuanto a ti, has ganado más que la gratitud del clan Zhelruka. Ve, descansa, festeja, cuídate. ¡Te llamaremos cuando lo encontremos!'

'¡Karazgar y su dragonzuelo fueron vistos volando hacia el norte, hacia el Brezal Marchito! ¡Debe estar dirigiéndose hacia el Yunque del Pico Invernal!
'Esto es terrible, ${PLAYER}. El Yunque está lleno de dragonzuelos de escarcha, y sabemos que se ha reabierto. Si Karazgar suma su número a sus fuerzas, será imparable, y si los rumores son ciertos, ¡el Heraldo del Invierno podría estar allí!
'Espera, ¿quién es ese? ¿Trajiste a alguien contigo?'

'¿Qué quieren esos Barbiluengos y Hachetón? ¿Qué hacen aquí?'
Le explicas que los Barbiluengos tienen un viejo asunto pendiente con Vethúg Menteinvernal y que los Hachetón desean ir al Yunque por su cuenta.
'Tsss... No me agradan esos vépro-vlasa Kambrada, pero si tú te responsabilizas de ellos, está bien. Has ayudado lo suficiente al clan Zhelruka como para que confíe en tu juicio... Mejor que se preparen bien, eso sí. Si el heraldo del invierno está realmente allí, ¡nos arriesgamos a entrar en la boca del lobo!
'Si tienes suficiente valor para enfrentarte a lo que pueda haber dentro del Yunque, reúne tus fuerzas y encuéntranos allí.'
<rgb=#FF0000>La instancia 'El Yunque del Pico Invernal' (12 jugadores) ya está disponible en el Buscador de Instancias. </rgb>

Has recibido noticias de que Karazgar está en movimiento, y los Zhelruka de Skarhald temen que pueda regresar pronto. Horin está liderando una expedición para investigar, y ha pedido que vayas con él.

'${PLAYER}, ¡veo que mi llamado ha llegado a tus oídos! ¡Bien!
'Ha llegado el momento de demostrar que eres un verdadero amigo de los Zhelruka. Inek me ha encargado liderar un grupo de caza, y quiero que seas uno de sus miembros. Nuestra presa: ¡El Guerrero Lloroso! Su ataque contra Skarhald no debe quedar sin respuesta. Y no debemos esperar a que reúna fuerzas y regrese como prometió. No, lo encontraremos y desbarataremos sus planes ahora, o mejor abandonamos nuestros planes en estas montañas.
'Uno de mis exploradores ha enviado noticias de que fue visto, así que lo seguiremos. Saldré pronto hacia el Paso del Dragón con los guerreros que pueda reunir. Encuéntrame allí.'

'${PLAYER}! ¡Estás vivo! Dréri y Nath acaban de regresar. ¡Podíamos escuchar el gran rugido del dragón desde aquí! ¡Cuéntanos todo!'
Le cuentas a Nori sobre la muerte de Vethúg, el fallido plan de Karazgar y su escape, y la furia de Hrímil Corazónhelado. Sacas el hueso de tu bolsa y se lo entregas. Lo mira con asombro.
'¡Ja! Si tan solo mis viejos huesos pudieran haber luchado a tu lado. ¡Los juglares seguramente cantarán canciones sobre eso durante años! Y gracias por esto. El rey Thorin estará complacido de escuchar sobre el final de ese dragonzuelo. Sin embargo, el Heraldo del Invierno...'
La expresión de Nori se vuelve sombría.
'El hecho de que se haya encerrado dentro del Yunque solo nos ha dado un poco de tiempo. Es un dragón de los días antiguos, con poder para rivalizar con Smaug mismo. ¡Quizás incluso superándolo! Erebor y los reinos del Norte no podrán ignorar tal amenaza por mucho tiempo. Tendremos que idear un plan para lidiar con esta amenaza, y cuando lo hagamos, estoy seguro de que pediremos tu ayuda, héroe.'

'${PLAYER}, ¡te seguimos tan rápido como pudimos cuando supimos que ibas a perseguir a Karazgar con los Zhelruka! Me gustaría pedirte un favor.'
Nori parece ligeramente incómodo y duda antes de volver a hablar.
'Como sabes, fracasamos en la misión que nos encomendó el rey Thorin. No pudimos derribar a ese maldito dragonzuelo Vethúg Menteinvernal cuando nos lo encontramos en Thikil-gundu. Yo... me culpo por esto. Si Dori y los demás no hubieran venido, seguramente habría perecido en esa antigua fortaleza. Si vas a enfrentarte a él y a Karazgar, te pido que hagas lo que nosotros no pudimos, y traigas un hueso del cadáver destrozado de Vethúg.'
Mira a su hermano. Dori asiente.
'Tengo vergüenza de pedirte esto, ya que Dori y yo hemos decidido que nuestros días de aventuras han quedado atrás. Por favor, haz esto por nosotros, para que podamos regresar a Erebor con honor.'

'Esos viejos Barbiluengos no hablan por nosotros. Dréri y yo estaríamos encantados de viajar contigo hasta el Yunque. ¡Nos espera la gloria de enfrentarnos a Karazgar y a los monstruosos dragonzuelos que hay dentro!
'Esta es la oportunidad perfecta para devolverle al Pueblo de Durin su amabilidad, y tratar de hacer las paces con el clan Zhelruka. Ah, pero me temo que puede que necesiten algo de convencimiento. Tal vez si hablas con ellos en nuestro nombre, nos permitan unirnos a su grupo.'

'Why, this is my favourite! Oh, thank you. Thank you!'
'Is that for me? It is? Hurrah!'
'Oh, thank you, ${CLASS}.'
'¡Muchas gracias!'
'A warm drink! I will share this with the others. Perhaps they will share their sweets with me.'
'I have never had one of these. Is it as delicious as it looks? Well, if I do not like it, perhaps I can trade with one of the others.'

'We heard all about it, traveller. About the Eagle as great as a horse, and someone was going to find all the sweets and bring them back. I am sorry, we did not believe it was true.
'But look, we were mistaken, and now I am so happy!'
'Please, good traveller. Visit the snowy realms of Middle-earth and recover the treats. They are hot cross buns, plum pudding, gingerbread, peppermint treats, a flask of wassail, and fruit cake.'

'Good traveller, I must enlist your aid. One of the Great Eagles was bearing a sack of sweets from far-off Gondor hither to Winter-home. Alas! The bag was rent, and the sweets fell from it as she flew.
'She realized her mistake only as the last sweet fell, and with her keen eyes watched as wintry beasts seized it and ran off into the snow. She had flown among the cold and snowy regions of Middle-earth, she told us, to avoid the sun's great heat and to keep the sweets from spoiling.
'It is much to ask, I know, but those sweets were destined for the poor children of Winter-home. Will you visit the frozen regions of Middle-earth and recover them? I fear they may all have been seized by the creatures of those parts. The sweets that were lost, you should know, were hot cross buns, plum pudding, gingerbread, peppermint treats, a flask of wassail, and fruit cake.'

'You have the sweets? Why look, they are all in one piece. The artisans of Gondor wrapped their gifts well!
'Quickly, will you deliver them to the children? They have been waiting - and it is you who should see the joy on their faces, by all rights.'

'Según mi mapa, hay un camino hacia Afhân-binnîn a través de la casa de banquetes de Amrâg-zahar. ¡Busquémoslo!'

'¡Qué terrible dragonzuelo frío! ¡Debemos matarlo antes de que pueda poner más huevos en Thikil-gundu!
'¿Qué ha sido de mi hermano?'
'¡Karazgar debe pagar por el mal que ha causado!'

'${PLAYER}...
'¡Lo que Karazgar ha hecho no puede quedar sin castigo! Ha matado a los nuestros, ha desatado la furia de los Dragones del Norte sobre la Montaña Solitaria y ha robado y profanado las salas de Thikil-gundu. ¡Los siete debemos enfrentarnos a él!'
Dori se vuelve hacia Nori.
'¿Hacia dónde se ha dirigido, hermano?'
Nori explica que Karazgar se dirigió hacia Zashar-tûmun, pero te advierte que muchos dragones ahora acechan en las ruinas habitadas de Thikil-gundu.
'¡Karazgar debe responder por el mal que ha causado contra el Pueblo de Durin! ¡Baruk Khazâd!'

'¡Con gran pesar, no podemos llevarnos los restos de Frór del Bastión de Acero! ¡Thikil-gundu mismo tendrá que servir como su tumba!
'El Rey bajo la Montaña exigió que regresáramos con un hueso de Vethúg Menteinvernal, pero regresar con la corona de Dáin podría hablar mejor de nuestros logros en las ruinas de Grárik!'
Dori coloca la corona en una mochila y comienza a estudiar nuevamente su mapa de Thikil-gundu.
'Debemos descender al tesoro del saber y continuar hacia las salas del norte. Si seguimos ese camino, llegaremos a Thikil-nesad. ¡Fue una vez el asiento de todo Grárik, y fue allí donde el Rey Dáin I gobernó antes de caer!
'Tal vez Nori se haya escondido antes del viejo trono de Thikil-gundu, pero temo que muchos más enemigos acechen en estas salas.
'Aun así, ¡debemos seguir adelante!'

'¡Dori! ¡No puedo creer lo que ven mis ojos!'
Nori se apresura y abraza a su hermano.
'Todo ha salido mal, hermano. Soy el último de mi expedición. El Guerrero Lloroso nos emboscó ante las puertas de Thikil-gundu y mató a los pocos de mi compañía que sobrevivieron a la Desolación.
'En venganza, me enfrenté a Karazgar en combate. Aunque acerté muchos golpes, ¡logró arrebatarme el hacha de la mano! ¡Es una forma de cobarde de evitar la lucha, creo! ¡Todo lo que tengo ahora es esta antorcha. Me ha mantenido caliente, pero no es un arma!'
Dori le entrega a Nori el hacha que encontraste antes de Thikil-gundu.
'¡Mi hacha! ¡Karazgar conocerá su mordida una vez más!
'Me has encontrado, hermano, y por eso te estoy agradecido... pero no puedo dejar que Karazgar escape de Thikil-gundu! ¡Busquemos nuestra venganza contra Karazgar juntos!'

'Escúchame bien, ${PLAYER}.
'Si estas viejas cartas son de fiar, Durûz-mazal debería encontrarse más allá de estas puertas. Era una gran sala construida en honor a los siete reyes Enanos y, en su centro, se excavó una gran cámara del tesoro. Se la conoció como Immêsh-khalt y contenía toda la riqueza de Grárik en sus profundidades.
'Si mi hermano vino en busca de los tesoros de Thikil-gundu, él y su expedición no habrían tenido que buscar más allá de Immêsh-khalt. ¡Y así es allí donde comenzaremos nuestra búsqueda!
'¡Esperemos que estos viejos engranajes sigan funcionando!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Si os separáis de Dori y la Compañía, podéis llamarlos a vuestro lado usando el Cuerno de Erebor. Además, podéis acceder al mapa de Thikil-gundu pulsando 'M'.</rgb>

'¡Está completamente congelado!
'¿Es esta alguna última ofensa de Vethúg Menteinvernal? Si así es como el gran dragonzuelo frío ha decidido guardar su oro robado, no habrá forma de recuperarlo... hasta que todos los salones del Bastión de Acero sean reclamados. Y muchos aún nos esperan, ${PLAYER}.
'Muchos de estos viejos engranajes están congelados o arruinados, pero debemos encontrar la manera de viajar más profundamente en Thikil-gundu. A menos que mis ojos me engañen, parece que los engranajes de algunos de los salones orientales están intactos. Si podemos llegar al antiguo tesoro de conocimientos de Afhân-binnîn por algún camino, nos permitiría acceder a muchas de las cámaras más profundas de Thikil-gundu. ¡Debemos encontrar la manera de llegar allí!
'Según las notas que Nori dejó, se puede llegar a Afhân-binnîn a través de un pequeño salón en el extremo norte de las forjas de Kall-khebâb.
'¡Encontrémonos un camino hacia Kall-khebâb, y luego veremos si podemos encontrar el camino hacia Afhân-binnîn! Además, creo que nos vendría bien calentarnos junto a las forjas.
'Pero... sería prudente mantenernos alerta. Tal silencio no me da ninguna tranquilidad.'

'Es peor de lo que temía....
'Los muertos recorren los pasillos de Thikil-gundu, y por medios viles, ¡Karazgar ha dominado la voluntad de Vethúg Menteinvernal!
'Hay poco que celebrar en este día, ${PLAYER}, pero hemos encontrado a mi hermano... ¡y eso es suficiente!
'Regresemos a Tharrazhâr y dejemos atrás este lugar doloroso.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Cuando completes esta misión, viajarás rápidamente a la Fortaleza de Tharrazhâr en Skarháld. Si no has terminado de explorar o buscar tesoros en Thikil-gundu, se recomienda esperar para hablar con Dori.</rgb>

'¿Cómo es posible que tantos espíritus malvados hayan sido atraídos a este lugar?
'Dwalin me contó una vez el destino de Skorgrim Duramanmo. ¿Conoces la historia?
'Hablaba mucho de espíritus, de Señores Demacrados, de manos ensangrentadas y de otras cosas de las que yo sabía muy poco, ¡pero tal vez eso era lo mejor! ¡Qué destino tan terrible para un Enano... incluso para uno tan cruel como Skorgrim!
'¿Qué ha pasado? ¿Ha caído una maldición sobre Thikil-gundu? Muchos Enanos han vuelto a la vida para servir al mal que ahora acecha aquí....'
Dori hace una pausa y observa a la compañía de enanos mirando una gran geoda en Afhân-binnîn.
'Espera un momento, ${PLAYER}. Hay algo familiar en ese enano....
'No... ¡no puede ser! Ese es Fror, el hijo perdido de Dain I. Después de que Dain cayera ante Vethug Cœurdhiver, Fror se sacrificó para que sus hermanos y parientes pudieran escapar de Thikil-gundu. No puede ser otro... ¡la corona de Dain I descansa sobre su cabeza!
'¡Debemos desterrar el mal que lo ha poseído!'

'¡Bah! ¿Orcos? ¿Hobotrasgos? ¡Se suponía que este era el camino más rápido hacia Afhân-binnîn!'
Dori estudia su mapa de Thikil-gundu y lo gira varias veces.
'Parece que hay otro camino hacia el tesoro del saber, pero para llegar a él, debemos pasar por la antigua casa de banquetes de Amrâg-zahar. Los engranajes fuera de sus puertas parecían estar congelados cuando me situé sobre la bóveda del tesoro, pero tal vez el calor de las forjas pueda aflojarlos.
'Hasta ahora hemos tenido suerte de encontrar solo unos pocos Orcos, pero temo que Karazgar y los dragones que habitan Thikil-gundu pronto se darán cuenta de nuestra presencia. Es un consuelo que esos espectros enanos no sean aficionados a los dragones, ¡pero tampoco son nuestros amigos!
'Cuanto más rápido encontremos a mi hermano, más rápido podremos abandonar este lugar. ¡Vamos!'
Sientes un viento helado que sopla desde las ruinas habitadas de Thikil-gundu...
¡Pareciendo anticipar vuestra llegada, Karazgar se encuentra bajo una gran grieta en el Cuerno de la Ira!
Después de sellar el pasaje occidental hacia Thikil-nesad, ¡Nori de repente nota a Dori y su compañía!
Para tu horror, un gran drake del frío descansa entre su prole en Thikil-nesad!
¡Athramóth cae derrotado, pero escuchas un gran alboroto a lo lejos!
Los restos de Frór, hijo de Dáin I, caen sin vida al suelo...
Engastada en oro y adornada con precioso mithril, la corona de Dáin no ha perdido su belleza...
La sala que conduce a Afhân-binnîn está sellada por escombros y ruinas...
Entre los restos en ruinas de Amrâg-zahar, un pasaje que conduce a Afhân-binnîn está abierto...
Hace mucho tiempo asesinado por Vethúg Menteinvernal, Frór, hijo de Dáin I, ha resucitado...
¡Las viejas forjas de Thikil-gundu están llenas de orcos!
Karkasht Alimenta Cuervos es derrotado y el calor de las forjas comienza a extenderse por todo Thikil-gundu...
Un increíble tesoro yace atrapado en el hielo bajo vuestros pies...
'¡Ven, ${PLAYER}. Veamos qué ha sido de Immêsh-khalt!'
'¡El salón de Afhân-binnîn debe estar en el extremo norte de las herrerías. Veamos si el camino está despejado!'
'¡Busquemos a Nori en Afhân-binnîn! Si mi hermano no está allí, podremos seguir otros pasajes hacia las cámaras más profundas de Thikil-gundu!'
En los pasillos de Thikil-gundu

Nori podría encontrarse en algún lugar de Afhân-binnîn, que se encuentra a través de Amrâg-zahar.
Habéis descubierto un pasaje hacia Afhân-binnîn y ahora deberíais buscar a Nori en las cámaras del saber de Thikil-gundu.

Frór el Perdido se encuentra en las alturas de Afhân-binnîn.
Has descubierto los restos de Frór, hijo de Dáin I, traído a la vida por un espíritu cruel en Afhân-binnîn. Deberías derrotarlo y permitir que finalmente descanse en paz.

Dori se encuentra en Thikil-gundu.
Has derrotado al espíritu maligno que habitaba los restos de Frór y recuperado la corona de Dáin, perdida hace mucho tiempo. Debes ofrecer la corona a Dori y averiguar qué hacer.

Thikil-nesad, el Trono de Acero, se encuentra en lo profundo de Thikil-gundu.
Temiendo que Nori haya sido descubierto por los habitantes del Bastión de Acero, Dori ahora espera encontrarlo antes que el viejo trono de Thikil-gundu.

Athramóth y su prole se encuentran en Thikil-nesad.
Has descubierto un gran drake del frío descansando entre su prole. Deberías derrotar a Athramóth y asegurar el viejo trono del Bastión de Acero.

Nori se encuentra en Thikil-nesad.
Nori ha huido a Thikil-nesad y se ha reunido inadvertidamente con Dori. Deberíais hablar con Nori.

Dori se encuentra en Thikil-gundu.
Os habéis reunido con Nori. Ahora deberíais hablar con Dori y averiguar qué hacer.

Zashar-tûmun, las ruinas habitadas de Thikil-gundu, se encuentran al oeste de la casa de banquetes de Amrâg-zahar.
Nori te ha advertido que Karazgar ahora prepara una gran fuerza de dragones en Zashar-tûmun. Deberías encontrar un camino hacia Zashar-tûmun y enfrentarte a Karazgar.

Karazgar se encuentra en algún lugar de Zashar-tûmun.
Nori te ha advertido que Karazgar ahora prepara una gran fuerza de dragones en Zashar-tûmun. Deberías encontrar y enfrentarte a Karazgar.

Karazgar se encuentra en las regiones occidentales de Zashar-tûmun.
Has encontrado a Karazgar, el Guerrero Lloroso, y ahora deberías intentar derrotarlo.

Dori se encuentra en Thikil-gundu. Si os habéis separado, podéis llamarle a él y al resto de la compañía usando vuestro cuerno.
Habéis repelido a Karazgar y rescatado a Nori de las profundidades de Thikil-gundu. Ahora deberíais hablar con Dori.

Dori se encuentra en Thikil-gundu. Si os habéis separado, podéis llamarle a él y al resto de la compañía usando vuestro cuerno.
Habéis venido a Thikil-gundu en busca de Nori y ahora deberíais hablar con Dori.

La cámara del tesoro de Immêsh-khalt se encuentra en el centro de Durûz-mazal, la Cámara de los Rostros.
Dori os ha indicado a ti y al resto de la compañía que busquéis en la cámara del tesoro de Immêsh-khalt señales de Nori.

Las forjas de Kall-khebâb se encuentran en los pasillos del este de Thikil-gundu.
Decidido a adentrarse más en Thikil-gundu, Dori te ha pedido que busques las forjas de Kall-khebâb para que puedas encontrar un paso hacia los otros pasillos del Bastión de Acero.

Karkasht Alimenta Cuervos se encuentra en las forjas de Kall-khebâb.
Has descubierto a un enorme hobotrasgo que lidera a los Orcos en las forjas de Kall-khebâb. Debes derrotarlo si quieres continuar más profundamente en Thikil-gundu.

Una sala hacia Afhân-binnîn se encuentra en el extremo norte de las forjas de Kall-khebâb.
Con las forjas libres de enemigos, ahora deberías buscar en ellas un camino hacia el tesoro de conocimientos de Afhân-binnîn.

La sala de banquetes de Amrâg-zahar se encuentra a través de las puertas más al norte de Durûz-mazal, la Cámara de los Rostros.
Ahora que el calor de las forjas se está extendiendo por todo Thikil-gundu, Dori espera encontrar otra forma de llegar a Afhân-binnîn y continuar la búsqueda de Nori.

Completa 'En la Grieta de Hierro'

'¿Otra vez tú, ${CLASS}? No voy a mentir. Ha sido difícil llegar hasta aquí, en las Montañas Grises. Difícil incluso para un pueblo que ha recorrido miles de leguas peligrosas y agotadoras.
'Aun así, los enanos somos gente resistente y no nos dejaremos intimidar. Cuando la situación lo requiere, pedimos ayuda... especialmente a aquellos que demuestran buena voluntad y son dignos de la tarea.
'¿Nos ayudarás en nuestros esfuerzos? ¡Hay mucho, sí mucho por hacer!'

'Ah, siempre hay más por hacer. Dicen que el trabajo de los enanos nunca termina, y eso es tan cierto hoy como lo fue en el pasado. ¡Explora las tierras de los enanos y ve sus trabajos hasta su conclusión! No dudo que más aventuras te esperan en la Grieta de Hierro y Ered Mithrin.'

'It would seem the mines are no longer safe. I will call back all dwarves at once.
'I knew this day would come, though a part of me did not want to believe it. Rukhûsh-minam!'
'Náin sent you? My friend, Easterlings are the least of our worries at Hammerstead. If only I knew what exactly it is that we should be worried about!'

'You have returned, and I see the look upon your face is one that carries dire news. Shadowy nameless things, lurking in the Iron Hills?! What could have caused this?!
'We must scout the mining entrances in Járnfast immediately!'
