'Speak with Grimbeorn and learn if there is aught he requires, ${PLAYER}. I feel a darkness settling upon the vales, and the master of the Beorninghús may know more of it. At any rate he will welcome any attempt to combat it and make safe his land and that of his neighbours.'

'As the Maiden's enchanted slumber fades, perhaps my memories will return to me. That is my fervent hope. I must know what happened, ${PLAYER}. I must know who caused my downfall and the deaths of my men. You must help me discover the truth, where it lies and wherever it leads!'

'Tell me your name, stranger. There is much I do not know, and I hope you will have the answers I seek.
'Shreds of fog cling still to my waking mind. The sleep I endured has not yet freed me from its grasp. The song of the Maiden was a balm for my restless thoughts, a soothing lullaby borne out of love, but that sleep seems now to me a prison, and I want it not! What I desire is recompense for my hurts, but I cannot tell where to aim any such vengeance!
'I remember little from the life I had. Fragments of memory drift like wisps of cloud before my eyes, and are gone. I swore an oath, ${PLAYER}, I remember that. I bore a token, a great weapon of the Enemy, and I vowed to bring it to Rivendell, where it could be protected by the Elves of that hidden haven. I failed in that task, to my shame, for we were set upon by Orcs, and...'
The shade pauses. He lifts his head and looks at you with haunted eyes.
'I was betrayed, ${PLAYER}. The ambush was carried out by Orcs, but they were given succor by one of my own! I cannot see the face of my betrayer, but I feel it with certainty that my company was not waylaid by mistake or misfortune. We were betrayed!
'As the Maiden's enchanted slumber fades, perhaps my memories will return to me. That is my fervent hope. I must know what happened, ${PLAYER}. I must know who caused my downfall and the deaths of my men and my sons. You must help me discover the truth, where it lies and wherever it leads!'

'This adventure has given me much to ponder, ${PLAYER}! It is a wonder to me that Elendil's son remains bound to the Gladden Fields where he fell, though he had been hidden from our sight for so long by the arts of Gultháva, Maid of the Gladden. Let it not be forgotten that he was hidden too from the searching of our enemies. She may not deserve our thanks, but not all that she worked here can be called evil.
'I believe it was the shade of Isildur that Marhairu Winter-hair followed so long ago; I think too that the song of Gultháva is responsible for the Northman's year-long disappearance. Isildur intended to do no harm; it is only my conjecture, but perhaps Isildur convinced the Maiden to release Marhairu? I cannot say with certainty, but it possesses the ring of truth.
'The shade of Isildur spoke of an oath he swore? It must be that vow that keeps him bound here beyond the span of his life, and I would learn more of it. It seems clear to me that there are two shades at work in the Gladden Fields, and unless I miss my mark I deem they are related. Can it be that this second shade, called by the Woodmen Vagári the Wanderer, might have sworn an oath of similar power? My heart tells me that Vagári has some connexion to the betrayal of Isildur, but what it might be I cannot say.
'There are so many questions, ${PLAYER}. As the Maiden's sorcery fades and his memory returns to him, the shade of Isildur may have much to tell us. Once I told you of the Disaster that befell Isildur and his men, as it was understood by the Wise. But now it seems there is more to the tale than we knew! Remain at the ready, my friend. I feel we are nearer than ever to knowing what befell the High King of Gondor following the defeat of Sauron.'

'A darkness has settled upon the Vales of Anduin, ${PLAYER}. Can you not feel it? The Beornings and the Woodmen have made homes for themselves among the hills and the trees; they are not strangers to the press of the shadow, but of late it has become deeper.
'Elrond's household will stay for a time at the Beorninghús before continuing on to Gondor for the wedding of his daughter Arwen. I doubt not that he will welcome any attempt to make safe his land and that of his neighbours.'

'I accept Master Elrond's warning, but it does not dissuade me from wishing to learn more about Vagári the Wanderer, and neither should it discourage you!
'I told you I encountered this shade long ago, and it is true. I walked these lands for many years, watching the trials of Men and Elves and lending my aid whenever I deemed it necessary. It was some time after the Battle of Parth Celebrant and the departure of the Éothéod that I walked by the side of the Anduin, pondering who would now defend the Woodmen against the ravages of the Orcs of the Misty Mountains. Then it was that I saw this very shade.
'I would have let it be, ${PLAYER}, had it not spoken. But it called me by a curious name, a name I had never heard before, and it drew me on. I pursued the shade into the swamp, and even from so great a distance I could feel the intense aura of its hatred. This spirit should not have been, and I knew that in the Éothéod's absence, such a hateful presence would endanger the Woodmen.
'I cast a spell of banishment upon the shade, and it vanished. I believed it had been gone for good, but now it has returned. I know not why.'

'I said the shade reminded me of the tales of Vagári the Wanderer, and it does, save one difference. As it approached I felt an overwhelming sensation of hatred, not just for the Orcs but for all living things, and it spoke without breath. It slew every Orc, chanting in its terrible voice, and I feared it would slay me as well were it to pay me any heed. But I feigned death and it did not notice me. Had it done so this Orc-wound would be the least of my troubles, and you would have only a corpse to bear back to my father!
'The words it spoke were not addressed to me, nor I think to the Orcs, but as it set about dispatching its foes it muttered these words without breath: \qson-of-no-blood,\q it said, \qson-of-no-blood,\q over and over. I am chilled to remember it!
'The tales my people tell of Vagári the Wanderer are different. That shade seemed to pose no ill will toward Marhairu Winterhair, and his account contained no report of such malicious intent or frightening chant. What can it mean, ${PLAYER}? I think my leg is well-enough to carry me home now, but the memory of this encounter will haunt me until the end of my days! Will I become as Marhairu Winterhair did, scorned by my people? But I know what I saw, and I know it is true!'

'I believe I chanced upon this very shade during my travels, long ago, and thought it gone, never to return. I will tell you of that encounter, but first I ask that you go outside and speak with Elrond. I would like to know what he thinks of Badwila's story, for he is counted highly among the Wise and I greatly value his opinion and the reach of his knowledge.'

The Maiden motions at the encircling hills with one slender arm.

'Blómgard was once a place of joy, but lately our spirits have fallen. We have toiled long, but ever our work is hard, and our lives become harder. We call it the Green Sadness, for are we not like the trees that reach for the sunlight but become crowded by the overhanging canopy of our hardships, and fall beneath the shroud of darkness?
'Seek out the folk of the village if you think it be not so.'

'I thank you for seeking to encourage my people, ${PLAYER}, even if the Green Sadness cannot be tamed with mere words. When the woods are made safe for even the children, perhaps then hope will return to our hearts.
'There is no easy solution, but we are a sturdy people and we will face our hardships as we have always done. With your help we may find the way forward.'

The Heart of the Mother

'You have done Blómgard a good service, for the village is defended and we are safe... for now, at least. You say that you have done this in the name of Radagast? Perhaps we will let you and Radagast stay here until this threat is no more.
'My guards have informed me that one of the injured spiders tried to escape, and he tracked the beast. Before it could disappear into the thick of the woods, it turned into some sort of... well, into some sort of man! We captured the wounded beast and have kept it under guard.'
You explain that this creature could be one of the Ungoledain, a group of skin-changers from Mirkwood who worship spiders and hold them to be sacred.
'If you know of these creatures, it seems to me that you are the one to speak with our captive.'

'There is something strange about these spiders, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot put my finger upon what it might be. They are hiding somewhere in Laerlad, I can tell you that, and I can tell you too that we have to help these people! You because you are an adventurer, and me because, well, I owe them that. Let us leave it at that, and speak no more of my faults for now. Oh, it is a worrisome thing to remember!'
Suddenly, you hear shouts from the eastern side of the village.
'They are on the attack again! You must defend the village. Go now, quickly and hastily and with great speed, ${PLAYER}!'

'Lóbruth cares not what some ${RACE} wants. He listens only to Mengris, our Tásakh, and will follow her to death or end of world. Voice in shadows, it tells her where to go. Woodmen are in the way, says Tásakh. Pah! It matters little to Lóbruth. If Mengris says slay you all, then you must die!'

'The Ungoledain, yes, that would explain a great deal... a great deal indeed! It seems I owe the Woodmen for not one failing but for two! Firstly, I abandoned Rhosgobel, leaving the Woodmen to face the harsh blades of war on their own. I had my reasons, of course I did, but looking back on it I question if they were worthwhile enough to leave the Woodmen so unprotected.
'And secondly, well, now they face an enemy of my own creation! Yes, ${PLAYER}, you did not mishear me. I am responsible, in part, for the creation of the Ungoledain. I made them, and though it was not on purpose, I should have known better! Looking back, it could have been so easily avoided!'

'Of course it worked, my friend! You see the waters shimmering? That is the true gift of the waters. It is the gift that will fool hate and spread kindness throughout the forest.'
'What a beautiful song, ${PLAYER}. Yes, I remember it now. The rivers and the streams shall cloud the minds of those who hate, but those who have kindness in their hearts will always find their way.'

'It is just speculation, of course it is. It may be nothing. Let us hope it is nothing!
'But for now, I need to work a magic of protection in order to keep safe my home of Rhosgobel and all of Laerlad while I am away. There is a calm in the woods now; do you hear it? There used to be an old song in these woods, a song that I heard once but have now forgotten. It was sung by all the rivers and streams here in Laerlad, but now it has gone into hiding. If you listen closely enough in the quiet woods you might hear it.
'It was a song of protection, of course it was. I can remember its name, Tauralindalë. If it were to be sung again, perhaps it could keep Laerlad and Rhosgobel well hidden from danger.'

Talk to Evorik
A Stone's Throw

'My folk have built sturdy wooden palisades to protect the village, but I fear it will not be enough. There are some old stone walls along the eastern side of the village. If we were to gather more stones from the forest's edge, we could repair the wall. Would you gather up some field stones for us so we could use them to repair the wall, and safe-guard the people of Blómgard?'

'I thank you for your service to Blómgard. No, do not concern yourself with building the walls! We shall see to it. I would not have you think we needed you to do everything for us! Gathering the stones was enough.
'This old wall was not built by us Woodmen. All I know is that when the wall was once maintained, the forest-demons kept afar.
'With the old wall mended, I see the village safe, and my spirits lift.'

The Ghost of Old Mad Ubb

'Oh my, a ${CLASS}! That is what you are, is it not? My name is Odulf and I need your help! My brother Vulmar says there is a ghost in Blómgard. Not just any old ghost though, no! It is the ghost of Old Mad Ubb! I saw it, I saw it! Well, I saw a barrel or a crate move, I did! Please catch the ghost, ${CLASS}! Please, oh please, will you?'

'Why, look who you found! What good fortune! I have been searching for this little one everywhere. Well, not everywhere, I suppose, for I found him not. Together, perhaps, we searched everywhere!
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I would say my friend here needs to be a little more careful. Indeed, I will say it! You should be more careful where you scamper off to, little one!'
'Why look who you found! I have been searching for this one everywhere. Thank you ${PLAYER}. My friend needs to be a little more careful, I would say.'

'Oh, that Vulmar! I'd wager he caught that squirrel and put it in there to make me think Old Mad Ubb was on the loose! Vulmar is always trying to trick me!'
Odulf starts to cry, but then he wipes his eyes and the sniffles stop.
'Do you know something? I think I have seen that squirrel before. He is friends with that funny man in brown who lives around here. You should bring him the squirrel! He probably misses his friend. I know I would! I wouldn't miss Vulmar, though, not at all! Let him find new friends if he seeks to keep tricking the ones he already has! I think you should scold Vulmar first, and then find the man in brown!'

Talk to Radagast at Rhosgobel

'Do you remember what that Ungoladan warrior Lóbruth said to you? He said his leader was answering a call, and that they were all hearing voices of some kind from the shadows! Did you find this leader at Côs Braen? No, of course you did not.
'Here is my guess, ${PLAYER}, and while it is supposition only, I believe you did not encounter this leader because she was away searching for the source of this mysterious call! After I departed Rhosgobel, when the woods grew too dangerous even for a Wizard, many spiders descended upon Rhosgobel. They took over the old Elf-ruins and turned it into a vile den of spiders. Could something about those spiders be calling the Ungoledain leader to Rhosgobel? Let us return to my home as soon as possible, and find out for ourselves!'
'Quickly now, we must get to Rhosgobel at once!'

'Mam Murgwid, Mam Murgwid. Mam Murgwid?
'This is not a name I have ever heard before. I have learned enough about the Ungoledain to know they refer only to the late Iphantemel as \qMother.\q Their pets are the last of Iphantemel's brood. It seems to me there is nothing left for the Ungoledain here. Mam Murgwid must be something else.
'They travel south, as do all the spiders that left Mirkwood. Could they be answering the same call? Oh dear, ${PLAYER}, this is very bad. Why have I not realized this until now? Their true mother must be calling to them. Not Iphantemel, no, not at all! Shelob calls to them. Shelob!'

Scuttling Through the Narrows

'We always meet in less than ideal circumstances, ${PLAYER}! Have you noticed? I certainly have. Do you know that some folk believe my arrival actually draws these problems with them? Preposterous, I know, but people do think so nevertheless!'

'Yes, I am Odahild, the leader of this village. The tales you have heard of scuttling shadows in the night are true, every word of them, and they have brought a number of adventurers here seeking to learn more.
'They brought this Wizard hither as well. He says you are a friend of his. Perhaps, then, you could kindly ask him to leave? He brings only ill omens with him on this visit!'

'Listen well, ${RACE}. I have heard troubling rumours from the south, and I would share them with you. They may be the falsest of lies, but then again they might be true. I cannot judge, so I leave it to you.
'These tales come from Blómgard, a village to the south, in Laerlad. They speak of shadows in the night and a frightful scuttling sound upon the roofs of the village. Now, I have not spoken with their leader Odahild since the Elves gave these woods to us, but she is not one to speak falsely. There are good men and women in that village, and if we can save them from this creeping danger we should do so! And if these are just tales, well, at least we will know for certain.'

The Stolen Gift

'I am glad you have returned, but Odahild wishes to speak with you first. I cannot blame her, for she has become impatient with us. It seems that speaking in hushed tones and whispers does not cause people to trust you, ${PLAYER}, did you know that?
'Well, tell her what you have accomplished for the people of Blómgard. I trust she will be more satisfied if she is kept up to date with our progress.'

'Once there was a group of Men who respected the land and nature, and saw the beauty of the mountains and the vales between them. I was unlike them, of course, being a Wizard, but I did see some of myself in them. More than a little! I gave them a gift: the gift of skin-changing. I taught them how to use it, and as they practiced the art they became closer to nature, and I was most glad for them. They were a good people, and they remained so to this day: the Beornings of the Vales of Anduin.
'But other Men became jealous of the gift. They captured one of the skin-changers, and tortured him, and in the end he gave away the secret art. These evil ones were driven mad by this new power, a power they were never intended to wield. These were the Gauredain, men of the wolf, and the Ungoledain, men of the spider.
'I should have been more careful, ${PLAYER}. I repented of the gift, for once it was stolen I could do nothing. Now the Woodmen face a peril of my own creation. We must find their encampment and protect them from the leader of the Ungoledain. Mengris Tásakh, did they call it?'

'So this Ungoledan encampment has been destroyed? Good. I felt the air change when you first entered the village, and although I did not know it at the time it truly must have been a good omen. I hope that you have done enough to persuade these beasts to never set foot in our woods again, and if you have not, that you will continue to persuade them until they do!'

'Odahild believes your arrival was a good portent? Ha! Perhaps it was. I am glad she is pleased with our efforts. Now I have some pressing matters to discuss with you concerning my home. I speak of Rhosgobel.'

Talk to Gwaihir the Wind-lord
The Growing Might of Gundabad

'Did you not say we would meet again after we departed in the Wailing Hills? It is pleasing to me that it has turned out to be true.
'But not all is good along the banks of the Anduin, for trouble brews to the north. I speak to you of the fortress called Gundabad, which has become home to many Orcs and winged drakes. It is a refuge of evil, but that evil does not stay there; it roams far afield and is a danger even to these lands.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. I have not forgotten the assistance you provided to me in the Wailing Hills that lay near to the Great River.
'I have seen goblins and many ill-hearted beasts on this side of the Misty Mountains. Some of them creep out of the Goblin-town, but from where the others hail I cannot say with certainty.'

'The several conflicts that embroil the lands hereabout are clear even to those who do not possess the eyes of my kind, ${PLAYER}. Neither the woods nor the mountains are safe, and the people who dwell in the vales between will suffer if nothing is done.
'I cannot overextend my reach or exceed my wingspan in this, ${PLAYER}. But I will keep an ever-watchful eye upon these lands. If I see aught that threatens, I will warn those below of the danger with a call that will echo in the valleys. That way much harm may be avoided.'

'You speak of Grimbeorn, and not out of hand, for you know I hold him in high regard. So too did I respect his sire Beorn. The tale of his great deeds carries on, though he is dead these past few years. His people mourn him, but more than that they protect the lands that were his, and that is memorial enough. He would have thought so too, I deem.
'Now the Beornings have sent you to me, ${RACE}. I will hear your request and perhaps favour this pact, but speak first to Landroval and to Meneldor. They will judge you accordingly.'

'I relent, ${PLAYER}. The time has come to reopen the trade route with the Elves, for evil will soon be driven from the Vales. It is customary to celebrate such an occasion with a feast, and today will not be the exception! You will be welcome at my table, ${RACE}.'
'Come! Let us prepare the feast!'

'Do you think Thranduil is displeased that his son has remained for so long in the Beorning-lands? You and he did spend a considerable time convincing this old man to reopen the trade route, and he has been several days away. Ha! As if an Elf must give any worry to the passage of time! Such displeasure will surely do him some good, and I will not beg his forgiveness for it!
'I do ask you to spend some time assisting my people and the Woodmen in the Vales of Anduin, for as you have proven, the war may be done but the fighting is not yet finished. There are still foes aplenty that wish us harm, and they will need to be dealt with before it will be truly safe along the Great River.
'We will speak again soon, I am sure of it.'

'And yet what is this? No sooner have we made this pact than I see evil on the very horizon! Winged drakes descend from the heights, and it seems they make for the mighty stone that Beorn named of old the Carrock. It was dear to him, and in memory of him I will not permit these drakes to spill innocent blood upon its surface!
'Anórohir, this is my command: take ${PLAYER} upon your wing, and fly to battle with the drakes. There is little time to spare!'

'You and Varthmath have returned in safety, and with a tale to tell. This wretched drake-scale tells an even finer tale, for it says to me that you fought bravely and the Carrock remains unsullied.
'It is good that Gwaihir and the Eagles will keep watch over the Vales, for if they spy out the threats we will be able to deal with them more easily, and together these lands will soon be made safe again.'
'We will bring you to the Carrock immediately. Get ready for flight, and then fight!'

Through the Vale

'Look around you, and tell me what you see. You see peace, and you see safety! It is not easily won, and even less-easily kept! My husband, Grimbeorn, fought many battles to make it so, and he has shown no sign of stopping any day soon. Let the darkness beware!
'I am Gírta, matron of the Beorninghús. My husband and our kin will fight to protect this way of life from each danger that threatens. If you search for such dangers, you will find them nearby.'

'Greetings again, ${PLAYER}. I waited at the Forest Gate until the Elves finally allowed me to pass through, a process that took much longer than I liked! I did not wish to anger my sire, so I did not complain very much to the Elves about their obvious reluctance to open the way.
'I have not left the Beorninghús since I returned. Langhár's stories about the Wolf-denes have filled me up with caution, and I do not plan to venture past the vineyard.'

'I am called Varthmath. I have recently come home after travelling in the Misty Mountains, where my people once lived. Alas for the dwarves and the Orcs, for their wars drove us out and now it is no longer safe to return. A pox on the cursed halls of Moria! So many evils have come out of the darkness of that place that now the mountains are lost to us. I do not know if it will ever be safe to return there.'

'I was shown kindness by the Elves of Felegoth, as I would not have expected. I told Grimbeorn my story of the foes that ambushed me, and of the evil that lurks within the Elf-woods. They say they have cleansed the forest, but I hold that no Beorning should take the risk. It is still \qMirkwood\q to me.'

'The darkness has spread across the mountains into formerly peaceful valleys, and these lands of mine are no exception. Orcs and wargs spy on my people from among the trees. Goblins creep from their holes in greater numbers than ever before. Even the beasts of the wood are angered... not just by strangers, but by me, once their trusted friend and companion!
'Speak to my kin in the vales, and every one of my people will confirm I speak the truth, and that it needs addressing! Once you have spoken to them, journey north to the edge of the Floodfells and find signs of the danger that creeps ever nearer to my home.'

'These trophies are certainly respectable, though they were not in life! Ha!
'They show what I expected them to show: that although the war may be done, its soldiers remain a threat to the Vales of Anduin. The trade route must remain closed, for the safety of my people.'

'I have made my decision. The Elves say they will help us, but only rarely do I see them leave the shelter of the woods, and I hesitate to call on them for aid. The dwarves and Men that live in the north have their own problems, as do we, and neither can be a help to the other while his own lands remain unsecured!
'I have not spent this time idly, ${PLAYER}. No, there is a solution, and it lies on the very edge of my land. On the edge... and upwards! I speak of the Great Eagles' Eyrie. Those noble birds have aided my people before, and they may do so again.
'You are a friend of Gandalf the Wizard, and he is one who has the respect of the Eagles. Speak to Gwaihir the Wind-lord on behalf of my people and request their aid. I will send Varthmath ahead to call upon the Eagles for a meeting.'

'Our paths cross once again, ${RACE}. I saw you once in the Garden of Galadriel, and now you fly high above your station to the very Eyrie of my people. It is most curious to me that you keep turning up, small one.'
'Ah, I believe Grimbeorn awaits us with his reply. Speak to the lord of the Beornings and learn what he has to say. Let us hope it will be good tidings for my father and for the Elves of Felegoth.'

'${PLAYER}, there you are. I have requested a summons. Anórohir has agreed to take only one of us up to the Eyrie. I think it should be you, for you are a friend of Gandalf, and that may help the Great Eagles decide to side with us!

Introduction: Vales of Anduin

King Thranduil requires your assistance in the Vales of Anduin. Thranduil has deemed Eryn Lasgalen safe and has opened the western road from Felegoth to the Vales of Anduin. He wishes for trade to continue between the Elves and Beornings. This was met with resistance from Grimbeorn, the leader of the Beornings, for reasons unknown. King Thranduil requires this dispute to be resolved hastily and diplomatically. The Elves, Men, and dwarves of the north all rely heavily upon trade. The security of the north is at stake.

'${PLAYER}, you have received my father's request. It is good to see you again. Your assistance in this delicate task is most appreciated. Now, it would be unwise for both of us to travel to the Beorninghús to meet with Grimbeorn together. He does not welcome guests and I do not wish for my task to fail. Would you speak with Grimbeorn? I wish to scout Eryn Lasgalen, and make sure roads are truly safe. Come find me again once you have Grimbeorn's answer.'
'Absolutely not. My decision has nothing to do with the King of the Greenleaves and everything to do with my people. However, I permit you to stay for as long as you need. I am not unkind.'

'You have done as I asked? Good, good! I have spoken to Grimbeorn and told him that we have done much to ensure the safety of his traders, should they pass into the woods. He did not respond one way or the other, but I knew better than to press the issue overmuch. Instead, I asked him what you or I could do to assist him here in his own lands. He told me that he would give it some thought and reply soon.
'I think we have made some progress, ${PLAYER}. After all, a refusal could have been given on the spot, and it was not.'

'I know that Thranduil wishes me to reopen the trade route into Mirkwood. I have heard of the hardships faced by the Dwarves of the Lonely Mountain and the refugees from out of the East, but my own family must come first. Go to the Forest Gate and tell the Elves there what I have decided.'

'The lord of the Beornings, like all of his kin, can be quite stubborn when he wants to be. And yet, I believe he can be persuaded if he is shown the need of it. I have a plan, ${PLAYER}, but I will need your help to see it done.
'First, you must defeat some of the threats that remain beneath the canopy in Eryn Lasgalen. Grimbeorn must be shown that the Elves value the safety of his traders. Once you have defeated some of the enemies that threaten peaceful travellers in the woods, meet me at the Beorninghús.'

The Fate of Honey-bell

'I have run into something of a snag with one of my tasks, and I tell you it may be a sign of something much worse! I have been keeping to the safety of the Beorninghús ever since the recent troubles, and feeding the cows seemed enough to keep me here. All of the animals have now been fed, save one, for Honey-bell is gone! Ha. It may be time to save one, indeed.
'Honey-bell may just have wandered off, but if she has, she has gone further than I would like to be searching. Help me find her!'

'Haldis took Honey-bell for a walk? It seems I sent you chasing for wild goose and worried myself for nothing! I am sorry, but the darkness that has settled upon the vales has me all on edge. I shall focus on my next task, which must surely cause me no alarm. How worrisome could mushrooms possibly be?'

'Oh no, that is Honey-bell's bell! Where did you find it? In a warg-den? Tragedy indeed, ${PLAYER}! She was such a good girl, faithful bovine companion, supplier of milk and cheese! We will mourn, not just for the products with which she supplied us but also for her dear loving and sweet demeanour. Poor Honey-bell, to perish in this way!'
Sterkist squints into the distance, looking at the far gate.
'One moment. Is that Haldis I see? And who is that with her?'

'You are a friend of Sterkist? I see that you found Honey-bell's bell! I took her out for a walk in the sunshine earlier today, for she seemed quite agitated about something and I thought a walk might do her some good. Her bell must have fallen off sometime while we were away and I did not notice it was missing until we returned.
'You found her bell in a warg den? I must say I am grateful you found the bell only, with no cow attached, and that Honey-bell was safe with me, and I with her! I am surprised Sterkist did not see us. We must have just missed one another.'

'Ainhard is right. There will be more people in danger if the goblins are left unchecked. We have work to do.'

'Goblins indeed! What did that one drop? Some kind of drawing? Is that supposed to be the Great Goblin?
'I do not know what to make of that drawing, but we should hold on to it for now. Let us return to Ainhard and send him on to Vegbár. It is clearly not safe for him to be out in the wilds by himself.'

'You came back! Are the demons still out there?'
You explain that the attackers were indeed goblins, and that there are still some lurking nearby. You tell Ainhard that he should head to Vegbár where it is safe.
'Ah, yes, that sounds like a good idea. But... I cannot leave with my home in such disarray, and my hounds missing! Will you help me?'

'The poor man is terrified! We should investigate the area and see if it was goblins that came through, or something else. Perhaps we can pick up the trail of... whatever it might have been... as well.'

'Who are you? Are you here to help?'
You quickly explain the situation and ask Ainhard to tell you what happened here.
'I cannot say for sure, it happened in the dead of night! But I can tell you what I saw, and what I heard.
'I was asleep with my hounds, when I was awoken by the sound of many scuffling feet, a horrid chattering of some beastly horde! I quickly looked out the window and saw hundreds of glowing eyes and the glinting of weapons in the moonlight! I am unsure what they were — Orcs, goblins, Taurogrim, but there were so many! I could only hide in my home while they trampled through and destroyed everything in sight.
'What do I do now? Pick up the pieces and carry on? But I am afraid they will come back at any moment!'

'This is where we part ways, ${PLAYER}. I am to rest and heal in Caras Galadhon until I am ready for travel. If all goes well, I will have recovered enough to continue to Minas Tirith with the wedding party.'

'Perhaps you are right. The power of Lady Galadriel herself was required to turn the beast. Lady Arwen's family has done so much for me, so I feel I must do the best I can in my service to them. 'I am glad to have finally met you, ${PLAYER}. We will meet again. Of that, I am sure.'

Baradal seems steady, but you can tell she is upset and attempting to suppress her emotions.
'I can recall little, but I do remember the massive warg attacking us. It dragged me by the leg. I am not sure I can walk or be of much use in a fight. Forgive me, ${PLAYER}, I let my guard down and now we are in grave danger.'

'Yes, I can get you inside. Let me know when you are ready.'

'Good to see you in one piece, ${PLAYER}. How fared your mission into Goblin-town?'
You tell Skalla that you believe you were able to even the odds between the hobgoblins and the Great Goblin. You also saw the hobgoblin warlord, Shárnakh, while you were inside.
'Shárnakh. At least we have a name for our enemy now. If you were successful, and it sounds like you were, the Great Goblin will want to press his advantage while he has it, before more forces from Gundabad arrive.
'Langhár has not yet returned, and was rather mysterious about where she was going. I hope you are ready to face the goblins without her.'

'So, you wish to enter Goblin-town. I overheard your plans. This seems incredibly risky, but I will not stop you. It may be our only path to success.
'I have a scout stationed near the Goblin-gate. She will be able to get you near to where the hobgoblins have holed themselves up. Find her.'

'I am not sure I have ever seen Skalla so concerned. There must be something we can do....'
Langhár trails off, lost in thought. A wry smile suddenly crosses her face.
'I have a crazy idea, ${PLAYER}, but it might just work. So, we have two goblin hosts to deal with, not enough Beornings to deal with either, and in the middle of it all the hobgoblins and the Great Goblin plan to fight it out? If their forces are closely matched, they might just kill each other off, and all we would have to do is mop up the survivors!
'Based on what you saw in Waldfast, I think the Great Goblin is at a disadvantage in numbers. Perhaps we should even the odds?
'I have some ideas for what we can do to pull this off. While you are dealing with things in Goblin-town, I am going to visit some good friends and see if I can get their help. Ask Skalla if he can help get you inside.'

The Woodfolk of Arhaim

'You have helped my people, so I will give you the information you seek. The dwarf ruin the Elf speaks of must be Shathur-munzu. It lies to the west. To find it, you must cross the territory of the Shadow Hunter.
'No one has seen his true form and lived. The few that have returned to us say he is shadow itself, slinking among the trees. They describe huge glinting fangs and glowing eyes, and his children stalk the woods as well, terrible demons all.'
'I understand the Elf's mission, but be warned: you continue at your own peril.'

'Demons, indeed. Superstitions will get us nowhere. Perhaps the dwarf ruin is inhabited by Orcs or the like, but it will not sway me from my charge. Prepare yourself, we will be heading west at once.'
'A dwarf fort? There is one to the west, but you must not go near! The wilds are filled with terrible demons! Many have lost their lives seeking treasures of dwarf-make!'
'Who are you, outsider? Why does that Elf look at me like that? I do not trust you. Go talk to the chieftain if you need something.'
'Don't go into the forest! The Shadow Hunter will steal you away, and you'll never be seen again!'
'I am Garsind, Chieftain of Arhaim. You come seeking information, but we have no reason to trust you. Help the village, and we will help you. That is a fair exchange.'
'Very well, if they require proof of our noble intentions, they shall have it. See if anyone in the village requires our aid. I will do my best to explain to the chieftain why I have come.'

'I was told that Arwen's brothers found Lady Celebrían in a ruined dwarf fort south of the Gladden Fields, and little else. It would be wise to gather more information before we venture into the wilderness in search of it. We should try speaking with the villagers here. They may be willing to share what they know.'

'Oh no... this is the village of Waldfast, and the goblins have completely destroyed it! There are a few goblins out here, but not enough to level the entire village. There must be more goblins hiding somewhere nearby! Hmm, what to do....

'And here we thought the goblins were just getting creative with their raiding! This is a serious situation, ${PLAYER}. This Great Goblin was happy enough to stay in his mountain tunnels and grow fat while his underlings squabbled over scraps, but the hobgoblins are another matter entirely. 'A unified Gundabad and Goblin-town is an immediate threat to the people of the Vales. If we do not act quickly, a flood of goblins will wash over us, and few will survive. We simply do not have the numbers to combat such a massive force.'

'This must be Arhaim. It is quite... primitive compared to the cities of the Eldar. The cities of Men are not all like this, correct? I am afraid I have little frame of reference. Most of my travelling has been between Imladris and Caras Galadhon with Lady Arwen, and not by this road.'
You realize from her words that Baradal might be quite young for an Elf. You describe some of the grander cities of Men, including Minas Tirith and Edoras, that you have visited in your travels.
'I see. I will travel to Minas Tirith myself in the coming days. I am looking forward to it. On to the task at hand. We need to speak to the Woodfolk here if we are to find where Lady Celebrían was taken. Let us hope they are open to speaking with outsiders.'

'Do you hear that, ${PLAYER}? The heavy breathing and scuffling feet of Orcs. I believe they lie in wait on the road just ahead, prepared to waylay any passersby. Unfortunately for them, today we are the ones passing by, and they will learn it to their sorrow! Let us hit them from the side, where they will not expect it.'
She stretches and shakes her arms, warming them up for combat.

'I am here at the behest of Lord Elrond. The wedding party will pass this way soon, and I am to make the way clear for Lady Arwen. 'Before you came to the Vales, their settlement of Hultvís was beset by wargs and goblins come down from the mountains. Its fences were splintered and its houses were singed with goblin-fire, but Hultvís endured. Alas, it proved a costly victory. Many hale men and a few of my kin were slain by the goblins, and now the chieftain of the Woodmen, Ríkmar, fears that he must face this tragedy on his own. He will not, and I have promised him my aid.
'My kin have served as guardians of the Woodmen for many years, and it is a time of great need for Ríkmar's people. With many of his hunters slain, his people grow hungry. Worse still, he lacks the men to defend his people should the fences of Hultvís fall to the goblins. Some days ago I sent one of my kin, Hárskor, to the woods' edge with a waggon of provisions, but he has not returned and he is needed here among us. I can spare no others for this task, and you have proven yourself trustworthy in my eyes. Deliver my message to Hárskor, and aid Ríkmar and his people as best you can.
'Perhaps he has remained in Hultvís for reasons of his own, but it is time he returned home!'

'I must admit, I did not expect Grimbeorn to send an outsider. If he has fulfilled his promise as I hoped, I suppose it is no matter!
'So, where are the provisions?'

The settlement of Hultvís can be found far to the south of the Beorning-lands in Woodsedge.

Nightmare's End

'You did not tell me you were a friend to the Wizard, ${PLAYER}!
'Radagast told me he had come to Hultvís on your behalf, and he knew at once that I was the man he sought. He spoke to me of your adventures together in distant lands, but he also told me what became of the Snatcher... Gollum... the hól-budlan once named Sméagol.
'I learned it was Radagast himself who drove Sméagol from Avabárg, but the creature escaped into the wilds and fled under the mountains for many years. When his power to walk unseen was stolen from him, he returned to the Vales... and that was when he stalked Hultvís once again. Not long after Beorn saved me, his kinsfolk drove the creature from the Vales and Sméagol was too fearful of their wrath to return. Radagast said what was taken from him gnawed at him greater than any hunger, and that he spent the rest of his days in pursuit of what was stolen from him... a simple trinket, Radagast said.
'Although at first I questioned his wisdom and how he could have come to know such things, I came to believe his words. Radagast is a Wizard, after all! His tale has done much to ease my mind, but I am sorry to have sent you on an unnecessary errand all the same. I am even more sorry that I did not trust your words... but you must understand what I have endured. What a sorry creature Sméagol became... he has my pity, but he is undeserving of forgiveness. If he had not perished in flames, I....'
Atta suddenly glances at the stone trinket you hold.
'But... what is that you have there, ${PLAYER}?'
You hand Amelina's trinket to Atta. In disbelief, Atta examines the trinket and runs his fingers along the old inscription. Atta clutches the trinket to his chest and begins to weep.
'Amelina... my dear sister. She was taken so long ago... but after all this time, part of her still lives. I will carry her memory with me always, ${PLAYER}.
'Do not worry for me, ${PLAYER}. You find the Wizard and I will set out to thank Grimbeorn for his father's kindness. After that, well... my sister and I will have much travelling to do.
'I am old in my years, but there is time for me yet!'

A Hunger for Vengeance

'Did you find Hárskor? What of the provisions?'
You inform Ríkmar that Hárskor was waylaid by Orcs on the road to Hultvís, but he escaped his would-be captors. You also explain that while most of the provisions were tainted or spoiled, you did manage to recover a few crates and Grimbeorn will soon know to send more to Hultvís.
'Oh, thank you! Our need is great, but this is more than enough for now, ${PLAYER}. I will see to it that none in Hultvís go hungry tonight!'
Ríkmar shuffles uncomfortably for a moment, but seems to steady himself.
'Ah, but I must admit, those Orcs sound more cunning than most! If we were meant to become their unwitting meals, I'm glad they've been driven out of our lands. Let the skin-changers and Elves see to them, I think!'

'Answer!'
Hárskor is noticeably exhausted, but his stature is no less imposing. You sheathe your weapons and explain that you followed Hárskor's path at the behest of Grimbeorn, and that you encountered a number of Orcs in the woods who had laid traps in the form of the stolen provisions.
'Indeed, there are Orcs in the hills, outsider, and they are an unusually cunning sort. I was waylaid on the road, and before I could overpower them I was rendered unconscious. When I awoke, I realized I had been borne away to a cave in the hills. In the darkness, I spied some of the Orcs feasting upon my horses. Deeper in the cave, I heard others prepare a fire and they shouted and cheered for a feast of Man-flesh. My senses returned, I rose from the ground in anger and changed my skin. All at once, the Orcs seemed to discover that they had not captured one of the Woodmen as they had thought. It was a mistake the survivors will not soon forget!
'Yes, before I fled the caves I slew a few of their number... but I was forced to abandon what remained of the provisions. The Orcs appear to answer to one called Durbkhat, if such nonsense is even a name in their tongue! I think without him these Orcs would not seem so clever!
'Slay him, outsider, and recover what he has stolen from us!'

'So you return, outsider! I feared the Orcs would get the better of you, but I know now why Grimbeorn sent you on this errand.
'I hope these provisions will be enough to keep the people of Hultvís from starvation. Once I return to the lodge, I will tell Grimbeorn what has happened and see that more provisions are sent to Hultvís. And in that time, let Durbkhat think on his cowardice. What he has done will not go unanswered by the line of Beorn!
'Deliver what you have found to Ríkmar, outsider, and offer my apologies to the people of Hultvís.'

'What would father have thought of me? What a fool I had been!
'I was no practised warrior... no hunter of beasts. I was a boy swinging a dagger in the rain!
'The Snatcher twisted and slithered away from me like some sort of demon-serpent. It cackled and sputtered at me, and with a single lunge, it wrest the dagger from my hand. A cruel delight gleamed in the Snatcher's eyes as it flung father's dagger into the Anduin, but there was no time to mourn its loss.
'The Snatcher bared its teeth with a dreadful, rotten grin.'

'I ran and I ran and I ran. I darted behind bushes, leapt over fallen trunks and branches, and cast down anything that might slow the Snatcher's pursuit.
'My throat was raw and my legs burned, but it did not matter. I knew if I gave in, if I dared to grow weary, the Snatcher would kill me. But what if it did? Would I see Amelina again? And what of mother and father? What would one more moment of pain in my life be worth?
'The Snatcher suddenly stopped. For a moment, it stood still as if transfixed by an unseen spirit, but then it began to speak. What a horrible voice it had! It choked between its words, but it seemed to be speaking to someone.
'As I watched it carry on in heated conversation, my breath returned to me. I began to hope that it had forgotten its pursuit.'
Atta falls silent.

'I did not understand. The Snatcher had fled in plain sight, and none in Hultvís pursued it. My father was dead. And for what?
'Sorrow turned to anger, and I ran to the home where my family had once lived. I tore through father's belongings with tears in my eyes, but it was not long before I found his dagger. If revenge was to be taken, I thought, it would have to be by my own hand.'

'I wandered for what seemed like hours. I should have given up, but I didn't.
'My thoughts turned to the family I no longer had. I remembered that father had allowed me to accompany him on a hunt not long before Amelina was taken. A hart was grazing in the lowlands, unaware that father's eyes were upon him. Father drew his bow, and though the creature must have sensed its peril, the arrow was loosed. The hart darted, but father's arrow had flown true. It pierced the hart's hind leg, and the beast stumbled. The hart fled as fast as its hooves could bear it, but father carefully followed its uneven, bloodied tracks.
'By the time we came upon it, the hart had collapsed in pain. Father slew it that its suffering might be ended, but as my thoughts returned to that dreary night, I felt no such duty.'

'I thought I was dead.'
'When I opened my eyes, I saw the skin-changer, Beorn, standing above me. It was a trick of the mind, some dying fantasy, I thought. But it wasn't.
'Beorn lifted me from the ground and held me in his arms. He tore some cloth from his own breast, wrapped me in it, and he delivered me to Hultvís.
'Without a word, Beorn left. I never saw him again.'

'It was very long ago, ${PLAYER}.
'The Snatcher had vanished for hundreds of years, and my people had abandoned their vigil. I was a boy then... only days past the start of my eighth year. My sister, Amelina, was nigh to her fourth, but her birth had taken our mother. If only it had ended there....
'One night, I woke to a great clattering. The shutters were open, and Amelina was gone. Muddied footprints had been left in Amelina's bed, but no other sign of her remained. After that day, my father rarely spoke. In the mornings, he rose with the sun to search for Amelina, and when darkness fell, he would stand watch at the gates of Hultvís.
'And so it continued. Until one night not one month later....'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, and don't you worry about us! Vilibald and I can bear it the rest of the way.
'Tell the chieftain that we'll be back to Hultvís in no time!'

'What was keeping the woodsmen of Tríubad, ${PLAYER}? Did they meet with some trouble?'
You tell Ríkmar of the Thyrsir, known to you and the Elves of Eryn Lasgalen as the Taurogrim, and of the misadventure that befell the woodsmen before you aided them. You explain that Clothar and Vilibald will soon deliver a number of hides and planks of lumber to Hultvís.
'While I am concerned that the wood-demons have returned to the forest, I'm pleased that Hultvís will soon be better defended. When Clothar and Vilibald return, I will set my people to the task of repairing the fences and other damage the Orcs caused during the war.
'You are a brave ${CLASS}, and we are fortunate to have you here with us in Hultvís... if only for a time.'

'I do not know you, traveller, but you would be wise to turn back. The Thyrsir... they have returned!'
You note Clothar's concern, and you then ask about the nature of the Thyrsir.
'They were wood-demons of legend, or so I thought! It is said the Elves long ago drove them from the forest, but how have they now come to be here in the vales? A shadow must still dwell in the forest! My cousin, Vilibald, and I only narrowly escaped the Thyrsir at Tríubad, but now... we have few hides and even less lumber left to bring to the chieftain.'
Clothar pauses and lets out a deep sigh.
'A great tree-demon followed in the wake of the Thyrsir, and though I tried to hew it, it wandered away with my axe still embedded in its trunk! That is the axe of my father and of my father's father, and now I have failed them and it is kept by a demon!
'But... if you do not fear the Thyrsir as we do, perhaps you could reclaim what was lost at Tríubad! Would you do this for me?'

'Ah! I did not expect to see you so soon, ${PLAYER}. I thought I might find you among the Woodmen of Hultvís, but instead, you have found me!
'What errand brings you to this place?'
You explain that a Woodman named Atta was hunted by a creature called Úbil the Snatcher in his youth. You also explain that he has been fearful of leaving Hultvís for many years because he presumes that the creature still lives. Radagast sighs.
'Yes, that name is known to me. It is the name the Woodmen gave to Gollum. You supposed as much, did you not? I had hoped he was forgotten to them.
'After I heard the tales of the Woodmen, I grew suspicious and, as I feared, I found Gollum in Avabárg. He did not look as he did when you chanced upon him not long ago, but it was him. Perhaps if I had better understood the tales of the Woodmen, I would have realized how he came to sneak into their villages without being seen. The Ring was far from my first suspicion, and it now seems foolish to think it might have been anything else. Even so, I placed warding spells upon Avabárg, and Gollum was forced to abandon it. He fled under the mountains, and I thought he would not trouble the Woodmen again. Gollum must have returned to the vales after the Ring was lost to him, but I heard that he was soon driven out by Beorn and his kin. Alas, not soon enough.
'In that time, I believe this cavern became Gollum's home. I have placed a warding spell upon it, but I think it will still be many years before the birds and beasts of the vales will draw near to it again.
'Perhaps something belonging to the Woodmen has been left behind within... but do not remain here long, ${PLAYER}. There is a foul air to this place.
'There is much to discuss when we meet again, but let us not speak of it now.'

'Perhaps I misjudged you, ${PLAYER}.'
Atta shuffles uncomfortably.
'It is difficult for me to speak of it, but if you wish to hear the tale of the night I met... Úbil, I will tell you.'

'You have done much for the people of Hultvís, ${PLAYER}, but I would ask one last thing of you.
'The eldest of our people, Atta, claims that he encountered some sort of demon in his youth. Ever since, he has refused to leave Hultvís, but none of us have ever seen the creature! And how could we? He claims the creature can move unseen!
'Many look upon him with pity, but some of my people have been needlessly cruel to him. I do not know what to believe! When the forest was still Mirkwood, I spied many evil things beneath its eaves and I have been told that demons dwell among the reeds of the Rushgore... but the creature Atta has described is unlike any of them. It's as if he believes that Old Mad Ubb is real! Whatever the truth of his memories may be, it has brought him great pain.
'He has grown wary of his own people over the years, and I do not blame him. Perhaps one as well-travelled and learned as you might convince Atta to speak of the demon.
'Will you speak to him, ${PLAYER}?'

'You've set the traps, have you?
Atta's eyes narrow.
'Indeed, I hunt a creature called... the Snatcher.
'The Snatcher was here long before I was born, and it has never left! It has eluded my people for many years, but still it watches... waiting for me to grow too comfortable in my old age.
'But I will not let it take me like the others!'

Atta can be found in Hultvís.
Ríkmar has told you to speak to a Woodman named Atta, the eldest man in Hultvís, who has refused to leave the settlement since the days of his youth.
Talk to Atta
Talk to Atta and complete 'Skulking the Wood'

'Yes?'
You tell Atta that Ríkmar sent you to speak to him about the demon he claims haunts the Vales of Anduin.
'I'm sure he did. Someone comes along who might convince old, mad Atta that it's only a legend? No... I don't think so.'
Atta lets out a gruff chuckle.
'My people fear things they don't understand. There are no demons in this world, no creatures of the mind... not in the way my people think of them! And what I fear is no demon... it is something much worse!'
Atta raises an eyebrow.
'Don't you have anything to say for yourself? Fine... then listen!'

Atta can be found in Hultvís.

Anduin's Bounty

'${PLAYER}! Where you travel, good fortune seems to follow. Will you hear my plight?
'Long have I cast my nets into Anduin, but never has its bounty been so meagre. It seems to me an omen... but of what?
'Will you go down to the banks of the Great River and gather fish from my nets? If Anduin is generous to you, perhaps my concerns were for naught.'

'Well? What did you find?'
You show Germund the fish you gathered from his nets.
'Hah, 'twas just a bad day of fishing, I think! I'm sorry to have tasked you with such a small matter, ${PLAYER}, but I deem it most worthwhile, for it eased my mind considerably! I'll see to it myself at dawn on the morrow.'

Blood of the North-men

'Ah, let's see what you have gathered!'
Germund takes the handfuls of beckberries from you and sets them into a small, woven basket. He takes one of the berries and bites into it. A pale, pink juice runs down his chin as he grins.
'These ought to do the trick! I will distill them into a tincture of my own recipe, and I will see that all in need drink of its extract!
'The North-men may have abandoned the vales long ago, but what a great gift they have left for us!'

'All is not well in Hultvís, ${PLAYER}.
'There is talk of Orcs in the hills and disease has come to the woods' edge. You see, the men who labour at Tríubad have come down with some awful cough, and many others of my folk still suffer injuries from the war.
'Although I wish to help them, I cannot do better than offer them fish! And trust me, none with a broken limb or gouged eye clamour for a fish to heal their ills!
'If I had some beckberries, though, I think I could do some real good for them. I have only known beckberries to grow upon Avabárg for they were tended by the North-men of old. And those who drank of their extract could endure great hardship and even the Plague! Indeed, it is said that beckberries run with the very blood of the North-men. And hale Men they were!
'Such a berry might offer my people a resistance to disease and harden their wills... and their bones, I hope! Will you go to Avabárg and see if you can find any beckberries for my people?'

From the Ashes

'Did you find anything, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Madelgard that you found the remains of a strongbox, but that its contents had been plundered. You also mention the curious tracks you discovered in Málvang.
'Alas! I suppose it was a fool's hope to think mere trinkets would survive the burning of Málvang. Although your search did not prove fruitful, you have my thanks. I am curious, though. Who or what do you think left those little tracks?'
You suggest that small goblins or a hobbit could have made tracks of that size.
'A hobbit? One alike in stature to the hól-budlan? Our tales speak of a time when a great number of the hól-budlan, or hole-builders, dwelt in tunnels carved into the foothills around the Gladden Fields. But that was long ago! Not even one of the hól-budlan has been sighted for many years, and it is thought among my people that they have left the vales never to return.
'Even if they had, who would believe me? Madelgard Twice-fool, they will call me! You are kind to indulge such questions, ${PLAYER}, but do not let me keep you from your adventures.'

'Are you the one called ${PLAYER}?
'I have heard tales of your adventures in the vales, but tell me, have you passed near to Málvang yet?
'Until recent days it was a farmers' village, but the Orcs came upon it in the night and set it aflame in some cruel sort of amusement as they travelled north on the road to Hultvís. My family was fortunate enough to survive, but others... were lost in the fires. Ríkmar told me the few remains of our kinsfolk that were found in Málvang had been given to their families for burial, but all else was lost.
'I have no reason to doubt the words of my chieftain, but I do not wish to believe it so! Couldn't some memory still linger in the ruins?
'Would you travel to the ruins of Málvang, ${PLAYER}? Search for anything that remains intact that I might return it to its keeper or honour its memory myself!'
A small, singed strongbox lies in the corner of this burned dwelling...
The old lock has been broken apart and the strongbox's contents have been plundered...
Brushwood has begun to overtake the charred remains of this dwelling, leaving little else behind...

'Will you lend me your ear, ${PLAYER}?
'I have suffered in silence since the ending of the War, but I cannot bear it any longer. My husband Beremud fell at Avabárg in the final days of the War. We had pushed our foes from the walls of Hultvís to the islet, and victory seemed certain... until Drokstaz came. Before either of us could loose an arrow at him, that terrible warg leapt forth and tore into Beremud's throat. With his last strength, my husband slashed Drokstaz's flank and loosed his entrails. The beast withdrew into the catacombs of Avabárg to die... or so I thought.
'But I have seen his eyes glowing in the night. They stare at me from across the waters of Anduin... from Avabárg. You must believe me! I promised Beremud that I would avenge him, but I cannot go back to that place... I cannot face that creature again, and Drokstaz knows my shame, and taunts me with it.
'I beg you, ${PLAYER}. Slay Drokstaz and put out those terrible eyes!'

Kindling to Wildfire

With the Taurogrim defeated and their twisted forms burned, the familiar crackling of firewood echoes through Tríubad. Although you suspect that the Taurogrim will soon return, you have done well to aid the Woodmen.

'Perhaps Tríubad is lost, but the wood-demons cannot come to Hultvís! They must be stopped, and I believe I know how it can be achieved!
'It was said in tales of old that the Thyrsir could not truly be slain. If one of the wood-demons fell to the axe, its mouldering remains would give rise to more of its kind. Only when they were put to flame could their evil be ended. Demons they may be, but they are demons wrought of wood, and that means they must fear fire!
'If you are to overcome the wood-demons, you must swiftly burn their remains after defeating them. For each of our sakes, let us hope the tale spoke true!'

'In mere days, all of our livestock was taken by some cruel sickness. Some believe the forest has become angry with us, but I say it is the work of the wood-demons. I have heard enough of the tales of the Thyrsir to know that their sap runs with blight!

'Hultvís was fortunate enough to endure the Orcs of the mountains, but many of our eldest hunters fell in battle before the War was ended. Those that remain hunt the beasts at the woods' edge, but your aid would be most welcome! If it is not too much trouble, I would ask that you gather meat from the boars at Málvang. 'I know this may seem a trivial task to you, but Hultvís must be prepared if the Orcs return.'

Spirits of the Taken

'The creature does not age as Men do, ${PLAYER}. As many of my ancestors grew old and died, it only grew more gaunt and wicked.
'Avabárg remains a place of great sorrow, and I'm grateful you have put the spirits of my ancestors to rest.'
Atta appears overcome with emotion.
'May they never be forgotten!'

Spirits can be found in Avabárg.
Atta has asked you to travel to Avabárg and put to rest the spirits of the unfortunate Woodmen that were taken by a terrible creature long ago.
Put spirits to rest in Avabárg (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Before the creature came to dwell at the woods' edge, it first made its home in the ruins of Avabárg. It was long after the North-men abandoned the old keep, but long ago just the same. Yea, long before even my grandfather was born....
'In the depths of Avabárg, the creature hid from the only thing it feared: the light. But in the dark of the night, it would creep forth. On some nights, the creature would merely sit atop the walls of Avabárg and peer across the river with its unblinking eyes. On others, it would sneak across the Anduin and... through some devilry, it would conceal itself from sight as it drew near to our villages. My people were taken from their homes... from their beds... and always the trail led to Avabárg. When my ancestors found gnawed bones in the depths of Avabárg, they could no longer deny what we feared. Our people were not only taken... they were devoured.
'I do not know what changed the mind of the creature, but it came to fear Avabárg and so it abandoned the islet. Yet its foul deeds are not forgotten to the stones of that old keep! The spirits of those who met their ends in Avabárg still linger... and they cannot rest.
'Please, ${PLAYER}, help them to find peace!'

Into the Gladdenmere

'${PLAYER}, dear friend, you have done much to help my home and those in my care among the Vales of Anduin. I need your help once more! Something seeps into the soil from the lake of Gladdenmere, and although I cannot tell what may be the cause, I can feel a deadly darkness all about it. The ruin of an old dwarf mine rests along the side of the lake, abandoned now for almost an age.
'The Beorning Varthmath knows a fair amount about dwarf-made structures, and of course my old friend and ally Gandalf is sure to have an opinion on the subject... more than one, I daresay! Look for him at the Beorninghús. After you have sought out the both of them, meet me in the Gladden Fields. Very well? Very well!'

'The Gladdenmere, you say? I thought the path to that vale was blocked by a rock slide, and we were better off for it; it is not a welcoming place. The old dwarf mine of Kidzul-kâlah stands there, they say, long-abandoned. Meet me on the mountain path that leads toward Kidzul-kâlah when you are able. There is an old dwarf-dock there where we can meet.'
'Radagast has been quite busy lately, assisting both Elves and Woodmen with their various troubles in Eryn Lasgalen and in the Vales. I will speak with him at once, if you say he wishes it.'

Radagast has travelled to the Woodmen village of Hultvís and seeks your assistance with strange shadows that have appeared along the River Gladden. Many Woodmen have noticed an eerie gloom near the entrance to the Gladdenmere. They came to Radagast seeking answers, and you should speak with him in Hultvís as soon as you are able.

'Do not bear the weight of it yourself, Radagast. Saruman deceived us all. I had hoped I could steer him from that path, but alas! It proved not to be.
'${PLAYER}, I charge you with the investigation of the Gladdenmere. I will stay here and converse with my friend Radagast, for there is much about which we must speak.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! The path here was freed of the stones that blocked it, but now shades and strange shadows descend upon the valley! The Elves I met on my travels here wish to assist us. Very few have ever ventured to the old dwarf mine of Kidzul-kâlah. I say we learn all that we can of this place, and then return with our report for Grimbeorn.'

'Gandalf, we have both seen that shades walk in the fields, but that is not the reason I called you here.
'I am sorry for what I have done! I was a fool to trust Saruman. Look at the destruction he has caused, and indeed I am partly responsible for the damage his machines have caused here in the Gladden Fields! And the trap into which you walked, all unawares... it was I that sent you into it! Will you ever forgive me for that, my old friend?
'I wish to right these wrongs, Gandalf. And I will begin here in the Vales of Anduin!'
The two wizards embrace and are soon deep in conversation

'It is kind of the Elves to assist us in learning more about the troubles that plague the Gladdenmere. I have conversed with our new companions and they agree we should investigate the ruins of Kidzul-kâlah. We will explore and observe the old dwarf mine, and return in safety. Do you agree?'

'What have you to report, ${PLAYER}? I see, this is all very strange. The waters flow with curious currents, and the dead keep close to those waters? I have not encountered anything like that before! Kidzul-kâlah was once part of Moria, yes? I believe it, for walking in that place caused me no end of unease, and so it is here! The bridge was destroyed recently, you say? Hmm.
'We will need to stay here longer if we are to learn more. Perhaps the Elves will lend us a boat with which we can cross the Gladdenmere.'

'You found these on the corpses of Orcs? It would seem the giants of the Misty Mountains have done some good for once! How odd to think that such an out-of-the-way place, no more than wilderness, really, might become home to so many ancient artifacts!
'I do not know what is important and what is not. How could I? But perhaps I will take these relics to the Elves. They are sure to know what to do with them.'

These Orcs must have worked the dredging machines of the Gladden Fields until curiosity or greed led them to stray from their tasks and up the River Gladden, towards the halls of Kidzul-kâlah. 'Look upon the hills across the Gladdenmere. I swear to you: I saw them move! Do you suppose it was the stone-giants who dwell there? Could it be they blocked the path to the Gladdenmere? Perhaps it was an errant rock-toss that cleared the path they once impeded! We should investigate the other side of the Gladdenmere and learn more. I have no quarrels with stone-giants but they are not known to be friendly. The Elves have provided a boat when you are ready to cross the water.'

'Then I was right when I guessed the stone-giant presence on the far side of the Gladdenmere! It appears the spirits of the dead intruded upon the domain of the stone-giants, and in turn the giants destroyed the bridge in order to keep them away. No wonder the stone-giants that you encountered were so frenzied! I shall return to Grimbeorn at once and relay to him what we learned here. Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}.'

The Fate of the Gladden Fields

Radagast can be found in the Gladden Fields.
After learning of several concerning matters, Radagast has asked you to meet him in the Gladden Fields.

'Ah, yes! The reason I've come to find you, ${PLAYER}....'
Radagast produces a small diary from his robes. He opens it, and you notice that most of the pages have been torn out. Appearing unconcerned by this, Radagast continues.
'Yes, yes! I have written it all down. It's just not here is all. You would do the same if you lost your writing to a bunch of Orcs! But I digress... I have heard a number of troubling tales about what has happened to the Gladden Fields in my absence.
'You have been of great aid to me in the past, ${PLAYER}, so I would ask that you ride far to the south and meet me on the eastern banks of the Anduin.
'Let us hope whatever hurts have been done to the Gladden Fields might still be mended.'

'I am glad you have come, ${PLAYER}.
'It has been too long since last I looked upon the Gladden Fields, but seeing them in such a state weighs heavily on my heart.'
Concerned by new threats and unfamiliar names come to the Vales of Anduin, Radagast has enlisted your aid to help mend the hurts done to the Gladden Fields.
Radagast gazes solemnly into the distance

Traitors to the Wilderfolk

'Tautila ought to keep his mouth shut. I told Sharkey we should've killed him!
'As for you, well... Sharkey wouldn't be too happy if he found out folks were poking their noses about in the warrens.'

'Do not speak to me as if you know my troubles... Sharkey looks after us better than that old fool Ríkmar ever did.
'And he'll pay a fine price for your head, too!'

'Sharkey told us that the swamp held treasures each worth more than a kingdom, but we have toiled for weeks and found nothing.
'Ah, but that weapon of yours looks worth a fair share of gold. Give it to me!'

'I had hoped some of them might realize their folly, but I had no such hope for Hathus.
'Like many of my kinsmen, he lost a great deal in the war, but he couldn't resist the chance to change his fortunes. We were all desperate, but to have fallen so low as to side with Sharkey? Unthinkable!
'Sharkey is no more than a demon in the skin of a Man. I only wish the others had seen that!'
Desperate to gain the riches Sharkey promised, Hoderna falls defeated!
Hathus could not be turned from his loyalty to Sharkey
Vulfila flees in fear!
This Woodman seems to have drowned when part of the tunnel collapsed
This Woodman appears to have been slain by Sharkey's Men, likely for cowardice or theft

'Listen to me....'
The imprisoned Woodman gestures for you to approach and begins to whisper.
'My name is Tautila. I was raised in Hultvís, but it has been many years since I last dwelt there. You see, I am a travelling merchant and something of a scholar among my people... or at least I was until those demons and ruffians ambushed me on the road!
'When they brought me to Sharkey's encampment, I understood why I was taken. I learned then that a few of my kinsmen had willingly joined Sharkey, and they knew I was well-learned in the tales of the hól-budlan. Sharkey told me to guide him to the old tunnels or he would slay me where I stood. I did as I was told. What choice did I have?
'But the others... they had a choice! They have abandoned the old ways for greed, and they will never again be welcome among the Woodmen. Not if I have any say in it!
'When I was taken, I saw five of them. Find them and defeat them before they can sway more of my people into the service of Sharkey!'

A Thunder of Drums

The bunting appears to have awaited your return. It points its beak at its leg, and you realize it intends to return to Radagast with the scroll.
You turn over the scroll and begin to write on the side Radagast left blank. You tell Radagast of victory over the Shapag-hai in the Vales of Anduin. However, you mention that the Orcs once loyal to Mazog now seek vengeance against the dwarves who escaped the downfall of the Iron Garrison. Whether they resurface in days soon to come or many years from now, the battle for Moria is not yet ended and a vigil must be kept.
You roll the scroll and bind it to the bunting's leg. It chirps in what you take to be a friendly farewell and flies off.

Lúlstrok can be found in the north-western reaches of the Gladden Fields.
A bunting has delivered a message on Radagast's behalf asking you to investigate and drive out the Orkish presence in the Gladden Fields.
Investigate Lúlstrok
Sabotage siege-tower wheels in Lúlstrok (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

As you stand and curiously look at the bunting, it lowers its beak to point at a small scroll bound to its leg. You take the scroll and begin to read it.
The scroll contains hasty writing which you swiftly identify as the writing of Radagast the Brown. As you read on, Radagast explains that a company of Orcs who survived the end of the War has now made camp at a place they call Lúlstrok in the Gladden Fields. Radagast's writing continues and he describes how until a few days ago the Orcs had apparently often feuded with the Men and half-orcs in the centre of the Gladden Fields, but they did not seem to pose a serious threat to the Wilderfolk. However, Radagast now fears they have been stirred by the words of a large Orc among their number and as a consequence, they have grown more bold in recent days. Troubled by the harm their siege engines might inflict on the Gladden Fields and concerned that the Orcs might soon attack the Beornings and Woodmen, Radagast concludes by asking you to drive off the Orcs and damage their siege engines beyond repair.
As the bunting remains perched nearby, you decide to investigate Lúlstrok.

Siege-towers can be found in Lúlstrok.
Aware that the Shapag-hai have siege-towers for some as of yet known purpose, you have been advised to sabotage the Orcs' siege-towers and keep them from inflicting more harm on the Gladden Fields.

The leader of the Shapag-hai can be found somewhere in Lúlstrok.

The bunting can be found near Lúlstrok in the Gladden Fields.
You have done much to repel the Shapag-hai in the Gladden Fields, and you should now return to the bunting and send it to inform Radagast that you have drive out the Orkish presence in the Gladden Fields.
Unmistakably held by the remnants of the Shapag-hai in the Vales, Lúlstrok is heavily-fortified
A tribe of Orcs known as the Shapag-hai has invaded the Gladden Fields, polluting its marshlands and threatening the inhabitants of the Vales of Anduin.
Saruman's Folly

'Ah, good! I am glad you've returned, ${PLAYER}. You have been a great help to me!
'My sparrow delivered the water sample you gathered to me, my bunting told me of your victory over the Orcs, but my thrush lost sight of you. I'd begun to worry that Sharkey proved a more formidable foe than I'd been led to believe! Is Sharkey defeated?'
You explain to Radagast that the leader of the ruffians in the Gladden Fields was an old half-orc named Garmog, who impersonated Sharkey in an attempt to amass a small fortune from the lost relics of the Gladden Fields.
'A half-orc? I had heard he was a Man, but now it seems that neither is true. Who is Sharkey?'
You tell Radagast that Saruman is Sharkey. Radagast falls silent for a long while.
'Gandalf told me that the Onodrim have imprisoned Saruman in Orthanc. Is that not so?
'When there is time at last, I will ride to Orthanc and question him myself!'

Radagast can be found in Hultvís.
You have discovered Sharkey's identity and made safe the Gladden Fields. You should return to Radagast in Hultvís.
Talk to Radagast in Hultvís

'I owe you my life, ${PLAYER}.
'I'll make for Blómgard with the goods that Sharkey - er, Garmog - and his demons stole and see if they don't belong to any of my kinsfolk there. I suppose I'll have to build a new waggon, but I can look after myself now.'
Tautila turns to leave, but quickly turns back.
'Don't you worry about me. You should get back to Hultvís and tell Radagast all about Sharkey!'
You have repelled the half-orcs and ruffians in the Gladden Fields, but it is your discovery of Sharkey's true identity that will be of greatest interest to Radagast.

Friends Far Afield
You notice a thrush! Perhaps this is one of Radagast's friends?
You notice a bunting! Perhaps this is one of Radagast's friends?
You notice a sparrow! Perhaps this is one of Radagast's friends?

'I was a fool, ${PLAYER}.
'When I discovered Orcs dredging the Gladden Fields many years ago, I sought counsel with the greatest of my order: Saruman the White. Saruman learned that Sauron believed the One Ring came to rest in the Gladden Fields, but he knew not where it had fallen. Surmising that the Orcs of Mordor were sent by Sauron, I offered great birds and beasts to Saruman to keep watch on the field and hinder Sauron's forces. I thought I had done what was right.
'In time, my birds and beasts abandoned me, and I began to grow suspicious. I told Gandalf of what had happened, but when Saruman soon allowed the White Council to confront the Necromancer, I had no reason to doubt his judgment. Once the Necromancer was cast out of Dol Guldur, I returned to the Gladden Fields to find that all of the Orcs had vanished, leaving only debris and their dredging machines behind. I travelled home, believing that Sauron's search had failed, but soon the Orcs of Mordor attacked and I was forced to abandon Rhosgobel. And so I wandered for many years....'
Radagast's kindly demeanour hardens.
'Far too late I realized Saruman's treachery, and I am ashamed to have been a tool of his deception. After Gwaihir returned from Orthanc, I learned the truth and Saruman's betrayal was at last undeniable. It was he who dredged the Gladden Fields, he who allowed Sauron's search to continue unhindered, he who desired the One Ring for himself, he who sent the Orcs to Rhosgobel, he who imprisoned Gandalf, and he who would betray any and all of our order to possess power of his own!'
Radagast appears to steady himself.
'What Saruman inflicted upon the Gladden Fields never truly healed, but I have sent my friends deeper into the marshland. I have given them instructions to guide you in investigating the Gladden Fields. Suffice it to say, Orcs are the least of our troubles. There is rumour of an upstart ruffian-lord in the marshes and I myself have discovered a strange blight taking hold of the flora and fauna in the Gladden Fields. Alas, I do not have time to see to all of these tasks, but they are all of great importance! I simply cannot be everywhere!
'It is a strange thing to be needed in so many places at once! Is this how Gandalf must feel? Seek out my friends in the Gladden Fields and aid them if you can. I must return to Hultvís at once!'

Radagast's friends can be found near to Lúlstrok, Sharkey's Slough, and the Gladden Falls.
Radagast has sent three of his friends into the Gladden Fields, and he has asked you to find them and aid them as best you can.
