'Is this a trophy from the dwarves? Why do they not present it to me themselves? I suspect they are a lazy bunch!
'Grr, I am not impressed, and yet it does not matter if I am or not! They should not be trying to impress me, for it is Grimbeorn whose approval they need, and that is an even greater challenge! Only Grimbeorn can make a pact for all Beornings to abide by. There is none other, so do not waste your time on me, ${CLASS}.'

'${PLAYER}, it is good to see you well. It was not long after you left Skarháld that Náth here and some others travelled from Erebor to assist us. Alas, our efforts took a turn for the worse. Some blamed a lack of leadership. Others were blamed for a failure to work together. I believe it was Gundabad that caught us off our guard.
'Skarháld is still well-defended, but for how much longer? The raiding parties from out of Gundabad are emboldened, and their numbers grow stronger with each passing day. What leadership there was at Skarháld sent emissaries from each clan to entreat the Beornings for assistance. We decided first to seek out the Beornings in the Thornholt at Skoghús. I am glad we got there when we did, or they would have all been slaughtered by an approaching warband!
'That was when we realized these Beornings have had no contact with the Vales in years. We offered to escort them to safety as a gesture of goodwill towards their people. Only hardship was found on our journey here. The path may never be clear of the evil that dwells in those woods!
'Now we await word from Grimbeorn. I hope he and the Beornings will aid us.
'Hmm, perhaps there is something we can do. I have heard that Beornings like good trophies as gifts, accepting them as a show of respect and goodwill. Yes, some Warg pelts would do, would they not? Would you mind gathering some Warg pelts for us? We are still resting from our arduous journey.'

'Well, I am out of ideas! I suppose we should just assist the Beornings as best we can, and wait here for Grimbeorn's reply. I do not like waiting. It makes me quite restless. Unless.... Hmm, I may have an idea, everyone!'

'The arrival of the Éothéod at the Field of Celebrant helped win the day and defeat the hosts of the East, saving the South-kingdom from ruin. As thanks for their aid, Cirion granted to the Éothéod the lands that Lord Cendric had spoken of, and which Eorl’s ancestors had desired since the fall of Wilderland. These were the green fields of Calenardhon, now all but emptied as the Dúnedain’s numbers dwindled. Swearing an oath of fealty forever to Gondor, Eorl accepted Cirion’s offer and sent riders to summon the rest of his people to join him in his new realm. Henceforth, the Éothéod, now known as the Eorlingas, would dwell in the Riddermark of Rohan, and Eorl and his descendants would be its kings.
'Let us return to Hlithseld, ${PLAYER}. It has been a long day.'

'There, I have traced the history of my people as best I could. I have filled in the gaps from the Ai-thúda to the Éothéod, and their journey to Rohan. I could not have done it alone. I thank you for your assistance, many times over!
'You are free to leave me here if you must. Yes, I have writing to do, and there is not a better place to write all this down than near the ruins of Framsburg. There are gaps yet to fill in the tale, this much I can see.
'I am still puzzled by many of the old tales and songs. What about the worm, Scatha, that Fram fought? Fram's deeds will need uncovering! The dwarves in the mountains must have played their part in history of the Éothéod too, yes? Hmm, I have much to think about. Perhaps I will call upon you again soon. Until then, my friend!'

'Nine years into Eorl’s rule, a man in green came to the Wells, bloodied and exhausted from long riding without rest. Borondir was his name, and he was of mixed Dúnadan and Thíuda blood. Cirion, Steward of Gondor, had sent him as one of six errand-riders in search of aid from the Northmen against an army of Orcs and Balchoth, Easterlings who had come to invade the South-kingdom in force.'
'Our time researching the Éothéod nears its end. This is a joyous finale, as it signals the birth of the Eorlingas. Let us continue!'
Birth of the Eorlingas

'I am Grandmother Madelgard Túcca, and you are quite the stranger! I'm only talking to you because you are the friend of an Eagle. We have great respect for the Eagles, but not much for... what are you? ${RACE}?! Hmm, perhaps you could earn more respect if you do something nice for Lyndelby. You see, I have been noticing snooping goblins nearby. If you send them away, I might rest a bit easier at night!'

'You sent those goblins running?! To be honest, I did not expect you to help us at all! It would seem the rest of the village is now working up the courage to meet such a helpful and peculiar stranger, such as yourself. Perhaps you would also like to meet the rest of us? We can be a shy people, but we will warm to you in time.'

'Oh, I am glad that the whole village was able to meet you! Well, all but two, I think. Yes, they went up into the mountains to explore some time ago. Following in the footsteps of the Fallohide. Anyhow, I would say you have been most helpful to Lyndelby. It nearly felt as one of our festivals, what with all the buzz in the air from having you around!'

'All the pies have been delivered and not a single slice dropped? I'm very relieved to hear that! Oh, my apologies. In my haste to have the pies delivered, I forgot my manners. Pies are my trade, but they're also an art form after all. I would hate to see even one slice go to waste! Thank you for helping out. I'll make sure Ubbo delivers twice the pies tomorrow!'

'Is Ubbo off fishing again? Then who's going to handle today's pie deliveries?! Hmmm, will you? That would be very kind of you! I baked these pies for Madelgard, Ogiva, and Erma. Leave Lyndelby

'Greetings ${PLAYER}. I am surprised the town of Lyndelby greeted you at all. Some of the younger Men who once lived in these parts befriended a few of the Holbytlan. They were considered a curiosity, yet with their elusiveness, their presence quickly fell to mere rumours among the Men. We Eagles have kept watch over the Holbytlan ever since. All I ask is that you speak to no one of Lyndelby. We wish for the simple lives of the Holbytlan to be not disturbed.'

'From now on, you may call me Maddy. Everyone else in the village does! Hmm, it looks like you mean to depart soon. Have you another adventure afoot?! I'm sure you do! Well, before you leave, you should say good-bye to everyone! It is the neighbourly thing to do after all! Farewell, friend!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. What brings you to Járnfast?'
You show Lord Náin the strange pendant you found in the Howling Pit.
'Now where did you find that? I had thought it lost forever! Ashmâr-abân is an ancient heirloom of my line, passed down with the Black Mattock, to be forever held by the Lord of the Iron Hills. The pendant gently thrums in your hand. Some ancient magic has awoken within it.
'Ashmâr-abân has awoken once more. It belongs to you now. May it be a guiding light in the darkness.'

Náin takes the pendant from you, holds it close to his heart, and murmurs something in Khuzdul you can't quite hear. The pendant begins to glow with a soft light. At the same time you notice that the pendant also emits a low tone, a soft humming sound. Náin hands it back to you.

Habla con Frethi
A Search for Answers

'It seems I must entrust this to you once more, friend. The stone must be taken far away from Erebor, but simply locking it away somewhere else will not be enough. It seems to possess a will of its own, seeking to be found in order to carry out some evil mischief or cause some grievous harm. From where did the stone come, and for what purpose?
'I know precious little myself, save that it was found long ago in Khazad-dûm. That is where you must begin your search for answers, dangerous though it will be. Yes, the mission of the Iron Garrison failed, and the dream of reclaiming Khazad-dûm is once more a dream only, but there are some dwarves still hiding in those caves. Large gatherings of dwarves could not remain, for the Orcs would find and crush them without difficulty! But here and there, some hardy Longbeards might still struggle to survive.
'Frethi the Explorer is one such dwarf. He may not still live, but he was without compare in his exploration of the deep places below Khazad-dûm. If he is still alive, he will be indispensable to you.
'I wish you luck, ${PLAYER}. Oh, and one more thing: if for some reason you cannot solve this riddle, cast that cursed thing into the deepest pit you can find and be done with it!'
<rgb=#FF0000> This difficult treasure hunt will require community teamwork and resources outside of the game itself. Good luck! </rgb>
'A hidden door! Let us see where it leads!'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}! There has been a great deal of Orkish activity in Khazad-dûm of late, but I hid myself down deep and they have not caught sight of me. What brings you all the way down here?'
You explain that King Thorin Stonehelm sent you to find him, and about the Secret Stone.
'Hmm.... Many secrets still lie hidden within the Foundations of Stone. If there are clues to be found about an artifact of Khazad-dûm that shares some connexion with the Nameless, this is a good place to start, if such a place could be called \qgood!\q I don't quite know for what we're looking, though. Let's see what we can find.'

'This chamber must be related to the Secret Stone in some way! We should continue looking around. I will see if I can read the rest of those runes. They are quite faded, but you have met no dwarf so tenacious as Frethi!'

You peer into the illusion of the stone within the hand of the troll. Vivid imagery appears in your mind once more.
The troll, stumbling around in a stupor induced by the stone, broke through the ice and became trapped. Come morning's light, he was turned to stone. There the Third Stone waited for some time, until a Dourhand Dwarf chanced upon the statue. You see the Dourhand climbing the troll, chiselling the precious artifact from its stone hand. He grins wildly as he looks deep into its black surface, and runs off with it under his arm.
It is clear you must track down this Dourhand in order to find the stone.

You have found the decayed corpse of a Dourhand Dwarf. You are unsure how long it has been here, but the illusion of the third stone in its hand clearly indicates this is the dwarf for which you were looking.

You see him running along the road alone at night. He is trying to get the stone somewhere in a hurry. Suddenly, he is ambushed by a trio of Blue Crag goblins! He evades them, running north toward the mountains. Eventually, he is cornered against the cliff. The goblins kill him, and steal the stone.

The illusions have become more vivid. When you peer into the illusion of the stone, the frozen moment in time springs to life. This time, you can hear it as well.
You see the Blue Crag goblins emerging from the mountains. They look around nervously, muttering to each other. You hear a twig snap somewhere nearby. They pause, and pull out their weapons. A gauradan howls and charges at them from a higher slope. He bellows something at the goblins, but you cannot make out the words. The goblins try to fight back, but are quickly overpowered by the hulking beast-man. The gauradan notices the strange stone still clutched in the hand of the dead goblin. He begins to peer into it, but then winces, and looks away, disgusted by the foul magic attempting to enter his mind. Still careful to look away, he picks up the stone, and hides it in a pouch under his furs. He then runs off toward his village.
It is clear you must track down the gauradan in order to find the stone.

The illusions next show you a different gauradan tribesman negotiating with two Angmarim cultists. You are now able to hear their conversation with surprising clarity.
'You were wise to inform us of this, wolf-man. This will bring you great favour with Angmar.' 'I care little for your favours, cultist of Angmar. Take that dark magic far from here!'
The Angmarim turn and leave. Surprisingly, this time when the stone changed hands, no bloodshed occurred. It is clear you must track down the Angmarim in order to find the stone.

The illusion now shows you the moment that the Angmarim cultists were ambushed at the cross-roads by Rangers of Eriador. They were both easily brought down by their arrows. The Rangers carefully look through the cultists' belongings, and find the stone.
'Oh ho, what is this? Some hidden treasure?' 'I've never seen anything like it. Let me look at it more closely....' 'Snap out of it! This thing had you completely entranced! Put it away, quickly!' 'This is clearly some artifact of immense evil. Just being in its presence puts me on edge.' 'What should we do? This may be too dangerous to bring back to camp.' 'It must be brought to Aragorn, right away.' 'But he is in the field! You would have to travel past Fornost!' 'It must be done. I will ride as swiftly as I can. You two must return to camp.'
It is clear you must track down the mounted Ranger in order to find the stone.

The illusion shows you the Ranger's end. He rode through the Fields of Fornost as fast as his mount would carry him.
'If I can make it to the Greenway, I should be safe!', he mutters urgently. But then a pack of barghests began to close in on him, barking and snapping at his heels. When they reached the shallow pond, the moon's reflection spooked the horse, who reared up, knocking the Ranger to the ground. The Ranger tried to fend off the beasts, but it was the end of them both. As a final act, the Ranger hurled the stone into the pond, hoping no one would find it.

Unfortunately, it WAS found. Mordirith, Steward of Angmar, came looking for the missing cultists carrying a powerful artifact. The water did not obscure the stone to one such as he. The dark powers of the Nameless glow like a beacon to the eyes of a wraith.

Habla con el rey Thorin
An Unexpected Request

'Well met, friend. Tell me, are you ${PLAYER}? I have heard much about you from King Thorin! I admit I had been hoping to meet you in person. There is something... secret... about which I must ask. Come, let us move somewhere a little more private.'
'Come, friend. Let us speak in private.'

'${PLAYER}, you stand before me accused of the murder of Grímyr of Durin's Folk. My guard discovered you standing over his body, weapon in hand! You would already be clapped in irons if they had not also found this....'
He pulls a small object from a pouch and shows it to you: a small, perfectly round stone, darker than the deepest cave, blacker than night. As you look into it, something within the stone pulls at your mind, bidding you to look deeper. This stone is known to you. Thorin quickly puts it back into the pouch.
'Indeed. This is the Secret Stone. I had ordered it to be moved from its place and hidden once more, but Grímyr must have discovered its location and stolen it away. You are a hero of Durin's Folk, ${PLAYER}, and in my eyes you are innocent of any wrong-doing; do we not know how this stone can affect the mind? But it is clear to me now that the stone cannot be kept safely in Erebor.'

Grímyr would like to speak with you privately.

The vision shows you an oval stone on this pedestal. This fourth stone must be out there somewhere, waiting for you to find it. You swear you can hear faint whispers, bidding you to look closer at the illusion.

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. What brings you all the way down here?'
You ask Márus if he knows anything about removing rune-stones set up as traps on doors and describe the state of the chamber you found.
'Oh ho, that's quite clever! You know, I have heard of some of our forefathers using rune-stones to protect their vaults from intruders. Aye, let me try to remember the specifics.'
He spends a few minutes mumbling to himself, lost in thought.
'Right! I remember now! I should be able to help you, but it will be tricky! To dismantle the trap, you will need a powerful rune-stone of your own to protect yourself from the searing flames. I can craft that for you with the right reagents, but, you will also need to track down the original chisel used to carve the rune-stone! Aye, the ancient dwarf-craft is not easily undone. Here, let me write this down for you. Good luck in your search. I fear a chisel that old may be gone forever!'
He quickly jots down a list on a piece of paper and hands it to you:
To Make Rune-stone: - Powerful fire-enchanted chisel - Copper and obsidian rune-stone base - Polished dwarrowgleam
- Don't forget the original chisel!

'Did you find the chisel?'
You show him the ancient chisel and hand over the rest of the items on his list. His eyes light up.
'By Durin's Beard! This truly is a chisel of the First Age! Just look at the craftsmanship! If nothing else, thank you for sharing this with me, ${PLAYER}. Ah, if only it were not so urgently needed. I will get started on your rune-stone now.'
He gets to work on the rune-stone. A short time later, it is complete.
'Here you are. This will protect you, and allow you to dismantle the rune-stone. Ah, to do that, all you need to do is hold the chisel directly in the middle of the stone, and hit it with something. A hammer, the base of a sword, anything heavy will do. It should be that simple!'

You have found the key to this chamber's lock, but judging by the charred bones and blast marks, you should not attempt to use it right away. Below the lock, a rune-stone adorns the door, its carvings glowing an ominous red. If you are going to safely open the door, you will need to find some way to remove the rune-stone.

Grimbeorn wishes to hear of your efforts in the Wells of Langflood. You should report to Grimbeorn as soon as you are able. Your words will assist in Grimbeorn's decisions on how to best defend the Langflood, and perhaps he will know whether assisting the dwarves will benefit all in the northern lands.

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. I have been wondering when you would return. What news have you brought me from Limlók?
'I see, it seems that you and Skarding were able to protect the Floodfells from forces in Misthallow. That is good! I will make sure that needed supplies are sent to Limlók immediately.
'I also see your efforts at Sundergrót with those dwarves prevented Gundabad forces from claiming even more of the mountains. Hmm, well I do not much care for dwarves, but they did save Vaskorn's life. For that I am grateful. Now, I have given much thought to their request. While I will not send my people to foolishly fight for treasure and riches, I will see to it that we assist them when the time is right. I will know when that is. The north is my home and I know when it is in true danger.
'Oh, and to hear of poor Threkmóth! So much bloodshed! Please light a candle for the elder and give my word to the dwarves that the Beornings will not let them down.'

'To tell you the truth, I was expecting Grimbeorn to never answer our request. These are dire times, and there is no one else to whom we could turn in the north. I am very glad that he responded and gave us his word! That will boost the spirits at Skarháld, indeed!
'Now then, my friends, we have been through an ordeal or two together. What do you say about one more? Let us return to Skarháld! This time we will not trudge through the Taurogrim infested wood, however! Let us take the path from Misthallow to Ered Mithrin. It should be less treacherous now that the trolls have been dispersed!'
Fate of the North

The only thing left to do is return the Secret Stone itself to its pedestal. Do what you must.

'${PLAYER}, what has happened? Explain yourself at once!'
You quickly explain that your pursuit of the Secret Stone's origin released the Shadowed King, a Nameless entity who takes the form of Durin the Deathless and seeks to release Throkhâr, an even greater horror. You tell him too that Frethi was injured during the escape.
King Thorin turns away, anger simmering within him. He takes a moment to calm himself before addressing you again.
'This is a disaster! I should have known that pursuing this mystery could lead to such a dangerous outcome! We have to act quickly if we are to undo this mistake before tragedy befalls!'

Another vision appears before you: the Secret Stone placed on one of the five pedestals in the chamber. As you contemplate the vision, you realize you can feel the stone vibrating in its satchel. You lift the stone from King Thorin's satchel and feel the pleasing warmth of it in your hand. Can this be possible? Is this the stone's purpose, to return to this chamber with the other four of its missing brethren? They must be found and reunited.

'Me llamo Ulthir, el mejor florista de toda la tierra. ¿Seguro que has oído hablar de mí? ¿No? Bueno, no hay contabilidad para el gusto, ¿verdad? Trabajo durante meses cultivando, cosechando y transportando mis renombradas flores y arreglos desde mi granja a varias ciudades. Esta semana tengo la desgracia de estar atrapado en este montón de rocas humeantes. Mmmf, mi cabeza.
'¿Dónde estaba? Ah sí, parece que bebí un poco más de lo que estoy acostumbrado anoche. ¡Ah, no me mires así! ¿Tienes alguna idea de lo difícil que es mantener las rosas frescas desde mi granja hasta aquí? ¡El estrés casi te devora vivo! ¡Probablemente he bajado una talla entera de túnica! Así que puede que haya bebido más de lo que debería. ¿Qué te importa? ¡No eres mi esposa! Espera, no eres mi esposa, ¿verdad?'

'No, no lo eres. Bien, escucha. ¡Me ayudas y te lo recompensaré!

'${PLAYER}, my friend! I am pleased you could return to my city in time of peace, with war safely behind us! We cannot lower our guard overmuch, it is true, but Mithrandir and the Council of Gondor both assure me that the threat of further war is at a low ebb, for now. My mind therefore turns from martial matters to those of the heart, for a day long prepared is nearly upon us. As you well know, Arwen my betrothed travels even now to Minas Tirith, where we shall be wedded before all of Gondor, and she will be the queen of my kingdom.
'Long have we waited for this day! It is very important to me and to my love that the ceremony be conducted properly, but my knowledge of such matters is not sufficient. Mithrandir insists that he has an understanding of the rituals, but some members of the Council questioned the depth of his knowledge concerning the customs of Gondor. The Council therefore selected a number of Gondorian representatives to decorate the city and make ready the ceremony. The woman responsible for the wedding ceremony is named Rodwen, and I would ask you to lend her your able assistance, if you have the time and the inclination.
'Arwen will be here soon with her household, and I want all the preparations to be made before she arrives.'

'The Council selected a Gondorian representative to make ready the ceremony and other preparations. Her name is Rodwen, and I would ask you to lend her your able assistance, if you have the time and the inclination.
'Arwen will be here soon with her household, and I want all the preparations to be made before she arrives.'

'Let us meet somewhere to discuss the preparations, ${PLAYER}. There is no point in disturbing the king with such details. Surely... surely you agree? Let us find a quiet spot to discuss them. If you leave the Tower of Ecthelion and turn north, you will see a doorway spanned by a garland of flowers. Slip past that garland and climb the steps to the wall... and that is where I will meet you.'

'Yes, hello. ${PLAYER}, is it? Hmmm... I see. You are to help me make ready the wedding ceremony? I assure you, we have things well in hand....'
Rodwen appears visibly nervous, and seems to be having some trouble meeting your gaze.
'Let us meet somewhere to discuss the preparations, ${PLAYER}. There is no point in disturbing the king with such details. Surely... surely you agree? Let us find a quiet spot to discuss them. If you leave the Tower of Ecthelion and turn north, you will see a doorway spanned by a garland of flowers. Slip past that garland and climb the steps to the wall... and that is where I will meet you.'

'I know you, ${PLAYER}. I have heard of your many heroic deeds, and word of your adventures has spread throughout the land. Is it true you can read the truth in someone's face despite their words? It is true, isn't it?'
Rodwen's face is pale, and you need no special ability to determine how nervous she is in your presence.
'Then I will just tell you, for you are sure to find it out anyway! I was an adventurer-for-hire, a champion of Gondor. My friends and I sought to earn coin by lending our swords and our skills to folk in need, but... we weren't very good at it. Our guardian Drafli was more brave than sensible, our minstrel Cuilinn never did learn the value of silence when enemies were about, and I have waylaid my sword at inopportune moments... more than once, I confess it! When the war ended, we decided it was best for all if we were to leave the adventuring life behind us. Cuilinn took up farming, the dear fellow, but it was a short-lived experiment and he has left that behind too; it did not suit him either.
'So we all came to settle within the White City, and through a series of misunderstandings and some ill-advised boasting my friends and I caught the attention of the Council of Gondor. The next thing I know, our lore-master Isteron is speaking before those noble lords and ladies, insisting that we are expert wedding-planners all! What do I know about weddings? Little enough! So we have stumbled our way into something of a real adventure, ${PLAYER}, and if we cannot perfect this wedding ceremony we will be in real trouble! Will you help us?'

You ask Rodwen what curious road took her out of the wilderness and gave to her the responsibility of planning a king's wedding. She raises her hands level to her shoulders with an energetic shrug.
'Would that I could tell you! The adventuring life was hard, and to be honest with you my friends may not have been entirely prepared for it. The road we thought to take north was crawling with Orcs, so we turned south and arrived outside the Pelennor Fields just as the Gondorian force returned from Mordor in triumph. Happy timing! We joined the celebrations, of course, and decided that perhaps it was safer to put our adventuring days behind us. 'Something old, something new, something borrowed, everything blue!'

'Well, Merry, everyone knows that in a Shire wedding you've got to follow the traditions. There are four elements that must be present if the ceremony is to be a success. The bride needs to carry or wear something old, right? And then she should pair it with something new, which represents the new life she's starting with her husband...'
Merry nods solemnly, which causes Pippin to break out into laughter again before resuming.
'...and then she needs something borrowed as well, maybe a garment or a cloth or a small pocket item of some kind, and then, most important of all... everything has to be blue!'
The two hobbits start laughing again, and through their gales of laughter you can just make out gasps of 'everything blue! All the decorations, everything, they've got to be blue!'

'Something old, something new, something borrowed... and everything blue!

Legolas speaks solemnly, but the son of Thranduil cannot completely mask his amusement.
'Not everyone is as familiar with hobbits as we are, ${PLAYER}. Am I right to suggest that this must be the doing of a certain Brandybuck and Took of our acquaintance?'

'There has been a lot of wedding chatter in the air, ${PLAYER}, and I'll have you know it's not the easiest thing for this Gamgee to talk about! Take that Isteron fellow. He spoke on and on about how grand this wedding should be, and how it'll be talked about for years and years, and maybe that's so, but I can't help but wonder if that's not the most important thing. Maybe I'm just a hobbit, with hobbit-ideas, but it seems to me that the wedding should be just as Arwen and Strider want it to be. Does it matter what the kingdom thinks of it, or for how long it's talked about?'
Sam falls silent and sniffs the air.
'Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, Mister Frodo and I weren't the only hobbits who spoke to the wedding planners. Merry and Pippin talked to them too, and when they finished they went off laughing, looking very pleased with themselves about something. It might be worth looking into, ${PLAYER}. Those two are always causing trouble of some kind or another, and if you follow the smell of their pipe-smoke, could be you'll get to the bottom of it!'

You ask Merry and Pippin about the preparations for the upcoming wedding, and they share a conspiratorial look before doubling-over with laughter. When Merry has once again caught his breath, he apologizes and tries to answer your question.

'What a relief it is to hear you will help us! Every wedding should be perfect, of course, but the weight of responsibility for this particular wedding is even greater, for all the eyes of the kingdom will be upon it! It means a great deal to me that you will not betray our secret. With your help, it should not matter that my friends and I know so little about such preparations! Already I have sent them throughout the city to get whatever help they can.
'Here, ${PLAYER}, I have penned some letters of introduction authorizing you to work on my behalf in all wedding-related matters. Bring these to our lore-master Isteron and he will tell you how best you can help us. You should find him outside the Tower of Ecthelion, in the Plaza of the Fountain.'

'Ah, you are here to help plan for the Great Wedding? There is so much still to be done, but do not let that frighten you away! I have often found that the largest tasks are the most rewarding, just so long as you do not give up before you are begun!'
You ask Isteron if he needs any help researching wedding customs, and he blinks at you, the smile frozen on his face.
'Oh no, I gave up on that,' he replies. 'Cúfaron and I did learn some interesting tidbits from a number of hobbits over there, but I did not find their advice very promising. Their hobbit-traditions felt very quaint to me, not at all appropriate for such a grand wedding as this must be, but you are welcome to consult with them, if you like. They are to the south of the Tower of Ecthelion, I believe.'

'${PLAYER}! How nice to see you during a time of celebration and not during time of war!'
You tell Frodo that you are helping Rodwen and her companions with the preparations for the Great Wedding, and he nods thoughtfully.
'That is very good of you. Aragorn is dear to me, and I want his wedding to be all for which he and his bride might hope. Are Rodwen and her companions up for such a challenge? I have spoken with a number of them now, and in each of these planners I admit to you I have recognized something.'
He smiles knowingly.
'They are in over their heads, just as I was during the Quest of the Ring! Just as were we all. Well, that turned out all right, in the end. So too might the wedding ceremony! If there is anything we can do, ${PLAYER}, let us know and we will help.'

'My fireworks? Ah, I am sorry, ${PLAYER}, but you may remember that it was a time of war until very recently! When Shadowfax bore me hither with young Peregrin Took, I did not have the luxury to bring any fireworks along with me.'
You apologize for disturbing him, and the Wizard raises his eyebrows at you with apparent amusement.
'Are you always in such a rush that you cannot wait for an old man to finish speaking? I said I did not bring any fireworks with me on the ride from Rohan. I did not say I no longer possessed any! Indeed, I have collected one or two such devices during the time since the war ended, and I have stored them in a small crate in my quarters. Now, there are not as many as I would like; it was my custom when lighting such crackers in the Shire to really fill the night sky with illumination. That was both for the delight of the hobbits and for my own, if I am speaking honestly.
'But perhaps the few crackers I have assembled will still bring some small measure of enjoyment to the attendees of the wedding, ${PLAYER}. Go to my quarters in the High Guest-house in the Seventh Circle and empty the crate of its contents, and I will see what can be done.'

'I don't know very much about this name \qCastamir,\q but I know it has something to do with a dark period in the history of Gondor. Corsair leaders calling themselves \qthe Heirs of Castamir\q caused us some problems on the journey from Rohan here to Minas Tirith, and I know it is a name that causes Aragorn some displeasure. That is enough for me; I do not need to know the particulars.
'For someone to invoke this name now, today? I do not like it, ${PLAYER}! Some villain here in the Splintered Shield snuck this paper among the others, hoping to disrupt the wedding! Find out who has done this, and we will make them pay for it!'

'What is the trouble, friend? I assure you that several of my finest barrels will be brought to the hall for the wedding-feast. I am a man of my word, and I will see it done. All I ask is that the lords and ladies attending the feast know that it was Degilion of the Splintered Shield who provided the drink.'
You tell Degilion that someone slipped a reference to Castamir the Usurper among the papers on Gimli's table while the dwarf and his companion were dozing.
'Men speak of Castamir... in my tavern? This is an outrage! I'll have you know that we of the Splintered Shield are kings' men all, and have nothing but respect for his bride-to-be, Elf though she be. I say that with all the love in my heart, ${PLAYER}! If you find any who say otherwise, or even so much as think it, I will have them cast out upon the street, never welcome again within these walls! I swear it, ${PLAYER}. Show me the man who speaks fondly of Castamir, the usurping king-slayer, and I will report him to the Guards of the Citadel!'

'Nobody saw anything? Ha! I wager my axe could make them talk, but this is not my kingdom and I should not wish to overstep my bounds. Not right before a wedding, anyway.
'Castamir! Bah! I remember the Corsairs that invoked his name at Pelargir, ${PLAYER}, and none of them would be welcome at a wedding such as this. No, not even if they cleaned themselves up and wore their finest garb! They were cruel-hearted and evil-minded, and from my gathering it sounds like their idol Castamir was twice as bad!
'You should go tell Gandalf that there are some, at least, who might wish to disrupt Aragorn's wedding. Maybe our Wizard could work some magic to sniff out these troublemakers and make them think better of it? I should say it is worth a try. If that does not do it, offer my axe in service of the task. That may prove even more effective than magic!'

'What has brought you back to me so quickly, my friend? Has Gimli exhausted his store of love-words? Or has he decided to save them for another wedding? It would not surprise me to learn that our dwarf has a poet's heart, as do many of his people.'
You tell Gandalf about the mention of Castamir that someone slipped among Gimli's papers in the Splintered Shield, and the Wizard nods without surprise.
'Yes, I expected something like this, ${PLAYER}. The folk of Gondor have long memories. Castamir's reign was the violent culmination of the Kin-strife, a chain of events that began with a wedding of which the populace did not approve. Rómendacil, twentieth King of Gondor, sent his son Valacar to make peace with Vidugavia, the self-proclaimed King of Rhovanion. Valacar did so, but he did more as well: he fell in love with Vidumavi, Northman daughter of the king, and the two were married.
'Many folk in Gondor were displeased with the match, believing that Valacar's marriage would lessen the royal Númenórean blood in any heir produced by the union. Unrest simmered throughout the kingdom. A child was born to Valacar and Vidumavi, and he was named Eldacar; the unrest continued to simmer, until at last he came to the throne. Unrest turned to violent conflict and Castamir, the Captain of Ships, brought war to unseat Eldacar. The Usurper ruled Gondor for ten years until Eldacar returned at the head of a Northmen army. Castamir was slain, but his sons and allies fled to Pelargir and Umbar, and the underlying discontent that caused the Kin-strife never truly disappeared.
'Will the people of Gondor accept the marriage of their king to Arwen Undómiel, the daughter of Elrond of Rivendell? The news you bring from the Splintered Shield tells me that some, at least, may not. We should bring word of this possibility to Elessar, though it pains me to trouble him with it. Perhaps you can do this, ${PLAYER}.'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}, so far from the place of our first meeting, and with so much having happened since!
'I have walked for many years in Middle-earth, but I feel something I have never felt before. I am like a young sapling, my life just now beginning. I assure you it is a peculiar sensation for one of the Eldar, ${PLAYER}!'

'The journey was a long one, but we would not miss Arwen's wedding! Let our younger sister heed the wisdom of her older brothers.'
Elladan gives you a playful smile.
'We are little more than a hundred years older than she, but that century makes all the difference in wisdom, ${PLAYER}. Ask anyone and they will tell you I speak true.'

'It is good to see you again, my friend, far from lands where it has been our custom to meet. There are few occasions that might draw so many from the Hidden Vale to the long road, but the marriage of Elrond's daughter Arwen Undómiel is one.
'She is to wed Elessar of Gondor, but that is not the only name he wore during their courtship. Aragorn he was, and Estel, and while others called him Strider that name brought laughter to her lips and amusement to her heart.
'It is a time for love's joy, ${PLAYER}, but there is sadness in it too, a father's sorrow for the daughter from whom he must be parted. That is another reason so many have come south, for even amid such joy their dear friend must lose something too, and that is a grief.'

'Mae govannen, ${PLAYER}. We have come a long way for the wedding of Arwen Undómiel to King Elessar of Gondor, but our journey is almost at its end.
'I have been chief counsellor of Elrond's household for many years, and he has long relied upon my wisdom and advice... but what of these have I to offer today? There are times a daughter's happiness must be set against a father's sorrow, but how often do the Sundering Seas lie between one and the other? Rarely, perhaps... but the choice having been made, for Lord Elrond and his daughter the answer appears to be always.'

'I greet you once again, ${PLAYER}, and name you friend. You and I have walked in dangerous places, but let us set aside the memory of them for now, for this is a time of celebration. That there may still be such as these is welcome indeed, though the time of my people draws near to an end.'

'Mae govannen, my friend. It is no small thing to bring so many across the mountains and to these distant lands, but for the love of my daughter all here would make the journey tenfold.
'The defeat of Sauron has made safer the lands hereabout. The road was not difficult, and though my grieving heart tried to slow my steps, the light of joy in Arwen's face kept steady my pace.
'For all the knowledge I possess, ${PLAYER}, I cannot solve this riddle. Arwen will be parted, from her kindred or from her betrothed, and none of my wisdom can ease that parting. Still I am here, and would be nowhere else on this day, or on any day that my daughter desired.'

'A time of great evil has passed, ${PLAYER}, and now hearts will be lightened with joy. Arwen has long-awaited this day, but its arrival was never certain. Now that it has come, let none stand in the way of love's bounty, lest they risk my granddaughter's ire or my own.
'I assure you: both may be fearful.'

The time of the wedding has arrived!
Rodwen is pleased at how well the ceremony was conducted, and now she wishes to speak with you outside the feast-hall of Merethrond in Minas Tirith (Midsummer).

'I understand the preparations are nearly complete?'
You tell Arwen that the Council of Gondor authorized a great number of plans and preparations for the wedding, and Aragorn believes they are nearing completion. When you tell her that Gimli had some suggestions relating to the vows she and her betrothed might speak during the ceremony, Arwen smiles fondly.
'I have already given the matter some thought, and chosen words of my own; my love is certain to have done the same. But my heart is warmed by the kind thoughts of Gimli, son of Glóin. May the words of our vows measure up to those of his devising!
'But is that my betrothed I see? Has he come down from the city to greet his bride?'

'The sight of my beloved has stolen all speech from me, my friend! For so long have we awaited this day, and now it arrives.
'Can it be so? Speak to me, ${PLAYER}, so I will know that is truly my Lady Undómiel, Arwen Evenstar, and no illusory dream of my hopeful mind!'
'Dare I believe that is the sight of my beloved, and not some illusion? For so long have we awaited this day!'
'After so many labours, at last it is time. Come with me, my friend. Together my love and I will ascend the levels of the White City, and tomorrow, on Midsummer's Day, we will be married at last.'

'I must say, my good friend, that it was a beautiful wedding, and everything went according to my plan. Indeed, in that way it was quite different than the plans of my adventuring days!
'Did you know that my friends and I have already been tasked with arranging further weddings later in the summer? All of a sudden, folk of high birth and low seem to require our services, and I have been unable to turn down a one!
'I do hope I am not making a mistake to say so, but this Great Wedding was more successful than any of my other recent endeavours... why, no one was injured or maimed at all, which might be worth recording!'
Book 1, Chapter 7: A Wedding at Midsummer

The Great Wedding will take place on Midsummer's Day, and it will be a time of celebration for all. Folk from lands near and distant will come to celebrate the joining of King Elessar and Arwen Undómiel.

'I imagine my kingdom has not seen a wedding like this for many, many years; I see it reflected in the fervour of my people's celebration! The war is ended, and they are gladdened to have joyful cause!
'We spoke of some trouble in the history of my kingdom, ${PLAYER}, do you remember? I told you I did not think it would be a problem, and so I still think. I have studied the faces of my people on this Midsummer's Day, and this I have learned: they will come to love their Queen. She will be a patient guardian of Gondor and all its folk, as I will be, and together we will restore what glory there is to be had in this age, and whatever ages may come.
'Thank you for all you have done, ${PLAYER}. I speak not only of your service against the forces of Sauron, but also for all you have done as my dear friend. When at last the history of Gondor is written, one will be counted more important than the other, but know that in my deepest heart I measure them equal, for Aragorn may be selfish where Elessar may not.'
He smiles at you, a wolfish grin that brings to mind the shadows of a distant tavern in Bree-land.
'But you will not hear me admit it again, my friend. The peace of Middle-earth must come above my own happiness.'

'It has been some time since Gondor saw such revelry, ${PLAYER}. The folk thirsted for it without knowing what they desired. Such a night of celebration will be good for them.
'The peace of Middle-earth is hard-won, my dear ${CLASS}, but it must be defended if it is to remain secure. Not all threats are gone with Sauron, as you well know, and other evils there are in the wide world that must be faced with bravery and resolve. Can I count on you to continue to stand against these dangers, ${PLAYER}, so that the love we celebrated today can last into the days and months ahead? A wedding is a beginning, my friend, and so is this Great Wedding, for there are those in the world that will see the joy of it and resent its presence.
'My time on these shores draws nigh, my friend, and I want to know that these lands will know peace beyond my departure. I will be counting on you for this, ${PLAYER}, or for those you choose to follow in your stead. Someone will need to defend the happiness we saw today. Someone will need to safe-guard the peace of Middle-earth.
'We will speak of these matters again, my friend. For now, you should do as does the city: eat, drink, and be merry!'
<rgb=#00FF00>The story continues in future updates....</rgb>
'Thank you for all you have done, dear ${PLAYER}.'
'You have my thanks and those of my kingdom for all you have done.'

'The hobbits insisted this be called a banquet, in honour of one or another chieftain of theirs. I am a little unclear on the details, but it seems to have something to do with the number and varieties of foodstuffs available?'
Merethien casts a weary look at her bench-mate Ioreth, who has been nattering constantly for the duration of the wedding-feast, and glances disapprovingly at Galathir, who has launched upon a long discussion of the various spices flavouring the many courses.
'Come, let us inquire with the hobbits. They seem to be amusing fellows, and I would learn more of this land of theirs.'

'The celebrations are not yet concluded; after all, there is still the wedding-feast to enjoy! Go to the feast-hall of Merethrond and speak to Merethien, the Master Foodmonger, once you have had your fill of merriment... there is still much of that to be had!
'Do be careful, my friend.'
Merethien, the Master Foodmonger, can be found inside the great feast-hall of Merethrond, where the festivities continue.
King Elessar and Queen Arwen Undómiel have slipped away from the celebration and are in the throne room of Minas Tirith (Midsummer).

'But what am I saying? The celebrations are not yet concluded; after all, there is still the wedding-feast to enjoy! Go to the feast-hall of Merethrond and speak to Merethien, the Master Foodmonger, once you have had your fill of merriment... there is still much of that to be had!
'Do be careful, my friend. If anything untoward happens at the feast and ruins the perfect wedding I planned, I will need to return to adventuring or find another profession, and I would rather not. Enjoy the wedding-feast, ${PLAYER}!'

'Thank you for lending such support as you have to my husband, ${PLAYER}, during your adventures and his. There were days when it seemed the Shadow would never pass... but it has lifted, and not on its own terms. No, it was through the efforts of many folk all throughout Middle-earth, and yours not least of all!
'Our wedding has been everything for which I hoped, and I am certain my husband feels the same.'
Arwen looks around the throne room, and in the dim light of the grand chamber you see an amused smile dance across her fair features.
'But we will need to do something about this throne,' she remarks.
'The King and Queen are in the throne room, ${PLAYER}. I understand they were awaiting you!'

'Dear me! I am pleased that Prince Faramir has made up his mind, but to be completely honest with you, ${PLAYER}, I had not quite gotten around to the advice I intended to give to him!
'Still, all is well when it ends well... which it will, if Lady Éowyn agrees to his proposal. If she does not, I fear the reputation of hobbit-wisdom may suffer in Ithilien and Gondor! Oh dear!'

'Who can say when we will all be once again together, ${PLAYER}? Each of us has business elsewhere: some in the north, some here in the south. It would have been a shame not to mark the occasion. Is that so unusual? We all feel a kinship with each other, borne of our shared duty; it is strange to me that we must now separate.
'Lothrandir wishes to return to Forochel, the land of the Snowmen, so I will travel with him part of the way with some others of the company. Techeron will reside once again in Evendim, but on the way we will pay a visit to Saeradan and learn the tale of his own return to Eriador with our fallen brothers. Idhrien and Langlas plan to stay for awhile at Esteldín with Mincham. Angwedh has not yet decided where he will travel, just that his road lies to the north. If he has a place in mind, he has not shared it with us; I think the wilderness calls to him.'
Radanir smirks at you.
'Do you know what calls to me? The food of the north-lands! The food at this feast is too richly-made, too covered in sauces, too soft, and there's too much of it. There isn't anything to sink your teeth into, ${PLAYER}. Give me the crusty bread and old cheese of the Forsaken Inn, a day's ride east of Bree... that is all I need.'

'The Grey Company rode from Eriador to aid the chieftain of the Dúnedain, and now many of us will return to our homes; but not all. We all have our own reasons, for the king has not set a bond upon us that we do not choose for ourselves.
'But there remains the question: what shall be done about the land that lies on Gondor's doorstep? Mordor lies there, the Black Land, and who knows what sorceries of the Witch-king may lurk within the Morgul Vale. I will help my king to combat these evils, and so too will Dagoras, and Faeron, and Mithrendan.
'Others of the Grey Company may decide to do the same... but they must choose for themselves. We have done what we intended, but I wager that some may discover they wish to do more. Gondor awaits an era of peace... but it will not arrive without we who are willing to fight for it.'

'I played my part as well as I could, ${PLAYER}! Were your friends able to surprise you?'
The wine steward glances at Thrymm Red-beard, whose long-winded description of past glories has shown no sign of cessation; indeed, he may have started anew.
'Perhaps you can go back upstairs and see if my services are needed? I am sure there must be a need for more wine... there simply must....'

'I hope you are enjoying yourself, ${PLAYER}. I confess to you that much of tonight has passed by with dizzying speed, but it is a joyful motion and I would trade it for nothing else.
'Might I ask a favour of you? Earlier I spoke with Faramir about a matter of some importance, and I am interested to learn if he has come to a decision. Would you speak with him and determine if this be so?'

'One of the wine stewards came by earlier, before our friend from Rohan launched into his... full-throated... tales of bravery. This steward asked if we would do him the kindness of delivering you to him if you chanced to come by our table.
'He said he would be downstairs, ${PLAYER}. Now that I have executed this charge, perhaps I will learn what else my daughter would hear of the new king of Rohan, and why the speaking of his name brings such a blush to her cheeks....'

'Ah, there you are, ${PLAYER}! I am pleased the Prince of Dol Amroth gave you my message, for it is urgent and I did not know where else I might turn. There is something of a problem, you see, and I need you to ensure it does not get any worse!
'Some rough sorts have gathered outside. I am afraid they might intend to disrupt the wedding-feast in some way. They were asking for you!
'Here, take these bottles of wine out to them. It could be that an offering of peace will send them happily on their way. And if not, well... your deeds are well-known, and such rough sorts as these may take one look at you and decide it would be best for them to go elsewhere!'

'And so, with our horses refreshed, we crossed the Mering-stream and rode hard through the Beacon Hills. We were so close, but not yet close enough: we were beset by Orcs and Variags near Amon Dîn! We broke through the line of Variags, but they did not pursue us. I think now I know the reason: they knew the road ahead would be held against us!'
Thrymm pauses in his tale, seeming to see you for the first time.
'Oh, ${PLAYER}, pull up a seat! I was just telling these fine folk of Gondor about some of my recent adventures!'

'It is a pleasure to speak with you, my friend. I saw you earlier, when our Halfling friends ran by the table on their way to do some mischief... it was a spirited chase, and brought a smile to my lips; that has been rare enough in the days since... well, in the past few days.'
Faramir falls silent, and you take the opportunity to ask if he has considered the topic about which King Elessar inquired. Faramir studies you quietly.
'He told you not the subject of our discussion? He is more subtle than I expected, or perhaps it is the hand of his Queen that makes him so! Ah, ${PLAYER}, you are a friend, so I will speak freely.
'The king knows that my heart has been captured by the Lady Éowyn of Rohan. She returned to the Riddermark in the company of her brother while they prepare for the funeral of Théoden, and while she has been gone my heart has been in darkness! Ever she occupies my thoughts, and I know I will never again feel happiness or joy while we are apart. I dare not hope she feels the same, and would not! For I would wish her no unhappiness.'

'I expect Grimbeorn and his animals will enliven Merethrond for a time. Good! It will give us a brief respite from all this celebration!
'Arwen and I would like to speak to you, ${PLAYER}, in a more quiet setting. Let us find one.'
A great commotion draws your attention to the west side of the feast-hall

Merethien, the Master Foodmonger of Minas Tirith, has some questions for Merry and Pippin concerning what qualifies as a 'banquet' at their home, the distant Shire. Furthermore, she is pleased to have an excuse to leave Ioreth's chatter and Galathir's lecture behind her.
Beregond and his family sit at Pippin's table with a number of Gondorian nobles.

'Thank you for rescuing me, ${PLAYER}. I intend no disrespect for any of the fine folk at my table, for they are all worthies of Gondor in their own ways... but some of them can be most tiring.
'Come with me, my helpful friend. I see the hobbits with whom I spoke right over there.'

'What do you think, Pip? What would old Flourdumpling have to say about the courses on offer here? Oh yes, Merethien, I think this wedding-feast can stand quite comfortably alongside the very finest of Shire banquets!'

'${PLAYER}, it is my pleasure to introduce you to my wife Gilithel, and I believe you have already met our son Bergil. He was quite the trouble-maker in Minas Tirith, running through the lower tiers with his friends, and he has found new ways to cause mischief in Ithilien. But he is a good lad, and at his age I was much the same.
'I must confess to you I did not think I would be welcomed back to the city for the King's wedding, but word was sent to Lord Faramir, and we could not refuse.'

'¡Pero yo soy solo un enano! No me atrevería a pedirte que recortaras las barbas de mis compañeros, pero ¿podrías hacerlas brillar por mí?

'¡Hola y ${PLAYERNAME:bienvenido[m]|bienvenida[f]} al Poney Pisador!
'¿Has venido a unirte a la celebración del Solsticio de Verano en Bree? Ciertamente no serás ${PLAYERNAME:el primero[m]|la primera[f]}, debo decirte. A menudo ha sido mi deber alertar a aventureros como tú sobre las necesidades de los demás, pero debo confesar que hoy, soy yo quien debe pedirte algo. Verás... incluso con Bob y Nob para ayudarme, estaba terriblemente desprevenido por la cantidad de clientes que el Solsticio de Verano traería a Bree-town!
'Antes de unirte a las festividades y encontrarte tan alegre como algunos de mis clientes, ¿podrías hacerme un favor? Algunos de los clientes han bebido un poco demasiado y se han encontrado encima de mis mesas. Normalmente, tales prácticas no me molestan, pero han comenzado a dañar mi vajilla y no tengo tiempo para salir a hablar con ellos yo mismo. Además, Nob me informó que han tomado la costumbre de dejar sus jarras en los lugares más extraños del Pony.
'Encuentra tantas jarras como puedas y persuade a los más borrachos de los fiesteros que bajen de mis mesas, ¿quieres? Pero no seas demasiado duro con ellos!'

'Ah, ¿te gusta la cerámica? Me temo que no tengo mucho para vender en este momento. Tuve que despedir a mi asistente después de que derribó un enorme estante de macetas, tazas, cuencos... oh, ni siquiera sé la extensión de lo que se perdió.
'Perdóname por extenderme. El Solsticio de Verano es una época tan ocupada para los pedidos y sin mi asistente... digamos, si por casualidad estás libre, ¡podría hacer que valga la pena tu tiempo!
'Solo necesito algunas cosas simples. Con tu ayuda, podría hacer mucho más. Ahora déjame pensar... mi asistente cortaba madera para mí, pero lo envié lejos antes de que la recogiera. Verás que ha talado pinos por toda el área. ¡El pino arde bien y caliente! Oh! Tenía un pedido especial para un juego de platos con impresiones de hojas de sauce. Hay un hermoso sauce llorón al sur de la ciudad, cerca del lago. Ahora, mientras estás por ahí, también tengo un pedido de encaje que necesita ser recogido de Maud Tatter.
'Déjame pensar, ¿es todo? Oh Dios mío, casi olvido lo más importante! ¡La arcilla! Recojo una arcilla rica y hermosa del estanque al noroeste de la ciudad. Si pudieras salir corriendo y ayudarme con esas pocas cosas, yo -- podemos salvar el día especial de muchas parejas felices!'

'The feast was meant to be a great celebration.'

'Sorrowing at the failure of his own wisdom, the Grey Wizard returned to Framabárg bearing grim tidings. Fram was, unsurprisingly, enraged in his turn; he sent the Wizard away as well in scorn.
'One would assume that Wandalb departed in sorrow, with the hope that he might return in time to bring together the two stubborn lords and make them understand each other when their heads had cooled. It would not be so.'

'Now, ${PLAYER}, I will explain why the treasures of Scatha were all made by dwarves. This is best told to you by the telling of the ill-fated feast:
'Fram invited the lords of neighbouring lands to his hall for a great feast to celebrate the slaying of Scatha. Both Thranduil of Felegoth and Thráin of Erebor sent emissaries, as did the lords of the Wood-men and the Lake-folk, distant kin to the Ai-thúda.'

'Fasthálla once stood here. Now we can only see the ruins of Framsburg, built upon Fasthálla's ruins, after Scatha's attack.'

'This truth is certain. A year after Durin’s folk departed the Ered Mithrin to follow King Thráin to Erebor, the great long-worm spilled forth from his secret cavern. Angry and ravenous, Scatha attacked the Ai-thúda, ravaging their herds and scorching Fasthálla itself with his destructive breath.'

'Scatha’s bite carried a flesh-rotting poison, such that Fram was forced to cut off his own father’s sword-arm to save his life. Even after this maiming, Frumgar remained sickly and weak for the rest of his days.
'Come, let us return to Framsburg. There is more to learn in the ruins there.'

'My friend, ${PLAYER}. I am glad that you are here. I have been pondering the well known Rohirric tale of Fram and Scatha. While I am certain that the tale is true, I have often questioned some of Fram's actions. If you would continue to be my guide in the north a little while longer, I would be ever so grateful, for I wish to continue learning and writing the story of my people.
'Fram is but half the tale I wish to learn more about. What of Scatha, the worm? Perhaps it was the dwarves’ arrival in the Grey Mountains that awoke Scatha from slumber. Perhaps it was the coming of the Ai-thúda, and the slaughter and flight of the Gundabad Orcs after Angmar’s fall. I believe that answers will lie in the north.'
<rgb=#00FF00>While it is not required, it is recommended that you have completed Léothred's journey through the Wells of Langflood before beginning the The Folly of Scatha and Fram.</rgb>

'Wandalb remained at Erebor for weeks afterward, pleading for Thráin to see reason, but the Dwarf-king never again spoke to him or counted him friend. It was a dark time.
'It makes me wonder if the necklace was cursed!'

'It is said that when Thráin received the gift of Scatha's teeth, he was furious. He believed Fram's missive to be a taunt, and would not be moved even by the Grey Wizard's most cunning words. He cast the necklace aside, proclaiming that such trinkets were poor substitutes for his people's birthright, and sent Wandalb away.'

'Now that we have safely arrived at Erebor, I would very much like to have a look around the grand hall under the mountain.
'When Thráin’s herald returned to Erebor with the necklace, Wandalb had accompanied the herald to speak on the Ai-thúda’s behalf. I assume that the Grey Wizard did all he could to help ease the tensions between the two people.'

'Have you helped the dwarves in Elderslade? Good, good! While you were away, we have been assisting the dwarves here at Annâk-khurfu. We also managed to verse each other in what we know. There are still some gaps in the story though, and something about that necklace does not sit right with us!'

'We have made it to Elderslade! While we are here, we should assist the dwarves as best we can. Perhaps you should defeat some more of those Gundabad forces that we have encountered on our travels together.
'Now Fróthi, where was I on Fram? Ah yes, Fram's death. Fram’s death brought new troubles for the Ai-thúda. It stirred the Orcs of the North, who had feared him, and though he left three sons, none were yet of age. The eldest, Gífica, was only ten when he succeeded Fram. The hordes of Gundabad seized upon the Ai-thúda's lack of an adult lord and caused much strife in the Wells for many years. Fram’s two elder sons died in battle with the Orcs. Gífica died in an ambush when he was only twenty-five years old, then his brother Gundamári just a year later, on a reckless quest to avenge him....'

'While we all search to discover the truth between Fram and Scatha, perhaps we should look more closely at how Fram's death affected the Ai-thúda. We may uncover some hidden truths on our search.
'Fróthi has told me that the dwarves march into Elderslade and have established a fortified post there. Elderslade so happens to be where Fram's body was found those many years ago. It is for that fact alone that we must march with the dwarves.'

'Fram’s people hailed him as a hero, and at his bidding Fasthálla was rebuilt in a manner grander than what came before. The Ai-thúda named it Framabárg in his honour. The treasures of Scatha's hoard adorned it.
'Could it be that some of Scatha's hoard still adorns the ruins of the keep? We should search the ruins for any signs of Scatha's treasures.'

'Fram then took the dragon's-tooth necklace for himself, and set about ordering the lands of his people.
'Did the necklace hasten Frumgar's illness? I can not say for certain. I am certain, however, that Fram's heart only held admiration for his father. There was never an ill wish between the two while their lives overlapped.'
'With him Fram bore two great sacks, which he poured out amid the rubble of his father's hall.'

'Yes, it is interesting that all of the adornments you have found are dwarf-made. This is no coincidence, and I will explain why soon enough.
'What I must tell you first is what Fram did with Scatha's bones. He made for his father a necklace of the dragon's teeth. When Frumgar received the gift, he was glad to be thus avenged. His happiness was to be short lived, however.'

'On the first day of spring in the year two-thousand, Fram returned. He emerged from the woods bedraggled and dirty, yet unharmed.
'Let us learn what we can of Fram's return from parts unknown.'

'Erebor! To say that the structures of dwarves are grandiose is but an understatement to beholding such structures with one's own eyes. Erebor is a wonder indeed! We have made it!'

'Let us rest here for a bit. I am very much looking forward to seeing Erebor. I have heard about the Lonely Mountain, but have not yet journeyed to this part of Middle-earth.
'Hmm, we have a ways to travel, do we not? Perhaps then we should not miss the opportunity presenting itself to us here in the wilds of Misthallow. Let us hunt for some meats to keep our bellies full until we reach the gates of Erebor.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Your skills at the hunt are impressive. Perhaps one day they will even rival that of Fram's hunting prowess. Now then, I am feeling rested enough to continue our journey towards Erebor. I am ready to depart when you are!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you continue this quest, you will swiftly travel to the gates of Erebor.</rgb>

'Fram assented to Wandalb's proposal soon after the Wizard's departure, for in truth he had come to dislike the reminder of his father's undoing, and was glad of an excuse to be rid of Scatha's teeth.
'${PLAYER}, my friend. I believe that it is the right time in this tale to begin following in the footsteps of Scatha, or at least his teeth! Would you be able to accompany me to Erebor? I would be most grateful if you did, as I know you are in good standing with those who dwell there now.'

'Working together may be the best way to complete the tale of Scatha and strengthen the bond between dwarves and Men. Fróthi, your knowledge will be most valuable. I would be honoured if you were to accompany us on this journey.
'Let us depart for Skarháld when we are all ready to leave.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: When you continue this quest, you will swiftly travel to Skarháld in Ered Mithrin.</rgb>

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! It is good to see you again! Your friend Léothred searches to pen the true tale of Scatha and Fram? Do not think me rude but I would say if a Man or dwarf were to pen this tale alone, it would not be the truth. The history of that Man and worm still pains both our peoples.
'Hmm, perhaps then, we should all work together! I myself have always been puzzled with the written history of Scatha and Fram. If there is more to the story, and I would expect there is, then what is to stop us from finding it?
'I will accompany you, if you'll have me. I will bring with us what remains of the necklace. I should warn you though, our journey will most likely have to take us to the Grey Mountains, where Fram's body was found. We will be at the doorsteps of war.'

'We should be careful going forward, my friend. The dwarves that gather at Skarháld, do so for war. Aye, a conflict is certainly coming with Gundabad.
'We should gather what supplies we need, and prepare for what lies ahead.'

'Thank you for gathering these much needed supplies. These will be crucial to our search for truth.
'Our journey is about to bring us ever closer to conflict. I believe that we are all in agreement to press on.'

'${PLAYER}, do you suppose that Scatha's necklace is still in Erebor after all these years, or did Thráin throw Fram's missive out of his hall?'
You explain, oddly enough, that you have encountered the necklace once before, or at least part of the necklace. The missive had indeed been kept by Thráin and left forgotten in Erebor until you had come to the Dale-lands recently. You suggest visiting Fróthi the Lore-master in Erebor as he is well versed in the history of Scatha, the Worm.
'Fascinating! I knew that you were the right ${CLASS} to call upon! I thank you for this story, my friend. Come, let us speak with this Lore-master, Fróthi.'

'Una boda perfecta puede ser el momento más memorable de una relación. Me aseguro de que para todos mis eventos, ese recuerdo sea encantador y agradable. Solo lo mejor es suficiente, por eso tengo envíos de los mejores suministros que llegan de toda la tierra. Alimentos raros, sedas exquisitas, flores exóticas: mis parejas piden y yo entrego.
Bueno, alguien más se suponía que debía entregar mis envíos, pero parece que están ocupados con otra cosa. Si por casualidad encuentras tu camino hacia el Tercer Círculo, y si por casualidad recoges mis tardías cajas de suministros mientras estás allí, te lo agradecería. Entrega los versos extraviados a Colladan

Colladan se encuentra en las Casas del Saber de Minas Tirith.
Entrega los versos extraviados a Colladan.

'¿Qué? ¿Me he vuelto a quedar dormido? Oh, hola. Me pregunto si has visto... bueno, esto es bastante embarazoso. He estado recopilando fragmentos de poesía y versos románticos... para, ehm, inspiración. Sí, eso es. Necesito un poema para leer en una actuación a la que asistirá mi amada... bueno, mi eventual amada, Lírveril. Le encanta la poesía y asiste al espectáculo anual aquí en Minas Tirith cada año.
'Recopilé algunos de los mejores versos de los viejos maestros del oficio y estaba en proceso de organizarlos en el mejor poema de amor que jamás haya existido. O, eso había sido, es decir. Verás, parece que me he quedado dormido, durante el cual algún tonto abrió una ventana cercana.
'Todas mis horas de arduo trabajo, mis años de anhelo, mi muy cuidadosa copia de los mejores poemas de amor - ah, eso es, reuniendo inspiración. ¡Todo! ¡Arruinado por una siesta! Dime, ¿tienes unos momentos para ayudarme a encontrar esas páginas, camarada? ¡Podría valer la pena! ¿Qué tan lejos podrían haber llegado? Estaba dormido apenas... bueno, ¡es mejor empezar!
'¡Oh, gracias, gracias! Miraré alrededor del escritorio aquí si buscas el resto de la biblioteca.'
Encuentra los versos extraviados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'¿Pudiste encontrar los versos? ¡Deben estar por aquí en algún lugar!'

'¿No te parece un poco sofocante aquí?'
La joven mira hacia donde está Colladan con una sonrisa burlona, luego vuelve a leer su libro.
'¿Pudiste encontrar los versos? ¡Ah, gracias, gracias! Debo volver a compilar, eh, escribir las palabras con las que ganaré el amor de Lírveril!'
El amor está en el aire

'¿Alguna vez has visto algo así? Diría que es la primera vez en todos mis largos años que mi gente ha experimentado tanta alegría.
'Aún así, hay trabajo por hacer. Varios jardines de Minas Tirith están bajo mi responsabilidad, pero me ha resultado más difícil atenderlos. ¡Hay tanta gente alrededor de la ciudad! Mis viejas piernas ya no me llevan tan bien como antes. Pero no quiero dejar que mis plantas se desperdicien; han sobrevivido a tiempos difíciles.
'Si pudieras ayudarme, el jardín que alberga la estatua del Intendente Egalmoth en el Tercer Círculo requiere atención. Las malas hierbas han brotado de la tierra y los arbustos necesitan riego.'

'¿Qué tenía que decir la dama Galadriel, ${PLAYER}?'
Le transmites a Gimli las palabras de Galadriel. Cuando mencionas que Galadriel sabe que sus caminos se cruzarán de nuevo una vez más, una sonrisa aparece en la cara de Gimli.
'¡Mañana habrá tiempo suficiente para hablar de días venideros, creo yo! ¡Disfrutemos de esta noche!

'Escúchame con atención.
'Ningún enano de buena reputación permitiría que una jarra de cerveza, aun siento tan buena, ¡hablara en su nombre!
'¡Ja! ¡Para eso te tengo esta noche, ${PLAYER}!
'¿Ves a la dama Galadriel sentada en la mesa nupcial? ¡Su resplandor no conoce igual! He atesorado el regalo que me dio cuando partimos de Lothlórien, y querría ofrecerle uno a cambio.
'Solo me gustaría pedir a la dama Galadriel que visite las Cavernas Centelleantes. Podrían pasar años antes de que mi trabajo haya terminado, pero no será mucho tiempo para los Elfos.
'¿Podrías hacerme ese favor, ${PLAYER}?'

Mientras le cuentas a Galadriel los planes de Gimli para los días venideros y le ofreces una invitación en su nombre, empieza a reír suavemente entre dientes.
'Puedes decirle a Gimli que no he olvidado nuestro encuentro en Lothlórien, ni he olvidado el momento en que nos separamos. Un regalo dado libremente no necesita ser devuelto.
'Aunque debo rechazar la invitación de Gimli, no pienses que es por descortesía. Ahora miro hacia el Oeste, ya que allí es donde me conduce mi futuro. Aún así, sé que nuestros caminos volverán a cruzarse una vez más antes del fin.
'No permitáis que vuestros corazones estén apesadumbrados en momentos de tal alegría. ¡Todavía queda mucho por ver!'

'Oh, ¿has visto alguna vez una belleza así?'
Gimli mira a su alrededor, aparentemente impresionado de la habilidad necesaria por parte de los artesanos de Gondor para la construcción de Merethrond.
'Muy bonito, en verdad, especialmente paral as manos de los Hombres. ¿Pero qué hay de las manos de los enanos? ¿Qué hay de MIS manos? ¡Verás, ya tengo planes para el futuro!
'¡Bebe conmigo, ${PLAYER}, y déjame contarte lo que pretendo hacer!'

'Es una lástima que todos nuestros amigos no puedan celebrarlo con nosotros, pero... el rey y yo llegamos a un especie de acuerdo.
'Verás, el rey apoyaba mi idea de cuidar a los niños y refugiados que todavía moran en la Antigua Casa de Huéspedes. ¡No hizo falta que le insistiera mucho, por suerte! Sin embargo...'
Pippin extrae una carta sellada de su bolsillo.
'... esta sí que fue una discusión más difícil.
'${PLAYER}, ¿por qué no le das esto a Beregond?'

'¿Qué es esto?'
Beregond abre la carta y empieza a leerla.
'Esta es la misma invitación que el príncipe Faramir recibió. Es la misma invitación que me permitió regresar a Minas Tirith para la boda del Alto Rey... y para ver a mis queridas Gilithel y Bergil.
'¿Esto ha sido obra tuya, Peregrin? ¡No sé qué decir!'
Pippin sonríe a Beregond.
'¡Gracias por darme la oportunidad de estar con mi familia en Minas Tirith, aunque solo sea por una noche!'

'¿Ves? ¡Los hobbits sabemos un par de cosas sobre cómo saltarnos las reglas!
'Gracias, ${PLAYER}.'

'¿Podrías bajar a las cocinas de Merethrond y conseguir tantos platos de comida como puedas llevar? Después de eso, bueno, simplemente date un paseo hasta la Antigua Casa de Huéspedes, ¡donde creo que mis amigos te estarán esperando!

'No permanezcamos más tiempo en el pasado, y miremos a los días venideros.
'Estoy separado de mi amor, pero no será así para siempre. Contemplar tal unión ha dado coraje a mi corazón.
'La próxima vez que vea a Éowyn, sabré qué decir.'

Farmir se encuentra en Merethrond.
Has inspeccionado el cuerno de Boromir, como Faramir te pidió. Deberías hablar con Faramir.

'¡Nunca había conocido un día de solsticio de verano tan alegre!
'Y aún así, estoy pensando en mis problemas. Aquí estoy, el Senescal de Gondor, pero el último de mi linaje. Cuando mi hermano cayó en las tierras de Rohan, su cuerno se partió en dos. Tiempo después llegó a manos de mi padre y ahora está en las mías.
'Es un símbolo del sacrificio de Boromir, ${PLAYER}, uno que no debe ser olvidado por los Pueblos Libres de la Tierra Media. Has conseguido grandes logros sirviendo a mi gente, así que permitiría que lo examinaras.
'Reflexionemos durante un momento recordando a Boromir, hijo de Gondor.'
Habla con Faramir
Examina el cuerno de Boromir

'Oh, si padre pudiera haber estado presente esta noche... y si Boromir también pudiera haberse unido al banquete...
'Padre luchó durante mucho contra la Sombra, y esta había sido su mayor esperanza para Gondor y toda la Tierra Media. Las palabras de Mithrandir en la ceremonia no pasaron desapercibidas, ${PLAYER}. Denethor era un hombre orgulloso, y esa no era su debilidad, sino la fuerza del Enemigo que le retorció la mente en sus últimos años. No pienso mal de él, ni nunca lo haré.
'Después de despertar en las Casas de Sanación, viajé a Rath Dínen. Allí, entre las ruinas de las Casa de los Senescales, recogí una piedra en recuerdo de mi padre.
'Con la coronación del Alto Rey y su boda con Arwen Undómiel, mi padre podrá al fin descansar.
'Toma, ${PLAYER}. Lleva esta piedra y entiérrala junto al esqueje. Que el recuerdo de mi padre se una con las mismísimas raíces del Árbol Blanco.'

'¡Oh, ${PLAYER}, esto es perfecto! Finalmente puedo ponerme a trabajar. Pintar escenas de Minas Tirith con ingredientes reunidos de la ciudad misma... Debo decir que me gusta la idea.
'Gracias por tu arduo trabajo. Una vez que termine, me pintaré un mapa para no perderme aquí nunca más.'

'Las festividades han sido bastante emocionantes, ¿no es así? Han pasado meses desde que pude producir una sola pintura, pero esta visita a Minas Tirith finalmente me ha dado inspiración.
'Desafortunadamente, no puedo poner un pincel en el lienzo hasta que obtenga los ingredientes de pintura. La ciudad es como un laberinto: ya me he perdido seis veces. Si me vuelvo a perder, ¡puede que no encuentre el camino de regreso!
'Quizás tengas mejor suerte. He pedido direcciones... bueno, seis veces antes. Busca al chef Ciriel para obtener carbón, a un alfarero de la Casa de Artesanía para obtener arcilla, y al jardinero Lebadar para obtener flores. Los dos primeros están en el Tercer Círculo, y Lebadar está en el Segundo.'

'¿Carbón de mi madera quemada? ¿Para qué? Oh, no importa. Toma, no lo necesito de todos modos.'
'¿Arcilla, dices? Bueno, claro que puedo darte un poco. Tenemos mucho.'
'¿Flores? Oh, esto es para ese joven pintor, ¿verdad? Lo conocí hace algunos días mientras exploraba la ciudad, pero no ha vuelto desde entonces. Aquí tienes. ¡Dile que le mando saludos!'

'${PLAYER}, your efforts have done what we could only hope: you turned the tide of the war in our favour! We have confirmed that Gorgar's forces have all pulled back to defend Gundabad. The time for the final battle is soon upon us. The others wish to speak with you, and Prince Durin has said he plans to reward you for all your hard work. The Longbeards owe you a great debt, friend!'

'I am not one for all this pomp and high praise, but I must admit, it has been a pleasure working with you, ${PLAYER}. May we fight side by side in the battle to come, and together see Gorgar dead at last!'

'${PLAYER}!'
The dwarf grabs your hand and gives it a hearty shake.
'We have done it! Gorgar's forces are on their last legs, and a great battle is upon us! I swell with pride just imagining it. Let us fight side by side when the time comes, and slay many Orcs together. We will reclaim Gundabad! For the Zhélruka!'

'${PLAYER}, as reward for your efforts, I grant you the rank of Azghzabad, and name you Hero of Durin's Folk. You will have a place in my vanguard as we lead the attack on Gorgar's forces and reclaim Gundabad!
'I must sincerely thank you for your part in this campaign. The war has not yet been won, but because of your actions, we no longer face insurmountable odds. Battle is soon upon us, and I plan to lead this grand army of dwarves to victory!
'You are a great hero, ${PLAYER}, and must receive a hero's reward. Hail, ${PLAYER}, Hero of Durin's Folk!'
The War Nearly Won
En lo profundo de las Montañas Grises, los hobotrasgos traman un plan para liberar a su ama....
Hórin bellows 'I know what they're up to!'
