'${PLAYER}, for your proven heroism, I grant you the rank of Uzkhas of the Gabil'akkâ! I trust you will continue this fine work until the war is won.
'I have another important mission for you. Ausma's scouts have learned of a hobgoblin operation deep in the Grey Mountains. I will allow her to fill you in on the details. Good luck!'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Here for the hobgoblins? This is what I have learned so far:
'We have discovered a hidden cave entrance in the Grey Mountains, on the eastern slopes of Thrumfall. The scouts report hobgoblin and Orc activity inside, but they could not get close enough to see what they were up to. Something about \qswarms of vicious worms\q. They could, however, hear the sounds of digging, or mining, and while I don't know what those Orcs are up to I agree that it warrants investigation.'

'I am glad to be back indoors, ${PLAYER}! That place had an unnatural chill, just like the Anvil. They must have been close to their goal. It is good we arrived when we did, or they might have succeeded in releasing the dragon!
'I will make sure some scouts are posted near the entrance to that cave, in case some hobgoblin gets the bright idea to try to resume their operations. But, to be honest, I have a feeling deep in my bones that we fight the inevitable. You had best be ready to fight her when the time comes, ${PLAYER}. I know I will be.'

'Is everything all right, ${PLAYER}? Hórin looks deathly serious.'
You tell Glóin of Hórin's concern about Hrímil Frost-heart.
'Aye, having such a powerful foe so near concerns me as well. Dragons and other evils slumbering in unknown places deep in the mountains have long caused anxiety for the Longbeards. I am almost ashamed that none of my clan could have joined Hórin on his expedition into the Anvil, but our soldiers had not yet come to Skarháld, and we had only just recovered Dori from the clutches of the drakes. What good would a few old dwarves have done storming into the den of an elder dragon? Hórin has proven he is one of the bravest among us for rushing to stop Karazgar's plot with so few at his side.
'We must carry on as dwarves have done for centuries: keep your eyes on your goal, and take your battles one at a time. I will speak with Prince Durin about ways of defeating that dragon once and for all, but first, we have a war to win!'

Deep in the Grey Mountains, the hobgoblins launch a plot to free their mistress....
Your mission is to investigate Akûl-lagam with Hórin.

'Aye, I overheard your conversation. It seems perfectly obvious to me what those drake-loving hobgoblins are up to! Digging east towards Winterstith can only mean one thing: They are trying to dig their way into the Anvil! We cannot allow them to free Hrímil Frost-heart or the rest of her Frost-horde! I don't know about you, but I think we have enough to deal with right now without the addition of a ferocious elder dragon!
'Let's go clear out that cave before it's too late. Yes, you heard me. I'm going with you!'

Miniaventura: El objetivo marcado

'Hemos pasado sin que nos vieran. Debemos continuar así. Estamos aquí para averiguar adónde irá Gorgar a continuación, y si se huele que tenemos esa información podría cambiar sus planes. ¡Quédate cerca de mí y si nos ven debes impedir que los orcos den la alarma!'

'Bien, hemos averiguado lo que necesitaba saber, pero no servirá. Este era importante y su muerte levantará sospechas. Mmm... tengo una idea.
'Si hacemos que esto parezca un conflicto entre esos dos orcos, nadie sabrá nunca que hemos estado aquí. Pero necesitaremos algunos accesorios. Intenta encontrar un poco de ese apestoso grog que beben. Haremos que esto parezca una trágica \qpelea de borrachos\q ¡Ja!'.

'¿Has encontrado algo de ese brebaje? Agh, puedo olerlo desde aquí. Dámelo.'
Le entregas las botellas de brebaje negro y lo vierte en la boca de cada uno de los orcos muertos, esparciendo luego las botellas por el suelo. Es un montaje bastante convincente.
'¡Así irá bien! Cualquier necio que encuentre a estos dos informará de que se han peleado después de beber demasiado. Algo frecuente entre los orcos. Tenemos la información que necesitábamos, así que volvamos a la base.'

'I will leave you to report our findings to Commander Glóin. It seems the prince's fears about our enemy's strength were well-founded. I will begin planning scouting missions with Hórin, representative of the Zhélruka clan. I hope you are prepared for the amount of work ahead of us!'

You tell Glóin of the massive Orc presence and fortifications at the gates of Gundabad.
'It is as we feared. This promises to be not a simple clash, but a lengthy siege! We must make preparations to prevent an overwhelming defeat on the battlefield and to keep the Orcs from holing up inside the mountains and waiting us out! I ask that you do your part to advance our War Effort. Work with Ausma and Hórin, and slowly, but surely, we will win this war!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Complete Missions to advance the War Effort!</rgb>

The gates of Gundabad are heavily fortified. Only by approaching with stealth will you remain unseen....
Your mission is to scout the main gates of Gundabad with Ausma.

'I hope you are ready, ${PLAYER}, because I will be putting you to work right away! Your first mission will be to scout the main gates of Gundabad itself, but do not worry. I will not be sending you alone. Go and speak with our Scout-master, Ausma. She will be accompanying you into enemy territory.'

'A pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I am Ausma of the Stout-axe clan. The Longbeard prince has named me Scout-master of his army. This was a wise decision, I think, for I possess some skills that the Longbeards and Zhélruka do not. A harsh life in Mordor required those of my clan to learn how to evade the notice of our captors, and of course...'
In a flash, there is a dagger inches from your throat. Ausma grins, and hides the dagger away again.
'...how to conceal our weapons and strike without warning. You may think that is not an \qhonourable\q way to fight, and maybe you are correct, but slaves do not have such luxury. To my people, there was only survival, and the use of such skills proved necessary. If the prince would like me to use my skills to remove the foul Orcs from such a sacred site of his people, I am happy to oblige. And you, ${PLAYER}, will help me in this. Let us begin.'
She points to Gundabad on the large map on the table in front of you.
'Our prize is heavily fortified and swarming with Orcs, trolls, and wargs of all kinds. We will wait until night, slip past their patrols, and see it with our own eyes. The first step of any strategy? The gathering of intelligence. We depart at dusk.'

Miniaventura: El asesinato de Gorgar

'Gorgar está aquí por alguna parte, probablemente tenga algunos de sus orcos con él, pero no sabemos mucho más. Debemos tener cuidado. Oh, y ten cuidado con los trasgos. Son sigilosos, y podrían superarnos en número rápidamente. No lo llaman Ciudad de los Trasgos por nada.'

'Este de allí es él, y el que debe ser el nuevo Gran Trasgo. Esto debe ser lo que los orcos consideran \qdiplomacia\q. Una puerta nos bloquea el camino, y no veo otra forma de pasar. Toma esto, a ver si puedes abrirla.'
Te entrega sus ganzúas.
'Sé que se te están pegando mis malas artes, no lo niegues. Hórin y yo vigilaremos. ¡Una vez que la puerta se abra, atacaremos!'

Ausma está claramente enfadada. Tiene los puños fuertemente apretados, al igual que los dientes bajo su bigote. Para un momento para tomar aire y calmarse.
'¡Maldito sea ese Gorgar! ¡Juro que conseguiré su cabeza algún día! Movámonos. Tenemos que informar de esto a Glóin.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. I know Ausma and Hórin are disappointed that Gorgar escaped, but your contribution to the war effort must not be discounted! Gorgar was forced to retreat, his tail between his legs, and furthermore his alliance with Goblin-town was shattered! Not only that, but much of his army is now in tatters! You will be commended for your hard work.'

Gorgar the Ruthless has been tracked to Goblin-town. Will you find and defeat him in time?
Your mission is to find and defeat Gorgar the Ruthless in Goblin-town.

'Fabarâl ${PLAYER}! I have urgent news!
'Ausma just reported that Gorgar arrived at the Goblin-gate a few hours ago! If her plan is to go ahead, the time is now! Report to her as soon as you can, and good luck! The Gabil'akkâ is counting on you!'

'Are you ready, ${CLASS}? We know where Gorgar is. Let us strike before he slips through our fingers! Oh, and Hórin here has requested to join us; he said something about wanting to do more than just stand around in an old fort!'
She shrugs and looks to Hórin, grinning. Hórin gets flustered, mutters about saying no such thing, and turns away, blushing.
'I will get us unseen through as much of Goblin-town as I can, but... we may have to wade through some goblins. Let me know when you are prepared!'

'I already told Glóin that we failed in our mission, but he wishes to speak with you himself.'
Ausma is clearly still angry about Gorgar's escape. You try to lift her spirits by telling her that although the particulars of the mission were failed, the defeat of the Great Goblin and the severing of the alliance between Goblin-town and Gundabad must count as successes. She sighs loudly and allows you to see the slightest hint of a smile.
'You are right of course, ${PLAYER}, but my quarry has evaded me, and I will not be satisfied until he lies dead. Go on, go talk to Glóin. Don't keep him waiting!'

'Bien, hemos conseguido que no nos vean. Ten, toma unos cuantos más de estos.'
Te entrega otra bolsa de pequeños explosivos.
'Si queremos causar tanto daño como podamos, ¡tenemos que abandonar el sigilo y empezar a utilizar la pólvora! ¡Destruye tantas armas y armaduras como puedas antes de que nos descubran! No te preocupes, nos sacaré de aquí antes de que nos superen.'

'Nos estamos quedando sin tiempo. ¡Hay demasiado aquí para poder destruirlo nosotros solos! Y nos hemos topado con algunos orcos, ¿pero dónde está el resto? Un fuerte de este tamaño debe tener más soldados, incluso aunque estuvieran preparándose para moverse... espera, ¿has oído eso?'

'¿Has oído eso? Debe ser el intendente. Sonaba como si los demás orcos estuvieran arriba, ¡y borrachos! Cambio de planes, ${PLAYER}.
'Propongo que vayamos silenciosamente al piso de arriba y terminemos con el que está al mando antes de que al resto de los orcos se les pase la borrachera y se den cuenta de que estamos destruyendo sus suministros. Sin el intendente estos orcos no podrán organizarse lo suficiente para continuar con sus planes de mover todo a Gundabad, y puedo enviar a otros exploradores a continuar con el trabajo. ¡En marcha!'

'${PLAYER}, for your continued effort, I grant you the rank of Izkhas of the Gabil'akkâ! It is well earned, my friend!
'There is little time to celebrate, however. I have another important mission for you. Our scouts have discovered the location of the Orcs' main armoury outside of Gundabad. It seems to be their main base for waging more extensive war in the region, but we fear they may soon move their weapon and armour stockpiles into Gundabad itself, preparing for a siege. We have an opportunity to prevent that from happening! Report to Ausma as soon as you can.'
'We made it back before we were overrun! Great work as always, ${PLAYER}. Go report our success to Commander Glóin!'

You tell Glóin of your successful attack on the armoury.
'That sounds rather harrowing, ${PLAYER}! I am impressed! Ausma has proven quite capable as well, but I am beginning to grow concerned that her plans are too reckless. It would not do to lose either of you, so take some care and temper Ausma's brashness with some caution! For now, go and get some rest. I will call upon you again soon.'

Dâr Brulku, a fort near Gundabad, holds the Orcs' main stockpile of weapons and armour....
Your mission is to infiltrate Dâr Brulku with Ausma and destroy the weapons and armour within.

'Ready for work, ${PLAYER}? We've had a lucky find!'
She points to an exterior fort near the main gate of Gundabad.
'This is Dâr Brulku. This fort holds the Orcs' main stockpile of weapons and armour. From it they arm their raiding parties and the guards that defend the gates. They know a battle is coming, however, and have begun to move the stockpile into Gundabad itself. If the two of us sneak past enemy lines and infiltrate that fort before they can move the stockpile, we can destroy it before they even realize what happened!
'We shouldn't wait too long, or we will miss this chance. We will need the cover of darkness to make it that far. Meet me here tonight.'

'Este es el lugar. Debo ser honesto, ${PLAYER}. Después de nuestro fallido asalto al Yunque, estoy ansioso por vengarme de la Horda de Escarcha y sus secuaces por el ataque a Skarháld. Y sobre todo, debemos hacer todo lo posible para evitar que Hrimil sea liberada. Si atacara a nuestro ejército durante la batalla, ¡sería catastrófico!'
Hace una pausa mientras se pierde en sus pensamientos. Puedes notar que su experiencia en El Yunque todavía le afecta mucho. Se da cuenta de que lo estás mirando y se sonroja.
'¡N... No me tomes por un cobarde, ${PLAYER}! ¡Estoy más que dispuesto a enfrentarme de nuevo a ese dragón! Algún día, tendremos que hacerlo para acabar con su reinado sobre estas montañas de una vez por todas. ¡Solo que no quiero que ese día sea hoy! Vamos, pongámonos a trabajar.'

'Este frío tan extraño... Llegamos justo a tiempo, ${PLAYER}. Juro que puedo oír a ese maldito dragón al otro lado de esta pared.
'Si hemos terminado, vámonos. ¡No tengo deseo alguno de quedarme aquí congelándome!'

'Esta puerta no es algo natural, ${PLAYER}. ¡Lo he visto antes! Esos hobotrasgos están invocando un frío antinatural con su magia oscura para bloquear el camino. ¡Tendremos que derrotarlos para poder avanzar!'

Miniaventura: La puerta principal

'Estamos cerca. Deberíamos salir del camino para evitar ser vistos por las patrullas orcas.
'El plan es avanzar hacia el puente evitando a tantos orcos como podamos y echar un mejor vistazo a las puertas principales. Quédate cerca de mí, y si nos descubren, ¡no dejes que llamen a sus aliados! ¡Termina con ellos rápidamente! No queremos que los orcos sepan que estamos aquí.'
'Tenemos que seguir moviéndonos. Alguien podría venir a investigar el ruido. ¿Continuamos?'

'No tenían ninguna oportunidad. Si fueran inteligentes, habrían enviado a uno de ellos a alertar al resto de nuestra presencia y a buscar refuerzos. Pero son orcos, y su orgullo les ha jugado una mala pasada.
'Ahora que estamos cerca, veamos cómo es la puerta principal.'
Mira al otro lado del río y hace una mueca.
'Está lleno de orcos, sin duda, pero no veo muchas barreras. Ese orco grande de allí debe ser Gorgar. Además, debemos suponer que esta multitud es solo una pequeña fracción de los orcos que viven dentro de la montaña. He visto y oído suficiente. Vámonos de aquí.'
Ves muchos orcos al otro lado del río, ¡incluyendo al que debe ser Gorgar!

'I have heard your mission was a success! Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. When next I call upon you, it will be to enter Goblin-town with Ausma and defeat Gorgar the Ruthless. Prepare yourself!'

To end this war, Gorgar the Ruthless must be defeated. But first, he must be found….
Your mission is to infiltrate Bekâr-zarakh with Ausma and find Gorgar's location.

Ausma greets you with a grin.
'We know now where Gorgar is heading next: Goblin-town! I'll prepare a plan of attack, and have the scouts watch the Goblin-gate. When he arrives, we will strike!'

'${PLAYER}, you have shown your worth to our cause. I grant you the rank of Fabarâl of the Gabil'akkâ! This is the highest rank I am able to give as your commander. Thank you for all you have done.
'Your efforts have significantly weakened the Orc forces, but we will not have won this war until Gorgar the Ruthless himself lies dead. You may be aware that Ausma has certain... talents... that will aid us in this endeavour. Report to her at once!'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. The time to cut the head off this snake has finally come!'
She whips out her dagger, and mimes slicing the head off an Orc, cackling gleefully.
'The prince has given me permission to plan the assassination of our nemesis, Gorgar the Ruthless. Without the son of Bolg, the Orcs and their allies will quickly fall to in-fighting as they try to determine who next gets to be in charge. During the chaos, we can easily mop them up and take our prize: Gundabad!
'But first, we need to find him. We will infiltrate this tower outside Gundabad's main gates.'
She points to a tower on the map, just outside the keep.
'We believe this is where they plan their troop deployments. If Gorgar intends to leave the mountain for any reason, they will deploy a number of guards to keep him safe. And he WILL leave at some point. If Orcs are to be kept in line, they need to see their chieftain in the flesh from time to time. I bet if we snoop around this tower, we will learn when and where Gorgar will next appear. Let me know when you're ready to head out.'

Miniaventura: La línea de suministro secreta

'Este es sin duda el túnel correcto. Los trasgos deben haber excavado en esta antigua mina Barbiluenga y descubierto que conduce directamente a Gundabad. ¡Menos mal que no hemos tenido que dar todo el rodeo! Ahora que hemos encontrado la línea de suministros, es hora de hacer algo de daño. Estos necios... pensaron que no nos daríamos cuenta de que estaban moviendo suministros bajo tierra y no asignaron muchos guardias para proteger la caravana, ¡pero somos enanos! Estamos tan a gusto bajo las montañas como ellos. ¡Se arrepentirán de su error!
'Necesitamos encontrar al capataz al cargo y derrotarlo. Supongo que estará cerca del frente. Toma esto.' \Saca una bolsa y te la entrega. Ausma sonríe maliciosamente mientras ves que dentro hay un buen número de pequeños explosivos.
'Quizá haya aprendido algunos trucos durante mi época en Mordor. Uno de esos debería ser suficiente para acabar con cada uno de esos carros. Destruye los suministros a medida que avancemos. Si tenemos éxito aquí, ¡podríamos paralizar la llegada de suministros a Gundabad durante semanas! ¡Vamos!'

'¡Mira lo que le han hecho a este lugar! Malditos orcos asquerosos. Tengo una idea. Podemos destruir esta repugnante profanación del arte enano y eliminar este túnel como ruta de suministro a Gundabad de una vez por todas.
'Deberías echarte un poco hacia atrás.'

'Good to hear, though I am not surprised! I assigned this important mission to you because I knew you would succeed! The Orcs will sorely miss those supplies, but we must keep up the pressure to prevent Gorgar from gaining the upper hand.
'Something about this troubles me, however. It was my understanding that Gundabad lost control of Goblin-town with the death of the Hobgoblin Warlord, Shárnakh. Does this mean a new Great Goblin has come to power, and he has opened diplomatic channels with Gorgar? I will send some scouts to look into the matter. Meanwhile, keep up the fight! This war is far from over!'

Deep in the Misty Mountains, the Orcs and goblins use a secret tunnel to move supplies between Goblin-town and Gundabad....
Your mission is to stop the supply trains in the secret tunnel between Goblin-town and Gundabad.

'${PLAYER}, for your contribution to the war effort, I hereby grant you the rank of Dumul within the Gabil'akkâ, the Unified Army of Dwarves.
'You have helped us tremendously, but this war is far from over! It is time to hit them where it really hurts: their supply lines! Report to Scout-master Ausma at once. She will fill you in on our plans.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. Commander Glóin has charged us with a pressing task. My scouts have discovered a secret tunnel in the Misty Mountains, connecting Goblin-town and Gundabad. We believe they are using it to move supplies into Gundabad to prepare it for a siege. If they still believe we do not know of these supply trains, they may not be heavily guarded. This is the time to strike!
'We will move out when you are ready, but don't take too long or we will miss this opportunity!'
'You do fine work, ${PLAYER}. We have surely set the Orcs back weeks in their efforts to prepare Gundabad for a long siege. You should inform Commander Glóin of our success.'

'¡Te doy la bienvenida, ${PLAYERNAME:aventurero[m]|aventurera[f]}! ¡La llamada a la guerra de nuestro príncipe debe de haberte llegado! Querrá hablar contigo de inmediato. ¡Sube a la sala de guerra a toda prisa!'

'Te doy la bienvenida, ${PLAYER}. Me alegra contar con la ayuda de aventureros valientes como tú. Hay mucho que hacer antes de la batalla que se avecina.
'Nos enfrentamos a un enorme ejército de orcos, troles, huargos, trasgos y quién sabe qué otras inmundas criaturas acechan en esa fortaleza de la montaña. Su líder es Gorgar el Despiadado, hijo de Bolg y nieto de Azog. Todos los enanos conocen esos nombres, pues nos enfrentamos a esos viles comandantes en la última gran Guerra de los Enanos y los Orcos.
'Tengo a un ejército de Barbiluengos, Zhélruka e incluso unos cuantos Hachas Recias respaldándome, pero me temo que nuestros enemigos nos superan en número con creces. Debemos ser astutos y hacer lo que podamos para debilitar a nuestros enemigos antes de enfrentarnos a ellos en el campo de batalla. Preséntate ante uno de mis comandantes a cargo de esta expedición de guerra, el héroe barbiluengo Glóin. Él dirigirá tus esfuerzos allí donde más se necesiten.'

Introduction: Elderslade

'Why the great ${CLASS} comes to the Rushgate! Humble Rúzat is very happy to see you again. You have done so much for the Zhélruka already! Now that you are here, Gundabad will certainly belong to the Zhélruka once more! Oh do not worry, other brave heroes are here too. I did not mean to put the weight of the entire march on your shoulders, my friend!'

You have received a summons from Agátur the Boastful to join him at the fortress of Skarháld in Ered Mithrin. The Longbeard Dwarves have called for all their friends and allies to proceed to Skarháld as soon as they are able. The time to retake Gundabad is at hand.

'${PLAYER}, I am glad to see you! The march to Gundabad has begun! Many of us have set forth from Ered Mithin with our paths taking us through Elderslade. All sights are on Gundabad! I knew that you, one of our greatest allies, would march by our side. When you are ready, travel west to the Rushgate. I will meet you in Elderslade at Annâk-khurfu.'

Quite surprisingly the letter is addressed to you....
'${PLAYER},
'It would seem that you have finally stumbled upon my true lair in the north. I find it unsurprising that you would be the first to discover Wyrmsgráf, for I consider you a formidable opponent. The other hideouts you have uncovered, mere decoys to appear careless to my adversaries. I am sure you knew that already. I do find it fitting to make my home in the north over the plundered hoard of Scatha, the Dragon I could not tame, the Dragon that cursed me so.
'There is no need to search for me here. I have left the north to rot. The Frost-horde and the dwarves shall do more damage to each other than I could have ever dreamt up. I wander east, to search for a cure. Until we meet again, ${CLASS}.
'Karazgar'

'I find it strange that Karazgar would leave a letter for you, his enemy. Could the former servant of Sauron one day be redeemed? I know not.
'Only one question remains. What happened to Wrothbláda? It is still missing after all of this. I hoped to find it among Karazgar's belongings. Alas, this has not come to pass. I would surmise Karazgar took Wrothbláda with him when he left the north. We know that he held a respect for the sword.'

'By Durin's Beard! We have found it! The lost hoard of Scatha, the Worm!
'I am stunned my friend. I never thought I would see this piece of history with my own two eyes. Would you collect some of the treasures for me so that we can bring them to the Longbeards as proof that the long lost hoard has finally been found? King Thorin will be pleased!'

'To think that we have been able to renew the legacy of Fram the Foremost! Even so, I consider his legacy in the lords of the Ai-thúda was brought to a proud conclusion with Thíudric.
'Thíudric proved the most beloved lord of the Ai-thúda since Fram, and his reign lasted longer than any lord during their time in the Wells. He threw back no fewer than five incursions by the Orcs of Hithaeglir.'

'That is correct, Fróthi. Thíudric even sent riders south for the first time in generations to attend the court of Steward Belegorn in Gondor. Under his rule of sixty-two years, the Ai-thúda prospered as never before.
'My friend, I cannot thank you enough for your company on this journey into my people's history. If not for you, I would not now be returning home to Rohan, ready to pen the history of the Rohirrim. I shall give you credit where credit is due in my writings as you made some of the historical discoveries that I will write about within the pages of my manuscript!
'Fróthi, ${PLAYER}, I thank you both deeply for your contributions. We shall see each other for a time at Annâk-khurfu, then we shall part our separate ways. Please, you are more than welcome to come visit me at any time in Rohan! Take care my friends!'
'Aye, Thíudric was seen well in the eyes of dwarf-sages. He befriended King Thorin and even gifted him some of the treasures Fram had kept from Scatha's hoard!'

'Now, there is but one final task remaining on this journey. We must enter the fabled cavern of Wyrmsgráf and search for what lies within. Will we find more signs of Karazgar? Will we find any of Scatha's hoard? Let us find out!'

'I am glad that you spotted the cairn! I did not see it!'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Gundolávi swore, as he entered the gates, that he would return bearing the heads of every Orc-chief he found within. Two weeks later, the gates opened again, and the Orcs flung out the heads of all who had entered, last of all Gundolávi and his sons.'

'Hmm, it seems the map ends here at this fork in the pass. Shall we rest a moment then? I will conclude my tale while we rest.
'Following Gundolávi's death, his brother Thíudric became lord at the age of seventeen. Thíudric was a more thoughtful man than his brother and father had been, and his first act was to declare that neither he, nor any other of his blood, would ever again seek to set foot inside the Mountain-hold.'

'There does not seem to be any other direction forward but to continue along the Drekvath River.'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Hildáric died of a sudden illness at the age of sixty-five. It has long been rumoured to have been poison. Gundobad appeared at his funeral to lay claim to lordship. He was challenged in this by Hildigar, Hildáric’s son, and the two fought for the right to rule the Ai-thúda. In the end, Gundobad cut Hildigar down, taking back rule over his people.'

'I knew there was a river here in Elderslade, but I did not know the Drekvath to flow from so far in the north.'
Fróthi interjects into Léothred's tale for a moment.
'Léothred, did you know that Hildáric is seen as a good leader in the eyes of dwarves? During his reign, the Dwarves of Erebor came north to settle the kingdom of Grárik in Ered Mithrin. Rather than dwelling on the troubles between their peoples, Hildáric made peace with King Thorin I and welcomed him to the north. Relations between Durin’s Folk and the Ai-thúda remained cordial, though seldom warm, during the rest of the time they dwelt beside each other.'

'Thank you Fróthi for that perspective. I say, had hot-headed Gundobad been lord when Thorin arrived, matters might have taken a much less friendly turn! It would seem the depiction of Hildáric in later tales has obscured this fact. According to the minstrels, Hildáric sought war against the dwarves, and it was only his death and Gundobad’s rise to take his place that kept that from happening! It is a shame when the truth of the matter becomes lost in years.'
Léothred pauses for a moment.
'Come, let us continue the journey along this river. The location the map leads us to can not be far!'

'I am sure that if we continue north, we will find the trail again.'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Gundobad's son, Gundolávi, was little better. He was a bellicose man who found joy in nothing more than hunting and battle, he is said to have slain more than thirty trolls and at least five giants. In the end, the pride of his line overcame him, and like his grandfather and father he sought to enter Gundabad. Unlike them, however, he succeeded, finding a way inside the Mountain-hold, accompanied by his two sons and many mighty warriors of his household.'

'It almost feels as if whoever made this map was hiding it from someone.'
Léothred continues his tale.
'At first Gundobad proved as poor a lord as Hildáric had feared, and made three bloody and rash attempts to enter the Mountain-hold before his own thanes begged him to stop spending the blood of his people on such folly. Afterwards, his temper eased, and he ruled indifferently to the age of fifty-three, growing fat from food and mead until his heart gave out.'

'Songs sung among the Ai-thúda call Hildáric a usurper, false and cruel, and even imply that he himself slew his brother to become lord. I believe that Hildáric was in fact a prudent ruler, if not kind, serving his people nobly but unremarkably, rather than following any lust for glory.'
Léothred pauses for a moment.
'Well then, I am eager to return to following this map. What say you, ${PLAYER}?'

'Yes, Karazgar knew that something was amiss when word reached him that Scatha's teeth, a quite offensive gift if I do say, had been given to dwarves. We can agree that Fram knew enough about the dwarves' disdain of dragons to know that a necklace of dragon's teeth would not be sufficient for Thráin. Scatha's hoard was entirely stolen dwarf riches after all! At this moment, Fram was no longer useful to Karazgar and so, in Karazgar's mind, Fram had to die.'

'Fram the Foremost never got the chance to make proper amends with Thráin. He set forth from his hall on a journey to Scatha's hoard, but never returned. When his sons went forth to seek him, they found him slain, pierced by dwarf-arrows and surrounded by the bodies of several dwarf warriors.'

'Unavoidably, the Ai-thúda blamed the dwarves, though King Thráin disavowed the deed and mourned his one-time friend. He made no more claim on Scatha's hoard, much of which remained lost, for Fram alone knew the exact whereabouts of the Worm's lair. The bond between the Ai-thúda and the Longbeards was not mended until this most recent war, the War of the Ring.'

'Fróthi and I have discussed everything that we have learned from our journey together. Yes, I believe that the map on Scatha's tooth was indeed carved by Fram. The visions you had help to answer the questions for which we have come searching. The truth that Fróthi and I agree upon is this:
'In Fram's dealings with Thráin, he very much wanted to share the treasures and location of Scatha's hoard. The blood pact Fram made with Karazgar certainly prevented this. Remember, ${PLAYER}, this is the same Fram who befriended the Holbytlan! The Holbytlan are a cautious people and would only befriend those with kindness in them! Yes, something about the blood pact clouded Fram's judgement and made him grow ever suspicious towards the dwarves. We believe, in a moment of clarity, Fram carved the route to Scatha's hoard on one of the Scatha's teeth.'

'Thanks to Fróthi for deciphering the map thus far. We have not lost the trail yet!'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Hildáric became lord of the Ai-thúda after his brother’s disappearance, though matters grew complicated six months later when Bryngertha, Gundáric's widow, gave birth to a son. She called the boy Gundobad, a play on the name of the hall where his father had vanished. When he was born, Hildáric promised to cede lordship to him once he came of age.'

'This pass is not on my map of Elderslade. Fróthi, what of yours? Hmm, it looks like the map on Scatha's tooth has led us to this rocky pass. Could this map lead to Scatha's cave or even his hoard? There is but one way to find out! First, let us rest here for a moment.'
Léothred continues his tale.
'When Gundobad learned the meaning of his name, and of his father's fate, a zeal awoke within him. He would succeed where Gundáric had not, and lead a host of Ai-thúda to conquer Gundabad! Hildáric begged him to reconsider, but he refused, so when Gundobad was of age, Hildáric refused to honour his promise, and remained Lord of Framabárg.'

'This is a very exciting discovery! If this map was carved by Fram, it certainly changes how we should perceive this missive to the dwarves. With all the layers of dust on this tooth, I would say the tooth had not been touched since Thráin discarded the necklace in some forgotten vault of Erebor.
'Now I have more questions than answers, as any historian should. What I do know, however, is that we must follow this map to see where it leads. We should head to the shores of Dvergvát as soon as we are ready!'

'It worries me that we did not find a cairn or some sort of marking here. Let us press on towards the next mark on the map in hopes that it lead us in the right direction!'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Sadly, Gisilhári met with tragedy himself soon after feasting his victory. Flush with pride, and plenty of ale, he declared his intent to name himself King of the Thíuda. He sought out the mearas, announcing his intent to tame and ride one. The attempt ended in failure, and not for the last time among the masters of the Ai-thúda. The mearh he chose threw him, and in the fall he broke his back. He was unable to walk afterward, and died at the age of forty-two, older than any lord of his people since Frumgar, but still far too young.'

'This cairn indeed looks quite old. Perhaps this is the starting point of the map! We must now seek the second marking on the map.
'While we travel, I will continue to recall the tales of Fram's legacy. I believe I had talked of Gundamári. After Gundamári's death, the lordship fell to Fram's youngest son, who had been just five years old when his father died. Gisilhári, who had always seemed less hot-blooded than his brothers, proved to be the most fortunate of the siblings. Under his careful command the Ai-thúda pushed back against the Orcs, winning several decisive battles before finally breaking them and slaying their chief in a great battle by Dvergvát, these very shores.'

'I believe that we are still on the trail. Let us continue.'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Gundáric was an adventurous youth, and had bragged that he would one day be the first Man to enter the Mountain-hold and behold the wonders within. Two years into his reign, he defied the warnings of his advisors, including his younger brother Hildáric. The fool rode to Gundabad's gates and was never seen again.'

'Ah, another cairn, similar to the one we found on the shores of Dvergvát. It would seem we are following the map correctly after all!'
Léothred continues his tale.
'Gundahári, Gisilhári's son, succeeded him and ruled unremarkably, but well enough. For the first time the Ai-thúda knew true prosperity in the Wells, and they flourished, building many homes in Misthallow and grazing their herds across the Floodfells and even into the valleys of Mithrin. He died peacefully at sixty, and was succeeded by his son Gundáric.'

'Hmm, let me take a closer look at these markings.... Yes, I see they are indeed carved. These markings are too precise to have been made from any battles the worm was in.... Hmm, for a moment I had wondered if this was a runic inscription, but I have studied much of Rói's Edda-stone in Erebor and these markings are not any form of dwarf-writing, that much is certain!
'Oh! Do you see this curved marking, with the round indent in its centre?! It is different than the others, and if I am not mistaken looks exactly like the lake of Dvergvát, here in Elderslade! I believe this is a map! It is a crude map, but a map all the same!'

'Fróthi and I agree that we should begin our search in Elderslade with the necklace made from Scatha's teeth. Since it is a relic of those days which we can closely examine, perhaps it will provide a clue as to where Scatha hid. I am no expert on beasts, but to a trained eye, a beast's teeth may tell one much about a creature's eating habits and natural surroundings.
'Perhaps you should take a closer look at the teeth, ${PLAYER}. You have much more experience with beasts than either Fróthi or myself.'

'The taking of Zudramdân was barely a battle, ${PLAYER}. Most of the Orcs just fled, instead of fighting. If you ask me, I found it quite odd. I would be grateful if you were to defeat some Orcs in Elderslade. Those who fled Zudramdân could not have gotten far.'
'Good work, ${PLAYER}. We will hold onto Zudramdân for as long as we can. I am weary of the growing numbers of Orcs by the walls of Gundabad. I see more with each passing hour.'

'I have just received word that the Gabil'akkâ have secured Zudramdân, to the north! This is indeed a victory, as Zudramdân is a strategic point for staging an assault against Gundabad. You must travel to Zudramdân immediately, as we will need as many warriors there as is possible. On your way there, place some banners along the road to bring strength to all in the Gabil'akkâ!
'I believe that our friend, Náth, was one of the group that took Zudramdân. If you see him, give him my thanks!'

A Rocky Obstacle

You have successfully cleared the road and put a halt to the rock slides that have been threatening all those who enter Elderslade. Tales of your deeds will surely reach Foreman Brumbur, who will certainly be pleased with your efforts. It concerns you, however, that the forces of Gundabad have done much to scar this sacred landscape.

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. I hope that your travels since Járnfast have been prosperous. Yes, I have decided to leave the iron mines for once and help my kin who journey towards Gundabad. You see, digging the mines in Járnfast is not that different from building a bridge. In fact I build bridges over chasms in the mines all of the time!
'Indeed, I consider it an honour to oversee the building of these temporary bridges and put my skills to good use! Now that we are able to safely set foot in Elderslade, there is another matter that needs attending. The road ahead is dangerous, for landslides seem numerous around here! Would you be able to tend to the road, and clear it of debris so that the path is once again safe for those who travel further west? If I had more time, I would investigate these landslides, for I believe something is causing them!'

To Drenghól

'How did you know that we were here, ${CLASS}?! Oh, Náth told you? I suppose that is all right then, as we captured Zudramdân together. A few of us went on to establish this small but very well hidden encampment. What do you think? Yes, it is quite well hidden!
'We are scouting the outer walls of Gundabad. Will you assist us? Good, good!'

'Did you find any hidden entrances into Gundabad or any weaknesses in the enemies defences? Nor did I! Bah, between these well organized Orcs and impeccable dwarf-craft, we are up against quite an enemy force here!'

'A few dwarves went on ahead, though I begged them not to. It is too dangerous to the west. I gave them a warning, but I am not here to argue with them. I am here to win this war. I would appreciate it if you would search for them. The last I heard they had found a cave under a statue. Drenghól I think it was called. I am sure they could use assistance. They are behind enemy lines, after all!'

'You have assisted everyone at Annâk-khurfu? You always seem to find a way to impress me, ${PLAYER}! Now then, let us see how your talents might best serve the Gabil'akkâ next.'

'Ah, there you are! What took you so long? Did Rúzat put you to work at the Rushgate? Bah, I knew it. Does he not know that time is of the utmost importance in order for the Gabil'akkâ to succeed?
'Now then, enough idle chatter, there is much to be done here at Annâk-khurfu! I know that I can count on you, ${PLAYER}. That is why I am giving you these important tasks. Come talk to me again when you have completed them!'

'We march to Gundabad, together. All of us who march, we are all the Gabil'akkâ, the Great Force!
'Are you on your way to Annâk-khurfu? You must be, as the Rushgate is but the start of the march! Could you do something for me on your way to Annâk-khurfu, my friend? I want to lift the spirits of all those in the Gabil'akkâ. Let us raise banners along the path, as it is now under control of the Gabil'akkâ!
'Oh and one more thing. Could you investigate the small encampment of Khadâsh-gâra for me? I am not sure what the dwarves there doing to keep themselves busy!'

'Ah the great fighter. We meet again! I wish that I was in a better mood to regale stories with you, ${CLASS}. It is not so, for a scouting party under my command has gone missing.
'We must find this scouting party. I know each of those who I send to scout Elderslade. They are all good dwarves and would do the same if either of us had gone missing. I know I shouldn't, but I fear the worst.'

A Call To War

'${PLAYER}, you have done much upon the battlefield and certainly assisted us in turning the tides of war. All those in the Gabil'akkâ are indebted to you. We will celebrate together soon enough!
'There is still much more to be done, however. When you are able, talk to Stálskeg Ironbeard at Annâk-khurfu. He is a trusted ally and has many tasks yet in our continued push towards the gates of Gundabad.'
'Zudramdân is lost. The bombardment from the siege engines was too great. It will be a hard push to break through the Gates of Gundabad from here.'
'${PLAYER}, I am ready for battle. Let us make the best of our skill on this day! I will do my part to keep the moral of the Gabil'akkâ high!'
'Have you come to assist us in the continued war efforts? Good! Hlóthi and I here have many tasks for you. The Gabil'akkâ will prevail!'
'I am glad that you have all safely returned from Drenghól. There is little time, ${PLAYER}. Gather what you can and prepare yourself. War is at hand!'
'Aye, we have established trenches where we were able and pushed back the first assault. Assist in the battle where you can, ${RACE}.'
'Do you hear that?! The drums of war! We must vacate our hidden camp at once and join the front lines, ${PLAYER}!'
The War of Three Peaks has begun!

Talk to Vídar
Talk to Yrsa Spearwife in Limlók
Talk to Vídar at one of his three favourite scouting locations
Glóin is focused on preparing the ravens. He has not noticed you.
'I need to think, and these constant questions are not helping!'

'Find Vídar on his patrol and ensure he does not run into harm. There are three places he enjoys to scout, to the south-east, south, and south-west of the village. Look for him at one of these locations and safe-guard Vídar, and I will remember your good-hearted assistance.'
'Your friends have gathered behind the lodge to release the messenger-ravens. You should join them.'
The bear cub snorts in your direction, but you cannot guess at its meaning. Is this Vídar? You hope so, both for your sake and his!

'Vídar returned and spoke of your prowess! Thank you for keeping an eye on him, ${PLAYER}.'
You are relieved to learn that the bear cub was Yrsa's son Vídar after all. On the journey back to Limlók you had not been entirely certain.
'Your friends have gathered behind the lodge to release the messenger-ravens. You should join them.'
'Are they ready or not? What is the delay?'

'Ah, these will do nicely, thank you. I need to decide how to phrase this message, and then copy it onto each of these papers. I need to...'
Glóin looks up with barely-disguised irritation.
'I need to concentrate, and this child has peppered me with questions ever since I began! Yes, yes, I told you once! This one is Vaka, and this one is Telgja. Their names mean Vigilant and Cutter, if you must know.'
Glóin masters his tone, and speaks again to you.
'And this one here is Hjála, which means Chatter, and I daresay he and this Beorning child have much in common! Can you keep this child entertained while I prepare these messages, ${PLAYER}? I need to think, and these constant questions are not helping!'

'Do they fly very high? How do they know where to go? What's the farthest they've ever flown before?'
Vídar pauses for air, and you manage to interject a question. The child considers it briefly.
'Have I any chores that need doing? Well, yes, I suppose. I am nearly a man grown, after all, and Mother says it is my job to scout outside Limlók once a week. I will go do that now, if you will let her know! You have already met her, yes? Her name is Yrsa.
'All right, I am leaving now. But I want to learn more about the ravens when I get back!'

'It is true, I told Vídar that as he grows into a man he must shoulder further duties around the village. That includes scouting the wilderness outside Limlók, but I did not expect him to choose to do so immediately after an attack by an Orc raiding-party!
'He has always been a bold boy. I should have expected it, after all! Perhaps you can ease a mother's worries by finding him on his patrol and ensuring he does not run into harm? There are three places he enjoys to scout, to the south-east, south, and south-west of the village. Look for him at one of these locations and safe-guard Vídar, and I will remember your good-hearted assistance.
'It will also keep him out from underfoot your dwarves, which I know they will appreciate. Vídar always has so many questions.'
'I am almost ready to go!'
'Will you ask Runerik for some parchment upon which I can write these messages of warning? I brought the birds, it is true, but I seem to have left my papers behind.'

'There is a box of parchment near the task board, and the people of Limlók use its contents to post requests and other messages on the board. You can give him some parchment from that box, if you must.'

'The ravens have been sent? Fine, fine.'
Runerik's brows crease with a new thought.
'I should have read the messages before your dwarf friend released the ravens. He has not called an entire company of dwarves here, has he?'
'The messages are sent. Now it is up to the Longbeards to do what must be done. I will decide for myself whether to continue with this endeavour.'
Glóin has attracted some attention while he readies his ravens

'Find Annâk-khurfu and see the great host that musters for the assault on Gundabad, ${PLAYER}.'

'Well if it isn't ${PLAYER}! Are you here to join Durin's great assault upon Gundabad? Perfect, perfect! Do you remember when we set afire to that goblin camp near the High Pass? Good times, my friend, great memories! I do not suppose you still have any of Gandalf's flammable draught with you, do you?
'Ah, pity. We will just have to make do with what we can, and find new and interesting ways to burn up the schemes of Gundabad. I have no doubt we will think of something, my combustible friend!'

'I am glad to see you are safe, ${PLAYER}. I was not in Khazad-dûm when the Iron Garrison fell, and it is hard to come by news of what happened within. I have heard enough to know it sounds bad.'
Slagvi shakes his head.
'I had gone back to the Iron Hills to collect some drawings I left in Járnfast. It is such a foolish reason! I wanted to compare the design of the Cooling Chamber with some plans I remembered drawing in my youth... and that is why I was not there when the Garrison failed. It may be why I am still alive today, and so many of the workers and miners with whom I toiled are not.
'When I learned that Prince Durin was assembling a great force to reclaim Gundabad, I could not refuse his call. Is this why I was spared? Perhaps, friend, perhaps. But I am glad to know you are here too. We accomplished much in the Great Delving, ${PLAYER}... for a time.'

'Hail, my friend! Once again we are on the doorstep of danger! We last met in the cave of Filgogân outside the walls of Moria, and you helped me learn the fate of my friend Lofrik: dead, alas! But he is here too, in a way, for I embedded his golden tooth in the haft of my axe, as I promised to do.
'Together Trausti and Lofrik will slay many Orcs on behalf of Prince Durin! Gundabad will be ours again!'

'So many have come to fight for us: Longbeards, Zhélruka, and even a number of Stout-axes! The Orcs who squat within Gundabad will tremble before this great force, this Gabil'akkâ! The Mountain-home is nearly ours again!'
Prince Ingór of the Zhélruka nods at your approach
Stóthkell's good eye lights up with recognition as you approach
Thettmárr and Líkmund are playing a runic dice game and gambling
Thorgest and Afwald greet you warmly and ask for news of your adventures

The war camp is bustling with dwarves preparing for their upcoming assault on Gundabad.
You should speak to the dwarves assembled on the lower level of Annâk-khurfu.

'I commanded the establishment of a war camp from which we will launch our assault upon Gundabad. Let us find it! Many old dwarf-keeps dot the foothills of Elderslade, and my warriors are certain to have chosen one of these. I do not know which one, but I do know the name it will be given: Annâk-khurfu, the camp of return, for is this not the first step in the return of my people to the Mountain-home?
'The war camp is likely to the north-west of here, inside one of the old dwarf-keeps.'
'Look for the war camp, my friend. I commanded it be established within one of the abandoned keeps that dot the foothills of Elderslade, and it is likely to be found north-west of here.'

'So you made it,' Prince Ingór says flatly. He hefts his weapon, testing its balance, and stares at you silently for a moment. When he speaks again, there is an edge to his words.
'Your deeds are well-known to all, even to the Zhélruka, and I do not doubt your mettle. But you are a friend of Durin and his Longbeards. Will you fight with such fervour on behalf of Zhélruka too? My brother Ótek is king now in the lands to the east, but he did not send me here to fight for Longbeards or their friends. He sent me here to reclaim the delvings that were promised to our ancestors of old.
'If you will help me and my people in this, we will have no difficulty fighting by your side. If not...'
The Zhélruka prince weighs his axe-handle thoughtfully, and turns away.

'You still live, ${PLAYER}! I take it your adventures had you clear of Khazad-dûm before the great resurgence of creatures that pushed us out? Ah, if you had been there perhaps things would have been different. No, that is probably folly. The Orcs were there in numbers far greater than any I had ever seen before, and they were the vanguard only. Behind them were worse things, glimpsed fleetingly by the survivors. If any saw their full horror, those dwarves are dead. Aye, I can tell you that: the dead saw them, and I do not envy them the sight. It chills me to think of it even now, here by the heat of the forge!
'There is no end to the work, my friend. I will continue to forge weapons for the Longbeards until my own furnace is extinguished, and I dare say that day is not yet upon us. And yet, this forge does not compare to the one I left behind in Khazad-dûm!
'Ah, the Heart of Fire. No forge ever burned as brightly or as hot as those in the Heart of Fire! I miss them dearly. But I was not about to let the Orcs or their vile allies have access to those forges! I sealed the door before we fled for the surface. The Heart of Fire, at least, will remain unspoiled until the very end of the world. It makes me smile to think of it there, hidden beneath the mountains, locked behind a name no Orc will know. Perhaps it is the little things after all, ${PLAYER}.'

'I feared our paths would not cross again, friend! We have all come quite a distance from Hrimbarg!
'Thorgest has recovered from his poisoned wound, but if you believed the experience would end his desire for adventure, well... you would be wrong! We received word that the son of King Thorin planned an assault upon Gundabad, and before you could say \qhammers in the deep\q Thorgest was on his way, and I behind him.
'I have done what I can to provision the armies, but such a number of fighters threatens to overmatch my supplies! I will need to amass more goods and food if we are to keep this force in prime fighting shape. And not only that, but if I do not keep watch over Thorgest, who will? Every day brings with it a challenge that needs meeting, ${PLAYER}, as you well know.'

'Welcome to Annâk-khurfu, ! This is not nearly so lonely an outpost as Hrimbarg, is it? So many doughty warriors have come to fight alongside Durin in his quest to reclaim Gundabad, many of them great heroes, but he will be most pleased that I and Afwald have made the journey!'
Thorgest throws his head back and laughs, drawing attention from several nearby dwarves. When he has again collected himself, he wears a more solemn expression.
'Ah, but I wish Thorkell was here. When we were just lads, we never suspected that Gundabad might one day be back in our grasp. And yet here I am, near to the doorstep, with one campaign left to fight before that happy day! But my brother is slain and will not see it. A pox on the worms of the Misty Mountains!
'I am glad you are here, ! You will not believe me, but Afwald is always going on about you. \qWhat do you think ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} is up to right now?\q Afwald is always asking me. Well, now he can ask you himself, and not pester me with the question, day after day!'

'I do not know what to do, my friend. I am consumed by a great sense of... I do not know how best to describe it.'
<u>Bróin, Mazog's Executioner</u> <rgb=#FFFF00>Axe-wielding:</rgb> 95 <rgb=#FFFF00>Survival:</rgb> 85 <rgb=#FFFF00>Hardiness:</rgb> 65 <rgb=#FFFF00>Resolve:</rgb> 15
'I do not think I am ready for another war, ${PLAYER}. Yes: I say \qanother.\q Make no mistake: the Iron Garrison was at war in the depths of Moria, and it was a war we lost. Not only is that foothold gone, but so too are many of the brave warriors with which it was claimed in the first place. I mourn my father most of all, but Brogur was not the first good dwarf to perish within Moria, nor the last, though he may have been the bravest. He was bolder by far than his son, that much is certain!
'Will I regain my courage before we pass through the gates of Gundabad? I survived my encounter with the Watcher in the Water within the Drowned Treasury, after all, and then I was alone, with only the dead for company. No, I was not entirely alone, for it was there I found Zigilburk, with which I kept the beast at bay. But the mithril axe is sealed away, never again to be wielded by anyone. It seemed the right choice then... but what if my courage was sealed away in the darkness with Zigilburk? Will I never find it again?
'Please, my friend, I beg you will tell no one of these worries. I bind you to secrecy on this matter. Will you do this? Will you <rgb=#00FF00>agree</rgb> not to tell Prince Durin of my mood or my fears? Please, ${PLAYER}.'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. I am here.
'My father Brogur would have come to fight alongside Prince Durin, if he could. I am here in his stead, for he will never again leave Khazad-dûm.
'I wish things were different.'

'The leaders of the Iron Garrison will be a strong addition to the Gabil'akkâ as we begin our assault on Gundabad, but...
'Can I ask you a question, ${PLAYER}? Do they seem in good spirits, despite the failure of the Iron Garrison to hold Moria? Do they still possess the courage I saw on their faces when they departed the Iron Hills on their expedition? Perhaps you can <rgb=#00FF00>appraise</rgb> them and learn if they possess the stomach for this endeavour.
'I will await the results of your observation.'
'I do not want to disappoint King Thorin or his son. I hope I will not.'

'Durin has gathered a mighty force with which to reclaim Gundabad. Will it be enough?'
<u>Bósi, Leader of the Iron Garrison</u> <rgb=#FFFF00>Diplomacy:</rgb> 75 <rgb=#FFFF00>Sagecraft:</rgb> 85 <rgb=#FFFF00>Hardiness:</rgb> 60 <rgb=#FFFF00>Resolve:</rgb> 20
'It will have to be enough, ${PLAYER}. It simply must.'
'What thinks my son of this army Prince Durin has assembled?'

'So the leaders of the Iron Garrison are prepared to fight again?'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You are a good friend.'

'I have just received word that more dwarves have arrived to swell my army's ranks! Go downstairs to greet them, ${PLAYER}. All are welcome if it is in their hearts to hate Orcs, and I understand that these dwarves hate Orcs more than most!'

'I am not surprised to see you here, ${PLAYER}, but it warms my heart all the same. I was at the Lonely Mountain when Durin sent word to his father that he intended to reclaim Gundabad from the Orcs, but I wanted no part of it. I feared to join him. No, not out of cowardice!'
Bósi frowns unhappily.
'I was tasked to secure Khazad-dûm, ${PLAYER}, but the Iron Garrison failed and my cousin Brogur was slain, along with many other good dwarves. How could I hold my head high after that? I feared my presence at Gundabad would bring nothing but ill fortune.
'And yet... King Thorin deemed otherwise, and commanded me to join his son. So I am here. May things go otherwise in Gundabad than they did in Moria.'

'My father has had a difficult time since the Iron Garrison was defeated in Moria, ${PLAYER}. I have told him repeatedly not to despair, but he pays me little heed. Did I despair at my imprisonment in Mirkwood, when the sorcerer Gorothúl held me captive within the dungeons of Dol Guldur?'
Bori gives you a wry smile.
'You are right: I did! But it turned out all right in the end, did it not? You saved my skin, and now both Gorothúl and his ally Mazog are slain. My point is this: do not close the book when things seem most drear, for it may be you are not at the end at all, but only the middle! The failure of the Iron Garrison is a tough defeat, but it may be the reclamation of Moria still lies ahead of us, and perhaps Gundabad will be the first step on that road.
'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}.'

'Did I hear you rightly? That trap was set not by the Orcs, but by Imák the Stout-axe? Is this true? Is he a fool, or has he been stricken with some madness? We have difficulty enough fighting the Orcs without having to worry about running afoul of traps set by our supposed allies!
'I cannot believe this! A pox on the Stout-axes! You must make this right! Find Imák and ask why he has chosen to fight dwarves and not Orcs! Does he not have enough enemies from which to choose that he must attack his supposed allies too?'
'You must make this right! Find Imák and ask why he has chosen to fight dwarves and not Orcs! Does he not have enough enemies from which to choose that he must attack his supposed allies too?'

'These Longbeards should save their breath! They will not cease hurling insults and threats at me, but I have weathered worse winds than these! What is the Greymaul Rebellion to me? They think I care about the stories of ancient dwarves? Bah. They are nothing to me!
'They think I was wrong to set traps for the Orcs? If these Longbeards paid more attention to their surroundings they would not blunder into one of my devices! You would not think they wanted to reclaim Gundabad at all, so unwilling are they to dirty their hands!
'Well, they will be happy to know this: I did not have time to put the rest of my plan into motion before the defenders emerged from Gundabad and marched on our position. 'This report details the health of bats under Angmarim care. They are raising and training bats for the Orcs -- perhaps this is what Gáfin discovered....'
A troubled expression falls upon Aighrig's face.
'The one who wrote this report is someone named... Latharn. ${PLAYER}, I recognize that name -- it belongs to an Angmarim who is an accomplished beast-tamer. But that is all I know.
'I believe I know where the Angmarim are raising their bats. May I ask you to bring this report to Rékkur? I am sorry, but I must investigate alone.'

'Lúkhag flew off not too long ago -- and where is Aighrig? This doesn't bode well.'
Rékkur patiently listens to your account of what happened before reading through the report you found.
'Why does Aighrig require such secrecy? Though I suppose we can only wait for her....
'The Orcs had a hand in Gáfin's death, and now the Angmarim might have too. Gáfin, my old friend, what did you get yourself into?'

'I was just feeding Lúkhag. She has been very brave lately. But yes, I would be happy to aid you in your hunt.
'I do not think a commander such as Uflúk will be caught off-guard wandering around. There must be a war horn in the Orc camp that we can use to trick him into emerging.'
A report lies crumpled among Uflúk's belongings

'Maybe we'll learn something if we set our sights higher.
'It's clear that Gáfin was killed by Orcs. According to the scouts, the Orc Uflúk commands the camp Zarkul-sulûn, to the west. If anyone has the information Gáfin was trying to bring back, it would be Uflúk.
'But I wouldn't ask for you to venture forth alone. This could be another chance for Aighrig to prove herself to us, if she is willing!'

'Not long ago, Orcs ambushed our supply train. We escaped and made camp. The next morning, our wounds were treated and bandaged! Though I never saw the kind soul who had saved us, I noticed that bat hanging overhead.

'The messenger wants you to travel to the ruins directly west of here -- Zarkul-sulûn. Find an overlook to the west of the path leading up to the ruins. Whatever is there may be important.'

'The time has come to bring this war to its end. Muster your allies and prepare for a fierce battle. Join me, ${PLAYER}, as we bring the fight to Gorgar the Ruthless, and claim Gundabad!'

'These dishonourable Orcs knew we would defeat them in battle, so they sprung a trap to cut us off from the rest of our forces!'
Durin fumes and grinds his teeth, furious at this turn of events. He looks around at the faces of the dwarves trapped with you on this side of the bridge. They show a mix of concern and anger of their own. Durin hardens his resolve and turns toward the open door to the arena.
'We cannot falter, ${PLAYER}. There are too many depending on us. Gorgar will have his way, for now. We will overcome any challenge put before us! Gundabad will be ours, this I swear!'

'The day is won, but a dragon-sized obstacle now stands in our way. Despite this new challenge, I will never give up. I swore to claim Gundabad for the dwarves, and that is what I will do. I would have you by my side, if you will continue to trust in my leadership.
'For now, we must regroup, tend to our wounded, and find a way to get through this ice! You have earned this reward, Champion ${PLAYER}. You have the thanks of the Longbeards, and the Zhélruka, and the Stout-axes!'

'${PLAYER}, I am glad to have you with us. I will soon call for the charge. We will face much Orkish resistance and I will challenge Gorgar the Ruthless for lordship of Gundabad. One final matter remains....
'${PLAYER}, I name you and your fellows Heroes of Durin's Folk! May we achieve glory and victory side by side!
'When you are ready, we begin the charge! Baruk Khazâd! Khazâd ai-mênu!'

'Well done, friend. Gunvald was right about your prowess. I suspect many will be the songs that sing of your glory when this is all over.'

'Gunvald's missive sends word that reinforcements are on the way. I must move on to my next scouting location, but if you are as resourceful as Gunvald says, you could be of great help.
'At the camp up the road there is a swarming nest of hobgoblins. Yes, that seems to be the source of that wretched stench.
'The hobgoblins are squatting in a gap between this mountain's two peaks. From there, they control the nearby river and the pass. Anything you can do to put a dent in their ranks would benefit our forces immensely. Take care when you move into their camp, friend, for they are a deadly foe. I shall circle 'round and meet with you when you reach the other side.'

'Permíteme felicitarte por tus logros, ${PLAYER}, pues realmente has llegado a lo tuyo y tus puños sin duda serán temidos por todos aquellos con quienes luches.
'Le agradeces a Hunward por el excelente equipo que forjó para ti y por sus amables palabras, y le preguntas cómo llegó a estudiar el arte de la lucha a puño limpio. Él ríe.
'¿Esperabas que un Hombre de Rohan prefiriera luchar a lomos de un caballo? Es cierto, la mayoría de los míos lo prefieren, pero yo elegí modelarme según el más legendario de todos los Luchadores. Has oído hablar de Helm Mano de Hierro, por supuesto. ¿Sabes cómo obtuvo ese sobrenombre? Cuando fue insultado por Freca, en cuyas venas corría sangre dunledina, Helm le ordenó que saliera, pues no se permitían peleas en la casa del rey.
'Freca se llenó de temor, y con razón, pues Helm era un hombre grande y fuerte, y ninguno de los hombres de Freca estaba lo bastante cerca como para ayudarlo. Pero vio que Helm no llevaba espada, pues la había dejado dentro del salón, y eso lo tranquilizó. No debería haberlo hecho, porque los puños de Helm eran más mortíferos que cualquier espada. Golpeó a Freca con un solo puñetazo, y esa fue su herida mortal.
'Helm se alza muy por encima de todos, ${PLAYER}, como un Luchador legendario. ¡Hagamos lo que esté a nuestro alcance para demostrarnos dignos de su memoria!'
Completa 'Implementos de Golpeo' para Hunward

'Necesitarás un equipo mejor si has de cumplir tu potencial como maestro del refinado arte de golpear cosas, ¡mi ${PLAYERNAME:nuevo amigo[m]|nueva amiga[f]}! Pero presta atención a mi advertencia, pues los materiales que necesitaré para forjarte tales artículos e implementos no serán fáciles de conseguir. Si has de convertirte en ${PLAYERNAME:el Luchador más temido de todos[m]|la Luchadora más temida de todas[f]}, sé que no tendrás dificultad alguna en encontrarlos.
'Y si no lo haces, entonces quizá no estabas ${PLAYERNAME:destinado[m]|destinada[f]} a destacar entre todos los demás Luchadores de nivel intermedio de estas tierras. Participarás en una pelea de taberna aquí, una refriega en un callejón allá, y te preguntarás qué podría haber sido. Siempre te preguntarás si podrías haber sido más.
'Con mi ayuda, puedes serlo. Piénsalo bien, .'

'¡Has regresado, y de una pieza! Bien hecho, . ¿Debo entender que derrotaste a cinco oponentes y les diste tal paliza que los ecos de ella servirán de advertencia a todos los demás enemigos en las Fundaciones de Piedra? ¿A qué enemigos derrotaste?'
Relatas la lista de tus oponentes, y con cada nombre los ojos de Bardag se abren un poco más.
'Esperaba que te enfrentaras a orcos y trolls, pero debo confesar que no anticipé que criaturas sin nombre de tal poder responderían a tu desafío. ¡Bien luchado, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}! Un combate tan bueno merece una recompensa acorde, aunque sé que para nosotros dos una buena pelea ya es recompensa suficiente.'

Hay aventureros de toda clase prestando su apoyo a la Guarnición de Hierro en Moria, pero estos Campeones, Guardianes y Cazadores no tienen lo que hace falta. Necesito un buen Luchador que sepa pelear y que no dependa de espadas, lanzas o flechas. ¿Eres tú? Si lo eres, ven a verme al Refugio Sombrío, en las Fundaciones de Piedra.
Bardag Manogranizo, Luchador de renombre

'I know not how this necklace came to the land of Mordor, ${PLAYER}, but I am certain now that this is the very same artifact that caused me so much trouble and grief on the deck of this very ship. What servant of evil could have brought it to that place, and for what purpose? I cannot say, but this I know: the Spirit of the Necklace is well and truly gone. I feel its absence as strongly as I feel the wooden deck beneath my feet.
'Gone too is the corruption that enveloped this necklace as a result of its stay in the Black Land. I think it is fitting that you take it now, and make whatever use of it you deem right. It no longer has any hold upon me, and I am left in peace at last. I hope Mal Stackwort and his fellows will find freedom from their own controlling spirit, Man though he be.'
You thank Umín for the gift of the necklace, and tell him you believe Elrond of Rivendell will be able to imbue it with some force for Good.
'I hope so, my friend. Go to Rivendell with my good wishes.'
'I'll think about it, but I make no promise that you will not see me again, Brawler.'
'Where next will you go? To Rivendell? I wish you good fortune, my friend.'

'See? It is just as I said: whatever force gave life to the traps within these caverns has fled. Was it the Spirit of the Necklace, or some other power? Whatever it might have been, it is gone now.
'But I hear voices ahead. Who else has come to this forsaken ship?'

'Well? Why does this fellow say I shouldn't take this ship and go a-pirating?'
You briefly describe Umín's experience with the Spirit of the Necklace, which culminated with the shade seizing control of the poor adventurer's body and turning him against his allies on this very ship's deck, before the spirit was finally defeated and Umín freed from its influence.
'He can't have been completely freed, can he?' Mal muses wryly. 'He came back here, didn't he? Are you certain this spirit was truly defeated? It sounds powerful.'
Others have come to the lost ship for some unknown purpose, and you should learn what they intend.
Mal Stackwort, former minion of Bill Ferny, leads a crew of cutthroats intending to free the forsaken ship from its trapped berth.
Mal Stackwort has no idea of the meaning behind Umín's words, and has asked you to explain them.
Umín has collected the necklace from where it lay, and he wishes to speak with you about it.
Umín stands outside the docked ship, waiting to speak with you.
Umín's words have had an effect on Mal Stackwort, but whether they will last remains to be seen.

Umín has returned with you to the forsaken ship where the Spirit of the Necklace was defeated, hoping to aid you in cleansing the corruption from the necklace you found in Mordor, and perhaps to find some measure of peace for himself.
Talk to Umín and return to the ship in the caverns beneath the Forsaken Inn
Habla con Anlaf el Despojado en la Posada Abandonada

'There is a foulness about this necklace. If you find Umín, he may help you to cleanse the corruption enwreathing it. I say it is time for you to return to the Forsaken Inn, my friend. Anlaf the Forlorn may know where you can find this Umín now.'

'I know why you have come, ${PLAYER}. If you are to journey beneath the shroud that covers Gorgoroth, you will need the aid of a light that can pierce the darkness. So it was with those who coveted this necklace when it contained malevolence, or the promise of direction. Now that it is just a necklace, perhaps it will aid you as it did not aid them.'
Elrond takes the Necklace of the Ordinary from you and dips it into the font beside him. When the artifact emerges from the glowing circle, light drips soundlessly from it and pools like water in the basin. Elrond smiles at the sight, and his voice contains both determination and joy when he speaks again.
'With the Light of Eärendil, you will be able to walk where the shadows lie, and overcome them.'
'I will meet you at the Haven of Orladion, ${PLAYER}.'

'I returned to those caverns once, ${PLAYER}. The riddle doors were open, the spike traps deactivated. It was as if the guiding force that hindered our progress had undone itself, its purpose spent. I came all the way to the ship, but like me it remained an empty vessel. I returned to the surface, aimless and disappointed.'
You ask Umín why he went back underground after his experience with the haunted necklace, and he stares off into the distance.
'I think I did it hoping the spirit would return, and tell me what to do... but I received no such guidance. In the weeks that followed I came often to the Forsaken Inn, waiting for someone to tell me what to do, someone to give me direction, but no one ever did.
'I will go with you now, ${PLAYER}, if you let me carry the necklace. If I can help you cleanse the corruption from it, perhaps my aimless days will be ended.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'What are... what are you doing here, ${PLAYER}?'
You hold up the broken necklace and Umín nearly falls off the rock.
'Why did... why did you bring it back to me?'
You hastily hide the necklace from his sight, and he takes a moment to calm himself. You ask what has him so troubled, and he frowns.
'Need you ask? You remember that heirloom of my family, the thief-stolen necklace we at last recovered from the tomb in the caverns beneath the Forsaken Inn? It guided my thoughts for so long, and when I finally unearthed it, the spirit held within so dominated my mind that I turned upon my friends! I was powerless to resist the spirit of the necklace, but worst of all... now that they are gone, spirit and necklace both, I do not know what to do! And now you have returned with the necklace that so occupies my every waking minute....'
You tell Umín that you found this necklace in Mordor. For it to be the same as the one that so troubled him seems unlikely, but Gandalf believes it might be possible to cleanse the corruption that envelops it.
'But it is so like the other. What if this corruption is the result of another spirit's presence, ${PLAYER}? What will we do then?'
'Umín was just here, actually. If you leave the Inn you might see him across the way. Whatever stupor he's in isn't caused by my drink, that I do know... he's just a defeated man!'
Anlaf the Forlorn tends the bar of the Forsaken Inn, in the Lone-lands.
Anlaf told you that Umín just left the Forsaken Inn, and if you hurry you might see him outside somewhere.

'I have studied the artifact that Ayorzén stole from the vault of Durthang. It bears a powerful corruption, but it was not made in the land of Mordor. It came from elsewhere, and the corruption that envelops it stems from its long stay in the Black Land. If this evil could be cleansed, I believe that Elrond could imbue it with a powerful and vital force for Good.
'Before that can happen, however, we must do something about the corruption that Mordor has worked upon it. There are different methods to accomplish this, though the Wise disagree upon the effectiveness of each. My preferred means for such a cure is to bring the corrupted item to the place where it was made, or to places of some significance upon its path, and to thereby diffuse the foul touch of Mordor that has, in the interim, claimed it. We must learn the story of this heirloom before it came to Mordor.'
The Wizard turns the artifact over in his hands, studying it for some clue to its origin. To your eye the heirloom is a golden necklace, ordinary save for the large ruby in its centre. The chain is broken and cannot have been easily worn for some time. It looks familiar to you.
'Familiar, you say?' Gandalf asks, stroking his beard. 'How so?'
You tell him that the necklace shares a resemblance with one worn by a man called Umín in tunnels beneath the Forsaken Inn of the Lone-lands. Umín had been ensnared by the villainous spirit inhabiting a necklace just like this one, and breaking its hold upon the man had not been easy.
'Let us hope no such spirit bedevils this necklace, ${PLAYER}, but there is some foulness about it all the same. If you find this Umín, he may help you to cleanse the corruption enwreathing it. I say it is time for you to return to the Forsaken Inn, my friend. Anlaf the Forlorn may know where you can find this Umín now.'

'You say you're looking for Umín? Why'd you want to do that?'
Anlaf scowls.
'He comes in here from time to time, lookin' for all the world as if he's thinkin' to just curl up in the corner and never move again! Doesn't buy so much as a single mug of ale, neither! He just sits, and stares, and eventually he gets up and every time he leaves I think I'll never be seein' him again... but I've never had the luck before and still haven't!
'He was just here, actually. If you leave the Inn you might see him across the way. Whatever stupor he's in isn't caused by my drink, that I do know... he's just a defeated man!'
