'Sí, Aran, creo que podemos colaborar para recolectar y preservar los recursos del bosque. La perdurabilidad del Bosque Salvaje es importante para la Liga del Hacha. ¿Será bienvenida la Liga del Hacha para comerciar y vender mercancías en Puente de Caballetes? Además, ¿qué opinas de mi propuesta sobre nuestras dos facciones?'

'Enid, la Liga del Hacha es más que bienvenida en Puente de Caballetes. Estableceremos un puesto comercial permanente en la ciudad para vosotros. Entonces está decidido: ya que ahora compartimos los mismos objetivos, unamos nuestros conocimientos y recursos y velemos juntos por el Bosque Salvaje. Tu propuesta es acertada. ¡De ahora en adelante nos conoceremos como la Liga del Bosque Salvaje!
'${PLAYER}, Enid y los miembros de la Liga son buena gente. Si no estuviéramos tan ocupados con nuestros propios problemas y dificultades en el Bosque Salvaje, quizá nos hubiéramos unido antes en nuestras causas. Supongo que es una lección aprendida. Me alegro de que hayamos encontrado un terreno común en este día. El futuro del Bosque Salvaje es, sin duda, prometedor.'
Los dos líderes están en plena conversación cuando llegas

Aran Verdduno y Enid Picortiga tienen previsto reunirse en el centro del Bosque Salvaje.
Debes dirigirte al punto de encuentro indicado.

'Ahora que la Hermandad de los Leñadores ha consolidado su presencia en el Bosque Salvaje y ha logrado grandes avances, creo que es hora de hablar con la Liga del Hacha sobre la propiedad del Bosque Salvaje. Convoquemos una reunión entre nuestros grupos en terreno neutral dentro del Bosque Salvaje. Espero que allí podamos encontrar una solución pacífica para nuestras dos facciones, que compiten por los mismos recursos.'

'Ahora que la Liga del Hacha ha consolidado nuestra presencia en el Bosque Salvaje y ha enriquecido la vida de cada uno de nosotros, creo que es hora de hablar con la Hermandad de los Leñadores sobre la propiedad del Bosque Salvaje. Convoquemos una reunión entre nuestros grupos en terreno neutral dentro del Bosque Salvaje. Espero que allí podamos encontrar una solución al hecho de que nuestras dos facciones compitan por los mismos recursos.'

'Ah, ya has vuelto de la inspección de la mina. ¿Cómo te ha ido? Ya veo que te has topado con cierta hostilidad por parte de bandidos y orcos. No me sorprende que quieran saquear la vieja mina.'
Le preguntas cuáles son las intenciones de la Liga respecto a la mina de Retoral.
'Queremos volver a hacer que la mina sea segura y extraer piedra para el comercio. Espero que eso te parezca aceptable'.
Ahora consideras a Enid una persona de carácter honorable y le revelas la información que has estado ocultando sobre las acciones poco recomendables de Nye Patacuervo y Addy Matajunco, así como sobre la tumba oculta de Arnor.
'Ya veo. Tenía mis sospechas sobre esos dos, pero no tenía pruebas para expulsarlos de la Liga. Te he estado enviando a expediciones con ellos para vigilar sus acciones en el Bosque Salvaje. Sabía que tu carácter era íntegro y que podía confiar en ti. Ahora debemos vigilar aún más de cerca a Nye y Addy. En cuanto a esa tumba oculta, la Liga del Hacha no está formada por saqueadores de tumbas. No me interesa una tumba antigua. Sin embargo, si trabajamos en las minas, protegeremos y preservaremos la tumba con orgullo.'

'Sí, soy Addy Matajunco. ¿Has venido para la expedición de exploración? ¡Me alegro de oírlo! Hay gente malvada en la Mina este y la Mina oeste de Retoral. Empecemos por hacerles la vida difícil en el Bosque Salvaje. ¡Destruir sus provisiones y las piedras extraídas debería bastar para cumplir esa tarea! Entonces podremos entrar en las minas sin ningún problema.'

'Buen trabajo, ${PLAYER}. ¡Parece que hemos puesto a esos sinvergüenzas a la fuga! Ahora es nuestra oportunidad de entrar en las minas. Me gustaría que te enfrentaras al capataz y al supervisor de Retoral. Estoy segura de que se merecen lo que les espera. Y ya que estás, ¿por qué no debilitas algunas de las vigas de soporte que hay ahí dentro? ¡Eso sí que les dejará las cosas claras!
Te sorprenden las palabras de Addy Matajunco y ahora ves que no es más honorable que Nye Patacuervo. Aceptas ayudar a Addy, pero elaboras tu propio plan mientras sigues cuestionando la reputación de la Liga del Hacha.
'Muy bien, ${PLAYER}, nos adentramos en las minas.'

¡Se nota un fuerte estruendo por toda la mina!

La Liga del Hacha está organizando una expedición de caza en el Bosque Salvaje.

'Has encontrado buena carne y animales allí, ¿verdad? Ja, y mírame a mí, con las manos vacías. Supongo que le pasa hasta al mejor de nosotros. Tú, en cambio, solo has tenido suerte de principiante, ¡eso está claro! Bueno, pasemos a la siguiente parte de nuestra expedición de caza. Cazar animales más grandes es más fácil si atraemos a las bestias hacia fuera. Quiero que pongas esos animales vivos que has capturado en las trampas para osos.
Te sorprenden las palabras de Nye Patacuervo y ahora ves que no es un hombre muy honorable. Aceptas ayudar a Nye, pero elaboras tu propio plan mientras empiezas a cuestionar la reputación de la Liga del Hacha.
'Muy bien, ${PLAYER}, ponte manos a la obra.'

'¿Cómo te fue en la expedición de caza? ¡Me alegro de oírlo! Esta carne nos mantendrá alimentados y garantizará la rentabilidad de la Liga. Has hecho un buen trabajo para nosotros'.
Le preguntas a Enid qué opina sobre usar animales vivos como cebo para presas más grandes.
'Bueno, ${PLAYER}, ¡espero que esas palabras sean solo una prueba de mi buen carácter! ¡Eso es cruel y carece del desafío y la habilidad que requiere la caza! La Liga del Hacha es un grupo de buena reputación, después de todo.'

'Sí, soy yo, Nye Patacuervo. ¿Todo listo para ir de caza? Vamos a empezar por revisar algunas de las trampas que la Liga ha colocado en el Bosque Salvaje. Los bandidos y su líder se han dado a la fuga por el camino al este del Embarcadero de los Comerciantes, en el Bosque Salvaje.

'¡Hola! Me llamo Minda Matosos, ¡y estoy viviendo una gran aventura! Bueno, a decir verdad, ha sido más aterradora que grandiosa. ¡Esos malditos ladrones de carromatos se han llevado mi poni y mi carromato lleno de provisiones! Por suerte, esta buena gente me encontró vagando por el camino y me trajo aquí. Aunque estoy muy agradecida, la Liga del Hacha no tiene tiempo para ir a buscar las provisiones de una insignificante hobbit. Si... si pudieras ayudarme con esta tarea, ¡haría que te valiera la pena!
'Los bandidos se adentraron en el Bosque Salvaje con Pisador y mi carro de provisiones. ¡Deberías haber visto cómo luchó Pisador contra ellos! ¡No se iba a rendir sin luchar, y mis provisiones salieron volando por todas partes! ¡Apuesto a que si sigues el rastro de los sacos que fueron lanzados, te llevará directamente hasta Pisador! Si te topas con alguno de esos bandidos o con su líder por el camino, ¡te animo a que te encargues de ellos rápidamente!'

'Gracias por venir a verme hasta aquí,. Sé que te he pedido mucho, ¡pero eras tú quien podía ayudarme! Te lo agradezco muchísimo.
'Imagino que te estarás preguntando qué hace alguien como yo tan lejos de casa. Tengo el honor de ser aprendiz de la maestra cocinera Lyn Madecedera. Ella me envió al Bosque Salvaje a recolectar ingredientes para la primera Fiesta del Bosque Salvaje de la historia.
'Pero, ¡ay! Ya sabes cómo acabó todo. Te agradezco mucho toda la ayuda que me has prestado y me da pena pedirte más... ¡pero te la voy a pedir! ¡Necesito desesperadamente tu ayuda para recolectar ingredientes, o el banquete se echará a perder! ¡Yo me echaré a perder!'

'¡Esas huellas son sin duda de las enormes patas de Pisador! ¿Pero unas huellas tan gigantes? ¡Ay, ay, ay! ¡Me temo que el pobre Pisador está a punto de convertirse en comida para los huargos! Por favor, ${PLAYER}, ¡tenemos que encontrarlo!'
'¡Pobre Pisador! ¡Debe de estar tan asustado! ¡Por favor, encuéntralo!'

'¡Pisador! ¡Lo has conseguido, ${PLAYER}!
'¡Ay, pero mi carro! ¡Mi precioso carro! ¡Está completamente destrozado! Bueno, supongo que debo dar gracias por lo que me queda. ¡Gracias, ${PLAYER}! Vamos, salgamos de aquí, no sea que vengan más bandidos o huargos en busca de sus amigos. He oído que hay un estanque cerca, y parece que a Pisador le vendría bien beber un poco. ¡Nos vemos allí!'
¡Pisador se dirige al norte!
¡Estas huellas parecen recientes! ¡Está cerca!
¡Has encontrado huellas!

'Hay muchas formas de ayudar a Puente de Caballetes. Una de ellas consiste en recolectar los recursos del Bosque Salvaje para que el pueblo tenga más productos con los que comerciar y ofrecer a los viajeros de paso.
'Uno de los recursos del Bosque Salvaje es su deliciosa savia, que se encuentra en algunos de sus árboles. Ya hemos perforado los árboles que producen esta savia y nos vendría bien alguien que nos ayudara a recolectarla. ¿Nos echarás una mano? La Hermandad te estará muy agradecida por tu ayuda.'

'¡Por favor, salva el banquete! ... ¡Y mi trabajo!'

'Uno de los invitados al banquete de mi señor es un apasionado de las ancas de rana. Con mantequilla, a la parrilla... ¡como sea, le encantan! Mis amigos de la Liga del Hacha me han dicho dónde hay un montón de esas criaturas. De hecho, hay tantas que están desplazando a las ranas más pequeñas de la zona. ¡Si me preguntas, les haremos un favor a esas pequeñas!
'¡Por desgracia, las ranas que necesito están en el lago y el foso junto al asentamiento enemigo! No hay forma de que pueda acercarme lo suficiente para recogerlas, ¡pero tú seguro que sí! Por favor, ${PLAYER}. ¡Salva el banquete y tráeme ancas de rana!'

'Mae govannen. Necesito tu ayuda para completar una serie de miniaventuras en la lucha por preservar el Bosque Salvaje.

'¿Me ayudarías completando varias de estas miniaventuras?'
'Te agradezco tu ayuda. Tus buenas acciones contribuirán a que el Bosque Salvaje siga siendo un lugar de belleza y tranquilidad en las Tierras de Bree.'

Dificultad 1: Aventurero
Completar esta misión cambiará tu nivel de dificultad actual.
Habla con el viajero curtido

'Saludos, viajero. Observo a quienes recorren los caminos de la Tierra Media en busca de desafíos y aventuras, y tú pareces de esa clase. De hecho, hay quienes prefieren retos aún mayores, y yo puedo ayudarte a conseguirlo.
'Si aceptas lo que te propongo, descubrirás que tus enemigos en los caminos y parajes de la Tierra Media se volverán más fuertes y peligrosos. ¿Es esto lo que deseas?'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Completar esta misión hará que el juego sea significativamente más difícil.
Completar esta misión antes del nivel 11 iniciará hazañas que se completarán si alcanzas los niveles 50 y 130 sin reducir tu dificultad de vuelta a Normal.</rgb>

'¿Seguro que deseas tomar esta vía? Es comprensible si recelas, pues tan arduas empresas no son, desde luego, para todo el mundo.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>¡Completar esta misión aumentará la dificultad de los enemigos en el mundo abierto y en las miniaventuras!</rgb>
<rgb=#FF0000>ADVERTENCIA: ¡Completar esta misión impedirá PERMANENTEMENTE completar las hazañas que dan títulos de la dificultad \qSin miedo\q!</rgb>
El camino que tienes por delante se ha vuelto más peligroso...
Completar esta misión aumentará la amenaza que suponen los monstruos que encuentres durante tu viaje por la Tierra Media, y te otorgará una pequeña bonificación a la experiencia obtenida en combate.

Habla con Mantoespino
Marca los tejos salvajes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Planta brotes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Pastorear un bosque es un equilibrio entre plantar y talar. Con tu ayuda, el Bosque Salvaje volverá a florecer.'

'Has hecho un buen trabajo aquí, ${PLAYERNAME:pequeño[m]|pequeña[f]}, juuum. Como prometí, te enseñaré qué árboles puede talar tu gente. A mi lado hay un tejo salvaje adulto, tuuum-jaruuum, y no debería estar aquí. Tal vez un pájaro trajo una semilla al Bosque Salvaje desde tierras lejanas. Tal vez los orcos trajeron las semillas con ellos, sin darse cuenta, como suelen hacer con casi todo. Sea como fuere, los tejos salvajes asfixiarán a los que tienen alrededor y les taparán el sol. Puedes marcar los que encuentres para que la gente de Puente de Caballetes los tale y los aproveche.
'Las semillas y brotes que recogiste aún no estarán listos para plantarse durante algún tiempo. Sin embargo, he traído conmigo semillas de árboles fuertes que ya se pueden sembrar. Ve, marca los tejos salvajes y planta lo que puedas, para que el Bosque Salvaje vuelva a crecer con fuerza.
'Yo seguiré hacia el sur, pues los árboles de allí susurran rumores inquietantes de los que deseo saber más.'

'Las trampas envenenadas son crueles y cobardes

'Saludos, ${CLASS}. ¡Soy Linnet Redholm, Cazadora del Bosque de los Trolls! ¿Quizás hayas oído hablar de mis hazañas? ¿No? Bueno, está claro que los bardos de Bree son unos holgazanes. He recorrido largas distancias por la Tierra Media, persiguiendo rumores de bestias legendarias y presas peligrosas. Me llegaron rumores de maravillosas criaturas acechando en el Bosque Salvaje y partí de inmediato hacia estos bosques.
'Imagina mi horror cuando me topé con trampas envenenadas, colocadas por los inmundos orcos y cazadores furtivos que se han infiltrado en estos bosques. El veneno es obra de cobardes, no de verdaderos cazadores. Estoy tras la pista de algo enorme, así que no puedo ocuparme de ello yo misma, pero si quisieras destruir cualquiera de las trampas con las que te topes, haría que te saliera más que rentable.'
Caza honorable

'Mmm. Robar cachorros es aún más reprobable que usar trampas envenenadas.'

'Mientras estabas fuera, me topé con una loba muy enfadada y acabé pasando un buen rato subida a un árbol para que no me viera. Temía que su furia se debiera a alguna enfermedad, pero cuando la seguí, encontré un campamento de cazadores furtivos con jaulas llenas de cachorros de lobo. No soporto a los cazadores furtivos. No les importa el impacto que su caza tiene en los bosques.
'Soy una cazadora, pero no una luchadora. ¿Liberarás a los cachorros de lobo y te encargarás de los cazadores furtivos? Por supuesto, me aseguraré de que te compensen.'
Libera a los lobos

'Se te ha escapado, ¿verdad? A veces las cosas son así. Quizá me lo encuentre algún día.
'Parece que tú también lograste una gran hazaña mientras estabas por allí. Supongo que te acercaste más a Gwengorn de lo que yo jamás pude.'
¡Gwengorn ha huido! ¡Se dirige hacia la colina!
¡Gwengorn no estaba huyendo! Te ha traído hasta aquí.

'Los rumores que me trajeron hasta aquí hablaban de Gwengorn, un ciervo con un pelaje blanco como la nieve y unas astas que se elevan por encima de las copas de los árboles. No me creo eso último, ¡pero un ciervo blanco sería todo un hallazgo!'

Derrota a las legendarias bestias del Bosque Salvaje
'Excelente trabajo. Puede que incluso llegue a admitir que se te da mejor la caza que a mí... Algún día.'

Las grandes bestias se encuentran por todo el Bosque Salvaje.
Linnet te ha pedido que derrotes al ciervo blanco Gwengorn, al gran jabalí Brundurch, al alce negro Dúgar y al huargo plateado Lhudblath.

'Nuestros amigos de aquí hablan de bestias poderosas que vagan por el Bosque Salvaje, algunas de las cuales atacan a todo lo que se cruza en su camino con total desenfreno. He seguido el rastro de algunas de ellas y estoy convencido de que su comportamiento no es natural. Sea cual sea la enfermedad que ha llevado a estos animales a tal violencia, no debe propagarse al resto del bosque.
'Vine aquí en busca de gloria, pero soy lo suficientemente sensata como para saber cuándo me superan. Si acabas con esas criaturas enfermas, me aseguraré de que los bardos conozcan tu nombre.'
La caza del Bosque Salvaje

'¡Bien! Has regresado sin que te hayan embestido. Esperemos que la locura de Brundurch haya desaparecido junto con el gran jabalí.'
Has derrotado a Brundurch, el gran jabalí

Brundurch, el gran jabalí, se encuentra en la parte norte del Bosque Salvaje.
Linnet te ha pedido que derrotes al jabalí enloquecido, Brundurch.

'Hay muchas cosas peligrosas en el Bosque Salvaje, pero la gente habla de Brundurch, el gran jabalí, con voz tensa y en voz baja. Algunos dicen que su locura fue provocada por la enfermedad de la espuma. Otros insisten en que hay una oscuridad en el propio Bosque Salvaje que poco a poco corrompe a las criaturas que lo habitan.
'Sea como fuere, Brundurch es despiadado y responsable de haber atacado a más de un grupo de mercaderes que intentaban atravesar el Bosque Salvaje. Hay que detener al gran jabalí, no sea que propague su locura o cause más daño.'

Carrera hacia Agoroth

Yrjänä asiente solemnemente.
'Un pacto está hecho. Ve a Salavathi y dile que Yrjänä te ha dado la llave de Arvedui. Ella es la guardiana de las cosas antiguas y de las historias de antaño. La encontrarás en la colina que domina el pueblo.
'Los Lumi-väki confían en ti, ${PLAYER}. No nos falles.'

'¿Qué te trae a Salavathi, ${PLAYERNAME:forastera[f]|forastero[m]} ?'
Le explicas a Salavathi que Yrjänä te ha dado el derecho de tomar la llave de Arvedui. Sus ojos se abren de par en par.
'Los Lumi-väki han conservado esta llave durante generaciones. Sabíamos que algún día alguien vendría a buscarla, como ocurrió con el anillo de Arvedui. Por la voluntad de Yrjänä, te la entrego.'
Salavathi se aparta y murmura una oración en la lengua de los Lossoth. Luego comienza a tararear un tono único desde lo más profundo de su pecho. Este tono hace vibrar las altas agujas de piedra que te rodean, y la nieve baila, revelando un cuadrado recortado en la roca que nunca habrías podido ver de otra manera. Levanta la piedra cuadrada, revelando un espacio hueco, y deja de tararear. Dentro descansa un modesto paquete de piel de alce, desgastado por el tiempo. Salavathi toma el paquete y lo abre, revelando una llave de metal finamente detallada. Ves que la llave es bastante grande, y que la estrella de siete puntas de Arnor sirve como asa. Esta debe ser la llave de Agoroth. Salavathi sostiene la llave hacia ti, permitiéndote tomarla.
'Nuestro negocio ha concluido, ${PLAYERNAME:forastera[f]|forastero[m]}. Que hagas grandes cosas con esto. El que se conoce como Lothrandir ha venido a encontrarse contigo. Salavathi ve mucho desde este alto lugar. Deberías ir a su encuentro.'

', regresas. Los Lumi-väki no esperaban volver a verte después de que se resolviera el asunto del anillo. Al menos, no tan pronto. ¿Qué quieres de Yrjänä?'
Le explicas que los Angmarim están buscando un tesoro en la fortaleza oculta de Agoroth, y que necesitas la llave que Arvedui dejó con los Lossoth antes de su muerte si hay alguna esperanza de ganarle a ellos.
'Yrjänä sabe de lo que hablas. Los Lumi-väki han mantenido este legado a salvo. Pero te pregunto, ¿sabes el verdadero significado de este objeto? Es más que una llave de metal para una puerta de metal. Los Lumi-väki lo saben. Mi gente tiene una memoria larga.
'Las canciones hablan de un tiempo muy lejano, cuando los hombres altos vinieron con armaduras de hierro. Le pidieron a los Lumi-väki paz y jurar un juramento ante una gran piedra, azul como el cielo en un día despejado. Los Lumi-väki juraron ayudar a los hombres altos a luchar contra sus enemigos, y a cambio, recibimos armas de metal forjado para luchar contra nuestros antiguos rivales, los Gauredain. Un buen trato, hasta que los Hombres de Hierro fueron a la guerra. Muchos Lumi-väki murieron en tierras extranjeras, enfrentándose a enemigos que no eran nuestros.
'Aun así, los Lumi-väki mantuvieron nuestro juramento y la paz con los Hombres de Hierro y sus descendientes. Un día, volvieron a Sûri-kylä. Dijeron que la piedra debía ser movida y escondida. Había otras piedras, con juramentos hechos por otros clanes, que fueron tomadas y corrompidas. Los Hombres de Hierro querían construir un nuevo Hogar-de-piedra aquí, en nuestras tierras. Los Lumi-väki estaban indecisos. Un enemigo capaz de corromper una magia tan poderosa no es un enemigo al que se le pueda hacer frente a la ligera. Sabíamos quién debía ser ese enemigo...
'Pero los Lumi-väki fueron obligados por su juramento y permitieron que los Hombres de Hierro construyeran su Hogar-de-piedra aquí. Ocultamos el camino con nuestra magia, porque sabíamos que si la piedra era encontrada y corrompida, los Lumi-väki quedarían atados a ese mal.
'Durante muchos años, los Hombres de Hierro fueron dejados a su Hogar-de-piedra. Rara vez, uno venía a Sûri-kylä para intercambiar suministros. Luego vino un viento fétido que traía el olor del mal, seguido de la peor tormenta en muchas generaciones. No vinieron más Hombres de Hierro después de ese día, y temimos que la piedra ahora debía estar desprotegida.
'Esta llave... abrirá la puerta de la Piedra-del-juramento. De esto Yrjänä está seguro. Se dará en intercambio, pero no por bienes o moneda, no... a cambio, Yrjänä pide que haga su propio juramento. Promete a los Lumi-väki que protegerás la piedra de Angmar, y promete a Yrjänä que encontrarás una manera de destruir la Piedra-del-juramento para siempre. Los Lumi-väki desean no estar atados a nadie. Daremos nuestra lealtad a quienes lo merezcan y lucharemos contra enemigos que entendamos completamente.
'¿Aceptas?'
Te acercas y escuchas la conversación de Lothrandir y Arvedui.

Sorprendentemente, Lothrandir ha obligado a Arvedui a acompañarlo al pueblo Lossoth. Lothrandir parece estar contándole una historia a Arvedui y no se ha dado cuenta de que te acercas.
Deberías escuchar su conversación.
'Arvedui nos ha mostrado el camino hacia Agoroth. Ahora debemos prepararnos para adentrarnos en ella. ¡Esperemos haber llegado antes que los Angmarim!'

'Está claro que no tenemos mucho tiempo si queremos llegar al tesoro de Agoroth antes que los Angmarim. Deberías ir a Sûri-kylä y preguntar al consejo de Lossoth si están dispuestos a intercambiar la llave de Agoroth. Son un pueblo honorable y harán un intercambio justo por ella. Mientras tanto, me gustaría hablar con el rey Arvedui en profundidad, dándole noticias del último milenio y escuchando historias de los Dúnedain de antaño.'

Encuentra a Lothrandir en Forochel
El que persiste
'La intuición del señor Elrond era correcta. El rey Arvedui era una fuente valiosa de información, pero los Angmarim saben que también buscamos Agoroth. ¿Hasta dónde nos llevan en esta carrera?'
'Partiremos hacia el Thoroval cuando estés listo.'

'Me gustaría tomar un momento más de tu tiempo antes de que te vayas, ${PLAYER}.
Aunque nuestra misión de frustrar los planes de Amarthiel y Mordrambor debe ser nuestro enfoque principal, lamento que la sombra de mi ancestro persista, cargada de gran remordimiento. Debe haber algo que podamos hacer para aliviar su espíritu.
Por favor, habla con el señor Elrond en mi nombre. Si alguien entre los vivos sabe lo que se puede hacer, será él.'

'¿De vuelta tan pronto, ${PLAYER}?'
Explicas que Aragorn desea encontrar alguna manera de poner a descansar la sombra de Arvedui y te envió a Elrond para que te ayudara.
'Estamos de acuerdo. Conocí al rey Arvedui en vida. Merece un destino mejor que persistir en los páramos helados, atormentado por su pasado. Sin embargo, aliviarlo de su carga no será tarea fácil.'
Elrond frunce el ceño, sumido en sus pensamientos.
'Francamente, no sé cuál es la mejor manera de ayudarlo. En mi experiencia, las sombras de los Hombres a menudo persisten en el mundo debido a algo inacabado: un juramento incumplido, un juramento roto. Tal vez si pasas tiempo con Arvedui, aprenderás por qué persiste y encontrarás una manera de aliviar su carga. Con ese fin, tengo una solicitud que podría conducir a la salvación del rey caído y también frustrar al Enemigo.'
Elrond hace un gesto hacia el libro sobre la mesa y lo abre en una página marcada con un trozo de tela con borlas. Ves que contiene una lista de muchas entradas fechadas, registrando algo. La estrella de siete puntas de Arnor ilustra una de las páginas.
'Como has visto, Angmar ha comprometido muchas fuerzas en Forochel, reclutando a los Gauredain locales en sus filas, enviando más soldados de los necesarios para el propósito que creíamos que poseían. Están buscando algo, y finalmente he encontrado una pista sobre lo que podría ser.
'Este registro recuperado de Annúminas detalla movimientos significativos de tropas desde los años 500 hasta 600 de la Tercera Edad. Allí, en esa página, se afirma que un gran contingente de soldados y el príncipe Elendur mismo trasladaron un \qobjeto de gran importancia\q desde Ost Forod hacia el Norte. No declara qué es este objeto ni dónde descansó exactamente. Tengo la sospecha de lo que podría ser y, si estoy en lo correcto, seguramente es lo que los Angmarim buscan en las tierras salvajes heladas del Forochel.
'Primero, te pediría que busques al Montaraz conocido como Lothrandir. Creo que todavía está entre los Lossoth, y si te encuentras con los Angmarim en fuerza, temo que necesitarás su brazo de espada. Juntos, lleven esta información a Arvedui. Como rey de Arthedain, puede saber dónde se escondió este tesoro secreto por los Arnorianos hace tantos años.
'Si el destino es amable, encontrarás el tesoro antes de que los Angmarim puedan apoderarse de él para sus oscuros amos. Si es aún más amable, también encontrarás una manera de poner a descansar el espíritu de Arvedui. Te deseo suerte, ${PLAYER}.'

'Hola, ${PLAYER}. ¿Qué te ha traído de vuelta a Forochel? ¿Todo va bien en Rivendel?'
Explicas la solicitud de Elrond de encontrar el tesoro arnoriano perdido antes que los Angmarim y de intentar poner a descansar la sombra de Arvedui.
'Traes noticias de una gran aventura, y sería un gran honor ayudarte a encontrar un tesoro perdido de los Dúnedain y conocer al propio rey Arvedui. ¡No debemos demorarnos aquí, entonces, si queremos encontrarlo antes que los Angmarim! ¡Viajemos al naufragio del Thoroval de inmediato!'

'Te doy la bienvenida de nuevo, ${PLAYER}. ¡La ligereza de tus pasos me informa de tu éxito! Por favor, cuéntame todo lo que ha sucedido.'
Le cuentas a Elrond todo lo que sucedió: tu promesa a los Lossoth a cambio de la llave, la realización de que el Helcessar estaba contenido en Agoroth, los Sardirath atados durante miles de años por un juramento, las batallas con los Angmarim y los Gauredain, la visión del momento de la muerte de Arvedui, la destrucción del Helcessar y, finalmente, la liberación de los Sardirath.
'Asombroso y una historia digna de ser registrada. Si bien me entristece escuchar sobre la destrucción de un artefacto de Númenor, quizás sea lo mejor. Muchos de los Vandassari ya han caído en manos del Enemigo a lo largo de los años, lo que ha llevado a calamidades. Sin duda, el Helcessar habría cambiado el rumbo de la guerra a favor de Angmar. Sin embargo, me alegra saber que Arvedui siente que podrá seguir adelante tras la coronación de su heredero. Sé que harás todo lo posible para ayudar a Aragorn a alcanzar ese objetivo, al igual que yo.
'Debes ser recompensado por todos tus esfuerzos. Este tabardo fue recuperado en Annúminas junto con el registro que te llevó a esta aventura. Por tu servicio al reino caído de Arnor, te lo has ganado.'

'${PLAYER}, debemos hablar. Siento que mi conexión con este mundo se desvanece, pero aún no puedo avanzar.
'Las palabras honestas de Glamagol, y el conocimiento de que mi linaje continúa, todavía me han liberado de la desesperación. Nunca podría haber imaginado que en la muerte finalmente daría un golpe significativo a Angmar.
'Mis más profundos agradecimientos a ti y a Lothrandir. Si no fuera por tus acciones, todavía estaría rondando el naufragio del Thoroval, abrumado por la desesperación hasta el fin de los días. Cuando regreses a Rivendel, ofrece mis saludos a Elrond y Aragorn, pero por favor, no compartas con mi heredero que solo puedo descansar con su coronación. Él lleva el peso del mundo tal como está. Le deseo suerte en las muchas batallas que están por venir.
'Adiós por ahora, ${PLAYER}. Permaneceré en las sombras, invisible, hasta el día en que pueda partir.'

'¡Lo hemos hecho! El poder combinado de Arvedui y los Sardirath fue suficiente para destruir el Helcessar para siempre. Hemos cumplido nuestra palabra con los Lossoth, impedido que el Rey Brujo corrompiera la reliquia y liberado a los Sardirath de su juramento, permitiéndoles descansar. Y parece que no son los únicos que han logrado una paz tan esperada.
'El espíritu de Arvedui parece haber cambiado por nuestras experiencias juntos, como si un gran peso se hubiera levantado de sus hombros. Deberías hablar con él y ver si esto es así.'

Y no debes olvidar que prometiste a los Lossoth que encontrarías una manera de destruirla para que ya no estén atados por su magia.'
Lothrandir cruza los brazos y mira hacia el hielo de abajo. Una sonrisa irónica aparece en su rostro, apenas visible bajo las sombras proyectadas por su capucha.

'We are so near to achieving our goal, ${PLAYER}! Gundabad belongs to my people, and neither Orc nor dragon will keep it from them any longer! Should Gorgar stand before us, he will be cut down! Should Hrímil Frost-heart seal the entrance with ice, as she has done, we will break through it... and then we will take her head and ensure she can never hinder us again!
'Every day, more dwarves arrive to swell this great force, this Gabil'akkâ of mine. Speak with Glóin and assess these new arrivals, and we will set them on tasks with which the Mountain-home shall be reclaimed!'

'The prince is right: more dwarves arrive every day. But I daresay he has not looked closely upon these new arrivals, or he should not speak so confidently of the help they will provide to us.
'These are not warriors! Most of the dwarves arriving now are peaceable folk: artists, craftsmen, and traders. They were lured here by the promise that Gundabad will once again be ours, and aye, so shall it be, but they seem to believe the war is done and the mountain is already ripe for the taking!
'Do you see there? More dwarves arrive, and I recognize one of their number from the halls of Erebor. Stáli the Hewer is so-named for his skill at sculpting, not for severing limbs from his foes! He is no fighter. Go tell him he has come too early, and should depart.'
'Tell Stáli to return to Erebor. He is an artist, not a warrior, and there are still battles to be won before he will do us any good here.'

'What's that? The mountain is not yet taken? What has Prince Durin's army been up to, then? I should have thought Gundabad would be well in hand by now!
'But you will not dissuade me. I have come all this way and will not return empty-handed. The Mountain-home has been held by the Orcs for too long, and it will take a sculptor's careful hand to restore the beauty it once possessed. Imagine the great works of art that must lie within, covered by the dust of years and ignored by the dismissive Orcs! Yes, the prince will need warriors... but he will need artists too, and I have answered the call he did not think to make. He will thank me, eventually.
'For now I need my luggage brought inside the fortress. You can help my apprentice with this task. Eskil! Carry my things! On the double, lad!'

At that grand meeting of the dwarves, the first held here in four thousand years, it was decided that a garrison would be left to hold the mountain; the greater portion of our armies departed for the last battle of that war, at Azanulbizar. Section the Second: Duties of the Sculptor =========================== The duties of the Sculptor shall only include responsibilities here listed. This is their full extent:
One (1): The Sculptor shall provide a weekly stipend of coin to the Apprentice, modified as described above in Section the First.
Two (2): The Sculptor shall provide instruction in the art of sculpting and the preparation of fine artwork (as time allows and at the Sculptor's inclination, informed by whether the Apprentice displays a natural propensity for the subject. This propensity is to be assessed by the Sculptor and by no other, save the King Under the Mountain, should the Apprentice choose to frivolously spend the king's time in this manner).

Section the Third: Ending the Agreement ========================== This agreement shall be binding for each of the listed parties, Apprentice and Sculptor alike, and it shall continue in effect until such time as Sculptor delivers to Dáin II, King Under the Mountain, a signed parchment containing the desire of both parties to terminate it. Without such a delivery, this agreement will continue in perpetuity.
May it be a fruitful and satisfactory apprenticeship for both parties!
Witnessed on this day the Third of October, in the Year 3018, with seals affixed, in the Hall Under the Mountain, by Dáin II Ironfoot, King Under the Mountain

Section the First: Duties of the Apprentice =========================== The duties of the Apprentice shall not be limited in any way by the omission of any particular duty in this section, but shall be deemed to include any such reasonable responsibilities that shall be suggested by the Sculptor. The meaning of \qreasonable\q for this section, and for any following section, shall be interpreted as \qthe course most likely to be favoured by the will of Dáin II, King Under the Mountain.\q
The duties of the Apprentice shall include, but be not limited to, the following responsibilities:
One (1): Acquisition of materials for the creation of any works of art required by the Sculptor, purchased with supplied coin. Any excess coinage is to be returned promptly and without fail. Upon discovery of such a failure, the excess will be tallied and deducted from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second).
Two (2): Thorough weekly cleaning of workshop space in order to foster creative work on the part of the Sculptor. Any spots missed in the cleaning shall be tallied and a percentage deducted from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second).
Three (3): Timely preparation of meals for the Sculptor, no earlier than eight in the morning for breakfast and no later than six of the clock for dinner; drinks to be made upon request. The Sculptor does not like berries of any kind on his plate, but he is partial to honey and any products made from it, such as mead. The appearance of berries anywhere near the Sculptor's table will be noted, and a deduction made from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second).
Four (4): Praise to be made for the Sculptor's work (when appropriate). Private criticism of such work will be noted, and a deduction made from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second). Public criticism will be noted twice, and count double.
Five (5): In the event of illness or maiming that causes the Apprentice to be unable to carry out his duties, be they daily or weekly in nature, he is to provide a substitute for the day or week in question. If the substitute is found lacking, such deficiency will be noted and a deduction made from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second). Similarly, if the Apprentice is deemed to be contagious and refuses to nominate a substitute, that will also be grounds for a deduction from his weekly stipend.
Six (6): Greeting guests of the Sculptor and assessing who is to be admitted and who is deemed unwelcome. The Sculptor's time is valuable and not to be wasted! Special consideration is to be given to those who bring gifts for the Sculptor, especially mead. The discovery that mead might have been given as a gift should the guest have been informed beforehand by the Apprentice will be met with disappointment, which is worse than anger. Disappointment in this case will take the form of a deduction from the Apprentice's weekly stipend (see Section the Second).

Preamble and Naming of the Parties ======================== Let it be known to all in the Lonely Mountain and its environs, and to every inhabitant of dwarfdom throughout this Middle-earth, that on this the third day of October, Dáin II Ironfoot, King Under the Mountain, did recognize and witness this agreement between two parties come before him.
The parties are named as follows, with due identification presented and accepted in the sight of King Dáin. Party the first: Stáli the Hewer, noted sculptor and artist of great renown, resident of Tumnu-dûm, the dwelling-halls, known herein as the Sculptor. Party the second: Eskil Bloodthumb, noteworthy accomplishments asked for by the first party but none were offered by the second and are therefore omitted; also a resident of Tumnu-dûm, the dwelling-halls, known herein as the Apprentice.
As a matter of course, the King Under The Mountain expressed his opinion that the parties enter into this agreement of apprenticeship of their own free wills, and that no undue influence was exercised upon either party.

'It's quiet here, ${PLAYER}, except for the sound of the wood creaking and the groaning of the support beams above, overtaxed by their heavy loads.
'Where are the guards? Where are Eskil's captors?'

'If you are here to slay Orcs, you have come too late! Ever since that cursed dragon arrived, raiding parties of hobgoblins have come through from time to time, but this last one was even worse than usual. It was all we could do to fight them off, and we paid for it!
'Garn! We sent for reinforcements from Gorgar, but they have still not arrived! We should have killed that goblin of his when we had the chance, and paid the consequence! But he is gone, and my boys all slain.
'The dwarf-prisoner? Glúrkub wouldn't let us eat him. Should have slain him anyway, and the goblin too. So what if Glúrkub had orders to keep him alive? He's still locked up, I expect. I don't think the hobgoblins were looking for him; they found me and the boys instead, and did us in. This injury could well be my last....'
'I will break the lock on Eskil's cell and release him. I do not think we will have much time before Gorgar's reinforcements get here, ${PLAYER}. Remain on guard!'

'Thank you for rescuing me, ${PLAYER}! I knew I should not have come to Deepscrave... but what choice did I have?
'My jailor was a goblin. Glúrkub he was called, I think, and the Orcs were afraid of him; it seemed to me that he must be high up in Gorgar's counsels. He forbade them from harming me. The last I saw of Glúrkub, he had Trausti's axe in his hand, but where he is now I do not know. After the hobgoblins attacked there was no more sign of him.
'Thank you both for coming to save me! I know I do not deserve it... I am no warrior, and can be of little help to the Gabil'akkâ!'

'Hail, friend! Are you here to study the tombs in the Houses of Rest? Well, it is not truly a scholarly mission that brought me hither; my father expects me to learn if the Orcs have defaced the tombs here during their long residence. But I am also interested in learning the names of the dwarf-families that lie here entombed, and thought I could accomplish both errands at once!
'Let us climb a little higher, ${PLAYER}. The path west of here eventually slopes upward to the north, near more of the crypts.'

'I find that Orc-sword quite curious. Did they fight among themselves for the privilege of ransacking the Houses of Rest?'
'As I climbed past the crypt-entrances, I tried to read the names of the families entombed within. It was not an easy task, for most of them have faded with the passage of the years, and I could not make many of them out.
'I saw markers for the Line of Arnvíth... the Line of Félag... Yngvi's Line...'
Bori stands up straight and rubs his chin.
'Perhaps the faded letters prevented the Orcs from disturbing the timeless sleep of the dwarves that lie within. For that let us be grateful. If the Orcs believed these dwarves had names of importance, they might have cracked open their tombs in search of wealth.
'I see signs that much else in the Pit of Stonejaws, and throughout the Mountain-home, was plundered and defaced. But how can this be so? Legend tells us that such villainy should have been prevented!'

'Many are the great stories that have come down through the ages to us, ${PLAYER}. They stir our passions and fill us with dwarf-pride. One of these tales concerns these very tombs: according to legend, the lords of Gundabad will one day rise from their crypts and walk once again among the living. When they see the evils perpetrated by the Orcs in Gundabad, they will unleash their wrath upon those who despoil the great dwarf-halls, slaying their enemies from sunrise to sunset. Then, when their day of reckoning is done, the great lords will return to the Houses of Rest and slumber again for eternity, the Mountain-home made free of their foes.
'<rgb=#00FF00>Look</rgb> out over the Pit of Stonejaws, ${PLAYER}, and tell me what you see.'

'Perhaps it is just a legend, after all. How could the dead lords of Gundabad stand by and watch for so many years, and do nothing?'

'Can you help me shift some of those rocks aside? I would like to take a look inside that room. It may be a tomb or memorial of some kind, and perhaps the debris kept the Orcs out even as it blocks our own passage.'

'No, my droll friend! My master Stáli did not send me here. His instructions were simple: \qFind me the Zabad'ibîn,\q he said. I reckoned they would be more likely found in dangerous places than in peaceful ones. A search of the chief-stead seemed in order. I found no gemstones, but there were plenty of Orc-skulls against which I tested the sharpness of my axe. Would that I had replaced my brother in his apprenticeship before this! Such fighting really gets the blood flowing, doesn't it?
'Perhaps Stáli will eventually teach me the ways of sculpture, but until then I think I will adopt axe-handling as my trade!'

'Mis hermanas están lejos de mí... No oigo sus cantos ni siento su suave aliento entre los árboles. Áridos están esos árboles, casi sin vida, ahogados por raíces hinchadas con algo que tiene un amargo sabor a hierro. ¿Dónde están mis hermanas, y qué tengo delante?
'No puedo ver más allá del rojo de esta tierra, pero percibo algo dulce entre los helechos amargos y las raíces hinchadas. ¿Eres real? ¿Sigo prisionera en la tierra?
'Hay vida en ti... lo siento. Debe de haber vida en algún otro rincón de estas tierras. Quizá pueda encontrar esa vida de nuevo y devolverla a la salud.'

La Doncella Roja está condenada (o eso parece) por la corrupción que han causado los Hombres en su tierra. Estos hombres se presentan ante ella, dispuestos a sacrificarse por la Doncella Roja, y merecen este destino... pero la nobleza de tu sangre será una recompensa aún mayor para ella. Cuando estos Hombres caigan por voluntad propia ante ella, sabrá la diferencia entre los que fortalecen y los que destruyen.

Los Créoth se sacrificarán a la Doncella Roja para restaurar sus fuerzas y su vínculo con la corrupción del pantano. Estos hombres no merecen más que la muerte, y tu presencia al oponerte a la Doncella Roja podría hacer que una parte de ella se dé cuenta de la insensatez de sus actos. Deberías dejar que los hombres mueran para fortalecer a la Doncella Roja, y luego derrotarla. Quizás así comprenda que la corrupción ha crecido demasiado y que debe regresar al mundo natural del que una vez formó parte.

'It is just as I said! This road may once have been little-travelled, but since their kingdom fell, the Angmarim have passed this way in great numbers.
'Cultists fled this way, but I do not think they came alone. If the Men of Angmar are like those I knew in Mordor, I am sure they filled their pockets with as much wealth as they could carry. I do not begrudge them that, though such riches are surely tainted by evil, and woe to those who seek to spend them! No, what worries me, and should worry you, is what else these cultists might have brought out of Angmar when their kingdom fell. Did they bring with them artifacts of fell power, relics of the Witch-king's rule? They might have brought anything from their defeated kingdom, ${PLAYER}.

'You are Durin the Seventh, and no Dragon-trick can change that. I will follow wherever you lead.'

'It is true: when Hrímil says \qtime to jump,\q Gorgar says \qhow high you want?\q But maybe she not trust her power over him. She summons Gorgar not to her lair, but to another place, called Lugroz by the Orcs.

Durin's breath still comes in ragged hitches, but he has for the moment mastered the fury that so seized him. He glowers at the encaged goblin with undisguised hatred, but now his expression contains something else: curiosity.

'Let this guide our next move. It will be dangerous, but it may yield treasure commensurate with the risk.'

'I did not want to hear the words of Glúrkub, ${PLAYER}, for they made me question many things I had long taken for granted. I thought the desire to reclaim Gundabad slept within the breast of any Longbeard; how could it not? To hear that the voice of a Dragon might have commanded it of me... I could not believe it.
'But it is one thing to hear a command, and it is another to obey. Hrímil may think she motivated the dwarves to strike against Gundabad too soon, the easier for her to destroy us, but she did not. It was the voice of a dwarf that I heard beyond the Anvil of Winterstith, ${PLAYER}, a dwarf-voice that drowned out the words of the Dragon. I will listen to that voice, and no other, and it spoke of victory in Gundabad.
'Depriving Gorgar of this mithril hammer is simply the first step. Next we will deprive him of his armies, and then we will take his life. And then we will come for his Dragon-master. She fears this hammer? Then let it be her undoing!'

'It was with the help of Glúrkub that Gorgar first acquired this hammer from Zul-mazal. If Hrímil fears it, I would see the chamber from where it came. Some clue to her fear might remain within, and this understanding may help us use it against her.

'Oh, it's you again. Do not forget that you owe me a favour! I did not have to release Eskil from his agreement with me, and chose to do so from benevolence only! You have surely noticed that my new apprentice has not retrieved the Zabad'ibîn for me, as you promised she would! You did not promise that? Well, someone did.
'But I do confess she has a better eye for artistry than her brother ever possessed. See this mosaic Fastrith brought to my attention? It is the perfect match to one that decorated the Hall Under the Mountain in Erebor, and which I was restoring before departing for Gundabad.
'My apprentice has somehow come into possession of numerous colourful stones with which I may be able to complete the mosaic. It will be another triumph by Stáli the Hewer, master sculptor!'

'Welcome back to Zul-mazal, ${PLAYER}! I understand that you helped dear Bróin collect stones and pebbles for me? Thank you for taking the time to do so... it can't have been easy!
'My master Stáli is very pleased that he may be able to complete this mosaic, although he tries not to show it. When I presented to him the pouch of colourful pebbles that Bróin gifted to me, he said he might begin my instruction in sculpture-carving sometime in the next ten years.

'With its thick walls and defensible approaches, my new stronghold of Biriz-zahar in the high mountains to the south was secure from any assault. My loyal Greymauls stood at the parapets of my city and gloated, insisting that Durin's warriors would be unable to ascend the heights and the former king would meet our demands.
'But I wondered, and I worried. The defences of Biriz-zahar were strong... but I feared they would not be strong enough. Word reached me that the former king had assembled a vast army of Longbeards, and even now he marched at its head to put down the revolt. We could not hope to match such numbers as Durin levied, and the size of the approaching host was more than double my own.
'In Biriz-zahar I had built my tomb. This truth came slowly to me, but it did not come to me alone.'

'Orc and dwarf and troll marched side by side in the Misty Mountains for the first time, and as Durin's own army approached Gundabad my combined force fell upon his with a ferocity he could never have anticipated. The rout was total and complete, and the finest warriors of Khazad-dûm fled from the hammers of the Greymauls and the fangs of the Orcs and the clubs of the mountain-trolls.
'Durin's eldest sons were slain by Orcs in that first battle, and I thought it meet; had I not lost my own sons, save Módvit, to such as they? It seemed little different to me at the time, though I had joined hands with the forces of Morgoth and his commander Sauron; it was Durin drove me to do so, and if there was to be blame let it lie with him!
'My forces returned in triumph to Biriz-zahar, and my commanders believed the war had reached a decisive end. I knew it was not so. I knew it for what it proved to be: the beginning only.'
Durin cannot understand why his namesake would have trusted Mótsog with the lordship of Gundabad.

'How could Durin the Deathless entrust one such as Mótsog with the rule of his kingdom? It beggars belief, ${PLAYER}! Were there no indications of Mótsog's evil, or of his treacherous nature?'

'Durin took the greater portion of the Longbeards with him to found the Dwarrowdelf of Khazad-dûm, and I governed those who remained behind. Those years were hard and bloody, for the Orcs had been emboldened by the exodus of so many dwarves; they sought to conquer Gundabad.
'We held them back, but with so few defenders the cost was high. Six of my seven sons were slain in those wars, and only the youngest, Módvit, survived to be named my sole heir. My heart grew cold, and only Orc-slaying could bring me any joy. The heads of our enemies adorned the gates of the Mountain-home.
'Some among my people whispered that Durin had abandoned us to the encircling Orcs. During the years that followed the whispers grew, and with them my own legend: noble Mótsog who stood alone against all the forces of Morgoth, fighting to preserve his people. My son Módvit became the fiercest of my adherents, and in time he had me believing what was said of me: that I was equal to, or perhaps even greater than, the king himself.'

'The sight of mithril weapons in the hands of the Elves had kindled a dark flame of greed and envy in my heart. How many of my people might have been spared had Durin given such true-steel to we who remained? How many of my sons might have survived battle with the Orcs and trolls that sought to conquer the Mountain-home, had they possessed weapons of such quality?
'Only one son remained to me on that dark day, and it was he who slew the Elf-captain. His people leapt to the defence, wielding their mithril blades with deadly skill, but Módvit was not alone, and my worthiest commanders stood with him.
'When the fighting was ended, my spear too dripped with the blood of my guests.'

'The two armies of the dwarves had won the day, but each had suffered grievous losses. And yet their wounds did not quench their battle-fury; Longbeard and Greymaul alike pursued the retreating Orcs, slaying them by the thousand. The Orc-host was so badly-defeated it would not trouble the Misty Mountains for the remainder of the age.
'Consumed with frustrated wrath, Morgoth's lieutenant Sauron witnessed his allies' defeat and fled with the surviving dragons back to Thangorodrim, where he would face his master's displeasure.
'Let us hurry. The memory of the charnel house that Biriz-zahar became pains my heart.'

'The Greymauls who survived the Sunder-battle, though they were few in number, were granted mercy. They were made to shear their beards short as penance for raising weapons against their proper king and for allying with the Orcs, and for generations after no child of a Greymaul was permitted to wear his or her beard longer than a hand's breadth.
'Many dwarves looked upon the Greymauls with distrust for years afterward, but none more so than Ragna the Fierce. She it was who suggested that dwarf-women should remain ever-vigilant in the halls of their folk, for hearth and home can be endangered when watchfulness fails. Ragna swore to never again allow such rebellion to grow and thrive in the halls of her people, and for all her remaining years and for those of her daughters, it did not.'

'A simple dwelling was fashioned in the caverns deep beneath Gundabad, and it was there that Mótsog went to live out his remaining years. I brought supplies and provisions to that deep cavern from time to time, for Mótsog refused to walk among the dwarves who lived in the halls above. As a hermit he lived, he who once pretended to kingship. He never again raised a weapon in anger.
'Was I his jailor or his friend, ${PLAYER}? I see now that I was both, but it was not I alone who kept him here. Mótsog remained in this place for the guilt he felt, and as the years passed, folk who lived in Gundabad and elsewhere forgot the dwarf he had been and remembered only his name and the ill repute of his deeds.'

By the time Ragna freed Durin, two thirds of the dwarves had perished to flame and black steel. 'Hear then the end of the tale, as I know it to be.

'Aye, Durin gave me my life, both mercy and punishment. I have remained in this chamber ever since, casting my dreaming gaze over the mountains, watching from afar the trials of the dwarves. I say it was mercy, for truly I deserved a usurper's death, but so too do I call it punishment, for I was unable to intervene or aid them in their struggles.
'On rare occasions one of those I watched would seem to catch a glimpse of me, but never in my own form. Was this a cruelty of the First Crafter, or some confounding jest? I cannot say. But this I know: only once did he to whom I spoke hear my words.
'It was Durin who heard me, Durin who returned again and again with new visage but the same spirit in his breast. Only Durin heard my words, my friend of old who showed me the mercy I did not deserve. So often had I sought to aid the dwarves in their trials, and so often failed. But when Durin stood before the Anvil of Winterstith I spoke to him of Gundabad and his right to rule the Mountain-home for all dwarves, and he listened. It must mean something. My long penance nears its end, and the prolonged hours of my dream must soon pass away. Soon I will wake, and Mótsog will be no more.'

'Were I not to be king when my father leaves the throne, I could say to Mótsog, \qBe gone. No, the injuries left by that conflict remain with us. Do Zhélruka and Longbeard not bristle at the perceived slights of the other, and ponder if something of the Greymaul spirit lives on behind their rival's clenched teeth? Do they not look upon the Stout-axe with distrust, brooding upon his long habitation in Mordor? The lesson of Mótsog was taught to the dwarves early, and did not diminish with the years.
'Were I not to be king when my father releases the crown, I could climb the secret stair to the known levels of Gundabad, leaving Mótsog and what I learned here behind. Then I ask you to seek out a leader of the Iron Garrison such as Bósi or his kin, Glóin of the Longbeards, Prince Ingór of the Zhélruka, and Imák the Stout-axe, and tell them to bring their companies of dwarves to the Thing-fold for Dwarrowmoot.'

'The time has come for me to call for Dwarrowmoot, a meeting of all the dwarves here in the Mountain-home. It was held at the Thing-fold in the Welkin-lofts whenever dwarves had grave matters to discuss or a need that could not be addressed without a consensus of many dwarf-lords. It was a ritual for the martialing of war or the making of peace, and was common at one time. When Gundabad was briefly reclaimed at the outset of the Sixth War, the first Dwarrowmoot in four thousand years was called at the Fold, and the course of that conflict was decided.
'I will call for Dwarrowmoot once again, ${PLAYER}. There I will explain the final steps we must take to drive Hrímil Frost-heart and her thrall Gorgar from Gundabad. Only then will the Mountain-home be ours again.
'Climb the secret stair back to Zul-mazal. Seek out a leader of the Iron Garrison such as Bósi or his kin, Glóin of the Longbeards, Prince Ingór of the Zhélruka, and Imák the Stout-axe, and tell them to bring their companies of dwarves to the Thing-fold for Dwarrowmoot.'

'${PLAYER}! What did you discover beyond those secret stairs? How fares the prince? Has he need of us? We are ready!'
You tell Bróin that Durin does have need of him, and indeed the prince calls for the rest of his kin to answer his call.
'Dwarrowmoot? Can it be? I will send word to the others, and at once! We shall assemble at the Thing-fold and there await Prince Durin!'

'Dwarrowmoot, eh? So we come to it at last. Good! The Zhélruka will hear what the Longbeard prince has to say, and we will await our reward when the fighting is done.
'Aye, there will be fighting, make no mistake of that. Durin calls for the dwarves to assemble at the Thing-fold in the Welkin-lofts, after all. Has he not considered how exposed that hillside is to the air? We will be meeting in full view of the peak, from which Hrímil watches over the lands all about.
'One thing is clear to me, ${PLAYER}. Dwarrowmoot will decide the fate of Gundabad, and of us all... one way or another.'

'Dwarrowmoot! To think I should live to see another! I remember the glory of the last, though I was just a lad. Thráin led a great attack upon the Fold, recovering it from the Orcs for the first time in thousands of years. He called for the lords to determine where the hammer stroke of our war should fall; we left Gundabad when it was decided, and only a small garrison remained. Much might have been different had the Moot chosen otherwise.'
Glóin shakes his head.
'But that was long ago, and now our concerns are with the Mountain-home and not at Khazad-dûm; we need not have our attention divided. I will gather the Longbeards, ${PLAYER}. My prince will have his Moot!'

'Dwarrowmoot? Is that what it sounds like?
'Well, you must forgive me, but I was not present at the last one! The Stout-axes had other things on their minds, as you might imagine! But I will attend this one. My people should be represented, for this Moot may determine the success of the conquest. There are few of my people here, but they will answer Durin's call.
'Durin can count on my attendance, and on my axe, if it comes to that.'

'I must thank you again, my friend, for all your help. We could not have retaken the Mountain-home without you!'

'You should have seen it, ${PLAYER}! The Orcs pressed in around us and I thought for sure it was the end. But then Fastrith and Bróin came rushing by, and they swung their axes so swiftly and in such concert they seemed to be one dwarf and not two! I have never seen anything like it!
'Their battle-dance was really something. You don't suppose Fastrith has a sister she hasn't mentioned? I never cared much for wooing before, but the sight of their spirited scuffle has made me want to find a deadly dwarf-woman with which to share such joyful combat, and let our enemies beware!
'You let me know if you find one, ${PLAYER}, and I shall tidy my beard and sharpen my axe-blade, the better to impress her!'

'You made it, ${PLAYER}! We did not have a good view of the peak, so I could not tell exactly what befell you once you departed up the slope, but Bróin assured me that you knew what you were doing.
'As for us, it turns out that Bróin and I complement each other in battle fairly well! I knew what his axe would do even before he did, and he knew the same for mine! I would prefer not to boast, but I daresay the Orcs will not choose to tangle with the two of us for some time! And if they do: beware!
'Once my master Stáli begins to teach me the art of sculpting, I should like to immortalize this battle in stone! Picture this, ${PLAYER}: me and dear Bróin back to back, axes at the ready, while a whirlwind of Orcs and hobgoblins encircle us. Our foes are carved from a single sweep of the rock, with no telling where one enemy ends and another begins! And for a name? Hmmm... perhaps I will call it \qThe Courtship!'
Fastrith blushes suddenly.
'Well, perhaps. We will see! Names are very difficult, aren't they?'

'When first I came to Elderslade, I asked you to keep a secret for me, ${PLAYER}. Do you remember? I feared I did not have the courage to fight another war like the one that claimed my father Brogur's life, in dark Khazad-dûm. And I did not. When the Dragon appeared above the Dwarrowmoot, it was as if I was back in the depths of that drowned treasury, scared and alone, but this time there was no Zigilburk near at hand, no hope of survival. I despaired, ${PLAYER}, and I thought to run.'
Bróin stares at his feet. When he looks up at you again, a fire blazes in his eyes.
'But then I saw Fastrith standing near, and a great courage rushed through me, a courage I never thought I could have again. I raised my axe, and without a word the two of us set upon the approaching Orcs, and our battle-dance was like nothing I had ever experienced. I would not have thought it possible! But so it was, and now Gundabad is ours!'

'This was a great victory for the Longbeards, and for Prince Durin! You know what that means: there will be a tremendous call for me to make statues of everyone involved, heroes in mighty pose with their weapons aloft! I will be kept busy for years, and will need to hollow out the mountain entire to have stone enough! Perhaps I should accelerate the training of my apprentice after all....
'But one thing still confuses me, ${PLAYER}. I am perplexed by the identity of the mysterious dwarf you accompanied to the peak. Do you know who he was?'
You stare at Stáli in disbelief, for surely the sculptor has spent hours working on mosaics depicting the likeness of Mótsog.
'You don't know either, I suppose,' Stáli continues. 'He did seem a regal and powerful figure. I wonder if he knows anything about the Zabad'ibîn?'
Mótsog gazes toward the western horizon.

'My day is nearly up, friend of my friend. The sun is setting.
'I will rest well with the knowledge that Durin is once again at home in Gundabad, as he should have been. And when he is king, he will lead all the dwarves into a new age of peace and prosperity, as was always his desire.'
Mótsog stands quietly for a moment. When next he speaks, his voice is low, as if he addresses someone you cannot see.
'In all the long years of my sleep, through which I watched all the trials of the dwarves, I have seen the end of countless days. But I have never seen a sunset so beautiful as this.'
Lost in his thoughts, he has forgotten you stand near. You decide to leave him in peace.
Mótsog gazes at the western horizon
The Gabil'akkâ celebrates its victory in Gundabad.
The Gabil'akkâ celebrates its victory in Gundabad.

'Hrímil Frost-heart is wounded, and we will need to deal with her, but for now let us enjoy the victory!
'What say my dwarves? What say my courageous allies?
'Let all take up the cheer: Gundabad is ours!'

'It is done, ${PLAYER}. Durin has agreed that the Zhélruka will have a place in Gundabad, and I am satisfied. Let the old rivalries wash away in the torrent of our shared hardships, and let new bonds be forged by the blood we spilled together.
'There will still be work to do to make a home for my people in Gundabad, but I welcome it. If you help us the work will be easier! What say you to this, ${PLAYER}? Good, good. The Zhélruka welcome your assistance!'

'We have done it, ${PLAYER}! Prince Durin has achieved what he swore to do, and the Mountain-home has been reclaimed!
'Aye, there remains a dragon to manage, but I saw her flight as she flew away, wounded, and I deem more than her pride was injured here. And without Gorgar to command, her grip over Orc-kind will surely be loosened.
'Enjoy the victory, but prepare for the next! It is a Longbeard saying, but all of the Gabil'akkâ would do well to keep it in mind!'

'We have the victory, ${PLAYER}! Gundabad is ours.'
Bósi nods with satisfaction despite his own injury.
'Brogur would be pleased at our success, but if I know my cousin he would be disappointed that he missed all the fighting. And yet, his son Bróin fought well when the Dwarrowmoot was interrupted, so perhaps fatherly pride would prove a balm for Brogur's heart.'
Bósi peers at you closely.
'Do you know something, my friend? During the battle, while you made your way to the peak, I thought I saw my cousin fighting alongside you. It must have been only a trick of the light, but for a moment I would have sworn it was Brogur. Well, it is a day for battle-shouts and tales of glory, and those were always my cousin's favourite days. Perhaps he could not resist one more.'

'When we set out for the Wells of Langflood from Skarháld, did you think this is where our journey would lead? I tell you now that I did, for the Zhélruka are noted optimists!'
Venko laughs long and loudly.
'Perhaps not, my friend. But both Durin and Prince Ingór have reached an understanding, and their agreement should end years of tension and conflict. A place will be made for my people in Gundabad, and we will work together with the Longbeards to defend it from any who would seek to take it from us, whether they be Orc or Dragon or any other fearsome foe!
'I will yet have a hearth above which to hang my brothers' swords, and I know both Lékhun and Dúsek would be pleased.'

'Are all such Dwarrowmoots so eventful, ${PLAYER}? You should have told me you planned to invite Hrímil Frost-heart and her armies!
'But the day belongs to us, and the Dragon has escaped to nurse her wounds. If Durin and the Zhélruka prince know what they are doing they will dispatch courageous warriors to put an end to the threat of her, and fast! Still, this is a great victory, and I intend to celebrate it. I advise you do the same!'

'Where has Mótsog gone? I wished to speak with him before the day was ended.
'It is not too late, is it? Will you come with me, ${PLAYER}? Let us find him in the chamber beneath Gundabad, if it is not already too late. There is something I wished to ask him, and I will regret it if I do not!'
Durin awaits Mótsog's reply, and does not speak.

'Good-bye, Mótsog. Once I called you friend, and once enemy. Let us part now as friends, for there will be no chance more to make it otherwise.
'Take your rest, last of the Greymauls, and know that on this, your last day, you were a son of Gundabad, and a proud dwarf.'
Durin studies the statue where Mótsog once stood.

'He is gone.'
Durin sighs deeply and peers around the now-empty chamber.
'Whatever distant sight was given to Mótsog by the First Crafter is gone with him, ${PLAYER}. I thought he might have advised me one way or the other, and so help me make this choice: should Khazad-dûm stay lost to us, or is it to be my task to reclaim it? But he guided me not.
'And yet, I still feel comforted by his words. Why should that be so? Perhaps it is because it is as he said: those who stand with me will lend me their courage. One day, perhaps, it will fall to me to lead another union of dwarves to the Doors of Durin, and on that day Khazad-dûm will belong to dwarves forevermore.
'In this age or the next, did he say? Let us work together, then, and see that the age that comes will be one of peace and prosperity for all the good folk of this Middle-earth!'
Durin takes one more look around the chamber and hefts the Red Axe in his hand.
'And in the end, perhaps the lesson of Mótsog will be this: not all stories end when they seem to, but rather they continue, and you cannot fully judge one's part in it during the telling! Both good acts and evil shape the world, in Gundabad no more nor less than anywhere else, and it is the duty of good-hearted folk to care for those who dwell in it. Will you take up this duty with me, my friend, and make that the legacy we leave behind?'
You assure Durin that he can rely on you.
'Very good, ${PLAYER}. We will begin in Gundabad, and who knows where else the adventure will take us? But we will meet it gladly, with courage in our hearts and our eyes on the horizon.'
Durin's face is burdened with expectation as he waits for Mótsog's response

'Where has Mótsog gone? I wished to speak with him before the day was ended.
'It is not too late, is it? Will you come with me, ${PLAYER}? Let us find him in the chamber beneath Gundabad, if it is not already too late. There is something I wished to ask him, and I will regret it if I do not!'

'We are not too late, ${PLAYER}, but I deem his time is short.'
Durin addresses the silent figure.
'Mótsog, I cannot forgive you for the treachery in your past, but I acknowledge the aid you provided to the Gabil'akkâ in the reclamation of Gundabad. For that you have not only my gratitude but that of every dwarf whose heart longed for the Mountain-home to be restored. So too do you have the thanks of dwarves not yet born, who will now know a world where Gundabad will never again be held by the Orcs.'
Durin nods, that business accomplished. When next he speaks his voice is tinged with curiosity and worry.
'This question is for me, Mótsog, not as a prince or a king to be, but as a dwarf only. Did you see in your dream whether I would one day have victory in Khazad-dûm? I would have us reclaim it, as we have with Gundabad... but I cannot tell if only failure awaits us as it did the Iron Garrison, and Balin before.'

'My dream is ending, Durin. I will watch no more.
'Your fate is your own, and will be the result of the choices you make. Whether those may lead to good ends or ill will be up to you, and to those who stand with you.
'But I have seen our kind face innumerable trials during the long years of my vigil. It is the belief of this dwarf that you will have success, in this age or the next, though it seem far away and nearly impossible to achieve.
'Farewell, Durin, both my oldest friend and my newest. Farewell.'

Habla con Glóin en Annâk-khurfu

${PLAYER},
A pesar de nuestros muchos triunfos, la Guerra de las Tres Cumbres ha tenido un gran costo. Para algunos de nuestros parientes entre los Gabil'akkâ, la victoria parece no estar más cerca que cuando el príncipe Durin hizo su juramento ante el Yunque del Pico Invernal.
Gorgar, hijo de Bolgo, todavía nos elude. A sabiendas o no, ese maldito dragón frío, Hrímil Corazónhelado, le permitió escapar de su destino. Es poco consuelo que no haya amor perdido entre los dos, ya que su odio hacia los enanos podría ser suficiente para dejar de lado sus enemistades al menos por el momento. No todo está perdido, y me mantengo firme en mis palabras, pero es difícil para los Enanos de los Gabil'akkâ ver la batalla en el umbral de Gundabad como algo más que un costoso revés. Y, para la mente del príncipe Durin, una derrota imperdonable.
Aunque no lo ha dicho en voz alta ni tan claramente, el príncipe Durin ha puesto sus pensamientos en la venganza. En verdad, contempla una gran ofensiva para romper las puertas y reclamar el Monte Gundabad a toda costa. No sobrepasaré los límites de mi posición, pero soy un enano lo suficientemente viejo como para saber que la caza de la venganza podría resultar tan mortal como cualquier arma que nuestros enemigos puedan empuñar contra nosotros.
El príncipe Durin conoce bien el valor de su consejo, y creo que juntos tu y yo podríamos convencerlo de sopesar el curso más sabio hasta el final de esta guerra. Y así, humildemente le pido que regrese a Annâk-khurfu.
Hablemos pronto, camarada.
-Glóin

Habla con Durin en Annâk-khurfu

'Me cuesta creer cuánto ha cambiado todo desde que partiste de Valle Ancestral. Me han dicho que estudiaste el relato de Hermáth sobre la Sexta Guerra, y quizás yo también debería hacerlo cuando finalmente regrese a la Montaña Solitaria. Mientras tanto, ¡tengo la suerte de tener a Martillotormenta a mi lado!
'La última sangre de Azog aún reside en el Monte Gundabad, pero cuando llegue la prueba final en esos sagrados salones, ¡seremos victoriosos! Ni Gorgar ni Hrímil nos impedirán alcanzar nuestro premio.
'Si no fuera por ti y Glóin, yo... gracias, camarada.'

<rgb=#00FF00>Se recomienda, pero no es obligatorio, que completes Los legados de Durin y las pruebas de los Enanos, capítulos 1-4 antes de jugar 'Sangre de Azog'.</rgb>
'Me alegra verte de nuevo, ${PLAYER}. No es la manera en que hubiera preferido reunirnos, pero me temo que no había otra opción.
'Aunque he intentado convencerlo de lo contrario, el príncipe Durin se culpa a sí mismo por el revés en las puertas del monte Gundabad. Lo considera una derrota, un fracaso y, quizás sobre todo, un reproche a su valía para llevar el nombre Durin. Aunque eso no sea cierto, temo que crea que la venganza podría ser su único camino hacia la redención ante los Barbiluengos.
'El príncipe Durin ha escuchado muchas historias sobre las hazañas de su abuelo, pero ni él ni siquiera el rey Thorin las conocen como yo. En mi juventud, aprendí de primera mano el costo de la venganza. ¡Estuve en Azanulbizar! ¡Sé bien el precio que se pagó para ver la cabeza de Azog puesta sobre una pica!
'Es cierto que Gorgar y Hrímil nos esperan más allá de las puertas del monte Gundabad, pero dentro del Hogar de la Montaña, la ventaja les pertenece a ellos. Si queremos ganar esta guerra y reclamar la montaña sagrada, nuestros soldados deben tener tiempo para atender sus heridas y prepararse para las batallas venideras.
'Ayudemos al príncipe Durin a guiar a los Gabil'akkâ hacia la victoria, camarada. Eso es todo lo que pido.'

Durin se encuentra en la sala de guerra de Annâk-khurfu.
Después de hablar con Hermáth Martillotormenta, Durin ha decidido que los Gabil'akkâ marcharán sobre el monte Gundabad en siete días. Debes hablar con Durin.

Tras la huida de Gorgar, hijo de Bolgo, y el sellado de las puertas del monte Gundabad por Hrímil Corazónhelado, el príncipe Durin se enfrenta a su primera prueba verdadera. Mientras Durin sopesa si la venganza o la sabiduría guiará su mano, los pensamientos del señor Glóin se vuelven hacia conflictos antiguos. Demasiado familiarizado con los triunfos y las penas del Pueblo de Durin, Glóin espera que una lección de historia pueda moderar el deseo del príncipe Durin de poner fin a la Guerra de las Tres Cumbres a cualquier precio.
