You cannot leave it in the possession of the Angmarim, for they will use it for some evil purpose. You must take it with you. Perhaps Hórin will know of a place where this artifact can be made safe?

'${PLAYER}, you return! Did you find anything in Mullach Cagar? Wait... something about your demeanour has changed. What has happened?'
You show Hórin the staff. His eyes widen and his skin blanches.
'What in the name of the First Crafter is THAT?'
You explain that you found it in the Angmarim camp and believe it to be a powerful artifact of evil. You tell him too that it resisted your efforts to destroy it.
'Well, I think you were right to take it. We can't let the Angmarim keep such an artifact of evil. But I am no expert on the subject of fighting such magic! Who knows what might be unleashed if we did manage to destroy it? I think it might just be best for you to hold onto it for now. You are the most powerful among us, and we don't have time to cart it off to your Wizard-friend Gandalf! We have a war to fight!'

If anything, the Orcs and hobgoblins are even more dangerous now, for they work in unison rather than tearing at each others' throats. 'The unknown factor in all of this is Loknashra. Hrímil was unable to control her, due to whatever dark magic the Angmarim instilled in her, and she spoke of revenge. I have a feeling she will soon make some move, and we must be ready for it... whatever form it takes.

'Bah, the bridge is out! I suppose I should not have expected the road to be in good condition after all these years. The Orcs certainly wouldn't maintain it! Let us see if we can find a way around by walking across that frozen lake down there. Hmm. Molkha should be around here somewhere. Keep an eye out for her signal.'

'Hello again, ${PLAYER}. Keep an eye on the sky, because this area is a drake hunting ground! A big one flies overhead quite often, hunting for goats. I've seen him pluck one right off the side of the mountain and carry it up to the cliff tops there, where I wager he has a nest of whelplings to feed!
'As for my report, I have both good news and bad. The good news is that I was able to observe the hobgoblins passing through here. The bad news is... well, I should just start from the beginning.'

'Now that the camp is ready to receive our reinforcements and provide us adequate shelter in this harsh place, it is time we venture out in search of our enemies. Ausma's apprentices Molkha, Kyrstig, and Klúso are out there in the wild somewhere, spying on the hobgoblin host. They are to signal us when they see us approaching and give to us their report. If we're lucky, they will have some information on why Dushtalbúk is all the way up here in the freezing cold!
'Let us begin by heading south up the Father's Path. It should wind all the way up the peaks, but who can say what condition the ancient road might be in? Lead the way, ${PLAYER}.'
'Let me start from the beginning. Here's what I saw....'

'It seems our enemies are forming alliances right in front of our faces! My blood boils to hear how they use fallen dwarves as bargaining chips in their games of state-craft! Even with those \qgifts\q, I did not foresee the Frost-horde accommodating the Angmarim in this fashion. From what I understood, Sauron's torture of Hrímil had made his former servants her hated enemies. I remember what she did to Karazgar, the Weeping Warrior! It may be that times change, or perhaps she has some nefarious plan in mind for her former foes? Bah, trying to understand the motivations of a Dragon feels like a waste of time. She means to use whatever is at her disposal to exterminate the dwarves, I'm sure!
'But I do think this news merits some investigation before we continue. We need to know why the Angmarim are up here in the first place, and we need to do something about this nest of drakes before they threaten Fellgát and our approaching reinforcements.'

'That is all I saw. Although the Orcs and hobgoblins are not on friendly terms, Dushtalbúk and Loknashra are forming alliances of their own. I expect that is bad news for us, yes?
'The Angmarim have set up camp to the south-east. They call it Mullach Cagar. I am afraid I do not know their aims, but that camp must be of some importance to them. They have poured no small effort into proving themselves valuable allies to the hobgoblins, seemingly to gain safe passage from the drakes. I hope you and Hórin can find out more. I have a very bad feeling about this.'

As you sift through the first few pages of Hermáth Stormhammer's account of the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs, you notice the author has written a foreword.

'It was at the behest of Dáin, my dear friend and King Under the Mountain, that I embarked upon writing a complete account of the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs. For too long, Durin's Folk had endured hardship after hardship, and it did not seem proper to dwell on such a sorrowful chapter in our history.
'Where my own memory and experiences did not serve the tale, I enlisted the accounts of others, chief among them the sons of Fundin and Gróin, and by his own request, King Dáin. For this, they have my truest gratitude.
'As a final note, I have laboured to construct this tale that the reader might see it through mine own eyes. If I should interject on occasion, it is only to make clear certain details or include aspects of the tale learned long after the war's end.'
Beneath the foreword, you notice a dedication.
'For Durin'

Become Hermáth Stormhammer!

'Alas, such are the disadvantages of being the grandson of the Lord of the Iron Hills!
'But you, my friend... I suspect you could pass among the others in this great Haban’akkâ without a second glance, even with that hammer of yours!'
In the distance, you see the Haban'akkâ of Thráin encamped at Amdân
As you walk among the Iron-folk, you catch sight of your friend Dáin

Dáin can be found among the Iron-folk at Amdân.
You should talk to Dáin.
Habla con Dáin en Amdân

'Hermáth, my friend! I was beginning to think we lost you on the Great-way!'
Dáin embraces you warmly.
'It is hard to believe that we are here at last. I have read the stories of old Azanulbizar, but none could describe it in such detail.
'It seems fitting that this war should end where it began, don't you think?
'And if what I have heard is true, we will not have to sit idle for much longer!'

'By the winter of T.A. 2799, King Thráin and his great reckoning-host, the Haban'akkâ, had made camp at Amdân, the ancient threshold of the kingdom of Khazad-dûm. It had been a long journey, for they had made a wide march around Lórien and come up from the south, treading the old stones of the Great-way.
'All through Amdân, Dwarves of the Seven Houses grew restless. I, like all of the Iron-folk, were camped near to the House of Thráin.
'Although few of us knew it at the time, it was to be the eve of battle.'

'As the battle continued on the slopes of Zirakzigil and Bundushâthur, I was recalled to Khur Azan. It seemed that Dáin's ruse had not gone as unnoticed as he thought, but more pressing matters were at hand.
'Indeed, the Iron-folk had marched forth from Amdân at last—not yet to join the battle, but to stand closer in reserve after King Thráin's vanguard burst through the Orkish encampment of Kamaz-kala, the furthest border of Azog's would-be realm.'

'As we heard at the council last night, King Thráin has ordered the Seven Houses to aid upon the fringes of the dale.
'Among them, the Landorrim, Narfanghoth, and Temámir have travelled to Zirakazhâr on the slopes of Zirakzigil. Once it is reclaimed from the Orcs, I fear they shall have to contend with the trolls we spied from afar.
'As for the Kámbrada, Zhélruka, and Abnúzhu... they have a harder path to take. If they can break through the Orkish outpost blocking the way to Tharkh Shathur, they intend to claim Ashmargathâl and set siege to Atrad-zarakh, the old warding-spire of Khazad-dûm.
'It is far too much, indeed, to ask of any one of the Seven Houses, but together, we will triumph! By Durin's beard, Azog will not live to see the morrow!'
Chapter 2: The Assault on Azanulbizar

'A moment, ${PLAYER}?'
King Thorin clears his throat, seemingly a bit uneasy.
'I believe it is time I spoke to Hermáth—both to offer him a proposal and to apologize.'

'My heart feels lighter this day, ${PLAYER}.
'I am pleased that Hermáth and I could finally speak plainly of our sorrows. And I am even more pleased that he has entertained the idea of joining the Gabil'akkâ!'

'Ah, good! Hersegg is home.
'It has been too long since last I spoke to Hermáth....'
King Thorin notes a look of surprise on your face. After a moment, he raises an eyebrow in what seems to be some sort of amusement.
'Hah! Hermáth may have grown old, but he is still a hale warrior—and very much alive! I thought that was clear, my friend!
'Hersegg seems quite engrossed in her reading. Would you find out if Hermáth is around?'

'Oh, I am sorry, ${PLAYER}. I didn't even hear you come in!'
You ask Hersegg if Hermáth is around, also noting the slight misunderstanding you had with King Thorin regarding her grandfather.
'Grandfather Hermáth? I never said he was dead!
Hersegg chuckles to herself.
'Yes, yes, of course. I'll let him know that King Thorin is here!'
'I think that went well, my friend.'

'Good, you're here! Are you ready to tear this place apart? Ausma must have gone to the throne room. We can't go the same way as last time. Trust me, I already checked: the hobgoblins removed the stairs! So, we're going to have to go through the front door, and through a lot of foes beside! If we make enough noise out here, maybe the distraction will help Ausma!'
'This must be the throne room! We might have to fight Warlord Dushtalbúk as soon as we enter. Are you ready?'
'Kyrstig wants to go in after Ausma? I am with her, of course! Stout-axes do not abandon their own!'

'Kyrstig wants to go after Ausma? Well, I applaud her bravery, but it seems risky to storm the hobgoblin fort with so few of us. And Ausma clearly ordered us to stay here. Hmm....
'All right, I'll do it, but if we get in trouble for disobeying her orders, you'll be the one to shoulder the blame!'
'It's decided then! The three of us will move towards Shakhajât. Come meet us when you're ready, and we will launch our attack!'

'And here we are, back at camp, all safe and sound.'
Ausma sighs deeply, clearly unhappy about the outcome of her mission.
'Honestly, my pride is more wounded than my body, but I will have to sit out on some of our upcoming missions. I will ensure Shakhajât has an adequate watch, and station myself in Vérnozal to oversee the Gabil'akkâ's operations. You and my apprentices have more to do, however! When it is time to make our move on the hobgoblins, I will send word to you to find Hórin. Until then, go, explore Gundabad, and win many battles for us!'

There are many Longbeard ancestors entombed in the Houses of Rest, and we cannot allow them to be drafted into an army of the dead. I am sending you and my apprentices to deal with this matter at once. You will split up and attack each tomb at the same time, preventing any of these Angmarim snakes from slithering away! I will keep watch on Shakhajât in the meantime, and warn you should the hobgoblins move to assist the cultists. Have you any questions?'
'When you are ready to depart, the four of you will attack at once. We will nip this wight problem in the bud.'
'Molkha and Klúso were right! Ausma is gone! Look around and see if you can find any sign of where she went. I really hope something horrible hasn't happened....'

'And so, the pyres burned away and so the ashen dale of Azanulbizar was abandoned. Although none beheld them at the battle's end, we later learned the Elves of the Golden Wood had borne witness to our deeds, spying the smoke from afar as it rose into the sky above the dale. As King Thráin had named them at Durin's Stone, the Marasrân—the Burned Dwarves came to occupy a place of great honour and reverence among Durin's Folk. Long after, among each of the Seven Houses, all a Dwarf needed to say about his ancestor was 'he was Marasrûn' and it would elicit grave nods and murmurs of respect.
'In time, the other Houses departed back to their homes, bearing the burdens of the arms and amour collected from their dead. As for the Iron-folk, we too departed, making the long journey back to Járnfast. Dáin became the Lord of Iron Hills in all but title, for Grór had become lost in his sorrows, surviving his father, brothers, and now his son alike with not one among them whose bones he could honour.
'Last of all, King Thráin and the exiles departed. They were few now and weary, having lost much and won little in the war, but south they went along the Great-way, until at last they returned to Zudrugund.
'The Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs was ended—the cost too great, the prize too small to hold.'

'Azog is slain, and the Ironfoot has taken his head. The Orcs should know the battle has turned against them!
'And yet, some of Azog's own clan still cling to their meagre holdings outside the Great Gates. It cannot stand!
'Slay these... Ufúrzrak, and drive the rest of his ilk back beyond the gates of Khazad-dûm! Azanulbizar will be ours!'

'Before the pass leading to the gates of Khazad-dûm, the survivors of the confrontation against Azog gathered anew. After the slaying of Azog, they had withdrawn from the encampment, anticipating another assault from the Orcs who still dwelt within Khazad-dûm. With them, they bore away only the head of Azog and the body of Náin Orcsfoe. Indeed, Náin's mail-collar had withstood Azog's blow, but the same could not be said for his neck. It snapped, and by all accounts, Náin had died in an instant.
'Little comfort this was to Dáin, who had remained silent ever since he ventured beyond the Great Gates. Even so, the head of Azog was the prize King Thráin had sought ever since Nár brought word of Thrór's death to the exiles at Zudrugund. And it had been won!
'Left nearly halt after Urro wounded him at Durin's Stone, King Thráin knelt among his guard, but his eyes would not be turned from Khazad-dûm.'

With the Black Mattock in hand and his horn at his side, the Lord of the Iron Hills knew well his duty, but if news did not soon come of victory, he would sound the horn-call himself and send the full fury of the Iron-folk against Azog.

'Ah, Hermáth. ¿Algo te preocupa?
'¿Debo recordarte la historia de Nafni el Invicto?'
Dáin se aclara la garganta y comienza su historia una vez más.
'En el año 1980 de la Tercera Edad, el Daño de Durin fue liberado en las Fundaciones de Piedra. Nafni estaba allí ese día, protegiendo a Durin VI mientras el rey mostraba a sus invitados elfos las espléndidas minas de Khazad-dûm. Durin cayó ante la furia del Balrog, pero ordenó a Nafni que sobreviviera y protegiera a su hijo, Náin. Y así lo hizo, ¡pues Nafni era ágil y logró escapar de la terrible criatura! Vio a ese demonio en todo su terror ardiente... y vivió. Al escuchar el relato de Nafni, Náin se enfureció y juró vengar a su padre a toda costa.
'Los valientes soldados de Khazad-dûm intentaron empujar al Balrog y a la horda Sinnombre que lo seguía hacia las profundidades, pero poco a poco, más y más del reino cayó. Un año después, el hijo de Durin, ahora Rey Náin I, reunió sus fuerzas y lanzó un último ataque desesperado contra el Balrog, asesino de su padre y objetivo de su venganza...'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Completar 'La caída de Khazad-dûm' en cualquier dificultad avanzará esta misión.</rgb>

Dáin continúa la historia de Nafni, que ahora se acerca a su final.
'Y así Khazad-dûm fue abandonada. Thráin I se convirtió en rey, apenas mayor que yo ahora, y finalmente condujo a nuestro pueblo a Erebor. Nafni se ganó su título \qEl Invicto\q por sobrevivir a su segundo encuentro con el Balrog, y se convertiría en un sabio consejero y amigo de confianza del Rey Thráin. Fue un gran y noble enano del Pueblo de Durin.'
Dáin parece aún más satisfecho con su relato más reciente de la historia de Nafni el Invicto.
'Khazad-dûm puede haber sido abandonada, ¡pero el espíritu del Pueblo de Durin nunca se ha apagado!'

'I was starting to wonder where you have gone off to? What did you find that had you across the tarn for such a length in time?!
'A giant toad had poisoned the goblins' minds?! I would have never guessed that to be the answer! All of your talk about this cavern of deep toads, and a broken, nameless shrine has me rethinking my curiosity, ${CLASS}.
'There are many strange creatures who have taken refuge in Gundabad during the absence of the dwarves. Perhaps we will all be better off if some of these creatures are just left alone.'

'Las reglas son muy sencillas: debes atravesar cada puerta y no puedes caerte de tu montura antes de que se agote el tiempo. '¿Te sientes a la altura de este desafío? ¡Solo los jinetes más audaces deberían siquiera intentar tal hazaña! Sin duda será muy peligroso, aunque tienes aspecto de ser resistente.'
'Es raro ver una monta tan excelente por estos lugares, ${PLAYER}. Estoy muy impresionado.'

Talk to King Shâlim Nightcloak

'What do you say, Hermáth? The journey will be long, but hardship has not stopped us yet!
'Will you aid our kin and cousins at Ashmargathâl?'

'Yes, Longbeard? Do you bring word from King Thráin?'
King Shâlim Nightcloak looks to you. You inform King Shâlim that you have come to aid the dwarves on Bundushâthur.
'At least someone means to do what must be done then! I grow tired of these Zhélruka and Kámbrada. Not their warriors, mind you, but Usk and Vélat. For dwarves I thought to be sworn enemies, they seem to grow closer friends with each passing hour. That is all well and good, but it seems they have forgotten there is a war to be won!
'The Abnúzhu have slain many Orcs this day, and we will slay many more before its end. I would not leave this battle empty-handed, friend. Orc-bones can make for fine trophies!'

'If King Thráin means to bolster us only with a single warrior, I hope he has chosen wisely!'
King Usk stares you down, and then chuckles to himself.
'I welcome any aid you would give us, Longbeard. After all, Vélat and his Zhélruka have spun enough tales to last three wars, but if we intend to rout our foes, someone must do the fighting. A-ha!
'Among the Orcs at Atrad-zarakh, their smaller cousins have proven difficult to overcome. Between the bat-tenders and those wielding their crude explosives, it has made our approach much more challenging than I had hoped.
'Do what you can, and that is enough!'

'What is this? Does King Thráin not trust us in our task?'
King Vélat smirks.
'I jest, Longbeard! Between the Zhélruka and the Abnúzhu, we have things well in hand. Oh, and I must admit that my friend, Usk, and his Kámbrada have played a part in our success as well. Hah!
'Ashmargathâl was an easy prize to win, but Atrad-zarakh still teems with our foes. It would be far easier to look ahead without those accursed bats flitting about our heads!'

'I've been told that ever since Bolg rallied folks to Erebor, things have gone downhill for us. Still, we didn't have outright war for a while; we were just surviving. Suppose you could call it a sort of peace.'
'But peace never lasts, not for us. Mordor came calling, and Gorgar answered.'

'You! Quit standing around like a limp worm! Don't you know we're about to go to war?
'Fill up the barrels 'round camp with weapons and deliver these orders to soldiers. Make it quick!'

'The end of the war brought trouble. Wasn't long before the hobgoblins came down from the north to overthrow Gorgar and claim Gundabad for themselves.
''Course, I don't need to tell you the end of that story, do I?'

'Gorgar would leave us to die and his generals would execute us for deserting. Right then I knew. Didn't matter if I was fighting hobgoblins, dwarves, or my own people -- if I kept fighting for Gorgar, I'd find myself bleeding out one day.
'After we lost the war in Elderslade, I'd hoped for a rebellion but, well... fear is a useful tool for dividing people.'

'That's why I want to leave. Far as I'm concerned, there's only death left for me if I stay in Gundabad.
'I-I mean no harm, honest.'

'Be wary, my friend, for the Orc speaks poisoned words. What does his kind care for other than destruction and slaughter? I've been faced with many a difficult choice throughout the years, but this situation is simple enough to understand.
'Still, I was... wrong to pull out the Black Mattock. The Orc may be luring us into a trap, but Féli is right. If there truly are dwarves to be saved, then we cannot leave them to their fates.'

'I am in your debt, ${PLAYER}. I let anger overtake me and cloud my senses. It was unbefitting of me as a leader -- nay, as a dwarf. I selfishly put my own thirst for revenge above the concerns of the Gabil'akkâ.'
He absentmindedly reaches for his beard before realizing that it's no longer there. A tired sigh escapes him.
'At least I have paid dearly for my actions.'

'You've done your part, Shúkurz. Féli will see to it that you and your party are escorted safely out of Gundabad.
'${PLAYER}, it looks like we'll want a small group of people for this job -- rescuing Lord Náin will go faster. If you have allies who can rally to us quickly, bring them along; if not, we'll work together instead.
'When you're ready, take the lift in the north-east all the way up to the catwalks. Find Dhúrstrok; I'll meet you there.'
Náin's fate is in your hands.

'My friend! This journal is amazing! It belonged to an Angmarim by the name of Bruidalg the Bloodletter.
'Look here, he wrote, \qThe way is secret, secret is the way. Only with the four shall the secret way be secret no more.\q Bruidalg continues on, rambling about, \qThe bones, the bones are leaking. The master is in the muck, the master and the bones and the crystals. All in the muck, dragons in the mire. Never will I breathe clean air again.\q
'Fascinating, no? Could there be a dragon here in Clovengap? Aside from our frosty lady, that is. But another, perhaps? A second dragon?! Mired in the muck somewhere? By Durin's beard, this is too exciting.
'Oh! I almost forgot. The journal mentions experiments on some of the frost-drakes that followed Hrímil into Clovengap. They have taken up residence at Frósthel, a set of ruins across the river. You go deal with that, and I shall have a look at the fragments you brought me.'
'Ah! You return. Tell me of the drakes!'

'Corrupted drakes? Terrible news! Glad am I that you have dealt with this situation, my friend.
'The lore-master has been asking after you. Do go see if he has made progress with the ripped paper fragments.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, you made it! Excellent. We certainly need your help.
'Welcome to Clovengap! Tier upon tier of overgrown wildwoods, crawling with intruders. But we shall reclaim these gardens, as is our right.

'${PLAYER}! Good cheer to you, friend! You made it, finally. Excellent. There is much work to be done.'

Ages ago, a great sundering shook loose the ceiling of this massive cavern. Once opened to the sky, Clovengap became an emerald swath of tiered gardens, unique among the dwarf-holds. Gone now are those gardens, replaced by dark forests and thick mists, in which prowl those with murderous intent.
Corrupting One's Own

'I know not why I am always surprised and horrified anew by the lengths the Angmarim will go to with their experiments, but this passage in the journal made my beard curl. Listen here:
'\qCrágacha has retreated back to her hole in the ruins, claiming the drakes she was working on are too powerful and deadly to be controlled. She had the audacity to suggest her tests on the drakes were a success and that maybe she could head back to the surface. Coward! Imbecile! Traitor!
'\qMy master has demanded more tests. More more more tests. My master in the muck. The bones are leaking. Leaking leaking. I told Crágacha that she was not done. Not done with the bones and the tests and the muck. She is now testing the crystals and the magic leaking leaking much magic spells the bones --\q'
Mother Amma breaks off, scanning the page and muttering.
'He goes on rambling for some time... what matters is that we know where they are holed up. Head over to the Angmarim camp and stop this madness!'
Defeat Crágacha

'Oh ${PLAYER}, you're back.
'We’ve been having a bit of a problem getting into some of the more resilient parts of the mountain recently. The blasting supplies we’ve brought over don’t seem to be cutting it against the frozen rock.

In the Wind

'You have them? Give them here, my friend!'
As Múta examines her axe and dagger, a smile forms at the corner of her mouth.
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. It'll be time to put them to use soon enough!'

'Did you find anything?'
You hand the orders to Múta. As she reads them, her eyebrows raise and lower a few times. After a moment, she scoffs.
'Bah! If these orders are to be believed, we and the Zhélruka have our work cut out for us. From what I can tell, the Iron Crown, as well as their Dourhand and Hill-men allies, now serve one named High Priestess Ásachal. I cannot be certain of it, but I would not doubt she is a descendant of the corrupt Men of Westernesse! It seems the Iron Crown has laid claim to that fortress across the valley—the Drearspire, they call it. It is said they seek something called \qCrûn Nasgadh\q, but I cannot glean anything else about it from these orders. Is it some sort of artifact? A spell of old Angmar? Whatever it is, I'm certain it won't be good for us or the Gabil'akkâ if they find it!
'Things are more urgent than they seemed, ${PLAYER}. Will you fetch me my weapons? The Dourhands took them and set them on a table over there—just out of my reach. I've an idea on how to escape from this cage, but I'd feel a lot better about it if I wasn't unarmed.'
Múta's axe is of a simple design, but it has clearly seen much use
Múta's dagger is stained black, perhaps from a crude dye or Orkish blood

'Before we set out, Múta warned us that some new purpose has kindled the spirits of the Dourhands and that they serve one of their own sworn to the Iron Crown: Brathar Crack-helm. We made every preparation... or so we thought.
'No sooner had we passed through the Witch-gate than we were caught in a trap! Múta was captured by the Dourhands, but I do not know what has become of Kársa or Uzvát. Alas, ${PLAYER}, I'm in no condition to mount a rescue.'
'I'm afraid you will have to manage that, my friend.'
As Gárjan braces his leg, you notice a lengthy gash in the armour covering his thigh.
'Bah, it looks worse than it is! At the very least, I can make it back to Bárgstad on my own to tell Ausma what has happened.
'Do not let these Dourhands get the last laugh, ${PLAYER}. Múta must be freed before it is too late!'

'${PLAYER}! What are you doing here?!'
Múta's voice shrinks to a gruff whisper.
'I didn't expect for help to be sent so soon, but given the circumstances, I'm more than happy to be wrong! When the Dourhands ambushed us, I saw Kársa and Uzvát escape to the east. But have you seen Gárjan?'
You tell Múta that Gárjan escaped and that he now intends to warn Ausma and Lord Glóin of the danger beyond the Witch-gate.
'It seems our efforts to foil the Iron Crown in Elderslade did not go as unnoticed as we hoped. After the Dourhands threw me in this cage, I overheard them mumbling about new orders from Brathar. Unfortunately, they were wise enough to continue their conversations where I couldn't eavesdrop on them.
'Why don't you see if some of them have been foolish enough to keep their orders on hand? I'll keep trying to free myself in the meantime!'

'Subtlety has served me well in the past, but from what I have learned, the Iron Crown answer only to two things: their self-styled masters... and force!'
'Within the orders you found, there was mention of a jailor dispatched to the Witch-gate to deliver me to the Iron Crown at the Drearspire. As I am swiftly learning, the Iron Crown seem fond of bestowing fanciful titles upon themselves and their followers. For instance, they call this would-be jailor a \qkey-warden\q. 'Unless my ears have deceived me, the Dourhands use some sort of summoning horn to communicate with the Iron Crown. Perhaps if you were to greet the key-warden in the Dourhands' stead, you might find the key to this cage!'

'Oh, hello! You are that hero of the realm, ${PLAYER}, correct? My, it must be wonderful to be free to wander Middle-earth in search of adventure and glory.
'I am Golodhril. My sister Sadorwen and I have come to see the fabled Forest Beneath the Mountain!'

'She continues to treat me like a child, I see. Very well, I suppose I will accept your service.'

'Mae govannen, friend. I see my dear sister still chafes at her imagined bonds.'
Sadorwen chuckles lightly.
'Golodhril is merely a few centuries old. She has not yet experienced all that ones such as ourselves have. I promised her that we could visit the places she reads about before we set sail for the West. However, I did not agree to allow her to become drake food.
'With your experience and skills, you could easily help her with some of the tasks she has set for herself. I am sure you are busy; however, you will no doubt pass by the weeds and vines she seeks. If you are interested, why not offer to go in her place for now.'

'You have my gratitude for your assistance with the fountains. I wonder if I might ask you for further help. I have read about three rare plants that grew here in Clovengap. One of them is said to cure stomach ailments, and I believe it could be useful for our eventual sailing trip to the West.'
She lowers her voice, glancing to be sure her sister is not listening.
'Sadorwen does not do so well with the rocking of boats, which is no doubt why she agreed to put off going for as long as we have. Sadly, my book is unclear on which plant has this property. The three plants are called daewath, fingloth, and elialas in Sindarin.'
She shows you a page with the image of three flowers, with illegible writing next to them.
'Gather some of each for me and bring them back here… ah, please.'

Map the Gap

'Welcome to Clovengap! I am Gerja Defthand, Master Architect and head of the restoration project for this area of Gundabad. Yes, yes. I am aware that we have not yet taken back the gap, but as our victory is a given, it is never too early to start planning. If you are of a mind to help, I would greatly appreciate it!
'Over the centuries, time and the gap’s unsavoury occupants have destroyed the gardens and farms. However, dwarf-hewn stone remains solid. We may discover once again the locations of these lost marvels.
'Let us start locally. The records state that north of here, burrowed into the very mountain itself, was a marketplace, Dashât-zahar. Will you go and survey the area? I am drawing up a map for our forces and I believe the location could be useful as a camp.'

'Right, let us return to the map. The honey jar gives me hope that the stories of Zigilmarn, the fabled Clovengap honey-wine, are true! I read that there were vineyards on the far shores of the Kurdushâlak. See what you can find, if you please? I shall meet you across the river, at Hagbuth.'

Nakrovak, a crystal-encrusted Warg, has asked you to listen to her tale.

'I am Nakrovak. My mate and I were captured many moons ago by Men in robes. They chanted over us and pierced our hides with crystals. The pain and the ensorcelled crystals drove my mate mad.
'The crystals had a different effect on me, however. My mind grew clearer. My body stronger. Rage and hunger were once all I knew. Now, there is sorrow, grief, and… something else I cannot explain. A softness….
'I managed to get away from my captors, but they found my den, weakened me with poison, and stole my cubs. As you have seen, I am not yet at my full strength.
'I dare not wait for the effects of the poison to wear off, for my cubs are in danger. Please, rescue them, and we will leave this place and go far away from two-legged peoples and their sorceries.'

'I owe you a great debt, ${RACE}. My intention is that our paths never cross again. If they do, however, and you require assistance, I will be there.
'My children and I will leave Clovengap once I have recovered.'

'Stay your hand, ${RACE}. I am in no shape to fight you.
'I can see that you are a formidable foe, and you seem not to be associated with the scum who stole my cubs. Listen to my tale, then decide whether I should be destroyed.'

Klátha is located in a camp north of Bazanmanar.
Nósni has asked you to speak to Klátha once more.

'Welcome back, friend. Yes, yes. I saw the display. And one of the merchants came by to apologize to Nósni for the late shipment. Nósni had me moved here for the spectacular view, did he not? He has always been so thoughtful in his deeds, but foolish with the timeliness of his words.
'Hmmm. They were quite the thing, weren't they. I suppose I might find it in my heart to forgive him.'

'Hello, hello! Now the truth will out. You see, I know that Klátha's favourite thing is fireworks. I arranged to purchase special ones from Feredis of Minas Tirith herself!
'I have been waiting for the right moment to set them alight for Klátha. I had her moved here so she wouldn't miss the display, but... well, the delivery was very late and... oh. I can of course see how she would think I was trying to protect her. It was supposed to be a surprise, but... well, I suppose things have dragged on with no real news from me. I was so focused on my plan that I lost sight of how confusing my actions must have been.
'Well, will you help me light these fireworks? It may not be enough to redeem myself, but I have to try.'

'Oh, ${PLAYER}. That was spectacular! And probably the first time fireworks have ever graced these halls. If that did not win her love, at least may it grant me her forgiveness. Would... would you check on her for me? See whether I am allowed to speak with her again?'

'You again?'
You give Klátha the message from Nósni.
'Look towards the river? Hmm. I suppose I can do that. Not that it will matter, of course. But I suppose I can.'
Klátha's heart has turned against Nósni, but he's not ready to give up.

'What... has happened? Who are you... and how did you come to this place?'
You introduce yourself to the old dwarf and explain that the Angmarim of the Iron Crown discovered the old delving after gaining entry to Gloomingtarn.
'It... should not be so, and yet... it is. I am... Thrástan.'
You ask Thrástan if he can stand. The old dwarf nods weakly.

'Of all the things I thought we might find in Mîn Lorg, another dwarf was not among them!
'It won't be long before the Iron Crown discovers what has happened. And despite his age, Thrástan looks a hale enough dwarf...
'We should leave this place while we still can, ${PLAYER}.'

'What... what is this place, my friend?
Hersegg glances around the entryway of what appears to be an ancient dwelling in the caverns of Gloomingtarn.
'It looks nearly untouched, ${PLAYER}, but how can that be so? Neither Orc nor dwarf have walked these halls in thousands of years, and yet, it is as neatly kept as any dwelling in the Lonely Mountain.
'Perhaps the notes of the Iron Crown were not so far from the truth after all. Could it truly be that Durin the Deathless once dwelt within this... house?
'We cannot allow the Angmarim to lay claim to it!'

'Another dwarf? What is he doing here?'
Hersegg looks at the Angmarim standing over an old dwarf.
'Let's listen for a moment and see if we can't learn more, ${PLAYER}. But if they even hint that they're going to harm him, I'm not going to let that happen!'
'We mustn't stay here, ${PLAYER}. Let us return to Watchers' Roost!'

'${PLAYER}, are you all right?
'When you and Hersegg did not return, my warriors feared the worst. And from what I can tell, that was very nearly the case!
'Who is this now?'
You tell Hermáth Stormhammer you discovered a dwarf named Thrástan captured by the Angmarim in Mîn Lorg.
'Very well! Let us speak more of this at Watchers' Roost... and I shall have to have words with my granddaughter as well!'

'We're cut off, ${PLAYER}. The only way out is through these Angmarim and we're outnumbered!'
Hersegg glances at Thrástan.
'Stay back, Thrástan. We'll protect you... no matter what.'

'Although we still do not know the truth of how Thrástan came to dwell in Mount Gundabad, I am inclined to aid him—especially now that he seems to have taken ill. If any good can come from his return to Abkân'aban, I shall not keep him from it! Let us—'
A scout's sudden arrival interrupts your conversation. The scout hands Hermáth a missive, and Hermáth begins to read it. After a moment, his brow furrows in concern.
'It seems we were fated to travel to Abkân'aban this day, ${PLAYER}. I have just received word that the Angmarim of the Iron Crown have gathered their forces and now make for the Stone of Wakening!
'To cede the sacred place of Durin's awakening to these wicked Men—it would be unthinkable! Let us go—all of us—and put an end to the Iron Crown's plans for Gloomingtarn!'

'I am not certain what we just witnessed, ${PLAYER}. Had I not seen it with my own eyes, I would never have believed it!
'That one of the servants of the First Crafter would come to our aid in our hour of need...'
Hermáth Stormhammer's eyes are wide with awe.
'What better omen of success could Prince Durin and the Gabil'akkâ have wished for?'

Instancia: El Despertar

'Lord Stormhammer need not concern himself with my safety, ${PLAYER}.
'As soon as I passed beyond the warding-runes at Zâram-mekhem, I understood what peril might await me in Gloomingtarn. And to be quite honest, I would sooner die than allow the Iron Crown to defile the Stone of Wakening.
'I will wield my axe as best I can, my friend. Let us hope it is enough!'

'Something stirs within me, ${PLAYER}, but I know not what it is...
'All I know is that the Shaper's hearth beckons to me! It is as if I were a stray ember returning to the forge...
'Will you accompany me up the old stairs, friend?

'I understand, ${PLAYER}. I see all that the Shaper wished of me!
'That I laboured as a servant of the great forge long before Durin laid dreaming beneath Mount Gundabad. And when my task was finished, so too did I rest for many years of the world.
'The time of my awakening has come—and my long slumber is at its end!'

'These stones... are familiar to me, ${PLAYER}.
'My memories seem clearer the nearer we draw to the Shaper's hearth. I came here once... I came with Durin...'
Thrástan trails off and begins mumbling to himself for a moment. After a moment, he grips his smithing hammer tightly.
'I must return....'

'Everyone is prepared then? Good.
'There is little time to waste!'

'I do not believe the Angmarim are the sort to make empty threats. But we have claimed the White Stone Forge... at least for the moment!
'If we have truly been led into a trap, it will not be long before it is sprung. In the meantime, escort Thrástan to the White Stone Forge. Even if our doom is soon to follow, I would do right by him and honour an old dwarf's last request.
'I and the others will prepare to make our stand—as hopeless as it may be!'

'By Durin's beard! What have we witnessed this day?!
'${PLAYER}, this is beyond all belief!'
'By Durin's beard! What have we witnessed this day?!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. I am the Forge-servant, Tamindur, wrought anew by the will of the Shaper... the First Crafter.... He Who Made The Dwarves!
'Invaders run rampant upon the Stone of Wakening, but no longer. By some lesser magic, they have come here unhindered, but they cannot oppose me nor my lord in the Uttermost West.
'Though you be not of the Eldest House, you shall be spared my wrath.'
Without hesitation, the Forge-servant strides forth

'For my part, I have heard tell that the Orcs have come to revere one of Gorgar's lieutenants, Hathnákh, and now call him 'curse-breaker'. It is no secret that it was a weapon of the Iron Crown that overpowered the warding-runes, but somehow this Orc has convinced his ilk out of the Deepscrave that it was by his own hand that the Orcs might now run rampant through the hallowed caverns of Mount Gundabad.
'Before we arrived in Gloomingtarn, Hathnákh must have commanded his sappers to destroy one of the clusters of columns and in so doing, toppled one of the ancient echo-horns. During our first encounter, it was struck by an errant axe and the sound it made drove many of the Orcs mad. Alas, the Orcs regrouped after the battle and Hathnákh surely leads them once more. If he desires to keep his newfound title, Hathnákh will not shy from battle this time!
'Find the toppled echo-horn along the thoroughfare and strike it. Do away with this 'curse-breaker' before he can lead more of his kind into Gloomingtarn!'

'Ah, but before you go, have you seen those dwarves casting stones into the Gloomingtarn? And Longbeards, no less. To desecrate the caverns where Durin the Deathless first awoke and in such a manner—it is unthinkable!
'I would be of a mind to reprimand them myself, but it seems I've already made something of a reputation for myself among the dwarves of Lord Stormhammer's expedition. Why, I've even overheard them call me names! Spall the Stuffy, they call me. Better stuffy than disrespectful, I say!
'Even so, something must be done. Would you tell those dwarves to stop casting stones into Durthuzâram? There will be time enough for idle amusement when the Mountain-home is reclaimed!'

'They've stopped? Very good! You are held in high regard by Prince Durin, and I knew they would listen to you... even if they disagreed with my reasoning.
'I appreciate you doing that on my behalf, ${PLAYER}.'

'When the others and I first came to Glittengrof, I thought this would be an easy task. Drive off the spiders, inspect the old crystals, perhaps learn a thing or two... and then back to Watchers' Roost by supper. How wrong I was!
'We expected to find a small colony of glass-spiders, but it's a lot and they've dug in. It seems most of these webs were made by an old spider known as Glérgangol—and she means to make a new lair of Glittengrof! And if what already happened to the others is any indication, I don't think she's too keen on guests. Too bad for her, I suppose, but these caverns belong to the Longbeards... and to Durin the Deathless!
'Lord Stormhammer has tasked us with reclaiming Glittengrof, and that means putting an end to Glérgangol and her daughters. Will you aid me, ${PLAYER}?'

'I have another task for you, ${PLAYER}.
'It is certain that the Orcs and the Men of the Iron Crown pose the most immediate threat to our efforts to secure Gloomingtarn, but we must not lose sight of our truest purpose in Mount Gundabad. I speak of course of its reclamation—and its restoration!'
Hermáth looks around the sprawling cavern of Gloomingtarn with a mix of awe and determination on his face.
'Merely winning a victory over our foes is not enough to honour the sacred halls of Durin the Deathless, we must become the new stewards of Mount Gundabad. When I first led this expedition into Gloomingtarn, I made note of several befouled crystal-lamps on the banks of Durthuzâram. Countless tales told of the glowing lights along the banks of the dark lake, and I would not make liars of my ancestors!
'Here, take my handkerchief. It is of a hardier cloth than you might think, and it has cleaned worse... believe me! Polish the crystal-lamps, ${PLAYER}, and set the banks of Durthuzâram aglow once more!'

'Very good, my friend! I trust my handkerchief served you well?
'Durthuzâram is sacred to the Longbeards—nay, to all dwarves! Through your efforts, all dwarves and their descendants shall be able to admire it for ages to come!
'You have my deepest thanks, ${PLAYER}.'

'You found Old Skárhogg, didn't you? I see it on your face. Well, what happened?'
You tell Orti that you managed to defeat Old Skárhogg, but that it had apparently also slain one of the Angmarim of the Iron Crown that drew too near its lair.
'What could those Men possibly want with the ukhrash? Bah, perhaps they just saw the same shimmering in the lake that I did and simply couldn't resist. It's a pity that Old Skárhogg didn't slay more of them, but I am certain our luck would have run out sooner or later!

'Do you remember how I told you that the ukhrâsh chased me off at Skelstrand? Well, the last time I was run off, I got lucky. I was ambushed by an enormous ukhrash, and it was very nearly upon me before I finally heard it. If I had reacted a second later, well... it would have been worse than this!'
Orti pulls back his sleeve to reveal a thin gash on his arm.
'And that was the smallest scratch, mind you! If it had been closer, I surely would have lost my arm. Aye, it's a sneaky one. Especially for one of its size!
'Old Skárhogg, as I call it, has grown a bit too long in the claw, I think. If it is allowed to stalk the banks of Durthuzâram, there is no doubt in my mind that it will endanger the dwarves of the Gabil'akkâ.
'If you go to Skelstrand, seek out some sign of its presence. I only hope that you find it before it finds you!'

'Ah! I almost didn't hear you, ${PLAYER}. As you'll soon learn for yourself, there are strange echoes in this place... strange, indeed.
'It seems I was perhaps misinformed of the state of things in Gloomingtarn. I arrived quite prepared to survey the sacred tarn as it was tasked of me by Prince Durin himself, but I did not expect my studies to be hindered by Orcs and wicked Men of all things!

'Although I wish it had not come to this, you have done well to put an end to Thrastring and his ilk. All the old tales spoke of a natural harmony in these caverns, but after what those Men of Angmar have done to the Mountain-home, I fear only discord will remain in their wake... at least for a time!

'Something has gotten to these worms, ${PLAYER}....
'I'm no lore-master, but I suspect the warding-runes did more than just keep the enemies of the dwarves out of Gloomingtarn. Ever since the Iron Crown made their way into these caverns, its creatures have been unwell, and I am afraid the glow-worms of Ormgren are no exception. Whatever balance was set in place long ago among these creatures has been broken with the warding-runes, and there is no craft or magic we possess that could repair them before the hour is too late!
'While I am thankful that many of the worms are still docile, a few have grown aggressive. They've begun to harass the miners and gnaw away at the ancient columns of Gloomingtarn. One among them, Thrastring, has even taken to devouring his own kind—and I worry he might develop a taste for dwarf too if we're not careful!
'If Gloomingtarn is to survive even after the Iron Crown are routed, we must put an end to Thrastring and his ilk.'

'It seems I had even more reason to send word to you than I first thought, ${PLAYER}.
'Do you see these runes, my friend? They read: \qALL MUST DEPART EXCEPT THE ELDEST HOUSE. DEATH AWAITS THE UNWELCOME.\q Not the most inviting, and for good reason! See what happens when some wicked Men render them powerless?
'Hersegg tells me that the Orcs' encampment lies directly in our path... or at least right beside it! As I am certain one as well-informed as you will have heard, Hersegg's grandfather, Lord Hermáth Stormhammer, has led an expedition into Gloomingtarn. Although it was said to have faced Orkish resistance upon passing through Zâram-mekhem, the Gabil'akkâ was able to secure a foothold deeper within the hallowed caverns—at an old overlook known as Watchers' Roost.
'That is where I wish to go, my friend. And now that you have come, perhaps Hersegg will finally allow me to begin my studies!'

'I must thank you for coming as soon as you did, ${PLAYER}. I have found myself in a bit of a bind.
'When my grandfather sent me to escort a new arrival to Watchers' Roost, I expected to find a capable warrior—not a lore-master of the Lonely Mountain. I mean him no insult, but a journey through the Ironfold is a much different task than the reclamation of the Mountain-home. I have no doubt that Spall means well, but as Prince Durin himself knows, the situation in Gloomingtarn is far more dire than we had hoped.
'The warding-runes were sapped of their ancient power by some fell artifact of Angmar, and without their protection, the Orcs and some wicked Men of the Iron Crown have invaded Gloomingtarn. Although we overcame the Orcs in our first encounter with them on our way to Watchers' Roost, they have bolstered their numbers from the Deepscrave and made camp at Drúkala.
'I am capable enough of escorting Spall on my own, but without some sort of distraction, I fear we will be waylaid by the Orcs before we reach our destination. As you might expect, Spall and I each have our own ideas of what might prove most effective in repelling the Orcs from Gloomingtarn. If you would combat the Orcs at Drúkala, I shall escort Spall and see that he can begin his studies in earnest at Watchers' Roost.
'And when you have finished with the Orcs, you should follow the thoroughfare and join us at the Roost. It is quite the sight to see, my friend!'

'Alas for Glittengrof!
'If it weren't for these accursed spiders, I could spend hours—nay—days admiring the crystals of Glittengrof! Even their webs have done little to dim their light! I must admit, my friend, I had intended to harvest some of these crystals for my studies, but now I find that I cannot bring myself to raise my pickaxe. To my mind, it would be like defiling an ancient museum!'
Seemingly blind to the danger of the glass-spiders, an awestruck Spall looks around Glittengrof. After a moment, something catches his eye in the distance.
'Wait a moment, ${PLAYER}... do you see that?
'A-ha! It seems that some of the old crystals have fallen to the ground and shattered. If they are just broken shards, I do not feel so badly about collecting them. After all, the spiders have no use for them!
'Will you help me collect some of the shards, my friend?'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}.
'It is a pity that these crystals were damaged, but I will learn what I can from them.'

'Now then, ${PLAYER}...
'I know this will come as some surprise, but my granddaughter has not shied from voicing her misgivings about your companion. However, I believe I see something of myself in him. Spall is a curious dwarf and he is well-learned in the history of the dwarves. Indeed, Spall might prove invaluable to this expedition. I was hesitant to allow him to begin his survey unaccompanied, but with you here, I see no reason to keep him from his studies!
'Besides, I need your help with another matter, my friend. After we established camp here at Watchers' Roost, I sent two companies to investigate some of the old passages of Gloomingtarn. One of my warriors, Vithin, led his company to Glittengrof, and another, Lokur, led his to Ormgren. My scouts spied a few glass-spiders near the entrance to Glittengrof, but I know little of Ormgren. Unfortunately, neither company has returned or even sent word—be it good or ill. Needless to say, I have become concerned. Either they have made some great discovery, or some terrible fate may have befallen them. If you find them in the course of Spall's survey, aid them as best you can. I would not leave any of my warriors behind!
'Go, ${PLAYER}, and tell Spall that he may begin his survey in Glittengrof and Ormgren—so long as you accompany him!'

'Lord Stormhammer has given me permission to begin my survey of Gloomingtarn? And you will accompany me? How wonderful!
'I had hoped to begin my survey at Abkân'aban, the great Stone of Wakening, but upon further thought, I suppose that is better left for last. Yes, Glittengrof and Ormgren shall be fine places to begin my studies!'
Spall begins to collect his things into his pockets and picks up a nearby axe.
'If it is all right with you, ${PLAYER}, I would like to set off at once!'

'By Durin's beard, you startled me! Did Lord Stormhammer send you?'
Vithin catches his breath and begins to whisper.
'Aye, I'm Vithin, but I'm afraid I cannot leave—not yet. Glittengrof and its crystals are indeed beautiful, but that doesn't mean much if it's overrun by spiders! Even worse, I've lost most of my company in these blasted webs!
'I can't just leave them! Will you aid me?'

'Have you heard much of Ormgren, ${PLAYER}?
'From what lore I've been able to gather, it seems that these were among the very first lodes delved in Mount Gundabad—and if legend speaks true, they were first mined by Durin the Deathless himself! I am eager to see how they have fared since the Elder Days, and I hope you are as well, my friend.
'Lord Stormhammer tells me that there is a small boat moored near Skelstrand that we might use to cross Durthuzâram to its eastern banks. I'm not certain how I feel about taking a boat out on the sacred tarn, but even I must admit that swimming seems a poor choice.
'Shall we then?'

'By Durin's beard, what has happened to this place?! The glow-worms have been devouring Ormgren from within!'
For a moment, Spall's face drains of colour and it looks as if he is about to faint. After a moment, he steadies himself.
'Perhaps... this was the will of the First Crafter. Yes... yes, it must be. And besides, ${PLAYER}, there is still much to be learned from these glow-worms. It is only a matter of knowing where to look!
'Are you familiar with how glow-worms digest what they eat, my friend? They possess complicated gizzards which become more effective when traces of stones and precious minerals are lodged within them. If we were to collect gizzards from these glow-worms, we might learn what ores and minerals they have recently devoured. And by we, I mean you, of course. I am a proud lore-master, not some butcher of beasts and insects!
'You don't mind helping me, do you? Oh, and only the adult glow-worms will have what I need, so you can leave the wormlets be!'

Even when the Haban’akkâ breached the Mountain-home during the Sixth War of the Dwarves and Orcs, we ventured no further than Máttugard. Even King Thráin deemed the Deepscrave too perilous to cross, and after all, Azog had yet to be slain!
'Perhaps he entered in the years that followed, but to elude the Orcs as far as Zâram-mekhem on his own is beyond the skill—or luck—of any dwarf I have ever known! 'Is everyone prepared to depart? Very good, ${PLAYER}.
'Let us return to Watchers' Roost and, at last, we can set about undoing the damage the Iron Crown has done to Gloomingtarn!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTE: You will swiftly travel to Watchers' Roost after advancing this quest.</rgb>

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, it seems our journey through Mount Gundabad shall have more than its fair share of surprises!
'My expedition and I will see to repairing the damage left by the Iron Crown, and we shall set the echo-horns across this great cavern into alignment once more. The warding-runes may never again repel our foes, but when the Mountain-home is ours again and evermore, I hope we find we have no need for them!
'I am certain Prince Durin and the others shall have need of your aid in the Clovengap and beyond, but I thank you for all you have done here, my friend. Without your aid, the secrets of our ancestors may well have been forgotten!
'Baruk Khazâd! For Gundabad!'

'You need not fear my wrath, ${PLAYER}. Approach, and let us speak!
'Long ago, when the Shaper's work was finished, I was bidden to rest beneath Mount Gundabad. In time, I awoke as Thrástan; different in form, but alike in mind and spirit to walk among Durin's Folk. In my long years of solitude, the two diverged, but I am now restored.
'At long last, my vigil nears its end and a new Age is soon to dawn. But fear not, I shall ward the Stone of Awakening from all evil that would seek to master it until I am called back to the Uttermost West.
'Yet many trials lay ahead for you, little one.'

'In light of what has happened here at Abkân'aban, I shall soon have to speak to Prince Durin.
'That a servant of the First Crafter would reveal himself to us is too unbelievable a tale to send by any missive! Only my voice might lend it any credibility... and even so, the Prince may have to see with his own eyes!
'Let us not trouble our new benefactor, ${PLAYER}. Our gratitude is enough, I think, and there are greater matters in this world for one of such power to lend his aid.
'You should speak to the others here and see if they are ready to depart. When that is so, come speak to me again!'

'I hardly know what to say, ${PLAYER}...'
Spall gazes up at the White Stone Forge where Tamindur now stands watch.
'I have seen more in one day than I dreamt of seeing in a lifetime.
'As for me, my survey will continue unhindered now that the Iron Crown have been driven out of Gloomingtarn. Who knows what other secrets lie hidden for us to discover? I, for one, relish the chance to find them!
'When Lord Stormhammer wishes to depart, I shall be prepared.'

'What an adventure, ${PLAYER}!
'From the Lonely Mountain to Elderslade and now to the very heart of Mount Gundabad... I am grateful our paths crossed when they did. Perhaps I was a bit too eager to confront the Iron Crown, but it all worked out in the end, didn't it?'
Hersegg smirks and looks to Tamindur.
'A victory hard won... and secured with as near a miracle as I've ever seen! The First Crafter himself must watch over us here in Mount Gundabad!
'I will be ready to depart in just a moment, my friend. Why don't you go and see if Spall is ready to set out?'

'Ah! There you are, ${PLAYER}!
'I was beginning to wonder if Lord Stormhammer forgot to mention where I'd gone, but no matter. Look out across the lake, my friend. Isn't Abkân'aban beautiful?'
Spall gestures to the massive island which rises out of the waters of Durthuzâram. His eyes are aglow with excitement and awe.
'It is the Stone of Wakening! It is said that it was upon those stones where Durin the Deathless first awoke—first of the Seven Fathers. What a sight to behold! Few Longbeards have been so fortunate to make such a pilgrimage, but would you accompany me?'
You tell Spall that Lord Stormhammer has asked you to aid Hersegg and the other warriors.
'I see. That is a shame, my friend, but I do understand. I shall continue my studies here then for a time before crossing the span, but I do hope you get to visit the Stone before you depart Gloomingtarn.'

'All right, ${PLAYER}. It's time we figured out just what the Iron Crown are after!
'Before you arrived, I spotted a small encampment to the north. It seems the Iron Crown have a few such camps leading down into Gloomingtarn from the Clovengap, but this one appears to be the largest of them—aside from Lochan Dúv. Although we haven't been able to recover any of them, I have seen the Angmarim of the Iron Crown carrying scroll-cases.
'If they didn't stop after stealing the Black Stone Anvil, who knows what else they might seek to pilfer? Scout the encampment to the north and see if you can't find one of those scroll-cases, ${PLAYER}. We've got to know what they're up to and what they've found!'

'What did you find, ${PLAYER}? Ah, give that here!'
Hersegg opens the scroll-case and begins reading the notes and research collected by the Iron Crown in Gloomingtarn.
'Oh, I don't like the sound of this at all!'

'As I was saying, ${PLAYER}...
'Your companion, Spall, was quite determined to continue his survey, and so I allowed him to continue onward to Abkân'aban. However, I did not send him alone. Hersegg and a few of my warriors accompanied him northward to Lugun-nâla, the ancient span to the Stone of Wakening. I am certain our warriors are more than a match for the Iron Crown, but I grow concerned that more of these Men of Angmar are arriving in Gloomingtarn with each passing hour.
'As much as Spall may wish to continue his survey with you at his side, I am afraid I now have a greater need for your aid. I ask that you join Hersegg and my warriors at Lugun-nâla, ${PLAYER}. Do let Spall know that I regret depriving him of his companion, but I am certain he will understand.
'Be swift, my friend. The Iron Crown cannot be allowed to lay claim to Gloomingtarn!'

The Secrets of Gloomingtarn

'A-ha! This must be it.
'Over here, ${PLAYER}.'

'I can't be sure it was their doing, but it looks like the Men of the Iron Crown have used some of the old crystal-lamps to light the way deeper into the cavern. At least we won't have to fumble around in the dark!
'Whatever they uncovered must be something of great power or worth, ${PLAYER}, and that worries me!'

'Hah! That worked better than I'd hoped! Now then, let's have a look at this....'
Hersegg produces the scroll-case she recovered from the Iron Crown commander and begins to read it. Her eyes widen, and she looks to you.
'It seems these Angmarim have discovered an ancient passage here in Gloomingtarn, and if these notes are to be believed, they suspect it was an early dwelling of Durin the Deathless. The eldest house... if such a thing can truly be!
'Among these writings were orders demanding that the passage—which they have named Mîn Lorg—be excavated and their findings gathered before the arrival of their master, Allaban, from Câr Bronach.
'From what I can tell, Mîn Lorg must lie somewhere within Lochan Dúv. We must find it, ${PLAYER}, and prevent the Iron Crown from defiling it!'

'It's worse than I thought, ${PLAYER}. There must be a hundred of them all told!'
Hersegg looks around Lochan Dúv, and her eyes stop when she spots a small metal cage.
'Ukhrâsh?! What use could these Men possibly have for them? More importantly, someone must be leading this expedition here in Lochan Dúv—and they will know what the Iron Crown has planned for Gloomingtarn.
'Hmm, I have an idea, ${PLAYER}, but it might be a bit risky!'
Hersegg rushes to your side!
Within the cavern, you hear distant Angmarim voices...

'Honourless villains! It was the Iron Crown that stole away the Black Stone Anvil of Durin the Deathless, and they do not intend to stop there.

It seems they seek to lay claim to everything in Mount Gundabad, but that shall not be so! The Angmarim gather to Lochan Dúv like moths to the flame, and I fear the tide of battle may soon turn against my grandfather's expedition—and the Gabil'akkâ.
'We must stop them here, ${PLAYER}, and strike at the very heart of their encampment!'

'Clever rat!
'Rethvárd must have freed himself while I was not looking. He caught me unawares when I brought him bread. Dourhands must truly have no shame!
'Was what he told you true at least? Of Skáilag? Of Toll Oivas? Have you made the Iron Crown suffer?'
You tell Skálo that you managed to defeat powerful Angmarim and put an end to their plans.
'At least not all of it was lies then! But, I fear our problems are just beginning....'
'Oh, he'll talk to you, will he? Bah!'

'Mézto sent you, did he?
'This one hasn't given me much, aside from his name: Rethvárd. Of course, I haven't been as... convincing as I would like to be!'
Skálo glares at Rethvárd.
'You are free to speak to him, ${PLAYER}, but I would not expect him to answer. If he continues to hold his tongue, I have other ways of making him talk!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. Our paths cross at last!'
Rethvárd chuckles to himself.
'Lord Brathar told us all about you—how you and the Longbeards slew Skorgrím at Gabilazan. A compelling tale, to be sure, but I knew better. That thing was not Skorgrím! It was the sorcery of Angmar given flesh!
'When I told Lord Brathar the truth of it, his fury could hardly be contained. At first, he could not believe it, but as Angmar grew weaker in the absence of its steward, he saw the Angmarim for what they truly were: power-hungry lickspittles that rob and abuse all peoples they deem inferior.
'We may appear to serve the Iron Crown, but only until our vengeance is done. In truth, we Dourhands ought to thank you for returning our king of old to rest!
'And so, I offer you a gift in good faith—a gift of information.'

'In the meantime, I shall speak with Múta about our next course of action against the Iron Crown. She is quite clever... for one of the cousins of the Kámbrada!

It is our right to explore them and reclaim them along with the rest of the Mountain-home. According to one of my miners, several others have been ensnared by the glow-worms and have become stuck in strands of glowing slime!

Realign echo-horns to unsettle the Orcs at Drúkala (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So Hersegg will escort me to Watchers' Roost? That is excellent news!
'As for these Orcs, I have noticed that they have found some means to alter the alignment of the ancient echo-horns—the Ugrur-melakh, as they were so named in the tongue of my ancestors. It is said that they once channelled the very acoustics of these caverns into a deep, reverberating resonance. According to the lore I have studied, it was also rumoured they were possessed of some enchantment from the Elder Days. Alas, I have seen no such evidence with my own eyes!
'However, Hersegg tells me the Orcs have made no attempt to attack Watchers' Roost. Perhaps it is merely coincidence and they fear the warriors of the Gabil'akkâ stationed there, but I do not think that is all that is happening. Many of the echo-horns still lie undisturbed at the old overlook, and I think many of the Orcs fear to draw any nearer to them.
'I spotted several echo-horns around the Orcs' encampment and along the thoroughfare through Gloomingtarn. With one of the Ugrur-melakh destroyed, we will have to realign the remaining echo-horns to capture the resonance, but I am confident it will drive off the Orcs—at least for a time!
'I am certain you can figure it out, ${PLAYER}. I hope to see you at Watchers' Roost!'

As several Orcs flee back into the Deepscrave, it appears that Spall's speculation that realigning the echo-horns around Drúkala has indeed unsettled the Orcs and hindered their efforts to gain a foothold in Gloomingtarn. Although some of the Orcs appear to be fighting stubbornly against their own discomfort, the others' flight from Gloomingtarn has undone any advantage Gorgar's forces may have held against the Gabil'akkâ.

Defeat Crótharc and collect his horns

A bounty posted at Grúmachath reads:
'After slaying no fewer than three—nay four—Zhélruka in the course of attempts to break him, I desire the horns of Crótharc as wergild for my fallen brethren. Crótharc was last seen roaming the eastern hillsides of Câr Bronach. Approach him with great care, lest you meet your doom! For the Zhélruka!
-Rádek'

'A bittersweet end, but the only one I could abide. Do not worry, friend, Crótharc did not actually slay any of my kin. But I was bested by a ram! I couldn't simply write out the truth of my failure for all to see—I had to employ my greatest skill: exaggeration! You understand, do you not?
'I only wish Crótharc had tolerated my saddle, but I could not be made to look a fool before my kin and kindred! A mighty, stubborn, but unwise ram he was—'twould have been better for the both of us if we had seen eye to eye!
'Take this for your troubles, friend. You have spared me a great deal of embarrassment and given me a trophy to carry home from this war!'
You claim Crótharc's horns as a trophy!

'It seems the Iron Crown is not content to bend other peoples' to its will. Within the cavern of Toll Oivas, the sorcerer Iärcagar has devised a means of binding fell spirits to the remain of bats.

'You have done well. We thank you for your assistance. Just as you have already done, I continue to make a name for myself in these lands.'

'It has been a long while, ${PLAYER}. I would wager that you did not expect to see those of the Trév Dúvardain and the Trév Gállorg working as one. Yet, here we are.
'You have met our leader, Domongart, before. He is on an urgent mission of diplomacy in the north. That is all that I can say. I have heard from Uzvát that you wish to assist us in our efforts. You have assisted me in the past. I know that you will be able to do so once more, old friend.
'The Trév Duvárdain have been sundered by choice. Many remain loyal to the Iron Crown. Those here see the folly in servitude. Assist us in our efforts here and then we will consider returning the favour to assist the Zhélruka.'

Return to Mézto with what you have learned
The Exiled Giant

'Go away!
'What?! You are still here?!
'You can ask me all the questions you you want. It does not mean that I will answer them!
'How could I even trust you? I can not even trust my own kind to make the right decisions. I can only trust these goats. If the goats trust you, then maybe I will answer a question for you.'

'${PLAYER}, have you returned! I was starting to wonder where you had gotten to!
'So the Grímklettar ally with the Dourhands, but not the Angmarim? I find this confusing! We know the Angmarim and the Dourhands work together! There is more at hand in Câr Bronach then I thought! Someone is driving a wedge in this alliance.'

'You have done as I asked, and the goats seem to find you acceptable. I will answer your question.
'Why am I here you ask? Crágan Bris was once a great settlement of my people. It is all I have left. You do not know much about Câr Bronach, I see. Then I will explain. This is where my ancestors came from. We once had a great city where the Drearspire now stands. Our home was taken from us by Men and we were chased away. Hraubrek wanted to reclaim our land. That is why we have returned. I followed Hraubrek because I believed in his wisdom. Now I am lost, for Hraubrek allies with our enemy. All our alliances have ended in death. How will this one be any different?!
'I have answered your question, now leave me be.'

The Dourhand Proposition
'Yes, the Dourhand is Rethvárd, our escaped prisoner. He has told me only what I needed to know. He would rather speak to you, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am glad that you came. Has Rethvárd filled you in? Good!
'I have been infiltrating Ásachal and her followers not for loyalty. Bah! They are nothing but an enemy to the Dourhand! I put my enemy close to see them fall! As we can both see, we have a common foe. I have been trying to get everyone to in Câr Bronach to work together. The hillmen are too timid, and as much as I have tried to sway the stone-giants, they seem to have other plans.
'I know that now is a good time to strike, while the Angmarim do not expect such an alliance to form. I also have heard, with good authority might I add, that atop the spire lies a stone of immense power! We can not let that artifact stay in the hands of the Iron Crown. Now, what do you say?
'Good. I am glad that you are with us! There will still be much work to accomplish after the Drearspire is taken. For that we will need the hillmen on our side. Let us rescue those who have been captured in an effort to show we mean to work together.'
'There you are, ${PLAYER}. So far, the Dourhands have kept their promise! We were able to take Agal Dûn and now sit at the entrance of the Drearspire. For Gundabad!'
Now is the time to strike the Drearspire!

'Your friend, Uzvát, has informed me that a representative of the Dourhands has a proposition for us. They wish to work together to topple High Priestess Ásachal and her reign over Tûr Fúar. I do not trust those who openly do the bidding of the Iron Crown. For that, we will not be involved.
'If you wish to listen to this Dourhand and work with them, that is for you and the dwarves to decide. I will think no less of you for what you decide, friend. Understand this: we will have no part in it.'

'Greetings. I bring direct word from Lord Brathar. He wishes to speak to you, ${PLAYER}. I will tell you where to find him. I assure you this is not a trap. I surrender myself again in good faith!
'Brathar has a plan. He has been building trust with the Angmarim, in order to crush them. All that is left in the plan is that he requires assistance from you and the Zhélruka!
'Please, just speak with him and Uzvát and I will make sure that the rest of your Gabil'akkâ remain at the ready.'
Uzvát nods with his approval of the plan.

'Hold a moment, ${PLAYER}. This place is a labyrinth of stairways and halls that seemingly go nowhere! We must scale the tower together! Here is a horn. May you use it if we become separated.
'The Dourhands said that while we should defeat as many cultists as we can, only a certain four would topple their hold in Tûr Fúar. High Priestess Ásachal is the obvious target, as is her second in command, Warlord Claghórd. We are also to target two powerful priestesses, Curcúan and Lasairë. The Rhudaur-stone

'I believe Brathar is lying. He wants nothing more than power. Even I believed that he was doing all this for the good of everyone under the subjugation of the Iron Crown. Now I saw the look in his eyes when we won but the Rhudaur-stone was missing. It was not the look of victory, it was the look of defeat.
'Do with me what you will, but know that I will follow Brathar Crach-helm no longer.'
'Brathar Crack-helm, you had that coming. You have caused more than enough trouble in these mountains. No more, Dourhand.'

'Well done everyone! This is a fine day for the Zhélruka. I knew this plan would work. That is why I came up with it after all! Ha, that will teach Durin to doubt the Zhélruka. I jest, ${PLAYER}. Durin's wisdom knows no bounds, even if he underestimates the resolve of the Zhélruka.'

'I must say, my plan was mostly a success, even if Prince Ingór will certainly take most of the credit! I can not blame him though. We would not be standing where we are if not for Prince Ingór's invaluable leadership!'

'That crafty Claghórd. He must have known the Rhudaur-stone was moved! That is why he did not care if we took the Drearspire. A lingering question then remains. Where was the stone taken? Where did Claghórd retreat to?'

'So it is true! ${PLAYER} returns to the north.
'I am sorry that the Trév Duvárdain have arrived late. I would have very much liked to speak to you at Eiricháv. An urgent matter had called me away. Soltakh has told me what you have accomplished. It seems we were right to not trust the Dourhands after all, though we should have taken the tower by your side.
'I was secretly meeting with Hraubrek, the Chieftain of the Grímklettar, in the north. The Trév Duvárdain and the Grímklettar have much in common. We have a common enemy, share these lands, and have been dealt many hardships for both our kind. I thank you for your assistance on this day. The Trév Duvárdain, and all free hillmen owe you much.'

'We do not need to see eye to eye, ${RACE}. In fact, I do not think we ever will.
'Yes, talking to the Angmarim and accepting gifts from the Dourhands were all a ruse, for my real intentions were to form a secretive pact with the Trév Duvárdain.
'While there has been many lives lost, including my own kin, I will not hold you accountable. The ends have justified the lives lost. As Gundabad is a sacred site to the dwarves, beneath this spire is the sacred city of my kind. It has been lost for so long. Now, the pilgrimage is complete for those of the Grímklettar who remain.
'If you and the dwarves let us be, then we will let you live under the mountain in peace. We will keep Câr Bronach free of the Iron Crown. You have my word. Now, please leave. You are not needed here any longer.'
The Rhudaur-stone is gone!

'Even if the Rhudaur-stone should belong to me, I had no intention of taking it! My plan was to destroy it! You do not believe me?
'Bah! How was I supposed to know that the Rhudaur-stone had already been moved to parts unknown?!'
Brathar clutches his chin in pain.
'Was that punch really necessary, Glóin?!'

Busca la Cabaña del Helechal, el hogar de los amigos de Ravaedron, más allá de la aldea de Glynafon al sureste
Habla con Ravaedron frente a la Cabaña del Helechal

'Si me acompañas a la cabaña de los Astaciervo y me ayudas a despedirme, me harías un favor, pues lo he estado posponiendo. Viven en una agradable cabaña al sureste, más allá de la antigua aldea de Glynafon.'

'Aquí es: la Cabaña del Helechal, hogar de mis amigos Maddoc y Glenys, y de su hijo Bran. Los Astaciervo fueron muy amables conmigo mientras me aventuraba por estas tierras, y los echaré de menos cuando me marche.
'Agradezco que estés aquí, ${PLAYER}. Decir adiós siempre es difícil, y me gustaría que mis amigos supieran que contarán con aventureros como tú para cuidar de ellos cuando yo no esté.'
'¡Salvaguardemos las tierras salvajes para la buena gente que habita en esta región! Quizá después me ayudes con la tarea que tanto he retrasado.'
Has llegado a la Cabaña del Helechal, hogar de los Astaciervo
Has derrotado a enemigos en el Ángulo para Ravaedron (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Enemigos peligrosos acechan los bosques rocosos del Ángulo, y Ravaedron desea que lo ayudes a combatirlos.
Ravaedron se encuentra en el camino que va hacia el sur desde el Bosque de los Trolls hasta el Ángulo.

'Mae govannen, ${PLAYERNAME:forastero[m]|forastera[f]}. Has llegado al Ángulo del Mitheithel, pero vas hacia el sur en lugar de hacia el norte. ¡Qué curioso! He descubierto que quienes viajan por estas tierras suelen hacerlo de paso hacia algún otro lugar, como es mi caso. No permaneceré mucho tiempo aquí en el Ángulo.'
El elfo sonríe brevemente.
'¡Pero qué modales los míos! Permíteme que me presente de inmediato: me llamo Ravaedron, y llegué al Ángulo hace algún tiempo por un encargo de los hijos de Elrond. ¡Ah! ¿Te conocen? Entonces seamos amigos también, pues compartimos el mismo propósito: ¡salvaguardar las tierras salvajes para la buena gente que vive en ellas! No te supondrá una gran molestia ayudarme con esto, ¿verdad? Hay algo que debo hacer, pero lo he estado posponiendo. Enfrentémonos primero a los peligros que se presentan aquí en el Mitheithel, y después tal vez vuelvas a ayudarme.'

'Muy bien, ${PLAYER:mi nuevo amigo[m]|mi nueva amiga[f]}. ¡Eres muy ${PLAYER:diestro[m]|diestra[f]} enfrentándote a este tipo de amenazas! No me extraña que Elladan y Elrohir confíen tanto en ti. ¿Te enviaron ellos a una misión como la mía? Me mandaron aquí en busca de oscuros sirvientes del Enemigo, jinetes de negro que burlaron las defensas de Imladris. Ah... tal vez no debería hablar más de ellos. Elrohir fue muy claro en que era un asunto secreto.'
Ravaedron hace el gesto de cerrar sus labios con llave y colgarla de una cadena invisible en su cuello.
'Digamos simplemente que no hallé rastro de nuestra presa, y dejémoslo ahí. Aun así, mi búsqueda no fue en vano, pues encontré algo que ahora me es muy querido. Entablé amistad con una familia de leñadores, los Astaciervo. Viven no muy lejos de aquí, y valoro mucho su amistad; la última amistad que hallaré en la Tierra Media, pues mis pasos me llevan ahora hacia los Puertos Grises y navegaré hacia el Oeste, dando fin a este capítulo de mi vida.'
Ravaedron ríe de repente.
'¡Aunque quizá los Astaciervo no sean la última amistad que haga aquí, ${PLAYER}, pues no contaba con conocerte! Viven en una agradable cabaña al sureste, más allá de la antigua aldea de Glynafon.'
'Aquí es: la Cabaña del Helechal, hogar de mis amigos los Astaciervo.'

'Siento que hayas tenido que presenciar esto, ${PLAYER}. Me duele decirlo, pero quizá Ravaedron no era un amigo tan cercano como pensábamos. Su pueblo y el nuestro deben de ser simplemente demasiado diferentes.
'¿Se hizo amigo nuestro... por pena? ¿Acaso todos los Inmortales ven a los hombres y mujeres del Ángulo como meras flores, tan frágiles y efímeras que hay que protegerlas y compadecerlas? Pensaba que nuestra amistad con Ravaedron era diferente, pero supongo que me equivocaba.'
