El destino del Ectheldur

'¿Qué es esto? ¿Un mapa? ¿Algún tipo de plano?
Por lo que puedo ver, parece que hubo algún gran diluvio hace mucho tiempo y que el lago nunca retrocedió. ¿Pero cómo puede ser? ¿Por qué no lo examinas más de cerca?'

'No estoy seguro de qué pensar sobre esto, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. Te pediría que recorras los bordes del Lago Evendim para inspeccionar sus aguas y tomar nota de lo que encuentres. ¡Hay algo inusual en esta marea!
Creo que deberás inspeccionar Annúminas desde varios lugares para entender estas marcas. Debes comenzar tu inspección aquí en Tinnudir, y luego continuar en las Agujas de la Linde, Men Erain y la isla de Tyl Ruinen. ¡Eso debería bastar! Toma prestado mi catalejo para ayudarte, pero cuida de él. ¡Es muy valioso para mí!
No eres ${PLAYERNAME:ajeno[m]|ajena[f]} a este tipo de trabajo, ¿cierto? Muy bien. ¡Esperaré tu regreso, !'

'¿Notaste algo interesante durante tu inspección, ${PLAYER}?'
Le cuentas a Tarneth que, según tu inspección, algunas de las marcas en el mapa de Naegir parecen corresponder a islas del Lago Evendim. Sin embargo, los lugares señalados parecen indicar islas y otras tierras que desde entonces han sido cubiertas por las aguas del Lago Evendim. Tarneth toma el mapa y lo estudia una vez más.
'¡Espera un momento, si esa marca es correcta, creo que podemos haber encontrado los restos del Ectheldur! No hay tiempo para explicarlo, ${PLAYER}. ¡Hay una isla cerca de una de estas marcas, y sospecho que allí encontraremos lo que buscamos!'

Tarneth se encuentra en Tinnudir, a orillas del Lago Evendim.

Habla con Tarneth en Tinnudir

'Según lo que hemos aprendido, los saqueadores de tumbas se han reunido en Rantost. Si los restos del Ectheldur estuvieran allí, los habríamos encontrado hace mucho tiempo, así que deben tener otro propósito en las ruinas.
Llegar a Rantost no es un viaje sencillo, pero eres ${PLAYERNAME:un Marinero experimentado[m]|una Marinera experimentada[f]}, ¿no es así? El Lago Evendim es vasto, sin duda, pero es solo una gota en el Gran Mar.
Expulsa a los saqueadores de tumbas de Rantost y fíjate si alguno lleva algo de importancia. ¡Parece que debemos recordarles una vez más que no tienen ningún derecho sobre las ruinas de Arnor!'

'¡Vamos! ¡Debemos llegar al Ectheldur antes de que los saqueadores de tumbas lo descubran por sí mismos!'
<rgb=#FF0000>Esta es una misión en solitario y no puede completarse con una Comunidad.</rgb>

'A duras penas puedo creer que encontramos el Ectheldur, y que incluso recuperamos el bastón forestal de Alwedion, pero debemos mantener en secreto lo que hemos aprendido hoy, ${PLAYERNAME:mi amigo[m]|mi amiga[f]}. La Dama Azul ha sido amiga de los Dúnedain durante mucho tiempo, y debemos devolver su bondad. Solo espero que algún día Gwindeth considere que es seguro bajar las aguas del Lago Evendim y que Annúminas pueda ver restaurada su antigua belleza.
Has prestado un gran servicio a los Dúnedain, , y tus acciones no serán olvidadas pronto. ${PLAYERNAME:Un Marinero[m]|Una Marinera[f]} de tu habilidad y experiencia será ${PLAYERNAME:un gran aliado[m]|una gran aliada[f]} en los días por venir, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. ¡Espero que volvamos a llamarte pronto!'

Quema las coronas de bruja (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Sant Lhoer: Semillas del mal
'Te doy la bienvenida de nuevo. Puedo ver por el humo que te rodea que has tenido éxito. Que tus acciones eviten que estas terribles creaciones se propaguen por Angmar y más allá.'
Quema las coronas de bruja (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Mae govannen. Mi nombre es Galasdil, y estaba viajando por Nan Amlug cuando me encontré con una planta tan extraña que pausé mi viaje para estudiar su origen. Mi investigación me llevó a través de las tierras arrasadas de Angmar, hasta aquí, a las puertas de Carn Dûm.
En los Sant Lhoer de Carn Dûm crecen numerosas plantas, torcidas y corrompidas por las aguas fétidas de los ríos que fluyen por la zona. Entre ellas se encuentra la corrompida corona de bruja, cuyas semillas se llevan fácilmente con el viento. ¡Incluso ahora veo pequeños copos de semillas flotando por el aire húmedo!
Si eres lo suficientemente valiente como para aventurarte en los Jardines Emponzoñados, quema cualquiera de estas plantas que veas. ¡No deben ser permitidas a propagarse por toda la Tierra Media!
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados.</rgb>

Galasdil te ha pedido que destruyas cualquier planta de corona de bruja que puedas encontrar dentro de Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados.
Sant Lhoer se encuentra en Carn Dûm.

Has quemado muchas coronas de bruja, y Galasdil estará feliz de escuchar sobre tus esfuerzos.
Galasdil se encuentra en Bail Avarc, fuera de Carn Dûm.

En Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados de Carn Dûm, crecen numerosas plantas, torcidas y corrompidas por las aguas fétidas de los ríos que fluyen por la zona. Si estas aberraciones logran salir de su jardín húmedo, podrían amenazar a las otras plantas, criaturas y pueblos de la Tierra Media.
Recoge muestras de agua (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Sant Lhoer: La corriente de Helchgam
'¡Ah, has regresado! Ven, déjame ver qué contienen las frascos.'
Muestras de agua recogidas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Tengo curiosidad por las aguas que fluyen a través de Sant Lhoer, los Jardines emponzoñados de Carn Dûm. Son menos potentes que las del resto de la ciudad, afortunadamente, pero también parecen poseer otros atributos, tanto corruptores como potenciadores para las plantas y criaturas cercanas.
'Toma estas frascos y tráeme muestras de los arroyos que fluyen, para que pueda estudiar el efecto que ha tenido la derrota de Helchgam. ¡Ten cuidado de no dejar que las aguas toquen tu piel! ¿Quién sabe qué venenos aún acechan en esas profundidades?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados.</rgb>

Sant Lhoer: Resultados de Oganuin

'Ah, has regresado. Sé que te he encomendado una tarea macabra. Dame las muestras que has recogido. Las llevaré a mi amigo, y quizás él tenga alguna idea de qué atrocidades se están cometiendo detrás de esas sucias paredes de cristal.'
Muestras de carne recogidas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Oganuin se ha encerrado en su Casa de Cristal, donde ella y sus seguidores experimentan con plantas y criaturas por igual. He visto algunos de los orcos que han sido sometidos a sus pruebas y los resultados me han impactado profundamente.
Conozco a un maestro cazador que desea estudiar la carne de las criaturas que ha alterado. Tráeme muestras de las criaturas dentro de sus Jardines Emponzoñados y la Casa de Cristal. El conocimiento de lo que ha hecho puede ayudarnos a detener e incluso revertir el proceso.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados.</rgb>

Sagroth: Probando las Aguas

'Me alegra escuchar que Lágsaith ha honrado tu solicitud. Tal vez eventualmente cuente estos detalles por sí misma, sin necesidad de recordatorios. Mientras tanto, Eávair y Borgach harán lo que puedan, mientras yo mantengo un oído atento.'
Muestras de líquido fétido recogidas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Eres un viajero, ¿no? ¿Has visto algo así antes?' Él muestra unas frascos de líquido viscoso y violentamente verde.
'La Corona de Hierro no mantenía bien sus alcantarillas. Recogimos muestras de allí para estudiarlas más a fondo, pero Eávair y Borgach -- Él asiente hacia las dos mujeres cercanas que están en profunda discusión. -- todavía están averiguando cómo descomponerlo y limpiarlo. Estas impurezas deben estar dañando la tierra de maneras que no entendemos.
'Lágsaith adora narrar nuestra expedición, aunque no se detiene en los detalles. Las historias que se transmiten de boca en boca pueden cubrir distancias mayores que las que nosotros mismos podemos viajar. Si ella describiera el líquido fétido a más viajeros como tú, alguien con nueva información podría presentarse y ayudarnos en nuestros esfuerzos.
'Si la buscas para conocer el relato completo, asegúrate de recordarle esto.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sagroth, el Antro de la peste.</rgb>
Usa el Buscador de Instancias para entrar en 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste' en cualquier dificultad.

Lágsaith ha descrito con gran detalle el líquido fétido que corre por las alcantarillas.
Debes contárselo a Náchtan en Bail Avarc.

Un líquido fétido se encuentra en 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste'.
Debes recoger algunas muestras.
Mientras Eávair y Borgach intentan resolver el problema de la limpieza de las alcantarillas, Náchtan dirige sus esfuerzos hacia la difusión de información y, con suerte, obtener algunas respuestas.

Sagroth: La atención a los detalles

'¿Lágsaith mencionó la inmundicia esta vez? Entonces estoy satisfecho. No quería sonar tan duro antes, pero ella ejerce poder con sus palabras, poder que puede ser usado para el bien.
Que su historia recuerde a los niños que deben mantenerse saludables, porque los seguidores de la Corona de Hierro no son las únicas amenazas a las que nos enfrentamos.'
Inmundicia no identificable destruida (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Una cara nueva. Debes ser la última víctima de Lágsaith, o lo serás pronto. Ella suele guardar sus relatos dramáticos para los niños, pero incluso los viajeros de paso no se salvarán.
'La expedición a las alcantarillas no fue tan emocionante como ella lo hace parecer. Ella omite por completo los \qmomentos aburridos,\q como ella los llamaría, por el bien de un \qmejor ritmo narrativo.\q Por lo tanto, se olvida de mencionar la inmundicia que quemamos en el camino.
'Los niños deberían saber que la infección y la plaga no es un asunto para tomar a la ligera. Asegúrate de que Lágsaith tampoco lo olvide.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sagroth, el Antro de la peste.</rgb>

Lágsaith ha contado, con detalles atroces, la asquerosa inmundicia que ella y sus camaradas encontraron en las alcantarillas.
Debes contárselo a Avlath en Bail Avarc.

Sagroth: Teatro de la Mente

'¿Confías en que el mapa te ayudó? Es rudimentario, sin duda, pero también útil. Sin él, podríamos habernos perdido para siempre.' Una pequeña sonrisa se dibuja en el rostro serio de Aighrig. 'Bromeo. Pero regresar a casa habría sido más difícil.
'El mapa solo muestra una fracción del sistema completo de alcantarillas. Espero que podamos completarlo en futuras expediciones. Después de todo, todavía queda mucho trabajo por hacer.'
Puntos de cartografía encontrados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Después de nuestras aventuras en el este, es extraño verte aquí en mi tierra natal, ${PLAYER}. Pero eres una visita bienvenida.'
Lukhag emite un chirrido de afirmación.
'Estoy segura de que Lágsaith desea contarte la historia de nuestra expedición, así que no te retendré por mucho tiempo. Pero quizás el conocimiento del diseño de las alcantarillas te permita apreciar más su relato.' Ella te entrega un mapa que ha sido dibujado a mano con cuidado. 'Rastreé nuestros pasos mientras estábamos allí abajo. Lágsaith nunca admitiría esto, pero necesitaba ayuda; su sentido de la orientación es atroz.
Puedes tomar prestado el mapa hasta que Lágsaith termine su relato.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes usar el Buscador de Instancias (Ctrl+J) para entrar en Sagroth, el Antro de la peste.</rgb>

El diseño de las alcantarillas de Carn Dûm es un desastre. El mapa de Aighrig está en progreso, pero también podría ayudarte a visualizar mejor la historia de Lágsaith.

Sant Lhoer, conocido como los Jardines Emponzoñados de Carn Dûm, es un lugar húmedo repleto de plantas, árboles y flores mortales, como pocas o ninguna se han visto antes en la Tierra Media. Más allá de las aguas fétidas de color verde berilo que fluyen por Sant Lhoer, se alzan inmensas estructuras de cristal, incluyendo Bâr Heledh, la Casa de Cristal. Es aquí donde la hechicera Oganuin practica su arte, experimentando con criaturas, plantas y personas por igual. ¿Con qué fin y para qué propósito? Solo se pueden suponer los más oscuros designios.

Dentro de Sant Lhoer has encontrado a un mago angmarim, Cráthair, y su compañero, el Jorthkyn Tarkka-oka. El último es como nada que hayas visto antes. ¡Esto debe ser uno de los horribles experimentos de Oganuin! Deberías derrotar a ambos.

Has descubierto una llave de hierro en el cuerpo de Cráthair. Dolág piensa que podría abrir una puerta que vio en el extremo norte de los Jardines Emponzoñados.
Deberías buscar y abrir la puerta del norte.
Dejas los Jardines Emponzoñados atrás y te diriges hacia enormes estructuras de hierro y vidrio. Deberías continuar buscando a Málruv.
Has descubierto enormes invernaderos de vidrio y hierro dentro de Sant Lhoer. Espera a que Dolág te alcance y luego habla con ella.

Te paras ante Bâr Heledh, la Casa de Vidrio de Carn Dûm. Dentro de sus muros de metal y vidrio, la hechicera Oganuin practica sus artes oscuras, creando abominaciones y retorciendo seres vivos hacia fines inhumanos. Debes derrotarla y buscar señales de Málruv.

Los Jardines Emponzoñados están ubicados en Carn Dûm.
Dolág te ha encontrado dentro de la puerta de los Jardines Emponzoñados y te está esperando para continuar. Deberías buscar a su hermano desaparecido.
Mientras explorabas Sant Lhoer, has encontrado un pabellón de cristal. Deberías buscar dentro por señales de Málruv.

Dentro de un pabellón de hierro y vidrio en Sant Lhoer, Tarkka-oka y su guardián Cráthair te tendieron una emboscada. Tras derrotarlos, encontraste una llave de hierro.
Dolág se ha unido a ti en el pabellón y está esperando para hablar contigo.

'Más allá de las puertas de hierro de Sant Lhoer se encuentran jardines mortales y casas de cristal llenas de hongos que expulsan esporas nocivas. ¡Algunas de las plantas dentro de los Jardines Emponzoñados pueden matar a una persona en un instante! Más allá de los jardines, a través de los ríos abarrotados de líquido verde, se encuentra Bâr Heledh, donde se dice que una hechicera angmarim está experimentando con plantas, criaturas y gente libre por igual. Hay cosas que nunca deberían ser intentadas, y temo que ella haya ido muy lejos de ese límite. Os ruego que pongáis fin a sus esfuerzos.
'Antes de aventuraros a Sant Lhoer, deberíais hablar con Dolág. Su hermano Málruv fue atacado y ella rastreó a sus secuestradores hasta aquí. Está casi tan afligida como para ir tras él por sí misma, pero si lo hiciera, temo que no regresaría.
'Por favor, ofrezca su ayuda si es posible.'

¡Viniste! Yo... admito que no esperaba que vinieras.'
Ella permanece en silencio un momento, y cuando vuelve a hablar, sus hombros están más firmemente decididos.
'Mi gratitud es profunda. Vamos entonces, pero ten cuidado. Las aguas aquí son repugnantes y tienen un aspecto amenazante. Te seguiré detrás.'

'¿Qué le ha pasado a este gigante? No se parece en nada al Jorthkyn que he visto antes. Hay algo extraño con las criaturas de este jardín. Los orcos y los trolls, y ahora el Jorthkyn, parecen mutaciones grotescas y retorcidas. Esto es obra de Oganuin, si se cree a Rhúnelleth. El Elfo estará encantado de saber que has puesto fin a esta abominación de la naturaleza.'
Le muestras la llave de hierro que encontraste.
'¡Una llave! Debe ser para la puerta al norte que vi más allá de las aguas venenosas. Dirijámonos hacia allí.'

'¡Mira allí, más allá de las paredes de cristal! Hay una extraña luz parpadeando dentro. Hemos encontrado Bâr Heledh, donde Rhúnelleth dice que Oganuin está creando las criaturas con las que has estado luchando. ¿Podría estar mi hermano dentro también?
'Recobra el ánimo, porque no dudo que ella tendrá más sorpresas aterradoras esperándote.'

'Yo... te saludo con alegría, ${PLAYERNAME:sureño[m]|sureña[f]}. Las cosas que planeaba para mí...'
Él se estremece.
'¡Llegaste justo a tiempo!'
'Las palabras por sí solas no pueden expresar mi alivio. Vamos, salgamos de este lugar infame. Encuéntrame de nuevo en Bail Avarc. Quiero llevar a mi hermano a un lugar seguro.'

'${PLAYERNAME:Bienvenido[m]|Bienvenida[f]} de nuevo, mi ${PLAYERNAME:nuevo amigo[m]|nueva amiga[f]}. Málruv está a salvo ahora, gracias a ti. Aunque está bien de cuerpo, los horrores que vio dentro de Bâr Heledh se quedarán con él para siempre, me temo.
'Sin embargo, ahora tengo la esperanza de que personas como tú ayudarán a crear un nuevo mundo donde la gente buena esté segura una vez más.'

¿Quién eres? No te conozco. ¿Rhúnelleth te envió? La elfa se mete y no ha dejado de molestarme desde que llegué aquí.'
Ella suspira y se recompone.
'En justicia, he apreciado su preocupación, y ella me ha mantenido alejada de lanzarme a esa maldita lugar sin un plan. He explorado en las puertas de los Jardines Emponzoñados, y veo mucho movimiento más allá de sus rejas metálicas. Dudo que pueda proceder contra tan grandes número de enemigos, pero tú pareces lo suficientemente formidable como para darme algo de esperanza.
'Si tú lideras el camino, yo te seguiré de cerca. ¡Quizás Málruv pueda ser encontrado dentro! Encontremos entonces, en Sant Lhoer.'
'¿Qué clase de mundo tan vil es este en el que vivimos?'
'¿No me ayudarás a liberar a mi hermano de la Corona de Hierro?'
Destruye el Fragmento de Tauressar
Derrota a Gurkrak
Derrota al Castellano Obáshurz
Derrota a la Suma Sacerdotisa Ásachal y al Gran Jefe Claghórd
Gwathrenost, la ciudadela del Rey Brujo -- nivel 1

Separado del Vandassar de Rhudaur, el Fragmento de Tauressar posee un terrible encantamiento capaz de influir en los corazones y mentes de aquellos que juran lealtad sobre él, ya sea voluntaria o involuntariamente.
Debes destruir el Fragmento de Tauressar.
Gurkrak vigila Gwathrenost y despacha brutalmente a aquellos lo suficientemente tontos o atrevidos como para entrar en la ciudadela del Rey Brujo sin ser invitados.
Uno de los últimos restos del reinado del Senescal de Angmar, el Castellano Obáshurz cuida de Gwathrenost y sirve fielmente a sus amos: la Suma Sacerdotisa Ásachal y el Gran Jefe Claghórd.

La Suma Sacerdotisa Ásachal y el Gran Jefe Claghórd se encuentran en Tham Mornarcham, la sede del Rey Brujo.
La Suma Sacerdotisa Ásachal y el Gran Jefe Claghórd deben ser derrotados antes de que puedan usar el Fragmento de Tauressar para subyugar a los Pueblos Libres de la Tierra Media.

Antiguamente sede del Rey Brujo de Angmar, la temible ciudadela de Gwathrenost proyecta una larga sombra sobre la ciudad de Carn Dûm. Casi abandonada tras la deposición del Senescal de Angmar, los restos de la Corona de Hierro han salido de las sombras, buscando dominar un artefacto perdido del Rey Brujo y reclamar el dominio de Angmar.

Debes ayudar a los Montañeses de Angmar y trabajar para oponerte a la Corona de Hierro en Carn Dûm.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes completar una de las siguientes en cualquier tamaño de grupo o nivel de dificultad: 'Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados', 'Thaurisgar, el boticario infame', 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste' o 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'.</rgb>

Muirál se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en Angmar.
Has hecho mucho para ayudar a los que se oponen a la Corona de Hierro en Carn Dûm. Debes hablar con Muirál.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Bail Avarc no es accesible inicialmente, solo a través de rutas de maestros de establo. Bail Avarc se puede alcanzar a través de los maestros de establos en Esteldín, Gath Forthnír y los establos de Rivendel.</rgb>
Completa 'Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados', 'Thaurisgar, el boticario infame', 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste' o 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'
Habla con Muirál en Bail Avarc

'¡Salve, ${PLAYER}!
'¿Estás aquí para unirte a la lucha contra la Corona de Hierro? Hay cosas viles en marcha en Sant Lhoer, Thaurisgar, Sagroth y dentro de los salones de Gwathrenost.
'Si nos ayudas a obstaculizar los esfuerzos de la Corona de Hierro en Carn Dûm, agradeceríamos tu ayuda.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes completar una de las siguientes en cualquier tamaño de grupo o nivel de dificultad: 'Sant Lhoer, los Jardines Emponzoñados', 'Thaurisgar, el boticario infame', 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste' o 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'.</rgb>

'Gracias, ${PLAYER}.
'Si seguimos luchando contra la Corona de Hierro, no pasará mucho tiempo antes de que los derrotemos!'

Los montañeses de Angmar y sus aliados trabajan para oponerse a los restos de la Corona de Hierro que vuelven a habitar dentro de los muros de Carn Dûm.

La botica ha sido invadida por los experimentos más retorcidos de los alquimistas. Están protegiendo la investigación vital que dejó Aniochán el Torturador.
Deberías derrotar a los gemelos.
Thaurisgar alberga muchas criaturas repugnantes y retorcidas, así como los viles ingredientes de la alquimia angmarim. Deberías investigar todo lo que contiene esta botica.

Las puertas que conducen a los niveles inferiores de Thaurisgar parecen estar cerradas.
Encuentra el mecanismo que desbloquea la puerta.

Has encontrado otra puerta, pero no tiene cerradura. Quizá haya un mecanismo que pueda abrir esta puerta.
Busca pistas sobre cómo abrir la puerta que conduce a la botica principal.

En las profundidades de Thaurisgar, innumerables criaturas nacidas de experimentos abominables y retorcidos vagan por las sombras, el terrible legado de Aniochán el Torturador. Antes de la caída de Carn Dûm, Aniochán trabajó incansablemente para superar a sus rivales y ganarse el favor del Senescal de Angmar. Entre sus herramientas para dar forma a sus creaciones estaba un curioso líquido conocido como la Bilis de Ifrinn. Se pensaba que se había perdido después de que un experimento desastroso le costara la vida a Aniochán, pero ahora esta sustancia fétida y vil corre el riesgo de liberarse en el mundo.

No hace mucho tiempo, un grupo de Trév Duvárdain derrotó a un mago de la Corona de Hierro en los alcantarillados de Carn Dûm. La historia es, como Lágsaith querría que muchos creyeran, bastante extraña.
Completa 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste'
El Antro de la peste
Habla con Lágsaith en Bail Avarc
Completa 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste' en cualquier dificultad

Completa 'Sagroth, Antro de la peste en cualquier dificultad.
Usa el Buscador de Instancias para entrar en 'Sagroth, el Antro de la peste'.

Lágsaith ha concluido su historia.
Deberías hablar con ella en Bail Avarc.
'Descendimos a las profundidades de los antiguos alcantarillados de Carn Dûm...'

'Diría que la historia ha llegado a su fin, pero el destino de nuestro amigo ratón sigue envuelto en misterio. Que encuentre algo de paz en la naturaleza... preferiblemente muy lejos de la Corona de Hierro.
'Gracias por escucharme. Ya he contado esta historia muchas veces, pero no creo que me cansaré nunca de ella. Ver a la gente reaccionar con sonrisas y risas es suficiente para mí. Después de todo, ¿qué hay de malo en un poco de diversión ligera en medio de días tan oscuros?
'¿Estaba mintiendo sobre el gran ratón? Bueno...'
Lágsaith te guiña un ojo.
'Eso es algo que solo yo sé y tú tendrás que adivinar. Si crees que te ayudará a tomar una decisión, vuelve otra vez para escuchar esta historia.'

'¿Quieres conocer todo el relato, eh? Bueno, supongo que puedo concederte ese privilegio.
'Una vez que mi querido Aighrig regresó del este, nuestro pequeño grupo comenzó a cazar a aquellos que aún creían en la Corona de Hierro. Rastreábamos a un tonto llamado Gárvadach por los alcantarillados de Dún Bándrath -- o Carn Dûm, como también se le conoce. Aparentemente, buscaba capturar y domesticar a una bestia de algún tipo. Los rumores de terribles monstruos que merodean bajo la ciudad van y vienen, pero...'
Lágsaith se acerca para un susurro conspirativo.
'Te aseguro que algunos de ellos han sido muy ciertos. Después de todo, ¿por qué la Corona de Hierro se preocuparía por cómo sus hechicerías han envenenado la vida silvestre?'
Ella sonríe, luego se recuesta.
'Gárvadach puede haber sido un tonto, pero cualquiera que perciba el mundo como algo a conquistar es peligroso. La tierra no perdona tal arrogancia, ni lo olvida.
'Y así, los seis lo perseguimos....'
Habla con Soltakh en Bail Avarc

'Es bueno verte, , pero me gustaría que nos hubiéramos encontrado de nuevo en días mejores.
'Mucho ha cambiado en tu ausencia, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. Me temo que nuestros problemas en Carn Dûm solo han empeorado desde que Crannog envió su mensaje.'

Encuentra a Crannog en Bail Avarc

\q${PLAYERNAME:Mi amigo[m]|Mi amiga[f]},
Después de que Carn Dûm fuera retomada de los sirvientes de la Corona de Hierro, yo y muchos otros creímos que huyeron hacia el este. Lamentablemente, parece que lo que los llevó allí no fue el miedo, sino la perspectiva de un regreso más pernicioso aún para conquistar Angmar. Ahora, los Angmarim de la Corona de Hierro que sirvieron al Falso Rey y las tribus de los Trév Duvárdain aún leales a ellos han reclamado la ciudad de Carn Dûm.
Los Trév Gállorg no han olvidado la ayuda que ofreciste a nuestra tribu contra el Falso Rey y los opresores de la Corona de Hierro, pero debo pedir tu ayuda una vez más. Cuando viniste por primera vez a Aughaire, te ofrecí un Fém: un propósito, un desafío y el deber de todos aquellos que se llamarían Trév Gállorg. Cumpliste tu Fém y lo llevaste a su fin. Hoy, te escribo para otorgarte un nuevo Fém: viaja a Bail Avarc y ayúdanos a expulsar a la Corona de Hierro de Carn Dûm, de una vez por todas.
Jefe y dos veces humillado miembro de la tribu de los Trév Gállorg, Crannog\q
Adjunto al mensaje de Crannog hay un pequeño mapa de Angmar que indica la ubicación de Bail Avarc.
A pesar de tus muchas victorias sobre la Corona de Hierro desde las heladas estribaciones del Forochel hasta los confines orientales del Monte Gundabad, el mensaje de Crannog te deja inquieto y un viejo temor llena tu corazón. ¿Está realmente disminuida la Corona de Hierro y solo juega a regresar a su antigua prominencia en Angmar? ¿O cada aparente derrota de la Corona de Hierro solo ha servido para avanzar algún plan mayor?
Pregunta tras pregunta llega sin ser invitada a tu mente. Habrá tiempo suficiente para pensar en todas ellas durante el viaje a Bail Avarc, decides, y seguramente Crannog y los Trév Gállorg tendrán las respuestas que buscas.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Bail Avarc puede ser alcanzado a través de los maestros de establos en Esteldín, Gath Forthnír y los establos de Rivendel.</rgb>
Angmar Renacido, Prólogo

Aunque los Angmarim de la Corona de Hierro y sus aliados entre los Trév Duvárdain fueron dispersados de Carn Dûm después de la caída del Falso Rey, el jefe de los Trév Gállorg, Crannog, ha enviado un mensaje pidiendo tu ayuda en Bail Avarc, sugiriendo que todo no está bien en Angmar.

'Welcome, mistress. Your presence in this war-torn land is welcome. The filth that fights in the Lord's name falters at every turn. Perhaps with our hand to guide them we will turn the tide and finally force our way south to discover the hidden Elven stronghold. Though it is beneath you, your first task is to meet with War-tyrant Akulhún. You will find him behind you shouting incessantly in the shadow of the totems. Be warned, he has a temper.'
'Here's a specimen ready for battle! Now, if only I could get the Lord of Angmar to recall the damned emissary he's sent here. Welcome to the front!'

'Pay attention, maggot! You are nothing! A speck. I don't know why Mordirith sent you here, other than to die like the rest! Ha! You need to make an impression or, at least an introduction. Make your way to the totems surrounded by bonfires. Find War-tyrant Akulhún and report in.
'Now, get out of my face. You sicken me.'

'You have just been hatched, broodling, but already you must play an important role. Mordirith sends you here to aid in the war against the Free Peoples. We have no time to waste. You must now get your feet wet. All of them.
'Seek out the War-tyrant Akulhún near the totems and bonfires. He is the ultimate leader in the Ettenmoors and will give you your orders!'

'Well... well... a new pup fresh from a litter in the mires of Angmar. Finally ready to wet your pelt with the blood of our enemies? Good, bare your teeth. Gird your loins. Your first task is to meet the War-tyrant. Akulhún stands before the totems near the bonfires. Make your way to him and report your arrival.
'Go now. Make the pack proud.'

Tutorial: El Poder de la Corrupción
Malavin, el emisario de Angmar, te indicó que regresaras al lugar donde comenzaste tu viaje en las Landas de Etten para hablar con el corruptor allí.
Speak with the emissaries

'The Krahjarn are born to lead. We remember the wars against the first. We recall the first lash against our backs and how to revisit that on our lessers. We know what it means to lead. To oversee the battle. To watch the flow of a fight. When to inspire and when to instill fear.'
He snarls.
'We know what makes a maggot a maggot and how to make a whelp a warrior. Stand alongside us, whelp and we'll make you a warrior yet.'

'The Scara know the hunt. The strength of sudden strike. The panic you instill from the shadow and tastiest, easiest places to tear flesh from bone. We teach the pack the way and it is for the warg or any to do the rest.'
He shakes his fur.
'We heed only brutality and cruelty to bring down our targets quickly and as painfully as possible. Our pack can teach you, but you must do the rest. We waste time by standing still. Choose us and run free.'
'Off with you until you have spoken to each of the emissaries. Return to me when you are done. I shall instruct you further.'

'Well done, I am amazed you had the attention span necessary to speak with them all. There may be hope for you yet. Now to the matter at hand. Choose. Choose a clan to represent while you fight for Angmar.
'All will welcome you. Freely shirk your allegiance like you have done your duty for so long. Drink of their blessing until you find a home that is welcoming to you. They are ordered to show no malice toward each other for now. This truce may not hold forever.
'Mordirith wants to see these Free Folk brought low. So the clans were convened to find the strongest among you in order to determine the best way to eliminate the forces here. Align yourself. That is all you need do.'
She smiles deviously.
'And when you tire of their boon, simply visit another to take their blessing in the first's stead. For the moment, it is simple. It shall not be forever. So do your best to prove to the master what clans should remain here in the Ettenmoors fighting and slaughtering the Free Folk.'

'Far be it from the Krahjarn to deny protocol. What, you think we're all war hungry tyrants like Akúlhun?'
He smirks.
'We are... some of us just hide it better. Talk with Malavin. That is the command. We will abide.'
'The pack is eager to hunt. The human is a barrier to our victory. Speak with her quick and then return to me.'

'I am Fathrug, and you look like you are ready to tear the flesh off a man. That is all we ask. Find the Men. Flay the Men. Leave their carcasses littering the earth to turn the grass bloody. The Tarkrîp clan will strengthen your skills, help you stay in the fight longer. You'll be rather brutal about your business of hacking and rending the enemy, and while we won't teach you how to dodge a really nasty sword blow, we'll teach you to shrug it off and keep going.
'The Tarkrîp clan prizes scrappy warriors above all else, willing to strike at the enemy relentlessly!'

'You look soft, maggot. I should know the Ongbúrz are the heartiest clan in all of Angmar. We are not afraid of battle. We thrive in it. We revel in the clash of hammers, axes, and all the tools those bearded bastards bring against us. We know little fear. Our prowess is in our staying power.
'If you want to swing your blade wildly without thought about tomorrow, go talk with the Tarkrîp or the dogs. If you want to stand tall above all the others then take our blessing into battle. Toughness like ours should never be underestimated.'

'Come closer. Smell that? Mushrooms. Slime. Herbs. Poultices. The trappings of healers. Oh, yes, the other clans will tell you that they are the most stalwart, or furious, or violent, or sinister, but we are the force that keeps them standing. We are the strength behind them all.'
He chuckles.
'Half the pain that they don't feel is because of our stinking sludges and fungal brews. We know how to pound a spike into a missing arm if things go terribly ill, too. Sometimes the victim even survives long enough to make it more permanent.
'The others will tell you tales, but it is we that let them keep tongues wagging. Without us, they'd all be face down in the dirt. Stand with us. Stand with the Blogmal Clan.'

'She is born of the first enemy of Elves. She feeds her brood well and gives them all they need to spread the faith of the Dark Lord. Gifts that sting deeply, secretly, and brutally. Her poison courses to seep into the flesh and twist it to the darkness where she dwells.'
The queen chitters.
'She burns the victims from within so they sting, sting, sting, longer and more painfully. She is the corruption that seeds the earth with malicious intent. She is mother to her brood. Join with her and earn the gift to inflict suffering most profound.'

'Sharkey orders us north to help fight. So we come. We see why these clans fail. Too unbalanced. Too dedicated to destruction, or defence. Too dedicated to mysticism or the darkness.'
He shakes his head.
'No temperance leads to a quick end. Learning the field of battle. Discerning the weakness and strengths of your enemy provides a clearer path to victory. It is an even path we walk. It is the teaching of our master that we prize. The method to strike hard. The method to stand tall. The method to withstand a strike and turn a blade.
'I would lead the White Hand against any of these other clans and leave them in shambles. Join us and you will see what I mean.'

You have spoken with Malavin

War-tyrant Akúlhun directed you to the war tent to speak with an Angmarim sorceress there named Malavin. Apparently she is here to assist, inspect, or guide the war effort. Whatever her purpose, it does not sit well with the War-tyrant.

'Listen here. A sorceress come from the north to tell me how the fight goes. Oh, she has the ear of the steward, but the arms are here, in the Ettenmoors. We've been fighting while they've been locked away in castles and steel barricades. What do they know about battling these people?'
It is a question expecting no answer.
'Bah... leadership back in Carn Dûm is looking for a new way to off these pesky Free Folk. So we got some new tricks available, meat. Each clan, and even the dirty dogs and sticky little spiders got their own emissaries here to help you new gits out. Oh and those southron Uruks too... talk to one of them and they'll give you a taste of what the leaders are thinking... don't get used to it though, maggot. These truces can only last so long....
'But first, they want me to send every maggot with snot dripping on their face up the hill to talk with her. Well... so be it. Better you go talk to her than me. She calls herself, Malavin.'
There is a short pause.
'If you get a chance, accidentally spit on her for me, would you?'

'Another veteran of the way? Or are you a new recruit? Honestly, I cannot tell the difference between a seasoned warrior and a whelp fresh from the pens or egg. I do, however know a thing or two about obedience and seeing that orders are carried out.'
She smirks wryly.
'Mordirith is displeased with the efforts here and organized an effort to entice you... warriors... with gifts. Each of the Orc clans, the Scara-pack, and Brood of Shelob send emissaries to entreat. He even allowed the White Hand at this table. Perhaps, in time there will be more. For now, it is these few.'
She pauses a moment to look you over.
'It appears that the steward of Carn Dûm is correct in his assessment. You are all in dire need of help. I invite you then to speak with the emissaries here in Gramsfoot. Learn what they offer you and choose their blessing. Each has been ordered, for now, to entreat with all of you. Provide for your until the council of our lord is complete.
'Run along now, and learn from each of the emissaries here and then return to me.'
'Orders is orders. You need to talk to the Priestess first.'
'Talk with the skinny witch, then you can talk to me.'
'Abide by the council's will and speak with Malavin.'
'Seek she who speaks for the lord of Carn Dûm. Our brood will wait our turn.'
'Sharkey's orders are clear, we let the woman speak... for now.'

<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Bail Avarc solo se puede acceder inicialmente a través de las rutas de los maestros de establos. Bail Avarc se puede alcanzar a través de los maestros de establos en Esteldín, Gath Forthnír y los establos de Rivendel.</rgb>
Completa 'La lucha por Carn Dûm (Diaria)' (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Habla con Muirál en Bail Avarc

'Oponerse a la Corona de Hierro con palabras no es suficiente, ¡debemos actuar si queremos liberar Carn Dûm y Angmar de sus males!
'Si continúas la lucha contra la Corona de Hierro y desafías su regreso a Carn Dûm, me aseguraré de que recibas una recompensa.
'¡Por aquellos que luchan por Angmar nos honran a todos!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Debes completar la misión 'La lucha por Carn Dûm (Diaria)' para avanzar en esta misión.</rgb>

'Nos has hecho un gran favor, ${PLAYER}.
'Rezo para que los males que acechan Carn Dûm sean finalmente desterrados de nuestra tierra!'
Desafiante de la Corona de Hierro (Semanal)
'La lucha por Carn Dûm (Diaria)' completada (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Los Pueblos Libres de la Tierra Media se esfuerzan por arrebatar Carn Dûm a la Corona de Hierro y derrotarlos de una vez por todas.
Report back to Uglash

You are to go to the training dummies behind the totems in Gramsfoot and use your skills so that you might familiarize yourself with how to fight the enemy.
<rgb=#00FF00>Remember, you cannot attack or use skills while you are <rgb=#FFFF00>marching</rgb>. You will need to disable the skill <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb> to begin attacking or use other skills.</rgb>
You have used both a ranged and a melee skill on a target dummy and should return to Uglash at Gramsfoot.
Successfully use <rgb=#FFFF00>Piercing Attack</rgb> on training dummy Kelsen, Jalessa, or Light training-dummy Orion
Successfully use <rgb=#FFFF00>Tainted Kiss</rgb> on a target dummy

'Let us see what you can do. Behind the totems are effigies of the enemy. Go to them. Use your skills against them and return me when you have struck blows upon the false enemies that we train against. Return to me when this task is done.'

'Ha! Don't you feel special, you little wretch? Oh... I hit a training dummy, look at me!
'Pathetic!
'Out there, in the 'moors, the enemy hits back! And most time they don't use pillows filled with feathers. Except maybe the rat-folk. Oh... and them rat-folk is good eatin'.'
Uglash seems lost in thought for a moment.
'Oh... what? I've got no more to teach you - for now.'
Tutorial: Killing In the Name Of...
You struck a blow with Piercing Attack!
You struck a blow with Tainted Kiss!
Uglash wants you prepared to fight for Mordirith and tasked you with trying out your skills before sending you off to fight the enemy in the Ettenmoors.
Arrive at the keep of Dâr-gazag
Use the skill <rgb=#FFFF00>Return to Gramsfoot</rgb> to return
Speak with Uglash

'Look at this maggot, fresh from a run to Dâr-gazag. Think you're ready to face the blades of the enemy? I bet your bowels would loose before an Elf cuts you gut to throat!'
Uglash looks you over.
'No, there's more that needs doing yet.'
You have arrived at Dâr-gazag
You have returned to Gramsfoot

Leave Gramsfoot by way of the hidden path along the mountainside to the west. Or, if you are feeling adventurous wander outside the main gate of Gramsfoot, but beware, the Freeps can attack you if you do not take the mountainside path. Your goal is to reach the keep, Dâr-gazag.

'Now, one last thing to do. The true power of our army lies at the end of a long path west out of the gates of Gramsfoot. There are other ways to get to the keep, but the safest path stays along the mountainside and keeps you above the fray until you are really ready to enter the fight.
'Go now, to the keep at Dâr-gazag and see the host assembled there to defend the Fragment of Mordirith's crown.'
Tutorial: The Keep at Dâr-Gazag
You reached Dâr-gazag and should now return to Gramsfoot to complete your training.
Now that you have returned to Gramsfoot, speak with Uglash, the task-master.

You have received your first reward for being a warrior in Angmar's army. Before you are unleashed with the remainder of the horde, you are tasked with visiting the true seat of the army's power in the Ettenmoors, Dâr-gazag.
Uglash can prepare you for the fight to come no longer. He advised that you speak with the War-tyrant and begin your battles in the Ettenmoors.
Return to Akulhún for your newest orders

'There is little else that I can do to prepare you for what is beyond that gate.'
Uglash laughs.
'Time to prove yourself. Go to the War-tyrant. Tell him you are ready.'

'Listen well, Uruk. There are expectations that I have of you and our race. You should lead - from the back. Whipping these lesser creatures into a frenzy and making sure that the taste of flesh stays fresh in their gullets.
'You are prepared. Do not fail...'
He leans in close.
'Or I'll skin you myself.'
Tutorial: Know Your Role!
It is time to put all you have learned together and return to War-tyrant Akulhún for your orders.
Choose a clan and receive their blessing
'I do not care for the choice you made, only that you made one.'
The time has come to choose your clan allegiance. All you need do is speak with one of the emissaries and choose to represent them on the field of battle.

'This choice is an important one, for certain. But as the master has deemed, you can freely choose what clan you shall represent in the battle for a time.
'You should feel free to approach whichever tribe you choose without fear that you must always represent that clan. No, little worm, you can freely change your allegiances the same as you choose your diet for a day.'
She offers you a weak smile.
'Simply choose an emissary and accept their blessing. If you decide later that you dislike the benefits that their clan provides I am certain that they will abide by the master's law and allow you to freely choose your clan affiliation for now.
'Was that word too big for you? You seem to be staring at me more slack-jawed than usual. Perhaps, you should go make your choice.'
Tutorial: Choose Clan Blessing
With your choice of clan made, you should return to the emissary, Malavan and speak with her.
Having met the emissaries of the clans, you must now make a decision. What clan shall you represent in the conflict of the Ettenmoors?

Debes superar los males reunidos en Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Debes completar 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo' en cualquier nivel de dificultad para avanzar en esta misión. Una vez que hayas completado 'Descubrimiento: Carn Dûm' viajando a Bail Avarc, utiliza el Buscador de Instancias para unirte a 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'.</rgb>

Grúmach se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en Angmar.
Has vencido a los maestros de la Corona de Hierro en Gwathrenost y finalmente has liberado Angmar de su influencia. Deberías hablar con Grúmach.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Bail Avarc solo se puede acceder inicialmente a través de las rutas de los maestros de establos. Bail Avarc se puede alcanzar a través de los maestros de establos en Esteldín, Gath Forthnír y los establos de Rivendel.</rgb>
Habla con Grúmach en Bail Avarc
Completa 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'

'¡Salve, !
'Debemos actuar contra la Corona de Hierro antes de que sea demasiado tarde. Si queremos poner fin a sus planes para Angmar, no tenemos más opción que atacar el corazón de Gwathrenost.
'Deberías reunir a tus aliados más poderosos, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. Una vez que estés ${PLAYERNAME:preparado[m]|preparada[f]}, ¡asedia la antigua ciudadela del Rey Brujo!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Para avanzar en esta misión, debes completar 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo' en cualquier nivel de dificultad. Una vez que hayas completado 'Descubrimiento: Carn Dûm' viajando a Bail Avarc, usa el Buscador de Instancias para unirte a 'Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo'.</rgb>

'Nos has hecho un gran favor, ${PLAYER}.
'Con la batalla contra la Corona de Hierro ganada, espero que nunca más tengamos que temer su regreso. Ninguno de los habitantes de Angmar olvidará tus hazañas!'
Asalto: Gwathrenost, la Ciudadela del Rey Brujo (Semanal)

Antiguamente sede del Rey Brujo de Angmar, la temible ciudadela de Gwathrenost proyecta una larga sombra sobre la ciudad de Carn Dûm. Casi abandonada tras la deposición del Senescal de Angmar, los restos de la Corona de Hierro han salido de las sombras, buscando dominar un artefacto perdido del Rey Brujo y reclamar el dominio de Angmar.

Speak with Gruglok

'A new recruit? Well then, let's get you outfitted and prepared for battle.'
The Orc seems all too pleased with his position.
'Once you start fighting and earning your keep in the Ettenmoors, I'll take commendations in exchange for my goods. You earn commendations for doing the work that no one else wants to do and slaughtering the Free Folk! Ha!'
<rgb=#00FF00>In Monster Play, completing quests and defeating Free People players awards <rgb=#FFFF00>commendations</rgb> and gold. <rgb=#FFFF00>Commendations</rgb> allow the purchase of not only skills, but also potions, food, and other items that provide short-term enhancements or immediate effects for your character.</rgb>
'Here, take this. Standard issue goods for all new recruits. Go on now. Open that up and see what I gives you!'

'There is hope for you, yet.'
The warg snarls.
'While using <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb>, you can speak with allies and interact with items in the world. However, you cannot use any of your other abilities to fight against the foe while you are marching, so best to be quick to stop marching when it comes time to fight!
'Use the skill now, then visit the vendor Nadar near the front gate to learn more.'
You used the skill March!
Gruglok instructs you to visit the vendor Nadar
Gruglok is your trainer in the Ettenmoors. Speak with them and learn about skills in the Ettenmoors.

Gruglok instructed you to speak with them again and learn the skill <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb>. Then, you are to use the skill so that Gruglok can see that you understand how to use the new skill you earned.
Speak with Gruglok and learn about training skills

'To strengthen your resolve, body, and abilities, you must earn skills and corruptions. In order to unlock the power of the corruptions and skills, you must speak with corruptors who will help you to unlock the deeper potency. As you grow in strength, so too will your access to greater and more malevolent corruptions.
'When you are prepared, speak with Gruglok. They will teach you more of your abilities, here in the Ettenmoors.'
<rgb=#00FF00>Some NPCs in the game world have several available roles. They can bestow quests, open shops, give hints, train skills, and any number of other interactions. When you speak with an NPC that has these additional roles, you will need to select the role you want to use from the context menu that opens when you speak with the NPC.</rgb>
<rgb=#00FF00>You have already been rewarded some traits that you can apply to your character. It is recommended that you speak with the corruptor and apply these corruptions to your character now.</rgb>
<rgb=#FFFF00>Optional:</rgb><rgb=#00FF00>Speak with the trainer again if you wish to purchase additional skills and traits.</rgb>

'Were you the runt of your litter? You look small. You look frightened. You should be frightened. Everything here, including the Orcs, the Uruks, the Angmarim, the spiders... they all want to kill you. Except the goblins of Grothum. They want to throw a saddle on you and ride into battle as some abominable, yet terrifying, hybrid.'
The warg growls.
'We're not about to let that happen. Speak with me again and purchase the skill <rgb=#FFFF00>March!</rgb>. Then, use the skill to prove that you have learned and know how to enable what you learn.'

'¡Hola! ¿Podrías prestarme tu oído? Soy Indagir.
'Es de gran importancia que me ayudes. No soy más que un humilde explorador que busca una forma de combatir las enfermedades que afectan a nuestra tierra.'
Indagir parece nervioso.
'Dentro de la bótica, hay una gran cantidad de conocimiento por descubrir.
'Mientras nuestro pueblo sufre por la plaga y la gran corrupción, existe dentro un panacea que curaría lo que nos aqueja. ¡Estoy seguro de ello! Por favor, no puedo ir solo.'

'Los salones están llenos de criaturas hostiles y repugnantes. No puedo defenderme solo, pero la información que hay dentro seguramente será beneficiosa para nuestra causa.
'Estoy agradecido de que hayas decidido ayudar. Te encontraré dentro de Thaurisgar. Conozco un lugar seguro. Es lo más lejos que iré, porque lo que merodea allí dentro solo puedo empezar a describirlo como... antinatural.'

'My husband so greatly desires to speak with his people and mend the pain of the hurts they suffered that I fear he will give no thought to his own protection, ${PLAYER}. I turn then to you, and to those others who hold him dear!
'I ask this of you, ${PLAYER}, and of my husband's boon companions: Legolas of Eryn Lasgalen and Gimli the Dwarf, of Erebor. Where Elessar wishes to venture, I ask that you three travel first, with your ears listening and your eyes sharpened. Look for any sign that the Heirs of Castamir remain a danger to the kingdom or to the King, and make the path he plans to travel as secure as you may.
'Only this will ease the burden of my heart.'

'You will do as my Queen requests? I think it will prove unnecessary, but I do not want my bride to worry if it might be prevented! Nor do I want my people to wait for any help I might have offered.
'It is not an easy riddle to solve, ${PLAYER}, but I think I have the answer. The three of you will go ahead of me to visit the towns and cities of my kingdom, keeping watch for any sign of the Heirs of Castamir or their supporters, as Arwen requests, but you will go not only in search of danger. You will also go as my emissaries, and to begin my own mission of aid, doing what you can to help the people with their concerns.
'When you have determined the Heirs of Castamir are of no real danger to myself or the kingdom, you will return to me and I will depart with my own travelling companions to further your work. If this will satisfy my Queen and my Council, then I suppose I must be content with the delay. It will be a balm to my spirit to know that you three, at least, will have begun my mission to heal the kingdom of its hurt.'

'Another adventure begins, ${PLAYER}, of a sort. It will not take long to learn if the Heirs of Castamir are truly gone, and when we have done so Elessar can tour his kingdom.
'Let us start by journeying to the Harlond, my friends. The south-harbour is nearest to the city, and from there we can proceed west in search of news.'
Glindor has brought you to the Tower of Ecthelion, where King Elessar and Queen Arwen await you.
King Elessar is ready to speak with you about his plans.
King Elessar and his advisors discuss his plan to tour the kingdom and heal the hurts caused by the war.
Thalhír, the Warden of Laws, is in the Tower of Ecthelion and has been called to answer whether the Heirs of Castamir remain a threat to the peace of Gondor.
King Elessar and his advisors discuss his plan to tour the kingdom and heal the hurts caused by the war.
'King Elessar and Queen Arwen will see you now.'

'We accomplished much good in the fight against Mordor and the forces of Sauron, ${PLAYER}, and prevented the triumph of terrible evil! The War of the Ring, for so I have heard it called in the days since its ending, has left its mark upon us and upon our lands. Our victory came at great cost, and the losses suffered in its achievement still wound those of us who remain. Perhaps they always will. And yet, if I can ease the hurts of my kingdom, I would do it. Can I count upon you to help me with this aim?'
You assure Elessar that you are with him, and he smiles.
'I knew our minds would be alike in this. This, then, is my purpose: I wish to travel my kingdom, from town to town, speaking with the people. I wish to hear what it is they lack, and to provide it; I wish to know how the war has injured them, and do what I can to repair those injuries. I want my people to know that their King is with them, not a distant figure in the Tower of Ecthelion, but a man who knows them and will strive every day of his life to prove he is worthy of Gondor.
'I want to tour the kingdom, and see what I can do to heal the hurts of the war.'

'I hesitate to mention it, my King, for I understand the majority of your people are overwhelmed with happiness at both the successful conclusion of the war and with your marriage to the Queen. I do not wish to spoil the broth of positive sentiment by dwelling upon the inclusion of one or two poor ingredients, and those in such tiny quantities.'
Thalhír clears his throat and looks uncomfortable.
'But there have been whispers of discontent in the city following your happy marriage, my King. Few perhaps, but some. I am sure they will disappear in time, as did those of the supporters of the Withered Tree, but as of yet they remain. I have heard tell from other members of the Council that people in the lower circles of the city speak wishfully of the Heirs of Castamir, praying for their return and believing they soon will.'

'It is to the Tower of Ecthelion we go, there to audience with King Elessar and Queen Arwen, the rulers of victorious Gondor.'
Glindor, King Elessar's herald, is outside the stables in Minas Tirith (Midsummer).
Gimli is north-east of the Harlond, in King's Gondor.
Legolas is north-east of the Harlond, in King's Gondor.

'A king has returned to Gondor, ${PLAYER}, and all the kingdom celebrates! And yet he is not content to rest on the laurels of his deserved victory over Sauron.
'I was instructed to bring you to see him. Will you come with me?'

'My feet are sore already, ${PLAYER}, and we have come to just the first of the places Aragorn told us to visit. His kingdom is larger than it looks on the maps, and Legolas and I have already crossed it once!'
Gimli falls silent.
'I named him Aragorn again, didn't I? He will have as many names as a Wizard next, but he has been a trusted companion through many adventures, and for that I will learn them all.
'He is not the king of any other kingdoms, is he?'

'We have come to the South-gate of the Rammas Echor, through which lies the Harlond, the south-harbour of Minas Tirith. It was held by Orcs of Mordor during the war, and they did not expect the arrival of Elessar aboard the ships of the Corsairs!'
Legolas smiles.
'They did not expect Legolas Greenleaf or Gimli, son of Glóin, either. That much was clear to all!'
'There will be fewer Orcs to fight inside the Harlond this time, I wager.'
Chapter 1.1: A King Should See His Kingdom
King Elessar, recently crowned and newly wedded, is eager to heal the hurts of his kingdom and to move Gondor into an age of prosperity.
Talk to Othanar inside the Harlond

'What do you want, stranger? Don't like what you hear, do you? It doesn't matter to me what you like and what you don't. Gondor changed once, and it can change again; folk like you might want to watch where you stick your noses.
'Friend of mine in Arnach heard the Heirs of Castamir are gathering in strength and will soon return. Their leader Balakhôr survived the fighting and slipped away to safety before he could be executed... such a pity for the upstart king! Now Balakhôr plans to overthrow the new king and his foreign bride. It was them, and people like them, that brought the war upon us: the land remembers it all. Won't be long before it has its revenge upon them, using Balakhôr as its instrument.'
You insist that Balakhôr is very dead, and Berthon snorts.
'That's not what my friend in Arnach says, and I think I'll be listening to him and not to you, stranger.'
'That went well, ${PLAYER}.'
'Now move on. I don't like the smell of you.'

'How goes the work, ${PLAYER}? Gimli and I have made ourselves useful.
'Some of the folk here seem... distrusting... of Elves and dwarves. It may be caused by fear or by superstition, but most have given us a wide berth even as they keep one eye upon us. It is nothing to me, but Gimli is bothered by it.'

'Bothered by it? You wound me, Legolas! I am no delicate crystal, and can give insult better than any of these cowards... should the need arise, which King Elessar should hope it does not, since we are here on an errand of peace and restoration.
'But has the Elf-hearing of which you often boast abandoned you? For I heard those men speak the name \qBalakhôr,\q and it is not so common a name that it could belong to anyone but the leader of the Heirs of Castamir, about whom we seek tidings!'
'See that gathering of Gondorians to the east? Approach them and <rgb=#00FF00>listen</rgb> to their conversation, and you will see I have not invented this worry!'
'Is this true? Do they really speak of Balakhôr the Scourge?'

'Begin by cleaning up rubble piles throughout the Harlond. Earlier today some folk offered to pick up loose wooden planks around the port, and left them leaning upright at several locations to the south-west; if you can gather those for me I would appreciate it. And also take care of the rat problem, if you would.'
'Your friends work still, by the docks to the south-east.'
'Most of these folk have given us a wide berth even as they keep one eye upon us. It is nothing to me, but Gimli is bothered by it.'
The crowd glares at you with distrust

Legolas suggested that someone to the south-west must be overseeing the repairs of the Harlond.
Othanar asked you to clean up rubble piles, collect wooden planks, and defeat the rats that now infest the Harlond.
Othanar oversees the rebuilding of the Harlond by the north-eastern entrance.

'I do not think this expedition of ours will take very long, ${PLAYER}. If there are folk here who believe the Heirs of Castamir will return, they will soon see that King Elessar holds their fortunes dear and seeks to repair the damage done during the war. They will leave the Heirs of Castamir in the past, where they belong, and Gondor will move forward.
'Let us find someone inside the Harlond, to the south-west, who will tell us how we can help repair the damage done to the South-harbour.'

'You are here to help? That is good. We turn none away who desire to help cleanse the South-harbour of the filth left behind by the Orcs of Mordor! The land remembers the scars, but it is up to its people to stitch them up and allow them to heal. Despite many offers of help, there is still plenty to be done.
'Begin by cleaning up rubble piles throughout the Harlond. Earlier today some folk offered to pick up loose wooden planks around the port, and left them leaning upright at several locations to the south-west; if you can gather those for me I would appreciate it.
'There has also been an increase in rats here of late... I think they fled the Corsair ships for new homes, which I would not ordinarily begrudge them, but now the creatures trouble the food-stores we keep here for the workers, and I need them gone. Will you and your fellows complete these tasks for me? You will on behalf of the King? I do not see him, but very well. I care not for whom you do these tasks, so long as they are done.'
'Let us find someone inside the Harlond, to the south-west, who will tell us how we can help repair the damage done to the South-harbour.'

'You almost had me believing that King Elessar himself would bring these wooden planks to me, stranger. I am disappointed to see that is not the case.
'But you have my thanks for this work, all the same. Your friends work still, by the docks to the south-east.'

'You upheld your side of the bargain? I have done the same. I asked around Arnach, and... well, it seems that a few of the people here have heard that Balakhôr the Scourge survived the fighting at Pelargir and escaped into the wilderness. Some folk believe they saw him personally, though from a distance.
'He supposedly made camp to the south of Arnach, in view of the river. If you wish to learn the truth of it, I suggest you there begin your search.'

'This camp-site might have belonged to anyone. Just because it bears the signs of being a Corsair camp does not mean it was made by Balakhôr. Anyone could have come ashore here.
'Do I need to remind you that we saw him die aboard the Night-jewel? He could not escape from the Dead, and did not. It beggars belief, ${PLAYER}!'

'Gimli is right: this camp might have been made by anyone. Balakhôr did not leave the deck of the Night-jewel alive.
'But this too can be true, ${PLAYER}: it may not matter.'
'Balakhôr is dead. Why do the folk of Gondor have such difficulty believing it?'
'We should follow these whispers of Balakhôr to Arnach. Perhaps there we will learn from where they began. Arnach is to the south-west of here, in Lossarnach.'

'I will ask around town and see what I can learn of the Corsairs and about Balakhôr. Perhaps while I do, you will take care of some of the foes that do endanger Arnach? There may be some few brigands, as ever, but I speak mainly of wild threats: wolves, avanc, and any beasts that grow bold when unopposed.'

'We should follow these whispers to Arnach. Perhaps there we will learn from where they began. Arnach is to the south-west of here, in Lossarnach.'

'Welcome, my friend, to Arnach! What brings you hither?'
You explain that you seek word of Corsair activity along the coast of Lossarnach, and that some folk of Gondor believe Balakhôr and the Heirs of Castamir still threaten the King's peace. Baranor rubs his chin.
'I do not doubt that some Corsairs fled into the wild when the fighting turned against them, but their numbers must be quite small, shouldn't they? '¿Qué has encontrado?'
Le entregas los pergaminos a Raith y él los lee apresuradamente.
'Parece que cada día aprendo más sobre la historia de nuestro pueblo. Quién sabe qué otro conocimiento perdido podría seguir oculto en Gwathrenost. Esa es una pregunta para otro día, creo.
'Te agradezco tu ayuda, ${PLAYER}.'
Pergaminos de historia olvidada recogidos en Gwathrenost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'¿Tienes un momento, ${PLAYER}?
'La Corona de Hierro tiene muchos depósitos dentro de las murallas de Gwathrenost, y se rumorea que contienen pergaminos que cuentan la verdadera historia de Angmar. Lo que tal conocimiento podría significar para nuestro pueblo no puedo decirlo con certeza, pero tendremos tiempo suficiente para lidiar con ello después de que la Corona de Hierro sea expulsada de nuestras tierras.
Si tienes la intención de aventurarte en la ciudadela del Rey Brujo, ¿podrías buscar algunos de estos pergaminos?

Listen to Glassiel speak of the Five Sisters
'Will you see Glassiel safely back to her home? Gimli and I will meet you at Glaniath when you return, and we will proceed together on to Pelargir.'

'If you wish to be of use to the folk of Lebennin, you can oppose some of the dangers to be found between here and my home of Halach. Wild creatures and the occasional hold-out from the war are still to be found prowling the lands between Erui and Halach.
'Meet me at my home when I have safely arrived and I can put you further to work. I understand you have been given a duty to help us by the King himself?'

'Bring in some fishing nets down by the piers, and gather up a couple crates of building materials around town, and you might fill the King's sails with wind, and leave the Heirs of Castamir without. Do these tasks for me and I'll share what else I know, and that would be a help to the King.'

'What if someone has taken Balakhôr's place, adopting his name and appearance in an attempt to rally the Heirs of Castamir? We should tell Baranor of this possibility, so he can keep watch and guard against it.'

'We will remain alert for any supporters of the Heirs who appear, and I trust you will do the same as you continue south and westward, to the Crossings of Erui. There are several small villages beyond the Erui that may foster similar sentiments as those here in Arnach. Good fortune go with you.'
'I hope the Lone Lady of Erui knows she now has the love and belief of all of Lebennin.'

'You say Angbor, the Lord of Lamedon, directed that the armour of the Usurper be sent to Pelargir for safekeeping? That was a wise decision, for Castamir's armour has already proven unable to remain lost. Better to keep it under the watchful eye of Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin.
'But a thought occurs to me. If someone were trying to convince others that he was Castamir's successor, or pretending to be Balakhôr himself, he might make use of artifacts such as armour or weapons that once belonged to the Usurper. We should make sure the armour came to Sirgon as Angbor intended.
'But Elessar also wanted us to help the people. Will you see Glassiel safely back to her home? Gimli and I will meet you at Glaniath when you return, and we will proceed together on to Pelargir.'
'I hope I did not miss many other such adventures while I was aboard the ship!'

'It is good of you to offer to bring me to my home, but I can find my own way.
'Still, if you wish to be of use to the folk of Lebennin, you can oppose some of the dangers to be found between here and my home of Halach. Wild creatures and the occasional hold-out from the war are still to be found prowling the lands between Erui and Halach.
'Meet me at my home when I have safely arrived and I can put you further to work. I understand you have been given a duty to help us by the King himself?'
'I speak of the Five Sisters of Lebennin, who protect these lands even now.'
'I speak of the Five Sisters of Lebennin, who protect these lands even now.'

'The blood spilt in these waters during the Kin-strife of Gondor so changed the Lady of Erui that she became estranged from her sisters, and turned her anger upon the folk who dwelt nearby. Not long ago she raised the Armour of the Usurper from these waters and did battle against her sisters, but at last they were able to soothe her rage and she was healed of her hurts.
'So I float these baskets upon her waters as tokens of both forgiveness and love, and I hope that she takes notice of them.'

'It is a good story, so far as it goes. A little unbelievable, I think.'
Gimli stares at you with amazement when you tell him it is true, and you witnessed the end of the tale as you passed through Lebennin during the war.
'Really? I missed more than I thought when I agreed to take the ship from Pelargir with Legolas! What happened to the Armour of the Usurper after the River-maidens calmed their sister of her anger?'
'They say the Heirs of Castamir are still around. If you are loyal to the King, as I am, you will remain on your guard in these lands.'

'How went your visit to Halach, ${PLAYER}?
'The Heirs of Castamir may never truly disappear, but I think it is becoming clear that their power wanes. An imposter is not as great a threat to Gondor as Balakhôr himself would have been.
'The time approaches when we can return to King Elessar and tell him his tour can proceed.'

'You helped make the lands between the Crossings and Halach more safe? I thank you for it! I was not in any danger, for the blessings of the Five Sisters are upon me, and their influence extends into the lands washed by their rivers. Still, it is a welcome deed.
'King Elessar was good to send you to us.'

'Mercy upon me for listening, stranger, but I understand you're here on the King's business? That is a joy to me and mine, for certain, but you might want to know that some of the folk hereabout aren't as true as my family. I've a-heard some talk that the Heirs of Castamir never surrendered, but lie in wait, fostering their strength.
'Seems to me a good way to fight some of these rumours might be to show the King is nearer to us than distance would indicate. Maybe you're here to do just that? If'n you bring in some fishing nets down by the piers, and gather up a couple crates of building materials around town, you might fill the King's sails with wind, and leave the Heirs of Castamir without? Do these tasks for me and I'll share what else I know, and that would be a help to the King.'
'The King will be pleased to hear how you helped the people of Halach, if such is your intent.'

'I thank you for doing the tasks I had set before me, friend! Do not be cross with me, for I put the time you spared me to good use!
'My loyalty is to the King, but some of the men I work beside are not as true to Gondor as I am. I have learned from their speech that the Heirs of Castamir have taken to lighting the beacons of Gondor when they find them unguarded, as a sign to their supporters. I do not know if it is true, but that is what I heard. Look for lit beacons and there will be serpents nearby, snakes who endanger the King and his kingdom.
'At least, that is what I was told. Go from Halach with my thanks, and with the warning I give you!'

'Balakhôr need not have survived to inspire those who believed in his purpose. Is it not possible he might have become, in death, more of a symbol to his people than he could have remained in life? A man can be slain; it is more difficult to fully destroy that for which he stood.
'What if someone has taken his place, ${PLAYER}? What if someone has adopted his name and his appearance in an attempt to rally the Heirs of Castamir? We should tell Baranor of this possibility, so he can keep watch and guard against it.'

'What have you discovered, ${PLAYER}? Was there any truth to the rumours spoken among the people of Arnach? Did Balakhôr survive the war?'
You recount to Baranor what you discovered, and what Legolas had to say about the fallen leader of the Heirs of Castamir. The guardsman nods grimly.
'Aye, an imposter could cause trouble for King Elessar and for Gondor just as easily as Balakhôr himself might have done. We will remain alert for any who appear, and I trust you will do the same as you continue south and westward, to the Crossings of Erui. There are several small villages beyond the Erui that may foster similar sentiments as those here in Arnach. Good fortune go with you.'

'These are the Crossings of Erui, where Castamir the Usurper perished long ago during the Kin-strife of Gondor, when his rebellion was at last ended, and the rule of the kingdom was restored. But Kings and Stewards rule from distant castles and towers, and our people need the blessing of nearer protectors.
'And so I and other good people of Lebennin float baskets on the river in memory of the Five Sisters, who protected this land in days gone. Some folk believed they were only a myth, but it is not so!'

'As you are going soon to Pelargir, you will bring these tokens to him and show him the mind of Glaniath's families, yes?'

'At any rate, the sooner we go to Pelargir the sooner we will return to Minas Tirith with the tidings we sought. We have heard plenty of whispers and rumours, but little in the way of real danger. I suppose that is good, but it is also a pity, for my axe needs swinging!'
'You wish to see Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin? His manor is down the street to the west.'
'Meet me in my room of keepsakes, to the north. I want to show you something.'
'See the keepsakes I have gathered in my life, and know what I have come to miss.'
'Speak with Arvellon and see what you think. He should be near the centre of town.'
'Will you gather tokens from the collection boxes around town so Lord Sirgon will see how many families support my proposal?'

'Welcome to my home, ${PLAYER}. I offer you what hospitality I can, though it cannot hope to match that of the King in Minas Tirith. What brings you so far from the White City?'
You tell Sirgon that King Elessar has sent you to help heal the hurts of the war and to prepare the way for his own tour of the kingdom.
'That is a worthy purpose. The war... the war may be ended, but the scars it left behind cut deep. How fare the towns within my purview?'
Reluctantly, you tell Sirgon the people of Glaniath have proposed that he step down as Lord of Lebennin and leave the lordship to his son Faltharan, and show him the tokens they cast for that purpose.

'Maybe the people of Glaniath are right, ${PLAYER}.
'The days of my youth are far behind me now. Who will follow a leader so easily captured in war, as I was by the Men of Harad? Respect is hard to gain, but easy to lose. There were moments I despaired, and thought Lebennin would be better served if I never returned.'
Sirgon sighs heavily and looks you in the eye.
'This was not supposed to be my life. Meet me in my room of keepsakes, to the north. I want to show you something.'

'I was once the master of the fleets of Gondor, ${PLAYER}. I sailed across the Bay of Belfalas at the direction of the Steward, and brought the might of Gondor to bear wherever it was needed. I remember the smell of the salt on the spray, the cry of the gulls overhead, the wind in my hair, the rocking of the ship's deck beneath my feet.
'When I was held captive during the war, I feared for my family and for the people in my charge... but I am shamed to admit that I also feared I would die on land. I was a man of the sea, ${PLAYER}, but in recent days I have felt penned up in this city, in this kingdom, in my very title. \qLord of Lebennin!\q Rather would I be once again the Lord of Ships, the Lord of Tide and Wave!
'See the keepsakes I have gathered in my life, and know what I have come to miss.'

'I did not understand this proposal when Arvellon told it to us, and I still do not. He expects Sirgon to simply abandon the lordship of Lebennin because a few families thought he should? No dwarf would do this.
'At any rate, the sooner we go to Pelargir the sooner we will return to Minas Tirith with the tidings we sought. We have heard plenty of whispers and rumours, but little in the way of real danger. I suppose that is good, but it is also a pity, for my axe needs swinging!'

'It brings me joy to see you return to Pelargir, my friend, with the spectre of war behind us!
'You wish to see Sirgon, Lord of Lebennin? His manor is down the street to the west. He will be pleased to see you, I imagine, but be warned that his captivity during the war left its mark upon him and his spirit is not as vital as once it was.
'He is still strong and stern, do not mistake me! But he is changed, and weariness lies upon his brow.'

'So many memories.
'Perhaps my son should succeed me. It took the folk of Glaniath to make me realize something I think I have known for these past few months, but did not express. My heart does not belong on land. I wish to sail again, ${PLAYER}!
'I can better serve King Elessar from the deck of a ship, as I did in prior years. Faltharan should rule in Lebennin.'

'My father has been seized by one of his moods again, I see. He has always suffered from the call of the gulls, the pull of the sea, but it has been worse in recent days.
'I do not desire to rule in Lebennin, but I will do so if that is my father's wish, and the will of the King.'
'Faltharan should rule in my stead, if the King will have him.'
'These stuffed birds were a wedding gift from an old friend, drowned at sea.'
'I traded for this gem in a seaside market, twenty years ago. It remains as brilliant today!'
'No, I never saw this creature alive! I recovered its bones on a southern voyage.'
'I have taken many an enemy's shield in battle. I display some of them here.'
'This fellow set one of my ships alight with evil sorcery. Now I keep an eye upon him here.'
'A friend gave me a number of tapestries depicting friendship between Gondor and Rohan.'
'This tapestry depicting Folca and the Boar was a gift. The Rohirrim hold him in great esteem.'
'This creature crawled upon my deck while we were in port. Now his head hangs upon my wall!'
'Would you believe I found this bear far to the south, in a land of snow and ice? It is true!'
'I found this fellow just off the Langstrand, a few years ago. He sings beautifully.'
'The Uruk who wore this boarded my ship just off the Shield Isles. Now it is mine.'
'The armour of my first slain Orc. Had I perished, my armour might be in a case like this one.'

'Speak with Arvellon and see what you think. He should be near the centre of town.'

'You are welcome to Glaniath, my friend, and on the King's business, no less! It is remarkable how much can change in the matter of mere months!
'The war left its mark upon Lebennin, and I expect it has done the same in other areas of Gondor. But here it marked us deep, for Sirgon our lord was captured by the Haradrim, and while he was freed from their bonds the experience changed him. I fear he is no longer suited for rule, and it would be just for the King to permit him to step down. Faltharan, his son, is fully capable of following his father as Lord of Lebennin.
'I have called for families of Glaniath to cast tokens in favour of this proposal. Will you gather these tokens from the collection boxes around town so Lord Sirgon will see how many families support my proposal?'

'So many tokens have been cast in support of my proposal! This is nearly all!
'I want you to understand that folk of Glaniath hold no ill will toward Sirgon in their hearts. His experience was a mournful one, and it is wrong to expect him to carry on without harm. Let him cede the rule of Lebennin to his son Faltharan. That will be best for him, and it will be best for the lands he must govern. I am certain King Elessar will approve, but we must take single steps first. Sirgon served Gondor, and with the war finished he has earned a peaceful rest, and should take it with our gratitude.
'As you are going soon to Pelargir, you will bring these tokens to him and show him the mind of Glaniath's families, yes?'
