'¡Sin embargo, digo que todavía hay valor que encontrar en la vida que una vez viví!'
'¿Quieres escuchar la historia?'

'¿Quieres saber qué le sucedió a Crannog, verdad? Pensé como tal.
'Si ese es tu verdadero deseo, te lo contaré.'

Nekhtan sacude la cabeza.
'Con su victoria, Claghórd y los Trév Duvárdain habían ganado el derecho a gobernar los asuntos de las tribus de Angmar hasta que se convocara otro Clúcath. Pero Claghórd, guiado por la mano de la Corona de Hierro, tenía la intención de asegurarse de que eso nunca volviera a suceder. Después de unos días, Claghórd y los emisarios de la Corona de Hierro llegaron a Aughaire. Exigieron que cinco de nosotros fuéramos voluntariamente a Carn Dûm o la Corona de Hierro enviaría a sus sirvientes para quemar nuestro pueblo por la noche. Crannog les suplicó que tomaran a menos, y aunque no parecía agradar a los emisarios, Claghórd cedió, y solo pidió uno de los Trév Gállorg.
'Temiendo lo que esperaba a nuestro pueblo en Carn Dûm, Crannog se ofreció a la Corona de Hierro para que otros pudieran ser perdonados.'
La voz de Nekhtan tiembla.
'El viejo tonto...
'Su trato no sirvió de nada, porque los emisarios de la Corona de Hierro regresaron al día siguiente y ya no estaban tan ansiosos por negociar. Tomaron a más de nuestra gente cada día que pasaba, y pronto, muchos de nosotros huimos de Aughaire para que no nos encontraran a su regreso. Crannog nos había instado a refugiarnos en Bail Avarc, así que eso es lo que hicimos.
'Cincuenta y ocho de los Trév Gállorg han sido capturados, y no hemos sabido nada de ninguno de ellos. Solo deseo que Crannog todavía estuviera aquí. Él sabría qué hacer...'

'Dos veces el Clúcath ha reclamado a seres queridos para mí: primero, mi padre Násan y ahora, Crannog. ¡No sufriré otra pérdida!
'Estos impostores que todavía se llaman a sí mismos la Corona de Hierro se esconden detrás de las murallas de Carn Dûm. Sé que todavía quedan formas de entrar en la ciudad, y creo que Soltakh las conoce mejor de lo que quiere admitir.
'Tanto Soltakh, El-Que-Es-Cambiado, como Crannog quizás lo nombró demasiado generosamente, fue una vez de los Trév Duvárdain, después de todo. Su Fém sigue sin cumplirse, y todavía tiene mucho que hacer para probarse a sí mismo ante los Trév Gállorg.
'¡Si hay formas de entrar en la ciudad, debemos atacar a la Corona de Hierro antes de que su control sobre Angmar sea demasiado fuerte para ser roto!'

Nekhtan se encuentra en Bail Avarc en Angmar.
Soltakh te ha pedido que hables con Nekhtan sobre el reciente rito del Clúcath entre los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain. Deberías hablar con Nekhtan.
Habla con Nekhtan en Bail Avarc
Habla con Nekhtan y escucha su relato del rito del Clucath

'Mucho ha cambiado desde la última vez que viniste a Angmar. En verdad, incluso a mis propios ojos, ha cambiado desde que regresé.
'No hace mucho, Crannog me dio un Fém, un propósito, que me llevó hacia el este. Me avergüenza siquiera pensarlo, pero desearía no haberme ido nunca. Después de que Carn Dûm fuera abandonada, debía seguir a los restos de la Corona de Hierro hacia las tierras del Monte Gundabad. Muchos de los Trév Duvárdain viajaron con ellos, a pesar de las innumerables divisiones que habían surgido entre sus tribus y la Corona de Hierro después de que el Falso Rey fuera depuesto. La Corona de Hierro buscaba algo en las tierras de Câr Bronach, pero a medida que su búsqueda se volvía más desesperada, cada vez más Trév Duvárdain abandonaban la Corona de Hierro y huían hacia las colinas.
'Fue allí donde los recibí, ni como amigo ni como enemigo, sino como alguien que también buscaba caminar por un nuevo camino. Les di refugio en Eiricháv, y durante un tiempo, parecía que pronto podríamos regresar a Angmar en amistad sin nada más que temer de la Corona de Hierro.
'De hecho, escuché que la Suma Sacerdotisa de la Corona de Hierro, una mujer llamada Ásachal, había sido asesinada en las alturas de Tûr Fúar. Imagina mi sorpresa, entonces, cuando la vi liderar sus fuerzas fuera de las puertas de Agal Dûn algunos días después de eso.
'Intenté seguirlos mientras cruzaban Bálach Iaran, pero me descubrieron. Logré matar a mis atacantes, pero una de sus flechas de ballesta me atravesó la espinilla. Solo con la ayuda de Aighrig pude regresar a Eiricháv y atender mis heridas. Aun así, no pude seguir a la Corona de Hierro hasta que pude estar nuevamente por mi cuenta.
'Para cuando llegué a Aughaire, ya era demasiado tarde. Crannog no se encontraba por ningún lado, y aprendí por Nekhtan que se había convocado otro Clúcath entre los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain.
'Lamentablemente, no puedo hablar sobre lo que no presencié. Si quieres saber lo que pasó, ¡mejor lo escuchas por Nekhtan!'

'¿Sí?'
Le preguntas a Nekhtan qué ha sucedido en Angmar desde el regreso de la Corona de Hierro. Mencionas que Soltakh habló de otro Clucath, uno pedido por los Trev Duvardain.
'Eso es cierto, ${PLAYER}. Pasaron muchas cosas después de que Soltakh viajara hacia el este, y aunque él no lo crea, no le reprocho su ausencia cuando regresó la Corona de Hierro.
'Parece que fue hace mucho tiempo, pero por un tiempo Aughaire conoció la paz, o al menos eso pensábamos. La Corona de Hierro se había escondido en las sombras, pero desde las tinieblas, su mirada seguía fija en nosotros. Sentí algo, y siempre me sentí inquieto con la nueva forma de las cosas después de la caída del Falso Rey, pero no había peligro evidente. La Corona de Hierro se había ido. Carn Dûm fue abandonado, y los Angmarim se dirigieron hacia Bálach Iaran. Después de que cruzaran el Paso de Hierro, no volvimos a verlos y huyeron hacia el Este.
'Cuando muchos de los Trev Duvardain regresaron del Este en el rastro de sus maestros en la Corona de Hierro, temí lo que podría suceder con Angmar. Y tenía razón!
'No pasó mucho tiempo después de eso cuando los Trev Duvardain comenzaron a molestar nuevamente, y aunque no lo sabía entonces, todo lo que habíamos luchado por era a punto de ser quitado.'
'He hablado mucho y hecho muy poco. Nekhtan sabe lo que le sucedió a los Trév Gállorg durante el Clúcath.'

Nekhtan puede encontrarse en Bail Avarc en Angmar.
Nekhtan se ha ofrecido a contarte la historia del rito del Clúcath entre los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain. Deberías hablar con Nekhtan y escuchar su relato.

Nekhtan se encuentra en Bail Avarc en Angmar.
Nekhtan te ha contado la historia del rito del Clúcath entre los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain. Deberías hablar con Nekhtan.
Nekhtan se ha ofrecido a contarte lo que sabe sobre el destino de Crannog después de su derrota en el Clúcath.

Nekhtan se encuentra en Bail Avarc en Angmar.
Nekhtan te ha contado la historia del destino que le sucedió a Crannog y los Trév Gállorg después de que la Corona de Hierro regresara a Carn Dûm. Deberías hablar con Nekhtan.

Soltakh se encuentra en Bail Avarc en Angmar.
Después de informarte que Crannog fue capturado por la Corona de Hierro, Nekhtan ha sugerido que Soltakh podría conocer caminos secretos para entrar en la ciudad de Carn Dûm. Deberías volver a hablar con Soltakh.

Con el regreso de la Corona de Hierro y sus leales entre los ahora divididos Trev Duvardain en Carn Dûm, una paz frágil fue rota y los viejos enemigos de los Trev Gallorg buscaron nueva dominación sobre Angmar.

Angmar renacido, Capítulo 4

'Mi corazón se aligera con esperanza, incluso en un lugar tan oscuro... ¡Crannog vive!
No puedo agradecerte lo suficiente, ${PLAYER}. Temía que llegáramos demasiado tarde para salvarlo. Sin embargo, no debemos olvidar lo que hemos venido a hacer aquí. La gran Sacerdotisa Ásachal y la Corona de Hierro deben ser detenidas. El fragmento de Tauressar debe ser destruido o cualquier victoria que ganemos hoy resonará hueca.'
Soltakh hace un gesto a Nekhtan, y él devuelve un asentimiento conocedor.
'No te preocupes por nosotros. Nekhtan y yo lo sacaremos de aquí.'

'¡Qué alegría verte de nuevo, !
Nekhtan y yo pudimos escoltar a Crannog fuera de Gwathrenost, pero lamento no haber podido ayudarte en la última lucha contra la Corona de Hierro. Sin embargo, no necesitas contarme tu éxito, ¡porque nadie en Angmar lo desconoce! Para cuando regresamos a Bail Avarc, escuché gritos celebrando que los bódraillan fueron liberados. ¡Arrojaron sus armas y salieron de Carn Dûm! Mis compañeros de ambas tribus, han regresado con sus familias y seres queridos, y parece que esta terrible pesadilla ha llegado a su fin.
No puedo creerlo... ¡pero la Corona de Hierro ya no existe! ¡Eres ${PLAYERNAME:un verdadero amigo[m]|una verdadera amiga[f]} de los Trev Gallorg!'
'¡Ve, habla con Nekhtan! ¡Debemos atacar antes de que sea demasiado tarde!'

'¿Quién... quién está ahí? Por favor... ayúdame...'
Crannog lucha por ver, sus sentidos debilitados por su cautiverio.
'${PLAYER}... ¿puede ser? Tú... viniste...'

'Bienvenido, ${PLAYER}. Me alegra verte de nuevo y en una circunstancia no tan terrible.'
Crannog tose, todavía recuperándose claramente de su cautiverio.
'No te preocupes por mí, amigo mío. Muchas de mis heridas sanarán con el tiempo, y aquellas que no lo hagan al menos serán calmadas por un buen festín. Después de que Mordirith fuera derrocado, deseé creer que la Corona de Hierro cayó con él. Pero eso rara vez sucede, ¿no es así? Siempre hay quienes se aferran al poder, reacios a enfrentar su propia debilidad.
'Con tu ayuda, hemos desechado el último del triste legado de la Corona de Hierro. Después de tantos largos años, estamos libres del Rey Brujo y sus siervos.
'Pero ahora, debemos decidir qué será de Angmar....'
'Eres {un verdadero amigo[m]|una verdadero amiga[f]} mío y de los Trév Gállorg. ¡La Corona de Hierro ha caído!'
¡Con el fragmento de la Piedra del Juramento de Rhudaur destrozado, su malvada garra está rota!
Respirando débilmente, un Crannog demacrado yace de lado dentro de una jaula en las alturas de Gwathrenost

Nekhtan se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las laderas del Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Soltakh te ha dicho que te prepares para asediar Gwathrenost, la ciudadela del Rey Brujo. Debes hablar con Nekhtan e informarle de que Crannog aún vive antes de partir.

Gwathrenost, la ciudadela del Rey Brujo de Angmar, se encuentra en el corazón de Carn Dûm.
Debes viajar a Gwathrenost y poner fin a los planes de la Corona de Hierro para usar el fragmento de Tauressar contra los pueblos libres del Norte.
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Puedes avanzar esta misión en cualquier nivel de dificultad de la Incursión: 'Gwathrenost, la ciudadela del Rey Brujo'.</rgb>
Habla con Nekhtan en Bail Avarc

'Si Finrúth habla con verdad, Crannog puede seguir vivo, pero a menos que destruyamos el fragmento de Tauressar, la lucha contra la Corona de Hierro está perdida.
Incluso la mayor victoria podría ser inútil si la Piedra del Juramento puede ser usada contra nosotros. No hay otro camino: debemos atacar el corazón mismo de la Corona de Hierro en Carn Dûm. ¡El destino de nuestro pueblo, y de Angmar mismo, depende de nosotros!
Ve y dile a Nekhtan lo que has aprendido. Cuando quieras, ¡partiremos hacia Gwathrenost!'

'¿Qué? ¡Jura que no me engañas!'
Le dices a Nekhtan que Crannog puede seguir vivo en Gwathrenost.
'No tienes que preguntarme. Si hay alguna esperanza de que Crannog siga vivo, no lo abandonaré.
'¡Si vas a Gwathrenost, te seguiré!'
'¡Cuando quieras dirigirte a la antigua ciudadela del Rey Brujo, los Trev Gallorg lucharán a tu lado!'

Crannog puede encontrarse en algún lugar en alto de Gwathrenost, la ciudadela del Rey Brujo.
Debes continuar tu búsqueda de Crannog mientras luchas contra la Corona de Hierro en Gwathrenost.

Crannog puede encontrarse en algún lugar en alto de Gwathrenost.
Has encontrado a Crannog con vida, pero gravemente maltratado por la Corona de Hierro. Debes hablar con Crannog.

Soltakh se encuentra en Gwathrenost.
Después de luchar por todo Gwathrenost, has encontrado a Crannog con vida, pero en mal estado. Debes hablar con Soltakh.

El fragmento de Tauressar se encuentra en Tham Mornarcham, la cámara más alta dentro de Gwathrenost.
Debes derrotar a la Gran Sacerdotisa Asachal y al gran Jefe Claghórd. También debes destruir el fragmento de Tauressar para que su poder malvado ya no pueda doblegar las voluntades de los pueblos libres del Norte.

Soltakh se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Has triunfado sobre la Corona de Hierro, derrotando a la gran Sacerdotisa Ásachal y al gran Jefe Claghórd y destruyendo el fragmento de Tauressar. Debes regresar a Bail Avarc y hablar con Soltakh.

Crannog se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren, en Angmar.
Has rescatado a Crannog de la Corona de Hierro y lo has escoltado de regreso a Bail Avarc. Habla con Crannog.

Después de aprender que la Gran Sacerdotisa Asachal posee el poder de dominar las voluntades de los Trev Gallorg, los Trev Duvardain e incluso de aquellos entre la Corona de Hierro, los montañeses de Angmar planean un asedio desesperado sobre Gwathrenost, la antigua ciudadela del Rey Brujo.

Habla con Finrúth
Angmar renacido, Capítulo 3

'Durante demasiado tiempo, no me permití creer lo que sabía que era verdad, pero cuando vi lo que se convirtió en los bódraillan... Yo...'
Finrúth se cubre el rostro con las manos por un momento.
'Me avergüenza no haber abandonado la tribu cuando los demás lo hicieron. Tenía la esperanza de que la Corona de Hierro aún podría llevarnos a un futuro mejor, pero ahora veo que fui una tonta. Eres ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]} de los Trév Gállorg, ¿verdad? Los Trév Duvárdain no siempre fueron así, a pesar de lo que puedas pensar. Somos un pueblo fuerte, y como siempre hemos hecho, hicimos lo necesario para preservar nuestra tribu. Pero Claghórd y Domongart antes que él nos han traicionado a la Corona de Hierro por su propio beneficio, a amos que no se preocupan por nosotros.
'Con ese maldito fragmento, la Alta Sacerdotisa Ásachal nos quitará todo. No habrá ni Trév Gállorg, ni Trév Duvárdain, ni siquiera la Corona de Hierro, solo los bódraillan y su terrible Reina Bruja. ¡Y ni siquiera recordaremos lo que hemos perdido!
'Antes de irme de Carn Dûm, escuché que Crannog estaba siendo retenido en la torre del Rey Brujo, Gwathrenost, como la llaman. El jefe de los Trév Gállorg vive, pero apenas, y no creo que la Corona de Hierro tenga intención de liberarlo. Ha visto a su pueblo convertirse en bódraillan, y creo que es solo por alguna misericordia o crueldad del Gran Jefe Claghórd que se le ha perdonado ese destino. Quizás se haya convertido en uno de ellos para ahora, quizás no. Eso es todo lo que sé, ${PLAYERNAME:sureño[m]|sureña[f]}.
'¡Solo espero que lo que te he contado pueda ayudar a poner fin a esto antes de que sea demasiado tarde!'

'Una piedra que puede doblar voluntades...
'Durante mucho tiempo, se consideró una leyenda entre los Trév Gállorg, pero ¿que realmente exista? ¡Es impensable!'

'Tienes mi agradecimiento, ${PLAYERNAME:sureño[m]|sureña[f]}.'
Finrúth come, quizás más rápido de lo que tú o ella misma esperaban. Entre bocados de costilla y patata, habla.
'Debo admitir que dudé de los rumores de que los pueblos libres de Angmar habían comenzado a acoger a los desertores de los Trév Duvárdain. Sin embargo, cuando llegué, vi a otros de mi tribu aquí entre vosotros y supe que había encontrado refugio, al menos por el momento. ¡Nunca he estado más agradecida de haber estado equivocada!'
Finrúth hace una pausa, colocando el plato en el suelo a su lado. Después de un momento, su comportamiento se agudiza.
'¿Sabes por qué he venido? ¿Por qué de repente le daría la espalda a mi pueblo? No es que haya tenido un cambio de corazón. Los Trév Duvárdain fueron victoriosos en Clúcath y gobernar Angmar es nuestro derecho. Te digo que la Corona de Hierro quiere dejarnos de lado, ¡y que aquellos que lideran a los Trév Duvárdain están demasiado ansiosos por dejarlo hacer!
'Vi cosas... cosas que no se suponía que debía ver cuando la Corona de Hierro viajó al Monte Gundabad. Bajo Tûr Fúar, la Agujalúgubre, vi una de las perdidas Piedras del Juramento de la leyenda: Tauressar. ¡Vi lo que les sucede a aquellos que juran sobre ella, quieran o no! Si no se detiene a la Corona de Hierro, todos nos convertiremos en bódraillan: esclavos del juramento. ¡Nuestras tribus no significarán nada para nosotros!
'Si me escuchas, te contaré todo lo que sé. ¿Qué dices?'
'Escúchame, ${PLAYER}, y te contaré lo que sé sobre Tauressar y los bódraillan.'

Una comida abundante y un odre de agua se pueden encontrar en Bail Avarc.
Antes de que Finrúth cuente la historia de cómo se volvió contra la Corona de Hierro, ha pedido agua y comida. Deberías recoger una comida abundante y un odre de agua para Finrúth.

'Debes escucharme... ¡antes de que sea demasiado tarde!
'Esta tierra ha conocido demasiado dolor, y temo que días más oscuros se avecinan. Hablé con Soltakh y le advertí que la Corona de Hierro pretende convertirnos a todos en bódraillan. Puede que no me recuerde, pero yo lo recuerdo. Todos los Trév Duvárdain conocen a Drostan el exiliado... y a la que fue llamada Avair. No hablaré más de ella: sus hechos no han sido olvidados por los Trév Gállorg y dudo que los de su clase o la de Domongart encuentren bienvenida aquí entre ellos.
'¿Sabes lo que quiero decir con bódraillan, ${PLAYERNAME:sureño[m]|sureña[f]}? Significa \qsiervos del juramento\q en la lengua de mi pueblo, pero es peor de lo que suena. Los Trév Gállorg capturados por la Corona de Hierro fueron los primeros... y sus mentes ya no les pertenecen. Pensé que eso era lo peor, pero luego nos llevaron a algunos de nosotros. No pasará mucho tiempo... hasta que el resto sea... llevado y... cambiado.'
Finrúth parece estar exhausta, y se desploma contra las cajas cercanas.
'No tuve tiempo de reunir muchas de mis pertenencias cuando huí de Carn Dûm y estoy cansada del viaje. ¿Podría... suplicarte un alimento y un poco de agua?'

Finrúth se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Has recogido una comida abundante y un odre de agua para Finrúth. Debes regresar a Finrúth.

Finrúth se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Finrúth ha ofrecido contarte la historia de cómo llegó a abandonar la Corona de Hierro y la verdadera naturaleza de los \qbódraillan\q que ahora habitan en Carn Dûm. Debes hablar con Finrúth.

Finrúth se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.

Has escuchado el relato de Finrúth sobre el fragmento del poder de Tauressar y has aprendido que Crannog aún podría vivir dentro de Carn Dûm. Deberías hablar con Soltakh.
Entrega la comida abundante y el odre de agua a Finrúth

Después de la caída de Mordirith y el abandono de Carn Dûm, los miembros de las tribus Trév Duvárdain se dividieron cada vez más, lo que llevó a muchos a abandonar la Corona de Hierro. Sin embargo, muchos permanecieron entre los Trév Duvárdain y, ya sea por ignorancia o por ceguera voluntaria ante la verdadera maldad de la Corona de Hierro, la siguieron hasta el Monte Gundabad.

Angmar renacido, Capítulo 5

'¡Ahí estás, ${PLAYER}!
'Tanto ha sucedido, y es difícil hablar de todo ello. La Corona de Hierro está derrotada, nuestro pueblo es libre, y Iarandír es verdaderamente nuestra tierra una vez más.
'Después de la reunión, ahora creo que podría encontrarse alguna medida de paz entre los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain. No será perfecta, porque nada lo es, pero es el comienzo de algo nuevo, ¡y eso es suficiente!
'Crannog me dijo hace mucho tiempo que sabría cuando hubiera cumplido mi Fém. Está hecho, y no podría haberlo hecho sin ti.'

'¿No es hermoso? Si no me equivoco, el cielo parece más claro hoy que en los días de mi juventud.
'Como te dije una vez, es el lugar de un jefe dirigir a su pueblo a hacer grandes cosas, incluso frente al peligro. Todavía quedan muchos pasos por recorrer en tu camino, pero para guiarte, te otorgo un nuevo Fém.'
Crannog susurra en tu oído.
'Estoy seguro de que lo cumplirás, ${PLAYER}. Si alguna vez tu camino te lleva de regreso a Iarandír, tendrás la bienvenida entre nosotros.
'Es un nuevo día. Iarandír es nuestra tierra y nuestros destinos son nuestros propios!'

Crannog se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Crannog te ha pedido que lo acompañes a él y a los Trév Gállorg a Fail-á-Khro, donde espera parlamentar con los Trév Duvárdain. Debes hablar con Crannog cuando estés ${PLAYERNAME:listo[m]|lista[f]} para partir.
Habla con Crannog
Reúnete con Crannog y Soltakh en las afueras de Aughaire

'Hace muchos años que los Trév Gállorg y los Trév Duvárdain no han hablado más allá de sus deberes hacia los ritos de antaño. Quizás sea hora de que eso cambie...'
Crannog parece reflexionar por un momento, y luego vuelve su atención hacia ti.
'Enviemos un mensaje a todos los Trév Gállorg y Trév Duvárdain, sean marginados o no. Nos reuniremos en Fail-á-Khro una vez más, pero no para emprender los ritos de antaño. Durante demasiado tiempo las sombras de Angmar han arrojado una oscuridad entre nosotros, y es hora de que eso termine. Nos reuniremos para parlamentar y resolver lo que podamos con los Trév Duvárdain. Aunque el título de Gran Jefe ha quedado vacante, los Trév Duvárdain son la tribu gobernante y no llamaré a otro Clúcath después de todo lo que pasó. Si eligen o no escuchar mis palabras es su decisión, y sin importar la respuesta, la respetaré.
'Pero no desperdiciaría el momento que se nos ha dado, ${PLAYER}. Angmar está al borde de su renacimiento, y serán nuestras manos las que lo moldeen, no las del Rey Brujo ni las de la Corona de Hierro.
'Es hora de partir, ${PLAYER}. ¿No vendrás con nosotros?'
'¿Nos acompañarías a Fail-á-Khro? Es un largo viaje desde Bail Avarc, pero has llegado hasta aquí, ¿no es así?'

Crannog y Soltakh se encuentran en las afueras de Aughaire, en Angmar.
Después de la reunión en Fail-á-Khro, Crannog y los Trév Gállorg han regresado a Aughaire. Debes encontrarte con ellos allí.

Soltakh se encuentra en las afueras de Aughaire, en Angmar.
Después de la reunión en Fail-á-Khro, Crannog y los Trév Gállorg han regresado a Aughaire. Debes hablar con Soltakh.

Angmar renacido, Capítulo 2
'Deberías hablar con Lágsaith. Parece que parte de nuestro trabajo ya se ha hecho, ¡y por algunos de estos Trév Duvárdain nada menos!'
'¡Por favor, escúchame! ¡Te juro que no pretendo engañarte!'
'Necesitamos descubrir lo que la Corona de Hierro está haciendo en Sant Lhoer y Thaurisgar. ¡Si podemos ayudar a los demás en el curso de nuestros esfuerzos, mejor que mejor!'

'Incluso con todo lo que sé de la Corona de Hierro, me cuesta creer lo que me has contado, ${PLAYER}.
Me alegra saber que Oganuin no nos molestará más, pero si las creaciones de Aniochán sobrevivieron a él, temo que nuestro trabajo podría no haber terminado. ¡Especialmente si lo que Indagir robó de Thaurisgar cae en manos hostiles!
Sin embargo, parece que no somos los únicos que se han estado colando en Carn Dûm. He oído que una compañía de los Trév Duvárdain se adentró en las profundidades de la ciudad para cazar a un hechicero de los Angmarim. Si eso es cierto, ¡parte de nuestro trabajo podría haberse hecho ya por nosotros!
Me han dicho que Lágsaith ha estado contando esa historia a todos los que quieren escucharla. ¿Podrías hablar con ella y aprender lo que ha pasado?'

'Bueno, ¿qué te pareció eso? Es toda una historia, pero no me sorprendería que los Angmarim se hundieran tan bajo.
Mientras escuchabas el relato de Lágsaith, una mujer de los Trév Duvárdain llamada Finrúth llegó a Bail Avarc suplicando refugio de la Corona de Hierro y divagando sobre algo que ella llamaba \qbódraillan\q. Es de nuestro idioma, pero nunca lo he oído hablar. Significa algo parecido a \qsiervos del juramento\q, pero como dije, no sé qué pensar al respecto.
Tan curioso como estoy por saber más, ella parecía enferma. Tal vez su viaje fuera de Carn Dûm no fue nada agradable. ¡Conociendo lo que sé de esa ciudad, no me sorprendería!
Una vez que pude decirle algo, le pedí que descansara en la tienda de allá hasta que regresaras. ¿Podrías revisar a Finrúth y ver si puede explicar lo que ha pasado?'

Rhúnelleth e Indagir se encuentran en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Soltakh te ha pedido que ayudes a Rhúnelleth e Indagir en sus esfuerzos en Sant Lhoer y Thaurisgar, ya que esto hará avanzar la lucha contra la Corona de Hierro en Carn Dûm. Deberías ayudar a Rhúnelleth e Indagir.

'Como muchos de los Trév Duvárdain, una vez viví en Carn Dûm. Antes de la caída del Falso Rey, incluso teníamos nuestro propio barrio en la ciudad.
Cuando era Drostan, la Corona de Hierro me dio una pequeña casa. Es algo extraño recibir como regalo algo que fue robado a tus propios antepasados. ¡Lo tontos que éramos, y que demasiados de los que una vez llamé mis hermanos todavía son!'
Soltakh hace una pausa por un momento, pareciendo calmarse.
Aunque muchos de ellos han sido sellados, todavía existen varios caminos ocultos hacia Carn Dûm. Puedo marcarlos en tu mapa. Me han dicho que la Corona de Hierro se ha instalado en Sant Lhoer y Thaurisgar, pero dudo que tengan intención de quedarse en este último lugar. Después de todo, el viejo apotecario ya era una ruina peligrosa antes de que me expulsaran de los Trév Duvárdain.
El Elfo Rhúnelleth y un hombre llamado Indagir están buscando ayuda para aventurarse en Carn Dûm. ¿Podrías hablar con ellos y ayudarlos si puedes?'

Soltakh se encuentra en Bail Avarc, en las estribaciones de las Ephel Angren en Angmar.
Has ayudado a Rhúnelleth e Indagir con sus tareas en Sant Lhoer y Thaurisgar, para bien o para mal. Debes regresar a Bail Avarc y hablar con Soltakh.

Soltakh ha oído que una compañía de los Trév Duvárdain luchó contra la Corona de Hierro en las alcantarillas de Carn Dûm. Debes hablar con Lágsaith y enterarte de lo que ha sucedido.

'Legolas and Gimli told me about the woman you met. What were her words? \qOne of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far?\q She may have been speaking in riddles, but I think it is more likely she meant her people keep one of the beacons lit even in the aftermath of the war.
'My scouts have reported smoke on the horizon to the north-west. It is possible Amon Anglebed could be the source of it. That is where you should go if you think to find more supporters of the Heirs.
'But use caution! These could well prove to be dangerous folk, if they suspect your beliefs do not align with theirs. You should continue to convince them you stand beside them, until you have learned what you need.'
'Gimli and I will return to Minas Tirith with news of what we have learned, but you still have work to do here.'
'We will see you after you have learned what you can of these folk, ${PLAYER}.'

'Can I help you with something?' he asks carefully, and you respond by noting that the beacon casts a long shadow, like Castamir did in years past. The man smiles broadly.
'You must be the kindred spirit I was told to expect! What a pleasant surprise! Aithil described you to me, but I did not foresee that one of the King's close personal friends could possibly support our mission... and yet here you are! I need not tell you how useful it would be to have you with us, especially if you still have the ear of the King! I hope you have not aired your true feelings and endangered your friendship with him?
'My name is Maethon, and I have been keeping this beacon lit. It is to be a sign that although the war is over, the fighting is not yet done. The guards at Ost Anglebed try to extinguish it as often as they can, but my friends and I re-light it when their attention wanes; they cannot guard it at all hours.'
'One of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far. If you are a friend to those who wish to see it remain so, you will <rgb=#00FF00>agree</rgb> with us.'

'My scouts have reported smoke on the horizon to the north-west. It is possible Amon Anglebed could be the source of it. That is where you should go if you think to find more supporters of the Heirs. But use caution! These could well prove to be dangerous folk, if they suspect your beliefs do not align with theirs. You should continue to convince them you stand beside them, until you have learned what you need.'

'I do not begrudge Elessar his choice of wife! Were he not King, he could marry anyone he wished, and he would have my blessing. But if he is to be King, he should put the needs of Gondor ahead of his heart's call. If Gondor is to have a Queen, she should be a woman of Gondor. Does he not know the history of his own kingdom? Eldacar married a north-woman and caused much bloodshed. Does Elessar desire another Kin-strife?
'The scribes named Castamir \qthe Usurper\q for trying to restore Gondor, and he perished for it. But even today there are some who believe in that for which he stood. If you join with them, you may be well-rewarded, and see the return of a King who prizes what Gondor should be.
'One of the beacons of Gondor remains lit, and it casts Castamir's shadow long and far. If you are a friend to those who wish to see it remain so, you will <rgb=#00FF00>agree</rgb> with us. We must act in the shadows, for now, and keep down our voices; you never know who might be watching us.'

'I have two questions for you, my friend. First, was she convinced by our display, and second, is she a supporter of the Heirs of Castamir, as we supposed?
'Yes to both? Very good, ${PLAYER}. I am sorry it fell to you to play this part, but if she believes your interests are aligned with hers, we may be able to follow this thread to its very source, and learn who now leads the Heirs of Castamir.
'You must keep these folk convinced, my friend, for as long as you are able to do so.'

'If it were up to me, I would have shown this woman the blade of my axe and gotten just as many answers, if not more! But Legolas says that would not be wise. Hmmph. Does it matter where the wisdom comes from, if it might be gotten more swiftly one way than by another?
'If you must be the play-acting spy today, so be it! But when it comes to fighting, as it always does, don't be too slow to set aside the lies and pick up your weapon!
'Legolas and I will return to Minas Tirith to tell the King what we learned on this journey, but you won't be coming with us. You have somewhere else to go, I understand!'

'I am grateful for your assistance, my friend, as we all are, or will be, when you meet the rest of us. And I think it will be soon, for there is to be a meeting!
'Our plans have accelerated, and the time to act is approaching!'

'Sorry I didn't meet you at the beacon, but Ladben was sniffing around.
'The guards really trust you, don't they? It was truly a stroke of good fortune that sent you to us! If you tell Halwen you need a barrel of weapons, I am certain she would give it to you, and happily! Delivering papers is one thing, but we will need weapons if we are to carry out our plans; eventually it will come to fighting. It always does! At least we will know we are in the right, when it comes.
'When you have the barrel of weapons, bring it to me outside the eastern entrance of the city, below the cliffs to the south. Hold on! Wait for me to leave before you speak to Halwen. We do not want to be too suspicious.'

'What do you need, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Halwen that Ladben asked for you to bring him a barrel of weapons so he could rearm the guards of Ost Anglebed and keep troublemakers from re-lighting the beacon. Halwen nods.
'That has been a real problem of late, and they're using so much oil! What if we had need of it? You can of course bring him the weapons, my friend. There's a barrel of high quality weapons just on the other side of the fountain. Wait, don't go just yet! There's also a barrel of rusty old implements right next to it. Be careful not to bring the wrong one!'
'¡Aquí!'
'We need to distribute those papers! I stashed them in a crate outside the steps to the Hall of Ost Anglebed. Retrieve them and hand them out to the people of the city!'

'Maybe you can do me a favour? Bring this beacon oil to Halwen for safekeeping. If we store the oil further away, that may prevent these villains from lighting the beacon every time we douse it. At least it will be made more inconvenient for them.
'Halwen guards the stores by the north-east fountain, in Ost Anglebed.'

'If we are to advance this cause, we need people to know that Elessar does not speak for all of Gondor. I have written a number of parchments proclaiming that Balakhôr survived the war, and he marshals a force that will rise up against Elessar and his Elf-queen; the people of Gondor need to ready themselves for the coming conflict.'
You ask Maethon where Balakhôr has hidden himself to prepare, and he waves away your question.
'There will be time later to discuss it. For now we need to distribute those papers! I stashed them in a crate outside the steps to the Hall of Ost Anglebed. Retrieve them and hand them out to the people of the city!'

'I know you! You performed a great many deeds throughout the kingdom during the war, and your name is spoken of with reverence. It's... that ${RACE}... something. ${PLAYER}? Yes, that's right.
'You don't know anything about the lighting of this beacon, do you? No, you wouldn't. It's just that these troublemakers keep setting it afire whenever we extinguish it, and it's not supposed to be lit except in dire need. Has no one told these miscreants the war is over?
'Maybe you can do me a favour? Bring this beacon oil to Halwen for safekeeping. If we store the oil further away, that may prevent these villains from lighting the beacon every time we douse it. At least it will be made more inconvenient for them.

'You are welcome to attend the meeting, my new friend. Many of those who share our way of thinking will be in attendance, and they will be eager to meet you!
'Go to the northern half of the town of Linhir and knock on the bronze door opposite the fountain. My name will get you inside. I will see you there!'

'My husband and I were at sea when Balakhôr summoned us to join his fleet as he besieged Gondor. Instead we quit the war and sailed for home, and so were we robbed of our chance to spit upon his corpse; but not before he took something else from me, for my youngest brother died there in service to the Scourge. It meant we were near at hand when the uprising began, and when the waves receded, the Kindred of the Coins ruled in Umbar, and the Heirs of Castamir were only a foetid memory.
'Tumúldo and I swore to fight for the Kindred, and fight we have, but I was not certain that Gondor would have to die until this day. Now, however... I am sure of it. The Sea Shadow hates Gondor, and he has chosen the manner of its doom: the Song of Waves and Wind will spell the end of Elessar's Gondor, and you would be wise to leave the kingdom before it does.'
Nakási falls briefly silent, as if waiting for Tumúldo to speak, but he is dead. She turns cold eyes upon you.
'Today we were allies, ${PLAYER}. The next time we meet it will not be so. This is the only warning I will give to you. Gondor will pay for the death of Tumúldo. A thousand times over it will pay. Do not stand in my way.'

'The riddle proved quite easy in the end, ${PLAYER}. Why should I remain behind in Minas Tirith while my husband sees his kingdom? Is it not now my kingdom also? Any who think to do him harm must first consider the daughter of Elrond, and to those who believe her to be defenceless, I say only this: beware!'
You ask Arwen if she knows anything about a \qSong of Waves and Wind,\q and the Queen thinks for a moment.
'I have not heard a song by that name, ${PLAYER}, but songs of every sort have a mysterious power, both upon the singer and upon those who hear them. Tumúldo Fierce-water lies on the cold stone floor in a pool of his own blood, a Gondorian blade buried in his back. His wife Nakási kneels by him, her eyes burning with fury and with unshed tears.

'We have friends across the kingdom, hidden in plain sight. If we can rally the people of Gondor to our side....
'Aye, it could be done, ${PLAYER}. The folk of Gondor do not wish to be ruled by Elessar and his Elf-queen; nor do they wish to be made subservient to Umbar! If the Kindred of the Coins thinks to challenge us for the rule of Gondor once our plans bear fruit and King Elessar is slain, perhaps they will find we are not so easily conquered. I have to believe this is the way it will be.'

'No, there is something about you that is different. You are not with this rabble, even as they seek to court you. Tumúldo and I know well that achieving a goal can at times mean you must ally with your enemies.
'Are you willing to die with these folk? Or will you stand with me to repay their treachery? The next one they stab in the back might be you, or it might be a friend, or it might be a lover. Tumúldo was all of these to me.'
'I have nothing to say to you. Count yourself fortunate I do not cut you down where you stand. You may have deceived Maethon, but I am not fooled by this part you play, ${RACE}.'
'Introduce yourself to my friends, ${PLAYER}, and then we will begin.'

'Ah, do not trouble yourself overmuch. They will warm up to you when they learn how useful you will be to us.
'I hope Elessar has enjoyed his kingship, for it nears its end!'

'It is said that when Balakhôr the Scourge met his end, it was at the hands of Dead Men that he met it. They say it was the King Elessar who commanded the killing blow, but others stood nearby: an Elf... a dwarf... a hero who bore the name ${PLAYER}.
'I had no love for Balakhôr, ${PLAYER}. Nakási and I preyed upon the ships he sent forth from Umbar before he came to power, but afterward, when we did not cease our roguery, he took one hand from each of us. They were ours to keep, and so we did, though we replaced them with these made of metal.'
Tumúldo raises his left hand, and it shines in the dim light of the cellar.
'The hands he cut from us were preserved, and now they decorate the cabin of our ship, each forever clasping the other, a sign of our love... and also of our desire for vengeance. Your part in the death of Balakhôr has robbed us of that vengeance.'

'I don't understand how this could have happened! We heard no word from the Heirs of Castamir who remained in Umbar, but I believed they would send messages as soon as they could. From where sprang this Kindred of the Coins, and how could they so easily overthrow our folk? The Heirs of Castamir were so established in the city... I cannot understand it....
'What has become of Saklaphêl, the widow of Balakhôr, or of Balakhâd his son? What are we now to do?'

'Nakási, my love... you were right...
'Gondor... must die...
'The Song...'

'None of these vermin remain alive in this place, Tumúldo. You are avenged upon them.'
Nakási turns her eyes to you.
'Let us leave this place. Go ahead of me; I will carry the body of my husband. He deserves to rest forever in the Sea, and not in these vile houses of stone.'

En sus estudios, había aprendido muchas cosas sobre Angmar en el momento de su caída y sobre las muchas maldades del Rey Brujo que nunca salieron a la luz. Aunque nada hablaba tan claramente de lo que encontraría, sospecho que conocía su naturaleza. Y lo quería, para tener éxito donde el Rey Brujo de Angmar había fracasado.
Uno de los suyos, Rúvaran, fue el hombre que robó Máltagar y con él, tenían la intención de arrebatar el poder del Rey Brujo en sus propias manos. Su trabajo la llevó a menudo a las profundidades de Tûr Fúar, pero nadie parecía saber dónde trabajaba.

Se decía que el alcance del Rey Brujo de Angmar se extendía hacia el este durante su reinado. Allí se encontraba una fortaleza conocida como Agal Dûn, y los Angmarim tenían la intención de reclamar los secretos olvidados que yacían dentro de ella. Sobre la fortaleza, la leyenda hablaba de una aguja rota que perforaba el cielo: Tûr Fúar, la Agujalúgubre, y se creía que poderosas herramientas de hechicería podrían encontrarse dentro de ella.
Todos entre los Angmarim tenían planes para encontrar el poder que buscaban. Con una herramienta robada de Barad Gularan, uno de ellos pensó en ascender al ahora vacante trono de Angmar. La herramienta que portaba se llamaba Maltagar, el Infame Excavador, y poseía una magia sobrenatural. Susurros y visiones de los Muertos llegaban a todos los que se acercaban demasiado a Maltagar, y su maldad parecía crecer como si se alimentara de nosotros.
Fue llevado a través de Balach Iaran y nosotros, los Trév Duvárdain, seguimos a la Corona de Hierro hasta Câr Bronach...'

'Is this Elf-magic, my Queen? The water is cool and refreshing, and even as it passed my lips I confess I felt my burdens lift!
'I cannot thank you enough for your kind words, and for this remedy. I will grieve for my family, and keenly, but you are right: if the dreams of Vanyalos were sent by the Powers, none would think her able to turn aside from them, or prevent the horrors so revealed. That would be arrogance unbefitting the Lady of Lossarnach, or indeed any woman of Gondor.
'Thank you for aiding Queen Arwen with this ritual of Elf-magic, ${PLAYER}. I appreciate what you have done, and will not forget it.'

'My friend Ioreth would tell you no remedy acts as quickly as we might wish, but I hope you will find the comfort you deserve, Vanyalos. Grieve for your husband Forlong, and for your brother Denethor, but think not to carry the blame of what befell them! In that you are blameless, and the fault lies with Sauron who wove it, or with the Valar who thought such dreams might be of use to you.'

'Arwen was able to provide some comfort to the Lady Vanyalos? I am pleased to hear it, but it is no surprise to me. She has always had a rare talent for putting folk at ease, which is only one of the reasons for which I am glad she accompanies me on this tour of our kingdom.
'She left me little choice, of course. But it will do Gondor much good to see its Queen.'
'I appreciate what you have done, and will not forget it.'
'I am pleased we were able to help.'

'How delightful to have been of service! When my Queen asked me to attend her on this tour of the kingdom, I never suspected we would be able to do such good, and so early on the journey! Of course, I never doubted her intent or her ability, but it does remind me of a saying from my youth, when I was just a young girl growing up among the flowers of Imloth Melui. It feels so long ago now, but of course that is natural, is it not? Anyway, this is the saying...'
You should likely return to the King, for once Ioreth begins a story it can often take her a long time to finish it.

'Arwen has taken one of the healers who accompanies us, and the two of them have gone to speak with the Lady Vanyalos. Will you attend them and learn if my Queen's administrations have eased her sorrow? The Hall of Lady Vanyalos is to the east.'

'The Queen and her healer Ioreth mean well, ${PLAYER}, but they can provide no healing for me. Mine is no ordinary grief! This is not the sorrow of a woman whose husband marched to war and perished there, or that of a woman whose brother ruled a city and fell when it burned.'
The eyes of the Lady Vanyalos shine with tears, but sadness alone does not line her face. Her expression is haunted too by guilt.
'Would that I had no part in this! Then might I grieve as does the rest of Gondor! But I have done as they did not, for I dreamed of what would transpire, and I did nothing to prevent it! It is as if I put the axe in the hand of he who slew my Forlong, or cast the torch that set aflame the city walls behind which my brother Denethor perished! It is as if I, Vanyalos, did these things, by failing to prevent them!'

'Not all dreams have the meaning you give to them, Vanyalos, but my people know well that some there are to whom the Valar grant the gift of foresight. \qGift,\q I say, but if so it must be an unwelcome one.'
Vanyalos nods unhappily, and Arwen briefly takes her hand.
'None disbelieve you, sweet woman. Your dreams came to pass in the way you foresaw, and great is the pain to grieve, especially when the grieving must begin before the loss is suffered. But to think you might have prevented what the Valar showed to you... can you really believe it might be so? Does the Lady of Imloth Melui stand among the ranks of such as they?'
The expression of guilt on Vanyalos's face disappears, replaced with shock. Arwen continues.
'Of course not, my dear. Let me help you ease this burden. ${PLAYER}, take this bowl and fill it with water from one of the fountains outside the hall. Then add to it some of the water that falls from the heights in the north-western reaches of Imloth Melui. This will help to soothe the mind of Lady Vanyalos.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'Idhido i nin hin, a caetho hend,' she says, and hands the bowl to Lady Vanyalos. She indicates the Lady of Lossarnach should take a sip of the cool waters. When Vanyalos has done so, Arwen smiles.
'My friend Ioreth would tell you no remedy acts as quickly as we might wish, but I hope you will find the comfort you deserve. 'I am sure the Queen will do whatever she can to comfort Lady Vanyalos. I will do my best, as well! Perhaps a story of some sort to take her mind from her troubles? I know many such tales! But which one will suffice? Oh, that is a difficult decision to make...'

'Even in time of peace, Gondor is wide and travel will take some time! After all, the King desires to speak with as many of his folk as he can, doing whatever might be done to ease their burdens after the war. Speak with him inside and learn what he wishes to accomplish in Imloth Melui before continuing his journey.'

'I too am concerned about the Kindred of the Coins, ${PLAYER}, but whatever power now controls Umbar is beyond the bay; we must first see to the well-being of our people, while we have the time to do so.
'Already we have come to some of the deepest wounds inflicted by the War of the Ring. The Lady Vanyalos dwells here in sorrow; she is the widow of my fighting companion Forlong, who perished on the Pelennor. Her grief is two-fold, for she also survives another: her brother Denethor, victim of Sauron's manipulations.
'Arwen has taken one of the healers who accompanies us, and the two of them have gone to speak with the Lady Vanyalos. Will you attend them and learn if my Queen's administrations have eased her sorrow? The Hall of Lady Vanyalos is to the east.'

'Oh! ${PLAYER}! I was just telling the Lady Vanyalos that all clouds will surely pass, and even in time of grief there will be a new dawning and the sun will shine out in the morn such as you could never expect in the night-time, when all seemed darkest! It is true that these have been sorrowful days, and many tears have been shed, but it is like I always say: there's a remedy for it, you just have to find the right one! And I learned a great deal about healing remedies when I was just a child in Imloth Melui.
'Yes, I grew up here, among all these flowers. Did I ever tell you that? It is true! Why, when I was just a girl, I never expected to see much further than just down the hill or past that curve in the road, and wouldn't you know that I went on to dwell in Minas Tirith, and in the Houses of Healing there would be a great many ailments that would take more than medicine, but also a soothing word or three! It is like I always say...'

'Will you speak with Baranor and learn if there is aught else we can do before departing? Perhaps he will have news of villages in Upper Lebennin that can guide our course?'

'The King wishes to know of news from Upper Lebennin? I have been in contact with Captain Imladir of Tumladen, and he says now the war is over the refuge is emptying, but slowly. Other than that I have heard little.'

'Ah, I see my sister has finished with the bow and quiver I lent to her. I hope she was not too disappointed not to bring down any prey.'
You tell Elrohir that Arwen is even now preparing the meat from her fruitful hunt, and he laughs.
'Even after so many years she has the skill for it? I had thought residing in Imladris these past years might have driven how it is done from her memory, but I suppose it is not so! She need not prove it to me, though perhaps it is the folk of Gondor she thinks need convincing? Anyway, thank you for the return of my bow and quiver.'

'Thanks to our efforts, the folk of Arnach will be well provided for in the weeks to come. I hope this will be a comfort to them, and to the memory of Forlong.
'Will you speak with Baranor and learn if there is aught else we can do before departing? Perhaps he will have news of villages in Upper Lebennin that can guide our course?'

'We do appreciate the work you have all done for us, of course we do. It is just that... well, the folk of Arnach are a little uncomfortable with their King doing such labour. It is not unwelcome! They are just unused to such things.
'They have taken hard the death of Forlong. If you encountered him in a tavern, he might buy ales for everyone in the place, and spin tales you couldn't help but believe, no matter how incredible they seemed! But he was one of us. Good old Forlong. This King and his Elf-queen... they seem well-intentioned, but it will take time for the people to warm to them. You understand.
'The King wishes to know of news from Upper Lebennin? I have been in contact with Captain Imladir of Tumladen, and he says now the war is over the refuge is emptying, but slowly. Other than that I have heard little.'

'What do the folk of Arnach need us to do, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Elessar that some of the folk believe he is here to punish them, as Kings and Stewards rarely came to their village before, but that others planned to pick berries and hunt for game to fill the village store-house.
'I am not going to punish them! They and their lord did more than could be expected of anyone during these past few months! We will help them with their tasks, my friend, and when we move on we will leave their store-house filled. Is that clear enough?'
'There should be some berry bushes south-east of the village.'

'This was my berry bush, ${PLAYER}. No, it is fine. The bounty of all these bushes will end up in the Arnach store-house. Mind not that I picked the finest berries from this bush before you arrived.
'While I chose to pick these berries, my sibling is more of a hunter, and brought down a deer not far from here. Perhaps you can start preparing the meat to bring back to Arnach? The deer should be just to the south-east of here.'

'I borrowed this bow from my brother Elrohir. I may be Queen, but I think it is important for the folk of Gondor to see that I work to provide for them, as does my husband. Will you return his bow and quiver to him while I finish preparing this meat? It has been some time since I had such a task, but I do know how it is done.
'Elrohir will be somewhere within Arnach, working alongside my husband.'
'My sibling is more of a hunter, and brought down a deer not far from here. Perhaps you can start preparing the meat to bring back to Arnach? The deer should be just to the south-east of here.'

'Will you return Elrohir's bow and quiver while I finish preparing this meat? It has been some time since I had such a task, but I do know how it is done. He will be somewhere within Arnach, working alongside my husband.'
'She need not prove her hunting skill to me, though perhaps it is the folk of Gondor she thinks need convincing? Thank you once again for the return of my bow and quiver.'

'Aye, Baranor surely speaks truth: Tumladen must be emptying of refugees now that the War of the Ring has ended and the people of Gondor return to their homes. I would like to hear how that proceeds, but perhaps we need not bring the company there in its entirety.'

'Lady Vanyalos is not the only resident of Lossarnach who grieves the loss of Forlong; he was a most popular figure, and treated all the folk of the lands within his governance as if they were his own children. Sometimes he treated me in this way, despite the difference in our ages!
'\qGood old Forlong,\q they used to cheer. We fought together on more than one battlefield, ${PLAYER}, and he was always a true friend, and big-hearted. Aye, and his frame grew to match! Good old Forlong. Alas for war!
'The people of Lossarnach will need to provide for themselves until another lord is raised to the station, and I doubt not they will; but it will take time to replace such a hole as Forlong leaves. Let us travel south to Arnach and see what the people there need.'

'The people of Lossarnach will need to provide for themselves until another lord is raised to the station, and I doubt not they will; but it will take time to replace such a hole as Forlong leaves. Let us travel south to Arnach and see what the people there need.'

'Is that... is that the King? What is he doing here?
'Have we done something wrong, stranger? What could bring one such as he to our little village? Is he here to punish us? Have we not suffered enough?
'Oh, if only Lord Forlong had returned from the fighting! He would speak to the King and tell him we have done all we should!'

'That is King Elessar! I would know him anywhere!
'My family attended the royal wedding, stranger. Well, we were among the crowd, but even at so great a distance I could tell the King and his Elf-bride would be so happy in each other's arms, and would rule Gondor fairly and well.
'But I did not expect either of them to come to Arnach! He's going to get mud all over his fine clothes! Oh dear, I am so ashamed!'

'That is the King? Doesn't he know he is supposed to stay in his tower? What's he doing here in Arnach? I don't think he's a very good King if he doesn't know what he's supposed to be doing.
'We're supposed to be picking berries and hunting deer to fill the store-houses, now that the men have come back from the war. He's not going to do that, surely?'

'Sirgon has been showing me the state of the Gondorian navy, ${PLAYER}, and I confess to you that it is worse than I feared. The Corsairs of Umbar knew where to strike and with precisely how much force, and the ships that were once the pride of Gondor lie now at the bottom of the bay, or burned along the coast. It is true we seized some of their own vessels, without which we could not have arrived at Minas Tirith in time, but most of those were in poor shape, or are now.
'We do not know how much of Umbar's sea-power has been inherited by the Kindred of the Coins, but unless it is very little we have scant hope of repelling it, should the Kindred cross the bay with ships of their own. I have accepted Sirgon's suggestion that he step down as the Lord of Lebennin in favour of his son Faltharan, but there is a condition: he must supervise the rebuilding of Gondor's ships, and he must do it with utmost haste.'

'My King has done me the great honour of allowing me to step down, and I will do the best I can to repay him for it tenfold, as will my son Faltharan! Gondor's fleet is at its lowest ebb now, but I hope to restore its glory to such a height as has not been seen in hundreds of years! Perhaps then I shall set sail once again, as I do in my dreams....
'But I have a task, and it will occupy my every waking moment. My son has his own task, and it involves clearing out some of the unsavoury folk that have taken to preying upon the folk of Pelargir. Ships cannot be built without craftsmen, and craftsmen cannot work if they are being burgled and harassed whenever they cross the city!
'Will you aid my son with his task, and make the port-city more safe for my workers and for their families?'

'I have accepted Sirgon's suggestion that he step down as the Lord of Lebennin in favour of his son Faltharan, but there is a condition: he must supervise the rebuilding of Gondor's ships, and he must do it with utmost haste.'

Will you aid my son with his task, and make the port-city more safe for my workers and for their families?'

'I do not know if I have the fortitude to follow my father as the Lord of Lebennin, but I will do my duty as best I can, ${PLAYER}. I have begun by trying to stamp out the brigands with whom my brother Lorvegil sought to seize the city, but they are many and well-hidden. Some may be allies of the Heirs of Castamir, and I have heard whispers that a new power rises in Umbar... I think they might seek to court it, if they can.
'But my father is right. If we are to resist foes from Umbar, we must repair and rebuild our ships. He planned to show the King how the work progresses, and you should catch up with them at the dry dock to the south-east.'

'I am not surprised to hear your report of the dwarves from Furukzahar, for I have heard the mutterings around Tumladen. The folk here wonder why the doors of the dwarves remained shut during the war and only opened when the danger had passed. I say they wonder, but that is not the truth; they know the reason, and resent the dwarves for it. Where was this help when it might have saved lives?
'I know each folk must look first after its own, but we could have used the assistance of Furukzahar before now. It is good you prevented the insults from turning to bloodshed; we have seen enough of it this year, at least, even if the Temámir stayed safely in their mountains and saw none.
'You go now to see King Elessar in Pelargir? Tell him of the agreement you brokered with Furukzahar, and also that the refuge of Tumladen stands strong, its purpose fulfilled, and with good fortune it will not need to be used again for many years.'

'It is good to see you back, my friend! How stands the refuge of Tumladen?'
You tell Elessar about the situation in Tumladen and of the expedition of Temámir Dwarves that came there to survey the state of the buildings, as well as the resentment felt toward them by some of the Gondorians.
'I understand their feelings, even as I wish it was not so. Perhaps I should accept the invitation of Furukzahar, ${PLAYER}, in order to repair the relations between my kingdom and theirs. But first there is work to attend to in Pelargir.'

'You go now to see King Elessar in Pelargir? Tell him of the agreement you brokered with Furukzahar, and also that the refuge of Tumladen stands strong, its purpose fulfilled, and with good fortune it will not need to be used again for many years.'
The dwarves stare at you warily.

'It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, and I trust you speak with the king's own authority? The captain with whom we spoke earlier did not, and he spent many words telling us so, wasting his time and our own. I am pleased you have taken his place.
'My fellows and I were sent here by Hámisar, ruler of the Temámir folk who dwell in Furukzahar, stronghold of the White Mountains. Long have we worked alongside the people of Gondor, helping to repair and rebuild their cities, but the recent devastation is worse than any in our memory, and requires a good deal more effort and resources if it is to be made right.
'To that end, Hámisar wishes to send more crafters and dedicate more blocks of stone to the work. Defári, Setényil, and I have come to survey the needs of this refuge. Can you assure us that the King of Gondor will give us appropriate payment for any work we here perform?'
You tell Asitám that King Elessar is known for his fair dealings, and he greatly desires that Gondor be restored. The dwarf smiles broadly.
'Then he will not regret hiring the Temámir Dwarves of Furukzahar, my new friend! Let us continue deeper into the refuge and see how much work will be required.'

'I hope the King of Gondor appreciates your work on his behalf, ${PLAYER}, for most of his folk may not. Would they think to aid us, if our stronghold was directly threatened while their own towns and villages were not? I know the answer, though they believe otherwise. Thank you for helping us here keep the peace.
'I will bring my report back to Hámisar, and will tell him that the King has, for now, agreed to these repairs. Our price will be fair, and the friendship between our folk... well, there is more to be repaired than just stone, it seems. Will you convey an invitation to your King on Hámisar's behalf? He is welcome to visit us at Furukzahar at his earliest convenience. After all, it is one thing to do business between reliable intermediaries such as you and I, but when rulers can meet face to face it seems to me much more can be accomplished, better and more quickly.
'Good day to you, my friend.'
'Good day to you, my friend.'

Hámisar turns his attention to you.

I would not think to bore you with such matters! I hope you will explore the beautiful corridors of Furukzahar and meet with my folk.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}. I did not expect the King of Gondor to accept the invitation to visit Furukzahar so swiftly! It reflects well upon him for respecting the will of Hámisar, and upon you for bringing word to him with such haste!
'I hope you enjoy your stay here, and that King Elessar and ruler Hámisar are able to arrive at a fair and equitable arrangement that will enrich both of their folk.'

'What has brought you to Furukzahar? I hope you do not think to involve us in your wars? The Temámir of Furukzahar have always welcomed visitors from the other dwarf families, but Hámisar shut the gates for a reason. He did not intend to invite Gondor's war to our doorstep.'

Sékhel permits himself a small smile, and then shakes his head regretfully.

We may need true-hearted allies in the days to come, and Gondor's stone-work could use the attention of such as these dwarves. What does my Queen say to this proposal?'

'Let us accept the invitation of the Dwarves of Furukzahar. What does my Queen say to this proposal?'

'You will want me along on this mission, of course. The Dwarves of Furukzahar are not Longbeards, but you cannot best a dwarf when it comes to speaking with other dwarves! They will want to hear what I have to say, even as they spare not a moment for the King of Gondor.
'It's true that you don't see Temámir in the North very often, but they did answer the call of the Sixth War of Dwarves and Orcs, and suffered losses as severe as any other house. Their stronghold of Furukzahar is hidden in a cleft of the White Mountains to the north of Pelargir? Then let us be off, and see if the hospitality of the Temámir is to be as noteworthy as their wisdom!'

'Gangur Farwend was just here, ${PLAYER}, and he told me what he said to you. I asked him to describe Khôltekh, and he did the best he could... he did say his memory for faces is not what it used to be. Caebar sketched a drawing from the description. Here it is.'
'You should examine the sketch Caebar made of Khôltekh the Cunning.'

'My hand shook as I drew the sketch, ${PLAYER}. I do not know if I am properly cut out for such an adventure as this! I hope you and the King find the drawing useful. Will you now know Khôltekh the Cunning if you see him?
'If you will not, the fault lies with me... I apologized to the King, for I am only an amateur artist, but he would not hear it. He is too good for such as I am.'
'Once you have studied the sketch, you can give it back to Caebar.'

'We have no choice now, my friends. We should get as much rest as we are able. Whatever Hámisar thinks to keep from us, whether it is the continued presence of Khôltekh the Cunning in Furukzahar or some other deception, we cannot reveal it if he chooses to keep it hidden.
'We will depart in the morning. Rest for now... but lightly.'

'I do not like this, ${PLAYER}. Hámisar is hiding something. I think he would have preferred not to speak to us of the Kindred of the Coins, and had we left him the choice he would not have spoken of them at all. I believe this Khôltekh came to Furukzahar, but I am less certain the meeting was as Hámisar presented it.
'We should remain on our guard while we are here. Something about this situation does not feel right.'

'That Hámisar is lying to us. I don't know about what, or why he seeks to deceive us, but I can see it as plainly as you can see the beard on my handsome face.
'I knew there was something afoot when he made us wait so long on the doorstep! It was not mere discourtesy... it was villainy of some kind! We have yet to discover what type of villainy, perhaps... but villainy nonetheless!
'Do you think it has something to do with the unpleasant sensation of dread we felt by that door south of the throne room, ${PLAYER}? What is Hámisar keeping in that chamber?'
'What is Hámisar keeping behind that suspicious door, ${PLAYER}? Perhaps you can investigate further, but do try not to draw attention to yourself.'
'I knew there was something going on when they made us wait on the doorstep for so long. Did I not tell you so?'

'You are a companion of the King of Gondor? Have we met? My memory for faces is not what it once was, and I am far from my home. I am here visiting, but I believe I have information you should know.
'Quietly! We should not speak here. Let us meet inside the armoury, across the water to the north-east. There will be fewer unfriendly ears to hear what I have to say, and the noise of the forges should help to hide our conversation.'

'When I first arrived here, the Temámir showed me a great deal of hospitality, and Hámisar gave me his personal welcome. I was most impressed, for while I have been warmly greeted at every dwarf-hold I visited on my travels, Furukzahar outshone them all. But then it all changed.
'A few days ago, an emissary from the Kindred of the Coins arrived. His name you know, for Hámisar told it to you, but he withheld his epithet and the folk to whom he belongs. His full name is Khôltekh the Cunning, and he is a dwarf of the Temámir who hails from some distant land. And yet it was not from Umbar he came, or at least not directly; he came from the west. From conversations I overheard I understand that he received delivery of some artifact from the north, and he brought it with him to Furukzahar.
'Hámisar told you this emissary of the Kindred departed, but I think he is still here; it is the dread of the artifact he bears that you sensed outside the door where he shelters. I do not know why the Temámir became so cold to me after he arrived, or why their leader lies to the King of Gondor, but I thought you should know. I will speak with King Elessar briefly, if it can be arranged in secret, but I think you should all leave this place before it is too late. Furukzahar may not be safe for you.'
'Not here! We should speak inside the armoury, across the water to the north-east. The noise will help to hide our conversation.'
'I feel as if I struggle to stay afloat in deep water, and something tries to pull me under. I have felt this way for most of my time in the employ of the King, and the Steward Denethor before him!'

'Hámisar told you this emissary of the Kindred departed, but I think he is still here; it is the dread of the artifact he bears that you sensed outside the door where he shelters. I do not know why the Temámir became so cold to me after he arrived, or why their leader lies to the King of Gondor, but I thought you should know. I will speak with King Elessar briefly, if it can be arranged in secret, but I think you should all leave this place before it is too late. Furukzahar may not be safe for you.'
'This is all so overwhelming. How did I come to be here?'

'Do you really think Hámisar is lying to the King? Why would he risk such a dangerous deception? You don't think he's in league with the Kindred of the Coins, do you?
'I am just a scribe, ${PLAYER}, and not especially accomplished at that. I am not an adventurer or a hero like you; I left my home in Ethring a few months before the outbreak of war. Ever since I came to Minas Tirith and the service of the City, I have become embroiled in great events I find myself unable to comprehend.
'It is all very overwhelming to me. What is Hámisar keeping from the King?'

'This hall is so cold... but the Queen wants me to speak, so I shall speak.
'Long ago, and for always, I dwelt within and beside the River Gilrain, and my music was the song of sunlight on the water, and of wind in the leaves. But it was a lonely song, for my sisters had gone away and I did not think I would see them again. Animals came to the stream to drink, and birds to bathe, but except for such creatures I was alone and felt the pain of it... until one day.
'An Elf-maid tarried by the river as she journeyed southward from a distant land. She was more beautiful and radiant than anyone I had ever seen. I sang to her and she delighted in my song, for it reminded her of home. She danced beside my stream, and I was so gladdened by her presence that the music I made held more enchantment than ever it had before. She slept on the bank of Gilrain, comfortable and safe, and I was no longer alone. I dreamt that once she awoke she would fashion a home for herself in my wood, and I would teach her my song and she would call me sister. She would have children of her own, Elf-children of merry eyes and high voices, and I would show them the flower-fields and the secret springs, and they would fashion brightly-coloured petal-crowns to wear, and their mother would delight in them.
'It was a happy dream, but it lasted too long, and when she at last awoke many seasons had passed. The Elf-ship that waited in distant harbour for her to arrive could wait no longer. With selfish hands I stole that life from her, and I grieve every day at the sorrow I caused her. I did not intend such sadness to befall, and I would take it back if I could! And yet it is my doing, and the guilt weighs heavily upon my every moment.'

'I know what cruelty is, Maiden of the Gilrain. The world is cruel, and has always been. Can you know my story and say it is not so?
'Amroth was a king among Elves, but to me he was more; he was my love, and the brightest star of my night sky. \qWe must depart, Nimrodel,\q he said to me, \qfor the dwarves have awoken terrible evil, and if we stay it will endanger our folk too,\q and I believed his words. I believe them still, for I know what befell in the centuries since, as he cannot.
'Amroth went ahead to make ready the ship. I travelled with a small company to join him at that distant harbour, but the passage of the mountains was hard. The high crags filled me with unease; the rocky way troubled my heart. When at last we descended to the low-lands, I danced in the woods and became separated from my folk, so grateful was I to leave the mountains behind. The sound of the River Gilrain was beautiful, and its music had magic in it, and whatever else befell I can still remember how it was, and know that I loved it. I slept in peace for too long, and by the time I awoke a fell wind had come from the north and driven my love's ship from the shore, never to return. It is said Amroth leapt from the ship and braved the waves that he might wait for me... but never again was he seen by Elf or by Man, though I walked the shore for uncounted days and innumerable nights.
'I dwelled in sorrow from that day forth, never far from the Bay where I lost my love, and I have worn this mourning veil for so long I cannot remember the sight of the sun without it. I have held my grief close, but so too has it held me. Until now I believed the weight of those heavy chains was only mine to carry. I did not know you sorrowed too, Maiden of the Gilrain. It was not for you to feel this way. Do not burden yourself with the grief that is mine. I spoke of cruelty? The greatest cruelty is that this sadness must snare more than one heart, and for so many years!'

'And so concludes my Queen's greatest purpose in this journey, ${PLAYER}. She desired to ease Roamingstar's burden, and I believed we would need to visit the Cave of the Avorrim to make the attempt. But we were fortunate that Nimrodel was here in the Palace of the Swan, and now we have saved some time.
'I said Arwen's purpose on this journey was ended, but of course mine is only beginning! We must speak with Prince Imrahil about the continued presence of the Corsairs that threaten Gondor's shoreline, and also about the rise of the Kindred of the Coins in Umbar, across the Bay of Belfalas! But we have already achieved some good today, for Roamingstar and Nimrodel each deserve the peace and the happiness that their sorrows stole from them. I hope we have helped lighten their burdens today. I think we have.'

'Many of the Prince's court and the greatest part of his swan-knights went with Imrahil to Minas Tirith for the waging of the war, but his daughter Lothíriel managed the rule of the city while he was away. That Dol Amroth still stands is a testament to her ability, and tells me she has learned much from her father!'

'Just one moment,' the Queen says to you seriously, retrieving a finely-crafted bowl and a glass jar from the recesses of her cloak. She removes the corked stopper from the mouth of the jar and slowly pours the crystal-clear water contained within into the bowl, spilling not a drop.
'Will you set this down on the floor just there?' she asks you.

I am certain my brother lives, for he has survived much worse than that, sturdy crab that he is.'
You tell Jajax that Prince Imrahil and King Elessar should be told of the situation he encountered in Umbar, and the Corsair tilts his head, weighing your suggestion against the potential for reward.
'It is good to be owed favours and coin by Kings and Princes, ${PLAYER}. I accept your offer. I have not been the guest of a royal court such as this before. Well, not an invited one, anyway.'

'I said to keep an eye on him, not to bring him to my court, ${PLAYER}. Why should I trust these things he says of Umbar, or of the Kindred of the Coins? How do we know he is not one of them?
'Why should I trust one of the Corsairs who so troubled our coasts during the war, and who continues to do so even now? Have you taken leave of your senses?'
'It is good to be owed favours and coin by Kings and Princes, ${PLAYER}. I accept your offer. I have not been the guest of a royal court such as this before. Well, not an invited one, anyway.'

'What is your name? Daxamat?'
Khôltekh nods idly, but behind his eyes you sense that he is paying very close attention to your face, and filing away your name for later consideration.
'Some there are who lead, and some there are who follow. Even the Kindred of the Coins is subject to this rule, my new friend. Azagath the Sea-shadow prides himself on leading; he does so with aplomb. Rothog the Storm carries out the wishes of those who give the commands, and they are made stronger with every swing of his mighty fists, and every bite of his sharp teeth. Ask the Heirs of Castamir who attended the half-troll's last bout before the Sea-stone Mutiny about those teeth...'
Khôltekh grins.
'A private joke, Daxamat. But heed these words, for they are also true: the wisest of all is he who knows when to lead and when to follow. The wisest is he who knows when to speak, and when to listen. Which are you, my new friend? And who do you follow? The Heirs of Castamir? Or perhaps the Church of the All Seeing? This city has many foes, and sometimes they require some... rooting out. The uprising in Umbar was thorough... but Azagath has mused aloud that he sometimes wonders if it was thorough enough.'
'You have to go, Dax, before Khôltekh remembers you are here. Quietly, through the northern exit!'

'Dax! This place is no longer safe for us! This Kindred of the Coins intends to imprison or put to death any freebooter and pirate that does not sail in support of them!
'There's no time... we have to leave this city! Quickly, back to the ship!'

'Ah, it is good to be home! The sea-breeze welcomes us back to Umbar! My name may be spoken of all across the world already, but it will mean a little more to hear it spoken in the streets of our city. No doubt my exploits will earn us a tankard or two of ale in the Crab and Cutlass, or in the Teeming Net Tavern. You were always partial to the Hungry Deep, weren't you, Dax?
'But we have work to do! The drinking will have to wait. But just a little while!'

'Something about the city is different, Dax. Do you feel it too?
'There are too many guards here. The Haradrim of Ordâkh seem to be gone, but in their place the guardsmen appear... more vigilant. What has happened to my City of Sails? I do not like this. Someone must answer for it... and they will answer to Jajax!'

'Dax! I haven't seen you in an age! I thought you perished in the war... but you must have escaped that fate, somehow! I take it some portion of your brother's good fortune must have transferred to you? We could have used some of that here!
'Were you in the battle? I heard the Corsairs who followed Balakhôr were slain by an army of Dead Men... and that they were led by the hated warrior Thorongil, who despised the Umbari so much he returned to life that he may slay even more! But that cannot be so. Still, there have been strange occurrences here in recent days, ever since the great earthquake that collapsed the Temple of the All Seeing. People say he is dead... if such a thing is possible. But the Empire of Ordâkh did not stand long against the uprising, and when the fighting ended the Kindred of the Coins announced that neither Sauron nor Ordâkh would rule again in Umbar.
'The Kindred claim they have ushered in a new age, but for people like you and me, Dax, and like your brother... I do not know if they mean it. The gaols are full of thieves and Corsairs alike; no opponent of the Kindred lives long after voicing it. If they learn that you sailed with any Heir of Castamir...'

'I do not want to go up there. King Elessar would understand if we do not, surely!'
'You are here on the King's business. You are not here to listen to the ramblings of a sad old man. Speak to the people of Morlad. Do what you came to do.'

'Do what you came here to do.'
'Oh, am I glad to see you, ${PLAYER}! A gang of toughs surprised me a few minutes ago and I had to run and hide. What if they come back?'
