'Do what you came here to do, then.'

'The King would expect us to slay any such members of the Ruthless Dead that we encounter in the Vale... or whatever passes for slaying such spirits. I am not entirely clear on that point. Legolas has tried to explain it to me, but it all seems rather complicated.
'What do I know? I know that if any of the Ruthless Dead think to trouble us or the folk who live nearby, we will inconvenience them. We will inconvenience them with sword or bow or axe, and let them return if they dare!
'They are sure to haunt the Hill of Erech at night, but they will be along the road to the Paths of the Dead at all times, I wager!'

'Oh, ${PLAYER}, a pall lies upon the Blackroot Vale, for it was caught in the grip of war, and all her young men were drawn away eastward. My sons, too, were caught in the whirlpool, and Duilin and Derufin will not come home again. My husband Duinhir thinks to spare me the details of what befell my boys... but there is evil in not knowing! If only I knew they perished quickly, and without pain...'
Lady Rosfin entreats you through eyes filled with tears, but when you hesitate she looks away.
'No, I will not ask it of you. I know Duinhir thinks to spare my feelings, the hard-headed man! I am stronger than he knows, and have always been so! It is not lost on me that he was not able to save our sons from death, he with his strong sword-arm and his thick shield, and I was forced to remain behind in Morlad; I, who might have been able to keep them safe!
'Life can be cruel, ${PLAYER}, but it is crueller still for a mother in time of war. I keep thinking I will hear the sound of my sons boasting and laughing on the wind, and then I will see Duilin and Derufin climbing the path through the village, alive and well and happy. But it is not to be so.'
'We should now go to Morlad. That is the main settlement in the Blackroot Vale, is it not?'

'I have told Rosfin over and over again that there was nothing I could do to save our sons, but she will not listen.'
Duinhir lowers his voice so he can speak only to you, out of his wife's hearing.
'Sometimes when I lie awake in the silent watches of the night, ${PLAYER}, I wonder if it is the truth I speak to my wife. I raised Duilin and Derufin to be bold and to be valiant, and they made me proud every day of their lives. But if I had raised them to be... less bold... to be less valiant...'
Duinhir chokes on his words and stifles a sob, turning his back on Rosfin to hide his face.
'Would my boys be alive today, ${PLAYER}, if I had not raised them to hold dear the same things as I? No, stop. Enough. You are here on the King's business. You are not here to listen to the ramblings of a sad old man. Speak to the people of Morlad. Do what you came to do.'
Lady Rosfin looks at you with sad, cold eyes, and says nothing.
'I've got nothing to say to you. Move along.'

'Someone loosed an arrow at me from hiding, ${PLAYER}. I am fortunate indeed that this is a town of Men and not of Elves, or it might have hit its mark.
'These folk are not happy to see us.'
'What is wrong with these people, ${PLAYER}? Do they not know we are here to help them? Do you think the Heirs of Castamir are to blame?'

'Supporters of the Heirs of Castamir? No, I do not think they are responsible for this; not in the Blackroot Vale.'
Duinhir looks directly into your eyes and holds your attention.
'My people have suffered much, as have we all, and King Elessar did not take the time to visit Morlad himself. There is no conspiracy here, ${PLAYER}. The folk of the Vale grieve, and their grief has made them angry. I understand it, for I am angry too.'

'Many were the shades of dead Men that followed in our train when we departed Erech, and they were the fighters who wrested control of Pelargir for the Grey Host. Without this army of the Dead, we could not have seized the Corsair ships that bore us to the Harlond, and Minas Tirith.
'The shades who gathered about King Elessar atop this Hill redeemed their oath, and recovered their honour. Should that make it pleasing to recall for we who were there? I do not believe it does. Speak with Caebar and Gimli, and afterwards we will proceed to Morlad on King Elessar's business.'

'I do not want to go up there. King Elessar would understand if we do not, surely!'

I never thought I would see such a day as this, for the Langstrand is so far from the White City and it seemed we were just as distant from their minds, if not further! 'I rejoice to hear you say so, stranger, but it is unnecessary. 'You took care of the beasts that threaten Melgobas, lynx and Corsairs both? Perhaps the King and Queen knew what they were doing when they brought you with them to visit the Langstrand!

'So near to the end, then? I worried it might have been so. What need was there for my husband to die, if the Men of the West were so near to their victory? 'You may leave me, ${PLAYER}. I have words to speak to Elessar, but they are not for your hearing. See the comforts of Lond Cirion, and know that Golasgil will not enjoy them again.'

'The King has come here to resolve the line of succession, hasn't he? Golasgil's heir is too young to rule, and has ceded some of his authority to his mother Marra, but there are some in Lond Cirion and elsewhere who believe she is not fit to govern in these trying times, and she still in mourning.
'There is another matter of some curiosity, stranger. It is known that before he departed for the war, Golasgil prepared a parchment containing his last wishes... but it cannot be found. You should tell the King, for the safety of Anfalas is affected, and that imperils the kingdom.'

Se dice que fue corrompida por la mano del propio Rey Brujo, y que los juramentos jurados sobre ella atan las voluntades de sus víctimas a la Piedra del Juramento. 'You found something written in Golasgil's hand? Aye, these notes are extensive, and see where he signed them, here at the bottom? He must have been very interested in the movement of the currents to have written so much! Let me compare the handwriting of these pages with his purported testament...'

'Thank you for your part in this, ${PLAYER}. I am glad to have heard Golasgil's wishes, for now we can see that they will be carried out. He was a good friend and a worthy soldier, and I want to honour his directives.
'There is still a question I want answered, but it is of a sensitive nature and I will first allow the audience to disperse. We will speak with the Lady Marra about this last question when we can do so without too many ears nearby to hear.'
The seal on these papers has indeed been broken, which is unusual for such a document
Pages with the heading 'Notes on the Currents' is signed by Golasgil and contains musings on the subject
A paper used as a bookmark has the notation 'Remember to buy fish,' but is unsigned

King Elessar has suggested that his scribe Caebar may be able to ascertain the provenance of the handwriting contained in Golasgil's purported testament.
The study of Lond Cirion may contain samples of Lord Golasgil's writing that can be used to prove he wrote the testament, and its provenance made secure.

'We are here to witness the last wishes of Lord Golasgil, as written in his final testament? That is a relief, ${PLAYER}! I was afraid I had done something wrong!'
Caebar turns a bright shade of pink at the realization that he has spoken loudly in the quiet room.
'O hush now, Caebar!' he chides himself under his breath. 'This is a solemn occasion.'

'This is my suggestion: let your son come with our travelling party as we journey to Pinnath Gelin. It is my belief that Orgolas will see this land with new eyes, and he will grow into the responsibility he must one day have.'
'If you permit Daeram to also join your travelling party, that he may attend my son and keep him safe, I suppose I cannot refuse.'

'I am surprised to learn that Lady Marra has agreed to allow Orgolas to depart with the King and Queen, but Pinnath Gelin is not far from here. I will do what I can to keep the boy safe among the green hills. Perhaps he will be less likely to slip my watch if he feels that he is on an adventure, and need not go in search of another one himself!'

'I am surprised to learn that Lady Marra has agreed to allow Orgolas to depart with the King and Queen, but Pinnath Gelin is not far from here. I will do what I can to keep the boy safe among the green hills. Perhaps he will be less likely to slip my watch if he feels that he is on an adventure, and need not go in search of another one himself!'

'Is it true? I am to depart with the King's party for Pinnath Gelin? That is wonderful news! That is where the Wave-hunter is currently docked, ${PLAYER}! Are we going to see the ship that my father left to me?'

'I gave you my thanks for not speaking what you suspected in front of Coruchon, King Elessar, but you will have my thanks a hundredfold if you do this now: I entreat you to forbid Orgolas from leaving Lond Cirion, no matter what his father has gifted to him. Already it is nearly impossible to keep him from sneaking beyond the walls, but perhaps a command from the King of Gondor would stay his steps?'
Queen Arwen has something she wishes to say to Lady Marra.
Lady Marra is in the main hall of Lond Cirion.
Daeram is outside the keep of Lond Cirion.

'I gave you my thanks for not speaking what you suspected in front of Coruchon, King Elessar, but you will have my thanks a hundredfold if you do this now: I entreat you to forbid Orgolas from leaving Lond Cirion, no matter what his father has gifted to him. Already it is nearly impossible to keep him from sneaking beyond the walls, but perhaps a command from the King of Gondor would stay his steps?'

'I understand this request you have of my husband, Marra, but I fear you may do more harm with the asking of this boon than you will prevent. Your son will not be kept from leaving your home if that is the purpose of his heart. Though the command be in the King's voice, Orgolas will know who wrote the words, and that knowledge can only breed resentment.
'You say Golasgil was a fine mariner, and I do not doubt he was! But what I have learned of your husband from my own is that he cared deeply for the people of Anfalas, and did not sail from them, or from you, without great need. Perhaps if Orgolas understood the cares and concerns of the folk he will rule when he comes of age, he will make the same choice, and the Wave-hunter will remain at its dock.
'This, then, is my suggestion: let your son come with our travelling party as we journey to Pinnath Gelin. It is my belief that Orgolas will see this land with new eyes, and he will grow into the responsibility he must one day have.'

'I do not know.'
Marra looks from the Queen to the King, and back again.
'What if this journey gives life to embers that might otherwise have been cooled? I do not see how such an adventure could prevent that which I fear for my son.
'But if you permit Daeram to also join your travelling party, that he may attend my son and keep him safe, I suppose I cannot refuse.'
Chapter 3.12: Grief and Duty
Orgolas is outside the keep of Lond Cirion.
Lady Marra has entreated the King to forbid her son from leaving Lond Cirion.
Talk to Caebar in the central yard of Lond Cirion and accompany him to the King
Talk to Marra in the main hall of Lond Cirion
Talk to King Elessar in the main hall of Lond Cirion
Talk to Marra in the main hall of Lond Cirion

'I am grateful for your discretion earlier, my King, for Coruchon would seek any advantage he could from this, and Golasgil would never forgive me should a widow's weakness endanger Orgolas's claim!
'But I broke the seal and read my husband's last wishes out of fear that he would do as he has indeed done: granted to his son and mine that cursed ship, Wave-hunter! How often did he speak of his intention for Orgolas to follow in his own steps, and become a great mariner like his father? Too often, and every time it cut me deeply! The Wave-hunter was harboured upstream in Pinnath Gelin during the war, to protect it from the Corsairs, and I have refused to summon it back here to keep Orgolas as far from its threatening decks as I can!
'When I saw such a bequest had been made, I did not know what to do. But I cannot disobey the command of the King of Gondor. Hindering Golasgil's wishes was bad enough, but I fear for my son's safety! He is so young, my King. You must understand.'
'Why did you break the seal upon your husband's last wishes, Marra?'
Caebar is in the central yard of Lond Cirion, where he has confided in you that he is worried about the service King Elessar has asked him to provide.
Lady Marra is in the main hall of Lond Cirion.
King Elessar is in the main hall of Lond Cirion.

'Will you accompany me, my friend? The King did not prohibit it, so far as I know, and I cannot imagine he would not allow you to be present at... whatever this duty turns out to be!
'I would just feel better if you were there, ${PLAYER}. Tell me you will come with me.'

'Thank you, my friend! I will not forget this!
'Let us meet with King Elessar at the appointed hour, and until that time comes I will try not to worry overmuch.'

'I am sorry, but it was very hard to hear these things. My husband was a man of great bravery and courage, and a generous heart, but to think of him writing these things, alone, without first taking my advice...
'I will shed no more tears. I wish this letter had not been read here today.'
Marra falls silent, her face a mask.

'I have to ask you something, Marra, and I do not wish to give you offence or cause you any further upset... but I feel that I must ask it.'
Elessar fixes his gaze upon the Lady of Anfalas. When next he speaks, his voice is gentle, but his eyes are stern.

'Rendis? Why I haven’t seen 'er in weeks. A fortnight at least... maybe longer, maybe. She was looking for a sturdy bag. 'Say - can I interest you in a bag? How's about a sack?'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}! I heard you were quite instrumental in assisting with the defence against the Enemy. I wonder if I might press you into service for something less grandiose, yet just as important to me.

'Well, would you look at that! Even the most stalwart of guards must take a break from their duty every now and then.'
Handir's smile fades as he continues gazing at the dog. 'I wonder what she is searching for. Did she lose something? Someone? Perhaps her master left home for the war and never returned.

'${PLAYER}, welcome! As you can see, we've been hard at work rebuilding our home. My heart should feel light, but ever since the war's end, I have been troubled by a string of mysteries.
'For the past few months, every now and then, someone has been leaving sacks of supplies at our doorsteps. Preserved boar meat, cut firewood, all harvested from the wild. The strange thing is, we don't know who is responsible. Of course, we were suspicious at first, but nothing about the supplies thus far has seemed amiss. I hope that the culprit is not a malicious person, but we cannot be too careful.
'Now, I suspect the meat we have been receiving has been hunted from a nearby boar wallow, to the north-east. Perhaps our culprit is there right now. But very few people here would be able to defend themselves out there, and they are all busy protecting Halach.
'Would you investigate the wallow for us?'

'Please, put down your weapons, ${CLASS}. I mean you no harm, and I am alone. My fellow soldiers fled long ago.
'You have come looking for me at the behest of the townspeople, yes? Rather, you have come looking for the one gifting them supplies. It is not much, compared to what my comrades and I raided from them during the war. But this is... repentance, I suppose.
'I will return home eventually, but not before I see some of the harm undone.'

For about ten seconds, Nasar squints at you with a look of intense concentration. His eyes then light up, and a grin spreads across his face.
'Hah! I remember you! Othor didn't think I would, but I do! How could I forget the one who supplied me with all of that ale? Ah, here, let me help you distribute the food....
'Othor hasn't told you why we came to Pelargir, has he? After the war, I went searching for other wayward Corsairs, and he came along to protect me. Not that I needed the protection, of course, but he's a good sort to have around!
'That's how we all found each other. We may be stranded here with no ships to take us home, but at least we are not alone.'
'What are you doing, feeding an army? Ah, I jest! The food will be ready in a moment; just wait right there.'

'${PLAYER}, what a surprise! I'm glad to see you again, now that those dark days are behind us.
'Ah -- yes, that's Nasar. I'm not sure if he would remember you on account of his drunkenness when you met him. As for how we've wound up here... that is a long story. Suffice to say that my men and I could not extract any useful secrets from him, even after he imbibed all the ale you collected. And with the aid of some shared drinks, we befriended each other instead.
'Actually, would you lend me your ear? I'm unfamiliar with Pelargir, and while my presence seems to put the residents at ease, my Corsair companions are also fresh faces to the city. Walking around freely would not go well. But after such a long journey, I was hoping to raise our spirits with some food.
'I've heard there is a food stall run by Haradrim somewhere south of here, near the docks. Would you mind ordering something for us?'
'Here you go. If your small army is still hungry afterwards, do come back!'

As you relay the situation to Celebros, she frowns. Her frown only deepens. Even after you have finished speaking, she remains silent a bit longer.
'I must say, this is troubling to hear. Pelargir still bears the scars left behind by the Corsair invasion, and the memory haunts us all. Although, these Corsairs... they are simply men seeking a way home. To be lost for so long, unsure if they'll ever return... I can understand that.
'I shall help them. Not as the Lady of Lebennin, but as myself.'

'Truth be told, this is a tight spot in which to be stuck. We cannot agree on how to move forward. Othor suggested approaching Lord Sirgon for help, but... even if Othor hails from Gondor, he is a stranger to them. I doubt they would entertain us.'

'Lady Celebros agreed to meet with us? And these papers with the seal of Sirgon -- now we may wander freely about the city. Despite every grudge she could hold against us... I can hardly believe it. We've found our way home.'
The soft smile on Nasar's face slowly transforms into a grin.
'No doubt the shipwrights of Pelargir have things to teach us, but I assure you, they shall not be the only ones teaching!'

'Lady Celebros' lockbox? She did not tell you what this was for, did she? Then I suppose I shall find the answer here...'
As Captain Thandor reads the orders, he raises an eyebrow.
'Well... I was not expecting her to part with her heirloom just to fund this endeavour... but it is a noble cause, and I am glad to see it.
'I shall take things from here. Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'

'Unfortunately, the war consumed most of our seafaring resources. We cannot spare a ship for your friends to return home. Do not fret; I may have a solution. If I can provide the materials and funds necessary, the Corsairs could work with our shipwrights to repair a damaged ship rather than build a new one entirely... and I daresay both groups could learn new things from each other.
'Please, wait right here. I must retrieve something.'
Celebros disappears into the manor. A while later, she returns with what looks like a collection of papers and a sturdy lockbox.
'Would you deliver these orders and the lockbox to Captain Thandor? He stands watch near the East Pelargir gates.
'And once that is done, please give your friends these papers, and let them know they are most welcome here. I would be happy to discuss the matter with them further.'

As you approach, Aerin holds up a finger, bidding you pause to let her finish a passage in the book she's reading. She scans the next few lines and laughs quietly to herself before bending a corner of the page and closing the book shut.
She spends a moment studying your face. You're not readily familiar to her. Maybe you've changed your appearance since your last meeting.
'${PLAYER}!' she recognizes you at long last. 'Have you been well? I certainly have. Though there has been some trouble brewing.'
It doesn't take much to get her to say more.
'Hata Kebir. It's been abandoned these past few weeks, but a few days ago some louts came scrounging around, no doubt hired by the Heirs of Castamir. Firiondur approached them and asked what they were doing here. They said they were here for a map of some kind, and that they weren't leaving until they found it. They even offered him coin if he were willin' to help them!'
She produces a map of Pelargir from her pocket. It's marked with various symbols whose meanings you can only begin to guess at.
'I assume this is the map they were lookin' for. What? Don't give me that look. I went searching through the place after it were abandoned. Anyway, the man says he won't leave until he finds the map, so I say let's give him what he wants.'
She produces another map, remarkably similar to the original, but the symbols are drawn in completely different locations.
'What do you think? I made it myself. If you're inclined to help us, go plant this fake map somewhere in Hata Kebir. If you happen to thrash some of those ruffians while you're at it, I certainly won't be complainin'.'

Reluctantly, Aerin tears her gaze from her book and smiles at you.
'Did you do it? Did you hide the map? Oh how delightful! I'm not entirely sure what the purpose of the original map is, but I can tell you that the map that I made points to nothing but sewer entrances! I hope they have fun rooting around in the muck.
'Now, if you'll excuse me, I'd like to see how this duel ends.'
She returns to her reading, quickly forgetting you're there.

'Have I not suffered enough? Must you trouble me so?! My wife is lost to me. There is nothing left for me in this world!'
Halgúr begins to well up.

'My beloved Melnith. So kind. So gentle. It is no wonder she spent many a twilight away tending to this area.'
Halgúr examines a ribbon on the wolf mother's neck.
'Nathemel. That is the name Melnith gave to this wolf mother.'

'I must apologize. I knew he would be reluctant to speak to you.
'I had hoped that your experience in the war would still his fervour. His will to continue on with meaning was lost... along with my mother.'
Sadrien steels herself before continuing.
'After the war, many parties retreating would often trouble us on the way to Pelargir. My father's homestead was raided, ransacked and pillaged of anything valuable. He tried to stand his ground, but those brigands chose to ruin his home. My mother Melnith was inside when the building collapsed.
'So you see, reminding him of that moment may have angered him. There is something you should see.'
Sadrien tells you of a place Melnith used to frequent daily.

'The Reaper of the Waves? I think we know this captain, ${PLAYER}.
'Nakási has reason to hate Gondor, and she told you herself that she planned to wreak vengeance upon my kingdom. It would not surprise me to learn she planned to raid every village along the river's edge in Pinnath Gelin, but the abduction of Thorongil caused her to change this plan. He may prove a useful hostage for the Kindred of the Coins.
'But I am getting ahead of myself. Right now we must bring this unwelcome news to Thorongil's mother Nauriel, and then perhaps we can do something to prevent Nakási from escaping Outer Gondor with Thorongil in her custody.'

'One of the Corsairs, a huge lout with muscles like I have never seen, lifted Thorongil up by one arm and dangled him over the river. \qIs this one of those halflings I have heard about?\q he asked, and Thorongil spat curses at him and said he was named Thorongil and would have all the Corsairs put to death if they didn't unhand him. They laughed at that, oh, did they ever! I can still hear the laughter, it's terrible!
'But there was something about that name they didn't like. \qThorongil, you say?\q the big fellow asked, drawing his sword. I think he would have killed Thorongil then and there, but an Elf among the Corsairs said something to him and his face became like a storm cloud. I couldn't really hear it from where I was hiding, but I think the Elf was saying the captain would want to keep Thorongil onboard her ship.
'The big lout put his sword away and hauled Thorongil onto their boat and they rowed out into the river and then they were gone. I know it was wrong and we shouldn't have come here! But I didn't know how to get out of it, and then it was all over and it was too late! The way they spoke about their captain... it fills me with terror even now!'

'I do not fully understand it, ${PLAYER}. The main Corsair ships must be anchored further down the river, for most of the raiders rowed here in secret, piloting small boats. Why then would they set fire to the hillside as they approached Iáphel, giving away their presence before they reached the village that was their destination?'
You suggest to Elessar that perhaps the Corsairs wanted to inspire fear in the hearts of the villagers, and he nods.
'Perhaps that is the answer. Still, it is good to hear that most of the villagers remain unharmed. We drove the Corsairs back to the river and most of them fled in their small ships. They may seek to return once they have licked their wounds, but I think it more likely they will not attack Iáphel again for some time.
'We should search along the shoreline and ensure that no Corsairs remain here in hiding. It is possible we overlooked some of the fleeing pillagers in our charge down the hill.'

'I'm sorry! I'm sorry!' Orgolas stammers nervously, overcome with fright. 'I told Thorongil it was wrong, and we should not follow the warriors, but he said if we didn't that my father Golasgil would know his heir to be a coward! And I am no coward, ${PLAYER}, but...'

Gwindir, the vintner of Iáphel, sits in a widening red pool and stares at you with glassy eyes, his clothes red-stained. You ask if he is injured, and he shakes his head.
'This is not blood,' he says. 'It is worse! My finest bottles were smashed beyond repair and their contents drained! I pray the King still has the bottles we gifted to him. They are irreplaceable now.'
Gwindir falls silent.

'We are fortunate, my friend. Most of the villagers are unharmed, for the Corsairs set the hillside aflame as they climbed up to the village, and the folk of Iáphel did not delay; they took shelter among these buildings at the first sign of the Corsair approach. Once we have put out the fires, most of the danger should be over.
'Just before you returned, I heard the dwarf Gimli shouting back in the main square. You should ensure he has all in hand; it could be more of the Corsairs hid themselves and thought to do some mischief when our backs were turned.'

'Why should we not burn this grove as a message to the folk of Gondor who live in Anfalas? We have set fire to their ships, but the ships come from elsewhere and are manned by crews selected by the Prince of Dol Amroth and by the King, far away in the White City.
'I say we burn this grove to show they are not safe in their homes. The waves bring us even to their shores, and they are not safe from us.'

'Nestinanessornë left with them, and sailed away on one of their ships. I did not want to fight, and I am glad, hoom, glad that I did not have to.
'But I hope my friend... is safe. He was not yet fully recovered from his wound, and could not hope to oppose the people of the ships... if it came to fighting.'

'I remember the marching ranks of the Orcs! My friends... I have to warn my friends... and the defenders of Helm's Deep...

'You are one of the long-lived ones, like my friend Ferien, hoom. But even poison can bring the Elves low, if it is of a bad sort. The poison used by these burárum, these Orcs, is of a very bad sort indeed. Any others struck by their arrows would have died at once, and never known there was poison to survive. An Elf might last a little longer, but without my Entish medicine you would have perished too. You are, hoom, lucky? Ents do not believe in such a thing, but Ferien used to speak of it to me, hoom, toom. Oh, she did!
'If I had not seen you on my return journey, you would surely be dead now. You have Ferien's luck, little Nestinanessornë. You slept for a long time, and will need to sleep longer if you are to be fully healed. What did Ferien used to say to me? \qYou are not... out of the woods yet...?\q Hoom, boom, toom! Imagine that, Nestinanessornë, hm, hm, hm.'

Leafshade appears in no hurry to speak any further, so you ask about the Elf-bow in the centre of his glade.
'Hrum, hoom! That is the bow of my friend, Nestinanessornë! He left it here when he... went away.'
The Ent sighs heavily, the breeze of his exhalation rustling the leaves of the trees.
'There was a gathering of my folk some... what is the word your kind would use, hm? Months, hoom. Some months ago. On my return, I came across a dying creature suffering from a poisoned wound. He reminded me of an old friend, an Elf I once knew. Ah, Ferien. Hm, hoom. She lived among the beeches, and sang so beautifully. Hoom...'
Leafshade stands in silence, his story unfinished, and you wonder if you should prompt him to continue.

'But you did not know Ferien, hm? No, you would not have. The lives of Ents are measured differently, hoom, hoom. Months! Months are the blink of an eye, or less, hm! I was thinking of Ferien when I carried this wounded creature, this Elf, back here to my home. I did not know if he would live, hoom. For Ferien I would try to save him. In time he did recover his strength, hm, hm, and that is when I named him Nestinanessornë, which is sapling-who-is-healed in the words Ferien taught to me.'

'There have been many strange happenings... of late...' the Ent rumbles. He slowly turns his head to look past the trees of the grove, and falls silent. After a long moment, he seems to realize you are still here. A long, windy sigh escapes from his mouth.
'It is most unusual... for so much to happen... to the Ents,' he murmurs, sleepily.
'I am called...' he begins, and after a time you realize that the sound rolling out among the twigs and branches of the grove, making them restless, is actually a long name spoken languidly in Old Entish.
'But you may call me Lathlum... or Leafshade...' he continues, his voice little more than a sigh.

'Yesterday I saw... the ships return...
'They sailed south until they disappeared... over the horizon...'
Leafshade's words rise in intensity until their booming shakes the branches of the trees of Strangdene.
'I hope you will... ensure Nestinanessornë is safe...'
Leafshade ceases his trumpeting, and quiet returns once again to Tumbamálë.
'He is... a friend...' he murmurs. 'So many others went away...'
You assure Leafshade that you will do what you can to help him, but the Ent says nothing more.

'We have only just arrived at Lond Cirion, ${PLAYER}. Did you learn where the ships are bound?'

'So Nakási does make for Umbar. I was not certain that would be so. It seems she knows the value of her captive to the Kindred of the Coins. But something else troubles you, my friend. I can see it in your expression.'
You tell Elessar, more briefly than it was told to you, of Leafshade's account of the past few months. The King puts a comforting hand on your shoulder.
'Your friend Corudan lives, ${PLAYER}, but he is in need of rescue. As it happens, we were already planning such a mission, for young Thorongil must be freed from his imprisonment as well. I feel in my heart this is the way it must be: both of these captives are being brought to Umbar, the City of the Corsairs. A small party of adventurers might infiltrate the city and rescue Thorongil and Corudan where a larger group must surely fail. I want you to lead this small party, my friend. I know you are the right choice for this task, though it prove most dangerous.
'You say that Corudan's sister Sigileth intended to investigate his disappearance near Helm's Deep? I will send a message to Erkenbrand that she be found and told of these new tidings.'
You cannot tell if Leafshade remains awake or if he has heard your words.

You remember Golasgil at the Battle of the Black Gate as he stood face to face with the mighty Olog that would give him his mortal wound, and you recall his final words.
'If there is a day to come after this,' he said, 'look to the people of Anfalas. Tell them their lord...'
You cannot say for certain what the Lord of Anfalas intended, for then he died, only moments before the fall of the Dark Lord Sauron and the rout of Mordor's armies. You relay his father's words to Orgolas, and Golasgil's heir rubs at a smudge on the floor with his shoe.

'My father's last thoughts were not for himself, or for what he was about to lose, but for the folk of Anfalas, so far away? How can that be true, ${PLAYER}? He left us behind to go to the war. If he truly cared would he not have remained here?'
You remind Orgolas that his father counted his family, his son, and his wife among those people of Anfalas he sought to protect, and it was on their behalf that he followed the King to war. Orgolas sighs again.
'Is that what you are telling me? To be a good ruler, you have to put the needs of your people ahead of your own? Is that what it means to be the son of the Lord of Anfalas? Is that what it means to be the heir of Golasgil? But it is so difficult. Thorongil would cast all that aside and charge off to battle, hoping to achieve glory, and before today I might have done the same. But I am not a fighter, not yet, and if I were seized by Umbar as was Thorongil... what would that mean for the people of Anfalas? I have to stay here. I have to help my mother and be here for my people. My father was a great mariner, and a mighty warrior, but I have not yet grown into the man he was. I must serve my people in another way.'

'I am pleased with the decision of Orgolas, ${PLAYER}. I will not say I expected it with complete certainty, but I believed the son of Golasgil was enough like his father to arrive there after some deliberation. The folk of Anfalas will be in good hands once the Lady Marra instructs her son about what she has learned of rule: a considerable amount!
'But our paths must now diverge, my friend. I charge you with the rescue of Thorongil and of Corudan, and look forward to your successful return aboard the Wave-hunter. Do try not to fan anew the flames of war with Umbar, ${PLAYER}. This must be a mission carried out in secret.'

'I know I can rely on you for this, ${PLAYER}, but you will need a ship to carry you and the crew you choose to bring to Umbar. I have already spoken with Orgolas about this, and have given the heir of Golasgil a number of things to consider, but as you will lead the expedition across the Bay you should be the one to hear what he has decided.
'I believe you will find him in his bedroom, somewhere upstairs.'

You remember finding Golasgil on the Pelennor Fields after the great battle, surrounded by the corpses of the Orcs that ambushed him. You recall too the look on his face when he learned how many of his friends perished before the walls of Minas Tirith, but such sorrow did not keep him from marching to the Black Gate with the Men of the West when his King required it.

'I will remain behind to help protect Anfalas and Pinnath Gelin from further attack by the Corsairs, for that is the best way for me to aid my people... but the King is right that someone must sail to Umbar and rescue Thorongil, if it can be done in secret. He has chosen you for this, ${PLAYER}, but you need a ship.'
Orgolas stands at attention and studies you seriously.
'The Wave-hunter was given to me by my father, and if he had not died in service of Gondor, one day he would have taught me to be a great mariner, as he was. But that was not meant to be. Instead, I give command of the Wave-hunter to you until Thorongil is returned safely to his hall. Use it well and wisely, and may the memory of Golasgil go with you, and fill the sails with wind to speed you on your journey! When Thorongil is rescued, and the threat of the Corsairs is ended, perhaps you will teach me what you have learned of sailing, and I will drive the Wave-hunter upon the Great Sea.
'But that will be in days yet to come! For now I must find how to protect the folk of Anfalas I will one day rule, and that is a lesson I will learn from my mother.'

'This is really happening? When the King asked me to accompany you to Umbar, I thought he was joking. I thought he said it in jest! But it was not so.

'The Wave-hunter was harboured upriver in Pinnath Gelin to protect it from the Corsairs during the War of the Ring; a decision that must have rankled Golasgil even as he saw the need for it. The ship's crew is likely eager to sail again, and you will need their talents and knowledge of the Bay to bring you to Umbar in secret.
'But your arrival at the City of the Corsairs will only be your mission's beginning, ${PLAYER}. To that end, I suggest you add to the Wave-hunter's complement of sailors such folk as you can trust or as have a stake in the quest's successful conclusion. You will not be able to keep Nauriel away, I think, and as a Knight of the Green Hills her combat prowess may be of use to you. Legolas and Gimli will go with you gladly, of course, and I think Sirgon of Pelargir will be no less eager to sail again; his knowledge of the Bay and of the folk that dwell along its shores may prove valuable. If you believe that Corudan's sister Sigileth will begin her search for him at Helm's Deep, the messages I have dispatched to Erkenbrand should reach her, and she will likely make her way to Gondor as soon as she can.
'There is another you should add to your crew, my friend, but I advise you to watch him carefully. I speak of the Corsair Jajax. It may be helpful to have him near as you adventure in Umbar... if you can trust him. Now bid farewell to the travelling company, ${PLAYER}, for we each have our own roads to walk and it may be some time before we see each other again.'

'Good fortune go with you, ${PLAYER}, and may you rescue the young heir of Pinnath Gelin from his captivity.
'You need not take my advice, but if you have a willing ear I might suggest that you bring my brothers with you when you assemble your crew. Elladan and Elrohir remained behind to aid the folk in Pinnath Gelin for a few days, but I know that they would be happy to accompany you when they have done there what they wanted.'

'Dearie me, ${PLAYER}, do take care of yourself! I hope the things I have heard about the City of the Corsairs are untrue, for it sounds a frightful and violent place! How do Corsairs behave when they are at home? I cannot even imagine!'
You tell Ioreth that your mission is supposed to be a secret, and she gives you a dramatic wink.
'My lips will remain sealed. You can count on me!'
She suddenly smacks her forehead with one palm.
'It is going to be very warm there. You will need to dress for the weather! A change of clothes may be warranted, ${PLAYER}! Umbar, can you imagine?'

'I understand you are leaving us, ${PLAYER}? Good luck to you, and to young Thorongil, the heir of Pinnath Gelin! I hope you are right, and the Corsairs will not harm their young captive. I would volunteer to come with you if I was not charged with maintaining the provisions for the King's travelling party, but what use could I be on such a quest? I am no fighter.
'But I do know food, ${PLAYER}. The fruits of Umbar are apples, dates, figs, grapes, melons, and plums. Vegetables include beets, cabbage, eggplant, fennel, onions, and turnips. The diet of the Umbarrim contains a great deal of fish and shellfish, but also beef, goat, mutton, and poultry, in lesser quantities.
'I don't suppose that helps you at all? I will miss you, friend.'

'You are leaving us on a secret errand, ${PLAYER}? Ioreth says you go to rescue young Thorongil from the Kindred of the Coins? No, do not seek to deny it! We both know it is true.
'If you do encounter any members of this Kindred, do not stay the killing stroke! They need to be taught not to interfere with the rule of Gondor.'
You tell Aphadaer you hope to rescue Thorongil without undue bloodshed, and he snorts.
'I am sure that is your hope, but nothing so risky was ever accomplished without bloodshed. When it proves impossible, you will remember my words, I warrant.'

'Farewell, ${PLAYER}! Líniel and I will watch out for the King on his return to Minas Tirith. You take care of yourself, for my heart tells me you are about to be in far greater danger than the rest of us!'

'I hope you know what you are doing, ${PLAYER}. Ioreth says you plan to sail to Umbar, and most of what I have heard of that place is... frightening. The King says Sauron is gone, and I have no reason to think he is wrong about that, but Sauron was worshipped for a long time in the City of the Corsairs. Can you be certain his cult is gone?
'Glindor and I will do what we can to keep the King safe. I hope the crew you assemble for your mission will do the same for you!'

Faranil, seeking more information on the sapling that you are raising, directed you to Ost Guruth, an outpost in the Lone-lands, where Radagast the Brown has been seen. She bid you visit him and share your tale of discovering and nurturing the sapling.

'Your continued efforts should not be empty. My frustration with my own limitations grows, but I believe that there is one to whom we can turn for assistance.'
She offers a light tilt of her head.
'Last I heard, Radagast the Brown, who is a staunch ally of nature, is in a tower in the Lone-lands within a settlement called Ost Guruth.
'I would have you visit him to explain your find and our actions thus far. He might provide his insight to us.
'Perhaps this master of the natural world can explain what it is that we are seeing.'

Radagast nods his head when your tale is done.
'I know of what you speak, the woodland is home to many such oddities. Oddities, no, that is the wrong word. Wonders. That is the word. Wonders that should be celebrated.
'You found a child. You are nurturing the child. I cannot say what the child will become, but it is clear that you discovered something that recognized, in you, a purity which it sought. So, it signaled to you, and you responded. A noble thing. A wondrous thing.
'You must continue your effort and know that your influence over the sapling will only grow. What you do for your newly found progeny will help it grow into a noble creature. It will not do so on its own. Too often the corruption of the land seeps through the roots and spoils the good in such things.
'I recall, in a swamp, far from here.... well, not so far, but far enough that I cannot simply walk there now, there was such a creature poisoned, corrupted, withered from its true purpose by a vileness that pervaded all that surrounded it. I wondered. \qWhat would you become were you not so befouled?\q It could not answer, of course, given how forsaken it was from nature. But, I hoped it would say a splendid creature that would give as it had received.
'Alas, it was not to be. You have another choice, ${PLAYER}. Do not spoil it. See your effort through and remain as true to the end as you were at the start.'
'I am in awe at this insight. Could it be that he speaks of the huorns? Have you rescued a sapling huorn? I agree with the Brown Wizard, friend. We should keep the path.'

'Elrond knows much of our history and stores more of it within the libraries of the Last Homely House. Please, take your tale to him and learn what he might know and then return to me.'

Elrond listens to your tale intently. Then he looks about him and when he speaks, it is as if he conjures the very trees that surround Rivendell.
'Your tale, friend, is one of interest and wonder. A sapling that stirs at your passage is a thing of which I have not heard since the Great Forest covered nearly all of Middle-earth. It is a rare thing these days. This portent and your involvement in it, must have greater meaning than any have yet discovered.'
Elrond pauses and then shakes his head.
'Yet, friend, there is nothing more I can offer you or the patron who assists you in the Ettenmoors.'
Sensing your disappointment, he continues.
'Do not despair.
'This is a good omen. Perhaps the land is healing, though the battle still persists. Go with that knowledge, and the hope that the tomorrow you make for the sapling you have found will be one of bright light.'

'I hoped that we would learn more, but Elrond is correct.'
She stiffens and smiles.
'We should not despair.
'Your discovery does have meaning, even if we have not yet determined what that meaning is.
'Onward friend.'

'There is something happening with the sapling, I think, friend. There is someone else with whom we must speak.'
Faranil looks somewhat melancholy.
'Seeking them out is a step that I must admit, I fear. Their sorrow is the sorrow of their entire kind.
'I only hope that they understand that this is not a sign of anything more than a new hope. I can only hope that we will give them a different type of hope and not a measure of false one.
'In a copse of trees, on the far side of Lake Evendim there is an Ent named Quickbough. Go to them. Tell them what you have found and all that we have learned.'

Quickbough stares, for what seems like several minutes, at the sapling. Suddenly, the sapling wiggles and Quickbough's eyes go wide.
'Hroom, throom, shoom.
'Not an Enting, no.
'Still... we will weep for the loss we suffer.
'But this... hroom...
'This little one... is... hope for a future...
'And you... throom... thrumm... humm...
'Have... made this... possible...'
You are not sure, but it appears that Quickbough's eye well with tears.
'Thank you... little one.
'Thrumm....'

'The Ents suffer a heavy loss. A sadness for what they have lost. Perhaps, this gift you discovered is a gift of a different kind. Perhaps it is the last gift left for the Ents. 'Ah, ${PLAYER}, was it? I am Annúngil, master of the wharf here in Dol Amroth. I heard you were instrumental in helping to break the siege on Dol Amroth. When word came of King Elessar's victory at Pelargir, the Corsairs here turned tail and sailed away fast as could be. We gave chase to some of them, of course, but mostly we were simply happy to see them go.
'However, in recent days, odd things have started failing on the ships that are docked here. Rigging pins slip their posts and tightly woven ropes snap like yarn. I have begun to suspect that we did not chase all of the enemy from our bay. I wonder if you might be able to assist. I need someone who can discreetly inspect pins and ropes on the ship moored here. 'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. What have you there for me?'
You hand him the accounts book and explain what happened. Angbor's face grows grave and he is silent for a few moments.
'Her methods were wrong, but I must think about how to deal with the situation. In the meantime, I will review the accounts you brought me to see what other rotten apples may be in this barrel. I thank you for your assistance with this.'

'You there! I charge you with assisting Calembel!'
As you draw near, the guard straightens and looks around to see if anyone is listening.
'I recognize you - word of your deeds has even reached those of us who spend most of our days underground. Dúnach, the other guard who works at the prison with me, has gone missing. I cannot leave my post any longer to search for him, but perhaps you could keep an eye out for him?'

'Relax, I shan't try to run from you. Yes, I killed Dúnach, and I would do it again, even knowing he'd wound me in return. But this cut across my flesh is as to nothing compared to that which he dealt my heart. Dúnach is the reason that the foul murderer Candúr was allowed to break free of Calembel's prison. That cur slayed my husband Horthir on his way to escape towards the mountains! I vowed to avenge Horthir, and so have I done. I will stand trial if I must, but I could not let Dúnach set any more prisoners free. Here, take this.'
She reaches a shaking hand into a pocket and withdraws a small book.
'I searched Dúnach's house one day while he was on duty and found this. It's an accounting of prisoners he has let free in return for bribes. How many other murderers, thieves, and traitors did he allow to slip their bonds?! If we cannot trust the law, we must take what measures we must.
'I will accept judgement, but I beg you bring this book to Lord Angbor and let him be the one who decides my fate. Go now. Eliaril is about to sew me shut and I do not wish for an audience.'

Fingaer has asked you to speak with soldiers in the Keep of the Swan-knights.
The Keep of the Swan-knights is in Dol Amroth.
You have listened to many stories from the soldiers in the Swan-knight's Keep. You should bring these stories to Fingaer who is waiting for you in Harper's Court.

'Stories of the battlefield, you say?'
She is quiet for some time.
'It was important. We did not really have a choice, did we? It was go to war or die, or go to war and die, as many of my friends, my family did. But we could not just wait for them to take our country and our lands, to kill and slaughter as they washed over us like a dark wave. It was important that I went, that we went. I just wish more of us had come back. But it was important.'

'The war? For a bard? I... I do not really remember it, truly. I think I do not want to. It comes in flashes to me in dreams - the noise of it. There is always a lot of noise. My captain yelling, the snarls of the Enemy, the sounds of metal on metal, or worse, on skin. The cries of the wounded, the horns propelling us forward - beacons of hope when it seemed all was lost.
'I do not wish to remember, but I fear I will never forget. I am just glad that we have won. My only hope is that none may ever need to experience such things again. Perhaps, because I and others met that bloody host on the field, our children will know peace. Perhaps none other will again have to carry these memories.'

'Wel- AACHOO! -come back. Do you have tales for me to write about?'
You pass along the stories you heard from the swan-knights. The bard's face grows pensive as you speak.
'It seems that along with glory, there is also much darkness in war. Too often our songs sing only of the honour to be won, the renown one might gain. You have given me much to think about, ${PLAYER}. I shall endeavour to write a song that encapsulates both the glory and the horrors of war, lest we are urged to go too soon to battle when other ways might suffice.
'Do not get me wrong, for our knights were fighting for the very world itself. But it is good to know of, and to share, both sides of this coin. You have my thanks for bringing me these tales.'

'Well met! I am ...achooo! Oh, pardon me. Do pardon me. I am not ill, merely suffering from having walked here by way of the stables. You see, horses make me incredibly ill, and Dol Amroth has them stuffed into every nook and cranny.'
The bard's words are interrupted by a procession of sneezes. He blows his nose noisily and smiles at you with watery eyes.
'Ahem. I am Fingaer, minstrel extraordinaire, and it is my calling to write about the great and glorious battles in which our brave swan-knights partook. ACHHOO! However, it is also my curse not to be able to get close enough to them without setting myself sneezing for days. Say, if you were to make your way to the Keep of the Swan-knights and listen to their tales for me, I would reward you for your time. What do you s...s…ssssSACHOO… say?'

'Well met. You seek stories of the battlefield? I wish I could tell you I was a hero and did great deeds, but in truth, I was sick with fever and never made it out of camp. You will not find tales of glory from me, I am afraid.'

'Tales of battle for a bard? Songs cannot but hope to encapsulate the glory, the terror, the rush of steel upon steel and the fear of the flesh in the presence of it all. There were Orcs and feral Men, flashes of blood and metal and fur, fighting by tooth and fang and claw. It was a thing I shall never forget... and from which my dreams will never be safe.'

'You wish to know of the battlefield? I have much to say, of course! Why, I myself was responsible for bringing down six Orcs! One after the other, they fell at my hand!
'I was even lucky enough to find myself back to back with Prince Imrahil at one point! We were set upon by a pack of vicious warriors, but they had nothing on my lord! You should have seen the way he swung his sword! Like it weighs nothing at all! His foes fell in great numbers before him - piled around us in droves!
'Glad am I that I was able to serve and save these lands, my Prince, and our King.'

'Everyone tells me what a help you have been today. If ever you decide to build a home in Gondor, come see me about sourcing your timber. I'm sure I could offer a more than fair price after everything you've done for us.'
'Greetings, friend! This camp has languished for too long, and there is much to do. Speak with others around the camp and see what they need.'

'Greetings, I am Calpheth, pottery merchant and worried daughter. My father, Myldil, was supposed to bring a shipment of pottery up to the city today, but he has yet to show.
'I am sure that he is fine, as he is wont to get distracted while working with the clay, but if you are heading down to Lothgobel, would you be so kind as to look for him? There are still dangerous folk lingering about Tathrendalf, and I fear my father may wander too close to their camp in search of supplies for his craft.'

'Huh? Who are you? Can you not see that I am busy?'
You explain that his daughter sent you to inquire after him.
'Calpheth? Oh, was that today? Well, I cannot go up to Calembel today, I have far too much to do! The weather is perfect for throwing pottery, so she will just have to wait.
'Hmm, you seem to have nothing better to do than interrupt old men working - why don't you make yourself useful!
'Since Calpheth is so worried, I will stay put and finish what I am working on while you gather me up some more clay. You should also head north and mine some quartz. I do not always need it, but I think this batch of pots will come out fine enough to need the very best glaze. Go on now! Go away so I can get back to this.'

'What? You're back already?'
He pauses to squint up at the sky.
'Oh, I suppose it has been a while. When the clay is working and flowing in your hands, you lose all sense of time, don't you? Well, I do. Hmph.'

You hand over the bite-ridden pack. Drambor's eyes widen when he sees the damage, and he hurriedly opens the pack's flap to peer inside. When he sees the missives within, he sighs dramatically, his shoulders sagging with relief.
'They're intact! And not covered in avanc drool. Oh, thank you, thank you!'

'Pssst, ${PLAYER}. Can I talk to you?'
You take a few steps to the side with Drambor so he can speak quietly to you.
'Having father home has been really wonderful, but even though he left me in charge of Calembel when he went to war, I think he thinks I'm still just a little kid. I've been volunteering to bring messages from the city to the two beacons to show him how responsible I am, but...'
He glances at his father Angbor and lowers his voice so much that you can barely hear him.
'Well, you see, I was on my way back from the beacons with a bag full of missives for my father when I was attacked by some annoyingly aggressive avanc. I managed to get away, but they snatched my bag from me! I haven't told him yet that I've lost it, but maybe with your help I won't have to!
'Can you look for it? Uhm, I admit I'm not sure I remember exactly where I lost it. There was a waterfall nearby! I remember that much! Listen, it was dark, all right? There is nothing you can do for the dying Corsair, but he has asked you to take his war-hound Kakhât with you.
You should approach Kakhât.

'Nothing you can do will hurt me, stranger. I'll be gone soon. Curse the warmongers that took me so far from home. May the seas take them all! May they --'
Whatever the Corsair intends to say next devolves into a series of dry, rattling coughs.
'Still listening to this dying man's last words? Then...' With a trembling hand, he reaches out to pet his war-hound. 'Take this whistle, and Kakhât will follow. He was never made for war. He doesn't deserve the same sad end that I do.
'Leave me, Kakhât. Go.'

'Had I known what was happening at that camp-fire... but I did not, and he was beyond help. To die nameless and forsaken in an unfamiliar place... I only hope your actions gave him some semblance of peace.'
Halnith reaches down to gently pet the hound, who only responds with a tired thump of his tail.
'I daresay he's found his new home.' A smile breaks across Halnith's face. 'Guarding the beacon doesn't sound like such a lonely task anymore.'
Kakhât sniffs your hand. Before the hound leaves his master's side, he looks to him -- for further commands, perhaps. But the Corsair utters no more words.
Kakhât abruptly trots over to Halnith's side and lies down. Something tells you that even if you used the whistle to call him, he would simply refuse to listen.

'For the last few days, smoke has been rising from Makham Mijann, perhaps from a single camp-fire. I can't imagine anyone would be eager to hide out in an abandoned Corsair war-camp, unless they held some sort of ill intent.
'Obviously, I cannot leave my post, but I see that you're quite familiar with adventuring. Will you investigate in my stead?'

'It's beautiful, isn't it? I do not have much time left — oh do not give me that look. I have lived a long and kind life. I have loved and been loved, and I have the privilege of passing in a time of peace. That is more than most can claim.
'If fate were to indulge me, this view would be the last thing I see before I go.'

'I do not remember much these days, but I remember you,' Borhador says by way of greeting.
His voice trembles and he has given up on stilling the tremor in his hands, but his spirit is brighter than you've seen before.
'Have you seen my sons? I'm very proud of them. I was afraid that when Dervorin came home, he and Arvaethor would quarrel over the lordship of the Vale, but it is as if the thought never crossed their minds. It does me good to see them working so hard for the people we are charged to protect, oh and Laerind too, of course, of course. She reminds me of my Halwen sometimes, yes, with her cleverness and fortitude. I am glad my Arvaethor has found a remarkable partner in her. If only Dervorin would settle down with someone. Hmm... are you wed? Ah forgive me, I do tend to ramble, a symptom of my age, no doubt.'
The awareness in his eyes flickers and he falls silent. He looks through you for a few long moments until some spark brings him back to the present.
'I remember that the last time you were here, the sky was so very angry. Now look at it. Look upon the beauty of the Vale in kinder light. Look upon Ethring as it was meant to be seen.'

'Welcome back to the Vale, my friend. I must thank you for looking after Dervorin at Minas Tirith and beyond. The tales he tells of those battles still the rhythm of my heart. It does me good to know a hero such as yourself was there on the field with him.
'But speaking of family, my father Borhador would love to see you. Now that it's no longer overrun with spiders, he spends much of his time at the beacon of Eilendoth. You can find him there.
'How have I been? Since the war ended, many of our fighting men have returned home. The luckiest have adjusted to the peace. Others have brought the war home with them. Laerind and I are doing our best to help. It is difficult work, distressing at times, but better than dealing with the Dead again.'

'Every day that passes brings my son further into danger, ${PLAYER}. There must be no more delay.
'I will join the crew of the Wave-hunter so I may ask the Kindred of the Coins to return Thorongil, but I will ask only once. If they refuse I will bloody my sword and dent my shield on their carcasses! They have remained unused for too long, anyway. My husband Carandolion always speaks of the need for patience, and for thinking things through, but see where that has gotten us! Our son stolen away by enemies of Gondor! Well, they have made an enemy of Nauriel, and she does not forgive as readily as Gondor. Recruit the crew you think we will need for the voyage, ${PLAYER}, but remember the need I have for haste.
'Will you retrieve my sword and shield from the armoury on the lower level? I have had the sword sharpened and the shield reinforced since the Corsairs raided Tûm Rost, and they should now be ready for me.'

'Will you retrieve my sword and shield from the armoury on the lower level? I have had the sword sharpened and the shield reinforced since the Corsairs raided Tûm Rost, and they should now be ready for me.'

'I am no fighter, ${PLAYER}, but that does not mean I do not want my son safely returned to his home. My wife has always been the firebrand, and she has temper enough for the both of us! But she matches it, nay, she exceeds it, with her martial skill. There are none more deadly in all the Green Hills with a blade than she!
'I am unlike my brother, you know. Duinhir rode to Minas Tirith with trumpets and banners, and when he came back he did so without his sons, for they were of fighting age. My Thorongil was not, but he has been taken away all the same, and now I must rely upon my dangerous wife to retrieve him. Do I risk losing them both? These are the thoughts that keep me awake at night, ${PLAYER}.
'I will remain here to oversee Pinnath Gelin while Nauriel is away, but my thoughts will sail alongside her as she rides the waves to Umbar. I will give her a favour to carry into battle, so she knows her husband's heart goes with her.'
'My husband was looking for you. Return to the lowest level and find him.'

'Thank you for bringing me my equipment, ${PLAYER}, and for speaking with my husband. I will carry his favour into battle on behalf of our son Thorongil, should battle prove necessary. My husband would be the first to tell you he is no fighter, but I love him all the more for it. I do our fighting for us, and without regret.
'Carandolion will see that Pinnath Gelin does not suffer in my absence, and when I return I will return with our son, and only his father will celebrate more loudly and happily than I.
'I will await your command, and the rest of your crew, at the Wave-hunter.'

'I hope my remedy does help your dwarf friend. Sea-sickness is not a pleasant thing for anyone.'

'I hope possession of this remedy will ease the turmoil of Gimli's stomach when the Wave-hunter sets out! He may not even need to ingest it, if he knows it is near-at-hand and might be taken if necessary. I will not tell him of the chance that it will do nothing, unless he asks directly. I will not lie to my friend, but this information can do no good in advance and may instead do harm.
'There was no need for you to come all this way to speak with me, ${PLAYER}! I of course will join you on your mission. The sea-longing has me and will not abate, but I understand the Wave-hunter will remain in the Bay and not pass out into the Great Sea. There are still things for me to see and to do before I begin that last voyage, and I count high in that number aiding you in the rescue of young Thorongil from the clutches of the Kindred of the Coins.
'I will be pleased to join your crew, my friend. Both I and Gimli will meet you by the Wave-hunter when you are ready to depart.'

'Legolas inquired on my behalf, seeking a remedy for it, and learned that an herbalist in Melgobas may prepare a suitable concoction. Will you go there and see if it is ready, and you may also ask the Elf if he desires to join your crew as well. I assume he will, but you should ask him yourself.'

'I know why you are here, my friend, and of course I will agree to sail with you into danger! I hope you did not expect me to refuse! But I have set foot upon one too many boats for my liking in these past few months, ${PLAYER}. I simply do not like them. Show me a dwarf who does and I will be very surprised!
'The folk hereabout say that the Bay is generally calm... generally... but I know that even the calmest waters can shake a boat to its very foundation. Do I say foundation? A boat has no such thing, and tosses and turns at the merest whim of the waves! Sea-sickness is a concern, friend.
'Legolas inquired on my behalf, seeking a remedy for it, and learned that an herbalist in Melgobas may prepare a suitable concoction. Will you go there and see if it is ready, and you may also ask the Elf if he desires to join your crew as well. I assume he will, but you should ask him yourself.'

'A sea-sickness remedy? You are the second person to ask for such a concoction today. The first was an Elf, and I will tell you what I told him: the effectiveness of such an elixir varies depending upon the person who takes it, and what works for one may not work for another. I do not give back the purchase price in the event you are dissatisfied!
'I sent the Elf to collect some Langstrand flowers and beast parts from the creatures hereabout, and while he has not yet returned, if you perform the same task as he the work may be finished more quickly. I make use of parts from crawlers, aurochs, and crabs in the various unguents and potions I create, and will appreciate any you bring back to me.'

'I sent the Elf to collect some Langstrand flowers and beast parts from the creatures hereabout, and while he has not yet returned, if you perform the same task as he the work may be finished more quickly. I make use of parts from crawlers, oxen, and crabs in the various unguents and potions I create, and will appreciate any you bring back to me.'

'Thank you for bringing me these; they will not all be used in the same mixture, but I assure you they will all be used in something! Your friend returned shortly before you did, and I have given him the sea-sickness remedy I promised. I give to you the same warning I gave him: it may not have the desired effect upon the dwarf for whom it is intended! It truly does vary based on the individual, and if it does not work as you expect it is not a failing of the potion, or of she who brewed it!
'But I hope it does help him. Sea-sickness is not a pleasant thing for anyone.'

'My wife and son want to speak to you. They think I am too old to be of use, but I tell you they are wrong.'

'It will be just like the old days, ${PLAYER}, when I sailed the waves and risked life and limb against the harsh elements! Oh, you never feel so alive as when you stand on the deck of a ship; any mariner will tell you so!
'I will meet you beside the Wave-hunter when you are ready to depart. I look forward to meeting the rest of your crew, my friend! Together we will rescue young Thorongil, and no Corsair shall prevent us... and live!'
'I will continue to perform my duties as Lord of Lebennin while my father sails with you on your voyage. Please return him safely at the end of your mission, ${PLAYER}!'
'Please watch out for my husband on your voyage. I do worry, even as I know he cannot stay.'

'I have already packed my trunk, hoping beyond hope that a ship would have need of an old sailor for its crew. By the Valar, it has come to pass! Will you bring the trunk in here for me? It is in the southern dining room of my manor.'
Sirgon, the sea-longing lord, has joined your crew!
Sirgon is delighted you have brought him his trunk
Sirgon already packed his trunk, and he wants you to carry it to him from the southern dining room.
Sirgon is inside his keepsake room in the northern part of his manor.
Celebros and Faltharan are in Sirgon's manor, and will want to speak to you.

'You return from your tour of Gondor with the King, and so quickly? What brings you back to my manor with such haste, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Sirgon of what befell young Thorongil of Pinnath Gelin, and of the mission to bring him safely back from Umbar. His eyes light up and he eagerly grasps your hand.
'I will be delighted to join your crew, my friend! I confess to you that thoughts of the Sea have occupied my dreams, and even my waking thoughts have dwelt upon it! Ever since I spoke with King Elessar and stepped down as the Lord of Lebennin I have desired to sail once again! My son Faltharan will take up the charge of rebuilding the vessels of the Gondorian navy; he is already well-acquainted with what must be done.
'I have a further confession: I have already packed my trunk, hoping beyond hope that a ship would have need of an old sailor for its crew. By the Valar, it has come to pass! Will you bring the trunk in here for me? It is in the southern dining room of my manor.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}! Tell me about the ship we will be sailing to Umbar! Ah, it has been too long!'
You tell Sirgon what you know about the Wave-hunter, little as it is, and he nods eagerly.
'Golasgil of Anfalas was a mariner of great skill and ability. I knew him well, and we sailed together more than once. I believe he was as I am: a man of the Sea, but one whose duties called him away from the waves, to his great regret. I remember him fondly. It is right that his prized vessel will bear us to Umbar on the King's mission.
'My wife and son will want to speak to you. They think I am too old to be of use, but I tell you they are wrong.'

'I understand you will sail with my father to Umbar on a mission of some secrecy, ${PLAYER}? No, I do not ask for any of the details. I think I have expected him to depart ever since I agreed to take over his duties as Lord of Lebennin. At least this seems to be on the King's behalf; my mother told me privately that she feared my father might sneak aboard a merchant ship and vanish in the night, just to set sail again. I do not think he would go so far... but it is better this way, I think.
'Do what you can to keep him safe, my friend. He is not the man he was in his youth, when he freely sailed the Bay of Belfalas at the Steward's command, and challenged Corsair ships among the waves.'

'My husband believes he is still the same man he was when he commanded the fleets of Gondor, but it is not so. Time marches onward, and while his mind is as sharp as ever it was, my Sirgon has lived long since those days.'
You ask Celebros if she wishes for you to withdraw your request, and she shakes her head.
'I do not ask this of you, for I know he can be of great help to you and to King Elessar; I do not say he should remain behind, for I believe it would do him an injury, ${PLAYER}. Aye, being left behind while others sail again on such an urgent mission would deal him a grave hurt, perhaps his last.
'He is a sailor, my Sirgon, and he has always been a sailor. He must go with you. But do keep a watchful eye on him, ${PLAYER}. I do worry, even as I know he cannot stay.'
The Crew: The Sea-longing Lord

'Why 'The Bolt-holes?'' This from a younger woman in hand-me-down armour and threadbare boots.
Her travelling companion, whose grey cloak obscured her appearance, worked some jerky in the corner of her mouth before answering. 'If the guard are after you, you bolt into a hole. You know, to hide. So if you commit a crime in Ethring or Barad Rill, 'The Bolt-holes' are where you go when you need to hide.'
'I suppose…'
'You don't like the name?'
'I think it sounds silly. Out east I heard there's a group of bandits making camp in a place called 'Thama Aklam'. That sounds so much more impressive.'
Grey Cloak sighed. 'It only sounds more impressive because the name isn't in Westron. Everyone who knows only one tongue thinks words from other languages to be dramatic and special just because they sound different. 'Thama Aklam' likely means something boring like 'The Big Camp.'
'As if you know more than one language,' Threadbare Boots scoffed.
'I do,' Grey Cloak said. 'For example, Nustatyë ve linquë tauramundo.'
'What does that mean?'
'It means, 'Your beauty outmatches the stars themselves' in Quenya.'
'Oh,' Threadbare Boots said, blushing. 'I think you are beautiful too.'

A Blackroot Delicacy

'Ah, you have them. Thank you!
'That ought to be enough to make a few pots of stew at least. Venison is pleasant enough, I'll admit, but I prefer a bit of variety in my meals. You understand, don't you? And there truly is nothing quite like these silkencaps!

Silkencaps, a pale mushroom native to the Blackroot Vale, can be found in the caverns of Lhingroth in the hills to the south-east of Sardol.
Sidharan has asked you to collect silkencaps from the caverns of Lhingroth, but he has warned you that spiders dwell in Lhingroth. You should collect the silkencaps and deliver them to Sidharan in Sardol.

'Ho there! It was ${PLAYER}, right?
'I remember the last time you were here—all that nasty business with spiders and the Dead! But that is in the past, and now, we have welcomed some of our proud bowmen back to Sardol. I only wish more of them had made it home from the War....'
Sidharan pauses for a moment and sighs.
'There are joys still be found, though, and one of mine is a delicious mushroom stew that my neighbour Garthwen makes every so often. Garthwen's a brilliant cook, though she's far too modest to say as much. For her stew, she uses a mushroom native to the Blackroot Vale that we call a silkencap on account of its pale hue. The trouble is that silkencaps only grow in a few places, but they are most plentiful in Lhingroth. I don't think I need to remind you that the spiders of Tarlang's Peaks can also be found within those caverns, but Garthwen's supply has run out. It may not be as dire a problem as the Dead or the Corsairs, but I would appreciate your aid just the same, my friend. Little joys are what keep us together, after all.
'Would you collect some silkencaps for me and Garthwen?'

Sabiendo ahora cómo se desarrolló la batalla en la orilla, deberías hablar con el marinero.
