'I am sorry about my mother - well, she was my husband's mother. He was a knight but... he did not return from the war.
'Megorneth has been full of rage since, and having our farm overrun by all sorts of beasts and brigands has done nothing to alleviate her pain. I thank you for your help.'

'I am sorry about my mother - well, she was my husband's mother. He was a knight but... he did not return from the war.
'Megorneth has been full of rage since, and having our farm overrun by all sorts of beasts and brigands has done nothing to alleviate her pain. I thank you for your help.'

'Who are you?! Here to plunder our farm too, are you?'
The younger woman places a gentle hand on the elder's arm and tries to sooth her. Cúronel says, 'I do not think they're one of the thieves, mother. I think they may be here to help.'
The elder woman glares up at you, saying, 'If that's the case, go kill as many of the thieves as you can! We may not be able to live here anymore, but I won't see our farm plundered!'

'You come bearing boar belly? Ah, how wonderful. I would not have been able to gather so much on my own. I will make mother's favourite dish tonight with some of this, and prepare the rest for curing.
'You have my thanks!'

'I like braised boar belly, but mother likes when I prepare it with herbs and wine, and roll it with twine and then bake it until crispy. I admit, I do also enjoy it prepared as such. At least these boars will be useful, especially if we can drive them out before they do too much damage.'

'Greetings, traveller. I am Cúronel, and I am sorry I can not welcome you fully to our farm. It has sadly been overrun by boars and brigands, and without my husband about to help drive them off, we have had to abandon our home. I have come here with my husband's mother to see if they've moved on, but no, they've made themselves quite at home... at our home.
'If you are going on ahead, will you bring me back cuts of boar meat? The fatty belly meat, in particular. I can prepare it so that it will last a good long time, and help see us through this. But take care, some of the boars seem to be ailing and their meat would be foetid. Just put those ones down, but bring boar belly from the others.'

'¿A eso llamas cantares marineros?
'¿Oh, te crees algún tipo de ${PLAYERNAME:Marinero[m]|Marinerqa[f]}, eh? ¿Has estado siquiera en el Mar alguna vez?'
Bill Helechal suelta una miserable risotada.
'Debería mandarte a la cárcel por torturar a esta buena gente con esa voz espantosa tuya, . ¿No es así, Harry?'
Harry Goatleaf asiente, aunque notas cierta renuencia en ello.
'¡O quizá debería ahorrarles la molestia!'

'¿Estás bien, ?'
'Perdona que haya intervenido, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}, pero no puedo permitir ese comportamiento en el Poney. Estoy seguro de que te habrías defendido admirablemente, pero este es un establecimiento respetable. Bill debería saber comportarse, aunque supongo que eso nunca lo ha detenido. Después de ese numerito, ¡tendrá suerte si consigue sus bebidas al triple del precio!
'Y no te tomes a pecho lo que dijo el viejo Bill. Mucha gente aquí, incluyéndome, disfrutó de tus cantares. No siempre tengo buen oído para la canción, ¡pero hasta yo me descubrí moviendo el pie detrás del mostrador!'
Barliman Butterbur sonríe amablemente.
'De hecho, ¿cantarías unos cuantos más para nosotros? Solo hasta que pare la lluvia, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}.'

Tengo muchos clientes esta noche, así que ¿por qué no actúas por todo el salón? ¿Por qué no empiezas por la entrada? 'No, ${PLAYER}. Tampoco creo que sea el Ectheldur. Algo no está bien...'
Tarneth mira alrededor, y un repentino crujido cerca de los árboles del islote llama su atención.
'Espera... ¿oíste eso?'

'¿Estás... estás bien, ${PLAYER}?'
Tarneth se toma un momento para recuperar el aliento.
'Si lo que Naegir dijo es cierto, entonces nos han tomado por tontos. Todo esto fue en vano, ¿no es así?'
Tarneth patea la arena.
'Todo en vano...'

'Bueno, bueno, ¿qué tenemos aquí?'
Naegir te mira con desdén.
'Se nota que seguiste mi mapa, ¿eh? Un trabajo ingenioso, ese. Tuve que dibujar tantos, pero sabía que atraparíamos a uno de esos Montaraces tarde o temprano.
'Sé que estos restos no son del Ectheldur. Si estoy en lo correcto, está en el fondo del lago, justo al sur de este islote. Supuse que si estuviera sobre el agua, habría sido saqueado hace siglos. Dejé fuera ese detalle, claro, pero ahora que sabemos dónde está, estoy seguro de que mi gente encontrará la forma de llegar a él. Deberían, al menos.
'¡Estuve tan cerca, sabes! Solo necesitaba un poco de ayuda para orientarme, y ustedes dos hicieron un buen trabajo guiándonos hasta aquí.'
Naegir sonríe con burla.
'No puedo agradecértelo lo suficiente.'

'Lo hemos logrado, ${PLAYER}. Fue un viaje más largo de lo que esperaba, pero tu remo fue una bendición. Después de todo, no me entusiasmaba la idea de cruzar el Lago Evendim nadando.
'Según pude discernir, el mapa de Naegir parecía señalar este islote, así que veamos qué podemos encontrar.'

'Nunca antes había conocido a la Dama Azul. Y que se me conceda el bastón forestal de Alwedion... es un honor más grande de lo que jamás imaginé.
'Me alegra que nuestra búsqueda no haya sido en vano, y más aún que sepamos el destino real del Ectheldur. Me reconforta saber que permanecerá fuera del alcance de los saqueadores de tumbas del sur.

Instancia: El Favor de las Estrellas
'Creo que es hora de que naveguemos de regreso a Mekhem-bizru, ${PLAYER}.'

'¡Ah, el Saervig es un buen barco. Y mira, el mismo Durin nos saluda!'
Byrski se detiene un momento para mirar alrededor en las cubiertas del Saervig.
'¡Muy bien! Comencemos nuestra búsqueda de la Corona de Durin, ${PLAYER}. Y recuerda, buscas siete estrellas con forma de corona. Yo empezaré por aquí, así que ¿por qué no miras desde babor?'

'¡! ¿Estás bien?
Estabas mirando hacia el Lago Espejo y luego me pareció que te quedaste perdido en una profunda ensoñación. ¿Es algo común? No quiero alarmarte, ¡pero han pasado casi diez minutos! ¿Qué ocurrió? ¿Viste la Corona de Durin?'
Le dices a Byrski que fuiste envuelto en una luz brillante, y que su calidez elevó tu espíritu y te dio un renovado sentido de propósito como ${PLAYERNAME:Marinero[m]|Marinera[f]}. Sugieres que podría haber sido la legendaria Estrella de Eärendil, aunque no estás ${PLAYERNAME:seguro[m]|segura[f]}.
'¿La Estrella de Eärendil? Pensé que era solo un viejo cuento de marineros: una estrella guía para encontrar refugio en el Mar. ¡Y además, yo no vi ninguna luz! Puede que me falte un ojo, ¡pero creo que habría notado algo así! Quizá tus aventuras recientes te han agotado, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}.
'Ah, pero estoy... bastante seguro de que vi la Corona de Durin. Tenía el número adecuado de estrellas y parecía tener forma de corona, así que creo que nuestra expedición ha sido un éxito!'

'¿Nada? ¿Sin suerte en absoluto?'
Byrski suspira.
'Esperaba que fuera más fácil que esto, mi amigo. Echaré un último vistazo y luego podremos navegar de regreso a Mekhem-bizru. ¡No quiero decepcionar a la Guarición de Hierro!'
¡Cuando miras hacia el Lago Espejo, una luz brillante te envuelve!

Listen to the concerns of your crew
'I am not much of a teacher, but I hope to be a help to you. What do you want to know?'
'The sails have been taken down, but we are not yet safe! There is a presence in the wind, and it seeks to batter our ship beneath the waves!'

'I have never been to Umbar, ${PLAYER}, and neither has my brother... unless he has somehow managed to escape my notice and had some adventure about which he has told me nothing! But I find that unlikely.
'I wonder if Elves live among the sea-folk that call Umbar their home? I will have to put this question to the Corsair Daxamat sometime in the next few days. It could be he has seen Elves in the city or along the cape during his time there, before the Kindred came to power.'
Gwallang the Limlinn hops excitedly up and down, occasionally cracking the shell of a snail he has caught on the railing of the Wave-hunter. He seems very happy to be sailing with Sirgon again.

'This blade has to earn its name, ${PLAYER}. I cannot give it a name that might prove to be the wrong one! Weapons are like children, or so I have heard it said.
'The Elves of Lórien called my brother Corudan \qthe River-walker,\q for he was often away from home, exploring the lands up and down the Anduin. Will this adventure now make him \qthe Sea-strider,\q or \qthe Bay-rider?\q
'I will have to tell him this when we rescue him. He will laugh to hear it, once he is safe.'

'I have not yet needed the seasickness remedy you and Legolas procured for me, ${PLAYER}, but all the same I believe I will stay below decks for now. Do you think I should share it with Caebar? I will have it ready if he asks me for it, but I do not want to give it all away, just in case.
'We are not yet out in the Bay, after all. Legolas says he expects the rocking of the ship to become more pronounced when we leave the river behind us.'

'I have given some thought to our voyage, ${PLAYER}. I believe the City of the Corsairs must remain a bustling port-city, despite the defeat of Balakhôr the Scourge and the Heirs of Castamir during the War of the Ring. Do you think the arrival of the Wave-hunter can go unnoticed when we draw near the port?
'I cannot decide if it is more or less suspicious of us to arrive by night. Perhaps some of Golasgil's sailors will give me their opinions.'

'How fares my husband Rossaran? No doubt he gawks at the scenery through which the ship passes?
'Oh, he is a dear man. Two things he loves besides me, ${PLAYER}: faithfully serving his King, and marvelling at the great feats performed by the prospectors and stonemasons of Gondor. Sometimes I wonder if he should have been born a dwarf!
'But I have been checking our store of food and water, and it seems that we should have enough for the voyage to Umbar and back. The Wave-hunter is well-prepared for the journey; I confess to you that it is our arrival at the City of the Corsairs that now most concerns me!'

'This ship is unlike those of my people, ${PLAYER}. No, I do not intend that to be an insult! Even a ship made of rough-hewn timber is still to be prized if it stays afloat and keeps you from a watery grave! I think it is simply the way of the Men of Gondor to value the use of a thing higher than the beauty of its form.'

'What's that? Oh, nothing. I am just thinking.
'What goods do you think the people of Umbar might value? If I were to establish a market along the docks of the city, what things would fetch the highest price? Will items from Gondor be considered valuable or worthless, ${PLAYER}? I cannot decide! At least I will have a few days to think it over.'
'Thank you for keeping me company, ${PLAYER}, but I will not ask you to remain below decks for the whole voyage! Feel free to go above and take in the fresh air.'

'I have not felt this youthful in years! Our course leads down the Lagorduin to the Bay of Belfalas, and then we will truly be on our way.
'Like young Caebar, not all of the Wave-hunter's crew have before been at sea. I suggest that you speak with the folk you recruited and learn how the river-passage treats them. The waters in the Bay will be more unruly than this, and if the rocking in Lagorduin disturbs them it may be helpful to know, and guard against further upset! I understand the dwarf Gimli has in his possession a remedy for seasickness? He may need to share it, with Caebar at least, and perhaps with others!'

'I am all right now, ${PLAYER}. It was simply the sight of Daxamat clambering out over the railing of the ship that made me feel queasy. I think I will remain below decks for the rest of the voyage, unless you need me above. I cannot imagine you will. The sailors of Anfalas seem very capable.'

'The one who abducted my son Thorongil, this Nakási Wave-reaper... you said you know who she is?'
You tell Nauriel of the cellar encounter between Nakási and the Heirs of Castamir that resulted in the death of her husband Tumúldo. Nauriel stares at you with narrowed eyes.
'She will have no sympathy from me. Bad things happen. If she does not return my son to me, unharmed, I will send her to see her husband at once. I may do this anyway. Let her and her masters beware: a Knight of the Green Hills does not grant mercy without good reason... and the mother of an endangered child never does.'

'I have been thinking about something, my friend. So much good stone is covered by rivers and by lakes... and by the Sea as well, I imagine! What precious gemstones lie hidden down there, out of our reach? Is that the secret of the Temámir? Do the arid lands of their birth yield such valuables to them more easily than ours? And yet they still need water to drink....
'I look forward to learning how it is done when we arrive in Umbar. The gemstone worn by Khôltekh the Cunning is an intriguing mystery, but it is one I intend to solve!'

'Oh, excuse me, ${PLAYER}, I did not mean to be rude. I was contemplating the bridge over the Lagorduin: such an impressive feat of stonework!
'The City of the Corsairs has been many things over the years, but for some of that time it was a sea-haven of Númenor. There must be architectural wonders there too, and I am eager to see them. My wife Bruidis cares less for such things. Where is she now? She has gone below decks, intending to assess our stock of supplies. I told her the voyage itself should not take more than a few days, but still she wanted to ensure we have food and water enough.
'I told you before, did I not? I am a swan-knight, and my martial skill is well-developed; but my wife Bruidis is the strategist of the family. If there is thinking to be done, she is the one to do it!'

'Thanks for checking in on me, ${PLAYER}. You say the Corsair Daxamat spoke about what we can expect when we reach Umbar? I should have liked to hear that... assuming it was good news!'
You tell Caebar what you learned, and he nods.
'A little good and a little bad, then? It sounds to me as if we have our work cut out for us when we arrive. At least the sailing has been easy. I expected worse!'

'The storm rages and the seas are wild! We have to take down the sails, or the wind will tear our masts to splinters! The sailors and the Elves have gone above, but I cannot tell if they are still alive!'

'The voyage is well underway, and now our thoughts turn to our arrival at the City of the Corsairs. What will we do if the Kindred of the Coins greets us at the dock, ${PLAYER}? I said we would once again become the Hidden Guard, but there is very little that will be hidden about our mission if our foes see us arrive from atop the walls or from the watch-towers of Umbar.'

'I am not much of a teacher. My brother Jajax is the talker in the family.
'But I hope to be a help to you. What do you want to know?'

'I know I suggested that you recruit the Corsair Jajax for the crew and he refused the offer, but I was under the impression that his brother Daxamat would be a little less... I don't know... a little less wild, perhaps? But he is clambering all over the Wave-hunter as if he has not a care in the world, and without the slightest thought that he might fall from any of these perches, each more perilous than the last!
'Will you <rgb=#00FF00>beckon</rgb> for him to come down? He is making me nervous!'

'The storm chewed up your ship and spat you out, stranger... but it must not have liked the taste of you. Most of the ships devoured by Shedax Khîn arrive upon the Shield Isles in more pieces than this, and with fewer survivors.
'Shedax Khîn? That is the Umbari word for the rocks that surround the island of Bakhjâd. It means \qthe Grinding Jaws,\q and theirs is the smile that welcomes strangers to these isles. But someone else must smile upon you and upon your crew, for while your ship will not sail again, you have your life, and that is more than some retain when they come here.'

'Mattân and I listened to the driving rain of the storm last night and it told the two of us a new wreck would decorate the islands this morn. We arose early, before any others, and came here in haste... but we were rewarded with disappointment. The isles have their new decoration, aye. But the Grinding Jaws did not finish their meal, and too many survivors guard the wreck.
'There will be little for us to salvage today. But I tell you this: life in the Shield Isles is hard, and not all who arrive here as you have can endure it. You survived the storm, but will you survive the week? Will you survive the day?
'Oh, it is no threat, stranger. I am simply making conversation.'
'These isles are not deserted, ${PLAYER}, and the men who live here may seek to do us harm.'

'I knew I did not like sailing, ${PLAYER}! How can it be that Sirgon missed it? A sailing-ship is a hateful thing, as unpleasant a creation as I have ever known!'
You remind Caebar that were it not for the strong hull of the Wave-hunter and its brave crew, he would not have survived the storm. Caebar shakes his head.
'Yes, yes,' he mumbles. 'I suppose it could always be worse. But I am done with ships! You mark my words, ${PLAYER}! From this day forward I will take the land-road, no matter how out of the way it may run!'
'You are more fortunate than most who come here, stranger.'
'An unguarded wreck is free to all who dare search it. Perhaps Mattân and I will come back tomorrow.'

'Do not look so crestfallen, my friend! You must see that the Valar smile upon the Wave-hunter, and upon our voyage! We have our lives, after all, and the successful conclusion of your mission still lies ahead! This is not an ending, but a beginning! I have lost friends to the rocks that guard the Shield Isles, it is true... but today the strong hull of the Wave-hunter and the resilience of his crew has delivered us here safely. Rejoice for that, and celebrate the good fortune and the blessing of the Powers that aided in its accomplishment!
'I have not set foot upon this island chain in many years, but it will take me only moments to refamiliarize myself with them. If you will go to several locations and <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb>, your report may help me remember the geography of these islands. Perhaps you can start at the beach across the lagoon to the south, a beach to the north-west of the Wave-hunter, and the beach on the western side of this island.'

'I have not set foot upon this island chain in many years, but it will take me only moments to refamiliarize myself with them. 'What did you see, my friend?'
You tell Sirgon what you saw from each of the locations you scouted, and he nods agreeably.
'Aye, it is coming back to me now. Let us see what I can remember.
'This island chain is a rocky archipelago composed of numerous isles running from north-west to south-east, but three of these are larger than the others. The southernmost island is the largest, Zamarzîr, and it lies in view of the cape upon which Umbar stands. It is a place of jungle and mountain, and when I served the Steward of Gondor in years past it was the haunt of pirates and freebooters. We left it alone as much as we could, for it was a dangerous place.
'The middle island is nearest to us, and it is Bakhjâd. The jagged rocks that surround Bakhjâd are responsible for the reputation of this place as the bane of sailors, for the dangerous currents surrounding the Shield Isles sweep strong ships and braver men to their dooms. I have lost good friends to those rocks, which the men of Umbar call Shedax Khîn. I understand that there may be a settlement somewhere in the centre of Bakhjâd, but I have not seen it.
'The northern island is uninhabited. I believe it is called Jeb Khâtel, but the steep cliffs surrounding it make it inaccessible from the coast.
'This is a place of adventure, ${PLAYER}! If we meet the challenge it sets before us, we are certain to survive and see the successful completion of our mission!'

You agree with the Corsair's assessment, and encourage him to help you recover the lost supplies.

'This is a good start, is it not? I will bring the supplies we recovered inside the Wave-hunter to protect them from the wind and the rain. We will be glad to have them if we must remain on the Shield Isles for some days, and the weather here is changeable.

'I wish my brother were here. I wonder what he is up to now?
'Ah, never mind, ${PLAYER}. I have to bring these supplies inside. There will be time for thinking later on, I do not doubt it. Right now is the time for survival!'

'How did the Elf fare on his own hunt? Did he prove as successful as we did?'

'Can I ask you to retrieve the birds and the arrows with which I felled them? You will find them along the route I took back here, to the south-west. Each bird took but a single arrow, my friend. My aim remains true, even among the trees of these islands and from such distance as necessity required I shoot.
'We will see you back at the Wave-hunter when you have done this.'

'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}. Our crew will eat well for as long as they must remain here among the Shield Isles, and that eases my mind. I am sure it eases yours as well.

I felled a number of the birds I saw winging among the trees of Zamarzîr, the southern island... but there was one target that I could not bring myself to down. It was a mighty creature, and though I saw it from a great distance it appeared to me of tremendous size. It brought to my mind the Great Eagles Gwaihir and his brother Landroval.
'I did not release my arrow. Whatever the creature may have been, something told me not to harm it. I do not know if it would give us the same treatment, ${PLAYER}. Walk carefully if you tread again on Zamarzîr, just in case.'

'The crew of the Wave-hunter will have food to eat tonight, thanks to the three of us, ${PLAYER}!
'Did Legolas tell you about the great bird he witnessed from afar? I told him it is probably not one of the Great Eagles, because while the flight for one such as Gwaihir or Landroval would not be as long a journey as it was for us, what reason would they have to make it? No, it must be something else. I say he should have filled it with arrows, because anything as large as he describes likely feasts upon anything smaller, and we surely qualify!
'I hope in this case I am wrong, and Legolas will not regret his choice to spare this creature. But if it was up to me I would not have hesitated. The Longbeards have little patience or mercy for monsters, and such a giant bird sounds like a monster to me until it proves it is a friend, as the Eagles have done.

Yahîm lowers his voice, and looks to either side before continuing in a hushed tone.
'The life of a Corsair is not what it once was, I confess it. I blame the Heirs of Castamir for that, but when I do so I make sure not to do so loudly, or when not in the company of those I know well. I make an exception for you and for your Elf companions, for if you cannot trust those who save your life, who can you trust?
'I promised you knowledge. Here it is: after the death of Balakhôr the Scourge in Gondor, his widow Saklaphêl thought to claim the rule of Umbar, acting as regent through their young son Balakhâd, but the rioting in the streets and the rise of the Kindred of the Coins caused her to abandon both that plan and the city; she fled to the Shield Isles, and now lives in exile here in Mâr Naphra. None see her. She issues orders to her servants through Galadaith, her spokesman. Supporters of the Heirs of Castamir believe she will organize the remaining Corsairs and attack the city and the Kindred who control it.
'But I have heard there is a reason she cannot. Some say Balakhâd died during the fighting when the city fell, but others say that the Kindred hold him hostage, and Saklaphêl dares not attack the city for fear he will be slain.
'Once again I thank you and those Elves for the rescue, and for the return of my sword. I hope my information is of help to you.'

'Yahîm said you should bring his sword to him at his home by the water on the eastern side of Mâr Naphra. It may be he will know something useful about the Heirs of Castamir or the Kindred of the Coins. Once you have spoken with him, we will meet you back at the Wave-hunter.'

'This is a very strange adventure, ${PLAYER}, where we must save our foes and rely upon what they can tell us to free our friends. My head spins, but I think Elrohir and I did the right thing. We could not leave Yahîm to be devoured by the kergrim, whether his allegiance is to the Heirs of Castamir or not. Corsair or no, he is still a Man, and he needed help.
'My brother feels the same, I am certain of it.'

'What did Yahîm have to say about the Heirs of Castamir and the Kindred of the Coins? Elladan and I would have rescued him no matter what information he had to share... but if his information is useful then so much the better.'
You tell Elrohir what the Corsair had to say, and he mulls it over for a moment.
'He does not know if the son of Balakhôr and Saklaphêl is alive and held by the Kindred of the Coins, but I think we have seen enough to know that they are the type to take prisoners. It could be Thorongil and Corudan and Balakhâd are all being held in the same dungeon, the easier to keep an eye upon them. The Kindred can then use each of them as leverage upon their respective families and friends.
'It is interesting, too, that Saklaphêl fled to Mâr Naphra. At least we will know from where the Heirs of Castamir might be organized, should they once again become a threat. It is worth keeping an eye upon, anyway. As if there was not enough to do already!
'Thank you for helping us with Yahîm, ${PLAYER}. Elladan and I will see what else we can help with around here.'
'Once again I thank you and those Elves for the rescue, and for the return of my sword. I hope my information is of help to you.'

'My brother and I thought to scout Bakhjâd and avoid the attention of the Corsair settlement we discovered in the island's interior, but it was not long before we heard the sound of someone calling for help from within the ruin atop this hill. We could not remain idle, ${PLAYER}, you understand. We went to investigate and only then discovered that he was clearly a Corsair; by most accounting he is a foe of our mission, but we could not leave him to be devoured by the kergrim that threatened him.
'We saved him and brought him back here. Have we done wrong?'

'You are a friend of these Elves? I am not accustomed to speaking with such as they, but I cannot deny that if they had not come along I would now be dead.
'My name is Yahîm, and I am not one to refuse aid when it is offered! It is true: I am a Corsair, and Mâr Naphra is my home, but I confess I am currently without a ship. If you hold a grudge against my kind, I understand it, but we are not currently at sea. On land can we not remain friendly?
'I appreciate the timely intervention of these Elves, and I do not mean to be ungrateful... but when I followed them to safety I left my sword behind. If you will return to the kergrim-infested ruin atop this island and retrieve my sword for me, I will see that you are rewarded. The Elves seemed more interested in what I might know than what valuables I might give to them, if you take my meaning. I will tell you what I know about the Heirs of Castamir and the Kindred of the Coins... if you bring my sword to me at my home by the water on the eastern side of Mâr Naphra. Unless I have misjudged your intent, that is what you want to know, is it not?
'If you will do this, can I ask for one more favour? Slay some more of the kergrim for me, will you? They are disgusting creatures, spreading filth and disease, and they should not remain among the old ruins. It is not right.'
'We saved him from the kergrim and brought him down here, though he is a Corsair and a foe of our mission. Have we done wrong?'
'Watch yourself among the wrecks, ${PLAYER}. The kergrim are dangerous.'

Gangur turns the corroded rock samples you retrieved over and over in his hands, but his scowl deepens the longer he looks at them.
'These rocks are like the others. The only difference is they are melted by the corrosive breath of the drakes. I admit it is not what I was hoping to see. I thought Khôltekh the Cunning might have gotten the shiny material that was embedded in his medallion from these islands, but if so its location remains a secret.'
He sighs heavily and then looks at you with a more open expression than you are accustomed to seeing on his face. He seems almost haunted.
'When I fell in the water I swallowed too much sea-water, and I felt the life leaving me. I cannot tell you now if my eyes were open or shut, but I believed them to be open, and before the blackness took me... I saw it.'
Gangur pauses, as if gathering the strength to go on. You let him wait until he is ready to continue.
'It was a great shelled beast, all tentacles and siphons, and its spiral shell was encrusted with the shining jewel of my dreams, glimmering like an opal but with every facet a riot of colour. Huge the creature was, but it paid me no mind even as it filled the great expanse of my vision. And then it was gone.
'Was this the dream of a dying dwarf, ${PLAYER}? Maybe it was. But I cannot forget the sight of it. That vision will haunt me to my last day... I know it.
'Thank you for listening to my story, but please do not tell anyone else of it. I will try to put it from my mind and help with the mission... as much as I can.'

You tell Gangur that you are relieved to see he still lives, for it was believed that he was lost overboard during the storm.
'That is exactly what happened. I know it was foolish of me to go up on deck during the storm, but I feared the ship would fill with water and I would have no hope of survival if I remained below deck. There was a tremendous wave and I was swept overboard. Someone was looking out for me, but I cannot imagine why. More deserving dwarves than I have been favoured by the First Crafter. I thought I was sure to drown, and I saw... well, never mind what I saw. I cannot believe it, myself.
'I lost my pickaxe and my satchel. I was fortunate enough to wash ashore; perhaps they have fetched up along one of these islands too. Do you think you could look for them for me? While you look for those, could you also retrieve some rock samples for me from the islands hereabout? I am curious about something. I will be... well, I will be right here. I am still too water-logged to go anywhere.'

'The Steward Denethor came to believe that Belondor cared more for the people of Umbar than he did for his native Gondor, and he distrusted the man he had named Warden of the Firth. He believed Belondor had fallen under the sway of the Church of the All Seeing, a religion that had at the time a small, though growing, presence in the city of Umbar. This was impossible to believe, and even today I do not believe it, but the Steward had other reasons to distrust Belondor.
'My old friend had fallen in love with an Umbari noblewoman named Mêshka. I do not know how the Steward came to learn of this, but the rumours eventually came even to the White City. There must have been spies aboard one or more of Belondor's ships, or lurking in the court of Mêshka's home... but I cannot say for certain. When paired with Belondor's recent missives, which counseled mercy and fairness for the Umbari people, these whispers painted a clear picture of betrayal that the Steward of Gondor could not disbelieve.
'He commanded the master of his navy to pursue the traitor Belondor, relieve him of his duties, and bring him back to Gondor. I could not refuse the command, ${PLAYER}.'

'I am not a man for whom deceit comes easily, ${PLAYER}, but I could not think my old friend a traitor without good cause. On any other day, a call to dinner at my manor-house would have been the signal for a time of merriment and joyful reunion, but on this day it was a lure. Belondor answered the summons, for he had no reason to suspect the orders given to me by the Steward Denethor. Over dinner I asked him where lay his loyalties... and his answer did not dispel my worries.
'\qThey lie with Umbar Baharbêl, the City of Sails, my old friend,\q he said to me. \qThey lie with my Mêshka, to whom I am betrothed. And only then do they lie with Gondor. Can a man not serve three loves equally in his heart, if he is wise and fair?\q
'\qThe Steward Denethor does not think so,\q I told him, and our raised voices would have proven to me that our friendship was at an end, even if the drawn swords had not followed. Each of us sustained injuries in that duel, and Belondor fled through the shadowed streets of Pelargir to where his ship lay moored. For three days I pursued him in my own vessel across the tumultuous Bay, when at last he dared draw too near the Grinding Jaws; among the rocks of Shedax Khîn his ship perished. Some of his crew we rescued, but of Belondor there was no sign, and I believed him drowned, lost at sea. The Steward Denethor praised me for the pursuit, but I mourned lost Belondor, and cursed the duty that made me drive my friend to his death. But I cursed it silently, for still I served the Steward.'

'Thank you for indulging me in this, ${PLAYER}. I owe you so much for allowing me to join the crew of the Wave-hunter and come with you on this voyage. I would follow you to the very ends of the earth, know that I would, and never complain or say to you a cross word. I have always done my duty as I saw it, first for the Steward of Gondor and then for the King Elessar, and now for you, as the leader of this mission. So I will not still my tongue now, and I will tell you the source of my fear. May it prove without base!
'The name spoken by the young scribe: Belondor. I knew a Belondor when I was a young man. He was born in Anfalas and grew up along the Langstrand, and we both served at the command of the Steward Denethor. Belondor and I were well-nigh inseparable, and together sailed this very Bay of Belfalas and up the coast of Gondor to more distant shores. He was at my wedding, by the Valar, and gave the toast before all the gathered company! Celebros had me keep the stuffed birds he gave us for a wedding-gift in my hall of keepsakes, even when later events made their reminder a painful one.
'We rose in the estimation of the Steward. Even as I was made master of the fleets of Gondor, Belondor was named Warden of the Firth, and worked faithfully to keep the city of Umbar under guard, its pirates quelled and under control. He was an empathic guardian of the city, fair and just to the Umbari people, and they loved him. But this love proved to have a cost.'

'I cannot know by what paths he returned to Umbar, but when he did it seems he found others who shared his mind. Did he rise through the ranks of the Kindred, or perhaps he was there at its founding? Now, at least, he holds a position with enough standing to warrant one of Saklaphêl's bounties!'

'After the Battle of Pelennor Fields, I wandered without purpose. I came to this land because I did not want to get involved, but even that proved a lie. I called myself Bymerë at first, and told myself Horn was dead. But as I lived here, drowning my old sorrows with ale and trying to forget what I had done and what I had been, I saw crimes I could not forgive; as I opposed them I took on a new name: Driftwood. I believed the Heirs of Castamir might again threaten Gondor... and if they had victory there, would not Rohan be next? So I made things difficult for them, as I could. I thought I might gain an audience with Balakhôr's widow if I claimed to have slain one of her enemies, and so end the threat of the Heirs of Castamir.
'Most of my plans ended in the bottom of a mug of ale, ${PLAYER}. When I was Horn, and fought alongside friends, it was different. Driftwood is alone, and accomplishes nothing. It is useless.'
You tell Horn that it could be different, and he shakes his head.
'This is my place now. I spend my days fighting Corsairs and my nights here, drowning in my cups. I suggest you defeat the Corsairs of the Shield Isles, for the sake of our past friendship, and then return to your ship. Horn is dead; only Driftwood remains, and he cannot help you.'
'Would Corudan come to your aid, if your positions were reversed?'

'This is my place now. I spend my days fighting Corsairs and my nights here, drowning in my cups. I suggest you defeat the Corsairs of the Shield Isles, for the sake of our past friendship, and then return to your ship. Horn is dead; only Driftwood remains, and he cannot help you.'

There can be no mistake. This is Horn of Rohan, though months of hard living on the road and in the wild have weathered his clothes. His face is still familiar, but the war and its worries have left their marks upon it, and he seems more aged than you remember.

You were always running... toward.'

'We each responded differently to Hámisar's command that the gates of Furukzahar be shut when Gondor went to war. Others, including some of the dwarves who work for me, turned to games to pass the time. Have you heard of this ridiculous Stacking Game they invented?
'Ah, I understand it, even as I think it is needlessly frivolous in such times as we live in. I allow them to pass the time as they see fit... so long as they quickly respond when I have a task for them! And this is the case today. 'Do you have an interest in history? You should hear my father Mulúgu's account of the battle from one who fought in it! Seek him by the throne of Furukzahar, for he often goes there to advise Hámisar about matters of importance to our folk.'

'My father was sleeping? Yes, I should have realized. He is old, and while I treasure his wisdom and the tales he tells, he does spend much of his day sleeping by the throne. Of all the places in Furukzahar, that is his favourite chamber; he told me once it reminds him of the Court of King Jegín the Enduring, ruler of the Temámir Dwarves.
'But I promised you would learn of the Battle of Azanulbizar! More than two hundred years ago, all the dwarf clans answered the summons of King Thráin of the Longbeards, and assembled on the very threshold of Khazad-dûm to answer the violence of the Orcs with vengeance of our own. My father Mulúgu, very young in those days, served King Jegín and fought bravely among the ranks of her Temámir in skirmish after skirmish. Many of those who followed her have now passed on, but my father Mulúgu still lives, as does the King herself; Jegín remains King of the Temámir in our lands far to the south-east.
'Every clan of the dwarves suffered terribly during the war and at Azanulbizar, and King Jegín was not alone in demanding some recompense for the losses her people had suffered. For their service during the War of Dwarves and Orcs, the Longbeards granted to the Temámir some of the mountain strongholds they could no longer maintain, including this fortress. And so Furukzahar became a home for the Temámir. We have gotten along with the neighbouring kingdom of Gondor for many years, and I hope that will continue for years to come.
'The Temámir have always been the wise voyagers of the dwarves, walking long roads and sailing the vast seas in search of opportunity, quite unlike those of other dwarf-families. Like them, however, we are also loyal to our friends and deadly to our enemies. It has been a pleasure to speak with you about my people, and perhaps some day I will introduce you properly to my father. Until then farewell, my fellow student of history!'
Mulúgu sleeps peacefully on one of the benches, and you decide not to wake him

'Welcome to Furukzahar! The fortress has not had many visitors of late, due to the war in Gondor, but I am pleased to see that Hámisar has ordered the gates open once again. A number of noteworthy visitors have come to the fortress since then, friends from near lands and distant. This is a city of the Temámir, wisest of the dwarves, and we have made this home for ourselves far from our ancestral lands.
'It was not always home to the Temámir. Are you familiar with the Battle of Azanulbizar? Yes, the last great conflict in the War of Dwarves and Orcs. Two hundred years ago it was, but it was so momentous a battle that it is still spoken of by all the clans of the dwarves, including my people! My own father Mulúgu fought in it and achieved glory, when he was young... I am fortunate he survived the fighting, or I would not be here today!
'Do you have an interest in history? You should hear my father's account of the battle from one who fought in it! Seek him by the throne of Furukzahar, for he often goes there to advise Hámisar about matters of importance to our folk.'
The Wise Voyagers

'Have you heard of a roc? Vicious, nasty creatures they are. Massive birds with talons like daggers, beaks strong enough to pierce the hull of even the sturdiest ships.
'Well, I represent a wealthy buyer who is interested in acquiring one of these beasts for himself. Fancies if he raises the thing from birth, it'll be loyal. Could you imagine? The power of a roc tamed.
'So here's the job: Go to the roc's nest south of here and nab one of their eggs. Bring it back to me, and you'll have enough coin to live comfortably for the rest of your life anywhere in the world.'
As you recall, Rocs are intelligent creatures, not the mere beasts that this brigand claims them to be. It may be worth warning the nearby rocs that someone has designs on their eggs.

'You are a friend to the Free City of Umbar; I see that now. I will tell none of your arrival here. The merchant road runs along the coast southward to Rakhatâb, where it turns north and passes by a small fishing village, Khûtra. Umbar Baharbêl lies just beyond the hills past the village, the shining jewel of Umbarkhîl. Go in peace, and with my best wishes for your health and happiness.'
'Let us ask someone in the nearby settlement how best to reach Umbar Baharbêl. The conclusion of King Elessar's mission awaits us there... but we cannot complete this quest until we reach the city.'

'You have come to Jax Phanâl with a curious group, stranger. I hope you and your friends will cause no trouble here, for if you do, the Kindred of the Coins will see that it is the last trouble you make. Umbar Baharbêl has been made a Free City once again, and under the rule of the Kindred the Haradrim of the Great Southern Empire have been driven out of Jax Phanâl and other villages along Umbarkhîl, the Cape of Umbar. The Empire of Ordâkh has no claim upon us, and never will again. They plundered our valuables when they fled, and even now they muster their warriors at a camp to the south. They have no interest in some of the things they stole... they wanted only to deprive us of them.'
Jâkin studies your face carefully.
'Are you a helpful sort? Or do you only wish to learn what you can and move on, leaving we who struggle here behind when we are not useful to you? Few come to Jax Phanâl without reason, and fewer still leave the Shield Isles without some ill intent. I wonder what my silence might be worth to you? There must be some who would be interested to hear of your little group of travellers. Unless you are a helpful sort. Then it might be different.'

'I think we should help this man, ${PLAYER}.
'He is not wrong, for in other lands we have done as he said: moved on when we learned what we could, remaining only for as long as we needed to learn where next to journey. Now, it was war! So I do not think we could have done otherwise! But if we can help the folk of Jax Phanâl and also keep our presence hidden from those who watch for us, I believe we should.
'What would Jâkin have us do?'

'Jâkin uses us cleverly, ${PLAYER}. I recognize the tactic from my days of... banditry.
'But he is not wrong about this: his silence will aid us more than an errant word to the wrong folk, and if we might accomplish some good for the people here at the same time, how should I put it? Everyone wins, or at least no one loses more than anyone else, which is a start, and for me a change.
'What would he have us do?'

'Are you a helpful sort? Or do you only wish to learn what you can and move on, leaving we who struggle here behind when we are not useful to you? Few come to Jax Phanâl without reason, and fewer still leave the Shield Isles without some ill intent. I wonder what my silence might be worth to you? There must be some who would be interested to hear of your little group of travellers. Unless you are a helpful sort. Then it might be different.'

'You are a helpful sort, then? I smile to hear it!
'When the magistrate's forces drove the Haradrim from Jax Phanâl, the occupiers fled with whatever valuables they could find, but they were not... how would you say it? Choosy. Some of them stole books of great value to me personally, and I would have them back. These are not worth any great amount of Phârzi or Gîmli, but they do contain stories and accounts that are very dear to me, and I want them back.
'The Haradrim will have them at their camp to the south. Retrieve my books and defeat any of the warriors you must, and you will prove yourself a helpful sort.'
'The Haradrim will have them at their camp to the south. Retrieve my books and defeat any of the warriors you must, and you will prove yourself a helpful sort.'

'I am most grateful for this service you have provided this day! These books are very dear to me, and I could not bear to think of them in the hands of the Ordâkhim, never to be read again. They did not know the worth of the treasures they stole from us!
'You are a friend to the Free City of Umbar; I see that now. I will tell none of your arrival here. The merchant road runs along the coast southward to Rakhatâb, where it turns north and passes by a small fishing village, Khûtra. Umbar Baharbêl lies just beyond the hills past the village, the shining jewel of Umbarkhîl. Go in peace, and with my best wishes for your health and happiness.'

'It is... almost like it used to be, isn't it?'
He gazes out past the buildings of Jax Phanâl, and you know he is thinking of Nona. He catches you looking at him and gives you a brief smile.
'Well, thank you for listening to me, ${PLAYER}. Let us return to the shore and see if the rest of the crew has made the crossing.'

'I think we have made life a little more safe for the folk of Rakhatâb, but something still bothers me about the murder of that aged man. Why would one of the Corsairs at Kan Skûrja commit such an act? He was a recent arrival to Rakhatâb, much like we are, and yet they did not depart their encampment to threaten us. 'I have had an idea. I will go keep the guards occupied. You find the evidence coffer and retrieve the old man's belongings from it before they can finish bringing it into the keep!. We may find a clue among them. Let us meet up on the beach to the south-east of the city after you are successful!'

'This man was just minding his own business; I heard him cry out as he fell. He was a stranger to Rakhatâb, that is true, but he has been here for a day or two. Some of them are camped even now to the north-east along the coast, and sometimes they adventure here to Rakhatâb to cause problems for the workers.
'Might one of them murdered this man? I think it likely.'

'Something smells fishy, ${PLAYER}. If my brother were here he would say \qit is the right of a Corsair to do as he likes!\q and think nothing of it, but there is something about this situation that feels wrong to me. Perhaps I am just not as bold a Corsair as my brother.
'But the camp of Corsairs to the north-east lies in our path. Perhaps we can help the people here by thinning their numbers, and when we return they may have captured the one who did this. What do you say to this idea?'

The woman flings one arm dramatically outward and holds the back of her other hand over her eyes.

She lowers her arms to her sides and laughs long and loudly.
'It is remarkable how simple it is to make people see what they want to see. I had all the folk of Rakhatâb believing they saw a tall bearded Corsair stab a man to death, right there in the open. Oh, the murder was real enough, and The Blade-twist did not see it coming. Weep not for him. No bounty-hunter should live as long as he did and remain in service. I will have the good sense to hang up my own knife before there is more life behind me than ahead.
'But I wanted to speak with you for a particular reason, ${PLAYER}. I would like to declare for ourselves a truce, and to work together where that is possible. The Blade-twist would share neither money nor information, and slay me with as little regard as I slew him; and that is familiar to me, and in this business that is right. But I observed you speaking with the man called Driftwood in Jax Phanâl, and I could not understand it. For what purpose did he ask you to help the people of that settlement? Not only for their silence. There was something else. I find that most interesting.
'Let us consider the Kindred of the Coins our mutual foe, then? I will help you find them, ${PLAYER}. The bounties belong to me... but it seems to me that you seek them for... other reasons. So long as our aims do not conflict, you may count Cruel Dancer among your allies... if not among your friends. It seems to me you may have friends enough. I trust you chose them carefully?'

'Could be so. Could be maybe not. With the famine going on, that's one of the only reliable sources of food around here, and it is barely edible.'

'I would have to ask some of my neighbours for the information you want, and while I'm asking I'm not bringing crab legs back to Khûtra, or collecting driftwood along the shore with which we can smoke the meat and improve the flavour. 'This was the beacon-tower of Calatirion, ${PLAYER}, constructed by Elendil as a mighty monument of Númenor. I have heard tales from Glorfindel of the Vandassar that stood within it for much of its history, Airessar, as clear as crystal, shining so brightly it could be seen even from far off in the bay.
'I know it was destroyed by the Bright Company to loosen Sauron's bonds upon the Men of Harad during the War of the Great Alliance. The tower itself survived that battle, and would stand for almost three thousand more years, but it would not stand forever. When the Church of the All-Seeing came to Umbar in the vanguard of the Empire of Ordâkh, there were servants of that church who resented that which Calatirion represented; they were the Nazgûl, with the Forsaken Reaver at their head. With sorcery he and his allies toppled the tower, and the memory of that day has lived on in whisper ever since. Even Glorfindel wished not to speak of it, but he told me the name by which folk of Umbar recall that day: Mût Tadaul, the Death of Light.
'The Forsaken Reaver must have perished with his master when Frodo cast the Ring into the Cracks of Doom, ${PLAYER}. But Calatirion remains toppled. It is a reminder to me that evil deeds are not undone by the destruction of those who wrought them.

Our roads are safer and travel and trade quicken their pace. Natural dangers remain, however: passage around the Cape is not always easy, and you may still prefer to visit the stables should you wish to journey to the fort at Rakhatâb, to the south! 'I was not certain you would dare come here. But since you have, you will hear my words before you and your friend die.'
Mêshka holds up her hand, signaling to her guards that they should await her command.
'For years after Sirgon drove my intended to his death, I lived a life of mourning. Believing he died at sea, I married, and it was a marriage of great happiness... at least until its ending, when my husband was seized by the Church of the All Seeing and burned alive, sacrificed to its Dark Lord.
'Why do I tell you this? I tell you this so you will know I am no wilting flower. I have been forged of tough steel, hardened by fire and by the salt-spray. There is a reason Belondor was my first intended, for he is the same: made durable by his experiences.
'For he did not perish beneath the waves when Sirgon pursued him through the rocks of Shedax Khîn. He survived as a castaway among the Shield Isles, sun-scorched and bitter, until he was taken aboard an Ordâkhai galley. In time he came to Umbar and served in the Fleet-fast, becoming one of its dedicated defenders, but the rule of the Heirs of Castamir rankled him.
'He began a friendship with Azagath the Sea-shadow and others who would come to supplant the Heirs. This Kindred of the Coins rules wisely and fairly, unlike either the Heirs of Castamir or the Steward of Gondor. What final words have you to say, Sirgon? Will you beg the forgiveness of my husband? I will give your words to him, if they please me.'

'I do not beg for forgiveness, Mêshka, for I know forgiveness is not deserved. If there is a message to give from me to your husband Belondor, it would be this: the wound I suffered the night we duelled after dinner was mortal. It was not a deep cut, not physically, but that wound has stayed with me since that night.
'I will not beg for forgiveness, or say that following the command of the Steward Denethor protects me from your reprisal. But know that I was forever changed by what I did to your husband Belondor, though I did not know it. But now I see that I was.
'I believed I missed the sea, and sailing, and traced my miseries to giving up that life. But I see now that it was my friendship with your husband that I truly missed, and the innocence of my youth before I committed the act by which I am now forever judged, and judge myself. If this is the wound that is to slay me now, I welcome it. I ask that you spare ${PLAYER}, who had no part in earning this, but I will not run from it.'
'What final words have you to say, Sirgon? Will you beg the forgiveness of my husband? I will give your words to him, if they please me.'

Mêshka stares at Sirgon for a long moment... and then motions for her guards to stand down.
'We were all wounded on that night, Sirgon, and none of us knew how deeply. Your words ring true to me. I have spent years dwelling upon my hatred of you for the treatment suffered by Belondor at your hands, and at the hands of Gondor, and though that land is ruled now by a King and not a Steward, I believe in my heart that it would be no different if those events happened today and not long years ago. I did not forgive you then, and I do not forgive you now.'
Mêshka shakes her head, and for the first time today you see her smile.
'But men are weak, Sirgon. Know this: when the streets of Umbar Baharbêl filled with soldiers of Ordâkh and the Heirs of Castamir sailed with the Corsairs to Gondor, my husband Belondor weighed his hatred for Gondor against them... and he dispatched a ship for Pelargir, bearing a warning for you. I counselled against it, but it seems it did not matter, for the ship never arrived. No doubt it was sunk by the Heirs, and no warning ever came to you.
'My first husband was a good man, slain by Ordâkh. My second husband, Belondor, helped to overthrow those who killed my first, and he established a new order in Umbar, the Kindred of the Coins, which will usher in an era of prosperity and peace. If he has any fault, it is that he forgives too readily, and is pleased to forget the sins of Gondor if it means Umbar will have a fresh beginning; this is not a fault that I share! Therefore I give you your life, Sirgon, but I banish you from the Upper Ward. If I see you return I will order my guards to slay you where you stand. Now begone. Our business here is done.'

'I have... much to think about, ${PLAYER}.
'Let us leave the Upper Ward. I believe Mêshka was serious, and it is not safe for us to remain here.'

'The woman Belondor loved was a noblewoman of the city, and she was called Mêshka. I believe her home must be somewhere within the Upper Ward, and the folk within may tell us where she lives with Belondor. It is a gamble, of course: the two may dwell now within the Citadel of Winds, as befits a leader of the Kindred and his wife. But it might not be so, and folk of the Upper Ward may tell us.'
'Yes, can I help you with something? What is it?'

'I have not seen Belondor today, but you just missed his wife Mêshka! She was heading south toward the Sail-haven. She may have been bound for the market of the Upper Ward that is on the way, or one of those in the Sail-haven, and if you hurry you might still catch her.'

You tell Phêlex that you found a bottle among the Shield Isles with a note inside it, and his mouth drops open with surprise. You show it to him and he reads it with interest.
'I never thought to see this again, stranger. You see... I wrote this note almost thirty years ago, when my ship was boarded by Corsairs. I did not think to escape alive, and indeed none others of the crew survived. But I... I am not proud of this, but I threw myself upon their mercy, and they took me into their crew. For more than twenty-five years I lived on that ship, raiding and pillaging, living the life of a Corsair, a brigand of the waves. I am not proud of it... but I was alive, and I intended to stay alive.
'I returned at last to my Khâsha. It would have been a short reunion, and bittersweet, had I not befriended a smuggler by the name of Tumúldo Fierce-water. He encouraged me not to sail with Balakhôr, one of the Heirs of Castamir, and in that way he saved my life, for all who followed Balakhôr to Gondor perished in the war. Ever since that day I have supported the Kindred of the Coins. Loyalty to any others, and the life of a Corsair, are both behind me now.
'I ask you to understand, stranger. I lived a criminal's life, yes, but it was the only life I had available to me. Tumúldo understood that, and so did Khâsha, and now I dedicate my life to serving each of them. It really brings me back, seeing that note in its bottle, but I was a different man when I wrote it, and I have become a different man than the man I became afterward.'

'It is not our place to judge this man. Have we not all done what we must to survive? She Who Remained is no stranger to need, and neither are you, ${PLAYER}. Will it be the same with my brother? Perhaps it will.
'I will continue searching for information that will help us with our mission, but it is good to know the conclusion to the mystery of the note we found in the bottle in the Shield Isles. I was curious, and now that curiosity has been satisfied.'

'It is said \qWherever Elves and dwarves go, trouble is sure to follow.\q
'I am not saying I agree with it, but this is something you will hear in Umbar, if you keep your ears open. 'The two of them are beloved by the folk of the Sail-haven, and have been ever since they helped us cast off the yoke of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing. 'Hurry back to the gaol! There is no time to waste! We have to get the guard to allow Itûr to withdraw his request for trial by combat!'

'I am happy to report that your friend has withdrawn his request for trial by combat. He does not want to remain imprisoned... but when I told him he had drawn Rothog as an opponent, he was unable to speak. Through the stammering I was able to discern that he preferred remaining a guest of the gaol for awhile longer. \qUntil Rothog has retired,\q he may have said, but if I were a wagering man I would not expect that to happen any time soon. The half-troll Master of the Tor-gardens loves fighting that much, even when there is no need for it.
'Our business is now done. I thank you for the donation to the Fleet-fast.'
'Here he is!'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. I know Itûr wanted to be set free, but I also know he would prefer to be alive than to face an unwinnable battle, and Rothog's reputation in the arena speaks for itself.
'I do hope you will take pity upon me if I need coin in the future. I gave the last of my money away as part of this endeavour, after all. It was worth it, was it not?
'Aye, surely it was worth it. But keep me in mind at meal-times, ${PLAYER}, or I will waste away to nothing.'
'Thank you for the... donation. The Fleet-fast will make use of it.'

'Itûr was no martial novice when I knew him, but he was never especially skilled in combat. I think his success in the arena will depend upon the Hûlaz against whom he is matched.
'Let us go to the arena and see if they have posted the match-ups for the upcoming contests.'

'Rothog the Storm? He is my favourite of all the Hûliz who fight in the arena! How can you not have heard of him?
'He is a mighty half-troll who began as a ferocious pit-fighter and rose to command a ship and crew of his own; the Crow-feeders, they were called, for a great mass of carrion birds followed in their wake. When Rothog crossed Balakhôr the Scourge, he found himself once again consigned to the arena, forced to fight his former crew and friends. Balakhôr thought he would die... but Rothog survived for more than a year, sometimes fighting as many as ten bouts in a week!
'He became the favoured champion of the people, and though Balakhôr commanded the master of the arena to execute the half-troll and be done with him, she refused the command. \qFight him yourself, if you wish so badly to see him dead!\q I heard she answered.
'But before he could, Balakhôr sailed to his death in Gondor. And now Rothog belongs to the Kindred of the Coins... but he still fights in the arena, because he enjoys it!'

'Who are the two combatants about whom you speak? Rothog the Storm?
'You need not tell me the other name. Rothog never loses!'

'I was in the stands of the arena the night of the rebellion, when the Kindred of the Coins came to power and cast off the shackles of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing, when the Heirs of Castamir lost their grip on Umbar.
'The ground shook, and we saw flames erupt away across the harbour. Rothog had been put to work fighting the few of his Crow-feeders that remained alive, as well as Men who had defied the Heirs. But that all changed when the whispered rumours became facts proclaimed: Mâkhda Khorbo, the temple of Sauron, had fallen. Rothog turned to face his opponents in the arena, and he spoke a single word. From where I stood I could not hear it, but as it was repeated by others it grew in volume and intensity, until the echo of that one word shook the very foundations of the arena.
'The word was \qHêlsi,\q and when the uprising of the Kindred was completed, Azagath Sea-shadow found Rothog the Storm sitting in the seats reserved for the Heirs of Castamir, surrounded by their half-eaten bodies. The half-troll did not join the Kindred of the Coins at once, but in time he did, and the people of the city love him. He still fights in the arena as often as he can, but now he does it for himself, and no other.
'What does \qHêlsi\q mean? It means \qFreedom.\q'
'Oh no. If Itûr must face Rothog the Storm in the arena, he has no hope for survival!'

'My friend Itûr has to withdraw his request for trial by combat! There is no possible way he can best Rothog the Storm in the arena! Perhaps if he was matched against someone else he would have some hope of victory... but Rothog is the most dangerous Hûlaz to ever fight in the Tor-gardens! Itûr could not have drawn a shorter straw than this!
'Take my money-purse, ${PLAYER}, and hurry back to the gaol! There is no time to waste! We have to get the guard to allow Itûr to withdraw his request!'

'Ni un solo paso en falso desde que llegaste a estas costas. Los informes sostienen que eres un ${CLASS} capaz con muchos talentos. Tienes una inclinación por el heroísmo, una cualidad que algunos consideran noble, y pareces compasivo por fuera.

'Si deseas saber más sobre los guardianes de los registros, por qué estamos aquí, por qué somos necesarios y cómo llegamos a ser, te lo explicaré.'
Ella asiente.
'Pero te advierto. Nuestra historia es... complicada. Nuestra razón de ser, aunque arraigada en el oscuro pasado, mira hacia un futuro prometedor.'

'En el pasado, nuestro papel era rastrear las acciones de aquellos que se oponían a la tiranía de los Herederos de Castamir. Lo hacíamos en secreto. Intercambiábamos la información que adquiríamos con el consejo de liderazgo a cambio de libertad del látigo o la horca.
'Cuando los Herederos cayeron y la Hermandad de las Monedas llegaron al poder, eligieron un nuevo camino para nuestros talentos... uno que preferimos bastante.'
Ella ofrece una sonrisa genuina.
'Comprendemos plenamente la necesidad de entender las acciones emprendidas a favor y en contra de nuestra sociedad en crecimiento. En su sabiduría, los Hermanos y Hermanas nos permiten honrar las buenas acciones realizadas para los ciudadanos de Umbar.
'Descubrirás que el pueblo de Umbar te proporcionará monedas que durante mucho tiempo se han considerado la moneda de nuestra tierra. Estas monedas son poco más que recuerdos. Las llamamos ûr en singular y ûri en plural. Si lo deseas, puedes intercambiar estas monedas con nosotros, y registraremos tus empresas en nuestros registros para que ganes respeto, honor y regalos representativos de nuestra cultura.
'Si no eliges usar las monedas, no importará. Permaneceremos listos para rastrear y conmemorar los esfuerzos realizados por Umbar Baharbêl y su gente. Registraremos tus esfuerzos solo cuando elijas que lo hagamos.'
Ella asiente con la cabeza.
'Hasta que ganes nuestra confianza más completamente, esto es todo lo que puedo decir.'

'My first customer was not a customer at all, for he did not buy anything. Disaster! No, I must try and stay positive. Perhaps he will tell his other wealthy friends. Why are you staring at me like this, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Galengam that the richly-dressed man was Azagath Sea-shadow, leader of the Kindred of the Coins, and that if Cruel Dancer had seen him out and about in the Sail-haven she would have likely killed him where he stood. Galengam frowns.
'We should be glad that she did not see him, then. That would have been quite bad for business! Really, ${PLAYER}, I think your priorities are somewhat askew. You will never make it as a merchant in this world if you have such trouble remembering what is important!'

'A man from Gondor has opened a new market stall in the Sail-haven?' the man asks you. As you tell him that is true, something about his manner strikes you as odd. You ask him if he has an interest in goods from Gondor, and he smiles.
'I do, my new friend. Why should that be unusual? We have had our differences, Umbar and Gondor, but my land desires only to maintain the stability it has earned. It has been different in Gondor, but it should not remain so, should it? My Kindred believes that peace between our lands is possible... if Gondor will meet us along that path. What did you say you were called?'
You answer with your name, and he responds with another charming smile.
'Enjoy your stay in Umbar Baharbêl, ${PLAYER}. Let Azagath Sea-shadow be the first to welcome you to his land. I will not be the last, I warrant. We are a friendly people, as you are certain to discover. Now I will go to see the goods your merchant friend has to sell.'
This man is Azagath, leader of the Kindred of the Coins!

'Post those notices around the Sail-haven for me, perhaps to the south, and soon the customers will swarm my goods and you will have to save me from drowning... drowning in gold phârzi and silver gîmli, that is!'

'I told you the customers would come here in droves, ${PLAYER}! None can resist my rare and valuable goods, or my name is not Galengam! The coin will be rolling in before this day's end!
'This man is my first customer, and...'
Galengam lowers his voice to a hushed whisper.
'...and see how finely he is dressed! This man has money to spend, and I will see to it that he spends most of it at my stall, and no others!'

'The overland route from Gondor has been treacherous of late, and few merchants have come to my city during the months following the conclusion of the war. Did you come by ship?'
Galengam happily chatters away, describing a dangerous voyage across the bay and a brief stay in the Shield Isles. Azagath nods sagely.
'You have done very well to make the journey up Umbarkhîl, for the Cape has had its own share of troubles of late: famine, blight, and unsavoury types among them. You are to be commended for bringing your wares this far.
'I must be about my own business now, but allow me to extend the welcome I gave to ${PLAYER} to you as well, Galengam. I hope you will find the custom in my city to your liking! Farewell, my friends. Perhaps I will see you again.'
'Please take your time, my wealthy friend! You are certain to see something you will want!'

'Carver Gírma has agreed to answer any questions I might have, ${PLAYER}, and I must admit that this is a much finer reception than that I was given in Furukzahar! The Shoreward Stone may be off-limits to me, but if he gives me the answers I seek I will forgive that refusal, and harbour no hard feelings about the matter!
'Then let me ask the first question. I understand that one member of the Kindred of the Coins is a Dwarf of the Temámir who goes by the name Khôltekh. He wears a medallion of some kind, and this medallion sparkles with a most unusual shine, the like of which I have never seen in any jewel buried within the earth. What is this material, and where may it be found? I have never seen anything like it... not while awake, in any case!'

'You speak of Abâshal, my new friend! It can be no other! Some call it \qsea-opal,\q but unlike other jewels the iridescence that gives it value can shine with every colour of the rainbow, and the forces involved in its shaping can cause even those to shift in truly remarkable fashion! You will typically find it cut into small jewels or fashioned into flat panels, if you find it at all; it is most rare, and its naturally-occurring form is brittle. Only the finest of stone-workers can mould it effectively. I blush to tell you I am one such craftsman. The knowledge is known only to few.
'The Empire of Ordâkh and the Church of the All Seeing that they brought with them to Umbar believed the ornamentation of Abâshal to be blasphemous; almost overnight as much of the jewel as could be salvaged was removed from the city and hidden away in secret vaults. When the temple collapsed at the moment of the Dark Lord's fall, it seemed clear the time of his church and the dominion of Ordâkh was ended. The Kindred of the Coins adopted Abâshal as a sign of not just wealth, but of defiance to foreign rule. You will not be surprised to learn that each of the Kindred's leaders possesses a medallion such as that you saw on Khôltekh's person, each one inlaid with a small piece of Abâshal.'

'Abâshal, the sea-opal! At last I have a name to apply to the most beautiful gemstone on which I have ever laid my eyes!
'I will have many more questions for my new friend here, ${PLAYER}. Do not let me keep you! I am disappointed the Shoreward Stone must be closed to outsiders, but I am delighted to know that not all of the Temámir guard their tongues as closely as the others I have met!
'I will remain and speak with Carver Gírma for a time. Abâshal! I would learn as much about it as I can!'

'It is my pleasure to speak of Abâshal! It has been a secret of my people, but as it grows in importance for Umbar I cannot avoid speaking of it to those who would hear more. That would not be right!'

'I see. If I believed most of the Corsairs' martial forces had perished at Pelargir, it seems that the Kindred of the Coins has rebuilt them enough to man the Fleet-fast, at least, very effectively. A frontal assault upon the Citadel of Winds is, in my opinion, out of the question.
'I could not utilize Rossaran effectively in the Fleet-fast, so I sent him to conduct his investigation within the Lower Ward. Seek him out in the Lower Ward to the north and find out what he learned while he was there.'

'Bruidis suggested I find some garb that would allow me to pass undetected within the Fleet-fast, but I refused her; it was not easy, but I do not want to skulk about in secret! If my swan-knight armour is not welcome here, then neither am I!
'She was not pleased about it, but she sent me into the Lower Ward to learn what I could about our opponents. I cannot say that what I have discovered will be of use to us, but I was able to learn how the people feel about some of the various leaders among the Kindred of the Coins.
'Azagath and Belondor are both well-loved by the people, who give them a large portion of the credit for the Sea-stone Mutiny. That is the name given to the overthrow of the Heirs of Castamir and the Church of the All Seeing, when the oppressors of the Empire of Ordâkh were cast out of the city.
'Hármelak, the Golden Queen, is respected more than she is loved. She is one of the wealthiest people in Umbar, but the folk of the Lower Ward distrust her riches; many of them believe she is indifferent to their plight, and would not spend a single coin on their behalf.
'Rothog the Storm is considered a champion of the Lower Ward, for no one lives there who has not heard of his exploits in the arena, or of the manner with which he dispatched many of the Heirs of Castamir during the Mutiny. They love him... but they fear him as well.
'Of the others I was not able to learn very much. I hope this information is of as much use to you as the recounting of the Fleet-fast's defences are to Bruidis! We shall see, I suppose. I will keep looking, ${PLAYER}.'

'I could not utilize Rossaran effectively in the Fleet-fast, so I sent him to conduct his investigation within the Lower Ward. Seek him out to the north and find out what he learned while he was there.'

'I am sorry, ${PLAYER}, but I am not really in the mood for talking right now. Do you think you could give me some time to walk outside the city? I would like to be alone with my thoughts for now.'
'I need some time to be alone with my thoughts for now.'

'I have been thinking, ${PLAYER}... I think I may have been wrong.
'These past few months have been difficult. I abandoned my kingdom, my friends, and the woman I love, and I thought it was for their own good. I punished myself for the weakness I saw in myself, and I believed my wife and kingdom would be better off without relying on such a man as I am. Horn perished on the Pelennor, and Driftwood was born. But that death, and that birth... they changed nothing. I told myself it was right, but it was not.
'I am done with being alone. I think once our mission is concluded... I might be brave enough to see Nona again. Will you go with me when that time comes?'
You tell your friend that you will, and he smiles grimly.
'I do not think she will be happy to see me, ${PLAYER}. I may need you to convince me to go through with such a meeting, if my courage fails me. But for now I intend it.'

'Friend, thank you for what you have done here. I will tell you that even further along the cape you will find others in need of assistance and the skills you possess. If you desire it, I will pay for your passage to Rakhatâb, a citadel to the south where you can continue to assist the people of Umbar. No? I knew I liked you, ${PLAYER}. But even so, it is to the stable-master you will want to go if you are to make the journey to Rakhatâb.
'Know that the citizenry here will remember you. More importantly, it is I who will remember you and speak well of you to my lord. In a place such as Umbar, it is good to have friends in places both high and low. You are well on your way to acquiring both.
'Good travels to you.'

'Thank you, friend. What you have done for the people here in Jax Phanâl will not be forgotten. We are learning to be free and what it means to breathe the air fresh and new.
'I know it seems that some of us are in a state of euphoria; perhaps we are. The shadow that long cast itself over these lands is no more; all around us there is light.'
She smiles.
'...and it seems that even outsiders can become our allies. Good travels to you. When you arrive in Rakhatâb speak with the overseer there. He has already been told that you are coming to their aid.'

'I offer you my sincerest thanks. Your efforts to assist our outpost will be on the lips of the citizens here for years to come.
'An outsider, from lands afar, taking up arms against our former allies who are now foes! It is the mark of a hero to take on the woes of others, to assist those without the means to meet their struggles head on.
'You are such a hero as this. The people of Jax Phanâl know it, and in time perhaps all of Umbar shall know it too. Go now, and in peace. Good travels to you.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}.

'What is your friend's station in life? That will determine not only if he can commit his theft and live, but also how rich a lifestyle he will be able to maintain... and the duration of it!'

'You want to know what will happen to your friend if he begins a life of theft and burglary? I do not have enough information to answer this for you. The reason? I do not know how skilled he is at this trade!
'Yes, I call it a trade. If you speak to others about this matter, they will tell you he will be caught or killed by the guards, or be sent to face Rothog the Storm in the arena, or fall to his death from an upper balcony when he seeks to escape notice. But I say differently.
'I think if he is well-practiced at the art of thievery, he might well escape and live a long and full life feasting upon the fruits of his labours! It can be so in other areas... why not burglary as well?'

'What might have happened had I succumbed to that pull again? Had I climbed through one of the windows of a mansion in the Upper Ward and stolen the valuables I found within, would I be seized by the guards? Would I have been brought to yon building, there to fight and die for my crime? Would that have been right?
'I am curious about this, friend. Ask some of the folk nearby what might have happened to me in that case. I am interested to know.'

'What did visitors to this place have to say about my future, ${PLAYER}? To what ending do they believe I will come to when I breathe my last?'
You recount the words of the folk with whom you spoke, and Driftwood listens intently.
'They are all right, my friend, and they are all wrong. How can this be so? It is because you asked them what would happen if I gave in to my thieving impulses and returned to my past life, and I do not doubt that I would arrive at one of those endings if I did.
'But it is possible for a man to change, even one such as I am. I strive every day to prove it. It is not easy. But it is worth it.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. None of those endings are mine today... and for today that is enough.'

'I should not remain in this district. It is not safe for me to stay here. Let us continue on to the Tor-gardens, ${PLAYER}. There we will speak, and I will find it easier to resist my more dangerous impulses.'

'I am curious about this, friend. Ask some of the folk nearby what might have happened to me in that case. I am interested to know.'
