'Will you help us? There are many goats in the hills north or east of here. Bring back as much of their fat as you can. You'll be rewarded for it, and you'll have my thanks.'

'Enough goat-fat for at least a week! This will keep the wheels of the forge moving for certain. You have earned my thanks, and your coin-purse has surely become... fat. Ha! Ha ha ha!
'Just my little joke, friend. We do what we must.'
Grease the Wheels
Collected blobs of goat fat (${NUMBER}/10)
The forge-master has asked you to go to the hills to the north or east of Rakhatâb and bring back goat fat for greasing the machines.

'That many? We must be working too quickly to repair them as we should. We will need to pay closer attention, if we can, or we will suffer for it! And if we suffer, the work suffers! But I cannot speak these words to the overseer.
'Thank you. This means more to me and the workers than you can know. I do not intend to bury any more of my men.'
Hûzo asked that you look at the support beams around the fort for signs of wear or cracking. If you find any, Hûzo asked you to repair the damaged supports.
Nearly all of the supports you examined were damaged or in a state of disrepair. You should return to Hûzo and inform him of this discovery.

'The foreman sent word that you helped in Jax Phanâl. I appreciate that, friend. There's another thing you could help us with, if you will.
'One of the stone supports collapsed last night. Two of my best workers died in the accident. These structures are old and weak, but we cannot stop our work to fix them; the overseer has threatened to cut our rations even further if our progress slows.
'Would you check the other supports by walls and archways for signs of wear, and reinforce any cracked supports you find? You'd have the gratitude of both myself and my workers.'
Unfortunate Accidents
Damaged supports repaired (${NUMBER}/6)
Hûzo asked you to check the stone supports around the town for signs of wear and to repair any cracks.

'So much around here needs maintenance, and it is my job to keep it all working. I must tell you, I am tired. If you are willing to help, multiple hands will make the work quick. The gears, fires, and pullies are all just around here.'
'We did it, ${PLAYER}! The forges of Rakhatâb are at full strength again! At least for now. No telling how long it will last. For the moment though, let us enjoy our successes!'
Taphis asked that you assist in the maintenance of the forges to help get them back to working at full capacity. Forges can be found throughout Rakhatâb.

'Our forges are almost back to full strength! The fires of the forges are a light for all of Umbar, and might be seen from as far away as Umbar Baharbêl itself! Can you help us finish the task and get these forges fully working again?

'This is more than adequate payment for this... bauble. Take it.'

The overseer holds the bag in one hand weighing it, measuring it.
'A little more than expected. Good. They know their place.

Speak with Foreman Nûrut
'I will pay for any gems or other shiny objects you may find. Though the pearl that the monstrous crab long the beach is worth most to me.'

'Nûrut tells me that you're a person who gets things done. I'm glad you were able to help him with his menial tasks. Perhaps you will be equally skilled at helping with mine: five workers that have gone into debt.
'We have given these workers many freedoms and much coin for their work. Every bit that we give them, every amount of credit we extend... they abuse! Many have spent more coin than they are given. We don't forget or forgive debts here.
'You should know this: if their debts are not paid in coin and on time, we will settle their debt to us in blood. Either way, the debt will be paid.'

'I have nothing to give. They already bled me drier than a stone and forced me to work many hours without compensation or food. If I had no other mouths to feed at home, I would make my way back to the sea or to the city. Please, can you speak to the foreman about this?'

'That's what she asked of you? I know those workers; they don't have the coin. They've used it on food, family, and rebuilding.'
He thinks.
'I may have an answer that saves their hides and pays the overseer her coin.
'To the south and east of here along the shoreline there is a Great Crab. It is rumoured to guard a large pearl.
'There is a merchant here, a collector of beautiful and rare things. I happen to know she will pay handsomely for that pearl.
'Please, ${PLAYER}, bring back the pearl to the merchant over yonder and give the proceeds to the overseer. These men will owe you their lives.'
Credits and Debits

'Thank you for trying. The fool knew the risks. I warned him.'
Tears well in his eyes.
'I am going to build a cairn for my brother down at the shoreline. I will try to remember our days of happiness and laughter. Feel free to visit me there.'

'He took enough to survive for some time out in the wild. There is a place we used to go as children. It is north, outside the fort here and then west down toward the shoreline. He must have gone there. Please, see if he is well.'
Ayaluk's brother is dead by Overseer Ulanor's hand
It appears that trail rations were taken
Ayaluk directed you to a location north-west along the shoreline
Ayaluk is concerned that the overseer in Rakhatâb has injured or killed his brother Zûfan.

'I wonder if you might help me. It is a delicate matter.
'My brother Zûfan has been shaving down his coins, you see, giving the overseer less than her share. I told him not to, but he said he would never get caught. He started doing it for some of the other workers as well.
'Well, this morning I heard a rumour that the overseer caught on to these ruses, and now my brother has vanished. Even if he has run away, I just want to know he's all right. He may be a fool, but he is family.
'Go to our home and see if you can find any clue to where he went. Please, ${PLAYER}, can you help me?'
You discovered that there was a missing pack, oil lantern, and trail rations taken from the home.
Zûfan likely went to the place where the siblings used to hide as children, north from the city and then west along the cliffs near the shoreline. Go there and ensure that the brother is well.
Ulanor found Zûfan before you and exacted the blood price for his debts. You need to deliver this sad news to Ayaluk.
Zûfan likely went to the place where the siblings used to hide as children, north from the city and then west along the cliffs near the shoreline. Go there and ensure that the brother is well.

'This is what we needed. Here, take these notes to the foreman and inform him there are witnesses who will pledge that these reports were never acted upon. Go quickly. I dare not leave for fear of retribution.'

'This is unconscionable! These lives have been damaged or lost! Their sacrifices were brushed away in the past, but the Kindred of the Coins pledged they would not allow such as this to happen here. This matter must be addressed.'
'Of course I have sent requests on behalf of injured or slain workers. How is it that nothing has been done to help their families? I pledge to stand witness.'

'I must supply reports when there are any incidents on site. How did you learn that nothing is being done about them? It does not matter. What matters is that you have my pledge. I will bear witness.'

'I will not send this information on to the foreman until I have the pledge of witnesses from the masters. It is our custom that there are those to bear witness against the accused and I will see that I follow our ancient rules. But, please, make haste.'
Received Kharishah's pledge
Received Beliash's pledge
Received Hûzo's pledge

Ayaluk says that he collected written requests from the different masters in the fort. He asked that you get their verbal agreement that they submitted these reports and requests and come back to him.
Gain Tankho's pledge

'Each foreman submitted reports of accidents, disappearances, and deaths, requesting the effects of the victims to be returned to their families, yet none of the families were compensated. Go to the different masters in the fortress and explain everything to them and gain their pledge that their reports were accurate.
'I would go, but I know I am being watched.'
'Yes, I have submitted those reports to the overseer. How were they never fulfilled? You have my pledge that I will bear witness.'

'Most recently, I sent a request to have pay sent to the family of a man who lost his arms in a terrible accident. He has not been seen since. I thought he simply returned home! I will stand witness to this.
'If the family was not recompensed and the man is missing there is something terrible at work.'

The foreman was not at his post. Where could he have gone? You hear a nearby whisper that there is a new overseer; perhaps you should go and check.

'I want to thank the foreman for his assistance. I know that my brother always held him in high regard and he was the only person in this encampment, aside from you, I felt I could trust.
'Could you tell him how grateful I am for the help he provided to us?'

'It appears that the news reached the ears of the Kindred of the Coins before we captured the overseer. Word arrived with a contingent bearing Rothog's symbol and colour. They took the overseer away and departed; they have already set sail toward the city. It is likely to be a sentence to the pits for the overseer.
'For me, as you can see, I am in a new arena of my own. I pledge, my friend, to do right by the workers here. I will see the work done and do my best to protect them all.
'Thank you, deeply, for your guiding hand in this difficult time. You have proven your worth to us and that service is well remembered, ${PLAYER}.'
The foreman is not at his post, you hear a shout '...to the new Overseer!'
Ayaluk asked you to return to the foreman to thank him for his aid and concern.
Find Ulanor and rescue Ayaluk
Report the news to Foreman Nûrut
Speak with Foreman Nûrut at Rakhatâb
'The guards informed me that that overseer was apprehended. You managed to also save the lad. We are indebted to your service, but this work is not yet done.'

'I will not stand idly by while Umbar withers from within. The Heirs of Castamir were right: the Old Ways are best! We should return to them before we allow scoundrels who do not pay their debts to ruin our future. You fool. You and this meddlesome dwarf obstruct me for the last time. Prepare to die!'
Ulanor yields as her guard arrives. You saved Ayaluk!
Nûrut directed you to inform Ayaluk that he will confront the overseer and that the brother is expected to stand witness. Find Ayaluk at his family home in Rakhatâb.
Ayaluk was not within his hovel. You discovered a small pool of fresh blood in his stead. Deliver this news to the guard.
Ulanor is taking Ayaluk to the Corsairs for some evil purpose. Stop her and save Ayaluk.

'We cannot allow this to continue. I will bring the matter to the master of the guard.
'Return to the young dwarf and tell him that we will seek justice! Ask that he meets us here so that we may go together to confront the overseer; for his brother and the families of those that the overseer harmed within this fortress.'

'Hear me, friend. The master of the guard informed me that the overseer left her post and headed east toward the Corsair camp with a prisoner. It appears that Ayaluk's fear of being watched was correct.
'I can only hope that we can get to him in time. The master of the guard said he can spare none to pursue the overseer, but they will follow after you when he can.
'Make haste east toward the Corsair camp and track down the overseer. If you can, rescue the lad.'
Confronting the Problem
With the overseer apprehended and Ayaluk safely returned to Rhakatâb you should make your way to the foreman and inform him of the good news.
You find only a small pool of blood where Ayaluk should be

The foreman wants to confront the overseer with the evidence of her covering-up and pocketing the personal effects of those suffering ill fates in Rakhatâb. He asked you to first collect Ayaluk to stand witness.
Determinación
Nûrut asked you to check in on Ayaluk and see if he is well and if he is satisfied with the outcome of the investigation and efforts to expose the overseer's crimes.
Find Ayaluk at his home and speak with him
'We should ensure that the young dwarf you rescued is well. There is little more that we can do to ease the pain that he surely feels, but the capture of the overseer should bring him some peace.'

'Justice will be served. That the overseer will meet the fate she deserves must be enough to honour my brother's memory. For the future, I hope that those chosen to take the lead in our rebuilding efforts will exercise care and good dealing! I would rather see the light that dawns on our lands than to dwell upon the shadow that obscures our past.'
Nûrut directed you to speak with the young worker and see how he is faring.
Speak with Ayaluk and complete 'Instance: Whispers of the Forge'
'We will wait for Ulanor to be on the long part of her walk. You distract the guard and I will slip in and out of her chambers to get the proof we need.'
'These notes are clear. The overseer is hiding something and we need the help of others if we are to expose it!'
Ayaluk asked you to meet him near the entry of the overseer's office.

'Friend, I have had a change of heart. The overseer here in Rakhatâb brings too much harm. My brother should not have been killed. I have watched the comings and goings of individuals with whom the overseer meets, and I believe that there is some rot here that must be cut out. I intend to slip into her chambers, get whatever information I can, and report it to certain folk who can do something about it.
'I only require a distraction long enough to cover my efforts. Will you help me?'
Whispers of the Forge
After assisting Ayaluk he returned to his family home with haste. He directed you to speak with him there.
Ayaluk asked you to distract the guards who watch over the overseer's office in the fortress. He is certain that there is something untoward happening here.

'Not that it's any of your business, but my wine is gone! All the trouble I've been through just trying to smuggle such acquired delectables to Umbar... I should be paid a king's ransom!
'You look fairly capable. If you're lookin' to make some coin, I'm lookin' for someone to retrieve what I've lost!'

'Well, would you look at that. You came through!

'You... look different. Not like them. Those filthy scoundrels. I never thought life would be like this. When I first set out for the isles....
'I've underestimated just how cruel and rough the life of a pirate is. Your life is constantly at risk and people walk all over you.
'But I've a plan. They don't take kindly to deserters but I've a boat near the western coast. If I could get the necessary supplies to make her sea-worthy I might just be able to be free.'
'You made it, and you have the things! I'll finally be able to go home! I can't thank you enough, stranger. These are dark times indeed, but the light shines forth where it can!'

Large crabs can be found to the south-east of Khûtra. Go there and return with crab meat to feed the hungry villagers.

Collect crab meat (${NUMBER}/10)
'Please, we have so many who are hungry. The crabs can be found to the east along the shore. Please hurry!'

'Help from outsiders? And you were sent by Roshat? He must be getting truly desperate.
'It's true we could use all the help we can get. Our lures are as good and our hands as quick as ever. It's the trout themselves that have changed. They have turned a pallid, slimy green, afflicted with some terrible disease. We know not why. Some of the hands have taken to calling it the stench, for obvious reasons. We cannot eat or sell any of the fish we catch, it makes any who eat it violently ill.
'I'll be honest with you, moreso than perhaps Roshat was – we really could use your help. We rely on the fish to fill our bellies and our coin pouches. I know Roshat has suspicions about the source of the disease, but he won't trust outsiders unless he sees your value.
'I don't know how to heal our fish, but I know how you could help fill our bellies and perhaps gain his trust. There are crabs to the east of here, along the shore, just beyond the village. They seem to be immune to the stench, at least so far. However, they fight back more than we gentle fisherfolk can handle.
'Would you go to the east and bring us back some crab to feed our people?'
'I am grateful. We are proud folk, but I'm not too proud to admit my people will have full bellies tonight thanks to you. You might want to talk to Elder Roshat again.'

'We are not paying by the day. With all due haste, I recall I said. We need that necklace back.'

'Thank you for retrieving this. It is priceless to the Yâshalam family. If anyone asks, nothing was found in the ruins, and we never asked for this. I'm sure you understand.

'Ah, the chick here? Say hello to our guest, little Berkha! Say hello! Ah, he's shy. You know how children that age can be.
'I found him alone not far from here. I do not know what became of his family, but if I did not adopt him as my own he surely would have died on these harsh isles. Though my kind are a far sight from his flock, surely our differences cannot be insurmountable. If you would like to be helpful to me, could you gather some insects for him to eat? 'Me? I'm an old friend of Raghda-gûn's here. I heard about this piece of flotsam asking around about roc eggs the other day. I didn't think much of it until one day I come out of the pub and he's not in his usual spot. Something feels wrong about it, so I gather Nekhama here–'
Nekhama grunts.
'–and I come to see Raghda-gûn. You know, just in case. Turns out we didn't have much to worry about here as this fool has as much sense as he does hygiene.'
Nekhama grunts again, but this one sounds like it might have been a laugh.
'Is he alive? He is, merely stunned by the thrashing we gave him. Hmm? Curious about who he meant to steal the egg for? Ah so are we. Tell you what, Nekhama here will carry this sea-sponge back to Halrax.'
Nekhama grunts disapprovingly.
'Meet her there later today and see if she hasn't learned anything. I'm going to stay a while longer and speak to my friend.'

'No matter how much I'd like to send more guards after Shúkurz, it'd only make things worse with that Man. But you're different; I'm sure he's the kind who'd trust you over an Orc.
'It won't be hard for you to track down Shúkurz. See that trail of footprints, leading out of the village? Heh, I bet he was a lousy scout in Gundabad.'

'I am sorry, ${CLASS}; I followed you from Mâr Naphra to find Kafagur. I had believed that it was a camp full of dangerous Orcs. Clearly, I was mistaken, and this investigation was faulty from the start.
'It's true that I am not from Umbar, but rather, Gondor. I... do not know if I can tell you what led me here, but you have my word: I will not harm the Orcs.
'Whether they believe me is another matter entirely. Though, after I judged them so rashly, I do not know if I deserve that trust.'

'Phocas doesn't seem like the bad sort. After all, he was willing to stop running long enough to listen to me. I'm sure we'll figure things out.
'I've got more I want to tell you, but I ought to take Phocas back to Kafagur first. I'll see you there.'

'Thanks for making sure I was all right, ${PLAYER}. Grúshul's right; I acted like a fool. Even during our journey out of Gundabad, we stuck to the wilds because we knew Men would kill us if they saw us. I should have been scared of Phocas.
'But... I remembered how we got out of Gundabad in the first place. With your help, and the help of others. I remembered Náin, and how he apologized to me.
'I guess I wanted to believe that sort of thing could happen again. Maybe it can.'

'If everyone splits up and checks different taverns in the city, we may more quickly learn of a means of rescuing Thorongil from Azagath.'

'I am worried for our rulers. I heard a rumour that the widow of Balakhôr the Scourge has offered bounties on the leaders of the Kindred of the Coins, and even now her trained killers are loose in the city! They say no one has seen Tumúldo Fierce-water in weeks, and even Tatháta the Beast is missing. She often walked the streets of the Lower Ward, her fighting-hounds by her side, but I cannot remember the last time she did.
'We owe the Kindred much for dealing with the Heirs of Castamir and releasing us from the shackles of Ordâkh. I hope they are all right.'

'The Hungry Deep Tavern is the finest in the city, if you ask me. Every time I come here I eat too much.
'The Kindred of the Coins? They mean well, and if you ask me they have done right by us, but I think they keep secrets from us all the same. Seven of them there are, you know that, but there has been turnover among their ranks since the uprising. Some say Guild-master Imilka was in league with the Heirs of Castamir and Tatháta was right to replace her in the Kindred... but I don't know. And there was another, a scholar whose name I misremember... whatever happened to him? He ruled in the Tor-gardens, but now he is gone and that half-troll, Rothog, has his place in the Kindred! He frightens me.
'Oh, when I eat too much I also speak too much! Favour me and tell no one of these things I have said.'

'I am not one for gossip, friend, but I have heard a thing or two about the Kindred of the Coins that you might find interesting! For the right price, that is....'

'I and my brother will stand with you to rescue Thorongil, ${PLAYER}. Will we not, Corudan? Or have you had your fill of this place already?'

'I will stand with you, ${PLAYER}, not only because of your rescue, and not only because of the adventures we shared in the Kingdom of Rohan. I will stand with you because it is right.
'I was not mistreated by the Kindred of the Coins, despite Nakási's words and her frequent promises to exact revenge upon any who aid Gondor. At sea I was given permission to walk freely about the ship, and I followed her commands quickly and well. Did my captivity chafe? I cannot say it did not, but I felt it was in service of a noble purpose, and that was enough. Tatháta suggested I be allowed to walk freely about the ships and the harbour when we docked, but the Wave-reaper feared my servility was an act, and commanded her kinswoman to keep me tied to the mast while Nakási was away. I cannot tell you with complete certainty if she was right, ${PLAYER}.
'But I can tell you this. The Kindred of the Coins value their captives only for so long as they retain value. Had I proven a burden or unmanageable, I think I would not have survived the voyage to Umbar. It may be the same with the young heir of Pinnath Gelin. If he loses his value as a hostage, I believe he will not long survive in the Kindred's company.
'Nakási brought him to Azagath Sea-shadow in the Citadel of Winds, from where the Kindred rule this city. I will help you as I can... but how do you intend to enter the most well-guarded district of Umbar Baharbêl?'
'We will stand with them, will we not, Corudan?'

'When my brother and I returned to Umbar, his plan had been for us to visit some of the taverns and inns of the city so we could learn what had happened while we were gone, recruit a larger crew, and Jajax could acquire a more suitable ship. That plan ran into some trouble! But I think at its heart it was still a good idea, because at taverns people speak more freely. If there is any way into the Citadel of Winds, someone at one of the taverns may unknowingly speak of it.
'I hope I am not being too forward with this suggestion! But it makes sense to me, ${PLAYER}. If everyone splits up and checks different taverns in the city, we may more quickly learn of a means of rescuing Thorongil from Azagath.'
'How do you intend to enter the most well-guarded district of Umbar Baharbêl?'

'Forgive Enât her distrust, stranger, but we have reason to be wary. Our master is very particular about the means by which we carry out his commands. We bring sea-water through the city to the fountains inside Sûr Birix, the Citadel of Winds, every morning, and every night those fountains are emptied to await our return the next morning. It is hard, heavy work, and there are fewer of us now than there used to be. Azagath has dismissed some of our fellows before now, but... no one seems to know where Sadûkh has gone.'
Enât hisses at Ushu to not say anything more, and the woman nods.
'He may be fine, and he may not. But without Sadûkh our work will be more difficult. Azagath smiles with his mouth, but his eyes are unmoved, and if we do not find some way to replace Sadûkh's burden we may be the next ones to disappear.
'Prove to me you can carry this bowl of sea-water without spilling a single drop, and perhaps you can accompany us into the Citadel. Bring it to the courtyard of the Teeming Net Tavern, to the south-east, and we will see if you are steady enough to join us.'
'We should not say anything.'

'Prove to me you can carry that bowl of sea-water without spilling a single drop, and perhaps you can accompany us into the Citadel. Bring it to the courtyard of the Teeming Net Tavern, to the south-east, and we will see if you are steady enough to join us.'

'You did well-enough, stranger. You may accompany us when next we perform our duties, and I will ask no questions of you. Your reasons for wanting to gain access to Sûr Birix are your own, but you must endanger none of my friends. If such treachery seems possible, I will alert the guards at once.
'Let this last warning guide your steps. Neither Enât nor I know what happened to Sadûkh, but of this I am certain: he saw something he was not supposed to see, some secret of the Sea-shadow, and now he has paid for it.
'Azagath is dangerous. We water-bearers may be beneath his notice... but it may not be possible to always remain so.'

'I would not seek to supplant any member of the Kindred of the Coins, for ours is a necessary council and Umbar is made better by our efforts. But this too is its strength: the Kindred itself is more important than any individual member. Were Azagath to fall during your rescue of the Gondorian hostage, that would be a most unfortunate turn, but the Kindred itself would survive... and that is everything.'
Hármelak holds your gaze but lowers her voice.
'Azagath returned to the city in the grip of a curious superstition. Every morning he instructs some among his servants to carry empty bowls down to the docks beside the Harbour Warden's tower. They fill these bowls with saltwater from the bay. Once this is done, they then carry these bowls of saltwater through the streets of the city until they reach the bridge beyond the Fleet-fast. The guards let them pass, without fail, and once inside they fill the fountains within the Citadel with the saltwater they carry. At midnight, the fountains are emptied... and at dawn the process begins again.
'No one pays attention to the servants who carry the water, ${PLAYER}, not the folk of the city, not the guards of the Fleet-fast, and not Azagath Sea-shadow. Among these servants you could gain access to the Citadel of Winds, and whatever might befall then... well, it would be for the benefit of the city, would it not?
'I trust this discussion has been as illuminating for you as it has been for me. Rothog will see you out.'

'Be gone now.'
Before you turn to leave, you quietly ask Rothog why he is helping you. The half-troll stares impassively down at you and says nothing.

'When Balakhôr perished in the war and the power of the Heirs of Castamir was broken, I knew the time had come to act. We will speak of it further in the garden.'

'The Kindred of the Coins was my idea, ${PLAYER}, inspired by the Corsair councils that once governed Umbar between the reigns of tyrants. A King or a Queen or a Steward can begin with the best of intentions, but they can be corrupted. They can make the wrong choice, but a group can guard against such wrong choices. A group can see all the sides of a problem. In a city such as Umbar Baharbêl, only a council can lead effectively for the good of all. That was my idea, ${PLAYER}: a council of leaders that would not be subservient to any outside force; not Gondor, not the Empire of Ordâkh, not the Dark Lord Sauron or his servants.
'During the rule of the Heirs of Castamir and the Church of the All Seeing, I asked Khôltekh to fashion seven medallions in the form of large coins that could be worn as necklaces. Each was made of a different material, signifying our disparate backgrounds and influences, but each had something in common. Khôltekh embedded a shard of Abâshal, the valuable sea-opal treasured by his people, into each coin.
'Only days after Balakhôr perished in Gondor, a tremendous quake rocked the city. The temple of Sauron crumbled and fell into the earth, and I knew it was the time to act. I sent the medallions fashioned by Khôltekh to my chief allies, and the uprising began. The Sea-stone Mutiny would spell the end of outside authority over Umbar: that of Ordâkh, that of Gondor, that of Sauron. The Kindred of the Coins would make Umbar Baharbêl a Free City again.
'Let us speak further in my office.'
'Let us speak further in my office, to the north.'

'Azagath is a Black Númenórean, a blood-ally of Balakhôr during the Scourge's rise to power. Their friendship soured when Balakhôr sought to claim rulership over all of Umbar in the name of the Heirs of Castamir. Azagath opposed his bid, a duel was fought, and Azagath suffered defeat; he received a scar upon his face and pled for mercy. It was granted, and he was banished. We did not see him for many years, and during that time Azagath's warnings were proven true. I called for his aid during the Sea-stone Mutiny, and when he returned to the city he did so as a beloved hero. \qHadôru,\q they called him, \qHe Who Returned.\q
'There was no celebration for me, ${PLAYER}. I never fled the city, so I had no need to return a hero! I was here always: steadfast! Unyielding! The Kindred was my idea, but when the seven of us cast our lots for who would lead us, it was Azagath who prevailed. He is charming, any can see that, and the others believed he could more easily inspire the Umbari people than I could. I have been patient through all these troubles. Is that not inspiring?'
Hármelak stares at you with eyes of ice, and despite her words you can tell that being passed over for leadership of the Kindred bothers her more than she is willing to say.
'Do not misunderstand me. I would be content for any to lead us if he or she held dear the interests of the city, ${PLAYER}. But I think it is not so for Azagath. He has some plan of his own, a secret he keeps from the rest of us: The Song of Waves and Wind. I know not what it is, but it cannot be in the interest of my city.'

'I take you to see her,' Rothog continues. Some of the people nearby stare at you and the half-troll member of the Kindred of the Coins, many of them backing away or preparing to run if his attention turns to them.
'Now, ${PLAYER}. Hármelak does not like to be kept waiting.'

'Thank you, Rothog.'
Hármelak studies you silently for a moment. When she speaks again, her lips turn upwards in a faint smile.
'Welcome to Umbar Baharbêl, ${PLAYER}. I could have invited the others of your group, but I prefer to speak to you alone about this matter. You understand. It is not often that I have the opportunity to speak to such as you. It is the matter of our hostage that brings you here, I understand?'
You keep your expression guarded, but Hármelak's smile becomes more pronounced.
'Khôltekh prides himself upon knowing everything that transpires in this city, but he does not share everything with us. I have eyes of my own, and they see a great deal at a variety of interesting places: outside the gaol in the Fleet-fast, by the home of Belondor and Mêshka in my very own Upper Ward, among the alleys of the Sail-haven. Your group has not remained hidden to my eyes, ${PLAYER}, and I know why you have come to my city.
'Let us continue our discussion by the fountain of my courtyard.'
'Let us continue our discussion by the fountain in my courtyard.'

'You stand in the presence of one of the wealthiest people in all of Umbar, ${PLAYER}, but know this: wealth does not grant complete power. How many of my rivals had riches but lacked the will to maintain their control? Now their wealth is mine. The folk of the city whisper that my fortune rivals that of many dwarf-lords, but their whispers are untrue: my fortune exceeds that of even the dwarf-kings! I am the matron of the most powerful merchant clan in Umbar, and we trade in all manner of expensive goods from across the Haradwaith: spices, jewels, silks, artwork, even relics of ancient days.
'I was widowed when I was young, and my husband's brothers sought to gain control of the business. They failed. It takes an iron will to prosper as I have. Did I not witness Mût Tadaul, the Death of Light, when I was but a young girl? I knew the evils of the Church of the All Seeing from a young age, but I saw too the value of maintaining the appearance of cooperation. In public I allied with the Ordâkhai occupiers and then with the Heirs of Castamir, but always I worked secretly against them. Quietly I set up a network of those opposed to the interlopers endangering my city. It brought me into contact with some who shared my goal of making Umbar Baharbêl a Free City: Azagath and Belondor, Khôltekh of the Temámir, the smugglers Tumúldo and Nakási.
'When Balakhôr perished in the war and the power of the Heirs of Castamir was broken, I knew the time had come to act. We will speak of it further in the garden to the north.'

'This is Lhanuch, the village of the Uch-lûth from which Nona came? I am pleased to see it. She did not speak of it often, but when she did her voice was fond... despite her attempts to prevent it, I think.
'You had better go on ahead, ${PLAYER}. Nona's people will remember you. Caebar and my sister and I will be considered... what was the word? Duvodiad? Yes, that was it.
'The three of us may be duvodiad, but in Lhanuch I believe you will be welcomed.'

'I knew you would one day climb this hill and come again to Lhanuch, ${PLAYER}. I saw it in the Pool of the King only weeks after my daughter Nona departed, following the dream that carried her away to fight another kingdom's war. She returned months afterward with a broken heart and a child in her belly, and I thought you would return in the company of this man, this Horn who was the father of the child. But sun and moon rose and fell, and it was not you who first came to Lhanuch with tidings.'
Suvulch frowns, and you remember that he considers himself more gifted with weapons than with words.
'It was a minstrel, an old one with white hair and a solemn face. He said he served a king of the horse-lords who perished fighting the Dark Lord, and he had sad tidings for Nona. \qHorn is dead,\q he said to her, and while she had raged with anger in the wordless months that passed, her fury was replaced all at once, and with sorrow. I wept with the two of them. Yes, even I! But I am her father, and I raised my Nona to be strong. Her tears showed to me how deeply she loved this Horn, even though she buried that love beneath the rage she held for him, and which he deserved! So I wept alongside them, and when the minstrel departed I embraced my daughter and I told her that I would never again say a cross word about the man Horn.
'I meant it even then, but in time I have come to understand he was a man of courage who believed he was not courageous, ${PLAYER}. That is a curious thing, and not common among the Uch-lûth. But perhaps not all can be as honest as Suvulch, who is certain of his courage and acts upon it every day.'
He roughly clasps your arm, and then points up the hill.
'My daughter sits by the summit of the village, by the fire on the right. She will be glad to see you.'

'${PLAYER}, my dear friend! It is good to see you again at last! If you waited a few more months you might meet my son or my daughter... but I am glad you did not wait.
'No, I do not yet know what my child will be! When the days feel longest I wonder if Hildegard would tell me whether I am having a son or a daughter... but I cannot bring myself to return to the soothsayer's cave. When Gléowine came to Lhanuch and told me of what transpired before the walls of Minas Tirith... it was as if I was hearing of it for the second time, seeing it again, feeling anew all the pain of it. So I will not return to Hildegard.
'Gléowine spoke also of your deeds, and I know Horn was avenged. I would have become Wadu's Ghost once more and done it myself, but you can see that I am somewhat occupied for now. So I thank you, and I know Horn does as well, and so does his child.'

'Stand aside, ${PLAYER}. To return here, after sending me away... his wits are more addled than they used to be! How can you explain his presence here?'
Nona's eyes boil with fury, but your keen eyesight reveals that the hand holding her brother's sword trembles. She does not want to become Wadu's Ghost again, despite her words and the anger she has nursed for Horn since he sent her away from the war. If only there was some way for you to break the tension. You cast your thoughts back to the days you spent travelling with Horn and Nona, and then you have it.
You recount your cautious steps within the deserted village of Dunfast, in Wildermore, when Nona had left your little party, leaving you in the company of Horn, the minstrel Gléowine, and Corudan. The Elf felt eyes upon your group, and it was with heightened senses that the four of you crept towards the bush that seemed to contain the unwelcome and hostile eyes. Horn valiantly approached the bush, his hand upon his sword, prepared to face whatever evil lurked within...
... and promptly fell down on his rump when the shrew within leapt out of its hiding-place

'I have not had time yet to rest and to speak with my brother, for we have gone from one danger to another. I look forward to hearing of Corudan's adventures and telling him of my own. Perhaps that time has come.
'It may not last, for while the Kindred of the Coins has claimed to make this a Free City, it would seem an evil has taken root within the membership of that council. I do not think your business in this land is yet finished, ${PLAYER}. Azagath remains a danger... and my heart tells me he is not the only member of the Kindred who is not as they appear.'

'During the sea-voyage that brought young Thorongil and me to Umbar, I did what I could to keep the boy out of trouble. It was not always an easy task, and I tell you truly that it was a thankless one... but I am relieved that both he and I survived the passage. That he has also been brought safely from the Citadel of Winds... it is a sign of your prowess and my memory of our shared adventures that I am less surprised by that!
'I look forward to hearing of my sister's adventures and to telling her my own. I still cannot believe that she is alive, but of course she was always... stubborn. She might say the same of me, but I believe Sigileth has always been more headstrong than I am. Since you have spent time with each of us, only you can tell us for certain.'
Corudan smiles.
'No, you can keep your answer. I know what it is.'

'My brother always has a plan or a scheme in mind, ${PLAYER}! Do you think he had this planned all along? Is this why he refused to join your crew? It must be, surely!'
You consider whether to dispel Daxamat's notion of his brother, and decide not to do so. You suspect that it would take a ship's hold full of evidence to lessen Daxamat's opinion of his brother, and even then it might not be possible.
'My brother is really something, isn't he?' Daxamat asks you, and you have no choice but to nod in agreement.

'I have listened to the account of what transpired within the Citadel, ${PLAYER}, and my mind is clear. Belondor has no love for Gondor, and who could blame him for that, but he is not a monster. Whatever evil lies at the heart of the Kindred of the Coins, my old friend is not the cause of it. He would have prevented Nakási from slaying their young hostage... I am sure of it.
'Azagath and the web he has woven has my friend caught, just as I was enmeshed by the commands of the Steward Denethor. Belondor is not beyond saving. Of this I am certain.'

'It is done, for now, is it not? We have carried out the commands of King Elessar, though they have brought us far from our homes.'
Caebar looks out over the water, and shrugs his shoulders.
'I suppose I don't really have a home any longer, do I? My mother and my uncle Carlong would not welcome me back to Ethring, not even if they knew the part I played on this grand adventure. Especially not if they knew. It wasn't that large a part, but I'd like to think I was some help along the way.
'It is up to me to make a new home for myself now, somewhere out here in the world. I was so afraid of... I cannot say what I was afraid of, exactly... I think it was the \qbigness\q of the world, that sense of vast, open spaces, far beyond the land in which I grew up. It is so different here, but perhaps that is a good thing for me. I could not find a place in which to belong in the land of my birth. Maybe I will find a place here.
'Thank you for bringing me along on your voyage! I will do whatever I can to help King Elessar bring peace to Gondor, and if that causes further conflict with the Kindred of the Coins, well... I will do what I can to help. All you need do is ask, ${PLAYER}. I will follow wherever you lead!
'Just... maybe not aboard a ship next time,' he says, with laughter in his eyes.
Jajax is by the Harbour Warden's tower.
Nimrodel is by the Harbour Warden's tower.
The successful completion of your mission to Umbar is the result of those who helped you, and many of them are now by the Harbour Warden's tower and want to speak with you.

'Our mission to Umbar is completed, ${PLAYER}, for both captives held by the Kindred of the Coins have been rescued. I will return with Thorongil to Anfalas as soon as it can be arranged. His father Carandolion will be very pleased, but not surprised, to learn that we have triumphed!
'There will still be work to be done here in Umbar. I know it.'

'Has it been so long that you have forgotten the most important rule of all, ${PLAYER}? Never count Jajax out of a fight, for he will return and surprise you! It is a lesson the Prince of Dol Amroth has now learned. You should have seen his face when it became apparent that only Jajax could turn defeat into victory!
'Aye, it seemed defeat was certain. He has spies in this land, a band of whisperers and movers-in-secret that go by the name \qCircle of the Eagle,\q and when they reported to him that your ship never arrived, he despaired. A plan was conceived, a desperate plan, but it was considered the only option left to save the captive boy. The Prince could not achieve it, nor could the King. Only a Corsair would do. Only THE Corsair would do, and that means Jajax!
'It is good to be owed favours by Kings and Princes, ${PLAYER}, and I shall be well-rewarded for my part in this deception. I admit I believed the water carried by Nimrodel was in some way enchanted and would prove more effective that it turned out... but all is well now. It must be the good fortune of Jajax coming through in the end once again.
'How did my brother fare on your voyage? I hope he did not make too great a mess of things without me there to set him right!'

'For long years I believed I was no longer a part of the world, ${PLAYER}, and I sheltered with the Avorrim and stood at a remove from all others. The kindness of Arwen, and the good heart of Roamingstar, have taught me I was wrong. In gratitude I offered to play a role in their drama... was it very different than the role I played for so long, the role of Dorthaneth?
'I have set aside my veil of mourning, ${PLAYER}. It is good to be of help to my friends, no matter the dangers. Their kindness is like the warm sun upon my skin, and I welcome it.
'But do not mistake me! The danger of Azagath remains. I judge that he is no ordinary man; I felt Sauron's mark upon him.'

'I have spoken with the others, and I still do not understand one thing. If the Corsair Jajax arranged with Khôltekh to gain access to the Citadel with his prisoner... why did the Temámir not accompany Jajax inside? If he believed Jajax's prisoner was truly Queen Arwen, would he not want to be present at the Kindred's triumph?'
Gimli strokes his beard.
'Unless... unless Khôltekh knew that Jajax had not actually captured Queen Arwen. But why would he help us rescue Thorongil? Is he secretly working against Azagath's aims?'
You tell Gimli that your audience with Hármelak has shown you the Kindred of the Coins may not be as united in their purposes as it seems from the outside.
'That is why the King Under The Mountain is so important, ${PLAYER}. I will keep thinking about it. Khôltekh's place in all this makes my head hurt!'

'I have listened to the account of what transpired within the Citadel of Winds, ${PLAYER}, and it seems to me that Azagath Sea-shadow is no mere man. Nimrodel says she felt the mark of Sauron upon him... do you think he may be one of the Gúrzyul? If so, he has kept his nature hidden from the others of the Kindred and from the Umbari people. Nakási Wave-reaper spoke to you of the Song of Waves and Wind before she left Gondor, and I understand Hármelak mentioned it when you met with her, but she knew little more than its name.
'Can it be that the Song of Waves and Wind has as its foundation some evil of Mordor? If that is so, we cannot leave Azagath to make use of it... whatever it may be. The adventure that brought us to Umbar is over... but our work here is not finished.'

'Many an ambitious soul has ventured east to Bax Garâkh in search of this treasure. Whether they've been successful, I cannot say I know. Perhaps the treasure does not exist after all.
'Ah, I've taken up enough of your time. Watch yourself, traveller. Not everyone here is as friendly as I.'

I am to obtain twenty heaps for delivery to the city. If you are willing to undertake this request, you will be paid very well.'

'I am surprised that I did not sense your arrival. Given the task you have just completed for me I thought I would have sensed you from a great distance. Strange that, yes? As promised, a generous reward for such a terrible request.'

As foul as the task may seem, it is a necessary one for the outfitters of Umbar: the collection of excrement from wild beasts throughout the Cape of Umbar for the production of tannins.

Abido expressed that the common folk have a less refined palette than those of the higher castes in the city. They do not desire more than the simple meat of boars to fill their bellies.

Abido, excited at the prospect of seeing Nêjagil, wants you to return to the black sands in the crags north-west of Umbar City to find and slaughter the beast. Collect its tail and return to him at the expedition encampment.

Abido, excited at the prospect of seeing Nêjagil, wants you to return to the black sands in the crags north-west of Umbar City to find and slaughter the beast. Collect its tail and return to him at the expedition encampment.

He shakes his head.
'Would that I could leave my post during the day to hunt down the beast.

'Zerkho and Dorshet do not believe that there is a threat posed by the sea hawks and bog-lurkers as you attempt to relieve them of their limbs and eggs. I respect their knowledge but question that advice. I would use caution, friend.'

'The hills and plains that meet the sea teem with an abundance of fauna, natural and corrupt. Cooks in the city use bits gathered from uncorrupted creatures to supplement the food served throughout the city.
'My role is to organize the collection and distribution of the materials the cooks require and reward any who aid in the effort. Discuss with Zerkho and Dorshet the benefits gained from gathering materials and the danger inherent to meeting the requests.'

'As you climb the hills far to the north and west of this expedition, you will see signs of uncorrupted fauna. Seahawks soar on the warm air rising from the land as it fights with cool breezes from the sea. Bog-lurkers, often mistaken for reeds or detritus, wander in large numbers.
'Cooks in Umbar draw the most value from these creatures.
'Sea hawks lay large flavourful eggs that epicures devour by the dozen. The profit gained exceeds the risk presented by disturbing the sea hawk's nests.
'Bog-lurker legs are a delicacy for the thin shaft of gelatinous meat drawn forth when boiled and the salty broth that remains after. Last, the seeds found on the lurker's back grow to stock our vegetable and spice stores.'

'I have no desire to harm the sea hawks making their nests in the northern part of the Cape of Umbar. Unlike the culinarians, I do not wish to steal their young. I want only to recover what they lose and what they find that was lost.
'I am sorry. I do not mean to be cryptic. The sea hawks lose their feathers, naturally and unnaturally. The sea hawks also find baubles and bits from shipwrecks.

'Speak with Dorshet and Zerkho. Their knowledge provides advantages in harvesting the materials my patrons require.'

'I do not care for the wanton slaughter of animals. I find it cruel and inhumane. However, I do support studying nature's mechanisms to comprehend how we might harness the natural powers and strength all around us.

'Once delivered, the cook's guild will further refine and separate the spice from the silt. The guild can include the spice in their recipes, package it for sale, and teach others the processes of refining the product.

'Merchant or magistrate, if you are a leader in Umbar, you dress in fineries offered by the outfitters who learned to refine the heavy silk of desert spiders into fine fibres and fabric.

'Use caution when collecting the silk from the spiders in the desert. They are known to entrap many travellers and beasts who stumble like newborn calves through their nests.'

'I am impressed with the care you took in harvesting this silk. Too often, I will find frayed fibres dragged through the dust and dirt. Few understand that such carelessness ruins much of the material, reducing the price the silk earns when sold at market.

'What the advisors teach you is learned from books and speeches. What I will tell is from experience of my own and that of travellers who make their way through the unforgiving desert.
'When there is a question of your safety move to the rocks.
'When your journey is beginning make sure to drink your water.
'Share your water with others only if they are trusted or of your kin.
'Do not linger on the hot sand too long.
'Now... you are as prepared as can be.'

Speak with the outfitter, Karbah

'The land to the east of the city and north of this encampment is barren and desert-like. There lay a wasteland where trees grow sparsely and danger lurks within the sand.
'Terrible creatures sift through the sand, spin it about them as they blow across the landscape, or, worse, lay traps to ensnare the unobservant.
'Above all else, one must be alert and informed when entering those lands.
'I advise consulting with the experts here within the expedition camp for their guidance and direction to understand why we hunt in the desert and what you should expect if you make your way there.'

'Khânai sent you to learn about why the chefs of Umbar desire us to explore and ravage the already ravaged desert land to the east of the city, eh?
'I will tell you, then. Across the desert grows an abundant array of aromatic and potent spices that give many of the dishes enjoyed by our aristocracy. It is for this reason that we send so many adventurers into the wastes.
'There are enemies there: grim winds that carry the spice, and worms that sift the sand to move, leaving spice in their wake, or, carrying the spice within themselves. These are each viable targets for the collection of the spices we desire.
'But be wary, the magical nature of the grim and the violent nature of the sand-worms should not be underestimated.'

'In the desert land east of Umbar Baharbêl, there is a great brood of spiders weaving deep nests and webs to ensnare beasts as large as water buffalo. It is these spiders that the aristocracy prizes. Not for anything other than the webbing and silk that the spiders weave.
'When worked through looms, the spider-silk can be turned into beautiful fabrics that are then dyed and manufactured to the specifications made by the great tailors of the guilds and sold to the well-to-do.
'Be warned, the spiders are foul creatures with a penchant for blood. And, sadly, they are very good at obtaining what they desire. You must simply be better at keeping yourself alive.'

'The reasons to hunt in the desert waste are many. As a scholar, the main reason that I choose is knowledge.
'We seek to understand the secrets of spider's weaving webs. We wish to know why the frill about a lizard's neck repairs itself as does a salamander's body. These mysteries are the puzzles that drive us back into the desert when we know the dangers are great.'

'Go north and do your best to find the pristine feathers in sea-hawk nests. If you must, kill the birds and collect the pristine feathers. When you collect enough to meet the quota return them to me here at the expedition encampment.'

'These shall do nicely. There are some jewellers who adorn their earrings, necklaces, and other jewellery with feathers. They pay a fair price for the trouble we incur to gather the feathers. I thank you for taking care to harm as few sea-hawks as you could.'

Luthana's patrons in Umbar Baharbêl use sea-hawk feathers when creating some jewellery. She asked that you do your best to collect moulted feathered from their nests and from live creatures if you must.

'I prefer if you can acquire feathers without killing the sea-hawks. There should be feathers that the birds lose in the process of moulting. If you do not find enough in the nests, you may have to kill the birds to meet our quota.
'Find the birds in the hills north of Umbar proper and far north from this encampment. I need fourteen pristine feathers returned to me.'

You collected enough feathers for Luthana. Return to the hunter's expedition in the south of the Cape of Umbar and deliver the feathers to her.

Recupera el mensaje del halcón marino
Recoge un trozo de carne de la plaza cerca del halcón marino
El halcón marino mira hacia arriba con expectación, y tú sujetas el mensaje de regreso a su pata.
'Estoy seguro de que hay una forma de atraer al pájaro desde esa altura para que puedas tomar el mensaje que lleva.'

'¡Ah, gracias por esto, camarada! La caída de los Herederos y el ascenso de la Hermandad disminuyeron la capacidad de Achardis para reunir información, pero ella persiste y aún espera nuestras solicitudes. Esta red de aves suyas... ella las llama los Vigilantes alados.'
Él saca una pequeña nota y te la entrega.
'Necesitamos enviar este mensaje de vuelta a ella. Ata el mensaje a la pata del halcón marino; él se encargará del resto. Vuelve a verme después de que el Vigilante alado se haya ido.'
Retiras suavemente el papel atado a su pata. El halcón marino no parece importarle, y de hecho parece estar muy cómodo intercambiando la información por la deliciosa cena que le has puesto delante.

'Ahora, camarada, esperamos. Te agradezco. Tu esfuerzo y atención evitaron el desastre, o peor, que mi locura habría causado.
'Espero verte de nuevo pronto.'
¿Quizás este trozo de carne atraiga al halcón marino desde su percha?
El halcón marino se lanza y disfruta de la cena. ¡Ahora es tu oportunidad!

Harthabor necesita ayuda para contactar a su líder en Umbar Baharbêl. Habla con él para saber más.
El halcón marino se encuentra en un tejado a través del arco y al este de Harthabor, en Jax Phanâl. Encuentra un método para atraer al pájaro, recoger su mensaje y devolverlo al agente.
Habla con Harthabor

'La amenaza de la Hermandad de las Monedas no puede permanecer desconocida. Después de la caída de la Mâkhda Dahak-'
Él sacude la cabeza.
'Perdóname. Soy Harthabor, y deberías llamar a ese lugar Mâkhda Khorbo, amigo mío. Mi error fue no usar el lenguaje local. Hazlo mejor que yo.'
Comienza de nuevo.
'Después de la caída de la Mâkhda Khorbo y los Herederos de Castamir, los susurros y advertencias de los águilas en todo Umbar cesaron. Peor aún, perdimos contacto con nuestro líder en la ciudad de Umbar.'
Se detiene y sacude la cabeza nuevamente.
'Los ciudadanos lo llaman Umbar Baharbêl, y tú también deberías hacerlo.
'¿Ves por qué necesito tu ayuda?'

'Nos dispusimos a restablecer el contacto con el líder de los canarios en Umbar Baharbêl, pero estábamos mal preparados. Abundan los errores y los agravios a los cambios de costumbres. Muchos de nuestros nombres están grabados en sus registros, y sé que no están allí por nuestro heroísmo.
'A través de este arco hacia el este, vi un halcón marino posado en un tejado. ¡Es un mensajero, estoy seguro! Cada día, ese pájaro llega y se posa allí buscando algo. ¡He visto un trozo de papel sujeto a su pata! Probablemente busca al águila que solía vigilar este puesto avanzado y tiene un mensaje que entregar.
'No puedo acercarme a él sin llamar la atención sobre mí, pero tú no has cometido ninguna ofensa ni has infringido ninguna costumbre. Puedes actuar como nuestro águila aquí.
'Persuade al pájaro para que baje de su percha y obtén ese trozo de papel, luego regresa a mí.'

'¿Ese halcón marino? La llamamos la Centinela alada. A menudo está allí arriba esperando que un trozo de carne caiga de un plato descuidado. No le importa mucho qué tipo de carne sea. Es inofensiva, como los pájaros.'
'Esa es la Centinela alada. Es un ave vigilante. Se posa en ese lugar cada día que está aquí. No se mueve a menos que sea por un trozo de comida o un objeto brillante. Es encantadora, ¿no es así?'
Capítulo 1 - Los ojos y oídos de la ciudad
Harthabor está esperando ver el mensaje que recuperaste.

El pájaro se ha ido. Harthabor espera tu regreso en Jax Phanâl. Ve al agente e infórmale que todo salió bien.
La piedra plana en el muro al noreste puede ser un lugar adecuado para atraer al halcón marino desde su percha.
Has hecho descender al halcón marino de su percha y ahora debes quitar el mensaje de su pata.

Recupera el último mensaje de la Centinela alada
'Envía el mensaje de regreso con el mensajero. Debo encontrar una manera de hacerte entrar en la ciudad y llegar a nuestro líder.'

'¿Qué nos trae hoy la Centinela alada?
'Veo que nuestra líder está viva y aún oculta de la Hermandad de las Monedas. Aunque parece que su alcance disminuyó después de la caída de los Herederos de Castamir, mantiene suficiente influencia en la ciudad para proporcionarnos estos detalles. Trabajaré para encontrar una manera de brindarle la ayuda que necesita.'
Él garabatea una nota.
'Adjunta esto al mensajero, como antes. Trabajaré para que puedas entrar en la ciudad y reunirte con nuestra líder, Achardis.'
Atas el mensaje de regreso a la pata del halcón marino y este te mira con ojos brillantes.
Retiras el último mensaje de la pata del Vigilante alado.
'Una vez más, debemos esperar. Cuando sea seguro para Achardis reunirse contigo, nos lo hará saber. Hasta entonces, debemos permanecer al margen de cualquier persona que pueda desearle daño.'

'Tus esfuerzos continuos para ayudarnos a garantizar que la influencia de la Hermandad de las Monedas no sea moldeada por manos externas te han ganado una audiencia con Achardis.'

'Encuentra tu camino hasta los muelles de la Flota Rápida en Umbar Baharbêl. Desde allí, viaja hacia el este hasta el Barrio Bajo y encuentra los baños de Achardis. Están ubicados en el lado norte del barrio.'

Hadorion has been pursuing a Corsair by the name of Khâshap since he showed in Anfalas. His pursuit has led him to the city of Umbar.
Posters in Lower Ward placed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Place posters in Lower Ward (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Hadorion in the Lower Ward
Hadorion plans to spread wild rumours about Khâshap in order to draw him out. The first step is to place these posters around the city to publicly paint a target on his back.

There hang posters all around the Lower Ward of the city. This should create a stir amongst the residents. You should tell Hadorion.
Hadorion can be found in the Lower Ward.

'We've made it to Umbar, ${PLAYER}.
'I tracked Khâshap all the way from the Langstrand through the Shield Isles. I believe he's made landfall here in Umbar, but we are among his cohorts so we must tread carefully. I have a plan to draw him out of hiding.
'What's more important to a Corsair and a cutthroat? Reputation. If we call into question that very reputation, they are bound to come forth in defence of it. We shall spread rumours of ill-gotten gains. Paint him as a betrayer to his people. We don't need anyone but Khâshap himself to believe in these rumours... and something tells me he will.'

'Tongues should start flapping. Whether or not it is believable should not matter.
'There exists within Umbar a healthy smattering of different allegiances. Now we wait for it to spread like a contagion.'
A Shadow Cast By Sea
The plan to draw out Khâshap has begun. With rumours beginning to spread, Hadorion aims to create chaos amongst Khâshap's rivals.
Corsairs in the Gut defeated (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Planted fake sashes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Corsairs in the Gut (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fake sashes planted (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hadorion seeks to sow chaos amongst Khâshap's rivals by framing him for acts of aggression.

You should tell Hadorion that you have created some chaos in the Gut and the fake sashes have been planted.
Hadorion can be found in the Lower Ward.

'This is the perfect storm. With the rumours spreading, and the chaos in the Gut - it is only a matter of time before Khâshap makes his move to clear his name.... and when he does, we will be there.
'Now, we wait.'

'Now that the rumours are spreading, it is time to sow the seed of discord.
'As I learned in Anfalas, Khâshap is prone to making mistakes when under duress. After some digging around and bribing the right people, I was able to learn that Khâshap does in fact have some rivals in the city. A rival Corsair group that, while not enthusiastic about snitching on a fellow, would have no choice but to respond to acts of aggression.
'This group routines the Gut, a part of the Lower Ward that is ill hospitable to outsiders. I've fashioned these sashes in the likeness of Khâshap's unique design. Let's just say, leaving it behind after roughing up a few of their number would work wonders towards turning their ilk against him.'
A Practice in Luring

Habla con Núrut en Rakhatâb
'Encuentra el saco en algún lugar al sureste, junto a las montañas, y entrégaselo a Aphamâr. Ella debería estar entre los trabajadores de Rakahtâb.'
'Aphamâr no está en su puesto en Rakhatâb. No puedo decir qué ocurrió. Por favor, consulta con el Núrut de Rakhatâb sobre el paradero de Aphamâr. Debemos entregar este registro.'
'Aphamâr no está en su puesto en Rakhatâb. No puedo decir qué ocurrió. Por favor, consulta con el Núrut de Rakhatâb sobre el paradero de Aphamâr. Debemos entregar este registro.'
'Si Aphamâr ha regresado a Umbar Baharbêl, estará en Rahâl Ghol. Ese es el distrito más alto de la ciudad. Apresúrate y entrégale el registro.'

'Aphamâr no ha pisado los pasillos de Rakhatâb durante casi un mes. Ulanor, el supervisor, encontró su presencia insostenible.

'Before I took up this station, the Captain of the Haven and many of his harbour-guards were loyal to Balakhôr the Scourge and the Heirs of Castamir. Nearly all of them were slain in the Mutiny, but as you might imagine, having fewer men has made my efforts to rebuild the Sail-haven far more difficult—and I will not be made to look the fool when Tumúldo Fierce-water returns from his voyage!
'Rumours abound of the Heirsworn and their plots in Umbar, but aside from the few that hurl insults from the decks of their ships in the harbour, I see no greater plan at play in the Free City. I only know what I have seen with my own eyes, and to speak plainly, I am not the young sailor I once was!
'To that end, I would ask that you speak to Zemirah, the new master of the sailors' guild, as well as Ahûd and Râmax, the foremen of the ship-yards in the Sail-haven. If there is an imminent threat to Umbar, they will know of it.'

'Greetings!
'Have you come seeking to join the sailors' guild? I must admit, you do not look the sort at a glance, but our membership is... thinner than it was before the Mutiny. If not for that reason, then speak quickly, for my time is not idly spent. What do you need?'
You inform Zemirah that Eshmun hopes to assess the threat of the lingering Heirsworn in the Sail-haven.
'The Heirs of Castamir had many supporters in Umbar and a great many of them were members of the sailors' guild. In fact, my predecessor was one of Balakhôr the Scourge's most ardent followers, but I digress. I have done what was necessary to put my house in order, if you understand my meaning, but it is no secret that the Scourge's loyal captains still maintain a foothold in the Haven. From what I have heard, they find shelter on the decks of their ships, cowering behind their crews, or in the taverns of the Sail-haven. That is all I know, ${PLAYER}.'

'Yes?'
You tell Ahûd that Eshmun hopes to assess the threat of the lingering Heirsworn in the Sail-haven. In addition, he wishes to learn if they have troubled the work at the ship-yards of Umbar Baharbêl. Ahûd nods and smirks.
'Tumúldo chose wisely, I think. Age has not slowed Eshmun in the least, and though he might seem a kindly old man at first glance, he is every bit as vicious as his predecessor. The only difference between the two of them is that Eshmun fights for the people of the Free City... and, of course, that he did not end up in the waters of the harbour with a spear through his back.
'Nevertheless, I can say with certainty that none of the Heirsworn have troubled this ship-yard. I have only employed shipmen from the sailors' guild since the Mutiny, and even so, I have conducted routine inspections of these ships at every stage of their construction. I have seen the Heirsworn cowering at their ships at the edges of the harbour, but aside from petty theft and harassment, they pose little threat to our work here in the Sail-haven. It seems they mean to pillage the city and scatter like rats before the Kindred can slay the last of them. I say let them! Death would be a kindness for them—let them suffer their shame in exile!'

'When I was made Captain of the Haven, Tumúldo said it had to be me—Kindred of the Coins or not, he knew I could keep watch on the Sail-haven. Like it was with poor Râmax, I have known Tumúldo since he was a boy, and though our friendship has been a complicated one at times, we have grown to trust each other without question.
'Before Tumúldo departed on his voyage, he told me to do whatever I must to protect Umbar Baharbêl and its people from those who still put their faith in Balakhôr the Scourge. While these Heirsworn may not fly the black sails of old, they are still at war—only instead of with Gondor, who was too mighty for them to overcome, they have turned their hatred upon their own. I have seen Umbar changed again and again through turmoil in the course of my life, but we have never been so close to true freedom. The Heirsworn cling to the past, and their grip loosens with each passing day, but how many more must be injured—or killed—before they are finally only a memory? I say none! We shall pry each of their fingers loose until their grip is broken, and when that is done, Umbar Baharbêl shall truly be a Free City!
'You are a hale adventurer, and though I do not know your journey, I know that you share my hatred of those who call themselves the Heirs of Castamir. Let us work together and put an end to them, once and for all!'

'YOU! I know you!'
Krûha stares at you as if he has seen a ghost.
'I was at Pelargir, ${CLASS}, but you don't remember me, do you? I know you serve the King of Gondor—that Elf-loving pretender! If you think the people of Umbar hate me, just wait until they learn who you really are!'

'You dare threaten me? I've killed better than you for far less, ${CLASS}.'
Medêshi glares at you and gestures to the others at the tavern.
'Let these fools relish their so-called victory because when the Scourge returns—Balakhôr or no—we shall have Umbar for our own!'

'I've lost, have I? Balakhôr is dead? You know nothing, ${CLASS}, and I will not be moved. Not by Eshmun, and certainly not by you!'
Grizagâr scowls at you, and chuckles to himself.
'The Sail-haven is ours by right!'

'Who are you to speak to me? Some foreign puppet of the Kindred?'
Jakham smirks at you.
'I should cut your tongue from your mouth!'

'After you returned, I sent my guards to investigate the rumours Zemirah spoke of, but unfortunately, the situation is far worse than I expected.
'From what I have learned, six of Balakhôr's captains remain in the Sail-haven: Medêshi, Grizagâr, Jakham, Krûha, Sikaru, and Akhâd. How they all managed to survive the Mutiny is a mystery to me, but the Kindred of the Coins cannot abide traitors in Umbar Baharbêl. I am told that some of them can be found on the decks of their ships at the edges of the harbour, but others may still haunt the local taverns.
'Need I tell you what must be done, ${PLAYER}? Confront them, and slay them to the last!'

'It is done? Excellent!
'It will take more than the Mutiny and time to wash away the stain of Balakhôr the Scourge, but you have done well to rid the Free City of his few remaining captains.
'May their names and deeds be forgotten!'

'Oh? One of the old man's lackeys finally grew a spine?'
Akhâd sneers at you and slams his mug onto the table. After a tense moment, he barks at one of the tavern-workers.
'Another round when this is done!'

'What is this? You think I answer to you or that old fool, Eshmun?'
Sikaru glares at you.
'No, you were dead the moment you stepped onto my ship!'

'In Umbar Baharbêl, we care for our own. It is true in most districts of the city, but it is more true in the Upper Ward than anywhere else. If a merchant loses his stall or his goods to the actions of an undesirable few, the others band together to see that he is made whole, and the wrongful parties are... dealt with. That is why we must do something about the upstarts who have taken over the Raven and Albatross. They tried to send a message to the proprietor of this inn, the House of Twisted Vines, by ruining some of his prized trellises, as you can see. But this cannot go unpunished.
'I am a representative of the community here in the Upper Ward, and my name is Dehêbix. I speak for myself, but more importantly I speak for the community. For the sake of its people you will tell me what you know about these upstarts.
'You did not see the attack? Then I shall count upon you to mete out the justice that is required. The upstarts that did this can be found fortifying the Raven and Albatross here in the Upper Ward. They will not be afraid to kill you, I am afraid, but the community will reward you if you risk this danger.'

'My associates have sent word of your deeds to me, and I approve. Those upstarts will think twice before crossing the Golden Queen again, and if they do they know what will happen to them.
'Did I not say before that I am an agent of Lady Hármelak? I believe I made it clear to you that I represent the community of the Upper Ward, and if you are to spend time here you must know, or must learn, this simple truth: Lady Hármelak IS the Upper Ward. It is her coin that remunerates you now, and her favour you have earned. Cherish it, for it is of great value.'

'For as long as I can remember, our buildings were always draped in black. The Church did not allow any other colours to be displayed. A silly thing to concern themselves with, perhaps, but hasn't it always been about control?
'That is why the scholars and I continue to do our research. With every colour we return to the city, we spit in the faces of tyrants who tried to control us... and come what may, the people of Umbar will endure.'

'There you are. Behold!'
Rimâti reaches into a sack and pulls out a banner. At first glance, the banner is simply pink. But then the cloth shifts, and you realize at certain angles, the colour transforms -- blue, then purple, then pink again.
'The scholars and I spent months researching this pigment. Bidulêkh, it is called -- Dawn-sheen. When Kamîr Kateb burned down, the recipe burned with it. The scribes and scholars who would have held that knowledge met their ends at the Church's hands.
'I came to the shrine to hang up the banners, but...' She gestures to the flag-poles before you and grins. 'Would you like to do the honours instead?'

Recording Recollections

'My childhood memories before Mût Tadaul -- the Death of Light -- are hazy. But Mût Tadaul itself, I remember as clear as water.
'Ordâkh soldiers flooded the streets, tearing down banners of all colours as they went. The cries and the screams of people echoed around me. Umbar burned. My family ran to the docks in hopes of fleeing by water. When we beheld the burning remnants of ships that had attempted to do the same, we could only turn back.
'Many good people died that day. Some days, I am still there, and Umbar is still burning.
'As a Harâph, I have spun countless stories for eager listeners. This is not a story that I enjoy telling, but it is one that must be told. It must be remembered.'

'When the riots started, I joined along with other Hûliz. Too long had we been used as the Heirs' executioners. Perhaps it was the rush of finally fighting back, but I knew we would succeed. After all, we outnumbered those in power.
'Some of my fellows died believing they had helped change things. And they did. But I watch as the Kindred replace the Heirs. I watch as our most vulnerable citizens continue to suffer, just in different ways. And I wonder what the future holds in store for Umbar -- if anything else will change.
'I no longer fight as a Hûlaz. I cannot bear it.'

'The colourful banners around the city still surprise me, every day. When will I get used to it? I do not know. But I wish Mother and Father were here with me to see this.
'Worshippers took them from our home. If our neighbours had not found and hidden me, I would have burned along with them. I survived only because I was lucky. I hate feeling like that.
'The Church may be gone from Umbar, but its shadow still exists.'

'Thank you, traveller. These accounts are not the ancient texts that many of my colleagues seek, but they are just as important.
'History tells us of how Umbar was passed from empire to empire. The Church may have tried to purge the past, but simply look around and listen -- not everything was destroyed. The Númenórean and Hamâti architecture, the sounds of Umbari, Westron, and Ordâkhai words. The people and their stories. We were here. We still are.'

'As one of the Kindred of the Coins, I respect what he has done for Umbar, but I must admit, I find him to be an odd fellow—charming, to be certain—but I'm never quite sure what he's after when I speak to him. I much prefer to let Tumúldo deal with him, to be perfectly honest.
'Here, my friend, let us toast to the future of Umbar.'
Eshmun hands you a mug, and you notice that it is not filled with ale, but instead with water.
'I know it is not the tradition, but I find ale to be a luxury of younger Men, and when you have been a sailor for as long as I have, you know the true worth of water.
'And so, I toast to you, ${PLAYER}, and to the future of Umbar Baharbêl! May the Free City endure until the end of all days!'
You and Eshmun toast.

'You wish to know about that spear, do you?'
Akálam glances at the spear, and in the flicker of the light, you catch sight of old burns upon his face.
'Do you know the tale of the bane of Umbar? He was like a half-giant among Men—dark-haired with eyes of grey—a great captain from some distant, unknown land.

Akálam's tale continues.
'And so, he came to Umbar like a spectre in the night. It was said that his blade was wreathed in flame, for the ships of the Sail-haven were set alight in his wake, and the harbour burned as if the water itself had turned to blackest pitch.
'Many were those who fell before him and his fleet, but none fought as bravely as my father, Akurga. He was Captain of the Haven on that dark night, and it fell to him to repel these interlopers lest all of Umbar be overthrown. Alas, before my own eyes, the villain slew my father at the doors of the Harbour-master's Tower. I was only a boy then, and rushing out from the doors, I stepped over my father to take up his spear. It seemed then that our enemy hesitated, and in that moment, I drove the spear into him with all of my might. Fleeing into the flames, he withdrew with his fleet, and he was never seen again.
'And surely I dealt him a mortal blow, for had I not truly killed him, would not he have returned to avenge himself upon us?'

'Oh, I see. Do you know why we called him the Ballast? He may not understand this, being so unused to a mariner's life, but ballast is a heavy material, usually iron, lead, or stone, placed in the hold of a ship to keep it steady. When used as a name for someone onboard a ship... it means that person is useless.
'He was just terrible, friend. During the days he was with us we encountered enough ill fortune and bad luck to fill a year. He tied the wrong knots, scrubbed the wrong floors, emptied the wrong pots, read the wrong weather signs, pointed out dangerous shoals as safe and safe shoals as dangerous. I have never seen someone less-suited to shipboard life. So I sent him away.
'We did not mean to hurt his feelings. Boys! I say we pass around the hat and raise some coin for the Ballast to begin a new life. Every man should put in some coin... and make his donation with the certainty that it will keep the Ballast as far from our ship as might be managed!'

'I will go to the Swain's Guild Hall, in the Lower Ward. I understand that is from where some of the caravans across the desert depart, and that is the new profession I have chosen for myself. I will see you there, friend!'

'This is a grand place for concerts and gatherings of large groups, it is true... but it also serves another purpose.
'A few months ago, I was drowsing on one of the seats here when the sun rose. To my great surprise, who should I see descending the steps but Tatháta the Beast herself, kinswoman of the Lower Ward? She is a towering, imposing figure; if you have ever seen her, you know she is not a woman with whom you should trifle! But on this morning she was not alone: she was walking two of her great hounds, the ones named Nûdil and Jôzi, around the amphitheatre. They worked up quite a sweat, the three of them, conducting great circuits of the structure.
'And it gave me an idea: if I did as Tatháta did, would I develop into as physical a specimen as she? So I have been coming here and walking down the steps, across the way, up the steps again, and following the curve of the seats back here. You should do the same! Why not make three circuits of the amphitheatre, friend? Be sure to start by running down the steps to begin!'
