'From this observatory, scholars in Umbar Baharbêl once gazed at the skies above, studying the night sky for wisdom. How distant was that age of knowledge? Too long ago for one lifetime, my friend; the observatory was destroyed, and has fallen into ruin in the years since.
'But I have dreamed about the things you might have seen from its balconies and from the rooftop viewing platforms. Will you do something for me? I am a scholar of sorts myself, but my subjects are more terrestrial than those of the folk who once worked in the building above us. Will you take this small leather bag and fill it with sand from several locations east of the city? I will reward you for this work, of course.'
'Will you fill the bag I gave you with sand from several locations east of the city? I will reward you for this work, of course.'

'Thank you for doing as I asked, my friend. Did you observe that the sand you collected from each location possessed its own characteristics?'
You tell Charzâd that some of the sand was damp and some was dry; some was coarse and some was fine; some of the sand was brightly-coloured.
'And yet they were all, in the end, still sand?' Charzâd answers with a raised eyebrow. 'It reminds me of how I envision the stars in the sky. From our position here they all seem to be the same: twinkling dots of light, like jewels affixed to the heavens. But look at this!'
Charzâd reaches into the small leather bag and removes a handful of the sand you gathered. She opens her palm and lets the sand fall, where the individual particles drift and float restlessly on the breeze.
'Like stars,' she says. 'How different might the stars be from each other if we could only see them up close? Might the scholars at the observatory above us have learned the answer if they were not slain, the observatory not shuttered, and their work not lost? I think they might have.
'Thank you for doing this for me, my friend. Not everyone would! I know: I asked them. But take this for your trouble and your time.'

Your mission is to protect the merchant ship Khâlbina on its trip to Jax Phanâl.
Speak to Malthak to travel.
You have successfully defeated the Corsairs! Return with the Umbari scout to the mission giver with this report.
Complete Mission: Protecting the Sea Lanes

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. We have need of assistance for our merchant ships. We have been attacked by freebooters several times in our ongoing efforts to get food and supplies to help support Halrax in the Shield Isles. The Khâlbina is ready to set sail later today for a run to the Isles. Would you go aboard and protect her during this journey? Halrax is counting on those supplies.'
'Well that is quite the tale. I am so glad you were there to take on those Corsairs and ensure the crew's safety. Thank you for your valiant deeds.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}, protect the Khâlbina at all cost. The hopes of the Khâlbina and her crew rest upon your able shoulders.'
Miniaventura: Protegiendo las rutas marítimas
You have been tasked with protecting the merchant ship Khâlbina on its trip to Halrax in the Shield Isles.

Your mission is to rescue the trapped dwarf-miners (and their treasure) before the cave permanently collapses!
Speak to Deshra to travel.
You have rescued the trapped miners and successfully escaped the cave! Return to the mission giver with this report.
Complete Mission: The Ill-fated Cave

'It's always good to see you, ${PLAYER}. I have an urgent mission this time. We have just gotten word from one of the Temámir Dwarves that a number of their miners has been trapped in a cave outside Rakhatâb, on the Cape of Umbar. Locals call it the Jid Phêsi, the cavern of whispers. There are reports they found a treasure of great beauty and cost. If you are able, please rescue both the dwarves and this treasure. Please, there is no time to lose! Rescue them before the cave further collapses!'
'That is a beautiful piece. I am glad you were able to rescue it, it will aid in the rebuilding efforts. What? Oh yes, the miners too, of course. I'm so glad they made it out with their lives.'
'${PLAYER}, please, rescue the trapped miners! And if you can, whatever treasure they were excavating. Quickly, there's not a moment to lose!'
Miniaventura: La cueva desafortunada
Rescue the trapped dwarf-miners (and their treasure) before the cave permanently collapses!

Your mission is to travel to Bakhjâd and obtain a great stolen treasure cache by whatever means necessary.
Speak to Deshra to travel.
You have successfully defeated the Corsairs and the Dead and recovered the cache! Return to the mission giver with this report.
Complete Mission: A Dark Treasure

'Always a pleasure, ${PLAYER}. We just got some exciting information. We have a credible report as to the location of a cache of riches stolen by freebooters from one of our merchant ships. Unfortunately, this report points us to Bakhjâd, in the Shield Isles. It's quite a dangerous place to go, but we could really use that stolen coin to help us rebuild Umbar. Will you help us recover it, for the good of Umbar?'
'I am touched beyond words. This will do much to repair the wounds and scars carved into our city. Thank you for your bravery, and your honesty in bringing this much coin to us.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}, recover that treasure cache at all cost. Don't let anyone or anything get in the way of that.'
Miniaventura: Un tesoro oscuro
You have been tasked with obtaining a great treasure cache in Bakhjâd in the Shield Isles before anyone else.

Your mission is to address the huorn problem on the Cape by paring their number back.

You have successfully defeated the huorn threat! Return to the mission giver with this report.
Complete Mission: A Natural Disaster

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. We have some troubling news from the Cape. A group of territorial huorns has been expanding there, destroying property and lives alike, both peasants and nobles on the road to Umbar. Please, take the fight to them and trim their branches back.'
'Thank you for addressing the threat. It warms my heart to know that our citizens can move along the Cape without fear. Thank you for your valiant deeds.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}, pare back the huorn menace on the Cape. Too many innocents have already lost their lives from their pillaging attacks.'

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. The Khâlbina is one of our finest merchant ships. She is sailing to Jax Phanâl on the morrow. There are rumours of huge beasts, giant crabs, and who knows what else, clamouring aboard ships near Jax Phanâl. These are simple merchant vessels, and their crews are not used to defending themselves from such beasts. Would you protect the Khâlbina and her crew on this perilous journey?'
'Well that is quite the tale. I am so glad you were there to take on those dreadful beasts and ensure the crew's safety. Thank you for your valiant deeds.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}, protect the Khâlbina at all cost. The hopes of the Khâlbina and her crew rest upon your able shoulders.'

Your mission is to aid in harvesting crabs in Zamarzîr and to fight off any crabs or beasts that get in your way.
Speak to Malthak to travel.
You have successfully harvested the crabs and defeated the greater cast-mother! Return with the Umbari scout to the mission giver with this report.
Complete Mission: A Taste for Crab

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. There is a new chef in Umbar, and he has been entertaining all of Umbar with his delicious crab creations. Now Umbar is running low on crab-meat! This may not seem like an emergency, but I can assure you it is. There are bountiful supplies of crabs on Zamarzîr in the Shield Isles, but large ferocious crabs have been sabotaging our traps and fighting off the workers. Please, aid the harvest on Zamarzîr in the Shield Isles.'

'Thank you for this. It may seem silly, but it's the little things that keep us going, our hearts strong and our will determined...
'And I just love crab.'
'Your mission is clear, ${PLAYER}, to aid in harvesting the crabs in Zamarzîr and to fight off any crabs or beasts that get in your way.'

'Well met, ${PLAYER}. We have been receiving disturbing reports from Jeb Khâtel in the Shield Isles. To the north, there is a series of small islands. Several ships have gone missing in this area, not to be seen again. Please, investigate these mysterious isles and figure out what happened to these ships and their crews.'
'That is disturbing news indeed. It's a tragedy what happened to those sailors, but due to your brave deeds, future ships venturing through those isles won't suffer the same fate.'
'Your mission is clear, ${PLAYER}, to investigate the northern Shield Isles of Jeb Khâtel and figure out what is happening to these disappearing ships and their crews.'

'Good to see you, ${PLAYER}. We have gotten reports of a great legendary beast, Tarasâd, the Beast of Belfalas. It was seen rampaging through north Zamarzîr. Growing up in Umbar, we all heard the stories of the great Beast of Belfalas, but most knew never to pay them much mind. Well, several captains have reported losing men to a great beast, as long as four men and as wide as three, in the last week.
'Please, investigate northern Zamarzîr and if you find the great beast, defeat it quickly, before it overcomes you.'
'Wow, I never thought I'd see the day. Look at the size of that claw. You truly are a mighty warrior, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for doing this.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}. Find the great beast Tarasâd in Zamarzîr, and subdue or defeat it.'

'Well met again, ${PLAYER}. We have need for some assistance for our merchant ships. They are being attacked by Corsairs while delivering food and supplies to our settlements on the Cape of Umbar. We believe these attacks are coordinated by a Corsair captain, Ghasaphâr, who makes his camp in Kan Skûrja on the Cape of Umbar. 'I am glad Ghasaphâr will no longer run rampant. All the hands on our merchant fleet will sleep easier tonight because of you. Thank you for all you've done.'

Umbar Baharbêl: Barrio Bajo
Meet with Gûshida in the Upper Ward of Umbar Baharbêl about rumours relating to the mistreatment of animals.
Meet with Gûshida in the Upper Ward of Umbar Baharbêl

'We've heard troubling rumours from Umbar Baharbêl about animal mistreatment. I appreciate what you did here for Khûtra's animals, so I know you understand how important our duty is, to protect and respect them. Their lives are as sacred as our own.
'These rumours tell of a street charlatan. They call him Ezôti. His words are sweet but his deeds are dark. He parades animals around for show. He whips them until they do his tricks.' Ilaya spits on the ground, to show her displeasure.
'He does not understand the pact between humans and animals. He does not see them as we do. To him, they are just a means to buy coin and praise. Cheap entertainment, to be used and discarded.
'Go to Umbar Baharbêl, find Gûshida. She can be found in the Upper Ward of the city. She is like you and I. She understands animals. She is looking to expose Ezôti and end his crimes. You've done much to help us and the animals here. Please, find Gûshida, and help the animals there. They don't have much time.'
'Ilaya sent you? Then I know you have a pure heart and devotion to animals. It is good that you've found me. We have much to talk about.'
A Vicious Rumour
Elder Ilaya has asked you to go to Umbar Baharbêl, the City of Corsairs, to investigate rumours of the mistreatment of animals by a man named Ezôti. You should meet with Gûshida in the Upper Ward.

'El ascenso de los Hermanados de la Moneda nos permite explorar, aún más, las maravillas que podemos crear. Nuestra renovada maravilla atrae las miradas de los ricos y los pobres y luchamos por satisfacer la demanda.

Speak with Malthak

On the northern Shield Isle Ghax-hophra, a distinguished Umbari scholar lost his priceless research when he was attacked by large beetles. Your mission is to recover the research and destroy these creatures' nests.
Speak to Malthak to travel.
You have successfully recovered the research and defeated the Ghax-hophra brood! Return with the Umbari scout to Malthak with this report.
Complete Mission: A Life's Work

'Always good to see you, ${PLAYER}. One of Umbar's most distinguished scholars just returned from a research trip to the Shield Isles. Unfortunately for him, it was not a productive trip. Far from it. Seems he was harried by great beetles on one of the northernmost Shield Isles, Ghax-hophra. He was so afraid he left his notebooks, which contain a lifetime of research into Umbari life and culture.
'For his sake and ours, we need to get those pages back. Will you venture out into the Shield Isles and retrieve his research? While you're there, destroy the nests of those vile creatures, that they may not harm others.'
'Future generations will have you to thank for preserving our knowledge about our past. Thank you for your bravery in securing these tomes.'
'Your objective is clear, ${PLAYER}, recover the research at all costs. If you aren't able to return with that research, a great deal of Umbari culture could be lost forever.'

'Parece que el mercado está muy animado. Sin duda, todos se han reunido para escuchar el testimonio de Khâshap sobre todas nuestras acusaciones. ¡Enfrentémoslo de una vez por todas!'

After escaping the Citadel of winds, Azagath Sea-shadow, Belondor, and Nakási Wave-reaper entered the Mâkhda Khorbo. You pursued them into the temple of ash and blood and now scour the depths for the trio.

After a battle at the Tower of Winds that crippled their ship, Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási, Reaper of the Waves flee to the cavernous underground beneath Mâkhda Khorbo. The subterranean harbour served as an illicit smuggler's den for the Temple of the All-seeing Eye, and the evil wrought by its inhabitant remains in the stone.

'I do not have a good feeling about this. That door leads outside!
'${PLAYER}, we must hurry. We cannot allow Azagath to escape us!'

'No... no...
'This cannot be! Azagath and his allies cannot have escaped us!'

'I beg you! Have mercy upon me and my fellows! We had no choice! Nakási Wave-reaper threatened to skin us alive if we did not help them cast off with utmost haste! There was a terrible light in her eyes, and I think she would have done it!
'Belondor's crew is fiercely loyal, and they manned the oars without argument. Even when Azagath told them their destination, they did not balk at it as I would have done!'
You ask the dock-worker where the leaders of the Kindred intended to row, and he shudders.
'Across the water, stranger. They made for the Temple of the All-Seeing. They made for the Mâkhda Khorbo.'
'For now they have escaped us, but not for long.'

'The guardsmen are in disarray. They speak of two groups: those loyal to Azagath and those who now question him. We should remain alert for the first, and learn what information we can from the second.'
Nauriel turns her gaze to the great hall, lingering briefly on the fountain in its centre.
'I wish you had waited for me to accompany you before you came here the first time, ${PLAYER}. Had you done so, we would not now need to make this venture... for Azagath's head would already be shorn from his body and I would be half of the way back to Pinnath Gelin!
'But what is done is done, and that undone remains undone. Let us speak to these women and learn if they support Azagath or oppose him.'

'When we aided you we did not think you intended to bring Gondorian sorcery to bear against the Kindred! We fled when the Corsair made your presence known to Azagath, but from the far side of the hall we witnessed the terrible creatures as they rose from the fountain. Where have they now gone? Do you plan to unleash them upon the city?'
You assure Ushu that the Five Sisters would not have harmed either her or her friends in any way, and now that Thorongil has been rescued they will not trouble the folk of the city. She considers your words.
'That is a comfort, but something yet confuses me. If these water-spirits answered to the call of Gondor, why were they dressed in Umbari garb? To my eye they were dressed as nobles of the city, and Enât told me the same.'
You tell Ushu that the Five Sisters did not appear that way to you, and she furrows her brow but does not seem surprised.
'For one thing to appear many ways is not unusual in these times. The Kindred of the Coins seemed to be one thing to us, and yet Azagath's words of late have cast another light upon it, a light fell and sickly.'

'Are you prepared, ${PLAYER}? We will likely face opposition from those still loyal to Azagath, and they will seek to keep us from reaching their master and his allies in the Kindred.
'Once we pass through this door, we must let none keep us from finding the treacherous leader of the Kindred of the Coins! Others of your crew will follow behind to keep Azagath from circling around us and escaping. Now let us fight!'
'The corridor to the south-east descends a long flight of stairs. Azagath and his allies must have gone that way!'

'Those warriors were guarding the north-east corridor, ${PLAYER}. That must be the way Azagath, Nakási, and Belondor fled.
'It is curious, but I see no one guarding the passage. Still, we must remain alert!'

'But you know, as I do, that such destruction is not always complete. Sometimes... something remains.'
'But what evils might he find buried beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo?'

'The boy Thorongil has been saved, but I still see a loose thread in the tapestry of evil that brought him, and all of us, to Umbar! One look at his mother's face reveals it, ${PLAYER}. No sum of gold or silver could make me dare to cross her, but the Kindred of the Coins has done so, and she has not forgotten!
'What does Lady Nauriel plan to do next?'

'Half of the job is done, my friend, but the other half remains, and its name is Justice.
'Three members of the Kindred of the Coins fled deeper into the Citadel of Winds when my son was rescued. They will not escape us. We must return to the Citadel and pursue them. Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási will pay for endangering my son.
'Speak to me when you are ready to return to that place.'
'What does Lady Nauriel plan to do next?'

'These foes will not escape us. We will pursue them into their very stronghold, and no hiding-place will remain unsearched. I will thrust my sword into every closet and cabinet within which one of these villains might hide!'

'Azagath has not escaped my Justice... he has only delayed it. Even as the water builds in power behind the dam that blocks the river, so will the strength of my vengeance increase for every day he remains unpunished. He will regret his flight.
'But what evils might he find buried beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo?'

'Bring me some relics from the Dead that walk near the temple, for they may allow me to learn the flavour of the evil that remains here. Bring me rusty weapons from the steps of the temple, gemstones from spectres and spirits, and finger-bones from the wights that lurk nearby.'

'Did you recover the items I requested?'
Sigileth examines the strange items you acquired from the vicinity of the Mâkhda Khorbo. After a few moments of study, she looks up at you.
'These blades are rusty from the salt of the sea breeze, and unsuitable for use. Only the Dead would wield these; no living servant of Sauron or of the Kindred would think to use such a weapon, unless there was no other choice.
'The gemstones are interesting. When such stones as these are found within the earth, they are usually quite clear, but the gems around which these spirits and spectres form are cloudy instead. See the shapes that seem to swirl within their foggy depths? They are most peculiar.
'I cannot read very much from the finger-bones you have brought to me. No, I do not need you to drag an entire wight here to me, as I threatened before! I have learned this, and it may be enough: these wights were given motion by spirits of evil. There must be a great number of such creatures still within the Mâkhda Khorbo, though Sauron himself be gone.'

'An Umbari woman has been watching us from down the hill to the east, ${PLAYER}. I do not think she intends to do us any harm, but whenever I face in her direction she quickly busies herself with some unobtrusive task.
'Perhaps you should see if she has any information for us, or at least determine that she does not mean ill?'
'What is it, Corudan?'

'I saw you speaking with those Elves near the ruined temple up on the hill. What purpose brought the three of you to that place? I have seen Elves of the Oasis from time to time, when I have gone to the markets of the city to sell my wares, but your companions do not seem to hail from across the desert. I judge they came from across the bay, perhaps from Gondor?'
You remain silent, and Rukân chuckles to herself.
'Worry not, stranger! I am no follower of the Church of the All-Seeing, and I steer clear from that temple, as should all goodly folk! Not long ago I witnessed Azagath Sea-shadow and some of his people disembark their ship in the cove beneath the hill, and I wondered what madness might have drawn them inside. Nothing good, I imagine. Pestilence and plague have troubled Khûtra in recent days, and something spoils the fish. After you have halted whatever evil drew you and Azagath to the Mâkhda Khorbo, you should return to me and I will tell you more about those ills.
'But for now let your companions know where Azagath and his allies debarked their ship. They possessed an evil intent... I am certain of it.'

'When the Golden Host of Lothlórien waged the Battle of the Tower in the forest of Mirkwood, I did not know of its success until many weeks passed... and every week felt as long as an age in the darkness beneath Dol Guldur. It was only when you delved deeply into those forgotten passages that I ceased to be She Who Remains and became once again Sigileth, ${PLAYER}, and learned that the Golden Host had achieved victory.
'But there was evil beneath Dol Guldur, and even today each of my senses are attuned to it. I feel the presence of Sauron's works here at the Mâkhda Khorbo, even as I did in those dark dungeons. It is not as strong here as it was in the Room of Voices, but still my senses are troubled by the feel of it.
'Bring me some relics from the Dead that walk near the temple, for they may allow me to learn the... I do not know the precise word to describe it, but this will have to serve... they may allow me to learn the flavour of the evil that remains here. Bring me rusty weapons from the steps of the temple, gemstones from spectres and spirits, and finger-bones from the wights that lurk nearby. Why finger-bones?'
Sigileth raises one eyebrow and you are surprised to hear mirth in her voice when she responds.
'I did not think you would want to drag a bunch of wights over here for my investigation, ${PLAYER}. Just their finger-bones will do.'
'The structure itself is not as damaged as I had thought it to be.'
'Azagath must think to acquire some evil beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo. He must be prevented from finding whatever it is he seeks, unless that be death.'

'I had forgotten how poor my sister is at keeping secrets, ${PLAYER}. I did not begrudge you your decision to go alone into the Citadel, no matter what Sigileth says!
'I would have gone with you, had you asked. But of course you know that!'
'An Umbari woman has been watching us from down the hill to the east. Perhaps you should find out what she wants?'

'What said our distant onlooker, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Sigileth that Azagath and his allies made use of a sheltered cove beneath the hill on which rests the Mâkhda Khorbo, and they have now gone inside the lower tunnels for some unknown purpose.
'Then that is where your road leads, is it not? Corudan and I will guard the path and ensure none think to flee this way, while you muster your allies and face Azagath beneath the temple.'
<rgb=#00FF00>If you wish to participate in the raid, this is when 'The Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo' raid takes place during the story.</rgb>
'For now let your companions know where Azagath and his allies debarked their ship. They possessed an evil intent... I am certain of it.'

'My sister's thoughts dwell upon the evils that might lie within the Mâkhda Khorbo, but I need not see them to know that a corruption lies within the very heart of the Kindred of the Coins.
'But Azagath is well-loved by his people. Do the folk of Umbar Baharbêl know that he has betrayed them?'

'We should travel by land to the outskirts of the temple and learn if the fleeing members of the Kindred have disturbed the ruin. It may be they seek only escape... but if evils of Sauron do remain beneath that structure, we cannot risk Azagath coming into possession of them.
'My brother and I will accompany you, ${PLAYER}. He would not say this to you directly, but privately he mourned to me that you ventured into the Citadel to rescue Thorongil without him.

'The structure itself is not as damaged as I had thought it to be. It is not difficult to believe the levels below-ground may also have survived the great quake that followed Sauron's fall, and remain somewhat intact.'

Talk to Belondor in the Sail-haven
'Sometimes word travels slowly, and on other occasions it can spread faster than wildfire.'

Belondor says nothing.

'I saw you in the Citadel, stranger. You were there. Were you also in the Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo?'
Belondor shakes his head sadly.
'The writing was there, but I did not see it until it was too late. There was cruelty in the Sea-shadow, as there was cruelty in all of us... but I believed it was needed against the evils arrayed against us. The Church of the All-Seeing, the Empire of Ordakh... these were foes against which we could show no mercy. The hatred I bore for Gondor...
'Aye, I would not show mercy to any warriors of Gondor who opposed us. But not children. The boy Thorongil was not yet a man, and Azagath would have drenched the stones of the Citadel with his blood. Nakási would have obeyed the command, and done whatever the Sea-shadow ordered. The writing was there, but even then I followed the two of them as they fled. In the Depths of Mâkhda Khorbo my crew paid for my inaction, my indecision. Azagath slew them with dark, unnatural magic, and their sacrifice meant nothing.
'Do you have a crew of your own, stranger? Do you know what it means to lose them all, and for nothing?'

'Have I heard anything of late concerning the Kindred of the Coins? I confess to you I have not paid very much attention to their dealings in recent days, for I have been much occupied with caring for my new friend Rûmina. She is asleep right now, but when she wakes she is like to cause quite a commotion, chasing either her tail or the rodents that infest the Lower Ward and the Sail-haven!
'She was the loyal companion of a Corsair captain and sailed from port to port with him, but now that he has retired from that trade he has given his ship-cat to me. She seems quite happy with her new circumstance, but she keeps me very busy!
'If you check back in with me perhaps you can help the two of us with something? That would be very good of you.'

'Keep your voice down, stranger! There are unfriendly ears about!
'Well, I do not know if there are, but it is better to stay on the side of caution, is it not? People say Azagath Sea-shadow was driven from the Citadel by a great beast, and only the swords of Nakási Wave-reaper and Belondor of the Fleet-fast saved his life! I have remained on guard for any sign of the sorcerers who unleashed the beast upon the Kindred, but so far I have not seen anything. They could be anywhere.
'You should come back to me when you have finished your own errands for the day. I may have learned something by then!'
'Will you return to the Upper and Lower Wards of the city and learn what people are saying about Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási?'
'Sometimes word travels slowly, and on other occasions it can spread faster than wildfire.'

'Pssst... stranger.'
The man stares at you with piercing eyes. After a moment you realize he is speaking to you nearly without moving his mouth.
'I saw a well-dressed man in blue and silver making for one of the north-south piers extending out into the waters of the Sail-haven,' he says. 'You might go see this man.'
He falls silent and says nothing further
The rumour was true: Belondor has returned to the Sail-haven

'I do not know which it will be. Sometimes word travels slowly, and on other occasions it can spread faster than wildfire. Will you return to the Upper and Lower Wards of the city and learn what people are saying about Azagath, Belondor, and Nakási?
'If tongues wag as I think they will, rumour that these leaders of the Kindred fled beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo in search of some evil will not be gladly received. At least... I hope it will not. Begin your search in the Upper Ward, for it is nearer.'

'Yes? You have caught me at a good time, my friend, for I have just come into a large sum of money! Or rather, I will have just as soon as I collect upon a daring wager I made at Dahâl Huliz, the grand arena within the Tor-gardens. What a glorious day it is today!
'How do I feel about the Kindred of the Coins? Oh, I think they are doing a very good job of things. They saved us from the rule of the Empire of Ordakh and the Church of the All-Seeing, after all. Let me just say this, friend. If the Kindred was not in power, I would not feel comfortable telling you about my winnings at Dahâl Huliz, for fear that the Church would take my winnings for their own. I do not think any of the Kindred would do so... unless the Golden Queen is made jealous by my newfound wealth!'
Mokhlêsh falls silent, considering this uncomfortable new thought.
'Hmm. If you return to me when you have a moment, I might have some work for you. I cannot be too careful when such a large sum is at stake.'

'What do I think of the Kindred of the Coins? I think they have ruled us well and fairly since the war's ending, and neither the Heirs of Castamir nor the Empire of Ordakh could have done better. I have heard some troubling rumours that there was fighting in the Citadel not long ago, and I hope the ones responsible will soon be apprehended. May justice come swiftly for the ones responsible!
'I heard there was fell magic involved. It is said a great beast with five heads emerged from a column of water and shook the Citadel to its very foundation, but that is not the most surprising thing I have heard! I heard each of the five heads bore a woman's countenance, and the beauty of each was matched only by her ferocity.
'Yes, it is preposterous, but this is a land where surprising things can happen! I was not there, and neither were you. I believe this beast lives, unless Azagath has already slain it. If you were a resident of this city you would know he is capable of great martial feats. Return to me when you have a moment and we will see who knows the city of Umbar Baharbêl, and who does not!'

'What do I think of the Kindred of the Coins? This is a difficult question for me to answer, friend.
'It is true they have promised a return to peace and an increase in prosperity since they came to power and cast out the Empire of Ordakh, and it seems this will be made so. But they also promised to heed the will of the people and hear their concerns, but the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja remains shut. Where once I saw Azagath and the other leaders of the Kindred walking through the city, that has happened less and less often of late. Where are Tatháta and her mighty hounds? Where are Tumúldo and his wife Nakási? The only leader of the Kindred I see with any regularity is the dwarf Khôltekh, and I do not like the look in his eye. He is plotting something within the Shoreward Stone, you mark my words.
'But for my part I believe the Kindred has our best interests in mind. Truthfully I would feel more at ease if they reopened Dâr Laja and kept their promise!'

'I know my words are just words, Belondor, and I have given you little reason to believe them. But I speak this from my heart: King Elessar is a good man, and he desires only what is best for his people and for yours. He wants peace between Gondor and Umbar, and prosperity for both.
'I know this is so. He is not the same as the Steward Denethor. Can the Kindred of the Coins come to see this, if Azagath no longer controls them? Can you, and they, work alongside the kingdom of Gondor, and not against it? Can you join hands with King Elessar, if it means setting aside war and conflict?'

'I hope we have repaired something of the friendship we once possessed, Sirgon, but I am not ready to say the same of that between Gondor and Umbar. Your King has much to prove to us, for we have heard sweet words before, and were deceived. It will not happen again.
'The Kindred of the Coins will survive without Azagath and Nakási. It was larger than both of them. It is larger than all of us, for it is Umbar. Your King will need to realize that if he believes there can be peace between our lands.'

'What kind of bird was that?'
You tell Rothog that the bird's name is Gwallang, and he is a Limlinn from across the Bay of Belfalas.
'Gwallang. Limlinn. I have not heard these names before. He is brave for one so small.
'But I came here for two purposes: to fight, and to fetch. I am disappointed there was no fight, but now you will come with me.
'Hármelak wants to see you again.'

'Gondorians and Umbari are both alike in this: each of them uses too many words.
'I came here for two purposes: to fight, and to fetch. I am disappointed there was no fight, but now you will come with me.
'Hármelak wants to see you again.'

'I appreciate you and the crew of the Wave-hunter agreeing to accompany me to this meeting with Belondor, ${PLAYER}.
'The Hungry Deep, and my fate, awaits me atop these steps.'

'Beneath the Mâkhda Khorbo he worked cruel magic, tearing the life from dear members of my crew, friends I have known for years. They died trusting me, Sirgon. They trusted I would bring them to safety, and trusted that their families would know they did not die for nothing.
'But Azagath spent their lives for no purpose! Their deaths were needless, and provided only the smallest of delays so the Sea-shadow could make his escape! He did not know those men, and he discarded them without thought... only I am left to suffer the grief of their loss.'

'I warned your friend Sirgon not to return to the Upper Ward! Does he think he remains out of reach and free from justice?
'Rothog has slain many such men who believed themselves to be untouchable, and for less reason that this. Belondor has not forgotten how easily Sirgon cast aside his long friendship and was rewarded for it! He followed the Steward Denethor's commands, and questioned them not!'

'What brings you to this city, stranger? I deem you have sought me out. Why?'
You tell Belondor that you have come to Umbar in the company of his old friend Sirgon. Belondor remains silent for a long time before speaking.
'It has been many years since I named Sirgon a friend, and it must be the same with he who is the Lord of Lebennin. Was he rewarded for his blood-red service by the Steward of Gondor? Did chasing me into the rocks of Shedax Khîn win him glory and fortune? He slew friends of mine in that pursuit... did he tell you? Has he come to Umbar Baharbêl to finish the job he began those many years ago? He would be wise to steer clear from my manor, for the wrath of Mêshka my wife will be more deadly to him than all the spines of the desert, or the pointed rocks of the Shield Isles.'
You tell Belondor that Sirgon has already spoken with Mêshka, and she made her opinion of him very clear. Belondor looks at you with surprise.
'And he did not clap her in irons? He is not here to drag us back to Gondor in chains? Has the King not sent you and he here to inflict his will upon us? If not... then why has Sirgon come here?'
You consider what you might tell Belondor, but decide upon the truth: that Sirgon feels the burden of his past with Belondor and Mêshka, and he hopes to reconcile with them, if such a thing might be possible.
'If what you say is true, let him speak these words to me himself. I will await him at The Hungry Deep Tavern. Now begone. I would be alone with my thoughts, as I was before. I have friends to mourn.'

'You have seen Belondor? What did he say to you, ${PLAYER}?'
You relay Belondor's message, and Sirgon thinks it over. At last he steeples his fingers in front of his face and closes his eyes. When he reopens them again, he has come to a decision.
'The Hungry Deep Tavern overlooks the Sail-haven, but it is located in the Upper Ward. Belondor's wife Mêshka commanded her guards to slay me should I return to that place.
'But I would speak again with Belondor and tell him what I have come to believe. I am not afraid of Mêshka's headsmen. I would bare my neck before them if it meant I could ease this burden from my back, ${PLAYER}. I have carried it for too long.
'Will you accompany me, my friend? Let me know when you are ready to leave.'
'Tell Sirgon to meet me at The Hungry Deep tavern. Now begone, for I have friends to mourn.'
'Then it is time. To the Hungry Deep we go.'

'And so you stand before me once again, ${PLAYER}. I am touched to hear of the reconciliation between Belondor and the man of Gondor who has so disturbed his heart for these many years. I trust this thaw will not make him weak? Without Azagath and Nakási, the Kindred of the Coins must appear strong now, stronger than ever before.
'The people must be reassured that the Kindred is here for them, despite the betrayal of the Sea-shadow. I have come to a decision, and I would like to ask you for help in seeing it done.'

'What are these? The keys to the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja? The last I heard, these were in the hands of Heirsworn down at the Sail-haven. It seemed to me the Kindred of the Coins were willing to let them keep them. Being already in power, they were in no hurry to reopen the Meeting-hall and hear from the people again.
'But I am to fashion a new lock and keys for Dâr Laja so it can be reopened? Those are very surprising tidings, both welcome and unwelcome, if you understand me. I recently lost an apprentice, you see, but there is just as much work as ever. If you return here when you have a moment, I might have some work for you.
'But for now I shall begin on this new task. It will be some time before everything will be ready.'

'What did you say? You recovered the keys from the Heirsworn, and a new lock is being made for Dâr Laja? I confess to you I did not think you would do it! But it warms my heart to know that Lady Hármelak's wishes are being carried out. The Meeting-hall will open and the Kindred will once again hear the voice of the people!
'It will take some time for everything to be ready, but I hope when all is prepared you will return to us, my new friend. It will be a new dawn for Umbar, and let none doubt the days of sunshine that lie before us!'
'For now I shall begin on this new task. It will be some time before everything will be ready.'

'We will reassure the folk of Umbar Baharbêl that the peace will continue, and prosperity will be theirs. The Kindred of the Coins will hear their concerns and act upon them. The Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja must be reopened. Its doors have remained shut for too long, and the voice of the people has grown distant.'
Hármelak's eyes shimmer in the light of her richly-decorated chamber.
'When you were last here, ${PLAYER}, I spoke some words concerning the Sea-shadow. You have now seen what I then believed, and still do: he was not trustworthy, and owed his allegiance to some other. I think now that he drew his powers and his strength from forces unnatural, from He-Who-Sees-All... from Sauron. For your part in deposing him, in driving him from Umbar, you have my gratitude. I know you are not from this land, but I believe you have a giving heart, a charitable will, and an understanding mind. Will you help me set right what Azagath and Nakási have disturbed?
'If so, speak with Jaith, who guards Dâr Laja here in the Upper Ward of the city. He will tell you what must be done to reopen the Meeting-hall. It may take some time, but with this decision I hope we take the first steady steps toward a brighter future for Umbar and its people.'

'Hármelak wants the Meeting-hall opened? Oh, I do not think we can do that.
'No, no, no, do not misunderstand me! I would leap at once to carry out the Lady Hármelak's command! It is just that the keys to Dâr Laja were stolen by the Heirsworn, and ever since those villains ran off with the keys, we have not been able to get inside. A new lock might be fashioned, given enough time, but it is not safe for us to proceed for as long as the Heirsworn hold onto the keys.
'If you are able to wrest the keys from them, we might be able to do something... but not until then. The Heirsworn can be found all over the Sail-haven, if you are ready for a fight. Once you retrieve the keys, if such a thing is possible, you should bring them to Yamin just north of the Grand Market to see about making a new set of keys and a better, more secure lock for the Meeting-hall. If you are able to do all that, come let me know! But I will not hold my breath until then. You understand: it is just that folk are always making big claims at sunset, and by dawn nothing has come of it.'

'Speak with Jaith, who guards Dâr Laja here in the Upper Ward of the city. He will tell you what must be done to reopen the Meeting-hall. It may take some time, but with this decision I hope we take the first steady steps toward a brighter future for Umbar and its people.'

Instance: Isle of Storms -- Tier 1

A great winged terror known to the people of Umbar as a Roc has been seen attacking ships sailing off the Cape of Umbar, swamping them with the winds from its vast wings and plucking the hapless crew out of the water. The lords of Umbar have requested that you find the nesting place of this monstrous bird and drive it from the Shield Isles. The Roc is believed to be roosting upon a deserted isle in the far reaches of the archipelago, once a haunt for pirates and brigands. Rumours say that they were driven out by strange and monstrous creatures, far greater in size than any beast should be....
Defeat the great beast guarding the entrance to the caves of the Isle of Storms.

Someone - or more likely something - has slain most the pirates who once frequented these caves and driven away any survivors. If you want to reach the Roc's aerie above, you're going to have to make your way past it....
The tunnels here howl with winds that blow down from the peak, making your progress treacherous - but it seems to be the only path leading to the Roc's aerie above.

Dahâl Huliz, La Arena - Nivel 1

'Any who have sat in the stands of Dahâl Huliz know the names of the favoured champions who do battle on the fighting sands. You will face one of these now! Use your wit, guile, and strength to survive, and perhaps your own name will be raised as high!
'Now will I call them forth!'

'I welcome you to my domain: Dahâl Huliz, the grand arena of Umbar Baharbêl! I consider these sands to be sacred ground; you should do the same. In this place, those who are accused fight for their freedom, and those who are not fight for greater glory.
'On this day we fight not to the death, for those who perish would be unable to entertain the crowds on the morrow. Instead we fight until a combatant's first submission. In that way those who lose can be spared, that they may gain in strength, and fight again on a future day.
'Be warned, for the Arena plays host to many surprises. May you fight well! Give all those who attend a magnificent show and you will have their approval, as I do!'

'We are honoured by your presence here today! I shall call forth the first set of the Khâbraghai, the blade-fodder, so you may warm up your muscles and get your blood flowing!
'The crowd wants to cheer for you, but on some days they can be fickle-minded. They want to see a good show. See that they do.'

'Your greatest challenge has arrived, my impressive friend. Will you face it with courage and with strength, or will its arrival send you screaming from these sands in fear?
'I believe in you, though all the crowd cheers for your opponent. They do not think you have what it will take to best this final opponent, and why should they? You must win them over. You must attain their belief with a great display of your prowess and your fighting skill!
'Your final challenge is this: you must defeat he who calls this place home. Rothog the Storm is your final opponent, my friend, and he is a mighty foe indeed. Can you take this crown from him? Can you defeat the Arena's favourite son and champion? We will see, friend. Show us now, and win glory for your name!
'Fight now! Dahâl Huliz will ring with the sound of battle, and let the cheering of the crowd ascend even to the stars above!'

'Well-struck, and well done. Every victory adds to the story of your name.
'But do not rest yet, for now I call forth the next round of Khâbraghai. Will you best these as you did the others? Do not let down your guard! The crowd will prepare themselves for the more challenging contest to come, but you must focus upon each battle as it is joined, and not look past them to the next!'

'You must forget those you have fought before. Your next foes will be far more dangerous, and if you cannot best them the story of your name will end here!
'But perhaps it is not to be so? Can it be we will see your true mettle here instead? I call forth your next challenge, and may you prove its equal!'

The gladiatorial pits of Umbar Baharbêl serve several important purposes: entertaining the masses, keeping their attention focused, and meting justice upon those who break the laws of the city.
Upon taking control of Umbar, the Kindred of the Coins altered the traditional rules of the arena. Most battles are no longer to the death, and the memory of such capital punishment has remained in the cruel past. Combat has become a sport for the masses, and any who dare can enter the fighting pits and attempt to enhance their glory. Gladiators bound to the arena serve their sentences by entering battle and fighting to the end.

'${PLAYER}, ya que no necesito seguir por este camino, ¿me harías el favor de entregar algo por mí? Llevo una carta sellada de Aragorn para los Montaraces de Tornhad. Cuando no puede hablar con ellos en persona, a veces les envía información o instrucciones de esta manera. ¿Puedo confiarte esta tarea?
Mientras viajas por tierra, es muy probable que te encuentres a un Montaraz vigilando a las afueras del pueblo... ¡Si consigues verlo, claro!'
Glorfindel se ríe y casi te parece oír el tañido de unas campanas claras en su voz.
'El Montaraz que vigila se asegurará de que caiga en las manos adecuadas. Si haces esto por mí, estaré libre para explorar el este.'

'¡Eh, tú! ¿Qué te trae por aquí?'
Le dices al Montaraz que vas a entregar una carta de Aragorn en nombre de Glorfindel, y el Montaraz se endereza.
'Sí, ya veo', dice, cogiendo la carta. La escruta y luego la guarda.
El Montaraz vuelve a apoyarse en la pared y te saluda con la cabeza.
'Gracias, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}. Agradezco que esté sin abrir. Muchas gracias en nombre de los Dúnedain.'

'¿Te gusta mi escudo? El tío Candaith dice que es de las Tierras Brunas. ¿Has estado alguna vez allí? ¿De dónde eres? ¿Has dicho que conoces a Halbarad? ¿Conoces al tío Candaith? Es muy valiente y fuerte.'
El muchacho te asalta a preguntas y no te permite contestar a ninguna.
'¡Voy a ser un Montaraz como él! Mataré orcos y trasgos, y tendré mi propio arco y espada. Viajaré por todo Eriador y haré cosas buenas por la gente, pero nunca lo sabrán. Así somos. Por cierto, ¿quién eres?
'Me llamo Barhador. ¿Vas a buscar más comida y a unirte a nosotros? ¡No tenemos nada de postre! ¿Te gustan las bayas? Al oeste de aquí crecen unas bayas que son dulces y ácidas a la vez, y te hacen poner esta cara.'
El chico frunce los labios y levanta las cejas todo lo que puede.
'Pasamos por allí antes, pero Ivoreth dijo que aún no podíamos detenernos. Si vas a recolectar, ¿puedes traernos algunas? ¡Están muy buenas, te lo prometo!'
'¡Cuántas bayas! Esto es excelente. Eres increíble, de verdad, ${PLAYER}.'

Continúa tu búsqueda más al este, hacia Tham Lumren

'¡Saludos y ${PLAYERNAME:bienvenido[m]|bienvenida[f]}, ! Vengo recientemente de la Casa de Elrond y me dijeron que podría encontrarme contigo en Haudh Erthaid.'
Su voz es musical y sus ojos brillan con una alegría que llena tu corazón.
'Es bueno que estés aquí, ¡ya que puedes aligerar mis cargas! Estoy vigilando las fuerzas del Enemigo a lo largo de los caminos que rodean Rivendel para cuando nuestros amigos mutuos elijan partir.
'¿También estás salvaguardando este camino? Entonces siento que no necesito repetir lo que ya has hecho, y ahora puedo dirigirme hacia el este del Bruinen. ¡Gracias, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}!'

Le dices a Ivoreth que el camino es seguro y que te encontraste con el señor elfo Glorfindel a las afueras de Tham Lumren.
'¡Oh, son unas noticias excelentes! ¡Sin duda estaremos a salvo! Gracias, ${PLAYER}, por todo lo que has hecho por nosotros. Que te vaya bien en el resto de tus viajes, por muy oscuros que sean los tiempos que se avecinan.'
No ves ningún huargo, pero deberías continuar más al este por el camino
Divisas más adelante a un elfo alto y hermoso, de poderosa presencia, que te llama
Sigue el camino hacia el este en dirección a Tham Lumren, hasta el cruce a veces peligroso que describió Ivoreth, mientras vigilas cualquier amenaza que pueda dificultar su viaje.

'${PLAYER}, te pediría una última cosa. No sería necesario si estuviera sola, pero con un niño en mi compañía, la situación es diferente. Debería haberlo dejado en Tornhad, pero el muchacho es persuasivo y le encanta escuchar las canciones de los elfos. Si nos hicieras un último acto de bondad, te pediría que exploraras el camino que hay por delante.
'Hay un cruce hacia el este donde este camino se encuentra con otro que va hacia el sur. Antes se han visto huargos por allí, y me gustaría asegurarme de que no estén ahí ahora. Nuestro destino, Tham Lumren, está solo un poco más al este de ese lugar. ¿Podrías explorar el camino y asegurarte de que está libre de peligros? Cuando regreses nos pondremos en marcha.'

Zanahorias silvestres recogidas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Te doy la bienvenida, ${PLAYERNAME:viajero[m]|viajera[f]}. ¿Qué te trae al Ángulo?'
Le dices que estás aquí a petición de tu amigo Elladan, y ella te sonríe.
'Los amigos de Elladan son mis amigos. Ven, únete a nosotros junto al fuego. ¿Has comido? Soy Ivoreth, y mi valiente guardián es Barhador. Estamos haciendo un encargo en Tham Lumren para intercambiar provisiones con los elfos y nos detuvimos aquí para descansar y comer algo. ¿Te unirías a nosotros? Es importante mantener las fuerzas cuando la tierra está llena de peligros.
'¿Vienes del norte? Agradecería cualquier noticia de esa parte del mundo. Es el deber de mi hijo Halbarad salvaguardar el norte.'
Le cuentas brevemente tus aventuras y las noticias que conoces.
'¿De verdad? Bueno, ahora debes unirte a nosotros para la comida, pero no estoy segura de que tengamos suficiente para alimentar a otro más. Ve a buscar algunas zanahorias, ¿quieres? Crecen de forma silvestre en una colina al sur, no muy lejos de aquí.'

Dahâl Huliz, The Arena -- Solo/Duo

'Any who have sat in the stands of Dahâl Huliz know the names of the favoured champions who do battle on the fighting sands. You will face one of these now! Use your wit, guile, and strength to survive, and perhaps your own name will be raised as high!
'Now will I call them forth!'

'I welcome you to my domain: Dahâl Huliz, the grand arena of Umbar Baharbêl! I consider these sands to be sacred ground; you should do the same. In this place, those who are accused fight for their freedom, and those who are not fight for greater glory.
'On this day we fight not to the death, for those who perish would be unable to entertain the crowds on the morrow. Instead we fight until a combatant's first submission. In that way those who lose can be spared, that they may gain in strength, and fight again on a future day.
'Be warned, for the Arena plays host to many surprises. May you fight well! Give all those who attend a magnificent show and you will have their approval, as I do!'

'We are honoured by your presence here today! I shall call forth the first set of the Khâbraghai, the blade-fodder, so you may warm up your muscles and get your blood flowing!
'The crowd wants to cheer for you, but on some days they can be fickle-minded. They want to see a good show. See that they do.'

'Your greatest challenge has arrived, my impressive friend. Will you face it with courage and with strength, or will its arrival send you screaming from these sands in fear?
'I believe in you, though all the crowd cheers for your opponent. They do not think you have what it will take to best this final opponent, and why should they? You must win them over. You must attain their belief with a great display of your prowess and your fighting skill!
'Your final challenge is this: you must defeat he who calls this place home. Rothog the Storm is your final opponent, my friend, and he is a mighty foe indeed. Can you take this crown from him? Can you defeat the Arena's favourite son and champion? We will see, friend. Show us now, and win glory for your name!
'Fight now! Dahâl Huliz will ring with the sound of battle, and let the cheering of the crowd ascend even to the stars above!'

'Well-struck, and well done. Every victory adds to the story of your name.
'But do not rest yet, for now I call forth the next round of Khâbraghai. Will you best these as you did the others? Do not let down your guard! The crowd will prepare themselves for the more challenging contest to come, but you must focus upon each battle as it is joined, and not look past them to the next!'

'You must forget those you have fought before. Your next foes will be far more dangerous, and if you cannot best them the story of your name will end here!
'But perhaps it is not to be so? Can it be we will see your true mettle here instead? I call forth your next challenge, and may you prove its equal!'
Ezaphir calls forth the fourth challenge!
You are victorious, and Ezaphir returns to the fighting sands
Ezaphir calls forth your final challenge: Rothog the Storm!
You have defeated Rothog the Storm, and the spoils of victory are yours!

Upon taking control of Umbar, the Kindred of the Coins altered the traditional rules of the arena. Most battles are no longer to the death, and the memory of such capital punishment has remained in the cruel past. Combat has become a sport for the masses, and any who dare can enter the fighting pits and attempt to enhance their glory. Gladiators bound to the arena serve their sentences by entering battle and fighting to the end.

La mujer te mira con ansiedad.
'Sé que no debería estar aquí. La Hermandad nos juró alejarnos. Sin embargo, vi a tres de ellos. Sacaron sus lanchas a la orilla y entraron en este túnel con sus tripulaciones. Fueron directamente hacia adelante.
'Sé que no se supone que debo estar aquí, pero sé un poco sobre el templo. Solía trabajar en un muelle aquí en mis días más jóvenes. Si necesitas adentrarte más en las ruinas, puedo ayudarte.
'Si puedes decirme la última habitación que entraste, puedo mostrarte un atajo a través de los túneles cercanos.'

El Mâkhda Khorbo, el asiento de los adherentes al Ojo que todo lo ve, se derrumbó cuando cayó el Señor Oscuro. Sin embargo, dentro del Templo de Ceniza y Sangre, un mal antiguo acecha los pasillos, se filtra en cada piedra e infesta a todos los seres vivos que hay dentro; ¿qué razón hay para invadir este lugar? Tienes la intención de descubrir por qué la Hermandad de la Moneda vino a este lugar.

A great winged terror known to the people of Umbar as a Roc has been seen attacking ships sailing off the Cape of Umbar, swamping them with the winds from its vast wings and plucking the hapless crew out of the water. The lords of Umbar have requested that you find the nesting place of this monstrous bird and drive it from the Shield Isles. The Roc is believed to be roosting upon a deserted isle in the far reaches of the archipelago, once a haunt for pirates and brigands. Rumours say that they were driven out by strange and monstrous creatures, far greater in size than any beast should be....
Instance: Isle of Storms -- Tier 2
Defeat the great beast guarding the entrance to the caves of the Isle of Storms.

Someone - or more likely something - has slain most the pirates who once frequented these caves and driven away any survivors. If you want to reach the Roc's aerie above, you're going to have to make your way past it....
The tunnels here howl with winds that blow down from the peak, making your progress treacherous - but it seems to be the only path leading to the Roc's aerie above.

'Hail adventurer! If yer willin', I've a humble request. The cats that roam these docks are wantin' for a meal, and me hands are tied up with this fella here. I've already taken care of a good number of them around, but could ye spare a moment to share some food with my feline friends that haven't been tended to yet with this here bucket of fish?
'There's Maedal, a sturdy fella with a grey coat. You're sure to find him at the training grounds nearby. He loves to watch the sparring and the folk there tend to share their scraps with 'em as well.
'Tathar and Heruin are twins. Skinny little orange critters that have taken it upon themselves to defend the lifts. Tathar will be close to here watching this one and his sister, Heruin, will fer sure be down at the southern lift. They keep an eye out for any suspicious individuals.
'While yer down south, I'm sure you'll find a friend with a fluffy black coat near the southern gate, that'll be Gwath. He is always sitting around the water, and Cúron will surely be that way as well. She will be the orange one nappin' out on the farthest pier where she watches the boats arrive and is sure to get plenty of scraps from the folk there.
'Hmm... and good ol' Dagnir'll be guardin' us from the north. He'll be the one with the dark fur at the gate. Oh, and of course ye can't forget about Meril, the most friendly little creature you'll ever meet, but scared of everything. You'll know it's her by her grey and white fur, and she'll surely be hiding somewhere off the main path.'

Trouble Stewing

'Well yer a sight for sore eyes. Back with a whole crate of bowls!
'Done our humble tavern a mighty favour ye have. The stew will be flowing and they'll be singing yer praises for this!'

'Bless ye for bringin' back the stew ingredients. You've proven yourself a most solid individual, you have! But, lo and behold, we're still in a bit of trouble. We're lackin' bowls, can ye believe it? Bowls we need to serve the meal, no less!
'If ye could do me one more favour adventurer and run off to the training grounds outside near the water. Ask the cook there, Hithudor, if they have any layin' about that they can spare. I'd be in yer debt, friend.'

'Well met, adventurer. What can I help you with?'
You tell the cook of the situation at The Brew and Bounty and their need for bowls.
'Bowls, ye say? Not a worry at all. We got more bowls than we know what do with. You can find a whole crate of 'em near the wall back here. If ye need more, just holler. Always happy to help the other folk here and Lornion is good folk.'

'Take a closer look at that coffer, my good and subtle friend. Tell me if you notice any weaknesses I might exploit... for the good of the city, of course. My heart weeps that the folk of Umbar Baharbêl have been deprived of my presence for so long, and I aim to make up for those lost years!'

'I am pleased for you to see your handiwork, ${PLAYER}. Yes, it was my resolve to open the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja, but it was you who recovered the keys from the Heirsworn and made my decision both safe and possible. I am grateful for it, and will not forget what you have done. You will come to see that we of Umbar Baharbêl have very long memories, if you have not learned it already.'
Hármelak smiles sweetly.
'Yes, ${PLAYER}, it is good that you have come, for there is a small matter about which we must speak. We have begun taking suggestions from the folk of the city to learn who they would have replace Azagath and Nakási in our ranks, but there is one other about whom we must speak. We must speak of Tatháta, ${PLAYER}. She remains Kinswoman of the Lower Ward, unless you have something to tell me that concerns her?'

'Welcome to the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja, where the Kindred of the Coins hear the voice of the people and act upon their concerns! Keep your weapons sheathed, speak with a civil tongue, and there will be no cause for trouble.'
Jaith smiles broadly as he notices you for the first time.
'${PLAYER}! It is good to see you! So many folk have passed through these doors that I confess I did not recognize you immediately, but that is now rectified. The Golden Queen has proven true to her word, and I see she made her choice of helper with wisdom! I did not think Dâr Laja would ever be opened again, and it would be my lot to guard a locked door for all the years of my life. But no! Even now the sound of agreeable conversation drifts from within!
'You may pass inside, ${PLAYER}. I will not forget how you helped Lady Hármelak reopen the Meeting-hall, my friend. What a fine day this has become!'
'You may pass inside, ${PLAYER}. I will not forget how you helped Lady Hármelak reopen the Meeting-hall, my friend. What a fine day this has become!'

'It is good to see you, ${PLAYER}. My brother has gone ahead to the main hall, but I wanted to wait for you. It has been a strange morning.
'Heralds sent by the Kindred travelled through the city, announcing that Dâr Laja would once again be opened. During the rule of the Heirs or the domination of Ordakh such a thing was considered impossible, and when the Kindred came to power the folk of the city believed it to remain so. And yet here we stand, within the great Meeting-hall of Umbar Baharbêl, and the Kindred of the Coins has come to listen to the wants and needs of their people. Rothog the Storm walked not three strides from me when he came inside, but his khopeshes remained strapped to his back, and he gave no indication that he might eat anybody! That is progress, is it not?
'I cannot help but think that it was your arrival on these shores that set the city upon this course, ${PLAYER}. I thank you again, as I have before, for making me a part of your crew.
'My brother is in the main hall of Dâr Laja, to the north-east. He will be pleased to see you as well, though he may not say so. You know how he is, of course.'

'This may not be easy, ${PLAYER}... but do they not say it is the hard thing that brings the greatest wealth and power?
'Folk have come from all over the city to bring their concerns before the leaders of the Kindred, but that is of no account to me. I am more interested in the guarded coffer that stands at the foot of Hármelak's dais, for that is where folk are bringing their suggestions as to what worthy persons should succeed the members of the Kindred who fled the city. The guards are vigilant, yes, but if I can put my name into the coffer many times, it may be that Jajax will become Kinsman of the Citadel, or of the Sail-haven! Azagath and Nakási are not likely to return, after all, and their districts cannot remain leaderless for long. Imagine how much wealth and power I might wield as a member of the Kindred of the Coins, ${PLAYER}!
'Take a closer look at that coffer, my good and subtle friend. Tell me if you notice any weaknesses I might exploit... for the good of the city, of course. My heart weeps that the folk of Umbar Baharbêl have been deprived of my presence for so long, and I aim to make up for those lost years!'
'My brother is in the main hall of Dâr Laja, to the north-east. He will be pleased to see you as well, though he may not say so. You know how he is, of course.'

'Is that so? Well, I am not one to speak against Khôltekh. If he has allowed you to use this entrance, I will not risk my neck to stop you!
'There are other entrances to Umbar-môkh from the city above, but this one was given to the Temámir to guard, and we take this duty most seriously. Continue north-west to Mekab-kuphâr and you will find an able helper there. His name is Birûk, and he drew the dull stone for the day; that means it will be his obligation to provide any of the help you will require. This is the command of Khôltekh, and therefore it is a command to follow.'

'Ah, you are newly-arrived to this guard-post of the Temámir? And at Khôltekh's command, no less?'
Birûk sighs heavily.
'I should have inspected the other stones and proven to myself they were truly shinier than the one I drew... but it cannot be helped for today. It is my duty to aid you. What brings you to Umbar-môkh?'

'Yes, yes, you gave me the password already. I am satisfied.

'Word has begun to spread among the people that Azagath fled from the city, and while the details vary, in most of these stories both Tumúldo Fierce-water and Nakási Wave-reaper followed him. You and I know the truth of that, but it is best that the people not yet know. Of Tatháta no tales tell, but she has not been seen in some time.
'Did I say \qno tale?\q This is not the truth complete, ${PLAYER}. Kinsman Khôltekh has spies everywhere, and this morning he related to me that some days ago one of these spies observed Tatháta engaged in combat with an Umbari woman he did not recognize. There was another who stood by, ${PLAYER}, and that other was you.'
Hármelak raises her hand to silence you as you begin speaking.
'I know the circumstances that brought you to our city... and I know too that Khôltekh delayed in relating this information to me, for reasons of his own. Learn what these reasons may be, keep me informed of them, and discover what you can of Tatháta's fate. We are allies now, ${PLAYER}, if perhaps not friends, and this matter concerns us both.'

'I thought you might come to speak to me, friend. I have heard you were among the last to see Kinswoman Tatháta in life, and the others of my order are most interested to learn where she has gone in the days since. Did she follow Nakási and Azagath when the two of them fled? No one seems to know.
'I can see you have an interest in this question as well! If so, then my resources are yours to command. Tatháta was last seen in Umbar-môkh, the tunnels beneath the city, and it happens that my people control a guarded entrance to those passages. With my password they will welcome you, and lend you the aid you might require.
'Speak these words to the dwarves inside the southern entrance to Khabârkhad, and they will let you pass: Ijebad-nê!

'Khôltekh delayed in relating this information to me, for reasons of his own. Learn what they may be, keep me informed of them, and tell me too of Tatháta's fate. We are allies now, ${PLAYER}, if perhaps not friends, and this matter concerns us both.'

'You seek to learn where Tatháta the Sea-beast has gone? I have not seen her for quite some time. Are you certain she remains somewhere within Umbar-môkh? She is the Kinswoman of the Lower Ward, and you will usually see her striding through the streets, her two great hounds by her side.'
You tell Birûk that Tatháta was last seen within a hidden harbour beneath the city, and none have marked her passage in the days since.
'Well, I will ask around. But I should warn you. One thing is true beneath the city as it is in the streets above: there is a price for every question answered. If the Temámir of Mekab-kuphâr are to help you locate your missing woman, you should do what you can to help them in return: consult the notice board across the way to the south-west to see what we need done, and perhaps you will accomplish some of those tasks for us while I ask your questions for you. It is only fair, is it not? In Umbar-môkh it is very important for things to be fair.'

'I spent some time on that ship, as you know, and I should be able to search it more quickly than you or my sister. Keep the Corsairs and their Heirsworn Captains busy while I search, and I will meet you back here when I have finished!'

'Let us do what we can to help. If we aid the Temámir here with the tasks they have posted on that notice board...'
Corudan falls silent.
'You have already done that, I see! You are a step ahead of us, ${PLAYER}, but I am pleased to see that these past few months have not changed your way of thinking: you still desire to provide help where you can. I did not doubt it, but it is nice to see it demonstrated, all the same.
'One of the dwarves here agreed to ask his fellows about Tatháta? What has he learned?'

'I spoke to some of my fellows about the missing Kinswoman Tatháta, and none of them have seen her of late. Most agree that she must have possessed a home of some kind within Umbar-môkh, for she did spend time in the tunnels when not at sea, but no one knows where it might be located. This is a place of secrets, after all. Even men and women of means and power may require a hiding-place from time to time. Them most of all!
'But you said she was last seen at the harbour where her ship is docked? The entrance to that place is not far from here. Elves are known for their skill at observation, I understand? It may be your friends will pick up her trail, or notice something you have missed, if you return to this harbour and search for sign of her.'
'It was a good deed, my friend, and one of the dwarves here agreed to ask his fellows about Tatháta? What has he learned?'

'Yes? It is a good plan, but we must be careful. The ships belonging to Nakási and Tatháta surely remain within that hidden harbour, even if their captains do not. Still, the Temámir is correct that there may be signs within that point to Tatháta's destination. We were all rather occupied with our own situations when last we were there, ${PLAYER}, were we not?'
Corudan laughs, a sudden and surprising sound in the damp and the dark of Umbar-môkh.
'I had a very good view of your battle with Tatháta's lions, it is true, but I would have preferred to be free to help you with them... and you have told me of the dangerous climb that brought you to that harbour the first time. 'We are outsiders in Umbar-môkh. We patrol these caverns and keep them as safe as we can, but we do not live here. When my day is done, I return to the Shoreward Stone. When yours is ended, I presume you seek food and shelter at one of the taverns of the city. It is not so for all who walk these tunnels.
'I speak of the unseen ones, those the Umbari call \qMâtrikhai.\q My people have another name for them; to us they are the \qTerâsi,\q the forgotten ones. They creep into places no others could, and move with such speed that should you catch a glimpse of them from the corner of your eye, by the time you turned to look they have gone. They are children of Umbar, I think, and move about Umbar-môkh by secret passageways unknown to any other. It is said the Terâsi prowl the markets of the Upper Ward and the Lower when they are most crowded, stealing goods and coin whenever they can, and then slipping back into the tunnels and caverns undetected.
'Temámir hearts warm to the Terâsi, for we see their hardships and take pity upon them. It has been our custom to leave food for these forgotten ones throughout Umbar-môkh on occasion. You explain your intention to learn what befell Tatháta in the days since she was last seen fleeing from the hidden harbour. Silence falls upon Ilmabiri for long moments. At last Tephísa's voice floats back to you.
'Many of us live in the tunnels, stranger: more than you might think. Our eyes see much that the Temámir do not, for we can reach places even they cannot go; perhaps they choose not to go there, but we have not that choice. All of Umbar-môkh is our domain, and while the city is big, Umbar-môkh has vastness of a different kind.
'A friend of mine witnessed Tatháta's flight. By secret paths he followed her, unseen, but he was not her only pursuer. An Umbari warrior-woman chased at her heels, deadly daggers flashing in the torch-light. He pursued them both into Kamrabezûr, but among those vaults he lost their trail. Many abandoned temples to the Church of the All-Seeing can be found in that place; it may be Tatháta gained entrance to one of those, and stays there now in hiding. Of the other, I cannot say. My friend believes Tatháta must have given her the slip as well, leaving her no choice but to return to the city above. That seems most likely to me.
'Good-bye, stranger. I thank you for the food and for the wine! I hope Tephísa has been a help to you.'
There is a brief rustling sound, and you know the girl has disappeared once again into the deeper darkness of Umbar-môkh.

'Reports from Kamrabezûr indicate that at least one terrible creature prowls the vaults and corridors of that place. Something must have escaped from the arena, and until Rothog's men can retrieve it that region of Umbar-môkh cannot truly be called safe. Be careful.'

'You have returned! Were you able to draw the notice of any among the Terâsi?'
You tell Birûk about what you learned from Tephísa, and he chuckles quietly.
'The net is closing about your prey, ${PLAYER}. Kamrabezûr? I have already sent your Elf friends into that place! Several of the circled areas on the map they showed to me indicated locations within those vaults, and the words of the Terâsi have confirmed that Tatháta's flight brought her to that place. You should look for your friends at Kên Taghlim in the north-western reaches of Kamrabezûr.'
Birûk prepares to go, but then he turns back to you, a concerned expression on his face.
'There is one more thing, ${PLAYER}. Reports from Kamrabezûr indicate that at least one terrible creature prowls the vaults and corridors of that place. Something must have escaped from the arena, and until Rothog's men can retrieve it that region of Umbar-môkh cannot truly be called safe. Be careful.'

'${PLAYER}, there you are! Let us move forward with care. There are several locations within Kamrabezûr that Tatháta marked on her map with charcoal, and any of them could indicate the place where now she hides.'
You ask Corudan if he or his sister have encountered any of the beasts rumoured to have escaped from the arena, and he shakes his head.
'No, but the folk we have met with speak of little else. Whatever was being kept in the holding-pens of the arena must have been ferocious indeed to frighten them so; the sound of it roaring in the darkness is apparently enough to make your blood run cold.'
Sigileth makes no sound, but you can tell she does not believe these reports. Her brother continues.
'We may encounter this creature or creatures if we continue our search of Kamrabezûr. I just want us to be prepared. Let me mark the locations we still must investigate on your map, and encourage you to combat any of the other dangers that cross your path.'

'What bounties could be more dangerous... than those placed by Saklaphêl... on the Kindred of the... of the...'
Frustration and sadness war upon her face as she lies dying in the moonlight.
'If only... I could have chosen a different road. But that was... not to be. In my heart, I was... always... Hazêphen.'
Galatâni's voice is little more than a whisper now.
'Tatháta... kept me alive... for days... ${PLAYER}. With her terrible, secret power... she could have slain me... easily. But she had... she had questions. Questions about... you, ${PLAYER}...'
'She is gone. We should make a place for her here. Let us find stones with which to mark the grave before the sun rises.'

The woman blinks up at you through bloodshot eyes and her face is familiar. You have found Cruel Dancer.
'${PLAYER}...' she manages, weakly. 'I do not have much... time... left to me...'

Cruel Dancer shakes her head, but the motion causes her great pain and she winces.
'I was the... deadliest woman... in all these lands, ${PLAYER}. But my luck... my fortunes... they have abandoned me. Did it happen... when I killed the Blade-twist? Ever since then I have had ill fortune. I never... considered... that Tatháta might possess... such power...'
The dying woman gathers what remains of her strength.
'I want to confess to you something, ${PLAYER}. Will you... bring me into the sunlight? I have spent... too long in darkness... too long as Cruel Dancer. I would be Galatâni again... instead.'

'Yes, we can do as she asks. But I do not think she has very long left to her, ${PLAYER}. She may not survive the journey aboveground.
'Still... we will make the attempt.'

Galatâni laughs weakly, a thin sound in the silence of the Umbari night.
'It was too much to hope for sunlight... I suppose,' she murmurs.
'I was not always as I am, ${PLAYER}. I was like you... an adventurer-for-hire, accomplishing the small tasks... that needed doing. It was a simple life, but a good one. There was food on the table for my husband, Jedûth, and my daughter Ashenâth. But it... did not last.
'My husband was accused... of stealing a vase from a wealthy nobleman, a man called Phirasâkh. He did not! I know he did not... but he was slain for the crime. I had to take on even more dangerous tasks to support my Ashenâth... even murder. That paid the finest of all, ${PLAYER}, but the first victim of my knife was the sweetest: Phirasâkh, the nobleman who falsely-accused my Jedûth. He deserved the death I gave to him.
'But I did not stop at Phirasâkh, for I had tasted the deadly nectar of death. I was away for longer and longer at a time; I told myself the coins I gave my neighbours to watch my daughter Ashenâth were all for her benefit. The name \qGalatâni\q no longer applied to me, for I had grown hard, and cold. I was now Hazêphen, \qCruel Dancer,\q and I delighted in the slaughter. Phirasâkh had deserved death. But he would not be the last, and some who died at the hands of Cruel Dancer deserved it less than he. Many did.
'It was best for Ashenâth that her mother remain only a memory... for I had grown addicted to... the danger, ${PLAYER}, and the sight of the blood I spilled. It had... become an obsession.'
She falls silent for a long moment, and you wonder if her life has ended, but then she coughs and sputters back to awareness.
'The city was not a place of safety... in those years. The Church of the All-Seeing saw its... enemies everywhere. The neighbours who watched after my daughter were taken in sacrifice to the Mâkhda Khorbo, and their home burned. On that day Ashenâth joined her father, but when I returned to the burned frame that had been a home there was no vengeance to be had. The Dark Lord worshipped by the Church of the All-Seeing was not like... not like Phirasâkh. I could not be certain He even lived, and if He did not live... could He be slain?
'I preyed upon the Church for a time, often for free, but when my coins ran out I had few choices left to me. I stopped returning to the burned husk where once I lived with my Jedûth and my Ashenâth. I only felt alive when I competed with other bounty-hunters for the most dangerous work I could find.'
