'As you search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell Thórvilon what we know of the Utûgi and their Thardúth masters. Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'As you search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell Thórvilon what we know of the Utûgi and their Thardúth masters. Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'So it is true: the Utûgi leave the lands in which they awoke and begin to threaten others nearby. Our mission grows more serious.
'But we cannot leave Imhûlar just yet. While you were gone, Thórvilon spoke to me of a woman about whom I must learn more. He says she is named Cúridwan, and she has been a friend to the Kintai for as long as he can remember.'
Inkanûsh looks at you closely, one of his eyebrows raised.
'Thórvilon is one of the Kinta Elves, ${PLAYER}, and his memory is long. How can it be that this woman has lived in this place for such a span? This mystery and others have prompted me to ask a number of questions I have not before thought to ask.
'I must speak with this woman. I must speak with Cúridwan.'

'I am almost... home. I have dreamt of living here once again in peace, but...
'For how long can I remain at Urmâkh, knowing that Shâra Mizâdi faces our enemies in distant lands? Her own husband Eshtali perished in recent days, and still she fights.
'But I know not if I am as strong as she.'
'I know not if I am strong enough to continue this fight.'

'It is always the same, ${PLAYER}. In this place I see young soldiers of old wars, fighting and dying in battles they did not cause and whose roots they cannot see. They fight against Ordâkh as I fought against Mordor, and they fight for Mizâdi as I fought for Gil-galad the High King. Do they think this will be the last battle they need fight, as I believed then? Did I call them young soldiers? Perhaps I am one of them after all, despite my years!
'I understand Mizâdi and her army will travel the longer way through Khûd Zagin into Mûr Ghala, avoiding the dangerous forest road, but Inkanûsh wishes otherwise. He would have us speak first with Thórvilon, the Kinta warden of the grove of Vartúlin. It is the Wizard's plan to take the forest road through what remains of the Emerald Wood, ensuring that the Utûgi did not go that way unseen.
'It seems a good idea to me. The creatures we fought at the Dagor Carlanthir were fearsome, and I do not want them to prey upon the Kintai. Our kindreds are long divided, but they remain Elves, and dear to me even from such distance.'
'I will follow Shâra Mizâdi even to death.'

'What brings you back to Vartúlin, ${PLAYER}?'
You tell Thórvilon that you have come with the Elf-lord Glorfindel and the Wizard Inkanûsh to secure the safety of the Emerald Wood on your journey to oppose the Empire of Ordâkh. The warden of the grove strokes his chin.
'My folk have noticed strange Orc-like creatures moving among the trees outside Vartúlin. We believed them to be Orcs at first, but these were dressed strangely and seemed a larger breed than the Orcs we have encountered before.'

'Inkanûsh wishes for us to speak first with Thórvilon, the Kinta warden of the grove of Vartúlin. It is the Wizard's plan to take the forest road through what remains of the Emerald Wood, ensuring that the Utûgi did not go that way unseen.
'It seems a good idea to me. The creatures we fought at the Dagor Carlanthir were fearsome, and I do not want them to prey upon the Kintai. Our kindreds are long divided, but they remain Elves, and dear to me even from such distance.'

'These creatures of Orc-kind of which Thórvilon speaks are almost certainly Utûgi, ${PLAYER}. If you will go search for sign of these invaders outside Vartúlin, I will tell him what we know of them and their Thardúth masters.
'Be careful. The Utûgi must be driven by some evil purpose if they dare approach the groves of the Kintai.'

'My folk have noticed strange Orc-like creatures moving among the trees outside Vartúlin. We believed them to be Orcs at first, but these were dressed strangely and seemed a larger breed than the Orcs we have encountered before.'

'Mizâdi intended to return to Urmâkh to regroup with her own soldiers before travelling south. Speak with her when you arrive, and give her my thanks. Her ambitions, and the army she commands to accomplish them, will be of great service to us if I am right and the Thardúth lurk within Mûr Ghala.'

'We will not travel alone, ${PLAYER}! Glorfindel has agreed to accompany us on our southward journey, and he waits for us at the town of Urmâkh, in Imhûlar. Once we have reunited with him, I suggest we meet with the Kintai at the grove of Vartúlin. Our road must pass deeper into what was once the Emerald Wood, but now that forest is changed and the Kintai will guide us safely within.
'Mizâdi intended to return to Urmâkh to regroup with her own soldiers before travelling south. Speak with her when you arrive, and give her my thanks. Her ambitions, and the army she commands to accomplish them, will be of great service to us if I am right and the Thardúth lurk within Mûr Ghala.'

'I am pleased to have your aid and support, friend, and that of the Wizard Inkanûsh! We reclaimed Kûr Anzar, but it was not enough. Even possessing the Crown of Renewed Hamât is not enough, for Bârshud remains alive to threaten my young kingdom and its people. We will only be safe when Bârshud has been slain and the Empire of Ordâkh knows the courage in our hearts and the strength of our sword-arms.
'Even now my soldiers heed this call. Stand by the gate and <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb> for the warriors that come from Kûr Anzar to join me on the southward road into danger.'
'Even now my soldiers heed this call. Stand by the gate and <rgb=#00FF00>look</rgb> for the warriors that come from Kûr Anzar to join me on the southward road into danger.'

'Give me a moment to rest, if you would. I am not so young in years that I feel not the road, nor the fighting I faced before it.
'Shâra Mizâdi wrested my home of Kûr Anzar from the Barkhûshim and Ordâkhai that held the city, and for that she will have my gratitude and my loyalty. Aye, unto death! Many others of my neighbours and my friends feel the same. We knew not that we might be Hamâti once again, but the coming of the Shâra wakened us to this truth: history is an unbroken chain that links the past to the present, even as it lies forgotten in the dust, or trampled underfoot.'

'I cannot say for certain, but when last we spoke Cúridwan had crafted a salve that could help fight against the Lâg Dávrit, the blight tainting the woods hereabout. She expressed a desire to bring it not only to the grove here in Imhûlar, but also to those further east, in Adagím. \qI must do this, Usakâr,\q she said to me. \qWhat is the hurry?\q I responded, but there must have been some need for haste after all.
'She has always been a friend to the Kintai, and if she possesses a means of curing their dying forest, she would share it without question. She has a big heart, our Cúridwan. Often she speaks of her purpose in these lands: to heal them, and to fortify them against evil.
'She would not appreciate these Orcs in her home, I know that! She must have gone already to Adagím, and missed their arrival entirely!'

'It is true. That was my favourite hat, but Luhum-gêna kept stealing it right off my head. Not only that, but no matter how often I think she is slain, Luhum-gêna somehow keeps coming back. Eventually I decided to just let her keep it.'

'Glorfindel and I will ensure it is safe out here, and we will join you within when we can. Go now, and hurry!'

'You are not an Orc, are you? No, you are not. That is a relief to me! It must be a relief to you as well, yes?
'If you are here to dine with Cúridwan, as I am, I must tell you that she is no longer here. Luhum-gêna was quite disappointed to learn of our friend's absence, as was I, but perhaps it is just as well. Neither of us expected the Orcs to find the hidden way into Kûgrun! Someone with more in the way of brains must have helped them find it, but they are not welcome.'

Eh... está bien, ¡derrota al troll de piedra!
Has encontrado a Olwir, junto con un troll enjaulado.

'¡Bien hecho! Me impacienté esperando y vine a ver cómo te estaba yendo, pero parece que lo hiciste bien sin mí. Ese troll de piedra está muerto, y parece que Olwir también. Pagó un alto precio por su crimen, robar una vaca a Filibert. Con él fuera del camino, estos enanos no deberían molestar mucho más al Pantano de los Juncos.
'Has hecho un buen trabajo hoy, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo mío[m]|amiga mía[f]}. Tienes mi agradecimiento. ¿Estás ${PLAYERNAME:listo[m]|lista[f]} para partir?'
Un regalo para el norte
Debes encontrar una manera de entrar en el campamento enano. Tal vez desafiar a los enanos a un combate los haga abrir la puerta.
Debes encontrar una manera de entrar en el campamento enano.
Los Duramano han abierto la puerta para responder a tu desafío. Deberías hacer algo que inicie el combate.
Has derrotado a los enanos que custodiaban la puerta. Deberías avanzar hacia el campamento en busca de Olwir o de un troll de piedra.
Has encontrado a Olwir, y tiene un troll de piedra enjaulado. Deberías derrotar a los Duramano que lo protegen.
Parece que Olwir ya no es un problema, pero ahora tienes uno más grande: un troll de piedra que debe ser derrotado.
Debes encontrar una manera de entrar en el campamento enano.
Los Duramano han abierto la puerta para responder a tu desafío.
Has encontrado a Olwir y derrotado a los guardias que lo protegían. ¡Tiene un troll de piedra enjaulado! Deberías enfrentarte a Olwir.

Has viajado a las afueras del campamento enano en el Pantano de los Juncos. Allí esperas poner fin al plan del enano Olwir de capturar un troll de piedra y dárselo como regalo al enano Skorgrím en el norte.

'¡Gracias, ${PLAYER}! Las arañas no muestran ningún signo de querer irse, pero tus esfuerzos en la cantera seguramente no harán daño tampoco.
'Aún así, me pregunto si debería mudarme a Bolgovado. Siempre me he llevado bien con los Bolger... mejor que con las arañas, en cualquier caso!'
Arañas en la cantera
Has derrotado a la mayoría, si no a todas, de las arañas en la cantera, pero la araña más importante aún permanece. Debes encontrar y derrotar a la Reina de los Campos Verdes.

Orcos Tarkrîp derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'¿Has acabado con el Despojador Rojo? ¡Robb se alegrará mucho de saber que has eliminado a esa bestia de orco! Yo también te doy las gracias por hacer del Camino Verde un lugar más seguro'.
La venganza de los Espinar

Los Montaraces de las Tierras de Bree están preocupados por la aparición de un enemigo al que han combatido durante mucho tiempo en el norte: los orcos Tarkrîp. Deberías derrotarlos para que la familia Espinar pueda volver a dormir tranquila por las noches.
Se ha cobrado una venganza justa contra los orcos Tarkrîp que capturaron y torturaron a Robb Espinar. Ahora es el momento de buscar a aquel a quien llaman el Despojador Rojo.
Se ha cobrado una venganza justa contra los orcos Tarkrîp que capturaron y torturaron a Robb Espinar. Ahora es el momento de enfrentarse a aquel a quien llaman el Despojador Rojo.

Los Montaraces de las Tierras de Bree están preocupados por la aparición de un enemigo al que han combatido durante mucho tiempo en el norte: los orcos Tarkrîp. Ya has matado a muchos, pero aún quedan bastantes. A Robb Espinar probablemente le vendría bien un poco más de venganza.
Robb Espinar ha sido rescatado de los orcos, maltrecho y apaleado, pero no se conforma con el rescate. Exige un castigo, especialmente contra el orco al que llaman el Despojador Rojo.
Escolta a Lalia hasta un lugar seguro.
Habla con Lalia
<rgb=#FF0000>Lalia debe sobrevivir</rgb>
Acércate a Lalia

'Vine aquí a buscar al \qÚltimo Príncipe\q, como en las historias del señor Mantecona. ¡Iba a encontrarlo, y luego estaría con él para siempre y sería su princesa! ¡Pero no estaba aquí! ¡Solo hay esqueletos, huesos y muertos que caminan! ¡No está bien engañar así a los jóvenes hobbits!
'Cuando estés con fuerzas para partir, ¿podrías ayudarme a regresar a casa en Bree? Antes no podía irme, pero ahora que tengo una compañía tan poderosa como tú, ¡estoy segura de que podrás llevarme a casa sana y salva!
'¡Ah, y perdí mi capa! ¡Tengo que encontrarla, o papá me va a gritar terriblemente!'
No lograste proteger a Lalia
Has escoltado a Lalia fuera de las Quebradas de los Túmulos con seguridad.

'¡Qué alivio! Parece que conozco bien a mi hija. De hecho, había ido tras ese \qÚltimo Príncipe\q suyo. Bueno, tal vez haya aprendido la lección y no sea tan tonta en el futuro. Sé que ciertamente nunca volveré aquí. 'Espero poder sobrevivir a su adolescencia. Tal vez entonces adquiera un poco de sentido hobbit. Tal vez...'
Paso Seguro de Lalia

Lalia te ha pedido que la ayudes a regresar a Bree de manera segura. Además, te ha pedido ayuda para encontrar la capa que dejó caer en algún lugar de la Quebrada de los Túmulos. Debes protegerla mientras busca su capa y luego abandona la Quebrada de los Túmulos.
Has encontrado a Lalia entre los Túmulos del Norte y el Pináculo de los Caídos, como se esperaba. Deberías hablar con la niña llorando.

Se esperaba que Lalia estuviera entre los Túmulos del Norte y el Pináculo de los Caídos, donde se dice que el \qÚltimo Príncipe\q fue enterrado, y es exactamente allí donde la encontraste. Deberías acercarte a la niña llorando.
La hija de Bob, Lalia, ha desaparecido, y Bob teme que haya ido en busca del \qÚltimo Príncipe\q, un personaje de uno de los cuentos que Cebadilla Mantecona relata a los viajeros.
Libera a Avorthal
Defiende a Avorthal

Localiza la Piedra de la Ira
Derrota a los Duramano (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

¿Vienes a liberarme? Skorgrim Duramano ha levantado un ejercito de trasgos en las gargantas de Rath Teraig y, a menos que lo detengamos, ¡arrasará todas las tierras libres!
No hay tiempo que perder, ${PLAYERNAME:mi amigo[m]|mi amiga[f]}. Tendremos que derrotar al capitán y a su tripulación si queremos escapar de Kheledûl con vida y advertir del peligro que crece en Rath Teraig.
El capitán volverá pronto. Rápido, ¡desátame las manos! ¡Tenemos que escapar de aquí!
Cajas de tesoro recuperadas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Duramano derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Debemos apresurarnos, ${PLAYER}. Skorgrim ha reunido un ejército de trasgos en Rath Teraig. Me temo que el ejército de trasgos no permanecerá mucho tiempo dentro de ese paso estrecho.
'Debemos regresar ahora.'
Rescate a la luz de la luna

Has recogido las cajas de tesoro y eliminado a muchos de los ocupantes Duramano de Kheledûl. Ahora debes llegar a la Piedra de la Ira, el barco que se prepara para llevar a Avorthal a un puerto desconocido en el norte.
Avorthal está en la cubierta de la Piedra de la Ira, aún amarrada en Kheledûl. Debes liberar a Avorthal.

Avorthal está retenido en la Piedra de la Ira, el barco amarrado en el puerto de Kheledûl.
A menos que lo liberes esta noche, la Piedra de la Ira llevará a Avorthal lejos del rescate y condenará a Ered Luin a una guerra entre enanos y Elfos.

Los Duramano controlan la ciudad portuaria de Kheledûl, donde Avorthal pronto será llevado a bordo de un barco con destino al norte. Este bastión Duramano también es donde se almacenan las cajas de tesoro robadas a los Barbiluengos por los Duramano.

Avorthal, el príncipe de los Elfos de Celondim, ha sido capturado por los trasgos y entregado a los malvados enanos Duramano. Se le ha transportado del campamento Duramano a la ciudad portuaria de Kheledûl, donde pronto se le subirá a bordo de un barco destinado hacia el norte, lejos de cualquier esperanza de rescatarlo.

¡Pampraush ha sido derrotado!
¡Pampraush ha venido a aplastarte a ti y a las uvas, y se ha quedado sin uvas!
Racimos de uva recogidos de las vides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'¡Ah, muy bien! Has hecho todo lo que podía pedir. Gracias por tus esfuerzos. ¡Esas criaturas malvadas aprenderán a no saquear mis bodegas en el futuro! Y gracias por las uvas restantes. Dentro de unos años, tus esfuerzos de hoy traerán gran alegría a muchos. El trabajo duro trae satisfacción, no solo en la elaboración del vino, sino en todas las cosas.'
Una añada excepcional
Se te ha pedido que recuperes frascos de vino de una cosecha rara y antigua de los trasgos que los robaron. Mientras estés en el Viñedo de Limael, deberías recoger las uvas restantes.
Has recuperado los frascos de vino de los trasgos que los robaron y recogido el resto de las uvas. Ahora deberías enfrentarte al líder de los trasgos, Pampraush.
Los trasgos han robado un vino excepcional de la vinicultora Brethilwen y están ocupando actualmente el Viñedo de Limael en Ered Luin.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador
Monstruosas arañas han invadido la cantera de Scary. Se te ha encomendado que ayudes a arreglar el problema antes de que las arañas ataquen el pueblo.
Has derrotado a las arañas que habían invadido la cantera de Scary. Deberías hablar con el extraño encapuchado para reclamar tu recompensa.
Completa la miniaventura: Arañas en la cantera

'Los trabajadores de una cantera en la Comarca han abierto una cámara oculta y liberado un enjambre de arañas. Los hobbits de Scary están bastante preocupados por este suceso, y la verdad sea dicha, no les culpo. ¿Te importaría ir hasta la cantera y ayudar a los habitantes de Scary? La plaga debe ser contenida antes de que las arañas se muevan de la Cantera dentro del pueblo.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>
'¡Me alegra oír que te has encargado de las arañas de la cantera! No me sorprendería que volvieran, pero de momento has hecho lo que has podido.'
'Dudo que los hobbits de la Comarca sean capaces de encargarse de estos enemigos por sí solos. ¡Si tienes disposición para luchar, no hay tiempo que perder!'
Miniaventura: Arañas en la cantera
Los trabajadores de la cantera de Scary han abierto una cámara oculta que contenía un nido de arañas, y las criaturas ahora han invadido toda la cantera.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador
'Has hecho un gran servicio tanto para los Elfos como para los Enanos de Ered Luin. ¡Y aún más para Avorthal! Gracias por todo lo que has hecho.'
Has rescatado con éxito a Avorthal y recuperado las cajas con los tesoros robados por los Duramano a los Barbiluengos.
Completa la miniaventura: Rescate a la luz de la luna

'Es bueno que estés aquí. Necesitamos ayuda urgentemente en Ered Luin. Avorthal, hijo de Cardavor, señor de Celodim, está prisionero de los enanos Duramano. Parece que planean llevarle hacia el norte en un barco con destino desconocido. La nave que se espera que le transporte se llama \qPiedra de Ira\q y está atracado en la ciudad portuaria de Kheledûl.
'Cuando estés en Kheledûl, verás algunos de los muchos tesoros robados por los Duramano a los Barbiluengos a lo largo de los años mientras ocupaban la Mansión de Thorin. La gente de Durin estará agradecida para siempre si puedes recuperarlos.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>
'No debes retrasarte, ${PLAYER}. Avorthal tiene que ser rescatado de los Duramano antes de que partan.'
Miniaventura: Rescate a la luz de la luna

Se te ha pedido que rescates a Avorthal, el príncipe de los Elfos de Celondim, de las garras de los Duramano. Cuando estés en la ciudad portuaria de Kheledûl, también deberás recuperar las cajas que contienen los tesoros que los Duramano han robado a los Barbiluengos.

Avorthal, el príncipe de los Elfos de Celondim, ha sido capturado por los trasgos y entregado a los malvados enanos Duramano. Se le ha transportado del campamento Duramano a la ciudad portuaria de Kheledûl, donde pronto se le subirá a bordo de un barco destinado hacia el norte, lejos de cualquier esperanza de rescatarlo.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador

Hay trasgos por todo el Viñedo de Limael y han robado un vino excepcional. Se te ha encomendado la tarea de recuperar las botellas que los trasgos todavía no se hayan bebido o destruido. También hay algunas uvas tardías de la temporada en las vides. Recoger suficientes le permitiría a Brethilwen producir un barril más de vino.
Has recuperado tanto vino como has sido capaz e incluso has recolectado suficientes uvas para que Brethilwen produzca un barril más de vino esta temporada.
Completa la miniaventura: Una añada excepcional

'Los trasgos están saqueando el Viñedo de Limael y recientemente un grupo de estas despreciables criaturas ha conseguido entrar en una antigua bodega, robando un buen número de botellas de una rara y antigua añada. No hay duda de que las malvadas criaturas ya estarán borrachas o habrán destruido la mayoría del vino, pero si puedes recuperar alguna de las botellas de los trasgos de esta zona, la vinicultora Brethilwen estaría en deuda contigo.
'Brethilwen también me ha dicho que ha sido una estación muy generosa y muchos de los viñedos están cargados de uvas. Si recogieras uvas de las viñas que estén todavía sanas y hermosas, Brethilwen se encargará de que un barril más se llene con el mejor de los vinos.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>
'Excelente trabajo, has salvado el vino. Tu recompensa está bien merecida. ¡Salud!'
'Si lo tienes todo listo, no hay tiempo que perder. ¡Los trasgos se estarán bebiendo todo el vino bueno mientras hablamos!'
Miniaventura: Una añada excepcional
Los trasgos han robado un vino excepcional de la vinicultora Brethilwen y están ocupando actualmente el Viñedo de Limael en Ered Luin.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador

'Lalia, una joven muchacha hobbit, ha desaparecido. Es la hija de Bob, un empleado aquí en el Poney Pisador. Le encantaban las historias del \qÚltimo Príncipe\q que Cebadilla relataba, cuya tumba está en las Quebradas de los Túmulos, supuestamente entre el Túmulo Norte y el Pináculo de los Caídos. Si tu corazón es lo suficientemente valeroso como para ayudarle a buscarla y traerla de vuelta a casa, es donde deberías comenzar tu búsqueda.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>

Según el relato de Mantecona, el túmulo del Último Príncipe estaría entre los Túmulos del Norte y el Pináculo de los Caídos, cerca de un gran monolito. Se te ha encomendado que busques en las Quebradas de los Túmulos a su hija desaparecida, quien podría haber ido allí en busca del \qÚltimo Príncipe.\q de la leyenda.
Completa la miniaventura: El paso seguro de Lalia
'Parece que has tenido éxito salvando a Lalia de los espectros... y de sí misma. Ahora está con su padre descansando, pero te transmito su gratitud y una recompensa de su parte.'
'¿Todo listo para enfrentarte a las nieblas de las Quebradas de los Túmulos? La pequeña desdichada podría quedarse en los túmulos mucho más tiempo que el que pretendía si no se la encuentra pronto.'
Miniaventura: El paso seguro de Lalia
Has escoltado a Lalia hasta un lugar seguro fuera de las Quebradas de los Túmulos, a pesar de su esfuerzo en toparse sin querer contra cada espectro de las brumosas colinas.
La hija de Bob, Lalia, ha desaparecido, y Bob teme que haya ido en busca del \qÚltimo Príncipe\q, un personaje de uno de los cuentos que Cebadilla Mantecona relata a los viajeros.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador

'En el pueblo de Ojo de Aguja en la Comarca, un enano llamado Ulfar ha descubierto el plan de capturar a un troll de piedra y llevárselo como regalo al resucitado Skorgrím Duramano, al norte. No debe permitirse que su plan prosiga. Afortunadamente, Ulfar ha averiguado dónde tienen su campamento Olwir y sus enanos, al norte del Pantano de los Juncos. Ve allí e impide que Olwir cumpla su objetivo.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>
Tienes la misión de entrar en el campamento de Olwir y frustrar sus planes de capturar a un troll de piedra para entregarlo a Skorgrím como regalo.
Has detenido los planes de Olwir y derrotado al troll de piedra. Deberías hablar con Ulfar y después informar también al extraño encapuchado.
Completa la miniaventura: Un regalo para el norte
'¡Ya he oído que lo has conseguido! Bien hecho. Skorgrím tendrá que conformarse sin ese troll. Aquí tienes tu bien merecida recompensa.'
'¿Todo listo para viajar al campamento de Olwir? Debes frustrar sus planes y si ha capturado un troll, ¡debemos terminar con él!'
Miniaventura: Un regalo para el Norte
Ulfar ha averiguado los planes de Olwir de capturar un troll de piedra que ronda por el Pantano de los Juncos para entregarlo como regalo a los Duramano del norte.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador
Te has encargado con éxito de los orcos Tarkrîp y el Despojador Rojo. Deberías hablar con Rose Espinar y después informar al extraño encapuchado.
Completa la miniaventura: La venganza de Espinar

'Un granjero local, Robb Espinar, fue capturado y torturado recientemente por una tribu de orcos del norte, los Tarkrîp. Espinar está de vuelta en casa recuperándose de este suplificio, pero su esposa Rose nos ha contado que Robb no puede dormir por las noches sabiendo que estos orcos están todavía ahí fuera. Debe vengarse de los Tarkrîp y en concreto de aquel que llaman Despojador Rojo. ¿Serás tú quien consiga doblegarlos?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>
'Te felicito. Robb Espinar por fin podrá descansar tranquilo y hay menos orcos Tarkrîp por los que la gente de las Tierras de Bree ha de preocuparse.'
'Avísame cuando lo tengas todo listo para vengar a Espinar. Hacerlo hará mucho más que ayudar a que la familia de Espinar duerma tranquila por las noches.'
Miniaventura: La venganza de Espinar
Se te ha encomendado la peligrosa tarea de entrar en el campamento Tarkrîp y vengarte en nombre de Espinar de los orcos que allí se encuentran.
Robb Espinar ha sido rescatado de los orcos, maltrecho y apaleado, pero no se conforma con el rescate. Exige un castigo, especialmente contra el orco al que llaman el Despojador Rojo.

'The people called for me to join the Ghad Imghêda; as harbour-warden I could not refuse. I sought not to elevate my position, but with so many of the Heirsworn gone from the city, it would seem my days must be less eventful. This will fill them up.
'To the Umbari who called for me to join this august body, I made this pledge: to remain vigilant, not only of our enemies but also of our friends, and our chosen leaders. It appears to this old sailor that much of the trouble began when Tumúldo sailed to Gondor, and that done at Azagath's command. The old Kindred should have sniffed out the Sea-shadow's evil before he could use it to deprive the city of such a hero as Tumúldo, who might have opposed him.
'Others might be deceived, but not I, and not now the Ghad Imghêda!'

'The Temámir and the Umbari people must work together, and not at cross-purposes. For that reason, I was chosen to join the Ghad Imghêda.
'I feel I must apologize for the actions taken by Khôltekh during the past few weeks, ${PLAYER}. I have explained to the Umbari and to my own people that I consider it a failing of my own that I did not determine his true allegiances in time to prevent the tragedies that befell the city. I need not tell you that he acted alone and for his own interests, and it was not with the authority of the Shoreward Stone that he fell in with Ordâkh or with the Orcs of Mordor that were seen upon one of the vessels as it passed the city. I am grateful for the assemblage of Temámir who came to Thargushakâl and informed me of his treachery during the early hours of the uprising. They will be rewarded!
'The actions of Khôltekh shame his people. The Umbari can rest more easily now that I have joined the Ghad Imghêda.'
'One mystery remains to be solved.'
Rothog smiles at you, and his grin seems more ferocious than ever.
'The people of the city loved my husband. I will rule as part of the Ghad Imghêda in his memory, and on their behalf.'
'The Heirsworn will no longer pose a threat to us. I will see to that.'
'The actions of Khôltekh shame his people and his city. The Umbari can rest more easily now that I have joined the Ghad Imghêda.'
'The Ghad Imghêda meets even now at Dâr Rapha, east of the city. That is where I am going, for I wish to get a look at them. On these wise counsellors we put our hopes!'
'My brother Dax stands with this new Kindred as if he were one of them! That is an oversight, surely?'

'One thing followed another, ${PLAYER}. I am not sure what happened. But I am glad to see you safe and alive!
'At first I was just trying to carry out your will, telling the people what you told me... but as more and more folk learned that Hármelak and Khôltekh had imprisoned you and my brother, they became angrier and angrier. You helped many Umbari and Temámir alike when you came to these shores, ${PLAYER}, and it seems you have made more friends than you know!
'What began in confusion became a rebellion, Ilma-ghôli, the rising tide, and then there was no stopping it! Try as I might, I could not convince those who flocked to us that I was not cut out to lead them... and now they have made me part of the Ghad Imghêda. I don't understand how this happened, and yet every step of the way has led me to this moment.
'Is this how you feel every day, ${PLAYER}? I cannot get used to this!'
'How might things have transpired if Dax was locked away, and I was left to manage the uprising? Now that would result in a truly impressive Ghad Imghêda!'

'I wear these burns proudly in memory of Belondor, ${PLAYER}. I believe he sails now in the company of his friend Sirgon, and they are not bound by the oceans of the world.
'I sought not to join the Ghad Imghêda, but the people of the city demanded it. I could not refuse them. They ask for strength, and I possess it. It would be impolite to abandon them.'
Rothog grins, a frightful sight.
'Besides,' he says, 'all of my things are here.'

'Despite the land where he was born, my husband was a man of Umbar. The wife of such a man must be prepared for the voyage on which he might not return, and I was.'
Mêshka smiles sadly.
'That makes it little easier, ${PLAYER}, but one thing has lightened my sorrow. The people of the city loved my husband, and they grieve with me. The burden is shared across every Ward of Umbar Baharbêl, and so made less.
'They asked me to join the Ghad Imghêda and to rule in Belondor's stead. I agreed, and so honour my husband's memory and the love he held for this city and its people.'
'Each member of the Ghad Imghêda is impressive. Until they learn I am not, I will stand beside them and do the best I can!'
Some familiar faces await you: the Ghad Imghêda of Umbar Baharbêl
Dâr Rapha is up the hill to the east of the Gate of Songs, outside the city.

'Our return voyage was not as eventful as the first that brought you to these shores, ${PLAYER}!
'Umbar Baharbêl seemed on the very precipice of the cliff's edge when we departed, but all is now as it was. Let us ask some of the people nearby what transpired while we were away.
'You go to the east and find someone willing to talk near the Northern Ship-yard. The workers there are always willing to spend the day in idle chatter, and the tidings we seek are the furthest thing from trivial!'

'How could you not have heard? The Kindred of the Coins was overthrown, and a new Kindred raised in its place: the Ghad Imghêda, the Kindred Redeemed!
'Hármelak Golden-hand and Khôltekh the Temámir were in league with Ordâkh, allying even with Orcs of Mordor! They thought to sell this city to its oppressors, but they counted not on us: the common men and women of Umbar, the ship-builders and the sailors, the merchants and the scholars, the fishermen and the labourers.
'The people of Umbar Baharbêl rose up against them, and with one voice we spoke to them: \qIt will not be so!\q we shouted. The uprising lasted for the better part of the day, and into the night. There was bloodshed, for not every soldier at Hármelak's command threw down his weapons, but many saw the rightness of our cause and joined the just throng.
'Another group opposed us during the uprising: the Heirsworn, who have long troubled the peace of the harbour. One of my workers fought against them on the night of the uprising, and can tell you more. Her name is Jínen, and she was on her way to the Gate of Songs north of the city just moments ago. If you hurry you may find her there.
'But that is in the past. May the new Kindred better serve the interests of the Umbari people, free of the influences of Ordâkh!'

'Someone will tell us what transpired while we were away. Umbar Baharbêl seemed on the very precipice of the cliff's edge when we departed, but all is now as it was! Find someone at the Northern Ship-yard. east of here, who is willing to talk.'

'Yes, I fought against the Heirsworn during the uprising; I am not afraid to speak of it.
'They have always been the weakened side of the ship's hull, still long at sea, and I am not surprised that it eventually burst! The passage by the city of the Ordâkhai ships was a hammer-blow to that imperfection, and the Heirsworn believed their time had come at last to fully seize control once again. What made them so bold? I cannot say for certain, but whispers tell that many of their number had been secretly leaving the city for a number of weeks, rallied somewhere by the son of Balakhôr himself.
'The uprising was short but effective, and a new Kindred has been formed to lead Umbar Baharbêl in the days to come: the Ghad Imghêda! They assemble even now at Dâr Rapha, up the hill to the east. That is where I am going, for I wish to get a look at them. On these wise counsellors we put our hopes!'
'May the new Kindred better serve the interests of the Umbari people, free of the influences of Ordâkh!'

'Most of the crowd has not yet thought to look for us in Umbar-môkh. We can follow these passages to safety!'

'Hold it right there, Hármelak.'
The Temámir meaningfully grips the haft of his spear and nods in the direction of Khôltekh.
'I will not use this unless I am commanded to do so... but I will obey the order if it is given.'

'Spare me your indignation, Hármelak: you know what happens to those who gamble with the lives of others without taking care to slant the odds sufficiently in their favour. The Song of Waves and Wind proved very useful, and it may be that Gondor lies in ruin even now, but you failed to manage the people of the city, and they have turned upon you. That they think to also hold me accountable for your blunder is... unfortunate.
'But the memories of the people are short. You will be kept safe and unharmed until such time as it is politically advantageous for the Temámir to produce you.
'The waggons to the north will transport you safely out of the city and beyond reach of the crowd that calls for your head. This is much finer treatment than you would receive from anyone else; let us say it is in remembrance of the tyrants we overthrew, and the Kindred we led together, if only for a short time.'

Khôltekh motions for you to speak to him.
'You have nothing to fear, my Lady. The doors of Dâr Laja are strong, and the men who guard them are even stronger! None of the shouting throng will get inside.'

'The area from Dâr Laja to Bith Gabâr is packed with residents of the city, a shouting throng. Many in the crowd carry weapons, but for now they have not wielded them against us. I think that will not change, but I cannot say that with certainty.
'You must stay inside, my Lady. It is not safe for you out there. I fear we cannot protect you if you leave the safety of the Meeting-hall!'

'Dâr Laja is not safe for us, Hármelak. I know you trust in your guardsmen to keep the unruly throng at bay... but I have not that faith in them.
'The city has come alive with anger, and that fury is directed at you... at us. If we remain here, I believe we will be slain.'

'Hármelak and Khôltekh are missing. None have seen them since the uprising began.
'The people of the city who chose us to form the Ghad Imghêda expect us to redeem the Kindred of the Coins, to live up to its goals and not succumb to the rot that festered within it from its early founding. I hope it will be so, but that will be made more difficult if we cannot learn what befell Hármelak and Khôltekh during the uprising.'
'They may have perished during the uprising. What do you think happened to them when the people arose?'

'I wonder...?
'It is most likely they were caught and killed by the people they betrayed, but if that is so, where are the bodies? None have come forth to confirm either of their fates, so every suggestion is a supposition only. We can only guess at it.
'I do not like guessing, ${PLAYER}. I like knowing for certain.'
'Oh! I had almost forgotten, ${PLAYER}! I have news for you of your friends Corudan and Sigileth!'
'The Ghad Imghêda will remain alert for the reappearance of Hármelak or Khôltekh... just in case.'

'That is... a curious sight...
'In what direction do these animals travel?'
'Hers may not... but mine do. You say this may not be Silirtas... but if it is, I have to speak to her! I have to tell her I am sorry!'

'I urged you to come with us, Silirtas, to face a great and unknown evil. I thought despite every danger that lay ahead of us, if any need perish, it would be Sigileth of Lórien. I thought I could keep you safe! I am so sorry!
'When you were slain by Azagath before the door of Utug-bûr, I fell into despair. I thought I too must die to atone for that terrible deed, for robbing you of the life you might have had; only the voice of drew me out of that darkness.
'${PLAYER:Her[f]|His} words made me realize something, dear Silirtas. Every moment of every day, for every person in this Middle-earth, is a gift: not of treasure, but of choice. Every point in time gives you the opportunity to decide how you choose to use that moment. You chose to fight the fading of your people. You chose to venture with an Elf and a you had known for less than a day to combat an evil of the Elder Days. Those choices were yours, Silirtas, and I am inspired by them! I celebrate them!
'But I have learned there is one more choice you might make, dear one!'

Sigileth wipes the tears from her eyes.
'I have said my part. I believe Silirtas heard my words... but I cannot know for certain.'

'Corudan lost a great deal of blood at Kasukhín before we could stem its flow, and that would explain a chill of the body.
'But for you to feel it as well makes me think there may be another cause, an outward cause. This cold is not natural.'

'The Kindred of the Coins was neither entirely evil nor entirely good, ${PLAYER}. Like Hyarmendacil II, they achieved both lasting good and enduring harm. Does one erase the other? Wiser scholars than I may be able to weigh the value of each... but I cannot. Must we forget the instrumental roles played by Azagath and Nakási in the freeing of Umbar from the Heirs of Castamir and the cultists of Sauron? Must we forget Khôltekh's deeds during the Dagor Carlanthir, or Hármelak's advice that Dâr Laja be opened to the needs of her people? Must their later crimes strike from the record their earlier heroics and wise governance?'
Caebar studies the ground intently.
'Must my mother's refusal to see me erase the happy years I spent as a child in Ethring, ${PLAYER}? I think it cannot. So we celebrate the good and we work to remedy the bad, and by so doing we mend what wounds we can, and seek to avoid inflicting further harm. That is healing, of a kind, is it not?'
The Gondorian scribe heaves a sigh and looks up at you again, forcing a smile.
'From conversation with the Umbari I have sketched the members of the original Kindred of the Coins, ${PLAYER}. Umbar will remember both their fine qualities and their faults, neither excusing the other, and with these drawings I hoped to capture that balance. Choose one of your liking and it is yours; the others I will give to the city of Umbar Baharbêl, that it may remember its history and not forget it.'
'Look for these papers among Corudan's belongings, and give them to Caebar.'

Caebar accepts the papers and briefly studies them.
'Wait... you say that Corudan found these in an Ordâkh encampment in the Fearwater? I do not want to pester him with questions, ${PLAYER}, so let us speak of this outside.'
'Give Caebar the papers my brother collected during our time in the Fearwater.'

You find Caebar excitedly studying the papers Corudan retrieved from the Ordâkhai of Sûg Nidar.
'The soldiers would not have understood the meaning of this parchment, ${PLAYER}, but I do. They must have found it among the ruins of Kasukhín while searching for treasure; thinking it unimportant, they kept it unguarded among their belongings, where it went overlooked until it was picked up by Corudan.
'These are the words of Vinyarion, twenty-fourth King of Gondor, who bore the title of Hyarmendacil II: \qthe South-victor.\q Set down by a trusted retainer in his old age, only days before his death, these words claim that he repented of his long campaign in Harad, and wept at the bones of Shâraban, a city he destroyed in the days of his youth. On the return journey of his tenth pilgrimage to the lands he once conquered, he rested at the hilltop fort of Kasukhín and died there, peacefully, in his sleep. Sigileth tells me the land around that fort is now changed, and what was once a hill is now an island; might Vinyarion's bones lie there to this day, kept isolated from discovery by the creation of the Fearwater?
'His story raises complicated emotions in my heart, ${PLAYER}; he is considered very differently in Shagâna than he is in Gondor, and it is difficult to reconcile those two perspectives. I am put in mind of the relationship the Umbari must now have with the Kindred of the Coins that preceded the Ghad Imghêda, the Kindred Redeemed.'
'Yes, I will tell you what transpired after you left us.'

'I cannot say with certainty that the spirit was Silirtas, or that she heard my words. But I believe it was, and she did. I will not hurry to join her, but when at last I come to that place, I hope she and I will reside in comfort and in peace, beyond the loneliness and fear that so troubled Silirtas when she contemplated the unknown days ahead.
'That is my desire, ${PLAYER}. I cannot know if it will come to pass, but if hope leads us ever onward, the pleasant dream of it will live in my heart until the last of my days arrives.'

Caebar flushes.
'Oh! I am sorry to interrupt, ${PLAYER}! I did not know you had returned! I have visited our friends every day while Corudan recovers, and they have spoken to me of your adventure in the Fearwater.
'Please, finish your visit! I will speak with you afterward.'
'Caebar has visited every day, and kept us informed of events in the city.'

'That reminds me. My brother collected some papers from the Ordâkhai while we adventured in the Fearwater. He intended to give them to Caebar, but the matter has slipped our minds until now. Look for them among Corudan's belongings, and give them to Caebar.'
And as a light breeze passes over the sea, thus ends 'The Song of Waves and Wind'

'You should visit them at Dâr Tabib, in the Tor-gardens of Umbar Baharbêl. I know Corudan and Sigileth will be pleased to see you!'

'${PLAYER}, my friend... my wound is well on its way to healing... but to see you return with victory... eases the pain. I understand Umbar has been saved from... Nakási and Balakhâd? Has Gondor too... escaped from their wrath?'
You tell Corudan that King Elessar and his soldiers fought bravely against the Song, and Gondor survived. He smiles weakly.
'Then the last of Sauron's schemes... has been frustrated, ${PLAYER}. I am glad for my part in it...'
You insist that Corudan rest, and you will speak with him when he is more fully healed.

'I understand Nakási is slain and the Song of Waves and Wind defeated, ${PLAYER}. May there now be peace for a time!
'I heard tell that five ships of the Song survived the passage to Gondor, and waged war upon the Harlond? More might have joined them, had the rapids of the Ikorbân not proved too perilous; we saw the ruin of many smaller ships dashed upon the rocks as we travelled this way from Sûg Nidar. The builders of the fleet likely intended that to be a one-way voyage, but they had not counted upon Cúridwan's damaging solution, or your great haste in opposing those who escaped it.
'The raft-bridge of the Wrackwade did not last long against the Narghâk cannons. When we rejoined Rahâzi at Iridír she said her mother intended to see it rebuilt. It would not surprise me to learn she has already done so! But I have gotten ahead of myself. There is more to tell.
'While you pursued the Song toward Umbar, my brother and I and Cúridwan made our own way westward. Our return journey... was not uneventful.'
'Our return to the city... was not uneventful. My sister... will speak of it to you.'

You should let Mizâdi know with all due haste, and bring what you found of Eshtali's. This is grim news indeed, but she will want to hear it, and from your lips.'

'I have a personal matter with which I would ask your assistance, ${PLAYER}.
'I have received word from my spies of a rumour that my husband, Eshtali, has recently been seen outside the Crypts of Esh-kimâkhi to the south of here. What he is doing there, I have no idea.
'The leader of the Barkhûshim, that accursed Okhíso, claimed to take him when he drove us all from Kûr Anzar. I thought my precious Eshtali long since dead. I know it is dangerous, ${PLAYER}, but I feel a dagger of hope in my chest.
'You have accomplished much with me here. There is no one I trust more with this mission than you. Please, make your way to Esh-kimâkhi and look for him. You will know him by the crimson robes he always wears. I have sent Razâl ahead of you to scout the terrain, speak with him when you arrive.
'And, ${PLAYER}? If you are to return with my husband, know that you will have given me a gift worth more to me than any victory in this war.'

'Thank you for that news, and for his effects. Hope is a cruel master, and one that has now abandoned me.
'I remember when I was a girl, my sisters and I would make shapes, shadows on the wall. We would make funny animals: ducks, and rabbits, and chickens. Oh, and the stories we would tell! The adventures those rabbits and ducks had! Such stories. Those days have long passed, but when I close my eyes I can still see those shadows; dancing, vaulting, gamboling. I still hear their peals of laughter.
'When my husband came home, I would first see him by the shadow he cast on the wall. So broad and powerful, that shadow was the harbinger of my precious Eshtali coming home to me. Just like my sisters, I sought comfort in that shadow, always steady, strangely solid.
'After he was taken, I am ashamed to say I forgot what his face looked like, once so familiar to me. I can no longer see his face. All I see of him now is that shadow on the wall, insubstantial like a wraith, endlessly dancing through my memories.'

'The banner? No, I have never seen something like that before. You should report this straight away to Mizâdi.'

'Yes, this is the outcome I feared to be true. Still, I appreciate the news, grim as it is.
'Thank you for bringing these to me. I fear there is some new group of fiends harassing our southern border.
'This banner? I have not seen it before. Strange. It is quite similar to my own banner. The lion... I wonder. No matter. If they are attacking my scouts, they are no friend of ours. We have quite enough to worry about with Okhíso in Kûr Anzar, but I will think on this more. Thank you, friend.'

'Surâsh, one of my scouts, has returned to me with a harrowing report from southern Imhûlar. The rest of her scouting party has gone missing, and haven't reconvened in a fortnight. 'Something you can do for me? Absolutely, get the word out. Mulnûri will not be beat, cannot be beat on these prices or this quality. Look at these tunics. You will find no higher quality anywhere in Shagâna. Umbar can only marvel at these textures, this softness, they cannot come close to matching me.
'Everyone needs to know. It's for the public good!'

'Help, for me? Unless you can get the smell of fire or this blasted soot out of the air, you cannot do anything for me. Why did I let my wife convince me to come back here? Blasted wars, terrible for business, and one's nose.'

'Thank you for your help setting up and helping usher in some of old Kûr Anzar.
'The people of Kûr Anzar will now look to us for a sense of normalcy. A warm belly and a new tunic may not seem like much, but they are more than many have had here in Kûr Anzar in some time.'
'There is still much to be done, and yet more to be celebrated! Please, help the vendors set up their wares and make both the residents and vendors feel welcome again.'
'It is so good to be home again. Help? No, no, no. I need nothing from you. I'm too excited for help... in a good way.'

'So much to do, so little time. Help? No, nothing I need, my dear. I'm just so glad to see people smiling again around here. At least I think they are smiling. Surely they are! It's hard to tell through the soot.'
'How is one supposed to turn a decent profit with all this rubble everywhere? Yes, you can help me. Get some of this rubble cleared away. My clothes are far too fine to be in a war.'

'Good to see you, ${CLASS}. Our scouts have discovered an Ekhamâti camp in Khûd Zagin and they appear to have an abundance of gold stored there. I ask that you travel to the camp and take as much gold as you can find so we can put it to better use supplying Mizâdi's forces.
'There have also been reports of brutal dôla in the camp by the names of Omurtóko, Khisónto, and Purombóro. I ask that you put an end to them while you are there.'

'I am glad for your return, ${CLASS}. This gold will do so much good in helping Mizâdi! I thank you! And putting a stop to those dôla will also be great news for our soldiers who have heard the stories of their cruelty.'

Se te ha encomendado viajar a Sûri-kylä, en Forochel, para encontrar un potencial visitante que pueda aceptar una invitación para visitar Isla Remota para el festival del Solsticio de verano. Deberías buscar por Sûri-kylä potenciales visitantes.

'En las tierras lejanas al norte de Eriador, hay un yermo helado llamado Forochel. Allí vive una gente sobre la que he leído, llamados 'Lossoth', que viven en la fría nieve. Creo que no les vendría mal un poco de sol y arena, ¿no crees?
'Dírete a su mayor ciudad, Sûri-kylä, y encuentra a alguien que acepte de buen grado la invitación. Intenta no molestar a la gente que no veas tan abierta para emprender tal viaje, o pensarán que eres un estorbo y empezarán a tener una pobre opinión de nosotros.'

'¡Vientos favorables para ti, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}! ¿Montas a caballo?
'En la hermosa tierra de donde vengo, nos enorgullecemos de nuestra raza de caballos, muy valorados no solo por su velocidad y resistencia, sino también por su coraje y lealtad. Tenemos una larga historia de grandes competiciones donde los jinetes muestran sus animales y sus habilidades, y quería traer un evento así a los visitantes de Zír Aktar.
'Si crees que puedes manejar uno de nuestros finos caballos, eres bienvenido a probar nuestro circuito de carreras. Sin embargo, te advierto que solo los jinetes más hábiles podrán dominar un camino tan complicado en el tiempo que hemos asignado.
'Las reglas de la carrera son muy simples: corre a través de cada puerta, y no debes caerte de tu caballo antes de que se acabe el tiempo. Encontrarás obstáculos y terrenos desafiantes, pero también es una maravillosa manera de ver la isla. Cuando veas dos puertas una al lado de la otra, debes elegir qué camino tomar, ya sea alto o bajo. Cada camino tiene sus propios beneficios e inconvenientes.
'¿Te sientes preparado para este desafío? ¡Solo los jinetes más valientes deberían siquiera intentar tal hazaña! Seguro que será muy peligroso, pero tienes un aspecto aventurero.'
Excelente equitación, ${PLAYER}! Estoy muy impresionado. ¡Toma estas fichas como recompensa por tu logro!'

<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Cuando continúes esta misión, viajarás rápidamente a Isla Remota en las Islas Escudo.</rgb>
¡Te doy la bienvenida a Isla Remota!
Ikhajât te ha llevado a Isla Remota, donde deberías presentarte a Khâtaphos.

'Saludos, ${PLAYERNAME:viajero. Eres un viajero[m]|viajera. Eres una viajera[f]}, ¿verdad?
'Como ya habrás adivinado, soy un visitante de una tierra lejana. Vengo de las Islas Escudo, en lo que ustedes llamarían la Bahía de Belfalas. ¡Vine aquí para difundir la palabra de que el Solsticio de Verano es el momento perfecto para visitar! Hay una isla llamada Zír Aktar, Isla Remota en Oestron, que está dando la bienvenida a los visitantes!
'En la isla encontrarás brisas marinas relajantes, hermosas playas y palmeras calmantes. Sin mencionar las deliciosas bebidas y las habitaciones relajantes en la Jarra Agrietada, la posada y taberna local. ¿Te gustaría tomar un descanso de este lugar y disfrutar de todo lo que Isla Remota tiene para ofrecer? Si quieres, podría guiarte allí y estarás bebiendo vinos especiados dulces en la playa más rápido de lo que puedes decir... algo. No sé a dónde quería llegar con eso. Será rápido.'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro de misiones cuando termine el festival actual.</rgb>
Habla con Khâtaphos dentro de la Jarra Agrietada
Habla con Ikhajât

'¡Saludos! ¡Te doy la bienvenida a Isla Remota! Es hermoso aquí, ¿no es así?
'Le ruego que me disculpe, pero esta es una nueva aventura para mi tripulación y para mí, y siempre podríamos usar algo de ayuda. Mientras nos visite, si desea colaborar y ayudar a la tripulación con sus tareas, será bien recompensado. Tenemos muchos de estos Símbolos del Solsticio de Verano que hemos... ah, conseguido, de nuestros vecinos en Gondor. No son de poco valor, ya que pueden ser intercambiados por muchos regalos maravillosos.
'Si nos echa una mano, puede ganar algunos de estos símbolos. ¡Muchos, de hecho! Puede hablar con Darôma o el cocinero Sâghlem aquí en la Jarra Agrietada; siempre tienen cosas que necesitan hacer. Afuera, encontrará a Merkhâma y Maghôrdo, quienes ambos tienen más trabajo diario del que puede hacer una persona. O dos. También puedo tener algo que pueda hacer por mí ahora que lo pienso. Pregúntame más tarde, si quieres.
'¡No te preocupes! Uso la palabra \qtarea\q ligeramente, ya que todo es más divertido cuando estás en la playa, ¿verdad? Por favor acepta este pequeño regalo de bienvenida por venir a Isla Remota.
'¡Disfruta tu estadía!'

'Navegar por las aguas de las Islas Escudo puede ser un verdadero desafío. Los vientos irregulares, las corrientes traicioneras y los arrecifes ocultos justo debajo de la superficie representan muchos peligros para los barcos si la tripulación no está a la altura. Por eso, no es raro encontrar restos de naufragios en las playas del sur. Tal vez no sea tan bueno para los visitantes ver estas cosas y recordar que los viajes aquí no siempre terminan como planeaban.
'¡Me harías un gran favor si eliminaras cualquier resto que encuentres en las playas del sur de Isla Remota!

'${PLAYER}, es posible que hayas notado que hay muchos gatos en el puerto. No estoy seguro de qué hacer con ellos. Entre mi gente, se cree que los gatos traen buena suerte. Ningún dromón de Umbar se atrevería a navegar sin uno. ¡Hacerlo traería mala suerte a cualquier viaje!
'Pero parece que entre nuestros visitantes, no todos aprecian a los gatos como deberían. Algunas personas se han quejado, llamándolos plagas, y un hombre afirma que le hacen estornudar!
'Amigo mío, eres un visitante. ¿Qué dices? ¿Deberían quedarse o deberían irse?'

'Se supone que tengo a alguien aquí para ayudarme, pero esos inútiles de filibusteros parecen alérgicos al trabajo cuando hay tierra bajo sus pies. Si quieres ganar algo de dinero, te pagaré para que me ayudes con las tareas domésticas. Tenemos varias cabañas para huéspedes a bordo de la Jarra Agrietada, y todas necesitan ser ordenadas diariamente.
Necesitan hacer las camas y limpiar los suelos. No debería tomar mucho tiempo hacerlo. ¡Quizás una vez que esos inútiles vean que han sido superados por un visitante, se pongan las pilas y se pongan a trabajar! Sin embargo, no apostaría por ello.'

Complete Mission: The Blood Spectre

'I have a task for you, ${CLASS}. The Ordâkhai are a fearful people and many of them have heard a story since they were children of a blood-stained spectre who steals the life right from the Men of the south when they sleep. We believe you can be that spectre to them, to ignite their fears.
'I ask that you travel to their camp to steal their torches and spill this hog's blood around to give the impression of the spectre. Then eliminate the dôla in the camp to spread the fear. You should try and avoid any guards while you are there to ensure the story will be believed, but do not hesitate to defeat any who happen to discover your presence.'
'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. That should stoke the fires and spread fear throughout their ranks. Take this as a token of gratitude for what you have accomplished this day.'

'¿Todos han recibido la ayuda que querían? ¡Muchas gracias por ayudarlos! Y con ellos, me refiero a mí.'

'¡Dios mío, estoy absolutamente sediento! Es importante consumir muchas bebidas mientras se disfruta de la playa, ¿sabes?
'Sé un encanto y corre a la taberna a conseguirme una bebida refrescante. Algo fuerte, si entiendes a lo que me refiero.'

'¿Un picnic, dices? ¿Oh, parecían estar cortejándose?'
El hombre se ríe mientras toma el cesto y comienza a llenarlo.
'Tengo justo lo que necesitan. Una botella de vino, algunas carnes curadas, una variedad de quesos, galletas de agua y unos higos. ¡Eso debería bastar!'
'Oh, esto es perfecto, amigo mío. Muchas gracias. Y envía mis saludos a Sâghlem.'

'¿No es esta isla un lugar tan mágico!?
'¡He oído que los bañistas se divierten enterrándose unos a otros en la arena! ¿Enterrados en la arena, digo yo!? Bueno, me digo a mí mismo, ¡creo que me gustaría mucho eso! Solo que como el enterrado no tengo enterrador. ¡Pero ahora has llegado tú!
'¡Te encargo la tarea de enterrarme en la arena!'
'¡Lo encontraste! Muchas gracias, tenía muchas ganas de leer lo que pasa después. Cielos despejados y vientos favorables para ti, mi ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}.'
'Oh sí, dámelo aquí. Esto es justo lo que necesitaba. Ahora vete, estás bloqueando mi vista.'

'¡Vientos favorables para ti! ¿Qué es lo que necesitas? Oh, ¿vienes a preguntar si necesito algo? Ahora que lo pienso, me encantaría estar leyendo mi libro en este momento, pero lo dejé en mi habitación en la posada. ¡Me temo que si me voy a buscarlo, alguien me robará el asiento en este banco!
'¿Te importaría ir a La Jarra Agrietada y traerme mi libro? Lo dejé en la mesita junto a la cama.'
'¡Ah! ¡Eso será perfecto! ¡Gracias!'

'Saludos, mi buen ${RACE}. Dado que pareces estar ayudando a la gente, me pregunto si nos harías un pequeño favor.
'Me temo que no planifiqué bien nuestro día, ya que sería un día perfecto para un picnic, pero, ay, no tenemos una cesta de picnic con comida. ¿Podrías pasar por la taberna y traernos un picnic?'

'¡Cielos, casi me das un susto!
'¿Necesito algo? Bueno... si no es mucha molestia, podría usar algo para sentarme. Estoy disfrutando mucho de la vista, pero esta arena... la odio. Es áspera e irritante, y se mete por todas partes. Creo que esas personas allá con una manta tienen la idea correcta. ¿Podrías traerme un cojín o algo por el estilo?'

'Debo quedarme aquí para poder ayudar a los clientes que me lo pidan. Muchos me preguntan dónde están los mejores lugares para nadar, ¡y admito que no lo sé! ¡Estoy aquí todo el tiempo!

Habla con Merkhâma

'Entonces, ${PLAYER}, ¿cómo fue la natación?'
Le dices que el agua es más cálida donde es poco profunda y que es más fácil nadar donde hay menos olas, y le aconsejas dónde están esos lugares.
'¡Gracias, me has sido de gran ayuda! Como marinera, normalmente me quedo en el barco y no termino en el agua. No entiendo a las personas que se meten al agua a propósito, pero cuando me lo pregunten, repetiré lo que me has dicho. ¡Tienes mi agradecimiento!'
Buscando lugares para nadar

'¡Vientos favorables para ti, ${PLAYERNAME:amigo[m]|amiga[f]}! ¿Alguna vez has volado un cometa antes?
'¡Míralos elevarse por el cielo como un gran pájaro! ¡Siente el viento tirar de tu cuerda; aprovecha el aire para tu disfrute personal! ...Oh, ¿ya estás familiarizado? Mis humildes disculpas. Bueno, entonces ya debes conocer la gloriosa maravilla que ofrecen los cometas. ¿Necesitas otro? No hay nada como tener un nuevo cometa para hacer que todos tus amigos te envidien.
'Soy Tâlugar y vengo de la famosa ciudad de Umbar Baharbêl, trayendo hermosos cometas desde las regiones más lejanas de la Tierra Media para intercambiar por una pequeña cantidad de monedas. ¡Estos cometas son de la mejor calidad! ...¿Lo pensarás? Eso es todo lo que podría pedir, por supuesto. No, me retracto. Hay una cosa que te pediría.
'Ya que ya estás familiarizado con los cometas, te ofreceré un pago si sueltas tu cometa favorito y lo dejas besar el cielo frente a las buenas personas que visitan esta isla. ¡Déjalos ver la diversión que tienes mientras tu cometa navega por los vientos como un barco que se eleva en los cielos! Si ven lo divertido que es, seguramente acudirán a mí para comprar uno propio!'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro de misiones cuando termine el festival actual.</rgb>
Habla con Tâlugar
'¡Ah, vuelves! ¡Pude ver tu cometa desde aquí! Tienes una forma excelente. Aquí está tu recompensa, como prometí.'

'Dime, ${PLAYER}, ¿te gustaría ayudarme? Esta misión te obligaría a salir de la isla nuevamente... pero no tengo dudas de que podrás encontrar el camino de regreso. También puede que tengas que viajar a tierras lejanas, algunas de las cuales pueden ser un viaje difícil. Cuanto más experimentado seas como viajero, más fácil debería ser, creo.
'Lo que necesito son más personas como Ikhajât, que salgan al mundo y encuentren a otros que puedan querer visitar Furtherholm. ¡Alguien para ayudar a correr la voz de que este es un lugar maravilloso para visitar y todos son bienvenidos aquí!
'Tengo algunos lugares específicos en mente donde podrías ir para encontrar personas que podrían necesitar unas vacaciones en un lugar cálido y amigable que tiene muchos buenos vinos. De hecho, ¡he hecho una lista! ¿Te gustaría verla?'
<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro de misiones cuando termine el festival actual.</rgb>

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, ¡has vuelto a mí! He oído que tuviste éxito y trajiste a otro visitante a la isla. ¡Eso es maravilloso! Sabía que podía contar contigo. Aquí tienes una recompensa por tus esfuerzos.'

Se te ha encomendado viajar a Nobotella, en la Comarca Allende, para encontrar un potencial visitante que pueda aceptar una invitación para visitar Isla Remota para el festival del Solsticio de verano. Deberías buscar por Nobotella potenciales visitantes.

'¿Conoces a los medianos? Hobbits es como me han dicho que se llaman a sí mismos. Gente pequeña de pies peludos. Quizá es solo una leyenda pero he escuchado que son muy alegres, ¡en especial cuando hay comida y bebida cerca! Suena a que son una maravillosa compañía y me encantaría ver a gente tan jovial entre nuestros visitantes.
'He oído hablar de un pueblo de los medianos llamado Nobotella en la Comarca Allende donde podría ser posible encontrar a uno o dos jóvenes hobbits que estén dispuestos a viajar, ¡especialmente si los tientas con comidas y vinos exóticos! Encuentra a alquien que pudiera aceptar de buen grado una invitación a Isla Remota. Intenta no molestar a la gente que no veas tan abierta para emprender tal viaje, o pensarán que eres un estorbo y empezarán a tener una pobre opinión de nosotros.'

'${PLAYER}, sabes que en general prefiero los hechos a la fantasía, pero hay una leyenda en particular que me intriga. 'Por tanto, te encomiendo una nueva misión. Una como ninguna otra. Parte ahora y busca en cada rincón de la Tierra Media hasta que encuentres este \qÁrbol de la Fiesta\q. Cuando lo encuentres... si es que lo haces, mira a ver si puedes convencer a uno de los asistentes a la fiesta para que acepten una invitación para unirse a nosotros aquí, en Zír Aktar. Intenta no molestar a la gente que no veas tan abierta para emprender tal viaje, o pensarán que eres un estorbo y empezarán a tener una pobre opinión de nosotros.'

No me gusta lo que su Reino ha hecho, pero me resulta difícil culpar al ciudadano medio de Gondor por todo esto.
'Ve a Minas Tirith y encuentra a alguien que pudiera aceptar de buena gana una invitación a nuestra bella isla. 'Al este de las Tierras de Bree, hay unas desoladas tierras salvajes llamadas las Tierras Solitarias. Allí, vive un pueblo llamado los Eglain. He leído que eligieron vivir entre ruinas en vez de en ciudades o pueblos, rechazando la vida de la gente más cultivada en favor de la libertad de lo salvaje. ¡Me gustaría conocer a esta gente! Es como escoger una vida en el mar en vez de las comodidades de Umbar Baharbêl.
'He oído que muchos de ellos se encuentran en Ost Guruth, unas ruinas junto al Gran Camino del Este. Ve allí y encuentra a alguien que pudiera aceptar de buena gana una invitación. Intenta no molestar a la gente que no veas tan abierta para emprender tal viaje, o pensarán que eres un estorbo y empezarán a tener una pobre opinión de nosotros.'

'${PLAYER}! I have not seen you since your steps brought you to Umbar-môkh. I have come aboveground to ask Khôltekh... but my errand can wait. Something troubles you?'
You quickly tell Birûk that Nakási Wave-reaper sails a hostile fleet toward the city, and the banks of the Ikorbân River are not safe.
'I will delay you no longer! Tell the Kindred of the Coins what you have told me!'

'You know there is little to be gained by dying here, ${PLAYER}.'
Khôltekh lowers his voice so only you can hear him.
'Hármelak might have pretended she first heard the name \qThe Song of Waves and Wind\q from you, when you visited her in her manor, but she is not as clever as she thinks herself to be. Wealth cannot buy wisdom; only experience can do that.
'When Azagath told us of the Song's existence, neither of us believed in it. If the Dark Lord of Mordor could not rely upon such a fleet, of what use could it be to us? But it seems Nakási has done the impossible. The Narghâk I sent her from Ashâgir will prove the difference, I think.
'When Gondor burns, the folk of Umbar Baharbêl will rejoice.'

'Looks like this is it, ${PLAYER}.
'We have to put our faith in Daxamat now.'

'A hostile fleet approaches? My business with the Kindred can wait!
'There is coin to be made, ${PLAYER}!'
Temámir archers hold you at bay. You can fight no longer
At a gesture from the Golden Queen, the guards encircle you
Jajax has come with you to Dâr Laja to warn the Kindred of the Coins about the approaching danger.
Hármelak stands upon the dais in Dâr Laja.
Hármelak stares at you in disbelief, waiting for you to answer her question with a <rgb=#00FF00>yes</rgb>.
Only the Kindred of the Coins can command the river gate be closed. You and Jajax must convince Hármelak to issue the order.
You and Jajax stand alone against the guardsmen in Dâr Laja.
'If by our warning we save the city, the Kindred will surely seek to reward us for our actions today, ${PLAYER}. Let us hurry!'

'Your face is lined with worry, ${PLAYER}. What brings you with such urgency to Dâr Laja?'
You tell Hármelak that Nakási Wave-reaper sails a secret fleet armed with Narghâk cannons and crewed by Orcs of Mordor and soldiers of Ordâkh down the Ikorbân River. She frowns uncertainly.
'So it is a fight, then. Fine! There are not enough of them to best both Jajax and ${PLAYER}!'
Instancia: La Puerta del Río
Khôltekh has stepped through the line of Temámir archers to address you.
You and Jajax have done what you could. Now it must be up to others.
The haste of your errand permits no delay: the Kindred of the Coins must be warned of the approaching danger!

'Through our efforts, most of the ships were damaged and cannot sail... but not all! Balakhâd and Nakási will sail the remaining ships of the Song down the River Ikorbân, endangering all the lands through which it flows!
'Mount your steed, ${PLAYER}! The city of Umbar Baharbêl lies at the mouth of the river, and if you bring word of the approaching ships to the rulers of the city, they may be able to close the river gate before the Song of Waves and Wind passes the city! Speak to me if you will do this!'
'We will follow behind you as we can, ${PLAYER}, but you must ride with as much speed as you can! You must get to Umbar before the Song of Waves and Wind!'
'If this fleet is as dangerous as you say it is, the city is in grave danger!'
Chapter 18.1: Outrun the Wind, Outrun the Waves
The Song of Waves and Wind must not be permitted to endanger the lands of Middle-earth.

'What did you say? A secret fleet sails toward the city? And I was not informed?'
You tell Jajax that Nakási Wave-reaper and Balakhâd have taken control of the Song of Waves and Wind and equipped its ships with dangerous Narghâk weapons. If it is not kept from leaving the Ikorbân River, all of Middle-earth will be in danger.
'You need the Kindred of the Coins to close the river gate? You will want my help with this, ${PLAYER}. Let me know when you are ready for us to speak with them.'
'The Kindred of the Coins will listen to me, you will see. No one can refuse Jajax!'

'It is not much, Dax, but you can stay here as long as you need. I have lived here ever since Kinsman Belondor ordered my release from the gaol following his return from Ikorbân. Many of my fellows were freed as well. I know not what Belondor saw there, but I am grateful for it!
'You can stay here until you learn what happened to your brother. There has really been no word of him since he and ${PLAYER} went to Dâr Laja?'

'A hostile fleet approaches from the river? Can this be so?
'I will share these tidings throughout the city!'
'A fleet of ships manned by the Heirsworn approaches from the River Ikorbân? How can this be?'
'Are we... are we in danger?'

'I know you for a friend of the city, ${PLAYER}. If you say a hostile fleet approaches Umbar Baharbêl, then it must be so.
'We must arrange for the defence of the city! We must get everyone away from the river!'

'What is this I hear, ${PLAYER}? Tell me what I can do!'
You ask Daxamat to spread the word to the people of the city that a fleet of dangerous ships carrying Orcs and Ordâkhai soldiers approaches from Ikorbân.
'I will! You should find my brother Jajax at the forum of Bith Gabâr... he will know what to do!'
'I will arrange for the defence of the city!'
You can waste no time. Warn the folk at the Waterway Market!
At last some of the folk give you their attention

The guardsman would not listen. You should hurry to the Waterway Market and <rgb=#00FF00>beckon</rgb> for the folk by the pool to heed you.

'You must hurry on to Umbar, ${PLAYER}! Bring your warning to the guards at the gate, and I will follow behind you!'
'A hostile fleet sails toward us down the River Ikorbân? That is absurd! What proof have you of this?'
'You must hurry on to Umbar! Bring your warning to the guards at the gate, and I will follow behind you!'
'How foolish! How absurd!'

Schemes and Misadventures
Deliver Shâr Bârshud's message to Mizâdi in Kûr Anzar.
Deliver Shâr Bârshud's message to Mizâdi in Kûr Anzar
Speak with Nimasi when you are ready to go

'We must get inside that camp and get close to that main tent in the back. I am sure whoever is in charge will be in there. If we hope to save Surâsh and end these attacks, we need to know who these people are and what they are planning.
'We also must locate Surâsh, but we should only free her after we've scouted the enemy and found out all we can of their plans, as the noise and commotion may waylay any intelligence gathering.
'We must be stealthy as we move. There are too many of them for a frontal assault. Are you ready?'

'I cannot believe Nimasi turned on us. This is most troubling. Most troubling. And the danger to you was grave, I must be better about who I allow into the Subuzûri.'
Mizâdi appears to steel herself. A sudden coldness overtakes her face.
'I don't care how many soldiers the Hûl has proffered him. He has not yet felt the might of the Subuzûri.
'Very well. If it is a war he wants, then he shall have one.
'But I will not allow the people of Kûr Anzar to feel war's cold comforts once more. I will meet him in open battle. War is coming, ${PLAYER}. War is coming to Imhûlar.'
'Are you ready? Steel yourself, we are about to go into the lair of these monsters.'
Speak with Nimasi outside the camp when you are ready to go.

Relay Nimasi's gratitude to Mizâdi

'What an interesting story! This is a simple matter, indeed. Nothing that some skull-crushing can't fix and quickly, if I do say so myself.
'Were it up to me, and not my queen, I would accompany this scout south, find the blasted fools scattering their distasteful and ugly artistry hither and yon, and split them in twain with a good iron blade. I know Mizâdi prefers me here in Kûr Anzar, however, to assist with the rebuilding.
'Perhaps you can see to the skull-crushing this time, ${PLAYER}?'

'I should hope there will be no need for skull-crushing, Numûru's wishes notwithstanding.
'You were able to quickly find the missing scouts last time, so I believe you, ${PLAYER}, are the perfect one to go with Nimasi. Hopefully this conclusion is a happier one than that of the other scouts. Will you help Nimasi?
'If so, please, tell Nimasi you will go down to the south to investigate this disappearance.'

'Hashtal-gûr, favoured outsider. I would request an audience with my Shâra, though I know it not proper. The situation I find myself in is that dire.
'The scout who brought you news of a southern incursion not so long ago, Surâsh? She is one of the scouts with which I patrol. She has herself now vanished. We were supposed to meet at a certain hilltop two nights ago. In her place I found this strange banner. I believe it to be the same standard you found with her not long before. She told me the story.
'Would you ask the Shâra if she can spare some forces to investigate Surâsh's disappearance? We southern scouts are being picked off one by one like zizani. I fear the worst for Surâsh, and, if I'm honest, for myself.'

'So strange. This is indeed the same banner you and Surâsh brought me. Who could be doing this?
'I need to think on this for a moment. You should ask Numûru his feelings on the matter.'

'I knew our Shâra was both just and benevolent! Please thank her for me, and thank you, for your eloquence in relaying this need.
'I will meet you just outside of Zahûmakh, the marsh to the south. That's where I found the new standard, and should be where we start our investigation for her.
'I will ride out now, and meet you down there. Please thank the Shâra for me.'

'You are the one to be thanked, not I. You will be the one going into danger, so my gratitude is with you for that. As it has each time you have braved your skin for ours.
'As to Nimasi and Surâsh, I must look after my people, or what kind of Shâra am I?'
This is the same banner you saw before: a silver lion's head similar to Mizâdi's standard
Speak with the scout Nimasi in Kûr Anzar.

'It appears one of my scouts has a message for me near the western gate. Would you receive them and see to their message?

'Ambarûl has grain enough for all of Ekhamât. We never wanted your cursed land. Your soil is fit for nothing but blood and oaths. Your Mizâdi danced right to the tune we played for her.

'Please, give this message to the Shâra. There is word from Khûd Zagin. Amalíbi requests aid against a great many Ordâkhai excursions - we are being overrun!'

'Everything is so calm in this moment, I scarcely recognize it. These past few days have been a whirlwind. I have not had a chance to stop the winds and listen, to find peace.
'I would have words with Amalíbi. She said many things in that hall, and I agree with all of them. Many of the things I said I do not agree with, but such is passion. I have many mistakes for which I must atone. Would you accompany me to see her?'

'I hear her words, but I do not yet feel them. Perhaps in time I will.
'Thank you, friend. Your presence has been a constant comfort, and one for which I am quite grateful.'
'Let us go then, to Amalíbi's encampment, to mend what wounds we can.'

'Thank you. I can dress the wound myself. It's the little things that make the days a bit more manageable, don't you think?'

'Oho, you've come to help us, have you? Aid us in our time of need? Well I have great need of you then, friend. Great need.
'The Umûn says I can't have any Khôrob. I know, it is a tragedy. Usually I'd just swipe it as soon as her back was turned, but with this bum leg, it makes any petty thievery a terrible bother. She thinks it makes for bad soldiers. I say it makes for the best soldiers. Or at least the happiest.
'What do you say? Can you make a bottle of Khôrob appear in these old hands?'

'You're helping those in the camp? That is very nice of you. I don't need much, I have a warm bedroll and enough bread to get by.
'Maybe I could tell you my story? These words in my head seem to weigh heavily on me, pressing me down. Unless you don't want to hear it?'

'I meant what I said. I will see these people restored to their homes. I will see them made whole.'
Mizâdi pauses, and her breath becomes hushed.
'I swear it.'

'Ah, it's good of you to ask. It's not much, but these bandages have frayed, and they are more dirt than cloth at the moment.
'Would you see if there are any fresh ones among the quartermaster's things? Nothing worse for the spirit than soggy dressings.'

'A hungry army is half-defeated before they take the battlefield. There is plenty of food in the hills of Ambarûl, but with most of the able-bodied taking up arms to defend her, there are few hands left to pick and harvest the fruits of the soil.
'Would you go to the local orchard and help the farmers there gather grain and fruit to feed our army? Every bit helps to keep morale high and minds sharp, ${PLAYER}.'

'Ah, yes I could use the help, much as it shames me to say it. These legs have borne strides enough for three men. I have been blessed to work this land for many years, but now the years feel much heavier on my bones than they once did. I am glad for the aid.
'You can start by gathering fruit from the orchard. Beware of the zizani - every year they grow fiercer and seemingly larger. Anything you can do to reduce their number would be greatly appreciated. After that there is some grain that is ready for harvesting in the northern field.'

'Quickly, you must warn Amalíbi in Ghalbûru and Girhâzi in Iridír. I have had some words with each and both are hearty and passionate fighters who want what is best for Shagâna.

'Oh now the Shâra will deign to meet with me? Now that my soldiers are bloodied, dead, scattered to the winds and lost in the Khûd? Where was this Shâra when I sent out my request for aid?

'If we can defeat him, it should cause his army to scatter to the winds. We could have peace in Shagâna, friend, real peace for the first time in a very long time.

'You want shields? Everybody wants shields. Sârgud is so popular all of the sudden.
