'Word spreads through the city that a hostile fleet approaches on the Ikorbân River, and that has been imprisoned for trying to stop it. Can this be true?
'My wife Khâsha and I name a friend. Any who seek to harm ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} must answer to us! My deadliest days are behind me, but I have mates enough throughout the Shield Isles and the Cape to make things difficult for the Kindred of the Coins if they truly have betrayed the city, as the whispering suggests.
'If the word of the advance scouts can be trusted, it seems likely: they say you can hear Orkish voices from at least one of the approaching ships.'

'Rumours spread like wildfire throughout the Lower Ward. Is it true that has been imprisoned by the Kindred of the Coins? I can think of no reason for ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} to languish in the gaol, especially if ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} sought to warn us about this approaching danger! Why would the Kindred support this attack?
'My husband owes a great deal to Tumúldo Fierce-water, who convinced him not to join Balakhôr during the war... but that was a different Kindred, and people say Tumúldo is slain.
'People also say you and your brother are 's close companions, Daxamat. Tell us what we must do to help, and we will do it!'

'The people turn to you for guidance, Dax!'
You stammer to Itûr that you don't know what to do. He rests an assuring hand on your shoulder.
'Ask yourself what ${PLAYER} and Jajax would do, if they were here.'

'Yes! That is exactly right, Dax!
'Today we begin to fight against those who would betray us! For ${PLAYER}, and for Jajax!'

'You are Daxamat, the brother of Jajax? I have been looking for you! I have tidings of him you should hear. I spoke to many people hoping to find you, but at last a rumour-monger directed me to this place. Now hear what I have seen!
'I was in Dâr Laja when your brother and my friend petitioned the Kindred of the Coins to close shut the river gate and prevent the approaching fleet from passing the city. Almost did I leave, but curiosity stayed my feet, and I watched from afar as they were seized by the guards! They were brought to the gaol, and are now captives of Hármelak... even Khôltekh has sided with her! I can think of no just reason for him to do this!
'I fear the Kindred of the Coins has betrayed the city. Even now I hesitate to return to the streets; they may keep watch for any who witnessed their duplicity! proved a friend to many of us in the city... how can they justify imprisoning ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} after such monumental deeds on behalf of Umbari and Temámir alike?'

'You need a way to pass unseen from this refuge without being seen by spies loyal to the Kindred of the Coins? I would not call this day fortunate... but perhaps in this matter alone I have some good fortune to share.
'Pass through the door behind me and take the stairs down to the cellar. You will see what I mean.'
'I fear the Kindred of the Coins has betrayed the city. Even now I hesitate to return to the streets; they may keep watch for any who witnessed their betrayal!'
'Pass through the door behind me and take the stairs down to the cellar. You will see what I mean.'

'Ah, I see what your friend has in mind. I know a waterway to Umbar-môkh when I see one. With this I can enter and leave the refuge without detection by spies loyal to Hármelak.'
Birûk shakes his fists in the air.
'I still cannot believe Khôltekh would endanger the city in this way! I have never known to lie, and ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} was most clear that a hostile fleet sails down the river toward us!
'I may be able to contact someone who can get a message to the prisoners. I will return and let you know if I succeed.'
'I may be able to contact someone who can get a message to the prisoners. I will return and let you know.'

'It will not be as you say. The people of the city will know why I could not close the river gate. If the Song of Waves and Wind could not leave the River Ikorbân, Nakási would have turned the Narghâk cannons upon Umbar Baharbêl! Should we have sacrificed our own city for the sake of Gondor?'
You ask Hármelak if she truly believes that Nakási or Balakhâd would have destroyed their own city, and she waves a dismissive hand.
'You believe the people of the city share your uncertainty, ${PLAYER}.'

'I have a message for you from one of the Temámir. He says \qThe work continues. We need many hands to mine the Abâshal, and will forge new medallions from it. Remain alert for its shine, and stay safe: the mine is treacherous, but there will be a light in the darkness.'
The girl turns to go, but she hesitates. She faces you again, and you try to remember where you have before heard this voice.
'We watched as the ships passed the city. One galley tried to block the way to open water, and it was sunk. The terrible smoke of the cannons smelled foul. We saw Orcs on the deck of one of the ships. They cheered as the ship of Umbar burned; the water could not quench the blue flames.'

You never saw her face before now, but it was in Umbar-môkh that you spoke to Tephísa. She is one of the Terâsi, the forgotten children who make their way through hidden paths beneath the city. It must have been the Temámir Birûk who gave her this message to bring to you and Jajax.
Tephísa studies your face closely.
'I watched the flames destroy my home once, stranger. They were orange and red then, the embers lit by servants of Barkhûsh, but a fire is a fire. Those ships will set ablaze the homes of Gondor, but they will return, and when they return the conflagration will spread to the homes of Umbar.
'I can help you escape, but I have a price.'

You tell Jajax that Hármelak is lying.
'Aye,' he agrees. 'She lied before, and she lies again.'

'The hidden harbour is just ahead. We must cut through these foes if we are to reach Tatháta's ship!'

'Ah, this is more like it. I have always been more at home aboard a ship, even if that ship carries me to dangerous battle in defence of Gondor, of all places! At least the legend of Jajax will continue to grow!
'We will leave the uprising against Hármelak and Khôltekh in Daxamat's capable hands. Ha! Capable? There is a first time for everything, I suppose.
'I hope we are not making a grave mistake, ${PLAYER}!'

'Sirgon has been upon my mind these last few hours, ${PLAYER}. What would he say to know that now I sail to his home of Gondor in a desperate bid to defend it from destruction?
'Ah, I know the answer. He would smile and clap me upon the back, and say he would do the same for my own home. What do Gondor and Umbar have in common? Sons and daughters who would die for them, against any threatening danger.'

'I am sad, ${PLAYER}.'
You ask Rothog why he is sad, and he grumbles something you cannot hear. When you ask him to repeat it, he heaves a heavy sigh.
'I did not think to bring Húrshauk with me when we came to rescue you from the gaol, and Tatháta says there is no time for me to go get him. Now he must stay behind in the city instead of joining the battle in Gondor.
'He will miss all of the fighting! Perhaps one of the members of Ilma-ghôli will bring him to Dâr Laja to slay Hármelak or Khôltekh? He would like that. Oh, I hope they do!'

'Sotóka is a fast ship, but the Song departed many hours before us. We may be too late to prevent Nakási from completing her mission.
'She is driven by vengeance, ${PLAYER}: not just for the death of Tumúldo, but for every injury and injustice she has suffered during her years of life. Each of these wounds has fed her hatred, and now she has been blinded by her desire for vengeance.'
Tatháta smiles grimly, a most rare sight indeed.
'That is the meaning of \qSotóka,\q ${PLAYER}: Vengeance. Is it chance or plan that speeds us in pursuit of Nakási aboard a ship of vengeance? I cannot say. The world is a curious place.'

'The Kindred of the Coins is dead, ${PLAYER}. It was created to protect the people of the city, not to burn them alive as did the Church of Barkhûsh. If the Umbari do not slay Hármelak and Khôltekh for their betrayal, I will do it myself.
'Below the city I witnessed Belondor and Rothog travelling with great speed, and pursued them. Had they supported Hármelak's treachery they would be dead already, but it seems these two have not abandoned their wits.
'We are to bring you by paths beneath the city to the hideout where the uprising began. Are you ready?'
You hesitate. Images of thatched Gondorian cottages wreathed by blue flame flash before your eyes, followed by homes in the Umbari style suffering the same fate. You remember a small voice asking you to destroy the ships and their masters.

'What is the cause for this delay, ${PLAYER}? The city above is a tinder-box ready to catch fire at the slightest spark, and Ilma-ghôli cannot now be stopped.'
You tell Belondor that you fear for the people of Gondor, unaware of the deadly danger that sails toward them, and for the people of Umbar. He nods.
'It had occurred to me that Nakási will not give up this fleet when her business in Gondor is completed,' he replies.
'She will return with it to Umbar Baharbêl, and any passing whim will be enforced by cannon and with Hungry Fire.'

'My ship Sotóka is moored in a hidden harbour not far from here, ${PLAYER}, and none can match her speed when her sails are full.'
You ask Tatháta if she would be willing to pursue the Song of Waves and Wind to Gondor, despite the danger, and she stares at you seriously.
'On my last voyage with Nakási, we sailed around the coast of Outer Gondor. Our purpose was to prove to the new King of Gondor that despite the defeat of Umbar in the war, the Kindred of the Coins was not without strength. Umbar would not be subservient; Umbar must be treated as a powerful neighbour, worthy of respect.
'But then Tumúldo was slain, and the light in Nakási's eyes changed. Hatred drove her. We encountered the grove of a tree-tender on the cape of Anfalas. Later I learned from Nestinanessornë that his name, at least in the tongue used by Elves and Men, was Leafshade. Nakási threatened to burn his grove as a message to Gondor, and I told her I wanted no part of it... but had Nestinanessornë not surrendered to her I know she would have burned that grove with fire and torches, and all of Gondor beside.
'Now she possesses the ability to do just that, ${PLAYER}. If my ship Sotóka can stop her, I cannot remain idly by and claim to have not aided her. For Leafshade, if not for any others, my ship is yours. Agents of Khôltekh and the Heirsworn stand between you and the hidden harbour. I hope you are ready.'

'The Song of Waves and Wind passing so near to the city has caused our numbers to grow. The people cannot disbelieve the evidence of their own eyes: that the Kindred allowed these ships to sink an Umbari galley. They have allied with Orcs, and by so doing are no better than those vile creatures!

'None would mistake me for one of the Corsairs of legend; my prowess is not in combat or swordplay. I spent many weeks in the gaol when the nobleman I thought to rob of his purse proved more vigilant than I expected, so I would not recommend you assign me tasks of thievery!'
Itûr laughs suddenly.
'There is one thing I can help you steal, Dax. Together we will steal the hearts of the people, right from under the noses of the Kindred! Folk have already come here searching for someone to lead them, and more are sure to come. We are going to need a place where we can make our plans.

'Folk have already come here searching for someone to lead them, and more are sure to come. We are going to need a place where we can make our plans. Maybe we should set up the room on the right so we can accommodate our growing numbers.'

'This is a start, but there is more to be done. The Kindred of the Coins has two places where their leadership can feel safe: within the Meeting-hall of Dâr Laja, and within the strong walls of the Citadel of the Winds. As our numbers grow, we will need to find some way of threatening these bastions, making the Kindred question its safety and the sources of its power.
'There is something else, too.'

'Hármelak and Khôltekh have imprisoned two of our most significant figures, Dax. The city will not forgive this outrage, and as word of it spreads, the dominion of the Kindred must begin to weaken. Did they underestimate how beloved ${PLAYER} has become to the people of Umbar Baharbêl? Did they underestimate the popularity of your brother Jajax?
'I think these were mistakes, Dax. But now we must ask ourselves an important question. For how long will the Kindred keep Jajax and ${PLAYER} in captivity? Are they still alive, and if they are, for how long will they remain so?'

'You are Daxamat, yes? The brother of Jajax? These men follow your command?'
Belondor looks you up and down, and releases his hand from the hilt of his sword.
'I should have known something was amiss, Daxamat. Hármelak's sudden interest in the Thardúth should have raised my suspicion, for always has she dismissed the servants of Morgoth we faced in Urash Dâr as less of a threat to Umbar than others. To ask Rothog and I to travel to Damarzâg, to learn if they have any presence there... it seems an obvious ruse, now, a means of keeping two members of the Kindred from interfering with her plans. When we departed I thought only that at last she was taking seriously the danger.
'But now we have returned, and we must decide what can be done. Where is ? We should ask ${PLAYER:her[f]|him} for ${PLAYER:her[f]|his} thoughts.'

'Rûmina and I can move unnoticed through the Lower Ward with great speed... until the moment we want to be seen, and to be heard. I am confident we can spread the news of Hármelak's betrayal of the city, and that Khôltekh may be aiding her. It will not be difficult: few of the Umbari failed to see the enemy ships as they passed the city, and it was apparent to all that their Corsair crews had joined hands with soldiers of Ordâkh and Orcs of Mordor. It is an outrage and a mockery!
'I understand there is a plan in motion to free your brother and ${PLAYER} from captivity? Has there yet been any word?'

'I bring good news from Umbar-môkh, Daxamat.
'My contact has spoken with . ${PLAYER:She[f]|He} and Jajax are being held within the Fleetfast gaol, and the Terâsi girl is willing to show us a secret way inside. She seemed very insistent that if she performs this task for us, we will see that the enemy fleet is destroyed. I know not if that is within our power... but I told her we would consider it.
'We need and Jajax freed. We can consider nothing until that happens, am I right?'
'One more thing! I understand there is a plan in motion to free your brother and ${PLAYER} from captivity? Has there yet been any word?'
'Something has happened upstairs! Are we discovered?'

'For now I relent. If you give me a reason to fight, I will not again lower my khopeshes until the battle is done!
'Belondor and I were away from the city, visiting the arid hills of Damarzâg and looking for evidence of the Thardúth. We found none, but when we returned to Umbar Baharbêl the shouting of its people could be mistaken by no one. Someone had allowed a fleet of Mordor and Ordâkh to pass by the city, and as it sailed into the Bay it turned its cannons upon Umbari ships! Even now the wreck of an Umbari galley smoulders with the blue flames of the Hungry Fire!
'Some members of my Kindred seem to have allied with this fleet, but only one arranged for me and Belondor to be away from the city when it arrived. This was the work of Hármelak! She knew this fleet was on its way, and she wanted to ensure Rothog did not stop it!'
You heave a sigh of relief as they lower their weapons

You tell Nakûr he should rest, for he will be of little use to Ilma-ghôli, the rising tide of rebellion, if he falls down from exhaustion. He smiles gratefully.

'You have given these folk their orders, Daxamat. What now is your role to play?'
You tell Belondor that you are ready to free your brother Jajax and the hero ${PLAYER} from the Fleetfast gaol, but before you can say anything else, he shakes his head.
'I think not, Daxamat. That is a dangerous undertaking. I cannot say how it has happened, but you have somehow become the leader of this rising tide, this Ilma-ghôli. Without you to focus these varied and disparate fighters, I think this uprising is snuffed out like a torch doused in sea-water. You must remain here at this refuge in order to coordinate the efforts of Ilma-ghôli.
'The rescue of ${PLAYER} and your brother must be left to others.'

'Rothog and I will lead this rescue mission. ${PLAYER} and Jajax are imprisoned by those we counted allies, even friends. The two of us must set this right.
'I will speak with the Temámir about this secret entrance he has discovered. Were it not now of use, I would rue its very existence! But it seems such a way into the gaol will now help us bring our friends to freedom, and about that I will not complain.
'Regret not that you do not accompany us! There will be danger enough for you here, Daxamat. All of the city will soon come alive with anger, and you must be ready to guide its furious voice!'
'The Harlond burns. We have arrived too late.'
The assembled fighters of Ilma-ghôli listen to your directives
Your gathered allies await their orders in the planning room to the right of the entrance to the refuge.
Your gathered allies await their orders in the planning room to the right of the entrance to the refuge.

'Imprisoned? We will need to do something about that.
'Something else troubles me. Some of the people with whom I spoke claim that Nakási commands the fleet, and she has joined hands with Balakhâd, the son of Balakhôr; their ships are crewed with Heirsworn Corsairs, Orcs of Mordor, and Ordâkhai soldiers alike. If this is true, fully half of the Kindred of the Coins have changed their loyalties: Nakási, Hármelak, and Khôltekh can no longer be trusted to lead.
'Where is Tatháta in all this? She has always been more solitary than the rest, but if she sides with the betrayers it will be difficult for Rothog and I to convince the city that our position is just. That way is certain to lead to bloodshed. I do not fear it! I would prefer not to slay my fellows if it might be avoided, but we need to remove the blight from the Kindred of the Coins in order to cleanse it, one way or another.
'But you are the leader of this band of fighters, Daxamat. Consider all that must be done, and give your people their commands. The uprising in Umbar begins now!'
'But you are the leader of this band of fighters, Daxamat. Consider all that must be done, and give your people their commands. The uprising in Umbar begins now!'

'Rûmina and I have many contacts within the Sail-haven and the Lower Ward. We will spread the news of Hármelak's betrayal, and rally the Umbari to march upon Dâr Laja. Corsairs and mariners, vendors and caravan drivers, even the troublemakers and brigands of the Gut... all these folk have reason to overthrow the rulers who think to sell us to Mordor or to Ordâkh!
'Even the Corsair Jeduth may join us in this. He has retired from the privateering trade, but he will see the rightness of Ilma-ghôli's cause!'

'I know of a place where many weapons are stored, Dax: beneath the Dahâl Huliz, in Kamrabezûr, are racks and racks of weapons for use in the arena. But that is not all we can take from there. The gladiators revere Rothog as both a great warrior and a leader of the city. If they are shown he sides with us to overthrow the villains who betray Umbar Baharbêl, we will have obtained not just weapons, but fighters to wield them as well.
'We must not underestimate the reputation of Rothog the Storm! The prospect of facing him in single combat was enough to keep me safely and content in the gaol. I knew not that Kinsman Belondor would free me from captivity without fighting only days later, but I did know not to face Rothog on the blood-sands for my freedom!
'But today I will fight for freedom from the traitors who pretend to speak for Umbar... but I fight beside the Storm, and not against him!'

'There is no need to draw stones, as is the custom among my people in Khabârkhad; I know what duty is set before me.
'First I will go to Mekab-kuphâr with this unpleasant news: Khôltekh has jeopardized the lives, safety, and wealth of the Temámir people. I will bring those of my fellows who agree with this position to the Shoreward Stone, where we will seek an audience with Inîk Jewel-brow, the Hall-father. One way or another, Khôltekh will be removed from power for his part in this calamity.
'While I do this, someone else must make use of the secret entrance into the Fleetfast gaol in order to free your brother and ${PLAYER}.'

The Hidden Fortress

'Bârshud has fled, but our work is not yet finished. The remainder of the Ekhamâti Umûni and their Ordâkhai forces are holed up inside the hidden fortress before us.
'Dun Shûma, built by an ancient Shâr of Nísaka, is said to hold many of our ancestral treasures. I suspect there is one treasure in particular that Bârshud seeks: the lost crown of Aragín the Queller. Holding such a thing would give his claim to the throne of Hamât legitimacy. We must prevent Ekhamât from seizing it, at all costs.'

'We are victorious. I now hold the Lion-crown of Aragín the Queller, and must make official my claim to the throne of Hamât. This, I fear, is just the beginning of a long campaign.
'That sorcerer has given us a parting gift, a secret he expected us to take to our graves: Ordâkh is manipulating Ekhamât, puppeteering Bârshud to fight their war for them. The new Hul must be eager to regain control of all Shagâna, and will use unwitting vassals to do so. Even if Bârshud’s claim over Hamât is defeated, my people will not be truly safe until the threat of Ordâkh is eliminated for good.
'You have been by my side through all of this, ${PLAYER}. For now, I have little to offer but my sincerest thanks, but once this war is finally won, the Kingdom of Hamât will forever be in your debt.'

'Cúridwan passed north-east in the direction of Laivárth. If you head that way too, might I trouble you to defeat some of the Orcs that lurk beside the path? They seem untroubled by the noisome fumes that now fill the air, and it is our burden to thin their numbers before they become emboldened. They have fashioned two camps near here, Mauthark and Mokh Grazádh, and if you defeat these creatures you will be aiding both the Kintai and your friend Cúridwan.'
'Your friend Cúridwan may be at the grove of Laivárth, to the north-east. You should look for her there.'

'The fungal corruption has begun to work on this grove as well, despite the efforts of its tenders to halt its spread. See the mark of the blight there, and there? My heart is heavy, and I have only just arrived! Imagine how it must feel to live in this wood, and watch the corruption advance with the passage of the hours, and of the days!'

'Your friend speaks the truth: it is difficult to watch the blight consume our land, twisting the trees in horrible mockery of their once-healthy forms. Some among my people believe the fungal contagion spews from a single entity: Sívigush, the Earth-terror; others believe the blight is itself alive, and Sívigush is in fact an evil composed of every tendril, mushroom, and spore released into the foetid air of Adagím.
'I know not what I believe. If you are willing to take this trowel and bring back a sample from several locations where the rot has taken hold, perhaps we can learn something that will be of use. I will speak with your friend while you conduct this study on my behalf, and help the two of you as I can.
'The rot is particularly bad to the north-east, north-west, and west of Laivárth.'

'If Cúridwan has gone ahead into Adagím, that is where our road must lead. But it is the foolhardy traveller who passes into an unfamiliar land without knowledge; we must not be unprepared.
'What can Thórvilon tell us of the woods into which we must go?'

'What can I tell you about Adagím that will not pain me? Very little, my friend. So much of the Emerald Wood has been tainted by blight and corruption that the beautiful forest of my youth seems somehow unreal. When the Ordâkhai came north, something they brought with them damaged the soil. The blight that slew the trees of Imhûlar began first in Adagím, taking the form of a terrible fungal rot. Many groves of my people were abandoned, until only Sul Madásh remained unspoiled.
'The Adagím of today is a nightmarish, boggy wilderness, despite the efforts of the Kintai. Some of us fled westward to Vartúlin, or to Shonith beside the Khûd, but I fear it is only a matter of time before the blight consumes every tree that once grew within the Emerald Wood of Nisigím.
'Perhaps Inkanûsh and Cúridwan together will be able to fight it, ${PLAYER}. I hope it is so! Hurry on to speak with Athgai at the border with Adagím, and hasten the meeting of these two wise ones!'
'It is the foolhardy traveller who passes into an unfamiliar land without knowledge; we must not be unprepared. What can Thórvilon tell us of the woods into which we must go?'

'Wait a moment, newcomers. Few come this way, save the Orcs, and it is my duty to keep watch for any who stray this far into the wood. What business have you in Adagím?'

'The road to discovery is often slow and riddled with setbacks. Such is the way of things.
'Your friend Glorfindel spoke to me of your search for Cúridwan. She has likely gone on ahead to Sul Madásh, largest of the Kinta groves within the Emerald Wood. But wait!
'Before you come to Sul Madásh, you should spend a moment at Tûl Ama, the Hill of the Mother. Look for it to the south-east, for it is on your way. The Old Mother, Amûma in my tongue, is unmistakable. You will know her at once, and Cúridwan is like to have stopped there herself.
'Farewell, my new friends.'

'Before you come to Sul Madásh, you should spend a moment at Tûl Ama, the Hill of the Mother. Look for it to the south-east, for it is on your way. The Old Mother, Amûma in my tongue, is unmistakable. You will know her at once, and Cúridwan is like to have stopped there herself.'

'I knew what to expect and still the sorrow cuts me deeply, ${PLAYER}. This great mother-tree of the Emerald Wood stood unharmed for untold years, but now the blight that savages Adagím works its evil even upon her. See the blood-red sap she weeps as she mourns!
'Can the Ordâkhai really have wrought this? The Kintai with whom we have spoken seem to believe this corruption began when that Empire crossed north... but how could they have caused such evil as this? Does it not seem beyond their capability, if not beyond their cruel intent?'

'For years I have pondered that question, friends of the Kintai, but no solution has come to me. I cannot conceive of such a thing: who would willingly inflict such harm upon this land, or upon Amûma and her children? I have long been the warden of this grove. Tending to her in this state has left me weak and sorrowful.'
Irsinith sighs heavily, and you are struck by the notion that she seems very much alike to the mother-tree she guards. You ask if there is anything you and Glorfindel might do to lighten her burden.

'Ulishár once took great joy in wandering far across the lands of Shagâna, west to the shores of Umbar and south to the fringe of the great desert of Gûl Sakhâsha. He would come back with tales of his adventures, much like the ones I believe you have had!
'Several years ago, he was captured by soldiers of Ordâkh. They imprisoned him in one of their cities, where he was made to labour. Ever since he returned, he has been unwilling to leave the bounds of Sul Madásh.
'Now I have told you all, and I ask that you please speak not of this to Ulishár. Come, our destination lies to the south-west: the Elderwell. I remember Ulishár used to visit this place with Cúridwan, in happier times.'
'Come, our destination lies to the south-west: the Elderwell. I remember Ulishár used to visit this place with Cúridwan, in happier times.'

'I had hoped my salve could put an end to the Lâg Dávrit, the Pale Blight, but alas! It is not enough. I must strengthen my salve, and for that I need to learn more.
'I spied crocodiles to the north-west as I climbed to this place. Collect their teeth and some samples of the blight near which they live, and bring them to me for study. My mind is awhirl with the possibility that this corruption can be beaten and its harm undone.'

'But how can this be?'
The Wizard's brow furrows.
'It is true that some things were left unknown to me by the Powers that sent me to Middle-earth, that I might best accomplish my purpose... but the number of my Order is five. Far have I travelled across Middle-earth to oppose the evils of Sauron and his servants, and Radagast too has played his part. Saruman was the highest of my Order, until he succumbed, but even in that I see the role Saruman played in the defeat of Sauron.
'Two others of the five travelled east into distant lands, and their fate is unknown to me. They serve the Powers, as I do. I am certain of it.'

'The number of Wizards sent to the northern lands may have been five, but I assure you these southern lands are vast. Do you think the Shoghór nomads would welcome you among them in the body you now wear? The Ghursâti, the \qPowers,\q as you name them, they sent their servants in form appropriate to the people they sought to aid. How might \qthe Golden Maiden\q or \qthe Sorceress in Green\q be received in the cold northern lands, I wonder?
'The Wizards of the northern line and the Wizards of the southern line must be different, or they must each fail in their purposes. In this I see the wisdom of the Powers that gave to us our missions, separate though shared they may be.
'It is not for an individual to see the entire breadth of the tapestry. That is reserved for those who sent us, is it not?'

'Earlier I was amused because Cúridwan reminded me of Inkanûsh... but I did not expect such similarities as these!'

'Thórvilon is dear to me, as are all of the Kintai. The Pale Blight is itself a symptom only, and not the source of the evil. A greater corruption emerged in Adagím, moving throughout the Emerald Wood, and my salves have proven less effective at dealing with this root cause of the blight.
'But I will not give up.'

'Ísman rules above them all, the Sky-master. In his lordly form he observed the comings and goings of the Shoghór as they crossed the great desert; it was in feminine aspect that Ísman lit the stars to show them the way.
'Jarângar the Water-friend brings healing and wards away the much-feared drought, and Shin-samêt the All-Shaper fashions the plants that grow beside the rivers and the animals that drink from the oases.
'Zangûr the Walker of the Wilds knows all the paths of the mountains and valleys, as well as the wild flowers of the hillside and the secrets of the blossoming forests.
'Bâkhlas the Doom-hand is feared and respected by the Shoghór nomads, for the domain of Bâkhlas is death. Better-loved are Arâmkal the Soothing Word, who brings rest and dreams to the Shoghór, as well as Garândi the Swift One, who endures all hardship to emerge triumphant and laughing at the end of suffering.
'The seven Ghursâti who gave me my purpose and sent me to aid the people of this land are opposed by the demonic figure Makhâl, but I will not speak of him. The Shoghór speak his name only in whispers, and then unwillingly.'

'Perhaps I am being foolish, but I spoke to my brother of this choice. I spoke of something I never considered before today, something I do not believe myself. Can such a land of peace and beauty truly exist beyond death? And why would such a place be open to my people, who were unwilling to follow Taknûn the Hunter to it when he sought to bring us there so many centuries before?
'Is it not better to remain in the land with which you are familiar, even if your memories fade and all that remains is the anger and disappointment of the Väiri? For all of my life I have been told this is the way of my people. I do not know what to think, ${PLAYER}.'

'On this subject my lips are sealed, ${PLAYER}. Ulishár and Baharúd lived their lives among the Kintai, and I will not speak against the traditions of their people.
'And yet in my heart I feel it is wrong to say \qtheir\q people. Perhaps they are truly \qmy\q people after all, though long divided by time and tradition.'
'For all of my life I have been told this is the way of my people. I know not what to think.'

'Never before have I sought to interfere with the traditions of the Kintai. What has happened to work this change in me, ${PLAYER}?
'I ask despite knowing the answer. It is the blight that holds Adagím in its grip that causes me to speak these words aloud! Rarely did I speak with Baharúd beyond the exchange of simple greetings and well-wishing, but some years ago his brother Ulishár was dear to me. It grieves me to see Ulishár's sorrow that his brother's spirit must remain trapped within blighted Adagím, when I know it might be otherwise.
'If the Sorceress in Green here remained, she might already have restored the Emerald Wood! But of her I have received no word.'
'The choice lies with Baharúd.'

'This is what I have been seeking, ${PLAYER}.'

'I must find the Väiri that was once Silirtas. I must tell her that the westward way to the Undying Lands is open to her. She is not doomed to the endless unlife of a wandering, rageful spirit, but can choose to accept the fate of the Eldar and pass into the Blessed Realm!
'This is my purpose for coming to this place, ${PLAYER}. I know it. I must bring these tidings to Silirtas, no matter how difficult or dangerous that task may be.'
'If the Sorceress in Green here remained, she might already have restored the Emerald Wood! But of her I have received no word.'

'Set aside these doubts, Ulishár, if you can. I know such words come more easily to the speaker than to he who hears them! And yet I ask you to heed them all the same, for I have cause to believe what Cúridwan has spoken today.
'Many of the Elven-wise dwell in the Blessed Realm beyond the circles of the world; they return not to Middle-earth. In the Undying Lands all weariness falls away, and there the warmth of the sunrise banishes all earthly concerns: pain, fear, and doubt have no hold upon that place, and those who dwell within.
'It is natural to fear that which you have not seen, Ulishár. But I believe Cúridwan has spoken true: the Eldar and the Kintai were fashioned as a single people, no matter the separate roads down which they walked afterward. Your people are a part of Elvendom, as is Glorfindel and these others. I believe the Kintai could share their fate, if they desired it.'
'Could one of the Kintai be welcomed in that distant place that lies beyond death?'

'I know not what your brother would choose for himself, Ulishár. None but Baharúd can know if he would choose to remain in this land he loved or if he would accept the fate given to Elvendom at its creation.
'We must all mourn him in our own way, but if you sing or speak of this choice, it may be he will hear you. The long traditions of the Kintai may have hidden this possibility from him, but they could not have taken it from him entirely.'
'It is natural to fear that which you have not seen, Ulishár. But I believe Cúridwan has spoken true.'

'Even if that were so...'
Ulishár stares sadly at the body of his brother Baharúd.
'Could one of the Kintai be welcomed in that distant place that lies beyond death? Or would he be considered a stranger and turned aside?

'This is my purpose for coming to this place, ${PLAYER}. I know it. I must bring these tidings to Silirtas, no matter how difficult or dangerous that task may be.'

The fire-eater Zurûsh, the twins Dârjo and Orukhíl... no word has come back of Khazín or Urûnam, but Imalêkh fears they must also have died in battle. She was wounded during the retreat before the mighty city and saw them no more.
'But the tidings are not all sad. Zimêlkha was held in reserve at the river-city and saw no fighting; her soldiers were driven south as Gondor advanced. And a fortunate star must shine upon Mashkânu, for Satagêra tells me he was wounded in the forest early during the fighting, and was not made to march upon Minas Tirith.
'I mourn for the friends who were so kind to me, ${PLAYER}, and I honour their memory! Despite this sorrow, my heart fills to once again see those of Têrkar's Travellers who remain to bring joy to the folk of Shagâna!'

'I am Satagêra, the widow of Têrkar, and I am the playwright of this company of travelling players. I am pleased to meet any friend of Ulishár, for the Kinta is dear to us all, as he was to my husband. It was Têrkar's Travellers that smuggled him from the captivity of Ordâkh before most of our company were sent to war, did he tell you that?'
Satagêra smiles fondly.
'\qOne last act of defiance,\q my Têrkar called it. I am glad we did as he bade, for Ulishár's treatment in that city was hard. I think he would not have survived among the Ordâkhai for many more months.
'I invite you to speak with the others of my company. A cloud hangs over us this day, but do not let it trouble you. It is a private matter, and one we can handle ourselves.'

'I mourn for the friends who were so kind to me, ${PLAYER}, and I honour their memory! Despite this sorrow, my heart fills to once again see those of Têrkar's Travellers who remain to bring joy to the folk of Shagâna!'

'I cannot...' he weeps, his body seized by tremendous shuddering cries as tears stream down his face.
'Friend of Ulishár... how can one such as you... befriend this monster? This is no man... he is a creature of death! I swore to slay him, if that could be in my power... but...'
Mashkânu struggles to speak through wracking sobs.
'I was pierced by an arrow in the side, loosed from in hiding by green-garbed men in the northern forest. Others of my company marched on the great city, and fell during the fighting, but I retreated with others of the wounded to Mordor. From the shadow of the Black Gate I witnessed as the armies of the West approached, and I saw the fighting's end! So it was I witnessed the arrival of this man you defend, and heard his name spoken aloud by the Men of Gondor. \qMithrandir,\q they called him, and even from so far away I knew him for a Wizard.'
Mashkânu's bloodshot eyes flare with anger and with fear.
'I watched as the Wizard Mithrandir threw his arms into the air, and the very earth rocked beneath his feet! \qThe hour of doom!\q I heard him command over the tumult. In answer to his spell, the mighty towers and rampart of the Black Gate crumbled into dust! Wherever he looked, death came to his enemies, and those that could not escape perished! I fled... but still I can hear the terrible voice of the Wizard and the death he caused!
'I swore to slay him, if ever I could... but now my sword-arm freezes... and I am unable to carry out my vow!'

'You are one of the theatre players who worked to free Ulishár from captivity when he was held by the Ordâkhai? I know you from the recent performance, and from the stories he has told to us of your company. Your name is Mashkânu, wardrobe-master of Têrkar's Travellers? But no one is one thing alone; you were a soldier pressed into service, forced to fight for Sauron against the Host of the West through threat or falsehood.
'You have been deceived again, Mashkânu, this time by your own eyes. It was no spell of mine that brought low the Black Gate or the Towers of the Teeth on the edge of Mordor. A great weapon of Sauron's was unmade, and its undoing heralded the destruction of all he had wrought, despite his terrible power.
'Some who had been held spell-enslaved by the Dark Lord of Mordor threw themselves into pits or fought desperate last stands, but many were of like kind as you, Mashkânu: held in thrall not by enchantment but by the fear of cruel commanders from Ordâkh and their tales of horrible monsters from Gondor and the North. Know now the truth, my friend, and be healed, if such a thing can be possible.'
'I swore to slay him, if ever I could... but I am unable to carry out my vow!'

'Be healed? I can never be healed, though my wounds have closed and I once again speak the words Satagêra has given to me, seeking applause and coin.
'But so many of my friends returned not from the northern forest, or the fields outside the great city, or the Black Gate of Mordor. We were told that gate could never fall, but fall it did, and the vast armies of Barkhûsh and Ordâkh with it!'
Mashkânu wipes his eyes.
'When I beheld the Wizard Mithrandir earlier this day and learned he answered to the name Inkanûsh, I could not believe it. Inkanûsh is a figure of mischief and a troublemaker... but in none of the legends is he cruel, or destructive. It is a balm for my heart to learn the devastation I beheld was not caused by the trickster sprite of myth at whom I laughed in my youth, but was instead a final cruel consequence of Barkhûsh's evil.'
'Know now the truth, my friend, and be healed, if such a thing can be possible.'

'I would remain and speak with Mashkânu a little longer, ${PLAYER}. Furthermore, my research is not yet complete. I must search for more information about the Urash-zâl, the Din of Stone, within the Kalmakhíla. I believe you should continue without me on the western road as it climbs into An Shêru. I will catch up to you when I have finished my studies in Zajâna, but until I have done so you must remain alert for the presence of the Thardúth in Mûr Ghala.
'I spoke to Glorfindel of this possibility, my friend. He will be waiting for you at the Overgate outside the city.'

\qThe sound was terrible and heard by all, but the devastation in the wake of the Urash-zâl was worst of all, and it changed the face of the land: cliffs crumbled, boulders fell from the height, great chasms opened in the earth along the whole of the Mûr. Even the great northern gate of Jajân cracked, so widespread were the effects of the tremors of the Urash-zâl.\q
'I may have found part of the answer I sought. Look here!'

'The people of Mûr Ghala named it Urash-zâl: the Din of Stone. It was a terrifying noise that could be heard all along the Ridge of Plenty, and its tremors changed the face of the land, opening great chasms, diverting the course of rivers, and drying lakes to their very beds. This was the cause of the Great Dearth that so affected much of Shagâna.
'One hundred and twenty years ago, the Hûl of Ordâkh committed a terrible act of change with effects that would ripple throughout all of Shagâna. His purpose was to open the way for his armies to conquer the lands to the north, but as we saw at Utug-bûr, I fear this act cleared the way for even greater evils. Now these ancient servants of Morgoth, these Thardúth, have broken loose from the enchantment that kept them preserved for thousands of years, and they stir again in the darkness beneath the earth.
'The Din of Stone revealed the hidden temple of Utug-bûr in which the Thardúth slept. How many other such hidden places might it have revealed elsewhere in Shagâna, ${PLAYER}?'

'Stand aside! The Wizard will pay for his crimes! I have come to slay this evil creature, this Mithrandir!
'The Wizard will die at my hand!'
'You have provided a balm for the pain of my heart.'
'I spoke to Glorfindel of this possibility, my friend. He will be waiting for you at the Overgate outside the city.'

'These tidings are unsurprising. I confess I expected Inkanûsh to remain here in Zajâna from the moment I set eyes upon the Kalmakhíla. Did he tell you about the Din of Stone?'
You tell Glorfindel that the Wizard seemed certain the Din of Stone may have revealed more vaults of the Thardúth than Utug-bûr alone, and the Elf-lord nods.
'He is rarely wrong, ${PLAYER}. These enchanted servants of Morgoth needed two things to threaten Middle-earth in the present age, and if Inkanûsh is correct they may have both of these things in Mûr Ghala: the end of their enchantment and access once again to the surface. We will take the road north-west as it climbs into An Shêru and keep watch for any sign of the Thardúth or their Utûgi warriors. Will Ulishár remain our guide on this road, or does he desire to remain in Zajâna with the travelling players now that they are reunited?'

'Though mine was a bittersweet reunion with Têrkar's Travellers, I was still most pleased to see them again! Even so, I made a commitment to guide you on the road through Mûr Ghala and I will not forsake that pledge!'
Ulishár smiles.
'In any event, Satagêra told me they must also take the westward road in a few days. She has been hired to write a new play for the Travellers to perform; it may be our paths will cross again.'
'Will Ulishár remain our guide on this road, or does he desire to remain in Zajâna with the travelling players now that they are reunited?'

'He has found his natural environment, as I knew he would! He has gone to the Kalmakhíla, the great library of Zajâna, and already he believes he has learned something of use, if not all of what he sought. He will tell you in person.
'The entrance to this word-fortress, the Khíla, is to the north-east of here, beside the commons.'

'I have not yet learned all that I sought by coming here, but I have confirmed one of my suspicions, ${PLAYER}.
'It seems to my thinking that the Thardúth who lay hidden at Utug-bûr required two things to happen before they could trouble Middle-earth anew. First, they must pass beyond living memory of all who knew of them, and that was accomplished by the defeat of Sauron. Second, the chambers in which they lay buried must be brought to the surface by some geologic change: the movement of the earth, the diversion of the waters, the alteration of the rocks.
'So it was at Utug-bûr, and ever my thought turned upon this matter: could it happen elsewhere? I may have found part of the answer. Look here!'

'Inkanûsh has gone to the Kalmakhíla, the great library of Zajâna, and already he believes he has learned something of use, if not all of what he sought. He will tell you in person.
'The entrance to this word-fortress, the Khíla, is to the north-east of here, beside the commons.'

The pages of the open book are weathered and faded, but still legible.
\q...would not have believed it ever ran so deep had I not seen it myself only months before, but the flow of the river was greatly diminished. By the third day following the great tremors it had slowed to a trickle. My friend insists that the Usâl and the Agâl too will never flow again as they had, and even the lake of Idagâl is now a cracked and dry basin. He named it Khadagâl, the Dry-whelm, but the herdsmen insist that is a name of ill omen and the lake must return. I think they are both right and wrong: I believe the name is ill-starred, but the waters of the lake have gone forever.
'Were the great tremors of the Urash-zâl a natural event, like the rising and setting of the sun or the passing of the seasons, or was it inflicted upon us by the whim of the Ghursâti? What could we have done to incur such wrath and vengeance?
'My friend thinks Shurash Hûl of Ordâkh is somehow to blame for the Urash-zâl, for the drying of the rivers has removed the last barrier to the northern progress of his armies. I say it must be happenstance, for the quakes were felt along the entirety of the Mûr. How could one man so change the face of the land, even one so ambitious as the Hûl?\q
'I may have found part of the answer I sought. Look here!'

If you deprive them of blades and bows with which they trouble folk on the road, you will be aiding the Shâra and any others who must travel this way. We can meet up at Gadim-ûn where the road leads into An Shêru and discuss our further plans.'

'Those brigands would surely have known not to trouble Shâra Mizâdi or her army, but most travellers have neither her numbers nor her ferocious mien! It is good you have shown them the road is not undefended.
'I felt a chill when I arrived here, and my companions say they felt the same. I suspect more than brigands haunt these ruins.'

'What have you found, my friend? From the look in your eye I deem you have discovered something that must concern us.'
You hand the ravings of the Ordâkhai sorcerer to Glorfindel, and he closely studies the parchment. After a moment he looks up at you.
'These words remind me of the Dagor Carlanthir, ${PLAYER}. To me this writing sounds like someone with less fortitude than Inkanûsh experiencing the mind-tampering of the Thardúth.'
'The Elf-lord Glorfindel will want to see that parchment, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps he will know what those ravings could mean.'

'This is not the first talk of this sort I have overheard. Every new ruler thinks to better the lives of their people, but when the time comes to make good on such promises they are found wanting!
'Is this Mizâdi any different? If she really wants to aid the people who must live in An Shêru, her followers must prove her good intentions. There are wights to be found at Naxar Dâl. Have you the courage to face them?'
You ask Mashdagâl why he ventures so near to tombs known to be inhabited by wights, and he chuckles.
'That is my own business, stranger. If they prove too fearsome for you to handle, I am certain your warrior-queen will be along shortly to recover your equipment and your body. I hear this Mizâdi is different than the others.'
'If this man has something to say, he should say it to my face!'
'If Mizâdi really wants to aid the people who must live in An Shêru, her followers must prove her good intentions. There are wights to be found at Naxar Dâl. Have you the courage to face them?'

'I found something, ${PLAYER}. Look here! This slain man wears the distinctive robes of a sorcerer. Did he come here in search of treasure? I said nothing back at Gadim-ûn, but I think that unmannerly scoundrel might be a treasure-seeker himself, if not an outright brigand. Should we tell him of this man's fate, it may encourage him to seek another profession!
'This corpse tells us the Ordâkhai have already pressed forward into An Shêru, and this man, at least, ran afoul of the wights. Has he anything upon him that might tell us the movements of his allies?'
'This slain man wears the distinctive robes of a sorcerer from Ordâkh. What led him to his death among these ruins? Search his body and we may learn the answer, or if his allies are nearby.'
'I understand one of my companions met you some time ago. His name is Shenzâmin, and he speaks most highly of you.'

'The air is thin and cold in An Shêru. I like it not! I much prefer the warmth and life of Ambarûl to this desolate height. Are pleasant villages so few here that we must shelter among crypts and tombs? But it was Shâra Mizâdi's command to scout this place for her foes, and we will do it.
'I understand one of my companions met you some time ago, ${PLAYER}. His name is Shenzâmin, and he speaks most highly of you. The other is named Kishâtal, and he has proven a sturdy ally to me as well, besting a number of brigands that thought to ambush us between Ingar-garâsh and the road through Kighân.'

'I am Shenzâmin of Kûr Anzar, ${PLAYER}. We last spoke outside the town of Urmâkh, in Imhûlar. I did not expect to see you again so far from where last we met, but the surprise is a pleasant one!
'It is Shâra Mizâdi's command that we watch the road through An Shêru for any sign of foes that might endanger her army as it travels. Rahâzi of Iridír says she does not like this place; I echo her thoughts, for the thin air and the cold fills me with unease.'

'Shâra Mizâdi entrusted us with scouting the Height of the Sky for any sign of Ordâkhai aggression. We are also to treat with the Temámir dwarves that are said to dwell in this place, and to offer them the friendship of Renewed Hamât.'
Kishâtal smiles with wry amusement.
'Shenzâmin and I have spoken of this curiosity before: that neither of us knew ourselves to be Hamâti before the rise of Shâra Mizâdi. Now each of us would die for her, and for Renewed Hamât. I hope it will not come to that, but if it does I will die knowing my death will be of some use for the Shâra and the welfare of my people, and hers.'
'It is Shâra Mizâdi's command that we watch the road through An Shêru for any sign of foes that might endanger her army as it travels.'

'What... what is it? What have you done?'
You show Arshûk the fancy blade of Ordâkh and he looks at you in amazement.
'You dared trespass near enough to Damudûr to retrieve this blade? That displays true courage, stranger!'

'It was a few nights ago. Under cover of the darkness, I crept near to the camp of the Ordâkhai soldiers. I thought I might be able to steal some of the unattended swords or other treasures. The Ordâkhai plunder the Ridge of Plenty for its wealth, and have always done so... how have they that right but I do not?
'I was about to slip into the camp when something made me pause. Believe me when I tell you I know this for certain: had I not stayed my feet, I would not be alive today. For as I hesitated, a group of figures emerged from the cleft of Damudûr and passed by the light of a fire. From their attire, I knew four of them to be nobles of Ordâkh, but their manner was striking. Had they not been so richly-dressed I might have thought them servants. They cringed and capered before the two most severe creatures I have ever seen.
'They were tall and gaunt, in appearance like the Kinta Elves you sometimes see throughout the Mûr. But where those folk possess a distant, preoccupied air, from these creatures I felt a sensation of intense hatred. A man and a woman they seemed in appearance, but the feeling of hatred radiating from them struck me as being quite otherworldly. They were flanked on two sides by great Orcs larger than any I have seen before; my blood ran cold and my breath stopped as they drew near to my hiding-place.
'The clowning Ordâkhai nobility guided their companions past the fires and into the darkness of the enveloping night, and as they faded from my view, but not my memory, never my memory, I heard them speak the name \qEmax Dûl.\q That is where the terrible creatures must be now, either the guests or the masters of Ordâkh.'

'It is clear to me from Arshûk's account that the large Orcs he saw from afar were Utûgi. They must serve the Thardúth of Damudûr even as those that slew my brother served the Thardúth of Utug-bûr.
'In Baharúd's memory will I continue to stand beside you, ${PLAYER}. The Utûgi may not fear a Kinta Elf such as Ulishár... but it may be they should.'

'As they faded from my view, but not my memory, never my memory, I heard them speak the name \qEmax Dûl.\q That is where the terrible creatures must be now, either the guests or the masters of Ordâkh.'

'I believe what Arshûk has told to us, but we know more about the Thardúth than he does, through no fault of his own. His fear of them is neither misplaced nor unfounded.
'Nobles of Ordâkh are not accustomed to subservience. For them to behave so in the presence of the Thardúth indicates to me they have some knowledge of their powers or abilities. The Ordâkhai are right to fear them; perhaps they believe such demonstrations will keep the creatures they discovered at Damudûr under control. On this they must be wrong. The Thardúth intend to manipulate the Ordâkhai and seize control of their empire.
'Each of these remain our foes. We will continue to oppose them, even as they prey upon each other. But Arshûk's tale has told me something else of use, ${PLAYER}. The madness that inflicted the others who strayed near Damudûr did not affect Arshûk. The Thardúth must be aware of an individual in order to invade his mind. This may be useful to us.'
'In Baharúd's memory will I continue to stand beside you, ${PLAYER}. The Utûgi may not fear a Kinta Elf such as Ulishár... but it may be they should.'

'The Ordâkhai encamp outside Damudûr. They must be searching for something, but what that may be remains unknown to us.
'I found someone who might know something of their purpose, but he is too terrified to speak any further on the subject. He is named Arshûk. Can you convince him to tell us what he saw at Damudûr?'

'I want to help you, but... but...'
Arshûk stammers with fright. Only when you place a reassuring hand on his arm does he calm sufficiently to make himself understood.
'If I speak, will you protect me from the terrible creatures that stand behind the Ordâkhai? Can you prove to me you have the courage to oppose them?'
'I found someone who might know something of their purpose, but he is too terrified to speak. He is named Arshûk. Can you convince him to tell us what he saw at Damudûr?'

'Arshûk began to tell Ulishár about something he saw at Damudûr, but then he was overcome with terror and would say nothing more. Whatever he saw, we must prove to him we have the courage to protect him or he will say nothing.
'One common element has emerged from the talk of the people with whom I have spoken, ${PLAYER}. Many of these folk have been impressed by the bright shine of the weapons wielded by the Ordâkhai, and by the gems and jewels that adorn their clothing.
'Perhaps if you retrieve a fancy blade of Ordâkh from the camp of Kôth Rau, Arshûk will see you have the courage to oppose this kingdom, and protect him from its soldiers. Then it may be his tongue will loosen and he will confirm what I have come to suspect: that the Thardúth walk in An Shêru.'

'The dragon Akhízi pursued Shurug-nîn northward in rage, and both disappeared into legend. But what befell the Elf Maethriel?'

'Some of the most inspiring songs end in sadness, ${PLAYER}. Glorfindel need not apologize for it.
'For the sake of Shurug-nîn and Maethriel I will fight on, and not be intimidated by the strength of our foes. The Thardúth and their Utûgi warriors are not unassailable, and they knew defeat at Sabûdamar. They will know it again, for I am the daughter of Girhâzi, a proud warrior of the Dumûri, and I follow the example of great Shurug-nîn, who knew no fear!'
'But let this not dampen your enthusiasm for cooperation between Elf and Shagâni! Great are the deeds and many are the accomplishments they achieved together before they faded into legend.'

'After Shurug-nîn freed the thralls at Lâkindar, her name and legend spread throughout all the lands of Shagâna. Around that time she was given a mighty sword of Elf-make, Orotheg, and she wielded it against the armies of the Orcs that threatened to subjugate her people once again.'
Rahâzi pauses thoughtfully.
'I have not given this much thought before now, ${PLAYER}. Of what significance is it that Orotheg was forged by the Elves? From where did the sword come? Is it possible that Glorfindel may know some details of this legend unknown to my own people?
'He intended to go to Khanâg Gur for his investigation into Damudûr. We should meet with him and see what he knows concerning Shurug-nîn and the blade Orotheg.'

'The blade Orotheg? That is a name I have not heard in some time, ${PLAYER}!
'Yes, it is known to me. During the war against Morgoth in the First Age, a great warrior of my own people sought a champion to stem the flow of Orcs from the lands of the south. Her name was Maethriel, and she carried the deadly sword Orotheg, Wrath-thorn. But she despaired, for the folk of the south were kept on the edge of starvation by cruel oppressors and the spark of rebellion was snuffed out wherever it threatened to catch.
'Tidings from Beleriand of one disaster after another reached Maethriel's despairing ears, and she knew she was nearly out of time. If she was to find a hero that could rally the people of Shagâna against Morgoth, she had to find that hero soon.
'Find her she did, for word of Shurug-nîn had begun to spread following the revolt at Lâkindar. Maethriel gifted her the blade Orotheg, and together the two great heroes loosened the hold of the Orcs upon the land and its people.'
'Glorfindel intended to go to Khanâg Gur for his investigation into Damudûr. We should meet with him and see what he knows concerning Shurug-nîn and the blade Orotheg.'

'I am inspired to hear of this cooperation between Elf champion and Shagâni warrior, Glorfindel! Maethriel's blade Orotheg would go on to greatness, for with it Shurug-nîn would face the fearsome dragon Akhízi and her terrible children on the shores of the lake of Idagâl. It is said in song that the bones of the three dragons lay at the bottom of the lake for thousands of years.
'The dragon Akhízi pursued Shurug-nîn northward in rage, and both disappeared into legend. But what befell the Elf Maethriel?'

'Word of Shurug-nîn had begun to spread following the revolt at Lâkindar. Maethriel gifted her the blade Orotheg, and together the two great heroes loosened the hold of the Orcs upon the land and its people.'

'The tales of your people are not so different than those of mine, Rahâzi, for if you continue a story long enough it often ends in sadness. Shurug-nîn's fate is not known for certain? Neither is that of Maethriel. Many and great are her deeds during the wars against Morgoth; it is said she stood fearlessly before one of his most terrifying servants, a balrog of legend... but what happened to her I cannot say. She vanishes from tale and song sometime before Akhízi pursued her chosen champion northward.
'But let this not dampen your enthusiasm for cooperation between Elf and Shagâni! Great are the deeds and many are the accomplishments they achieved together before they faded into legend.'

'I hoped the Thardúth had all perished at Utug-bûr, even as I knew such evils could not be so easily-defeated. \qEasily,\q say I? I dishonour the memories of Surdûsha and the others who fell at Sabûdamar, the red-rush battle!'
Rahâzi frowns mournfully and stops speaking, lost in her thoughts. Eventually a light appears in her eye and she looks at you closely.
'During the battle you reminded the fighting Dumûri of our great hero Shurug-nîn, do you remember? Many are the songs we sing of her and how she came to be known as Nebunûru, \qthe Shining Light,\q but one of these songs has made itself particularly known to me as we travel along the Mûr. Before she became our great hero of legend, many thousands of years ago, Shurug-nîn laboured in the mines of Lâkindar. Those mines would have been located somewhere in the far south-west of what today is called An Shêru.
'Will you humour me with a visit to this place, ${PLAYER}? If we must once again face the Thardúth and their Utûgi warriors, I would draw upon the inspiration of Shurug-nîn to strengthen my sword-arm and bolster my courage.'

'Before she became our great hero of legend, many thousands of years ago, Shurug-nîn laboured in the mines of Lâkindar. Those mines would have been located somewhere in the far south-west of what today is called An Shêru.
'Will you humour me with a visit to this place? If we must once again face the Thardúth and their Utûgi warriors, I would draw upon the inspiration of Shurug-nîn to strengthen my sword-arm and bolster my courage.'

'That is the way to what had once been the mines of Lâkindar, where Shurug-nîn toiled. She was of no royal line, and her family had not been part of any upper caste in the kingdom of Nêshak, but she possessed exceptional strength and courage. When her brothers perished in the mines, she led a revolt against her oppressors.
'That was not so unusual in those days, but what is surprising is that she succeeded. The freed thralls escaped into the sunlight and Shurug-nîn became a legendary figure. It is said she could not know defeat.
'But that was long ago, and Lâkindar must now be greatly-changed. Let us see what has become of it.'

'I am ready to resume our westward journey, ${PLAYER}. Meet me on the eastern side of the dry Usâl River, west of here and beyond Khanâg Gur.'

'This is where the Ordâkhai seized me, ${PLAYER}. I have not returned here since I escaped from Emax Dûl with the help of Têrkar's Travellers.
'I remember standing on the bank of the dry river-bed, imagining that I could hear the rushing of the water that once flowed within. So vivid was the fantasy I could almost see the torrent! But it was not so, and I felt rough hands upon me, breaking me from my reverie; the Usâl remained dry.
'I learned later the soldiers had not sought a Kinta in particular, but the nobility of Ordâkh valued my kind for captives. I was treated no better than any others, but they enjoyed the sight of my labours.'

'Of our company, only Ulishár has walked into Idagâl. Will he tell us what to expect, and where first we should go?
'Even mighty Shurug-nîn would hesitate to knock upon the gates of Emax Dûl, knowing the Ordâkhai and the Thardúth have joined hands within!'

'Emax Dûl has borne many names over the span of its history, each chosen by the power that controlled it: the Menûns of Nísaka, the Khôrthan League, and now the Ordâkhai.
'But Rahâzi is right. We should not make directly for Emax Dûl. Instead let us pass into Idagâl and follow the road northward. There we will find a pleasant settlement beside a green oasis. It is called Ahâba, and the Beltáni herdsmen who dwell there showed me kindness while I wandered, a few years before I was imprisoned by the Ordâkhai. If Malgârzor lives there still, he may help us. I knew him not, but by his reputation he was a man of influence among those who live by the water.'

'So many wayfarers come to this statue to appeal to the Menundâri for his return. They leave various keepsakes at the base of the statue as offerings for him, but I call it a futile endeavour! The Eternal Ruler will return at a time of his choosing, not of ours. Until that moment, all we can do is watch over his sacred sites.
'At night I have heard a terrible wailing, as of an anguished wind, and in the morning assorted items have been taken from the base of Uzûr. I care not for the keepsakes that are taken, but sometimes stones go missing, and because they belong to Uzûr they are sacred.
'I have never caught them doing it, but I suspect the scavenging beasts called kergrim are to blame for these thefts. If you retrieve these sacred stones from their dens to the north-east, you will prove yourself a friend to the people of this land, and to the memory of the Menundâri.'

'Malgârzor named this great statue \qUzûr\q and said many wayfarers and pilgrims travel great distances to see it. Perhaps you can speak with some of these travellers and learn what they can tell us of the Ordâkhai presence in Idagâl. They will likely not know anything concerning the Thardúth... but keep open your ears.'

'I suspect the scavenging beasts called kergrim are to blame for these thefts. If you retrieve these sacred stones from their dens to the north-east, you will prove yourself a friend to the people of this land, and to the memory of the Menundâri.'

'Let us leave Rahâzi to contemplate the dragon bones in peace. I would take a closer look at the great statue that stands beyond the edge of the lake-bed to the west. Malgârzor named it the Dawn-warden, and it watches over this land from a great height.'

'The Dawn-warden is a most impressive construction even when seen from afar, but more so when seen from below! I understand a similar statue stands to the north, in Khûd Zagin, but that one lies in ruin.
'In his own language Malgârzor named this great statue \qUzûr\q and said many wayfarers and pilgrims travel great distances to see it. Perhaps you can speak with some of these travellers and learn what they can tell us of the Ordâkhai presence in Idagâl. They will likely not know anything concerning the Thardúth... but keep open your ears.'
'Have you come from afar to worship Uzûr, the great statue of Izighûz Menundâri, the Eternal Ruler? The time of his return is nearly at hand, when he will deliver Shagâna from its enemies!'

'I dare not hope the Menundâri will return during my lifetime. Why has he not already come back to us? What more suffering could be required before he will take pity upon us? Has there not been war and bloodshed enough to merit his return?'

'After the defeat of Sauron during the War of the Ring, the Thardúth tested the will of any who strayed too near their vault in Damudûr. Did they compel the soldiers and sorcerers of Ordâkh to seek them out, to finish what the Din of Stone had begun, clearing the blocked way into Damudûr? I feel certain they did, ${PLAYER}, but some to whom they spoke may have resisted. The pryings of the Thardúth are ungentle; an unprepared mind could not withstand such invasion, and with resistance would be broken.
'But we have an advantage, my friend. The Thardúth slumbered within their vaults for thousands of years, and during that time these servants of Morgoth possessed no knowledge of the outside world. They emerged from their hidden vaults like children, children who know nothing of present days and who must be taught. The Thardúth have chosen the Ordâkhai to teach them, and while the Empire of Ordâkh remains a danger to us, it still reels from Sauron's defeat during the War of the Ring.
'If the Thardúth are to learn the state of things from their Ordâkhai teachers, their classroom is sure to be within the fortress of Emax Dûl. You will need to find a way inside, ${PLAYER}.
'For now, go to north-east Ahâba and ask Ulishár what he can tell us.'
'We must make our plans, and make them well. For now, go to north-east Ahâba and ask Ulishár what he can tell us.'

'I told you we would see Têrkar's Travellers again!
'They have been employed to perform a new play for the Ordâkhai, but Satagêra has been having some trouble finishing it to her satisfaction.'

'I have written more plays than I can count on ten fingers, ${PLAYER}, but this one is proving more difficult than those others.'
Satagêra shakes her head with disgust.
'The Ordâkhai have commissioned us to perform a new play that will inspire their people. They want it to be called \qThe Great Triumph of Mordor and Ordâkh,\q and it is intended to convey that their defeat in the war was actually a victory, and their greatest triumph is still to come!
'Coin is coin, ${PLAYER}, and the performance of this play will keep Têrkar's Travellers fed and comfortable for many months... but these are all lies!'
'I told you we would see Têrkar's Travellers again!'

'I trust you were not sight-seeing, ${PLAYER}?'
You explain that you were gathering information about the Ordâkhai presence in Idagâl and their relationship with the newly-awoken Thardúth of Damudûr, and the Wizard chuckles.
'My chiding was unserious, my friend; but I see you have already learned some of what I came to tell you! It was with haste that I joined Têrkar's Travellers after I finished my investigation in the Kalmakhíla. Their road aligned with mine, for their next engagement is within the walls of Emax Dûl itself, and I knew your search would bring you near to that city.
'Listen now to what I have learned! I have made some connexions between subjects about which we knew little, and now I know a great deal!'

'In the year 2890 of the Third Age, Shurash Hûl of Ordâkh raged against the River Usâl, for it blocked the passage of his armies north. With the aid of agents of Mordor, his sorcerers devised and cast deadly spells that cracked the earth about the springs of the river. The rituals triggered great tremors in the foundation of Mûr Ghala, collapsing reservoirs beneath the surface and causing the Usâl to run dry.
'The quakes continued for weeks, one after another, and the ensuing noise caused by the shifting of the rocks came to be known as the Din of Stone, which the Zajâni scholars I have read named Urash-zâl. I showed you some of these accounts, ${PLAYER}; there are others, which shed more detail upon the scope of the injury inflicted during the Din of Stone.
'The Usâl was not the only geologic casualty of Ordâkh and Mordor's fell cooperation. The wells of the Usâl's sister-river, the Agâl, were partially-blocked, and the Idagâl lake emptied, becoming a ruin of cracked and broken mires. More than one hundred years after the Din of Stone, the lake has shown no sign of restoration. Where the water might have gone, I cannot say; perhaps great caverns beneath the surface are now flooded where once they were not. The sorcerers of Ordâkh have much for which to answer.'

'Comparing the records I found in the Kalmakhíla with the tales of the Kintai of Sul Madásh, I have come to a realization, ${PLAYER}. I believe the Din of Stone unleashed the fungal blight that now consumes Adagím.
'Note my use of the word \qunleashed,\q rather than \qcreated.\q For I think the entity the Kintai name Sívigush, the Earth-terror, dwelt beneath Nisigím for untold ages of the world. It would have remained there forever, had not the Ordâkhai cracked the earth during the Din of Stone. It may be the fungal blight was fed by newly-flooded caverns beneath the Mûr, but of that I am less certain.'

'The ritual commanded by Shurash Hûl of Ordâkh damaged bastions along the entirety of Mûr Ghala, from Emax Dûl to the northern gate of Zajâna. Much of this damage was superficial, causing a spider's web of cracks to form along the outside of buildings and knocking items off of shelves.
'It was worse for the Temámir. The Din of Stone collapsed mines up and down the entirety of the Ridge, and thousands of dwarves were lost. Jiret-menêsh survived, but its ruler sealed the fortress in the following years and took little notice of events in the wider world.
'Agents of the Temámir that dared to leave Jiret-menêsh attained much influence elsewhere in Middle-earth. I wonder if Khôltekh would have become a Kinsman of the Kindred of the Coins in Umbar if the Temámir of Jiret-menêsh had played a larger role in the region in the years following the Din of Stone?'

'Ever since the Dagor Carlanthir was fought, I have believed the Thardúth must possess more hidden vaults than the one we discovered at Utug-bûr. After all, a fox might gain access to one hen-house, and if that is where you keep all of your hens, you will soon find yourself without eggs. The hobbits of the Shire with whom I am well-acquainted would not risk a breakfast without eggs, ${PLAYER}!
'No, it seemed clear to me the Thardúth must possess more than one hidden vault. Like Utug-bûr, another vault would be concealed within the rocks, the better to protect the Thardúth until the enchantment that preserved them came to its end. And also like at Utug-bûr, this vault would not be accessible unless the face of the land was to be changed.
'Shurash Hûl of Ordâkh knew nothing of the Thardúth, but the Din of Stone he caused would enable them to emerge when the time was right. I suspected the location of this second vault might be within An Shêru, but I see you have confirmed it for me.'
'Go in peace, and remember: the Ordâkhai remain a danger in the Mûr, despite their defeat in the north.'

A new Hûl will come to power in Ordâkh. The surest sign of our fortunes changing would be for the Menundâri to return to us first!

'Khóbagach was in poetic mood when he named Barkhûsh's fleet \qThe Song of Waves and Wind,\q believing it would be the greatest accomplishment he would oversee as Hûl. The wide, dark mere was new and appeared on no map, overlooked only by the skeletal gaze of the ruins of Kasukhín, and it was large enough to hold a vast number of warships. The River Ikorbân remained navigable all the way to the sea, and with sharp-eyed archers and spearmen stationed upon the bounds, the lake and its accompanying shipyard could remain a secret for as long as it proved necessary.
'Nisigím lay nearby, but its trees were blighted and it rapidly became a ghost-forest; few of its timbers were suitable for firewood, let alone for shipbuilding. Timbers for the fleet and stone for the ship-yard and its wharves had to be carted by mûmakil from the Mûr. Waggons departed from Khanâg Valoyar and elsewhere every few days, the Temámir accepting payments of silver and gold and asking few questions.
'Khóbagach Hûl died of the gout long before the Song was completed, but Mordor and Ordâkh worked together to finish the weapon that could destroy their shared enemy. The arrival of the Song of Waves and Wind on the shores of Gondor would signal the beginning of the war, but for some unknown reason Barkhûsh launched the attack before the fleet was ready. It stood idle at Sûg Nidar, the Fearwater, for the duration of the war. It stands there still, even as a new king rules in Gondor and all believe Ordâkh to be defeated. - Prepared for Góramul Sai by Laghíl of Emax Dûl, Scribe of Ordâkh'

'You know I have eyes everywhere. Sometimes they see things of interest to me... and to those of my friends I can trust.
'Know you of the vast lake at the head of the Ikorbân? I thought not, for it appears on few maps, and none in Umbar. Any who stray too near this lake, Sûg Nidar, the Fearwater, are slain before they can report of its existence. What deserves such secrecy? I have learned the answer, my friends, and I ask that you hear me out complete before you disregard my words.
'Decades ago, following the destruction of Umbar and the burning of its fleet at the hands of the hated Thorongil, the Dark Lord of Mordor commanded the creation of a new fleet to replace the one that was lost. Barkhûsh ordered the creation of this new armada at Sûg Nidar, far from the prying eyes of Dúnadan and Gondorian spies. \qThe Song of Waves and Wind\q it was named by its builders, and in number it would far exceed even the most grand of the Corsair fleets of history. The work continued for many years, but for reasons unknown to me Barkhûsh began his war without waiting for the Song to be ready; only now does it near completion.
'Let me forestall your objection, my friends! This Kindred exists to oppose the Church of Barkhûsh, and allies with none who worship that Dark Lord, though he be gone. But the Song of Waves and Wind is not of itself evil. It is a tool, a weapon to be used, and just because Barkhûsh set it down does not mean others might not pick it up and use it for their own defence, and for their own aims. This fleet could be a gift to Umbar, and to those who must now lead it through dangerous days.'

'Escucha, he oído que alguien ha robado la pipa de Ferdibrand Tuk y que la tetera de la vieja Ethelinda Burr ha desaparecido. ¿Cómo se pierde una tetera entera? Mientras intentaba escuchar a escondidas a Ethelinda, oí a Sarabeth Bajorivera decir que no podía encontrar su libro. Además, estaba charlando con Himloc Grouse, y me dijo que la jarra favorita de Ferumbras Attereeve había desaparecido.
Ahora sé lo que vas a decir: \q¡Nunca confíes en un Grouse!\q pero creo que dijo la verdad. Y luego, como si eso no fuera suficiente, estaba haciendo unas compras en la armería de Entibo, solo curioseando, ya sabes, y oí a Pell Hojapiedra decir que su cuchillo de talla favorito había desaparecido. Los cuchillos de talla no crecen piernas y se van caminando, como dicen.
Y por si fuera poco, Gammy Cenagales, que es muy confiable, debo decirlo, me dijo que Ponto Sotomonte no puede hacer su trabajo porque dice que le robaron su pala. Ella, por supuesto, piensa que es bastante posible que solo esté diciendo eso para poder tomarse un descanso e ir a pescar, pero creo que fue robada de verdad. Quiero decir, mira todas las otras cosas que han sido robadas.
Ahora, no sé si conoces al viejo Maginard Zorronillo, pero dice que ha visto rascacuevas merodeando por la noche. ¡Rascacuevas, si puedes creerlo! Bueno, le dije, márcame estas palabras: esos rascacuevas son ladrones sin ninguna duda.
Te garantizo que si entras en ese extraño túnel encontrarás todos estos objetos perdidos junto con una compañía de rascacuevas ladrones.'
