'Hoy, stranger! You must be new here. All glory to the Hûl!'
You repeat the sentiment, and Onúkho nods pleasantly.
'It warms my heart to hear it! The Orcs claim to share our purpose here, but I do not believe it. If they thought Mordor had the advantage they would turn on us in the span of a breath! And the Corsairs down at Bâkhridar and at Starkhaven mumble their oaths, but they resent the Hûl, I am sure of it. I wish Ordâkh had no need of either, but this great work began before I was even born, and I was not consulted! It has taken great cost in lives to build the Song of Waves and Wind, and now we wait only for the signal to sail!
'You are fortunate to join us today, stranger. Habâti the Dwarf has just arrived, and he brings goods and provisions from far away. He comes back every few weeks and sets up shop. His arrival is always welcome... it helps to break up the monotony of our days, which are spent mostly in waiting. His prices could be lower, though, I admit it.'
'If you cause no trouble, no trouble will come to you. That is something the Orcs could stand to learn, and the Corsairs would do well to remember!'

'I did not expect to see you here, my friend, but it is a welcome surprise! We must each share the paths we have trod to arrive in this place, but quickly, for the days are dangerous and time is short! I believe the Kindred of the Coins has allied with Orcs of Mordor and the Empire of Ordâkh to construct this fleet of warships.
'Using this fleet, the Song of Waves and Wind, its masters might threaten all of Middle-earth!'

'Look who I found: an unexpected friend! Corudan, his sister Sigileth, and Cúridwan the Golden Maiden are elsewhere in Sûg Nidar. Now that they have laid eyes upon the Song of Waves and Wind, they intend to counter it, if such a thing is possible. Together we will do this!'

'By listening to the conversation of the Ordâkhai, I have learned something of their associates in the Fearwater. Orcs have established an encampment to the east of here at Drushkála, a fort that was drowned when the lake of Sûg Nidar was formed. During the reign of Barkhûsh, the Orcs and the Ordâkhai were made to work together; now that he is gone, the two groups find it more difficult to coexist, and there has been fighting between the two.
'The map you saw contained markings on the other side of the river for a place called the Haven of Bâkhridar, which seems to be a Corsair encampment. The Ordâkhai need crews to sail the ships, but I am not certain how they convinced these sailors; there is little love between Umbar and Ordâkh these days. Beyond Bâkhridar, the wharfs and jetties of Starkhaven must serve as the primary shipbuilding location for the Song.
'Let us first travel eastward toward Drushkála. After we have seen the Orcs, we will turn our attention to the other side of the river.'
'We should get a closer look at this encampment of Orcs to the east.'
'Look there!'

'So many ships, and they all ready for war! You told me what you learned in Emax Dûl, that the fleet has been in construction for so many years... but it is different entire to see the evidence with my own eyes!
'Let us descend the slope toward Drushkála. Go carefully! Remain alert for anything out of the ordinary.'
'We should get closer to the Orc encampment. But be cautious, and remain alert for anything out of the ordinary!'

'What have you learned of the Heirsworn Corsairs? Are they prepared to sail?'
You tell Rahâzi that the Corsairs spend their time in idleness, but that supply crates within the Haven of Bâkhridar have much of what they would need to set sail on the ships of the Song.
'They will go nowhere until their leaders tell them to depart. If we put an end to Nakási and to Balakhâd, they will be content to remain here. Has not the fleet lingered here, unused, for many years?'

'My study of this camp has revealed to me some things of interest. The Corsairs support Balakhâd; they believe he has picked up the mantle set down by his father Balakhôr, and they think he will lead them to victory over Gondor and over Ordâkh alike. They are uncertain of Nakási's loyalty, and they hate the Orcs. They believe she is the one forcing them to work alongside the creatures, and they resent her for it. Many hope Balakhâd will break ties with her and seize control of the Song for himself.
'I agree with Rahâzi. If we can kill or capture these leaders, we will have struck a major blow against those who might wield the Song of Waves and Wind against us.'
'These Corsairs are ready to sail for war, if it is commanded of them. We must do something about any who might issue such a command!'

'My sister and I departed Sul Madásh after you left with Inkanûsh and Glorfindel, making once again for Utug-bûr. Sigileth believed we could put the spirit of Silirtas to rest, but alas we found no sign of her. What we found instead set our course: waggon-tracks, ${PLAYER}, waggon-tracks sunk deep into the rocky ground from the weight of the goods they carried. The tracks travelled from west to east, and when I convinced my sister that we must learn from where they came, my deepest fears were realized. The guards at Ashâgir were slain, and the stockpile of Narghâk contained within was gone. Few only knew of the dangerous substance held within Ashâgir, and only one might command such waggons to transport it away. They were waggons of Temámir design, ${PLAYER}.
'Nakási Wave-reaper has taken command of this fleet, and Khôltekh has supplied it with Narghâk, the Hungry Fire. We may not yet know their full purpose... but I can make some guesses. That is the bad news! There are good tidings as well: Sigileth and I encountered Cúridwan as we followed the road towards Sûg Nidar, and with her aid we were able to slip past the border-guards. Let us walk to the other side of the river and we will speak more about what we have learned.'

'And so the three of us came to the Fearwater, where we have worked to sow dissent among the groups that labour to finish the fleet. As a result, each group is now alert to anything suspicious... I am afraid you will not be able to walk among them without combat any longer, ${PLAYER}!
'I have seen Balakhâd, the son of Balakhôr, from afar; he seems to command the Corsairs of this place. I know not where Nakási may be found, but my sister believes she might have established a command post on the island to the south-east. If Khôltekh is with her, he has remained out of sight. It is also possible he remains in Umbar, and arranged for the delivery of the Narghâk only through his agents.
'We have arrived outside the Haven of Bâkhridar, which seems to be an encampment of Corsairs loyal to the Heirs of Castamir who have now sworn to follow Balakhâd. Let us search the camp and see how well-supplied the Corsairs are, and if they are ready to sail. Then we will meet up on the other side of the Heirsworn camp.'
'Search the crates within the Heirsworn camp and we may learn how prepared they are to sail. I will meet you on the other side of the camp!'
'Search the crates within the Heirsworn camp and we may learn how prepared they are to sail. I will meet you on the other side of the camp!'

'I see you found your way here. Have you brought the Wizard Inkanûsh with you? He will be most interested to hear what I have learned!'
You tell Cúridwan that, regretfully, Inkanûsh remained behind when you came in search of the Song of Waves and Wind, but you are also interested to hear of her discoveries. Cúridwan motions at the submerged boat.
'After you and Inkanûsh left Sul Madásh, my steps took me to Laivárth, and the Kinta Shadalith spoke to me of her experimentation with the Lâg Dávrit. She told me that you helpfully provided a number of blight samples, ${PLAYER}, but when you added them to water, in time they damaged the integrity of the bucket that held it; the wooden slats of the bucket fell apart, spilling the water onto the ground.
'I have done the same with this row-boat I found moored alongside this island. In a matter of moments, a small sample of the blight has damaged the seals that held together this boat, causing it to take on water and sink. Most curious.
'I am ready to return to Fearwater Notch, if you are. My investigation here is complete, and in it I see a means to destroy the fleet these enemies of the natural order think to wield against the Kintai and the other peoples of Shagâna. Sûg Nidar may yet become a watery grave for the Song of Waves and Wind!'
'The light of hope shines upon Sûg Nidar! It may yet become a watery grave for the Song of Waves and Wind!'

'Has Cúridwan found what she sought, ${PLAYER}?'
You briefly relate what you understand of the Golden Maiden's discovery, and its potential use for sinking the warships before they depart the Fearwater.
'A means of utilizing the blight to destroy the Song of Waves and Wind? Let us hope she is right, for our sake and for that of all Middle-earth! But it is not enough to sink the ships. We must also combat the crews here mustered, and the leaders who drive them to war.'
'You should look for Cúridwan by the water's edge to the north-east.'

'But we should not get ahead of ourselves: first we must rejoin my sister and Cúridwan. Sigileth intended to make camp on the island that lies to the south-east of here. High atop that rocky place stands the ruin of Kasukhín, and my sister suggested making camp somewhere in its shadow. Cúridwan says the fort once perched atop a hill that was a meeting-place for travellers, but that was before the floods claimed the valley.
'A single bridge stretches to the island, and it will be a long journey to the south-east along the shore to reach it. Find my sister beneath Kasukhín, but take special care as you pass through Starkhaven; that place is surely crawling with Heirsworn and Ordâkhai alike.'

'Sigileth intended to make camp on the island to the south-east, in the shadow of the ruined keep. A lone bridge stretches to the island, and it will be a long journey to the south-east along the shore to reach it. Take special care as you pass through Starkhaven; that place is surely crawling with both Heirsworn and Ordâkhai.'

'Welcome to Sûg Nidar, ${PLAYER}. I have taken this campsite from the soldiers who made it. I have named it Fearwater Notch, and it is now mine. Should they return they will not live long enough to inform anyone of our presence here. These others dislike the Ordâkhai as much as we do, and have offered their services to us. For now they have my trust.
'Did my brother tell you that we encountered Cúridwan on the road to this place? She has gone down to the water north-east of here, intending to perform an investigation of some sort. I pressed her not on the subject, but what I understood from her mumblings and musings was that she hoped to find some means of sinking the Song to the bottom of the lake?
'You should see if the Golden Maiden found success. Such a thing would be very helpful to us!'
'You have joined us?'

'I have made an unpleasant discovery, friend. While I searched for the Narghâk stockpile, I was surprised by a number of Heirsworn Corsairs and it came to fighting. But they were not content to engage in combat with their blades alone, and they threw glass jars containing a small quantity of an oily substance at me.
'I evaded this attack with little difficulty; am I not an Elf of Lórien? But when the jar shattered upon the ground it exploded with blue flame.
'Some of Balakhâd's Corsairs have been given jars of Narghâk to use in battle, ${PLAYER}. We must retrieve these jars from them. Afterwards let us meet back here.'
'Even a small quantity of Narghâk can inflict grievous harm! We must retrieve as many bottles of this deadly substance from the Heirsworn as we can.'

'Did you separate the bottles of Narghâk from their bearers? Good, for I have done the same. I also found a stack of parchment within an encampment of the Ordâkhai. I think the soldiers knew not what to make of these papers. They are yellowed with age, and when we have finished here I will take some time to study them.
'We found not the stockpile we sought, but I think we discovered the reason for that: the Hungry Fire has already been loaded onto the ships of the Song, and any excess considered unnecessary for their siphons and cannons have been given to the Heirsworn.
'It is more necessary than ever that we prevent the Song from setting sail. May Cúridwan have the time she needs to distribute the blight among the vessels of the fleet, and may we capture or kill the ones who might give the command to sail! But for now we have done what we can.'

I know not for how long Khôltekh has been working in secret with her, but he had his eye upon the stockpile of Hungry Fire from the moment we discovered it within Ashâgir. 'The timing no longer matters. What matters to us now is that we prevent the Song from being equipped with weapons capable of using the Hungry Fire against its enemies. If we can destroy the Narghâk stockpile these weapons will stand empty and unused.'

'I never expected to use the blight for a good purpose, but this is truly a day for surprises.
'Some of the mysteries that plagued Imhûlar and Adagím have been made clear to me now that I see what has transpired within the Fearwater. For many years I believed the floods cascading into Adagím from the north were caused when spring rains overfed the Ikorbân River, but it was not so. The Ordâkhai dredged an old tributary channel, carving a path south from Sûg Nidar. Now the floods that might have destroyed their wharves were instead spilled upon Adagím, already suffering from the blight. Was the extent of the Lâg Dávrit worsened by these annual floods and the noisome bog to which they contributed? It must have been.
'But now I have need of the blight to counter this Ordâkhai fleet, and its pervasive reach will be of use to us! Pods of the blight push into Sûg Nidar from Adagím, and they have taken root within a narrow vale just outside the eastern entrance to Starkhaven, not far from the long bridge that leads to this island. Take this sack and trowel and collect samples of blighted pods for me while you combat some of the creatures that even now push into Sûg Nidar. I will meet you outside that blighted place once you have done this.'

'I need you to collect samples of the blight I can use to disable the fleet. Pods of the blight push into Sûg Nidar from Adagím, and they have taken root within a narrow vale just outside the eastern entrance to Starkhaven, not far from the long bridge that leads to this island. Take this sack and trowel and collect samples of blighted pods for me while you combat some of the creatures that even now push into Sûg Nidar. I will meet you outside that blighted place once you have done this.'
'The trowel I gave to you will enable you to collect samples of the blight I can use to disable the fleet.'

'Have you done as I asked? Thank you, ${PLAYER}. When handled with care, such samples as these may prove that even evil has its uses... for if the Song of Waves and Wind can be made unseaworthy then even the Lâg Dávrit may save some lives.
'I will continue my work applying the blight to the water by the ships of the Song. In time no vessel will remain afloat, and the designs of Ordâkh and Mordor will be ruined. Sigileth is right that the leaders must be captured or slain to truly end this threat... but sinking the Song is an important step on that road. Thank you again for your efforts.'

'Balakhâd and Nakási must be somewhere within the ruins of Kasukhín that sit atop the island; from that high place they can survey the fleet. It will not be long until they begin to see the effects of Cúridwan's interference. We must hurry.
'They will have defenders posted on the bridge that leads to the ruins, ${PLAYER}. Prepare for a fight!'

'My childhood was one of tumult, ${PLAYER}. My mother and my father spoke often to me of Castamir, instructing me that it was our duty to follow his example. Often I wondered if they were right. Was it true that Elves would always seek to keep our people underfoot, subject to their laws and their shadowy rule?
'Could my parents have been wrong? From time to time I saw Elves of the Oasis, the Kintai, in the markets of Umbar Baharbêl, and they seemed otherworldly to me but never sinister. In truth, much of the evil I saw came at the hands of Men! Did not the Kindred of the Coins hold me captive and chase my mother into hiding at the conclusion of their uprising? Was I not threatened with torture by Azagath Sea-shadow and Nakási Wave-reaper?
'But then I beheld the terrible battle where the waterfalls ran red, and I saw the monstrous Orcs that emerged from Utug-bûr. I heard the battle-cries of the ferocious Utûgi, and I saw the corpses piled at their feet. I perceived the name of their masters, ${PLAYER}, and they were called the Thardúth. From afar I heard the Wizard Inkanûsh speak of them as he strove against their powers, and I knew them for what they were.
'They are Elves, ${PLAYER}. A terrible evil of the ancient world has awoken to endanger the lands of Men, and it is in form and nature precisely what my father believed it would be. Castamir was right, and my parents were right, and in their names I have gathered those who would fight to save our world from Elf-kind. Nakási and I have set aside our quarrel. With her ships and my loyal Heirsworn, we will free all of Middle-earth from the grasp of the Elves, and those who aid them.
'If you will stand with me, I would welcome your prowess. You know how dangerous the Thardúth can be.'
Instancia: En la Cima de la Isla
Balakhâd has attempted to convince you of the rightness of his position.
Sigileth has tracked Balakhâd and Nakási to the island of Kasukhín, in the middle of the Fearwater.
Sigileth is waiting for your signal to confront Nakási and Balakhâd atop the island of Kasukhín.
Rahâzi is atop the island of Kasukhín.

'Are you ready to deprive this fleet of its leaders, ${PLAYER}? You have only to give the word and we will search the ruins for Nakási and Balakhâd. They cannot escape the four of us: you, me, my brother, and the Dumûri warrior Rahâzi.
'Meanwhile, Cúridwan will continue to use the blight to damage the seaworthiness of the Song. It will not be long before every vessel lies at the bottom of the lake! We must give her time enough to distribute the blight to every vessel of the fleet.'
'I am ready if you are. They will not long hide from us.'
'This is bad, ${PLAYER}! Corudan lies bleeding, and Balakhâd and Nakási escape us! They will sail the surviving ships of the Song of Waves and Wind downriver... to war!'

El palacio de Ekal-nêbi es la joya de la corona de Emax Dûl, una opulenta residencia de los gobernantes del reino de Nêshak, Nísaka... y ahora también de Ordâkh. Oculta entre bastidores de la vida palaciega, Thothril la Enredadora, Thardúth de Damudûr, comenzó a ejercer silenciosamente sus encantamientos sobre las mentes de sus habitantes. Ahora que los soldados de la alianza de Mizâdi se encuentran a las puertas del palacio, ella afirma su control definitivo sobre el palacio.

Malavin te indicó que regresaras con Cinaid, cerca de la puerta principal de Gramsfoot. Él te ayudará a seguir preparándote para luchar en las Landas de Etten.

'Familiarizarte con los distintos clanes es el primer paso para curtirte en el campo de batalla. Para continuar con tu preparación, regresa a la puerta principal y habla con Cinaid. Él te dará más instrucciones y te preparará para la batalla que se avecina.
'Una vez más, hermana, bienvenida a la lucha. Que los verdaderos hijos les muestren a estas criaturas inferiores cómo se debe pelear una guerra.'

'Me alegra verte aún aquí, señora de la oscuridad. Las lecciones que tengo para enseñarte son muchas y importantes. Te serán de gran ayuda en esta tierra fétida.'
Hace una pausa por un momento.
'Creo que es hora de prepararte como corresponde.'

'Do my eyes deceive me? No! You have returned to stand with us against the Corsairs of Umbar, ${PLAYER}? I only hope you have not arrived too late!
'When we travelled with King Elessar to Outer Gondor that he might hear the concerns of his people and help them rebuild from the war, I did not think we would so soon be thrust once again into such horrors as have come to the Harlond this day!
'It was my duty, and Lornion's, to safeguard the King. But how can we protect him against a fleet that wields such terrible weapons, and is crewed by every enemy that ever vowed to destroy Gondor: Corsairs, Haradrim, and Orcs, all united in hatred against us?
'King Elessar has established a camp on the overlook atop this sloping path, ${PLAYER}. Go to him and learn what can be done against these invaders, if there be anything!'
'You will find King Elessar at the top of this path! Go to him with haste!'

King Elessar turns to face you, his expression brightening as he recognizes your return from distant lands.
'You return to Gondor in its time of need, my friend; I deem that is no coincidence. Tell me everything you know of this fleet and the villains who captain it!'

'Gondor cannot be without defenders! Where are its knights? Where are its fighters? The King of Gondor would not permit an incursion so near to the White City to remain unmet... unless he had no choice.

'Belondor tells me Nakási has broken with the Kindred of the Coins, and I believe him.'

'We must prove to the Orcs and Haradrim that Gondor is not without courage!'

You assure Aphadaer that the Heirsworn will not have victory, despite their initial success, and that the counter attack will begin at Elessar's command.
'Of course, of course. Heed not my jumbled thoughts!'

The King's expression is already greatly-changed from when you first encountered him today. His weariness has been replaced with determination.
'This is the hour in which we fight back against the invaders,' he says.
'Belondor tells me that Nakási has broken with his Kindred, and is an enemy too of Umbar. I believe him. He counts himself no longer a man of Gondor, but today we will fight side by side to prevent Nakási and her allies from endangering our lands and our homes, though they be not shared.'

Elessar sighs when you finish your account, and you can tell the events of the day have taken their toll.
'The death of Nakási's husband Tumúldo at the hands of the Heirsworn was an injustice, but it cannot warrant such an attack as this. Had she remained in Umbar, nursing her hatred of Gondor, that would be a sorrow, and I would share her grief. But for her to seize command of this fleet and these weapons and bring them to bear against my people... that cannot be forgiven.
'Five ships have come to the Harlond wielding the Hungry Fire I thought was gone. Nakási captains the largest of these. Two others are crewed by Haradrim soldiers, and one has Orcs aboard. I could not see who commands the crew of the last ship, but from your account I deem it must be Balakhâd, son of Balakhôr the Scourge. The Heirs of Castamir remain to trouble us, it seems.
'It has been a losing struggle to this point, ${PLAYER}, but perhaps your arrival will help to turn the tide. Speak to my attendants here on the overlook and we will begin to fight back against these invaders!'

'It has only been a matter of weeks since I travelled with you in Anfalas, ${PLAYER}, but so much has happened! Is it true that the son of Balakhôr the Scourge captains one of these ships against us? Are the Heirs of Castamir behind this attack?'
You tell Aphadaer that Balakhâd supplied Corsair crews for some of Nakási's fleet, but most of those ships were damaged before they could sail to Gondor. You ask him what you can do to help fight against the five ships that made the journey.
'There was much chaos as we retreated to this overlook, ${PLAYER}, and we were pursued by our enemies. As the King's groom, it is my job to see to the horses, and I did as best I could, but two of them slipped from my tending and fled toward the main street that runs through the centre of the Harlond. They were crazed by the flames, you see. Who among us was not? If you find Agladal and Gaeranor, send them back to me, if they still live!'

'The ships sailed into the Harlond with no warning, ${PLAYER}. Their crews of Orcs and Haradrim set the port ablaze in the span of a single hour. They came ashore and we met them with sword and spear, but we were unprepared for such ferocity in time of peace. Our counter attack will come, and it must come soon!
'Face any of those who now pillage the Harlond, and you will help us regain the advantage!'

'King Elessar rode bravely from the White City and led a sortie against the invaders, but we were pushed back to this hill. During the retreat, some of our soldiers dropped their weapons on the slope. Retrieve these weapons as you descend from the overlook, and leave them in the weapons barrel that has been placed by the graveyard. They will be used again!'
'Speak to my attendants and learn how we can fight back against Nakási and Balakhâd!'
'Can you pick up the weapons we dropped on the path as we climbed to this overlook? After you have them, leave them in a barrel by the graveyard for other soldiers to wield in defence of Gondor!'

'Always have I been loyal to the Heirs of Castamir, ${PLAYER}! I gave them whatever tidings I could of Elessar's plans, and the woman Ioreth proved a font of information! Indeed... it was most challenging to determine what news could be of use amidst all of her ramblings!
'I lost contact with Maethon shortly before the King departed for Outer Gondor, and received no further word from the other supporters of the Heirs; I had to decide what actions to take on my own. That stayed my hand for a time, but always I sought for some means of separating the King from his defenders while we ventured in Anfalas and Pinnath Gelin.
'But now that Balakhâd has assumed his rightful mantle, I can die knowing I have done what I could to support his rise! If I must die, then I will die for him! Praise the memory of Castamir, and all his heirs!'

You can tell the King will not long remain abed. Already he desires to get up and move around, despite the instructions of his healers! You advise that he lay still and not aggravate his injury, and he shakes his head with amusement.
'The battle has ended, but there is something I need you to do, ${PLAYER}.
'Nakási's attack on Gondor must reshape the Kindred of the Coins, for it is my understanding that some of that body supported her in this and others did not. Belondor died in our defence, but Rothog and Tatháta also fought on our behalf, and they survived. What befell those who remained behind in Umbar?
'I ask that you speak to Jajax here in the infirmary and prepare to return with him to his city, ${PLAYER}. We must learn what we can of the situation in Umbar now that the threat posed by the Song of Waves and Wind has been eliminated.'
Ioreth sputters to herself with disbelief.
Queen Arwen smiles at you and turns her attention to her injured husband.

<rgb=#00FF00>When you complete this quest, you will sail back to Umbar with Jajax to carry out King Elessar's wishes.</rgb>
'Yes, I understand. When we sailed from Umbar Baharbêl, the city was in turmoil, and my brother was somehow in the middle of it! Let us return to the Sail-haven and learn what happened while we were gone. I will speak with you not far from the Beacon-gate when we have arrived. I have many questions.
'Does the Kindred rule still? Might there be a reward for those of us who fought to protect both Gondor and Umbar from the ravages of the Song? King Elessar is not the only one who wants answers, ${PLAYER}! Let us go at once!'
'Speak to Jajax and return with him to Umbar. I must know the state of that city, and the position of its ruling Kindred.'
Queen Arwen and the healer Ioreth arrive at the King's bedside
King Elessar recovers from his wound in the Harlond infirmary.
Queen Arwen and Ioreth the Healer have come to the Harlond infirmary.
'He has asked to see you. Disturb him not overlong! But I would not dare to keep you from him, lest I risk either your ire or that of the King!'

The King smiles at you, and you are reassured to see the return of his strength.
'My friend, I am glad to see you survived the battle! The reports I have heard tell me the threat of the Song is ended.'
You tell King Elessar that Aphadaer has paid for his treachery, and both Nakási and Balakhâd perished during the fighting. He nods.
'Would that we could have dissuaded them from this course, but alas! Only rarely is that possible. I confess to you it never occurred to me that Aphadaer could have been the supporter of the Heirs of Castamir whose presence we suspected in Minas Tirith. The gaze of my suspicion turned always to those who wielded greater power than my groom of horses! And yet the Heirsworn prized his reports, believing he was always only moments away from wielding the blade that would end my life. Surely there were opportunities to be had before today, ${PLAYER}?
'This I believe, for it seems to fit every fact. While the Harlond burned, Aphadaer stood near enough to me to whisper his battle-cry in my ear. \qFor the Heirs of Castamir!\q he said as he slipped his knife beneath my armour, and I all unsuspecting. How then did his blade not pierce a vital organ? How could he inflict this wound with such murderous intent and yet not spill the last of my life's blood?
'I think our tour of King's Gondor planted a seed, ${PLAYER}. When he travelled with us to Anfalas and to Pinnath Gelin, he did so intending to serve the interests of the Heirs of Castamir, but I think our journey caused a sapling to grow within his heart. When today he saw the opportunity to carry out his intention, I believe he was unable to fully wield the blade that could end my life, and his aim went astray, despite his purpose.
'None can say if this be truly so, but that is my belief. I weep not for Aphadaer, but I hail him for my life, even as he sought the taking of it.'
'Do not make the King wait! He wants to speak to you and hear that the battle is ended!'

Ioreth sputters madly, for once at a loss for words.
'The Queen asked me to attend her as she came to the Harlond. Is it true that Aphadaer thought to attack the King? Oh me! Oh my!'
You tell Ioreth that the groom attempted to kill the King, but was unsuccessful in the attempt and perished defending Balakhâd, son of Balakhôr. She nods sagely, overcoming her surprise.
'I always suspected he was a villain, ${PLAYER}. Did I not tell you as we journeyed in Outer Gondor that he was up to no good? Let none say Ioreth fails to see things as they are!'

Arwen smiles at you warmly.
'I am once again in your debt, dear ${PLAYER}! My husband is ever eager to charge near and far in support of his people. Perhaps this bed will keep him from embarking upon foolish errands for a time!
'A short time only, I suspect. I am told his wound is shallow, and it would take one of more severity to keep him from tending to the needs of his people! But today he will rest, and for that I am grateful.'
'I mourn the loss of so much life, but I am grateful for such heroes as you, my friend. Without your aid the cost of this day would have been much worse.'

'I fear my knowledge has reached its limit. There is much we still do not know about this terrible blight. We need specialists to contend with this irrepressible pestilence. There are scholars with much more experience than I in Kighân.
'You should journey to Sormedân. The Pohâni Khâbakh lives there. He has special knowledge about diseases and pestilences. Despite that, I believe you will find his company quite warm and agreeable!
'Seek out Elder Jurmêna, she will know where to find Khâbakh.'

'Yes, I know where Khâbakh is. But he is not here, and I do not know you. I will offer you a fair deal. Help our people with some of their troubles, and I will know you mean both Khâbakh and us no harm. Do that, and I will tell you where he has gone.'

'Yes, you have proven you mean us no ill will. You may go in peace, and with our blessing, outsider.
'Khâbakh was on his way to Zajâna, when he was waylaid by the warleader encamped south-west of here, in Ingar-garâsh. I know not where he is now. Though she says she means no harm to the people of Kighân, I don't trust this warleader. You should have words with her, she will know Khâbakh's whereabouts.'

'It is you! A fine sight for sore eyes you are, ${PLAYER}. We have much to discuss.
'Khâbakh? Yes, he came through here. Numûru questioned him for knowledge as to the Ordâkhai movements, but he had none. As a scholar - I believe they call them Pohâni here - he had little enough knowledge that could help us. He moved on to Zajâna. However, while you are here, there are several matters in which I would request your counsel.'

'Could I have a moment of your time, outsider? I work the land, and for many years the orchards and the bees have both been kind to my family and our village. But recently, that has all changed.
'We have long worked with the bees of Medân Makhai, growing their hives and taking a share of their honeycomb to feed our families. However, a new, dark queen recently took root, driving out the former queen. The bees are newly aggressive, stinging us if we even go near their hives. We rely on their honey to feed our families and to trade with others for their goods. This winter will be a harsh one indeed if the hives remain closed to us.
'Will you defeat this new queen? I managed to save the existing queen, though she was injured. Defeat the new queen, and I will be able to return the old queen back to her proper place in the hive.'

'There are precious few who see more into Adagím than we here in Sormedân. The trees are unnatural there, restless and malevolent, with an ill will toward Men and beasts. There is a rot in Adagím, that long have we spent our energy pushing back. Recently, that rot has moved fully to our outskirts.
'There is an orchard overtaken with this rot not far from here, the Moulder-grove. Some call it Shádhag. By any name it's evil, a source of the rot flooding in from Adagím. There the trees have made their camp and seek to spread that rot further into Kighân.
'We cannot allow that. The whole of Kighân relies on our orchards and cattle. If that rot comes any closer, I fear not just for our lives, but for all of Kighân.
'Will you go to the Moulder-grove, burn the afflicted saplings of the malevolent trees, that their rot not spread further into Kighân?'

'Trees shouldn't move - unnatural things. Sormedân is in your debt, and Zajâna too. All of Kighân relies on us to keep their bellies full, and you have given us more time before this blight encroaches once more.'

'I propose we find a way into the servant's quarters of the palace and see for ourselves if the staff remains and if they need our help. Not every person from Ordâkh need be our enemy.'

'It seems you are being put to work! Apologies, friend!
'While you are helping the locals, we will negotiate with Unusâli. Ahâba would be a perfect staging area for our soldiers to gather, but I will not force anything upon the Beltáni if they are unwilling to join our fight.'

'Unusâli seems to be a hard woman, but I suspect she only wishes to protect her village. The Ordâkhai have caused these people much grief over the years, and I do not blame her for being slow to trust.
'This will be my first real chance to prove myself to Mizâdi as her diplomat. I believe I can make headway on this negotiation by appealing to our shared enemy, and their similar pasts....'

'I believe your Shâra when she says she wants to protect us from the Ordâkhai, but I sense you want something from us in return. We are not ones to trust outsiders so easily, not after our many years of resistance to Ordâkh. If you want an alliance, you will need to prove yourselves to us.
'It is simple. Help the Beltáni, and we will help you.'

'My people are pleased with your work. You may stay.
'While you were gone, Mizâdi and I spoke of how she became Shâra of Renewed Hamât. We share a bond: the cruelty of Ordâkh took both our husbands. We have agreed to help each other claim vengeance.
'When the forces of Hamât gather before they march to make war on Emax Dûl, they may make camp in Ahâba. We will then add who we can to your host. May the Beltáni finally be free.'

'Our captured soldiers are inside the prison or the nearby pit-mine somewhere, I am sure of it, but they are not the only ones. The Ordâkhai have sent captured people from all over Shagâna here to work themselves to death. A few of these thralls have managed to escape. I found them first, and they showed me this place. It is not much of a camp, but it is safe.'

'Another woman seeking to overthrow the Ordâkhai, eh? I expect us all to become fast friends!
'Hanâbu hides it well, but I can tell from the way he speaks of her that this Damakhêra Ardu is more than just his superior. I do not think she will be arriving with the host he expects, based on his sullen demeanor.
'I have a feeling we will be meeting her sooner than later to fight this war together. I look forward to hunting the Ordâkhai down with yet another powerful woman with a grudge! Haha!'

'There is much to discuss with your diplomat, and there is much to do to prepare the camp before our host arrives, but I have a request for you in the mean time, ${PLAYER}.
'Some of my men were taken by the Ordâkhai. We believe they are being held in Esh Mêkag, the Silent Mouth. I know little about it, save its reputation: a prison where Men are taken to have their spirits and bodies broken. I sent a scout, Arâniz, to find the prison and to see if he can get our soldiers out, but he has yet to report back. Find him, and see what you can do to help.'

'Captain Hanâbu seems grateful for our aid. A promising start, but Damakhêra Ardu is not an easy woman to impress. At least, not from what I have heard. From all accounts she is both fearless and ferocious!
'While you are assisting with the situation in Esh Mêkag, I will be negotiating on behalf of our Shâra. Once the Aradûni arrive, we will lead them to our gathering point: Ahâba. Bring anyone you can free from the prison with you when you return. We will need as large a force as we can possibly muster to face the fortress Emax Dûl.'

'Worry not! I will help the Aradûni cross the desert when they arrive. Now go, for you are needed elsewhere! There are many Beltáni captive in Esh Mêkag, as well. You can tell me of your success when we next meet.'

'They were no match for the Subuzûri. We now hold this side of the bridge, but we do not want the Ordâkhai to know this quite yet. Our plan depends on it.'

'Even if we cannot be sure that Kotráka Saiya's help will turn the tide of the coming battle in our favour, the time to act is now. Góramul Sai knows we are here, and will attack Ahâba again unless we can push him into a defensive position in his fortress. You will begin that push.
'There is an Ordâkhai camp between here and Emax Dûl called Jolakhúro. I want you and Captain Hanâbu to attack it. This will both force them to retreat behind their walls, and clear the road for the rest of our troops to get into position to siege the city.

Ishími, the Anguished Wind

'The howling wind had abated! You have truly done it! You have truly proven yourself friends of the Aradûni.
'I will speak with Mizâdi on behalf of Damakhêra Ardu. I believe an alliance would benefit both Hamât and Aradûn. Together, we will attack Emax Dûl and push the Ordâkhai from these lands!'

'It is as I thought. Ishími is enraged by our attempts to banish it. Look, it manifests on the ridge near the statue of Izighûz Menûndari! It gathers for a final attack! Ready yourself!
'We must place a ward near that whirlwind, forcing it to coalesce itself into something we can fight.'

'It is done. Ishími is banished, and should no longer trouble the Aradûni.
'You must understand, however, that it is not banished for good, it has just been forced to move. I may be the elder Kâparai, but even I am not powerful enough to permanently banish a spirit of such malevolence. I fear Ishími may haunt Shagâna forever, lest we discover what it really is, and what unleashed it.'

'I am Captain Hanâbu of the Aradûni, the Servants. Like Hamât Renewed, we have risen to reclaim our ancestral lands from Ordâkh. What was once Nísaka will be Aradûn, by will of our leader, Damakhêra Ardu.
'I have led this group of soldiers ahead to scout Idagâl, in preparation for our larger force to arrive. We mean to make war on the Ordâkhai, starting with their fortress at Emax Dûl. I thought it fitting to make our first camp under the Dawn-warden, the hero-king Izighûz Menûndari himself, but perhaps he does not look favourably upon us!
'Something haunts this place: a foul, torturing wind. It keeps us from Emax Dûl! We cannot even think straight, let alone plan our invasion!'

'It is good I came with you. I will banish Ishími from this place, and you will assist me.
'Take these wards. We will place them around the camp, and tend to the Aradûni's broken spirits. This will enrage Ishími, and he will manifest to stop us. We will be ready.'

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. I am Tálbiral and this grove is Laivárth. Welcome.
'You do not seem familiar with Adagím. This marsh can be quite dangerous. Please, allow me to tell you more.'

'While travelling through the marsh, you have seen for yourself the rot that has consumed the forests of Adagím, or as it is better known in this time, the Moulderwood. This rot is known as the Pale Blight. You may have seen how it affected some of the lands to the west as well.
'The Kintai here are doing everything we can to fight back against this infection, but our efforts seem to be a losing battle. This used to be a beautiful and green land until years ago when the Ordâkhai invaded and cracked the earth with the Din of Stone. That unleashed a pestilence that killed the trees, poisoned our waters, and caused fungal growths to appear everywhere.'
Tálbiral looks distraught from recalling the events.
'Sorry, friend. I need but a moment.'

Tálbiral clears his throat and readies himself to speak again.
'Thank you. These events have caused us so much pain. They can be difficult to recall.
'We are doing what we can, but my people have abandoned many of our groves already and left them to fester with rot and become overwhelmed with the beasts of the forest, now twisted by the blight consuming them.
'This grove, Laivárth, and the main settlement to the east, Sul Madásh, are the last that remain unspoiled. Though as you can see, it is not without a cost.
'I worry this land and my people will eventually fall. You are either brave or naive to come here, ${CLASS}. Though if you wish to help, there is much you can do in these marshes.'

Faeron turns to you, looking deeply concerned.
'I don't like this, ${PLAYER}. These people need our help. Let's return to camp and speak with Rhadrog.'
He turns back to face Nabatínu.
'We must return to two of our company, camped to the south. With your permission, I would like to bring them here, and together we will do what we can to help you. You aren't the only ones who have been forced into labour by evil. King Elessar did not leave the Nurnhoth or the Stout-axes to suffer, and I would not leave yours, if I can help it.'
Nabatínu nods his consent.
'Good. ${PLAYER}, I will meet you back at the camp.'
'Ah, you return. I was just talking to Faeron. It seems we came here looking for one foulness only to find another. I agree that something must be done. It's time to break camp.'

'Alas, no, there is not enough life remaining in An Shêru for such rot to take hold. No, the danger I speak of comes in the form of a new breed of Orc, with size and strength unlike any other I have known. They patrol the roads, killing any they come across, though they often take some prisoner. I shudder to think what becomes of those poor souls.
'There are also two strongholds of Ordâkhai of an unusual sort. They are zealots who do not believe Barkhûsh is truly defeated. They continue to worship him and believe that upon his return, he will reward their loyalty with power untold. They are fools, but are dangerous fools. They are led by a coven of Bokhór, witches with the power to ensnare Men's will.
'In fact...'
The man looks around at his fellows, dirty and hungry, living uncomfortably within a crypt.
'We were all once such thralls. Játsakori, we were called. Our wills were taken from us, and we were forced to work in mines for the Ordâkhai. I was able to break my mind free from their spell at the moment Barkhûsh was defeated, as the casters of the spell suffered a moment of weakness. I was able to escape, and since then, I have been helping as many people as I can break free from thralldom.
'Many have left to seek life and healing elsewhere, but those of us who remain do so intending to free the others. We have found the last of our number increasingly difficult to save. Their minds are bound tightly with the evil magic.'

'Who... who are you?'
The man nervously grips his weapon, but does not threaten you with it. You tell him that you are travellers and are curious about them.
'There is no such thing as a traveller who just happens to be passing through here. But I think you should speak to our leader, Nabatínu. You will find him within.'

'And who are you, strangers, who traverse this land without fear? You are no Ordâkhai, and this one is a Man of the West who makes no effort to hide his origin. If you are enemies of Ordâkh, know that you are among friends.
'If your heading is further west, then I must caution against it. Only death and danger lie in that direction.'

'You surmise correctly that we are enemies of Ordâkh. We are capable warriors, however, and would travel west no matter the danger, should our business take us there. It was only a short time ago that we were in the cursed land of Mordor. I have my doubts that An Shêru has more danger to offer than the very lair of the Enemy.
'Tell me more of this danger to the west. I search for signs of an evil blight infecting the land, covering it in rot and sickness.'
The guard has directed you to speak with his leader, Nabatínu, inside Gadim-ûn, a place in north-eastern An Shêru.

'There is but one way to solve the mystery of who these people are, and that is to speak with them. Let us approach with caution and greet them with kindness, and see what comes of it. Go on, I will be right behind you.'
The Plight of the Játsakori
Faeron suggested talking to these people to learn more about them. You should talk to the guard at Gadim-ûn, a place in north-eastern An Shêru.

'You appear to be a traveller. Are you travelling westward? I am on an important errand on behalf of Doorward Azagâya. If you are going to An Shêru, might I accompany you? It is a perilous land, and I dare not travel alone. In fact, to tell you the truth, I had already joined a caravan that had not gotten far on the road before it was attacked.'
She looks like she might start to cry, but is able to compose herself after taking a deep breath.
'Despite this event, I must carry on. I will not return to Zajâna in disgrace. Instead, I need more capable travelling companions, and you look quite capable indeed. If you would not mind travelling together, I will meet you at a place near a cross-roads that I think would be a good spot to rest for the night. I can show you on the map.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}! Let us make haste!'

'You're here, good. I did a little scouting, and it looks like the Utûgi are the ones watching over the prisoners. I think it's safe to assume that the Utûgi gaolers are the ones who will have the keys to the cages. You'll have to defeat them to find the keys.
'When you free the captives, send them in my direction, and I will get them safely out of the camp. Meet us back here when you are done, and we will bring them with us to Gadim-ûn.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! Let us make haste!'

'I cannot believe it, Tâklu lives! I can never thank you enough, ${PLAYER}. Truth be told, we only knew one another briefly, but thinking that I alone survived the attack was a heavy burden to carry. I still mourn for the others that did not make it, but Tâklu being here is a miracle!'

'I owe you my life, and I can never repay you. I thank you with all of my heart. I have a daughter in Zajâna, and all I could think about inside that cage was that I would not get to see her grow up.'
You ask him what the Utûgi and Ordâkhai were doing with captives.
'Torturing us. Asking us questions to which everyone knows the answer. What cities are the largest, who rules where, that sort of thing. I told the truth, there is no reason not to! But Râkdakul, the Elder Orc leader, accused me of misleading them, and the torturers continued their horrific acts.
'The most unfortunate of the prisoners are brought up the pass and inside the mountain. They do not come out. Rumour has it, they only come out in pieces. It is Ombátha enjoying her playthings, we were told. I don't know what they were interested in, other than our suffering. I am sorry that I cannot tell you more.'

'This is disturbing news. I'm most glad we were able to get those people out of there. This Ombátha sounds just as dreadful as Nabatínu described her. Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for your role in this. It seems that you have saved these people from a fate worse than death.
'The leaders at Kôth Rau will need to be dealt with eventually, but we can only wait to see what tomorrow brings. I suggest waiting until the time is right, and in the meantime, you can maybe help Khagâmi with her quest to find the home of the Temámir in An Shêru.'

'Indeed, ${PLAYER}! This belonged to Tâklu, one of my companions from Zajâna! Where did you find this?'
You tell her about Kôth Rau and the prisoners you saw there.
'Níkhu! Then he may yet live! And others as well! I thought myself the only survivor. When they attacked us, I fell and... well, to tell you truly, I rolled down a hill, and out of sight of the horrific scene. I am no warrior and remained hidden for quite some time. By the time I gathered my courage to return to the road, there was nothing left of the caravan but blood soaking into the sand.
'Please ${PLAYER}, you must rescue them!'

You explain the situation to Rhadrog, and he nods.
'We cannot in good conscience leave those people there. I would also like to know why Utûgi are capturing people and bringing them to the Ordâkhai. We must free the captives and see if they know what the Ordâkhai are planning.
'I will go with you. Meet me outside Kôth Rau, and we will make a plan from there.'

Talk to Andûmu in Gadim-ûn

'I cannot help but be curious about the people buried here. They are unlike any Shagâni I know. How long ago did they live? Why are there so many, and why are they in this place?
'It is common in many cultures to include personal items when they lay their dead to rest. It is bad luck to disturb the dead in their graves, but these poor souls are already disturbed. If you would be willing to humour me, would you mind taking a look at some of the graves and examining their belongings? There are many graves to be found in Naxar Dâl to the north, and Khâb Daku to the south. Perhaps the items they were buried with could tell us something of their story.'

'Tell me, friend. What did you learn?'
You tell him that many of these people appear to have been wealthy and learned, and traded with the Temámir as well as Gondor. They were not without soldiers but were probably not particularly warlike, and are likely the ancestors of the Shagâni living here today.
'Do you think they lived in Zajâna of old? Much trade happens there, I believe. They say it was founded by the Kingdom of Nísaka, which fell even before my grandfather was born. The Ordâkhai destroyed Nísaka on their march northward. Zajâna is all that remains of that kingdom.
'Well, Zajâna, and perhaps this boneyard! I fear these wights, as any sane man should, but it is also fascinating to me that these bodies belonged to people of a different time. It sounds like many of them had good lives.
'Thank you for taking the time for this.'

'I see you have made it out of the crypts in one piece. And there were more supplies inside, as I suspected! It gladdens me that I did not send you into that horrid place for no reason! I will begin taking inventory of what you have gotten for us immediately.

'Hashtal-gûr.'
The man bows to you politely.
'Is it true that you have come to help us? My name is Andûmu and Nabatínu has put me in charge of our supplies. One of the reasons we are here in Gadim-ûn is that there was a long-forgotten Ordâkhai supply cache left in this place, which we have been able to live off of for a time. Unfortunately, we are quickly running out of these supplies.
'I have a suspicion that there are more supply crates hidden away inside the crypts, but I am unfit for that sort of... adventure. I am sure you have noticed that the Dead in An Shêru are not at rest and pose a great danger to us.
'You, however, seem to be able to handle them. If you would go into the crypts and search for more supplies, it would surely increase our chances of survival.'

'It is not unusual for jázgai to come skulking around our tents at night. The smell of our food must draw them to us. I fear it is only a matter of time before those scavengers become brave or desperate enough to attack someone. Once, they feared people, but they seem to be getting a little too comfortable with us.
'Do you think you would be able to thin their numbers before they try to steal our supplies, or worse yet, hurt somebody? It would do us much good if they feared us once more. Their den is on a hill south of here called Spoiler's Crag.'
'You have taken care of the jázgai, ${PLAYER}? That is wonderful news. Many people will sleep better at night, myself included. Thank you!'

Gíshgi is uncomfortable with the nearby wights. She has a theory that they may fear flames enough that placing lit torches at the entrances to the crypts would keep the wights within, and has asked you to try it. There are crypt entrances at Gadim-ûn, Naxar Dâl, and the Crypts of Khâb Daku in north-eastern An Shêru.

You have placed lit torches at the entrances of the crypts in north-eastern An Shêru in an effort to ward off the wights and keep them inside, where they belong. You should return to Gíshgi in Gadim-ûn and tell her of your success.
Talk to Gíshgi in Gadim-ûn

'I do not like it here, surrounded by these wights. They are ghastly, but Nabatínu insists they are what keep us hidden. The Ordâkhai dare not come here to the Mashâli Barrens for fear of them, and says the mindless things unknowingly protect us!
'The wights are just as likely to kill us as the Ordâkhai, so I do not know how this is better. It does seem to me, though, that these wights shy away from fire. I cannot help but wonder if placing burning torches at the crypt entrances would keep them confined and away from our camp.
'Would you try it? Three torches at the entrances to the three main crypts should do.'

'I am glad you have not joined the unliving! Did you place the torches?'
You tell her you did.
'We will wait and see if it helps contain them. Whether it does or not, I am grateful to you.'
A Barricade of Light

'${PLAYER}, I loathe these wights so. Why are they tramping about instead of lying in their graves where they belong?
'You are courageous and do not fear them as I do. Do you think if you entered the crypts below, you would find some clue as to why they are not at peace?'

You tell Gíshgi of the disturbing whispers and wailing you came across in the crypts, and how you were able to dispel them by countering them with a happier song.
The woman gasps.
'${PLAYER}, this must be what they call Ishími! The Anguished Wind. People have been claiming to sometimes hear it since Barkhûsh fell. I know not if it has any truth to it, but some say it is the voice of one who was a king in these lands, long ago.
'I cannot imagine what that has to do with Barkhûsh, though. Thank you for your bravery!'

'As you have seen, I am very welcoming to most anyone who would spend their coin at Khanâg Gur. Several nights ago, there was a bit of a scrap in the Camel and Chimes, our tavern. I have no problem with the men settling arguments with their fists, but on this particular night, a woman in my service was brutalized and killed by men from Zakhûr.'
The expression on Khanda-mashár's face grows dark.
'We may disregard certain laws, but we are civilized men, not beasts. This sort of thing will not be tolerated, and this act will not go unpunished. Should you happen to find yourself in Zakhûr, I ask that you defeat some of those animals in combat. Do so in my name, and you will be rewarded with my favour as well as my coin.'
'It is done then? The animals of Zakhûr have been defeated? I am impressed, ${PLAYER}, as well as grateful. Here is your reward, as promised.'

Birêt-kibur collected (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gôbezhir has asked you to keep an eye out while travelling through An Shêru for birêt-kibur, iron fallen from the sky. Birêt-kibur could be found anywhere in An Shêru.

'Well met, ${PLAYER}! Your arrival at Jiret-menêsh is grist for the mill, as they say! You are quite the lively topic of conversation. I have not spoken to a visitor in one hundred years!'
The jovial dwarf chuckles and bows to you.
'But how rude of me, I should introduce myself! I am Gôbezhir Firmhand, master smith of Jiret-menêsh. I have heard you are well-travelled! I envy the sights you have likely seen, though I am no warrior and am happy to live a quiet life.
'I wonder, though, if you would be willing to keep an eye out for something for me. Since returning to the surface, I have had unusual dreams. I dream of a starlit night with falling stars trailing fire, streaking across the sky. They look so close, you could almost touch them. It is not unheard of for such things to be seen from the Height of the Sky, but I cannot help but feel like these dreams bear a message.
'When these stars land, they leave iron ore unlike any from a mine. It is stronger, resistant to rust, and must be worked at a higher temperature. We call it birêt-kibur, 'the noble iron'. I believe in my heart that I am to use birêt-kibur to craft an axe. Not just any axe, but my life's masterwork. I must do this thing, but I am only suited for the forge, not for adventures in the wilds.
'If you happen to come across birêt-kibur during your travels in An Shêru, would you collect it and bring it to me?'

'The Ordâkhai mine is an open pit to this day? Zigêt! I hope that one day we are able to oust those worthless wretches. Or better yet, someone else does it for us! This Arch of Adazâr is intriguing. From your description, it sounds like it is the work of Shagâni Men, before the coming of Ordâkh.
'Well, ${PLAYER}, you have given me much to think about! Thank you for sating my curiosity.'

'Well met, traveller. I have a question, and I was wondering if you could help me find the answer. Historically, we have had many problems with Men coming to An Shêru to pillage its once rich resources. The result is the landscape you see around you today.
'In an earlier age, we went to war with Men who wanted the greatest treasure of all, Jiret-menêsh. This war ended with an agreement that Men were allowed to mine in other parts of An Shêru, but there were provisions that they cause no harm to the land and do not mar its beauty. Their king swore an Oath to this, and for many generations of Men, the Oath was kept.
'When these Ordâkhai arrived from the south, they did not know of this oath, though it was made on behalf of all Men. But I do not think they would have cared, even if they had known about it. They cut down and hauled off all of the trees to fuel their war machine. They dug pit-mines... horrible things, those.
'Their final blow was the Din of Stone, causing massive unnatural earthquakes that surely collapsed many mines and stopped the flow of the Usâl River. It was then that Châmelek Gêta had had enough of Men and sealed the doors of Jiret-menêsh shut to the outside world.
'I cannot help but wonder, though, did all of the other mines collapse? Could any of them be reopened? In what state will we find the pit-mines? Since you are unafraid to traverse this land, would you be willing to visit these locations and tell me how they fare? I am most curious about Erakúndo, Gebarakór, Adazâr, and Lâkindar.'

'${PLAYER}, what brings you to me?'
You ask Halshûm if he has any interest in a trade agreement with a Temámir jeweller from Jiret-menêsh.
'Interesting... I myself am not, but I know many people and may still be able to help you. I would need you to do something for me first, of course.
'I sell supplies to the Ordâkhai at Kôth Rau. It is why they allow us to keep Khanâg Gur in business. Among those supplies are foodstuffs that resist spoilage - very useful for an army. I happen to find myself with more of these rations than the Ordâkhai wanted to buy, and I need to sell them. There is gold invested in them, and I need it back.
'Should you find yourself in Kôth Rau, and the rations they bought from me happened to go missing, they would need to replace their lost supplies. Do you follow me? If this thing happens, I will see to it that this jeweller of yours has a buyer.'

'${PLAYER}, you were gone so long, I thought you had forgotten me, but you went all the way to Zajâna on my behalf? I do not know that I am worthy of such effort, but thank you! I have many rings and pendants ready to trade, but I look forward to talking to this Zarzûmir about what is best for selling, and make more of that!
'This brings me so much joy, ${PLAYER}! I cannot wait to get back to my workbench!'

Upon seeing you return with the crates, Halshûm laughs.
'You did it! If you want to become a Khanda-khêl, let me know. I think you would fit in well.
'I do not want those rations, though. My men have finer tastes than Ordâkhai soldiers do, and I do not expect the dullards to buy them for a third time.'
He chuckles before waving his hand in the air dismissively.
'Do with them what you will. Just get them out of here.'
'Now, on with our business. In Zajâna there is a man named Zarzûmir. You will find him lingering in one of the marketplaces. He would give your jeweller a fair price, and he has caravans that pass through An Shêru, so he could pick up the goods.
'I do business with him myself. He pays me to ensure his caravans make it through An Shêru without being attacked by bandits. Which is very easy to do. I just order them to leave him alone.'
Halshûm laughs again at his own cleverness.
'Anyway, tell Zarzûmir Khanda-mashár sent you, and he will not refuse your offer.'

'${PLAYER}, you return! But why?'
You present the Ordâkhai rations to the leader of the Jatsakóri and ask Nabatínu if he wants them.
'By the stars, yes! You know we would not turn away any unspoiled food. Thank you for remembering us. You are a treasure.'

'Saráz záro-dan, what can Zarzûmir do for you?'
You tell the man that you were sent by Khanda-mashár and that there is a Temámir jeweller in Jiret-menêsh who is looking for a partner to whom she can sell her creations.
'Jewellery? Made by a dwarf in the legendary Jiret-menêsh? Yes, I think I could sell those kinds of goods, no problem, and make a tidy sum at the same time.
'Not that it seems I have a choice, but you do not need to tell me twice to do something that brings in coin. I will assume Khanda-mashár will want a cut, but I will work that out with him. He will also tell me where to find Jiret-menêsh. There are few things he doesn't know. Thank you for bringing me this.'

Talk to Mêshaget
'Ah, we have our invite. Come, let us not waste any time.'
'Oh, that is a handsome treasure indeed! Yes, she would find that agreeable. I already sent a messenger inside to request an audience. They should be back at any moment.'

'That went well! She was in a good mood today!'
Mêshaget laughs at your skepticism.
'Truly, if she did not like you, she would have said very little and would have told you to finish your business here and be on your way.'

'My grandson speaks very highly of you. I wonder if you are truly worthy of his praise.'
You bow and hand her the box of treasure. She opens it and briefly appraises the gold and gems within.
'You have done well. I am told this was taken from the Ordâkhai of Shêru. A difficult deed as well as a noble gesture, though I am sure you received counselling from one who knows me well.'
She hands the box off to her steward as Mêshaget's cheeks grow flush with embarrassment.
'It is of no matter. Thank you for the fine gift. For the sake of all, I hope you did not lead our enemy to our front door. I know not if you are aware of the danger Mêshaget has put himself and some of our kin in. My grandson fought hard to have the doors of Jiret-menêsh reopened. It is an understandable desire for those of less than one-hundred years, but it is foolhardy nonetheless.
'Though Barkhûsh is no more, evil has not died with him. Evil lives ever on in the hearts of Men, and has broken the land beyond repair. Even the Avabár-kinta have not the power to heal this land. But still, the mountain provides all that we need. We do not need to involve ourselves with anything outside of our Halls, and to do so is to invite disaster.
'Mêshaget is naive and does not know what the real world is like. He and others of his generation have been sheltered their whole lives. I understand the yearning for more, but the world that they yearn for does not exist. I must allow them to make their own mistakes, and only hope that the lesson does not cost them their lives.
'After much debate, I relented and allowed those who wished to surface to do so, with some terms. My first priority is to protect these halls and the dwarves within. Therefore, should we be subject to attack, the doors will close immediately. We will not hold them open for anyone, including my grandson. We will send no help, and they will be left to whatever fate befalls them.
'Honestly, I regret my decision to allow this. I see no good that can come of it. But a promise from a Gêta will not be broken.'
She leans back in her throne.
'You may come and go as you will, ${PLAYER}, but know this: should you lead the Ordâkhai to Jiret-menêsh, you would be responsible for the deaths of many innocent dwarves.'
Time to go!

'I would like to introduce you to Châmelek Gêta. She can be a stubborn old mule, though. I can say this only because she is my grandmother!'
He gives you a hearty laugh from his belly, and you get the sense that, despite his words, he loves the \qstubborn old mule.\q
'She is not fond of us being on the surface at all, so I expect her to be disagreeable about having visitors. I suggest that by bringing her a gift worthy of a Gêta, she would look upon you with a more open mind.
'The Ordâkhai outpost of Onabóha is comically close to Jiret-menêsh, considering the men there have yet to notice us! It would be more humorous if they didn't pose a deadly threat to us. Should Kôth Rau send them troops to support an attack on us, we would stand very little chance of survival.
'Regardless, if you went to Onabóha and stole a treasure from the Ordâkhai, it would be doubly impressive! Not only would you give her a treasure, but one from her feared enemy! Not being able to pay their soldiers would also make things difficult for them. It would also show the Gêta that they are not as invulnerable as she seems to believe.'

'${PLAYER}, there you are! I wanted to thank you for all you have done. Getting me here safely was no small thing, and rescuing Tâklu was an extraordinary act. I dare say I have never met another like you, so willing to help others. I will make sure Doorward Azagâya knows of your heroism.'
Khagâmi gives you a respectful bow.

'Who is this, then, a friend of Mêshaget? A ${RACE} offering help, no less! Interesting indeed!
'I am Mísikir and see after the safety of all at Jiret-menêsh. I assume you are quite trustworthy, else Mêshaget would not have sent you to me. Aye, there is one simple task for which I could use someone's help. I apologize that it is not very exciting, but still, it must be done!
'An Shêru is as dry as Châmelek Gêta's sense of humour, and standing guard is thirsty work. Please, take this water-skin to Cherêka, who is keeping watch over the road that all must take to approach the mountain. She will be somewhere nearby, looking down upon the road.'

'By my mother's beard! You have good timing, my friend. My own water-skin is empty, and I was just thinking of my thirst.
'I must tell you that I have never spoken to a ${RACE} before. You are taller than I expected! Only recently has the Gêta allowed us to come to the surface, and I am a mere forty-seven years of age, so I have only recently seen the open sky for the first time. Its vastness is intimidating, and I have no love for the wind!
'This is a good experience, though. One must be comfortable with being uncomfortable if they wish to travel, or so I am told, and I would like to see the Shoreward Stone one day!
'My thanks for the water, friend, and send the captain my thanks as well.'
'I thank you for your help! A woman came by earlier, asking after your whereabouts. She said she wanted to talk to you, but I am unsure where she went.'
'Khagâmi's words speak true, my friend. Your willingness to help people tells much about your noble nature. You are exceptional, indeed!'

She dubbed him \qthe Sky-hungry\q and cast him out from the city, telling him that if he craved the sky so much, he could go die under it.
'I expect she thought he did just that, but the world is not as perilous as she believes. He has had many adventures and has returned to An Shêru. He can often be found in Khanâg Gur.

If you were able to collect eight of these glands, I could sell them to the right buyer for enough to cover my debt. Would you aid an old, battered dwarf?

Talk to Châmelek Gêta

'Châmelek Gêta, you are wise, and only want what is best for all of us. That, I understand and respect. I was not unaware of what lurks within the Quelling-house, and I chose to enter this forbidden place, risking my own life, for the chance to bring safety to our people without sacrificing their freedom.
'I do not believe that things must be only one way or the other. We can have both security and freedom if we fight for it! Barkhûsh and his priests are gone. Ordâkh has no Hûl... or perhaps too many Hûls, I am not sure. By all accounts, they should be weakened! We can surely defend ourselves against them, and can do so with allies, if only we allowed ourselves to make some.
'If Zajâna were to find value in trading with us, they would likely be willing to help defend us, should it become necessary. Evil does not lurk in the hearts of all Men. It was Men who killed the Hûl in Gondor, and it is said that the same Men helped bring Barkhûsh to his knees. And what of the Shoreward Stone? As Temámir, we are not friendless or alone.
'I only ask that you examine the works of Semayâti the Unyielding, and allow for further discussion.'
Mêshaget bows to the Gêta respectfully as he ends his argument.

After a moment of silence, Châmelek Gêta responds.
'It will be as you say. I will look upon what is in this book, and we will discuss your proposal. You have not won, Shakâr-inik, I only agree to a discussion!'
She leans forward conspiratorially.
'Speak to me, ${PLAYER}, do you have children? Grandchildren? If not, avoid it at all costs! I fear that as Mêshaget comes into his own, he is becoming more stubborn than I am! One day, he will be Gêta and may do as he wills. Why he is impatient and chooses to spend all of his time fighting with me, I will never know.
'There is a part of me that wishes to punish you for allowing him to endanger himself on such an unwise adventure, but I do not think you would have been able to talk him out of it if you had tried. Instead, I suspect that you are the only reason the fool is still alive. Am I correct?
'Thank you for returning my rough gem to me. I am glad he has you for a friend.'

'I am relieved you came! This place has a foul air. It strikes fear in my heart and makes my hair stand on end! I do not think I could enter were I alone.'
Mêshaget is sweating, visibly afraid of this place and is fighting to gather his courage.
'It is said that inside Lâkindar lies the tomb of a legend, Semayâti the Unyielding. At the time of Lâkindar's height, she was a celebrated Temámir crafter, inventor, and engineer. It is said that there was nothing she could not do well!
'It is believed that upon her passing, she was entombed with her journal, which was filled with many inventions and designs that were never made into reality. According to the history I have read, one of these designs was a plan to fortify Jiret-menêsh against attackers.
'We have been relying on secrecy and ignorance to protect ourselves for one hundred years, ${PLAYER}. It is only a matter of time before those who envy our great wealth decide to take it for themselves, and our lives with it. We will find the tomb of Semayâti the Unyielding and recover her journal. I will convince Châmelek Gêta to make these designs a reality so that we may live as part of the world, and yet also live without fear.
'Please go in ahead of me. I should remain behind for a few minutes to ensure neither of us has been followed, and then I will catch up to you inside.'

'That went better than I expected, ${PLAYER}! Châmelek Gêta may be stone-headed, but she is not blind to reason when it is in front of her. Jiret-menêsh has a bright future ahead, and she will soon see that.
'Thank you for all the help you have given me. You are a steadfast friend, and you came at the right time for when I truly needed one. Sâdikiz crafted his own fate, which I know in my mind, but my heart hurts for what I have done, regardless.
'Should I have shown him mercy? I do not think he would have shown me any, but does that make my wrath warranted? Was a death blow truly necessary? It will be some time before I can sleep easily at night, I think.
'I wish you the best on your travels, ${PLAYER}. May we meet again in more prosperous times.'

'Explain yourselves! Why is my grandson injured, and why is he in my hall instead of my hale-house?'
Châmelek Gêta appears to be furious. Mêshaget hobbles forward and kneels before her, holding out the journal of Semayâti the Unyielding. She snatches it out of his hands and looks it over, flipping through the pages before she pauses, and her look of anger is replaced with one of wonder.
'What is this?'
Humble, and without looking up, Mêshaget says, 'The designs of Semayâti the Unyielding, that we may use to build defences to protect Jiret-menêsh and its people.'
She sets the book aside as Mêshaget returns to his feet.
'You fools went into the Quelling-house!? Did I not tell you that this place is forbidden? Tell me why you disobey me, Mêshaget!'

'I am relieved you came!'

'${PLAYER}, when you met Sâdikiz, what was your opinion of him? Did you think him honourable? It pains me to question the motivations of one I have long considered a mentor and friend, but since we have succeeded in opening the gates, he has started asking many questions he should not. He seems to have no ill will for the hall of his fathers, but I cannot help but wonder now if it was all a lie. A false face to earn my trust and then use me to the ruin of our people.'
The young dwarf looks thoughtful for a moment.
'There is something I must do, and I wonder if you would help me. To the south lies the ruin of Lâkindar. Many refer to it now as The Quelling-house. Lâkindar was once a wealthy mine of the Temámir, but many years ago, the priests of Barkhûsh turned it into a slaughter-house and sacrificed many innocent people there, Man and dwarf alike, to their wicked deity. As you may imagine, Châmelek Gêta has forbidden us from going there. The place is surely cursed.
'But go there I must. Would you accompany me? I will tell you more of our purpose once we arrive. Meet me at the top of the great stair. You will know it when you see it.'

'${PLAYER}, I should tell you of my task and destination. I am on a quest to find an ancient dwarf city called Jiret-menêsh. Tales claim that it has been in An Shêru longer than the sun has been in the sky. It is well documented in the libraries of Zajâna that the Temámir were avid trading partners with Zajâna and others for centuries.
'When Urash-zâl, the Din of Stone, shook the ground and dried the Usâl, the people of Zajâna had their own difficulties. It went unnoticed for some time that all contact with Jiret-menêsh had been lost. Most believe that the Temámir were either all killed or they abandoned this forsaken land, which is quite plausible.
'However, there have recently been whispers that the hearty Dwarves of Jiret-menêsh have emerged from the ground, where they have been hiding in isolation for one hundred years. Doorward Azagâya sent me to investigate the rumours and see if this is true. Should it be so, I am to establish friendly relations with them, and if possible, negotiate terms of establishing trade between our cities.
'Surely you can imagine being the first to... what was that?'

'You were asking about the Pale Blight, yes? I have some information from some tomes I gathered whilst you were attending to the garden. The Kintai are our best source of knowledge for the plight of Adagím. They are reclusive, but our Pohâni have travelled throughout Adagím and Shagâna to document their history and beliefs.
'Several accounts in this \qHistory of Adagím\q mention the Ordâkhai. These Kintai mention Sívigush, some sort of monster or legendary beast, but others blame the coming Ordâkhai who managed somehow to dry the rivers and dam up naturally flowing waters near Adagím. This resulted in Adagím becoming much more marsh and swamp-like, as waters from nearby lakes and ponds overstrode their bounds. Without the rivers to sweep them through, they festered, creating bogs where previously the land had been green and rich with forests.
'The Ordâkhai likely had a hand in creating the conditions for this Pale Blight. I know not how to improve the situation in Adagím, but the forces of Ordâkh ensconced in Emax Dûl may have more answers.'

'You were asking about the Pale Blight, yes? Here it is. Travelling scholars mention a legend among the Kintai that may be relevant. They speak of Sívigush the Earth Terror, a great beast of unimaginable size and ferocity. These accounts say that Sívigush carried within it a great plague, that corrupted all it touched, turning the forests pale and dead wherever it strode.
'These accounts attribute this Pale Blight to Sívigush, and claim it emanated from a place in Adagím once said to be Sívigush's abode. This site was later settled by a group of Men who excavated the area. It is known amongst the Elves as Nagakhêdi's Folly. Apparently the Men who were excavating the site were building a grand abode for their king, Nagakhêdi. Reports disagree here on the details, but each claim that the workers perished to a man within the cursed tunnels.
'This is all rumour and happenstance. But if you are indeed searching for the source of this Pale Blight, you might explore Nagakhêdi's Folly in Adagim. Then tell me what you find. I would love to publish something new about Adagím - as long as I don't have to go there myself. Dreadful place.'
