'You have a look that is familiar to me, friend: the look of a wayfarer! I know it because I possess this same look, the same appearance of one who lives upon the road and travels to distant lands, and never minds the danger!
'I have returned of late from just such a journey, and I am exhausted. Perhaps you can help me finish the task I have begun? It will help protect my village from any who threaten it!
'Take these stones I collected on my latest pilgrimage, and use them to complete the cairn I began by the road just north of Hanamíku. Once you have applied the finishing touches to my incomplete cairn, the enchantment will almost be ready.'
'Use the stones I gave you to complete the cairn I began by the road just north of Hanamíku. Once you have applied the finishing touches to my incomplete cairn, the enchantment will almost be ready.'

'You have done as I asked? I delight to hear it! May the spirit of the Menûndari protect Hanamíku from its enemies!'
You ask why Rashlût believes these cairns will have this effect, and he smiles.
'It is because the distant place from which I have now returned is the mighty statue of the Dawn-warden, far to the north, and the stones with which we complete these cairns are from that sacred ground!
'Here, take these last few stones and complete the cairn I began by the road south of the village. Then the blessing of the Eternal Ruler will keep Hanamíku safe!'
'Use those stones I gave you to complete the cairn I began by the road south of the village. Then the blessing of the Eternal Ruler will keep Hanamíku safe!'

'Let us see what you experienced among the brigands, friend helper!'
Lakhêpi studies the weapons you recovered and listens to your account of the battles you fought.

'When Pasumín came to live in Hanamíku, many years ago, he left his old life behind and started anew, using his skills as a woodworker to repair the buildings and fences of the village. But it was the carving of wooden toys for the children that brought him the most joy; whenever I saw him engaged in that pursuit I saw the light in his eye, and I knew the deeds of his past were far from his thoughts.'

'Everything seems so unreal, ${PLAYER}. We watched the Hamâti soldiers training, and we were captivated by their strength and their force of arms. Their swords shone so brightly! How could they lose against the cowardly Ordâkhai?
'But they were not the ones who did battle at Nakársong! It was the toy-maker Pasumín who fought for us, and it was he who fell defending us! He was no soldier! He was just a toy-maker! Why would he do battle with the Ordâkhai? Why did he fight for us?
'We were cruel to him, ${PLAYER}, and he died to save us. But we did not mean for it to happen.'

'Know this, ${PLAYER}: you are a friend of this guardsman, but not only that. You are a friend of Hanamíku too, and I hope you will remain so. Good fortune and safe journey on your travels.'

'The Ordâkhai passed through my fields as they hurried south, pursued by the forces of Shâra Mizâdi. They were not so hastened they could not cause my farm a great deal of damage, and this they did, burning crops, spilling my grain, and scattering my tools.
'Can you help me put these things right? I also ask that you speak encouraging words to my son Namtâru. He is so dispirited that he refuses to work, and that is unacceptable!'

'How can we hope to carry on? The Ordâkhai would have left our farm alone if they were not being pursued by another army! They only left Kirzâmur in ruin because they did not want Shâra Mizâdi's forces to make use of it!
'My father is too soft-hearted. He should rage against these villains, each and every one, but instead he simply accepts whatever ill fortune comes to him. I cannot believe it!'
'Can you help me put my farm of Kirzâmur right? I also ask that you speak encouraging words to my son Namtâru. He is so dispirited that he refuses to work, and that is unacceptable!'
'Thank you, friend. All things considered, I would say Kirzâmur will recover. We will rebuild the farm, and in mere weeks it will be as if the Ordâkhai were never here.'

'It is only a bit of glass. It is not a gemstone at all, and while it sparkles like a diamond, its true worth to me is one of memory. My wife Ayâri is many years in the ground now, but she fashioned that shovel and its incomparable decoration for me when we first came to Pahar Hatokáli and built our home here at Kirzâmur.
'Namtâru has long believed that if our fortunes run ill, we could sell that shovel and make a new start, and I have not told him otherwise. But even were it a diamond embedded in that shovel, I would not part with this gift of his mother Ayâri. It is simply too precious.

'Well done, my friend. You have now experienced what life is like in my boots for a day. It is a lot of hard work, but I know that without me the work of the soldiers who follow Shâra Mizâdi would be made more difficult, and that keeps me moving forward!

'Tell me a <rgb=#00FF00>story</rgb>!'

'I feel as if this story you have told me teeters right on the edge of something darker. Mohóto's deception is an interesting tale of its own... but what of the man with the beautiful face who spoke to him of the treasure in the first place?'
Lakhêpi shivers.
'I think I would not tell this story. There is something about the man no one knows that fills me with unease.'
'Tell me a <rgb=#00FF00>story</rgb>!'

'Yes, this story is the most complex of all. To the people of Pahar Hatokáli, Shâra Mizâdi is a shining figure who fights before a willing army to free them from the shackles of Ordâkh: she is a symbol of freedom.
'But she is a woman too, and one who has suffered grief and sorrows enough to cause many others to give up her mission. Yet she fights on. I cannot say if her story is a triumph or a tragedy. I wonder what she would say herself?'
Lakhêpi the Far-faring gazes at you expectantly, and you spread your arms wide: you have exhausted the stories you collected. She smiles.
'You have done well, friend helper. These stories will keep me going for many days to come, and I thank you for them, and for your friendship. In honour of that friendship, I will keep the worrying tales of Mashdagâl's ancient mind-tamperers to myself. It is the least I can do.'

'Ebnûr's son Namtâru believed his farmer father possessed a shovel with a diamond embedded in the haft? I am not certain anyone would believe this story, but I see the comic potential within, and perhaps something else: the value we give to our possessions is not always measured in coin. Indeed, they may be far more precious to us than the value for which they would sell.
'An amusing tale, and a valuable message.'
'Tell me a <rgb=#00FF00>story</rgb>!'

'Will you say the name of the sword again? Ugu-muhatap-zamânya?'
Lakhêpi the Far-faring sighs.
'I make my living with my words, but I am never going to remember that name. I will need to change it to something else. But one thing is clear: the sword had many bearers, seven by my count, and there is a tale in there somewhere.
'Aye, seven. Hulûrmakh who lost it to the man of Ordâkh, who lost it to you, who gave it to Hulâda, who gave it back to you, who gave it to Kagûlu the Armsman, who gave it back to Hulâda.
'Hmm. Perhaps I will be able to remember the name of the sword after all!'
'Tell me a <rgb=#00FF00>story</rgb>!'

'This man Kishâtal is a soldier? Because this story sounds to me as if you are trying to find him a wife. All I have heard is \qHe is so strong he breaks every sword he uses.\q I suppose he is handsome as well?
'It may be the kernel of a story about a comic marriage, but it will need some more work. Still I thank you for it. What else have you experienced, friend helper?'

'Ah, gracias. Veo que has vencido al enemigo. La sombra que oscurecía mis pensamientos ha desaparecido. Sepa que los montaraces le están agradecidos, pero ahora debo apresurarme a regresar al campamento.'
La fortaleza de Olnathron
Entra en las ruinas de Tham Lorn y enfréntate a la oscuridad que hay dentro.
Ahora que los ídolos han sido destruidos, puedes unirte a Olnathron. Es hora de enfrentarse al espíritu cruel.

Extraños ídolos se encuentran por todo Tham Lorn, vomitando nubes verdes nocivas. Debes desactivar los ídolos y detener la propagación de la corrupción de este lugar malvado antes de enfrentarte a Olnathron.
Has llegado a Tham Lorn, la fortaleza de Olnathron en los Campos de Fornost al oeste. Deberías buscar en las ruinas y poner fin al espíritu cruel que reside aquí.
Derrota a Colmillosombrío
Destruye altares corruptos (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Entra en el campamento de los orcos
Derrota al Maestro de la manada Tarkrîp
Derrota a Drukordh
Altares corruptos destruidos (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Los orcos Tarkrîp se ven reforzados por altares corruptos
El Maestro de la manada Tarkrîp ha sido derrotado
Colmillosombrío ha sido derrotado
'¡Ah, lo has conseguido! ¡He escuchado los lamentos de los orcos desde el pueblo! ¡Has velado por la seguridad de Lin Giliath, ${PLAYER}, y por esto te doy las gracias!'
Los orcos de Nan Wathren
Estás en la entrada norte de Nan Wathren. Entra en el campamento para sembrar el caos entre los orcos.

Los orcos de Nan Wathren parecen temer y respetar al Maestro de la manada Tarkrîp y a alguien llamado 'Colmillosombrío'. Deberías encontrarlos y derrotarlos.
También parecen estar reforzados por altares corruptos dentro del campamento. Deberías encontrarlos y destruirlos también para interrumpir sus planes de atacar la aldea élfica de Lin Giliath.

Has sembrado el caos entre los orcos acampados en Nan Wathren al derrotar a Colmillosombrío y al Maestro de la manada Tarkrîp, y al destruir sus ídolos corruptos. Ahora debes encontrar y derrotar a Drukordh, el líder uruk de esta banda.
Has llegado a Nan Wathren, en las Quebradas del Norte. Entra en el campamento de los orcos y encuentra una forma de arruinar sus planes de atacar la aldea élfica de Lin Giliath.
Habla con el extraño encapuchado en el Poney Pisador

'El señor elfo Gildor Inglorion de la Casa de Finrod solicita tu ayuda, ${PLAYER}. Está preocupado por Lin Giliath, un pequeño pueblo élifco en las Quebradas del Norte, que ha sufrido recientemente un ataque de los trolls de piedra que los ha dejado escasos de comida y suministros. Todavía tienen que recuperarse pero han averiguado que los orcos de Nan Wathren pronto marcharán contra ellos.
'Los exploradores han informado que estos orcos están liderados por un gran uruk de Angmar llamado Drkordh. Quizás si este uruk fuera abatido, Lin Giliath evitaría un daño mayor.
'Si asaltaras Nan Wathren, derrotaras a Drukordh y desalentaras a sus orcos, sus planes para dañar Lin Giliath se verían frustrados.'<rgb=#FF0000>NOTA: Esta misión se eliminará de tu registro cuando finalice el festival actual.</rgb>

Se te ha encomendado que vayas al campamento orco de Nan Wathren y hagas lo que puedas para frustrar los planes de Drukordh, el líder uruk que pretender atacar el aldea élfica de Lin Giliath mientras es vulnerable.
Tu ataque a los orcos de Nan Wathren ha conseguido impedir sus planes de asaltar el aldea élfica de Lin Giliath. Deberías hablar con Candaith y después informar al extraño encapuchado.
Completa la miniaventura: Los orcos de Nan Wathren

'Tus acciones han ayudado mucho a proteger a los Elfos de Lin Giliath de nuevos ataques, y librado de ellos también a Puente de Caballetes. Has marcado una gran diferencia para la gente de las Quebradas del Norte.'
'¿Te has preparado para la batalla? Drukordh y los orcos de Nan Wathren no seran rival fácil, pero su ataque a Lin Giliath debe ser frustrado.'
Miniaventura: Los orcos de Nan Wathren
Los orcos de Nan Wathren están planeando un ataque contra la aldea élfica de Lin Giliath, que aún no se ha recuperado de un ataque por parte de los trolls de piedra.
Sabotea una caja sólida (${NUMBER}/6)
Sabotea una jaula sólida (${NUMBER}/6)
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: Esfuerzos inexorables
Cajas sólidas saboteadas (${NUMBER}/6)
Jaulas sólidas saboteadas (${NUMBER}/6)
'Cuando intenten recolectar los escorpiones, se encontrarán con el mismo resultado que antes. Las cajas y las jaulas fallarán. Regresemos al campamento.'

Tus esfuerzos por ralentizar la incursión de los Ordâkhai hacia el pueblo invadido al oeste de su asentamiento han resultado difíciles. Los exploradores de Mizâdi desean cambiar de táctica. Sabotea los materiales que los Ordâkhai usarían para contener y transportar a los escorpiones.
Con las cajas y las jaulas saboteadas, estás listo para regresar al campamento. Busca al explorador de Mizâdi cerca de donde llegaste y regresa a salvo.

Las fuerzas ordâkhai están demostrando ser implacables en su intento de recuperar los escorpiones que perdieron. Se te pide que disminuyas aún más su capacidad para recuperar los escorpiones saboteando sus contenedores.
Derrota a los Utûgi restantes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Derrota a los Ordâkhai restantes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: El asalto final
Utûgi derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Rezagados Ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'El enemigo ha sido derrotado, y no podrán reunirse con sus hermanos al sur. Hemos ganado esta victoria. Regresemos ahora.'
Las fuerzas de Mizâdi quieren que no muestres piedad. Caza a los rezagados que intentaron escapar hacia el sur y dales un final acorde a un enemigo tan terrible.

Regresaste a la orilla y encontraste un pequeño número de rezagados. Después de una rápida incursión en el pantano, saliste victorioso. Ahora encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi y regresa al campamento.
Con sus naves de escape destruidas, las fuerzas restantes de los Ordâkhai y los Utûgi están atrapadas en la orilla norte del río. Es el momento adecuado para aplastarlos de una vez por todas.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Bóra ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Miniaventura: Termina la supervisión
Bóra ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Nada devolverá a los desaparecidos entre nosotros, pero se ha hecho justicia a sus opresores. Regresemos.'
Regresa a la fortaleza ordâkhai y elimina a los supervisores que infligieron dolor y sufrimiento a los constructores que rescataste de la cautividad.
Los bóra han sido eliminados. Ya no pueden hacer daño a los trabajadores. Deberías regresar con el explorador y luego al campamento de Mizâdi.
Las personas que has rescatado cuentan historias de crueldad por el simple hecho de ser crueles. Esto no puede permitirse, y los supervisores que causaron este sufrimiento deben ser detenidos.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Derrota a Khómabekh Dôlo
Miniaventura: La picadura del escorpión
Khómabekh Dôlo derrotado
'Deberíamos regresar a nuestro campamento. Creo que ha habido suficiente violencia por hoy.'
El dôlo ha sido derrotado. La amenaza para las fuerzas de Mizâdi se ha reducido, por ahora. Regresa con el explorador y al campamento para compartir la noticia.

La información contenida en las órdenes que has recuperado ha sido descifrada y se ha revelado la identidad del dôlo responsable de esta operación. Ve al pueblo y contrarresta las maquinaciones del dôlo antes de que logre recuperar los escorpiones.
Por fin, el maestro de las fuerzas que intentan retomar el control del pueblo y los escorpiones ha sido revelado. Ha llegado el momento de eliminar al dôlo Ordâkhai que lidera este esfuerzo.
Derrota a los rezagados utûgi (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Derrota a los guerreros ordâkhai (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: Ahuyentar al enemigo
Rezagados utûgi derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Guerreros ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Nuestra distracción fue algo exitosa. No todos los enemigos fueron derrotados, y nos hicieron huir antes de que pudiéramos rescatar a los trabajadores. Debemos encontrar otra oportunidad para liberarlos.'

No está claro si las fuerzas de Utûgi y Ordâkhai en el suroeste de las Colinas de Hatokáli tienen la intención de atacar o huir a través del río. Pero eso no importa a los exploradores de Mizâdi. Quieren que la amenaza sea eliminada.
Has derrotado a un gran número de Ordâkhai y Utûgi. Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi para regresar al campamento.
Después de aprender que la madera que trajeron los Utûgi y los Ordâkhai está tratada y preparada para su uso en el agua, los exploradores de Mizâdi quieren eliminar a los enemigos.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Derrota a Ródruho Dôlo
Miniaventura: Eliminar al jefe de asedio
Ródruho Dôlo derrotado
'¡El jefe del asedio ya no existe! Nos hemos ganado un largo descanso.'
La venganza está cerca, ahora que se ha revelado la ubicación y la identidad de un líder. Sus crímenes son brutales e innumerables y solo hay un castigo adecuado.
La amenaza de Ródruho Dôlo ha terminado. Deberías volver a la entrada y hablar con el explorador.
Los exploradores de Mizâdi han descubierto el nombre y la ubicación del jefe de asedio que lidera las fuerzas ordâkhai en su fortaleza al sureste.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Derrota a los desertores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destruye el campamento improvisado de los Ordâkhai (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Miniaventura: Una dura verdad
Desertores ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tiendas destruidas en el campamento de los desertores ordâkhai (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'No queda rastro de las atrocidades que cometieron. Esos miserables no merecían otro destino. Vamos, regresemos.'

Los bandidos nunca tuvieron la intención de unirse a las fuerzas completas de los Ordâkhai al norte. Se les pagó grandes sumas de riquezas robadas para proteger la fuga de muchos desertores de los Ordâkhai. Tus esfuerzos frustraron la fuga de muchos, y los que quedaron atrás ahora pueden enfrentar la justicia.
Los desertores han sido derrotados y lo que quedaba de su campamento ha sido destruido. Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi para regresar al campamento.
Los desertores ordâkhai pagaron generosamente por ayuda para escapar, pero tus esfuerzos los han acorralado.
Recupera las órdenes del bóro de los Ordâkhai
Miniaventura: Quién, qué y por qué

El explorador lee las órdenes.
'Ahora lo entiendo mejor. Hay un dôlo entre estas fuerzas, decidido a tener éxito donde otro ha fracasado. Su ambición es grande, al igual que su determinación.'
Has recuperado las nuevas órdenes del bóro
'No deberíamos perder tiempo, amigo. Debemos regresar al campamento.'

Los exploradores de Mizâdi han descubierto que un nuevo mensajero ha llegado al campamento cerca del cruce de caminos. Creen que el propósito, el método de recuperación y el líder que encabeza este esfuerzo están contenidos en las órdenes. Se te ha pedido que recuperes las órdenes.
Has recuperado las órdenes. Encuentra al explorador y entrégale las órdenes.
Todos tus esfuerzos no han logrado detener el avance de los Ordâkhai, que están decididos a recuperar los escorpiones del pueblo cerca del cruce de caminos al sur de Emax Dûl.
Entrega las órdenes al explorador de Mizâdi
Quema las cajas vacías (${NUMBER}/10)
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: Las cajas están vacías...
Cajas vacías quemadas (${NUMBER}/10)
'Veremos si esta acción detiene las acciones de los Ordâkhai, o simplemente ralentiza su avance.'
Encuentra y destruye las cajas en el área antes de la intersección. Los Ordâkhai tienen la intención de usar las cajas para almacenar y entregar los escorpiones del pueblo cercano.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi.

Después de que recuperaste las órdenes, los exploradores de Mizâdi se infiltraron en las filas de los Ordâkhai y determinaron que están organizando cajas para recoger los escorpiones que escaparon al pueblo al oeste de su campamento.
Complete the mission: Weaken Their Position
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: Discovering Intent
Complete the mission: The Crates Are Empty...

'It seems that there is a greater force driving the Ordâkhai than fear and fire can dissuade. So it is that we must use greater force ourselves. Will you return to their location and destroy their tents? We will not let them find comfort and rest if they dare pursue their goals.'

'You have done well this day. My scouts will watch the cross-road, and with luck, and your strength of arms and cunning, we shall see them press their position no further.
'Go now, friend. Enjoy a well-earned respite from battle and these necessary distractions. I am certain that tomorrow will hold more for you and me to do.
'Thank you.'

'We shall not waste this good fortune afforded to us. The Ordâkhai would recapture the scorpions that overran the village west of their cragged camp. Even now they move crates and cages that will carry the scorpions to places we would occupy. We must destroy them and slow their plans.'

Your caution in retrieving the orders from the courier at the Ordâkhai encampment affords Mizâdi's forces an opportunity they had not expected; infiltration. You must not waste this opportunity to further hamper the Ordâkhai forces.

'${PLAYER}, since our arrival, my task has been watching the roads and tracking the movements of the Ordâkhai throughout the Hatokáli Fells.
'My scouts are relentless in their duty, and have sent reports from the west, south of Emax Dûl, and between the forsaken town infested by scorpions, and the craggy rise where the Ordâkhai are entrenched.
'Something brews among the Ordâkhai. What, is unclear. We need assistance in learning the secrets they keep.'
'We must be cautious in how we approach this, my friend. Be secret, be swift, eliminate only the courier, so that we might gain better insight through subterfuge.'
Hatokáli Mission: Retaking the Shipments - Day 1

Mizâdi's scouts are being cautious to deter any potential Ordâkhai footholds from being established any further within Hatokáli. You have been asked to stop a plot to retake the town lost when the Ordâkhai lost control of the scorpions.

Mizâdi's infiltrator escaped while you destroyed the crates the Ordâkhai brought to their makeshift camp. As they fled, they saw that the Ordâkhai were not deterred. In fact, they returned from the crags with tents to make a more formidable forward camp.
You destroyed the tents the Ordâkhai meant to use as shelter in the coming night. Perhaps this will be enough to stop their advance. You should return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp and speak with her.
The Ordâkhai erred badly, and sprung a terrible trap upon themselves in the area south of Emax Dûl. Now an ambitious captain seems set on recovering the lost cargo and setting the trap anew.
Destruye los botes en la orilla del río (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: Negar su escape
Botes destruidos en la orilla del río (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Hemos cortado la vía de escape del enemigo. Ahora necesitamos cazar a estos remanentes y asegurarnos de que nunca puedan reunirse con sus amos.'

Los trabajadores liberados explicaron a los exploradores de Mizâdi que las fuerzas a las que te enfrentaste estaban buscando escapar cruzando el río hacia la jungla. ¿Por qué? Los trabajadores no lo saben, pero se vieron obligados a construir botes para cruzar el río. Puedes impedir la fuga del enemigo.
Los botes yacen en cenizas. Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi y regresa a su campamento.
Después de rescatar a los trabajadores, explicaron que fueron obligados a construir botes que cruzarían el río, permitiendo a los Utûgi y Ordâkhai escapar hacia la jungla en el sur.
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi

Registra tus hallazgos sobre las herramientas

Planchas de madera destruidas (${NUMBER}/6)
Las herramientas están destinadas a la construcción de barcos
'Interesante... estos son materiales para la construcción de barcos. Regresemos al campamento con esta información.'
Las planchas están destruidas y las herramientas documentadas. Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi para regresar al campamento.
Encuentra el sitio de trabajo de los Ordâkhai y Utûgi al oeste. Examina las herramientas que trajeron consigo y registra tus hallazgos antes de entregarlos a los exploradores.
Has registrado información sobre las herramientas en tu diario. Ahora destruye las planchas de madera para que no puedan ser utilizadas.

Los Ordâkhai y Utûgi que transportan madera, herramientas y conducen a los trabajadores a un terreno plano cerca del gran río al sur deben ser investigados para entender qué amenaza pueden representar para las fuerzas de Mizâdi en las Colinas de Hatokáli.
Recoge el tesoro robado del campamento
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi a lo largo del camino hacia el norte
Enfréntate al supervisor de los Hatokáliri
Habla con el supervisor de los bandidos

Derrota a los brutos de los bandidos de Hatokali (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destruye las barricadas de los bandidos (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Miniaventura: Detener el avance de los bandidos de Hatokáli
'Los Ordâkhai no estaban reclutando a los bandidos, sino que buscaban una forma de cruzar el río. Esto es una buena señal, amigo mío.'
'¡Pagarás por los hombres que me has costado!'

'Me han vencido. Mi vida no vale lo que los Ordâkhai nos han pagado.'
Hace una mueca.
'Muchos de ellos han perdido la fe y desean huir al otro lado del río. Pagaron una suma considerable en tesoro por el acceso a nuestro cruce, pero no daré mi vida para protegerlos.
'Más están destinados a llegar dentro del día. Solo sé que dijeron que vendrían desde el este.
'Ve al interior de nuestro campamento. Recupera el tesoro que pagaron. No lo guardaré si se impone un tributo de sangre contra nosotros por tenerlo.'
Has recogido el tesoro
¡El supervisor se rinde!
El supervisor de los bandidos ordena a sus hombres que se rindan
Tiradores de los bandidos de Hatokáli derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Brutos de los bandidos de Hatokáli derrotados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Barricadas de los bandidos destruidas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Debemos llevar esta noticia a Kusâg en el campamento de Mizâdi.'
Tienes el tesoro y la información que debes entregar a Kusâg en el campamento de Mizâdi.
Los bandidos de Hatokáli se preparan para abandonar su campamento y dirigirse hacia el norte, probablemente para reforzar las filas de los guerreros Ordâkhai en el norte. Debes detener su avance.
Has destruido las barricadas construidas por los bandidos y atacado su posición. Enfréntate al supervisor.
El supervisor, sabiendo que está derrotado, te suplica que te detengas y lo escuches.
El supervisor de los bandidos dijo que el tesoro no valía la pena morir por él y pidió que recuperaras el precio pagado dentro de su campamento.
Tu intento de frustrar la colusión entre los bandidos y las fuerzas Ordâkhai parece haber fracasado, y una fuerza expedicionaria de bandidos se dirige al norte.
Regresa al lugar donde entraste y habla con el explorador
<rgb=#ff00000>No te dejes atrapar por el supervisor</rgb>

'Muchos fueron rescatados hoy. Aquellos que sobrevivieron a las horribles acciones de los usurpadores Ordâkhai llorarán a los muertos y celebrarán su libertad recién ganada. Regresemos.'
Los exploradores de Mizâdi sugirieron que grupos de constructores y trabajadores están retenidos contra su voluntad en la fortaleza al sureste del campamento de Mizâdi. Necesitan ser liberados.
Los trabajadores han sido liberados. Regresa al lugar donde comenzaste y encuentra al explorador.
Después de destruir los materiales y evitar que ocurriera un asedio, se te informó que más ciudadanos de Mûr Ghala están siendo retenidos contra su voluntad por los Ordâkhai.

Regresa al valle de abajo sin ser detectado

'Revisaré estas órdenes y informaré a Kusâg. Decidiremos el próximo curso de acción.'
Has recuperado las órdenes del mensajero. Dirígete al explorador escondido en el valle de abajo sin ser descubierto.
Retírate más abajo por la colina y encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi para regresar a su campamento.

Encuentra al mensajero, un bóro que desciende del campamento Ordâkhai en los riscos al sur, pero ten cuidado de no alertar ni ser descubierto por las fuerzas que custodian los caminos hacia las colinas.
Un esfuerzo clandestino para interceptar información antes de que llegue a un frente en expansión entre una ciudad invadida por escorpiones y un bastión de la fuerza Ordâkhai en Hatokáli.
Derrota a los adiestradores de felinos Ordâkhai (${NUMBER}/12)
Encuentra al explorador de Mizâdi
Miniaventura: Manejo de los Adiestradores
Adiestradores de felinos Ordâkhai derrotados (${NUMBER}/12)
'Sin los felinos para controlar los escorpiones, los Ordâkhai seguramente fracasarán. Regresemos.'

Los adiestradores de felinos entre los Ordâkhai son capaces de reunir y controlar a los escorpiones. Reducir su número seguramente disminuirá la capacidad de las fuerzas Ordâkhai para recuperar y usar los escorpiones contra las fuerzas de Mizâdi.
Has derrotado a los adiestradores de felinos. Regresa al lugar donde llegaste y busca al explorador que te llevará de regreso al campamento.

Aunque sus métodos son desconocidos, los adiestradores de felinos Ordâkhai y sus mascotas entrenadas parecen capaces de reunir y controlar a los escorpiones. Los exploradores de Mizâdi creen que eliminarlos de las filas Ordâkhai detendrá su intento de recuperar los escorpiones.
Libera a los trabajadores cautivos (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Trabajadores cautivos liberados (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
'Hemos hecho una gran obra aquí. Regresemos a la seguridad del campamento.'
Los exploradores de Mizâdi no dejarán que el pueblo de Mûr Ghala sufra a manos de los Utûgi o los Ordâkhai. Te han pedido que regreses y liberes a los trabajadores de su situación.
Has liberado a un gran número de constructores y trabajadores. Buscarán refugio con Mizâdi. Debes encontrar al explorador de Mizâdi y regresar al campamento.
Con la amenaza principal de los Utûgi y los Ordâkhai eliminada, es hora de regresar y liberar a aquellos que han sido forzados a trabajar para estos enemigos.
<rgb=#ff0000>No te dejes ver por los bandidos</rgb>

¡Has sido ${PLAYERNAME:visto[m]|vista[f]} por el enemigo!

'Es desafortunado que un emisario haya llegado al campamento, pero aún no debemos perder la esperanza, amigo. Deberíamos hablar con Kusâg para determinar nuestro próximo movimiento.'
'Regresemos al campamento de Mizâdi.'

Llegaste demasiado tarde. Un emisario llegó a los bandidos. Después de una breve discusión que no pudiste escuchar, el emisario entró en el campamento de bandidos. Debes regresar al explorador de Mizâdi a lo largo del camino hacia el norte.

Después de haber sido rechazados en el cruce de caminos y en la orilla, la desesperación ahora se apodera de los Ordâkhai. Un emisario ha sido enviado hacia el campamento de bandidos Hatokáli, al sur.

Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: The Scorpion Sting

'I have learned of your victory over Khómabekh Dólo. It is fortuitous news, as my scouts from the south bring me ill-tidings. News of Utûgi and Ordâkhai warriors dragging wood and tools southward, driving bound labourers ahead of them.
'I fear the success you achieved this day will be overshadowed by the continuing tide of woe that covers this land.
'For now, my friend, rest. I shall give news tomorrow on what more I learn.'

'${PLAYER}, my plans were perfect, and then another group of Ordâkhai, accompanied by Utûgi, passed further to the south. I had need to reposition my scouts in the west to track their progress and now must ask the unthinkable of you.
'Khómabekh Dólo will shortly arrive and press his position. Should he succeed and recover the scorpions, we will need to dedicate more resources to tracking him and others.
'I have need of your assistance again.'
'Khómabekh Dólo will travel with at least two others. He will fight fiercely, and without abandon. Use your wits, steel your nerve. Be safe.'
Hatokáli Mission: Retaking the Shipments - Day 3
Khómabekh Dólo is making his final approach to the overrun village. You have been asked to face him, defeat him, and put an end to the threat he poses.
After defeating Khómabekh Dólo, Mizâdi's scout to the south arrived. They asked that you make your way back to speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp.
The Ordâkhai erred badly, and sprung a terrible trap upon themselves in the area south of Emax Dûl. Now, an ambitious captain seems set on recovering the lost cargo and setting the trap anew.
Complete the mission: The Who, What, and Why
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: Inexorable Efforts
Complete the mission: Handling the Handlers

'I wish to thank you for your continued assistance, and beg of your skill-at-arms, once again. While you fought back the cat-handlers, a courier snuck around the battlefield and made their way to the cross-roads. They delivered new orders to the combatants there.
'We must learn what is in those orders.'

'We now know the name of the Ordâkhai who is driving the effort to recover the scorpions, Khómabekh Dólo. We also know they desire to recover the scorpions to deliver them against Mizâdi's forces. The who, the what, and the why.
'We are spread too thinly to have discovered this without you, ${PLAYER}. Again, we are in your debt.
'I shall draft plans to deal with Khómabekh. Return to me on the morrow.'

'You are a treasured ally, friend. One I fear we must rely on again, and so soon after your return.
'Scouts reported movement coming from the crags. Ordâkhai with cats, capable of taming the scorpions, if only for a time are making their way toward the cross-roads.
'They must not be allowed to join their brethren there.'

'${PLAYER}, it is good to see you again. Our victory over the enemy yesterday is short-lived. My scouts report that under the cover of night, the Ordâkhai descended from the crags and set up at the cross-roads of the road south of Emax Dûl. If their intent were not so nefarious I may admire their resolve. Instead, I must ask you once again to aid us against this foe.
'They are proving to be a most grueling enemy.'
'Use your cunning again, my friend. But ensure that the crates and cages that would keep safe the scorpions are made brittle and easily broken.'
Hatokáli Mission: Retaking the Shipments - Day 2

Mizâdi's scouts tracked the movements of the Ordâkhai of the crag overnight as they descended to the cross-roads south of Emax Dûl. A small force was left behind to defend cages and crates. With some clever activity, you may be able to sabotage these materials.
After delivering the orders you recovered to the scout, you were directed to return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp and speak with her.

Your success at sabotaging the containers to store and transport the scorpions may be for naught.
Mizâdi's scouts report movement from the crag brings cat-handlers making their way to the cross-roads. By some means, these handlers and their cats can herd and control the scorpions. They must be stopped.

Despite your efforts, the Ordâkhai are still driven to recover the scorpions from the overrun village. A new set of orders, delivered whilst you were dealing with the cat-handlers, must be recovered to learn what the Ordâkhai intend, who leads them, and why their resolve is so strong.
The Ordâkhai erred badly, and sprung a terrible trap upon themselves in the area south of Emax Dûl. Now, an ambitious captain seems set on recovering the lost cargo and setting the trap anew.
Complete the mission: Workers Released
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: Investigative Efforts of the Hatokáliri
Complete the mission: Drive the Enemy Away
'A victory, but hollow. My scouts drew many of the Utûgi gaolers from the labourers they watch, but not all. We must return once more to release the workers from their bonds.'

'As ever, you are a gracious hero, my friend.
'We are speaking with the labourers you rescued, and learning there is more we can still do. We are certain to have need of your service again soon, ${PLAYER}.'
'My scouts will let you draw the Utûgi and Ordâkhai away from the captives. We will save their captives, and disrupt whatever devious plans they have. Be resolute, friend.'

You reported back that the wood was treated to withstand the rigors of waves and water, and the tools are meant for a shipwright's hands. The scouts are planning to cause a distraction to draw the Utûgi and Ordâkhai away from the captives.

'Despite their best effort, my scouts were discovered by the Utûgi and Ordâkhai as they followed them south. They watched as they left the southern road just north of where brigands have built shelter. They could not catalogue what they carried with them.
'I ask that you find where they went. Examine the wood and tools they brought with them and record what you discover. I will have my scouts keep a distance and collect your findings, if you are willing.'
'Once we better understand what the Utûgi and Ordâkhai mean to do with the labourers, wood, and tools, we can plan our strategy to remove them without threatening the lives of their captives.'
Hatokáli Mission: A New Distraction? - Day 4
Mizâdi's scouts were discovered, but not before they saw the Utûgi and Ordâkhai head west off the south road from Emax Dûl. You have been asked to finish the work they would have done.
Mizâdi's scouts were not able to free the labourers before the Utûgi returned. Kusâg asked that you return to the site and release the workers.
You defeated the enemy and rescued their captives. You should return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp to ensure that all you rescued are safe and counted.
Ordâkhai and Utûgi forced labourers to carry wood and tools southward on the road from Emax Dûl. Their intent is unclear, and Mizâdi's scouts have asked for your assistance.
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: Deny Their Escape
Complete the mission: The Final Assault

'This is a true victory, ${PLAYER}.
'We saved many lives. We defeated many enemies and denied them a chance to regroup further to the south.'
She pauses.
'I see the look on your face, and I will admit, I have my own thoughts. This may have been a distraction for something else, or someone.
'For now, my friend, let us share in the joy of the lives we saved, and those we may still save.'
'Do not show mercy to the enemy. They showed no quarter to the labourers they captured. We will show them none in return.'

The boats burn on the riverside, and the scout who retrieved you suggested they found the remaining camp of Ordâkhai and Utûgi on the north side of the river. Kusâg sent you to finish off the stragglers.

'The labourers explained that a few boats were constructed and that the surviving members of the Utûgi and Ordâkhai have been ferrying themselves across the river. They intended to leave the labourers on the north side of the river.
'We should strand the enemies we can, and visit righteous judgement upon them.'
'Find and burn the boats. Let us deny the enemy an escape route.'
Hatokáli Mission: A New Distraction? - Day 5

After being rescued, the labourers explained they built a few boats, and the enemy is using them to ferry their numbers in retreat across the river and into the jungle. This presents an opportunity to strand the enemy and visit righteous judgement on them.
The enemy has been defeated and the scout advised that you return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp.
Ordâkhai and Utûgi forced labourers to carry wood and tools southward on the road from Emax Dûl. Their intent is unclear, and Mizâdi's scouts have asked for your assistance.
Complete the mission: Stop the Hatokáli Bandit Advance
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: A Harsh Truth

'${PLAYER}, I do not wish you to think me overly cruel.'
She pauses, looking over the camp.
'I, too, question sometimes if my motivation is borne of justice or vengeance. It can be hard to discern.
'The oppression levied upon our people by the Ordâkhai was severe. Now, in the light borne by Mizâdi, we may have a future where we are free. The thought of our oppressors returning from the south one day-'
She shakes her head.
'It is justice for the years they have stolen... the pilfered wealth... the death they wrought... justice.'

'We cannot allow the Ordâkhai to escape. Their crimes are too numerous and heinous for them to escape justice. My scouts discovered they are camped not far from the bandit encampment. Our time to strike is now.'

'Our efforts to contain the Ordâkhai have failed. They reached the bandits, and it seems the bandits are convinced to march north to join the Ordâkhai encampment.'
She shakes her head.
'This cannot happen. We must put an end to this uprising now, before our nearest foes grow even stronger.
'Please ${PLAYER}, help us end this alliance before it can be forged.'

'You will find that the bandits have left the relative safety of their camp, beginning to expand northward. They construct new barricades, and extend the reach of the towers. We cannot afford to have such a force combine with the Ordâkhai. We must be swift and final in this assault.'
Hatokáli Mission: Emissaries and Adversaries - Day 7

At the bandit camp at the terminus of the road south of Emax Dûl, the bandits appear to be gathering in force. This can only mean an alliance is being considered between the bandits and the Ordâkhai. It must be severed quickly.

Among the bandits you discovered riches and wealth given to them by Ordâkhai deserters, paying for passage across the makeshift ferry at the bandit camp. Your action foiled the plot, and recovered the stolen wealth, but the Ordâkhai deserters still remain.
You defeated the last of the Ordâkhai deserters. You should return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp to alert her to your victory.
Scouts in the west believe they have seen collusion beginning between the Ordâkhai in the north and the bandits in the south. These two forces must not be allowed to unite.
Complete the mission: Emissaries from the Ordâkhai
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp

'We cannot know how long they have been exchanging messages and information. We do know that the flow of information is now interrupted. We should prepare for the worst, I fear.
'We will, of course be ready should there be movement from the bandits.'
Though you did all you could, it appears that emissaries have previously made contact with the Hatokáli bandits. Return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp to determine further action.

'The scourge of the Ordâkhai continues, and it seems that they are not done with their machination in the west. Scouts have been tracking emissaries making their way from the crag hills in the north to the Hatokáli bandit camp located at the water's edge in the south.
'I fear these forces may be on the verge of unifying. We cannot have these forces allying.
'Will you help us to put a stop their potential unification?'

'You may not find the emissaries on the main road. My scouts have warned they are moving silently, under the cover of shadow and off of the beaten road to avoid detection. Find them all, and deny them new allies.'
Hatokáli Mission: Emissaries and Adversaries - Day 6

Scouts have tracked messages being exchanged between the Ordâkhai from the crags west of Mizâdi's camp and the Hatokáli bandits encamped on the river's edge at the terminus of the south road from Emax Dûl. Mizâdi's forces cannot afford these forces allying with one another.
Scouts in the west believe they have seen collusion beginning between the Ordâkhai in the north and the bandits in the south. These two forces must not be allowed to unite.
Complete the mission: Before the Bombardment Begins
Complete the mission: End the Oversight
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp
Complete the mission: A Harsh Punishment
'Again, the matter of vengeance or justice rises. Still, my friend, I think it is justice we bring when we punish those who visited such terrible harm on the innocent.'

'We have spoken to the survivors you rescued and they tell us that there are more still held against their will. My scouts will find them.
'There is more yet to do, ${PLAYER}. Now, however, we rest.'
'They treat the people who cannot fight, or will not fight, as cattle... forcing them to build the machines of war. We will remove the yoke about their necks and free them from their oppressors.'

'As one flank weakens, another grows in strength.
'Our efforts in the west reduced the threat posed by the Ordâkhai encamped there, but my scouts here in the east and the south have reported disturbing activity within striking distance of this encampment.
'Siege weaponry materials have been moved from a fort the Ordâkhai control to the south to rocky outcroppings to our south-east. If they are able to assemble these weapons, we would be under immediate bombardment.
'We cannot let them build those machines of war.'

'Beyond the battlefield where our numbers fight for control of this land, you will see the shadow of a fallen ruin occupied by Orcs. In that shadow, the Ordâkhai aim to make the flat and weathered stone a wall of siege weaponry to drive us from this camp. We will not let that happen.'
Hatokáli Mission: The Engines of War - Day 8
With the materials to craft the weapons destroyed, Kusâg is told that more citizens of Mûr Ghala are captive within the fortress to the south-east. You are asked to intervene.

Ordâkhai in the south-east continue to forge an offensive against Mizâdi's forces. A bold effort by the Ordâkhai endangers the camp as siege machinery is being prepared on the rocky outcroppings to the south-east of Mizâdi's camp. You have been asked to assist.

You freed the captive builders and saved them from a horrific fate. You discovered, however, a chain of overseers; cruel men who would visit terrible harm upon the captives. The scouts wish justice for those harmed by these wretches.
The overseers are removed. Return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp.
With the threats diminished in the west, Mizâdi's scouts turn their attention to a looming threat in the south-east.
Complete the quest: Harvester's Flight
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp

'There are murmurs from those you recently freed that a powerful leader rises in the ranks of the Ordâkhai. Perhaps we can catch them, and hopefully end the oppression and more, the war.
'My scouts will keep searching, ${PLAYER}.'

'We discovered that the last large group of captives has been toiling at the river's edge, beneath the broken bridge in the shadow of the great water works.
'We have a chance to both eliminate their captors and rescue more Mûrai, if we can catch them off guard.
'My scouts will clear the roads, allowing you to assault the captors and free those harvesting wood in the shadow of the bridge and water works.'
'We will continue our efforts until all of Mûr Ghala is free. Let us take the fight to the enemy and free those who we can.'
Hatokali Mission: The Engines of War - Day 9

Another opportunity to do right by those oppressed by the hand of the Ordâkhai arises. Far to the east, where the river grows rapid and the bridge that crossed that river is crumbled, Ordâkhai overseers drive captive workers to harvest wood for the machine of war.
You have defeated the overseers and rescued the labourers who toiled in the shadow of the fallen bridge. Return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp.
With the threats diminished in the west, Mizâdi's scouts turn their attention to a looming threat in the south-east.
Complete the quest: Ending the Siege-lord
Speak with Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp

'My scouts reported to me that you were victorious. The cur was put down, as he should have been.
'We will remain diligent, as there are certain to be other upstarts and warriors that we must contain.'
She smiles.
'We have a true victory, ${PLAYER}. We have this victory because of you; for this I, and the scouts who work to see a brighter future for our people and our lands, are grateful.'

'At last, ${PLAYER}, we have a name and location on the siege-master who would force the Mûrai into servitude and bring war machines to bear against our forces.
'We will make this a fitting end.'
'Find this villain and take him down, ${PLAYER}. We will have victory and know a moment of peace when this is done.'
Hatokali Mission: The Engines of War - Day 10

Within the walls of the fortress to the south-east, a threat looms. The siege-leader who means to build the machines of war to launch an assault against Mizâdi's mountain camp. You have an opportunity to bring an end to this campaign.
Though the battle was fraught, you were victorious over the siege-lord. Return to Kusâg at Mizâdi's camp.
With the threats diminished in the west, Mizâdi's scouts turn their attention to a looming threat in the south-east.

'I am still shaken by what I witnessed here in Emax Dûl, but my resolve is still firm to finish our mission, and bring Bârshud to justice.
'My scouts saw his flight take him south, through a town called Hanamíku, in Pahar Hatokáli, what locals call the Hatokáli Fells. That is where we must next go. Meet me in Hanamíku, friend, when you are able.'
Speak with Shâra Mizâdi in Hanamíku. Hanamíku can be found in Pahar Hatokáli, which is south of Idagâl, within Mûr Ghala.
Speak with Mizâdi in Hanamíku
'It is you! It is so good to see you again, ${PLAYER}! I have great need of your skills this day.'
A Glorious Hunt

Mizâdi, Shâra of Hamât Renewed, requests your presence in Pahar Hatokáli. She calls for your aid in finishing her hunt of the pretender Shâr Bârshud, who fled Emax Dûl into the wild scrubland of Pahar Hatokáli.
Gather new bandages for Zâgsha
Find whetstones for Nushâba (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Gíshu in Hanamíku
Speak with Zâgsha in Hanamíku
Speak with Nushâba in Hanamíku
Gather some skins of fresh water for Gishu (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Bârshud? Yes, I saw the man - when he was in the Palace in Emax Dûl. He was looking for something. I am sorry - my mouth is dry, my throat quite parched.
'Could you gather me some water? I am happy to tell you what I know, but I feel quite light-headed, and it's hard to speak.'

'I'm not bothering anyone here, am I?
'Bârshud? I did not see him, but I saw his servant, Sudûgul, in the confusion around Emax Dûl. Damn this blade! It could not cut the hair on my head, let alone slice through a servant of Ordâkh here in the fells.
'Would you gather me a whetstone or two? I cannot concentrate - a dull blade brings about a dull mind.'

'Yes, I saw Bârshud. When he was fleeing Emax Dûl. He was fleeing at great speed - he made no attempt at helping children or civilians either, saving only himself, with that frightening servant of his.
'There was something in his hand, ah! My shoulder! It is burning in pain - I cannot think properly. Please, get me a large shoulder bandage - once this is wrapped properly, I will tell you what I know.'

'Yes, Bârshud.
'There was so much chaos and confusion, but I did see him - he was looking for a staff. He was yelling at his second, Sudûgul. Something about the Dead. I believe they thought this staff could command them - command the Dead. I know not if he found it, just that he was looking in the Palace for it. I wish I could be more helpful to the Shâra.'

'Ah, yes. Dry and well-stitched. That will do nicely.
'Yes, Bârshud, of course. He was yelling at his Ordâkhai guards to move faster in his flight. Then he said something about a tomb in Hatokáli. I believe that was where he was headed. I know not what tomb, I am from Imhûlar, this area is quite foreign to me. Maybe the Shâra knows of this tomb.'

'These will do the job. Never have a dull sword or a dull mind, I say. But if you have to have one, make it the dull mind - ha!
'Bârshud, right. I saw him - a staff? He did not have a staff, but his sorcerer did - I think they call that one Sudûgul. It was a long staff, it looked to be made of bone or something unnaturally white, with the end carved in the shape of a dragon's skull. I know not its import, but Bârshud did possess it through this Sudûgul.'
Found whetstones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gathered skins of fresh water (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Shâra Mizâdi in Hanamíku. Hanamíku can be found in Pahar Hatokáli, within Mûr Ghala.
Speak with each of the Subuzûri witnesses Shâra Mizâdi mentioned in Hanamíku.
Speak with Shâra Mizâdi in Hanamíku

'It is you! It is so good to see you again! I have a powerful need for familiar faces in this foreign land.
'Several of my warriors saw Bârshud or his new Ordâkhai ally, Sudûgul, on their flight from the Emax Dûl.
'In the chaos, I have not had the time to gather their reports. We know Bârshud came down here, to the Hatokáli Fells. We know not his purpose or location here, however.
'Would you speak with each of the Subuzûri who saw him? Gíshu, Zâgsha, and Nushâba are their names - they will be with the other Subuzûri here in Hanamíku. Let them know I sent you. Thank you, ${PLAYER} - just seeing you here again is like a great weight has been lifted from my shoulders.'

'Interesting. I do not know where the dead lie here in Pahar Hatokáli.
'A tomb? I will have Razâl scout for such a place. Thank you, my friend. This has been a great help. In the meanwhile, there is another task I would ask of you, if you are willing.'
A Fresh Lead
Collect each of the items for which Gíshu, Zâgsha, and Nushâba asked. Each can likely be found somewhere in or near Hanamíku in Pahar Hatokáli.
Speak once more with the Subuzûri warriors Gíshu, Zâgsha, and Nushâba in Hanamíku.

Mizâdi tells you that several Subuzûri reported seeing Bârshud or his aide, Sudûgul, on their flight from Emax Dûl. She asks you to gather their reports.
Speak with Shâgigal Held-silver in Hanamíku
Speak with the merchant Shâgigal Held-silver about his grievances

Collect deadfall wood in Kirzâmur (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroy Shâgigal's burnt market stalls in Hanamíku (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Better? Yes, I suppose it is better. But you did not have to destroy the old ones! You looked to be stomping around like a great alap-nâri!
'Never mind, never mind. Yes, I suppose Mizâdi has done more for me than the Ordâkhai, so her presence is not altogether terrible here in Hanamíku.
'What would really seal the deal is for you to purchase some of my oranges.
'What do you mean you just gave them to me? That doesn't mean I can't sell you some of the finest fruits and vegetables in the Fells! Wait, come back!'

'You! I saw you speaking with Mizâdi - surely you are important!
'What, you aren't fleeing my sight? Excellent, excellent.
'What do I want? My business returned to me, of course! I sell oranges - only the finest in all of the Fells! But you can see, the Ordâkhai burned my stalls and stole my oranges - and no one has provided recompense or made me whole!
'It is Mizâdi's fault the Ordakhai fled through Hanamiku, she should be the one to repair my stalls and bring a fresh supply of oranges.
'You will help? Well, it is about time someone listened to Shâgigal.'

Pieces of wood collected (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Burnt stalls destroyed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Shâra Mizâdi in Hanamíku. Hanamíku can be found in Pahar Hatokáli, within Mûr Ghala.
Speak with the merchant Shâgigal Held-silver about his grievances with Mizâdi's army. Shâgigal can be found within Hanamíku near the market stalls.

'The Ordâkhai have done much harm to the people here. We should be welcomed. But I am not blind, friend - my presence here is tolerated, not celebrated.

'Aye, our stores are running dangerously low. Our Subuzûri are loyal. They will follow the Shâra to the ends of the world, so I do not fear mutiny in our ranks.
'That being said, they are quite far from home, and no one swings a blade well on an empty stomach.
'Razâl and Lumgâna spoke to me of a place not far from here. The locals cleared out, either killed or fled from the savage beasts that took over. It sounds dangerous, but in their haste I believe they may have left supplies enough for the trouble it will cause to recover them. You should speak with Lumgâna for the details.'

'Yes, there is a place near here. Mûl Erebu, the locals call it. it's a terrible tragedy - it seems the locals were killed by great beasts that moved into the area.
'Razal scouted Mûl Erebu and reported that there seem to be stores of grain and kegs of wine. All the stories say the locals fled quickly, with naught but what they could carry on their backs. I believe there is still much food and ale within Mûl Erebu.

Speak with Unagâr the tool-maker in Hanamíku

'A key? You have a mould for it?
'Yes, and quite a large one you'll need, looking at that mould. I do not have the iron on hand for it. There is some in the mountains west of here. Be warned, it is dangerous - a band of thieves keeps their camp in the mountains to the west.
'There is another matter, that of payment. We will breach that topic once you have brought me the iron I need for the key.'

'I will tell you what I know. Swear to spare my life!
'I have heard rumours of Mizâdi - they say she is honourable. If she swears to spare me, I will tell you everything I know about Bârshud. I have information. He visited Bolo Thúki on his way south.'

'He wants mercy? I doubt that he deserves such clemency, but we seldom need to make deals with the best of Men, do we?
'Very well, tell him I will spare his life in exchange for what he knows about Bârshud. He leaves Hatokáli though, and heads further south. I do not want him in Mûr Ghala.'

'Very well. I have heard rumours of the Shâra. None of those rumours claim that she is dishonorable. I will help you in exchange for safe passage out of these lands.
'I bear on my person a mould for a key. It was given to me by Bârshud, should I need to enter the depths of Mut-hûru. That is where he is going - the tombs south of here. I know not why.
'You will find the mould in my tunic. Yes, there. You need only to bring it to a tool-maker, someone that can forge iron. It is a heavy door - it will require quite a bit of metal for such a key.'

'Ah yes, that is more than enough iron for the key.
'As I said, however, there is still the matter of payment. I do not want your coin. You see, I live just outside of Hanamíku, to the west. This past month, I have been harried day and night by huge stinging wasps. They wait outside my home. Such pests they are! Kill those cursed wasps. By the time you return, I shall have your key forged and ready for you.'

'Just in time. There it is, quite heavy too.
'No, I do not require proof. You travel with Shâra Mizâdi, I trust you are honourable and true to your word, as she is.
'I shall sleep soundly for the first time in months - thank you, friend. I hope the key brings you that which you seek.'

'¡Vaya, tienes verdadero espíritu festivo! ¡Espero que lo estés pasando bien en el Festival de Aniversario!
'Has hecho mucho, ¡espero que no estés demasiado cansado! Quizá disfrutes de algunas de estas recompensas. ¡Aquí tienes!'

'${PLAYERNAME:¡Bienvenido, amigo![m]|¡Bienvenida, amiga![f]}
'Si has venido por el Festival de Aniversario, te recomiendo que eches un vistazo y participes en las muchas actividades divertidas que hay por aquí. Y si no has venido por el festival… ¡quizá deberías hacerlo!
'Quienes participen en muchas de nuestras actividades podrían llevarse alguna recompensa, ¡así que anímate!
'Ah, casi lo olvido: ¡este año hay actividades nuevas! Creo que el Extraño Encapuchado tiene algunas aventuras nuevas en las que podrías participar. Eso sí, no hagas nada demasiado peligroso. Recuerda: es una fiesta, ¡diviértete!'

'When last we came this way, we marched toward the unknown. None of us knew what awaited us at the Black Gate. Even having been there and seen it with my own eyes I cannot fully believe what transpired: the fall of Sauron and the defeat of his armies!
'New masters thought to rule Mordor in the days following the destruction of Sauron, but none could match that Dark Lord in power or potency. And that is a good thing for Gondor, and for all of Middle-earth, but we must not underestimate their evil or their desire to do great harm. The reports I have heard of Lhaereth's contagions...'
Orthonn shudders.
'Well, let us make sure she has not returned to Seregost to perfect them. She may not rival Sauron in power, but if she is not his equal in hatred I deem she may at least approach that vile one in malice, and in evil intent!
'Gwaebad will carry me beyond the Black Gate and into Mordor. We are not afraid.'

'I am in no hurry to return to Mordor, ${PLAYER}, for the challenges we faced in Minas Morgul remain etched in my memory... but I know this mission is important.
'We must pass by the Black Gate and return once more to Mordor if we are to learn if Lhaereth has come back to Seregost. Our ride continues.'

'The hush is peculiar.
'Has this become an empty land, or do its occupants hide from us, lying in wait and watching us as we pass?'

'I would rather fight a score of foes than wait for an equal number of minutes, ${PLAYER}! It has always been thus!
'When I agreed to come with your scouting party I believed there would be fighting! Let us hope Seregost does not disappoint!
'Of course I am not wishing Lhaereth's evil upon Middle-earth! You know my meaning, ${PLAYER}. This infernal quiet has me on edge. Let us continue onward, and perhaps this appalling silence will soon be broken!'

You tell Thrymm that you are only lately returned, and he laughs heartily.
'From the talk I have overheard, it sounds as if you will not be here long! Well do I understand the need for combat and for excitement. Why, that is what has brought me to the Splintered Shield nearly every day since the wedding of the King of Gondor! But I am not supposed to speak of it. Know only that these muscles will tire before my martial spirit, and if that happens the grave must accept me!
'But the war is done, and it seems we shall be beset by peace! I cannot return to my own land and my own wedding if I believed danger still threatened. Share with me your secret worries and Thrymm will aid you in besting them!'
With Orthonn's permission you share with Thrymm the fears of Faeron and Rhadrog, and he eagerly insists that he accompany you to Seregost.

'Our mission is urgent, but if its success depends upon the departure of one storm-cloud, we have already failed. Trust that we have time enough!
'If we must return to Mordor, let us do so wearing dry clothes!'
'We have travelled far already, but there is much further to go. Let us stop for a few moments to let both horse and rider rest.'

'One last adventure, ${PLAYER}, and I will return to Wildermore and wed my Cyneberg. I seek not to delay that happy day, but if danger brews anew in Mordor no man of Rohan could remain idle, and Thrymm Red-beard less than any!
'My betrothed will understand. Is she not a shieldmaiden of Rohan, and no stranger to battle herself? What courage she displayed when the terrible giant Núrzum blanketed Wildermore in ice and snow! Why, if it was Cyneberg who overheard your talk in the Splintered Shield and not Thrymm Red-beard, I believe she would be the one riding to Mordor with you on this day!'
Thrymm pats the neck of his steed.
'I borrowed this fine fellow from the stables of Minas Tirith with the permission of the grooms there, and gave to him the caparison of a horse of Rohan that perished on the Pelennor. Stylhóf I have named him, for though he was not bred of Rohan I wanted him to have a Rohirric name: \qSteel-hoof\q is its meaning. He carries the name, and me, very well indeed!'

'It is good to learn that Lhaereth has not returned to Seregost, but unless I am mistaken we have discovered further dangers!
'I will ride back to Minas Tirith and bring these tidings to the King. Doubt not that he will dispatch scouts to these new lands, for Gondor must learn if servants of Sauron are active elsewhere as they were on Gorgoroth!
'Go forth in safety, and trust in your companions! We do not know what dangers await you in the further reaches of Mordor!'

'Yes, I know ${PLAYER}, and I would name us friends! My name is Harthalín, and I fought beside the Last Alliance of Men and Elves at the Battle of Dagorlad, three thousand years ago. I believed Sauron was destroyed, but it was not so. Through some sorcery Sauron survived to trouble Middle-earth.
'When I received word that the Dark Lord had been defeated once again, only months ago, I disbelieved it and returned to this land. It was then that I met ${PLAYER}, and we worked together to put an end to any of Sauron's still-living schemes.
'I believe now that the Dark Lord is truly gone, and that many of his servants have joined him in death. Many, I say... but not all.'

'It was a dream, ${PLAYER}, a dream that filled me with a sense of foreboding. Three times have I dreamed this dream, but familiarity has not made its meaning more clear to me, nor its presence more welcome. The phantasmal images chill me to my very bones, though I have stood with courage against some of Middle-earth's most frightening terrors.
'I dreamed of a stone chamber, a chamber with neither entrance nor exit. I knew not how I came to be there, and while the dream persisted I could sense no means of leaving the chamber. Only waking could free me from that place, but while I was held by that dream it was no dream at all, and seemed as real to me as anything I have experienced in all my years of life. There was an evil about that inaccessible chamber; it lay heavily upon the stones, but I could not identify its source.'
Harthalín shakes her head to clear away the ill-feeling memory.
'My people are not quick to disregard the meaning of dreams. When that same dream returned on subsequent nights, I bent all my thought upon deciphering it. If the chamber with no doors is not a real place, what might it represent? I believed it might represent the keep of Seregost, accessible only by the air or by those who might climb such a great height. And so I made the climb thinking Lhaereth might have come back to Seregost, and some force for good wanted me to confront her. I searched the keep for any sign that she might have returned and begun anew the work she had halted.'

'${PLAYER}, my friend! You are just the person I was hoping to see. I have received a message from my kinsman Faeron, and I desired to speak with you concerning its contents.'
Orthonn pauses as a peal of thunder rumbles in the distance.
'We spent time enough in the wilderness to learn how quickly rain-clouds can spoil a pleasant day, have we not? Dagoras and I intended to meet in one of the taverns to discuss Faeron's message. We should take advantage of its roof before the rain arrives!'

'I believe this connexion betwixt Gorgoroth and these lands was not traversable until recently, ${PLAYER}. The creation of this narrow pass began with the great shaking of Mordor following the fall of Sauron, and has only recently settled enough to grant us passage.
'I am not ashamed to say it: despite the unknown dangers that lie ahead of us, I am happy indeed to leave the swamps of Agarnaith! Even within this ravine the air feels fresher than that of the bog behind us!'

'Summer thunderstorms may be short-lived, but they can arrive swiftly and with great ferocity! Together let us hurry to the Splintered Shield. There we can discuss the message sent to me by Faeron as he adventured in Harad, and decide what can be done about the tidings he shares.'

'If these bats flew from Agarnaith above the Mithram Spur and came thus to Heledhris, they overcame whatever illness they might once have suffered; I see in them no sign of Lhaereth's contagion. We should not lower our guard overmuch, but I do not think the Lady of Blight has come to this place.'

'Lhaereth may not have come to this land, but it remains part of Mordor and may therefore conceal any number of hidden threats. The ferocious fighters against whom Thrymm is eager to test his blade tells me that, if nothing else will this day!'

'Has my excitement betrayed itself? I confess to it!
'You already know of my interest in cartography, ${PLAYER}, and here we have an opportunity to expand the borders of our known map! We must remain alert to any threats as we travel eastward, of course... but I will also remain alert to any notable geologic features we encounter, and when we stop to rest I will add them to the map I intend to prepare.
'Onward, then, with haste and with awareness of every footfall!'

'We must remain alert to any threats as we travel eastward, of course... but I will also remain alert to any notable geologic features we encounter, and when we stop to rest I will add them to the map I intend to prepare. Onward, with haste and with awareness of every footfall!'

'The crevice through which we came here from Gorgoroth seems of recent creation. Mordor has always been a land of tumult, but during the years of Sauron's return, Mount Doom regularly erupted with violence. With the eye of my mind I can see towering cliffsides sheared away, their rocky burdens cascading from the heights into the valleys below. Is it any wonder we overlooked this passage until now?
'We are dependent upon this rocky pass, but those with wings are not! Agarnaith is much nearer for them than it seems to us, and if the bats I see around us came from that swamp, we should study them for any sign of experimentation by Lhaereth or her servants. They may tell us if the Lady of Blight came this way from Seregost before we arrived.'

'The wind whips across these hills, picking up tiny shards of stone and casting them in our faces! Already have I been stung by this grit, and made unwelcome!'

'But the wind carries something else upon it, ${PLAYER}. Hear you the sounds of battle, and the harsh cries of warriors? There are fighters not far from here, and their guttural cries remind me of the Orcs I have slain. You introduce yourself and say you have travelled far from your home to oppose the dangers that stalk this valley and threaten to spill from it. The stout woman laughs.
'Evil for you is like jug of water? Spill it and let disappear? Ha! Khemozêl not believe that.
'Others like you nearby? Kâl-maka-Hôi meet them?'
'Others like you nearby? Kâl-maka-Hôi meet them?'

'I did not expect to see one of the Woses in this place! Her people must be estranged from her kin in the Drúadan Forest, for that is many miles from here and surely they cannot have maintained contact over that span without the Men of the West knowing of it.
'It was only through the guidance of the Wild Men that my people reached Minas Tirith in time during the War of the Ring, and for that alone she has my friendship and the use of my sword-arm!'

'There is a settlement of Drúedain at Bhol Rûdh in Agarnaith. When I searched that swamp for the presence of Lhaereth and her servants, I befriended the Red Sky Clan and they were of great help to me. They must have become separated from others of their people over the years, though record of their lost kin survived.
'We should assist Kâl-maka-Hôi as much as we can, for her familiarity with this land could be invaluable to us.'

Orthonn stares at the Khemozêl woman with astonishment.
'I was never able to meet any of the Drúedain of the Drúadan Forest, ${PLAYER}, for I was aboard one of the Black Ships when King Théoden and the Rohirrim encountered them. I am filled with delight at this meeting!
'Think you that Kâl-maka-Hôi will introduce us to others of her people? They are certain to know if Sauron's influence extended into this valley, and if it remains a danger.'
'Friends different as stripes in stone!'

'Prêkh-weni-Pâsh sent you here? He use sad stories as excuse not to fight.
'I hear these stories and learn something else. I learn Dhol Têg in danger. I learn Khemozêl cannot hide forever.
'Some of my people go to Nan Ogol. Even grand-daughter of the chief go! They intend to fight. Kâl-maka-Hôi want to join them... but still deciding. Not easy choice.'

'You listen to stories? Then you know Khemozêl very brave, but elders and youth disagree on best course of action.
'I not afraid to fight! But youth not understand history of our people. Youth hear tales of past and think storytellers stretch truth. But it not so.
'This land once belong to Khemozêl, but no longer. Now were-wolves have dominion.'

'Many lifetimes Khemozêl spend in hills, keep Dhol Têg safe from enemies. If you wish to be friend, you keep secret too. \qKhem-khai\q we name it: gaining and losing of trust. One slow; one fast.
'Meet my people in village. Go to TBD, TBD, and TBD. With <rgb=#00FF00>bow</rgb> you befriend Khemozêl, and show you are friend.'

One of the Khemozêl standing nearby sees you studying the wooden carving and begins to speak in a low, sonorous tone. She tells you that this carving represents many of her people that have been slain by the were-wolves in the woods of Nan Ogol to the north. It was the habit of the crafter who fashioned this reminder of the fallen to etch additional wounds onto it for each new victim of the beasts... but after the passage of several years there was no more space on the carving for this practice to continue.

The Khemozêl woman follows your gaze to this second carving and relates the story of a once-respected warrior of her people who slew his rival in a fit of passion and fled from the village, never again to be seen by any who live in Dhol Têg.
She tells you the carving represents the victim, Bhêg-buri-Chât, and that the name of the murderer is no longer spoken aloud for fear of calling him near.

As you turn your attention to this third carving, the Khemozêl woman clasps her hands together and murmurs something just beyond the range of your hearing. When you look at her quizzically, she repeats herself for your benefit.
'Triumph for Khemozêl,' she says, 'but also sad.'
She goes on to tell you about the hunting-party of her people that were surprised by one of the were-wolves that stalked from Nan Ogol. Rather than lead the beast back to the village, a dozen of the Khemozêl attacked it together. They grappled it into a fiery crevice of magma and perished alongside their prey, and are remembered as heroes.
'Always remember the TBD,' she says with finality, you know she is done telling stories to you today.

'Now you know what dangers Khemozêl face, even more willing to help?'
'Craftsmen of Dhol Têg use hides and claws from many beasts for their work. Help Prêkh-weni-Pâsh collect these things? He will meet you at TBD MIDDLE HUB to the south-east once done. That place to the TBD, and creatures found all about.'
'There is more going on here than we yet understand.'

'Craftsmen of Dhol Têg use hides and claws from many beasts for their work. Help Prêkh-weni-Pâsh collect these things? He will meet you at TBD MIDDLE HUB to the south-east once done. That place to the TBD, and creatures found all about.'
'You bring hides and claws? Prêkh-weni-Pâsh pleased at this, but heart not full of gladness! You keep secret from him.'

Prêkh-weni-Pâsh speaks first of the Gaurhoth, mightiest of the were-wolves that served Sauron. Bred by the Dark Lord long ago and imbued with powerful fell-spirits, they grew to tremendous size and became the largest and most intelligent of his wolf-kind, sires of a cruel and vindictive bloodline. Steeped in twisted sorcery, the Gaurhoth possess the power of speech and use it to cow lesser beings, though the Khemozêl proudly tells you that his people are resistant to such intimidation and choose death over servitude. The Gaurhoth form the leadership of the were-wolf power structure in north-eastern Mordor, and they gave to this land the name Draugardh: the Wolven-lands.
Prêkh-weni-Pâsh further tells you that unlike the wargs and wolves with which you may be familiar, Gaurhoth bites are venomous and can inflict a terrible madness in their victims.
'If survive bite,' he says meaningfully.
'Listen to Prêkh-weni-Pâsh. He share wisdom of our foe.'

Prêkh-weni-Pâsh speaks to you of another creature of wolf-kind created by the Gaurhoth and made to serve their fell purposes: the Draugrim, lesser in power and size than their masters but rivalling them in malice. These lesser were-wolves can stand upright, but fall to all fours to run at great speed after their prey.
The people of Dhol Têg feel a great loathing for the Draugrim, for in the melding of man-like and beast-like features they see a cruel mockery of the Khemozêl.
'Draugrim found in greater numbers than their masters,' Prêkh-weni-Pâsh continues. 'But Gaurhoth quick to punish servants, even with death. Draugrim not dare to disobey.'
'Listen to Prêkh-weni-Pâsh. He share wisdom of our foe.'

Prêkh-weni-Pâsh tells you not to underestimate any of the were-wolves you encounter, whether they be powerful Gaurhoth or fierce Draugrim.
'One more foe,' he continues. 'This one not were-wolf. This one Man.'
The Khemozêl describes a clan of nomadic warriors, the Khashkhilar, who came out of the East and devoted their lives to the worship of the Gaurhoth. They live now on the rocky grassland of Parth Rhavas and revere the were-wolves even as they are slain by them.
With a noise that sounds to your ear quite rude, Prêkh-weni-Pâsh makes it clear what he thinks of the Khashkhilar.
'Listen to Prêkh-weni-Pâsh. He share wisdom of our foe.'

'I am grateful to Prêkh-weni-Pâsh for describing the villains arrayed before us, ${PLAYER}, but his explanation has raised further questions in my mind.
'Where were the were-wolves during the War of the Ring? Wolves and wargs fought alongside the armies of Sauron, but I have heard no report of such evils as the Gaurhoth or their bipedal Draugrim servants engaging in battle at the Black Gate or on the Plateau of Gorgoroth. Why would the Dark Lord not make use of every servant at his disposal, unless he possessed some reason unknown to us? It is a mystery to me.
'You know of the Masters of Mordor who fought among themselves following the fall of Sauron, ${PLAYER}; there were no were-wolves among their ranks. Judging from the words of Prêkh-weni-Pâsh, I would have expected one or more of the Gaurhoth to covet power in Mordor. If the pass to Draugardh was clear, why did they not emerge to challenge the others for dominance? There is more going on here than we yet understand.'

'I am confused, friend. Prêkh-weni-Pâsh speaks of these were-wolves as if they possess the thoughts of men. Are they not beasts?'
Thrymm's eyebrows knit together as his forehead creases with thought. A sudden realization lightens his features.
'Or perhaps they are skin-changers, like old Grimbeorn? Do they take on the form of a wolf as he takes on the form of a bear? Have I solved this mystery?'
'Beware wolf-kind, in all its forms! They are cunning hunters, with no shortage of evil scheme at hand.'
