'We will find this wolf-creature and slay it, Harthalín, and you are welcome to join us on our hunt. We will search too for Thelaron, for hope may be dimmed but it will not be extinguished so long as we draw breath.'
'I am honoured by the friendship of these Elf heroes! Let your hunt of the terrible wolf shadow end in victory for the Great Alliance, and foretell the ending of the siege itself!'

'The wolf-creature Morlang eludes us, it is true, but despair not! Many are the evils we have opposed on this hunt, and much is the good we have done, Harthalín! The Orcs we have slain will take no more captives, and though it seem Sauron's supply of the creatures must be endless, it cannot be so.'

'Was this creature the wolf-shadow that so troubled the camps of Men? We will return to Adambel and give Anárion these tidings. If the attacks on his soldiers cease, we will know it was Morlang we ended on this day. If not... well, Sauron's wolf-pack has one fewer of the creatures to trouble us.
'You want to stay? Well, do not stay long. The Orcs and their warg master are defeated, but there are other foes in the Black Land, as you well know.
'We will see you back at Echad-in-Edhil, Harthalín.'
Harthalín mourns, remembering a fruitless search
Celeborn, former leader of the Bright Company and still involved in its pursuits, provided much wisdom to High King Gil-galad at the encampment of Echad-in-Edhil during the many years of siege.
King Anárion of Gondor had much to say of an evil that troubled the camps of Men during the siege of Mordor.
The success of the forces that composed the Great Alliance depended upon each of them working together as a union.
The former and current leaders of the Bright Company, Celeborn and Glorfindel, had some thoughts to share about the High King's plan.

'I never wished to return to this land.
'Many were the fell deeds I beheld in this place, and many the comrades I lost, before it was named Udûn. The shining light of the Bright Company was nearly snuffed out by the evil we pursued here.'
Celeborn shakes his head, banishing painful memories.
'Glorfindel leads the Glánnothrim now, and it was at his request that I passed again into Mordor. We will see Sauron defeated, and this last servant of the Great Enemy will trouble us no more. Let that knowledge lighten your burden, Lady Harthalín!'

'You speak truth when you name it a darkness, my lord, even before I speak of it!
'It is a terrible creature in the shape of a wolf, and yet it is unlike any wolf of which I have heard tell. Swifter than any shadow this wraith is, and it steals into our camps and tears apart any man unfortunate enough to lie in its path. Then it vanishes, as quickly as it came, leaving only blood, mangled flesh, and the sound of its terrible yowling on the night air. I have heard the sound more than once, and it turned my heart to ice.
'My brother and my father both speak of the Elves as hunters unmatched by any in all the world. Can it be your people might find and slay this terrible beast, where our own trackers and trappers have failed?'

'Gil-galad says the Bright Company has never known defeat, and that may be so, but victory in battle often comes at a cost. Well do I know the price of these victories, for they are measured in grief... every one.
'Take care of yourself on your hunt, Harthalín. This is a land of sorrow.'

'No... doors...?
'It cannot be. You must have misheard the creature! Why do you speak so? What do you mean by this?'
Harthalín stares at the unfortunate shepherdess, but her entreaties come to nothing. Anagúl will speak no more.

'Some of the raiders escaped from Narchraw, and I believe they slipped away with the others of their captives still in tow. Alas for Anagúl! But we cannot abandon the others while they may yet live.
'They make for Nan Ogol, and therefore so must we!'
'Onward, ${PLAYER}. We pass beneath the eaves of the forest and into the fell vale of Nan Ogol. Our companions await us just ahead.'

'Narchraw must not have intended the Draugrim to escape him; he pursued them all the way from Ata-gabar and into Nan Ogol.
'But I do not see the bodies of the captives. We must hope they escaped during his attack, and fled deeper into the fell vale. At least we may take some hope in the knowledge they did not perish here, not yet.
'Khálya will mourn Anagúl when we return, but if we act swiftly it may be she need not grieve for the others of her people that were taken.'

'Some months ago, Kâl-maka-Hôi was asked for her hand in marriage.
'Stôr-weni-Kûl say he love her, and she should be his wife. For some weeks she consider question, but then Stôr-weni-Kûl leave Dhol Têg. He say she should come too, but Kâl afraid... afraid of fell vale, afraid of Thyrsar that live there, afraid of becoming wife.
'She loves Stôr-weni-Kûl? She thinks she loves him. But she afraid. Cannot decide what to do.'

'By the time we reached Ata-gabar, the raiders that survived Narchraw's attack had already moved on, with the two of you still held captive. We found the shepherdess Anagúl atop the hill, but she was beyond saving and near to death.'
Harthalín pauses.
'Before she succumbed to her wounds, the shepherdess said the creature Narchraw spoke... upsetting words. It was not clear to me what said the wolf... something about a secret verse? Something concerning a door? Did you hear these words?'

'What can it mean that I dream the same dream as Narchraw, ${PLAYER}?'
Harthalín turns frightened eyes upon you, and the sight of such terror on the face of one so courageous freezes your blood.
'I am once again beside that wall in Gorgoroth, with the shadow of Morlang upon me. Will I never be free of this fear?'

'You get used to life in the wilderness, do you not, ${PLAYER}?
'But listen well when I tell you that a dry place by the fire cannot be overvalued!'

' knows this story; indeed, ${PLAYER:she[f]|he} knows some of it I myself do not, for I spent no small portion of it with no memory of those events! And yet I came to myself by the end, and saw Núrzum defeated!
'He was a stone giant, a mighty creature that should have lived peacefully within the mountains, but he was cast out by his people. It was Saruman the Wizard who healed his hurts and guided him to vengeance against my people, binding to his back an ancient artifact that should never have resurfaced: the Stone of Thangorodrim. Wherever Núrzum and the Stone went, snow and ice followed, until at last we faced him in glorious combat and severed his connexion to the evil Saruman had worked. Now he is encased in a tomb of ice, and troubles my people no more.
'He was a mighty foe, but in the end Thrymm Red-beard proved the stronger man, despite the giant's height and the size of his sinews! Ah, it was such a contest. I wish you might have seen it, Prêkh-weni-Pâsh!'

'I do not delay my marriage to the lovely Cyneberg out of fear! If that were so she would not wish to have me for a husband, and I would hold her blameless!
'But I cannot return to Wildermore while servants of Sauron remain to trouble these lands. Would you abandon a quest with it still undone, ${PLAYER}? Would a craftsman leave the object of his art half-finished? So it is with Thrymm, and with Cyneberg too, for that matter. Only when there is peace will the wedding-bells ring again in Forlaw.'
You think he has finished, but after a moment he continues in a quieter voice.
'In all the Mead Halls of my home they name me the Hero of Wildermore, and I tell you I have earned the title. But... is that to be the last of my deeds? When the last of Sauron's servants have been slain, and peace is assured... will there be no further adventures for Thrymm Red-beard? Is that to be the end of his glories, ${PLAYER}?'
Thrymm shakes his head and laughs.
'No, of course it will not be so! There is evil still to be faced before we must think of such things as that!'

'Ghôl hunting in forest not long after last and mightiest shaking from Mountain of Fire. He find blood spattering leaves, trail of droplets leading into thicket. He follow signs, and find Mûlazar dying.
'Ghôl knew him at once. What Khemozêl would not? But it seemed to Ghôl that cruel master of Draugardh tried to flee from Were-wolves he used to rule; now they rule, and savage him with teeth and claws as he escape. Not quick enough, and not for good! Now Ghôl-buri-Prân is his jailor. Ghôl-buri-Prân decide what to do with him.'

'These lands were given to ME, not to those ungrateful pups! I earned their hatred over many years, it is true, but is that not always how it lies with the governed? How many examples of disobedience and failure from them must my Master have stomached? For me once only would have sufficed, but chance after chance my Master gave to them!
'The wolves waited for their moment. That much is clear to me now. When I returned to Bâr Guruthos on that day of confusion when my Master fell, they attacked without warning. I fought them off with sword and spell, but Thothrach seized me in his jaws and shook me, trying to break my back. It was his one chance to slay me, but he failed as he faileth at all things! He will carry the scar I gave him until he dies.
'I managed to reach Nîlugru and he took to the air, but he was wounded as I was, and I fell from his back somewhere over the vale. I knew nothing else until I awoke a prisoner, not of the wolves but of this cursed jailor. He will pay for this as will Thothrach.'

'None remain to oppose us, my warriors! Search the tower!'

'That one was a young Gaurhoth warrior named Narchraw, a firebrand from the days of his youth in the pits of Mordath under Barad-dûr. He spoke out against me and the other Gúrzyul, against the nine Nazgûl, and against Sauron the Master of all. Before long he had acquired a following large enough to challenge Iurithil, the Lord of Beasts who ruled the Gaurhoth at that time.
'Iurithil lost his throat and his life in the battle that followed, and Narchraw gained the jewelled torc of the Lord of Beasts. He was now Skárashakh and ruled from Bâr Guruthos, a mighty keep in Nan Ogol. He continued to speak, and the wolves continued to listen.'

'Narchraw argued there was no better time to rise up and search Barad-dûr for the secrets that would restore the lost greatness of the Gaurhoth. The Ringwraiths ruled in Mordor, but their strength was abated in the absence of Sauron, and even the powerful Gúrzyul lacked His darkness to fire them. Narchraw believed they might seize the Nine Rings... possibly even the One! And then they would be free of the dominion of Sauron.
'He was a fool. Even then I knew of it. Long had I suspected treachery, and I commanded a host of Orcs and Men to meet the Were-wolves in battle. This would come to be known as the Were-wolves' War, the Wolf-strife, and it would have lasting effect upon the land of Mordor and the domain of Sauron.
'Accompanied by one of the Nazgûl, my host of Orcs and Men engaged the wolves in battle upon the fields of Parth Rhavas.'

'It was Borangos the Horror who betrayed us on that day. Leading a host of dark spirits from his caverns in Nargroth, he fell upon my host with terrible fire, leaving us open to attack from Narchraw's wolves. Orcs and Men scattered before that terrible onslaught, and even the mighty Nazgûl perished. Without my Master to restore him, the wraith languished, powerless to return; nine became eight, and the wolves saw the path to their victory.
'With most of my soldiers slain, I was forced to flee before the combined might of Borangos and Narchraw.'

'The forging of the Rings of Power in Eregion heralded the end of Sauron's reliance upon the Were-wolves. They were among the few in Mordor to whom He revealed that design in those early days, and they greatly desired the rings for their own. It was never His intention to bestow the rings upon the Gaurhoth, but He allowed them to believe it while it suited His purposes. So 'twas that He went alone into Orodruin, toiling for days to shape the One Ring, a master ring to rule all the others.
'When at last He emerged from the mountain, the Gaurhoth sensed the terrible power that had been harnessed, and they coveted it.'

'Sauron commanded His servants to seek an alloy with which He might forge mighty weapons, the better to channel the power of the One Ring. The Gaurhoth found early success with the green crystal delothlín, mined from the forested vale where they dwelt, but it proved harmful even to those who bore it; many wolves perished attempting to refine it. Their incompetence threatened to undermine my Master's plans, and they were punished for this failure and others. But at last Sauron achieved His desire, for the metal-workers of Udûn devised a mix of materials that gave rise to Morgul-steel.
'With the use of the Morgul-steel, Sauron could now fashion stronger and more loyal servants than the Were-wolves had ever proved. He called us to Him, and gave to us a mighty gift he gave to few others.'

'The Gaurhoth were so low in my Master's esteem at this time they knew nothing of His plans. When they learned He had been captured by the King of Númenor and brought to that island kingdom in chains, they despaired, for their power and their very lives depended upon the spirits on which they fed, and it was only His power that provided them.
'They knew not that Sauron's surrender was only the first step in His scheme to see that nation destroyed. He hid the One Ring in some secret place unknown even to His loyal Gúrzyul, and left the Nine Nazgûl to rule Mordor during His absence.'

Thrymm stares blankly at the wall.
Harthalín stares down into the darkness, and does not notice you.
Kâl-maka-Hôi stares at you with surprise.

'What happened to you, ${PLAYER}? We very busy here!
'But where are Harthalín and Ranger? Where is Thrymm?'

'I told you I would catch up, ${PLAYER}!
'Thrymm has begun to improve somewhat, but he is still too weak to carry a sword. I blush to tell you that I had to bodily lift Harthalín away from the pit with which she was fascinated, and I was not gentle... but as we drew further away she began to recover.
'But we should not delay here any longer. Let us escape into fresh air and freedom!'

'There are wolves ahead, ${PLAYER}, but they have not yet seen us.
'Let us approach them from the rocks on the right and see what has so taken their attention. It may be someone or something else will provide us the distraction we need to at last put Bâr Guruthos behind us, and not a moment too soon!'
Thrymm stares blankly forward and does not respond when you call his name. He is covered in blood from an unpleasant wound to his arm, but he is alive.

'What sort of jailor keeps a prisoner in a cell without a door, ${PLAYER}?'
Orthonn stares for a moment at Thrymm sitting weakly on the floor, and then the Ranger's eyes light with realization.
'They have ensured he won't try to leave. If that wound is from the jaws of one of the Gaurhoth...'

You call Harthalín's name, but she does not seem to hear you. Instead she claws at the grate on which she crouches, seeking to pry it loose from its fastenings.
'I have to get down there,' she mutters, straining at the metal bars. You seize her by her shoulders and attempt to pull her from her position atop the grate, but though she remains oblivious to you her muscles tense and seem to be made of steel.
'They call to me!' she cries. 'They call!'

'Listen to me, ${PLAYER}. Something is wrong with Harthalín, and I think Thrymm's wound has left him too weak to fight. I need you to go ahead of us and clear the way back to the surface, or none of us will have any hope of escaping from Falch Lhoss.
'No, argue not with me! I will lead our companions behind you, but I need you to clear the way or we will all perish. I will see you at the top... trust me in this!'

'The Khemozêl will guard the way out for us, ${PLAYER}!
'The rest of us must delve onward and downward in search of Thrymm!'

'Bâr Guruthos have ugly reputation among Khemozêl. None come here without good reason... but rescue of Red-Bearded One seem like worthy reason for Prêkh and his friends.
'Hold tight to your courage, ${PLAYER}. Prêkh not know what we find down here.'

'I feel... light-headed. I am sorry... I know not what has come over me.
'It must be the choking atmosphere of this place. I will be... I will be fine in a moment.'

'You have nothing for which to apologize, Harthalín! This place smells fouler than I would have thought possible, and I will be happier when we emerge once again into fresh air.
'I will lead the way. Stay behind me, and breathe not too deeply of the miasmic cloud that fills these passages!'

'One thing is certain to me, ${PLAYER}. Orthonn has been spending too much time with you, because now he has developed a fondness for giving speeches.
'Let us hope he grows out of it.'
Orthonn stands in the Splintered Shield as he did not long ago, when your journey began.

Your companions speak of the events that transpired on your journey through the Wolven-lands.
Harthalín is greatly disturbed by the events that transpired deep beneath Guruthos.

'Much has happened since then, has it not?
'But let us not delay. Our friends should be waiting for us ahead. Let us join them!'

'I speak in jest, ${PLAYER}. I know it is not fair to say such a thing!
'To learn of an enemy's presence is of value to us, for only then can we adequately prepare to oppose him. But better still is to make the acquaintance of a new friend!
'I am pleased to have met these Khemozêl! I understand they drew some attention outside, for people of the city have not seen visitors such as Prêkh-weni-Pâsh and Kâl-maka-Hôi before now. I know they will be made welcome.'

'I cannot remember anything that transpired in the dungeons below Bâr Guruthos, ${PLAYER}... it is only through the reporting of Orthonn that I know of these events, and they feel as if they happened to someone else. But there is something else that troubles me, beside even this.
'It is bad enough to think I was overcome by a fleeting madness, and the words I spoke there were untrue. But it is worse by far in this case: what if my crazed words in the dungeons were words of truth? What is it that lies beneath Guruthos? What are the verses of victory?
'And why do they fill me with a sensation of fear beyond any I have ever felt in all of my days?'

'Bodhoi mulom, stranger. You are welcome in our lands so long as you make no disturbance and harm no herd.
'Kol Sákla is a difficult land, but she is ours, at least for now. These are not our ancestral homelands, but they are open, and our herds find enough for sustenance. That is all we require.
'We do not have much, but what we do have we share with those we find worthy. You should speak with Niyoz to learn more.'

'Bodhoi mulom. May your herd find their way home.
'Kol Sákla is where we have made our home, though for many our hearts lie elsewhere. But those lands are closed to us now, and we, like our cattle, have to press on to new pastures.
'If you help the Têtikir within Parth Rhavas, we will see it, and reward you for it. We are not a trusting people, ${PLAYER}. We have seen too much bloodshed to trust easily. But for those who earn it, we are fiercely loyal. Prove to us you bring goodwill and loyalty to the Têtikir, and we will reward you handsomely for it.'

'We are happy to have you in Kol Sákla, as long as your aims are peaceful and your weapons stay sheathed.
'We Têtikir trust what we see, and the actions you take. Prove loyal to the Têtikir, and you will scarcely find a more welcome place than Kol Sákla. Prove yourself an enemy to the Têtikir, and you will find something else entirely.'

'${PLAYER}, ¡es bueno verte! Sabía que con la ampliación de la grieta del Fragmento volverías a encontrar tu camino hacia Mordor.'
'Sigue el camino del valle en Heledhris hacia el este y baja por las laderas hasta las llanuras de Parth Rhavas. Allí encontrarás a Thurindol y su campamento.'

'En mi viaje desde Minas Tirith, mis compañeros y yo pasamos por el Valle de Morgul. Allí nos encontramos con los Montaraces de Ithilien y héroes de Gondor por igual. Mientras intercambiábamos historias, se reunió un pequeño grupo de aliados, para guiarnos y explorar los confines desconocidos de Draugardh. A través del valle de Lhingris escalamos, y a través de las llanuras llenas de ceniza de Talath Úrui marchamos. El camino hacia la grieta del Fragmento finalmente se nos hizo conocido cuando llegamos a las montañas de Agarnaith.
'Este grupo de aliados te es conocido, ${PLAYER}. Su líder, Thurindol de los Guardabosques de Ithilien, habló muchas veces de tu valentía. Esta pequeña banda de aliados ha explorado por delante de nosotros. Thurindol me aseguró que establecerían un campamento, no muy lejos de aquí, en el borde occidental del Lothfold. Debes buscar a Thurindol y contarle lo que hemos aprendido durante nuestro tiempo en Heledhris.
'Tu compañía ha sido muy útil a través de la grieta del Fragmento de Heledhris. Por un momento, debemos separarnos, mientras espero mis órdenes.'

'Have you had a moment to test the water samples that you and Thurindol collected? I have asked Zapharo if we might use his people's belongings. He did not mind our curiosity.'

'These findings in the water samples you have collected from the Dread-mere are indeed fascinating. Perhaps something foul seeps into the waters, high at the river's source? It may be a while before we are able to return to this mystery. The source of the River Ascarant is far from us.
'Let us do what we can to make travel safer in Parth Rhavas. I see the Têtikir as a great ally. We should assist in their efforts as much as we are able. Ingold has suggested retaking Obalang. I agree with his judgement.'

'I shall tell you of the Khashkhilar. This clan has lived in Draugardh for many years. It is said they revere the Were-wolves and follow the Gaurhoth in worship. It is strange to see a clan following the Wolf-way with such devotion. I speak the truth when I say that the Khashkhilar will never be an ally of the Têtikir.'

'The Sûhalar are a fractured clan. They lost many to a war in the west, a war they did not need to fight in. Now they have no home, no guidance, and no true leader.'
You tell Zapharo of the Sûhalar you encountered at the Pelennor Fields and the Black Gate.
'Yes, that is the battle the Sûhalar speak of. Few survived, and are now stranded in Parth Rhavas, for none can return east. If you encounter the Sûhalar in Parth Rhavas, each camp will treat outsiders differently. Some may be hostile, some may be welcoming. Each splinter of the Sûhalar will find their own way.'

'You wish to hear of my people, the Têtikir? We are a herding-clan of the Zalang.
'I shall not speak of the disaster that has befallen my ancestral lands. It is too much to bear. What I will say is that after the devastation, we became nomadic, travelling ever east. At last, we came upon the slopes of Parth Rhavas, where great beasts graze. Now we try to make this land our new home.'
'Thurindol has told me of what has transpired at Obalang. I believe we may be of some assistance to the Têtikir.'
'I hope to find you and your friends rested. Oh, you wish to assist us in reclaiming Obalang?!'

These lands may be harsh, but there is an abundance if you know where to look. Obalang was to be our new home. Now, the other clans squabble over it.

'You and your companions are very kind in wanting to help us reclaim Obalang. There are many preparations to be made before we can achieve such a victory.
'I shall first tell you about our retreat from Obalang. The Khashkhilar attacked at dawn, without warning. We Têtikir may live a peaceful life, but we are not without conflict. We all study weapons and seek retribution by blade, if our people are wronged. I believe we would have fended off the Khashkhilar that day, if it were not for a band of Sûhalar. I do not know if they truly work together, but on that day the Khashkhilar and Sûhalar found a common goal. Their numbers overwhelmed. We took what we could carry and fled.
'Since we fled in such haste, there are many valuable supplies in Obalang still. I believe we could reclaim some of these supplies if we were to sneak into the village. Are you up for such a task? I know you seek a forge as well. There is a working forge in Obalang that you may use if you feel safe to do so.'

'Greetings stranger, I am Sumbula, leader of Kol Sákla. You bring word from Zapharo and Khushba? I see. I am saddened to hear what has befallen Obalang. We had hoped it would be a strong village, as the grazing lands around Obalang are perfect for raising herds of great beasts.
'I will begin the preparations necessary for sending supplies and warriors westward. This task will take time, ${CLASS}, as we have also been attacked recently.
'Perhaps there is something you could assist me with to quicken the pace? I have been dealing with a captive Khashkhilar warrior. It is strange. She appeared in town, alone, with no weapon in hand. May you have better luck with her ramblings than I have!'

'Ha! What have we here?! Are you lost or some sort of wanderer? Well wanderer, if you free me, I promise you that I am not here to harm you or a single Têtikir.
'Oh, do you not believe me? I respect that! Sumbula would have stopped listening to me by now. You, on the other hand, stay. I respect that as well! A test of my word then?
'I shall provide you with information that will prevent the village of Kol Sákla from being raided. There are three watch-towers that dot the eastern cliffs of Parth Rhavas. One of the towers hides a Khashkhilar raiding party. Defeat the raiding party and save the village. It is that simple.'
'There was a raiding party in one of the ruins? What wonder! Now you will free me? No? Your loss, wanderer!'

'You return with an offer of an alliance from Sóghut Bastukh?! I am amazed that Arzheki's words have once again proven true! Perhaps the story she told me rings true as well. Oh, you did not hear her tale? You should ask her to tell you what she has told me. Go, free her from the shackles I had placed on her, and escort her to where she needs to be. Arzheki has earned my trust.
'After you have freed Arzheki, the supplies for Khushba and Zapharo are ready. Retrieve the supplies before you venture west again. Thank you, for all that you have done, ${CLASS}.'

You hand Sóghut Bastukh the ceremonial axe and tell him what has transpired.
'I see, I see. Bagatur lives! I am glad that my warriors will return soon. Time will tell on the fate of Armanjarsi, however.
'Your deeds have shown me a valuable lesson on this day. There are many dangers in Parth Rhavas and I must remember to stay vigilant. It would also behoove me to seek an alliance, as I wish not to lose more men to the dangers of these lands. If your bond to the Têtikir rings true, would you give them this peace totem on my behalf?'

'I must thank you, ${CLASS}. If it were not for you, the Têtikir would have failed my test! I could have escaped Kol Sákla at any time. Instead, I waited and hoped they would pass my test. I arrived, alone and weaponless, in the hopes Têtikir could become a trusting ally. You see, I need allies for my people, my family. I will tell you more as we travel, ${PLAYER}. I must return to Nan Ogol.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. I report that the matters at Sutun Baka have been resolved.

'Thank you for returning with supplies, ${PLAYER}. Ingold and Candúr have been invaluable assistants to us while you and Thurindol were away.

'Perhaps it is best I start at the beginning. Upon Sóghut Bastukh's request I led a hunting party north. The first night we made camp I went to fetch brambles for the fire. That is when Armanjarsi came and overpowered my men with his poisonous concoctions. I tracked Armanjarsi to his farm where he put my friends in cages, forcing his vile draughts upon them. I waited for the moment to free my men, but that moment never came. A hunting party of Draugrim attacked, stealing my men, as Armanjarsi ran for the hills. The Draugrim took my friends into the Pillar-gardens, and that is where you found me! That is my tale of ill fortune.
'Thurindol has agreed to assist me in retrieving the rest of my men from the Pillar-gardens. You should return to Sóghut Bastukh. He will be most eager to hear what has transpired in Sutun Baka. Take this ceremonial axe. If it is not covered in blood, then Sóghut Bastukh will know you speak the truth, and that I have given it to you.'

'Have we reached an agreement? The Summer Crow will tolerate our pact.
'Seek out the Khûrz-hai and free my people. Seek out the Draugrim and sow the seeds of discord. Seek out Tupanyel Bêk, within the audience hall, deep inside the ruins of Rhuvendír, and halt the fool's plans. This I ask of you.'

'A moment of your time is all I require. You must listen well.
'I both admire you and despise you. Yet, fine allies we would make. I am Yazluk-garga, the Summer Crow.
'I have seen you from afar, destroying my people. For that, we are enemies. I have seen your strength, unmatched. For that you will assist these brittle bones and a sharp mind of the Summer Crow. I have seen many leaders of the Khashkhilar rise and fall. All have followed the Wolf-way, as they should. All that is, but Tupanyel Bêk. He leads the Khashkhilar astray, to a certain death that he does not see. The Summer Crow sees it all too well. Tupanyel Bêk seeks power. To obtain that power, he is sacrificing more of us to the Draugrim, to be shaped into Khûrz-hai. If he is not stopped, the Khashkhilar will soon be no more.
'I will give you the information you need to defeat Tupanyel Bêk. He meets with the Draugrim in Rhuvendír as we speak. In return, all I ask is that you spare those who truly follow the Wolf-way. The Summer Crow has spoken.'

'This Tupanyel Bêk is sacrificing his own to be shaped into Khûrz-hai? Zapharo has told me of the Khûrz-hai.
'They are those purposely afflicted with Wolf-sickness from the venom of the Gaurhoth. They are heedless, ferocious trackers and fighters used like hounds by the Were-wolves with no regard for their lives.'

'The Draugrim have occupied Rhuvendír? Zapharo has told me of the Draugrim.
'These lesser Were-wolves do not have the strength of the Gaurhoth. They have lost that strength by adding the blood of Men to their lines. The Gaurhoth rule over them with disdain.'

'Could it be possible the Gaurhoth oversee the Draugrim in Rhuvendír? Zapharo has told me of the Gaurhoth.
'They are Were-wolves of old, bred through dark sorcery. It is said they have lived in Mordor since the First Age, and can bend the will of most any beast.'
'It is as Yazluk-garga said it would be. I hear many voices arguing on the other side of this door.'

'I am certain that Yazluk-garga cannot be trusted. However, there are times when enemies find a common goal. Perhaps this is one of those times. I have no hatred of the Khashkhilar. I only wish for them to leave the Têtikir be. Yazluk-garga also wishes for the bloodshed to be over. I believe we should accept the Summer Crow's offer, ${PLAYER}. We will need to investigate Rhuvendír either way.
'If the Draugrim and Khashkhilar work together in Rhuvendír, we must stop them from gathering strength in Parth Rhavas. I see no other way, if I am to protect the Têtikir in these lands.'

'Do you see the old woman on the bridge as well, or are my eyes playing tricks? You see her too. That is good! She seems to be beckoning you to meet with her.'

To Nan Ogol
'When you have finished here in Parth Rhavas, I will meet you at Urotar in Nan Ogol.'

'While you have earned my trust, you have not earned the trust of my clan, the Yokhut-oba. They will be suspicious of you. That I am certain. However, there is one who will believe us. My plans in Parth Rhavas were her idea, after all.
'I have spoken to my sister, Tasila. I have told her of your bravery and trials in Parth Rhavas. She will trust you, for our bond is strong. She will speak with you now.'
'You are the cunning warrior of which Arzheki speaks so highly? Your skills will be put to the test soon enough. Tell me, what do you really know about the Gaurhoth?'

'I must return to my family at once. They are in dire need of assistance. There are no allies in Nan Ogol, only ghastly horrors!
'The land of Nan Ogol is our home. We must try to halt the horror there, for no one else will. We will not flee. We have our reasons and those reasons will be shown to you in time.
'I went to Parth Rhavas on a mission to search for assistance. When you passed my test, I knew you would be able to assist the efforts of my family.
'With your aid, as well as our Têtikir and Sûhalar allies, my family might survive.'

'Have you returned with meat for the journey? We will need it.
'I hope my family will welcome you, for you have helped me greatly with my tasks. The joy of returning will be short, however. You, and all of Parth Rhavas, are ill prepared for what horrors lie ahead.'

'You have done much to lift our spirits, ${PLAYER}. When we first settled upon Parth Rhavas, I thought this was the end of the Sûhalar. The pain, the death, the endless wars, had all taken its toll. We could not return home, so we came to Draugardh to slowly fade away.
'Now I see a new beginning. The Têtikir prove to be a strong ally! They have even offered us shelter at Obalang, once the village is rebuilt. In return, I will work to bring the rest of the Sûhalar under my banner. It may be a fool's errand, but I must try. They are my brethren, after all!'

'Are you prepared to complete your task, wanderer? I would very much like to see my family and report to them what has transpired in Parth Rhavas.
'You must understand that they are my blood. My family and I have denounced the Khashkhilar way for our own way. There are no allies for my family in Nan Ogol, yet we must stay there. We have been marked for our decision.'

'You are to guide Arzheki back to her family? I am glad that you are making good on your word, ${PLAYER}. Sumbula of Kol Sákla will be pleased. We know not of Arzheki and her family, but I hope this splinter group of Khashkhilar will be an important ally of the Têtikir. I thank you again for your efforts in helping my people.'

'This is where we must part ways, ${PLAYER}. My orders are to keep the road through Parth Rhavas clear. You alone must guide Arzheki to her destination.
'I assure you there will be enough adventure for both of us. My companions and I feel it is important that we investigate the fog below the southern cliffs. I find the clouds beneath Bôk Jekir and Gáyadali unsettling. It reminds me of Thuringwath. I may call upon you again, my friend. Fare well on your travels.'

The wizened old woman gazes at you silently for a time, before she turns to her son and begins to speak.
'Bhôd. Pêk was not a child, and listened only to her own mind. If she does not listen to Mêj-dhug-Mêj, what makes you think she would do whatever Yêm-pulo-Wêgh tells her to?
'I do not think ${PLAYER} would lie. If ${PLAYER} says they were in love, then I think it was so. Yêm did not make her die. Bhôd did not make her die. Kwôhu, and only Kwôhu, killed Pêk. You want to hate? Hate Kwôhu.'
She nods in way that indicates finality.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER} for your telling of events. You may sit at the fire of Mêj-dhug-Mêj any time you like.'

Bhôd sits in silence for a time, ruminating on his mother's words.
'Mêj-dhug-Mêj speaks only the truth. If Pêk loved Yêm, she would not want me to blame him. If they truly loved and wanted to wed, then I shall love Yêm-pulo-Wêgh as a son, to honour Pêk. I give to Pêk everything a father can, and this time I will give respect to her choices.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for keeping your word, and returning to us with the news, terrible though it is. It is better to know, than to always be worrying.'

'I... I foretold this, and yet it still comes as a shock. My child is dead?'
Your friend Bhôd-buri-Mêj looks for a moment like he might be sick.
'I have lost everything. But no, I still have Mêj, and when I lose my mother as well, the rest of the Khemozêl will look to me for guidance. My clan is my family.
'But that zhek, Yêm! I did not know of this betrothal. Did he hold sway on her thoughts? Was it his words that led her to Nan Ogol, when her father and wise Clan-mother forbade it? It is his fault she is dead. He might not hold the knife, but he killed her, just the same.'
You assure Bhod that their relationship started only after they reached Nan Ogol, and that their love for one another was genuine. He listens and looks skeptical.
'${PLAYER}, would you meet me in Dhol Têg? Mêj-dhug-Mêj must know of this, and she will want to hear your tale, as you were there. It would mean much to us both.'
You recount your tale of the events in Nan Ogol to the Clan-mother. She listens intently, and has little reaction. When your story ends, she pats the ground next to her, inviting you to sit.

'The survivors fled north, tailed closely by Sauron's army, invigorated by their victory and the presence of their lord. Seeking to deny the refugees of any place to find succour, a Rogmul called Bragollúth assaulted the bastion of Minas Elendúr. Trapped, all inside were slaughtered to the Elf.

'So, ${PLAYER}, how do my fighting skills compare? Am I not the equal of our companions?'
You tell her that she has no reason to doubt herself, and she fought quite well, and is assuredly their peer.
'Oh, that is such a relief! I did think so, but when so many people dismiss you for so long, it is difficult to not start believing in their judgements, baseless though they may be.
'Thank you for your help. I will remain steadfast in my self-pride. If they cannot see my worth, their blindness is their own, and not my concern.'
'I am ready to spar whenever you are, ${PLAYER}. Are you prepared?'
Wynflad has asked you to spar with her, and then with some of the other scouts to see how her skill with the sword compares with theirs. You should talk to Wynflad when you are ready to spar.
You have sparred with Wynflad and many of the scouts in order to see how her fighting skills compare to the rest of the group. You should talk to her about what you have learned.

'Though tending the horses is my given task, it is not why I volunteered for this expedition. Long have I trained for battle, but the men above me make every effort to keep me away from the battlefields.
'I wanted to learn the sword at first just to be able to defend myself. The confidence and feeling of strength that comes from competence with a blade is intoxicating, though, and I continued to train beyond the basics. Though I am no master, I believe I can handle myself in battle as well as any man.
'No woman of Rohan can be called weak, but we are expected to only be strong of heart. I can say that I am strong in arms, and the men discourage me from such things, asking why I have no husband and children yet, as if that is all a woman should ever want. It fills me with anger and makes me question my worthiness.
'Brorda dismissed me when I spoke of the sword, so I challenged him to spar. The churl denied me, saying he did not wish to harm a woman! It is infuriating, and yet there is a lingering part of me that wonders if he is correct, and I am not worthy.
'${PLAYER}, he and the others would not dismiss a hero such yourself. Would you spar with me and then with the other scouts and tell me how I compare to them?'

'I would like to put myself to a true test, but I am not so foolhardy as to run off into battle alone. I would like to combat an intelligent foe, not just unthinking beasts.
'Bhôd-buri-Mêj spoke of a Warg-lair on a mountainside called Mal Rakhúrz. Would you join me one more time, to fell some Wargs? Take your own path, and I will meet you at Mal Rakhúrz, to the east.'

'${PLAYER}, I am relieved you made it! This place is larger than I expected it to be.
'I wish to test myself, but I know better than to venture into such a place alone. I do think though, that if we split up we can bring about confusion, and they will not know which way to go.
'You should approach them from this path here, and I will slip around and attack them from the west. When we have each had enough of Wargs, meet me back here.'

'I think I've had quite enough of Wargs today. What say you, ${PLAYER}?
'Let us return to Dorngol and talk there. I have some thinking I must do on the journey back.'

'${PLAYER}, thank you for your friendship. I no longer doubt myself, and know for a fact that I can fight as well as any man in this company. I would prefer it if they agreed, but I cannot govern the minds of others. What I do have control over is how I view myself, and I now know that what I believe is not untrue.
'While Brorda and the Men that hail from Gondor may never give me the respect I am due, I think Lord Haereldir is different. Elf-maidens have oft joined the fight against darkness, so to him it is not so an unusual thing.
'But I digress. I just wanted to thank you.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.
'It has always been our tradition to leave the fallen where they fell. It is respectful to not move them from the place of their battle. Their body returns to the earth in that place, feeding the life that goes on around it.

'Ah, there you are! While you were away, I spent some time watching Hêg-maka-Chêrd hit her rocks together. This will be easy.'
Brorda takes the gloom-glass and strikes one with a knapping rock, breaking the whole thing in half.
'That one must have had a weakness or crack already in it. Let's try another.'
As he continues, it becomes apparent to Brorda that all of the gloom-glass you collected must have had cracks or other weaknesses in them. Soon, all he is left with is pieces too small to be spear points, and it doesn't seem to occur to him that maybe he lacks skill or knowledge.
'I suppose that is what I get for not collecting them myself. Not that I blame you, ${PLAYER}, you were only trying to help.'

You watch as Hêg-maka-Chêrd hits the gloom-glass with another rock in precise locations, using the perfect amount of force to break off shards. With each shard that is removed, the larger piece takes on the shape of a spear point. After allowing you to watch her for a time, she finally speaks.
'I would like to see Horse-rider hunt with a \qrock on a stick\q. If we are so simple next to the Horse-people, he should be able to do it easily, yes?'

'She thinks I should give it a try, does she?'
Brorda laughs.
'Even a babe can clap two rocks together. I accept her challenge!
'${PLAYER}, I shall need some of this gloom-glass. Would you gather some for me?
'I would like a good amount, as I may need a little practice. I recall seeing a lot of it on the northern slope, just outside Khel Wêro.'
Gloom-glass collected (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hêg-maka-Chêrd, a Khemozêl hunter, overheard Brorda criticizing their primitive weaponry and didn't seem pleased. You should talk to her.
Offended by Brorda's judgement that Khemozêl weapons are primitive and ineffective, Hêg-maka-Chêrd commented that she would like to see Brorda make his own spear.

'${PLAYER}, it amazes me that these people can survive as well as they do with such primitive weaponry. They fight and hunt with what amounts to simply a rock on a stick! It is a wonder that they can hunt boars with the things. How can they defend themselves from the likes of Were-wolves and Olog-hai without good steel? I cannot imagine that their so-called \qspears\q are very effective.'
You notice a Khemozêl hunter listening to your conversation with an unhappy expression. Perhaps you should talk to her.

'A carving? What about trade?
'Horse-man says he has many tales. I would like to hear a telling.'

'Well, I think the tale of most interest to a Wild Man is the one I spoke of briefly already....'
Brorda tells a colourful tale of how six thousand Riders of Rohan rode to the aid of a besieged Minas Tirith, and would not have made it were it not for the Khemozêl's kin to the west. He describes in detail the exhaustion of the weeklong march, as well as the glory of riding his steed as they thundered across the quaking fields of the Pelennor.
He spoke of monstrous mûmakil, black wraiths with fell flying steeds, and the chaos of battle. Only when the day was won and the fighting ended, did he realize he was greatly injured, and only lived because he was able to get treatment in the Houses of Healing.
Chêl-buri-Chêl listens to the tale with rapt attention, slack-jawed with amazement.

'Good tale!
'I like the good end. Khemozêl tales mostly have bad ends.
'When far-away mountain burst, ground here shakes, and our mountains burst, too, and bleed fire. Great rocks flying through the air... and the air! So much ash, and hot. Hard to breathe. Many Khemozêl die.
'My brother, he went missing. He was a great warrior, and bore the necklace of our fathers. It passed down for long time from many fathers. Now? No more. He die in the ash.
'Here, carving for you, Horse-man. Brorda. Good tale.'
He hands a small carving of a wolf to Brorda.

Brorda told a tale of the Battle of the Pelennor Fields and the events leading up to it, thoroughly entertaining Chêl-buri-Chêl. The Khemozêl then shared that his people's tales of recent events are all sad ones, sharing with you both the loss of his brother, along with their family heirloom.

'It is a beautiful thing that you did, ${PLAYER}. I am proud to have played a part in it, small though it was.
'The tears are those of sadness and not joy, but it will begin the healing of his heart, of that I am sure.'

'${PLAYER}, I find the fate of the Westfold almost pleasant compared to what these people have endured.
'I have a thought. Chêl's brother cannot be returned, but maybe that necklace could be. Let us search for it! Let this man have some sort of joy! There is is little of it here, and I know how it feels to lose everything, and be the one that somehow must live on.
'Ah, but alas, I cannot. I have duties given to me from Lord Haereldir that tether me to Khel Wêro at present.
'But you may come and go as you wish! ${PLAYER}, would you search for this necklace Chêl spoke of?'

Chêl-buri-Chêl is speechless as you hold out the necklace, wordlessly confirming that this is indeed his family's necklace.
He tentatively takes it from you as tears well up in his eyes.
You may be able to help Brorda get a token of the Khemozêl. You should talk to a carver.
On Brorda's behalf, you asked if Chêl-buri-Chêl would part with one of his carvings. He offered an exchange for one of Brorda's adventurous tales.

'Meldir said to me that the Khemozêl are the same manner of folk as our Woses back home. I have heard tales of the Wild Men of the Woods since boyhood, but never have I seen one in the Westfold.
'I was among the Riders of King Théoden as we rode to the aid of Gondor, and it was rumoured that we were being guided through the secret paths of the forest by Woses. I did not get to see one with my own eyes, though I wished to.
'When I return to the lands of my fathers, I will have so many tales to tell! ${PLAYER}, do you think one of the Khemozêl would allow me to have one of their carvings? It would please me greatly to have a token to remember this adventure.'

Bâr Guruthos, the Houses of Fear
'I will lead you to the citadel, Bâr Guruthos, when you are prepared.'

'That did not play out how I had hoped, but nevertheless, the Gaurhoth host is scattered and leaderless. This is a victory for the Free Peoples.
'It does trouble me that Elugor escaped, however. The way his people rallied around him, called him their chosen one, went to war for him? That kind of inflated ego doesn’t just dissipate on its own. We have not seen the last of him, and when he shows his face again, he will be out for revenge.
'I will keep an eye on Bâr Guruthos and call for you if he surfaces. Until then, journey well, my friend.'

'I will gather the Scouts and meet you at Bâr Guruthos. We will stay hidden, and see how this ‘wolf civil war’ plays out.
'Help the Unadorned army defeat Thothrach. We already know he is a danger to the Free Peoples. But what will Elugor do with his new-found power, should he win? I don’t trust whatever it is will be in our best interests.
'I know you have been working with him, and perhaps this is… unsavoury… but if those two wolf armies destroy each other, and we’re in position to end this for good….
'Don’t think about it for now. Go to Bâr Guruthos and help the Unadorned. I will find you when I can.'

'We look to Elugor for hope because he is not like us. Broken. Lesser. The first in a long time.

'Oh, este dibujo es un desastre -- ¡un desastre! Puede que esté completo, pero ¿hermoso? Lo dudo. ¿Por qué pensé que podría representar todo ese color y luz?
'${PLAYER}, ¿podrías encontrar un nuevo sujeto cerca, por favor? Preferiblemente un animal, para un cambio de ritmo muy necesario. No soporto mirar esto por más tiempo.'

Cuando señalas la tortuga, él no dice nada al principio, solo la mira fijamente. Pasan unos momentos de silencio antes de que parezca recordar dónde -- o cuándo -- se encuentra.
'Acabo de recordar... no importa. Qué criatura tan magnífica.
'¿Por qué no te unes a mí para dibujarla, ${PLAYER}? Tengo papel y lápices de cera de sobra, y podremos compartir nuestro arte una vez que hayamos terminado. Ah, puedo probar los lápices de cera que creé con esas flores.'

'¡Eso fue un respiro bienvenido! Los lápices de cera que hice son aceptables; dejo la calidad del pigmento al paso del tiempo.'
Una ligera sonrisa se forma en su rostro mientras examina su dibujo de la tortuga. Esta es una vista de corta duración; en el momento en que dirige su atención a su dibujo del paisaje, su sonrisa se rompe y desaparece.
'Por supuesto, termino prefiriendo la pieza que creé por capricho. Perdóname, ${PLAYER}, por haberte traído aquí y no producir nada.'
Antes de irse, Emmathron estudia la tortuga en silencio por última vez, como si intentara grabarla en su memoria.
Este castor parece preferir nadar que quedarse quieto.
¡Esta tortuga sería perfecta para que Emmathron la dibujara!
Un animal menos asustadizo podría ser una mejor opción.
Esta rana puede ser demasiado pequeña y propensa a saltar.
Puede que haya animales más cerca del agua...

'No pensé que fuera el caso... pero si tú lo dices.'

'Dibujé algo que me gustó. ¡Dibujé algo que me gustó! Algunos aspectos podrían haberse dibujado un poco mejor, pero -- oh, ¿importa la perfección? Dibujé algo y no quise quemarlo de inmediato. Casi había olvidado lo que se siente.
'Casi había olvidado lo que era pasar tiempo con Melur, también. Rechacé su compañía durante tantos meses. Pero me has mostrado que no es demasiado tarde para cambiar -- que todavía puedo arreglar las cosas entre nosotros.'

'Contempla mi arte, o más bien la ausencia de arte! Nada más que blanco -- ¡cómo detesto el blanco! El color de la nada, del fracaso. ¿Soy realmente tan incapaz de ilustrar este paisaje?'
Su rostro se cae cuando le muestras el dibujo descolorido de la tortuga.
'Entonces la flor que estaba probando no será adecuada para mis lápices de cera. Perfectamente encantador. Ese dibujo no se dejó en las mejores condiciones, pero...
'Para explicar: he estado intentando replicar estas escenas para un amigo -- Melur, aquel sobre el que me preguntaste. Ya no puede viajar muy lejos, así que cuando vea mi arte, quiero que sienta que realmente está allí. Lamentablemente, puedes ver dónde me han dejado mis intentos.
'¿Cómo puedo ofrecerle un arte tan imperfecto?'

'Ah, un momento: hay una planta allí que me gustaría examinar. ¿Te importaría vigilar mi cuaderno de dibujo? No tengo intención de dibujar el paisaje hoy; siempre llevo mi cuaderno conmigo. La inspiración es caprichosa, después de todo. Aunque últimamente, parece evitarme más de lo habitual.
'Mira las páginas, si quieres. Lo único embarazoso que hay son piezas mediocres.'

El cuaderno de dibujo es una cosa monstruosa, con sus cubiertas sujetas para evitar que se caigan las hojas sueltas. Al hojearlo, encuentras representaciones vívidas no solo de lugares, sino también de animales y personas. Bastantes tortugas aparecen a lo largo del libro, ¿o son varios bocetos de una sola?
Es más fácil de decir con sus retratos de personas, ya que un rostro en particular aparece con más frecuencia que los demás: un Hombre con una sonrisa cálida. Parecería intocado por el tiempo, si no fuera por las sutiles marcas de la edad que se infiltran en cada retrato posterior.
Tal vez Emmathron te diga quién es.

'No creo que esa planta sea adecuada para mis lápices de cera... Pensé que coincidía con algunos bocetos que había visto, pero era la planta equivocada...'
Preguntas por el Hombre cuyo retrato has visto repetido a lo largo del cuaderno de dibujo.
Su ojo tiembla, lo que le hace suavizar su expresión con un asentimiento y una rápida sonrisa. 'Ah... ¿quieres saber sobre él? ¿Por qué? Es solo alguien que conozco, eso es todo -- '

'Está bien, me quedaré aquí mismo. Pero no hagas que esta conversación sea fácil para ella.'

'Estabas acompañando a mi hermana ese día en la taberna, ¿verdad? Quizás un tercero neutral sea lo que necesitamos las dos.
'Sí, soborné a los pregoneros; estos métodos fueron particularmente despiadados, incluso para mi padre. Pero Brútha no puede seguir aferrándose a este pequeño y tonto sueño suyo. Nuestro padre nos encomendó una responsabilidad antes de fallecer, y yo soy la única que cumple sus deseos.
'Sinceramente, reconozco que esto es una pérdida de tiempo. Debería detenerme -- las constantes discusiones me agotan. Sin embargo, a pesar de eso, persisto en intentar acercarme.'

'¿Preguntando de qué hablábamos? No sé qué te importa, pero no es como si ella me hubiera pagado para que me callara.'
Se encoge de hombros.
'Nos ha estado diciendo a todos que ignoremos a cierta fabricante de juguetes. ¿Se llama Snítha? Parece que hay un rencor y una historia detrás, pero no tengo ni idea más allá de eso.'

'¡Terminado! ¿Listos para entrar? Todo ese hablar y caminar me ha dejado hambrienta, y estoy deseando un asado de cerdo. Pero -- ¿pasó algo?'
Mientras le detallas lo que has descubierto, las fosas nasales de Brútha se dilatan.
'¿Snítha ha estado intentando sabotearnos? ¡Pero yo no le he hecho nada! Y si está haciendo esto para obligarme a volver a casa, ¡no sé por qué lo intenta! No necesita mi ayuda -- ¡nuestro padre se aseguró de ello!'

Brútha fija sus ojos entrecerrados en la espalda que se aleja de Snítha.
'Cuéntame lo que te dijo.'
Mientras le detallas la conversación que tuviste, la mirada de Brútha no se disipa; de hecho, comienza a apretar la mandíbula.
'Si quiere enmendarse, debería dejarme en paz.
'Olvídate de preparar esa comida; ya no tengo hambre.'
'Negociar con los pregoneros, ver a Snítha... este podría ser uno de los peores días que he tenido recientemente.'

'Veremos si podemos hacer que este tonto se enderece, ¿eh?'

'¡Ah, ahí está! Eso es lo que te da envejecer, ¿eh? Muy agradecido.'
'Escuché la puerta cerrarse antes... supongo que era Emmathron saliendo. Fui demasiado duro con él allá atrás, ¿no? Tal vez eso fue siete meses de ira acumulada, o tal vez no. Tal vez todavía me queda más ira por liberar.
'Después de todo, probablemente solo vino a verme ahora por algo que dijiste. Ese viejo tonto necesita un empujón en la dirección correcta cada vez que se queda atrapado dando vueltas en círculos.
'Oh, parece que el té está listo. ¡Oi, Emmathron!'

'Emmathron me está evitando, y no es solo porque esté enojado con él. ¿Por qué desapareció en primer lugar?
'¿Qué tal si hacemos un poco de planificación durante el té, ${PLAYER}? Podría ser el momento de pasar una tarde de jardinería juntos en el patio. Con tu influencia, estoy seguro de que Emmathron no se negará.'

'Sin embargo, la solicitud de Aslaug ha echado un poco por tierra la idea... ir en su contra estropearía las cosas entre nosotras. Podría crear una figura de caballo con patas ajustables en su lugar.
'Aun así, ¿cómo puede ella juzgar la fortaleza de Astrith? Solo Astrith lo sabría, y no puede aprender cuándo tomar un respiro si no se le da esa oportunidad en absoluto.

Cuando preguntas sobre la fascinación de Astrith por los caballos, Aslaug deja escapar un suspiro de cansancio.
'Oh, mi niña tonta... sueña constantemente con montar a caballo algún día. Tener un caballo está fuera de cuestión y, además, ¿cómo podría montar uno en su delicado estado?
'Es natural que hayas llegado a la conclusión de hacerle un juguete de caballo. Aunque ya tiene suficientes, no te impediré crear otro. Sin embargo, tengo una sola petición: por favor, no hagas algo que fomente la actividad física. El estrés adicional no le haría bien.
'¿Eso es suficiente información, sí? Entonces te acompañaré hasta la puerta.'

'Gracias por venir.
'Como he mencionado, me gustaría que hicieras un juguete para mi hija, Astrith. La enfermedad a menudo la aqueja y pasa días languideciendo en casa; por lo tanto, sus amigos son pocos y distantes.
'Si me sigues, podría tener más pensamientos que compartir sobre el asunto.'

'Aquí, te devuelvo el cubo.
'Sin duda has visto a las musarañas correteando por ahí. Son pequeños y graciosos, pero no puedo permitir que desentierren mis plantas. Ahuyéntalos.'

'Tengo los cubos justo aquí. Debería haber pedido a uno de ustedes que me acompañara; ¡transportarlos me ha costado toda mi fuerza!
'Toma uno y empieza a regar las plantas.'

'Lo siento. Me dejé llevar.
'Voy a buscar unos cubos de agua para nosotros. Mientras tanto, los dos pueden arrancar las malas hierbas.'

'Ha pasado bastante tiempo desde la última vez que estuve en el jardín de Melur. Lo ha manejado bien en mi ausencia; veo que incluso está cultivando pastel ahora. ¿Cuántas tardes podríamos haber pasado juntos si no me hubiera ido...?'

'Un momento, hay algo que me gustaría dibujar. Por favor, Melur, no dudes en interrumpirme si hay alguna tarea que deba hacerse. Pero... hace tanto tiempo que no encuentro inspiración, temo que se me escape si espero.'
Emmathron se pone a trabajar con su cuaderno de dibujo y su lápiz de cera, concentrándose intensamente en cada trazo que hace en el papel. Es casi extraño verlo trabajar sin detenerse a fruncir el ceño ante su creación.

'Déjalo en paz -- sé cómo es cuando el arte lo consume. Tiene esa mirada en los ojos, como si estuviera viendo, pero en realidad no está allí. Pasarán horas antes de que diga otra palabra.'
Una media sonrisa cruza su rostro.
'Puedes quedarte mientras tanto.'

'Intenté abandonar la Comarca una vez, cuando era mucho más joven y lamentablemente desprevenido. Mi abuela acababa de emprender otra de sus aventuras, y yo deseaba con todas mis fuerzas unirme a ella.
'Intenté seguirla desde la distancia, sin que ella lo supiera....'

'Esa fue la última vez que la vi. Así que me quedé en la Comarca, hasta que el misterio que dejó atrás comenzó a molestarme.
'Por supuesto, he estado desobedeciendo los deseos de mi abuela para resolver ese misterio. ¿Habría estado frustrada conmigo? ¿O orgullosa? Ambos, quizás.

'¿De qué estaba parloteando ese viejo enano? Puede que haya adivinado correctamente el nombre de la abuela, ¡pero nunca la vi actuar de manera imprudente! Debe estar recordando mal, confundiéndola con alguien de mala reputación.'
Haldo se suena.
'Bueno, ¡recojamos todo lo que necesitamos para poder salir de este clima!'

'Esta lista de ingredientes es un buen punto de partida, pero debo confesar que no puedo imaginar que alguno de ellos valga la pena. ¡Venir hasta aquí solo por el condimento! ¿En qué estaría pensando la abuela? Pero aquí estoy, siguiendo sus pasos solo para poder probar este plato de nuevo.
'Ahora solo queda encontrar y recolectar estos....'
'Tal vez encuentre todas mis respuestas aquí y no tenga necesidad de viajar más lejos. Eso reduciría drásticamente mis posibilidades de ver a otro oso, ¿no crees?'
'¿Cómo puede la gente soportar vivir así? Simplemente no lo entiendo....'

'¡Por fin!'
Los dientes de Haldo castañetean mientras lucha por decir la palabra.
'¡Me alegrará dejar todo esto atrás!'

'Ten la seguridad de que me he asegurado de que no haya nadie en casa nuevamente; todos deberían estar planeando la fiesta de cumpleaños de mi primo. Y la enormidad de esa tarea ciertamente los ocupará durante horas.'

'Lamento haber interrumpido tu descanso, ${PLAYER}. Viejos recuerdos de los tiempos que Rikháwi y yo pasamos aquí comenzaron a atormentarme, así que renuncié a dormir.
'No expliqué completamente por qué quería acampar aquí. Quería estar cerca del océano, pero más que eso: quería ver si todavía le tenía miedo.
'Por supuesto, cualquier buen marinero le teme al mar. Sin embargo, ese miedo nace del respeto. Mi miedo proviene de otro lugar: un terror paralizante que me invade cuando doy un solo paso en el agua. Yo... intenté ignorar ese sentimiento, como puedes ver. Pero...'
Ella suspira.
'¿Has tenido sueños con los muertos antes, ${PLAYER}?'

'Tengo un sueño que vuelve como las mareas, una y otra vez, de estar en una orilla sin nombre y vacía. Veo a Rikháwi de pie en el agua, lejos de la orilla, mirándome. Intento alcanzarla, pero solo me hundo en las profundidades. Entonces despierto.'
Una risa seca se escapa de ella, pero no hay humor en ella.
'No necesitas decirme lo que significan tales sueños.
'Durante una tormenta, el barco sufrió filtraciones en las cubiertas inferiores. Una carga pesada me atrapó la pierna e impidió que escapara. Luchar no sirvió de nada; el agua subía cada vez más. Pero Rikháwi me ayudó a liberarme, me dio mi vida a cambio de perder la suya. ¿Qué hemos hecho para merecer tales destinos?
'La tripulación y yo fuimos los únicos que la lloramos. Como yo, ella no tenía a nadie en tierra.
'Pasé el último año tratando de evitar pensar en ella. Sin embargo, cuanto más lo intentaba, más furiosos se volvían estos recuerdos. No me dejaban olvidar.
'Dime ${PLAYER}: ¿crees que la paz es posible para los vivos?'
Te quedas dormido...

'El mar todavía me asusta. Incluso mientras trabajaba en el barco, no podía ignorarlo: ese leve temor que me pica en la parte posterior de la mente. Depender tanto de una fuerza que fácilmente podría reclamar mi vida... que ha reclamado la vida de alguien cercano a mí.
'Me pregunto si esos sentimientos alguna vez desaparecerán. Tal vez se atenúen con el tiempo. Sin embargo, esta noche, permaneceré despierta y observaré las estrellas.
'Quédate un rato, si lo deseas. La noche es solitaria y no me importaría tu presencia.'

Mientras contemplas las estrellas juntos, el mundo silencioso que os rodea continúa su sueño.
El amanecer llega, antes de mucho tiempo.
Encuentras el saco de dormir de Golwen vacío. ¿Ha ido a la orilla del agua?

'Nuestra llegada aquí fue más tardía de lo que esperaba, pero no hay más culpable que yo misma. Debería haber tenido en cuenta mi pierna y el ritmo lento que impondría.
'Trabajaré rápidamente para preparar nuestros sacos de dormir y la fogata. Mientras tanto, debería haber ramas secas cerca para que las recojas.'
Golwen echa un vistazo al mar por encima del hombro y se limpia las palmas en los pantalones.
'Date prisa, antes de que caiga la oscuridad.'

Pronto, un fuego de campamento crepita alegremente sobre la arena.
'Esto mantendrá a raya el frío de la noche.'
Los ojos de Golwen ya han dejado el fuego crepitante, fijándose nuevamente en el mar.
'Creo que es hora de retirarse. Caminar hasta aquí requirió bastante esfuerzo, y agravar más mi pierna no sería lo ideal.
'Buenas noches, ${PLAYER}. Hasta la mañana.'

'Ahora bien, ¿cuánto tiempo debemos dejar las tortillas sobre el fuego?'

'Espero que ese tendero no haya causado demasiados problemas. Regatear no es... mi fuerte. Te agradezco por asumir esa carga. Permíteme romper los huevos.'
Golwen se pone a trabajar. Entra en un ritmo de romper dos huevos a la vez con destreza, un ritmo cómodo con el que parece estar bastante familiarizada. En este fugaz momento, su ceño, normalmente fruncido, se ha relajado.
Los dos pasan el resto de la comida comiendo en silencio.

Golwen mastica un bocado pensativamente y lo traga.
'Estoy... contenta de que hayamos podido hacer esto juntas. Ha pasado bastante tiempo desde la última vez que cociné esto yo misma. Más de un año, de hecho.
'Mantenía esta tradición con una amiga, para señalar el final de un viaje y el comienzo de otro. Obviamente, ya no es el caso.'
Ella guarda silencio y picotea el resto de su comida, frunciendo el ceño todo el tiempo.

'Espero que cocines mejor que yo. La vida de un marinero no exige nada más que \qcomestible.\q
'Primero...'
Suspira al ver la bulliciosa plaza del mercado.
'Por favor, consigue huevos del tendero. Haré espacio para que cocinemos en el Barrio de los Artesanos, al noreste.'

'Al menos esta historia tiene un final feliz.'
Los ojos brillantes del pájaro siguen cada movimiento de Rikháwi, pero no intenta evitar sus manos cuidadosas. Su respiración laboriosa expone aún más su estado de agotamiento.

Golwen rasca la parte inferior del mentón del gato, y su ceño normalmente rígido se suaviza.
'Qué criaturas tan nobles y hermosas. Cumplen con su deber en la caza de plagas, sin importar si nos acompañan en nuestros barcos o se quedan en los muelles.
'Espero que no te importe quedarte aquí un poco más. Mi pierna protesta ante la idea de dar otro paso.'

'No creo habértelo mostrado todavía.'
Golwen te entrega la flauta para que la examines: de madera, rudimentaria, pero aún bastante funcional.
'Fue tallada por una amiga mía. De hecho, ella talló todos nuestros instrumentos.'
Mientras contempla el mar, algo se le atraganta en la garganta. Traga con dificultad.
'Si no te importa -- mientras descansamos aquí, tengo una historia que contar sobre ella.
'Durante un viaje, un pájaro aterrizó bajo su cuidado....'

Golwen distraídamente pasa sus manos por el pelaje del gato que ronronea.
'Me temo que esta historia no tuvo un final feliz. Espero que tengas una mejor para compartir.'

A medida que cuentas tu historia, el tiempo se escapa entre las sombras que se profundizan de la tarde. Golwen no parece darse cuenta.
Es solo cuando terminas tu historia que finalmente habla.
'Gracias por complacerme, ${PLAYER}.
'Ahora, la naturaleza no es lugar para un gato. Seguramente una vida vagando por el puerto de Dol Amroth sería mejor. La llevaré a los pescadores allí, y ellos la colmarán con los frutos del mar.'

'¡Estoy salvado!'
Aunque Haldo ha dejado de temblar, el temblor en su voz permanece.
'M-muchas gracias, ${PLAYER}. L-lo lamento, que hayas tenido que presenciar una exhibición tan embarazosa de mi parte. No me llevo bien con los osos, y lo dejaré así.'

'D-deja que piense, deja que piense... ¿qué haría la abuela?'
Cierra los ojos con fuerza, concentrándose en alguna imagen en su mente.
'Ella... ella simplemente le pediría al oso que se fuera.'
Abre los ojos frunciendo el ceño.
'E-eso probablemente no funcionaría.
'T-tienes alguna idea, ${PLAYER}? ¿Deberíamos rugirle? ¿Intentar asustarlo? ¿Qué tal si -- '

La palabra sale como un chillido.
'¡Frambuesas!'
El pobre Haldo tiembla como una hoja azotada por el viento en una rama.
'Y-yo estaba picoteando...'
Con una mano temblorosa, saca unas frambuesas.
Podría ser mejor desechar estas frambuesas en otro lugar para alejar al oso. Intentas explicarle tu plan a Haldo, pero él no da señales de escucharte.
Debe haber algún lugar cerca del arroyo donde puedas depositar las bayas. Con suerte, el oso los dejará ir en paz.
'¿Podemos irnos ya? He tenido suficiente emoción por hoy.'
Escuchas los pesados pasos del oso. ¡Es hora de irse!
¡Este podría ser un buen lugar!

'Para ello, necesitaré quedarme en algún lugar lejos de mi familia. No pueden saber lo que estoy haciendo, pero su curiosidad debería estar satisfecha por ahora. Les conté una larga historia sobre un amigo muy enfermo, ya ves.
'Todo esto debe sonar bastante extraño para ti, pero por favor, considera mi solicitud.'

'Gracias por aceptar mi solicitud. Hay algunos objetos relacionados con el misterio que deberías examinar: pertenencias queridas que no me atrevo a sacar del smial de mi familia. Conociendo a mi familia, puede que pase un tiempo antes de que pueda encontrar un momento en que nadie esté en casa. Pero te lo haré saber.'

'El capitán puede haberme prohibido trabajar, pero seguramente no puede molestarse por la ayuda extra. Con suerte, mis acciones y tus palabras lo persuadirán de que estoy capacitada para regresar.'

La noche se pasa entre caras amigables y buena comida.

Suspira y cierra los ojos.
'No son los nervios lo que me afecta, sino la idea de interpretar esta canción con todos excepto Rikháwi. Durante el último año, he mantenido mi parte de la canción para mí misma; podría continuar haciéndolo fácilmente, para siempre. Sin embargo, eso no puede ser lo que ella querría para mí.'

'Hace años, Mullen y yo estábamos de excursión en algún lugar más alejado. Una ventisca nos sorprendió. Todo lo que podíamos ver era blanco, blanco, blanco. Apenas podíamos ver nuestras propias manos frente a nosotros. Y mientras avanzábamos a tientas hacia lo que parecía ser una cueva, ¡Mullen tropezó con un cuerpo!
'Era un Hombre, perdido y congelado, pero aún vivo. Con la fuerza que nos quedaba, lo arrastramos a la cueva, y Mullen se puso a trabajar de inmediato. Mientras yo lo atendía, ella cocinó una comida con nuestras escasas provisiones. Esa comida lo trajo de vuelta de la muerte, me atrevería a decir.
'Una vez que la ventisca amainó, lo llevamos a un pueblo cercano. No escapó de esa ventisca sin heridas, pero al menos tenía su vida.'

'Nosotros... lo hicimos. No es exactamente como lo recuerdo, pero está muy, muy, muy cerca. Si no lo hubiera cocinado yo mismo, habría jurado que lo hizo la abuela.'
Haldo entrecierra los ojos ante un bocado de cerdo, la curiosidad tiñendo sus rasgos más que la decepción.
'Quizás mi memoria de este plato ya no sea fiable, o falta algo más.
'Pero está bien. Estoy lo suficientemente satisfecho como para declarar resuelto este misterio y continuar. Hay otros platos que me gustaría probar, otros lugares que me gustaría visitar. ¡Quizás otro viaje al norte sea necesario!'
Delante de ti hay un plato de cerdo y rábanos, coronado con un condimento bien viajado. Con un bocado, saboreas una mezcla armónica de sabores suculentos.
'Nunca olvidaré esta noche.'

'Debo hacer algunos preparativos, por supuesto. Por ejemplo, tendré que decirle a mi familia que invité a un amigo de la abuela. Los rumores y chismes no serán agradables, pero no dejaré que sigan fingiendo que ella nunca existió.

Suspira.
'En el fondo, ya lo sabía, pero... saberlo no hace que las cosas sean más fáciles.
'Puedo indicarte dónde ella y yo cosechamos stingóst, pero me gustaría acompañarte, si no te importa. Por el bien de los viejos tiempos.'

'¿Cómo pudo la abuela no haber mencionado nunca a Gisti? Viajaba con ella. ¡Conocía su flor favorita! ¡Me conocía a mí! Había toda una vida allí, y ella nunca me lo contó. Pensaba que no tenía lugar en la Comarca, pero yo estaba allí...'
Hace una pausa.
'Yo estaba allí, y también el resto de nuestra familia.
'Tenían miedo de ella, ¿no? Miedo de sus historias sobre lugares lejanos. Todavía tienen miedo. Si supieran lo que estoy tramando....
'¿Qué piensas de todo este asunto, ${PLAYER}?'

'Puede que sea así, pero todo lo que hizo pertenece al pasado. Lo único que me queda son sus recetas.'
Haldo saca su pañuelo y se seca las lágrimas que se le forman en los ojos.
'Me... me gustaría regresar y hablar un poco más con Gisti. Sus historias quizás me hagan bien.'

'¡Excelente! Si quieres, toma asiento, yo prepararé esto y lo echaré en la olla!'

'${PLAYER}, ¿ves todas esas cosas esparcidas? ¡Si esos Hombres son bandidos, lo están haciendo muy mal!'
Él duda.
'Me defenderás si son bandidos, ¿verdad? Porque de lo contrario, deberíamos detenernos y echar una mano. ¡Si mi abuela se enterara de que dejé pasar hambre a unos extraños, me daría una buena reprimenda!'

'Un guiso debería ser lo suficientemente fácil de cocinar aquí. ¿Puedes cazar conejos?'
El rostro de Haldo se ilumina ante los asentimientos de los viajeros.
'¡Entonces podemos hacer guiso de conejo! Mientras tanto, construiré un fuego para nosotros.
'${PLAYER}, vi algunos manzanos y champiñones al otro lado del río. ¿Podrías recoger algunos de ambos?'
Baja la voz a un susurro para que solo tú puedas escucharlo.
'Parecen ser personas decentes y honestas. Me atrevo a decir que no tendremos que preocuparnos después de todo.'
'¡Date prisa, antes de que cambien de opinión!'
'Aquí tienes: ¡guiso de conejo! Desafortunadamente, no hay muchos condimentos, pero tengo fe en la receta de mi abuela.'

'¡Qué experiencia tan reveladora! El peligro acecha en cada esquina fuera de la Comarca...'
Haldo tiembla.
'Acabo de dar la receta de guiso de mi abuela a dos bandidos, pero... no creo que ella estuviera decepcionada conmigo. ¿Es eso extraño?'
Frunce el ceño mientras observa los restos del fallido robo de los bandidos.
'Quizás necesitaban esa pequeña bondad.
'¿Por qué no regresamos por donde vinimos? ¡Odiaría toparme con nuestros amigos bandidos de nuevo!'

'¡La planificación del cumpleaños de mi primo debería haber llevado mucho más tiempo! Mi familia no puede verme aquí ahora; ¡tendrán tantas preguntas sobre por qué estoy aquí y qué estoy haciendo con un extraño!
'¡Espera! -- No pueden verme ellos, ¡pero tú sí! ¡Finge que mi primo te contrató para llamar a todos de vuelta! ¡Diles que la planificación del cumpleaños no ha terminado!
'Una vez que eso esté hecho, encuéntrame cerca del molino al sureste.'

'¡Todo hecho! Hiciste un trabajo admirable. Yo, eh, espero que tus brazos no estén adoloridos. Ahora...'
Haldo toma con cuidado una pizca de un condimento y lo prueba. Pasan unos momentos de silencio mientras frunce el ceño concentrado. Luego pasa al siguiente condimento y repite los mismos movimientos. No es hasta después de que vierte todos los condimentos juntos y prueba la mezcla que finalmente se vuelve a ti.
'Después de todo, los enanos de Gondamon tenían conocimientos valiosos que compartir. Aun así, falta algo.'

'¡Me atrevo a decir que nadie me vio! ¡Eres un mentiroso natural! No, no, perdóname, eso estuvo mal dicho... um...

'Golwen se equivoca. No me preocupan sus capacidades, sino el estado de su mente. Ha comenzado a pensar en sí misma solo en términos de su utilidad para el barco y sus funciones. Esperaba que enviarla lejos la obligara a reconsiderar, pero parece que mis acciones solo han empeorado las cosas. Necesita tiempo para sanar, lejos del mar.
'No le quedan seres queridos en tierra. No escuchará a sus compañeros de tripulación, y ni siquiera yo puedo detenerla. Sin embargo, me pregunto, ${PLAYER}, si un extraño como tú puede.
'Si tienes la intención de ser su amigo, entonces te encomiendo este deber: asegúrate de que pase algún tiempo simplemente viviendo.'

Golwen despliega una parte de la vela para mostrar su trabajo: una colección de parches y costuras cuidadosas que abarcan la tela, asegurando el funcionamiento continuo de la vela para futuros viajes.
'El capitán entiende el valor del trabajo honesto. Háblale ahora, y me permitirá regresar a la tripulación.'

'Las órdenes deben ser claras y concisas: haz esto, repara aquello. Una orden de descansar no tiene sentido. ¡Uf! Sin embargo, es una orden que debo seguir; la cuestión es cómo. Sin el barco, no tengo nada que hacer y ningún lugar a donde ir.
'Tus esfuerzos por persuadir al capitán pueden no haber tenido éxito, pero te estoy agradecida de todos modos.
'Ven. No me queda mucho aquí, al menos por ahora.'
'Volveré algún día. Debo hacerlo.'

'Tal vez un paseo por los alrededores de la Comarca me haga bien. Estará lo suficientemente cerca de casa para que no entre en pánico, pero lo suficientemente lejos para que todo parezca extraño.

La receta requiere cerdo y nabos como ingredientes principales. Aunque la receta parece completa a primera vista, te das cuenta de que las instrucciones solo hacen referencias vagas a los condimentos. La lista de ingredientes no contiene información relevante.

'Mi abuela solía cocinar esto para mí porque era la única manera de que comiera nabos. He estado tratando de completar la receta durante años, pero no puedo replicar la mezcla de condimentos. Tampoco puedo describir con precisión cómo sabía: todo lo que tengo son recuerdos vagos.
'Si los enanos son la única pista que tenemos, entonces haremos planes para visitarlos. Podemos preguntar sobre los condimentos locales, con suerte obtener las respuestas que he estado buscando y luego irnos de inmediato.
'Puede ser prudente viajar a la ciudad más cercana. Preferiría no alejarme demasiado de la Comarca si no es necesario.'
'Quizá finalmente resuelva este misterio.'

Una cubierta de cuero gastada y descolorida mantiene unidas las páginas de este diario. Las páginas en sí están en mucho mejor estado, mostrando hojas y flores secas que han sido cuidadosamente prensadas sobre el papel.
La mayoría son ciertamente locales de la Comarca; otras provienen de otros lugares, particularmente de la región norte de Ered Luin.

Estas notas consisten en páginas sueltas, pero ordenadas, con información sobre varias plantas y sus aplicaciones en la cocina. Todo lo mencionado parece ser local, pero la autora detalla meticulosamente todo lo que hay que saber sobre cada planta. Es como si estuviera dirigiendo estas notas a alguien que nunca ha puesto un pie en la Comarca.

Dentro de esta caja de madera anodina, descubres trozos de pergamino. Cada uno presenta una receta escrita con letra pequeña y ordenada.
Un salpicado de manchas y borrones adorna los bordes de las recetas, señalando un uso frecuente en el pasado. Dudas de que ese sea el caso ahora.

'¿Algunas de esas plantas del diario venían del norte? ¿De donde viven los enanos? Mi abuela a menudo salía de la Comarca para recoger y probar nuevos ingredientes para la cocina, pero eso es todo lo que sé. A nadie le interesaba averiguar a dónde iba o qué hacía. Ni ella estaba dispuesta a decirme nada.
'¿Pero por qué ir al norte? ¡Seguramente los enanos no tienen nada que justifique viajar tan lejos de casa!
'Es que... simplemente no puedo imaginar que haya algo mejor allá afuera que lo que ya tenemos aquí. ¡Vaya, casi me atacan bandidos y un oso, un oso! ¡Y estos incidentes ocurrieron justo a las afueras de la Comarca!'
Haldo hace una pausa para respirar profundamente y calmar su creciente angustia.
'Perdón de nuevo... qué vergüenza. Si voy a resolver este misterio, necesito ser tan valiente como lo fue mi abuela.
'Hablando del misterio...'
Rebusca en la caja de recetas antes de sacar una en particular.
'Esta es, justo aquí.'

'Debemos tener tiempo de sobra antes de que mi familia regrese. Desaprobarían enormemente si supieran lo que estoy haciendo, y lo más probable es que estropeen mis esfuerzos. ¡Los rumores dañarían nuestra reputación, ya ves, y nos importa mucho.
'Aunque es más que eso...'

Haldo saca algunos objetos de contenedores polvorientos.
'Perdona el polvo; lo mantengo como elemento disuasorio. Nadie se ha molestado en hurgar entre mis cosas, pero nunca se puede ser demasiado cuidadoso. ¡Me molestaría mucho si lograran poner sus manos en las pertenencias de mi abuela ahora!
'Aquí tienes. Pensé que te dejaría echar un vistazo a sus cosas, por si notas algo que yo no haya visto.'
